* Computational Metrics: Employ tools such as BLEU, BERTScore, and embedding distance to assess fidelity to the original and to high-quality existing translations.
* Iterative Feedback: Integrate scholarly and computational feedback into model refinement cycles.

Deliverables

1. Open-Source Framework: Codebase for neural-semantic mapping, conceptual embedding, and translation generation.
2. Annotated Neural Corpus: A publicly accessible, ethically anonymized dataset linking brain activity to Qur’anic verse comprehension for 50 pilot verses.
3. Theological-Linguistic Evaluation Toolkit: Tools to assess alignment between AI outputs and both linguistic structure and doctrinal meaning.
4. Peer-Reviewed Publications: Articles in leading journals across AI, neuroscience, digital humanities, and Islamic studies.
5. Public Engagement: Host interdisciplinary symposia and scholar-ethicist workshops to disseminate findings and explore implications for faith communities and AI governance.

Key Scientific and Ethical Considerations

* Framing Divine Intent: This project does not claim to access divine knowledge directly. Rather, it tests the hypothesis that divine intent is partially encoded in conceptual structures that can be approximated through cognitive and semantic analysis.
* Technical Feasibility: Acknowledges the current limits of semantic decoding from brain data. The project is structured in scalable pilot phases to ensure iterative validation and practical refinement.
* Bias Mitigation: Proposes use of adversarial debiasing, Qur’an-centric pretraining, and theological pluralism in model development to reduce sectarian or ideological skew.
* Transparency and Ethics: Ensures transparency in neural data handling, theological boundaries, and interdisciplinary interpretation.

Conclusion

This proposal introduces a novel, ethically grounded, and scientifically feasible framework to pursue meaning-aligned Qur’anic translation informed by both human cognition and AI capabilities. By embedding this endeavor within rigorous theological, technical, and ethical standards, the project aspires to redefine how sacred texts can be respectfully and accurately translated in the digital age.

6. Estimated Budget (in $1000)

| Item | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 | Total |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Salaries (10 researchers) | 500 | 500 | 500 | 1,500 |
| fMRI/EEG Equipment Access & Ops | 100 | 100 | 50 | 250 |
| AI Infrastructure & Model Training | 150 | 200 | 150 | 500 |
| Interdisciplinary Workshops & Scholar Review | 50 | 50 | 50 | 150 |
| Admin & Reporting | 50 | 50 | 50 | 150 |
| **Total Estimate** | | | | **2,550** |

Terminology

* AI-Driven Semantic Modeling: This involves using artificial intelligence (especially deep learning models like transformers) to analyze language and build meaning-based representations of text. Semantic models can be trained to match patterns in neural data with linguistic concepts, helping to decode how ideas are represented in the brain.
* BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) is used to understand text contextually by reading it bidirectionally (both left-to-right and right-to-left). It is trained using Masked Language Modeling (MLM) that randomly masks some words and trains the model to predict them and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP) that determines whether one sentence follows another.
* BERTScore is an automatic evaluation metric for comparing two texts (e.g., a translation vs. a reference) by computing semantic similarity between their token embeddings using models like BERT.
* BOLD (Blood Oxygenation Level-Dependent) is brain signal When reciting the Quran.
* Cognitiveeuroscience: The study of how the brain enables us to understand language, meaning, and thought. It involves recording neural activity (e.g., via fMRI or EEG) while someone is reading, hearing, or thinking about Qur’anic verses.
* Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors in a high-dimensional space. It is commonly used to compare the semantic similarity between two texts after they have been converted into embedding vectors (numerical representations of meaning).
* EEG (electroencephalogram) is a test that measures the electrical activity of the brain. During the test, small metal discs called electrodes are placed on the scalp to detect these electrical signals, which are then recorded and displayed as brain wave patterns.
* fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) is a type of brain imaging technique that measures brain activity by detecting changes in blood flow.
* Hermeneutics (علم التأويل / أصول التفسير): Is the method of interpretation, especially of sacred texts like the Qur’an by providing the theological, linguistic, and contextual framework to ensure that any interpretation (or translation) is faithful to the intended message.
* mT5 (Multilingual Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer): It generates text across many languages in a unified text-to-text format by using cases involving translation, summarization, question answering across 100+ languages.
* Transformer is a neural network architecture.

Key Brain Regions and their functions

| Function | Brain Area |
| :--- | :--- |
| Thought / Intention (language independent) | Prefrontal cortex, angular gyrus |
| Semantic memory | Inferior parietal lobule |
| Language formulation | Broca’s area (language-specific motor planning) |
| Phonological buffer | Left inferior frontal gyrus |
| Speech articulation | Motor cortex (mouth, tongue control) |

title: Theme of Surat Al-Qiyamah (القِیَامَة) (The Resurrection) (75)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Al-Qiyamah (القِیَامَة) (The Resurrection) (75)

Surah Al-Qiyamah offers a powerful reminder of the reality of resurrection and the certainty of divine accountability. It serves as a…
content:
Theme of Surat Al-Qiyamah (القِیَامَة) (The Resurrection) (75)

Surah Al-Qiyamah offers a powerful reminder of the reality of resurrection and the certainty of divine accountability. It serves as a basic resource in Dawah to refute those who deny the afterlife. It offers strong arguments to prove not only the possibility but also the necessity of resurrection, using rational, moral, and spiritual arguments.

The Surah begins with a powerful oath affirms the certainty of the day of resurrection and the inescapability of its judgment:

لَآ أُقۡسِمُ بِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ (١)
By the Day of Resurrection. (75:1)

The Surah then confronts the mindset of those who reject resurrection—not due to intellectual doubt, but due to a desire to live without moral restraint:

أَيَحۡسَبُ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ أَلَّن نَّجۡمَعَ عِظَامَهُ ۥ (٣) بَلَىٰ قَـٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُ ۥ (٤) بَلۡ يُرِيدُ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ لِيَفۡجُرَ أَمَامَهُ ۥ (٥)
Does man think that We will not assemble his bones (3). 4 In fact, We are able to make whole his very fingertips. (4) Yet man wants to deny what lies ahead of him. (75:3-5)

This response emphasizes not only the feasibility of resurrection but Allah’s precision in re-creating every detail—down to the fingertips.

The Surah then shifts to the Day of Judgment, where each person will be confronted with their deeds:

يُنَبَّؤُاْ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ يَوۡمَٮِٕذِۭ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ (١٣) بَلِ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌ۬ (١٤) وَلَوۡ أَلۡقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ ۥ (١٥) لَا تُحَرِّكۡ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعۡجَلَ بِهِۦۤ (١٦) إِنَّ عَلَيۡنَا جَمۡعَهُ ۥ وَقُرۡءَانَهُ ۥ (١٧) فَإِذَا قَرَأۡنَـٰهُ فَٱتَّبِعۡ قُرۡءَانَهُ ۥ (١٨) ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيۡنَا بَيَانَهُ ۥ (١٩)
On that Day, man will be told what he put first and what he put last. (13) Truly, man is a clear witness against himself, (14) despite all the excuses he may put forward. (15) Do not move your tongue to receive in hurry. (16) It is our responsibility to collect it and read it. (17) When We read it follow our readings. (18) Then it is our responsibility to make it clear. (75:13-19)

Note: Verses 16 to 19 are often interpreted as addressing the Prophet’s eagerness to memorize the revelation by trying to repeat the revelation while it is still underway. He is told not to rush in repeating the revelation, as Allah will ensure its collection and explanation in your heart. However, the verses could also be seen, in context, as describing the Day of Judgment, when the record is read and the person and he is asked to listen in silence until it is fully recited and explained:

The Surah paints a vivid scene of death for those who denied the truth:

كَلَّآ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلتَّرَاقِىَ (٢٦) وَقِيلَ مَنۡۜ رَاقٍ۬ (٢٧) وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡفِرَاقُ (٢٨) وَٱلۡتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ (٢٩) إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ ٱلۡمَسَاقُ (٣٠)
“Truly, when the soul reaches the collarbone; (26) when it is said, ‘Could any charm-healer save him now?’ (27) when he knows it is the final parting; (28) when the legs are intertwined together: (29) (it will be said to him) on that day you will be driven to your Lord.” (75:26-30)

This moment of helplessness and final realization is a warning to all who ignore the truth in life. The dying soul is surrounded by people, but no one can help—only Allah remains.

The Surah concludes by reinforcing its opening message: man will not be left without purpose or accountability. The final verses invite reflection on human origin to prove Allah’s power to resurrect:

أَيَحۡسَبُ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ أَن يُتۡرَكَ سُدًى (٣٦) أَلَمۡ يَكُ نُطۡفَةً۬ مِّن مَّنِىٍّ۬ يُمۡنَىٰ (٣٧) ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً۬ فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ (٣٨) فَجَعَلَ مِنۡهُ ٱلزَّوۡجَيۡنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰٓ (٣٩) أَلَيۡسَ ذَٲلِكَ بِقَـٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحۡـِۧىَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ (٤٠)
Does man think he will be left unchecked? (36) Was he not just a drop of spilt-out sperm, (37) which became a clinging form, which was created and made in due proportion. (38) and from it made the two sexes, the male and the female, (39) Does He who can do this not able to bring the dead back to life? (75:36-40)

title: Theme of Surat Al-Muzzammil (المُزمّل) (Enfolded) (73:
excerpt: The main theme of Surat Al-Muzzammil is the essential training for bearing the weighty responsibility of delivering Allah’s message. This training builds physical strength, spiritual discipline,…
content:
The main theme of Surat Al-Muzzammil is the essential training for bearing the weighty responsibility of delivering Allah’s message. This training builds physical strength, spiritual discipline, patience, and unwavering trust in Allah. These qualities are needed to endure opposition and tolerate the expected challenges from the detractors. requirements are necessary to face the expected adversity and challenges from the relentless opposition. The primary method of this preparation is long night prayers.

The Surah begins by calling for standing in prayer at night as a means of spiritual fortification and clarity of mind to carry the weighty message and fulfil your prolonged occupation by day:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمُزَّمِّلُ (١) قُمِ ٱلَّيۡلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ (٢) نِّصۡفَهُ ۥۤ أَوِ ٱنقُصۡ مِنۡهُ قَلِيلاً (٣) أَوۡ زِدۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ تَرۡتِيلاً (٤) إِنَّا سَنُلۡقِى عَلَيۡكَ قَوۡلاً۬ ثَقِيلاً (٥) إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱلَّيۡلِ هِىَ أَشَدُّ وَطۡـًٔ۬ا وَأَقۡوَمُ قِيلاً (٦) إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّہَارِ سَبۡحً۬ا طَوِيلاً۬ (٧)

“O you who wrapped in your cloak, (1) Arise [to pray] throughout the night, except a small part of it, (2) Half of it, or make it a little less, (3) or a little more and recite the Quran slowly and distinctly. (4) Indeed, We will send down to you a weighty discourse. (5) Truly, rising by night (for prayers) is more effective on (purifying) the self and most suitable for understanding the word. (6) Surely, in daytime, you are kept busy for long periods.” (73:1-7)

The Prophet is instructed and thus all who are engaged in Dawah, to be patient and to leave the disbelievers to Allah’s judgment:

وَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱهۡجُرۡهُمۡ هَجۡرً۬ا جَمِيلاً۬ (١٠) وَذَرۡنِى وَٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ أُوْلِى ٱلنَّعۡمَةِ وَمَهِّلۡهُمۡ قَلِيلاً (١١) إِنَّ لَدَيۡنَآ أَنكَالاً۬ وَجَحِيمً۬ا (١٢) وَطَعَامً۬ا ذَا غُصَّةٍ۬ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمً۬ا (١٣)

Bear patiently what they say, and part with them in a beautiful manner. (10) And leave to Me those who deny the truth, the people of luxury, and give them respite for a little while. (11)  We have fetters and blazing ﬁre, (12) food that chokes, and agonizing torment in store for them.” (73:10-13)

The Surah ends by Allah acknowledging the difficulty of sustained lengthy night prayer and thus lightening the initial command, allowing flexibility for prayer due to people’s varying circumstances and obligations and reminding believers of what lies ahead:

إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعۡلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدۡنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَنِصۡفَهُ ۥ وَثُلُثَهُ ۥ وَطَآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَعَكَ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّہَارَ‌ۚ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحۡصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ‌ۖ فَٱقۡرَءُواْ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ‌ۚ عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرۡضَىٰ‌ۙ وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضۡرِبُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَبۡتَغُونَ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۙ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ فَٱقۡرَءُواْ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنۡهُ‌ۚ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنً۬ا‌ۚ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُواْ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنۡ خَيۡرٍ۬ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيۡرً۬ا وَأَعۡظَمَ أَجۡرً۬ا‌ۚ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمُۢ (٢٠)

“Indeed, your Lord is well aware that you spend nearly two-thirds of the night at prayer –– sometimes half, sometimes a third –– as do some of your followers. Allah values the night and the day. He knows that you will not be able to keep up doing in regular way, and He has turned to you in mercy, so recite as much of the Qur’an as is easy for you. He knows that some of you may be sick, and others travelling through the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and yet others ﬁghting in Allah’s way. Therefore, recite as much as is easy for you, keep up the prayer, pay the Zakah, and advance to Allah a good loan. Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allah better and greater in reward. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful. (73:20)

Even after Allah made the night prayers lighter and rendered them optional, the companions of the Prophet continued to observe them, recognizing their immense spiritual value. A powerful example of this is seen in the life of Caliph Omar ibn Al-Khattab. Despite ruling over a vast empire and bearing great responsibilities during the day, he remained committed to worship during the night.

On one occasion, his governor in Azerbaijan came to visit him and arrived in Madinah late at night. Not wanting to disturb the Caliph at home, he went to the mosque instead. There, in the darkness, he saw a man praying and overheard him saying:

ربي هل قبلت توبتي فأهنئ نفسي أو رددتها فأعزيها.

“My Lord, if You have accepted my repentance, then let me rejoice; but if You have rejected it, then let me console myself.”The governor asked, “Who are you, may Allah have mercy on you?”The man replied, “I am Omar, the Leader of the Believers.”

The governor, surprised, said, “I thought you would be sleeping, so I didn’t want to disturb you at home. O Leader of the Believers, don’t you sleep at night?”

Omar responded:

إني إن نمت ليلي كله أضعت نفسي أمام ربي ، وإن نمت نهاري أضعت رعيتي.

“If I sleep all night, I neglect my duty to my Lord; and if I sleep all day, I neglect my duty to my people.”

Appendix: Night Prayers and the 40% Rule

When your mind urges you to quit—due to exhaustion, stress, or mental fatigue—you’ve likely only used about 40% of your true potential. The remaining 60% is often blocked by mental resistance, not physical limitation. This rule is about training your mind to recognize that discomfort is no danger — it’s a signal that growth is taking place.

Application Examples:

Before Fajr:The alarm rings an hour before Fajr. You’re drained and tempted to stay in bed. Remind yourself:“This is just my mind resisting. I’m only at 40%.”Recite  some dhikr and Istighfar for a minute and  get up, and begin your Tahajjud.

Studying or Work:After 90 minutes of deep focus, your mind starts to drift. Instead of stopping, take a quick 5-minute break. Then commit to another 30 focused minutes. Often, breakthroughs and best ideas come just after that mental quit point.

title: Theme of Surat Al-Muddathir (المدثر) (The one enveloped) (74)
excerpt: Following the call to spiritual training in Surat Al-Muzzammil through night prayers, Surat Al-Muddathir marks the beginning of the Prophet’s (PBUH) public mission. It opens with a divine command to…
content:
Following the call to spiritual training in Surat Al-Muzzammil through night prayers, Surat Al-Muddathir marks the beginning of the Prophet’s (PBUH) public mission. It opens with a divine command to arise and deliver the message, emphasizing the importance of both inner purification and outward presentation in Dawah:

ـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمُدَّثِّرُ (١) قُمۡ فَأَنذِرۡ (٢) وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرۡ (٣) وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرۡ (٤) وَٱلرُّجۡزَ فَٱهۡجُرۡ (٥) وَلَا تَمۡنُن تَسۡتَكۡثِرُ (٦) وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصۡبِرۡ (٧)

“O you wrapped in your cloak, (1) stand up and warn, (2) proclaim the greatness of your Lord; (3) purify your clothes; (4) avoid all impurity; (5) do not do a favor to anyone expecting more in return, (6) and be patient for the sake of your Lord.” (74:1-7)

The Surah then shifts to warning about the Day of Judgment:

فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِى ٱلنَّاقُورِ (٨) فَذَٲلِكَ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ يَوۡمٌ عَسِيرٌ (٩) عَلَى ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ غَيۡرُ يَسِيرٍ۬ (١٠)

“When the Trumpet sounds, (8) that day will be a difficult day, (9) Not easy for the disbelievers.” (74:8-10)

The Surah vividly describes Hellfire and issues a stern warning to arrogant deniers of the Qur’an:

سَأُصۡلِيهِ سَقَرَ (٢٦) وَمَآ أَدۡرَٮٰكَ مَا سَقَرُ (٢٧) لَا تُبۡقِى وَلَا تَذَرُ (٢٨) لَوَّاحَةٌ۬ لِّلۡبَشَرِ (٢٩) عَلَيۡہَا تِسۡعَةَ عَشَرَ (٣٠)

“I will throw him into Saqar (Hell). (26) What made you know what Saqar is? (27) It spares nothing and leaves nothing; (28) it scorches the ﬂesh of humans. (29) Appointed on it nineteen (angels).” (74:26-30)

While some books of Tafsir link these verses to the actions of Al-Waleed ibn Al-Mughirah (the chief of the Banu Makhzum clan), this person is not the cause of their revelation. Rather, his actions fit the pattern the verses describe and serve as a warning to anyone who behaves like him.

The Surah draws attention to number 19 which is the number of angels guarding Hell. The significance of Number 19 is discussed in the Appendix.

The Surah emphasizes personal accountability, quoting the confessions of those in Hell:

مَا سَلَڪَكُمۡ فِى سَقَرَ (٤٢) قَالُواْ لَمۡ نَكُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُصَلِّينَ (٤٣) وَلَمۡ نَكُ نُطۡعِمُ ٱلۡمِسۡكِينَ (٤٤) وَڪُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ ٱلۡخَآٮِٕضِينَ (٤٥) وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ (٤٦) حَتَّىٰٓ أَتَٮٰنَا ٱلۡيَقِينُ (٤٧)

“What brought you into Sakar (Hell)? (42) They will reply: ‘We were not among those who prayed. (33) and we did not feed the poor, (44) and we indulged in false/vain talks with those who indulged in them.  (45) and we denied the Day of Judgement (46) until the Certain End came upon us.” (74: 42-47)

The Surah concludes with affirming the divine nature of the Quran:

ڪَلَّآ إِنَّهُ ۥ تَذۡكِرَةٌ۬ (٥٤) فَمَن شَآءَ ذَڪَرَهُ ۥ (٥٥) وَمَا يَذۡكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ هُوَ أَهۡلُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ وَأَهۡلُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِ (٥٦)

“Truly this (Quran) is a reminder. (54) Let whoever wishes to remember: (55) they will not heed unless Allah wills.  He is the only one worthy of being heeded and He is the One worthy of granting forgiveness.” (74:54-56)

Appendix: The significance of Number 19

In Surat Al-Mudathir (73), In Surat Al-Muddathir, Allah highlights the number 19, stating it is the number of angels appointed to guard Hell:

عَلَيۡہَا تِسۡعَةَ عَشَرَ (٣٠)

Over it are nineteen (angels). (73:30)

Allah explains that this number serves multiple purposes:

وَمَا جَعَلۡنَآ أَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةً۬‌ۙ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا عِدَّتَہُمۡ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةً۬ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيَسۡتَيۡقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَيَزۡدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِيمَـٰنً۬ا‌ۙ وَلَا يَرۡتابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ‌ۙ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِہِم مَّرَضٌ۬ وَٱلۡكَـٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِہَـٰذَا مَثَلاً۬‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَہۡدِى مَن يَشَآءُ‌ۚ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَمَا هِىَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡبَشَرِ (٣١)

And We did not make wardens of the Fire but angels and did not make their number (number 19) but as a trial for the disbelievers, so that the people of the book (Jews and Christians) will be certain (about the Quran) and the believers will increase in belief, and that  no doubts may be left for the people of the Book and the believers.  And so that those with disease in their hearts and the disbelievers will say, “What has Allah meant by this example?  Thus, Allah lets go astray whom He wills, and guides whom He wills. And no one knows the soldiers of your Lord but He. This is nothing else but a Reminder for mankind.” (Al-Muddathir 74:31)

Key points form the verses:

1. These are the first revealed verses in which Allah mentions the people of the book (Jews and Christians).
2. These verses include the first revealed number in the Quran, and this is number 19.  (Note: There are 38 individual numbers mentioned in the Quran, 30 are whole numbers and 8 are fractions)
3. Allah mentioned 4 purposes for this number:
    1. A test for the disbelievers.
    2. Certainty for the people of the book regarding the divine nature of the Quran.
    3. Strengthening faith of believers.
    4. Removal of doubts from hearts.
4. A warning to those who dismiss the number due spiritual disease.
5. Affirm that only Allah knows the extent of His forces

وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ (٣١)

And no one knows the soldiers your Lord but He.”  (Al-Muddathir 74:31)

While many researchers focus on mathematical patterns involving 19, the verses imply a message accessible to believers and the People of the Book, even without Arabic or technical analysis.

Consider this: among all women, only Maryam (Mary) is mentioned by name in the Quran, and she is honored with an entire Surah—Surah Maryam, which is Chapter 19 of the Quran.

Maryam’s name appears 34 times in the Quran: 23 times in relation to ‘Isa (Jesus), and 11 times by herself.

In Surah 19, her name first appears in verse 16:

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ مَرۡيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتۡ مِنۡ أَهۡلِهَا مَكَانً۬ا شَرۡقِيًّ۬ا (١٦)

“And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her people to a place facing East.” (Maryam 19:16)

And the last mention of her name in this Surah is in verse 34.

ذَٲلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ‌ۚ قَوۡلَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ يَمۡتَرُونَ (٣٤)

“That is Jesus, son of Mary. (it is) a statement of truth, about which they are disputing (Maryam 19:34)

From verse 16 to 34 = 19 verses

Thus, Maryam’s story is told in exactly 19 verses — in Surah 19. This simple and observable pattern may be what Allah refers to as a reminder for the People of the Book.

Could Number 19 Also Symbolize Divine Forces? The verse concludes:

وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَمَا هِىَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡبَشَرِ (٣١)

And no one knows the soldiers of your Lord but He. This is nothing else but a Reminder for mankind.”  (Al-Muddathir 74:31)

Some reflections link 19 to historical calamities that shook humanity:

• COVID-19 pandemic.
• The Black Death peaked in 1349 (19 × 71).
• The Spanish Flu hit hard in 1919.

Could these be reminders from Allah—forces that awaken human awareness of divine power and the Day of Reckoning?

Is it all just coincidence? Or is 19 a sign, a key, and a call to reflect?

title: Theme of Surat Nuh (Nuh) (نُوح) (71)
excerpt: Surat Nuh highlights the unwavering patience, persistence, and dedication of Prophet Nuh (Noah) in calling his people to the worship of Allah. Despite his tireless efforts, the Surah captures the…
content:
Surat Nuh highlights the unwavering patience, persistence, and dedication of Prophet Nuh (Noah) in calling his people to the worship of Allah. Despite his tireless efforts, the Surah captures the moment when he concludes that neither his people nor their descendants will believe, ultimately asking Allah to destroy them.

The Surah opens with the divine mission common to all prophets: to warn their people of the consequences of rejecting Allah’s message:

إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦۤ أَنۡ أَنذِرۡ قَوۡمَكَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ۬ (١) قَالَ يَـٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّى لَكُمۡ نَذِيرٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ (٢) أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ (٣)

“Indeed, We sent Nuh (Noah) to his people (saying): ‘Warn your people before a painful punishment befalls them.’” (1) He said: O my people, I am a clear warner to you (2) that you should worship Allah, be mindful of Him, and obey me.” (71:1-3)

Prophet Nuh invited his people consistently, day and night, in public and in private. He promised them Allah’s forgiveness, blessings, and prosperity if they would repent. Yet, they rejected his message with stubborn defiance:

قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِى لَيۡلاً۬ وَنَهَارً۬ا (٥) فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ dُعَآءِىٓ إِلَّا فِرَارً۬ا (٦) وَإِنِّى ڪُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمۡ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِہِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَہُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارً۬ا (٧) ثُمَّ إِنِّى دَعَوۡتُہُمۡ جِهَارً۬ا (٨) ثُمَّ إِنِّىٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارً۬ا (٩)

“He said: ‘O my Lord! My Lord, I have called my people night and day.’” (5) “Yet the more I call them, the further they run away (from the truth).” (6) “Every time I call them, so that You may forgive them, they thrust their ﬁngers into their ears, cover their faces with their garments, persist in their rejection, and grow more insolent and arrogant” (7) “I called them openly. (8) I spoke to them publicly and privately.” (71:5-9)

He urged them to seek Allah’s forgiveness, assuring them of abundant blessings:

فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ غَفَّارً۬ا (١٠) يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارً۬ا (١١) وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٲلٍ۬ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡہَـٰرً۬ا (١٢)

“I said (to them): Seek forgiveness from your Lord, verily, He is Most-Forgiving; (10) He will send down rain from the sky to you in abundance, (11) and will provide you with wealth and children, and grant you gardens and rivers.” (71:10-12).

He also appealed to their reason by pointing to the signs of creation:

مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارً۬ا (١٣) وَقَدۡ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَطۡوَارًا (١٤) أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَـٰوَٲتٍ۬ طِبَاقً۬ا (١٥) وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيہِنَّ نُورً۬ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجً۬ا (١٦) وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتً۬ا (١٧) ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيہَا وَيُخۡرِجُڪُمۡ إِخۡرَاجً۬ا (١٨) وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِسَاطً۬ا (١٩) لِّتَسۡلُكُواْ مِنۡہَا سُبُلاً۬ فِجَاجً۬ا (٢٠)

“What is the matter with you? Why do you not fear Allah’s majesty, (13) when He has created you stage by stage? (14) Have you not seen how Allah created seven heavens, one above the other, (15) and made the moon as a light in them and the sun as a lamp, (16) And Allah made you spring forth from the earth like a plant, (17) And He will return you into it and then bring you out again, (18) And Allah spread the Earth out for you (19) to walk along its spacious paths?” (71:13-20).

Despite all this, they persisted in rejection. Nuh identified the root cause: they blindly followed the wealthy and powerful rather than the truth.

قَالَ نُوحٌ۬ رَّبِّ إِنَّہُمۡ عَصَوۡنِى وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَن لَّمۡ يَزِدۡهُ مَالُهُ ۥ وَوَلَدُهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا خَسَارً۬ا (٢١)

“Noah said, ‘My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed those whose wealth and children only increase them nothing but loss.’” (71:21).

In the end, Nuh realized there was no hope for his people or their descendants and prayed for their destruction:

وَقَالَ نُوحٌ۬ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا (٢٦) إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرۡهُمۡ يُضِلُّواْ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓاْ إِلَّا فَاجِرً۬ا ڪَفَّارً۬ا (٢٧) رَّبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِى وَلِوَٲلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيۡتِىَ مُؤۡمِنً۬ا وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارَۢا (٢٨)

“And Noah said, ‘My Lord, do not leave a single disbeliever on the earth (26) for if you leave them, they will mislead Your servants and beget none but wicked disbelievers. (27) “My Lord, forgive me, my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer and all believing men and women. And do bring nothing but ruin upon the evildoers!” (71:26-28)

Note: Prophet Nuh’s realization that his people would not believe may have come through divine revelation, not personal judgment. This is indicated in Surat Hud:

وَأُوحِيَ إِلَى نُوحٍ أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ

“And it was revealed to Nuh: None of your people will believe except those who have believed already. So do not be distressed by what they have been doing.” (Hud: 11-36)

Appendix: The Power of Seeking Forgiveness
It is reported that a man once complained to Imam Al-Hasan Al-Basri (الحسن البصري) about poverty, and he advised him, Seek forgiveness from Allah (استغفر الله). Others came complaining of drought, and he gave the same advice. Another man said his wife could not bear children, and again, the Imam told him to seek forgiveness.

Someone in the gathering asked, “Why do you give the same answer to everyone?”

Imam Al-Hasan replied, “Have you not read the words of Allah?”:

فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ غَفَّارً۬ا (١٠) يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارً۬ا (١١) وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٲلٍ۬ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡہَـٰرً۬ا (١٢)

“I said (to them): Seek forgiveness from your Lord, verily, He is Most-Forgiving; (10) He will send down rain from the sky to you in abundance, (11) and will provide you with wealth and children, and grant you gardens and rivers.” (Nuh 71:10-12)

title: Theme of Surat Al-Jinn (الجنّ) (72)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Al-Jinn (الجنّ) (72)

The central theme of Surat Al-Jinn is the universality of the Quran as a divine message sent to both humans and jinn, affirming that Islam addresses all…
content:
Theme of Surat Al-Jinn (الجنّ) (72)

The central theme of Surat Al-Jinn is the universality of the Quran as a divine message sent to both humans and jinn, affirming that Islam addresses all intelligent beings—both visible and invisible. The Surah emphasizes that both humans and jinn are accountable to Allah and have free will to believe or disbelieve.

The Surah opens by revealing that a group of jinn listened to the Prophet (PBUH) as he recited the Qur’an. They immediately recognized it as divine guidance and committed to spreading it among their kind:

قُلۡ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسۡتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا قُرۡءَانً۬ا عَجَبً۬ا (١) يَہۡدِىٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشۡدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦ‌ۖ وَلَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدً۬ا (٢)

“Say: ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened (to the Quran) and said: we have heard a wondrous Quran. (1) It guides to the right path, and we have believed in it, and we will never associate partners with our Lord.” (72:1-2)

Upon hearing the Quran, the jinn expressed astonishment that both humans and jinn have lied about Allah by saying:

وَأَنَّهُ ۥ تَعَـٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَـٰحِبَةً۬ وَلَا وَلَدً۬ا (٣) وَأَنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيہُنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ شَطَطً۬ا (٤) وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبً۬ا (٥)

“Exalted is the nobleness of our Lord; He has taken neither a wife nor a son. (3) And the fool among us used to say absurd things about Allah. (4) And we thought that no human or jinn would ever lie about Allah.” (72:3-5)

Lying about Allah is described in the Qur’an as a grave sin. Imam Al-Ghazali noted:

” لئن يرتكب العوام الكبائر فذلك أهون من أن يقولوا على الله ما لا يعلمون ” .

“ For the common people to commit major sins is less dangerous than for them to speak about Allah without knowledge.”

The Surah warns against seeking protection from jinn, a practice some humans engaged in, which only led to greater humiliation:

وَأَنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ رِجَالٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمۡ رَهَقً۬ا (٦)

“Some men from among humans sought refuge with males among the jinn, but they (jinn)only increased them in burden.” (72:6)

This Ayat is a warning from the righteous Jinn to humans against taking refuge or seeking help from jinn, as it only leads to fear and exploitation.

The righteous jinn show remarkable wisdom and humility in response to the Qur’an’s message:

وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعۡنَا ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ‌ۖ فَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخۡسً۬ا وَلَا رَهَقً۬ا (١٣) وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلۡمُسۡلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ‌ۖ فَمَنۡ أَسۡلَمَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ تَحَرَّوۡاْ رَشَدً۬ا (١٤) وَأَمَّا ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبً۬ا (١٥)

“When we heard the guidance (the Quran), we believed in it. Whoever believes in his Lord shall have no fear of being denied his reward or being wronged. (13) And among us some are Muslims, and among us are the unjust “Al-Qasitoun”. Those who embraced Islam, have found the Right Path.  (14) And as for the unjust “Al-Qasitoun”, they will be the fuel for Hell.” (72:13-15)

The Wisdon of the ROghtous Jinn

A linguistic note: Although the words Muqsit (مُقْسِط) and Qasit (قاسِط) share the same root (ق-س-ط), they have opposite meanings:
• Muqsit (مُقْسِط): Just, fair. إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ “Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.” (Al-Mumtahina 60:8)
• Qasit (قاسِط): Unjust, oppressive. وَأَمَّا ٱلْقَاسِطُونَ فَكَانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبًا “As for the unjust, they will be firewood for Hell.” (Al-Jinn 72:15)

The Surah closes by shifting from the unseen world of jinn to the Prophet’s message to mankind. It affirms the Prophet’s limited knowledge of the unseen and his sole role as a messenger:

قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَدۡعُواْ رَبِّى وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِهِۦۤ أَحَدً۬ا (٢٠) قُلۡ إِنِّى لَآ أَمۡلِكُ لَكُمۡ ضَرًّ۬ا وَلَا رَشَدً۬ا (٢١) قُلۡ إِنِّى لَن يُجِيرَنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدٌ۬ وَلَنۡ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلۡتَحَدًا (٢٢) إِلَّا بَلَـٰغً۬ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَـٰلَـٰتِهِۦ‌ۚ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ۥ فَإِنَّ لَهُ ۥ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًا (٢٣)

Say, “I only call upon my Lord and do not associate anyone with Him.” (20) Say, “I have no power to harm or guide you.” (21) Say, “No one can protect me from Allah, and I have no refuge except in Him. (22) My duty is only to convey from Allah His messages.” And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell; wherein they will live forever. (72: 20-23)

The Prophet is also instructed to acknowledge his limited knowledge of the timing of the Hereafter:

قُلۡ إِنۡ أَدۡرِىٓ أَقَرِيبٌ۬ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ أَمۡ يَجۡعَلُ لَهُ ۥ رَبِّىٓ أَمَدًا (٢٥) عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ فَلَا يُظۡهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيۡبِهِۦۤ أَحَدًا (٢٦) إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرۡتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍ۬ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ يَسۡلُكُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ رَصَدً۬ا (٢٧) لِّيَعۡلَمَ أَن قَدۡ أَبۡلَغُواْ رِسَـٰلَـٰتِ رَبِّہِمۡ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيۡہِمۡ وَأَحۡصَىٰ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ عَدَدَۢا (٢٨)

Say, I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or my Lord has set it for a distant time.’ (25) [He is] the Knower of the Unseen, He reveals it to none. (26) but to a messenger of His choice whom He surrounds with watching guards before and behind him. (27) To ensure that they have delivered the messages of their Lord. He fully encompasses all that is with them and keeps count of everything. (72: 25-28)

title: Theme of Surat Al-Ma’arij (المعَارج) (The Ways of Ascent) (70)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Al-Ma’arij (المعَارج) (The Ways of Ascent) (70)

Surat Al-Ma’arij (The Ways of Ascent) addresses the human struggle with impatience, particularly regarding belief in the Hereafter. It…
content:
Theme of Surat Al-Ma’arij (المعَارج) (The Ways of Ascent) (70)

Surat Al-Ma’arij (The Ways of Ascent) addresses the human struggle with impatience, particularly regarding belief in the Hereafter. It rebukes those who deny the afterlife for their demand to witness it now, driven by impatience and short-sightedness. In contrast, believers overcome this instinct through the discipline of prayer, which instills patience and certainty.

The Surah opens by affirming the certainty of the Day of Judgment, explaining that the perception of its delay is a result of human impatience and misunderstanding of time’s true nature. What seems distant to people is in reality, very near in God’s sight. The remedy for this impatience and heedlessness is to cultivate patience.

سَأَلَ سَآٮِٕلُۢ بِعَذَابٍ۬ وَاقِعٍ۬ (١) لِّلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ لَيۡسَ لَهُ ۥ دَافِعٌ۬ (٢) مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذِى ٱلۡمَعَارِجِ (٣) تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ فِى يَوۡمٍ۬ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُ ۥ خَمۡسِينَ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ۬ (٤) فَٱصۡبِرۡ صَبۡرً۬ا جَمِيلاً (٥) إِنَّهُمۡ يَرَوۡنَهُ ۥ بَعِيدً۬ا (٦) وَنَرَٮٰهُ قَرِيبً۬ا (٧)

“A questioner asked about a punishment bound to happen (1) — for the disbelievers, none can avert it — (2) from Allah, Lord of the Ways of Ascent, (3) through which the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him on a Day fifty thousand years long. (4) So be patient with gracious patience. (5) They see it as far off, (6) but We see it as near.” (70:1-7)

To shake the heedless out of their denial, the Surah offers a vivid and terrifying image of the Day, where even close relationships offer no refuge, and every person would wish to sacrifice everything to save themselves, but such ransom will not be accepted. The punishment for those who deny the truth is severe and inescapable.

يَوۡمَ تَكُونُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ كَٱلۡمُهۡلِ (٨) وَتَكُونُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ كَٱلۡعِهۡنِ (٩) وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمً۬ا (١٠) يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡ‌ۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِى مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِٮِٕذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ (١١) وَصَـٰحِبَتِهِۦ وَأَخِيهِ (١٢) وَفَصِيلَتِهِ ٱلَّتِى تُـٔۡوِيهِ (١٣) وَمَن فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعً۬ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ (١٤)

“On the Day the sky will be like molten brass (8) and the mountains like tufts of wool, (9) and no close friend will ask about his friend, (10) though they will see one another. The sinner will wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his sons, (11) his wife, his brother, (12) and his clan who sheltered him, (13) and everyone on earth, if only it could save him.” (70:8-14)

But such pleas will be rejected:

كَلَّآ‌ۖ إِنَّہَا لَظَىٰ (١٥) نَزَّاعَةً۬ لِّلشَّوَىٰ (١٦) تَدۡعُواْ مَنۡ أَدۡبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ (١٧) وَجَمَعَ فَأَوۡعَىٰ (١٨)

But no! There is a raging ﬂame (15) that strips away the skin, (16) and it will claim everyone who rejects the truth, turns away, (17) accumulates wealth and hoards it.” (70:15-18)

The Surah then explores the innate human traits of impatience, anxiety, and stinginess-as universal, but teaches that these can be overcome through sincere prayer, charity, and moral discipline. True believers are characterized by regular prayer, generosity, honesty, and self-restraint.

إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا (١٩) إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعً۬ا (٢٠) وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلۡخَيۡرُ مَنُوعًا (٢١) إِلَّا ٱلۡمُصَلِّينَ (٢٢) ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِہِمۡ دَآٮِٕمُونَ (٢٣) وَٱلَّذِينَ فِىٓ أَمۡوَٲلِهِمۡ حَقٌّ۬ مَّعۡلُومٌ۬ (٢٤) لِّلسَّآٮِٕلِ وَٱلۡمَحۡرُومِ (٢٥) وَٱلَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ (٢٦) وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنۡ عَذَابِ رَبِّہِم مُّشۡفِقُونَ (٢٧) إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّہِمۡ غَيۡرُ مَأۡمُونٍ۬ (٢٨) وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِفُرُوجِهِمۡ حَـٰفِظُونَ (٢٩)

“Indeed, man was created anxious: (19) fretful when harm touches him, (20) and stingy when good fortune reaches him. (21) Except those who pray (22) and are constant in their prayers, (23) and give a rightful share of their wealth (Zakat) (24) to the one who asks and the deprived; (25) who believe in the Day of Judgment (26) and fear their Lord’s punishment — (27) for none feels secure from it — (28) and guard their chastity (70:19-29)

Those who are committed to their prayers are always trustworthy and those who possess these honorable traits are promised honor in Paradise.

وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِأَمَـٰنَـٰتِہِمۡ وَعَهۡدِهِمۡ رَٲعُونَ (٣٢) وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِشَہَـٰدَٲتِہِمۡ قَآٮِٕمُونَ (٣٣) وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِہِمۡ يُحَـٰفِظُونَ (٣٤) أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ فِى جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ مُّكۡرَمُونَ (٣٥)

They fulfill their trusts and promises; (32) who bear true witness (33) and are faithful in their prayers. (34) They will be honored in Gardens of bliss.” (70:19-35)

The surah concludes by confronting the arrogant disbelievers who mock the Prophet and remain heedless of the Hereafter: It reminds them that their denial will not prevent the coming of the promised Day, when they will face the consequences of their actions.

فَمَالِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ قِبَلَكَ مُهۡطِعِينَ (٣٦) عَنِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ (٣٧) أَيَطۡمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِىٍٕ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ أَن يُدۡخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ۬ (٣٨) كَلَّآ‌ۖ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَـٰهُم مِّمَّا يَعۡلَمُونَ (٣٩) فَلَآ أُقۡسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلۡمَشَـٰرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغَـٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَـٰدِرُونَ (٤٠) عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيۡرً۬ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَسۡبُوقِينَ (٤١) فَذَرۡهُمۡ يَخُوضُواْ وَيَلۡعَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ (٤٢) يَوۡمَ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ سِرَاعً۬ا كَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ۬ يُوفِضُونَ (٤٣) خَـٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَـٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةٌ۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمُ ٱلَّذِى كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ (٤٤)

“What is wrong with the disbelievers that they rush towards you, (36) from the right and left in crowds? (37) Does each of them hope to enter a Garden of bliss? (38) No! We created them from what they know. (39) By the Lord of the Easts and the Wests, We are fully capable (40) of replacing them with better people. (41) So leave them to idle talk until they face the Day they are promised — (42) the Day they will rush from their graves as if racing to a banner, (43) eyes lowered, covered in humiliation. That is the Day they were warned of.” (70:36-44)

Appendix 1: Understanding the “Fifty Thousand Years

“تَعْرُجُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ”
“The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years.”
(Al-Maarij 70:4)

This verse describes a metaphysical phenomenon: the angels and the Spirit (identified as Jibreel) ascend to Allah on a Day whose duration is quantified as fifty thousand years. This is not a reference to human perception of time but rather to a cosmic or divine timescale that transcends earthly measurement. It conveys the vastness, magnitude, and transcendence of that Day — pointing to an objective reality beyond the human frame of reference.

While the Qur’an sometimes refers to the Day of Judgment using immense time scales, Hadith literature clarifies that individual human experience on that Day will vary based on moral and spiritual standing. For example, in a Hadith recorded by Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ states that those who withheld zakat will endure torment throughout a Day measured as fifty thousand years:

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: “ما من صاحبِ ذهبٍ ولا فضةٍ لا يؤدِّي منها حقَّها، إلا إذا كان يومُ القيامةِ صُفِّحَتْ له صفائحُ من نارٍ، فأُحْمِيَ عليها في نار جهنمَ، فيُكْوَى بها جَنْبُهُ وجَبينُهُ وظَهْرُهُ، كلما بَرَدَتْ أُعيدَتْ له في يومٍ كان مقدارُهُ خمسينَ ألفَ سنةٍ، حتى يُقْضَى بين العبادِ، فيُرَى سبيلُهُ: إما إلى الجنةِ، وإما إلى النار.”رواه مسلم (987)

“Any person who possesses gold or silver and does not pay what is due on it (i.e., the Zakat); on the Day of Resurrection, sheets of silver and gold will be heated in the Fire of Hell and used to brand his forehead, flanks, and back. When they cool, they will be reheated and the process repeated throughout a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years—until judgment is passed among the servants and he is shown his destination, either Paradise or Hell.” (Muslim)

This suggests that the duration is not necessarily literal for every individual but serves to emphasize the severity and gravity of divine accountability.

A related verse in Surah Al-Sajdah (32:5) states:

يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ

“He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.” (Al-Sajdah 32:5)

This illustrates that divine time is distinct from human time. The Quran uses such descriptions to underline the metaphysical gap between the created world and the Creator — reminding us that our conventional understanding of time does not apply in the realm of the unseen.

Appendix 2: One East, Two Easts, and Multiple Easts – Qur’anic References to Directions in Time and Space

The Qur’an refers to the East and the West in several ways, including:

1. Singular form: “رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ”
“The Lord of the East and the West.” (Al-Shu‘ara 26:28; Al-Muzzammil 73:9)

2. Dual form: “رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ”
“The Lord of the two Easts and the two Wests.” (Ar-Rahman 55:17)

3. Plural form: “فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشَارِقِ وَالْمَغَارِبِ”
“But no! I swear by the Lord of all points of sunrise and sunset.” (Al-Ma‘arij 70:40)

The Qur’an’s shifting expressions — from one, to two, to many — reflect not inconsistency, but depth. They point to the scientific precision, poetic eloquence, and spiritual breadth of the Qur’an’s worldview. These expressions invite reflection on the vastness of creation, the relativity of time and space, and the unlimited knowledge and power of Allah.

Possible Explanation of the Variations:

These variations are layers of meaning reflecting the complexity of creation, motion, and perception of time and space.

• The singular form refers to the general reality of East and West as fixed directions relative to the observer on Earth.
• The dual form likely reflects the seasonal shifts — the point of sunrise and sunset during the winter solstice and summer solstice. These two extremes represent the two farthest points the sun reaches in its annual journey across the horizon.
• The plural form (as in 70:40) indicates the daily variation in sunrise and sunset across different days, locations, and latitudes. Each point on Earth has its own “East” and “West” depending on the time and place. It also reflects the diversity and multiplicity of Allah’s creation, and perhaps even cosmological dimensions beyond our world.

Broader Implication in 70:40:

In Surah Al-Ma‘arij (70:40), Allah says:”فَلَآ أُقۡسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلۡمَشَـٰرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغَـٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَـٰدِرُونَ”
“But no! I swear by the Lord of all Easts and Wests — We are surely capable…”

This oath emphasizes Allah’s supreme control over the entire cosmos — over all rotations, orbits, directions, and temporal realities. The multiplicity here may symbolize:

• The countless sunrises and sunsets across the globe.
• The relativity of direction in the universe depends on planetary position.
• Or even metaphysical or multi-dimensional realities beyond human perception.

title: Theme of Surat Al-Haqqah (الحَاقَّة) (The Inevitable) (69:1:52)
excerpt: Surat Al-Haqqah presents a vivid and powerful portrayal of the Day of Judgment—one of its many names being Al-Haqqah (الحَاقَّة), meaning the Inevitable, the Truth, or the Reality. The Qur’an uses…
content:
Surat Al-Haqqah presents a vivid and powerful portrayal of the Day of Judgment—one of its many names being Al-Haqqah (الحَاقَّة), meaning the Inevitable, the Truth, or the Reality. The Qur’an uses several names to describe the Day of Judgment, each highlighting a distinct aspect of its terror and certainty, such as Al-Qari’ah القارعة ُ (The Striking Calamity – 101:1), At-Tammah ٱلطَّآمَّةُ (The Overwhelming Disaster – 79:34), Al-Azifah ٱلۡأَزِفَةُ (The Imminent – 53:57), and Al-Qiyamah (The Resurrection – 2:85).

The Surah begins by drawing our attention to the seriousness of this Day, repeating the name Al-Haqqah three times in a rhetorical challenge:

ٱلۡحَآقَّةُ (١) مَا ٱلۡحَآقَّةُ (٢) وَمَآ أَدۡرَٮٰكَ مَا ٱلۡحَآقَّةُ (٣)

“The Inevitable! (1) What is the Inevitable? (2) And what made you know what the Inevitable is?” (69:1-3)

Before depicting the dramatic events of that Day, the Surah reminds us of the worldly destruction faced by past nations who denied the truth:

• Thamud (ثَمُودُ), the people of Prophet Ṣaliḥ
• ‘Ād (عَادُ), the people of Prophet Hūd
• Pharaoh, who opposed Prophet Mūsā
• The Overthrown Cities (ٱلۡمُؤۡتَفِكَـٰتُ), referring to the people of Prophet Lūṭ
• and the people of Prophet Nūḥ

Their destruction serves as a warning of the consequences of rejecting divine truth.

Then the Surah transitions to the awe-inspiring scenes of the Day of Judgment:

فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفۡخَةٌ۬ وَٲحِدَةٌ۬ (١٣) وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً۬ وَٲحِدَةً۬ (١٤) فَيَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ وَقَعَتِ ٱلۡوَاقِعَةُ (١٥) وَٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَهِىَ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ وَاهِيَةٌ۬ (١٦) وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآٮِٕهَا‌ۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ ثَمَـٰنِيَةٌ۬ (١٧)

“When the Trumpet is blown with a single blast. (13) And the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with one blow. (14) Then on that Day the Event will occur. (15) The sky will be torn apart, for it will be fragile that day. (16) And the angels will be at its borders, and eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day.” (69:13-17)

The Surah then describes the fate of two categories of people, distinguished by how they receive their record. This record is the ultimate proof of their deeds and will determine their eternal destiny. The hand with which one receives their record is not a choice; rather, it reflects the life they lived. On that Day, no secrets will remain hidden, and every soul in the world will be able to read their book with perfect clarity.

Those given their record in their right hand will rejoice:

فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِىَ كِتَـٰبَهُ ۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقۡرَءُواْ كِتَـٰبِيَهۡ (١٩) إِنِّى ظَنَنتُ أَنِّى مُلَـٰقٍ حِسَابِيَهۡ (٢٠) فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍ۬ رَّاضِيَةٍ۬ (٢١) فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ۬ (٢٢)

“As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, ‘Here, read my record! (19) Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account.’ (20) So he will be in a pleasant life, (21) in an elevated Paradise.” (69:19-22).

One can almost imagine the joy of that moment—holding your record with pride and gratitude.

In stark contrast, the one given his record in his left hand will be overcome with despair:

وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِىَ كِتَـٰبَهُ ۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَـٰلَيۡتَنِى لمۡ أُوتَ كِتَـٰبِيَهۡ (٢٥) وَلَمۡ أَدۡرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهۡ (٢٦) يَـٰلَيۡتَہَا كَانَتِ ٱلۡقَاضِيَةَ (٢٧) مَآ أَغۡنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهۡۜ (٢٨) هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلۡطَـٰنِيَهۡ (٢٩) خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ (٣٠) ثُمَّ ٱلۡجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ (٣١) ثُمَّ فِى سِلۡسِلَةٍ۬ ذَرۡعُهَا سَبۡعُونَ ذِرَاعً۬ا فَٱسۡلُكُوهُ (٣٢)

‘As for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, “I wish that I had not been given my record, (25) And had not known what is my account. (26) I wish it had been the end (death)! (27) My wealth has not helped me; My authority has gone from me.” (28) (Allah will say), “Seize him and shackle him; (30) Then throw him in the blazing Fire. (31) Then bind him with a chain seventy cubits long!” (32)’ (69:25-32).

The Surah then explains the root causes of this tragic fate, his failure in two core responsibilities: his duty to Allah and his duty to humanity:

إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ (٣٣) وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلۡمِسۡكِينِ (٣٤)

“Indeed, He did not believe in Allah, the Most Great, (33) nor did he encourage the feeding the poor.” (69:33-34)

This connection between disbelief and neglecting the needy suggests that true faith must manifest in compassion and social responsibility. Those who are capable—or discourage others from doing so—should reexamine the sincerity of their belief.

The Surah affirms the authenticity of Prophet Muhammad’s message and warns against fabricating anything in Allah’s name:

إِنَّهُ ۥ لَقَوۡلُ رَسُولٍ۬ كَرِيمٍ۬ (٤٠) وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوۡلِ شَاعِرٍ۬‌ۚ قَلِيلاً۬ مَّا تُؤۡمِنُونَ (٤١) وَلَا بِقَوۡلِ كَاهِنٍ۬‌ۚ قَلِيلاً۬ مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٤٢) تَنزِيلٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٤٣) وَلَوۡ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيۡنَا بَعۡضَ ٱلۡأَقَاوِيلِ (٤٤) لَأَخَذۡنَا مِنۡهُ بِٱلۡيَمِينِ (٤٥) ثُمَّ لَقَطَعۡنَا مِنۡهُ ٱلۡوَتِينَ (٤٦) فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنۡ أَحَدٍ عَنۡهُ حَـٰجِزِينَ (٤٧)

“Indeed, this is the word of a noble Messenger. (40) It is not the word of a poet, but little do you believe! (41) Nor is it the word of a soothsayer (foreteller), but little do you remember! (42) This is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. (43) And if he (the Prophet) had made up about Us some (false) sayings, (44) We would have seized him by the right hand (45) and severed his life artery. (46) And none of you could have prevented Us from (punishing) him.” (69:40-47)

This is both a confirmation of the Quran’s truth and a stern warning to anyone who conveys Allah’s message, emphasizing that the Prophet himself was bound by the highest standards of truth and integrity.

The Surah concludes by reinforcing the truth of the Qur’an and warning those who reject it:

وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَتَذۡكِرَةٌ۬ لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٤٨) وَإِنَّا لَنَعۡلَمُ أَنَّ مِنكُم مُّكَذِّبِينَ (٤٩) وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَحَسۡرَةٌ عَلَى ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ (٥٠) وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَحَقُّ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٥١) فَسَبِّحۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ (٥٢)

“And is in fact a Reminder for those who have Taqwa (48) And verily, We know that there are some deniers among you. (49) And indeed, this (denial of the Qur’an) will be anguish for the disbelievers. (50) And it is surely the true certainty (51) So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.” (69:48-52)

Allah describes the Quran as “ḥaqq al-yaqīn” (حق اليقين) (the certainty of truth), the highest level of certainty. In Islamic epistemology, there are three levels of certainty:

1. ‘Ilm al-Yaqīn (علم اليقين) – Certainty through knowledge (from a trustworthy source),
2. ‘Ayn al-Yaqīn (عين اليقين)– Certainty through seeing with one’s own eyes,
3. Ḥaqq al-Yaqīn (حق اليقين)– The ultimate certainty, confirmed by direct experience and irrefutable reality. The Quran is given the status of (حق اليقين) because every word in it is proof of its divine source.

Surat Al-Haqqah leads us through these levels—warning us, preparing us, and calling us to live a life aligned with it.

Note: The only other reality that is given this level of certainty (حق اليقين) in the Quran is that based on the actual experience of those people when they are in Hell.

وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ (٩٢) فَنُزُلٌ۬ مِّنۡ حَمِيمٍ۬ (٩٣) وَتَصۡلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ (٩٤) إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٩٥) (Al-Waqi’ah 56:92-95)

“However, if he is one who rejects the (truth) and goes astray. (92) For him is a welcome of scalding water, (93) and burning in Hell-fire. (94) Indeed, this is the ultimate certainty.” (Al-Waqi’ah 56:92-95)

The other forms of certainties are given in:

كَلَّا لَوۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ عِلۡمَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٥) لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلۡجَحِيمَ (٦) ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّہَا عَيۡنَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٧) (At-Takathur 102:5-7)

“If you only know with certainty of knowledge. (5) You shall indeed see the Hell, (6) Then you shall see it with certainty of sight.” (At-Takathur 102:5-7)

title: Theme of Surat Al-Qalam (القَلَم) (The Pen), or Noon (نٓ‌ۚ) (68:1-52)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Al-Qalam (القَلَم) (The Pen), or Noon (نٓ‌ۚ) (68:1-52)

Surat Al-Qalam focuses on the principles of Dawah and the essential qualities required of those who call others to Islam,…
content:
Theme of Surat Al-Qalam (القَلَم) (The Pen), or Noon (نٓ‌ۚ) (68:1-52)

Surat Al-Qalam focuses on the principles of Dawah and the essential qualities required of those who call others to Islam, emphasizing patience, steadfastness, and moral integrity.

The Surah presents two examples for those engaged in Dawah. The first is the model of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), who demonstrated perseverance in delivering Allah’s message despite facing intense opposition and false accusations, including being called insane. Allah refutes these accusations by affirming the Prophet’s noble character and promising him endless reward:

نٓ‌ۚ ‌ۚ وَٱلۡقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسۡطُرُونَ (١) مَآ أَنتَ بِنِعۡمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجۡنُونٍ۬ (٢) وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجۡرًا غَيۡرَ مَمۡنُونٍ۬ (٣) وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ۬ (٤)
“Nun. By the pen and what they write. (1) By the Grace of your Lord, You are not insane (2) And indeed, you will be an endless reward. (3) And you are, surely, on an exalted (standard of) character.” (68:1- 4)

The second model is a cautionary one: Prophet Yunus (AS), who gave up and left his people prematurely after facing rejection and hardship. The Surah warns against impatience and emphasizes perseverance.

The accusation of insanity against those who engage in Dawah is not new. The Surah opens and closes with this charge to highlight the pattern:
وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزۡلِقُونَكَ بِأَبۡصَـٰرِهِمۡ لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجۡنُونٌ۬ (٥١) وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرٌ۬ لِّلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٥٢)
“And indeed, those who disbelieve seem to trip you up with their glances when they hear the Reminder, and they say: “Verily, he is a madman!” (51) But it is nothing else than a Reminder to all the worlds.” (68:51-52)

Those who call to Allah must expect insults but remain undeterred. Their mission is a noble one: to offer humanity a divine reminder, enduring abuse only to save others from Hellfire, and earning endless reward from Allah.

The Surah opens with Allah’s oath by the pen, highlighting the importance of knowledge and literacy as foundations for effective Dawah. Since Al-Qalam was the second Surah revealed after Al-Alaq—where Allah’s first command was “Read”—the centrality of learning is clear. Yet, it is shameful that illiteracy remains high in many Muslim countries, and even those who can read often neglect reading.

The accusation of insanity also reveals ignorance about the true meaning of madness. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions once passed by a mentally ill person. The companions called him mad (مجنون). The Prophet (PBUH) said: No, he is merely afflicted. The truly mad is the one who disobeys Allah (لا بل هذا مبتلى ، المجنون من عصى الله). Thus, rejecting Allah’s call is true insanity.

The surah gives warning the Prophet (PBUH) and by extension, all believers—not to follow or obey certain types of people who exhibit the following specific set of corrupt moral traits.

ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِين Deniers of the truth
يُدْهِنُون Wish for compromise in truth
حَلَّافٍ مَّهِينٍ Excessive swearer, despicable
هَمَّازٍ Slanderer/backbiter
مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ Scandal-monger/gossip spreader
مَنَّاعٍ لِّلۡخَيۡرِ Prevents good
مُعۡتَدٍ Transgressor
أَثِيمٍ Habitual sinner
عُتُلٍّ Cruel and violent
زَنِيمٍ Disgraceful character and lineage
ذَا مَالٍ۬ وَبَنِينَ Arrogant due to wealth and children
يَقُولُ أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ Claims Qur’anic verses are legends

Those who possess these traits are warned that they shall be disgraced and humiliated if they persist in such traits. The expression used to describe this fate is:
سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى ٱلۡخُرۡطُومِ – “We shall brand him upon the snout (nose).” (verse 16)

The Surah then offers a parable illustrating the consequences of rejecting Allah’s message and commands. It recounts the story of brothers who owned a lush garden but, in their greed, decided to withhold charity. Planning to harvest the fruits early before the poor could come. But when they went, they found their garden destroyed overnight by divine punishment:
إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَـٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّہَا مُصۡبِحِينَ (١٧) وَلَا يَسۡتَثۡنُونَ (١٨) فَطَافَ عَلَيۡہَا طَآٮِٕفٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآٮِٕمُونَ (١٩) فَأَصۡبَحَتۡ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ (٢٠)
“We have tested them (those who reject the divine message) as We tested the owners of the garden, when they swore to harvest its fruit in the [early] morning (17) And do not make any exception. (18) So there came upon the garden an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep. (19) And it became s though harvested.” (68:17-20)

The punishment of the owners of the garden serves as a worldly example of divine retribution, but Allah warns that the punishment of the Hereafter is even greater:
كَذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡعَذَابُ‌ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُ‌ۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
“Such is the punishment (in this life), but truly, the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they but knew.” (68:33)

The Surah concludes by exhorting those involved in Dawah to remain patient and not to give up, referencing the story of Prophet Yunus (AS) as a warning against impatience. The message is to wait for Allah’s decision and to persist in the mission with trust and resilience:
فَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكۡظُومٌ۬. (القلم)
“So be patient for the Decision of your Lord, and do not be like the Companion of the whale — when he cried out (to Us) in distress.” (Al-Qalam 68:48)

In summary, Surat Al-Qalam teaches that successful Dawah requires knowledge, patience, steadfastness, and moral excellence, using the examples of Prophet Muhammad (to emulate) and Prophet Yunus (as a caution) to guide those who call others to Islam.

Regarding Prophet Yunus (AS), some raise the question of whether he was already a prophet when he abandoned his mission or he was acting under another prophet’s directive. The view that he was a prophet is mainly based on Biblical traditions, which may not be entirely accurate. Understanding this issue needs a complete study of all the references of his story in the Quran.

title: Theme of At-Taghabun (التغابن) (The Sorrow) (64)
excerpt:
Theme of At-Taghabun (التغابن) (The Sorrow) (64)

The central theme of Surah Al-Taghabun is the deep regret that people will feel on the Day of Judgment, primarily due to worldly distractions that…
content:
Theme of At-Taghabun (التغابن) (The Sorrow) (64)

The central theme of Surah Al-Taghabun is the deep regret that people will feel on the Day of Judgment, primarily due to worldly distractions that kept them from fulfilling the commands of Allah. The key verse of the Surah is:

يَوۡمَ يَجۡمَعُكُمۡ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡجَمۡعِ‌ۖ ذَٲلِكَ يوم ٱلتَّغَابُنِ‌ۗ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ وَيَعۡمَلۡ صَـٰلِحً۬ا يُكَفِّرۡ عَنۡهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِۦ وَيُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيہَآ أَبَدً۬ا‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ (٩)

“(Be mindful of) the Day when He (Allah) will gather you on the Day of Assembly, that is the Day of sorrow (for lost opportunities). Whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He (Allah) will expiate his sins and admit him to Gardens under which rivers flow to dwell therein forever. That is the supreme success.” (Al-Taghabun 64:9)

The word Al-Taghabun (التغابن)—meaning mutual loss—is one of the names of the Day of Judgment. It marks the day when all will regret missed opportunities: the condemned for trading eternal bliss for fleeting pleasures, and even the successful—those who enter Paradise—for not doing more to attain higher ranks in Paradise.

We often cherish our families, wealth, and social standing. But the essential question is: do these attachments bring us closer to Allah, or do they distract us from Him? Allah issues a clear warning:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٲجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَـٰدِڪُمۡ عَدُوًّ۬ا لَّڪُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡ‌ۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ (١٤)

“O you who believe! Indeed, among your spouses and children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon, overlook, and forgive—then surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Taghabun 64:14)

This verse does not imply that all spouses or children are harmful. The Arabic word “من” indicates that only some may lead a person astray—by pushing them toward materialism, neglecting religious duties, or prioritizing worldly comfort over spiritual growth. They are not enemies in the traditional sense, but their influence may cause regret on the Day of Judgment.

Yet, Allah urges us to deal with our families not with hostility, but with forgiveness, patience, and compassion— recognizing that their behavior often stems from ignorance, not malice.

In the next verse, Allah generalizes the test:

نَّمَآ أَمۡوَٲلُكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَـٰدُكُمۡ فِتۡنَةٌ۬‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُ ۥۤ أَجۡرٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١٥)

“Your wealth and your children are but a trial, but with Allah there is a great reward. (Al-Taghabun 64:15)

Unlike the previous verse, this one treats all wealth and children as a universal test. Success lies in maintaining our faith and obedience to Allah despite these attachments. That means earning and spending money lawfully, raising righteous children, and resisting greed or worldly temptation.

While wealth and children are tests, they can also become sources of ongoing reward—if managed properly. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

إِذَا مَاتَ الْإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ، إِلَّا مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ [مسلم عن أبي هريرة]

“When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for him.” (Muslim, Tirmidhi)

To help us succeed in this test, Allah commands:

فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرً۬ا لِّأَنفُسِڪُمۡ‌ۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ

“So have Taqwa of Allah as much as you can; listen and obey; and spend in charity—that is better for your souls. And whoever is saved from his own greed, they are the successful.” (Al-Taghabun 64:16)

Recognizing that our love for wealth may hold us back, Allah offers a divine bargain:

إِن تُقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنً۬ا يُضَـٰعِفۡهُ لَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (١٧)

“If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and will forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative, Most Forbearing.” (Al-Taghabun 64:17)

One of the greatest losses on the Day of Judgment will be realizing that one was deceived into rejecting the truth—denying resurrection and dismissing messengers for being human. Allah says:

ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ ۥ كَانَت تَّأۡتِيہِمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ فَقَالُوٓاْ أَبَشَرٌ۬ يَہۡدُونَنَا فَكَفَرُواْ (٦)

“That is because their Messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said: ‘Shall mere men guide us?’ So, they disbelieved.” (Al-Taghabun 64:6)

زَعَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَن لَّن يُبۡعَثُواْ‌ۚ قُلۡ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّى لَتُبۡعَثُنَّ ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِمَا عَمِلۡتُمۡ‌ۚ وَذَٲلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ۬ (٧)

“The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: ‘Yes! By my Lord, you will certainly be resurrected. Then you will be informed of all that you did, and that is easy for Allah.” (Al-Taghabun 64:7)

The Surah then confirms the prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH) and the divine origin of the Quran:

فَـَٔامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَٱلنُّورِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلۡنَا‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ۬ (٨)

“So, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the Light which We have sent down. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.” (Al-Taghabun 64:8)

The Quran is often referred to as Nour (نور), meaning “light,” as it provides divine guidance to humanity. The Qur’an is called “Light (نور)” because it provides clear guidance from Allah.

title: Surat Al-Munafiqun (The Hypocrites) (المنافقون) (63)
excerpt: Surah Al-Munafiqun warns against one of the gravest internal threats to the Muslim community—hypocrisy. This danger undermines unity and weakens the bonds of brotherhood among believers. Hypocrites…
content:
Surah Al-Munafiqun warns against one of the gravest internal threats to the Muslim community—hypocrisy. This danger undermines unity and weakens the bonds of brotherhood among believers. Hypocrites are those who outwardly profess Islam but conceal disbelief and corruption in their hearts.

From the opening verse, the Surah exposes the lies and deceit of the hypocrites:

إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقُونَ قَالُواْ نَشۡہَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ ۥ وَٱللَّهُ يَشۡہَدُ إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ لَكَـٰذِبُونَ (١)

“When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.’ And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are truly liars.” (63:1)

The Surah outlines several traits of the hypocrites:

1. Using oaths to fake honesty:
ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَيۡمَـٰنَہُمۡ جُنَّةً۬ فَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ إِنَّہُمۡ سَآءَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ (٢)
They have taken their oaths a cover. Thus, they averted others from the path of Allah. Surely, evil is what they have been doing. (63:2)

2. Polished appearance and smooth speech used for deception, along with paranoia:
وَإِذَا رَأَيۡتَهُمۡ تُعۡجِبُكَ أَجۡسَامُهُمۡ‌ۖ وَإِن يَقُولُواْ تَسۡمَعۡ لِقَوۡلِهِمۡ‌ۖ كَأَنَّہُمۡ خُشُبٌ۬ مُّسَنَّدَةٌ۬‌ۖ يَحۡسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيۡحَةٍ عَلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۚ هُمُ ٱلۡعَدُوُّ فَٱحۡذَرۡهُمۡ‌ۚ قَـٰتَلَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۖ أَنَّىٰ يُؤۡفَكُونَ (٤)
And when you see them, their appearance pleases you; and when they speak, you listen to what they say (for their eloquence). Yet they are like propped up beams of timber. They think that every shout (they hear) is against them. They are the enemies, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them! How deluded they are! (63:4)

3. Arrogance preventing repentance:
وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ يَسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ لَوَّوۡاْ رُءُوسَهُمۡ وَرَأَيۡتَهُمۡ يَصُدُّونَ وَهُم مُّسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ (٥)
And when it is said to them: “Come so that the Messenger of Allah may ask forgiveness for you”, they turn their heads away, and you see them evading in arrogance. (63:5)

4. Miserliness and discouraging charity:
هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لَا تُنفِقُواْ عَلَىٰ مَنۡ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ حَتَّىٰ يَنفَضُّواْ‌ۗ وَلِلَّهِ خَزَآٮِٕنُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ (٧)
They are the ones who say: “Do not spend on those who are with Allah’s Messenger, until they desert him.” But to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand. (63:7)

Based on these and other verses, the key characteristics of the Hypocrites are:
1. Lying: Using false oaths to gain trust.
2. Paranoia: Assuming all criticism or warnings are directed at them.
3. Deceptive appearance: Presenting themselves well to mislead others.
4. Eloquent speech: Masking their falsehood with charm and intellectualism.
5. Sharp tongue: Quick to insult and belittle others.
6. Arrogance: Refusing to admit faults or seek forgiveness.
7. Miserliness: Reluctant to give charity or support righteous causes.
8. Two-faced behavior: Displaying different personalities in public and private.
9. Untrustworthiness: Breaking promises and betraying agreements.
10. No benefit to others: Adding no value to the community.
11. Lack of understanding: Unable or unwilling to grasp the truth.
12. Discouraging good: Serving as a demotivating force for righteousness.

These traits reflect a deeper disconnection between a person’s outward appearance and inner reality. To better understand the nature of hypocrisy, we must recognize that truth and falsehood manifest in three key areas: speech, actions, and beliefs.

• Truth in speech (صدق الأقوال): When a person conveys information that aligns with reality. If their words contradict the truth, it is lying in speech (كذب الأقوال).
• Truth in action (صدق الأفعال): When one’s actions confirm their claims. If actions contradict their words, it is lying in action (كذب الأفعال).
• Truth with oneself (صدق النفس): When speech reflects one’s genuine beliefs. If it contradicts what they truly believe, it is self-deception (كذب النفس). Hypocrisy is a form of this self-deception—when a person professes what they do not truly believe.

This framework explains why hypocrisy is so dangerous: it corrupts truth at every level— words, deeds, and intentions.

The Prophet ﷺ summarized the traits of a hypocrite in a well-known hadith:
عن عبد الله بن عمرو ، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أربعٌ من كنَّ فيه كان منافقاً خالصا ومن كانت فيه خصلة منهن كانت فيه خصلة من النفاق حتى يدعها، إذا حدث كذب، وإذا وعد أخلف، وإذا خاصم فجر وإذا عاهد غدر (رواه الشيخان)
“There are four traits that make someone a pure hypocrite. Whoever possesses one of them has a characteristic of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; when he disputes, he transgresses; and when he is trusted, he betrays.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

The Surah references an incident involving Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the chief hypocrite in Madinah, who arrogantly insulted the Prophet (PBUH):
يَقُولُونَ لَٮِٕن رَّجَعۡنَآ إِلَى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لَيُخۡرِجَنَّ ٱلۡأَعَزُّ مِنۡہَا ٱلۡأَذَلَّ‌ۚ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (٨)
They (hypocrites) say: “If we return to Al-Madinah, the more honorable will expel the more humble.” But honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, though the hypocrites do not know.” (63:8)

This verse is a powerful warning: If you do not feel honored by your association with Islam, beware—you may carry a trait of hypocrisy. Reflect on the words of Khalifa Umar ibn Al-Khattab (RA):
نحن قوم أعزنا الله بالإسلام ومهما ابتغينا العزة في غيره أذلنا الله.
“We are a people whom Allah has honored through Islam. If we seek honor through anything else, Allah will humiliate us.”

Because wealth and children often distract people, Allah warns the believers not to let these blessings divert them from His remembrance:
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُلۡهِكُمۡ أَمۡوَٲلُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَـٰدُڪُمۡ عَن ذِڪۡرِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٲلِكَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرُونَ (٩)
“O you who believe, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does so—it is they who are the losers.” (63:9)

The Surah concludes with a stern call to give charity before it is too late. Generosity protects the heart from hypocrisy:
وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِىَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنِىٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ قَرِيبٍ۬ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّ  ـٰلِحِينَ (١٠) وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهَا‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ (١١)
“And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you, and he says, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short while, I would give charity and be among the righteous.’ (10) But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.” (63:10-11)
