Theme of Surat As-Saffat (Devotional Ranks)

Surat As-Saffat, revealed in Mecca, emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah’s commands even when the wisdom behind them is unclear to us. The Surah opens by identifying creations of Allah who stand in complete obedience, ready to receive and fulfill His commands.

وَٱلصَّـٰٓفَّـٰتِ صَفًّ۬ا (١) فَٱلزَّٲجِرَٲتِ زَجۡرً۬ا (٢) فَٱلتَّـٰلِيَـٰتِ ذِكۡرًا (٣)

By those who are lined up in rows. (1) those who dispel evil with serious cry to stop them. (2) those who recite the exalted remembrance of Allah. (37:1-3)

The Surah doesn’t reveal the identities of the obedient beings who carry out Allah’s orders and maintain universal order by stopping disruptions. These beings could be various types, including angels and even stars, as the Surah will explain. Despite their weighty duties, these creations never forget to remember Allah. Their unwavering obedience serves as a contrast to humanity, encouraging a greater level of submission to Allah’s will.

Following the introduction of these creations, Allah affirms that He is the one who has created and sustains everything in the universe:

إِنَّ إِلَـٰهَكُمۡ لَوَٲحِدٌ۬ (٤) رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلۡمَشَـٰرِقِ (٥)

Indeed, your God is One, (4) Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the points of sunrise. (37:4-5)

Following the affirmation of Allah’s oneness, this Surah reveals another group of creations dedicated to safeguarding the confidentiality of Allah’s messages. These creations act as a barrier, preventing jinn from eavesdropping on divine commands and potentially deceiving humans with knowledge of future events. Any jinn who dares to intercept these messages is destroyed by these protectors.

إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلۡكَوَاكِبِ (٦) وَحِفۡظً۬ا مِّن كُلِّ شَيۡطَـٰنٍ مَّارِدٍ۬ (٧) لَّا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَإِ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ وَيُقۡذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ۬ (٨) دُحُورً۬ا‌ۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ۬ وَاصِبٌ (٩) إِلَّا مَنۡ خَطِفَ ٱلۡخَطۡفَةَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ۥ شِہَابٌ۬ ثَاقِبٌ۬ (١٠)

Verily! We have adorned the near heaven with an adornment of the stars. (6) And to guard against every rebellious devil. (7) They cannot listen to the transcendent assembly (of angels) for they are pelted from every side. (8) Repelled, and for them is a constant punishment. (9) Even if one of them snatch a trace (of the divine message), he is pursued by a piercing flame.” (37:6-10)

Note
These Ayat raise questions about how Allah communicates His messages and how Jinn might listen to them. What does it mean if one of them snatches a trace, a trace of what? This is a fascinating subject that I discussed in my previous talk on “The straight Path to Richness.

The Surah then explores human stories of submission. These include stories related to prophets Abraham (Ibrahim), Moses (Musa), Aaron (Harun), Elijah (Elias), Lot, and Jonah (Yunus). The Surah focuses particularly on Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismael, as well as Prophet Yunus.

The story of Prophet Ibrahim and Ismael exemplifies unwavering obedience. Despite being very old and having finally got blessed with a son, Ismael, he was instructed by Allah to slaughter him. Without hesitation or questioning, Prophet Ibrahim accepted the command, demonstrating complete submission.

Similarly, young Ismael willingly accepted Allah’s instructions to be sacrificed, displaying a profound level of submission to Allah’s command. The Surah emphasizes that even if one doesn’t understand the wisdom behind Allah’s directives, complete submission is expected due to the faith in Allah’s ultimate wisdom.

The Surat provided details on the life of Prophet Ibrahim by describing his conflict with his people who tried to burn him for refusing to worship their idols. Following this, he declared his intention to leave them and prayed to Allah for a righteous offspring.

وَقَالَ إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَہۡدِينِ (٩٩) رَبِّ هَبۡ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (١٠٠)

And he said (after his rescue from the fire): “I am going to (where I am ordered by) my Lod. He will surely guide me!” (99) “My Lord, grant me (offspring) from among the righteous.” (37:99-100)

Allah (SWT) answered his prayer and granted him his son, Ismael.

فَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهُ بِغُلَـٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ۬ (١٠١)

“So, We gave him the glad tidings of a forbearing boy. (37: 101)

Imagine the joy of Ibrahim, an elderly man living far from his homeland, when he finally had a son, Ismael. However, his happiness was soon tested by a challenging command. Ibrahim received a divine vision instructing him to sacrifice Ismael. Despite the emotional turmoil, Ibrahim recognized the importance of obeying divine commands. With a heavy heart but unwavering faith, he approached Ismael to share the news:

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡىَ قَالَ يَـٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ (١٠٢)

“And, when he (his son) was at the age to walk with him, he said: “O my dear son! I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think!” (37:102)

His inquiry to his son stemmed not from doubt, but from a desire to share the reward of submission. Ismael’s response mirrored this unwavering faith:

‌ قَالَ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُ‌ۖ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ (١٠٢)

“He said: “O my dear father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the patient.” (102)

This exemplified complete submission to Allah. Ultimately, Ibrahim’s son was spared, and both Ibrahim and Ismael were rewarded for their faithfulness.

فَلَمَّآ أَسۡلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ ۥ لِلۡجَبِينِ (١٠٣) وَنَـٰدَيۡنَـٰهُ أَن يَـٰٓإِبۡرَٲهِيمُ (١٠٤) قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآ‌ۚ إِنَّا كَذَٲلِكَ نَجۡزِى ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (١٠٥)

And when they had both willingly submitted (to the Will of Allah), and he (Ibrahim) put him (Ismael) down on his face (for sacrifice) (103) We called out to him: “O Ibrahim” (104) You have fulfilled the vision!” and thus We do reward those who do good. (105)

In contrast, Prophet Jonah’s story highlights the importance of strictly following divine instructions. Prophet Yunus left his people before receiving Allah’s permission, which led to his trial in the belly of a whale.

وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (١٣٩) إِذۡ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلۡمَشۡحُونِ (١٤٠) فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُدۡحَضِينَ (١٤١) فَٱلۡتَقَمَهُ ٱلۡحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ۬ (١٤٢)

And indeed, Yunus (Jonah) was among the messengers. (139) [Mention] when he ran away to an already laden ship. (140) and then he (agreed to) cast lots and was of those who lost. (141) and the whale swallowed him while he was blameworthy. (142)

فَلَوۡلَآ أَنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسَبِّحِينَ (١٤٣) لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطۡنِهِۦۤ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ (١٤٤)

And had he not been of those who exalt Allah, (143) He would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected. (144)

Through his experience, Prophet Yunus and in turn us learned the importance of complete submission. No matter how challenging a situation may seem, we must always trust in Allah’s guidance.

The Surat highlights the importance of your associations, you must be careful with whom you associate. On the day of judgment, some will blame those who misguided them:

وَأَقۡبَلَ بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ (٢٧) قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَأۡتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ (٢٨) قَالُواْ بَل لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ (٢٩)

And they will turn to one another, throwing blame. (27) The mislead will say, “it was you who deluded us from the right way.” (28) Their leaders will reply, “Nay, but you were not believers yourselves.” (29)

Here is the scene of those who are careful, and do not blindly follow anyone:

فَأَقۡبَلَ بَعۡضُہُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ (٥٠) قَالَ قَآٮِٕلٌ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ إِنِّى كَانَ لِى قَرِينٌ۬ (٥١)

And they will turn to one another, inquiring about each other. (50) A speaker among them will say, “Indeed, I had a companion (on earth) who used to question my faith.” (51)

This Surat describes a unique tree that will be seen by the people in Hell to contrast it with the delightful food and drink that will be served for the believers in Paradise:

أَذَٲلِكَ خَيۡرٌ۬ نُّزُلاً أَمۡ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ (٦٢) إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَـٰهَا فِتۡنَةً۬ لِّلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (٦٣) إِنَّہَا شَجَرَةٌ۬ تَخۡرُجُ فِىٓ أَصۡلِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ (٦٤) طَلۡعُهَا كَأَنَّهُ ۥ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينِ (٦٥)

Is Paradise a better accommodation or the tree of zaqqum? (62) Indeed, We have made it a torment for the wrongdoers. (63) Verily, it is a tree that springs out of the bottom of Hell-fire. (64) The shoots of its fruit-stalks are like the heads of devils. (65)

What do you think the heads of the devils look like? Are they as ugly and scary as we imagine them?

The Surah also describes the forced submission of the wrongdoers on the day of Judgement. Those who refused to submit willingly to Allah’s commands in this life will be forced to submit on that day.

وَقِفُوهُمۡ‌ۖ إِنَّہُم مَّسۡـُٔولُونَ (٢٤) مَا لكُمۡ لَا تَنَاصَرُونَ (٢٥) بَلۡ هُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مُسۡتَسۡلِمُونَ (٢٦)

“But stop them there, Indeed, they are to be questioned. (24) “What is the matter with you? Why do you not help one another (as you used to do in the world)?” (25) Nay, but that day they shall surrender. (26)

Surah As-Saffat issues warnings to those who refuse to submit, indicating that by rejecting Allah’s guidance, they are essentially opposing the inevitable. Ultimately, Allah’s plan will prevail.

وَلَقَدۡ سَبَقَتۡ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (١٧١) إِنَّہُمۡ لَهُمُ ٱلۡمَنصُورُونَ (١٧٢) وَإِنَّ جُندَنَا لَهُمُ ٱلۡغَـٰلِبُونَ (١٧٣)

“And, Our Word has already come to pass in favor of Our slaves, the Messengers (171) that they would surely be victorious (172) and that Our hosts, they would be the victors.” (37:171-173)

The Surat concludes by exalting Allah, asking for Allah’s blessings for his messengers, and offering praise for the Lord of the worlds.

سُبۡحَـٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلۡعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ (١٨٠) وَسَلَـٰمٌ عَلَى ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (١٨١) وَٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٨٢)

Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of Majesty, above what they attribute (to Him). (180) And peace upon the messengers. (181) And praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds. (182)

title: Theme of Surat Saba’ (Sheba) (سَبَإ) (34)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Saba’ (Sheba) (سَبَإ) (34)

The theme of Surat Saba is that preservation of civilization is directly linked to acknowledging and showing gratitude for the blessings bestowed by Allah.…
content:
Theme of Surat Saba’ (Sheba) (سَبَإ) (34)

The theme of Surat Saba is that preservation of civilization is directly linked to acknowledging and showing gratitude for the blessings bestowed by Allah. The Surah discusses two contrasting types of civilizations. The civilization of Prophets Dawud and Suliman who consistently displayed gratitude towards Allah. And the civilization of the people of Saba who rejected Allah’s blessings and refused to submit to His will.

The civilization established by Dawud and his son Suliman was granted by Allah many resources and knowledge. The great blessings that Allah granted to prophet Dawud included:

وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُ ۥدَ مِنَّا فَضۡلاً۬ۖ يَـٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِى مَعَهُ ۥ وَٱلطَّيۡرَۖ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلۡحَدِيدَ (١٠) أَنِ ٱعۡمَلۡ سَـٰبِغَـٰتٍ۬ وَقَدِّرۡ فِى ٱلسَّرۡدِۖ وَٱعۡمَلُواْ صَـٰلِحًاۖ إِنِّى بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ۬ (١١)

Indeed, We bestowed on Dawud (David) great favor from Us (saying): “O mountains, echo with him! My praise and you birds (also)! And We made iron pliant for him.” (10) Saying: “Make perfect armor of (metallic) rings and do righteous deeds. Truly, I am All-Seeing of all that you do.” (34:10-11)

These blessings were:
1. The gift of hearing the Tasbeeh (the glorification of Allah) of the mountains and the birds.
2. The ability to soften steel in his hands rendering it malleable steel without the necessity of heating it to 2200°F (1230°C). This enabled him to form steel into special armor of chains of interlocking rings that provided both protection and comfort for the fighters, giving them a great advantage over his enemies. At that time, the armor was made of forged steel plates that were heavy and cumbersome, restricting the fighter’s mobility.
3. The blessing of a righteous and wise son, Prophet Suliman, who also received great blessings from Allah.

The great blessings that Allah granted to prophet Suliman included:

وَلِسُلَيۡمَـٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ غُدُوُّهَا شَہۡرٌ۬ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَہۡرٌ۬ۖ وَأَسَلۡنَا لَهُ ۥ عَيۡنَ ٱلۡقِطۡرِۖ وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ مَن يَعۡمَلُ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّهِۦۖ وَمَن يَزِغۡ مِنۡهُمۡ عَنۡ أَمۡرِنَا نُذِقۡهُ مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ (١٢) يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُ ۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَـٰرِيبَ وَتَمَـٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانٍ۬ كَالۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورٍ۬ رَّاسِيَـٰتٍۚ (١٣)

And to Suliman (Solomon) (We subjected) the wind, its morning was a month’s (journey), and its afternoon was a month’s (journey) And We caused a spring of (molten) brass to flow for him; and of the jinn were those who worked in front of him, subjugated by the permission of his Lord, And whosoever of them turned aside from Our Command, We made him taste the penalty of the blazing Fire. (34:10-12) They made for him what he willed of elevated chambers, statues, bowls like reservoirs, and stationary kettles. (34:12-13)

These blessings included:
1. The ability to control the wind, allowing him to direct it to wherever necessary to benefit his vast kingdom. He would be able to send and receive anything that would take a month of travel twice daily, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. This helped him overcome the problem of transportation in his vast kingdom.
2. The skill to melt and cast brass (ٱلۡقِطۡرِ) (a Copper-Zinc Alloy) with a melting point of 1700°F (920°C).
3. Control over the Jinn, supported by Allah’s intervention to punish any Jinn who defied his commands. The Jinn built for him:
   1. Mahariib (محاريب) which are places of worship or tall chambers for worship.
      1. This led scholars to conclude that the Mosques need to be high and grand because after all they are the houses of Allah. Mosques need to be in a place by themselves that nothing over them. Therefore, it is discouraged that mosques be built in apartment buildings where apartments will be over them.
   2. Tamaathil (تماثيل) interpreted as statues but also potentially mockup models, possibly representing weapon systems to be manufactured.
   3. Jifaan (جفان) oversized cooking pots capable of serving over 1000 people. Due to their size, they were often placed underground as reservoirs.
      1. Note: in Arabic, there are different names for a cooking pot based on size: The word (القَصْعَةَ) is a pot used to cook for 10 people. The word (الصَّحْفَة) is a pot used to cook for 5 people. The word (المِيْكَلَة) is a pot used to cook for two or three people. The word (الصَّحِيْفة) is used to cook for one person.
   4. Qudoor (قدور) which are cookware or kettles that are very large that require them to be fixed in place.

Allah instructed Prophets Dawud and Solomon to demonstrate gratitude for these blessings through actions, rather than mere verbal expressions of appreciation.

ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُ ۥدَ شُكۡرً۬اۚ وَقَلِيلٌ۬ مِّنۡ عِبَادِىَ ٱلشَّكُورُ (١٣)

“O family of Dawud, work for thanks!” But few of My slaves are thankful. (34:13)

Expressing thanks to Allah through actions involves:
1. Attributing the blessings to Allah, the provider of the blessings.
2. Utilizing the blessings in the obedience of Allah’s command and directives.
3. Guarding against becoming preoccupied with the blessings to the extent of neglecting the One who provided them.
4. Avoiding the trap of becoming arrogant or feeling superior to others due to the blessings received.
5. Consistently and continuously praising and thanking Allah for His blessings.

It’s worth noting that the Ayah concludes by highlighting that only a minority truly express gratitude to Allah. An incident involving Khalifa Omar illustrates this point. Upon hearing a man praying to be among the minority (اللهم اجعلنا من هؤلاء القلّة), Omar inquired about the nature of the supplication. The man explained that he wished to be counted among the few mentioned by Allah (وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ). Reflecting on this, Omar humbly acknowledged his own lack of understanding, recognizing the wisdom in man’s words.

The subsequent verse underscores a significant fact regarding the limitations of the Jinn:

فَلَمَّا قَضَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مَا دَلَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَوۡتِهِۦۤ إِلَّا دَآبَّةُ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ تَأۡڪُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُۥ‌ۖ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلۡجِنُّ أَن لَّوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ مَا لَبِثُواْ فِى ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡمُهِينِ (١٤)

Then when We decreed death for him [Suliman)], nothing informed them (jinn) of his death except a little worm of the earth, which kept (slowly) chewing his stick, so when he fell down, the jinn saw clearly that if they had known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating torment. (34:14)

This Ayah clearly states that the Jinn have no knowledge of the future or the unseen (الجن لا يعلمون الغيب). If they had known that Prophet Sulaiman died, they would have surely stopped work immediately. This should refute all claims by unscrupulous and deceitful individuals who assert that they possess knowledge of the future through communication with the Jinn. The Ayah does not specify how long they continued working while Suliman was deceased, but this detail is not crucial; the essential point is their lack of knowledge regarding the unseen.

The civilization of Dawud and Sulaiman serves as an example of a society in which devout believers expressed their gratitude to Allah through actions. Consequently, Allah preserved their civilization and ensured their security and happiness.

Subsequently, the Surah illustrates the civilization of Saba (Sheba) as a contrasting example—a civilization whose people failed to show gratitude to Allah and even dismissed His blessings. As a consequence, they faced punishment, annihilation, and the destruction of their civilization.

The people of Saba resided in what is now modern-day Yemen. Saba was a significant kingdom that endured for over 1000 years, from the 8th century BCE until the 3rd century CE. Their capital was the city of Ma’rib. The Sabaeans were renowned for their affluence and prosperity, primarily attributed to agricultural and trading activities. (Note: The Quran previously mentioned Saba in the encounter between Prophet Sulaiman and their Queen).

The people of Saba were blessed advanced knowledge of construction that allowed them to build a large dam, known as the dam of Ma’rib, also referred to as the Dam of ‘Arim (سَدّ الْعَرِم). This dam facilitated their agricultural prosperity by regulating the water flow from seasonal floods of two rivers. Controlled irrigation channels enabled the Sabaeans to cultivate crops in an otherwise arid environment. Allah describes His blessings upon Saba by saying:

لَقَدۡ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ۬ فِى مَسۡكَنِهِمۡ ءَايَةٌ۬ ۖ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ۬ وَشِمَالٍ۬ۖ كُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ رَبِّڪُمۡ وَٱشۡڪُرُواْ لَهُۥ‌ۚ بَلۡدَةٌ۬ طَيِّبَةٌ۬ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ۬ (١٥)

Indeed, there was for Saba’ (Sheba) a sign in their dwelling place; two gardens on the right and on the left (and it was said to them) “Eat the provision of your Lord, and be grateful to Him, for an exceedingly good city and an Oft-Forgiving Lord! (34:15)

Furthermore, in addition to those blessings, Allah also favored them with safe and convenient travel routes to other nations. Along these routes, Allah provided a series of towns closely spaced together, ensuring travelers’ security as they always found towns for protection, sustenance, and shelter. This facilitated the development of a prosperous commercial network.

وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَہُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقُرَى ٱلَّتِى بَـٰرَڪۡنَا فِيہَا قُرً۬ى ظَـٰهِرَةً۬ وَقَدَّرۡنَا فِيہَا ٱلسَّيۡرَ‌ۖ سِيرُواْ فِيہَا لَيَالِىَ وَأَيَّامًا ءَامِنِينَ (١٨)

And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns easy to be seen, and We made the stages (of journey) between them easy (saying): “Travel in them safely both by night and day.” (34:18)

However, rather than expressing gratitude, they disregarded and diminished Allah’s blessings. Consequently, deprived them from these blessings:

فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا بَـٰعِدۡ بَيۡنَ أَسۡفَارِنَا وَظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَہُمۡ فَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقۡنَـٰهُمۡ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ۬ شَكُورٍ۬ (١٩)

But they said: “Our Lord! place longer distance between our journey,” and they wronged themselves, so We made them as tales (in the land), and We dispersed them all, totally. Verily, in this are indeed signs for every steadfast grateful (person). (34:19)

Not only did Allah withdraw the ease and comfort of their trading routes due to their ingratitude, but He also deprived them of agricultural blessings by unleashing a significant flood that breached their dam, the Ma’rib Dam, destroying their gardens and dwellings. Allah says:

فَأَعۡرَضُواْ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡہِمۡ سَيۡلَ ٱلۡعَرِمِ وَبَدَّلۡنَـٰهُم بِجَنَّتَيۡہِمۡ جَنَّتَيۡنِ ذَوَاتَىۡ أُڪُلٍ خَمۡطٍ۬ وَأَثۡلٍ۬ وَشَىۡءٍ۬ مِّن سِدۡرٍ۬ قَلِيلٍ۬ (١٦) ذَٲلِكَ جَزَيۡنَـٰهُم بِمَا كَفَرُواْ‌ۖ وَهَلۡ نُجَـٰزِىٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡكَفُورَ (١٧)

But they turned away (from the obedience of Allah), so We sent against them the flood from the Arim dam, and We converted their two gardens into gardens producing fruits of bitter taste, and tamarisks, and some bushes of wild lotes (thorny brushes). (16) Thus, We punished them because of their ungratefulness. And never punish in such a way except for the ungrateful. (34:16-17)

Those who refuse to show gratitude for Allah’s blessings are confirming Satan’s plan to entice people to be ungrateful to Allah.” Allah remarks regarding the people of Saba:

وَلَقَدۡ صَدَّقَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ إِبۡلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٢٠) وَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ عَلَيۡہِم مِّن سُلۡطَـٰنٍ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱلۡأَخِرَةِ مِمَّنۡ هُوَ مِنۡهَا فِى شَكٍّ‌ۗ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ حَفِيظٌ۬ (٢١)

And indeed Iblîs (Satan) did prove true his thought about them, and they followed him, all except a group of believers among them. (20) And he (Iblîs) had no authority over them, except that We might distinguish who believes in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is watching protectively over everything. (34:20-21)

The above Ayah serves as a warning not to follow Iblis’ calls and to always remember that he is our true enemy. Stay vigilant and on guard against this relentless enemy. Ways to disappoint Iblis include:
1. Exercise patience and forgiveness when someone provokes you, thereby thwarting Iblis’s aims.
2. Extend your assistance to those in need to defy Iblis’s intentions.
3. Refrain from lying for personal gain and always uphold the truth, thus disappointing Iblis.
4. Fulfill your obligations and honor your commitments even when betrayal seems advantageous, thus disappointing Iblis.
Iblis can only suggest and insinuate; he lacks control over you and cannot compel you to act. Disappoint him by refusing to heed his suggestions and instead follow Allah’s commandments.

Towards the conclusion of the Surah, Allah instructed the Prophet (PBUH) to convey four statements to anyone who harbors doubt regarding his role as a messenger:

قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٲحِدَةٍۖ أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَفُرَٲدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَڪَّرُواْۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ۬ لَّكُم بَيۡنَ يَدَىۡ عَذَابٍ۬ شَدِيدٍ۬ (٤٦)
قُلۡ مَا سَأَلۡتُكُم مِّنۡ أَجۡرٍ۬ فَهُوَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ شَہِيدٌ۬ (٤٧)
قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّى يَقۡذِفُ بِٱلۡحَقِّ عَلَّـٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ (٤٨)
قُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَمَا يُبۡدِئُ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ (٤٩)
قُلۡ إِن ضَلَلۡتُ فَإِنَّمَآ أَضِلُّ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِىۖ وَإِنِ ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِىٓ إِلَىَّ رَبِّىٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ۬ قَرِيبٌ۬ (٥٠)

Say, “I advise you to do one thing: and that is to stand up before Allah, in pairs, or in singles, and then reflect. You will realize that your companion is not afflicted with madness. He is none but a warner to you of an impending severe torment.” (46)
Say, “No reward do I ask you, the reward is yours. My reward is only from Allah. He is the witness to everything.” (47)
Say, “My Lord sends forth the Truth and He is the knower of the Unseen.” (48)
Say, “The Truth has come, and falsehood has no power to produce or reproduce (anything).” (49)
Say: “If I am in error, I shall carry the burden thereof; and if I am rightly guided, it is because of what my Lord has revealed to me. Truly, He is All-Hearing Ever Near.” (34:46-50)

Then the Surat ended with warnings to all who will not reflect on these statements:

وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذۡ فَزِعُواْ فَلَا فَوۡتَ وَأُخِذُواْ مِن مَّكَانٍ۬ قَرِيبٍ۬ (٥١) وَقَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ مِن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدٍ۬ (٥٢) وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِهِۦ مِن قَبۡلُ‌ۖ وَيَقۡذِفُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ مِن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدٍ۬ (٥٣) وَحِيلَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ مَا يَشۡتَہُونَ كَمَا فُعِلَ بِأَشۡيَاعِهِم مِّن قَبۡلُ‌ۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ فِى شَكٍّ۬ مُّرِيبِۭ (٥٤)

And if you could only see when they are terrified but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a place nearby. (51) And they will [then] say, “We believe in it (the message)” But how can they grasp it from a place far away? (52) And they had rejected it before and would cast (slanders) on the unseen from a position far off. (53) And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in perplexing denial. (34:51-54)

History of the Arabs

The Arabs are classified into three groups based on lineage:
1. Perishing Arabs (العرب البائدة): These ancient Arabs of whose history little is known, notably the tribes of Ad and Thamud that were mentioned in the Quran.
2. Arabized Arabs (العرب المستعربة): Descendants of Prophet Ishmael, also known as ‘Adnanian Arabs (العرب العدنانية).
3. Pure Arabs (العرب العاربة) specifically the Qahtanian Arabs (العرب القحطانية). They trace their lineage back to Ya’rub bin Yashjub bin Qahtan (يَشْجُب بن يَعْرُب بن قَحْطَان).
Following the destruction of the Dam, this tribe split into two factions:
   1. Himyar (حِمْيَر) remained in Yemen.
   2. Kahlan (كَهْلان) migrated from Yemen to various parts of the Arabian Peninsula, dividing into four main groups:
      1. A faction under the leadership of Imran bin ‘Amr (عمران بن عمرو) settled in Oman (عُمَان).
      2. A faction led by Tha‘labah bin ‘Amr (ثَعْلَبة بن عمرو مزيقياء) relocated in Madinah with some of their descendants becoming the Aws and Khazraj.
      3. A group led by Haritha bin ‘Amr (حارثة بن عمرو), known as Khuza‘a (خزاعة), wandered in Hijaz until they conquered Makkah and settled there after displacing its inhabitants, the tribe of Jurhum Jurhum (لجراهمة).
      4. A faction led by Jafna bin ‘Amr (جَفْنَة بن عمرو) migrated to Syria, where they established the kingdom of Ghassan near the Byzantine Empire’s borders.

During the Umayyad Dynasty (العصر الأموي), conflicts erupted between the Qahtani tribes (القبائل القحطانية) and the Adnani tribes (القبائل العدنانية), resulting in wars that weakened the Umayyads and eventually led to the downfall of their empire (سقوط الدولة الأموية).

content:
Theme of Surat Al-Ahzab (الاٴحزَاب) (The confederates) (33)

Surat Al-Ahzab (الأحزاب) was revealed in Madina. The theme of the Surah is maintaining submission to Allah even in difficult and embarrassing situations.

While all Muslims profess belief in Allah, such claims require evidence. The depth of belief in Allah is gauged by one’s acceptance of His will and adherence to His commands. While people may submit to those more powerful or to their own desires, believers recognize Allah's supremacy and thus submit to Him without questioning or hesitation.

Difficult situations often test a believer’s submission to Allah. These situations may involve physical danger, embarrassment, or the risk of losing something valuable. Surat Al-Ahzab provides examples of such challenging circumstances that may lead individuals to compromise their obedience to Allah.

To underscore the central theme of submission and obedience to Allah, the term “obedience” (الطاعة) is mentioned seven times and “honesty” (الصدق) eight times throughout the Surah. The opening Ayah instructs the Prophet (PBUH) not to obey anyone other than Allah.

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا (١)

“O Prophet! Keep your duty to Allah, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Verily, Allah is Ever All-Knower, All-Wise.” (33:1)

Furthermore, numerous other verses in the Surah convey a similar message. For example:

وَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ وَدَعۡ أَذَٮٰهُمۡ وَتَوَڪَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَڪِيلاً۬ (٤٨)

“And obey not the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and do not harm them. And put your trust in Allah, and Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.” (33:48)

The Surah presents various challenging situations to exemplify submission to Allah under diverse conditions.

1. Submission to Allah in facing enemies:

The situation that Muslims faced in the battle of confederates (Al-Ahzab) (الأحزاب غزوة); also called the battle of the Trench (غزوة الخندق) was extremely difficult. The following Ayah describes the tough situation the Muslims faced:

إِذۡ جَآءُوكُم مِّن فَوۡقِكُمۡ وَمِنۡ أَسۡفَلَ مِنكُمۡ وَإِذۡ زَاغَتِ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلۡحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ (١٠) هُنَالِكَ ٱبۡتُلِىَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ زِلۡزَالاً۬ شَدِيدً۬ا (١١)

“When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes grew wild and the hearts reached the throats, and you were harboring doubts about Allah. There, the believers were tried and shaken with a mighty shaking.” (33:10-11)

Yet, the Muslims’ reaction in this difficult situation was:

وَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابَ قَالُواْ هَـٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥ‌ۚ وَمَا زَادَهُمۡ إِلَّآ إِيمَـٰنً۬ا وَتَسۡلِيمً۬ا (٢٢)

“When the Believers saw the Confederate forces, they said: “This is what Allah and his Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger told us what was true.” And it only added to their faith and their zeal in obedience. “(33:22)

And in return those Muslims received wonderful testimony from Allah for their trust in Him:

مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ۬ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَـٰهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡهِ‌ۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحۡبَهُ ۥ وَمِنۡہُم مَّن يَنتَظِرُ‌ۖ وَمَا بَدَّلُواْ تَبۡدِيلاً۬ (٢٣)

“Among the Believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah: of them some have completed their vow (to the extreme), and some (still) wait but they have never changed (their determination) in the least.” (33:23)

The Surah was named “Al-Ahzab”, meaning “the parties”, “the confederates”, “the allies” because there were many parties opposing the Muslims in this battle. Also, besides the external parties on the enemy side, the following two internal parties among the Muslims contributed to the challenge:

1. The hypocrites (حزب المنافقين)

هُنَالِكَ ٱبۡتُلِىَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ زِلۡزَالاً۬ شَدِيدً۬ا (١١) وَإِذۡ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ۬ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا غُرُورً۬ا (١٢)

There, the believers were tried and shaken with a mighty shaking. (11) And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease (of doubts) said: “Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion!” (33:11-12)

1. The frightened and hesitant (حزب المترددين الخائفين)

وَإِذۡ قَالَت طَّآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ يَثۡرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمۡ فَٱرۡجِعُواْ‌ۚ وَيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُ فَرِيقٌ۬ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوۡرَةٌ۬ وَمَا هِىَ بِعَوۡرَةٍ‌ۖ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارً۬ا (١٣) وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡہِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُٮِٕلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأَتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِہَا إِلَّا يَسِيرً۬ا (١٤)

And when a party of them said: “O people of Yathrib (Al-Madinah)! There is no stand (possible) for you (against the enemy attack!) Therefore, go back!” And a band of them ask for permission of the Prophet saying: “Truly, our homes lie open (to the enemy).” And they lay not open. They but wished to flee. (13) And if the enemy had entered from all sides (of the city), and they had been exhorted to Al-Fitnah (i.e. to renegade from Islam) they would surely have committed it and would have hesitated thereupon but little. (33:13-14)

وَلَقَدۡ كَانُواْ عَـٰهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مِن قَبۡلُ لَا يُوَلُّونَ ٱلۡأَدۡبَـٰرَ‌ۚ وَكَانَ عَهۡدُ ٱللَّهِ مَسۡـُٔولاً۬ (١٥)

And indeed, they had already made a covenant with Allah not to turn their backs, and a covenant with Allah must be answered for. (33:15)

Despite the huge challenge that faced Muslims from all the different parties, sincere Muslims exhibited unwavering trust in Allah. As a result, Allah rewarded them by sending a powerful storm that dispersed the external enemies causing them to flee the area. Allah says:

فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡہِمۡ رِيحً۬ا وَجُنُودً۬ا lَّmۡ تَرَوۡهَا‌ۚ وَڪَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرً۬ا (٩)

“…We sent against them a hurricane and forces that you did not see…” (33:9).

2. Submission to Allah in opposing social norms.

The second difficult situation that is presented in the Surah involves submission to Allah in areas that may cause embarrassment because they go against the social norms of society. This difficult situation is related to the divorce of Zaid (زَيْد) from Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA) (زينب بنت جحش) and the Prophet’s (PBUH) subsequent marriage to her:

وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِىٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِى فِى نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَٮٰهُ‌ۖ (٣٦)

“And (remember) when you said to him (Zaid bin Harithah) on whom Allah has bestowed Grace and you have conferred favor on him: “Keep your wife to yourself, and fear Allah.” But you did hide in yourself that which Allah has brought to light (i.e. that Allah has already made known to you that will marry her). You are afraid of the people (i.e., what they will say about you) whereas Allah is more deserving to fear Him. (33:36)

فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدٌ۬ مِّنۡہَا وَطَرً۬ا زَوَّجۡنَـٰكَهَا لِكَىۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ۬ فِىٓ أَزۡوَٲجِ أَدۡعِيَآٮِٕهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡہُنَّ وَطَرً۬ا‌ۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولاً۬ (٣٧)

So, when Zaid had completed the necessary formalities (i.e. divorced her), We gave her to you in marriage, so that (in future) there will no difficulty to the believers in respect of (the marriage of) the wives of their adopted sons when the latter have no desire to keep them. And Allah’s command must be fulfilled. (33:37)

This situation illustrates the significant social pressure that led the Prophet (PBUH) to initially resist what Allah had informed him would come to pass. Allah had revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) that Zayd would divorce Zaynab, and upon this occurrence, the Prophet was to marry her. However, the Prophet hesitated, mindful of societal norms and the anticipated attack from disbelievers and hypocrites.

So, he (PBUH) kept counseling Zayd not to divorce Zaynab, but Zayd persisted in his decision. Ultimately, Allah’s decree unfolded, compelling the Prophet (PBUH) to submit to His will. Zayd divorced Zaynab, and the Prophet (PBUH) married her.

Regrettably, some Muslim scholars continued the falsehoods propagated by disbelievers and hypocrites concerning this event. They misinterpreted the Quranic verse (وَتُخۡفِى فِى نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ) to imply that the Prophet harbored secret affection for Zaynab, whereas its true meaning pertains to concealing Allah’s command to marry her post-divorce. They overlooked Zaynab’s familial relation to the Prophet (PBUH) and her marriage to Zayd at the Prophet’s encouragement, indicating her obedience to him.

Allah instructed the Prophet to marry Zaynab to abolish the practice of adoption, which was relevant to Zayd, a former slave liberated and adopted by the Prophet (PBUH). For an extended period, the Prophet referred to Zayd as “Zayd ibn Mohammad” until Allah revealed verses clarifying that a man does not have two fathers. Subsequently, Zayd’s name was changed to “Zayd ibn Harithah” (زيد بن حارثة) after his biological father.

مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ۬ مِّن قَلۡبَيۡنِ فِى جَوۡفِهِۦ‌ۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزۡوَٲجَكُمُ ٱلَّـٰٓـِٔى تُظَـٰهِرُونَ مِنۡہُنَّ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمۡ‌ۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدۡعِيَآءَكُمۡ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكُمۡ قَوۡلُكُم بِأَفۡوَٲهِكُمۡ‌ۖ وَٱللَّهَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهۡدِى ٱلسَّبِيلَ (٤)

ٱدۡعُوهُمۡ لِأَبَآٮِٕهِمۡ هُوَ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٲنُكُمۡ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَمَوَٲلِيكُمۡ‌ۚ وَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ۬ فِيمَآ أَخۡطَأۡتُم بِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمۡ‌ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمًا (٥)

“Allah has not placed two hearts in any man’s body: nor He has granted you wives whom you may back away from, to act as if they are your mothers: nor has He made your adopted sons to be your own sons. Such is your own statement made by your mouth. But Allah tells the Truth, and He guides to the (right) Way. (4)

Call them after their own fathers: that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know who their fathers are, then (call them) your brothers in Faith, or your wards (dependents, protégés). There is no blame on you if you have made a mistake; what counts is what your heart have done intentionally: Yet, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.” (Al-Ahzab 33:4-5)

The Prophet’s marriage of Zayd’s former wife caused embarrassment and provided an opportunity for the hypocrites to attack the Prophet (PBUH). Although the Prophet (PBUH) sought to avoid this situation, Allah intended to preempt any future restrictions, explaining this rationale in following Ayah:

مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ مِنۡ حَرَجٍ۬ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۖ ۥ سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِى ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُ‌ۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرً۬ا مَّقۡدُورًا (٣٨)

“There is no blame on the Prophet in that which Allah has made legal for him. This has been Allah's Way with those who have passed away of (the Prophets of) old. And the Command of Allah is certain destiny. (33:38)

So, despite the social pressure and the potential embarrassment, the Prophet (PBUH) submitted to Allah’s command.

3. Submission to Allah in face of family pressure

The third challenging circumstance pertains to family matters, a significant aspect due to the fact that numerous husbands find themselves unable to adhere to the commands of Allah due to pressure from their wives. This predicament was encountered by the Prophet (PBUH) when his wives urged him to provide them with additional financial resources. While their request was not unreasonable, primarily seeking comfort, Allah intended to establish them as examples for Muslim women and the Prophet (PBUH) as an example for Muslim men.

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٲجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحً۬ا جَمِيلاً۬ (٢٨) وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلۡمُحۡسِنَـٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمً۬ا (٢٩)

“O Prophet; say to your wives: “If you desire the life of this world, and its glitter, then come! I will make a provision for you and set you free in a handsome manner (divorce). “But if you desire Allah and His Messenger, and the home of the Hereafter, then verily, Allah has prepared for the good doers among you an immense reward.” (33:28-29)

This verse elucidates that if a wife places financial demands on her husband that lead him to compromise Allah’s commands to satisfy her, he should contemplate divorcing her, regardless of his affection for her. This should also serve as a clear warning to the wife.

4. Submission to Allah’s rulings without hesitation.

Submission to Allah’s commands should be wholehearted, without hesitation or pretext, even if one does not comprehend the underlying wisdom. Allah says:

وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنٍ۬ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥۤ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡ‌ۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَـٰلاً۬ مُّبِينً۬ا (٣٦)

“It is not for a believer, man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter that they should have any option in their decision. And who disobeys Allah and His messenger, he has indeed gone astray in a plain error.” (33:36)

5. Submission to Allah’s covenant

The Surah reaffirms that obedience to Allah’s covenant is a command given to all the Prophets of Allah. Allah says:

وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِيثَـٰقَهُمۡ وَمِنكَ وَمِن نُّوحٍ۬ وَإِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَ‌ۖ وَأَخَذۡنَا مِنۡہُم مِّيثَـٰقًا غَلِيظً۬ا (٧) لِّيَسۡـَٔلَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ عَن صِدۡقِهِمۡ‌ۚ وَأَعَدَّ لِلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمً۬ا (٨)

And (remember) when We took from the Prophets their covenant, and from you (O Muhammad SAW), and from Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), and Isa (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary). We took from them a strong covenant. (7)

That He may ask the truthful about their truth. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful torment. (33:7-8)

If submission to Allah’s covenant is a command to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), it is also a command to all his followers who are instructed to emulate him:

لَّقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِى رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ۬ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأَخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرً۬ا (٢١)

Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good role model for him who hopes for (the Meeting with) Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much. (33:21)

6. Submission of women through modest attire

Submission of women through modest attire is emphasized by Allah, demonstrating His concern for Muslim women and prescribing a means for their protection:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٲجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يُدۡنِينَ عَلَيۡہِنَّ مِن جَلَـٰبِيبِهِنَّ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن يُعۡرَفۡنَ فَلَا يُؤۡذَيۡنَ‌ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ا (٥٩)

“O Prophet! Tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments over themselves (when they go abroad). That will be better, so that they may be recognized and not annoyed. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.” (33:59)

7. Submission through frequent remembrance of Allah and invoking blessings upon the Prophet (PBUH)

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ ذِكۡرً۬ا كَثِيرً۬ا (٤١) وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكۡرَةً وَأَصِيلاً (٤٢) هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَلِّى عَلَيۡڪُمۡ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَتُهُ ۥ لِيُخۡرِجَڪُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ‌ۚ وَكَانَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَحِيمً۬ا (٤٣)

“O you who believe! Remember Allah with very frequent remembrance (42) And glorify Him morning and evening. (43) He sends blessings to you, as do His angels, so that He brings you out from the depths of Darkness into light: and He is Merciful to the Believers.” (Ahzab 33:41-43)

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَتَهُ ۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّۚ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيۡهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمًا (٥٦)

“Allah and His Angels send blessings to the Prophet: O you who believe! Ask blessings for him and salute him with a worthy salutation. (Al-Azab 33:56)

8. Submission by fulfilling our entrusted responsibilities.

We have previously explored these verses, and thus I will interpret them in light of our previous discussion.

إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَہَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡہَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ ظَلُومً۬ا جَهُولاً۬ (٧٢) لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقَـٰتِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكَـٰتِ وَيَتُوبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ‌ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ا (٧٣)

“(To demonstrate to man his unique capabilities compared to other creation) Allah projected the Trust (the guardianship on earth following His guidance) to the Heavens and the Earth and the Mountains; but they were unable to bear it because of their limited capacity and softness. But man (whom Allah equipped with special capabilities) was given the trust. (But if man does not recognize the capabilities and the talents that Allah endowed him with) He will be truly unjust and foolish. (72)

(Therefore) Allah punishes the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the idolatrous men and the idolatrous women (those who commit injustice against themselves and do not protect the trust). And Allah pardons the believing men and the believing women (those who acknowledge the resources that Allah endowed them with and protect the trust), and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. “(Al-Ahzab 33: 72-73)

title: Surat As-Sajdah (Prostration)
excerpt:
Surat As-Sajdah (Prostration)

Surat As-Sajdah was revealed in Mecca. The theme of the Surat is the willing submission to Allah. This may suggest why the Prophet (PBUH) often recited this Surat in…
content:
Surat As-Sajdah (Prostration)

Surat As-Sajdah was revealed in Mecca. The theme of the Surat is the willing submission to Allah. This may suggest why the Prophet (PBUH) often recited this Surat in the Friday morning prayer. There are two kinds of submission to Allah: Compulsory submission and Voluntary Submission.

The compulsory submission is physiological in nature. Our bodies submit to Allah’s control over the functions of breathing, digestion, genetic codes, biological changes, etc.

The voluntary submission is manifested in several ways such as:
1. Ritualistic submission as symbolized by physical prostrations (السجود).
2. Psychological submission by accepting Allah’s decree in times of trial.
3. Behavioral submission by firm adherence to Allah’s commands.

The Surat highlights the ritualistic submission through prostration as an attribute for those who believe.
إِنَّمَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُڪِّرُواْ بِہَا خَرُّواْ سُجَّدً۬ا وَسَبَّحُواْ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّہِمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ ۩ (١٥)
“Only those people believe in Our signs who when they are reminded of them, fall in prostration, and glorify the Praises of their Lord, and they do not show any arrogance.” (32:15)

This Ayat tells us that reflecting on Allah’s Ayat (signs) is the way to know Allah and believe in Him because Allah Himself cannot be seen but His signs are seen. When seeing the signs of Allah, a believer should prostrate in submission as an expression of awe of Allah. Since the Quran emphasizes the importance of reflecting on Allah’s signs in the universe, many scholars suggest that studying the signs of Allah in the universe is an important act of worship. Abu-Aldarda (أبو الدرداء) and Hassan Al-Basri (الحسن البصري) said that contemplation for one hour is better than spending all night praying (تفكر ساعة خير من قيام ليلة).

The Surat provides another picture of the believers. While sleeping represent rest and relaxation; the bodies of those who truly believe in Allah refuse to sleep due to the extent of their fear of hellfire and their longing for Paradise.
تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّہُمۡ خَوۡفً۬ا وَطَمَعً۬ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ (١٦)
“Their sides forsake their beds, calling on their Lord in fear and hope, and spend (in charity) out of what We have bestowed on them.” (32:16)

Notice the brilliance of the expression (تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ) “Their sides forsake their beds” (32:16). This Ayat has an explicit meaning and an implicit meaning. The explicit meaning is that the believer’s body refuses to go to sleep because it rather worships Allah and supplicates to Allah. The implicit meaning is that their bodies do not relax in this life because they focus on preparing for the Hereafter.

The Ayat also provides the balance of the believer’s feelings between fearing Allah and hoping in Allah’s mercy. The believers neither have killer fear nor silly hope.

Then the Surat presents an example of two people and in a way asks everyone: who represents you the best?
أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤۡمِنً۬ا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقً۬ا‌ۚ لَّا يَسۡتَوُ ۥنَ (١٨)
Is he who is a believer like him who is defiantly disobedient? Surely, they are not equal. (32:18)

Does anyone really think that Allah will treat those who obey Him as those who disobey Him? Since these two groups are not equal in this life, they surely will not be equal in the Hereafter. Thus, their eternal compensation will be dramatically different. The reward for the believers who submit freely to Allah will be:
أَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتُ ٱلۡمَأۡوَىٰ nuzulā (١٩)
As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are the gardens of retreat, an honorable hospitality for what they used to do. (32:19)

This Ayat makes it clear that paradise requires belief and the righteous deeds to validate the belief. The promise of Paradise with all what it will have, should make the believers live happily in this life even when facing hardships. To illustrate that awaiting a huge reward can ease current pains, let us consider the case of a poor man who is continuously in debt. This man inherited a huge wealth, but it will take two years to settle the legal matters before he will get the money. What do you think this man feels about his poverty within these two years? Most likely, he would not care about his poverty because of the promise of the money he would get in two years. A believer should feel the same by focusing on the promise of Allah of Paradise.

If we look at this illustration and consider the relative time between the time on earth and the time with Allah, we will recognize that all difficulties one faces on earth are merely a fraction of an hour. Allah highlights the relativity of time by saying:
يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ يَعۡرُجُ إِلَيۡهِ فِى يَوۡمٍ۬ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥۤ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ۬ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ (٥)
He directs [every] matter from the heaven to the earth (i.e., all that exist in the universe); then it (every matter) will ascend to Him in a day whose length is like one thousand years of those which you count. (32:5)

This means that Allah sends His commands to all who exist in the universe and receives the response to His commands in one day. So, all the record of a human being who lives 100 years will be equivalent to less than 2 1/2 hrs in that time. Keeping in mind that there is another Ayat in the Quran that refers to a day with Allah as 50,000 years. This means that our life on earth is extremely short when we look at the hereafter.

But there are those who are willing to sacrifice happiness in eternal time for the enjoyment of part of an hour by their continuous disobedience and transgression. For them, the reward will be:
وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُواْ فَمَأۡوَٮٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ‌ۖ كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡہَآ أُعِيدُواْ فِيهَا وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ (٢٠)
And as for those who are defiantly disobedient, their retreat is the Fire. Whenever they desire to come out of it, they will be turned back into it, and it will be said to them: Taste the torment of the Fire that you used to deny. (32:20)

It is of Allah’s mercy on those who are defiantly disobedient that Allah will give them warnings in this life by giving them a taste of suffering, so they may return:
وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ (٢١)
And verily We make them taste the lower punishment (in this life) before the greater punishment, in order that they may return (in repentance). (32:21)

Reflecting on this Ayat, one may note that people fall in four groups:
1. A righteous group who lives happily in his life.
2. A righteous group who lives miserably in his life.
3. A disobedient group who lives happily in his life.
4. A disobedient group who lives miserably in his life.

A happy life for the righteous group and a miserable life for the disobedient group should generally be expected. The righteous group who lives miserably in this life indicates that Allah loves it and tests it to grant it additional rewards. The worst group is the one who lives happily in his life because this implies that Allah has abandoned it. The disobedient group who lives miserably is a group that Allah did not abandon, as addressed in the above Ayat.

If you note that a bad thing happens each time you commit a sin, it means that Allah loves you and thus sends you warning messages. Imagine you are walking and suddenly someone slaps you on the back, you turn around looking very angry for what happened to you but when you look back, you see a scorpion that fell off your back. You should be grateful to the person who slapped your back because he saved you from harm.

Those who ignore all the chances given to them to repent commit the fatal mistake by rejecting their meeting with Allah:
وَقَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا ضَلَلۡنَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَءِنَّا لَفِى خَلۡقٍ۬ جَدِيدِۭ‌ۚ بَلۡ هُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّهِمۡ كَـٰفِرُونَ (١٠)
And they say: “Is it that when we disappear in the earth, shall we really come into a new creation? Nay, but they deny the meeting with their Lord!” (32:10)

But they must be assured that they will leave this life and will be resurrected to face Allah:
قُلۡ يَتَوَفَّٮٰكُم مَّلَكُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ ٱلَّذِى وُكِّلَ بِكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ تُرۡجَعُونَ (١١)
“Say: “The angel of death, who has been assigned for you will take your soul. Then you will be brought back to your Lord.” (32:11)

Unfortunately, some people will remain heedless and will not recognize the truth about the Hereafter until they face the consequences:
وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِہِمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ رَبَّنَآ أَبۡصَرۡنَا وَسَمِعۡنَا فَٱرۡجِعۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَـٰلِحًا إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ (١٢)
And if you only could see when the criminals (sinners) hanging down their heads before their Lord (saying): “Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back (to the world), we will do righteous good deeds. Verily! We now believe with certainty.” (32:12)

But it would be too late because Allah has already decreed that He will not compel anyone to believe:
وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَأَتَيۡنَا كُلَّ نَفۡسٍ هُدَٮٰهَا وَلَـٰكِنۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ مِنِّى لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ (١٣)
If We had so willed, We could have imposed Our guidance upon every human being: but My word had come true: “I will most certainly fill Hell with jinn and humans, all together.” (32:13)

The Surat directs us to Bani Israel to inform us that Allah honored those of them who are guided, patient, and had certainty in their belief:
وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۡہُمۡ أَٮِٕمَّةً۬ يَہۡدُونَ بِأَمۡرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُواْ‌ۖ وَڪَانُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا يُوقِنُونَ (٢٤)
“And We made from among them (Children of Israel), leaders who give guidance under Our command because they were patient and used to believe with certainty in Our Ayat (signs).” (32:24)

To achieve this honor, the person must be committed to guiding others, have patience, and have certainty in belief. No one is allowed to judge people’s belief because judgment is for Allah alone:
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ فِيمَا ڪَانُواْ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَ (٢٥)
Verily, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, concerning that wherein they used to differ. (32:25)

This Ayat should warn those who go around passing judgement on others and thus create divisions and enmity. The Story of the Prophet’s companion Othman ibn Mazoun (عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ) that has been reported by Um Al-Ala’ (أم العلاء) gives a clear warning regarding this. When Othman died, she said:
رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَا السَّائِبِ , شَهَادَتِي عَلَيْكَ لَقَدْ أَكْرَمَكَ اللَّهُ ,
“Mercy be on you Aba Alsa’ab, I am sure that Allah has blessed you (meaning with paradise)”.
The Prophet (PBUH) said: “How do you know that Allah has blessed him?” She said: “I do not know” (لَا أَدْرِي , بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي).
The Prophet (PBUH) said:
أَمَّا هُوَ، فَقَدْ جَاءَهُ الْيَقِينُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ , وَإِنِّي لَأَرْجُو الْخَيْرَ له , وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي , وَأَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ , مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي
As for him, he met the truth from His Lord and I wish good for him, by Allah, I don’t know, and I am the messenger of Allah, what will be done with me.
She said: (وَاللَّهِ لَا أُزَكِّي أَحَدًا بَعْدَهُ أَبَدًا) “By Allah, I will never ascribe purity to anyone after him ever.”

The Prophet (PBUH) gave through another story major warning to those who appoint themselves as judges of others’ fate.
قال أبو هريرة سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول “كان رجلان في بني إسرائيل متواخيين فكان أحدهما يذنب والآخر مجتهد في العبادة…”
There were two very good friends from Bani Israel. One of them was very pious in his worship and the other used to commit sins. The pious friend used to always advise his friend to stop committing sins until one day he found him committing a sin and he told him: “By Allah, Allah will not forgive you and will not admit you to paradise.” On the Day of Judgment, Allah asked the pious man: “Did you have knowledge of Me? Or were you in control of what is in My hand?” Then Allah said to the sinner: “Go and enter Paradise by My mercy,” and said to the other: “Go to the Fire.”

In addition to patience, the leader must have certainty in belief because both are interlinked. Satisfaction with Allah’s decree is a sign of certainty. As it was said:
(الرضا بمكروه القضاء أرفع درجات اليقين) “The highest level of certainty in belief is by being satisfied with the disliked decree.”
Also, Imam Al-Shafie (الشافعي) said:
إذا كان سرورك بالنِقمة كسرورك بالنِعمة فقد رضيت عن الله .
“If your happiness with a misfortune is as your happiness with a blessing, you are then satisfied with Allah.”

To see Allah’s warning regarding disbelief, He preserved for us the archeological effects of previous generations who were destroyed because of their disbelief:
أَوَلَمۡ يَهۡدِ لَهُمۡ كَمۡ أَهۡلَڪۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ يَمۡشُونَ فِى مَسَـٰكِنِهِمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ‌ۖ أَفَلَا يَسۡمَعُونَ (٢٦)
Do they learn no lesson by recalling how many generations We have destroyed before them; in whose dwellings they now walk? Verily, in that are signs. Will they not then listen? (32:26)

Muslims of today should learn from what happened to Muslims in Spain 500 years ago. Their divisions and turning away from the commands of Allah led to their downfall. Other signs of Allah that we can learn from are those related to natural science:
وَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا نَسُوقُ ٱلۡمَآءَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡجُرُزِ فَنُخۡرِجُ بِهِۦ زَرۡعً۬ا تَأۡڪُلُ مِنۡهُ أَنۡعَـٰمُهُمۡ وَأَنفُسُہُمۡ‌ۖ أَفَلَا يُبۡصِرُونَ (٢٧)
Have they not seen how We drive water to the dry land that has no vegetation, and therewith bring forth crops providing food for their cattle and themselves? Will they not then see? (32:27)

Through both History and natural sciences, people learn that they must submit to Allah. But despite all signs, the arrogant still ask:
وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَـٰذَا ٱلۡفَتۡحُ إِن ڪُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (٢٨) قُلۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَتۡحِ لَا يَنفَعُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِيمَـٰنُهُمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ (٢٩) فَأَعۡرِضۡ عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون (٣٠)
They say: “When will this decision be (regarding the Day of Judgment), if you (believers) are truthful?” Say: “On the Day of Decision, no profit will it be to the disbelievers if they (then) believe! Nor will they be granted a respite.” So turn away from them (O Muhammad) and wait (for Allah's judgment); they (too) are waiting. (32:28-30)

For those who are arrogant, and no sign of Allah impacts them, they do not deserve the attention of the Prophet or the believers. We should focus on ourselves. As the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسولُ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لرجلٍ وهو يَعِظُه: ((اغْتَنِمْ خَمْسًا قبلَ خَمْسٍ: شَبابَكَ قبلَ هِرَمِكَ، وصِحَّتَكَ قبلَ سَقَمِكَ، وغِناءَكَ قبلَ فَقْرِكَ، وفَرَاغَكَ قبلَ شُغْلِكَ، وحَياتَكَ قبلَ مَوْتِكَ))
“Seize the advantage of five matters before five other matters: your youth, before you become old; your health, before you fall sick; your wealth, before you become poor; your free time, before you become busy; and your life, before your death.”

title: Theme of Surat Al-Ankaboot (The Spider) (29)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Al-Ankaboot (The Spider) (29)

Surat Al-Ankaboot was revealed in Mecca close to the time before the Hijra when Muslims were facing major difficulties from the disbelievers. The theme…
content:
Theme of Surat Al-Ankaboot (The Spider) (29)

Surat Al-Ankaboot was revealed in Mecca close to the time before the Hijra when Muslims were facing major difficulties from the disbelievers. The theme of the Surat is that life is a series of trials and success will always be for those who are truthful in their belief in Allah and face these trials with patience and resolve. The Surat starts with:

أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ (٢) وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ‌ۖ فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَـٰذِبِينَ (٣)

Do people think that they will be left (at ease) because they say: “We believe,” and will not be tested. (2) Indeed, We have tested those before them. So, Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars. (29:2-3)

This Ayat addresses the often-raised question: “Why are we subjected to trials since Allah knows everyone’s response in advance?

The literal translation on the term (فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ) is “So Allah will surely know”. This literal translation contradicts the attribute that Allah knows everything. We need to realize that Allah speaks to us in a language that we understand while taking int account our constraint of time and space. But when we speak about Allah’s actions, we should consider that He is neither constrained by time nor by space and thus associating Allah’s actions with time is not valid. We also need to realize that while Allah is All-Knowing, His knowledge has no influence on our actions. Ina addition, it is an element of absolute justice that a judge does not use his own special knowledge to make a ruling, Therefore, Allah will only judge us based testimonies, recordings, and eyewitnesses.

The trails that we are subjected to are different levels. Everyone will be tested according to his/her capabilities. Every person will be judged based on his/her response to these trials. A general grade of pass or fail will be given to everyone in the Hereafter. Within each general grade, there are rankings to distinguish between high performers. We all aspire not only to have a passing grade but also to achieve the highest grade that allows us a place in the Ferdous Al-Ala. Those who receive a failing grade will have their ranking with the worst ranking given to the hypocrites who will deserve a place in the worst place in Hell.

Trials are different, the most challenging trial is that involving belief to differentiate between true believers and hypocrites. Allah says:

وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِىَ فِى ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتۡنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَئِن جَآءَ نَصۡرٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمۡ‌ۚ أَوَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعۡلَمَ بِمَا فِى صُدُورِ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٠) وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ (١١)

Among the people there are those who say: “We believe in Allah”, but if they are harmed for their belief in Allah, they consider the trial of the people equal to the punishment of Allah, and if victory comes from your Lord, they will say: “Verily! We were with you (helping you).” Is it not that Allah knows well what lies in the hearts of all creations. (10) Verily, Allah will certainly know those who believe, and He will certainly know the hypocrites. (29:10-11)

Note: Reflecting on the current condition in Gaza, when the people of Gaza gain victory, insha’Allah, I wonder how many people, particularly those leaders of Islamic countries, will claim that they were supporting them.

Every time we pass a test from Allah, we build up the chest of our treasure in eternity. This is what the Prophet taught us. Whether we are tested with misfortune or with fortune, our success in passing the test depends on the nature of our reaction to it. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ أبي يَحْيَى صُهَيْبِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ  قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ الله ﷺ: عَجَباً لأمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إنَّ أمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ لَهُ خَيْرٌ، وَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ لأَحَدٍ إلاَّ للْمُؤْمِنِ: إنْ أصَابَتْهُ سَرَّاءُ شَكَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْراً لَهُ، وَإنْ أصَابَتْهُ ضَرَّاءُ صَبَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْراً لَهُ. رواه مسلم

“I wonder about the state of a believer, it is all good. And this is for no one but the believer. If he receives fortunes, he thanks Allah and that is good for him. And if misfortune inflicts him, he is patient and that is good for him”. (Muslim)

One of the difficult trials that is mentioned in the Surat is that by one’s own parent who pressure their child to associate others with Allah while the child is commanded by Allah to be kind to them. Allah gives the guidance regarding how to balance kindness with lack of obedience:

وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ بِوَٲلِدَيۡهِ حُسۡنً۬ا‌ۖ وَإِن جَـٰهَدَاكَ لِتُشۡرِكَ بِى مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ۬ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَآ‌ۚ إِلَىَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (٨)

“And We have enjoined on man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. To Me is your return and I shall tell you what you used to do.” (29:8)

The word “Shirk” does not necessarily mean to worship another god. Shirk is broader. It includes attempts by the parents to convince their children to comprise their morals to achieve some materialistic gains on the belief that their fortune in life is in the hands of other people. Also, parents may intercede on behalf of someone to force their children who are in position of authority to give a position to an undeserving candidate. Parents may also push their children to violate Allah’s command thinking that this will help them in securing jobs. This may happen regarding proper Islamic dress for girls. Those parents forget that Allah says:

وَڪَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ۬ لَّا تَحۡمِلُ رِزۡقَهَا ٱللَّهُ يَرۡزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمۡ‌ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ (٦٠)

And how many creatures there is that does carry its [own] provision. Allah provides provision for it as well as to you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. (29:60)

The Surat narrates many trials involving Prophets such as Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Lut (Lot), Shu’aib and Musa (Moses) (Peace upon them) and how they faced trials. Prophet Nuh’s trial was the responsibility of delivering the Da’wa to Allah and his trials lasted for 950 years.

وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامً۬ا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمۡ ظَـٰلِمُونَ (١٤) فَأَنجَيۡنَـٰهُ وَأَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلسَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلۡنَـٰهَآ ءَايَةً۬ لِّلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٥)

And We sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years. Then the flood seized them, and they were wrongdoers. (14) But We saved him and the people of the ship, and We made it a sign for all the worlds. (29:14-15)

The Ayat referring to the Prophets’ trials show that their patience and perseverance have always led to success and comfort. Realizing the extent of the Prophets’ trials should help us to endure our trials which are certainly much less difficult than those of the Prophets. We also realize from the stories of the Prophets that Allah’s assistance will also come with the trials.

The Surat highlights the worldly punishment of those who failed in their trails and insisted on their disbelief and rejection of the guidance delivered to them by Allah’s messengers.

فَكُلاًّ أَخَذۡنَا بِذَنۢبِهِۦ‌ۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ حَاصِبً۬ا وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ خَسَفۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَغۡرَقۡنَا‌ۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظۡلِمَهُمۡ وَلَـٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ (٤٠)

“Thus, We seized each one of them for his sin. To some of them We sent a violent wind (tornado), and some of them we seized by the acoustic blast, and some of them we caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah was not to do injustice to them, but it was they who did injustice to themselves.” (29:40)

Typically, when people face trials, they automatically rush to Allah. But, once they are out of the difficulty, they may revert to other than Allah after Allah removes their suffering.

فَإِذَا رَڪِبُواْ فِى ٱلۡفُلۡكِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّٮٰهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ إِذَا هُمۡ يُشۡرِكُونَ (٦٥)

And when they embark on a ship (and face storm), they supplicate Allah, having their faith purely to Him. But when He saves them (and brings them) to the land, at once they associate others with Him (29:65)

In the following Ayat, Allah gives a parable of people who seek guardians and refuge in others than Allah:

مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡعَنڪَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتۡ بَيۡتً۬ا‌ۖ وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلۡبُيُوتِ لَبَيۡتُ ٱلۡعَنڪَبُوتِ‌ۖ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ (٤١)

“The example of those who take guardians other than Allah is the likeness of a spider who builds (for itself) a house, while indeed the frailest of houses is the spider’s house, if they but knew. (29:41)

Those who turn to others than Allah are like seeking help from weak and fragile resources that cannot even protect themselves. Allah sets parables in the Quran as an educational tool to give people a clearer idea about the subject and thus these parables need to be seriously studied to draw lessons from it. But understanding these parables is a measure of the reader’s skills and knowledge. Thus, early Muslim used to cry if they don’t understand a parable as it will be a statement about the lack of their intelligence since Allah says:

وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡأَمۡثَـٰلُ نَضۡرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ‌ۖ وَمَا يَعۡقِلُهَآ إِلَّا ٱلۡعَـٰلِمُونَ (٤٣)

And We cite these examples to the people, but no one will grasp their meaning except the knowledgeable ones. (29:43)

So, when Allah sets for us a similitude, we should seek to understand the relevance. So why did Allah use the frail spider web as a similitude? Would anyone go to a frail weak structure for protection? Studying spider webs proved that the spider web is not a frail structure. Spider silk is five times stronger than steel. However, such a strong material does not offer security for any insect that seeks shelter and protection in a spider web. The insect gets stuck on the sticky web and gets stung by the spider to keep the insect alive but paralyzed. The insect suffers a slow death as the spider repeatedly sucks its blood while keeping it alive for as many days as it would last.

The insect focused on the materialistic strength of the web but failed to comprehend the horrible destiny that its decision led to. In other words, what looked like a safe haven, turned out to be a trap for extended suffering and total destruction. Similarly, people who seek security by someone other than Allah will end up being captured, paralyzed, enslaved, and abused by those who provided what appeared to be a safe haven. Just like spider webs for unwary insects!! (If you are teaching this Ayat to the Youth, ask him to study the spider because there are many elements about its nature that give more insight to this parable.)

We should always remember that no matter how long a trial may take in worldly life, it is extremely short in terms of the infinity in the Hereafter. Allah gives a comparison between this worldly life and the life in the Hereafter by saying:

وَمَا هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا لَهۡوٌ۬ وَلَعِبٌ۬‌ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ لَهِيَ ٱلۡحَيَوَانُ‌ۚ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ (٦٤)

The life of the world is nothing but amusement and a play, whereas the home of the Hereafter is the only real (and true) Life, if they but knew. (29:64)

In the Quran, when Allah referred to this life, He used the term Hayat (حياة). But when Allah referred to life in the Hereafter, He used an exaggeration term for life which is the unique term (الْحَيَوَانُ) “Hayawaan”. Allah ended the Ayat with “if they but know”, to motivate us to search for the meaning of this word. Here one finds that it linguistically means a life without end, a unique life, and a true life.

Allah identified for us the tools that will help us in facing any trial. These are reciting and conveying the Quran, establishing prayers and remembrance of Allah.

ٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ‌ۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِ‌ۗ وَلَذِكۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَصۡنَعُونَ (٤٥)

Recite (Convey to others) what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer restrains one form shameful deeds and evil (deeds that run counter to reason and pure instinct). And the remembrance of Allah is indeed greater. And Allah knows what you do. (29:45)

While prayers are a form of remembrance of Allah that is intended to cleanse the person’s heart from the temptations of engaging in evil deeds, continuous remembrance of Allah is required to ensure that one does not fall into temptations while engaged with the rest of society in his affairs. Therefore, the remembrance of Allah is greater in the sense that it is 24 hrs a day activity. Also, remembrance of Allah is not a mere uttering of Allah’s names, but it is state of mind.

The Surat ends with an Ayat that should comfort the believers that Allah. It says that Allah will help them to ensure that they do not fail their tests.

وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَہۡدِيَنَّہُمۡ سُبُلَنَا‌ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (٦٩)

As for those who strive in our ways, We will surely guide them to Our paths, and indeed Allah is with the Muhsineen (those who do good by always being aware of Allah’s presence). (29:69)

This Ayat was revealed in Makkah when military Jihad had not yet been decreed. Thus, this Ayat refers to striving against oneself in facing the trials. As if it says, ‘If you strive against yourselves and succeed, you are guaranteed victory over the internal and external enemies.

The Surat identifies the four key attributes of those who are successful in the hereafter. These attributes are belief, doing good deeds, patience, and reliance on Allah. Allah says:

وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ غُرَفً۬ا تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡہَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا‌ۚ نِعۡمَ أَجۡرُ ٱلۡعَـٰمِلِينَ (٥٨) ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّہِمۡ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ (٥٩)

And those who have believed and done righteous deeds – We will surely accommodate them in mansions of the Paradise beneath which rivers flow, where they will live forever. Excellent is the reward of the workers (58) Who have been patient and upon their Lord rely. (29:58-59)
