content:
The Theme of Surat Al-Naml (The Ants)

Surat An-Naml was revealed in Mecca.  The theme of this Surat is the importance of technological advances in supporting the propagation of Allah’s message.  Conveying Allah’s message is more effective when Muslims are leaders in science and technology.  As we all note, nations that are leaders in science and technology have financial and military supremacy.  They are well positioned to influence the morals and beliefs of other nations.  Surat Al-Naml provides the story of Prophet Suliman (Solomon) and his kingdom as an example of the effectiveness of combining faith and technical superiority.

The Surat highlights that Allah favored Prophet Dawud and Suliman with knowledge.  It is knowledge that was the key to their preference over others.  Allah says:

وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُ ۥدَ وَسُلَيۡمَـٰنَ عِلۡمً۬ا‌ۖ وَقَالَا ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ۬ مِّنۡ عِبَادِهِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (١٥)

And indeed, We gave knowledge to Dawud (David) and Suliman (Solomon), and they both said: “All the praises and thanks are to Allah, Who has favored us over many of His believing slaves!” (Al-Naml 27:15)

In a subtle way, the Surat directs our attention to the importance of learning different languages.  Mastering foreign languages is key in advancing knowledge and facilitating interaction with others.  Allah says:

وَوَرِثَ سُلَيۡمَـٰنُ دَاوُ ۥدَ‌ۖ وَقَالَ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ عُلِّمۡنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ‌ۖ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلۡفَضۡلُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (١٦)

And Suliman (Solomon) inherited (the knowledge of) Dawud (David). He said: “O mankind! We have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given of all things. Indeed, this is an evident grace (from Allah).” (Al-Naml 27:16)

Learning different languages does not only improve communications, but is could also prevent any unintended harm to others.  An example is in this account:

وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيۡمَـٰنَ جُنُودُهُ ۥ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ وَٱلطَّيۡرِ فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ (١٧) حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ وَادِ ٱلنَّمۡلِ قَالَتۡ نَمۡلَةٌ۬ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمۡلُ ٱدۡخُلُواْ مَسَـٰكِنَڪُمۡ لَا يَحۡطِمَنَّڪُمۡ سُلَيۡمَـٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُ ۥ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ (١٨) فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكً۬ا مِّن قَوۡلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِىٓ أَنۡ أَشۡڪُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنۡعَمۡtَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٲلِدَىَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَـٰلِحً۬ا تَرۡضَٮٰهُ وَأَدۡخِلۡنِى بِرَحۡمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (١٩)

And mustered for Suliman (Solomon) his forces from among the jinn, the humans, and the birds.  All of them are kept under (his) control (17) When they came to the valley of the ants, one of the ants said: “O ants! enter your dwellings, lest Suliman and his army crush you unknowingly.” (18) So, he (Solomon) smiled, amused at her speech, and said: “My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor that You have bestowed on me and on my parents, and that I do good deeds that will please You, and admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous slaves.” (Al-Naml 27:17-19)

These Ayat illustrate the importance of communication technologies.  In a previous talk, we discussed the issue of speaking and sound transmission.  This was discussed when we addressed how Allah translated to Arabic in the Quran the speeches of many creations who did not speak Arabic, including in this case the ants.  You can review the presentation on a YouTube Video entitled: “The Straight Path to Richness – The Quran’s Multi-Billion Dollar Ideas.”

The Surat also records a discussion between Prophet Suleiman and a Hoopoe. This discussion implied some scientific knowledge about the Hoopoe that is still undiscovered.  We note that immediately after Prophet Suleiman heard the warning of the ant, he asked about the Hoopoe.  When he discovered its absence, he made a serious threat against it.

وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيۡرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِىَ لَآ أَرَى ٱلۡهُدۡهُدَ أَمۡ ڪَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَآٮِٕبِينَ (٢٠) لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ ۥ عَذَابً۬ا شَدِيدًا أَوۡ لَأَاْذۡبَحَنَّهُ ۥٓ أَوۡ لَيَأۡتِيَنِّى بِسُلۡطَـٰنٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٢١)

And he checked the birds and said: “Why I do not see the hoopoe or is he among the absent. (20) “I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will slaughter him, unless he brings to me a clear excuse.” (Al-Naml 27:20-21)

This raises a question regarding the role of the Hoopoe and whether his absence has relevance to the warning of the ant that made prophet Sulieman threats to punish him with death.  This requires a study on the characteristics of the Hoopoe.  One could speculate that the Hoopoe’s role is reconnaissance to provide advanced warnings on issues that the leader (Prophet Suliman) should know of.  Therefore, as soon as prophet Sulieman heard the cry of the ants and did not hear the early warning from the Hoopoe, he realized his absence.  Although the hoopoe is a tiny soldier; this account shows that everyone in an army is important.

The Surat continues to give us a demonstration that everything in the universe is conscious of Allah and worships Him.  In this account, we realize that even this tiny bird is committed to the mission of Prophet Suliman.  The Hoopoe flew from Jerusalem to Yemen which is about 1400 miles for reconnaissance to check on the people there.

It appears that Hoopoe made this trip on his own and was planning to join the army when he returns.  But it seems that he was delayed a little and thus his return was not long from the time when his absence was noted.  As soon as the Hoopoe returned, he went to Prophet Suleiman and addressed him directly:

فَمَكَثَ غَيۡرَ بَعِيدٍ۬ فَقَالَ أَحَطtُ بِمَا لَمۡ تُحِطۡ بِهِۦ وَجِئۡtُكَ مِن سَبَإِۭ بِنَبَإٍ۬ يَقِينٍ (٢٢)

But the hoopoe did not take long, he said (to Suliman): “I have discovered what you did not know, and I have come to you from Saba’ (Sheba) with sure information. (27:22)

The Hoopoe appeared to have resilience and a high level of observation and intelligence.  He travelled long distances and studied the situation very well.  He brought accurate information on that nation’s belief and economic and military power.  He said:

إِنِّى وَجَدتُّ ٱمۡرَأَةً۬ تَمۡلِڪُہُمۡ وَأُوتِيَتۡ مِن ڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَلَہَا عَرۡشٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (٢٣) وَجَدتُّہَا وَقَوۡمَہَا يَسۡجُدُونَ لِلشَّمۡسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَہُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ أَعۡمَـٰلَہُمۡ فَصَدَّہُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَہُمۡ لَا يَہۡتَدُونَ (٢٤)

“I found a woman ruling over them”, all sorts of things are given to her, and she has a great throne. (23) “I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has beautified their deeds for them, and has averted them from (Allah’s) Way, so they are not guided.” (27:23-24)

He also displayed his belief commitment by being upset about their disbelief.  He said:

أَلَّا يَسۡجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى يُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡخَبۡءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تُخۡفُونَ وَمَا تُعۡلِنُونَ (٢٥) ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ ۩ (٢٦)

” How can they not prostrate to Allah, Who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and who knows what you conceal and what you reveal. (25) Allah, there is no God but He, the Lord of the Supreme Throne. (27:25-26)

Here we need to realize that the stories in the Quran are not only intended to help us draw lessons but also to help in expanding the cognitive capacity of Muslims, particularly the young.  This is achieved by leaving gaps in the story for the reader to fill.  The missing information leads the young mind to search for new knowledge or speculate on new technologies, yet to be discovered.  The reader of this story should be encouraged to study the characteristics of the Hoopoe.  But one can also consider that the Hoopoe’s trip from Jerusalem to Yemen and back was about 2800 miles.  Data shows that the maximum flying speed of a Hoopoe is 25 mph.  This means that if the Hoopoe is to fly 24 hrs per day, he will be absent from Prophet Suliman court without permission for about 5 days.  This is a long time for the Hoopoe to be absent and thus one must speculate on the knowledge that could have allowed him to travel this long distance in a far shorter time.

The Surat continues to highlight the importance of technology in the communications between Prophet Suliman and the Queen of Sheba.  This technology was demonstrated by the transfer of the Queen’s throne form Yemen to Palestine in a blink of an eye.

قَالَ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمَلَؤُاْ أَيُّكُمۡ يَأۡتِينِى بِعَرۡشِہَا قَبۡلَ أَن يَأۡتُونِى مُسۡلِمِينَ (٣٨) قَالَ عِفۡرِيتٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ أَنَا۟ ءَاتِيڪَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ‌ۖ وَإِنِّى عَلَيۡهِ لَقَوِىٌّ أَمِينٌ۬ (٣٩) قَالَ ٱلَّذِى عِندَهُ ۥ عِلۡمٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ أَنَا۟ ءَاتِيڪَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَرۡتَدَّ إِلَيۡكَ طَرۡفُكَ‌ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسۡتَقِرًّا عِندَهُ ۥ قَالَ هَـٰذَا مِن فَضۡلِ رَبِّى (٤٠)

He (Suliman) said: “O chiefs! Which one of you can bring her throne to me before they come to me submissively?” (38) A strong one from the jinn said: “I will bring it to you before you rise up from your place; and I am indeed powerful, and reliable.” (39) The one who has knowledge of the Book said: “I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.” And when he (Solomon) saw it (the throne) well placed before him, he said: “This is by the grace of my Lord.” (Al-Naml 27:38-40)

These Ayat clearly showed the benefits of technology.  The Ayat imply that teleportation is feasible.  Current research on quantum entanglement suggests this possibility.  Though the technology of teleportation is still in its infancy, Muslim researchers should have an edge because they already know that it is feasible.  It has been suggested that when Allah does not mention the name of the person who conducted what appeared to be a miracle, this miracle will be materialized in the future by others through knowledge.  But miracles that Allah granted to messengers to support their role and message, are beyond human knowledge/duplication.

The Surat presented another technology that Prophet Suliman demonstrated to the Queen as follows:

فَلَمَّا جَآءَتۡ قِيلَ أَهَـٰكَذَا عَرۡشُكِ‌ۖ قَالَتۡ كَأَنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ‌ۚ وَأُوتِينَا ٱلۡعِلۡمَ مِن قَبۡلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسۡلِمِينَ (٤٢) وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعۡبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ إِنَّهَا كَانَتۡ مِن قَوۡمٍ۬ كَـٰفِرِينَ (٤٣) قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلصَّرۡحَ‌ۖ فَلَمَّا رأَتۡهُ حَسِبَتۡهُ لُجَّةً۬ وَكَشَفَتۡ عَن سَاقَيۡہَا‌ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُ ۥ صَرۡحٌ۬ مُّمَرَّدٌ۬ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ‌ۚ قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمۡتُ نَفۡسِى وَأَسۡلَمۡتُ مَعَ سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٤٤)

So, when she came, it was said (to her): “Is your throne like this?” She said: “It seems to be the same as it.” And (Suliman) said: “We have been given Knowledge before her and we have been Muslims.” (42) And she was prevented (from submitting to Allah) by that which she used to worship instead Allah. Indeed, she was of a disbelieving people. (43) It was said to her: “Enter the “Sarh” (palace, hall) but when she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her legs. He (Suleiman) said: “it is a “Sarah” (palace, hall) made of glass placed over glasses.” She said: “My Lord! I had surely wronged myself, and I submit with Suleiman (Solomon), to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.” (27:40-44)

In these Ayat, most interpreters suggested that the queen was amazed by the use of transparent glass in the construction of the hall in which the throne was placed, and this made her embrace Islam.  This interpretation seems unconvincing for two reasons:
1. Even after she saw her thrown, the Ayat states that what she used to worship prevented her from the worship of Allah (وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعۡبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ).
2. Just be being impressed by a construction of a building would not make people change their religion, let alone a powerful Queen.

Perhaps, the key to her conversion is related to entering the “Sarh”.  The term “Sarh” came in reference to Pharaoh in both Surat Al-Qasas (28:38) and Surat Ghafer (40:36).  In Suat Ghafer, Allah says:

وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَـٰهَـٰمَـٰنُ ٱبۡنِ لِى صَرۡحً۬ا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَبۡلُغُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَـٰبَ (٣٦) أَسۡبَـٰبَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَـٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُ ۥ ڪَـٰذِبً۬ا‌ۚ

And Pharaoh said: O Haman! Build a “Sarh” (tower) for me, perhaps I could reach the ways. (36) The ways to the heavens, and may look upon the God of Moses, though I think that he is a liar. (Ghafer 40:36-37)

The term “Sarh” was translated as tower because the goal of Pharaoh is to see the God of Moses in heaven.  But would building a tower really allow Pharaoh to penetrate the sky to see the God of Moses.  And why he needs a tower, he could have gone on the top of the great Pyramid which is 480 ft and it existed over 100 years before Prophet Musa.

If one is to investigate the sky, he would likely be using a telescope.  It would seem reasonable that the term “Sarh” refers to an observatory that contains a telescope.  The reference to pure glass in the construction of the “Sarh” of Prophet Sulieman reinforces this idea.  The lens of a telescope is made from a very pure glass, optical glass.  This may also explain why the Queen of Sheba believed in Allah and overcame her worship of the sun when she looked and saw the existence of many stars that are like the sun and even bigger than it.

The Surat reference to other scientific issues that are related to the knowledge of the planets and stars and implying the movements of the earth and the existence of life outer space.  In Ayat 86, Allah says:

أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلَّيۡلَ لِيَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبۡصِرًا‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٨٦)

Did they not see that We have made the night for them to rest therein, and the day to make them see? Surely, in this there are signs for the people who believe. (27:86)

The Ayat refers to the day and the night that occur due to the Earth rotating on its axis.

Ayat 87 sheds light on the debate regarding the existence of extraterrestrial intelligent beings, Allah says:

وَيَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ وَكُلٌّ أَتَوۡهُ دَٲخِرِينَ (٨٧)

And (remember) the Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will be terrified except those whom Allah wills. And all shall come to Him humbled. (27:87)

The Ayat refers to the presence of intelligent life outside our planet, the earth.  These beings will return to Allah on the day of judgement for accountability.  This Ayat Is not the only Ayat in the Quran that talks about the existence of intelligent beings in other places in the universe.  For Muslims the mention of extraterrestrial beings in the Quran is sufficient evidence to resolve Fermi paradox that refers to the conflict between the lack of evidence for intelligent extraterrestrial beings and the various high estimates for their existence as suggested by Drake Equation that estimates the existence of 300 million intelligent civilizations in our Milky Way Galaxy.

In Ayat 88, Allah says:

وَتَرَى ٱلۡجِبَالَ تَحۡسَبُہَا جَامِدَةً۬ وَهِىَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِ‌ۚ صُنۡعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتۡقَنَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (٨٨)

And you will see the mountains and think that they are stationary, but they pass away as the passing away of the clouds. The work of Allah, Who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Well-Acquainted with what you do. (Al-Naml 27:88)

The scientific knowledge embedded in this Ayat refers to the movements of the mountain that is quite complex and its speed is relative for us and only absolute for Allah.  The speed is relative because we cannot measure it from a fixed place since everything in the universe is moving.  The earth rotates around its axis at 1000 miles/hr and rotates around the sun at 67,000 miles/hr and rotates with others in the solar system around the center of the galaxy at 490,000 miles/hr and moves with the galaxy at 2.24 million miles/hr and so on.  Even the edge of the universe that is located 13.8 billion light years away from us is also moving at over 150,000 miles/hr, Only Allah knows the exact location and the true speed of everything.

After demonstrating the importance of the technological excellence, Surah Al-Naml shifts to display Allah’s power in the universe using six rhetorical Questions so that people may think and not be lured by civilization and forgets Allah, the Creator.  Thus, a balance is established between civilization and faith in Allah, who has indeed power and authority over everything.

Say: Praise belongs to Allah, and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better or that which they associate with Him?
قُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَـٰمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰٓ‌ۗ ءَآللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ أَمَّا يُشۡرِڪُونَ (٥٩)

Is not He (best), the One who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky wherewith We cause to grow glamourous gardens. It was not within your ability to grow their trees. Is there any God along with Allah? No, but they are people who ascribe equals (to Allah).
أَمَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآٮِٕقَ ذَاتَ بَهۡجَةٍ۬ مَّا كَانَ لَكُمۡ أَن تُنۢبِتُواْ شَجَرَهَآ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ۬ يَعۡدِلُونَ (٦٠)

Is not He (best), the One who has made the earth firm to live in; made rivers in its midst; set thereon mountains for making it firm; and made a barrier between the two seas? Is there any God along with Allah? No, but most of them do not have knowledge.
أَمَّن جَعَلَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ قَرَارً۬ا وَجَعَلَ خِلَـٰلَهَآ أَنۡہَـٰرً۬ا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَٲسِىَ وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ حَاجِزًا‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ بَلۡ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (٦١)

Is not He (best) the One who responds to the distressed when he calls on Him and removes the distress, and Who makes you (mankind) vicegerents of the earth? Is there any God along with Allah? No, but little you heed to advice.
أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلۡمُضۡطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكۡشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجۡعَلُكُمۡ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ قَلِيلً۬ا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٦٢)

Is not He (best), the One who guides you through the depths of darkness on land and sea, and who sends the winds as bearing good news before His mercy? Is there any God along with Allah? No, Allah is far greater than the partners they ascribe to Him.
أَمَّن يَهۡدِيڪُمۡ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَمَن يُرۡسِلُ ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ بُشۡرًۢا بَيۡنَ يَدَىۡ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۤ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ تَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٦٣)

Is not He (best), the One who originates Creation, then will reproduce it and who gives you provisions from the sky and the earth? Is there any God along with Allah? Say “Bring your proof if you are telling the truth!” (27:59-64)
أَمَّن يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۥ وَمَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ قُلۡ هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَـٰنَڪُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (٦٤)

Surat Al-Naml ends as it starts with reference to the Quran.  It started with:

طسٓ‌ۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَڪِتَابٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ (١) هُدً۬ى وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٢)

Tâ Sîn; these are the Ayat of the Qur’an, an enlightening book. (1) A guidance and good news for the believers. (Al-Naml 27:1-2)

And it ended with:

وَأَنۡ أَتۡلُوَاْ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ‌ۖ فَمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَہۡتَدِى لِنَفۡسِهِۦ‌ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَقُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۟ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنذِرِينَ (٩٢) وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ فَتَعۡرِفُونَہَا‌ۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَـٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ (٩٣)

And that I should recite the Qur’an, so whoever is guided, he is guided for his own good, and whoever goes astray, say (to him): “I am only one of the warners.” (92) And say: “All the praises belong to Allah. He will show you His signs, then you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.” (Al-Naml 27:92-93)

title: Theme of Surat Al-Rahman (الرحمن) (55)
excerpt:
Theme of Surat Al-Rahman (الرحمن) (55)

The main theme of Surat Al-Rahman is the overwhelming and boundless mercy and blessings of Allah upon His creations. It highlights the numerous favors of…
content:
Theme of Surat Al-Rahman (الرحمن) (55)

The main theme of Surat Al-Rahman is the overwhelming and boundless mercy and blessings of Allah upon His creations. It highlights the numerous favors of Allah, urging humankind and jinn to recognize, appreciate, and be grateful for these blessings. This central message is reinforced by the recurring rhetorical question: “Which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?” (فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ), prompting self-reflection and instilling a deep sense of gratitude and acknowledgment of His countless blessings. Anyone who reads Surat Al-Raham and answers the question that Allah asked 31 times by not denying any of the blessings, there should be no excuse to continue rejecting Allah’s message.

The Surat also makes it clear that Allah’s last Message, the Quran, is directed to both mankind and Jinn. Addressing both mankind and Jinn, Allah says:

سَنَفۡرُغُ لَكُمۡ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلَانِ (٣١) فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٣٢) يَـٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْ‌ۚ لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلۡطَـٰنٍ۬ (٣٣)

“Soon, We shall attend to you, O you two weighty classes (jinn and men)! (31) Then which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both deny? (32) O assembly of jinn and men! If you have power to penetrate the regions of the heavens and the earth, then penetrate them. But you will never be able to pass them, except with (Our) sanction.” (53: 31-33)

The Surat identified numerous favors and blessings that He has bestowed upon humanity and jinn. These favors are presented as signs of His mercy, power, and wisdom. Here are the key blessings mentioned in the surah:

1. The Gift of Revelation and Knowledge
* Allah’s teaching of the Qur’an
(ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ (١) عَلَّمَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ (٢)) [Al-Rahman (1) He taught the Quran (2)]
* The creation of humanity and teaching them speech and communication
(خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ (٣) عَلَّمَهُ ٱلۡبَيَانَ (٤)) {He created man (3) He taught him clear speech (4)]

2. The Natural Order and Balance
* The creation of the heavens and establishing a balance
(وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ (٧)) [He raised the sky high and has place the scale (7)]
* The command to maintain fairness and avoid transgressing the balance
(أَلَّا تَطۡغَوۡاْ فِى ٱلۡمِيزَانِ (٨) وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ (٩)) [So that you do not defraud the scales. (8) Observe the correct weight with equity, and do not make the balance deficient. (9)]

3. The Earth and Its Provisions
* The creation of the earth for all beings
(وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلۡأَنَامِ (١٠)) [And the earth He laid [out] for the creatures. (10)].
* The blessings of fruits, palm trees, grains, and fragrant plants
(فِيہَاَ فَـٰكِهَةٌ۬ وَٱلنَّخۡلُ ذَاتُ ٱلۡأَكۡمَامِ (١١) وَٱلۡحَبُّ ذُو ٱلۡعَصۡفِ وَٱلرَّيۡحَانُ (١٢)) [`In it are fruit, palm trees with date stalks, (11) and grain with husks, and aromatic plants. (12)]

4. The Creation of Humanity and Jinn
* The creation of humans from clay
(خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِن صَلۡصَـٰلٍ۬ كَٱلۡفَخَّارِ (١٤)) [He has created man out of sounding clay, like pottery, (14)]
* The creation of jinn from smokeless fire
(وَخَلَقَ ٱلۡجَآنَّ مِن مَّارِجٍ۬ مِّن نَّارٍ۬ (١٥)) [ And created the Jinn from smokeless flame of fire (15)]

5. The Gifts of Nature and the Universe
* The seas, from which emerge pearls and coral
(يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡہُمَا ٱللُّؤۡلُؤُ وَٱلۡمَرۡجَانُ (٢٢)) [ From both the seas comes out pearl and coral. (22)}
* Ships that sail through the sea like mountains
(وَلَهُ ٱلۡجَوارِ ٱلۡمُنشَـَٔاتُ فِى ٱلۡبَحۡرِ كَٱلۡأَعۡلَـٰمِ (٢٤)) [His are the ships displayed upon the sea like banners. (24)]
* The harmonious motion of celestial bodies like the sun and the moon
(ٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُ بِحُسۡبَانٍ۬ (٥)) [The sun and the moon are (bound) by a (fixed) calculation. (5)]

6. Signs of Divine Power
* The vastness of creation and the inability of humans and jinn to escape Allah’s domain
(يَـٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْ‌ۚ لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلۡطَـٰنٍ۬ (٣٣)) [O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority [from Allah]. (33)]
* The eventual accountability of all beings on the Day of Judgment
(يُعۡرَفُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ بِسِيمَـٰهُمۡ فَيُؤۡخَذُ بِٱلنَّوَٲصِى وَٱلۡأَقۡدَامِ (٤١)) [The wicked will be recognized by their appearance, then will be seized by `their` forelocks and feet. (41)]

7. The Reminder of Accountability and the Fate of the righteous and the wrongdoers.
* The description of two gardens for the righteous
(وَلِمَنۡ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ جَنَّتَانِ (٤٦)) [And whoever is in awe of standing before his Lord will have two Gardens. (46)].
* The promise of eternal peace, happiness, and proximity to Allah
(هَلۡ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡإِحۡسَـٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِحۡسَـٰنُ (٦٠)) [Is there any reward for goodness except goodness? (60)]
* The terrifying scenes of Hellfire for those who deny Allah’s blessings
(هَـٰذِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِى يُكَذِّبُ بِہَا ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ (٤٣) يَطُوفُونَ بَيۡنَہَا وَبَيۡنَ حَمِيمٍ ءَانٍ۬ (٤٤)) [They will be told,˺ “This is the Hell that the wicked denied.” (43) They will alternate between its and scalding water. (44)]

After the Prophet (PBUH) recited this Surah to his companions and they were listening attentively dead silent, he (PBUH) told them:
عن ابن عمران أن رسول الله قرأ سورة الرحمن على أصحابه فسكتوا فقال: ما لي أسمع الجنّ أحسن جواباً لربه منكم؟ ما أتيت على قول الله تعالى [فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان] إلا قالوا: لا بشيء من نعمك نكذب فلك الحمد
Why I hear the Jinn better than you in responding to Allah’s question. Each time I recited (فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ) “Which of these favors of your Lord, that you deny?” they said: (لا بشيء من نعمك نكذب فلك الحمد) “None of your favors we deny, all the praises are for You” (At-Tirmidhi)

Surat Al-Rahman includes several unseen truths and natural phenomena, each of which demands careful study and could warrant a dedicated lecture. These include:

1. Whom did Allah teach the Quran before creating humankind?
ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ (١) عَلَّمَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ (٢) خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ (٣)
Al-Rahman (1) He taught the Quran (2) He created man. (55:1-3)

2. What is meant by Al-Mizan (The balance)?
وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ (٧) أَلَّا تَطۡغَوۡاْ فِى ٱلۡمِيزَانِ (٨) وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ (٩)
He raised the sky high and placed the scale (7) [So that you do not defraud the scales. (8) Observe the correct weight with equity, and do not make the balance deficient. (55:7-9)

3. Where are the two Easts and the two Wests, and are there others?
رَبُّ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقَيۡنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبَيۡنِ (١٧)
“He is˺ Lord of the two easts and the two wests.” (55:17)

4. What limit has Allah set for mankind to travel in space, and have we reached it yet?
يَـٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْ‌ۚ لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلۡطَـٰنٍ۬ (٣٣)
“O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority [from Allah]. (55:33)

5. Does Allah’s affirmation that the sun and moon follow precise calculations justify using astronomical calculations to establish lunar months?
ٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُ بِحُسۡبَانٍ۬ (٥)
The sun and the moon are (bound) by a (fixed) calculation. (55:5)

6. Does the term (ٱلۡجَوَارِ) refer to something unique belonging to Allah, distinct from ships owned by human beings?
وَلَهُ ٱلۡجَوارِ ٱلۡمُنشَـَٔاتُ فِى ٱلۡبَحۡرِ كَٱلۡأَعۡلَـٰمِ (٢٤)
His are the ships towering upon the sea like banners. (55:24)

7. What is the nature of the barrier that Allah placed between different seas to preserve their unique properties?
مَرَجَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ يَلۡتَقِيَانِ (١٩) بَيۡنَہُمَا بَرۡزَخٌ۬ لَّا يَبۡغِيَانِ (٢٠)
He has let loose the two seas (the salt and the fresh water) meeting together. (19) Between them is a barrier so that they do not transgress. (55:19-20)

8. Since everything was already decreed before the creation of the heavens and the earth, what does it mean that Allah is engaged in a matter?
يَسۡــٴَـلُهُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ كُلَّ يَوۡمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأۡنٍ۬ (٢٩)
All those in the Heavens and the earth beseech Him (for their needs). Every day He is engaged in a matter. (55:29)

9. The Surah describes two groups of people, with each individual in these groups receiving two gardens in Paradise. However, the gardens differ in their qualities. Who are these two groups, and which of them has the superior gardens?
وَلِمَنۡ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ جَنَّتَانِ (٤٦) فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٤٧)
And whoever is in awe of standing before their Lord will have two Gardens. (46) Which of the favors of your Lord will you deny? (55:46-47)
وَمِن دُونِہِمَا جَنَّتَانِ (٦٢) فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٦٣)
And below these two ˹Gardens˺ will be two others. (62) Which of the favors of your Lord will you deny? (55:62-63)

These verses highlight profound themes that blend spiritual insights with natural and cosmic phenomena, inviting deep reflection and study.

One East, Two Easts, and Multiple Easts – Qur’anic References to Directions in Time and Space

The Qur’an refers to the East and the West in several ways, including:
1. Singular form: “رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ”
“The Lord of the East and the West.” (Al-Shu‘ara 26:28; Al-Muzzammil 73:9)
2. Dual form: “رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ”
“The Lord of the two Easts and the two Wests.” (Ar-Rahman 55:17)
3. Plural form: “فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشَارِقِ وَالْمَغَارِبِ”
“But no! I swear by the Lord of all points of sunrise and sunset.” (Al-Ma‘arij 70:40)

The Qur’an’s shifting expressions — from one, to two, to many — reflect not inconsistency, but depth. They point to the scientific precision, poetic eloquence, and spiritual breadth of the Qur’an’s worldview. These expressions invite reflection on the vastness of creation, the relativity of time and space, and the unlimited knowledge and power of Allah.

Possible Explanation of the Variations:
These variations are layers of meaning reflecting the complexity of creation, motion, and perception of time and space.
* The singular form refers to the general reality of East and West as fixed directions relative to the observer on Earth.
* The dual form likely reflects the seasonal shifts — the point of sunrise and sunset during the winter solstice and summer solstice. These two extremes represent the two farthest points the sun reaches in its annual journey across the horizon.
* The plural form (as in 70:40) indicates the daily variation in sunrise and sunset across different days, locations, and latitudes. Each point on Earth has its own “East” and “West” depending on the time and place. It also reflects the diversity and multiplicity of Allah’s creation, and perhaps even cosmological dimensions beyond our world.

Broader Implication in 70:40:
In Surah Al-Ma‘arij (70:40), Allah says: ”فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشَارِقِ وَالْمَغَارِبِ إِنَّا لَقَادِرُونَ”
“But no! I swear by the Lord of all Easts and Wests — We are surely capable…”
This oath emphasizes Allah’s supreme control over the entire cosmos — over all rotations, orbits, directions, and temporal realities. The multiplicity here may symbolize:
* The countless sunrises and sunsets across the globe.
* The relativity of direction in the universe depends on planetary position.
* Or even metaphysical or multi-dimensional realities beyond human perception.

The diagram shows how the sunrise and sunset directions (azimuth angles) change throughout the year. This illustrates how the Qur’an’s reference to multiple Easts and Wests reflects the natural variation in the sun’s path due to Earth’s tilt and orbit.

title: Surah Al-Mu’minun (المؤمنون) (The Believers) (23)
excerpt: Surah Al-Mu’minun was revealed in Mecca. This Surah lists the most important traits of believers. It provides a score card for the believers to judge themselves before they are judged by Allah. It is…
content:
Surah Al-Mu’minun was revealed in Mecca. This Surah lists the most important traits of believers. It provides a score card for the believers to judge themselves before they are judged by Allah. It is important to note that these traits include both morals and rituals (الأخلاق والعبادات) and they are the key to paradise. Omar ibn Al-Khatab reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

(عن عمر بن الخطاب – رضي الله عنه – قال : قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم …..”أُنْزِلَ عَلَيَّ عَشْرُ آيَاتٍ مَنْ أَقَامَهُنَّ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ : ” قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ “، حَتَّى خَتَمَ عَشْرَ آيَاتٍ) الترمذي

“Ten Ayat were revealed to me. Whoever abides by them (practices their commands) will enter paradise. Then He (PBUH) recited (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) “Indeed the believers had succeeded” until He finished the ten Ayat off Surah Al Mu’minun [Tirmidhi]

Note: When the term (قد) comes before a present tense verb, it implies doubt and thus can be translated as “may be”, such as: (قد ينجح فلان) “such and such may succeed”. But, if the term (قد) comes before a past tense verb, it implies confirmation and assurance and thus it is translated as “indeed or truly”, such as (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) “Indeed, the believers had succeeded”, i.e. success has already been achieved.

We note that the term (قد) came before a past tense verb in the form (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ) in the Quran in three places to give assurance by Allah that success is indeed achieved. The three places are:

( ﴿ قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا ﴾) سورة الشمس
“Indeed, he who purified his own self had succeeded.” (Ash-Shams 91:9)

( ﴿ قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى ﴾) سورة الأعلى
“Indeed, he who is purified had succeeded.” (Al-Ala 87:14)

( ﴿ قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ ﴾ ( سورة المؤمنون )
“Indeed, the believers had succeeded”. (Al- Mu’minun 23:1)

The Surat identified six traits of the believers. These six traits include three worship traits followed by three manner traits. These six traits are:

1. Reverent (have Khoshoo) in their prayers. (ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ فِى صَلَاتِہِمۡ خَـٰشِعُونَ)
2. Abstaining from vain talk. (وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ عَنِ ٱللَّغۡوِ مُعۡرِضُونَ)
3. Actively working to pay the Zakat. (وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِلزَّكَوٰةِ فَـٰعِلُونَ)
4. Chaste by guarding their private part.
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِفُرُوجِهِمۡ حَـٰفِظُونَ (٥) إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزۡوَٲجِهِمۡ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَـٰنُهُمۡ فَإِنَّہُمۡ غَيۡرُ مَلُومِينَ
5. Faithfully observe their trusts and their covenants.
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِأَمَـٰنَـٰتِهِمۡ وَعَهۡدِهِمۡ رَأْعُونَ
6. Carefully maintain their prayers. (وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ عَلَىٰ صَلَوَٲتِہِمۡ يُحَافِظُونَ)

Whosoever truly fulfill these six traits wins the divine prize that is guaranteed by Allah:

أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡوَٲرِثُونَ (١٠) ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلۡفِرۡدَوۡسَ هُمۡ فِيہَا خَـٰلِدُونَ (١١)

These are indeed the inheritors who shall inherit Paradise where they shall live therein forever. (23:10-11)

It is important that we evaluate ourselves according to these traits and ensure that we are continuously improving. The wisest among us is the one who holds himself accountable before he will be held accountable by Allah. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي يعلى شداد بن أوس – قال : قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم : ” الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت ، والعاجز من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله – عز وجل .” [رواه البيهقي والترمذي وابن ماجه]

“A wise person is one who holds himself accountable and strives for that which will benefit him after death; and the incapacitated is one who subordinates himself to his temptations and expects from Allah the fulfillment of his futile desires.” (Tirmidhi and others)

Let us examine these 6 traits and assess where we stand:

Reverence (Khoshoo) in the prayers (الخشوع فى الصلاة): The “Khoshoo” (الخشوع) is the attentive humility and the feeling of an awe of Allah that resides in the heart and is manifested by the limbs (الخشوع محله القلب ، ومظهره في الجوارح). What is the quality of our prayers? Do you concentrate on what you are saying while praying? What is the score we give to ourselves with respect to concentration in the prayer? Do you feel an awe of Allah in front of Whom you are standing? A sign of the lack of “Khoshoo” (الخشوع) in the prayer is the excessive unnecessary movements.

Abstaining from vain talk (عروض عن الغو): Are your talks free from words that could cause problems or hatred? Do we stop your tongue from gossiping and useless speech? Do we abstain from attending assemblies where people talk badly about each other?

Maintaining Chastity (حفظ الفرج): How much do you safeguard your heart from unclean feelings/thoughts, and preserve your eyes from mischievous sights? How far do you abstain from all avenues that could lead to adultery and fornication? It is reported that Prophet Isa (PBUH) said:

ورد في الأناجيل للسيد المسيح عليه الصلاة والسلام : أنه ليس الشريف الذي لا يقترف الخطيئة ، بل هو الذي يهرب من أسباب الخطيئة

“The honorable is not the one who escape from the sin but the honorable is the one who escapes from its causes.”

In the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus (PBUH) said:

«قَدْ سَمِعْتُمْ أَنَّهُ قِيلَ لِلْقُدَمَاءِ: لاَ تَزْنِ. ٢٨ وَأَمَّا أَنَا فَأَقُولُ لَكُمْ: إِنَّ كُلَّ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى امْرَأَةٍ لِيَشْتَهِيَهَا فَقَدْ زَنَى بِهَا فِي قَلْبِهِ. ٢٩ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ عَيْنُكَ الْيُمْنَى تُعْثِرُكَ فَاقْلَعْهَا وَأَلْقِهَا عَنْكَ لأَنَّهُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ أَنْ يَهْلِكَ أَحَدُ أَعْضَائِكَ وَلاَ يُلْقَى جَسَدُكَ كُلُّهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ.»

You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery. (28) But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart. (29) If your right eye causes you to stumble, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell. (Matthew 5:27-30)

Faithfully observe trusts and covenants (الامانة): How much do we cling to honesty, whether in minor issues or major ones? Issues such as distributing copyrighted materials, identifying deficiencies in anything you sell, or borrowing something and never returning it. How about our covenant with Allah to believe in none but Him and to seek help from none but Him (إِيَّاكَ نَعۡبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسۡتَعِينُ). Also, how about our commitment to spread the message of Allah. How about making a commitment just to avoid the argument while you have no intention to fulfill it.

Maintaining the prayers (المحافظة على الصلاة): Do we pray regularly and on time? Are we keen on praying in groups and in the Masjid? Note that Allah sandwiched the attributes between two attributes associated with prayers. This clearly emphasizes the criticality of prayers. No one can truly claim belief without performing the prayers. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن جابرِ بنِ عبدِ اللهِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهما، قال: سمعتُ النبيَّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم يقول: ((إِنَّ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلِ وَبَيْنَ الشِّرْكِ وَالْكُفْرِ تَرْكَ الصَّلَاةِ )) صحيح مسلم

“Indeed, between a person and the shirk (polytheism) and the kufr (unbelief) is the abandonment of the prayer”.

The Surat continues to provide additional traits the believers:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنۡ خَشۡيَةِ رَبِّہِم مُّشۡفِقُونَ (٥٧)
Surely, those who are anxious out of awe of their Lord. (23:57)

وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّہِمۡ يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٥٨)
And those who believe in the Ayat of their Lord. (23:58)

وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِرَبِّہِمۡ لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٥٩)
And those who do not associate any partner with their Lord. (23:59)

وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡتُونَ مَآ ءَاتَواْ وَّقُلُوبُہُمۡ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّہُمۡ إِلَىٰ رَبِّہِمۡ رَٲجِعُونَ (٦٠)
And those who give whatever they (have to) give with their hearts trembling at the thought that to their Lord they must return. (23:60)

For the believers who have these traits, Allah made divine testimony about them by saying:

أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلۡخَيۡرَٲتِ وَهُمۡ لَهَا سَـٰبِقُونَ (٦١)
It is these who hasten in the good deeds, and they are indeed foremost in attaining them. (23:61) [i.e., they never miss a chance for getting more reward from Allah.

Upon hearing the Ayat (وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡتُونَ مَآ ءَاتَواْ وَّقُلُوبُہُمۡ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّہُمۡ إِلَىٰ رَبِّہِمۡ رَٲجِعُونَ) “And those who give whatever they (have to) give with their hearts trembling at the thought that to their Lord they must return”, Sayeda Aisha asked the Prophet (PBUH), are those who drink Alcohol (Khamr) and steal? The Prophet (PBUH) said:

سألتُ عائشة أم المؤمنين رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم عن هذه الآيةِ {وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ} قَالَتْ عائشةُ: أَهُم الذينَ يَشْرَبونَ الخَمْرَ وَيَسْرِقونَ؟ قَالَ: لا يا بِنْتَ الصِّدِّيقِ، ولَكِنَّهم الذينَ يَصومونَ ويُصلُّونَ ويَتَصدَّقونَ وهم [يَخافونَ أَلَّا تُقْبَلَ منهم، أُولئكَ الذينَ يُسارعونَ في الخَيْراتِ وهم لها سابقونَ ] الترمذي وابن ماجه

“No, O the daughter of As-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), they are those who fast, pray, and give charity but are afraid that they (their good deeds) may not be accepted (by Allah) from them. They are those who hasten in the good deeds, and they are indeed foremost in attaining them.” (Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah)

All the traits that Allah identified for the believers are feasible for every person to achieve because Allah will never impose on people requirements beyond their capacity, as He said:

وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا‌ۖ وَلَدَيۡنَا كِتَـٰبٌ۬ يَنطِقُ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (٦٢)

And We task not any person except according to his capacity, and with Us is a Record which speaks the truth, and they will not be wronged. (23:62)

The Surat also gives accounts of the people’s response to past prophets. Some prophets are mentioned by name such as (نوح، موسى، هارون عيسى، ابن مريم) and others were not. Allah says:

ثُمَّ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتۡرَا‌ۖ كُلَّ مَا جَآءَ أُمَّةً۬ رَّسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ‌ۚ فَأَتۡبَعۡنَا بَعۡضَہُم بَعۡضً۬ا وَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ أَحَادِيثَ‌ۚ فَبُعۡدً۬ا لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٤٤)

Then We sent Our Messengers in succession. Every time there came to a nation their Messenger, they denied him; so We made them follow one another and We made them as examples. So away with a people who do not believe!” (23:44)

Generally, those who disbelieve reject two issues:
1. The oneness of God.
2. The resurrection.

The Surat presented their argument regarding resurrection as follows:

أَيَعِدُكُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ إِذَا مِتُّمۡ وَكُنتُمۡ تُرَابً۬ا وَعِظَـٰمًا أَنَّكُم مُّخۡرَجُونَ (٣٥) ۞ هَيۡہَاتَ هَيۡہَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ (٣٦) إِنۡ هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنۡيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحۡيَا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَبۡعُوثِينَ (٣٧)

Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones that you will (again) be brought forth? (35) How too improbable is what you are being promised. (36) There is nothing but our worldly life – we die and live, but we will not be resurrected. (23:35-37)

بَلۡ قَالُواْ مِثۡلَ مَا قَالَ ٱلۡأَوَّلُونَ (٨١) قَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا مِتۡنا وَكُنَّا تُرَابً۬ا وَعِظَـٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ (٨٢) لَقَدۡ وُعِدۡنَا نَحۡنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا هَـٰذَا مِن قَبۡلُ إِنۡ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ (٨٣)

Rather, they say as the earlier people had said. (81) They said, “Is it that. when we have died and become dust and bones, are we to be resurrected? (82) This is what has been promised to us and to our fathers before; this is nothing but the fables of the ancients.” (23:81-83)

The belief in resurrection is critical because without it, there will be no accountability and thus there will be no ultimate justice. Also, without it, the belief in One God becomes inconsequential.

Therefore, belief in resurrection was emphasized as part of explaining the cycle of man’s creation in the following Ayat:

وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِن سُلَـٰلَةٍ۬ مِّن طِينٍ۬ (١٢) ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَـٰهُ نُطۡفَةً۬ فِى قَرَارٍ۬ مَّكِينٍ۬ (١٣) ثُمَّ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلنُّطۡفَةَ عَلَقَةً۬ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡعَلَقَةَ مُضۡغَةً۬ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡمُضۡغَةَ عِظَـٰمً۬ا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلۡعِظَـٰمَ لَحۡمً۬ا ثُمَّ أَنشَأۡنَـٰهُ خَلۡقًا ءَاخَرَ‌ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحۡسَنُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقِينَ (١٤) ثُمَّ إِنَّكُم بَعۡدَ ذَٲلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ (١٥) ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ تُبۡعَثُونَ (١٦)

We created man from an extract of clay, (12) Then We made him as a sperm-drop in a firm resting place, (13) then We developed that drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into fetus lump of flesh, and We made from the lump bones, and clothed the bones with flesh. Then We developed him into another creation. So glorious is Allah, the best of Creators, (14) After this you shall surely die. (15) Then you will be raised up again on the Day of Judgment. (23:12-16)

The Surat challenges the disbelievers by asking them questions to make them realize the disconnect between what they really know about Allah and what they claim:

قُل لِّمَنِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهَآ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ (٨٤) سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ‌ۚ قُلۡ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٨٥)

Say: “To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you have knowledge?” (84) They will say: “To Allah.” Say: “Will you not then remember?” (23:84-85)

قُلۡ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ ٱلسَّبۡعِ وَرَبُّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ (٨٦) سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ‌ۚ قُلۡ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ (٨٧)

Say: “Who is Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Great Throne?” (86) They will say, “All belongs to Allah.” Say, “Will you not be conscious of Him?” (23:86-87)

قُلۡ مَنۢ بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُوَ يُجِيرُ وَلَا يُجَارُ عَلَيۡهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ (٨٨) سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ‌ۚ قُلۡ فَأَنَّىٰ تُسۡحَرُونَ (٨٩)

Say: “In whose hand is the dominion of all things – and He protects while none can protect against Him – if you have knowledge?” (88) They will say: “[All belongs] to Allah.” Say: “Then how can you be so deluded?” (23:88-89)

These questions are concluded by rationalizing why what Allah has revealed is the truth and all what they claim is mere lies.

بَلۡ أَتَيۡنَـٰهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَكَـٰذِبُونَ (٩٠)

The fact is that We have brought to them the truth, and they are absolute liars. (23:90)

Also, if they use their logic, they will conclude that Allah is the only God.

مَا ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِن وَلَدٍ۬ وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُ ۥ مِنۡ إِلَـٰهٍ‌ۚ إِذً۬ا لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَـٰهِۭ بِمَا خَلَقَ وَلَعَلَا بَعۡضُہُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬‌ۚ سُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ (٩١) عَالِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّہَـٰدَةِ فَتَعَـٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٩٢)

Allah has not taken any son, nor has there ever been any god with Him. Had there been so, then each god would have taken away what he created, and each one of them would have sought to overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe. (91) He is the Knower of the invisible and the visible. So, He is far above what they associate [with Him]. (23:91-92)

The Surat ends by re-emphasizes again the fact that everyone will face death and will be resurrected for facing the Judgement of Allah. The Surat presents a clear scene of the state of the disbelievers:

حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ (٩٩) لَعَلِّىٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَـٰلِحً۬ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُ‌ۚ كَلَّآ‌ۚ إِنَّہَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآٮِٕلُہَا‌ۖ وَمِن وَرَآٮِٕهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ (١٠٠) فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَلَآ أَنسَابَ بَيۡنَہُمۡ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ وَلَا يَتَسَآءَلُونَ (١٠١)

Until, when death comes to one of them (the disbelievers), he says: “My Lord, send me back. (99) So that I might do righteousness in that which I left behind.” No, it is only a word he is saying; and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected. (100) When the trumpet is blown, no ties of kinship will there be among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another. (101)

فَمَن ثَقُلَتۡ مَوَٲزِينُهُ ۥ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ (١٠٢) وَمَنۡ خَفَّتۡ مَوَٲزِينُهُ ۥ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَہُمۡ فِى جَهَنَّمَ خَـٰلِدُونَ (١٠٣) تَلۡفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَهُمۡ فِيہَا كَـٰلِحُونَ (١٠٤)

And those whose scales are heavy [with good deeds] – they who are the successful ones. (102) But those whose scales are light – they are the ones who have failed themselves. In Hell they are to remain forever. (103) The Fire will scorch their faces, and they will be disfigured therein. (23:99-104)

While people may feel that this worldly life is long, on the day of judgment, it will seem that it was too short.

قَـٰلَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ (١١٢) قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمٍ۬ فَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡعَآدِّينَ (١١٣) قَـٰلَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً‌ۖ لَّوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ (١١٤) أَفَحَسِبۡتُمۡ أَنَّمَا خَلَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ عَبَثً۬ا وَأَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡنَا لَا تُرۡجَعُونَ (١١٥)

[Allah] will say, “How long did you remain on earth by number of years?” (112) They will say, “We remained a day or part of a day; ask those (angels) who can enumerate.” (113) He will say: “You did not stay but for a little – if only you had known. (114) So, did you think that We created you nothing and that you will not be brought back to Us?” (23:112-115)

Surat Al-Mu’minun closes with a supplication for the believers, who may have erred or failed to always maintain the traits of the believers. Allah comforted them by teaching them to ask for His forgiveness and mercy.

وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ وَٱرۡحَمۡ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٲحِمِينَ (١١٨)

“And say: “My Lord! Forgive and have mercy, for You are the Best of those who show mercy!” (23:118).

content:
The Theme of Surat Ta-Ha (طه) (20)

Surat Ta-Ha (طه) was revealed in Mecca. Its theme is: life becomes easy when following Allah’s guidance and becomes difficult when deviating from Allah’s guidance. This theme is summarized in two verses:

مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِتَشۡقَىٰٓ (٢)
“We have not sent down the Qur’an unto you to cause you difficulty.” (20:2).

وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِڪۡرِى فَإِنَّ لَهُ ۥ مَعِيشَةً۬ ضَنكً۬ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُ ۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ (١٢٤)
But whosoever turns away from My Message (the Quran) verily, for him is a life of hardship, and on the Day of Resurrection We shall raise him up blind.” (20:124)

The Surat discusses in some details the story of Prophet Musa to illustrate that Allah’s message is intended to make life easy and comfortable and Allah’s support will always be with those who follow it and deliver it. Allah says:

وَهَلۡ أَتَٮٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ (٩) إِذۡ رَءَا نَارً۬ا فَقَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارً۬ا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنۡہَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوۡ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدً۬ى (١٠) فَلَمَّآ أَتَٮٰهَا نُودِىَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰٓ (١١) إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۟ رَبُّكَ فَٱخۡلَعۡ نَعۡلَيۡكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسِ طُوً۬ى (١٢)
And has there come to you the story of Musa (Moses)? (9) When he saw a fire, he said to his family: “Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire, perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire. (10) And when he came to it (the fire), he was called: “O Musa (Moses)! (11) “It is Me, I am your Lord! So, take off your shoes, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. (20:9-12)

In these verses, Allah commanded Prophet Musa to take off his shoes without any explanation regarding its significance. Allah leaves the understanding of the relevance of this command to the readers to come up with an understanding that is consistent with the theme of the Surat. The books of Tafseer offer two primary explanations:
1. Prophet Musa’s shoes were made of the skin of a dead donkey and are not befitting to enter with them the sacred valley of Tuwa.
2. Prophet Musa was asked to take off his shoes so his feet could touch the scared valley.

These explanations are questionable for several reasons: 1) Shoes are made of the skin of the dead animals and after tanning they are clean. 2) The Prophet (PBUH) used to pray in his shoes and his companions also prayed in their shoes. He (PBUH) said:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم “خالفوا اليهود فإنهم لا يصلون في نعالهم ولا خفافهم”.
Be different from the Jews, who do not pray in their shoes or in their leather slippers (khufoof).”
The Prophet (PBUH) also said:
إذا جاء أحدكم إلى المسجد فلينظر ، فإن رأى في نعليه قذراً أو أذى فليمسحه وليصل فيهما
“When any one of you comes to the Masjid, let him look if he sees any dirt on his shoes, let him wipe it off and pray in them.”

In addition, this unique command was mentioned only once in the Quran and in this specific Surat which has the theme of making life easy.
Considering the theme of the Surat, taking off the shoes suggests putting one at ease and comfort. It is like when a person enters his home and takes off his shoes to relax and be comfortable. So, Allah is telling Prophet Musa to be comfortable and at ease because he is now with his Lord.

The way Allah communicated with Prophet Musa when He informed him of his role as Allah’s messenger was also meant to put him at ease. He (AS) was given the permission to supplicate to Allah to make his difficult task easy:
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشۡرَحۡ لِى صَدۡرِى (٢٥) وَيَسِّرۡ لِىٓ أَمۡرِى (٢٦) وَٱحۡلُلۡ عُقۡدَةً۬ مِّن لِّسَانِى (٢٧) يَفۡقَهُواْ قَوۡلِى (٢٨)
[Musa] said: “O my Lord, expand my chest (with assurance and contentment) (25) “And ease my task for me (26) “And untie the knot from my tongue (27) “That they may understand my speech. (20:25-28)

Allah guided prophet Musa and his brother Harun to deliver the message to Pharoah in a soft tone. Allah told them:
ٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكۡرِى (٤٢) ٱذۡهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّهُ ۥ طَغَىٰ (٤٣) فَقُولَا لَهُ ۥ قَوۡلاً۬ لَّيِّنً۬ا لَّعَلَّهُ ۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ (٤٤) قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفۡرُطَ عَلَيۡنَآ أَوۡ أَن يَطۡغَىٰ (٤٥) قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ‌ۖ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسۡمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ (٤٦)
Go you and your brother with My signs and do not slacken in My Remembrance. (42) Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, verily, he has transgressed. (43) “And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear (Allah).” (44) They said: “Our Lord, indeed we fear that he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress.” (45) He (Allah) said: “Fear not, verily! I am with you both, I hear and I see. (20:42-46)

Allah’s support and comfort to Prophet Musa was clear during the challenge that he had with the magicians. When the magicians threw their ropes and sticks and it started moving, Prophet Musa feared that they may succeed in refuting his miracle of changing the staff into a snake, but Allah comforted him and assured him of his success.
فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمۡ وَعِصِيُّهُمۡ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيۡهِ مِن سِحۡرِهِمۡ أَنَّہَا تَسۡعَىٰ (٦٦) فَأَوۡجَسَ فِى نَفۡسِهِۦ خِيفَةً۬ مُّوسَىٰ (٦٧) قُلۡنَا لَا تَخَفۡ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ (٦٨) وَأَلۡقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلۡقَفۡ مَا صَنَعُوٓاْ‌ۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيۡدُ سَـٰحِرٍ۬‌ۖ وَلَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيۡثُ أَتَىٰ (٦٩)
Then behold, their ropes and their sticks seemed to him from their magic they are moving. (66) So, Musa (Moses) sensed fear in himself. (67) We (Allah) said: “Fear not. Surely, you will have the upper hand. (68) “And throw that which is in your right hand. It will swallow up that which they have made. What they have made is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may attain.” (20:66-69)

When Prophet Musa threw his staff and it became a snake and it swallowed what the magicians threw, all the attendees were stunned but such clear miracle did not change the attitude of Pharaoh and his associates. But the magicians prostrated and declared their belief.
فَأُلۡقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدً۬ا قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَـٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ (٧٠)
So, the magicians were led down prostrating. They said: “We believe in the Lord of Harun (Aaron) and Musa (Moses).” (20:70)

Many interpreters suggested that what led the magicians to prostrate and the belief in the God of Musa was their overwhelming by the miracle of Prophet Musa. But where in history did people ever believe as soon as they saw a miracle that made them to immediately change their religion and risk being subjected to major suffering and rejection. Certainly, such a clear miracle did not change the attitude of Pharaoh and his associates.
But the verb (أُلۡقِىَ) is a passive verb that means that someone led the magician down in prostration. This may suggest that Allah is the One who made the magicians prostrate and declare their belief. Allah also inspired them with what to say in response to the severe threats of Pharaoh when he told them (لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُم مِّنۡ خِلَـٰفٍ۬ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمۡ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخۡلِ) “I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date-palms.” Their response is clearly a revelation from Allah and cannot be just their own thought on the moment. They said to Pharaoh:
قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا‌ۖ فَٱقۡضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ‌ۖ إِنَّمَا تَقۡضِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ (٧٢) إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغۡفِرَ لَنَا خَطَـٰيَـٰنَا وَمَآ أَكۡرَهۡتَنَا عَلَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحۡرِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ۬ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓ (٧٣) إِنَّهُ ۥ مَن يَأۡتِ رَبَّهُ ۥ مُجۡرِمً۬ا فَإِنَّ لَهُ ۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحۡيَىٰ (٧٤) وَمَن يَأۡتِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنً۬ا قَدۡ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَـٰتُ ٱلۡعُلَىٰ (٧٥) جَنَّـٰتُ عَدۡنٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا‌ۚ وَذَٲلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ (٧٦)
They said: “We will never prefer you over the clear signs that have come to us, and over Him (Allah) who created us. So, decree whatever you will decree, for you can only decree regarding the life of this world. (72) Verily, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our faults, and the magic to which you did compel us. And Allah is better and more lasting (in reward). (73) Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, then for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live. (74) But whoever comes to Him (Allah) as a believer and has done good deeds, for such are the highest ranks. (75) Eden gardens, under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. And that is the reward for those who purify themselves. (20:72-76)

The Surat continued with giving the details of the escape of Musa with Bani Israel from Egypt and their crossing of the sea. Allah says:
يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ قَدۡ أَنجَيۡنَـٰكُم مِّنۡ عَدُوِّكُمۡ وَوَٲعَدۡنَـٰكُمۡ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنَ وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰ (٨٠)
O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of Mount Tur, and We sent down to you Manna and quails. (20:80)

This story is followed by verses that offer commentary on it and clarify the main objective of the Quran:
كَذَٲلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدۡ سَبَقَ‌ۚ وَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَـٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِڪۡرً۬ا (٩٩) مَّنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَنۡهُ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ يَحۡمِلُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ وِزۡرًا (١٠٠)
Thus, We relate to you some information of past events. And We have given you a Reminder (this Qur’an) from Our presence. (99) Whosoever turns away from it (this Quran), verily, he will bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection. (20:99-100)

The Surat presents an account of Prophet Adam to further emphasize the theme of the Surat that obedience leads to an easy life while disobedience leads to hardship.
وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُ ۥ عَزۡمً۬ا (١١٥) وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ (١١٦) فَقُلۡنَا يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا عَدُوٌّ۬ لَّكَ وَلِزَوۡجِكَ فَلَا يُخۡرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ فَتَشۡقَىٰٓ (١١٧) إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ (١١٨) وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظۡمَؤُاْ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضۡحَىٰ (١١٩)
And We made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We did not find in him a firm resolve. (115) And when We said to the angels: “Prostrate to Adam.” So, they prostrated, except Iblees (Satan); he refused. (116) Then We said: “O Adam! Verily, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So, let him not get you both out of Paradise, so that you be in difficulty. (117) “Verily, you will have (in Paradise) neither hunger nor go naked. (118) “And you will suffer neither from thirst therein nor from the sun’s heat. (20:115-119)

Despite Allah’s warning, Satan was able to deceive Adam on the account that eating from that tree will grant him immortality and a kingdom that never decays.
فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ قَالَ يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكٍ۬ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ (١٢٠) فَأَڪَلَا مِنۡہَا فَبَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٲتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡہِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ‌ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُ ۥ فَغَوَىٰ (١٢١)
Then Satan whispered to him, saying: “O Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and to a kingdom that will never decay?” (120) So, they both ate of it, and so their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten upon themselves with the leaves of Paradise. Thus, Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he went astray. (20:120-121)
We note that Allah never placed the blame on Hawa (Eve); Allah put the blame of disobedience solely on Adam.

Following this account, the theme of the Suart is re-emphasized that even on earth if people follow Allah’s guidance, they will not be in hardship:
قَالَ ٱهۡبِطَا مِنۡهَا جَمِيعَۢا‌ۖ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ۬‌ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّڪُم مِّنِّى هُدً۬ى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشۡقَىٰ (١٢٣)
He (Allah) said: “Go down from here (from Paradise) all of you, some of you enemies of some others. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance shall neither go astray nor fall into difficulty and hardship. (20:123)

Obedience to Allah requires perseverance and the means of achieving perseverance are patience and prayers. Allah says:
فَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِہَا‌ۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآىِٕ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلنَّہَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرۡضَىٰ (١٣٠)
“So, be patient over what they say, and glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset and during some hours of the night, and at the ends of the day, so that you may be pleased.” (20:130)

In this verse as in many other verses in the Quran, Allah states that patience and prayers are the foundation of obedience. Therefore, commanding one’s household to pray is an important command from Allah as He said:
وَأۡمُرۡ أَهۡلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۖ لَا نَسۡـَٔلُكَ رِزۡقً۬ا‌ۖ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكَ‌ۗ وَٱلۡعَـٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰ (١٣٢)
And order your family to pray and be patient with them. We do not ask of you a provision; We provide for you. And the best end is that of Taqwa. (20:132)

Allah gives important advice that commanding one’s household to perform prayers requires patience. Following this important command of Allah can resolve many family problems.
