# The Theme of Surat Al-Anbiya (الاٴنبیَاء) (The Prophets)  (21)

Surat Al-Anbiya (الاٴنبیَاء) was revealed in Mecca.  The theme of the Surat is the role of the Prophets which is to deliver a singular message that there is no god but Allah, so worship Him.

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيۡهِ أَنَّهُ ۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۟ فَٱعۡبُدُونِ (٢٥)

And We did not send any Messenger before you, but We revealed to him that: “There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.” (21:25)

And theme affirms that none of the prophets ever claimed to be gods.

وَقَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ وَلَدً۬ا‌ۗ سُبۡحَـٰنَهُ ۥ‌ۚ بَلۡ عِبَادٌ۬ مُّكۡرَمُونَ (٢٦) لَا يَسۡبِقُونَهُ ۥ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَهُم بِأَمۡرِهِۦ يَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٧) يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيہِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ وَلَا يَشۡفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرۡتَضَىٰ وَهُم مِّنۡ خَشۡيَتِهِۦ مُشۡفِقُونَ (٢٨) ۞ وَمَن يَقُلۡ مِنۡہُمۡ إِنِّىٓ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَذَٲلِكَ نَجۡزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ نَجۡزِى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (٢٩)

And whosoever says: “The Rahman has taken a son.” Exalted is He! Rather, they (the prophets) are [but] honored slaves. (26) They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command. (27) He knows what is in front of them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede on behalf of anyone except for whom He approves of and in awe of Him, they are apprehensive. (28) Should any of them say, ” I am god besides Him”, We will recompense with Hell. Thus, do We recompense the wrongdoers.” (21:26-29)

The surah starts with stating that the main reason for the deviation of people from the path of Allah is heedlessness (الغفلة) and thus a key mission of Prophets is to awaken people from such heedlessness.

ٱقۡتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ فِى غَفۡلَةٍ۬ مُّعۡرِضُونَ (١) مَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن ذِڪۡرٍ۬ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحۡدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسۡتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمۡ يَلۡعَبُونَ (٢) لَاهِيَةً۬ قُلُوبُهُمۡ‌ۗ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجۡوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ هَلۡ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ۬ مِّثۡلُڪُمۡ‌ۖ أَفَتَأۡتُونَ ٱلسِّحۡرَ وَأَنتُمۡ تُبۡصِرُونَ (٣)

“Draws near for mankind their reckoning, while they are in heedlessness turning away. (1) Even when a message comes to them from their Lord, they listen to it while they play. (2) With their hearts occupied in trivialities. The wrongdoers whisper in secret: “Is he but a human being like you? Do you then yield to sorcery even as you see (his reality)?” (21:1-3).

Heedlessness (الغفلة) is such a dangerous illness that infects people and societies and results in taking them away from the path of Allah.  The Ayat indicate that heedless may be manifested in three symptoms:

- Dismissing the existence of the Hereafter (مُّعْرِضُونَ).
- Not taking the revelation seriously (هُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ)
- Having preoccupied hearts with trivialities (لاَهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ)

The Surat names 16 Prophets and referred to two without naming them (Prophet Isa and Muhammad). The 16 prophets who were named are:

مُوسَىٰ وَهَـٰرُونَ و إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ و لُوطًا و إِسۡحَـٰقَ ويعقوب وَنُوحًا وَدَاوُ ۥدَ وَسُلَيۡمَـٰنَ وَأَيُّوبَ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلَ وَإِدۡرِيسَ  وَذَا ٱلۡكِفۡلِ‌ وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ وَزَڪَرِيَّآ وۥ يَحۡيَىٰ

Musa (Moses), Harun (Aaron), Ibrahim (Abraham), Lut (Lot), Ishaq (Isaac), Ya’qub (Jacob), Nuh (Noah), Dawud (David), Sulaiman (Solomon), Ayyub (Job), Isma’il (Ishmael), Idris (Enoch), Dha’l-kifl (Ezekiel), Dhal-Noon (Yunus /Jonah), Zakariyya (Zechariah) and Yahya (John)

In total, the Quran named 25 Prophet. The 18 mentioned in this Surat plus: Adam, Hud, Saleh, Yousef (Joseph), Shu’aib, Ilias (Elias), and Al-Yasa’a (Elisha).

There are many other prophets and messengers who were not mentioned in the Quran.  It is reported that Abu Dhar asked the Prophet (PBUH) about the number of the Prophets and the number of messengers, and the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال أبو ذر : قلت يا رسول الله: كم وفاء عدة الأنبياء ؟ قال : مائة ‏ألف ، وأربعة وعشرون ألفا ، والرسل من ذلك: ثلاثمائة وخمسة عشر ، جما غفيرا .‏).

The number of the prophets is 124 thousand.  And the number of messengers is 315.

The Surat highlights for each Prophet his relationship with Allah regarding worship and obedience and his relationship with the people regarding calling to Allah. This should teach us that we should consider both our relationships; the relationship with Allah through our worship and the relationship with the people through our Da’wa (inviting the people to Allah).

The Surat emphasizes the importance of study and rational thinking because these are the tools that allow people to easily accept the message of the prophets to believe in and worship none by Allah.

One of the common justifications that people used in rejecting the Prophets is that they are merely men. Allah responds by directing them to study history to realize that all prophets were mortals, and that Allah have always supported His Prophets:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا قَبۡلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالاً۬ نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۖ فَسۡـَٔلُوٓاْ أَهۡلَ ٱلذِّڪۡرِ إِن كُنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ (٧) وَمَا جَعَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ جَسَدً۬ا لَّا يَأۡڪُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُواْ خَـٰلِدِينَ (٨) ثُمَّ صَدَقۡنَـٰهُمُ ٱلۡوَعۡدَ فَأَنجَيۡنَـٰهُمۡ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ وَأَهۡلَڪۡنَا ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ (٩)

And We did not send messengers before you (O Muhammad) except men whom we inspired with revelation. So, ask the people (having knowledge) of the revealed message if you do not know. (7) And We did not create them (the Messengers, with) bodies that ate not food, nor were they immortals. (8) Then We fulfilled to them the promise, so We saved them and those whom We willed, and We destroyed the exceedingly rebellious. (21:7-9)

Another reason used by people to reject the prophets has been questioning the existence of only one God.  Allah said:

لَوۡ كَانَ فِيہِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا‌ۚ فَسُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ (٢٢) لَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفۡعَلُ وَهُمۡ يُسۡـَٔلُونَ (٢٣) أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦۤ ءَالِهَةً۬‌ۖ قُلۡ هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَـٰنَكُمۡ‌ۖ هَـٰذَا ذِكۡرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكۡرُ مَن قَبۡلِى‌ۗ بَلۡ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ‌ۖ فَهُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ (٢٤)

Had there been gods besides Allah in the heavens and the earth, both of them would have been ruined. Glorified is Allah, the Lord of the Throne, from what they describe. (22) He cannot be questioned as to what He does, while they will be questioned. (23) Have they taken gods besides Him? Say: “Bring your proof”.  This (the Quran) is the reminder for those with me and the reminder for those before me. Yet, most of them know not the truth, and therefore they are turning away. (21:22-24)

Allah appeals to reason by asking the disbelievers a rhetorical question on who protects them night and day:

قُلۡ مَن يَكۡلَؤُڪُم بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ‌ۗ بَلۡ هُمۡ عَن ذِڪۡرِ رَبِّهِم مُّعۡرِضُونَ (٤٢)

Say: “Who can guard and protect you in the night or in the day from the (punishment of the) Most Gracious?” Nay, but they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord. (21:42)

The Surat directs attention to the significance of studying the science of creation to further appreciate the Creator and His creation:

أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ ڪَانَتَا رَتۡقً۬ا فَفَتَقۡنَـٰهُمَا‌ۖ وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ حَىٍّ‌ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٣٠) وَجَعَلۡا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٲسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَا فِيہَا فِجَاجً۬ا سُبُلاً۬ لَّعَلَّهُمۡ يَہۡتَدُونَ (٣١) وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقۡفً۬ا مَّحۡفُوظً۬ا‌ۖ وَهُمۡ عَنۡ ءَايَـٰتِہَا مُعۡرِضُونَ (٣٢) وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّہَارَ وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ‌ۖ كُلٌّ۬ فِى فَلَكٍ۬ يَسۡبَحُونَ (٣٣)

Have those who disbelieve not observed that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, then We parted them? And We have made from water every living thing. Would they still not believe? (30) And We have placed on the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We placed therein broad highways for them to pass through, that they may be guided. (31) And We have made the sky a protected roof. Yet they turn away from its signs. (32) And He it is One who has created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each gliding in an orbit. (21:30-33)

Allah also points out how the creation will end:

يَوۡمَ نَطۡوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ ڪَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلۡڪُتُبِ‌ۚ كَمَا بَدَأۡنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلۡقٍ۬ نُّعِيدُهُ ۥ‌ۚ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡنَآ‌ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَـٰعِلِينَ (١٠٤)

And (beware of) the Day when We shall fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll for books. Just as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it. (That is) a promise binding upon Us. Truly, We shall do it.” (21:104).

The most recognized scientific model today for the beginning of the universe i the big bang model that suggests that the universe began 13.8 billion years ago as a tiny, dense fireball that exploded. Hope one young Muslim scientist can contribute to the model for the origin of the universe guided by what is mentioned in the Quran on the folded scroll.

The Surat reminds the readers with the two facts that everyone will die, and everyone will face Allah for just judgement:

كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ ذَآٮِٕقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ‌ۗ وَنَبۡلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلۡخَيۡرِ فِتۡنَةً۬‌ۖ وَإِلَيۡنَا تُرۡجَعُونَ (٣٥)

Everyone is going to taste death, and We shall make a trial of you with evil and with good, and to Us you will be returned. (21:35)

وَنَضَعُ ٱلۡمَوَٲزِينَ ٱلۡقِسۡطَ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسٌ۬ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا‌ۖ وَإِن ڪَانَ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةٍ۬ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلٍ أَتَيۡنَا بِہَا‌ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَـٰسِبِينَ (٤٧)

And We shall set up balances of justice on the Day of Resurrection, then none will be dealt with unjustly in anything. And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And Sufficient are We to take account. (21:47)

The Surat presents key phases of the different prophets including the supplication of some of them and how Allah answered their supplications:

Musa and Haroun:

وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَـٰرُونَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ وَضِيَآءً۬ وَذِكۡرً۬ا لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٤٨) ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّہُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ مُشۡفِقُونَ (٤٩)

And We gave Musa and Harun the criterion and a light and a reminder for the God conscious. (48) Who have awe of their Lord without having seen Him and are apprehensive of the Hour (of Judgement). (21:49)

Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub:

وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ رُشۡدَهُ ۥ مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَـٰلِمِينَ (٥١) إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَـٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَـٰكِفُونَ (٥٢) قَالُواْ وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَـٰبِدِينَ (٥٣) قَالَ لَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُڪُمۡ فِى ضَلَـٰلٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٥٤) قَالُوٓاْ أَجِئۡتَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ أَمۡ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّـٰعِبِينَ (٥٥) قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمۡ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۟ عَلَىٰ ذَٲلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ (٥٦)

And earlier, We had given Ibrahim his sound judgement, and We know him well. (51) When he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are devoted?” (52) They said, “We found our fathers worshippers of them.” (53) He said, “You and your fathers are certainly in manifest error.” (54) They said, “Have you come to us with truth, or are you of those who jest?” (55) He said, “[No], rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I am one of those who bear witness to it. (21:51-56)

وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥۤ إِسۡحَـٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ نَافِلَةً۬‌ۖ وَكُلاًّ۬ جَعَلۡنَا صَـٰلِحِينَ (٧٢) وَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ أَٮِٕمَّةً۬ يَہۡدُونَ بِأَمۡرِنَا وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِ فِعۡلَ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٲتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّڪَوٰةِ‌ۖ وَكَانُواْ لَنَا عَـٰبِدِينَ (٧٣)

And We blessed him with Ishaq and Yaqub in addition, and all [of them] We made righteous. (72) And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them to do good deeds, establish prayer, and pay zakat; and Us alone they worshipped. (21:72-73)

Lut

وَلُوطًا ءَاتَيۡنَـٰهُ حُكۡمً۬ا وَعِلۡمً۬ا وَنَجَّيۡنَـٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَت تَّعۡمَلُ ٱلۡخَبَـٰٓٮِٕثَ‌ۗ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمَ سَوۡءٍ۬ فَـٰسِقِينَ (٧٤) وَأَدۡخَلۡنَـٰهُ فِى رَحۡمَتِنَآ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (٧٥)

And to Lut, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that was committing wicked deeds. Indeed, they were the people of evil, defiantly rebellious. (74) And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous. (21:74-75)

Nuh

وَنُوحًا إِذۡ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥ فَنَجَّيۡنَـٰهُ وَأَهۡلَهُ ۥ مِنَ ٱلۡڪَرۡبِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ (٧٦) وَنَصَرۡنَـٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَآ‌ۚ إِنَّہُمۡ ڪَانُواْ قَوۡمَ سَوۡءٍ۬ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ (٧٧)

And [mention] Nuh, when he called (for help) earlier, so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the terrible agony (great flood). (76) And We supported him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil. Therefore, We drowned them, all. (21:76-77)

Dawud and Suliman

وَدَاوُ ۥدَ وَسُلَيۡمَـٰنَ إِذۡ يَحۡڪُمَانِ فِى ٱلۡحَرۡثِ إِذۡ نَفَشَتۡ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ وَڪُنَّا لِحُكۡمِهِمۡ شَـٰهِدِينَ (٧٨) فَفَهَّمۡنَـٰهَا سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ‌ۚ وَڪُلاًّ ءَاتَيۡنَا حُكۡمً۬ا وَعِلۡمً۬ا‌ۚ وَسَخَّرۡنَا مَعَ دَاوُ ۥدَ ٱلۡجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحۡنَ وَٱلطَّيۡرَ‌ۚ وَڪُنَّا فَـٰعِلِينَ (٧٩) وَعَلَّمۡنَـٰهُ صَنۡعَةَ لَبُوسٍ۬ لَّڪُمۡ لِتُحۡصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأۡسِكُمۡ‌ۖ فَهَلۡ أَنتُمۡ شَـٰكِرُونَ (٨٠) وَلِسُلَيۡمَـٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً۬ تَجۡرِى بِأَمۡرِهِۦۤ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلَّتِى بَـٰرَكۡنَا فِيہَا‌ۚ وَڪُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَـٰلِمِينَ (٨١) وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ ۥ وَيَعۡمَلُونَ عَمَلاً۬ دُونَ ذَٲلِكَ‌ۖ وَكُنَّا لَهُمۡ حَـٰفِظِينَ (٨٢) ۞

And [mention] Dawud and Suliman, when they judged concerning the tillage in which the sheep of other people overran it at night (and destroyed it), and We were witness to their judgement. (78) And We enabled Suliman to understand i. And to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjugated to Dawud the mountains to exalt [Us], and the birds as well. And We were the One who did it. (79) And We taught him the skill of making armor as garments to protect you [in battle). So, will you then be grateful? (80) And to Suliman [We subjugated] the violent wind, that blew under his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing. (81) And of the devils were those who dived for him and did work other than that. And We kept watch over them. (21:78-82)

Ayyub

وَأَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ ۥۤ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٲحِمِينَ (٨٣) فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥ فَكَشَفۡنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّ۬‌ۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَـٰهُ أَهۡلَهُ ۥ وَمِثۡلَهُم مَّعَهُمۡ رَحۡمَةً۬ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَذِڪۡرَىٰ لِلۡعَـٰبِدِينَ (٨٤)

“And (remember) Ayyub, when he called his Lord saying: “Adversity has touched me, and you are the Most Merciful of the merciful.” (83) So, We answered his prayer and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of Allah].  (21:83-84)

Ismael, Idris and Dhul-Kifl

وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلَ وَإِدۡرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلۡكِفۡلِ‌ۖ ڪُلٌّ۬ مِّنَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ (٨٥) وَأَدۡخَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ فِى رَحۡمَتِنَآ‌ۖ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (٨٦)

And [mention] Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient. (85) And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous. (21:85-86)

Yunus (Dhul-Noon)and his supplication when he was in the inside the belly the whale

وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَـٰضِبً۬ا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ إِنِّى ڪُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (٨٧) فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥ وَنَجَّيۡنَـٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَمِّ‌ۚ وَكَذَٲلِكَ نُـۨجِى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٨٨)

“And (mention) DhuL-Noon, when he walked away in anger and thought that We would never out him in trouble.  Then he called (Us) in the depth of darkness, saying: There is no God but You, glory to you. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers. (87) Then We accepted his prayer and rescued him from the distress and this is how we rescue the believers. (21:87-88)

Note: This supplication(لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ إِنِّى ڪُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ) (There is no God but You, glory to you. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.)is important to remember and say anytime one is in a state of distress and worry because Allah said in response to this Dua:“And this how we rescue the believers “.

Zakariyaand Yahya:

وَزَڪَرِيَّآ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ ۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرۡنِى فَرۡدً۬ا وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡوَٲرِثِينَ (٨٩) فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥ وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥ يَحۡيَىٰ وَأَصۡلَحۡنَا لَهُ ۥ زَوۡجَهُ ۥۤ‌ۚ إِنَّهُمۡ ڪَانُواْ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلۡخَيۡرَٲتِ وَيَدۡعُونَنَا رَغَبً۬ا وَرَهَبً۬ا‌ۖ وَڪَانُواْ لَنَا خَـٰشِعِينَ (٩٠)

And (remember) Zakariya when he called his Lord: “O My Lord!  Do not leave me alone (with no heir) and You are the Best of the inheritors.”  (89) So, We responded to him, and gave him Yahya, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten towards the good deeds and supplicate Us with hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive. (21:89-90)

In reference to Prophet Isa:

وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحۡصَنَتۡ فَرۡجَهَا فَنَفَخۡنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلۡنَـٰهَا وَٱبۡنَهَآ ءَايَةً۬ لِّلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٩١)

And [mention] the one who guarded her chastity. So, We blew into her (a life) through Our spirit (Archangel Gibril), and We made her and her son a sign for all the worlds. (21:91)

In reference to Prophet Mohammad and his primary mission of mercy and warning to those who reject him:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ إِلَّا رَحۡمَةً۬ لِّلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٠٧) قُلۡ إِنَّمَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُڪُمۡ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ وَٲحِدٌ۬‌ۖ فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ (١٠٨) فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَقُلۡ ءَاذَنتُڪُمۡ عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ۬‌ۖ وَإِنۡ أَدۡرِىٓ أَقَرِيبٌ أَم بَعِيدٌ۬ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ (١٠٩)

And We have not sent you, [O Mohammad], but as a mercy for all the worlds. (107) Say, “What is revealed to me is simply that your God is but one God. So, will you be Muslims (submit to Him)?” (108) But if they turn away, then say (to them), “I have announced to [all of] you equally. And I do not know whether what you have been warned of is near or far. (21:107-109)

The Surat includes mention of some key signs of the end of time with its reference to Gog and Magog.  Also, the Surat emphasizes the expected punishment for those who reject the prophets’ message and worship anyone other than Allah:

حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُتِحَتۡ يَأۡجُوجُ وَمَأۡجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن ڪُلِّ حَدَبٍ۬ يَنسِلُونَ (٩٦) وَٱقۡتَرَبَ ٱلۡوَعۡدُ ٱلۡحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِىَ شَـٰخِصَةٌ أَبۡصَـٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَـٰوَيۡلَنَا قَدۡ ڪُنَّا فِى غَفۡلَةٍ۬ مِّنۡ هَـٰذَا بَلۡ ڪُنَّا ظَـٰلِمِينَ (٩٧) إِنَّڪُمۡ وَمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا وَٲرِدُونَ (٩٨) لَوۡ كَانَ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةً۬ مَّا وَرَدُوهَا‌ۖ وَڪُلٌّ۬ فِيہَا خَـٰلِدُونَ (٩٩)

Until when Ya’gog and Ma’gog (Gog and Magog) let loose, and they descend from every mound. (96) And the true promise draws near, then the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring [in horror, while they say], “O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this; rather, we were wrongdoers.” (97) Indeed, you (disbelievers) and what you worship other than Allah are the firewood of Hell that you will be coming to [enter] it. (98) Had they been gods, they would not have come to it, and all of them will remain there forever. (21:96-99)

The Surat ends with an affirmation that the earth belongs to the believers.

وَلَقَدۡ ڪَتَبۡنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلذِّكۡرِ أَنَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحُونَ (١٠٥) إِنَّ فِى هَـٰذَا لَبَلَـٰغً۬ا لِّقَوۡمٍ عَـٰبِدِينَ

“And We have written in Az-Zabur [the written text that was given to any messenger) after the reminder (refers to what is written in the preserved tablet Al-Lawh Al-Mahfouz) that the earth will be inherited by My righteous slaves. (105)  Surely, in this (message) an all-sufficing Message for people who worship Allah.” (21:105-106)

content:
The Theme of Surah Al-Hajj (الحج) (The Pilgrimage) (22)

Surat Al-Hajj was partly revealed in both Mecca and Madina. The theme of the Surat is The Hajj is a journey that should inspire the pilgrims to reaffirm their belief in the Oneness of God and their commitment to embrace the values of unity, humility, and social responsibility.

The Surat starts with describing the last day and the feeling of those how will witness it:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّڪُمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّ زَلۡزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَىۡءٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١) يَوۡمَ تَرَوۡنَهَا تَذۡهَلُ كُلُّ مُرۡضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرۡضَعَتۡ وَتَصَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمۡلٍ حَمۡلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُڪَـٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُڪَـٰرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ۬ (٢)

O mankind, have Taqwa of your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the (final) Hour is something terrible. (1) The Day you shall see it, every nursing mother will become utterly diverted from what she is nursling, and every pregnant woman will abort her fetus, and you shall see mankind as if they are drunk, while they are not drunk, but rather the torment from Allah is very severe. (22:1-2)

Then the Surat summarizes the human life from conception to resurrection:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمۡ فِى رَيۡبٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡبَعۡثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقۡنَـٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍ۬ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةٍ۬ ثُمَّ مِنۡ عَلَقَةٍ۬ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضۡغَةٍ۬ مُّخَلَّقَةٍ۬ وَغَيۡرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ۬ لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمۡ‌ۚ وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّى ثُمَّ نُخۡرِجُڪُمۡ طِفۡلاً۬ ثُمَّ لِتَبۡلُغُوٓاْ أَشُدَّكُمۡ‌ۖ وَمِنڪُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنڪُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرۡذَلِ ٱلۡعُمُرِ لِڪَيۡلَا يَعۡلَمَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ عِلۡمٍ۬ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا‌ۚ وَتَرَى ٱلۡأَرۡضَ هَامِدَةً۬ فَإِذَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡمَآءَ ٱهۡتَزَّتۡ وَرَبَتۡ وَأَنۢبَتَتۡ مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجِۭ بَهِيۡجٍ۬ (٥) ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُ ۥ يُحۡىِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَأَنَّهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬ (٦) وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ۬ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيہَا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلۡقُبُورِ (٧)

“O People, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then [consider that] We created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, and then from a lump of flesh, shaped and unshaped – so that We show (our power) to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, and then [We develop you] so that you reach your maturity. And among you there is one who dies, and among you there is one who reached the worst part of age, so that he knows nothing after [once having] knowledge. And you see the earth barren, but once We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and puts forth pairs of every beautiful kind. (5) That is because Allah is the Truth and because He gives life to the dead and because He is powerful to do everything. (6) And surely, the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it; and certainly, Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves. (22:5-7)

The Command for the believers to perform the Hajj started with a command from Allah to Prophet Ibrahim to call people for Hajj.

وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَجِّ يَأۡتُوكَ رِجَالاً۬ وَعَلَىٰ ڪُلِّ ضَامِرٍ۬ يَأۡتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ۬ (٢٧) لِّيَشۡہَدُواْ مَنَـٰفِعَ لَهُمۡ وَيَذۡڪُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ۬ مَّعۡلُومَـٰتٍ … (٢٨)

And proclaim to the people the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep and distant highway. (27) So that they witness benefits for them and mention the name of Allah in known days … (22:27-28)

Allah commanded Prophet Ibrahim to call people to the Hajj while he was standing in the middle of the desert. How can his call reach people all over the world? Impossible, but it is easy for Allah. Prophet Ibrahim followed Allah’s command without any hesitation or doubt and the results as Allah said, billions of people responded to that single call from all over the world.

Yes, Prophet Ibrahim must act and make the call because the action is necessary, but it is in no way sufficient to achieve this dream results. It is the power of Allah that delivers the results. If our actions are guided by the command of Allah in every step, Allah will transform our sincere yet small efforts into something far bigger than we can imagine. But the key is that our action must follow Allah’s command in every step without any compromise.

Immediately following that Ayat that describe the Hajj, comes that Ayat that gives Muslims permission to fight those who commit injustice against them and trust that Allah will grant them victory. Similar to the call of the one person, Prophet Ibrahim, that Allah made it realized, Allah can grant victory to the weak who fight to remove injustice.

أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَـٰتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ ظُلِمُواْ‌ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ نَصۡرِهِمۡ لَقَدِيرٌ (٣٩) ٱلَّذِينَ أُخۡرِجُواْ مِن دِيَـٰرِهِم بِغَيۡرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ … (٤٠)

Permission (to fight) is given to those who are being fought because they have been wronged, and surely, Allah is Able to give them victory. (39) (They are) those who have been expelled from their homes without any just reason except that they say: “Our Lord is Allah”…. (22:39-40)

Muslims are not only commanded to fight to remove the injustice committed against them, but they are also required to fight to defend all places of worship including the non-Muslim ones. Allah says:

وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَہُم بِبَعۡضٍ۬ لَّهُدِّمَتۡ صَوَٲمِعُ وَبِيَعٌ۬ وَصَلَوَٲتٌ۬ وَمَسَـٰجِدُ يُذۡكَرُ فِيہَا ٱسۡمُ ٱللَّهِ ڪَثِيراً‌ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُ ۥۤ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ (٤٠)

For had Allah not been repelling some people by means of some others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques, where Allah’s name is abundantly mentioned would have been demolished. Allah will definitely help those who help His (Cause). Truly, Allah is All-powerful, All-Mighty. (22:40)

One may wonder how a Muslim is commanded to fight and sacrifice his life to protect the places of worship for the followers of other religions that may have elements of shirk. The reason is that freedom of religion is a right granted by Allah to every human being and Allah alone has the authority to judge between the followers of all religions. Thus, the Suart highlights a very important rule on the day of Judgement. The rule is that no one but Allah can decide the fate of anyone else. Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ وَٱلصَّـٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَـٰرَىٰ وَٱلۡمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَہُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ ڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ شَہِيدٌ (١٧)

“Those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabaeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who ascribe partners to Allah – Indeed Allah will judge between them on the Day of Judgement. Indeed, Allah is Witness over all things.” (Al-Hajj 22:17)

This Ayat emphasizes that Allah is the only One who declares judgements. This includes those who believe in Allah by following Prophets, or believe in Allah without following any Prophet, or even associate others with Allah. No one has the right to make decisions on behalf of Allah.

However, Allah provides the attributes of those who will be successful on the day of judgment, Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدۡخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡہَـٰرُ يُحَلَّوۡنَ فِيہَا مِنۡ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ۬ وَلُؤۡلُؤً۬ا‌ۖ وَلِبَاسُہُمۡ فِيہَا حَرِيرٌ۬ (٢٣) وَهُدُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيِّبِ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَهُدُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٲطِ ٱلۡحَمِيدِ (٢٤)

Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be (of) silk. (23) They were guided [in worldly life] to good speech, and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy. (22:23-4)

وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ قُتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡ مَاتُواْ لَيَرۡزُقَنَّهُمُ ٱللَّهُ رِزۡقًا حَسَنً۬ا‌ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٲزِقِينَ (٥٨) لَيُدۡخِلَنَّهُم مُّدۡخَلاً۬ يَرۡضَوۡنَهُ ۥ‌ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ۬ (٥٩)

And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah and then were killed or died – Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And surely Allah is the best of providers. (58) He will definitely admit them to an entrance they will be pleased with, and indeed, Allah is All-Knowing Forbearing. (22:58-59)

And Allah provides the attributes of those who will be punished, Allah says:

وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَـٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍ۬ وَلَا هُدً۬ى وَلَا كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّنِيرٍ۬ (٨) ثَانِىَ عِطۡفِهِۦ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ لَهُ ۥ فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا خِزۡىٌ۬ وَنُذِيقَهُ ۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ عَذَابَ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ (٩) ذَٲلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ يَدَاكَ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيۡسَ بِظَلَّـٰمٍ۬ لِّلۡعَبِيدِ (١٠)

Among the people is one who disputes about Allah with no knowledge, no guidance or no enlightening book. (8) Turning his side away in arrogance to mislead [people] from the way of Allah. For him, there is disgrace in the world, and We will make him taste the punishment of fire on the Day of Judgement. (9) (and will say to him) “That is for what your hands have put forth and because Allah is never unjust to [His] slaves.” (22:8-10)

هَـٰذَانِ خَصۡمَانِ ٱخۡتَصَمُواْ فِى رَبِّہِمۡ‌ۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُواْ قُطِّعَتۡ لَهُمۡ ثِيَابٌ۬ مِّن نَّارٍ۬ يُصَبُّ مِن فَوۡقِ رُءُوسِہِمُ ٱلۡحَمِيمُ (١٩) يُصۡہَرُ بِهِۦ مَا فِى بُطُونِہِمۡ وَٱلۡجُلُودُ (٢٠) وَلَهُم مَّقَـٰمِعُ مِنۡ حَدِيدٍ۬ (٢١) ڪُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡہَا مِنۡ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُواْ فِيہَا وَذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ (٢٢)

These are two adversaries who have disputed over their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have garments of fire tailored for them, and boiling water shall be poured upon their heads. (19) By which everything in their bellies and [their] skins will be melted. (20) And for them, there are hooked rods of iron. (21) Every time they want to get out of Hellfire from anguish, they will be returned back to it, and [it will be said], “Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.” (22:19-22)

وَيَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمۡ يُنَزِّلۡ بِهِۦ سُلۡطَـٰنً۬ا وَمَا لَيۡسَ لَهُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ۬‌ۗ وَمَا لِلظَّـٰلِمِينَ مِن نَّصِيرٍ۬ (٧١) وَإِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ءَايَـٰتُنَا بَيِّنَـٰتٍ۬ تَعۡرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلۡمُنكَرَ‌ۖ يَڪَادُونَ يَسۡطُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ءَايَـٰتِنَا‌ۗ قُلۡ أَفَأُنَبِّئُڪُم بِشَرٍّ۬ مِّن ذَٲلِكُمُ‌ۗ ٱلنَّارُ وَعَدَهَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ‌ۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ (٧٢)

And they worship beside Allah that for which He has never sent down an authority and about which they have no knowledge. And for the wrongdoers there is no helper. (71) And when Our Ayat are recited to them as clear evidence, you (can) recognize the denial in the faces of those who disbelieve. They are almost on the verge of assaulting those who recite to them Our Ayat. Say, “Shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that? [It is] the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieve, and it is an evil final destination.” (22:71-72)

The Surat highlights the danger of making false claims about Allah:

وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَـٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍ۬ وَيَتَّبِعُ ڪُلَّ شَيۡطَـٰنٍ۬ مَّرِيدٍ۬ (٣)

And among the people there are one who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil. (22:3)

وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَـٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍ۬ وَلَا هُدً۬ى وَلَا كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّنِيرٍ۬ (٨)

And among the people there are one who disputes about Allah with no knowledge, no guidance, and no enlightening Book. (22:8)

The Surat gives a critical warning to Muslims regarding superficial beliefs. A sign of a superficial beliefs is manifested by improper responses to tests from Allah:

وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفٍ۬‌ۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُ ۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦ‌ۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأَخِرَةَ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (١١) يَدۡعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُ ۥ وَمَا لَا يَنفَعُهُ ۥ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَـٰلُ ٱلۡبَعِيدُ (١٢) يَدۡعُواْ لَمَن ضَرُّهُ ۥۤ أَقۡرَبُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِۦ‌ۚ لَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَلَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡعَشِيرُ (١٣)

And among the people there is one who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns his face back. He loses both this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss. (11) He supplicates to someone, instead of Allah, who can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the extreme error. (12) He invokes one whose harm is more likely than his benefit – how wretched is such protector and how wretched is such companion. (22:11-13)

Allah provided a compelling demonstration of the helplessness of those whom people worship besides Allah.

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ۬ فَٱسۡتَمِعُواْ لَهُ ۥۤ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَن يَخۡلُقُواْ ذُبَابً۬ا وَلَوِ ٱجۡتَمَعُواْ لَهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَإِن يَسۡلُبۡهُمُ ٱلذُّبَابُ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا لَّا يَسۡتَنقِذُوهُ مِنۡهُ‌ۚ ضَعُفَ ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلۡمَطۡلُوبُ (٧٣)

O mankind, a similitude has been set forth, so listen to it. All those whom you invoke besides Allah, cannot create (even) a fly, even if all come together for that purpose. And if the fly snatches something away from them, they cannot release it from it. Equally weak are (both) the invoker and the invoked. (22:73)

There is a specific reason for why Allah specified a fly, in particular, in this Ayat. A fly eats by dropping its saliva on the food. The saliva contains a chemical called amylase. This amylase breaks down the food into simple chemicals. The fly then sucks up the liquid. Then, the liquid food moves through the fly mouth into its digestive system, where the food is further broken down. So, when the fly grabs something, you will never take it back from it because it changes its chemical composition before it even takes it. Thus, even if you extract it from the fly, you will not get the same material it took it from you.

Following this example, Allah gives the real reason why people associate others with Allah and this reason is that they don’t know Allah:

مَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦۤ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ (٧٤)

They have not made a rightful estimate of Allah. Indeed, Allah is the most powerful, All-Mighty. (22:74)

Only those who give Allah His rightful estimate will truly submit to Allah. The essence of Hajj is that it makes you feel that the whole universe is in total submission to Allah. On the day of Arafa, you witness that you are not the only one who prostrates to Allah and calls on Him; but people from every corner of our planet are doing the same. You, all, join in a collective act of submissiveness to Allah. This is evident in Allah’s saying:

أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسۡجُدُ لَهُ ۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَڪَثِيرٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلنَّايۡ

Have you not seen that whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the beasts and many human beings willingly prostrate themselves to Allah. (22:18)

The Surat ends by emphasizing the key responsibilities for the believers.

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱرۡڪَعُواْ وَٱسۡجُدُواْ وَٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ وَٱفۡعَلُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ ۩ (٧٧) وَجَـٰهِدُواْ فِى ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦ‌ۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَٮٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجٍ۬‌ۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيڪُمۡ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ‌ۚ هُوَ سَمَّٮٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِى هَـٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَہِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُہَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّڪَٰوةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَٮٰكُمۡ‌ۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ (٧٨)

O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good so that you may succeed. (77) And strive for the cause of Allah a strive that is due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Ibrahim. In this, as in formal scriptures, Allah has named you “Muslims. So that the Messenger will be a witness over you and you will be witnesses over the people. So, establish prayer and pay the zakat and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector. How excellent He is as a protector, and how excellent as supporter. (22:77-78)

In addition to the well-known responsibilities of the believers to perform prayers, do good deeds and striving for the sake of Allah to defend themselves and others, these Ayat identifies one major responsibility for Muslims will do on the day of Judgement and thus they must prepare themselves for it. This responsibility is to make themselves qualified to testify in front of Allah against those who associate others with Allah that they have delivered to them the true message of Allah. This responsibility is the same responsibility of the Prophet (PBUH) who will testify that he (PBUH) delivered the message of Allah to us. Based on this testimony of the Prophet (PBUH), Muslims will be judged and based on the testimony of the Muslims all other people will be judged.

Before I wrap up, there is one more verse in this Surat that I would like to comment on to clarify some false narratives regarding its interpretation. Unfortunately, such false narratives propagated into a number of well-known Islamic books such as Al-Tabari (الطبري), Ibn Abi Hatim (ابن أبي حاتم), and Al-Bazar (البزار). The verse says:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ۬ وَلَا نَبِىٍّ إِلَّآ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰٓ أَلۡقَى ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ فِىٓ أُمۡنِيَّتِهِۦ فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يُلۡقِى ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ ثُمَّ يُحۡڪِمُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ۬ (٥٢)

“And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he had a wish (for people to accept Allah’s revelation), Satan threw (obstacles) in his wish. But Allah annuls whatever Satan casts. Then Allah confirms His Ayat. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise. (22:52)

The Arabic word (تَمَنَّى) means “to wish” and “to desire”. But strangely enough, it is misinterpreted to mean “recite” (تلى). This misinterpretation creeped in most translations as follows:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ۬ وَلَا نَبِىٍّ إِلَّآ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰٓ أَلۡقَى ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ فِىٓ أُمۡنِيَّتِهِۦ فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهَ مَا يُلۡقِى ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ ثُمَّ يُحۡڪِمُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ۬ (٥٢)) الحج

And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or recited], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding]. But Allah annuls whatever Satan casts. Then Allah confirms His Ayat. And Allah is All-Knowing and Wise. (22:52)

This false interpretation led the myth known as Al-Gharaniq (الغرانيق) “the Cranes”. Though this myth story never happened, it crept into some Islamic books, then it was propagated further by both naïve Muslims and those who want to create doubts and spread falsehood about Islam.

The false story claims that one day the prophet (PBUH) was sitting near the Ka’bah and reciting Surah al-Najm (النجم). After the prophet (PBUH) reached these two Ayat:

أَفَرَءَيۡتُمُ ٱللَّـٰتَ وَٱلۡعُزَّىٰ (١٩) وَمَنَوٰةَ ٱلثَّالِثَةَ ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰٓ (٢٠) [النجم]

“Have you thought on al-Lat and al-Uzza (19) and Manat, the other third?” (Al-Najim 53:19-20)

Satan influenced the Prophet (PBUH) and made him follow by saying:

تلك الغرانيق العلى وإن شفاعتهن لترجى

“These are high ‘Gharaniq’ whose intercession is sought.”

Then the prophet (PBUH) continued with the recitation of the proper Ayat. It does not require much intelligence to know that this story is false because the following Ayat say:

إِنۡ هِىَ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءٌ۬ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِہَا مِن سُلۡطَـٰنٍ‌ۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُ‌ۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّہِمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ (٢٣)

“Indeed, (what they worship) are nothing but mere names you and your forefathers have invented; Allah has sent down no authority attached to them. They are following nothing but mere guess and what they themselves desire, while guidance has truly come to them from their Lord.” (Al-Najim 53: 23)

This story was rejected by many scholars such as ibn Khuzimah (ابن خزيمة), ibn Al-Arabi (ابن العربي), Al-Qadi Eiad (القاضي عياض) and many others as false and illogical because nothing the Prophet (PBUH) can utter in the Quran but divinely protected. When it comes to revelation, the Prophet (PBUH) is infallible and cannot make any mistake whether it is an addition or deletion. Allah says in the same Surat (Surat Al-Najm):

وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ (٣) إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحۡىٌ۬ يُوحَىٰ (٤) عَلَّمَهُ ۥ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡقُوَى (٥)

“And he in no way speaks out of whim. (3) It is but a revelation revealed (to him). (4) It is taught to him by the one of potent powers.” (Al-Najm 53:3-5)

content:
The Theme of Surat Al-Shu’ara (The Poets) (26)

Surat Al-Shuara (الشعراء) was revealed in Mecca. The theme of the Surat is the effective methods for inviting people to Islam (Dawah). The Surat highlights the importance of the mass media and the importance of learning public speaking and the art of debate to properly convey the message of Islam to mankind.

The Surah starts with:

تِلۡكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ ٱلۡمُبِينِ (٢) لَعَلَّكَ بَـٰخِعٌ۬ نَّفۡسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ (٣)

These are the Ayat of the clear Book (2) It may be that you (O Muhammad) are going to kill yourself with grief, that they do not become believers. (26:2-3)

The Ayat clearly shows the degree of grave concern the Prophet (PBUH) had for those people who did not believe. This concern is motivated by his sincere care for them because he (PBUH) knows of the dire consequence of their disbelief. How about us? Do we care to follow in our Prophet’s footsteps and care for our friends, neighbors and colleagues who are disbelievers? Almost all of us will say we care, but we don’t know what to do. This Surat is helping us with what to do. It identifies the importance of using mass media and effective communications in delivering the message of Islam.

The form of mass media continuously changes with time and thus the most effective mass media should be identified and used. As examples, the most effective mass media during the time of Prophet Musa was magic demonstrations while it was poetry during the time of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH). In recent times, radio became the dominant mass media starting 1920 and television became the key one starting 1950 and now the most effective mass media now is the internet.

Since the most effective form of mass Media at the time of the Prophet (PBUH) was poetry, the prophet (PBUH) used encourage the poet Hasaan ibn Thabit to write poems to expose the wrongdoings of those who fought the Muslims to defend Islam and Muslims. The Prophet (PBUH) told encouraged Hasaan ibn Thabit:

قالت عائشة سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لحسان   : إن روح القدس لا يزال يؤيدك ما نافحت عن الله ورسوله ] ينافح معناها يدافع أو يرامي

“That the Holy Spirit (holy Angel Gabriel) will continue supporting you as long as you are defending Allah and his Messenger.”

While poetry was a great mass media to during the life of the Prophet (PBUH) and thus the name of the Surat, like any mass media it can be used to guide people to righteousness or to mislead them and corrupt their morals. The last Ayat of the Surat warned of using poetry to mislead and identified how to use it for guidance, and the same principle can be applied to any other form of mass media.

وَٱلشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ ٱلۡغَاوُ ۥنَ (٢٢٤) أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّهُمۡ فِى ڪُلِّ وَادٍ۬ يَهِيمُونَ (٢٢٥) وَأَنَّہُمۡ يَقُولُونَ مَا لَا يَفۡعَلُونَ (٢٢٦) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَذَكَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرً۬ا وَٱنتَصَرُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ‌ۗ وَسَيَعۡلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَىَّ مُنقَلَبٍ۬ يَنقَلِبُونَ (٢٢٧)

“As for the poets, they are followed by the erring people. (224) Did you not see that they wander in every valley (speak about every subject)? (225) And that they say what they do not do. (226) Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and remember Allah much, and defend themselves after they have been wronged. And the wrongdoers will soon know to which place they are going to return.” (26:224-227)

The Surat contains several stories to guide us in the proper way to create a dialogue with the disbelievers. Different public speaking success factors were raised in the different dialogues presented in the stories of the Prophets Musa, Ibrahim (Abraham), Noah, Hud, Saleh, Lot and Shu’aib. The different dialogues prepared the Prophet (PBUH) to begin his public preaching.

For example, prophet Musa identified the importance of diction (correct and clear pronunciation) as a key to successful public speech, learning public speech. He said:

وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلاَ يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَـٰرُونَ (13)

“And my chest becomes strained, and my tongue is not fluent. So, send for Harun (Aaron) (to come along with me)”. (26:13)

The dialogue between Prophet Musa and the Pharaoh of Egypt offers great example of effective dialogue by focusing on the main message and avoid being distracted by any personal attacks. Prophets Musa and Haroun went to speak to Fira’un (Pharaoh), as Allah instructed them to say:

فَأۡتِيَا فِرۡعَوۡنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٦) أَنۡ أَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ (١٧)

“And go. both of you, to Fir’aun, and say: ‘We are the Messengers of the Lord of all the worlds. (16) You must send the Children of Israel with us.” (26:16-17)

But Fira’un ignored what they are saying and wanted to discredit Prophet Musa by attacking him as ungrateful and criminal by saying:

قَالَ أَلَمۡ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدً۬ا وَلَبِثۡتَ فِينَا مِنۡ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ (١٨) وَفَعَلۡتَ فَعۡلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلۡتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ (١٩)

(Pharaoh) said (to Musa): Did we not raise you up among us as a child? And you lived with us for years of your life. (18) And then you did the blunder you did (i.e. the crime of killing a man), still you are ungrateful.” (26:18-19).

Obviously, these are damaging accusations. How did Prophet Musa respond? Prophet Musa closed the door of the criminal accusation by acknowledging what happened but provided the justification for it:

قَالَ فَعَلۡتُهَآ إِذً۬ا وَأَنَا۟ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ (٢٠) فَفَرَرۡتُ مِنكُمۡ لَمَّا خِفۡتُكُمۡ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُڪۡمً۬ا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (٢١)

I did that when I was mistaken. (20) Then, I fled from you when I feared you. But my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers. (26:20-21).

He also provided a rebuttal for the Pharaoh’s allegation of him not being grateful.

وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِى إِسْرٰءيلَ

“And for the favor with which you are obliging me, it is you have enslaved the Children of Israel” (26:22).

At this point the exchange of accusations ended and the Dawa dialogue started. The dialogue went as follows:

قَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٢٣) قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَآ‌ۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ (٢٤)

“(Pharaoh) said: “And what is the Lord of the worlds?’ (23) (Musa) said: “Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, if you should be convinced.” (26:23-24).

Losing this line of argument, Pharaoh used a different type of attack by engaging his people to support him:

قَالَ لِمَنۡ حَوۡلَهُ ۥۤ أَلَا تَسۡتَمِعُونَ (٢٥)

“Fir’aun said to those around: “Are you not hearing (what he says)?” (26:25)

Prophet Musa did not want to engage others in the dialogue responded by expanding on his response of who is Allah:

قَالَ رَبُّكُمۡ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآٮِٕكُمُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ (٢٦)

(Musa) said: “Your Lord and the Lord of your early forefathers!” (26:25-26).

Pharaoh went back to the personal attack:

قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرۡسِلَ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمَجۡنُونٌ۬ (٢٧)

He (Fir’aun) said: “Your Messenger who has been sent to you is indeed a mad man!” (26:27)

But Prophet Musa ignored the personal attack and went back to the main issue to expand on who is the Lord of the worlds:

قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَآ‌ۖ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ (٢٨)

(Musa) said: “Lord of the east and the west, and all that is between them, if you are able to understand!” (26:28)

At this point Pharaoh did not want the discussion to continue and thus threated prophet Musa with imprisonment:

قَالَ لَٮِٕنِ ٱتَّخَذۡتَ إِلَـٰهًا غَيۡرِى لَأَجۡعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجُونِينَ (٢٩)

[Pharaoh] said, “If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned.” (26:29)

One more time Prophet Musa intelligently turned the dialogue to where he could show his strength: the miracle that Allah gave him.

قَالَ أَوَلَوۡ جِئۡتُكَ بِشَىۡءٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٣٠)

“(Musa) said: “will you (do this, i.e., imprison me) even if I bring you something clear (and convincing)?” (26:30)

Fir’aun agreed and Musa demonstrated how he could transform his cane into a snake. This must have relieved Fir’aun because he was confident that his media personalities, the magicians, could discredit Musa. Fir’aun’s inner circle who were attending suggested that the best way to humiliate Musa is for the Magicians to defeat him in public gathering. The meeting was set, and the scene was as follows:

فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُواْ لِفِرۡعَوۡنَ أَٮِٕنَّ لَنَا لَأَجۡرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡغَـٰلِبِينَ (٤١) قَالَ نَعَمۡ وَإِنَّكُمۡ إِذً۬ا لَّمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ (٤٢) قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلۡقُواْ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلۡقُونَ (٤٣) فَأَلۡقَوۡاْ حِبَالَهُمۡ وَعِصِيَّہُمۡ وَقَالُواْ بِعِزَّةِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّا لَنَحۡنُ ٱلۡغَـٰلِبُونَ (٤٤) فَأَلۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلۡقَفُ مَا يَأۡفِكُونَ (٤٥)

When the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, “Will there be a sure reward for us if we are victorious?” (41) He said, “Yes, and indeed, you will be among the closer ones.” (42) Moses said to them, “Throw whatever you will throw.” (43) So, they threw their ropes and their sticks and said, “By the might of Pharaoh, we will be the triumphant.” (44) Then Moses threw his staff, and in no time, it swallowed what they falsified. (26:41-45)

Musa was clearly victorious, and the magicians prostrated and declared their belief in the God of Musa. Obviously, this had major impact of Egyptian who started to recognize the falsehood of Pharaoh’s religion. The impact of this outcome would be like if the Pope and his cardinals convert to Islam after an open debate with a Muslim scholar.

The Surat continues with the story of Prophet Ibrahim to present another style of presenting Allah’s message through a rational dialogue. Prophet Ibrahim questioned his people about the logic of their idol worship:

قَالَ هَلۡ يَسۡمَعُونَكُمۡ إِذۡ تَدۡعُونَ (٧٢) أَوۡ يَنفَعُونَكُمۡ أَوۡ يَضُرُّونَ (٧٣)

“He (Ibrahim) said: “Do they hear you, when you call (them)? (72) Or do they bring benefit to you or do they harm (you)?” (73)

All the response he got was:

قَالُواْ بَلۡ وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٲلِكَ يَفۡعَلُونَ (٧٤)

They said, “No, but we found our fathers doing this.” (26:74)

When he received no rational answer, he expressed his utter rejection of what they worship:

قَالَ أَفَرَءَيۡتُم مَّا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡبُدُونَ (٧٥) أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُڪُمُ ٱلۡأَقۡدَمُونَ (٧٦) فَإِنَّہُمۡ عَدُوٌّ۬ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٧٧)

“He said: “Have you ever considered what you have been worshipping. (75) You and your ancient fathers. (76) They are my enemies, except the Lord of all the Worlds.” (77)

The Surat ends with emphasis on Allah’s final revelation to mankind, the Quran:

وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٩٢) نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلۡأَمِينُ (١٩٣) عَلَىٰ قَلۡبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنذِرِينَ (١٩٤) بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (١٩٥)

This (Quran) is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, (192) Which the trusted Sprit (Gabriel) has brought down, (193) To your heart (O Mohammad) so that you may be one of the warners. (194) In a clear Arabic tongue. (195)

It is noted that Ayat 195 did not say that the Quran was revealed in Arabic language, but it said in the clear Arabic tongue (tongue is stronger than language).

The Arabic language is the only language that preserved almost all feature of the Proto-Semitic language.
The Arabic language has more roots than any other language, it has 16,000 roots while the Hebrew language has only 2,500 roots.
The Arabic language is very rich with synonymous, as an example the word lion has about 10 synonymous in English, while in Arabic it has more than 300 synonymous.
The Arabic language is rich in derivatives, as example the word good in English, has only one derivative which is goodness, while in Arabic you can get more than 10 derivatives from one word.
The Arabic language can express the thought with minimum words, as example in English you say: “I said to him” (4 words), in Arabic you say: “Qultulahu” (One word).
The Arabic language is known to be a language of the fifth level because even a single letter can have a meaning.

But the emphasis on the Ayat that the Quran is revealed in the clear Arabic tongue suggests that the Arabic tongue is the only mean to express the complex themes of the Quran in a clear and eloquent way.

Surat Ash-Shu’ara teaches us two main lessons:
When calling people to Allah, Muslims must use the most effective and eloquent ways in addressing people and create dialogue with them.
Muslim must take advantage of the most effective mass media to deliver the message of Islam.

Observation 1:
The combination of Allah’s names (Al-Aziz Al-Rahime) came in the Quran 13 times, 9 of which are in Surat Ash-Shu’ara.

إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

And indeed, your Lord in the Mighty, the Merciful. (26:9, 68,104, 122, 140, 159, 175, 191)

This may be to emphasize that while Allah is merciful and his mercy that encompasses everything, it does not mean that He is not Mighty. His mercy comes from a position of strength and not from a position of weakness.

Observation 2: Focusing on the letter (kaf) in the word (كَانَ), note the differences between these Ayat with each story:

إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (٨) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٩)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (٦٧) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٦٨)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (١٠٣) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (١٠٤)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا ڪَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (١٢١) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (١٢٢)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡmِنِينَ (١٣٩) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (١٤٠)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَڪۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (١٥٨) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (١٥٩)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (١٧٤) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (١٧٥)
إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (١٩٠) وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (١٩١)

“In this there is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. (121) And indeed, your Lord in the Mighty, the Merciful. (122)”

Observation 3: The People of Hud (The nation of Ad)

وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَخۡلُدُونَ (١٢٩)

And take for yourselves factories that you may live forever. (26:129)

What are these life extending factories? (Ref: Secrets of the Great Pyramid by Peter Tompkins Book) Some suggests that the pyramids were used as life extending machines. The Egyptian took the technology from the people of Aad after they were destroyed. This suggests that the pyramids were not tombs but machines. Allah knows best.

title: The Theme of Surah Al-Nur (The Light) (24)
excerpt:
The Theme of Surah Al-Nur (The Light) (24)

Surat ln-Nur (النور) was revealed in Madina.  The Surat focuses on the social manners (الآداب الاجتماعية) that regulate the personal life of people at home…
content:
The Theme of Surah Al-Nur (The Light) (24)

Surat ln-Nur (النور) was revealed in Madina.  The Surat focuses on the social manners (الآداب الاجتماعية) that regulate the personal life of people at home and relationships among people in Muslims’ societies to ensure harmony and high morality. The Surat sets rules emphasizing the prohibition of gossiping and spreading malicious rumors.

Surat An-Nur was revealed after the spread of a very damaging rumor against the honor of Sayeda Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (PBUH) and the daughter of the most honorable companion (Sayedna Abu Bakr). This rumor started by the hypocrites and spread even by the believers. The vindication of the honor of Sayeda Aisha is made by Allah and the prohibition of spreading malicious rumors are set:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةٌ۬ مِّنكُمۡ‌ۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرًّ۬ا لَّكُم‌ۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرٌ۬ لَّكُمۡ‌ۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِىٍٕ۬ مِّنۡہُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ‌ۚ وَٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُ ۥ مِنۡہُمۡ لَهُ ۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١١)

“Indeed, those who came with the wicked slander are a group among you. Do not think that this incident is bad for you; rather it is good for you. For every person among them shall be charged with the sin he had earned, and as for he who took the greater share in spreading it, for him there shall be a great punishment. (24:11)

Allah says that this slander against Sayeda Aisha is good (لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرًّ۬ا لَّكُم‌ۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرٌ۬ لَّكُم) “do not consider it bad for you, rather it is good for you”.  What is the good in it, may be the following:

1. All Islamic societies throughout the ages learnt from this incident.
2. If an innocent woman is falsely accused in her honor, the accusation of Sayeda Aisha serves to ease the pain when facing such an accusation.
3. The incident provides a real example to demonstrate the value of the social rules established in this Surat.
4. It sets the moral responsibility of all Muslims regarding their response to rumors, and this is to think highly of each other:

لَّوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتُ بِأَنفُسِہِمۡ خَيۡرً۬ا وَقَالُواْ هَـٰذَآ إِفۡكٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (١٢)

“Why, when you heard it, the believing men and believing women did not think good about their own selves and say, “This is an obvious lie?” (24: 12)

In this Ayat, Allah emphasizes that the believers should automatically think highly of each other, exactly as you think of yourselves. The Ayat highlights that an ill-talk about any believer should be considered an il- talk about oneself.

The following Ayat emphasizes the rule for addressing any slanderous accusation which is to demand four witnesses, otherwise the accuser is considered a liar in the sight of Allah:

لَّوۡلَا جَآءُو عَلَيۡهِ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُہَدَآءَ‌ۚ فَإِذۡ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِٱلشُّہَدَآءِ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡكَـٰذِبُونَ (١٣)

Why did they [who slandered] not produce four witnesses? Since they do not produce the witnesses, then they are liars in the sight of Allah. (24:13)

The requirement of four witnesses in this Ayat is a reemphasis of Allah’s divine rule regarding those who make an accusation against a woman’s honor (حد القذف that came early in the Surat. Allah says:

وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَـٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُہَدَآءَ فَٱجۡلِدُوهُمۡ ثَمَـٰنِينَ جَلۡدَةً۬ وَلَا تَقۡبَلُواْ لَهُمۡ شَہَـٰدَةً أَبَدً۬ا‌ۚ وَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَـٰسِقُونَ (٤) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ وَأَصۡلَحُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ۬ (٥)

And those who accuse chaste women (of immorality), and do not produce four witnesses, flog them with eighty stripes, and do not accept their testimony forever; they indeed are the transgressors. (4) Except those who afterward repent and make amends, (for such) Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (24:4-5)

The punishment of those who make the accusation and don’t have four witnesses is:
1. They will be flogged with 80 stripes in public.
2. They will never be allowed to provide any testimonies in the future.
3. They will be designated as sinful, and liars and it is allowed for anyone to insult them.

But Allah gave them a way out of the two continued punishments, and this is to make sincere repentance and show their remorse and mend the harm they have caused by admitting that they are liars to remove all the doubts about the woman they accused, and these two punishments will be removed from them after one year. But they must be punished by flogging and there is no expiation for this punishment, and it cannot be waived even if the woman forgave the person.

Note: The punishment rule applies even after the death of the accused woman. There is a story that seems fable but it is reported by شهاب الدين ابن حجر الهيتمي [Imam Shab Eldin Ibn Hajar al-Shafi in his book “the masterpiece of the needy”] (الشافعي في تحفة المحتاج) that during the time of Imam Malik (الإمام مالك) time, a woman mortician who washes the dead in preparation for burial said to herself while washing a dead woman, I wonder how many times this woman committed adultery and suddenly her hand got stuck to the body of the deceased woman and it cannot be separated by force. Several hours passed and people were perplexed regarding what to do to separate the woman mortician's hand from the deceased and they started considering to either cut the woman mortician hand or to cut the part of the deceased woman. They went and asked Imam Malik (الإمام مالك), he said don’t do any of that, go and flog the woman mortician 80 stripes. They did that and on the 80th stripe her hand was separated from the body of the dead woman.

Allah reprimanded the believers for slandering a woman without having sure knowledge by saying:

إِذۡ تَلَقَّوۡنَهُ ۥ بِأَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيۡسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ۬ وَتَحۡسَبُونَهُ ۥ هَيِّنً۬ا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١٥)

“When you were receiving it with your tongues, and uttering with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge, and you thought it a little thing, while it is enormous with Allah.” (24: 15).

Notice the words selected here: “receiving the rumor with your tongues”. Receiving rumors is never with the tongue but it is with the ears, but Allah says that they did not even process what they were hearing with their minds but it went from their ears to their tongues directly.

تَحۡسَبُونَهُ ۥ هَيِّنً۬ا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ
“You think it a little thing, while it is enormous with Allah.” (24: 15).

The next two Ayat establish the proper behavior that Allah expects from the believers:

وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ قُلۡتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَڪَلَّمَ بِہَـٰذَا سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ هَـٰذَا بُہۡتَـٰنٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١٦) يَعِظُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُواْ لِمِثۡلِهِۦۤ أَبَدًا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (١٧)

When you heard it, you should have said: “It is not befitting for us to speak of this. Glory be to You (O Allah)! This is a monstrous slander.” Allah forbids you from ever doing the like of it again, if you are believers. (24: 16-17)

The Surat starts with a unique introductory Ayat. It starts by Allah designating it as Surat and it is ordained (meaning its rules are obligatory) and its Ayat are clear and distinct:

سُورَةٌ أَنزَلۡنَـٰهَا وَفَرَضۡنَـٰهَا وَأَنزَلۡنَا فِيہَآ ءَايَـٰتِۭ بَيِّنَـٰتٍ۬ لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ (١)

(This is) a Surat that We have sent down and ordained (its legal laws) and in it We have sent down clear Ayat that you may remember. (24:1)

The 2nd Ayat directly lists the penal law for committing adultery.

ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِى فَٱجۡلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَٲحِدٍ۬ مِّنۡہُمَا مِاْئَةَ جَلۡدَةٍ۬‌ۖ وَلَا تَأۡخُذۡكُم بِہِمَا رَأۡفَةٌ۬ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأَخِرِ‌ۖ وَلۡيَشۡہَدۡ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٢)

The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each of them with one hundred stripes. Let not pity for them withhold you from obedience to Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment. (24:2)

However, it should be noted that such punishment can only be applied by the Islamic government; it cannot be applied by individuals.

There is major confusion regarding the punishment for this crime regarding whether the 100 stripes apply to all adulterers or only to those who are not married (the penalty for the married is stoning to death). This penalty of stoning is not in the Quran but it is in the Sunna. Some scholars argue that the stoning punishment was revealed before the revelation of Surat Al-Nour and it was superseded by the 100 stripes. Those who argue that it was superseded use the following Hadith:

عن الشيباني سألت عبد الله بن أبي أوفى هل رجم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال نعم قلت قبل سورة النور أم بعدها قال لا أدري

Al-Shaibani asked Abdullah bin Abi Awfa: Did the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) stone? He said: Yes. I said: Before Surat Al-Nour or after it? He said: I do not know. (Bukhari)

It must be noted that confirming the crime is adultery is extremely difficult because it requires 4 witnesses who saw the actual act. This is to ensure that the punishment is applied only in cases of public lewdness.

The requirement for having four witnesses will not be feasible in a case where one accuses his wife. In such a case, Allah sets the rule of Al-Lian (the mutual oaths):

وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ أَزۡوَٲجَهُمۡ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُمۡ شُہَدَآءُ إِلَّآ أَنفُسُهُمۡ فَشَهَـٰدَةُ أَحَدِهِمۡ أَرۡبَعُ شَهَـٰدَٲتِۭ بِٱللَّهِ‌ۙ إِنَّهُ ۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ (٦) وَٱلۡخَـٰمِسَةُ أَنَّ لَعۡنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡهِ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰذِبِينَ (٧) وَيَدۡرَؤُاْ عَنۡہَا ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَن تَشۡهَدَ أَرۡبَعَ شَهَـٰدَٲتِۭ بِٱللَّهِ‌ۙ إِنَّهُ ۥ لَمِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰذِبِينَ (٨) وَٱلۡخَـٰمِسَةَ أَنَّ غَضَبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡہَآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ (٩)

And for those who accuse their wives (of adultery) while they have no witnesses except their own selves, let the testimony of one of them be four testimonies (oaths) by Allah that he is of those who speak the truth. And the fifth (oath) should be that the Curse of Allah be upon him if he is of those who tell a lie. But it shall avert the punishment from her if she bears four testimonies (oaths) by Allah that he is indeed a liar. And the fifth (oath) should be that the Wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of those who speak the truth. (24:6-9)

The Surat sets the following rules to protect the society from immorality: (see appendix for references)
1. Proper Protocol for visiting Peoples’ homes.
2. Respecting the privacy of family members.
3. Decency in interaction between men and women.
4. Modesty of women dress.
5. Helping young people to get married.
6. Prohibition of prostitution.
7. Prohibiting the spread of vice.
8. Prohibition of spreading rumors and defamation.

The Suat is named Al-Nour (The Light) may be to emphasize that the rules stated brighten the social life of people and clear it from the darkness of rumors and immorality.

Allah is the Light of the heavens and the Earth, and His light is the one that brings clarity and purity to any society that seeks it. The light that Allah brings on societies that follow His revelations is like the light of a very bright lamp that is in a dark and small niche. Allah says:

ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشۡكَوٰةٍ۬ فِيہَا مِصۡبَاحٌ‌ۖ ٱلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِى زُجَاجَةٍ‌ۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّہَا كَوۡكَبٌ۬ دُرِّىٌّ۬ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ۬ مُّبَـٰرَكَةٍ۬ زَيۡتُونَةٍ۬ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةٍ۬ وَلَا غَرۡبِيَّةٍ۬ يَكَادُ زَيۡتُہَا يُضِىٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارٌ۬‌ۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ۬‌ۗ يَہۡدِى ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ‌ۚ وَيَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَـٰلَ لِلنَّاسِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ۬ (٣٥)

Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The parable of His Light is that of a niche in which there is a lamp, the lamp is in glass, the glass looks like a brilliant star, lit from a blessed tree, an olive, which is neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow forth (of itself), though no fire touched it. Light upon Light! Allah guides to His Light whom He wills. And Allah sets forth parables for mankind, and Allah is All-Knower of everything. (24:35)

Where does the light of Allah shine? It shines in and from the houses of Allah as He says:

فِى بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرۡفَعَ وَيُذۡڪَرَ فِيہَا ٱسۡمُهُ ۥ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ۥ فِيہَا بِٱلۡغُدُوِّ وَٱلۡأَصَالِ (٣٦)

“In houses (mosques) that Allah has permitted to be raised and in them His Name is remembered, and His purity is pronounced in the morning and in the evening” (24:36).

On whom does this light shine? On those whom Allah describes as:

رِجَالٌ۬ لَّا تُلۡهِيہِمۡ تِجَـٰرَةٌ۬ وَلَا بَيۡعٌ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَإِقَامِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءِ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ‌ۙ يَخَافُونَ يَوۡمً۬ا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ (٣٧)

“Men whom neither trade nor sale (business) diverts them from the remembrance of Allah nor from establishing prayers, nor from giving the Zakat. They are fearful of a day in which hearts and eyes will be overturned.” (24: 37).

But for those who reject Allah’s revelations, they will be deprived from Allah’s light, and they will remain in darkness as Allah says:

وَٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُوٓاْ أَعۡمَـٰلُهُمۡ كَسَرَابِۭ بِقِيعَةٍ۬ يَحۡسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمۡـَٔانُ مَآءً حَتَّىٰۤ إِذَا جَآءَهُ ۥ لَمۡ يَجِدۡهُ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا وَوَجَدَ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُ ۥ فَوَفَّىٰهُ حِسَابَهُ ۥ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ (٣٩) أَوۡ كَظُلُمَـٰتٍ۬ فِى بَحۡرٍ۬ لُّجِّىٍّ۬ يَغۡشَٮٰهُ مَوۡجٌ۬ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ مَوۡجٌ۬ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ سَحَابٌ۬‌ۚ ظُلُمَـٰتُۢ بَعۡضُہَا فَوۡقَ بَعۡضٍ إِذَآ أَخۡرَجَ يَدَهُ ۥ لَمۡ يَكَدۡ يَرَٮٰهَا‌ۗ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَجۡعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُ ۥ نُورً۬ا فَمَا لَهُ ۥ مِن نُّورٍ (٤٠)

“As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty person thinks it is water, until he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, but he finds Allah there, Who will render him his due (Hell). And Allah is Swift in taking account. (39) Or [the state of a disbeliever] is like the darkness in a vast deep sea, overwhelmed with waves topped by waves, topped by dark clouds, (layers of) darkness upon darkness: if a man stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it! And for the one to whom Allah does not provide light, there is no light. (24:39-40)

One notes in this Surat that after every part that speaks about Allah’s rule, there is another part that encourages repentance and affirms the mercy of Allah.

إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ وَأَصۡلَحُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ۬ (٥)
“Except those who repent thereafter and do righteous deeds, (for such) verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (24: 5).

وَلَوۡلَا فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَتُهُ ۥ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَڪِيمٌ (١٠)
“And had it not been for the Grace of Allah and His Mercy on you (He would have hastened the punishment on you). And that Allah is the One Who accepts repentance, All-Wise” (24: 10).

وَلَوۡلَا فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡڪُمۡ وَرَحۡمَتُهُ ۥ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَءُوفٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ۬ (٢٠)
“And had it not been for the Grace of Allah and His Mercy on you, (Allah would have hastened the punishment on you). And that Allah is full of Kindness, Most Merciful” (24: 20).

وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ (٣١)
“And all of you, the believers, repent to Allah that you may be successful” (24: 31).

The Surat ends with an affirmation that no one can hide from Allah:

أَلَآ إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۖ قَدۡ يَعۡلَمُ مَآ أَنتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَيَوۡمَ يُرۡجَعُونَ إِلَيۡهِ فَيُنَبِّئُہُم بِمَا عَمِلُواْ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ۬ (٦٤)

Certainly, to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. Surely, He knows every condition you are in; and (He knows) the Day when they will be returned to Him, then He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is All-Knower of everything. (24: 64)

Appendix 1: The background of the story about Sayeda Aisha

It was the custom of the Prophet (PBUH) to take one his wives with him on any military campaign.  During one of the campaigns, Sayeda Aisha (RA) accompanied the Prophet (PBUH). On their way back, they stopped at a place to spend the night. Before the army left the next morning, Sayeda Aisha (RA) went out of the camp for some purpose and lost her necklace made of Yemeni beads. While searching for it, she missed the departure of the army.

The Prophet (PBUH) called on the army to start moving. The men who lead her camel did not recognize that her Howdah (the carriage on the camel) was empty because she was young and light in weight. When she came back and found the army had already left, she sat down in the same place expecting that someone would come back for her.

But it was the practice of the Prophet (PBUH) to keep somebody in the rear of the army, to kook for anything left behind. Safwan bin al-Mu’attal al-Sulami happened to be that person. When he reached where she was, he recognized her as he had seen her before the commandment of Hijab was revealed. He brought his camel near her and she rode it while he walked leading the camel until they reached the army at the next stop.

Abdullah bin Ubai Ibn Salool started a rumor that spread by the rest of the hypocrites that Sayeda Aisha (RA) committed adultery with Safwan bin al-Mu’attal. This rumor spread in Madina for about a month. The Prophet (PBUH) was extremely distressed.

Muslims argued about that matter: some were puzzled; some did not believe it at all; and some did. After a month, Allah revealed the Ayat of Surat An-Nur (11-20) declaring her innocence.
