Proper Protocol of visiting Peoples’ homes

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ بُيُوتًا غَيۡرَ بُيُوتِڪُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تَسۡتَأۡنِسُواْ وَتُسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِہَا‌ۚ ذَٲلِكُمۡ خَيۡرٌ۬ لَّكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ (٢٧)

“O you who believe! Do not enter houses other than your own, until you have been given permission and greeted their people. That is better for you, in order that you may remember.” (24: 27)

Respect the privacy among family members.

يَـٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَـٰنُكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَبۡلُغُواْ ٱلۡحُلُمَ مِنكُمۡ ثَلَـٰثَ مَرَّٲتٍ۬‌ۚ مِّن قَبۡلِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡعِشَآءِ‌ۚ ثَلَـٰثُ عَوۡرَٲتٍ۬ لَّكُمۡ‌ۚ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ جُنَاحُۢ بَعۡدَهُنَّ‌ۚ طَوَّٲفُونَ عَلَيۡڪُم بَعۡضُكُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬‌ۚ ڪَذَٲلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَيَـٰتِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ۬ (٥٨)

“O you who believe! Let your slaves and slave-girls, and those among you who have not come to the age of puberty ask your permission (before they come to your presence) on three occasions: before morning prayer, and while you put off your clothes for the noonday (rest), and after the night prayer (Isha). (These) three times are of privacy for you, other than these times there is no sin on you or on them to move about, attending (as they may) to each other. Thus Allah makes clear the Ayat to you. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.” (24: 58)

وَإِذَا بَلَغَ ٱلۡأَطۡفَـٰلُ مِنكُمُ ٱلۡحُلُمَ فَلۡيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُواْ ڪَمَا ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِہِمۡ‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ۬ (٥٩)

“And when the children among you come to puberty, then let them (also) ask for permission, as those before them used to ask. Thus Allah makes clear His Ayat to you. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.” (24: 59)

Decency of visual interaction between men and women:

قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَـٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ (٣٠) وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَـٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ

“Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and protect their private parts. That is purer for them. Verily, Allah is All-Aware of what they do. And tell the believing women to lower their gaze, and protect their private parts.” (24: 30-31)

The modesty of women dress:

وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَـٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا‌ۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ‌ۖ

“And tell the believing women to lower their gaze, and protect their private parts (and not to show off their adornment except only that which is apparent and to draw their veils all over Juyubihinna (i.e. their bodies, faces, necks and bosoms, etc.).” (24: 31)

Helping young people get married:

وَأَنكِحُواْ ٱلۡأَيَـٰمَىٰ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ مِنۡ عِبَادِكُمۡ وَإِمَآٮِٕڪُمۡ‌ۚ إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغۡنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٲسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ۬ (٣٢)

“And marry those among you who are single and (also marry) the fit of your (male) slaves and maid servants. If they be poor, Allah will enrich them out of His Bounty. And Allah is All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Knowing.” (24: 32)

Prohibition of prostitution:

Allah warned those who force female members of a family to commit adultery as a means to gain financial resources.

وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَہُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ‌ۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَـٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرً۬ا‌ۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَاتَٮٰكُمۡ‌ۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَـٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنً۬ا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا‌ۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِكۡرَٲهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ۬ (٣٣)

“And do not force your maids to prostitution, if they desire chastity, in order that you may make a gain in the goods of this worldly life. But if anyone compels them, then after such compulsion, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (to those women, i.e. He will forgive them because they have been forced to do this evil action unwillingly).” (24: 33)

Prohibiting the spread of vices:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَن تَشِيعَ ٱلۡفَـٰحِشَةُ فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ۬ فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأَخِرَةِ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ (١٩)

“Verily, those who like that illegal sexual intercourse should be propagated among those who believe, they will have a painful torment in this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah knows and you know not.” (24: 19)

Prohibition of spreading slanders

This is a command to all those who spread the news of scandals and distort the reputation of others.

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَـٰتِ ٱلۡغَـٰفِلَـٰتِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ لُعِنُواْ فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأَخِرَةِ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (٢٣)

“Verily, those who accuse chaste women, who never even think of anything touching their chastity and are good believers, are cursed in this life and in the Hereafter, and for them will be a great torment.” (24: 23)

title: Allah’s name Al-Lateef (اللطيف)
excerpt: The name Al-Lateef is derived from the root “la-ṭa-fa” (لَطَفَ) with the “fatha” on the letter “ta” that means being gentle, kind, and merciful. It is also derived from the root “la-tu-fa” (لَطُفَ)…
content:
The name Al-Lateef is derived from the root “la-ṭa-fa” (لَطَفَ) with the “fatha” on the letter “ta” that means being gentle, kind, and merciful. It is also derived from the root “la-tu-fa” (لَطُفَ) with “damah” on the letter ‘tu” that means being subtle, not overbearing and undetectable.  Therefore, Allah’s name Al-Lateef is an attribute that combines kindness and compassion with detailed knowledge of every hidden and minute detail.

From this glorious name of Allah, one may learn the following:

- Allah, Al-Lateef, knows the minute details of everything including what a person thinks. Therefore, His kindness and compassion will be fit for every specific condition.
- Allah, Al-Lateef, knows our ultra-fine and unapparent interests and therefore delivers what benefits us in a gentle way.
- The attribute of Al-Lateef is only realized when the ultimate knowledge and the ultimate gentleness come together. Therefore, it is inconceivable for such perfection to exist except with Allah.

This combination of the above attributes in the name, Al-Lateef, makes it difficult to translate into English.  Therefore, depending on the context, Al-Lateef is translated as “The Subtle” or “The Knower of Subtleties” when the focus is on Him knowing all minute details and as “The Gracious” or “The Kind” when the focus is on His kindness.  In this presentation, the Arabic name Al-Lateef will be used.

Allah’s name Al-Lateef came in the Quran seven times.  It is paired five times with Allah’s name Al-Khabeer (The All-Aware), one time with Allah’s name Al-Hakeem (The All-Wise) and one time by itself.

ذَٲلِڪُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡ‌ۖ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۖ خَـٰلِقُ ڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ فَٱعۡبُدُوهُ‌ۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَڪِيلٌ۬ (١٠٢) لَّا تُدۡرِڪُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرَ‌ۖ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ) الأنعام (

This is Allah, there is no God but He, the Creator of all things. So, worship Him.  He takes care of all things. (102) No sight can encompass Him, but He encompasses all sights. He is Al-Lateef, Well-Acquainted with all things. (Al-Anaam 6:102-103)

وَأَسِرُّواْ قَوۡلَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱجۡهَرُواْ بِهِۦۤ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ (١٣) أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ (الملك(

“Whether you keep your talk secret or make it loud. Verily He knows well what lies in the heart. (13) Shall not He Who has created know? And He is Al-Lateef, the All-Aware. (Al-Mulk, 67:13-14)

وَاذْكُرْنَ مَا يُتْلَى فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ لَطِيفًا خَبِيرًا   ) الأحزاب(

“And recite what is rehearsed to you in your homes, of the Signs of Allah and His wisdom: for Allah is Lateef, All-Aware. (” (Al-Ahzab 33:34)

يَا بُنَيَّ إِنَّهَا إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُنْ فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ ) لقمان(

“O my dear son, if there be anything to the measure of a mustard-seed, and it be hidden in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Surely, Allah Lateef, All-Aware.” (Luqman 31:16)

Note: While Luqman is emphasizing to his son that Allah is aware of everything no matter how small it is and how far it had been concealed meaning he cannot hide anything from Allah, He used Allah’s name Al-Lateef that assures the son that Allah’s knowledge of all details is for his own benefits, and it is not something that makes him concerned or afraid.

أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ فَتُصۡبِحُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مُخۡضَرَّةً‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ۬ (الحج(

“Did you not see that Allah has sent down rain from the sky, whereby the earth becomes green? Surely, Allah is Lateef, All-Aware. (” (Al-Hajj 22: 63)

The often pairing of Allah’s attributes Al-Lateef with Al-Khabeer should teach us that being gentle, kind, merciful, subtle, and not overbearing does not conflict with us trying our best to being knowledgeable and fully acquainted (Khabeer) with all that exists.

وَقَالَ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ هَـٰذَا تَأۡوِيلُ رُءۡيَـٰىَ مِن قَبۡلُ قَدۡ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّ۬ا‌ۖ وَقَدۡ أَحۡسَنَ بِىٓ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجۡنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡبَدۡوِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ بَيۡنِى وَبَيۡنَ إِخۡوَتِىٓ‌ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌ۬ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ (يوسف(

“He (Yusuf) said: “O my dear father, this is the fulfilment of my early vision.  Allah has made it come true. He favored me when He released me from prison and brought you out of the desert after Satan had sown enmity between me and my brothers. Surely, my Lord is Lateef to whatever He wills, He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.” (Yousuf 12:100)

Note: Allah’s attribute of Lateef in the case of Prophet Yusuf made Prophet Yusuf’s prominence of authority in the grab of slavery.  This example should make us aware that whatever Allah decrees from difficulties upon us is intended to lead to something of great benefits and thus we should realize that whatever we hate may actually has hidden in it great benefits as Allah says(وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئاً وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ).

The account of Prophet Yousuf should make us realize that every achievement we enjoy is managed by Al-Lateef. There were thousands of invisible strands that converged to produce the conclusion of the story of Prophet Yousuf.  Allah, Al-Lateef only discloses a few of these strands to us to allow us to feel accomplished of our own success. If we are truly righteous, Allah, Al-Lateef, may disclose more details to make us realize that nothing short of a miracle has just fallen into our laps. This should move our hearts and find ourselves whispering with humility and awe saying:

ٱللَّهُ لَطِيفُۢ بِعِبَادِهِۦ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ‌ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَوِىُّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ( الشورى(

“Allah is Lateef (kind) to His slaves. He extends provisions to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Mighty.” (Al-Shura 42:19)

Nothing can be as empowering as knowing that our guardian is Al-Lateef, who knows our fear, and knows how to render it harmless. It suffices to rely on Him to prevent these fears from reaching us.

The attributes of Allah’s name Al-Lateef are continuously manifested in our lives in many subtle ways.  For example, Allah has protected us from seeing and hearing many of the things around us.  Can you imagine how miserable we would be if we could hear and see all the sound and visual waves around us (i.e., the complete electromagnetic and audio spectrum)?

It is Allah, Al-Lateef, who did not give us the ability to see any of the spiritual creations that are surrounding us whether they are angels or Jinn. If He did not, we would have been overwhelmed by their presence.  Allah, Al-Lateef, limited our ability to only hear and see the range that is beneficial to us.    (Note: According to several hadith, we have ten angels always accompanying every person and this is addition to the Jinn. If we would have been able to see then, we would have been suffocated by their presence.)

Our certainty of the knowledge and gentleness of Allah, Al-Lateef, that permeates every minute element in the universe all the time, should make us feel secure.  Allah informs us that He knows everything that happens on earth, no matter how minor it is.  Allah says:

وَعِندَهُ ۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ‌ۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبٍ۬ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٥٩)

“And with Him are the keys of the Unseen. No One knows them but He.  He knows what is in the land and the sea. No leaf ever falls but that He knows about it, and there is no grain in the darkness of the earth, or anything fresh or dry that is not in a clear record.” (Al-Anaam 6:59)

لَا يَعۡزُبُ عَنۡهُ مِثۡقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ۬ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَآ أَصۡغَرُ مِن ذَٲلِكَ وَلَآ أَڪۡبَرُ

“Not an atom or less or greater than that whether in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him.” (Saba 34:3)

Now we know that the universe is interconnected and what happens in one place influences the rest of the world. These effects have been evaluated by meteorologists who called the concept the “Butterfly effect”. This concept suggests that if a butterfly flaps its wings in China, it affects a hurricane forming in Houston. This effect is framed mathematically in terms of nonperiodic flow that is part of the chaos theory.

The manifestation of Allah’s name Al-Lateef is that He made it attainable for people to receive infinite rewards and achieve eternal happiness in return for small efforts during a short period of time, i.e., one’s lifespan on this earth.

Elements of Allah’s Name to Adopt in our Character.

1/ Realizing the extent that Allah’ attribute Al-Lateef and how no one has ever been kind, compassion, gentle and subtle in His actions towards us but Him, should make our love of Him sincere, deep, and natural. Such love can only be expressed by following His commands that He revealed through His messenger Mohammed (PBUH) as He said:

قُلۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى يُحۡبِبۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡ‌ۗ

“Say, (O Mohammad): If you love Allah, follow me; and Allah will love you and forgive you your sins.” (Al-Emran 3:31)

2/ We should periodically reflect on this blessed name, identifying its manifestations in our life and invoke it when seeking Allah’s support for our future needs.

3/ As Allah is Lateef with us, we should be a source of gentleness for others.  We should always be kind and discreet when helping others. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أَن النبيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفقَ. )رواه مسلم(

“Allah is Gentle and loves [seeing] gentleness.” (Muslim)

4/ We should strive to always understand the details of every task that we will be involved in to ensure that is done properly and with ease. These details go beyond the technical ones but include legal, ethical, and human factors.  It is the lack of our understanding of the details that results in hurting us and others.

title: The Theme of Surat Maryam (مريم) (Mary) (19)
excerpt: Surat Maryam (مريم) was revealed in Mecca. The theme of the Surat is that the most important strategy to preserve any religion is through having offspring. The Surat links children to the inheritance…
content:
Surat Maryam (مريم) was revealed in Mecca. The theme of the Surat is that the most important strategy to preserve any religion is through having offspring. The Surat links children to the inheritance of religion.

It is a natural inclination for people to want to have children to maintain their lineage and enjoy their presence. Allah made loving one’s children an instinct (فطرة) that Allah instilled in people. After having children, the main preoccupation of the parents becomes to secure a comfortable life for them and ensure their proper education and even to have enough savings for them to inherit. But parents should balance this preoccupation with the concern of having their children successful in this life and the Hereafter.

The Surat presents two types of parent-children religious connection.

The first type is a child born to a righteous parent who wanted the child to protect and propagate the religion of Allah. If the child fulfills this desire, the child will be the joy of his parents and will always receive their support. But if the child fails to carry the banner of their parents’ religion and deviates from the path of Allah, he will be a cause of major distress to the parents. Therefore, a major lesson is that parents must fulfill their duty by giving major care to the children’s religious education and practices as they take care of their academic education.

The second type is a child born to a disbelieving parent who also wants the child to propagate their own false religion. But in this case, the child may be the one who serves as a catalyst to correct the parent’s religion. However, in this case the child is expected to face major problems from his own parents, particularly if the parents’ financial interest is tied to the false religion.

The Surat gave examples of the two situations:

The case of righteous parents who sought righteous children as the case for Prophet Zakariya (Zachariah) and his son Yahya (John) (زكريا ويحيى), Maryam (Mary) and her son Isa (Jesus) (مريم ابنة عمران وابنها عيسى), Ibrahim (Abraham) and his sons Isma’il (Ishmael) and Ishaq (Isaac), and his grandson Yaqub (Jacob) (إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب).

The other case is the case of disbelieving parent whose child was righteous as the case for Prophet Ibrahim (righteous child) and his father who was an idol worshipper.

The Surat starts with an example of the first case, the account of Prophet Zakariya (Zachariah) and his son Yahya (John) (زكريا ويحيى). In this account, we learn that Prophet Zakariya’s (زكريا) wished for a child to inherit the religion:

ذِكۡرُ رَحۡمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبۡدَهُ ۥ زَڪَرِيَّآ (٢) إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ ۥ نِدَآءً خَفِيًّ۬ا (٣) قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَهَنَ ٱلۡعَظۡمُ مِنِّى وَٱشۡتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأۡسُ شَيۡبً۬ا وَلَمۡ أَڪُنۢ بِدُعَآٮِٕكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّ۬ا (٤) وَإِنِّى خِفۡتُ ٱلۡمَوَٲلِىَ مِن وَرَآءِى وَڪَانَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتِى عَاقِرً۬ا فَهَبۡ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّ۬ا (٥) يَرِثُنِى وَيَرِثُ مِنۡ ءَالِ يَعۡقُوبَ‌ۖ وَٱجۡعَلۡهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّ۬ا (٦) يَـٰزَڪَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَـٰمٍ ٱسۡمُهُ ۥ يَحۡيَىٰ لَمۡ نَجۡعَل لَّهُ ۥ مِن قَبۡلُ سَمِيًّ۬ا (٧)

“(This is) a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His slave Zakariya. (2) When he called out to his Lord a call in secret. (3) He said: “My Lord! My bones have grown feeble, and gray hair has spread on my head, and I have never been unblessed in my invocation to You, O my Lord! (4) “And verily I fear my relatives after me, since my wife is barren. So, give me from Yourself an heir. (5) “Who shall inherit me, and inherit (also) the posterity of Yaqub (Jacob). And make him, my Lord, acceptable (to You). (6) (it was said to him) O Zakariya! Verily, We give you the glad tidings of a son, whose name will be Yahya (John). We have given that name to none before (him).” (19:2-7)

The Surat describes the character of this son (Yahya) and the divine commands to him:

يَـٰيَحۡيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبَ بِقُوَّةٍ۬‌ۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَـٰهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمَ صَبِيًّ۬ا (١٢) وَحَنَانً۬ا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَوٰةً۬‌ۖ وَكَانَ تَقِيًّ۬ا (١٣) وَبَرَّۢا بِوَٲلِدَيۡهِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّ۬ا (١٤) وَسَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيۡهِ يَوۡمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوۡمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوۡمَ يُبۡعَثُ حَيًّ۬ا (١٥)

“O Yahya! Hold fast the Scripture (Torah)]” And We gave him wisdom while he was still a child. (12) And (made him) sympathetic to people as a mercy (or a grant) from Us, and pure from sins (Zakat); and he was devout, (13) And he was dutiful toward his parents. And he was not oppressive, disobedient. (14) And peace be on him the day he was born, and the day he dies and the day he shall be raised alive.” (19:12-15).

The Surat continues with the mention of the miraculous pregnancy of Maryam, who was pledged by her mother to the service of Allah. Then it addresses the birth of Isa and his role as a messenger of Allah and corrects the false belief about him.

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ مَرۡيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتۡ مِنۡ أَهۡلِهَا مَكَانً۬ا شَرۡقِيًّ۬ا (١٦) فَٱتَّخَذَتۡ مِن دُونِهِمۡ حِجَابً۬ا فَأَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرً۬ا سَوِيًّ۬ا (١٧) قَالَتۡ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّ۬ا (١٨) قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۟ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَـٰمً۬ا زَڪِيًّ۬ا (١٩) قَالَتۡ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَـٰمٌ۬ وَلَمۡ يَمۡسَسۡنِى بَشَرٌ۬ وَلَمۡ أَكُ بَغِيًّ۬ا (٢٠) قَالَ كَذَٲلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ۬‌ۖ وَلِنَجۡعَلَهُ ۥۤ ءَايَةً۬ لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحۡمَةً۬ مِّنَّا‌ۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرً۬ا مَّقۡضِيًّ۬ا (٢١) ۞ فَحَمَلَتۡهُ فَٱنتَبَذَتۡ بِهِۦ مَكَانً۬ا قَصِيًّ۬ا (٢٢) فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلۡمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذۡعِ ٱلنَّخۡلَةِ قَالَتۡ يَـٰلَيۡتَنِى مِتُّ قَبۡلَ هَـٰذَا وَڪُنتُ nَسۡيً۬ا مَّنسِيًّ۬ا (٢٣) فَنَادَٮٰهَا مِن تَحۡتِہَآ أَلَّا تَحۡزَنِى قَدۡ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحۡتَكِ سَرِيًّ۬ا (٢٤) وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيۡكِ بِجِذۡعِ ٱلنَّخۡلَةِ تُسَـٰقِطۡ عَلَيۡكِ رُطَبً۬ا جَنِيًّ۬ا (٢٥) فَكُلِى وَٱشۡرَبِى وَقَرِّى عَيۡنً۬ا‌ۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡبَشَرِ أَحَدً۬ا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرۡتُ لِلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ صَوۡمً۬ا فَلَنۡ أُڪَلِّمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ إِنسِيًّ۬ا (٢٦)

“And mention in the Book (the story of) Maryam (Mary), when she withdrew in seclusion from her family to a place facing east. (16) She placed a barrier to hide from them. Then We sent to her Our Spirit [angel Jibril], and he appeared before her in the form of a man in all respects. (17) She said: “Verily! I seek refuge with Al-Rahman from you, if you are God-Conscious.” (18) (The angel) said: “I am only a Messenger from your Lord, (to announce) to you the gift of a righteous son.” (19) She said: “How can I have a son, when no man has touched me, nor am I unchaste?” (20) He said: “So (it will be), your Lord said: ‘That is easy for Me (Allah): And (We will) appoint him as a sign to mankind and a mercy from Us (Allah), and it is a matter (already) decreed).” (21) So, she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place. (22) And the labor pains brought her to the trunk of a date-palm. She said: “O I wish I would have died before this, and had been forgotten and out of sight.” (23) Then he (the baby Isa) called her from beneath her, saying: “Do not grieve; Your Lord has provided a water stream under you; (24) “Shake the trunk of date-palm towards you, it will drop fresh ripe-dates upon you.” (25) “So, eat and drink and be glad, and if you see any human being, say: ‘I have vowed for Al-Rahman and therefore I shall not speak to any human being this day.’” (19:16-26)

The Surat provided the description of the role of Isa in his own words that he uttered when he was a baby to clear his mother from any accusation.

فَأَشَارَتۡ إِلَيۡهِ‌ۖ قَالُواْ كَيۡفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلۡمَهۡدِ صَبِيًّ۬ا (٢٩) قَالَ إِنِّى عَبۡدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَٮٰنِىَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّ۬ا (٣٠) وَجَعَلَنِى مُبَارَكًا أَيۡنَ مَا ڪُنتُ وَأَوۡصَـٰنِى بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّڪَوٰةِ مَا دُمۡتُ حَيًّ۬ا (٣١) وَبَرَّۢا بِوَٲلِدَتِى وَلَمۡ يَجۡعَلۡنِى جَبَّارً۬ا شَقِيًّ۬ا (٣٢) وَٱلسَّلَـٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوۡمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوۡمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوۡمَ أُبۡعَثُ حَيًّ۬ا (٣٣)

“Then she pointed to him. They said: “How can we speak to someone who is a child in the cradle?” (29) He (Isa) said: “Verily! I am a slave of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a Prophet.” (30) “And He has made me blessed wheresoever I be, and has enjoined on me Salat and Zakat, as long as I am alive.” (31) “And (He made me) dutiful to my mother and did not make me oppressive, unblessed.” (32) “And Salam (peace) be on me the day I was born, and the day I shall die, and the day I shall be raised alive again. (19:29-33)

In both two cases, the Surat did not only focus on the role of the children in delivering Allah’s message, but also how they were dutiful to their parents. This attribute was emphasized for Prophet Yahya in (وَبَرّا بِوٰلِدَيْهِ), “And dutiful towards his parents” (19:14), and for prophet Isa in (وَبَرّاً بِوَالِدَتِى) “And dutiful to my mother” (19:32).

The Surat discussed the second case represented by the example of a child, Ibrahim, who was born to a disbelieving father who worshipped idols. The Surat mentions the challenges Ibrahim faced in his attempts to bring his parents to the path of Allah.

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقً۬ا نَّبِيًّا (٤١) إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعۡبُدُ مَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ وَلَا يُبۡصِرُ وَلَا يُغۡنِى عَنكَ شَيۡـًٔا (٤٢) يَـٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى قَدۡ جَآءَنِى مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مَا لَمۡ يَأۡتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعۡنِىٓ أَهۡدِكَ صِرَٲطً۬ا سَوِيًّ۬ا (٤٣) يَـٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعۡبُدِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنَ‌ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ عَصِيًّ۬ا (٤٤) يَـٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ فَتكُونَ لِلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ وَلِيًّ۬ا (٤٥)

“And mention in the Book (the Quran) Ibrahim (Abraham). Indeed, he was a man of truth, a Prophet. (41) When he said to his father, why do you worship something that can neither hear nor see and cannot help you in anything? (42) “O my dear father! Verily! There has come to me a knowledge that has not come to you. So, follow me. I will guide you to a Straight Path. (43) “O my dear father! Do not worship Satan. Satan is surely disobedient to Al-Rahman (44) “O my dear father, I fear lest a punishment of Al-Rahman should strike you, and you become a companion of Satan (in the Hellfire).” (19: 41-45)

Unfortunately, the advice of the righteous son Ibrahim went unheeded. But in spite of the major threat that Ibrahim received from his father, he continued to be polite in his attempt to guide his father.

قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنۡ ءَالِهَتِى يَـٰٓإِبۡرَٲهِيمُ‌ۖ لَٮِٕن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ لَأَرۡجُمَنَّكَ‌ۖ وَٱهۡجُرۡنِى مَلِيًّ۬ا (٤٦) قَالَ سَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيۡكَ‌ۖ سَأَسۡتَغۡفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّىٓ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ بِى حَفِيًّ۬ا (٤٧) وَأَعۡتَزِلُكُمۡ وَمَا تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَدۡعُواْ رَبِّى عَسَىٰٓ أَلَّآ أَكُونَ بِدُعَآءِ رَبِّى شَقِيًّ۬ا (٤٨)

(The father) said: “Do you reject my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not stop, I will definitely stone you. Now get away from me for a long time (before I kill you).” (46) (Ibrahim) said: “Peace be on you! I will seek Forgiveness for you from my Lord. He has always been Most Gracious to me. (47) “And I shall keep away from you and from those whom you invoke besides Allah. And I shall call upon my Lord; and I hope that I shall not be unblessed in my invocation to my Lord.” (19:46-48)

The youth should learn how to advise the elders in their family from the example of Prophet Ibrahim. He showed a high degree of concern and compassion and addressed his father with softness.

The Surat continued with the case of Prophet Ibrahim after he left his father and how Allah granted him offspring of his own to inherit the religion.

فَلَمَّا ٱعۡتَزَلَهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَهَبۡنَا لَهُ ۥۤ إِسۡحَـٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ‌ۖ وَكُلاًّ۬ جَعَلۡنَا نَبِيًّ۬ا (٤٩) وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِنَا وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُمۡ لِسَانَ صِدۡقٍ عَلِيًّ۬ا (٥٠)

“So, when he went away from them and from those whom they worshipped besides Allah, We blessed him with Ishaq (Isaac) and Yaqub (Jacob). And We made each one of them a Prophet. (49) And We bestowed on them Our Mercy and We made them highly honored.” (19:49-50)

The Surat discussed Prophet Ismael and his effort in emphasizing prayers and charity to his family.

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ إِسۡمَـٰعِيلَ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ صَادِقَ ٱلۡوَعۡدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولاً۬ نَّبِيًّا (٥٤) وَكَانَ يَأۡمُرُ أَهۡلَهُ ۥ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ مَرۡضِيًّ۬ا (٥٥)

And mention in the Book (the Quran) Ismail (Ishmael). He was indeed true to his promise, and he was a Messenger and a Prophet. (54) He used to enjoin Salat and Zakat upon his family and his Lord was pleased with him. (19:54-55)

After mentioning all these examples, the Ayats make a contrasting example between the attributes of the righteous progeny and the attributes of those who are deviant. Regarding the righteous, Allah says:

أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡہِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ ءَادَمَ وَمِمَّنۡ حَمَلۡنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ۬ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّةِ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَإِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ وَمِمَّنۡ هَدَيۡنَا وَٱجۡتَبَيۡنَآ‌ۚ إِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ خَرُّواْ سُجَّدً۬ا وَبُكِيًّ۬ا (٥٨)

“Those are the people whom Allah has blessed with bounties, the Prophets from the offspring of Adam and of those whom We carried (in the ship) with Nuh (Noah), and of the offspring of Ibrahim and Israel, and from among those whom We guided and chose. When the Ayats (verses) of Al-Rahman were recited to them, they fell down prostrate and weeping.” (19:58)

Regarding the deviant progenies of righteous parents, Allah highlights the two main causes that led to their deviation:

فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفٌ أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّہَوَٲتِ‌ۖ فَسَوۡفَ يَلۡقَوۡنَ غَيًّا (٥٩)

“Then, they were succeeded by a later generation who have neglected prayers and followed lusts. So they will meet with Ghayya (destruction/punishment in Hell Fire).” (19:59)

This is a warning to parents to consider this risk of their children deviating from the religion and that they should do their part in focusing on ensuring that their children pray and train them to control their desires. The responsibility of the parents is to ensure that their children follow the message of Allah and be among those whom Allah has blessed with His bounties” (ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡہِم) and not be among those who have given up on prayers and followed their lust (أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّہَوَٲتِ‌).

As we come to the end of the Surat, the Ayat moved to alleviate any confusion regarding the love of children and having a son. The Surat rejected in very strong terms those who claim that Allah has a son:

وَقَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ وَلَدً۬ا (٨٨) لَّقَدۡ جِئۡتُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِدًّ۬ا (٨٩) تَڪَادُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ يَتَفَطَّرۡنَ مِنۡهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلۡجِبَالُ هَدًّا (٩٠) أَن دَعَوۡاْ لِلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ وَلَدً۬ا (٩١) وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لِلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا (٩٢) إِن ڪُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ عَبۡدً۬ا (٩٣)

And they say: “Al-Rahman has begotten a son”. (89) Indeed, you have come up with such a terrible evil thing. (90) Whereby the heavens might almost be torn, and the earth will burst apart, and the mountains will fall crumbling. (90) For they attribute a son to Al-Rahman. (91) While it is not befitting for Al-Rahman to have a son. (92) There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to Al-Rahman as a slave. (19:88-93)

While the rejection of any claim that Allah has a son came in a very strong tone, when Allah was talking about people’s need to have offspring, the tone was tender with terms such as mercy and its derivates.

Why was the Surat named Maryam?

While the Surat refers to several males who delivered the lantern of religion to their children (Ibrahim, Zakariya, and Ismail), the Surat was named after a female, Maryam. The reason may be that Allah wants to honor the status of women and emphasize the important role of the female in preserving the message of Allah. Also, Allah mentioned the personal name of Maryam to emphasize that the name of a woman is not disgraceful to be mentioned in public as may be considered in many societies.

Additional Comment:

We note that the number of Surat Maryam is 19. We also note that the first mentioned of Maryam in the Surat is in verse 16 and last time the name is mentioned in the Surat is in verse 34. These are 19 verses. Is this coincidental that Allah summarizes the story of Maryam in 19 verses of Surat number 19? Could this be the reason that Allah placed emphasis on number 19 in Surat Al-Muddathir (74) in which Allah mentions the number of angles around the hell fire and says:

وَمَآ أَدۡرَٮٰكَ مَا سَقَرُ (٢٧) لَا تُبۡقِى وَلَا تَذَرُ (٢٨) لَوَّاحَةٌ۬ لِّلۡبَشَرِ (٢٩) عَلَيۡہَا تِسۡعَةَ عَشَرَ (٣٠) وَمَا جَعَلۡنَآ أَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَـٰٓأٮِٕكَةً۬‌ۙ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا عِدَّتَہُمۡ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةً۬ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيَسۡتَيۡقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ‌ۙ …. (٣١)

“And what will make you know what exactly Hell Fire is? (27) It neither spares (any disbeliever) nor does it leave (anything unburnt). (28) Burning the skins. (29) Appointed on it are nineteen (wardens). (30) And We did not make wardens of the Fire but (from) angels and did not make their number (number 19) but as a test (trial) for those who disbelieve, in order that the people of the book (Jews and Christians) may arrive to certainty (the Quran is the truth) and those who believe may increase in belief, and that no doubts may be left for the people of the Book and the believers. (Al-Muddathir 74:27-31)

Note that Allah mentioned 4 functions for this number:
1. Test to those who disbelieve.
2. Give certainty to the people of the book regarding the divine nature of the Quran.
3. Increase the belief of the Muslims.
4. Remove any doubt that may still left in the heart of the people of the book and the Muslims.

content:
## Allah’s name Al-Haleem (الحليم) (The Forbearing)

The name Haleem is derived from the root h-l-m (حِلم) (with kasra under the letter (حِ) (h) that has the following classical Arabic connotations: forbearance, leniency, clemency, gentleness, deliberate, moderation.

With these meanings of the term “Hilm”, we can appreciate that “Hilm” is a very noble attribute, so much so that it has been said:

* “Hilm is the master of all good characters.” (الحلم سيد الأخلاق)
* “The one who is haleem can almost be a prophet.” (كاد الحليم أن يكون نبياً)

“Haleem” is commonly translated as “Forbearing”. In other words, it is the attribute that gets one to delay the punishment to give the wrongdoer a chance for correcting the wrong. The attribute of Hilm is not forgiveness or overlooking the transgression. It may lead to eventually imposing the punishment but not hastily.

To further clarify the attribute of being “Haleem”, let us look at what Haleen is not:

1/ The “Haleem” does not intentionally delay imposing the punishment on the person who commits wrong to encourage him to continue in his transgressions to impose on him severer punishment.

2/ The “Haleem” does not delay imposing the punishment because he has no power to punish the wrongdoer and hopes that he may get the power in the future to impose the punishment.

Allah’s name Haleem (Forbearing) came in the Quran 11. In all cases it is paired with other names to provide better understanding of the name. It is mentioned 6 times with the Forgiver (غفور), 3 times with the All-Knowing (عليم), one time with the Self-Sufficient (غني) and one time with the Appreciative (شَكُورٌ). Examples of the Ayat that includes Allah’s attribute of Hilm (forbearance) include:

(لَّا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) البقرة
“Allah does not call you to account for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.” (Al-Baqara 2:225)

(وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُ ۚ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) البقرة
“And know that Allah knows what is in your hearts, so beware of Him, and know that Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.” (Al-Baqara 2:235)

(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا مِنكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُوا ۖ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) آل عمران
“Surely, those of you who turned back on the day when the two armies met, it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of that they have earned. Now Allah has forgiven them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.” (Al-Imran 3:155)

(تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّمَاوَاتُ السَّبْعُ وَالْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ ۚ وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ ۗ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا) الإسراء
“The seven heavens and the earth and all those who are in them declare His glory, and there is not a single thing but glorifies and praises Him, but you do not understand their glorifying; surely He is Forbearing, Forgiving” (Al-Isra 17:44)

(لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُم مُّدْخَلًا يَرْضَوْنَهُ ۗ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ) الحج
“Verily He will admit them (the martyrs among the immigrants) to a place with which they shall be well pleased: for Allah is All-Knowing, Forbearing. (Al-Hajj 22:59)

(وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَلِيمًا) الأحزاب
“And Allah knows (all) that is in your hearts: and Allah is All-Knowing Forbearing.” (Al-Ahzab 33:51)

(قَوْلٌ مَّعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِّن صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُهَا أَذًى ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمٌ) البقرة
“A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by causing harm. And Allah is Rich (Free of all needs) and Forbearing” [Al-Baqarah 2:263]

(إِن تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا يُضَاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) التغابن
‘If you advance a good loan to Allah, He will multiply it for you and will forgive you, for Allah is Appreciative, Forbearing.” (Al-Taghabun 64:17)

Allah, Al-Haleem, has full awareness of all people, those who reject Him and those who obey Him. He has the full capability to impose immediate punishment on those who reject Him, but He delays their punishment to give them chances to repent in order to forgive them. In the meantime, Allah, Al-Haleem, continues to support all people, even those who reject Him. Thus, the delayed punishment of Allah, Al-Haleem, will only be imposed on those who really deserve it.

Why Allah’s attribute of “Hilm” Forbearance is very important for us. All of us are daily recipients of His Hilm because all of us make mistakes and sometime suffer from heedlessness. Allah, Al-Haleem allows us the opportunity to rectify our wrong deeds and regain our closeness to Him.

Allah’s forbearance is manifested in Him ignoring the wishes of the foolish among the transgressors who ask for the quick punishment of Allah. Allah does not respond to their stupidity and still gives them a chance to change and repent and throughout history many have done that.

(وَإِذْ قَالُواْ اللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَـذَا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ أَوِ ائْتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ) الأنفال
“And they said: O Allah! If this is indeed the truth from you, then rain down stones on us or bring upon us a painful punishment.” (Al-Anfal 8:32)

(وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا مِن دَابَّةٍ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى) النحل
“If Allah were to punish the people on account of their wrongdoing, He would not have left on earth a single creature. But He gives them respite for a stated Term.” (Al-Nahl 16:61)

However, Allah’s forbearance does not mean delayed punishment for everyone, because there are situations when the punishment cannot be delayed for those who will be uncontrolled if they left without punishment.

In the Quran Allah described Prophet Ibrahim with the attribute of being Haleem and his son Ismael too.

(إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُّنِيبٌ) هود
“Most surely Abraham was forbearing, tender-hearted, oft returning (to Allah)” (Hud 11:75).

(فَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِغُلَامٍ حَلِيمٍ) الصافات
“So, We gave him (Ibrahim) the glad tidings of a boy [Ishmael] forbearing.” (Al-Saffat 3:101)

The Prophet (PBUH) used to invoke Allah’s name Al-Haleen in his supplication when he is in a state of distress. He used to say:

عن ابن عباس: أنَّ نبيَّ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقولُ عند الكربِ :لا إله إلا الله العظيمُ الحليمُ، لا إله إلا الله ربُّ العرشِ العظيمِ، لا إله إلا الله ربُّ السماواتِ وربُّ الأرضِ وربُّ العرشِ الكريمِ
There is no god but Allah, the Majestic, the Forbearing. There is no god by Allah, the Lord of the grand throne. There is no god by Allah, the Lord of the Heavens, the Lord of the earth and the Lord of the honorable throne. (Bukhari)

Like knowledge, forbearance is something that can be developed in one’s character. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي الدرداء قال،قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما العلم بالتعلم وإنما الحلم بالتحلم. (رواه الطبراني وغيره)
“Verily, knowledge only comes by learning and forbearance only comes by cultivating forbearance.”

Forbearance is a character that Allah loves and thus we need to develop it in our character The Prophet (PBUH) said to one of his companions “Al-Ashajj Abdul-Qays” (الأشج عبد القيس):

عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأشجِّ عبدالقيس: “إن فيك خَصلتينِ يُحبُّهما الله: الحِلمُ، والأناةُ”؛ رواه مسلم.
“You have two qualities that are beloved to Allah. They are forbearance and deliberate judgment.”

Forbearance (Hilm) is one of those attributes with which we should beautify our characters. It involves patience, self-control, and self-confidence. We should always ensure that our reaction to any wrong is always reasonable and measured and that we should challenge our ego and lean more towards mercy by giving the wrongdoers a chance to change.

Forbearance allows us also to show mercy towards the ignorant who just don’t know. It has been said: the most compelling reason for forbearance is mercy towards the ignorant. Forbearance reflects self-honor by having the ability of not giving any weight to those who wrong you when you can punish them.

The life of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is exemplary in demonstrating the character Him (Forbearance) for us. One of the examples is that account of his return from Al-Taif to which he travelled to inform them about Islam and seek the support of the leadership of the tribe of Thaqif. He made this trip on the 10th year of his mission when the people of Mecca made it impossible for him to deliver the message of Allah. But he (PBUH) was ridiculed by the chiefs of Thaqif. And, as he was leaving the city, the chiefs sent a mob of their slaves and youth to pursue him insulting and throwing stones at him and his companion Zayd ibn Haritha. Blood flowed down both the prophet’s legs; and Zaid, endeavoring to shield him, was wounded in the head. The mob did not desist until they had chased him over two miles outside the city.

Heart-broken and grieved, the prophet (PBUH) set out on the way of Mecca. He was heedless of anything around him until he suddenly looked up and saw a cloud casting its shade on him and saw Gabriel in it. He stopped and Gabriel addressed him saying: Allah has heard the response of your people and He sent with me the angel of mountains so you can order him with whatever you wish.

The angel of the mountains greeted the Prophet (PBUH) and said:

يَا مُحَمَّدُ، إِنَّ اللهَ قَدْ سَمِعَ قَوْلَ قَوْمِكَ لَكَ، وَأَنَا مَلَكُ الْجِبَالِ وَقَدْ بَعَثَنِي رَبُّكَ إِلَيْكَ لِتَأْمُرَنِي بِأَمْرِكَ، فَمَا شِئْتَ، إِنْ شِئْتَ أَنْ أُطْبِقَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَخْشَبَيْنِ
O Mohammad, Allah has heard the response of your people and sent me to do whatever you want. If you wish I can bury them under the two mountains Akhshabain (الأخشبين) [Abu Qubais (أبو قبيس) and Qu'ayqa'an (قُعَيْقِعَان) mountains].

Do those people deserve swift punishment for the harm they did to the Prophet (PBUH). The answer is yes. But here the Prophet’s character of Him (forbearance) is clearly demonstrated. Instead of looking at the moment, the Prophet (PBUH) looked at the future and responded to the angel of the mountains saying:

( فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : بَلْ أَرْجُو أَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ مِنْ أَصْلَابِهِمْ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ لَا يُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا .)
“No, I hope that Allah will bring from their loins those who will worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him.

Here the Prophet (PBUH) did not want an immediate punishment but wanted it delayed in the hope that they would have children who become good believers and they also may change and become believers. In a fact this is what happened and later the people of Al-Taif became Muslims and committed ones and played major roles in Muslims’ battles against the Persian and Roman empires. Because the high literacy among the tribe of Thaqif, many of them served in important administrative positions in the Muslims states.

Elements of Allah’s name Al-Haleem to Adopt in our Character.

1. We should learn not to react out of anger nor to be hasty in punishing. This is so important when it comes to family members.
2. We should always give a grace period to the wrongdoer to know his wrong and correct it.
3. Be forbearing because no one likes a harsh, unforgiving person who is quick to judge and punish.
4. Give people the chance to realize their mistakes and take steps to mend their actions before holding them accountable.
5. When you see someone making a mistake, do not shame him/her. Treat people gently when they do something wrong. They will appreciate your forbearance.
6. Understanding how forbearance makes us feel and its effect on others should encourage us to extend it to all.

excerpt:
