content:
The Theme of Surat Hud (هود)

Surah Hud was revealed in Makkah during a hard time for the Prophet (PBUH). It was the time during which the Prophet was rejected by all the surrounding tribes and was harshly treated by the people of the Taif when he (PBUH) went to invite them to Islam. During that time, he also lost his two main supporters: his wife (Khadija) and his uncle (Abu Taleb).

The theme of the Surat is outlining the proper approach that Muslims should take in response to oppression and injustice. The proper response under these conditions is presented in two pivotal Ayat:

فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ وَمَنْ تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا ۚ إِنَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (١١٢)
"So, stand firm as you have been commanded, as well as those who turn in repentance with you, and do not transgress. Surely, He (Allah) is All-Seer of what you do." (11:112)

وَلَا تَرْكَنُوا إِلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا فَتَمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنْصَرُونَ (١١٣)
"And do not incline to those who have done injustice, lest the Fire should touch you; you have no protecting friends other than Allah, and afterward ye would not be helped (if you incline to the unjust)" (11:113)

In these two Ayat, Allah points out the three keys to navigating times of oppression and injustice:

1. Endurance (الاستقامة): “stand firm,” (فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ) means to continue and persist with patience. And never lose hope in face of difficulties.
2. Avoid transgression (عدم الطغيان): “do not transgress” (وَلَا تَطْغَوْا) this is the Quranic expression of rashness and resorting to violence.
3. Avoid inclination (عدم الركون): “Do not incline/submit” (وَلَا تَرْكَنُوا) to the ones who commit injustice. In the Quran, this expression refers to the inclination to the enemies and this leads to embracing them as guardians instead of Allah.

In commenting on these Ayat, Imam Hassan Al-Basri (حسن البصري) said:
“Glory to Allah who made moderation between two negations: do not transgress and do not incline.”
(سبحان الذي جعل اعتدال هذا الدين بين لاءين وهي لاَ تَطْغَوْاْ ولاَ تَرْكَنُواْ)

To emphasize the theme, the Surah lists the story of several prophets who faced oppression and injustice. The Surat begins with reminding Muslims of the nature of the Quran and its purpose:

الر ۚ كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ (١)
“Alif, Lam, Ra. A book whose Ayat (verses) are perfected and then explained in detail from the One who is All-Wise and All-Aware.” (11:1)

The second Ayat presents the balanced approach of delivering Allah’s message between warning and glad tidings:

أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّنِي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ (٢)
"You should worship none but Allah. (Say) “Verily I am (sent) to you from Him to be Warner and deliverer of glad tidings.”" (11:2)

Then the Surat moves to highlight the time taken for the creation of heavens and earth. Allah says:

وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ (١١:٧)
“And He (is The One) Who created the heavens and the earth in six days” (11:7).

Although Allah does not need any time to create the universe, He probably mentioned the duration of creation to emphasize that success does not come overnight, it takes time. This is a very important lesson for those who face oppression.

The Surat also highlights human nature during hard times:

وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً ثُمَّ نَزَعْنَاهَا مِنْهُ إِنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ كَفُورٌ (٩)
"And if We give man a taste of Our mercy and then take it from him, he becomes highly desperate and ungrateful." (11:9)

While one notes that in most of the Ayat in the Quran combines righteous deeds with belief (ءامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّالِحَاتِ), here in Surat Hud (Ayat 11), Allah says:

إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ (١١)
"Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward." (11:11)

Combining patience with righteous deeds is another tool for those who face injustice.

The subsequent Ayat identifies the key danger of impatience. The Ayat identified this risk by directing the speech to the Prophet (PBUH) saying:

فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ أَنْ يَقُولُوا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ ۚ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ نَذِيرٌ ۚ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ (١٢)
“So perchance you (O Prophet) may give up part of what is being revealed to you, and that your chest may feel straitened by it, because they say: ‘Why is not a treasure sent down for him, or an angel come with him?’ But you are only a Warner, and Allah is Guardian over all things.” (11:12)

Obviously, the Prophet (PBUH) neither wanted to leave anything from what was revealed to him, nor his chest was strained by delivering the message. But through this Ayat, Allah wants the believers to focus on delivering the true message of Islam and to never conceal any information in their attempt to make Islam appealing to others.

The Surat continued by discussing the stories of seven prophets (Nuh, Hud, Saleh, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu’ayb, and Musa - نوح وهود وصالح و ابراهيم و لوط وشعيب وموسى عليهم السلام). All the stories are intended to serve not only as reinforcement for the believers to remain steadfast and to never capitulate to the transgressors but also as warning to those who continue with their transgression. Allah says:

وَكُلًّا نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الرُّسُلِ مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ ۚ وَجَاءَكَ فِي هَٰذِهِ الْحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٢٠) وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ اعْمَلُوا عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنَّا عَامِلُونَ (١٢١) وَانْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنتَظِرُونَ (١٢٢)
"We narrate to you all such stories of the messengers to strengthen your heart. And in these (stories) come to you the truth, as well as a good counsel and a reminder to those who believe. (120) Say to those who do not believe: “Do whatever you can: we are doing (what we can). (121) “And wait. We too are waiting.”" (11:120-122)

The first story was about Prophet Nuh. The story demonstrates endurance, firmness, and stability. It is worth mentioning that Surat Hud contains the longest account of Prophet Nuh in the Quran. Nuh invited his people to Allah for 950 years without much success. Not only that, but they also gave him all kinds of ridicule and abuse. Thus, he is a good model and example of endurance. Allah says:

وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (٢٥) أَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ ۖ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ (٢٦)
“We sent Nuh (Noah) to his people (saying), “I am here to warn you that you. (25) That you should worship none but Allah, (otherwise) I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.”” (11:25-26).

We can clearly see the firmness and patience of Prophet Nuh (AS) by the degree of stubbornness of his people in their rejection of him to the point that they challenged him to bring on them the punishment of Allah:

قَالُوا يَا نُوحُ قَدْ جَادَلْتَنَا فَأَكْثَرْتَ جِدَالَنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٣٢)
They said: “O Nuh (Noah)! You have argued with us and prolonged this dispute; so, bring on us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful.” (11:32)

Even after they asked for the divine punishment, Nuh (AS) did not give up and continued preaching them:

قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ إِنْ شَاءَ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ (٣٣)
He said: “Only Allah will bring it to you, if He so wills, and you will not be able to escape it! (11:33)

Prophet Nuh did not stop his attempt to call his people to Allah until it was revealed to him to stop:

وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (٣٦)
“And it was revealed to Nuh: “None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. So, do not be distressed by what they have been doing.” (11:36)

Question: Based on interpreting the Quran, how long do you think Prophet Nuh took to build the arc? Hint: based on the following verse:
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا (٢٩:١٤)
“We sent Nuh to his people. He stayed among them one thousand (Sana’t) years, less fifty (A’am) years.” (29:14)

Although the story of Prophet Nuh (AS) in the Surat is longer than that of Prophet Hud (AS), the Surat was named after Prophet Hud (AS). This might be because Prophet Hud (AS) faced the strongest nation on earth:
(الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ) “The like of which was never created in the lands” (89:8).
and thus standing against their rejection and transgression demand super patience and great dedication.

The people of prophet Hud (the nation of A’d) did not only reject the divine message but they also threatened him. But his firmness was clear from his response to them:

قَالَ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ (٥٤) مِنْ دُونِهِ ۖ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ لَا تُنْظِرُونِ (٥٥)
“He said: “I make Allah my witness and you bear witness that I have nothing to do with what you take as gods besides Him. So, plot against me, all of you, and give me no respite. (11:54-55)

He continued to assure them that he will never compromise with them regarding the divine message and at the end he gave them the final warning that Allah will wipe them out and replace them with others:

فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ مَا أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْكُمْ ۚ وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ رَبِّي قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ وَلَا تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئًا ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ (٥٧)
“So, if you turn away, I have already conveyed to you the Message with which I was sent to you. My Lord will replace you with some other people, and you can not do Him any harm. Surely, my Lord is Guardian over all things.” (11:57).

The Surat continued with the stories of five other prophets, Saleh, Ibrahim, Lot, Shuaib and Musa, to demonstrate the fate of those who stand against Allah’s message and the fate of those who remain steadfast on the right path and deliver Allah’s message. Allah emphasizes that His destruction of these nations was only a result of them wronging themselves and that nothing of what they worshipped came to their help. Allah says regarding these nations:

ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّهُ عَلَيْكَ ۖ مِنْهَا قَائِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ (١٠٠) وَمَا ظَلَمْنَاهُمْ وَلَٰكِنْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ۖ فَمَا أَغْنَتْ عَنْهُمْ آلِهَتُهُمُ الَّتِي يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ لَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ ۖ وَمَا زَادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ (١٠١) وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَا أَخَذَ الْقُرَىٰ وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ ۚ إِنَّ أَخْذَهُ أَلِيمٌ شَدِيدٌ (١٠٢)
"That is a part of the stories of the (destroyed) towns that We narrate to you. Some of them are (still) standing, and some have been wiped out. (100) We did not wrong them, rather they wronged themselves. So, their gods whom they used to invoke beside Allah did not help them in anyway, when came the command of your Lord, and they added nothing to them except destruction. (101) Such is the Seizing of your Lord when He seizes the (people of) towns when they are transgressing. Indeed, His Seizing is painful, severe. (11:100-102)

After all these stories, Allah provided His key commands to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and in turn to all those who engage in correcting the transgression and the injustices in their societies. Allah says:

فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ وَمَنْ تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا ۚ إِنَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (١١٢)
"So, stand firm as you have been commanded, as well as those who turn in repentance with you, and do not transgress. Surely, He (Allah) is All-Seer of what you do. (11:112)"

وَلَا تَرْكَنُوا إِلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا فَتَمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنْصَرُونَ (١١٣)
"And do not incline towards those who have done injustice, lest the Fire should touch you; and you have no supporters other than Allah, then you would not be helped (if you incline to the unjust) (11:113)"

Following these commands, the Surat gives the tools and practices to achieve the core message of the Surat:

وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ۚ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ذِكْرَىٰ لِلذَّاكِرِينَ (١١٤)
Establish the prayer at both ends of the daytime and in the early hours of the night. Surely, good deeds wipe out evil deeds. This is a reminder for those who remember. (11:114)

At the end of the Surat, Allah makes it clear that there will always be differences among people regarding the divine path:

وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ النَّاسَ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً ۖ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ (١١٨) إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ ۚ وَلِذَٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ ۗ وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ (١١٩)
“And if your Lord had so willed, He could surely have made mankind one Ummah [community], but they will not cease to differ. (11:118) Except those whom your Lord has blessed with Mercy and for that He has created them. And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled (His Saying): 'I shall surely fill Hell with jinns and men all together.' (11:119)”

Please note that Allah is not saying that He forced people to differ. He is saying that as a result of granting human beings the free will, they will differ.

While some nations were punished by destruction in this life, the real punishment is in the hereafter:

إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً لِمَنْ خَافَ عَذَابَ الْآخِرَةِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ وَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ (١٠٣)
Indeed, in all these accounts there is a sure lesson for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which all mankind will be gathered together, and that is a Day to be witnessed by all. (11:103)

At this specific time those who follow the divine path will be rewarded with Paradise and those who reject it will be punished with Hell:

يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ (١٠٥) فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفِي النَّارِ لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ (١٠٦) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ (١٠٧) وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا فَفِي الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ ۖ عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ (١٠٨)
“When the Day (of Judgement) comes, no one shall speak except by His (Allah’s) permission. Some among them will be wretched [the dwellers of Hell] and some will be blessed [the dwellers of Paradise]. (105) As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, crying and howling. (106) They will remain there forever, as long as the heavens and the earth remain intact, unless your Lord wills (otherwise). Surely, your Lord does whatsoever He intends. (107) And those who are blessed, they shall be in Paradise, living there forever as long as the heavens and the earth remain intact, unless your Lord wills (otherwise). It will be an award never to be ceased”. (11:105-108)

A question is often raised regarding the phrase (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ) “They will remain there forever, as long as the heavens and the earth remain intact, unless your Lord wills (otherwise)” and whether this ending negates the eternity in hell and heaven. This phrase should not imply the ending of life in paradise because Allah ended it with (عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ) “It will be an award never to be ceased”. But regarding Hell, the phrase ended with (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ) “Surely, your Lord does whatsoever He intends.”

Therefore, some interpreters suggested that Hell is not eternal based on opinions attributed to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud.

Ibn Abbas (اِبْن عَبَّاس) said:
} خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتْ السَّمَاوَات وَالْأَرْض} لَا يَمُوتُونَ, وَلَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يُخْرَجُونَ, إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّك { . قَالَ : إِسْتِثْنَاءُ الله . قَالَ : يَأْمُرُ النَّارَ أَنْ تَأْكُلَهُمْ .
Regarding {خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتْ السَّمَاوَات وَالْأَرْض} “{They will remain in it for ever as long as the heavens and the earth are intact” it means that they will not die and will not come out of it as long as the heavens and the Earth. And the exception “unless your Lord wills otherwise” {إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّك} suggests that Allah made the exception and will order the fire to eat them.

Ibn Masoud (اِبْن مَسْعُود) said:
لَيَأْتِيَنَّ عَلَى جَهَنَّمَ زَمَانٌ تَخْفِقُ أَبْوَابُهَا لَيْسَ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ ، وَذَلِكَ بَعْدَ مَا يَلْبَثُونَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا
“The time will come when the Hell destroys its doors and there will be no one in it and this is after they stayed in it for long time” and quoted Allah’s saying:

إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا (٢١) لِلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا (٢٢) لَابِثِينَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا (٢٣)
“Surely, Hell is a place of ambush (21) A dwelling place for the rebellious people, (22) They will stay in it for ages.” (Al-Nab’a 78:21-23)

title: Reflection on Surat Al-Fatiha
excerpt:

content:
Reflection on Surat Al-Fatiha

The Fatihah is the most important Surat in all of Allah’s revelations including the Quran.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ مِثْلَ أُمِّ الْقُرْآنِ، وَهِيَ السَّبْعُ الْمَثَانِي، وَهِيَ مَقْسُومَةٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي، وَلِعَبْدِي مَا سَأَلَ».. رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ وَصَحَّحَهُ وَالنَّسَائِيُّ
“Allah had never sent in the Torah, the Injil, anything like the mother of the book and it is the seven repeated verses”. And Allah said: It is divided between Me and my slave and to my slave what he asks.”

Surat Al-Fatiha has many names such as: The mother of the Quran, the mother of the Book, the seven repeated verses, and the Glorious Quran.  This short surah, that contains seven verses, gives a very concise summary of the message of Allah and therefore it is essential for every Muslim to know it in the Arabic Language.  It is one of the very earliest revelations and it was the first Surat that was revealed in its entirety at the same time.  This Surah should be read by every Muslim at least 17 times a day as part of the five obligatory prayers.

You must have heard my talks and read many articles about Surat Al-Fatiha and its meaning, therefore I am only going to focus on this talk on two issues:

The first issue is related to some practical lessons we learn from Surat Al-Fatiha that we apply and should teach our children to apply. There are many but I’ll identify three:

We note that the Surat can be divided into three parts.  The first part is praise and glorification of Allah.  The second is declaring our servitude and reliance on Allah.  And the third is Dua, supplication to Allah for guidance.  The practical lesson that we learn is that we follow the same in any of our Dua, start with glorifying Allah, follow by expressing your submission to Him and then make whatever Dua you want.

Part of the Dua that we make in the third part of the Surat is that we do not be of those who earn Allah’s anger (ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ) nor of those who go astray (ٱلضَّآلِّينَ). Those who earn Allah’s anger are those who have been given knowledge but don’t act according to this knowledge.  The practical lesson here is that we should take advantage of the knowledge that we learn to do the right thing. This can impact all our actions, if we learn that certain things are good, we should apply it and if they are bad, we should avoid it.  Knowledge has no value unless one acts upon it.

On the other hand, those who go astray are those who act without having knowledge and thus can cause harm to themselves and to others.  The practical lesson is that we should never engage in any action unless we first gain knowledge about it.  True knowledge, not superficial knowledge, is an essential element to the success of any activity.  The Caliph Omar Ibn Abdel Aziz said:
«قال عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله : « مَنْ تَعَبَّدَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ كَانَ مَا يُفْسِدُ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا يُصْلِحُ
“Whoever worships Allah without knowledge, will cause more harm than good.”

The second issue of my talk is related to the attribute of Allah “مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ” or sometime read “مَلِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ” which is generally translated as “The Master of the Day of Judgment”. If we examine the word “الدِّينِ” (Al-Deen) which is translated as “Judgment”, it is the same word that also means religion “الدِّينِ” (Al-Deen); it is also the same word for the term “debt” (دين) (Dayn).

These three meanings “Judgment”, “Religion” and “Debt” are interrelated.  The “Deen” meaning religion is the system that teaches us what we need to do as payment for the debt that we owe Allah, and we will be held accountable for on (يَوْمِ الدِّينِ) “the Day of Judgement”.

We are indebted to Allah for everything that we have, the air, the earth, the sun, the water, the plants, the animals, the sight, the hearing, the motion, etc.  This debt requires payment and the time to settle this debt is in the Day of Judgment which is called (Yawm Al-Deen يَوْمِ الدِّينِ).  The question is what is the nature of payment for this debt?

The payment for the debt that we owe Allah involves two parts:  The first part of the payment is the expression of thanks and gratitude to Allah (الشكر) and the second part of the payment is full obedience to Allah (الطاعة).

The first part of the debt payment is offering sincere thanks to Allah (الشكر).  The amazing thing is that thanking Allah results in benefiting ourselves.  This is what Luqman, the wise, emphasized to his son as Allah informs us:
وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا لُقْمَانَ الْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ وَمَنْ يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ
And indeed, We granted wisdom on Luqman saying, give thanks to Allah. and anyone who thanks Allah does it to benefit himself. (Luqman 31:12)

Why thanking Allah is rewarding ourselves, for two reasons:

1. First: expressing gratitude is directly linked to joy. The famous speaker, Dr. Berne Brown, Univ of Houston, College of social work, found a direct link between joy and gratitude. Her 12 yrs research showed that there is no joy without gratitude.
2. Second, when we offer thanks to Allah, Allah will increase His favors and blessings upon us, as He said:
وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ
“Your Lord has decreed, if you thank me, I will increase my blessings upon you.” (Ibrahim 14:7)

So, the more we thank Allah for his favors, the more favors He gives to us and interesting that this will increase our debt to Him.  But the problem is that most people are not grateful and do not give thanks to Allah, as Allah says in many surahs.  In Surah Al-Baqara, Younes and Ghafer:
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ )البقرة(
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ )يونس(
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ )غافر(
“Indeed, Allah is full of bounties to the people, but most people do not give thanks. (Al Baqara 2: 243, Younes 10:60, Ghafer 40:61)

Many people think that expressing thanks to Allah means that you merely utter the words of thanks by the tongue by saying Alhamdulillah (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ).  But giving thanks to Allah is more than just saying these two words, it involves work.  Expressing thanks to Allah involves transforming these words into action as Allah says:
اعْمَلُوا آلَ دَاوُدَ شُكْرًا وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ
“Sons of David, work for expressing thanks! But few of My servants are grateful!” (Sabaa 34:13)

In this verse Allah commands the family of David to work for expressing thanks because thanking Allah is an active process that involves at least six elements:

1. Attributing the blessings to the provider of the blessings, Allah. (As example, never think that what you have achieved is because of your intelligent.  With a single blood clot in the brain, the person can become completely invalid.)
2. Applying the blessings in the obedience of Allah and using them in accordance with His commandments. (As example, don’t use the blessing of intelligence to cheat people or use the blessing of money to spend on something prohibited)
3. Ensuring that one does not squander the blessings by wasting them. (Examples are wasting food by either overeating or throwing away food and wasting one’s health either by using improper substances or living sedentary life.)
4. Ensuring that one does not get busy with the blessings at the expense of the provider of the blessings, Allah. (As example, don’t use the blessing of having a successful business to distract you from coming on time for the Friday prayer.)
5. Ensuring that one does not take advantage of the blessings to act superior and arrogant toward other servants of Allah. (As example, don’t have any form of arrogance creeping in your heart and feel that you are better than anyone.)
6. Thanking and praising Allah for His blessings. (This is by often saying الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ).

The second part of the debt payment is the full obedience of Allah (الطاعة).  Allah is not interested in half-hearted commitment, and partial obedience.  Allah desires your full devotion and full commitment. The Quran gives us many examples of the nature of full obedience, the type that Allah expects from His slaves.

The most compelling examples of full obedience are those of Prophet Ibrahim.  His obedience was clearly demonstrated when Allah ordered him to leave his infant and only son (Ismaeal) with his mother (Hajar) alone in the arid desert in Mecca.

Then, later when the son grew to be an impressive young boy, Allah commanded Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice him. Also, the reaction to his son, Ishmael, when he was informed by his father of Allah’s command to sacrifice him; the scene is presented to us by Allah in the following verse:
فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ قَالَ يَا بُنَيَّ إِنِّي أَرَى فِي الْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانْظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَى قَالَ يَا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ
“Then, when (the son) reached an age at which he can work with him, he said: “O my son! I have seen in my dream that I am slaughtering you: so consider what is your view!” (the son) said: “O my father! do as you are commanded: you will find me, if Allah so wills, among those who are patient!”. (Al-Safat 37:102)

Full obedience means that you should do everything exactly as Allah has commanded, and at the exact time He specified without delays or procrastination.  All parents know that delayed obedience is really disobedience.

Full obedience means that you obey without objections or reservations and without asking for clarification.  Allah does not owe us any explanations. While understanding can wait, obedience cannot.

In fact, obedience to Allah’s commands must be done with full contentment and ease of the heart.  Allah Says:
وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلَا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا مُبِينًا
“It is not befitting for a Believer, man or woman, when a matter has been decided by Allah and His Messenger, to have a choice in their matter: and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger is indeed on a clearly wrong Path.” (Al-Ahzab 33:36)

Partial obedience by cherry picking the commands to obey and ignoring others is not full obedience and Allah gives very serious warning to those who engage in this behavior as He says:
أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَى أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
“Do you believe in part of the scripture and disbelieve in others?  The reward for those who do so is shame in this life and the most grievous doom on the hereafter. For Allah is aware of what you do” (Al-Baqara 2:85).

Full obedience to Allah means that you should fulfill all His commands whole heartedly, joyfully and with enthusiasm.  It is important that we do obey both the letter and the spirit of Allah’s commands.  Let me remind you of the example in the Quran of what happened to those who obeyed the letter of the command but not the spirit:

There was a village belonging to Bani Israel that is located on the seashore and its inhabitants were fishermen.  Allah commanded Bani Israel to take the Sabbath (Saturday) a day of rest and prohibited them from doing any commercial work on that day.  So, the letter of the law is not to do any work on Saturday.

But Allah wanted to test their commitment to His obedience.  So, on Saturday the fish would come very close to the shore with their fins above the water clearly visible.  But as soon as Sunday comes and for the rest of the weekdays when they are allowed to fish, the fish do not come near the shore, and they had to struggle to catch them in the sea.

To get around the prohibition, they devised a scheme that involved casting their nets on Friday, so when the fish comes on Saturday, it will be caught by the nets.  And on Sunday, they collect the nets and get the fish.

While they did not violate the letter of the law of not working on Saturday, they violated the spirit of the law by working around the law to take advantage of what Allah made available to them on Saturday and for this Allah condemned and humiliated them by changing then into apes as He Said:
وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنْكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ
And you know very well those from among you who transgressed in the Sabbath; We said to them: “Become apes, despised and rejected. (Al-Baqara 2: 65)

Allah did not tell us this story as entertainment, but for a purpose that He made very clear as He said:
فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
So, We set them up as a warning example for their own time and for all times to come, as well as an admonition to all who are conscious of Allah. (Al-Baqara 2: 66)

The focus should never be on how and who from Bani Israel became apes and whether they have descents or not; these are irrelevant information.  The focus should be on why they were humiliated this way to ensure that we don’t follow their footsteps.

If Muslims engage in the same type of tricks by going around Allah’s commands, they will face the same level of humiliation.  While Allah will not physically transform them into apes, they will be humiliated in the eye of others as apes.  Therefore, it is very important to take Allah’ commands seriously by not only avoiding any prohibition but by also ensuring that we don’t try to find loopholes to go around Allah’s command.  (Interesting that there are several Islamic books entitled: (الحيل الفقهية) “Jurisprudent Loopholes”.)

Gratitude and obedience (الشكر و الطاعة) are the two forms of payment that Allah will accept as recompence for our debt.

But, if you think about it, we will never really be able to pay for the debt that we owe because the more we thank and obey Allah, the more He gives us.  This means that we get more and more in debt to Him.

But, have no fear, because Allah multiplies the rewards for anything that we do, no matter how small.  This is why a good deed is rewarded by 10 credits and even more, but a bad deed will only be counted as one.
مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَى إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ ) الأنعام(
“Whoever comes (to the day of Judgment) with a good deed shall have ten times the like of it in reward and whoever comes with bad deed he will only be requited with no more than the like of it and they shall not be wronged”. (Al-An’am 6: 160)

But it even goes more than that, when we do a bad deed and follow it with a good deed, the bad deed will be erased as Allah says:
وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ ذَلِكَ ذِكْرَى لِلذَّاكِرِينَ) هود
“And establish prayers at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night.  Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds.  That is a reminder or those who remember.” (Hud 11:114)

But it even goes beyond that, our bad deeds can be replaced with good deeds.  In Surah Al-Fourqan, Allah says following his description of “عِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ” The slaves of Allah, Al-Rahman:
فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَـٰتٍ۬‌ۗ
“Allah will substitute their evil deeds with good deeds.” (Al-Furqan 25:70)

So, Allah tells us that when one does a good deed, it will either erase his bad deed or will cause the bad deed to be substituted with a good deed.

But can a bad deed erase the credit of a good deed.  It is from Allah’s mercy that this does not happen except under two circumstances: the “shirk” which is associating others with Allah and the (مَنِّ) which is boasting about the good deed that has been done.

Regarding the “shirk” associating others with Allah, Allah says:
وَلَقَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ وَلَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ) الزمر
And verily it has been revealed to you and to those before you that if you were to associate any partner to Allah, all your (good) deeds will be utterly futile and you would be among the losers. (Al-Zumur 39:65)

The second cause for erasing the reward of a good deed is (مَنِّ) which is boasting about the good deed:
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقَاتِكُمْ بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذَى)   البقرة
“O you who believe, do not nullify your charity with boastful reminders and harm (Al-Baqara 2:264)

We pray to Allah to help us protect us from both the “shirk” and the “ma’an” (مَنِّ) and to purify our heart and strengthen our faith to be steadfast on his thanks and obedience.

content:
The Theme of Surat Yunus (Jonah) (يونس) (10)

Surat Yunus was revealed in Mecca and its theme is the principle of predestination and the belief in the Divine decree (الإيمان بالقضاء والقدر). The Surat alleviates the confusion regarding the belief in the divine decree that often results from the apparent conflict between Allah’s foreknowledge and human free will. The “freedom” of the choices that people make is often called into question since Allah knows exactly what will happen (right down to every choice a person makes). This apparent conflict is often framed in questions such as:

1. Is man compelled or have free will? (هل الإنسان مسيّر أم مخيّر)
2. Why does Allah (SWT) decree to guide some people to the right path and thus save them and not others?
3. Why does Allah who is aware of what we will do make us live through circumstances of His making and then judge us according to them on the Day of Judgment?
4. Are those who do wrong justified when they say if Allah willed for us not to do the wrong, we would not have done it?
5. If it is already recorded with Allah (SWT) who of us will be the dwellers of Paradise and who will be sent to the hellfire, why do we have to work since whatever we do will not change our eventual status?

The principle of predestination and the belief in the Divine decree are important to understand. While we are not in control of everything in our lives, we are always free to choose to either follow Allah’s commands or reject them. This point is discussed through the Surat and emphasized in its last Ayat to confirm that everyone is responsible for his/her own decisions.

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدۡ جَآءَڪُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡ‌ۖ فَمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَہۡتَدِى لِنَفۡسِهِۦ‌ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۖ وَمَآ أَنَا۟ عَلَيۡكُم بِوَڪِيلٍ۬ (١٠٨)

Say: “O you mankind; the truth has come to you from your Lord. So, whosoever is guided, he does so for the good of his own self, and whosoever goes astray, he does so to his own loss, and I am not responsible for your affairs.” (10:108)

It is critical that we realize that Allah’s full knowledge of all events, past, present, and future and that nothing can happen without His will. However, none of these attributes of Allah negates our free will to choose our actions and thus be accountable for them. The confusion regarding predestination and other unseen articles of belief results from make assumptions and not willing to accept the truth that can only be derived from Allah’s revelation, the Quran. Therefore, we note that in this Surat there is a word that is repeated far more often than any other Surat in the Quran and this word is Al-Haqq (the truth); it is mentioned 23 times in this Surat. This is to emphasize the importance of following the truth and refraining from following falsehood and mere assumptions. Allah refutes any claim that people have no control on their actions by saying:

سَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَآ أَشۡرَڪۡنَا وَلَآ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمۡنَا مِن شَىۡءٍ۬‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ حَتَّىٰ ذَاقُواْ بَأۡسَنَا‌ۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ عِندَڪُم مِّنۡ عِلۡمٍ۬ فَتُخۡرِجُوهُ لَنَآ‌ۖ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَخۡرُصُونَ (١٤٨)

“Those who associate partners with Allah will say: “Had Allah willed, we would have not taken partners with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have anything prohibited.” Likewise belied those who were before them, till they tasted Our punishment. Say: “Do you have any sure knowledge that you can produce to us? Indeed, you follow nothing but guess and you do nothing but conjecture.” (Al-Anaam 6:148)

Allah sent messengers to deliver His revelations to all people to inform them of what they must do to be successful in this life and in the hereafter and through these revelation people will know the truth and avoid falsehoods. From the start of the Surat, Allah emphasizes the immense wisdom that stands behind His message to people.

الٓر‌ۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ (١)

“Alif-Lâm-Râ; these are the ayat (Verses) of the Wise Book” (10:1)

Allah’s revelation clearly emphasizes that people should refrain from taking associates with Allah.

وَأَنۡ أَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفً۬ا وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ (١٠٥)

And keep your face (your focus) entirely towards the religion in upright manner and never be one of those who ascribe partners to Allah (10:105)

وَلَا تَدۡعُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكَ وَلَا يَضُرُّكَ‌ۖ فَإِن فَعَلۡتَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (١٠٦)

“And do not invoke besides Allah that which will neither profit you, nor hurt you because if you do, you shall certainly be one of the unjust. (10:106)

But the grave error that some people make is that they reject Allah’s message because they don’t accept that Allah will assign people as His messengers. Allah highlights this false reasoning by saying:

أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَبًا أَنۡ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ رَجُلٍ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ أَنۡ أَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ قَدَمَ صِدۡقٍ عِندَ رَبِّہِمۡ‌ۗ قَالَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرُونَ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا Lَسَـٰحِرٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ (٢)

Is it wonder for mankind that We have sent Our Revelation to a man from among themselves (saying): “Warn mankind and give good news to those who believe that they shall have sure footing with their Lord?” (But) the disbelievers say: “This is indeed an evident sorcerer”. (10:2)

Those people follow their own whims because they want to restrict Allah’s choices. Allah affirms that He reveals His message to whomever He wants, and there is always a great insight behind every choice that Allah makes. Then, Allah confirms His dominance over the universe:

إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ۬ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِ‌ۖ يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ‌ۖ مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِذۡنِهِۦ‌ۚ ذَٲلِڪُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّڪُمۡ فَٱعۡبُدوهُ‌ۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٣)

“Surely your Lord is Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then set himself over the Throne, conducting the Command (regulating and governing all things; directing all things; disposing and governing the affairs of all things) In no way is there any intercessor (ever) except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord; so, worship Him. Will you then not be mindful?” (10:3)

The absolute authority of Allah (يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ‌ۖ) in directing, regulating, and governing the affairs of all things recurs all through the Surat emphasizing Allah’s wisdom and control. All people will return to Him and face His judgement based on what they have done on their own free will.

إِلَيۡهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعً۬ا‌ۖ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقًّا‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۥ لِيَجۡزِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمۡ شَرَابٌ۬ مِّنۡ حَمِيمٍ۬ وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمُۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ (٤)

“To Him will be your return altogether, the promise of Allah, truly (binding). Surely, He begins the creation; thereafter He brings it back again to recompense the ones who have believed and done deeds of righteousness with equity. And the ones who have disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful torment for that they have been disbelieving.” (10:4)

The Surat draws the attention to Allah’s creation and management of the universe. It invites people to contemplate and study Allah’s creations to help recognize His wisdom and flawless decisions and actions.

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ ضِيَآءً۬ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ نُورً۬ا وَقَدَّرَهُ ۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَ‌ۚ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٲلِكَ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأَيَـٰتِ لِقَوۡمٍ۬ يَعۡلَمُونَ (٥) إِنَّ فِى ٱخۡتِلَـٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّہَارِ وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يَتَّقُونَ (٦)

“He is the (One) Who has made the sun an illumination, and the moon a light and determined it by phases that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. In no way has Allah created that except with the truth. He explains the signs in detail for people who know. Surely, in the alternation of the night and the daytime and whatever Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are indeed signs for a people who have Taqwa.” (10:5-6)

The confusion regarding the divine decree is created when people ignore that Allah does not do injustice against anyone, and His punishment only befalls those who commit injustice and cause mischief based on their own choice. Thus, any suggestion that divine decree can lead to injustice is based on faulty logic because it clearly contradicts Allah’s attribute of absolute and total justice. Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ ٱلنَّاسَ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ أَنفُسَہُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ (٤٤)

Surely, Allah does not wrong people at all; but people wrong themselves. (Yunus 10:44)

وَٱلَّذِينَ كَسَبُواْ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ جَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةِۭ بِمِثۡلِهَا وَتَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةٌ۬‌ۖ مَّا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۡ عَاصِمٍ۬‌ۖ

As for those who commit evils, the recompense of an evil deed is proportionate to it and humiliating disgrace will cover them and there is none to save them from Allah. (10:27)

وَلَقَدۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا ٱلۡقُرُونَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَمَّا ظَلَمُواْ‌ۙ وَجَآءَتۡہُمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤۡمِنُواْ‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ نَجۡزِى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ (١٣)

And indeed, We destroyed generations before you, when they committed injustice while their Messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not willing to believe. This is how We punish the guilty people. (10:13)

The Surat emphasizes that Allah gives people many chances to correct their path.

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُسَيِّرُكُمۡ فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ‌ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا كُنتُمۡ فِى ٱلۡفُلۡكِ وَجَرَيۡنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ۬ طَيِّبَةٍ۬ وَفَرِحُواْ بِہَا جَآءَتۡہَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ۬ وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡجُ مِن كُلِّ مَڪَانٍ۬ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّہُمۡ أُحِيطَ بِہِمۡ‌ۙ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ لَٮِٕنۡ أَنجَيۡتَنَا مِنۡ هَـٰذِهِۦ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّـٰكِرِينَ (٢٢) فَلَمَّآ أَنجَٮٰهُمۡ إِذَا هُمۡ يَبۡغُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۗ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغۡيُكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِڪُم‌ۖ مَّتَـٰعَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱLDُّنۡيَا ثُمَّ إِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَنُنَبِّئُڪُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ (٢٣)

He it is Who enables you to travel through land and sea, till when you are in the ships and they sail with them under a favorable wind, and they are pleased with it, there comes upon them a violent wind and the waves come to them from every direction, and they think that they are surrounded from all sides. Then they pray to Allah, having faith in Him alone, (saying): “If You (Allah) deliver us from this, we shall truly be grateful. (22) But when He delivers them, they start rebelling in the earth wrongfully. O people, your rebellion is, in fact, against your own selves. It is only worldly life that you are enjoying and then (in the end) to Us is your return, and We shall tell you what you have been doing.” (10:22-23)

This Surat refutes any connection between predestination and free will and between divine decree and injustice by giving two examples of past nations. One example describes the fate of the people of Prophet Yunus and the second example describes the fate of the Pharaoh and his army. In both cases the people disobeyed their prophets and were destined for a disgracing punishment. And in both cases, the Prophets Yunus and Moses left the people. In the case of Prophet Yunus, he got frustrated from the rejection of the people and left them. In the case of prophet Musa (Moses) he left to escape the injustice of the Pharaoh. And in both case, Allah’s decree of punishment was in his way to befalls them because of their rejection and transgression against their prophets. This rejection was done based on the people’s own free will, but the divine decree of punishment was the consequence of the people’s actions.

The Surat tells us that the divine decree that was intended for the people of Prophet Yunus was lifted while it befell the Pharaoh and his army. The reason is that even without having a prophet, the people of prophet Yunus took the matter in their hands and repented their wrongdoings. They decided to believe in the message of prophet Yunus and as a result the decree of their punishment was lifted, as Allah says: “We removed from them the torment” (كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡہُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخِزۡىِ). Allah says:

فَلَوۡلَا كَانَتۡ قَرۡيَةٌ ءَامَنَتۡ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَـٰنُہَآ إِلَّا قَوۡمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّآ ءَامَنُواْ كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡہُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخِزۡىِ فِى ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱLDُّنۡيَا وَمَتَّعۡنَـٰهُمۡ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ۬ (٩٨)

If only there had been a community (of all those that were destroyed of old) that believed and profited by its belief as did the people of Jonah! When they believed We removed from them the torment of disgrace in the life of the world and gave them comfort for a while. (10:98)

But the situation was different for the pharaoh who decided not only to continue his disbelief but also to pursue Prophet Musa (Moses) and his followers to kill them. In this case the divine decree of destruction befell him and his army: Allah says:

وَجَـٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَجُنُودُهُ ۥ بَغۡيً۬ا وَعَدۡوًا‌ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَڪَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُ ۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتۡ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓاْ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۟ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٩٠) ءَآلۡـَٔـٰنَ وَقَدۡ عَصَيۡتَ قَبۡلُ وَكُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ (٩١) فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنۡ خَلۡفَكَ ءَايَةً۬‌ۚ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنۡ ءَايَـٰتِنَا لَغَـٰفِلُونَ (٩٢)

And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh with his soldiers followed them in oppression and enmity, till when drowning overtook him, he said: “I believe that that there is god but the God that the Children of Israel believe, and I am one of the Muslims.” (90) Now (you believe) while you refused to believe before and you were one of the evil-doers. (91) So, this day We shall save your (dead) body that you may be a sign to those who come after you! And indeed, many among mankind are heedless of Our Ayat (signs). (10:90-92)

The Surat contrasts these two similar situations (people of Yunus vs. Pharaoh) to confirm that Allah punishes only those who insist on the wrongdoings. But those who repent, Allah’s forgiveness is always available for them as long the people repent before the surety of death reaches them. These two examples clarify how people can control their own fate and destiny.

However, one may ask; since Allah knew that the people of Yunus would eventually believe why Allah decreed the punishment on them in the first place to remove it later. Does this create confusion regarding the extent of Allah’s knowledge? Doesn’t this create confusion regarding Allah’s attribute of perfect knowledge?

To address these questions, we need to have a closer examination of the interpretation of the verse addressing the people of Prophet Yunus. No doubt Allah is All-Knowledgeable, All-Wise, All-Just and All-Merciful. Therefore, it is illogical to even think that Allah would compel someone to do something wrong and then punish him/her for it. Likewise, it is illogical that Allah would arbitrarily decide who will be the dwellers of paradise and who will be the dwellers of the hellfire. Nothing in Allah’s decisions is random or arbitrary. Allah has established rules/laws/regulations that govern the universe. He clearly revealed the outcome for those who violate them. Allah also established that people can always change the outcome by changing their actions before the decree befalls them, Allah said:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوۡمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُواْ مَا بِأَنفُسِہِمۡ‌ۗ

“Surely, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change themselves.” (Al-Rad 13:11)

Those who are still convinced that their improper actions are predestined and decreed by Allah have misunderstanding of the nature of Allah. Allah is not subjected to the same laws and constraints that we are subjected to. We are finite and Allah is infinite. We are constrained by space and time. But Allah is not constrained by space or time. We should not describe anything about Allah that refers to past, present, and future because Allah is not constrained by time. Since Allah is not constrained by time, everything that is happens in the universe from its creation until its end Allah sees it in zero time.

This concept that time is only relative (i.e., not absolute) is well recognized by renown physicists such as Albert Einstein who concluded that the past, present, and future exist simultaneously. He once wrote: “… the separation between past, present, and future is only an illusion, although a convincing one.” According to the general relativity theory if a person was able to travel at the speed of light, time would cease completely. Such a person would exist in timelessness. In other words, this person would be seeing past, present, and future events simultaneously.

To simplify the concept of shrinking of time and space, let us consider a 3-hour movie. If you run the movie at a high speed, you can watch the entire movie in one hour instead of three. If you can watch it at an extremely high speed, you will see all the events in the movie happening in almost zero time. If I watch the same movie at the normal speed, it will take me 3 hours to see all the events. In other words, you will know all the events in the movie hours before me. Yet, your advanced knowledge of the future events that I did not know yet, would have no impact on any of the events or the people involved in the events.

Another example of the concept of shrinking time and space is dreams. In your dreams, you experience events that may take days/years and occur in various locations. Yet, the dream lasted only a few minutes and you did not move from your bed. In summary, the key to answering the above questions is in realizing that the constraints of time and space do not apply to Allah.

Another approach to demonstrate the failure of our logic when we try to interpret Allah’s knowledge and actions is the mathematical concept of infinity. When infinity is involved, there will be no valid equation because infinity goes beyond our experiences. When are speaking about Allah’s knowledge we are entering the realm of infinity and there our human logic fails. The following simple mathematical example illustrates the failure of our logic when a finite approach is applied to infinite conditions. For example,

If X + Y = X + Z
The common logic will let us conclude that Y = Z
But this conclusion is only true if X is a finite number.
If X is infinite, the conclusion is wrong.

Because Allah and His knowledge are infinite, using the logic that is applicable to finite conditions is faulty.

At the end, I want to emphasize that the issue of divine decree is in the realm of the unseen that must be accepted based on belief that the source for the information is 100% accurate and, in our case, it is the Quran and the massively transmitted hadith of the Prophet (PBUH). In the famous hadeath about Islam, Eman and Ihsan that was narrated by Several companions including Omar, Abu Hurairah, Abi Dhar, Anas, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Abu Musa Al-Ashary and Gurair Al-Balkhy;

(1) أبي هريرة (2) وعمر (3) وأبي ذر (4) وأنس (5) وابن عباس (6) وابن عمر (7) وأبي عامر الأشعري (8) وجرير البجلي

The holy angle Jabreel (جبريل عليه السلام) came and asked the Prophet (PBUH) while his companions are present about Islam, Imam, Ihsan and the signs of the day of judgement. On the question about Imam, the Prophet (PBUH) replied:

الإيمان أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وتؤمن بالقدر خيره وشره

Imam is to believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Day of Judgment, and the Divine Decree, the good and the bad.”

These 6 elements constitute the articles of faith for every Muslim that are the essence of Islamic creed, Aqidah. While differences among Muslims can exist in issues related to Fiq, jurisprudent, and such differences are tolerated, no difference should exist among Muslims regarding the elements of Aqidah and differences are not tolerated. During the time of the Prophet’s companions, no difference existed among the Muslims regarding the Aqida. Unfortunately, the generation after the companions started introducing additional elements in the Aqidah and thus creating differences that resulted in the formation of sects who started verbal condemnation and even physical conflicts between each other. Believing in the six elements of Aqidah should result in only one thing which is to motivate Muslims to always do righteous deeds by following the commands of Allah based on the firm recognition that Allah is seeing all they do and that they will be held accountable on the day of Judgement.

The fundamentals of the religion of Islam are very easy and straightforward and these are key attributes to ensure their universality and finality. My advice to you is to accept these fundamentals as Allah revealed them and make them the driver for you to perfect your righteous deeds. Heed Allah’s waring and don’t discuss elements of the unseen that cause conflicts and have no added benefit to anyone other than cause divisions.

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَہُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعً۬ا لَّسۡتَ مِنۡہُمۡ فِى شَىۡءٍ‌ۚ إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُمۡ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُہُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ (١٥٩)

“Surely, those who have made divisions in their religion and broke up into sects, you have nothing to do with them. Their case rests with Allah: He will tell what they have been doing.” (Al-Ana’am 6:159)

content:
Allah’ Name Al-Haqq (الحَقِّ), The Truth

This name of Allah, Al-Haqq (The Truth) is mentioned in the Quran 10 times.  The word truth is the opposite of falsehood. Allah says:

ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ هُوَ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِىُّ ٱلۡڪَبِيرُ [الحج: 62]

“That is because Allah, He is the Truth, and that whatever they involve beside Him is the false, and that Allah, He is the High, the Great.” (Al-Hajj 22:62)

Al-Haqq (The Truth) is the name of Allah that means Allah is the ultimate reality.  Allah Al-Haqq means that His presence is a reality standing on its own merits, and the presence of anything/anyone else is only possible through Him.

Al-Haqq also means that Allah’s actions are true/real and not an imagination in someone’s mind.  He gives everything what it truly needs.  Allah, the Truth, permits the truth to manifest itself and He creates everything as His wisdom dictates. Everything that exists is created by Him, and to Him is its ultimate end.

This name of Allah, Al-Haqq is always associated with majestic things.

وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦ‌ۖ وَيُرۡسِلُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَفَظَةً حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ تَوَفَّتۡهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ (61) ثُمَّ رُدُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَوۡلَٮٰهُمُ ٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ وَهُوَ أَسۡرَعُ ٱلۡحَـٰسِبِينَ [الأنعام]

“He is Dominant over His slaves. He sends guardians over you until, when death comes unto one of you, Our messengers takes his soul and they neglect nothing (from their duties). (61) Then all of them will be returned to Allah, their Lord, the Truth. Undoubtedly, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of those who take account.” (Al-Anaam 6:61-62)

وَيَوۡمَ نَحۡشُرُهُمۡ جَمِيعً۬ا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْ مَكَانَكُمۡ أَنتُمۡ وَشُرَكَآؤُكُمۡ‌ۚ فَزَيَّلۡنَا بَيۡنَہُمۡ وَقَالَ شُرَكَآؤُهُم مَّا كُنتُمۡ إِيَّانَا تَعۡبُدُونَ (28) فَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَہِيدَۢا بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ إِن كُنَّا عَنۡ عِبَادَتِكُمۡ لَغَـٰفِلِينَ (29) هُنَالِكَ تَبۡلُواْ كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّآ أَسۡلَفَتۡ‌ۚ وَرُدُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَوۡلَٮٰهُمُ ٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۖ وَضَلَّ عَنۡہُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ [يونس]

“On the day when We gather them all together, then We say to those who ascribed partners with Allah: Wait in your place, you and your partners! Then, We will separate them, and their partners will say: It was not us that you worshipped. (28) Allah suffices as a witness between us and you, that we were totally unaware of your worship. (29) There, everyone will know what one had earned before, and they will be brought back to Allah, their Lord, the Truth, and whatever they used to invent (as partners with Allah) will vanish from them.” (Yunus 10:28-30)

قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمَّن يَمۡلِكُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرَ وَمَن يُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡحَىَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ وَيُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَىِّ وَمَن يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ‌ۚ فَسَيَقُولُونَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ فَقُلۡ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ (31) فَذَٲلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ‌ۖ فَمَاذَا بَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ إِلَّا ٱلضَّلَـٰلُ‌ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصۡرَفُونَ [يونس]

“Say: Who provides you sustenance from the heaven and the earth, or Who controls (the power of) hearing and seeing; and Who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living; and Who regulates everything? They will say: Allah. Then (you) say: Will you not then fear Him? (31) Such is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. What is there after the truth but the error? To where then, are you turning away! (Yunus 10:31-32)

وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُ ۥ فِئَةٌ۬ يَنصُرُونَهُ ۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا (43) هُنَالِكَ ٱلۡوَلَـٰيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ هُوَ خَيۡرٌ۬ ثَوَابً۬ا وَخَيۡرٌ عُقۡبً۬ا [الكهف]

“There were no supporters to help him against Allah, nor was he able to defend himself. (43) There, the (only) protection comes from Allah, the Truth. He is the best in rewarding and the best to in requitting.” (Al-Kahf 18:43-44)

فَتَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡحَقُّ‌ۗ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يُقۡضَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدۡنِى عِلۡمًا [طه]

“High above all is Allah, the King, the Truth! Do not hasten with the (recitation of) Quran before its revelation to you is concluded, but say “O my Lord! increase me in knowledge.” (Taha 20:114)

ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُ يُحْيِ الْمَوْتَى وَأَنَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ [الحج: 6]

“Indeed, Allah is the Truth, and He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.” (Al-Hajj 22:6)

ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيۡلِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ (61) ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ هُوَ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِىُّ ٱلۡڪَبِيرُ [الحج]

“That is because Allah merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. (61) That is because Allah, He is the Truth, and that whatever they invoke beside Him is the false, and that Allah, He is the High, the Great.” (Al-Hajj 22:61-62)

أَفَحَسِبۡتُمۡ أَنَّمَا خَلَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ عَبَثً۬ا وَأَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡنَا لَا تُرۡجَعُونَ (115) فَتَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ [المؤمنون: 116]

“Did you think that We created you for nothing, and that you will not be brought back to US? (115) High above all is Allah, the King, the Truth. There is no god but He, the Lord of the Noble Throne.” (Al-Mumenoon 23:115-116)

يَوۡمَ تَشۡہَدُ عَلَيۡہِمۡ أَلۡسِنَتُهُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيہِمۡ وَأَرۡجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ (24) يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ يُوَفِّیہِمُ ٱللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ ٱلۡمُبِينُ [النور]

“On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do. (24) On that Day Allah will pay them their just dues, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.” (Al-Noor 24:24-25)

أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ كُلٌّ۬ يَجۡرِىٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّ۬ى وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (29) ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِىُّ ٱلۡڪَبِيرُ (30)

“Do you not see that Allah merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He has subjugated the sun and the moon, each running its course for an appointed time, and that Allah is fully aware of all that you do? (61) That is because Allah, He is the Truth, and that whatever they invoke beside Him is the false, and that Allah, He is the High, the Great.” (Luqman 31:29:30)

In addition, many Ayat make it clear that the name of Allah “Al-Haqq” is manifested in His words and actions. Allah says:

هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاء وَالْقَمَرَ نُورًا وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعْلَمُواْ عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ مَا خَلَقَ اللّهُ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ بِالْحَقِّ [يونس:5]

“He is the One who made the sun a glow and the moon a light, and determined their stages, so that you know the number of years and the calculation (of time). Allah had not created all this but in truth.” (Yunus 10:5)

وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَا لَـٰعِبِينَ (38) مَا خَلَقۡنَـٰہُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ [الدخان]

“We did not create the heavens, the earth, and all between them for mere play. (38) We did not create them but with truth.” (Al-Dukhan 44:38-39)

أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ (19)

“Have you not seen that Allah has created the heavens and the earth with truth?” (Ibrahim 14:19)

وَيُحِقُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِكَلِمَـٰتِهِۦ وَلَوۡ ڪَرِهَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ (82)

“And Allah will establish the truth by His words. Even if the sinners hate it.” (Yunus 10:82)

وَيَمۡحُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلَ وَيُحِقُّ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِكَلِمَـٰتِهِۦۤ‌ۚ

And Allah wipes out falsehood and establishes the truth by His Words.” (Al-Shura 42:24)

وَأَشۡرَقَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّہَا وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبُ وَجِاْىٓءَ بِٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَٱلشُّہَدَآءِ وَقُضِىَ بَيۡنَہُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (69)

“And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the book (of everyone’s deeds) will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and matters will be decided between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.” (Al-Zumur 39:69)

وَاللَّهُ يَقْضِي بِالْحَقِّ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لَا يَقْضُونَ بِشَيْءٍ

“Allah judges with truth, while those to whom they invoke beside Him cannot judge anything.” (Ghafer 40:20)

The Prophet (PBUH) used Allah’s name Al-Haqq in his supplication when he would wake up during the night for night prayers, he (PBUH) would say:

اللهمَّ لك الحمدُ، أنت نورُ السماواتِ والأرضِ، ولك الحمدُ، أنت قَيَّامُ السماواتِ والأرضِ، ولك الحمدُ، أنت ربُّ السماواتِ والأرضِ، ومن فيهنَّ أنت الحقُّ، ووَعْدُكَ الحقُّ، ولقاؤُكَ الحقُّ، وقَوْلُكَ الحقُّ، والجَنَّةُ حقٌّ، والنَّارُ حقٌّ، والسَّاعةُ حقٌّ، اللهمَّ لكَ أسْلَمْتُ، وبِكَ آمَنْتُ، وعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وإلَيْكَ أنَبْتُ، وبِكَ خاصَمْتُ، وإلَيْكَ حاكَمْتُ، فاغْفِرْ لي ما قَدَّمْتُ وأَخَّرْتُ، وأَسْرَرْتُ وأَعْلَنْتُ، أنْتَ إلَهِي لا إلَهَ إلَّا أَنْتَ

” O Allah, all Praise is due to You! You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and everything in them! All Praise is due to You! You are the sustainer of the heavens and the earth and everything in them! You are the Truth. Your speech is the truth.  Your promise is the truth. Meeting with You is the truth. Paradise is the truth. Hell is the truth. The Hour [of Judgment] is the truth. O Allah, to You I have submitted myself. In You I have believed. On You I have relied. To You I have returned. For Your sake I have disputed with others. Based on Your truth I have arbitrated. O Allah forgive whatever I have done in the past and will do in the future, and what I have concealed and what I have revealed. You are my Lord! There is no god but You!” (Bukhari)

We should not only be aware of Allah, Al Haqq, in our worship but we should also maintain this attribute “The Truth” in all our words and actions. We should let the Truth be part of our lives by always being truthful and calling each other towards the truth to ensure that we do not become among the losers:

إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ لَفِى خُسۡرٍ (2) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَتَوَاَصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ (3)

Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who believe, do good deeds, urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to steadfastness.” (Al-Asr 103:2-3)

Allah praises the nation that always implement the truth to ensure justice:

وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ [الأعراف:181]

“And among those whom We created there is a nation that guides with the truth and establish justice therewith.” (Al-Araf 7:181)

وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ فَاحْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ وَلاَ تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءهُمْ عَمَّا جَاءكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ [المائدة: 48]

“We sent down to you the Book with the truth, confirming the book before it, and a dominant over it. So, judge between them according to what Allah has sent down to you and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you.” (Al-Maeda 5:48)

We can maintain our remembrance of Allah Al-Haqq by maintaining the truth in our lives by giving everyone his/her rights without excess or neglect.

The Messenger of Allah (PBUH)) said:

حَقُّ اللهِ على العِبادِ أن يَعبُدوه ولا يُشرِكوا به شَيئًا، وحَقُّ العِبادِ على اللهِ ألَّا يُعَذِّبَ مَن لا يُشرِكُ به شَيئًا

“The right of Allah upon His servants is that they should worship Him alone and ascribe no partners with Him. And the right of the servants upon Allah is that He should not punish those who do not associate any partners with Him.”

Elements to Adopt in our Character.

2. We should maintain unshakable belief that Allah’s attributes, revelations, and promises are the absolute Truth.

3. We should reflect on Allah’s attribute, the Truth, by striving to always be truthful in all our affairs even when the truth is difficult to bear, and we should not be among those who hate the truth or conceal it. Allah says:

لَقَدۡ جِئۡنَـٰكُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَكُمۡ لِلۡحَقِّ كَـٰرِهُونَ [الزخرف: 78].

“Indeed, We brought the Truth to you, but it is the truth that most of you detest.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:78)

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ [آل عمران: 187]

“When Allah took a pledge from those who were given the book to make it known to people, and not to conceal it.” (Al-E-Imran 3:187)

3. We should always say, stand for and seek the truth to ensure that justice prevails. Allah commands:

يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوْ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا (سورة النساء)

“O you who believe, stand firm, all the time for justice bearing true witness for the sake of Allah even if it is against yourselves, or your parents, or your nearest relatives regardless of whether one party is rich and the other is poor for Allah can best protect both. Do not follow your whim (the lust of your heart) such that you swerve or distort testimony or turn away from the truth. Indeed, Allah is all aware of all that you do.” (Al-Nisa 4:135)

(يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلَى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ) [المائدة: 8]

“O you who believe stand out firmly for Allah, as witnesses for justice, and do not let the hatred of some people induce you to deviate from justice. Be just: that is next to Taqwa (Piety): and Have Taqwa of Allah. For Allah is well-aware of all that you do” (Al-Maeda 5:8)

Truth is the key to justice and Allah will always expose the truth whether in this life or in the day of Judgement. To illustrate the criticality of truth, Allah sent revelations to vindicate a Jew who was going to be subjected to injustice based on false testimony.  A Muslim stole a shield and to avoid being caught with the shield, he gave to a Jew to keep it for him.  The owner of the shield discovered the theft, and the shield was found at the Jew’s house.  The Jew claimed his innocence and said that the Muslim gave it to him, and the Muslim denied.  The Prophet (PBUH) was on the verge of declaring the guilt of the Jew based on the facts in front of him.  But Allah did not want injustice to be committed against the Jew, and a verse was revealed:

إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما (النساء:105).

“Indeed, We have sent down the Book to you with the truth to judge between people by what Allah has shown you. So do not be advocate for those who betray their trust” (Al-Nisa 4: 105)

Justice is so important that Allah revealed a verse to ensure that injustice was not committed even against a non-believer. Muslims should know that only through the truth (al-haqq) justice can prevail in the world.

4. We should know that all what Allah says in the Quran regarding His rules, the fate of the religion of Islam, and His promises to the believers are not something to comfort the believers, but they are the truth that will surely be fulfilled. Allah says:

إِنَّ اللّهَ لاَ يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُواْ مَا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ [الرعد:11]،

“Surely, Allah does not change the condition of a people unless they change themselves (“ (Al-Rad 13:11)

يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطۡفِـُٔواْ نُورَ ٱللَّهِ بِأَفۡوَٲهِهِمۡ وَٱللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِۦ وَلَوۡ ڪَرِهَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرُونَ (8) هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرۡسَلَ رَسُولَهُ ۥ بِٱلۡہُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلۡحَقِّ لِيُظۡهِرَهُ ۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦ وَلَوۡ كَرِهَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكُونَ (9)

“They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths. But Allah will bring His Light to perfection even though the disbelievers hate (it). (8) He is the One who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He makes it prevail over all (other) religions even though the disbelievers dislike it.” (Al-Saff 61:8-9)

وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ [البقرة:186]

“And when My servants ask you about Me.  I am indeed near.  I respond to the supplication of the supplicant when he calls on Me” (Al-Baqara 2:196)

وَفِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزۡقُكُمۡ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ (22) فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِنَّهُ ۥ لَحَقٌّ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمۡ تَنطِقُونَ (23)

“And in Heaven is your fortunes and whatever you have been promised. (22) By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, this is the truth, as sure as the fact that you can speak.” (Al-Zariyat 51:22-23)

We should know that Allah guaranteed our individual fortunes in this life.  While we are requested to compete to create our fortunes, this competition must be based on the truth and justice.  We should know that none of us will leave this life without having fully used all his/her divinely prescribed fortune.

Note that your fortune in life is not what you earn but what you consume and personally use. Any extras that you earn will be fortunes for others. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ - صلى الله عليه وسلم - " إِنَّ نَفْسًا لَنْ تَمُوتَ حَتَّى تَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهَا وَإِنْ أَبْطَأَ عَنْهَا فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَجْمِلُوا فِي الطَّلَبِ خُذُوا مَا حَلَّ وَدَعُوا مَا حَرُمَ " .

“No soul will die until it has received all its provision, even if it is slow in coming. So, fear Allah and be moderate in seeking provision; take that which is permissible and leave that which is forbidden.” [Sunan Ibn Majah])

While most people may consider their fortune in life merely their financial resources, it goes far beyond that. Your fortune is anything that you personally benefit from and bring enjoyment to you. This includes money, health, relationships, peace of mind, etc,

title: The Theme of Surat Al-Tawbah (التوبة) (9)
