content:
Allah’s Name the All-Knower of the Unseen and the Seen (عالم الغيب و الشهادة)

Allah’s name “Alim Al-Ghayb and Al-Shahadah” (عالم الغيب و الشهادة) is generally translated as “The All-Knower of the unseen and the seen”. It is also translated as the All-Knower of the invisible and the visible, and the All-Knower of the hidden and the manifest.

The term Ghayb refers to anything that are unseen or investable to human senses or incomprehensible to the human brain. The term Shahadah refers to anything that a human can see whether by the eye or instruments.

Allah’s name “Alim Al-Ghayb and Al-Shahadah” (عالم الغيب و الشهادة) The All-Knower of the unseen and the Seen appeared in the Quran in 10 Ayat. It came five times alone and the other five times it came associated with other names: “The All-Wise, the All-Aware” (ٱلۡحَڪِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ), “The Most Great, the Most Supreme” (ٱلۡڪَبِيرُ ٱلۡمُتَعَالِ), “The All-Mighty, the Most Merciful” (ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ), “The Rahman, the Most Merciful” (ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ), and “The All-Mighty, the All-Wise” (ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَڪِيمُ). Allah says:

( وَقُلِ ٱعۡمَلُواْ فَسَيَرَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمۡ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ‌ۖ وَسَتُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَـٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُڪُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (التوبة – الآية 105 )

“Say: “Do (what you do); Allah will see your deeds, as well as His Messenger and the believers. And you shall be returned to the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen. Then He will inform you of what you used to do.” (Al-Tawba 9:105)

( وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۖ وَيَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ڪُن فَيَڪُونُ‌ۚ قَوۡلُهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ‌ۚ وَلَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ يَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ‌ۚ عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ‌ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَڪِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ ( الأنعام – الآية 73 )

“He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and on the Day (of Resurrection) He will say: “Be!”, and it will become. His Word is the truth and His is the kingdom on the Day when the trumpet will be blown. He is the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen. He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.” (Al-Anaam 6:73)

( ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَحۡمِلُ ڪُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامُ وَمَا تَزۡدَادُ‌ۖ وَڪُلُّ شَىۡءٍ عِندَهُ ۥ بِمِقۡدَارٍ (٨) عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ ٱلۡڪَبِيرُ ٱلۡمُتَعَالِ ( الرعد )

“Allah knows what every female bears, and by how much the wombs fall short (of their time or number) or exceed. Everything with Him is in (due) proportion. (8) He is the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Most-Supreme.” (Al-Rad 13:8-9)

( يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ يَعۡرُجُ إِلَيۡهِ فِى يَوۡمٍ۬ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُ ۥۤ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ۬ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ (٥) ذَٲلِكَ عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ ( السجدة )

“He manages (all) matters from the heavens to the earth: then (every matter) ascends to Him in a day whose measure is one thousand years according to the way to count. (5) Such is He, the All-knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.” (Al-Sajda 32:5-6)

( هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۖ عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ‌ۖ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ ( الحشر – الآية 22 )

“He is Allah, there is no god but He; the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Rahman, the Most Merciful.” (Al-Hashr 59:22)

( إِن تُقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنً۬ا يُضَـٰعِفۡهُ لَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (١٧) عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَڪِيمُ ( التغابن )

“If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and will forgive you, for Allah is Appreciative, Forbearing. (17) The All-Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.” (Al-Taghabun 64:17-18)

Allah’s name “Alim Al-Ghayb and Al-Shahadah” (عالم الغيب و الشهادة) The All-Knower of the unseen and the seen refers to the fact that is present in all aspects of creation, yet He cannot be perceived directly by human senses. This concept is central to Islamic theology, which emphasizes the importance of the belief in the unseen "al-ghayb" and this was the first command in the Quran, Allah said:

( ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ‌ۛ فِيهِ‌ۛ هُدً۬ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٢) ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ )

That is the Book (the Quran), there is no doubt about it, it is a guidance for those who are God-Conscious. (2) Who believe in the Unseen. (Al-Baqara 2:2-3)

Believing in Al-Ghayb (unseen) is critical because we have limited capacity in even recognizing what exists in our physical world, let alone comprehending the metaphysical world such as God, our creation, what happens after death, the day of Judgment, Hell and Heaven, other creations of Allah, etc. Information on these unseen things must come to us through authentic revelations.

To appreciate the very limited capabilities of our senses such as sight, we realize that the electromagnetic spectrum covers electromagnetic waves with frequencies ranging from below one hertz to above 300 exahertz, corresponding to wavelengths from thousands of kilometers down to one picometer. The part of this electromagnetic spectrum that is visible to the best human eye is in the wavelength range from approximately 400 nanometers (violet) to 700 nm (red). {nanometer is one billionth of a meter and picometer is one trillionth of a meter. Exahertz is 10^18 hz}.

The frequency range of electromagnetic spectrum is divided into separate bands, and the electromagnetic waves within each frequency band are called by different names starting with the radio waves at the lowest frequency (long wavelength), to microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and ending with the gamma rays at the high frequency (short wavelength).

While certain things may be “ghayb” unknown to some, they may be known to others, but Allah’s knowledge of “al-ghayb” (الغيب) the unseen is absolute and all-encompassing because He is in control of everything that exist. In this regard “al-ghayb” (الغيب) “the unseen” can be classified into 4 types: 1) restricted absolute ghayb, 2) unrestricted absolute ghayb, 3) restricted relative ghayb and 4) unrestricted relative ghayb.

1. Restricted absolute “ghayb” refers to information that are only known to Allah.

( قُل لَّا يَعۡلَمُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبۡعَثُونَ ( النمل )

“Say: None in the heavens and the earth has the knowledge of the Unseen except Allah; and they do not know when they will be resurrected (for judgement).” (Al-Naml 27:65)

( إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُ ۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ‌ۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِى نَفۡسٌ۬ مَّاذَا تَكۡسِبُ غَدً۬ا‌ۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِى نَفۡسُۢ بِأَىِّ أَرۡضٍ۬ تَمُوتُ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ (٣٤) )

“Indeed, the knowledge of the Hour is with Allah (alone); and He sends down the rain, and He Who knows what is in the wombs. No one knows what he will earn tomorrow, and no one knows in which land he will die. Surely, Allah is All-Knowing, All- Aware.” (Luqman 31:34)

( وَعِندَهُ ۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ‌ۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبٍ۬ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ ( الأنعام )

“With Him are the keys of the unseen, no one knows them but He. And He knows whatever there is in the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls, but he knows it, and there is not a grain in the darkness of the earth nor anything fresh or dry but is written in a clear record.” (Al-Anaam 6:59)

2. Unrestricted absolute “ghayb” refers to information that are only revealed by Allah to a selected messenger. Allah says:

( عَـٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ فَلَا يُظۡهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيۡبِهِۦۤ أَحَدًا (٢٦) إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرۡتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍ۬ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ يَسۡلُكُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ رَصَدً۬ا ( الجن )

“(He is) the Knower of the Unseen, and He does reveal any of His unseen to anyone. (26) except whom he chooses as a messenger, and then He appoints watching guards before him and behind him (to protect the information from being received or tampered by anyone).” (Al-Jinn 72:26)

3. Restricted relative “ghayb” is related to information of events that occurred in the past and thus were known to those who were present, and Allah revealed to His messenger.

( ذَٲلِكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيۡكَ‌ۚ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيۡهِمۡ إِذۡ يُلۡقُونَ أَقۡلَـٰمَهُمۡ أَيُّہُمۡ يَكۡفُلُ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيۡهِمۡ إِذۡ يَخۡتَصِمُونَ (٤٤) )

“This is from the news of the unseen; we reveal it to you. You were not with them when they were casting their pens (to decide) who from among them should be the guardian of Maryam, nor were you with them when they were disputed.” (Al-E-Imran 3:44)

4. Unrestricted relative “ghayb” involves all information that is absent from the senses because of distance of time (future) or place or otherwise until that veil of the temporal or spatial dimensions is removed.

( فَلَمَّا قَضَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مَا دَلَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَوۡتِهِۦۤ إِلَّا دَآبَّةُ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ تَأۡڪُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُ ۥ‌ۖ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلۡجِنُّ أَن لَّوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ مَا لَبِثُواْ فِى ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡمُهِينِ (١٤) )

“When We decided death for him (Suliman), nothing indicated his death to them (the Jinn) except an earthly creature that has eaten up his scepter (mansa). So, when he fell down, the jinn realized that if they knew the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment.” (Saba 34:13)

We note that Allah’s name is “Alim Al-Ghayb and Al-Shahadah” (عالم الغيب و الشهادة) the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen. Since Allah states that He knows all that is unseen and this is recognized by mankind, why He needs to state that He also knows all that is seen. Also, by Allah placing his knowledge of “the seen” after his knowledge of “the unseen” in His name suggests that knowing “the seen” would be more fascinating and powerful for us than Him knowing “al-ghayb” (الغيب) “the unseen” which is expected.

To illustrate that by Allah placing His knowledge of the seen after His knowledge of the unseen may suggest to us the subtlety of us knowing the seen. To illustrate the reason why the structure of Allah's name suggests that “knowing the seen” is higher level of knowledge than “knowing the unseen”, let us consider a student in high school who passed the highest level in mathematics which is calculus. If you want to acknowledge the progress of his knowledge on mathematics, you will say: The student knows algebra and calculus. But you would not say: The student knows calculus and algebra; because him knowing calculus directly indicates that he knows algebra that he took in middle school. An example that illustrates the point of sequence is that Allah says that we should stop the outward sins, and the inward sins:

وَذَرُواْ ظَـٰهِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ

“Leave the outward (open) and the inward (secret) sin.” (Al-Naam 6:120)

Outward sins come first in the command because they are easier to stop than the inward sins. If one stops the inward sins, he/she will obviously be stopping the outward sins.

The structure of Allah’s name may intend to indicate for us that Allah’s knowledge of what is seen and our knowledge of them is completely different. One key difference between Allah’s knowledge of the seen and our knowledge of the seen is the time. We don’t know what is seen and revealed in front of us except after some time passed from their occurrence while Allah knows them at the exact time of their occurrence.

If someone is setting in front of you and speaking, you neither see what he is doing nor what he is saying at the time of the occurrence. What you are seeing and hearing now is what such a person did in the past, only Allah knows what he did as the time he was doing it.

It is impossible for us to know the present; but we can only know the past? Let me explain the reason:

1. For you to see, the light is reflected off a person and travels in a straight line into your eye through the cornea and focuses on the back of the eye projecting the image on the retina.
2. The photoreceptors in your retina translate the image into electrical impulses that travel along the optical nerve and into your brain.
3. Your brain makes sense of the signals and tells you what the person did.

Obviously, these steps take time. So, by the time your brain deciphers what the person did, you will only know what he has done in the past time and not at the time he was doing it. Because the speed of light is so fast, it is 186,282 miles per second, if the person is setting say 6 feet from you; it takes at least 6 million femtoseconds for you to see what he has done. So, in fact what you saw is what he did 6 million femtoseconds ago and not now.

Regarding hearing, the speed of sound in air is 1127 feet per second. Therefore, what you hear from a person who is setting 6 feet away from you is what he said 5 trillion femtoseconds ago.

What is a femtosecond? A femtosecond is 10^−15 of a second (one quadrillion of a second, i.e., divide the second billion time and then take one of these parts and divide it again million time). The 1999 Noble prize in chemistry was awarded to Dr. Ahmed H. Zewail, California Institute of Technology for his development and use of ultrafast laser technique that produces flashes of light just a few femtoseconds long and thus allow the mapping the atoms in the transition state of chemical reactions. This may make you appreciate that the 6 million femtoseconds that it takes you to see what a person sitting 6 feet from you did is relatively long time.

This means that what every one of us is seeing and hearing are what has been done at different past times. Only Allah sees and hears exactly every motion and sound at the exact time of its occurrence. In fact, Allah even knows what we plan to do or say as soon as our brain creates the electrical signal that gives order to our body to act. This means that Allah knows what we will say and do before we say or do anything. This may refute the common argument about: If Allah knows everything before we did it, then we are not free to do or not to do.

( رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ تَعۡلَمُ مَا نُخۡفِى وَمَا نُعۡلِنُ‌ۗ وَمَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىۡءٍ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ (٣٨) )

“Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we reveal. Nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah.” (Ibrahim 14:38)

( يَعۡلَمُ خَآٮِٕنَةَ ٱلۡأَعۡيُنِ وَمَا تُخۡفِى ٱلصُّدُورُ (١٩) )

“He knows the treachery of the eye and whatever is concealed in the hearts.” (Ghafir 40:19)

{ وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ }

“We verily created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein” (Qaf 50:16)

Based on images from the James Webb telescope, astronomers identified that the farthest star to earth lies 13.6 billion light years away. So, we are seeing this star for the first time where it was 13.6 billion years ago, where is it now, no one knows but Allah. Only Allah knows the location and the condition of this star now as He knows where everything in the universe is in real time.

[ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡہَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيہَا‌ۖ وَهُوَ مَعَڪُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ : 4 ]

“He knows all that enter the earth and all that emerge from it, and all that come down from the sky and all that ascend from it; and He is with you wheresoever you may be. And Allah is Seer of what you do.” (Al-Hadeed 57:4)

Allah does not only know where every star in this vast universe is and what every human is doing and thinking, but He also even knows when a leaf falls from a tree and where it falls. Allah says:

( وَعِندَهُ ۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ‌ۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبٍ۬ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٥٩) )

“And with Him are the keys of the Unseen. No One knows them but He. He knows what is in the land and in the sea. No leaf ever falls but that He knows about it, and there is not a grain in the darkness of the earth, or anything fresh or dry that is not in a clear record.” (Al-Anaam 6:59)

While we believe that Allah knows the “ghayb” the unseen, what is compelling is that Allah knows the seen because everything is seen by Allah no matter how small or large and there is nothing hidden or concealed from Him all the time. We can understand that Allah sees the large but there are several Ayat in the Quran that informs us that Allah sees the subatomic particles. Allah refers in Surat Saba that He knows everything whether it is the size of an atom or even smaller than an atom:

عَـٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ لَا يَعۡزُبُ عَنۡهُ مِثۡقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ۬ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَآ أَصۡغَرُ مِن ذَٲلِكَ وَلَآ أَڪۡبَرُ

“(He is) the Knower of the Unseen. Not an atom’s weight, or less than that or greater, in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him.” (Saba 34:3)

But what would be smaller than an atom that Allah identifying for us. This can be inferred from Surat Al-Nisa in which Allah informs us that He does not wrong anyone the weight of “dhara” and even the “naqeer” or even the “fateel”. Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ۬‌ۖ

“Allah does not wrong (anyone) even to the weight of “dhara” (Al-Nisa 4:40)

( ١٢٤ ) وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ مِن ذَڪَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنٌ۬ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ نَقِيرً۬ا

“Whatever, male or female, does of good deed and is believer, such people shall enter paradise, and they shall not be wronged even the ‘naqeer’.” (Al-Nisa 4:124)

( ٤٩ ) أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَہُم‌ۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً۬

“Have you not seen those (who claim sanctity for themselves. Nay, but Allah sanctifies whom He wills, and they shall not be wronged even the measure of “fateel”.” (Al-Nisa 4:49)

The definition of these terms in the books of tafseer were based on the limited knowledge that the interpreters had at the time and thus “dhara” is defined as a grain or an ant, or a dust particle. They interpreted “fateel as a thread of a date stone and “naqeer” as a dent in a date stone. Restricting the Quran to these interpretations conceals highly scientific insight.

It is now common that the term “dhara” means an atom. What is smaller than the atom? It is the proton, neutron and electron. What is smaller than the proton is the quark and what is the smaller than the quark is the string. Protons and neutrons are made of three quarks; and quarks are made up of dynamic strings; Quarks move back and forth at a speed close to the speed of light, and in random directions and this can be simulated by clicking “Naqr” (نقر) motion. Therefore, the three verses can be translated as follows by inferring to subatomic particles that we know today and are smaller than the atom.

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ۬‌ۖ

“Allah does not wrong (anyone) even to the weight of an atom” (Al-Nisa 4:40)

( ١٢٤ ) وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ مِن ذَڪَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنٌ۬ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ نَقِيرً۬ا

“Whatever, male or female, does of good deed and is believer, such people shall enter paradise, and they shall not be wronged even the measure of a quark. (Al-Nisa 4:124)

( ٤٩ ) أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَہُم‌ۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَـمُونَ فَتِيلاً۬

“Have you not seen those (who claim sanctity for themselves. Nay, but Allah sanctifies whom He wills, and they shall not be wronged even the measure of a (subatomic) string.” (Al-Nisa 4:49)

Elements to Adopt in our Character.

1. If you are with Allah, the knower of all that is ghayb, you should be assured that He will guide you to make the right decision that is beneficial for you if you are worthy of His support by your sincerity and true belief.
2. Knowing that there is nothing in the universe that Allah does not know, you should feel comfort and not worry about the future. Rely on Allah to make it brighter for you and your family, providing you are sincere in your belief. This does not mean that you stop planning and taking advantage of all the resources that Allah has afforded to you to ensure the high chance of success.
3. Knowing Allah’s name, the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen should promote in us humility and humbleness regarding the extent of the knowledge we know and also promoting in us the sense of responsibility regarding our actions whether open or secret. (Al-Ghazali)

title: The Theme of Surat Al-Maeda (5:1-120)

The Theme of Surat Al-Maeda (5:1-120)

Surat Al-Maeda was the last Surat in the sequence of revelation, it was revealed post the conquest of Mecca and parts of it was revealed during the Prophet’s farewell pilgrimage and part was revealed shortly before his death. The Surat includes the affirmation by Allah that He has completed the religion of Islam by saying:

ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أَكۡمَلۡتُ لَكُمۡ دِينَكُمۡ وَأَتۡمَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعۡمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡإِسۡلَـٰمَ دِينً۬ا

This day I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you and have chosen Islam as your religion. (Al-Maeda 5:3)

The theme of this Surat is revealed in the first Ayat:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعُقُودِ‌ۚ

“O you who believe fulfill your pledges.” (Al-Maeda 5:1)

So, the theme of the Surat is about fulfilling our pledge, as believers. This pledge includes the commitment to obey Allah’s commands and honor the terms of all agreements and contracts that we enter. You may consider that this Surat is giving the finishing touches to the Shariah and thus it also gives attention to the relationship with the people of book whom Muslims will often be engaging with. Since the theme of the Surat is fulfilling pledges and covenants, it includes discussion on Bani Israel as example for the nation that Muslims must not follow because of their continued violation to their covenant with Allah.

The Surat starts with Allah calling upon those who declared their belief by saying: “O you who believed” (يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ). There are 68 calls by Allah to those who believed in 8 Surat in the Quran. These are Surat Al-Baqara, Al-E-Imran, Al-Nisa, Al-Maeda, Al-Anfal, Al-Tawba, Al-Nour and Al-Ahzab. Surat Al-Madea includes the largest number of these calls, it includes 16 calls by Allah to those who believed. Sayeda Aisha (عائشة) said regarding this Surat:

عن جبير بن نفير قال : حججت فدخلت على عائشة رضي الله عنها ، فقالت لي : يا جبير تقرأ المائدة ؟ فقلت : نعم قالت : ” أما إنها آخر سورة نزلت فما وجدتم فيها من حلال ، فاستحلوه ، وما وجدتم من حرام فحرموه . ” رواه الحاكم وقال حديث صحيح على شرط الشيخين

“It is the last Surat that was revealed. So, whatever you find in it as halal, allow it, and whatever you find in it prohibited abandon it.”

In addition to the 16 calls by Allah to the believers, the Surat includes two calls from Allah to the Messenger (PBUH) and two call to the people of the book and three calls by the Prophet (PBUH) to the people of the book.

The 16 calls to the believers addressed the following commands:

1. Fulfilling the contracts.
2. Respecting the sanctity of the designated marking of Allah during the Hajj. And following this command comes the dietary prohibitions.
3. Observing the physical purification requirement for performing the prayers.
4. Standing up for Justice.
5. Acknowledging Allah’s favors by protecting you.
6. Committing to seek the means to be near to Allah by sacrificing for His cause.
7. Prohibiting certain allegiances.
8. Not reneging from the religion to avoid being replaced by others who are more committed.
9. Boycotting those who mock the religion.
10. Avoiding the prohibition or restricting the enjoyment of the blessing of Allah.
11. Ensuring the prohibition of intoxicant and gambling.
12. Being aware of Allah’s tests during Hajj.
13. Respecting Allah’s restriction of killing animals during the Hajj.
14. Avoiding the excessive questioning on Halal and Haram.
15. Focusing on oneself and not being distracted by those who do not want to believe.
16. Ensuring the proper authentication, the will of a deceased person.

Two calls by Allah to the Messenger (يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ) commanded him with:

1. Refraining from being sad and concerned about those who reject Allah’s message.
2. Delivering Allah’s message and not fearing of any harm because he is being protected by Allah.

The two calls by Allah to the people of the book focusing on commanding them to follow the messenger (PBUH)

The three calls by the Prophet (PBUH) to the people of the book demanding them:

1. Not to take revenge against the believers.
2. Follow the Torah and the Injil.
3. Stop all the excesses they invented in their religion.

The Surat starts with Allah’s commands to honor the pledges and to maintain discipline during the key ritual of the Hajj by not hunting animals and by respecting the rituals:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعُقُودِ‌ۚ أُحِلَّتۡ لَكُم بَہِيمَةُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ إِلَّا مَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَيۡرَ مُحِلِّى ٱلصَّيۡدِ وَأَنتُمۡ حُرُمٌ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ (١)

O you who believed: Fulfill your pledges. The grazing animals have been made lawful for you, except those which are being mentioned to you; but hunting is not allowed while you are in the state of Ihram (for Hajj). Verily Allah commands whatever He wills. (5:1)

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُحِلُّواْ شَعَـٰٓٮِٕرَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا ٱلشَّہۡرَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ وَلَا ٱلۡہَدۡىَ وَلَا ٱلۡقَلَـٰٓٮِٕدَ وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلاً۬ مِّن رَّبِّہِمۡ وَرِضۡوَٲنً۬ا‌ۚ وَإِذَا حَلَلۡتُمۡ فَٱصۡطَادُواْ‌ۚ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّڪُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ أَن تَعۡتَدُواْ‌ۘ وَتَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ‌ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٲنِ‌ۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ (٢)

O you who believed, do not violate the prescribed rituals instituted by Allah (during Hajj) neither the sacred months, nor the animals for sacrifice, nor those marked with collars, nor the people coming to the Sacred House seeking the bounty and the pleasure of their Lord. Once you have completed the Hajj, you are free to hunt. And do not let the hatred of some people—who once barred you from the Sacred Mosque—lead you to commit aggression. Help one another in goodness and Taqwa (God-consciousness), and do not help one another in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; surely Allah is severe in punishment. (5:2)

Following the prohibitions during Hajj, Allah listed general dietary prohibitions by saying.

حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحۡمُ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡمُنۡخَنِقَةُ وَٱلۡمَوۡقُوذَةُ وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيۡتُمۡ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسۡتَقۡسِمُواْ بِٱلۡأَزۡلَـٰمِ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكُمۡ فِسۡقٌ‌ۗ

Prohibited for you (for food) are: the dead animals, the blood, the flesh of swine, those upon whom the name of other than Allah has been invoked, the animal that has been strangled, the one that has been beaten to death, the one that died of a fall, the one that has been gored by horns, and that which has been eaten by wild beasts—unless you were able to slaughter it (before its death)—and that which is sacrificed at stone-altars. Also (prohibited) is that you seek your fortune through divining arrows; that is an act of sin. (5:3)

The verse concluded with declaring the completeness of the religion of Islam and giving an exception when one is forced to eat the prohibited food because of severe hunger:

ٱلۡيَوۡمَ يَٮِٕسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِ‌ۚ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أَكۡمَلۡتُ لَكُمۡ دِينَكُمۡ وَأَتۡمَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعۡمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡإِسۡلَـٰمَ دِينً۬ا‌ۚ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ فِى مَخۡمَصَةٍ غَيۡرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ۬ لِّإِثۡمٍ۬‌ۙ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ۬ (٣)

This day those who disbelieve have given up all hopes of (ever harming) your religion; so do not fear them, but fear Me. This day I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you and have chosen Islam as your religion. But if one is forced by severe hunger, with no inclination to sin—then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (5:3)

Continuing with dietary rules, Allah addresses a question that was asked to the prophet (PBUH) regarding hunting with trained animals:

يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمۡ‌ۖ قُلۡ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتُ‌ۙ وَمَا عَلَّمۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ تُعَلِّمُونَہُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۖ فَكُلُواْ مِمَّآ أَمۡسَكۡنَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡهِ‌ۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ (٤)

They ask you about what is lawful for them (as food). Say: “Lawful to you are all kind of good things (Tayyibat) and what you have taught the hunting animals to catch for you, training them as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of Allah over it; and have Taqwa of Allah. Surely, Allah is swift in taking account. (5:4)

Then Allah addressed the relationship between the Muslims and the people of the book (mainly Christians and Jews) regarding their food and marriage:

ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتُ‌ۖ وَطَعَامُ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ حِلٌّ۬ لَّكُمۡ وَطَعَامُكُمۡ حِلٌّ۬ لَّهُمۡ‌ۖ وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَـٰتُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَـٰتُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ إِذَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ مُحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَـٰفِحِينَ وَلَا مُتَّخِذِىٓ أَخۡدَانٍ۬‌ۗ وَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلۡإِيمَـٰنِ فَقَدۡ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ ۥ وَهُوَ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرِينَ (٥)

This day good things have been made lawful for you and the food of the people of the book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And (lawful to you in marriage) are chaste women from the believers and chaste women from those who were given the book before you, when you give them their dowries, desiring to be chaste, neither committing adultery nor taking them as secret lovers. And whoever rejects faith, then his work has become worthless and in the Hereafter, he will be among the losers. (5:5)

The Surat continues with Allah’s call to those who believed to purify themselves before standing for the prayers:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا قُمۡتُمۡ إِلَى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ فَٱغۡسِلُواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيَكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡمَرَافِقِ وَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِرُءُوسِكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡكَعۡبَيۡنِ‌ۚ وَإِن كُنتُمۡ جُنُبً۬ا فَٱطَّهَّرُواْ‌ۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ۬ مِّنڪُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآٮِٕطِ أَوۡ لَـٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءً۬ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيدً۬ا طَيِّبً۬ا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِڪُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُم مِّنۡهُ‌ۚ مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجۡعَلَ عَلَيۡڪُم مِّنۡ حَرَجٍ۬ وَلَـٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَڪُمۡ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتَهُ ۥ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَشۡڪُرُونَ (٦)

O you who believe! When you rise for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and (wash) your feet up to the ankles. And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity (Junub), then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. (5:6)

So far, the commands of Allah are indented to purify our body with pure food, purify our life with chaste marriage, and purify our soul with prayers. Then Allah gave another call to those who believed focusing on maintaining justice:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٲمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُہَدَآءَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۖ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّڪُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْ‌ۚ ٱعۡدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰ‌ۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ (٨)

“O you who believed be steadfast for Allah as witnesses for justice, and do not let the hatred of some people lead you to be unjust. Be just, for it is closer to Taqwa. And have Taqwa of Allah; surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do.” (5:8)

The Surat moves to focus on Bani Israel and their failure to fulfill their pledges and honor their covenant with Allah:

وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ وَبَعَثۡنَا مِنۡهُمُ ٱثۡنَىۡ عَشَرَ نَقِيبً۬ا‌ۖ وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّى مَعَڪُمۡ‌ۖ لَٮِٕنۡ أَقَمۡتُمُ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَيۡتُمُ ٱلزَّڪَوٰةَ وَءَامَنتُمۡ بِرُسُلِى وَعَزَّرۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَأَقۡرَضۡتُمُ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنً۬ا لَّأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنڪُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَلَأُدۡخِلَنَّڪُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ‌ۚ فَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٲلِكَ مِنڪُمۡ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ (١٢)

Allah made a covenant with the Children of Israel and We raised among them twelve Chiefs, and Allah said: “I am with you if you establish the prayers and give the Zakat and believe in My messengers and honor them and lend Allah a good loan. Then I will certainly remit your sins and admit you into gardens underneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after this, has indeed strayed from the right way.” (5:12)

But they betrayed their covenant and thus deserved Allah’s curse:

فَبِمَا نَقۡضِہِم مِّيثَـٰقَهُمۡ لَعَنَّـٰهُمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَا قُلُوبَهُمۡ قَـٰسِيَةً۬‌ۖ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ‌ۙ وَنَسُواْ حَظًّ۬ا مِّمَّا ذُڪِّرُواْ بِهِۦ‌ۚ وَلَا تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَىٰ خَآٮِٕنَةٍ۬ مِّنۡهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ مِّنۡهُمۡ‌ۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡہُمۡ وَٱصۡفَحۡ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (١٣)

And because of breaking their covenant, We have cursed them and made their hearts hard. They altered the words from their proper places and forgot a portion of that whereof they were reminded. And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except for a few. But forgive them and overlook (their misdeeds). Verily, Allah loves those who are Muhsineen (doers of good). (5:13)

Then the Ayat narrated the story of Bani Israel and their refusal to obey Prophet Moses to enter the sacred land (5:20-26). Following this, Allah gives the story of the two sons of Adam and the first crime of murder in human history (5:27-31). This story was given as a preamble to the decree regarding the killing of a human soul:

مِنۡ أَجۡلِ ذَٲلِكَ ڪَتَبۡنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُ ۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفۡسَۢا بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسٍ أَوۡ فَسَادٍ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعً۬ا وَمَنۡ أَحۡيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحۡيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعً۬ا‌ۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرً۬ا مِّنۡهُم بَعۡدَ ذَٲلِكَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَمُسۡرِفُونَ (٣٢)

“Because of that We decreed for the children of Israel that whoever kills a person not in retaliation for a person or for corruption done in the land, it is as if he had killed all of mankind. And whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved the life of all of mankind. And surely, our messengers came to them with clear signs; yet even after that, many of them became transgressors in the land.” (5:32)

(Note: a talk on the story of the children of Adam can be found on 2019 YouTube video entitled: “The First Crime of Murder in Human History” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5VSeYeXPOuY)

After this account that focused on Bani Israel, Allah calls upon those who believed by reminding them of the means to their success:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱبۡتَغُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡوسِيلَةَ وَجَـٰهِدُواْ فِى سَبِيلِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ (٣٥)

O you who believed, have Taqwa of Allah, and seek the way of nearness to Him, and strive in His way so that you may succeed. (5:35)

The Surat moves to present Allah’s call to the prophet (PBUH) not be disturbed by the attitude of the people of the book towards him and gives the prophet an advice to demonstrate to them their hypocrisy by demanding them to follow their own revelations in the series of Ayat from 41 to 50 that start with:

۞ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ لَا يَحۡزُنكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلۡكُفۡرِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ ءَامَنَّا بِأَفۡوَٲهِهِمۡ وَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِن قُلُوبُہُمۡ‌ۛ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ‌ۛ سَمَّـٰعُونَ لِلۡكَذِبِ سَمَّـٰعُونَ لِقَوۡمٍ ءَاخَرِينَ لَمۡ يَأۡتُوكَ‌ۖ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوَاضِعِهِۦ‌ۖ (٤١)

“O Messenger do not feel grief from those who race towards disbelief among those who say: “We believe” with their lips but their hearts do not believe; or from those who are among the Jews who listen to lies and listeners to others who have never come to you. They change the words from their proper places —. (5:41)

And end with:

أَفَحُكۡمَ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ يَبۡغُونَ‌ۚ وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ حُكۡمً۬ا لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يُوقِنُونَ (٥٠)

“Is it the judgement of the days of ignorance that they seek? Who is better in judgement than Allah for a people who have firm belief. (5:50)

Following the discussion on those who rejected the Prophet (PBUH), followed lies and created confusion from among the people of the book, Allah calls upon the believers not to take them as guardians:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلۡيَہُودَ وَٱلنَّصَـٰرَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ‌ۘ بَعۡضُہُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ بَعۡضٍ۬‌ۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّہُم مِّنكُمۡ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ مِنۡهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (٥١)

O you who believes, do not take the Jews and the Christians as guardians. They are guardians of one to another. And whoever among you who take them as guardians, then he becomes one of them. Allah does not guide those who are unjust. (5: 51)

A problem sometime arises when the word “Awlia” (أَوۡلِيَآءَ‌ۘ) is translated as friends which is obviously wrong because Allah will not command the believers not to take the Jews and Christians as friends when He has already early in the Surat (Ayat 5) allowed them to marry their women and this relationship requires friendship and love. The command prohibits the allegiances in which the Muslims are inferior that leads to a Muslim losing his identity. Allah expands on this command by identifying the character of those whom Allah prohibits Muslims from having alliance with them by saying:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمۡ هُزُوً۬ا وَلَعِبً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَٱلۡكُفَّارَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ‌ۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (٥٧)

O you who believed, do not take as guardians those who take your religion as a mockery and fun from among those who received the Book before you (mainly Jews and Christians), nor from among the disbelievers; and fear Allah if you i are true believers. (5:57)

Then Allah identifies for the believers who are their true guardians by saying:

إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّڪَوٰةَ وَهُمۡ رَاڪِعُونَ (٥٥) وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَإِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡغَـٰلِبُونَ (٥٦)

Indeed, your guardian (Wali) is none other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, – those who establish the prayer and pay the Zakat and they bow down. (55) And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as his guardians, then surely the party of Allah are the victors. (5:55-56)

Allah gives a warning to the believers who may renege on their belief, He will replace them:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَن يَرۡتَدَّ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَسَوۡفَ يَأۡتِى ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمٍ۬ يُحِبُّهُمۡ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ ۥۤ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ يُجَـٰهِدُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوۡمَةَ لَآٮِٕمٍ۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٲسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٥٤)

O you who believe, if any of you turn back from his religion, Allah will bring forth people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, stern towards the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah and not fearing the blame of any critic. That is the favor of Allah which He bestows upon whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. (5:54)

Allah confirmed in the Surat that the religion of Islam is completed, and this requires the assurance that the Messenger (PBUH) delivered the message in its entirety:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغۡ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ‌ۖ وَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلۡ فَمَا بَلَّغۡتَ رِسَالَتَهُ ۥ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡصِمُكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ (٦٧)

O Messenger, proclaim all that has been sent down to you from your Lord. For if you do not then you would have not delivered His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Surely, Allah does not guide the disbelievers. (5:67)

The Surat progresses to verse 90 in which Allah calls upon the believers with the command prohibiting intoxicants and gambling:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡخَمۡرُ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرُ وَٱلۡأَنصَابُ وَٱلۡأَزۡلَـٰمُ رِجۡسٌ۬ مِّنۡ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ فَٱجۡتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ (٩٠)

O you who believed; intoxicants, gambling, idols and divining arrows are filth, made up by Satan. So avoid them so that you may succeed. (5:90)

In verses 101 and 102, Allah gives the believers a special call with the command not to keep asking the Messenger (PBUH) too many questions that may lead to more commands being revealed:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡ أَشۡيَآءَ إِن تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ تَسؤۡكُمۡ وَإِن تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡہَا حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡہَا‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (١٠١) قَدۡ سَأَلَهَا قَوۡمٌ۬ مِّن قَبۡلِڪُمۡ ثُمَّ أَصۡبَحُواْ بِہَا كَـٰفِرِينَ (١٠٢)

O you who believe, do not ask of things which, if they were made known unto you, would trouble you; but if you ask of them while the Quran is being revealed, they will be made known to you. Allah has forgiven that; and Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing. (101) People before you asked such questions and then they became disbelievers on account of them. (5:101-102)

In verse 105, Allah calls on the believers to be responsible for themselves and to remain committed to their faith:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡ‌ۖ لَا يَضُرُّكُم مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُمۡ‌ۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعً۬ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (١٠٥)

O you who believe! It is incumbent upon you to safeguard your own souls. Those who will go astray will not harm you if you have followed the guidance. Unto Allah is the return of all of you together, then He will inform you of what you used to do. (5:105)

This verse does not mean giving up on others; it only means that as a believer you cannot be a follower of the majority if they are doing the wrong things.

In the closing section of the Surat, Allah reveals that He will gather the Messengers to ask them about the response they received to their messages:

يَوۡمَ يَجۡمَعُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ مَاذَآ أُجِبۡتُمۡ‌ۖ قَالُواْ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّـٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ (١٠٩)

“In the day, Hereafter, Allah assembles all the messengers and say to them: What has been the response that you received? They will say: “We have no knowledge; You alone have full knowledge of all the unseen things.” (5:109)

The ending of the Surat focuses on the questioning of Prophet Isa, Jesus (PBUH) regarding what he delivered to his followers:

وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَـٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِى وَأُمِّىَ إِلَـٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِىٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِى بِحَقٍّ‌ۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُ ۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُ ۥ‌ۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى نَفۡسِى وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى نَفۡسِكَ‌ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّـٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ (١١٦) مَا قُلۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَمَرۡتَنِى بِهِۦۤ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبَّكُمۡ‌ۚ (١١٧)

And when Allah said: “O Isa (Jesus) son of Maryam (Mary), did you say to the people; “Take me and my mother as gods beside Allah? He said: Glory to You, it does not behoove me to say what is not right for me. If I said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my mind, and I do not know what is in Your Mind. You alone have full o! knowledge of all that is unseen. (116) I have not said to them anything but what You have ordered me to say, that is Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. (5:116-117)

The Suart ends with the declaration that Truth is the only thing that Allah values and rewards for:

قَالَ ٱللَّهُ هَـٰذَا يَوۡمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ صِدۡقُهُمۡ‌ۚ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٌ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيہَآ أَبَدً۬ا‌ۚ رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡہُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ (١١٩) لِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا فِيهِنَّ‌ۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرُۢ (١٢٠)

“Allah said: This is a day on the truth shall benefit the truthful. For them there are gardens underneath which rivers flow, where they will live forever, Allah is well-pleased with them, and they are well-pleased with Allah. That is the great triumph. (119) To Allah belongs the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lies therein, and He has power over all things.” (Al-Maeda 5:119-120)

content:
Allah’s Name Al-Qahhar (القهار) – The Subduer, The Irresistible

Linguistically, Allah’s name Al-Qahhar (القهار) is derived from the verb Qahar (قهر) that means to subdue, to subjugate, to overpower, to compel against one’s wishes, to prevail, to conquer, to vanquish, to humiliate, etc. Also, Al-Qahhar (القهار) is an emphatic form of the name “Al-Qahir” (القاهر) and thus implies exaggeration of the degree and extent of the domination.

Allah’s name Al-Qahhar (القهار) which is translated as the Subduer, the All Dominant, the Ever-Dominator, the Irresistible, Almighty, the One who hold absolute sway over all that exists, the All-Prevailing, and the Supreme came in the Quran in six verses, all of them are associated with Allah’s name Al-Wahid “the Only One”.

{يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ}(يوسف:39)،
“(Yusuf said) “O fellow prisoners, are different gods better or Allah, the One, the Subduer” (Yusuf 12:39)

{قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ}(الرعد:16)،
“Say: “Allah is the Creator of all things: He is the One, the Subduer.” (Al-Rad 13:16)

{يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ}(إبراهيم:48)،
“The day on which the earth will be changed to a different earth, and so will be the skies, and (all) will appear before Allah the One, the Subduer.” (Ibrahim 14:48)

{قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُنذِرٌ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ}(ص:65)،
“Say: I am only a warner, and there is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer” (Sad 38:65)

{لَوْ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا لَاصْطَفَى مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ}(الزمر:4)،
“Had Allah wished to take to Himself a son, He could have chosen whom He wished out of those whom He had created: but Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.” (Al-Zumur 39:4)

{يَوْمَ هُمْ بَارِزُونَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ}(غافر:16)،
“The Day when they will (all) come out, nothing of them will be hidden from Allah. To whom belongs the kingdom today? To Allah, the One, The Subduer.” (Ghafir 40:16)

The combination of Al-Qahhar and Al-Wahid emphasizes that Al-Qahhar cannot be but only one and that it is impossible that He would have a partner with Him. Kingship, ability, power, and glory belong to Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar (الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ) and everything else is subdued, dominated and under His control.

In addition to Allah’s name “Al-Qahhar” which is an emphatic form, the name “Al-Qahir” (القاهر) which is the non-emphatic form came in the Quran in two Ayat:

(وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ) (الأنعام: 18)
“And He (Allah) is the Dominant (Al-Qahir) over His slaves, and He is The All-Wise, the All-Aware.” [Al-Anaam 6:18]

{ وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُم حَفَظَةً حَتَّىَ إِذَا جَاء أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمْ لاَ يُفَرِّطُونَ } (الأنعام: 61)
“And He (Allah) is the Dominant (Al-Qahir) over His slaves, and He sends guardians (Angels) over you, until when death approaches one of you, Our Messengers take his soul, and they never neglect their duty.” [Al-Anaam 6: 61],

Allah’s name Al-Qahhar should fill the heart with fear, it should also fill the heart with confidence and hope because no one else has any power except to the limit granted by Allah.

Allah’s name Al-Qahhar came in the Quran explicitly and implicitly in Ayat that demonstrates Allah’s power of domination. His power is manifested in our lives in many ways:

1/ Allah “Al-Qahhar” subdues the non-existence into existence by brining all things into existence by His word “Be” and He is able to send all that exist into non-exitance again by His word “Perish!”. All things maintain their existence only by His Divine sustenance and protection. Compare an active living person, who is in full power and energy, moving, thinking, judging, acting, seeing, hearing, smelling, touching, feeling, taking attitudes, running businesses, and building up human civilization, to a motionless dead body! The difference between a dead body and a living person full of energy and power is simply such Divine blessing from Al-Qahhar who compels non-living matter to become a living human being.

2/ Allah, Al-Qahhar, has subdued all beings by death, even the angel of death. And when Allah decrees death on anyone or anything, nothing can prevent it. Allah says:

كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ [آل عمران:185]
“Every soul will taste death.” (Al-E-Imran 3:185)

لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ [يونس:49]
“For every nation, there is an appointed term. When their time comes, then they cannot put it off an hour, nor hasten it.” (Yunus 10:49)

قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَى عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (8)
“Say: “Indeed, the death from which you are running a way will truly meet you: then you will be sent back to the Knower of the Unseen and the seen, and He will tell you what you used to do.” (Al-Jumma 62:8)

The time will come when the whole universe perishes. Only Allah, Al-Wahid Al-Qahar (الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ) will exist. Then Allah will bring them back to existence to face His final Judgement. Allah says:

(كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ) [القصص:88]،
“Everything is bound to perish except His eternal self. (Al-Qasas 28:88)

3/ Allah, Al-Qahhar has compelled the contradictory forces to be complementary. As an example: hydrogen is highly flammable, and oxygen is the most effective in supporting combustion, yet Allah combined these two elements to form water, which is used in putting off fires. Allah combined the soul which is a weightless non-material heavenly thing with the human body that is made of a massy material to create mankind.

4/ Allah, Al-Qahhar compelled the stars in the universe to keep moving in their orbits to prevent collapsing the whole universe into an immense mass. Allah “Al-Qahhar” reminds mankind of this by saying:

إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولَا وَلَئِنْ زَالَتَا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا
“Verily! Allah grasps the heavens and the earth lest they should move away from their places; and if they were to move away from their places, there is none who could grasp them after Him. Truly, He is Most Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving” (Fatir 35:41)

5/. Allah, Al-Qahhar who subdued many things in support of humankind and without Allah compelling them, man cannot survive. Allah reminds us of this by saying:

هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ ذَلُولًا فَامْشُوا فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِهِ وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
“He is the One who has made the earth subjugated for you, so walk through its tracts and eat out of His provisions, and to Him the Resurrection” (Al-Mulk 67:15)

Allah subjugated many animals to man. Thus, a child is able to totally control a camel, a cow, a horse, etc. Allah reminds us by saying:

وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ
“And that We have subjected them to their (use), so some of them are their means of transport, and some of them they eat.” (Ya Seen 36:72)

6/ Allah provided us with a clear example on how He can compel tyrants to do what he wants. The Pharaoh who wanted to slaughter all the male infants of the children of Bani Israel in order to prevent fulfillment of a dream that he saw. He dreamt that a male infant from among the children of Israel would destroy his kingdom. Allah, Al-Qahhar, forced him to raise Moses in his own palace, the one infant who would destroy the Pharaoh’s kingdom. Truly, Allah is in control as He says:

وَاللهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَى أَمْرِهِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ [يوسف:21]
“And Allah has full power and control over His Affairs, but most of the people do not know.” (Yusuf 12: 21)

7/ There are many other examples that demonstrates Allah’s full domination regarding how to address the injustice and transgressions from some people. Allah uses many approaches including:

7/1 Allah brings results contrary to what is expected. The brothers of Yusuf wanted to kill him, but their evil plan resulted in making Yusuf the most powerful person in the most powerful nation at that time, Egypt.

7/2 Allah interferes to fail evil plans: The people of Quraish raised the biggest army to destroy the Muslims in the battel of the trench (معركة الخندق) but Allah forced them to withdraw without even engaging the Muslims’ army.

7/3 Allah compels the transgressors to self-destruct. Allah granted Muslims victory over the Jews by putting fear in their hearts and forcing them to destroy their own defenses. Allah says:

هُوَ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ لِأَوَّلِ الْحَشْرِ مَا ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ مَانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَاعْتَبِرُوا يَا أُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ
“He is the One who expelled the disbelievers of the People of the Book from thier homes unto the first exile. You did not expect that they would leave, while they deemed that their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from where they did not expect and cast fear in their hearts so that they destroyed their homes with their own hands and with the hands of the believers. So, learn a lesson, O you who have eyes to see!” (Al-Hashr 59:2)

7/4. Allah, Al-Qahhar, compels the transgressors to destroy each other. Allah says:

” وَكَذَلِكَ نُوَلِّي بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضاً ” [الأنعام:129]
“Thus, We set the wrong-doers on one another because of that of which they have earned.” (Al-Anaam 6:129)

7/5: Allah, Al-Qahhar, destroyed many past nations such as the people of Nuh, the people of Ad, the people of Thamud, the people of Lot and the people of the Pharaoh. Allah says:

أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ (6) إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ (7) الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ (8) وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ (9) وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ (10) الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ (11) فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسَادَ (12) فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ (13) إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ [الفجر]
“Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with (the people of) Ad. (6) Of Iram, the men of tall pillars. (7) The like of which were not created in the land? (8) And (with the people of) Thamud, who had carved out rocks in the valley (to make dwellings). (9) And with Pharaoh, the man of firm of might, (10) Who has rebelled in the lands, (11) And spread a lot of mischief therein. (12) So, the Lord let loose on them the whip of tournament. (13) Surely, your Lord is ever on the watch.” (Al-Fajr 89:6-14)

Elements to Adopt in our Character.

1/ To personify Allah’s name Al-Qahhar, one must subdue his/her own Nafs, and vanquish all desires and deeds that are violating Allah’s commands, and this can be done by repentance and seeking forgiveness (الاستغفار والتوبة).

وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَى (40) فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى [النازعات]
“And for the one who feared that standing before his Lord’s (tribunal) and restrained his self from its (evil) desires. (40) The Paradise will be the Abode.” (Al-Naziat 79:40-41)

2/ One also needs to subdue his ignorance through knowledge and subdue tyrants by seeking refuge in Allah alone, and by patience and Taqwa as Allah commanded prophet Moses to command Bani Israel as means for overcoming the Pharaoh.

{قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللّهِ وَاصْبِرُواْ إِنَّ الأَرْضَ لِلّهِ يُورِثُهَا مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ} [الأعراف:128]
“Musa said to his people: “seek help from Allah and be patient. Surely, the land belongs to Allah. He lets whomsoever He wills inherit it from among His servants, and the end-result is in favor of those who have Taqwa.” (Al-Araf 7:128)

3/ By always remembering Allah, Al-Qahhar makes us humble, forgiving, and kind. It helps us in shunning arrogance, revenge, and rudeness.

4/ By Invoking the meanings of Allah’s name Al-Qahhar, the person will not fear anyone by Allah:

إِنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (175)
“It is only Satan who frightens associates, so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.” (Al-E-Imran 3:175)

The Prophet (PBUH) stated that those who fear of Allah in this world will feel safe and secure in the Hereafter, He (PBUH) said:

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: ” يَقُولُ اللهُ ـ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ـ: وَعِزَّتِي لَا أَجْمَعُ عَلَى عَبْدِي خَوْفَيْنِ، وَلَا أَجْمَعُ لَهُ أَمْنَيْنِ، فَإِذَا أَمِنَنِي فِي الدُّنْيَا، أَخَفْتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَإِذَا خَافَنِي فِي الدُّنْيَا، أَمَّنْتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ” [ابن حبان والبزار والبيهقي وابن المبارك وأبو نعيم وصححه الحافظ ابن حجر و الألباني]
“Allah the Almighty says: By my Glory, I do not combine two fears in the heart of my servant, nor do I combine two securities for him. If he felt secure from me in this world, I will put fear in Him on the Day of Judgement and if he fears Me in this world, I will make him secure on the Day of Judgment.”

5/ Beware that nothing happens but by the decree of Allah and no plan will ever get materialized unless it is part of Allah’s plan. The Prophet (PBUH) advised Ibn Abbas (عبد الله بن عباس) by saying:

عن ابن عباس، رضي الله عنهما، قال: ” كنت خلف النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم، يوماً فقال: ” يا غلام إني أعلمك كلمات: ” احفظ الله يحفظك، احفظ الله تجده تجاهك، إذا سألت فاسأل الله، وإذا استعنت فاستعن بالله، واعلم: أن الأمة لو اجتمعت على أن ينفعوك بشيء، لم ينفعوك إلا بشيء قد كتبه الله لك، وإن اجتمعوا على أن يضروك بشيء، لم يضروك إلا بشيء قد كتبه الله عليك؛ رفعت الأقلام، وجفت الصحف ” (رواه الترمذي)
“Be watchful of Allah (Commandments of Allah), He will preserve you. Safeguard His Rights, He will be ever with you. If you beg, beg of Him Alone; and if you need assistance, supplicate to Allah Alone for help. And remember that if all the people gather to benefit you, they will not be able to benefit you except that which Allah had foreordained (for you); and if all of them gather to do harm to you, they will not be able to afflict you with anything other than that which Allah had pre-destined against you. The pens had been lifted and the ink had dried up”. (Tirmidhi)
