title: On Aayaat Motashaabayhaat – Allegorical, Figurative, Symbolic (by Yousuf Habib)
excerpt:
On Aayaat Motashaabayhaat – Allegorical, Figurative, Symbolic (by Yousuf Habib)

(Al-E-Imran 3:7) – “It is Allah who has sent upon you from on high this Qur’an, containing messages that are clear in…
content:
On Aayaat Motashaabayhaat – Allegorical, Figurative, Symbolic (by Yousuf Habib)

(Al-E-Imran 3:7) – “It is Allah who has sent upon you from on high this Qur’an, containing messages that are clear in and by themselves [‘aayaat mohkamaat’] – these form the essence of the Qur’an – and messages that are allegorical [aayaat motashaabayhaat’]. Now those whose hearts tend to move away from the truth, these people go after that part of the Qur’an which has been expressed in allegory, seeking out what is bound to create confusion, and arriving at the allegorical narrative’s final meaning in an altogether arbitrary manner. But no one except Allah knows its final meaning. Hence, those who are deeply rooted in knowledge, say: ‘We believe in it; the whole of this Qur’an is from our Sustainer’. Meanwhile, no one takes this to heart except the men of understanding – those who are endowed with insight (insight coming from their deep reflection upon the message).”

The respected scholar Tabari regards ‘aayaat mohkamaat’ as those statements or ordinances of the Qur’an which do not allow more than one interpretation because they are clear in and by themselves – decisive and determined with little room for more than one meaning. Additionally, ‘Aayaat mohkamaat’ are described as the ‘essence of the Qur’an’ because they consist of the fundamental principles underlying the Qur’an’s overall message and, in particular, its ethical and social teachings.

Let us now move to the focus of this talk: aayaat motashaabayhaat. Translators of the Qur’an have used various terms for these aayaat: aayaats that are not entirely clear; unspecific aayaats; aayaats that have several possibilities, that are symbolic, aayaats that are ambiguous. We translated aayaat motashaabayhaat here as allegorical passages because an allegory is a symbolic narrative, including parables, that conveys a meaning that is not explicitly set forth in the narrative. In other words, aayaat motashaabayhaat are those passages or statements of the Qur’an which are expressed in figurative or symbolic manner with a meaning or meanings that are implied but not explicitly stated and, so, they may be interpreted in more than one way.

However, an aayat motashaabayhaat can be correctly interpreted only on the basis of the clearly enunciated principles underlying aayaat mohkamaat. Why? Because, as we just said, mohkamaat are clear in and by themselves and they consist of the fundamental principles underlying the Qur’an’s overall message - in particular, its ethical and social teachings.

Mufassir Mohammad Asad has suggested that without a proper understanding of what is implied by or what underlies the allegorical or symbolic verse, that is, an aayat motashaabayhaat, much of the Qur’an is liable to be – indeed, it has often been – largely misunderstood both by believers and those who refuse to believe in Qur’an’s divinely-inspired origin. Another scholarly work states that this verse is perhaps the most direct discussion of the science of Qur’anic interpretation.

However, in order to appreciate the use of allegory or symbolism in the context of the Qur’an, one must relate this Qur’anic use of allegory or symbolism to another concept that the Qur’an touches upon at the very beginning in aayat 3 of Surah Bakaraah - the concept of al-ghayb: the existence of a “realm of reality that is beyond the reach of human perception”. Indeed, al-ghayb is the concept that is the basic premise for understanding of the call of the Qur’an. As a matter of fact, all truly religious understanding arises from and is based upon al-ghayb – the fact that “only a small segment of reality is open to man’s perception and his imagination. By far, the largest part of this reality escapes man’s comprehension altogether”.

[Note: Actual Universe is currently estimated by scientists to be 250 times the size of the Observable Universe. Of the Observable Universe, 95% is unknown (dark energy and dark matter) and only 5% is known (matter). Therefore, today’s science has enabled Man to grasp a barely 0.0002% of the Actual Universe, all the while the expansion of the Actual Universe continues! Self-humility, not arrogance, is called for.]

Meanwhile, we cannot ignore the fact that “the human mind and his thought process can operate only on the basis of perceptions experienced by that very mind. The human mind cannot visualize or form an idea of something that is totally outside the realm of that mind’s previously realized experiences.” And this is why the Qur’an insists that a true believer believes in the concept of al-ghayb.

As soon as we realize that the human mind can only operate on the basis of his understandings and his perceptions, we are faced with a challenging question: How can the metaphysical ideas of religion that relate to a realm beyond the reach of human perception or experience be successfully conveyed to man? How can man grasp the ideas which have no counterpart in any of the perceptions that he has arrived at empirically through his experiences?

The answer, however, for a thinking intellect is obvious: We can grasp such ideas that are “beyond the reach of our perception” by means of images derived from our own experiences. And this is the ultimate purpose of the term and the concept of al-motashaabayhaat, as used in the Qur’an. Symbolic passages appeal to us because through symbolic messages we can relate readily to metaphysical ideas.

The Qur’an itself clearly points out that many of its passages must be understood in a symbolic, figurative, allegorical sense and, so, it could not have been conveyed to us in any other way. Therefore, if we took every Qur’anic passage only in its outward, literal sense and disregard that the passage or the statement or the expression may be symbolic, we would be offending against the very spirit of the Qur’an.

Consider Allah’s Being: His Being is indefinable; it is infinite in space and time, and it is utterly beyond man’s comprehension. We cannot imagine Him. We can only realize what He is not: He is not limited in space and time; He is not definable by way of comparison; and no category of human thought can comprise Him. Hence, the idea of His existence and His activity is conveyed in Qur’anic references to man by very generalized metaphors. So, for instance, when the Qur’an speaks of Allah as being “in the heavens” or “established on His throne (al-arsh)”, we cannot take these phrases in their literal sense. Doing so would imply that Allah is limited in space. But such a limitation contradicts the concept of an Infinite Being. And so, without any doubt, we know that the “the heavens” and the “throne” and Allah’s being “established” on the throne are only linguistic means to convey to us an idea that is, as a matter of fact, outside of our experience. And what is that idea? It is the idea of Allah’s almightiness and absolute control over all that exists. The heavens and the throne and Allah established on that throne are symbols that convey the idea of Allah’s almightiness and all-controlling aspect of His Being. In the same fashion, that Allah is “all-seeing”, “all-hearing” and “all-aware” simply convey, in terms understandable to us, the idea of Allah’s eternal Presence in all that is or all that happens. The idea underlying these terms, by way of symbols, are meant to convey to us His eternal Presence in all of creation and all of the activity of the creation.

Man is not expected to realize Allah’s Existence directly because the Qur’an itself states in Surah An’aam, aayat 103: “la tudrikohool abswaaro” -“No human vision can encompass Him [Allah]”. Furthermore, because of the limitations of the human language that arise from the limitations of the human mind, Allah’s activity cannot truly be described to man. Instead, the Qur’an uses many symbolical expressions that relate to Allah’s activity and Man is expected to realize Allah’s Existence through observing the effects of His ongoing activity. Just as it is impossible to imagine or define Allah’s Being, the true nature of His creativeness and of His plan of creation remains beyond man’s grasp. But, since the Qur’an aims at conveying to us the ethical teachings based precisely on the concept of Allah’s purposeful creativeness, this creativeness of His can only be translated into categories of thought that are accessible to man. And, so, the use of such expressions as Allah’s ‘wrath” or “condemnation”; His “pleasure” at good deeds or His “love” for His creatures; or His “asking” a wrongdoer on Resurrection Day about his wrongdoing – all such verbal “translations” of Allah’s activity into human terminology are unavoidable because we – men and women - are expected to follow the ethical principles that have been revealed to us by means of a human language. But keep in mind a key point for the believer: As Muslims, our belief in Allah’s existence does not solely depend on our grasping the unfathomable “how” of Allah’s Being. The Qur’an tells us that a believer is he who, among several tenets, believes in al-ghayb, because no human vision can encompass Allah.

Let us now look, by way of illustration, at an issue connected with man’s own existence: the idea of life in the Hereafter. An intellectual comparison between the two stages of human existence – in this Duniya and in the Hereafter - is limited because our thinking and imagination is connected with concepts of finite time and finite space. We cannot imagine the infinity of the Hereafter and, so, we cannot imagine existence that is independent of space and time. Also, man’s psyche is so constituted that it cannot accept any proposition relating to himself without being given a clear expression of its purpose. So how could man be made to understand the nature of the consequences of all his conscious actions and his behavior in this life and, thus, the quality of life that awaits him after death? After all, the Qur’an asserts that man’s resurrection will be “a new act of creation” and, so, the life that will follow after this new act of creation will be entirely different from anything that man experiences in this world. Well, if that is the case then it is not enough for man to be told that “if you do wrong in this world, you will suffer in the Hereafter” or “if you behave righteously in this world, you will attain to a happiness in the life to come”. Such statements are too general and abstract to appeal to man’s imagination and, thereby influence his behavior. What is needed is a more direct appeal to man’s intellect that results in a kind of ‘visualization” of the consequences of one’s acts and omissions. Such an appeal can be produced effectively by means of allegories and metaphors – by aayaat motashaabayhaat. Allegories and metaphors - symbolic and figurative – stress the dissimilarity of all that man will experience after resurrection from whatever he experienced in this world.

So, take a look at the descriptions of paradise and hell. In both cases, Qur’anic descriptive method is the same. It’s as if the allegorical descriptions describing paradise suggest the following: “Imagine the most joyous sensations accessible to man – indescribable beauty, physical and spiritual love, perfect peace and harmony – and now imagine these sensations intensified beyond anything imaginable in this world and totally different from anything imaginable”. Now you get an inkling of what is meant by paradise. Similarly, “Imagine greatest suffering, bodily as well as spiritual, which man may experience: burning by fire, utter loneliness, bitter desolation, condition of neither living nor dying; and imagine this pain, this darkness and this despair intensified beyond anything imaginable in this world and at the same time entirely different from anything imaginable: and you know, however vaguely, what is meant by hell”. This is what the Qur’an is getting across man, through allegories, symbols and metaphors about the notion of heaven and hell. This is what the aayaat motashaabayhaat pertaining to the metaphysical aspects of Allah’s Being and of heaven and hell, as examples, are being conveyed to man whose comprehension is limited to his physical, earthly sensory experience.

All that said, however, in the final analysis, there can be no bigger mistake than to think that these attempts at “translations” of Allah’s Being and paradise and hell, as examples, could ever enable us to define and describe the Undefinable and the Undescribable. This is why aayat 7 of Aalay Imran, after it has introduced in its first part the concept of mohkamaat and motashaabayhaat, in its second part the aayat makes it clear that “there are those whose hearts tend toward moving away from the truth. They are the ones who go after that part of the Qur’an which has been expressed in allegoric term, that is, they go after these aayaat motashaabayhaat. And they come up with such aayat’s final meaning in a most arbitrary manner that suits them, and thereby they create confusion among people. Verse 7 of Aa’lay Imran, meanwhile, goes on to say that no one except Allah knows its final meaning. The verse, in its third part, then closes by asserting that those who are deeply rooted in true knowledge, say: ‘We believe in it; the whole of this Qur’an (all its aayaat) is from our Sustainer’. This comprehensive belief of the believer, that is mentioned here in verse 7, is squarely grounded on his belief in “al-ghayb “: that realm of reality that is totally outside of man’s comprehension and imagination. It is in the spirit of that belief in al-ghayb that the believer understands the allegorical narrative of the Qur’an. And the verse finally ends with Allah’s dictum that “no one takes this – that with Allah alone resides the final meaning – no one takes this to heart except the men of understanding – those who are endowed with insight (an insight coming from their deep reflection upon the message).”

The apparent ambiguity embedded in motashaabayhaat has led to multiple interpretations of these through the centuries. Many of these elucidate; others confuse. For a lay person, this can be altogether overwhelming. As Mohammad Asad points out: A true allegory is always meant to express in a figurative manner something which, because of its complexity, cannot be adequately expressed in direct terms or propositions. It can be grasped only intuitively, and not as a series of detailed ‘statements’: and this seems to be the meaning of the phrase in 3:7, ‘none save Allah knows the final meaning’.

I’d like to end this discourse with what mufassir Yusuf Ali wrote almost 90 years ago when commenting on aayaat motashaabayhaat: He said: “It is very fascinating to take up such aayaat and exercise our ingenuity about its inner meaning. However, these aayaat refer to such profound spiritual matters that human language is inadequate to it. And although people of wisdom may get some light from these, no one should be dogmatic, insisting that their interpretation is the right one, because the final meaning is known to Allah alone. The wise man will understand that throughout the Qur’an there is an essence of Qur’an (mohkamaat) and there is an illustrative clothing given to that essence (motashaabayhaat). We must try to understand as best we can, but not waste our energies in disputing about matters beyond our depth.”

None of this work is mine. I have merely taken mufassir Mohammad Asad’s work on this topic and put it in front of you. His explanation of the Qur’an remains, on most occasions, my go-to source in matters Qur’anic.

In the final analysis, of course, Allah, alone, knows best.

Terminologies of related terms expressed above:

Allegory: Representation of an abstract or spiritual meaning through concrete or material forms; a symbolical narrative.
Metaphor: Something used symbolically to represent something else; suggesting a comparison/resemblance (‘the head of company’ is a metaphor).
Figurative: Not literal but metaphorical (e.g., ‘head’ in ‘She is the head of the company’).
Metaphysical: Something highly abstract, subtle, out-worldly; philosophy concerned with abstract thought or subject (e.g., existence, truth, causality); something concerned with ‘first principles’ (e.g., time, substance, a being)

title: Allah’s Name Al-Muqsit (المقسط) – The Equitable One
excerpt: There are two Arabic words that refer to justice, and these are Qist (قسط) and Adl (عدل). From the word Qist comes Allah’s name Al-Muqsit (المقسط) and from the word Adl comes Allah’s name Al-Adl…
content:
There are two Arabic words that refer to justice, and these are Qist (قسط) and Adl (عدل). From the word Qist comes Allah’s name Al-Muqsit (المقسط) and from the word Adl comes Allah’s name Al-Adl (العدل). Both names Al-Muqsit (المقسط) and Al-Adl refer to the authority of ruling with justice.   But since Al-Muqsit (المقسط) goes far beyond ruling with justice to include having the authority and the power to implement the just ruling, many scholars consider Al-Muqsit (المقسط) as one of Allah’s names, but Al-Adl (العدل) is not one of the names because it is already covered under the name Al-Muqsit (المقسط).

The translators translate Adl as justice and fairness, and they translate Qist as equity or as maintenance of justice.  However, most translators translate Qist as equity and thus translate Allah’s name Al-Muqsit (المقسط) as ‘The Equitable One”.

The command for both Adl and Qist came in in the following Ayat in Surat Al-Hujurat:

وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا فَإِن بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الأُخْرَى فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّى تَفِيءَ إِلَى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ فَإِن فَاءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَابِالْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُواإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ (سورة الحجرات).

“If two parties among the Believers fight each other, seek reconciliation between them.  If one of them commits aggression against the other, fight the transgressor until it complies with the command of Allah. If it complies, make reconciliation between them with justice, and be equitable: for Allah loves those who are equitable.” (Al-Hujerat 49:9)

The use of Adl and Qist in the same Ayat emphasizes that Qist requires enforcement to apply the just rules.

Allah commands mankind to stand for Qist and this requires them to possess power which is implied by emphasizing the importance of iron which is the essential metal element in all industries.  Allah says:

لَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۖ وَأَنزَلۡنَا ٱلۡحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأۡسٌ۬ شَدِيدٌ۬ وَمَنَـٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ ٢٥

“We have indeed sent Our Messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the book and the Balance (justice), so that mankind may keep up Qist (equity). And We send down iron in which there is mighty power as well as many benefits for mankind.” (Al-Hadid 57:25)

Inference to Allah’s name Al-Muqsit is derived from the actions of Allah that refers to His ruling with Qist (قسط) and this came in five Ayat:

شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُ ۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ قَآٮِٕمَۢابِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۚ

“Allah testifies that there is no god but He, and (so do) the angels and those who have knowledge, standing for Qist “justice”.” (Al-Imran 3:18)

وَنَضَعُ ٱلۡمَوَٲزِينَ ٱلۡقِسۡطَ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسٌ۬ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا‌ۖ وَإِن ڪَانَ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةٍ۬ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلٍ أَتَيۡنَا بِہَا‌ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَـٰسِبِينَ (٤٧)الأنبياء(.

“And We set the Qist “just” scales for the Day of Judgment so that no soul is wronged in the least. Even if it (a deed) is a measure of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And We are enough to take an account.” (Al-Anbiya 21:47)

إِنَّهُ ۥ يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۥ لِيَجۡزِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۚ  [يونس: 4]

“Surely, He begins the creation, and repeats it, so that He may reward with Qist “justice” those who believe and do righteous deeds.” (Yunus 10:4)

وَلِڪُلِّ أُمَّةٍ۬ رَّسُولٌ۬‌ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ رَسُولُهُمۡ قُضِىَ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ [يونس: 47]

“For every people (there is a messenger: when their messenger comes, they will be judged (in the hereafter) with Qist “justice” and they will not be wronged”. (Yunus 10:47)

وَلَوۡ أَنَّ لِكُلِّ نَفۡسٍ۬ ظَلَمَتۡ مَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَٱفۡتَدَتۡ بِهِۦ‌ۗ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ‌ۖ وَقُضِىَ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۚ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ [يونس: 54]

“If anyone who committed injustice possesses all that on the earth, he would want to ransom himself with it.  They will conceal their regrets when they see the punishment: but the judgment between them will be with Qist “justice”, and they will not be wronged.” (Yunus 10:54)

Allah’s name Al-Muqsit (المقسط) infers five authorities:

* Instituting the rules of justice.
* Demanding Justice from those who are designated as judges.
* Ruling with Justice.
* Ensuring equity for both the wronged and the wrongdoer by considering the conditions and circumstances for both.
* Enforcing the just judgements.

Allah’s name Al-Muqsit is manifested in Allah’s actions in many ways including:

* All the rules that Allah instructed people to follow are intended to ensure universal justice.
* A promise of great rewards to those who ensure that justice prevails on earth.
* A grave warning to those who commit injustice on earth.
* He created people with the innate nature to love justice and hate injustice.
* The greatest injustice people can commit is kufr and even here Allah does not punish those people unless they receive from Him a clear message.
* The declaration of Allah’s love to all those who always judge with Qist and Allah’s love means that He will place for them the love in the heart of all who are in heavens and earth.

Allah commands that people must judge with Qist and this obligation came in ten Ayat such as:

يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَبِالْقِسْطِشُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ (سورة النساء(

“O you who believe, stand firm, all the time for Qist “justice” bearing true witness for the sake of Allah.” (Al-Nisa 4:135)

“وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان” (الآية 9 سورة الرحمن)،

“So establish weight with justice and fall not short in the balance.” (Al-Rahman 55:9)

لَّا يَنۡهَٮٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَـٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَـٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡوَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْإِلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ) الممتحنة (

“Allah does not forbid you to deal justly and kindly with those who did not fight against you on account of religion nor drove you out of your homes, from dealing kindly andjustlywith them. Indeed, Allah loves thosewho are just” (Al-Mumtahina 60:8)

Establishing Qist is not limited to a legal setting, it includes treatment within a family and in business, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (RA) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عبدالله بن عمرو   قال رسول الله صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم” إنالمقسطينعند الله ِعلى منابر من نور, عن يمينِ الرحمن عزَّ وجل , وكلتا يديه يمين , الذين يعدلون في حكمِهم وأهليهم , وما ولوا “. )  صحيح مسلم)

“The equitable people (Al-Muqsiteen) will be with Allah on pulpits of light.  They are those who are just in their judgment with their families and those of whom they oversee”.(Related by Muslim)

While people are commanded to judge with Qist but judgment by man can never reach the level of Qist of Allah for possible two reason:

1/ The proper justice of people is to be blind, meaning that it is unbiased, and the same law applies to everyone. But with Allah, many things that are unique to every individual  such as socioeconomic will be considered in His rulings to ensure that the punishment commensurate with the exact wrong the person committed.

2/ In human justice, when a crime is committed, punishment must be imposed.  But how does a blind justice account for repentance to satisfy the person against whom the crime is committed. Only Allah can link the satisfaction of the one wronged to the satisfaction of the wrongdoer who repented or committed his wrong under special circumstances that only Allah can properly assess its relevance.   Linking the satisfaction of the one wronged to the satisfaction of the one who committed the wrong is achieved by Allah compensating the one being wronged until he forgives the one who wronged him.  Khalifa Omar narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال رسول الله صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم: رجُلانِ من أمَّتي جَثَيا بين يدي ربِّ العزَّة يوم القيامة فقال أحدهما : يا ربيّ خذ مظلمتي من هذا – يوم القيامة –  فقال الله عزَّ وجلَّ للظالم : رُدَّ على أخيك مظلمته . فقال : يا ربِّ لم يبقَ من حسناتي شيء . فقال عزَّ وجلَّ للمظلوم : كيف تصنع بأخيك ولم يبقَ من حسناته شيء ؟ قال: يا ربِّي ليحمل عني من أوزاري .. فالمظلوم أخذ كلَّ حسنات الظالم ، ولم تفِ بحقِّه ، فقال المظلوم : ليحمل عني أوزاري .. قال : ففاضت عينا رسول الله صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم بالبكاء وقال: إنَّ ذلك ليومٍ عظيم ، يوم يحتاج الناس أن يُحمل عنهم من أوزارهم قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : فيقول الله عزَّ وجلَّ للمتظلِّم ارفع بصرك فانظر في الجِنان . فقال يا ربِّي أرى مدائن من فضَّة وقصوراً من ذهبٍ مكلّلَةً باللؤلؤ لأيِّ نبيٍ هذا القصر !؟ أو لأيِّ صدِّيقٍ هذا القصر!!؟ أو لأيِّ شهيدٍ هذا !!!؟ قال الله عزَّ وجلَّ : لمن دفع الثمن . فقال المظلوم : يا ربّ ومن يملك ذلك الثمن !؟ فقال : تملكه أنت . قال: بماذا يا ربِّي !!? قال : بعفوك عن أخيك . إذا عفوت عنه دفعت ثمن هذا القصر . فقال : يا ربِّ لقد عفوت عنه . يقول الله عزَّ وجلَّ : خذ بيد أخيك فأدخله الجنَّة .. ثم قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : اتَّقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم ، فإنَّ الله يعدل بين المؤمنين يوم القيامة .

‘Two men from my community fell on their knees before the Lord of Power (ربِّ العزَّة) on the Day of Judgment,and one of them said:“O Lord, let this one make restitution to me for the way he has wronged me.”Allah said:“Make restitution to your brother for the wrong you did to him.”The man said:“O Lord, I have no good deeds left.”

Allah said to the one who was wronged: “How will you manage with your brother since he has no good deeds left?”The man said:“O Lord, let him relieve me of some of my burden of sin.”

Then the prophet (PBUH) said: ‘What a mighty day that will be, when people will need others to relieve them of their burdens (إنَّ ذلك ليومٍ عظيم ، يوم يحتاج الناس أن يُحمل عنهم من أوزارهم).

The Prophet (PBUH) continued and said:‘So Allah, great and glorious الله عزَّ وجلَّ, said to the one who had been wronged: “Lift your eyes and look at Paradise.

The man said:I see cities of silver and palaces of gold decorated with pearls. To whom do they belong, my Lord?”Allah said:they belong to whoever pays the price.

The man would say:But who can come with that price?Allah said:You have the price?The man said:But with what, O Lord.Allah said:By forgiving your brother, if you forgive him, you would have paid the price.The man said:O Lord, I have already forgiven him.

Allah said:Take your brother’s hand and lead him to Paradise.

The Prophet (PBUH) them said:Fear Allah and make peace among yourselves, for Allah treats His servants equitably” (اتَّقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم ، فإنَّ الله يعدل بين المؤمنين يوم القيامة).

It is important to know that while the word Al-Muqsit (المقسط) and its plural is Al-Muqsiteen (المقسطين), refer to those who are just and equitable, the word Al-Qasit (القاسط) and its plural is Al-Qasetoon (الْقَاسِطُونَ) refer to those who are unjust and transgressors. Al-Muqsit (المقسط) is derived from the verb Aqsat (أقسط) that means to establish justice, but Al-Qasit (القاسط) is derived from the verb Qasat (قسط) “that means to act unjustly.

The negative name Al-Qasetoon (الْقَاسِطُونَ) is used in the following Ayat in Surat Al-Jinn:

وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلۡمُسۡلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ‌ۖ فَمَنۡ أَسۡلَمَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ تَحَرَّوۡاْ رَشَدً۬ا  وَأَمَّا ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبً۬ا

And there are among us (the Jinn) some who are Muslims and there are among us some who are Al-Qasetoon (ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ‌) “the unjust”. As to those who have submitted to Allah, they have taken the right path.  And as for Al-Qasetoon (ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ) “the unjust”, they shall be the firewood for hell.  [Al-Jinn 72:14-15]

Regarding the confusion from these two terms, even those who speak Arabic can fall into it.   A man was brought to the council of Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, the famous governor of Iraq because he was accused of criticizing Al-Hajjaj.

Al-Hajjaj asked the man, who am I? (من أنا ؟)  The man replied:(أنت قاسطٌ عادل)“You are Qasit Adel “   Al-Hajjaj ordered his guards to chop the head of the man.

The people sitting with Al-Hajjaj were shocked and said: why are you killing him, he just gave you a complement, he is saying you are equitable and just.

Al-Hajjaj said” You don’t understand what he said is (أنت ظالمٌ كافر) “you are unjust and disbeliever”.   They asked: How can this be (كيف؟).   He said: When he described me as (قاسط) he was referring to what Allah said: as for Al-Qasetoon (ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ) “the unjust”, they shall be the firewood for hell (وَأَمَّا ٱلۡقَـٰسِطُونَ فَكَارُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبً۬ا).    And when he described me as (عادل), he was referring to what Allah said: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ وَٱلنُّورَ‌ۖ ثُمَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّہِمۡيَعۡدِلُونَ) الأنعام (

“Praise be to Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, and made the darkness and the light. Yet those who disbelieve Ya’adiloon (يَعۡدِلُونَ) (hold others as equal to Allah).” (Al-An’am 6:1)

## Elements to Adopt in our Character.

* Refrain from committing injustice against anyone because you will be held accountable. If you ever do, repent because only then Allah Al-Muqsit will compensate your victim on your behalf.
* If you are in position of authority to create rules, ensure that they are fair and reasonable and apply to them with equity (Qist).
* Strive to bring justice to all those who are oppressed and force the unjust to give restitution.
* Do not always insist on taking revenge against anyone who commits injustice against you, focus on forgiveness and seek Allah’s restitution for your suffering in the day of judgment. This is particularly important with family members and friends.

content:
Maryam Masjid: Fajr Club Assignments

1. The assignments are intended for the youth, not the adults (unless specifically stated). However, the adults can help the youth.
2. Each assignment has a specified financial reward that will be given to all who submit the answers by the deadline.
3. The main objective of these assignments is to encourage the youth to engage with the Quran and take advantages of the tools the Quran uses to help them develop their cognitive capacity. The Quran uses 4 approaches: stories, examples (Amthal), questions and hints to natural sciences.
4. All answers should be submitted as “text file” by the deadline to mamdouh.salama@comcast.net

=======================================

This assignment is for the adults of the Fajr Club

In Surat Yunus (10), Allah established two conditions for those who are the Awlia of Allah, they are the believers and the Mutaqeen. Allah says:

أَلَآ إِنَّ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ (٦٢) ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَكَانُواْ يَتَّقُونَ (٦٣)

“Indeed, the Awlia of Allah shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve. (62) Those who believe and have Taqwa (fully conscious of Allah)”. (Yunus: 10:62-63)

The assignment is:

1/Study all the Ayat in the Quran that define the traits of those who are believers and those who have taqwa and develop a combined list of the traits without duplication.

2/ For each trait, identify performance metric that involves quality and quantity parameters to establish what would be acceptable performance vs outstanding performance.

Hint:

1. The traits of those who have Taqwa are given in Ayat 3, 4, 177 and 183 of Surat Al-Baqara (2), and Ayat 16 and 17, and Ayat 133 to 135 of Surat Al-E-Imran (3).
2. The traits of the Mumenoon are given in: Ayat 2 to 4 of Surat Al-Anfal (8), Ayat 71 of Surat Al-Tawba (9), Ayat 1 to 8 of Surat Al-Mumenoon (23), and Ayat 36 to 39 of Surat Al-Shura (42).
3. Since performing prayers will be one of the traits, you need to study that ayat that describes those who pray such as Ayat 19 to 33 of Surat Al-Maarij (سُوۡرَةُ المَعارِج) (70), and Ayat 45 of Surat Al-Ankaboot (29).
4. Also, since being patient will be one of the attributes, you need to study the Ayat of those who are patience are such as Ayat 155 to 157 of Surat Al-Baqara.

Assignment Date: Sunday March 12, 2023

Deadline: The last Friday of Ramadan (the likely date of April 21) (Send your “typed” answers as “text file” in English to mamdouh.salama@comcast.net .

=======================================

The assignment:

* Identify 6 things that you are prohibited from doing or saying to your friends and people in general based on Ayat 11 and 12 of Surat Al-Hujurat (49).
* Identify the one thing from the above list that if you do during Ramadan, you will be breaking your fast even if you don’t eat or drink.

Assignment Date: February 26, 2023

Submission Deadline: March 12, 2023 (Send your “typed” answers as “text file” in English to mamdouh.salama@comcast.net .

title: The Theme of Surat Al-E-Imran (آل عِمرَان)
excerpt:
The Theme of Surat Al-E-Imran (آل عِمرَان)

Surat Al-E-Imran (آل عمران) was revealed in Madinah. It falls in order after Surat Al-Baqara and it is considered as its sister. The Prophet (PBUH) said:…
content:
The Theme of Surat Al-E-Imran (آل عِمرَان)

Surat Al-E-Imran (آل عمران) was revealed in Madinah. It falls in order after Surat Al-Baqara and it is considered as its sister. The Prophet (PBUH) said: Recite the two bright ones (الزهراوين), Al-Baqara and Surat Al-E-Imran.

The theme of Surat Al-E-Imran is to emphasize the importance of perseverance on the straight path of Allah (التبات على هذا المنهج) that was defined in Surat Al-Baqara and offers motivation and strategies to overcome both the internal and external distractions that are caused mainly by confusion and materialistic desires (شبهات و شهوات).

The Surat starts with defining the guide and the source for helping Muslims to remain steadfast. The Guide is the Quran, and the source is Allah, Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum:

الٓمٓ (١) ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ (٢) نَزَّلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ

“Alif, Lam, Mîm. Allah, there is no god except He, the Ever Living, the Self-Sustained and the Ever Sustainer of all that exists. (2) He is Who has sent down the Book to you with truth.” (3:1-3)

The Surat ends with what reinforces Muslims to stay on the right track and this is by being patient, helping others to be patient, and remaining at guard to face and fend off any danger whether it is a foreign army, a misleading thought, or mere suspicion:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱصۡبِرُواْ وَصَابِرُواْ وَرَابِطُواْ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ

“O you who believe! Be patience and motivate others to be patient and remain at guard and have Taqwa of Allah that may be successful”. (3:200)

The Surat identified six strategies to ensure perseverance on the straight path. These are:

1. Mental Perseverance
Mental perseverance is assured by proper understanding of the Quran by following the “Mohkam” Ayat (i.e., Ayat that have well-established meaning that cannot have but one interpretation) and ensure not straying of the straight path by the misinterpretation of the Motashabh Ayat (i.e., allegorical Ayat whose meaning is not well-established and thus can have more than one interpretation):

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِنْهُ آيَـٰتٌ مُّحْكَمَـٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَـٰبِهَـٰتٌ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَـٰبَهَ مِنْهُ ٱبْتِغَاءَ ٱلْفِتْنَةِ وَٱبْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَٱلرَّ‌ٰسِخُونَ فِى ٱلْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِّنْ عِندِ رَبِّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُوْلُواْ ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ

“He is the One Who has sent down upon you the Book, whereof are “Mohkam” Ayat (clear/concise Ayat) that are the essence of the Book, and others “Mutashabh” (allegorical) Ayat. So, as for those in whose hearts is swerving, they follow the “Mutashabh” parts seeking confusion and seeking its (unique) interpretation; and in no way does anyone know its interpretation except Allah. And those who are firmly established in knowledge say: “We have believed in it; all is from our Lord.” And in no one can always be in state of awareness except those who are endowed with intellects.” (3:7)

2. Connecting to Allah with Special Dua:
رَبَّنَا لاَ تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْوَهَّابُ

“Our Lord do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us and bestow upon us mercy from Your own. You, and You alone are the One who bestows in abundance.” (3:8)

3. Maintaining Intellectual Steadfastness
Intellectual steadfastness is critical in face of the confusing arguments made by some people such as the people of the book (Christians and Jews). The Surat identified eight steps for any discussion with others in any interfaith dialogue. These steps are:

• Fortify Your Belief
Muslims who engage in dialogues with others need to be firm in their own belief. The Surat offers reinforcements by verses such as:

شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُ ۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ قَآٮِٕمًۢا بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۚ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَڪِيمُ (١٨)
إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡإِسۡلَـٰمُ‌ۗ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡعِلۡمُ بَغۡيًۢا بَيۡنَہُمۡ‌ۗ وَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ (١٩)

“Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the Angels and the ones endowed with knowledge (also bear witness). (He) maintains His creation with Justice. There is no god except He, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. (18) Truly, the religion with Allah is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture did not differ after knowledge had come to them except through envy of each other. And whoever disbelieves in the revelations of Allah, then surely, Allah is Swift in calling to account.” (3:18-19)

أَفَغَيۡرَ دِينِ ٱللَّهِ يَبۡغُونَ وَلَهُ ۥۤ أَسۡلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ طَوۡعً۬ا وَكَرۡهً۬ا وَإِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُونَ

“Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submitted all who are in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly. And to Him shall they all shall return.” (3:83)

وَمَن يَبۡتَغِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡإِسۡلَـٰمِ دِينً۬ا فَلَن يُقۡبَلَ مِنۡهُ وَهُوَ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرِينَ (٨٥)

“And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter, he will be one of the losers” (3:85)

• Clarify Your Belief
Muslims need to clarify their position regarding relationship with past Prophets and scriptures:

قُلۡ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَـٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِىَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدٍ۬ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُ ۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ

“Say, “We have believed in Allah, and in whatever has been sent down to us, and whatever was sent down on Ibrahim and Ismael (Ishmael) and Ishaq (Isaac) and Yaqoob, (Jacob) and the Tribes (grandsons) and in whatever was given to Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus) and the Prophets from their Lord; we make no distinction between any of them, and to Him (Allah) we are Muslims.” (3:84)

• Identify Points of Agreement
It is important to find a common ground before getting deeper in any debate:

قُلۡ يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ تَعَالَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ڪَلِمَةٍ۬ سَوَآءِۭ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ أَلَّا نَعۡبُدَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَلَا نُشۡرِكَ بِهِۦ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعۡضُنَا بَعۡضًا أَرۡبَابً۬ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَقُولُواْ ٱشۡہَدُواْ بِأَنَّا مُسۡلِمُونَ

“Say: “O people of the Book: Come to a word that is common between us and you, that we worship none but Allah, and that we do not associate anything with Him, and that none of us shall take others as lords besides Allah. If they turn away, then say: “Bear witness that we are Muslims.” (3:64)

• Use Logic to Offer Counter Argument
It is important for your message to offer logical and rational explanation. The Surat provides examples of logical arguments:

إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَ‌ۖ خَلَقَهُ ۥ مِن تُرَابٍ۬ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ ۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ

“Surely the likeness of Isa (Jesus) before Allah is as the likeness of Adam. He created him of dust, then (He) said to him: “Be” – and he was.” (3:59),

يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِىٓ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَتِ ٱلتَّوۡرَٮٰةُ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۤ‌ۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ (٦٥)
هَـٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ حَـٰجَجۡتُمۡ فِيمَا لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ۬ فَلِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِيمَا لَيۡسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ۬‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ (٦٦) مَا كَانَ إِبۡرَٲهِيمُ يَہُودِيًّ۬ا وَلَا نَصۡرَانِيًّ۬ا وَلَكِن كَانَ حَنِيفً۬ا مُّسۡلِمً۬ا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ (٦٧)

“O people of the Book (Jews and Christians)! Why do you argue about Ibrahim (Abraham), while the Torah (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel) were not revealed till after him? Have you then no logic? (65) Verily, you are arguing about that of which you have knowledge. Why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? Allah knows, and you do not know. (66) Ibrahim (Abraham) was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true Muslim, and he was not one of those who associate others with Allah. (3:65-67)

مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُؤۡتِيَهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡحُكۡمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُواْ عِبَادً۬ا لِّى مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَكِن كُونُواْ رَبَّـٰنِيِّـۧنَ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَبِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَدۡرُسُونَ (٧٩) وَلَا يَأۡمُرَڪُمۡ أَن تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةَ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ أَرۡبَابًا‌ۗ أَيَأۡمُرُڪُم بِٱلۡڪُفۡرِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ أَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ (٨٠)

“It is not (possible) for any human being to whom Allah has given the Book and the laws and the Prophethood to say to the people: “Be my worshippers rather than Allah’s.” On the contrary (he would say): “Be you lordly (true worshipers of Allah), because you are teaching the Book, and you are studying it. (79) Nor would he order you to take angels and Prophets for lords. Would he order you to disbelieve after you have become Muslims”. (3:79-80)

• Offer Heart-Touching Evidence
If after providing logical and rational evidence, denial and contradictory arguments continue, turn to touching their hearts and emotions.:

يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لِمَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَنتُمۡ تَشۡهَدُونَ

“O people of the Book: “Why do you disbelieve in the revelations of Allah, while you witness their truth”. (3:70)

يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لِمَ تَلۡبِسُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِٱلۡبَـٰطِلِ وَتَكۡتُمُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ

“O people of the Book: Why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know it?” (3:71)

فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جَمَعۡنَـٰهُمۡ لِيَوۡمٍ۬ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ وَوُفِّيَتۡ ڪُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّا ڪَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ

“So, how (will it be) when We (Allah) have gathered them for a day that there is no doubt about it, and every soul will be paid in full for whatever it has earned, and they shall not be wronged.” (3:25)

• Be Ready to Invoke (Al-Mobahala)
If none of the above works, you can call for Al- Mobahala “المباهلة” (invocation). When the Prophet (PBUH) offered this challenge to the Christians from Najran, they refused to accept it:

فَمَنۡ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ فَقُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ نَدۡعُ أَبۡنَآءَنَا وَأَبۡنَآءَڪُمۡ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَڪُمۡ وَأَنفُسَنَا وَأَنفُسَڪُمۡ ثُمَّ نَبۡتَهِلۡ فَنَجۡعَل لَّعۡنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلۡڪَـٰذِبِينَ

“So, whoever argues with you concerning him, (i.e., Jesus) even after this knowledge has come to you, then say, “Come! Let us call our sons and your sons, and our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves; then we pray and invoke the curse of Allah on those who lie.” (3:61)

• Do Not Blame Yourself for Failing to Convince Others
You need to know that your role is just to present an honest and logical argument and it is up to others to analyze and accept. Allah gave people the free will to accept or reject Islam. Our responsibility is to deliver a clear and concise message in a polite and honorable way:

فَإِنۡ حَآجُّوكَ فَقُلۡ أَسۡلَمۡتُ وَجۡهِىَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِ‌ۗ وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ ءَأَسۡلَمۡتُمۡ‌ۚ فَإِنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْ فَقَدِ ٱهۡتَدَواْ‌ۖ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلۡبَلَـٰغُ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ

“In case they argue with you, say, “I have surrendered myself to Allah and so have those who follow me. And say to those who were given the Scripture and to those who are illiterates (Arab pagans): “Do you (also) submit yourselves (to Allah)?” If they do, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the Message; and Allah is All-Seer of (His) slaves.” (3:20)

• Do Not Give Up Because People are Different.
You must be just and fair in your assessment of the People of the Book because they are not the same.

لَيۡسُواْ سَوَآءً۬‌ۗ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ أُمَّةٌ۬ قَآٮِٕمَةٌ۬ يَتۡلُونَ ءَايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَهُمۡ يَسۡجُدُونَ

“Not all of them are alike. Among the people there are those who are steadfast, they recite the revelation of Allah during the night hours, and they prostrate themselves.” (3:113)

وَمِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ مَنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِقِنطَارٍ۬ يُؤَدِّهِۦۤ إِلَيۡكَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِدِينَارٍ۬ لَّا يُؤَدِّهِۦۤ إِلَيۡكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ قَآٮِٕمً۬ا‌ۗ ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّہُمۡ قَالُواْ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡنَا فِى ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ سَبِيلٌ۬ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡڪَذِبَ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ

“And among the people of the Book is he who, if entrusted with a Qintar (a great amount of wealth), will readily return it back to you; and among them there is he who, if entrusted with a single dinar (silver coin) will not return it unless you constantly stand demanding, because they say: “There is no blame on in the matter of the unlettered (Gentiles/Arabs).” But they tell a lie against Allah while they know it.” (3:75)

4. Full Awareness of the Temptations
The Surat defines the types of the temptations that Muslims encounter and provides reinforcement to them to overcome these temptations and to comfort them if they temporally deviate.

زُيّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ ٱلشَّهَوٰتِ مِنَ ٱلنّسَاء وَٱلْبَنِينَ وَٱلْقَنَـٰطِيرِ ٱلْمُقَنطَرَةِ مِنَ ٱلذَّهَبِ وَٱلْفِضَّةِ وَٱلْخَيْلِ ٱلْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَٱلأَنْعَـٰمِ وَٱلْحَرْثِ ذٰلِكَ مَتَـٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُ حُسْنُ ٱلْمَـآبِ

“Adorned for mankind is the love of joys (that come) from women, sons, heaps and heaps of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle, and well-tilled land. Such are the enjoyment of the worldly life; but with Allah is the best final resort.” (3:14).

In order for those who deviate not to be discouraged, the Surat presents the case of some companions of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) who fell short and did not resist the fleeting pleasures of this life:

وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَڪُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُ ۥۤ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦ‌ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَـٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَٮٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ‌ۚ مِنڪُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنڪُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ‌ۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَڪُمۡ عَنۡہُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَڪُمۡ‌ۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنڪُمۡ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (١٥٢)

“Allah has surely fulfilled His Promise to you when you were fighting them (your enemy) with His Permission; until (the moment) you lost your courage and disputed about the order and disobeyed after He showed you what you loved (the booty). Among you were some who desire this world and some who desire the Hereafter. Then He made you flee from them (your enemy), that He might test you. But surely, He forgave you, and Allah is Most Gracious to the believers”. (3:152)

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسۡتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ بِبَعۡضِ مَا كَسَبُواْ‌ۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡہُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (١٥٥)

“Those of you who turned back on the day the two troops faced each other (i.e., the battle of Uhud), it was Satan who caused them to backslide (run away from the battlefield) because of some of their deeds. But Allah has forgiven them. Surely, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Forbearing”. (3:155)

The Surat reminds us of the disciples of Prophet Jesus (Al-Hawâriyyûn) who were committed to support Allah’s cause, but doubt came in their hearts and thus Jesus sought their commitment:

فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنۡہُمُ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ قَالَ مَنۡ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ قَالَ ٱلۡحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحۡنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَٱشۡہَدۡ بِأَنَّا مُسۡلِمُونَ

“So, as soon as Isa (Jesus) perceived of their disbelief, he said: “Who will be my helpers in Allah’s Cause?” The disciples said: “We are the helpers of Allah; we believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims.” (3:52)

5. Repentance
It is expected that Muslims may suffer some weaknesses and fall in temptations and the solution is repentance. The Surat encourages hastening to repentance in many Ayat:

ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ

“Those who say, “Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins, and protect us from the torment of the Fire”, (3:16)

وَسَارِعُواْ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مّن رَّبّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا ٱلسَّمَـٰوٰتُ وَٱلاْرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ

“And race with one another for forgiveness from your Lord and for a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the pious” (3:133).

6. Sustaining Perseverance
The Surat identifies five elements for perseverance on the straight path.

6.1. Turning to Allah with Dua (اللجوء إلى الله)
The Surat provides many examples of Dua:

رَبَّنَا لاَ تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْوَهَّابُ

“Our Lord do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us and bestow upon us mercy from Your own. You, and You alone are the One who bestows in abundance.” (3:8)

وَمَا كَانَ قَوۡلَهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسۡرَافَنَا فِىٓ أَمۡرِنَا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ (١٤٧)

“And they said nothing but: “Our Lord! Forgive us our sins and our excesses in our conduct, make firm our feet, and give us victory over the disbelieving people. “(3:147).

فَـَٔاتَٮٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَحُسۡنَ ثَوَابِ ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (١٤٨)

So Allah gave them the reward of this world, and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the good doers. “(3: 148)

رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعۡنَا مُنَادِيً۬ا يُنَادِى لِلۡإِيمَـٰنِ أَنۡ ءَامِنُواْ بِرَبِّكُمۡ فَـَٔامَنَّا رَبَّنَا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَڪَفِّرۡ عَنَّا سَيِّـَٔاتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ ٱلۡأَبۡرَارِ (١٩٣) رَبَّنَا وَءَاتِنَا مَا وَعَدتَّنَا عَلَىٰ رُسُلِكَ وَلَا تُخۡزِنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَـٰمَةِ ۗ إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ (١٩٤)

“Our Lord, we heard a caller calling to belief, “Believe in your Lord.” So, we believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins, and expiate for us our iniquities, make us die among the righteous. (193) “Our Lord” grant us what You have promised us through Your Messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of the Resurrection; You never break your promise.” (3:193-194)

فَٱسۡتَجَابَ لَهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ أَنِّى لَآ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَـٰمِلٍ۬ مِّنكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ‌ۖ بَعۡضُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡضٍ۬‌ۖ

“So, their Lord accepted their prayer: “I do not allow the work of any of you, male or female, to go to waste.” (3: 195).

The Surat gives glowing examples to demonstrate the importance of Dua and the great results that it can achieve. It gives us the examples of the Dua of the wife of ‘Imran and Prophet Zakariya (Zachariah)”

رَبِّ إِنِّى نَذَرۡتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطۡنِى مُحَرَّرً۬ا فَتَقَبَّلۡ مِنِّىٓ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ

“O my Lord! I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated for Your services, so accept this, from me; indeed, You are the All-Hearer, the All-Knowing” (3:35).

فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ۬ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنً۬ا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا‌ۖ

“So her Lord (Allah) accepted her with goodly acceptance. He made her grow in a good manner and put her under the care of Zakariya (Zachariah).” (3:37)

هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَڪَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ ۥ‌ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبۡ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً۬ طَيِّبَةً‌ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ (٣٨)

“There Zakariya prayed to his Lord saying: ‘O my Lord! Grant me from You, a good offspring. You are indeed the All-Hearer of prayer.” (3:38).

فَنَادَتۡهُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآٮِٕمٌ۬ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلۡمِحۡرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحۡيَىٰ مُصَدِّقًۢا بِكَلِمَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَسَيِّدً۬ا وَحَصُورً۬ا وَنَبِيًّ۬ا مِّنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (٣٩)

“Then the angels called him, while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary (in the temple), (saying): “Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya (John), confirming the Word from Allah, noble, chaste, and Prophet from among the righteous.”(3:39)

• Prayers in a Secluded Place
The Surat encourages us to pray in a secluded place to allow sincere communication with Allah because good things happen when one is praying to Allah without any distractions as happened to Sayeda Maryam and Prophet Zakariya:

كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيۡهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزۡقً۬ا‌ۖ

“Whenever Zakariya visited her (Maryam) in the sanctuary, he found supplies of sustenance.” (3:37)

فَنَادَتۡهُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآٮِٕمٌ۬ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلۡمِحۡرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحۡيَىٰ

“Then the angels called him, while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary (in the temple), (saying): “Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya (John).”(3:39)

6.3 Commit to Dawa to Allah (الدعوة إلى الله)
The best way to master any subject is to teach it. Therefore, the Surat contains several Ayat that encourage Muslims to perform Dawa:

وَلْتَكُن مّنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنْكَرِ وَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ

“Let there arise out of you a group of people inviting to all that is good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is evil; They are the ones who are the successful.” (3:104)

كُنتُمۡ خَيۡرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخۡرِجَتۡ لِلنَّاسِ تَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنڪَرِ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ‌ۗ وَلَوۡ ءَامَنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ لَڪَانَ خَيۡرً۬ا لَّهُم‌ۚ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَأَڪۡثَرُهُمُ ٱلۡفَـٰسِقُونَ

You are the best nation ever raised for mankind: you command what is good and forbid what is evil and believe in Allah, had the people of the Book believed (i.e., followed your Dawa), it would indeed have been better for them; some of them are the believers, and the majority of them are deviant.” (3:110)

6.4 Remembrance of Allah
Perseverance is supported by always being in a state of remembrance of Allah, reflection on the creation of the universe and recognition of the Hereafter:

ٱلَّذِينَ يَذۡكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَـٰمً۬ا وَقُعُودً۬ا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمۡ وَيَتَفَڪَّرُونَ فِى خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقۡتَ هَـٰذَا بَـٰطِلاً۬ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ

“Those who are always remembering Allah, standing, sitting, and lying down on their sides, and think deeply about the creation of the heavens and the earth, (saying): “Our Lord! You have not created (all) this without purpose, glory to You, save us from the torment of the Fire.” (3:191)

6.5 Unity and Brotherhood (الأخوة)
Brotherhood is a great blessing from Allah that must be maintained:

وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِحَبۡلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعً۬ا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُواْ‌ۚ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ كُنتُمۡ أَعۡدَآءً۬ فَأَلَّفَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِڪُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم بِنِعۡمَتِهِۦۤ إِخۡوَٲنً۬ا

“And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope (Covenant) of Allah and do not be divided, and remember Allah’s Favor on you, for you were enemies but He joined your hearts together, so you became brethren that by His Grace.” (3:103)

وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُواْ وَٱخۡتَلَفُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتُ‌ۚ وَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١٠٥)

“And do not be as those who were disunited and differed among themselves after clear evidence came to them. It is they for whom there is an awful torment.” (3:105)

An important strategy to ensure unity is consultations and tolerance to all opinions:

فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡہُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ‌ۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ

, “… So, pardon them, and seek forgiveness for them, consult them in the command. Once you have taken a decision, place your trust in Allah. (3:159)

Final Comment
The Surat devoted large part on highlighting symbols of steadfastness, the wife of Imran and Sayeda Maryam. The devotion and pure intentions of the wife of Imran to promote Allah’s religion resulted in the birth of Maryam (AS) and later Prophet Isa (AS).

title: Allah’s Names Al-Hayy (الحي) – Al-Qayyum (القيوم)
excerpt: Allah’s name Al-Hayy (الْحَيُّ) (The Ever Living) is a unique name because Allah’s life is different from the life of anything else.  Allah is eternally Living, there is no start point for Allah’s…
content:
Allah’s name Al-Hayy (الْحَيُّ) (The Ever Living) is a unique name because Allah’s life is different from the life of anything else.  Allah is eternally Living, there is no start point for Allah’s existence and there is no end point. Allah has no beginning because there was nothing before Him and has no end because there is nothing after Him.  Allah existence all the time and before the existence of anything means that He is completely self-sustaining and has no need for anything or anyone to maintain His existence. This is an element of Allah’s name Al-Qayyum.

Allah’s name Al-Qayyum (القيوم) has two elements:

1. Allah is self-sustaining, He needs no help ever from anything or anyone. Therefore, there is nothing that can influence Allah’s existence or the perfection of his attributes.

2. Allah is ever-sustainer; everything that exists needs Allah’s help and support for their existence and He is the only One Who has the authority for the decisions that impact and control everything that exists.

Linguistically Al-Qayyum (القيوم) means that Allah is the One who:

1. Stands alone as the master with full authorities and responsibilities for everything under His control, For Allah, everything in the universe and beyond is under His control.

2. Stands on his own and does not need any outside help to maintain his attributes

3. Stands without any change and cannot be eliminated or removed

4. Stands for justice and enforcer of His just judgement.

The name Al-Qayyum (القيوم) is related to Allah’s other names such as Al-Samad (ٱلْصَّمَدُ) (The needing of none and the satisfier of needs for all), Al-Muhaymin (ٱلْمُهَيْمِنُ) (the Guardian) and Al-Razzaq (ٱلْرَّزَّاقُ) (the Provider).

The combined names Al-Hayy and Al-Qayyum came in the Quran 3 times:

ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ‌ۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُ ۥ سِنَةٌ۬ وَلَا نَوۡمٌ۬‌ۚ لَّهُ ۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ  [البقرة : 255].

Allah! There is no god but He, the Ever Living, the Self-Sustaining and the Ever Sustainer. Neither dozing overtakes Him not sleep.  To Him belongs all that in the heavens and all that in the earth.” (Al-Baqara 2: 255)

ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ (٢) نَزَّلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ [آل عمران].

“Allah! There is no god but He, the Ever Living, the Self-Sustaining and the Ever Sustainer. (2) He has revealed to you the book in truth.” (Al-Emran 2:2-3)

وَعَنَتِ ٱلۡوُجُوهُ لِلۡحَىِّ ٱلۡقَيُّومِ‌ۖ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنۡ حَمَلَ ظُلۡمً۬ا  [طه : 111]

“All faces shall be humbled before (Allah)― the Ever Living, the Self-Sustaining and the Ever Sustainer, and the loser will be the one who bears (the burden of) injustice.” (Taha 20:111)

While Allah’s name Al- Qayyum came only in the Quran in these three places, Allah’s name Al-Hayy came by itself in two additional places:

وَتَوَڪَّلۡ عَلَى ٱلۡحَىِّ ٱلَّذِى لَا يَمُوتُ [الفرقان : 58].

“Put your trust in the Ever-Living who does not die.” (Al-Fourqan 25:58)

هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱدۡعُوهُ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَۗ [غافر : 65].

“He is the Ever-Living, there is no God but He.  Call upon Him, making (the practice of) the religion exclusive for Him.” (Ghafir 40:65)

Allah is the only One who can be described as Al-Hayy because everything else starts their life from a state of non-existence and end their life to a state of nonexistence. Also, Allah Al-Hayy is the source of life for all living things, and He is the One who created both life and death as He said:

ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلاً)  سورة الملك(

“He who created death and life, so that He may test as which of you is better in his deeds.” (Al-Mulk 67:2)

The life of all human beings started from non-existence; Allah says:

هَلْ أَتَى عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئاً مَذْكُوراً   )الإنسان(

“There has come upon man a period in which he was nothing worth mentioning.” (Al-Insan 76:1)

Also, everything that exist will end to nothing and only Allah will remain:

كُلُّ مَنۡ عَلَيۡہَا فَانٍ۬ (٢٦) وَيَبۡقَىٰ وَجۡهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلۡجَلَـٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ  )الرحمن(

“All that is on earth will perish. (26) And only your Lord’s Face will remain, Full of Majesty, Full of Honor.” (Al-Rahman 55:26-27)

كُلُّ شَىۡءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجۡهَهُ ۥ‌ۚ لَهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ  )  القصص)

“Everything (that exists) is going to perish except His Face. To Him belongs the Command, and to Him you (all) will return.” (Al-Qasas 28:88)

If you put your trust on anyone other than Allah, such a person will die someday and leave you.  But intelligent people put their trust on Allah because He will always be there because He is Al-Hayy, the Ever-Living:

وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ )سورة الفرقان)

“Put your trust in the Ever-Living who does not die.” (Al-Fourqan 25:58)

Allah Al-Qayyum (القيوم) is responsible for all phases of the life of all creations. He decides when they come into existence and when they die and as long as they are living, He is responsible for providing them with all that is necessary for their survival.  Allah says:

وَمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا كُلٌّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ )سورة هود(

“There is no moving creature on earth, but its sustenance depends on Allah: He knows its permanent and its temporary place. Everything is in a clear Record.” (Hud 11:6)

To appreciate Allah, Al-Qayyum (القيوم), let us consider that you were given the responsibility of being a Qayyum over your street. This means that you are responsible for everyone’s food, water, and air.  You are also responsible for operating everyone’s bodily functions such as breathing, digestion, blood filtration and blood circulation systems, etc. In addition, you are also responsible for the air composition and the ozone protection.  And don’t overlook that you are also responsible for every pregnant woman to protect her fetus and ensure that when she delivers, she will have milk that is suitable for the infant.  Be sure to also take care of every inspect, bird, animal, and plant in your street. These are some of the responsibilities that you will have to take care of if you are Qayyum over one street.  To fulfill this responsibility, you obviously, can never die or even get sick. Now, consider Allah who is Qayyum over all the universe whether they reside on earth, in earth, in seas, in other planets at the same time and all the time.

أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَائِمٌ عَلَى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ بِظَاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ

“Is He Who Qayyum (standing, watchful) over every soul and over all that it does (equal to their false deities)?  Yet, they ascribe partners to Allah. Say: “Give their names.  Is it that you will inform Him of something He does know on earth, or is it (just) empty words?” (Al-R’ad 13:33)

In order for Allah Al-Qayyum (القيوم), to control all things all the time, He must have the additional and very unique attribute: (﴿لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ “slumber does not overtake Him, nor does sleep.”

Nothing in the universe but is under Allah’s control all the time and nothing is out of His sight even for a split second.  If Allah ignores things for a split second, the whole universe will be destroyed.   Bani Israel asked Prophet Moses: Does your God sleep?  Allah inspired Moses to bring two glass bottles and let one of the people to hold them in his hands and ensure that he does not drop them.  When the man slept, the glass bottles fell and broke.  This is what will happen if the one standing in control over the earth and heavens dozes even a little, the whole universe will be destroyed.

It is known that most car accidents happen because the driver gets distracted for a mere second and therefore the 3 second rule for safe following distance is established to allow the car driver one second to react under good driving conditions at about 30 miles per hour.   Imagine if you are driving a vehicle whose weight is 6 billion trillion metric tons at a speed of 67,000 miles/hr.  This is the weight of the earth and the speed of the earth around the sun.  So, if Allah dozes a split second the earth moves off its track or even if the speed is not held constant and changes a little, nothing will be stationary on earth.

To appreciate the nature the role and the relationship between us and Allah, Allah is the master, and we are His slaves. Who should be staying up all the time taking care of the other’s affairs?  Should the master be staying up all night to meet the needs of his slave or the slave should be the one staying up all night to meet the needs of his master?

But Allah, the Master stays awake all the time to take care of all our needs while we, His slaves, sleep.   Who is running your heart while you are sleeping, who is running your lungs while you are sleeping, who is controlling the very complicated chemical plant in your body while you are sleeping, who ensures that all your defensive systems are ready to repel any foreign attack against your body while you are sleeping.

The slaves go to sleep and have dreams while the Master does not even doze for a split second.  Shouldn’t we be honored by being His slaves! Our Master, Allah Al-Hyy Al-Qayyun is telling us go to sleep, have a rest because I am standing and awake all the time for you.  Allah, Al-Qayyum is not only awake all the time, but He has full control over all things that exist in the universe because (لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ); to Him belong all things that are in the heavens and on earth.  This should make you comfortable that nothing will ever be out of His control because He is the creator of all that exists and in control of all that exists all the time. Allah says:

اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ )  الزمر(

“Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the trustee of all things.” (Al-Zumur 39:62)

Allah is Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum, is there anyone who deserves to be worshipped other than Him!  Is there anyone that should be loved more than Him!   True Monotheism means that we cannot associate anyone or anything “with” Allah.   A true believer cannot love anything “with” Allah.  Yes, we can love many things “for” Allah (الحب في الله) but not “with” Allah (الحب مع الله). We love the Prophet (PBUH), the companions, the scholars, the righteous people, we love the House of Allah, the Book of Allah, we love Ramadan, and we love every good deed for Allah but not with Allah.

The love with Allah (الحب مع الله) is the core of shirk. If you violate Allah’s commands because of your love of someone or because you expect a benefit from someone, you will be loving that person with Allah, and this is Shirk.   When Allah selects special times, spaces, or people, it is not intended to make them unique but rather to make them examples for all times, all places, and all people. We love these times, spaces and men for Allah but not with Allah.

When you go to Mecca and enjoy the spirituality and nearness to Allah, you should feel similarly in other places because Allah is everywhere.  When we come regularly to the House of Allah in Ramadan, is it because of our love of Ramadan or because our love of Allah. If we love coming to Masjid because of Allah, the Masjid is the house of Allah in Ramadan and in other than Ramadan.  But if you love coming because of Ramadan, this is love with Allah and this is Shirk.

The one person who loved the Prophet (PBUH) more than anyone else and the Prophet (PBUH) loved him more than anyone else is Sayedna Abu Bakr, but when the Prophet (PBUH) died, he said:

من كان يعبد محمداً (من دون أي لقب) فإن محمداً قد مات ومن كان يعبد الله فإن الله حي لا يموت

“Whoever worshipped Mohammad, Mohammad died (without giving any title for him) but whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and will never die”.

This shows the true level of Abu-Bakr’s belief in Allah.  He knew exactly who the Prophet is and who Allah is.  He loved the Prophet (PBUH) greatly, but he never had any element of Shirk, even a small or hidden one in his heart.  Abu Bakr loved the Prophet (PBUH) but He worshipped the Ever-Living God. The Prophet (PBUH) warned us of the hidden shirk as he said:

أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي الشرك الخفي

“My worst fear on my nation is the hidden shirk”.

But Allah is not only Ever-Living, He is also Qayyum who has control over all things. Therefore, how can a believer in Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum ever fear.   In fact, fear is caused by shirk.  Allah says:

سَنُلۡقِى فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلرُّعۡبَ بِمَآ أَشۡرَڪُواْ بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمۡ يُنَزِّلۡ بِهِۦ سُلۡطَـٰنً۬ا‌ۖ

“We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they ascribe unto Allah partners, for which He had sent no authority.” (Al-Imran 3:151)

If you are with Allah, Al-Hayy, your heart will be alive, and you will always be in a state of tranquility and comfort.  Allah says:

ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَطۡمَٮِٕنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ أَلَا بِذِڪۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَٮِٕنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ )الرّعد(

“Those who believed and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah, Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest” (Al-Ra’d 13:28)

Since the death that we know is just a transition to another life, the question is whether, we will be with the Ever-Living God, Al-Hayy, to see Him

وُجُوهٌ۬ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ نَّاضِرَةٌ (٢٢) إِلَىٰ رَبِّہَا نَاظِرَةٌ۬

“Some faces that Day shall be shining and radiant. (22) Looking at their Lord.” (Al-Qiyamah 22-23)

Or will be of those who will be shielded from Him.

كَلَّا‌ۖ بَلۡۜ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِہِم مَّا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ (١٤) كَلَّآ إِنَّہُمۡ عَن رَّبِّہِمۡ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ لَّمَحۡجُوبُونَ

“Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts. (14) Nay, but surely on that day they will be veiled from seeing their Lord” (Al-Mutafifeen 83:14-15)

In our lives, we may make things but lose control over them either by us getting rid of them or by us dying and leaving them.  But Allah creates everything and maintains the control over them all the time. For Allah, everything is under His full control

وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطًا

What is in the heavens and in the earth belongs to Allah. Allah encompasses all things. (Al-Nisa 4: 126)

We should never forget that whatever happens to us does so by Allah’s will and is surely ordained for a purpose. We have no recourse other than taking refuge in Him because there is no protector or helper other than Him:

أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ

Do you not know that Allah is He to Whom the kingdom of the heavens and the earth belong and that, besides Allah, you have no protector and no helper? (al-Baqara 2: 107)

We can only assure our protection by seeking it from Allah because He is in full control over all things, and He does not share this control with anyone.

وَلَا يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَدًا  ) الكهف (

He does not share His Command with anyone”. (Al-Kahf 18:26)

The belief that Allah is in control of all things and that He does not share this control with anyone else is very critical because it differentiates between pure Monotheism and shirk.  You should know that nothing will ever happen to you except by the will of Allah because there is no place or moment in the universe independent of Allah. Therefore, relying on and putting our trust in the One Who is in control is key in facing anything in your life, Allah teaches us to say:

قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا هُوَ مَوْلَانَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ

Say: “Nothing can happen to us except what Allah has ordained for us. He is Our Master. It is in Allah that the believers should put their trust.” (At-Tawba 9:51)

Allah’s names Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum is considered by interpreting the hadith of the Prophet (PBUH) to be the greatest name of Allah if He is called upon thereby, He answers and if He is asked thereby, He gives.

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( اسْمُ اللَّهِ الأَعظَمُ فِي سُوَرٍ مِنَ القُرآنِ ثَلَاثٍ : فِي ” البَقَرَةِ ” وَ ” آلِ عِمرَانَ ” وَ ” طَهَ ” ) .رواه ابن ماجه

“The greatest name of Allah is in three surat of the Qur’an: al-Baqarah, Aal ‘Imran and Ta-Ha.” (Ibn Maajah) (The name in these three Surat is Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum)

It was narrated from Anas that he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), and a man was praying then he said in supplication:

عن أنسٍ رضي الله عنه أن رجلًا دعا فقال : اللهمَّ إني أسألُك بأنَّ لك الحمدُ، لا إله إلا أنت المنَّان، بديعُ السماوات والأرضِ، يا ذا الجلال والإكرام، يا حيُّ يا قيوم، فقال النبي ﷺ : «لقد دعا باسمِه الأعظم الذي إذا دُعيَ به أجاب، وإذا سُئل به أعطى ».

“O Allah, I ask You by virtue of the fact that all praise is due to You; there is no god but You, the Bestower, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of majesty and honor, Ya Hayy, Y Qayyum”.

The Prophet (PBUH) said: “He has asked Allah by His greatest name which, if He is called upon thereby, He answers and if He is asked thereby, He gives.” (Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawood, Al-Nasaa’i and Ibn Maajah)

Elements to Adopt in our Character

1/ By understanding the meaning of Allah Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum, you should call upon him with these names when you face any hardship. Whenever the Prophet (PBUH) faced any hardship, he used to supplicate to Allah with these two names.  It is reported by Anas Ibn Malik that whenever anything happens that distresses the Prophet (PBUH), He would say:

“كان النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم إذا كربه أمر قال: يا حي يا قيوم برحمتك أستغيث”

“Ya Hayy – Ya Qayyum, I take refuge in Your mercy.” (Ibn Hibban)

The Prophet (PBUH) advised his daughter Fatima to make the following Dua every morning and every evening:

عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لفاطمة رضي الله عنها : قولي إذا أصبحت وإذا أمسيت : يا حي يا قيوم برحمتك أستغيث ، أصلح لي شأني كله ، ولا تكلني إلى نفسي طرفة عين.  ]رواه النسائي والحاكم في المستدرك والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات ، وغيرهم.[

‘Ya Hayy Ya Qayyum by Your mercy I seek assistance, rectify for me all of my affairs and do not leave me to myself, even for the blink of an eye.

Imam Ibn Al-Qayyim said: “Asking Allah by His names Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum has a great effect in Him answering your supplications, and in relieving any difficulties or hardships.  Therefore, ask Allah with these names to restore any weakness of your life, meaning any weakness in your health or to remove any pain that affects your abilities and actions”.

2/ Invoke Allah’s name Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum to give spiritual life to your heart because our hearts need to be alive to know the truth when one commits a sin or any bad act. If the heart is dead, it will not feel this pain of regret.

3/ Have firm trust that Al-Hayy Al–Qayyum will take care of your affairs and bring ease to you by always reflecting on His greatness, and perfection and the extent of what He provides to you and every one of His creations.

4/ Do your best to be Qayyum on others, extend a helping hand to others. Bring ease to others whenever you can.

title: Religion (الدين) and Religiosity(التدين)
