content:
Surat Al-Hijr (الحجر) (Thamoud’s Habitation) (15:1-99)

Surat Al-Hijr was revealed in Makkah after Surat Yusuf (يوسف). It was revealed in a time when the Prophet (PBUH) and his companions were subjected to all forms of verbal and physical abuse. The Theme of the Surat is that Allah is the protector.

The Surat was revealed to reassure the Prophet (PBUH), his companions and all his future followers that Allah will always protect them and grant victory to His religion. The Surat motivates the believers not to be afraid or overwhelmed by the power and influence of their enemies. They should not get distracted or distressed by any verbal attacks and ridicule. They should persevere and stay on the straight path and focus their efforts on delivering the message of Allah.

In the beginning of the Surah, Allah says:

الٓر‌ۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ وَقُرۡءَانٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (١) رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُواْ لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ (٢) ذَرْهُمْ يَأْكُلُوا وَيَتَمَتَّعُوا وَيُلْهِهِمُ الْأَمَلُ ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ (٣)

Alif-Laâm-Ra. These are the Ayat (Verses) of the Book, and a clear Quran. (1) How often will those who disbelieve wish that they were Muslims. (2) Let them eat and enjoy life, and let them be preoccupied with (false) hope for they shall soon come to know (their ultimate end). (Al-Hijr 15:1-3)

At the end of the Surah, Allah says:

فَٱصۡدَعۡ بِمَا تُؤۡمَرُ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ (٩٤) إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ (٩٥) الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ ۚ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ (٩٦) وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ (٩٧) فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُن مِّنَ السَّاجِدِينَ (٩٨) وَاعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ (٩٩)

Proclaim openly that which you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists. (94) Surely, We are sufficient for you against those who mock (you and your religion), (95) Those who set up another god along with Allah, but they shall soon come to know (the reality). (96) We know that your heart feels distressed from what they say (97) So, glorify the praises of your Lord, and be among those who prostrate themselves (before Him) (98) and worship your Lord until comes to you the certainty (i.e., death). (Al-Hijr 15:94-99)

These verses reiterate that Muslims should not be distracted by any derogatory and insulting comments. Muslims should have full trust that Allah is sufficient to take care of those who mock the Prophet (PBUH) or the religion of Islam (إِنَّا كَفَيۡنَـٰكَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَہۡزِءِينَ). The best proof that Allah is the protector of his religion is to see how many people throughout history who made insulting and derogatory statements against the Prophet (PBUH) became Muslims and served Islam beyond expectations.

Let us look at to one example from the time of the Prophet (PBUH) and this is the example of Suhayl ibn ‘Amr (سهيل بن عمرو) who was the most eloquent orator in Mecca and a man whose opinion carried weight among his people. He dedicated his gift to insulting the Prophet (PBUH) and mocking Islam.

In the battle of Badr, he was taken as prisoner. Syedana Omar suggested to the Prophet (PBUH) that they should pull out his front teeth to disable him from speaking against the Prophet (PBUH) in the future. But Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) whom Allah said about him “وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ إِلَّا رَحۡمَةً۬ لِّلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ” “We have not sent you but a mercy for all the worlds” (Al-Anbiya 21:107) refused and told Omar: “I would not mutilate anyone lest Allah mutilates me even though I am His Prophet.” And said: “Omar, perhaps Suhayl will do something in the future that will please you.”

As you know Suhayl ibn ‘Amr was the man representing Quraysh in the famous truce of Hudaybiyyah. When the agreement was being written, Suhayl refused to include in it the word Mohammad the messenger of Allah and insisted that it will only include Mohammad ibn Abdullah. He also imposed in this agreement several difficult requirements on Muslims that caused distress to many Muslims including Sayedna Omar.

When the Prophet (PBUH) entered Mecca victorious and in a voice full of compassion and tenderness asked: (يا معشر قريش، ما تظنون أني فاعل بكم؟) “O people of the Quraysh! What do you think I will do with you?”

It was Suhayl ibn Amr who replied: (نظن خيراً، أخ كريم وابن أخ كريم) “We think well, noble brother, son of a noble brother”. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “Go, for you are free (اذهبوا فأنتم الطلقاء).” Moved by the Prophet’s unsurpassed compassion, nobility and greatness Suhayl ibn Amr announced his Islam and submission to Allah. In spite of his late acceptance of Islam, he was transformed into a selfless worshipper and a great fighter in the path of Allah.

When the Prophet (PBUH) passed away, the Muslims everywhere were plunged into a state of confusion and dismay. In Madinah, Sayedna Abu Bakr quelled the confusion with his decisive words: “Whoever worships Mohammad, Mohammad is dead. And whoever worships Allah; Allah is indeed Living and will never die.”

In Makkah, Suhayl performed the same role. He called the Muslims together and in his brilliant and salutary style, he affirmed to them that Mohammad (PBUH) was indeed the Messenger of Allah and that he did not die until he had discharged his trust and propagated the message and that was the duty of all believers after his death to apply themselves persistently by following his example and way of life. He ended his speech to the people of Quraysh by saying:

يا معشر قريش، لا تكونوا آخر من أسلم وأول من ارتد، والله إن هذا الدين ليمتدن امتداد الشمس والقمر من طلوعهما إلى غروبهما في ظلام طويل

O people of Quraysh do not be the last to become Muslims and the first to recoil. By Allah, this religion will extend as broad as the extension of the Sun and Moon from their rise to their setting.

When the news of Suhayl’s stand in Makkah and of his persuasive speech reached the Muslims of Madinah, Omar ibn al-Khattab remembered the words of the Prophet (PBUH) and said: The day had come when Islam benefitted from the two middle teeth of Suhayl that Omar wanted to pull out.

A recent example from our time is the Dutch politician Arnoud Van Doorn who produced an anti-Islam Film entitled ‘Fitna’ (sedition) in which Islam is portrayed as a religion of violence and terrorism and depicted Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) with a bomb on his head. The same Arnoud Van Doorn declared his Islam after reading more about Islam and performed Hajj and said: “I felt ashamed standing in front of the Prophet’s grave. I thought of the grave mistake which I had made by producing that sacrilegious film. I hope that my tears of regret will wash out all my sins. I hope that Allah will forgive me and accept my repentance.” He later produced an international film entitled ‘Mohammad: Master of Human Beings’, that highlights the noble traits of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH).

Another recent example of a person who was the worst Islamophobe in Europe is Joram van Klaveren who became Muslim and is now the strongest voice in support of Islam in Europe. He wrote a good book entitled “Apostate: From Christianity to Islam in time of secularism and terror.

Truly Allah is sufficient to stand against those who mock the Prophet (PBUH) and the religion of Islam. Our reaction to negative comments by others is to focus on our own worship through Dhikr, prostrating to Allah, and ensuring that we remain steadfast and consistent in our actions until the end of our life as Allah instructed us.

فَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّـٰجِدِينَ (٩٨) وَٱعۡبُدۡ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَكَ ٱلۡيَقِينُ (٩٩)

Glorify the praises of your Lord and be of those who prostrate themselves (to Him). And worship your Lord until there comes unto you the certainty (i.e., death). (Al-Hijr 15:98-99)

These commands are not only provided in this Surah, but they are also provided in Surah al-Imran whose theme is the perseverance on the path of Allah (التبات على هذا المنهج) against both intellectual confusion and materialistic temptations. In Surah Al-Imran, Allah commands that Muslims responds to insults and propaganda by patience and Taqwa as He said:

لَتُبۡلَوُنَّ فِىٓ أَمۡوَٲلِڪُمۡ وَأَنفُسِڪُمۡ وَلَتَسۡمَعُنَّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِڪُمۡ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَڪُوٓاْ أَذً۬ى كَثِيرً۬ا‌ۚ وَإِن تَصۡبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ فَإِنَّ ذَٲلِكَ مِنۡ عَزۡمِ ٱلۡأُمُورِ

“You shall certainly be tried and tested in your wealth and properties and in your personal selves, and you shall certainly hear a lot that will grieve you from those who received the Scripture before you and from the idolaters, but if you persevere and have Taqwa, then that is of the determining factor in heart of all matters”. (Al-Imran 3:186)

The Surah gives comfort to the believers that there are several things that Allah took responsibility for their preservation and protection, and these are essential for human survival in this life and success in the Hereafter. Six things were identified in this Surat:

First: The preservation of the Quran, the final guide to mankind and its protection from any form of corruption:

إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ ۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ (٩)

Indeed, We are Who have sent down the Dhikr (i.e. the Qur’an) and surely, We will guard it (from corruption) (Al-Hir 15:9)

This verse confirms that Allah is the one who will preserve His Book, the Quran, and He will also be the one who will protect those who follow the book and invite others to it.

Second: The preservation of the beauty of heaven for mankind to enjoy and protecting it from any Satan who attempts to listen to news about the future and confuse people in their belief:

وَلَقَدۡ جَعَلۡنَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجً۬ا وَزَيَّنَّـٰهَا لِلنَّـٰظِرِينَ (١٦) وَحَفِظۡنَـٰهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيۡطَـٰنٍ۬ رَّجِيمٍ (١٧) إِلَّا مَنِ ٱسۡتَرَقَ ٱلسَّمۡعَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ۥ شِہَابٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (١٨)

And indeed, We have put grand constellations in the heaven and We beautified it for the beholders. (16) And We have guarded it from the intrusion of every outcast devil. (17) And whoever sneaks to listen is pursued by a clear flaming fire. (Al-Hijr 15:16-18)

Third: The preservation of the earth to make it suitable for mankind.

ٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَدَدۡنَـٰهَا وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا فِيهَا رَوَٲسِىَ (١٩)

“And the earth, We have spread out and placed in it firm mountains.” (15:19).

Fourth: The creation and protection of rizq (sustenance) on this earth for the survival of all the creations on it:

وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَدَدۡنَـٰهَا وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا فِيهَا رَوَٲسِىَ وَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيہَا مِن كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ مَّوۡزُونٍ۬ (١٩) وَجَعَلۡنَا لَكُمۡ فِيہَا مَعَـٰيِشَ وَمَن لَّسۡتُمۡ لَهُ ۥ بِرَٲزِقِينَ (٢٠)

And the earth, We have spread out and placed in it firm mountains and caused to grow therein all kinds of things in due proportion. (19) And We created in it sources of sustenance for you and for those for whose sustenance you are not responsible. (20)

وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا عِندَنَا خَزَآٮِٕنُهُ ۥ وَمَا نُنَزِّلُهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا بِقَدَرٍ۬ مَّعۡلُومٍ۬ (٢١) وَأَرۡسَلۡنَا ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ لَوَٲقِحَ فَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ فَأَسۡقَيۡنَـٰكُمُوهُ وَمَآ أَنتُمۡ لَهُ ۥ بِخَـٰزِنِينَ (٢٢)

And there is not a thing, but its treasures are with Us; but We do not send it down except in a determined measure. (21) And We send the winds fertilizing, and causing water to descend from the sky, and gave it to you to drink and you are not able to store it.” (15: 19-22)

The Ayat (فَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ فَأَسۡقَيۡنَـٰكُمُوهُ وَمَآ أَنتُمۡ لَهُ ۥ بِخَـٰزِنِينَ) is an interesting Ayat. The common interpretation for it is that people cannot store the water that Allah sends to them from the sky and the interpreters suggest that the verse indicates that Allah is the One Who stores the water for them in rivers, springs, and underground. But we know the people have collected rainwater and stored it, though obviously not all of it.

However, a serious examination of the Ayat suggests that Allah is not talking about the rainwater in general but only the specific water that we drink as implied by the word (فَأَسۡقَيۡنَـٰكُمُوهُ) that means *gave it to you to drink or make you drink it). The Ayat suggests that our body cannot store the water we drink. This Ayat is a sign from Allah to demonstrate the divinity of the Quran because the inability of our body to store the water we drink is highly scientific medical issue. It is now known that a human body which is made of about 70% water. Since we cannot store the water we drink, we need fresh supplies of water every day. Water is necessary for blood, digestive fluids, urine, and perspiration, and is contained in lean muscle, fat and bones. But almost all the water we drink every day is lost through the lungs, skin, urine, and stool. If the body of a person retains water, this is a sign of kidney, heart, or liver diseases.

Fifth: The protection of the believers from Satan:

Stories that are mentioned in any Surat are intended to stress the objectives of the Surat. The story of Adam and Iblis are presented in many Surat including this one. But in others surahs the focus was on Adam and in this Surat, Al-Hijr, the focus is on Iblis himself as presented in verses 31-40 to let us know that even Satan knows that He has no influence on the believers because they are under the protection of Allah:

قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَغۡوَيۡتَنِى لَأُزَيِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَأُغۡوِيَنَّہُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ (٣٩) إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنۡہُمُ ٱلۡمُخۡلَصِينَ (٤٠) قَالَ هَـٰذَا صِرَٲطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسۡتَقِيمٌ (٤١) إِنَّ عِبَادِى لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْغَاوِينَ (٤٢)

[Iblîs (Satan)] said: “O my Lord! Because you allowed me to go astray, I shall beautify for them evil on the earth, and shall lead all of them astray. (39) Except Your chosen slaves among them. (40) “(Allah) said: “This is the Way which will lead straight to Me. (41) Certainly, you shall have no authority over My slaves, except those of the deviators who will follow you.” (15:39-42)

Sixth: It is further gratifying that Allah is protecting the believers from the Hellfire and preserving paradise for them:

إِنَّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَعُيُونٍ (٤٥) ٱدۡخُلُوهَا بِسَلَـٰمٍ ءَامِنِينَ (٤٦) وَنَزَعۡنَا مَا فِى صُدُورِهِم مِّنۡ غِلٍّ إِخۡوَٲنًا عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ۬ مُّتَقَـٰبِلِينَ (٤٧) لَا يَمَسُّہُمۡ فِيہَا نَصَبٌ۬ وَمَا هُم مِّنۡہَا بِمُخۡرَجِينَ (٤٨)

“Indeed, those who have Taqwa will be in gardens and springs. (45) (It will be said to them): “Enter here (Paradise) in peace and security”. (46) And We have removed whatever malice they have in their hearts, (thus making them) brothers, sitting on thrones facing each other. (47) No sense of fatigue shall touch them, nor shall they (ever) be asked to leave from there.” (15:45-48)

The believers should have full sense of security that Allah is not only protecting the book that serves as their divine guidance on earth, but He is also protecting them from Satan and preserving for them all the means for their survival in earth and happiness in the Hereafter. With all these protections, how can a believer ever feel afraid or depressed.

After all the levels of protection that Allah has established for the believers, the Surat discussed the accounts of several nations who rejected their messengers and deserved Allah’s punishments. Then Allah gives warning to those Muslims who fragment the Quran and follow parts of it and disregard others, He says in verses 89 to 93:

وَقُلۡ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱلنَّذِيرُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (٨٩) كَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡمُقۡتَسِمِينَ (٩٠) ٱلَّذِينَ جَعَلُواْ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ عِضِينَ (٩١) فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَسۡـَٔلَنَّہُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ (٩٢) عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ (٩٣)

And say: “I am indeed a plain warner.” (89) Such as We send down for those who make division, (90) Those who break the Qur’an into parts. (91) So, by your Lord, We shall question all of them, (92) Of what they used to do. (Al-Hijr 15:89-93)

As final comment, why the Surat that focuses on Allah’s protection was given the name (Al-Hijr) (the rocky valley) referring to the tribe of Thamud, the people of Prophet Saleh, who were destroyed. Also, why those people specifically when the Surat included the account of others who were also destroyed such as the people of Prophet Lot and the People of Prophet Shu’aib (people of Madyan)?

The reason of selecting the name may be to emphasize the point that there is no protection except through Allah because in the case of the tribe of Thamud who rejected their Prophet Saleh and did not heed his warnings were convinced that they are secure from Allah’s punishment building their houses in the mountains of Al-Hijr, the ‘rocky valley’. But no wall or mountain was able to protect them from the punishment of Allah. Allah reminds us of this account in verses 80 to 84.

وَلَقَدۡ كَذَّبَ أَصۡحَـٰبُ ٱلۡحِجۡرِ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (٨٠) وَءَاتَيۡنَـٰهُمۡ ءَايَـٰتِنَا فَكَانُواْ عَنۡہَا مُعۡرِضِينَ (٨١) وَكَانُواْ يَنۡحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا ءَامِنِينَ (٨٢) فَأَخَذَتۡہُمُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ مُصۡبِحِينَ (٨٣) فَمَآ أَغۡنَىٰ عَنۡہُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ (٨٤)

“And verily, the dwellers of Al-Hijr (the stone valley) denied the Messengers. (80) We provided them with Our Signs, but they turned away from them. (81) They used to carve out houses from the mountains (thinking themselves) secure in them. (82) But the deadly blast seized them then in the early morning. (83) So, Whatever affluence they had earned did not avail them.” (15:80-84).

If we are wise and truly believe in the Quran, we will realize that the only protection for us and for our loved ones is from Allah. This is the message of Surat.

content:
The Rise and Return of Jesus Between Affirmation and Denial

The return of Jesus (PBUH) to kill the antichrist (Dajjal) and rule over the world has been well accepted by Muslims for centuries, but during the last century a group of Muslim scholars denied the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) based on what they mainly argued four reasons:

1. The return of Jesus is not mentioned in the Quran.
2. The authenticity of all the hadith that discusses the return of Jesus Christ to kill the dajjal and rule over the Muslims is questionable.
3. Accepting this opinion reinforces the foundational Christian dogma that justifies the divinity of Jesus. This suggests that the idea has creeped in the Islamic knowledge from Christianity.
4. Since Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is the last prophet as clearly stated in the Quran, the return of Jesus contradicts the Quran.

The vast number of scholars who support the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) make their decision based on five reasons:

1. The return of Jesus (PBUH) is clearly stated in massively transmitted hadith that discuss the major signs of the day of Judgement. The return was reported by 10 of the Prophet’s companions in about 70 hadith. Twenty-nine (29) of these hadith are considered authentic based on the different hadith authentication criteria, and several are reported in both Bukhari and Muslim. About 40 hadith are designated authentic by some scholars and weak by others based on their rating of the accuracy of the narrators. (Some Hadith are given in Appendix 1)
2. Refuting the authenticity of all these hadith leads to refuting many of the major signs of the Day of Judgement such as the coming of the antichrist (the Dajjal), the Mehdi and the obliteration of Gog and Magog (يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ) as major signs of the Day of Judgement. Note that Gog and Magog (يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ) are mentioned in the Quran in both Surat Al-Kahf (18:94) and Surat Al-Anbiya (21:966).
3. The rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) are implied in over 10 verses in the Quran.
4. The return of Jesus does not contradict that Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is the last prophet because when Jesus returns, he will return as a follower of Prophet Mohammad and merely serve as a Khalifa for the Muslims.
5. The rise and return of Jesus refute the claims by the Jews that they killed him and negates a fundamental pillar of Christianity regarding the original sin and importance of Jesus’s death to cleanse people from this sin and thus it negates the divinity of Jesus.

There is danger in discussing an unseen issue like this that has no spiritual or practical value to be gained, other than creating division among Muslims. Worst is that many scholars condemn those who deny the return of Jesus as kafir (disbeliever) because they consider believing in the return of Jesus is a matter of Aqidah (belief) since it has reference in the Quran that has been expounded with mass transmitted hadith that are clear and unambiguous. This raises an important question regarding whether believing in the return of Jesus is really an element of Aqidah.

Any element of Aqidah must be derived from a mass transmitted knowledge (الخبر المتواتر) that is clear and unambiguous. Therefore, they should be no differing opinions about it among Muslim scholars. Since scholars differed with both sides presenting their basis, the matter should not be treated as element of Aqidah. But those who believe in the return of Jesus accuse those who deny it as kafir because they reject what the prophet (PBUH) said and argue that accepting what the Prophet (PBUH) said is an element of Aqidah because Allah commands in many verses that we should obey the Prophet (PBUH) and that he does not say out of his own desires.

However, the assertion that those who deny the return of Jesus are rejecting what the Prophet (PBUH) said is misrepresentation of their position because none of them reject any saying of the Prophet (PBUH), they reject the authenticity of the narrations and believe that the Prophet (PBUH) never said these narrations. It is, however, unfortunate that those who deny the return of Jesus do not offer good reasons for rejecting the hadith that affirms the return. They neither argue against the credibility of the narrators which is the “Sanad” nor against the meaning of the hadith which is the “Matn” since these hadith discuss something of the future.

In addition, the lack of explicit statements in the Quran regarding the rise and return of Jesus does not justify rejecting the hadith as basis because the role of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) was to explain some of the non-explicit verses as Allah commanded him to do by saying

وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلذِّڪۡرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيۡہِمۡ

“And We sent down the Reminder (The Quran) to you, so that you explain to the people what has been revealed to them” (Al-Nahl 14:44)

Keeping this discussion in mind, my objective of making this presentation is to engage in an intellectual analysis to show how people can look at the same text and give different interpretations. But, since the group who denies the rise and return of Jesus reject the authenticity of all the hadith that provide many specific details about the return, I plan to solely consider the applicable verses of the Quran.

1. Surat Al-Emran Verse 45

إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ يَـٰمَرۡيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ۬ مِّنۡهُ ٱسۡمُهُ ٱلۡمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ وَجِيہً۬ا فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأَخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ (٤٥)

“And (Recall) when the angels said: “O Mary, Allah gives you the good news of a Word from Him whose name is the Messiah Jesus, the son of Mary, a man of honor in this world and in the Hereafter, and among those who are near (to Allah).” (Al-Emran 3:45)

The key terms in this verse are: (وَجِيهً۬ا فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأَخِرَةِ) ”a man of honor in this world and in the Hereafter”, and (وَمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ) “among those who are near (to Allah)”

Those who believe in the rise and return of Jesus point out to the phrase (وَجِيهً۬ا فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأَخِرَةِ) ”honored in this life and in the Hereafter” and suggest that while Jesus (PBUH) was not honored by all people in this life when he was on earth, he must return to earth to rule and be honored in this life. They also state since Jesus (PBUH) is being (مِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ) “among those who are near to Allah’ this implies that he was physically raised to heaven to become physically near to Allah.

But Those who deny the rise and return propose that (وَمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ) means that Jesus is near to Allah in status and not physically near to Him. They suggest that Jesus (PBUH) is not unique regarding him being (وَمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ) since Allah states that all the righteous people are near to Him:

فَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ (٨٨) فَرَوۡحٌ۬ وَرَيۡحَانٌ۬ وَجَنَّتُ نَعِيمٍ۬ (٨٩)

“Thus, if he is from among those who are near (to Allah), (88) Then (for him) there are comfort and fragrance and garden of bliss.” (Al-Waqia 56:88-89)

Regarding Jesus being (وَجِيهً۬ا) “honored”, thy argue that he is honored by Allah and not necessarily by all people. Jesus (PBUH) in this case is similar to prophet Moses who was not honored in this life by all people, but he is honored by Allah as Allah said using the same term (وَجِيهً۬ا):

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَاذَوۡاْ مُوسَىٰ فَبَرَّأَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِمَّا قَالُواْ‌ۚ وَكَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَجِيہً۬ا (٦٩)

“O you who Believe, be not like those who slandered Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they alleged, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.” (Al-Ahzab 33:69)

However, those who believe in the rise and return counter argue that the verse referring to Prophet Moses is nor relevant since the verse states that “he was honorable in the sight of Allah” (عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَجِيہً۬ا) while the verse regarding Jesus refers to him being “honorable in this life” (وَجِيهً۬ا فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا) and does limit his honor only to” the sight of Allah. Allah”.

2. Surat Maryam Verse 32

وَبَرَّۢا بِوَٲلِدَتِى وَلَمۡ يَجۡعَلۡنِى جَبَّارً۬ا شَقِيًّ۬ا (٣٢)

“And (He has made me) kind to my mother, and He did not make me tyrant or ill-fated. (Maryam 19:32) This statement was made by Jesus (PBUH) when he spoke in the cradle.

Those who believe in the rise and return suggest that by him stating that he is not (جَبَّارً۬ا) “tyrant” indicates that the people will accuse him of being tyrant and this accusation can only be committed against someone who is has control over the people. Since Jesus (PBUH) was example of humility during his time on earth, this accusation must be made after his return to fight the Dajjal and the disbelievers and rule over the world.

Those who deny the return suggest that by him refuting that he is not (جَبَّارً۬ا) “tyrant” is merely to emphasize his humility and remove the doubt in the mind of his enemies that his actions were motivated by his desire to be the king of the Jews.

3. Surat Al-Emran Verse 46

وَيُڪَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلۡمَهۡدِ وَڪَهۡلاً۬ وَمِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (٤٦)

“He shall speak to the people while still in the cradle and (Kahla’n) in maturity and he shall be one of the righteous.” (Al-Emran 3:46)

The dispute in the verse is in the definition of the word (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬). The general definition is that it is the stage beyond the youth age as indicated by gray hair. There is no single definition of the starting age of being (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬). The known definitions for the age of being (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬) are: 40 to 60, 35 to 55 and 30 to 40.

Those who believe in the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) consider the age of being (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬) starts at 40 years. Based on biblical references, Jesus (PBUH) died when he was 33 years old and thus, he must return and live to reach the age of 40. They also argue that by Allah declaring that Jesus (PBUH) will speak when he is (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬) is to emphasize his return since speaking at that age is common and there will be no reason for this declaration unless it adds a new meaning to the verse.

Those who deny the rise and the return of Jesus (PBUH) argue that age of being (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬) is from 30 to 40. Since Jesus mission ended when he was 33 years old, he was already (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬). Regarding the emphasis that he will speak when he is (kahla’n) (ڪَهۡلاً۬), they consider that this is merely to avoid someone from claiming that he was possessed by evil spirit when he spoke in the cradle and Allah wants to emphasize that he will also speak about Allah on his mature age.

4. Surat Al-Nisa verse 157

وَقَوۡلِهِمۡ إِنَّا قَتَلۡنَا ٱلۡمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَـٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمۡ‌ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ لَفِى شَكٍّ۬ مِّنۡهُ‌ۚ مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ‌ۚ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينَۢا (١٥٧)

“And for their (the Jews) saying: “We killed Messiah ‘Īsā (Jesus), son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah,” – while in fact that neither killed him nor crucified him, but they were deluded by resemblance. Those who disputed in this matter are full of doubts about it. They have no knowledge of it, they follow nothing but conjecture. It is certain that they did kill him. (Al-Nisa 4:157)

Those who believe in the rise and return interpret this verse to mean that Jesus (PBUH) was physically raised to Allah alive, body and spirit, since he was neither killed not crucified. The verse also indicates that even people at that time were confused about this matter and were not sure of the killing of Jesus. Supporting this suggestion is that Allah states that whoever was on the cross resembled Jesus (PBUH) but was not him.

Those who deny the rise and return argue that the verse only refutes the claim by the Jews that they killed him but does not refute that the Romans are the ones who killed. They also argue that if the verse refute that he was killed, it implies that he died naturally before he was put on the cross and thus the confusion is related to their thinking that they killed him while he was dead already. They also raise the question to those who believe that someone else was in the cross, if it was not Jesus, then who?

Those who believe in the rise and return respond to this question regarding who was in the cross by saying that Allah did inform us and thus any answer is mere speculation. They also suggest that those who ask who was on the cross miss an important teaching principle in the Quran, and it is not to waste our curiosity on issues that achieve no benefits, but we should direct it to what is beneficial for us mankind.

5. Surat Al-Emran Verse 55

إِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَـٰعِيسَىٰٓ إِنِّى مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُواْ

“Allah said: O Jesus! I am “Muwafeek” and raising you up to Me and cleansing you of those who disbelieve.” (Al-Emran 3:55)

Those who deny the rise and the return, insist that the term (مُتَوَفِّيكَ) “Muwafeek” means “making you die” and argue that for (مُتَوَفِّيكَ) “Muwafeek” to be interpreted as sleep or anything other than death, there must be additional qualification in the verse to confirm this definition, as in the following verse:

ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلۡأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوۡتِهَا وَٱلَّتِى لَمۡ تَمُتۡ فِى مَنَامِهَا‌ۖ فَيُمۡسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيۡہَا ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَيُرۡسِلُ ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّى‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٤٢)

“Allah (Ya’tawafa) takes away the souls at the time of their death, and of those who do not die in their sleep. Then He keeps those on whom He has decreed death, and sends others back, up to an appointed term.” (Al-Zumur 39:42)

They also suggest that the divine action (وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ) means “elevating your rank with Me” or “elevating your soul to Men” and not raising you alive.

Those who believe in the rise and return of Jesus interpret this word (مُتَوَفِّيكَ) “Muwafeek”, to mean “Taking you in full”, body and spirit. They argue that the term “wafa’at” (وفاة) does not always mean real death, but it refers to the state of in-action such as the state of sleeping as Allah says:

وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يَتَوَفَّٮٰڪُم بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا جَرَحۡتُم بِٱلنَّہَارِ ثُمَّ يَبۡعَثُڪُمۡ فِيهِ لِيُقۡضَىٰٓ أَجَلٌ۬ مُّسَمًّى‌ۖ

“He it is the One Who (Yatawafakoun) “recalls your souls” by night and know what you do by day, then He make you rise-up again so that a fixed term is fulfilled.” (Al-Ana’am 6:60)

They support this interpretation by the divine action (رَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ) “raising you up to Me”. And this raising cannot only be by the spirit because the spirit of every person will be raised to Allah. Therefore, the raising of Jesus (PBUH) must be unique, and this can only be by both body and spirit. In addition, by Allah saying (مُطَهِّرُكَ) “cleansing you” emphasizes that he was never placed in the cross because the Jewish teachings say that anyone who is placed on the cross is cursed (Deuteronomy 21:23). [anyone who is hung on a pole is under God’s curse.]

In addition, those who believe in the rise and return of Jesus argue that even if one is to consider (مُتَوَفِّيكَ) to mean “making you die” rejecting his return can be refuted because in the Arabic language the article (و) “and” between مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ (making you die and raising you up) does not imply sequence and thus the sequence can be as well “raising you up and making you die” (وَرَافِعُكَ وَمُتَوَفِّيكَ). As an example, Allah says:

وَلَقَدۡ رَٲوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيۡفِهِۦ فَطَمَسۡنَآ أَعۡيُنَہُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ (٣٧)

“And they tried to tempt him against his guest, but we blinded their eyes, Now taste you My punishment and My Warnings.” (Al-Qamar 54: 16) (Here the real sequence was first the warnings and then the punishment)

They also counter argue that (وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ) cannot mean “elevating your status with Me” because Allah used the term (إِلَىَّ) means “to Me” and it is not proper language to say: “elevating your status to Me” but the obvious meaning can only be “raising you physically to Me”. Also, it cannot only be raising the spirit because the spirit of every person will be raised to Allah. Therefore, the raising of Jesus (PBUH) must be unique.

6. Surat Al-Nisa Verse 158

بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡهِ‌ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمً۬ا (١٥٨)

“But Allah raised him up to Him. And Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise”. (Al-Nisa 4:158)

Regarding raising him up to Allah, the two opinions are presented in the previous discussion of verse 55 of Surat Al-Emran.

7. Surat Al-Nisa Verse 159

وَإِن مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ إِلَّا لَيُؤۡمِنَنَّ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ مَوۡتِهِۦ‌ۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيۡہِمۡ شَہِيدً۬ا (١٥٩)

And there is none of the people of the book (Jews and Christians) but must believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them” (Al-Nisa 4: 159)

The difference between those who support and those who deny the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) focuses on the word “his” in (قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ) “before his death”.

Those who believe in the rise and return argue that ‘his” refers to Jesus (PBUH) and thus he will return so every Christian and Jew will believe in him (Jesus) as man before Jesus dies natural death.

But those who deny the rise and return argue that the word “his” refers to every Christian and Jew who will believe in him (Jesus) as man at the time of his own (the person) death.

8. Surat Al-Zukhruf Verse 61

وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَعِلۡمٌ۬ لِّلسَّاعَةِ (٦١)

“And he shall be a Sign for the Hour (of Judgment).” (Al-Zukhruf 43:61)

The verse refers to Jesus (PBUH) as being a sign for the Hour (لَعِلۡمٌ۬ لِّلسَّاعَةِ). The reason why this verse is recognized to be referring to Jesus (PBUH) because of the context, the preceding verses were discussing him. Verse 57 says:

وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ مَثَلاً إِذَا قَوۡمُكَ مِنۡهُ يَصِدُّونَ (٥٧)

“When the example of the son of Mary was cited, your people laughed at it.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:57)

Those who believe in the rise and return argue that him being a sign for the hour means that his return and killing the Dajjal (antichrist) and ruling the world is a fulfillment of one of the major signs of the hour.

Those who deny the rise and the return of Jesus argue that Jesus (PBUH) being a sign of the hour mainly mean that by him being able to revive the dead with Allah’s command, shows that surely Allah will resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgement and thus his actions is a proof of the hour of judgement. They also propose that (وَإِنَّهُ) in (وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلۡمٌ۬ لِّلسَّاعَةِ) does not refer to Jesus (PBUH) but rather refers to the Quran, meaning that the Quran is the sign for the coming of the hour.

9. Surat Al-Maeda Verses 116-117

وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَـٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِى وَأُمِّىَ إِلَـٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِىٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِى بِحَقٍّ‌ۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُ ۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُ ۥ‌ۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى نَفۡسِى وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى نَفۡسِكَ‌ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّـٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ (١١٦) مَا قُلۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَمَرۡتَنِى بِهِۦٓ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبَّكُمۡ‌ۚ وَكُنتُ عَلَيۡہِمۡ شَہِيدً۬ا مَّا دُمۡتُ فِيہِمۡ‌ۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِى كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۚ وَأَنْتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ شَہِيدٌ (١١٧)

“And when Allah said: O Jesus, son of Mary! Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as gods beside Allah? He said: Glory to You, it does not behoove me to say that to which I had no right. If I had ever said it, You would have known it. You know what my thinking is, and I do not know what is in Your thinking. Indeed, You alone have full knowledge of all that is unseen. (116)

I did not say to them except what You commanded me to say, that is: “Worship Allah, my Lord, and your Lord” and I was a witness over them while I was with them. But when you (twafaitani) took me, You were the Watcher over them. You are Witness over everything.” (Al-Maeda 5:116-117)

Those who deny the rise and return suggest that these verses present a scene in the day of Judgement during which Jesus (PBUH) denies that he told the people to worship him. If Jesus (PBUH) was to return to earth to preach the religion of Islam, this denial will not necessary because when he returns and rules, all people will be Muslims.

Those who believe in the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) suggest that these verses present a scene that occurred after he rose to Allah during which Jesus (PBUH) denied that he told the people to worship him. This also infers that he will return to correct the false belief that was propagated after his rise. They also suggest that it cannot be a scene in the day of Judgment because if it was, Jesus would have referred to the teachings of the messenger who came after him who is Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who confirmed that Jesus never claimed divinity.

10. Surat Al-Maeda Verse 75

مَّا ٱلۡمَسِيحُ ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ۬ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ

“The Messiah (Jesus), son of Mary was but a messenger, like many Messengers who have passed away before him.” (Al-Maeda 5:75)

Those who deny the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) argue that this verse is general and thus refute the uniqueness of Prophet Jesus (PBUH) to rise alive and return to complete his mission and follow Prophet Mohammad (PBUH). They also argue that if Jesus’s return will result in having all people become believers and follow the religion of Islam and him ruling over them as one ummah is contradicting the Quran that people will always differ, as Allah says:

وَلَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ أُمَّةً۬ وَٲحِدَةً۬‌ۖ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ مُخۡتَلِفِينَ (١١٨) إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَ‌ۚ وَلِذَٲلِكَ خَلَقَهُمۡ‌ۗ (١١٩)

“Had the Lord so willed, He could have made mankind a single nation, but they will continue in their difference (118) Except those whom the Lord blessed, and for that He has created them. (Hud 11:118-119)

Those who believe in the rise and return of Jesus (PBUH) argue that the verse merely states that Jesus is like all the other messengers regarding his role to deliver Allah’s message to the people. This verse is similar to the verse referring to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) whose mission is the same as all prophets, yet he was unique as he was send to all mankind and he is the seal of prophets Allah says:

وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ۬ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ‌ۚ

“Mohammad is but a messenger. like many Messengers who have passed away before him.” (Al-Emran 3:144)

The similarity of all the messengers regarding the mission does not negate his uniqueness such as his birth and his speech as infant and thus his rise and return could also be unique.

Appendix 1: Some Hadith Confirming the Return of Jesus

Companions who narrated hadith on the subject: Abu Hurairah, Ibn Masoud, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-A’as, Abi Ummamh, Uthman ibn Abi Al-A’as, Maajma ibn Jariah, Hudhifa ibn Usaid and Ibi Shurihah

أبو هريرة., عبد الله بن مسعود, عبد الله بن عمرو. , أبو أمامة, عثمان بن أبي العاص, عبد الله بن مغفل , مجمع بن جارية, النواس بن سمعان

1. Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

عن أبي هريرة قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَيْفَ أَنْتُمْ إِذَا نَزَلَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ فِيكُمْ وَإِمَامُكُمْ مِنْكُمْ [ البخاري – مسلم ]

“How will you be when the son of Mary descends upon you while your leader is among you?” [Al-Bukhari 3449 and Muslim 155]

2. Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

عَنْ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ” وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لَيُوشِكَنَّ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ فِيكُمْ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ حَكَمًا عَدْلاً، فَيَكْسِرَ الصَّلِيبَ، وَيَقْتُلَ الْخِنْزِيرَ، وَيَضَعَ الْجِزْيَةَ، وَيَفِيضَ الْمَالُ حَتَّى لاَ يَقْبَلَهُ أَحَدٌ، حَتَّى تَكُونَ السَّجْدَةُ الْوَاحِدَةُ خَيْرًا مِنَ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا فِيهَا “. ثُمَّ يَقُولُ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ وَاقْرَءُوا إِنْ شِئْتُمْ {وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَكُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا}.

“By Him in Whose Hands my soul is, surely (Jesus,) the son of Mary will soon descend amongst you and will judge mankind justly (as a Just Ruler); he will break the Cross and kill the pigs and there will be no Jizya. Money will be in abundance so that nobody will accept it, and a single prostration to Allah (in prayer) will be better than the whole world and whatever is in it.” Abu Huraira added “If you wish, you can recite (this verse of the Holy Book): — ‘And there is none Of the people of the Scriptures (Jews and Christians) But must believe in him Before his death. And on the Day of Judgment, He will be a witness Against them.” (Al-Nisa 4.159) [al-Bukhari]

3. Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

عَنْ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ” وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَيُوشِكَنَّ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ فِيكُمْ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَكَمًا مُقْسِطًا فَيَكْسِرُ الصَّلِيبَ وَيَقْتُلُ الْخِنْزِيرَ وَيَضَعُ الْجِزْيَةَ وَيَفِيضُ الْمَالُ حَتَّى لَا يَقْبَلَهُ أَحَدٌ “

“By Him in Whose hand is my life, the son of Mary (ﷺ) will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will break crosses, kill swine and abolish Jizya and the wealth will pour forth to such an extent that no one will accept it. (Muslim)

4. Hudhaifa b. Usaid Ghifari reported that Allah’s Messenger (PBUH) came to us all of a sudden as we were (busy in a discussion). He said:

“What do you discuss about? We said. We are discussing about the Last Hour. Thereupon he (PBUH) said:

قال حذيفة بن أسيد رضي الله عنه: “اطلع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم علينا ونحن نتذاكر، فقال: ” ما تذاكرون ؟ ” : قالوا: نذكر الساعة قال: ” إنها لن تقوم الساعة حتى تروا قبلها عشر آيات فذكر الدخان، والدجال، والدابة، وطلوع الشمس .من مغربها، ونزول عيسى ابن مريم، ويأجوج ومأجوج، وثلاثة خسوف: خسف بالمشرق وخسف بالمغرب وخسف بجزيرة العرب، وآخر ذلك نار تخرج من اليمن تطرد الناس إلى محشرهم” (أخرجه مسلم)

“It will not come until you see ten signs before and (in this connection) he made a mention of the smoke, Dajjal, the beast, the rising of the sun from the west, the descent of Jesus son of Mary (Allah be pleased with him), the Gog and Magog, and land-sliding in three places, one in the east, one in the west and one in Arabia at the end of which fire would burn forth from the Yemen, and would drive people to the place of their assembly”. [Muslim]

5. Jaber ibn Abdullah reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال جابر بن عبدالله سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: (لا تزال طائفة من أمتي يقاتلون على الحق ظاهرين إلى يوم القيامة، قال: فينزل عيسى ابن مريم عليه الصلاة والسلام، فيقول أميرهم: تعال صلِّ بنا، فيقول: لا، إن بعضكم على بعض أمراء؛ تكرمة الله هذه الأمة)؛صحيح مسلم

“A section of my people will not cease fighting for the Truth and will prevail till the Day of Resurrection.” He then said, “Jesus, son of Mary, would then descend and their (Muslims’) commander would invite him to come and lead them in prayer, but he would say, ‘No, some among you are commanders over some (among you). This is the honor from God for this Nation.” (Muslim)

– — وروى مسلم (ج 18 ص75)، والإمام أحمد (ج 2 ص 166)، عن عبدالله بن عمرو جاءه رجل، فقال: “ما هذا الحديث الذي تحدث به، تقول: إن الساعة تقوم إلى كذا وكذا؟ فقال: سبحان الله، أولاً لا إله إلا الله، أو كلمة نحوهما، لقد هممت ألا أحدث أحدًا شيئًا أبدًا، إنما قلت: إنكم سترون بعد قليل أمرًا عظيمًا، يحرق البيت ويكون، ويكون، ثم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:«يخرج الدجال في أمتي، فيمكث أربعين، لا أدري أربعين يومًا أو أربعين شهرًا، أو أربعين عامًا، فيبعث الله عيسى ابن مريم كأنه عروة بن مسعود، فيطلبه فيهلكه، ثم يمكث الناس سبع سنين ليس بين اثنين عداوة، ثم يرسل الله ريحًا باردة من قبل الشام، فلا يبقى على وجه الأرض أحد في قلبه مثقال ذرة من خير أو إيمان، إلا قبضته، حتى لو أن أحدكم دخل في كبد جبل، لدخلته عليه حتى تقبضه

وروى مسلم (ج 18 ص63)، والإمام أحمد في المسند (ج 4 ص181): عن جبير بن نفير عن النواس بن سمعان، قال: “ذكر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الدجال ذات غداة، فخفض فيه ورفع، حتى ظنناه في طائفة النخل، فلما رحنا إليه عرف ذلك فينا)؛ الحديث، إلى أن قال: (فبينما هو كذلك، إذ بعث الله المسيح ابن مريم، فينزل عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق بين مهرودتين، واضعًا كفيه على أجنحة ملكين، إذا طأطأ رأسه قطر، وإذا رفعه تحدر منه جمان كاللؤلؤ، فلا يحل لكافر يجد ريح نَفَسه إلا مات، ونَفَسه ينتهي حيث ينتهي طرفه، فيطلبه حتى يدركه بباب لد، فيقتله، ثم يأتي عيسى ابن مريم قومه قد عصمهم الله منه، فيمسح عن وجوههم ويحدثهم بدرجاتهم في الجنة، فبينما هو كذلك، إذ أوحى الله إلى عيسى إني قد أخرجت عبادًا لي لا يدان لأحد بقتالهم، فحرز عبادي إلى الطور، ويبعث الله يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون، فيمر أوائلهم على بحيرة طبرية فيشربون ما فيها، ويمر آخرهم فيقولون: لقد كان بهذه مرة ماء، ويحصر نبي الله عيسى وأصحابه، حتى يكون رأس الثور لأحدهم خيرًا من مائة دينار لأحدكم اليوم، فيرغب نبي الله عيسى وأصحابه، فيرسل الله عليه النغف في رقابهم، فيصبحون فرسى كموت نفس واحدة، ثم يهبط نبي الله عيسى وأصحابه إلى الأرض، فلا يجدون موضعًا في الأرض إلا ملأ زهمهم ونتنهم، فيرغب نبي الله عيسى وأصحابه، فيرسل الله طيرًا كأعناق البخت، فتحملهم فتطرحهم حيث شاء الله)؛

عن نافع مولى أبي قتادة عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (كيف أنتم إذا نزل فيكم ابن مريم، فأمكم منكم)، فقلت لابن أبي ذئب: إن الأوزاعي حدثنا عن الزهري عن نافع عن أبي هريرة: (وإمامكم منكم)، قال ابن أبي ذئب تدري: ما أمكم منكم؟ قلت: تخبرني، قال: فأمكم بكتاب ربكم تبارك وتعالى، وسنة نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم

وروى مسلم في كتاب الفتن (ج18 ص220): عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (لا تقوم الساعة حتى ينزل الروم بالأعماق أو بدابق، فيخرج إليهم جيش من المدينة من خيار أهل الأرض يومئذ، فلما تصافوا، – قالت الروم: خلوا بيننا وبين الذين سبوا منا نقاتلهم، فيقول المسلمون: لا والله لا نخلي بينكم وبين إخواننا، فيقاتلونهم، فينهزم ثلث لا يتوب الله عليهم أبدًا، ويقتل ثلثهم أفضل الشهداء عند الله، ويفتتح الثلث لا يفتنون أبدًا، فيفتتحون قسطنطينية، فبينما هم يقتسمون الغنائم قد علقوا سيوفهم بالزيتون، إذ صاح فيهم الشيطان: إن المسيح قد خلفكم في أهليكم، فيخرجون وذلك باطل، فإذا جاؤوا الشام خرج، فبينما هم يعدون للقتال، يسوون الصفوف، إذ أقيمت الصلاة، فينزل عيسى ابن مريم فأمهم، فإذا رآه عدو الله، ذاب كما يذوب الملح في الماء، فلو تركه لانذاب حتى يهلك، ولكنه يقتله الله بيده، فيريهم دمه في حربته)

وروى الإمام أحمد في المسند (ج 2 ص406 و 437): عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (الأنبياء إخوة لعلات، أمهاتهم شتى، ودينهم واحد، وأنا أولى الناس بعيسى ابن مريم؛ لأنه لم يكن بيني وبينه نبي، وأنه نازل، – فإذا رأيتموه فاعرفوه، رجل مربوع إلى الحمرة والبياض، عليه ثوبان ممصران، كأنه رأسه يقطر، وإن لم يصبه بلل، فيدق الصليب ويقتل الخنزير، ويضع الجزية، ويدعو الناس إلى الإسلام، فيهلك الله في زمانه الملل كلها إلا الإسلام، ويهلك الله في زمانه المسيح الدجال، وتقع الأمنة على الأرض حتى ترتع الأسود مع الإبل، والنمار مع البقر، والذئاب مع الغنم، ويلعب الصبيان بالحيات لا تضرهم، فيمكث أربعين سنة ثم يتوفى، ويُصلي عليه المسلمون)

وروى الإمام أحمد (ج 3 ص 367): عن أبي الزبير عن جابر أنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (يخرج الدجال في خفقة من الدين وإدبار من العلم)؛ الحديث إلى أن قال: (ثم ينزل عيسى ابن مريم، فينادي بالسحر، فيقول: يا – أيها الناس، ما يمنعكم أن تخرجوا إلى الكذاب الخبيث؟ فيقولون: هذا رجل جني، فينطلقون، فإذا هم بعيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام، فتقام الصلاة، فيقال له: تقدم يا روح الله، فيقول: ليتقدم إمامكم، فليصل بكم، فإذا صلى صلاة الصبح، خرجوا إليه، قال: فحين يرى الكذاب ينماث كما ينماث الملح في الماء، فيمشي إليه فيقتله، حتى إن الشجرة والحجر ينادي: يا روح الله، هذا يهودي، فلا يترك ممن كان يتبعه أحدًا إلا قتله)

. عن عبدالله بن يزيد قال: سمعت مجمع بن جارية الأنصاري – وكان أحد القراء الذي قرؤوا القرآن – يقول: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (يقتله ابن مريم بباب لد) –

حدثنا هاشم بن القاسم، حدثنا ليث يعني ابن سعد، حدثنا ابن شهاب أنه سمع عبدالله بن ثعلبة الأنصاري يحدث عن عبدالرحمن بن بني عمرو بن عوف، يقول: سمعت عمر مجمع بن جارية يقول: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: (يقتل ابن مريم الدجال بباب لد)

عن علي بن يزيد، عن أبي نظرة، قال: “أتينا عثمان بن أبي العاص في يوم جمعه؛ لنعرض عليه مصحفًا”؛ الحديث إلى أن قال: “وينزل عيسى ابن مريم عند صلاة الفجر، فيقول له أميرهم: روح الله، تقدّم صلّ، فيقول: هذه الأمة أمراء – بعضهم على بعض، فيتقدّم أميرهم فيُصلي، فإذا قضى صلاته أخذ عيسى حربته، فيذهب نحو الدجال، فإذا رآه الدجال ذاب كما يذوب الرصاص، فيضع حربته بين تندوته، فيقتله وينهزم أصحابه، فليس يومئذ شيء يواري منهم أحدًا، حتى .“إن الشجرة لتقول: يا مؤمن هذا كافر، ويقول الحجر: يا مؤمن هذا كافر

## Introduction to the Quran

This is an introduction to a series of talks focusing on the themes of the different chapters (Surat) in the Quran. This introduction highlights some attributes of the Quran as Allah’s final message to mankind.

## Introduction

The Quran includes 114 chapters that are called Surat (سورة). The term Surat is derived from the word “Sur” (سور) that means “fence”. This implies that the Surat is like a fence that encircles its content which are called Ayat (آيات). Ayat which are translated as verses. An Ayah (verse) (آية) in Arabic means a sign from Allah to mankind. Since the Arabic words, Surat and Ayah, convey deeper meanings than the words chapter and verse, I plan to mostly use the Arabic words.

## Validating the Divinity of the Quran

The Quran is a unique scripture. Its authenticity and divinity can be examined using scientific approaches including the falsification test. This test implies that anyone who proposes a theory should identify tests to validate it. The general relativity theory was proposed by Einstein in 1915 but was only accepted by the scientific community when he identified three tests to prove its validity. The three tests were:

1. Planet Mercury does not return to the same spot every time it completes its elliptical orbit.
2. Light rays are bent near a massive body.
3. Time dilates in a gravitational field, meaning that clocks run slower as they approach the mass that is producing the gravity field.

The Quran offered the following falsification tests:

1. You will never find an error or a contradiction in it.
2. You will never find someone who would be able to produce a Surat similar to any of its.

أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلَا فًا كَثِيرًا (النساء ٨٢)
“Do they not ponder on the Quran? Had it been from other than Allah, they would surely have found discrepancies in it.” (4:82).

وَإِن ڪُنتُمۡ فِى رَيۡبٍ۬ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةٍ۬ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُہَدَآءَڪُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (٢٣) فَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفۡعَلُواْ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ‌ۖ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ (٢٤)
“If you are in any doubt about what We have revealed to our servant, then produce a Surat (Chapter) like it and call in your supporters other than Allah, if you are so truthful. (23) But if you do not - and surely you cannot - then heed the fire whose fuel is mankind and stones that has been prepared for the disbelievers ” (Al-Baqara 2:23-24).

قُل لَّٮِٕنِ ٱجۡتَمَعَتِ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتُواْ بِمِثۡلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ لَا يَأۡتُونَ بِمِثۡلِهِۦ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ۬ ظَهِيراً (٨٨)
“Say. If the entire mankind and the jinn were to get together to come up with the like of this Qur’an, they would not come up with anything like it, even if they were supporters of one another” (Al-Isra 17:88)

While the style, artistic and aesthetic qualities of the Quran stunned the Arabs during the life of the Prophet, miracles of the Quran are inherent in its content. The Quran includes Ayat addressing topics in many scientific fields (e.g. geology, astronomy, botany, biology, anthropology, sociology, meteorology, history, geography, etc.) that were not known during its revelation.

The words used in the Ayat (verses) of the Quran were so carefully selected so that they describe the scientific information very accurately to a specialist in the subject field. Yet, they did not cause any confusion to a layperson. No other book can be read, understood, and be equally beneficial to laymen and experts. No other book has been read by the same person 100s of times and yet is still exciting to read every time.

## The Divine Preservation of the Quran

The Quran is divinely protected and thus no entity in the universe can ever change a single letter in it. The Quran is preserved by several means including:

1. First, in paper and digital forms
2. Second and the most important is in the heart/brain of those who memorize it.

The amazing feature of the Quran is that Allah has facilitated its memorization to many, and this does not exist for any book in the world. Imagine if a natural disaster happens and the entire paper and digital records of all world books are destroyed. People will never be able to replicate an exact copy of any book but the Quran. The reason is that the Quran is the only book in the world that is memorized verbatim from its first letter to its last by several millions of Muslims around the world and thus new copies can be easily replicated. This is a fulfillment of Allah’s promise that He will preserve it as He said:

إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ ۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ (٩)
Indeed, It is We Who sent down the Dhikr (the Qur’an) and surely, We will preserve it. (Al-Hijr 15:9)

لَا يَأْتِيهِ الْبَاطِلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ) سورة فصلت
“No falsehood can approach it from its front or from its behind: it is sent down by the All-Wise, the Worthy of all Praise.” (Fusulat 41:42)

إِنَّهُ ۥ لَقُرۡءَانٌ۬ كَرِيمٌ۬ (٧٧) فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مَّكۡنُونٍ۬ (٧٨) لَّا يَمَسُّهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُطَهَّرُونَ (٧٩) تَنزِيلٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
It is indeed a noble Qur’an (77) In a Book kept well protected (78) Which none touches it but the purified ones, (79) A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. (Al-Waqia 56:77-80)

## Why Allah Preserved the Quran

There are many reasons why the Quran was preserved by Allah; these include:

1. Finality
Prophets were sent to specific people for certain time and then be followed by other prophets to renew Allah’s message. But Allah decreed that Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) will be his last prophet and the Quran will be His last message to mankind. Allah said:

مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍ۬ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمۡ وَلَـٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَۗ وَڪَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيماً (٤٠)
“Mohammad is not a father of any of your men, but he is a messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets. And Allah has the knowledge of everything,” (Al-Ahzab 33:40)

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ إِلَّا ڪَآفَّةً۬ لِّلنَّاسِ بَشِيرً۬ا وَنَذِيرً۬ا (٢٨)
“And We have not sent you (O Mohammad) but to the entire mankind, as a bearer of good news and as a warner.” (Saba 34:28)
Therefore, Allah’s last message requires special protection which cannot be left to mankind to do it.

2. Universality:
All previous messengers were sent to specific groups and their message was of a local nature and thus its applicability would be limited. As an example, the messenger who preceded Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) was Jesus (PBUH) who clearly stated that he was only sent to Bani Israel, as he said: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” (Matthew 15:24)

Therefore, the responsibility of preserving such messages were left in the hand of those to whom the message was sent.
But, in the case of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), Allah decreed that the message that he will receive will be universal and directed to all mankind as Allah said and commanded Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) to declare:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ إِلَّا ڪَآفَّةً۬ لِّلنَّاسِ بَشِيرً۬ا وَنَذِيرً۬ا
“And We have not sent you (O Muhammad) but to the entire mankind, as a bearer of good news and as a warner.” (Saba 34:28)

قُلۡ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡڪُمۡ جَمِيعًا
“Say: O Mankind I am a messenger from Allah to all of you. ” (Al-Araf 7:158)
Therefore, it is logical that Allah would decree that this universal and final message will be protected by Him.

3. The integration of the miracle and the message
All Allah’s Messengers preceding Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) were provided with messages and were supported with physical miracles to convince their people that they were messengers from Allah. In the case of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) the message (the Quran) that he received was the miracle to prove his truthfulness as Allah’s messenger. Therefore, the preservation of the Quran is critical not only to ensure the accuracy of Allah’s final message but also to prove to all people the truthfulness of Prophet Mohmmad as Allah’s messenger. This responsibility of preserving the message and the miracle cannot be ensured except by Allah.

4. Comprehensiveness
Unlike the previous divine messages that were revealed to specific people, the Quran is revealed for all people until the end of time. Therefore, it is a comprehensive message that is independent of time, place, and culture. Allah says regarding the Quran:

وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)
“And We have sent down to you the Book explaining all things, a Guide, a Mercy and Glad Tidings for the Muslims.” (Al-Nahl 16:89)

أَفَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡتَغِى حَكَمً۬ا وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ إِلَيۡڪُمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مُفَصَّلاً۬‌ۚ (١١٤)
[Say] “Shall I seek a judge other than Allah while it is He Who has sent down to you the Book (the Quran) with detailed explanations. (Al-Anaam 6:114)

Since the true understanding of many of the knowledge in the Quran will be discovered by people at different times, its text must remain intact to allow reaffirming its miracle as people advance in knowledge. The preservation of the text can only be assured by Allah because if it was left for people, they would have adulterated it whether intentionally or unintentionally, as was done in all previous revelations to incorporate their selfish interest and/or to reflect their understanding at that time, as Allah informed about what happened to previous revelations.

وَإِنَّ مِنۡهُمۡ لَفَرِيقً۬ا يَلۡوُ ۥنَ أَلۡسِنَتَهُم بِٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لِتَحۡسَبُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡڪَذِبَ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ (٧٨)
“And verily, among them (the people of the book) is a group who distort the book by twisting their tongues, so that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book, and they say: “This is from Allah,” but it is not from Allah; and they tell lies about Allah knowingly.” (Al-Emran 3:78)

مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ
“Among the Jews there are those who distort the words from their contexts. ” (Al-Nisa 4:46)

5. Reference for all past revelations
Realizing that past revelations have been adulterated by people, the last message from Allah to mankind is intended to serve as the reference and the criterion to verify the divinely revealed text from the humanly falsified text in in past revelations. Allah says:

وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقً۬ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ وَمُهَيۡمِنًا عَلَيۡهِ‌ۖ ۚ (٤٨)
We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming previous scriptures, and superseding them. [Al-Maeda 5:48]

تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى نَزَّلَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِهِۦ لِيَكُونَ لِلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ نَذِيرًا (١)
Blessed is He Who sent down the criterion (this Qur’an) to His slave that he may be a warner to the ‘Alamin (mankind and jinn). (Al-Furqan 25:1)

إِنَّ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ
Indeed, this Qur’an guides to that which is most straightforward. [Al-Isra 17:9]

The Quran serves as the standard to validate the accuracy of any information in past revelations. Therefore, it must be preserved by Allah who can assure its absolute preservation.

6. Preservation of the Quran cannot be trusted to any group including Muslims
Allah entrusted the preservation of previous revelations to their followers, and they have failed. Could Muslims been able to preserve the Quran? My answer is absolutely not. The number of fabricated hadith that creeped into the Islamic references supports my answer. If the Quran was left to them, there would no assurance against the deletion of some verses and the inclusion of fabricated ones.

Despite that no one could have added or removed any verse from the Quran, some have propagated a devious plan to create doubt about the Quran as eternal document whose teachings are valid for all times and places. This has been the idea behind the existence of abrogation in the Quran. This is no more than an unholy plan to create suspicion about the Quran’s completeness and the finality of its rules by suggesting that there are three types of abrogation in the rules of the Quran:

1. Abrogation of the ruling but preserving the divine text (نسخ الحكم و بقاء التلاوة)
2. Abrogation of the divine text and preserving the ruling (نسخ التلاوة و بقاء الحكم)
3. Abrogation of the ruling and abrogation of the divine text (نسخ الحكم ونسخ التلاوة)

The issue of abrogation in Quran is totally rejected on the basis of the falsification test that was previously mentioned:

أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلَا فًا كَثِيرًا (النساء ٨٢)
“Do they not ponder on the Quran? Had it been from other than Allah, they would surely have found discrepancies in it.” (Al-Nisa 4:82).

The abrogation supporters claim that some verses are abrogated to eliminate what appears to be contradictions and conflicts in the rulings and instructions in the Quran. Certainly, there are no contradictions or conflicts in the Quran. The verses they reference are there to cover special cases or certain occasions.

If Allah did not guarantee the preservation of the Quran, it would have been feasible for Muslims to modify the original text of the Quran to satisfy their erroneous concept of abrogation. But because this could not be done, some have introduced another devious idea, proposing that the hadith can abrogate the Qur’an. Since the hadith can be fabricated, this would allow changing the divine rules in the Quran without physically modifying its verses.

## Why the Quran is Revealed in the Arabic Language

Obviously, the message that any of Allah’s messengers received needs to be in the language that is spoken by the Messenger and his people and in case of Prophet Mohammad he spoke Arabic. Allah says:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوۡمِهِۦ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمۡ‌ۖ
“We did not send any messenger but (to teach) in the language of his people, in order to make (things) clear to them.” (Ibrahim 14:4)

But the Question that is often raised is why Allah chose Arabic to be the language of His final message to mankind while most of the people do not speak Arabic. In order for Allah’s final message to be universal, the vehicle for it must be in a language that have special attributes. Some of the unique attributes of the Arabic language include:

1. The Arabic language allows for the brevity of the text and allows for expanding the message in each verse as people advance in maturity and knowledge. The Arabic language packs a number of ideas in the least number of words. A single statement can have many messages embedded in it. This way, the Quran will continue to reveal new meanings/interpretations over time in order to accommodate mankind progress and the continuous change human needs across the globe.
2. The Arabic language has the largest number of roots compared to any other language. The Arabic language has 16,000 roots while the Hebrew language has 2,500 and the English language has 1,000.
3. The Arabic language is the clearest in pronunciation because every letter in a word is pronounced. One can slowly read a word by sounding every letter separately without creating discomfort to the listener.
4. The Arabic language is an original language that has not been derived from other languages. The Aramaic and Canaanite languages (اللغة الآرامية و اللغة الكنعانية) that were the basis for the Hebrew language were derived from the Arabic language.
5. The vocabulary of the Arabic language is extremely rich and so also the number of derivatives from the same root. A word can have many meanings and an object can have many names. As an example, the word (عين) has over 50 meanings (e.g., eye, spring, spy, chief, value, etc.) and the object (أسد) (lion) has over 300 names with every name presenting a different condition for the lion such that one name cannot replace another without changing the message about the lion.
6. While the vocabulary of the Arabic language is extremely rich, it has no synonyms, and this makes it impossible to fabricate the Quran because you cannot replace a word with a similar one without changing the meaning.
7. Some of the scientific miracles in the Quran are related to differentiating between the male and female and the Arabic verbs allow for such differentiation. As an example, Allah uses the feminine verb when speaking in Surat Al-Nahl (16:67-68) about the bees that make the honey. The discovery that honey is only made by the female bees was made in 1,737 which is over 1,000 years after the Quran made this assertion.
8. No other language was provided with the atmosphere and conditions to grow and develop like the Arabic Language. The greatest intellectual accomplishment of the Arabs was their poetry. Despite pre-Islamic Arabs being highly skilled in Arabic, the most eloquent Arabs found the Qur’anic diction unmatched.
9. There is a speculative unique advantage of the Arabic language that may be proven essential for translating the Quran to other languages and this is related to the nature of the acoustic signal created when reciting the Quran properly. Could this signal be converted to an electrical signal as is done by the ear for the brain to interpret. Could this electrical signal be translated to other languages to provide an exact translation of the Quran.

## The Approach of Studying the Quran

1. The Methodology
The Quran is a message from Allah to mankind. Its purpose is to communicate with everyone on a personal level. Understanding the Quran requires that one ponders, deliberates, contemplates, and analyzes its Ayat (verses). Allah says:

كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (ص)
“(This is) a Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings that they should ponder over its Verses, and those endowed with understanding may remember.” (Sad 38:29)

أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ أَمْ عَلَى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَا )محمد(
Will they not ponder over the Quran or are there locks on the hearts.” (Mohammad 47:24)

It is really encouraging to know that Allah has promised to teach and make the Quran clear to us if we are truthful about our serious commitment to study it. Allah said:

وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۖ وَيُعَلِّمُڪُمُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ۬
“Have Taqwa and Allah will teach you and Allah is all knowing of all things.” (Al-Baqara 2:282)

Allah promised to help anyone who struggles to study the Quran, as He said:

وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (سورة العنكبوت)
“Those who struggle to reach Us, We will guide them to Our ways and surely, Allah is with those who excels.” (Al-Ankabout 29:69)

2. The Quran includes many books
In Surat Al-Bayinah, Allah points out that the Quran includes many valuable books:

لَمۡ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأۡتِيَہُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَةُ (١) رَسُولٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتۡلُواْ صُحُفً۬ا مُّطَهَّرَةً۬ (٢) فِيهَا كُتُبٌ۬ قَيِّمَةٌ۬ (٣)
Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Book (Jews and Christians) and the polytheist were not about to change (from their wrong belief) until there comes to them clear evidence (1) A Messenger from Allah, reciting (the Qur’an) purified scrolls (2) Containing valuable books. (Al-Bayinah 98:1-3)

This means that the Quran is an assembly of many books. To learn a topic from the Quran, you must assemble all the verses related to the topic to establish a coherent picture on the subject. Therefore, one should never use one verse, without assembling all the verses related to it and harmonizing them to ensure unity. It is helpful in this integration to consider the context of the events at the time of revelation. Without knowing the unified message and the context, misunderstanding of the proper meaning can result.

Allah warns those who fragment the comprehensive message of the Quran by saying:

وَقُلۡ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱلنَّذِيرُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (٨٩) كَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡمُقۡتَسِمِينَ (٩٠) ٱلَّذِينَ جَعَلُواْ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ عِضِينَ (٩١) فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَسۡـَٔلَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ (٩٢) عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ (٩٣)
And say: “I am indeed a plain warner.” (89) Such as We send down for those who make division, (90) Those who break the Qur’an into parts. (91) So, by your Lord, We shall question all of them, (92) Of what they used to do. (Al-Hijr 15:89-93)

3. The Two types of verses
The Quran contains two types of verses: Mohkamat (Concise) and Motashabihat (Ambiguous and open for interpretation). The Mohkamat are the foundation for the articles of belief and the basis for Jurisprudence. The Motashabihat are allegorical in nature and their meanings and interpretations are affected by culture and human development. Allah says in Surat Al-Imran:

هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَـٰتٌ۬ مُّحۡكَمَـٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَـٰبِهَـٰتٌ۬‌ۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِہِمۡ زَيۡغٌ۬ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَـٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦ‌ۗ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ‌ۗ وَٱلرَّٲسِخُونَ فِى ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلٌّ۬ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَا‌ۗ وَمَا يَذَّڪَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَـٰبِ (٧)
“He is the One Who sent down the Book to you, wherein are clear unambiguous verses (ayat) that are the essence (Literally: the mother) of the Book, and others ambiguous (multiple-meaning, allegorical). So, as for those in whose hearts is swerving, they follow the ambiguous parts seeking confusion and seeking their interpretations. But none knows their (ultimate) interpretation except Allah and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: “We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.” And none is truly mindful but those who are endowed with intellects.” (Al-Imran 3:7)

4. Definition of Quranic Terms
Meanings and definitions of words/terms in the Quran are best interpreted by their use in the Quran. Arabic Lexicon should be used when a term has been used in the Quran only once. The Quran includes 77,449 words, only 1620 words came only once in the Quran. When interpreting these unique words using the Arabic Lexicon, one needs to differentiate between the common meaning (الراجح) and uncommon meaning (المرجوح). The interpreter cannot use the uncommon meaning unless there is a major justification for it such as avoiding attributing to Allah something that is not proper if one uses the common meaning.

5. The Need for Additional Knowledge
Verses that are related to natural sciences are best understood by experts in the related subjects. Major injustice occurs when some Islamic scholars insist on freezing the interpretation of verses referring to natural sciences to those made by early scholars when the scientific knowledge was still in its infancy. This is a misguided approach as stated by the great Maliki jurist Imam Al-Qarafi who said: “The stagnation in interpreting the meanings of the text is misguided and leads to misguidance”.

6. The Character of the Student of the Quran
Only those who have pure heart and are conscious of Allah will be able to benefit from the Quran. The Quran highlights this important requirement in its beginning as Allah says:

ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ‌ۛ فِيهِ‌ۛ هُدً۬ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
This is the book (the Quran) , in it a sure guidance for those who are God Conscious. (Al-Baqara 2:2)

The purification of the soul of the student of the Quran is a prerequisite to ensure a level of honesty and sincerity that inhibits the person from manipulating the revelation for self-interest. This prerequisite is very clear in the Quran, as Allah made it a required step before gaining knowledge and wisdom, as Allah says:

كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِيكُمْ رَسُولًا مِنْكُمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِنَا وَ يُزَكِّيكُمْ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ
“Even as We have sent unto you a messenger from among yourselves, who 1) rehearse for you His signs, 2) purifies you, and 3) teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you that which you did not know”. (Al-Baqara 2: 151)

## Value of group study of the Quran

The Prophet (PBUH) Said:
إذا مررتم برياض الجنة فارتعوا، قالوا: وما رياض الجنة؟ قال: حلق الذكر. ] أحمد و الترمذي والبيهقي [
If you pass by gardens of paradise avail yourselves of them.
The companions asked: What are the gardens of paradise?
He (PBUH) said: The circles of Dhikr (Studying the Quran and expressing gratitude to Allah). (Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and others)

عَنْ أَبِى هُرَيْرَةَ رضي الله عنه قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم : (… وَمَا اجْتَمَعَ قَوْمٌ فِى بَيْتٍ مِنْ بُيُوتِ اللَّهِ يَتْلُونَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَيَتَدَارَسُونَهُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِلاَّ نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّكِينَةُ وَغَشِيَتْهُمُ الرَّحْمَةُ وَحَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَذَكَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِيمَنْ عِنْدَهُ) رواه مسلم
Any people who gather in one of the Houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves, except that tranquility descends upon them, and Mercy envelops them, and the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them amongst those who are with Him” (Muslim)

عن أنس بن مالك –رضي الله عنه- عن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: «ما من قومٍ يذكرون الله -عز وجل- لا يُريدون بذلك إلا وجه الله؛ إلا ناداهم منادٍ من السماء: قوموا مغفورا لكم قد بدلت سيئاتكم حسنات» (أخرجه أحمد)
Whenever people gather remembering Allah-the Almighty while needing nothing from Him but His pleasure, a caller will call them from Heaven saying: “depart with forgiveness and with your sins have been converted to good deeds. (Ahmad)

عن أنس رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من صلى الفجر في جماعة، ثم قعد يذكر الله تعالى حتى تطلع الشمس، ثم صلى ركعتين، كانت له كأجر حجة وعمرة تامة تامة تامة . ) سنن الترمذي بإسناد صحيح
“Whoever prays Fajr in congregation then stays in remembrance of Allah until the Sunrise and then pray two rakka, he will have the reward of Hajj and Ummrah, complete, complete, complete. (Al-Tirmidhi)
