content:
Allah’s Name Al-Hameed – The Praised One

Allah’s glorious name Al-Hameed came in the Quran several times. It came by itself, and it came associated with Allah’s names Al-Ghani (The Rich), Al-Aziz (The Mighty), Al-Wali (The Guardian), Al-Majeed (Full of Glory) and Al-Hakeem (All wise).

Allah’s name Al-Hameed is derived from the noun, Al-Hamd (الحمد) that means thank, gratitude, appreciation, and praise. Therefore, it is similar to Allah’s name Al-Shakour. But there is subtle difference between Al-Hamd (الحمد) and Al-Shukr (الشكر). Al-Shukr is to express gratitude to the one who did you a favor. While Al-Hamd is broader because it means expressing gratitude and praise to the one possessing good attributes such as generosity, kindness, wisdom, achievements, etc.

Al-Hamd reflects deep recognition of the worthiness of the one to whom you are giving Hamd. Therefore, the only one who is truly worth of Hamd is Allah. Not only that one of Allah’s names is Al-Hameed but also Allah starts the Quran with His Hamd (ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ) “All the praises be to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds”. This declaration is repeated 5 times in the Quran. The assertion Alhamdulillah (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ) ”All the Praise be to Allah” came in the Quran to acknowledge Allah’s creation of the heavens and the earth, revealing the perfect Quran, showing us His signs in the universe, guiding us, fulfilling his promises, etc.

It is of Allah’s mercy that he taught us how to thank Him by using only two words, Alhamdulillah (ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ). It is interesting that when we want to give thanks and praise to someone important, people innovate on the expressions they use, but with Allah there is no innovation, just say Alhamdulillah. Therefore, we should thank Allah not only for all the materialistic pleasures that He granted us but also for teaching us how to thank him by using these two simple words. By this, Allah equalized between all people independent of their abilities to articulate and express their gratitude.

Allah’s name Al-Hameed reflects three elements:

1. Allah, Al-Hameed, means that He is deserving to be thanked and praised.

Allah deserves to be thanked for everything that we have and every opportunity that He creates for us to succeed. Allah is the only One to whom we give our “Hamd” thanks, gratitude, and praise even when we encounter difficulty because we have no doubt that there is a great wisdom behind everything that happens. When we see evil happens to Muslims, we should always look at ourselves and search for what we need to change because it could be admonition from Allah to bring us back to the straight path and help us avoid the eternal wrath as He said:

﴿ وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ الْأَدْنَى دُونَ الْعَذَابِ الْأَكْبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ ﴾ ( سورة السجدة )

“And indeed, We will make them taste of the penalty of this (life) prior to the supreme penalty in order that they may (repent and) return.” (Al-Sajda 32:21)

2. Allah, Al-Hameed, means that Allah guides to doing good, supports the ones who want to do good and praises them for having the honorable character to do good.

Allah creates for us the opportunities to make money and ensures that we get it and when we spend it in charity; He praises and appreciates our generosity, even though the money is His. As an illustration of this point, consider a father who gives his child money, and the child buys a gift for his mother in Mother’s Day. The father will praise the child and show appreciation for what he did, even though the money is from the father. So, Allah grants you His blessings and guides you to use them for what is pleasing to Him; then He praises and thanks you for what you have done.

3. Allah, Al-Hameed, means that Allah gives praise to Himself for His perfect essence, attributes, and actions.

While we learnt that one should not give praise himself, in the case of Allah it is necessary for Him to praise Himself to make us aware of Him to seek His help and blessings. As mere illustration of this point, consider a person who is very wealthy, but his modest appearance does not give indication of his wealth. He sees a person in need of money and offers to help him, but the needy person disregards the offer because the appearance of the man does not indicate that he has anything to give. In this case, if the man tells the person that he is very wealthy, he will not be saying this to brag about his wealth but to make it known so people will seek his help when they are in need. So, when Allah praises Himself, it is intended for people to know Him to seek His help and support.

When we examine the verses in which Allah’s name Al-Hameed is mentioned we can draw other lessons:

1/ Allah’s name Al-Hameed (الحميد) came individually in the following verse:

وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَهُدُوا إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْحَمِيدِ ( سورة الحج ) .

“For they have been guided to the purest of speech; they have been guided to the Path of Him Who is Worthy of (all) Praise.” (Al-Hajj 22:24)

The pure speech that uses proper and honorable words leads to the way of Allah, Al-Hameed (الحميد). It is critical for Muslims to learn how to speak properly and to ensure that they only say what is pure and wholesome because Allah, Al-Hameed commands us to speak properly and in the best manner as He said:

. وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً ( سورة البقرة) .

“And say to the people what is good.” (Al-Baqara 2:83)

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

إن الرجل ليتكلم بالكلمة لا يلقي لها بالاً يهوي بها في جهنم سبعين خريفاً) .[ الترمذي عن أبي هريرة(

“A man speaks a word without giving it any thought that will make him fall in the hell fire for seventy years”.

) . لا يستقيم إيمان عبد حتى يستقيم قلبه ولا يستقيم قلبه حتى يستقيم لسانه) [أخرجه الإمام أحمد عن أنس بن مالك [

“The belief of a person will not be upright unless his heart is upright, and his heart will not be upright unless his tongue is upright.” (Ahmad)

2/ Allah’s name Al-Hameed came in association with Allah’s name Al-Aziz:

ڪِتَـٰبٌ أَنزَلۡنَـٰهُ إِلَيۡكَ لِتُخۡرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّہِمۡ إِلَىٰ صِرَٲطِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَمِيدِ (سورة إبراهيم)

“This is a Book that We have revealed to you, so that you may deliver the people, out of all sorts of darkness into light, by the will of their Lord, leading them to the path of the Almighty the worthy of all Praise.” (Ibrahim 14:1)

We note that in this verse the darkness (ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ) came as a plural while the light (ٱلنُّور) came as singular. This is because falsehood takes many forms and shapes while the truth is singular and there is only one path to Allah, Al-Aziz, Al-Hameed.

3/ Allah’s name Al-Hameed came in association with Allah’s name Al-Wali:

وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ وَيَنشُرُ رَحۡمَتَهُ ۥ‌ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَلِىُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ (٢٨)

“He is the One who sends down rain after they have lost hope and He extends His Mercy. And He is the Guardian Worthy Of all Praise.” (Ash-Shura 42:28)

When Allah Al-Hameed is your Wali He will take care of your affairs and acts as your Guardian, Protector and Defender as He said:

﴿ اللَّهَ يُدَافِعُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا ﴾ ) سورة الحج الآية : 38 (

“Indeed, Allah will defend (from ill) those who believe:” (Al-Hajj 22:38)

4/ Allah’s name Al-Hameed also came in association with the name Al-Majeed:

﴿ قَالُوا أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ ﴾) سورة هود (

“They said: “Do you wonder at Allah’s decree? The grace of Allah and His blessings be on you, O you people of the house, For He is indeed worthy of all praise, full of all glory!” (Hud 11:73)

The association of Al-Hameed and Al-Majeed in reference to the blessing that Allah granted Ahl-Albayt (the prophet’s family) came also in the hadith that taught us what to say in the second part of the Tahiyaat. The Prophet (PBUH) was asked by the companions on how can they do Salat on Ahl-Albayt? He (PBUH) answered:

عن البخاري من حديث كعب بن عجرة رضي الله عنه أنه قال : سألنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلنا : يا رسول الله كيف الصلاة عليكم أهل البيت ؟ قال :” قولوا اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد ، كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد ، اللهم بارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد .”

Say: “O Allah, bless Mohammad and the members of his household as You have blessed Abraham and the members of his household. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, be gracious unto Mohammad and the members of his household as You were gracious unto Abraham and the members of his household. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.” (Bukhari)

5/ The name Al-Hameed is also associated with Al-Hakeem (The Wise) when Allah is addressing the protection of the Quran from any interferences to maintain its perfection as it was revealed:

). لَا يَأْتِيهِ الْبَاطِلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ) سورة فصلت

“No falsehood can approach it from its front or from its behind: it is sent down by the All-Wise, the Worthy of all Praise.” (Fusulat 41:42)

6/ The name Al-Hameed is also associated with Al-Ghani (The Rich) to make people realize that no matter how wealthy they are, they are still poor and always in need for Allah and only Allah is the truly rich who can provide them, and He is the One deserving all the praise.

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنْتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ ﴾ .) سورة فاطر (

“O you mankind! it is you who are the poor, utterly in need of Allah: and Allah who is Rich (Free of all needs), the Worthy of all praise.” (Fater 35:15)

Expressing gratitude to Allah by declaring His Hamd is often associated with declaring Allah’s perfection by saying Subhan Allah (سبحان الله). Therefore, we say (سبحان الله و بحمده) “Subhanallahi Wa Bihamdihi”. Saying Subhan Allah means declaring the infinite perfection of Allah’s essence, names, attributes, and actions beyond any human measure. While it is difficult to translate Subhan Allah with simple words to reflect its meaning, it is often translated as “All Glory is to Allah.” The best words we express our gratitude to Allah by combining tasbih (glorification) and hamd (praise).

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

كَلِمَتانِ خَفِيفَتانِ علَى اللِّسانِ، ثَقِيلَتانِ في المِيزانِ، حَبِيبَتانِ إلى الرَّحْمَنِ، سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ وبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ.

“Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy on the balance and very loved to Al-Rahman (ﷻ) is Glory and praise to Allah, glory to Allah the Almighty. “Subhan Allahi Wa Bihamdihi Subhan Allahil Azeem”. (Bukhari)

The Prophet’s wife Juwairiyah bint Al-Harith (May Allah be pleased with her) said:

عن جويرية بنت الحارث رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من عندها بكرة حين صلى الصبح وهي جالسة في مسجدها ثم رجع بعد أن أضحى وهي جالسة فقال: ما زلت على الحال التي فارقتك عليها؟! قالت نعم، قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لقد قلت بعدك أربع كلمات ثلاث مرات لو وزنت بما قلت منذ اليوم لوزنتهن: “سبحان الله وبحمده عدد خلقه ورضى نفسه وزنة عرشه ومداد كلماته”. (مسلم

The Prophet (PBUH) came out from my apartment in the morning as I was busy in performing the dawn prayer. He came back in the forenoon and found me sitting there.

The Prophet (PBUH) said, “Are you still in the same position as I left you.” I said: Yes.

The Prophet said, “I recited four words three times after I had left you. If these are to be weighed against all you have recited since morning, these will be heavier. These are: Glory and praise to Allah as many times as the number of His creatures, in accordance with His Good Pleasure, equal to the weight of His Throne and equal to the ink that may be used in recording His words.” [Sahih Muslim]

These two words (سبحان الله و بحمده) “Subhanallahi Wa Bihamdihi” are the ones that are used by everything in the universe to glorify and praise Allah. Allah said:

وَيُسَبِّحُ ٱلرَّعۡدُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ مِنۡ خِيفَتِهِ ) الرعد (

“The thunder proclaims His purity with His praise, and so do the angels out of His awe.” (Al-Rad 13:13)

تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيہِنَّ‌ۚ وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورً۬ا (الإسراء )

“The seven heavens and the earth and all those proclaim His purity, and there is not a thing but proclaim His purity with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification Surely, He is forbearing, Most Forgiving.” (Al-Isra 17:44)

When we give glory and Hamd to Allah, you will be in a state of harmony with everything in the universe including every cell in our body. Our reward for ensuring this harmony from Allah is our great happiness of paradise. Therefore, the ultimate expression of our gratitude to Allah in paradise is to repeat what we used to say in every rakaa in our prayers which is (ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ) “All Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds!” as Allah informs us:

دَعۡوَٮٰهُمۡ فِيہَا سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُہُمۡ فِيہَا سَلَـٰمٌ۬‌ۚ وَءَاخِرُ دَعۡوَٮٰهُمۡ أَنِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ

“There (paradise), their invocation shall be: “Glory to You O Allah!” and their salutation in it shall be “Peace”! And the last of their prayers shall be: “All Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds!” (Yunus 10:10)

Elements to Adopt in our Character

1/ Our tongue must always be praising and giving thanks to Allah. Each time we recite “all praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds” (ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ), we should reflect and recognize all of Allah’s favors and blessings. We get so overwhelmed with our busy life that we often fail to recognize the blessings that Allah grants to us. How many times do we go to our homes, eat our dinner, and have a good night sleep and never give a second thought to the greatness of these blessings. The Prophet (PBUH) used to say: “Whoever gets up in the morning and has health in his body, security in his travel and food for his day, he would have owned this world”.

2/ Reflect on the character for those who came before us and help us understand what Alhamdulillah meant to them. Once a messenger from Azerbaijan came to see Khalifa Omar who ruled over most of the civilized world at his time and when the time of dinner came, Omar offered him the choice to either eat dinner with him or with other Muslims in Al-Madinah. The messenger expressed his interest to eat the dinner with the Khalifa. When they arrived at Omar’s house, Omar asked his wife, Umm Kalthoum, what food she has for dinner. She said: all I have is bread and salt. Omar said: Alhamdulillah, this is great. He and the messenger ate; the messenger was shocked because he was expecting to have a fancy dinner at the home of the leader of the largest kingdom on Earth. After they finished eating Khalifa Omar said: (ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى أَطۡعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسۡلِمِينَ) “All praise to Allah who fed us and gave us water and made us Muslims”.

How many people do you think will give thanks to Allah if they go to their house accompanied by a friend and when he asks his wife to prepare the dinner, he discovers that there is only bread and salt?

3/ Don’t be shy in acknowledging the gifts and the talents that Allah granted you. This is not to brag about yourself but to ensure that people know about them to seek your help when needs arise. Also acknowledge the gifts and talents that Allah granted to others and help them in nourishing them.

4/ We should train ourselves to be satisfied with everything that we face and always see that all Allah’s decisions deserve our thanks and gratitude. A believer cycles between the states of gratitude and patience as his life cycles between ease and hardship and between reward and testing. Expressing thanks to Allah means that you are always pleased with Allah and the ultimate pleasure is when He grants you paradise:

قَالَ ٱللَّهُ هَـٰذَا يَوۡمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ صِدۡقُهُمۡ‌ۚ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٌ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيہَآ أَبَدً۬ا‌ۚ رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡہُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ

“Allah will say: “This is a day on which the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, their eternal home. Allah is well-pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him: that is the magnificent triumph.” (Al-Maeda 5:119)

Once a man was circumambulating around the Kabbah saying: O’ Allah, are you pleased with me. A man behind him said: But are you pleased with Allah. The man was intrigued and said: “how can I be pleased with Allah when all I wish is for Him to be pleased with me? The man said: “when your happiness when a tragedy befalls you equals to your happiness when a blessing is given to you, you are satisfied with Allah.” The man inquired: Who are you? The man replied: I am Mohammad ibn Idreas Al-Shafia.

How does one achieve this high state of spirituality of being pleased with Allah no matter the difficulty one faces? This state is even higher than patience. The key is the Tasbeeh and the Hamd as Allah said

وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِہَا‌ۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآىِٕ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلنَّہَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرۡضَىٰ

“And proclaim the purity and praise of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset and in some hours of night, and at parts of the day also, so that you may be pleased”. (Taha 20:130)

title: Allah’s Name Al-Shakour – The Appreciative
excerpt:

content:
Allah’s Name Al-Shakour – The Appreciative

Allah’s name Al-Shakour (الشكور) “The Appreciative” is revealed in the Quran in four verses. It came three times associated with Allah’s name Al-Ghafour (الغفور) “the All Forgiving” and once associated with Allah’s name Al-Haleem (الحليم) “the Most Forbearing”.

لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدَهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ  )فاطر(
“That He (Allah) will pay them their rewards and increase for them out of His grace. Surely, He is Most-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.” (Fater 35:30)

وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ  )فاطر(
“And they will say: “All the praises be to Allah, who has removed all sorrow from us, for our Lord is indeed Most-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.” (Fater 35:34)

وَمَنْ يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْنًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ
“And whoever performs a good deed, We will give him an increase of goodness. Surely, Allah is Most-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.” (Al-Shura 42:23)

إِنْ تُقرضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا يُضَاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (التغابن)
“If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will double it for you, and will forgive you for Allah is Most Appreciative, Most Forbearing.” (Al-Taghabun 64:17)

If you commit a sin, Allah is Ghafour (غفور) Most-Forgiving and if you do a good deed, Allah is Shakour (شكور), Most-Appreciative of your good deeds and if you spend in charity, Allah will not only forgive any of your deviations, but He is also Shakour for your charity and Haleem (حليم), Most Forbearing (Lenient, Tolerant and Patient) for your deviations.

Allah’s name Al-Shakour (الشكور) is an exaggerated form (صيغة مبالغة) for the name Al-Shakir (الشاكر) “the Appreciative” that appears in the Quran twice associated with the name “Aleem: (عَلِيم): “All-Knowing”.

إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ اللّهِ فَمَنْ حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَإِنَّ اللّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ (سورة البقرة)
Verily, As-Safa and Al-Marwah (two mountains in Makkah) are among the marks of Allah. So, whoever comes to the house for Hajj or ‘Umrah, there is no sin for him by making rounds between them and whoever does good voluntarily, then Allah is indeed Appreciative and All-Knowing.” (Al-Baqara 2:158)

(This verse was revealed prior to the Prophet’s conquest of Mecca when Muslim felt uncomfortable traversing between the mountains when idols were still standing on them during their Hajj or Umrah.)

. مَّا يَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِڪُمۡ إِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ وَءَامَنتُمۡ‌ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ شَاڪِرًا عَلِيمً۬ا (سورة النساء)
“What would Allah get by punishing you if you are grateful and believe? Allah is Most-Appreciative, All-Knowing” (Al-Nisa 4:147)

Allah, Al-Shakour is the one who returns many folds for all goodness and rewards with eternal happiness even for the smallest effort you spent in worship. Realizing the unlimited multiplication factor of Allah’s rewards for your good deeds will help you realize that Allah is truly the most appreciative. How much pleasure do you feel when you get praised by someone important? Imagine when Allah praises you for your good deeds. Allah praises your work even though He is the one who helped you and supported you to do it.

No one is smarter and luckier than the one who deserves to be praised by Allah. And when you express your gratitude, Allah will increase His favors and blessings upon you as He said

وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ
“Your Lord has decreed, if you thank Me, I will increase My blessings upon you.” (Ibrahim 14:7)

So, the more you thank Allah for His favors, the more favors He gives you. When we thank Allah, we are benefiting ourselves. This is what Luqman, the wise, emphasized to his son by saying:

وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا لُقْمَانَ الْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ وَمَنْ يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ
And indeed, We granted wisdom on Luqman saying, give thanks to Allah. and anyone who thanks Allah does it to benefit himself; but whosoever is ungrateful Allah is indeed free of all wants, worthy of all praise. (Luqman 31:12)

This is also what Prophet Suliman was affirming when he saw the throne of Sheba in front of him:

فَلَمَّا رَآهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِنْدَهُ قَالَ هَذَا مِنْ فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ وَمَنْ شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ (النمل)
“When he (Solomon) saw it placed before him, he said: “This is by the Grace of my Lord – to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful! And whoever is grateful, truly, his gratitude is for (the good of) his own self, and whoever is ungrateful, (he is ungrateful only for the loss of his own self). Certainly, my Lord is Rich (Free of all wants), Bountiful.” (Al-Naml 27:40)

Therefore, one will never be able to give Allah His due thanks because as Prophet Dawud (David) said:
نبي داود عليه السلام  يارب كيف اشكرك وشكرك نعمة تحتاج إلى شكر
“My Lord, how can I thank you when my ability to thank you is a blessing from you that deserves thanks.”

It is unfortunate that most people take advantage of the blessings that Allah grants them but never give thanks. Allah says:
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ (البقرة)
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ (يونس)
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ (غافر)
“Indeed, Allah is full of bounties to the people, but most people do not give thanks. (Al-Baqara 2:243, Yunus 10:60 and Ghafer 40:61)

But how do we thank Allah? Is it by merely uttering the words of thanks such as Alhamdulillah (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ) or Al-Shukrulillah (الشكر لله)? No, this not sufficient because expressing thanks to Allah involves transforming these words into actions as Allah said:

اعْمَلُوا آلَ دَاوُدَ شُكْرًا وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ
“The Family of David, work for expressing thanks! But few of My servants are grateful!” (Sabaa 34:13)

In this verse Allah commands the family of David to express their thanks by action. Thanking Allah should involve five elements:

1. Attributing the blessings to Allah since He is the source of all goodness. Never think that what you have achieved is because of your intelligence but realize that Allah can with a single blood clot in the brain make you completely invalid.
2. Using the blessings in accordance with Allah commandments. Never use Allah’s blessing of intelligence to cheat people or use His blessing of wealth to spend on something prohibited or not pay the due Zakat.
3. Ensuring to not get distracted by the blessings from fulfilling the commands of Allah. Don’t use the blessing of having a successful business to distract you from coming on time for the Friday prayer.
4. Ensuring to never allow arrogance to creep in your heart because of the blessings and feel that you are better than anyone else.
5. Thanking and praising Allah for His blessings by often saying Alhamdulillah ( الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ).

Allah Al-Shakour means that He grants you His blessings and then appreciates you when you use them in venues that are pleasing to Him. Allah shows His appreciation in many ways such as:

1. Placing your love in the heart of people. When Allah loves a person, He orders Gabriel to love him and Gabriel will call to all those in heaven and earth and say Allah loves so and so, so love him. (إذا أحب العبد أمر جبريل أن ينادي في الخلائق إن الله يحب فلان فأحبوه)
2. Facilitating His obedience and distracting you from committing sins and giving your patience and perseverance.
3. Praising you in front of the angels as Allah says in Hadith Qudsi: Whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I will mention him in a gathering that is better than his. (ومن ذكري في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير منه)
4. Influencing people to always remember you with goodness and kind words (يلقي له الشكر بين عباده فيكون ذا سيرة عطرة بين الناس)
5. Rewarding you with additional blessings for your gratitude.
6. Making you among the first to enter paradise. The Prophet (PBUH) said “أول من يدعي إلى الجنة يوم القيامة الحامدون الذين يحمدون الله في السراء والضراء” - “The first to be summoned to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will be those who praise God in prosperity and adversity.” Al-Tirmidhi.
7. Allowing you to see Him in paradise. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عَنْ صُهَيْبٍ رضي الله عنه عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ : ” إِذَا دَخَلَ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالَ : يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى : تُرِيدُونَ شَيْئًا أَزِيدُكُمْ فَيَقُولُونَ أَلَمْ تُبَيِّضْ وُجُوهَنَا أَلَمْ تُدْخِلْنَا الْجَنَّةَ وَتُنَجِّنَا مِنْ النَّارِ قَالَ فَيَكْشِفُ الْحِجَابَ فَمَا أُعْطُوا شَيْئًا أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ النَّظَرِ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَهِيَ الزِّيَادَةُ ثُمَّ تَلَا هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ ( لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنَى وَزِيَادَةٌ ) [ رواه مسلم في صحيحه ]
“When the inhabitants of the Paradise enter the Paradise, Allah, the Glorious and Exalted, will say to them: ‘Do you wish me to give you anything more?’ They will say: ‘Haven’t You made our faces bright? Haven’t You made us enter the Paradise and saved us from the Hell?’ Then Allah will remove the Veil and they will feel that they have not been awarded anything more beloved to them than looking at their Lord and this is the extra that Allah promised when He said: “For those who do good, there is the best and something more.” (Yunus 10:26). [Muslim]

Elements to Adopt in our Character

1/ Always be aware of Allah’s blessings and express your gratitude to Allah for them. Allah also says:
وَذَڪِّرۡهُم بِأَيَّٮٰمِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ۬ شَكُورٍ۬) سورة إبراهيم
“And remind them of the blessings of Allah. Verily in this there are Signs for those who are firmly patient and constantly thankful.” (Ibrahim 14:5)
As people will soon celebrate the thanksgiving holiday with their families, we should thank Allah for the blessings of our family and friends. Give thanks to Allah thru prayers as the Prophet (PBUH) used to do. His wife Sayeda Aisha said that the Prophet (PBUH) used to stand in prayers for so long until his feet were swollen. So, I said to him: O messenger of Allah why are you doing this when Allah has already forgiven all your past and future sins. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
وعن عائشة ـ رضي الله عنها ـ قالت : ( كان رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – إذا صلى قام حتى تفطر رجلاه .. قالت عائشة : يا رسول الله أتصنع هذا وقد غُفِرَ لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ؟! ، فقال – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : يا عائشة أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا )(مسلم)
“Shall I not be a grateful servant.” (Muslim)
The long prayers of the prophet in gratitude to Allah has been noted by several of his companions and when enquired his response was the same. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah (الْمُغِيرَةَ بْنَ شُعْبَةَ) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) would pray until his feet were swollen. It was said to him, “Why do you do this when Allah has already forgiven your past and future sins?” The Prophet said, “Shall I not be a grateful servant?” [Bukhari and Muslim]

2/ Never attribute Allah’s blessings to yourself without acknowledging Allah and thanking Him for them. The Quran teaches us about the fate of several people who attributed the blessings of Allah to themselves. As example is Qaroun who attributed his wealth to his own knowledge by saying (قَالَ إِنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ عِندِي) “I have been given it only on account of knowledge I possess”. (Al-Qasas 28:78). The consequence of this ingratitude based arrogant was:
فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِ وَبِدَارِهِ الْأَرْضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُ مِن فِئَةٍ يَنصُرُونَهُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُنْتَصِرِينَ
So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. Then he had no one to help him against Allah, nor was he of those who could save themselves. (Al-Qasas 28:81)

3/ Learn the good Dua of Prophet Suliman:
رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِىٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٲلِدَىَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَـٰلِحً۬ا تَرۡضَٮٰهُ وَأَدۡخِلۡنِى بِرَحۡمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ
“My Lord! Grant me the grace that I may thank You for the favors that You have bestowed on me and on my parents, and that I may do good deeds that will please You.” (Al-Naml 27:19)

4/ Do not focus only on the worldly gains because Allah said:
مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلۡعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلۡنَا لَهُ ۥ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ لِمَن نُّرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا لَهُ ۥ جَهَنَّمَ يَصۡلَٮٰهَا مَذۡمُومً۬ا مَّدۡحُورً۬ا (١٨) وَمَنۡ أَرَادَ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعۡيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنٌ۬ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ كَانَ سَعۡيُهُم مَّشۡكُورً۬ا (سورة الإسراء)
“Whoever opts for the immediate enjoyment of this world, We will readily grant him what We will for whom We like. Then, We assign Hell for him where he shall enter disgraced and rejected. (18) And whoever opts for the Hereafter and strives for it as necessary while he is a believer, then the effort of those people is appreciated (by Allah).” (Al-Isra 17:18-19)

5/ When Allah grants you a blessing, do not hide it. Some people hide their blessing out of fear of envy (حسد), but Allah wants you to show it and express your gratitude to Him. Allah says:
وَأَمَّا بِنِعۡمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثۡ (١١)
“And talk about the bounty of your Lord” (Al-Dhuha 93:11)

6/ Be always optimistic and only fluctuate between the two states of a true believer and these are being thankful to Allah or being patient. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
“عجبا لأمر المؤمن، إن أمره كله خير، وليس ذلك إلا للمؤمن، إن أصابته سراء شكر فكان خيرا له، وإن أصابته ضراء صبر فكان خيرا له”
“Amazing is the affair of the believer. All of his affairs are good. This is for no one but the believer. If something good happens to him, he is grateful, which is good for him. And if something bad happens to him, he has patience, which is good for him.” (Muslim)

7/ Allah may use people to deliver to us His blessing and He commanded us to thank those who do good to us. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
لا يَشكرِ اللهَ من لا يشكرِ الناس . رواه الإمام أحمد وأبو داود .
“Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.” (Ahmad and Aby Dawud)
إن أشكر الناس لله عز وجل أشكرهم للناس . رواه الإمام أحمد .
“The one who is most frequent in thanking of Allah is the one who is most thankful of people”. (Ahmad)
Expressing thanks to those who do good to you should be independent of the person’s belief. The Prophet (PBUH) was always acknowledging the favors that people had done for him and his family, even if those people were non-Muslims.

8/ Follow up on those whom you may have supported and express your appreciation for their success and achievements.

content:
Basics of Islam: Foundational Rules of Fiqh

Jurists have identified several foundational rules, principles, axioms, on which the Fiqh is based. These rules were derived from the Quran and the Sunnah. The key rules are expressed by brief statements such as:

1. Deeds are judged by intentions (الأمور بمقاصدها)
2. Certainty is not removed by doubt (اليقين لا يزول بالشك)
3. Hardship requires dispensation (المشقة تجلب التيسير)
4. Customs are applied (العادة محكمة)
5. Actions have consequences (الاعمال بمآلاتها).

1. Deeds are judged based on intentions

This principle is derived from the famous Hadith:

عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه ، قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : (إنما الأعمال بالنيّات ، وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى ، فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله ورسوله ، فهجرته إلى الله ورسوله ، ومن كانت هجرته لدنيا يصيبها ، أو امرأة ينكحها ، فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه ) ]رواه البخاري ومسلم [

“Actions are but by intentions and every person shall have what he intended. He whose migration was for Allah and his Messenger his migration is for Allah and his Messenger. And he whose migration was to achieve some worldly benefit his migration is for that for which he migrated.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

The importance of the intention is also supported by the Quran, as Allah said:

وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ

“And they were not ordered but to worship Allah with sincerity.” (Al-Bayyina 98:5)

While the worship is the outward deed, sincerity is its important inward element which is demonstrated by the intention.

The intention is very important because it differentiates between the devotional act and the habitual act. There are certain devotional acts that are only valid if the person declares his/her intention prior to engaging in the act. The declaration of the intention does not need to be by the tongue, it can be by the heart.

The devotional acts that require declaration of intention as a prerequisite for their acceptance are those acts whose purpose is not understood or the steps of their implementation are unique, or they are the same as other actions for different purpose. But the devotional acts whose purpose is understood and their implementation steps are clear, they are accepted even if the intention is not declared in advance.

As an example, prayers require a declaration of intention prior to performing them because we don’t know why we pray in that specific form and the same form is used for obligatory and optional prayers. Therefore, the prayer of a Muslim who is forced to pray when he has no intention to do it is not accepted and his sin of not praying remains, though he has gone through the motion of praying.

For divine commands whose purpose is understood, performing them is accepted and rewarded by Allah even if the intention is not declared in advance. These include kindness to one’s parents, fulfilling one’s oath, payment of debt, supporting one’s family, etc.

The reason why differences may exist between jurists regarding whether the intention is a pre-requisite for acceptance, is their views on whether the reason behind the command is clear. Jurists who consider the reason of a certain command is clear don’t consider declaring the intention a pre-requisite. While those who consider the reason of the command is not clear make the declaration of the intention a requirement for acceptance.

For example, if a jurist considers that the benefits of paying the zakat are obvious, he will consider that the person who pays it without declaring his intention in advance or the one who is forced to pay the zakat has already fulfilled this obligation. But a jurist who considers that the steps for implementing the zakat are ambiguous because he cannot rationalize the basis for the different percentages, he makes the declaration of intention in advance a prerequisite for their acceptance. In this case, the person who is forced to pay the zakat and he pays it without the proper intention, he is still sinful for not paying the zakat.

Another example is related to whether one needs to declare his intention before performing the Wudu or taking a bath is sufficient. Those who consider that the purpose of the Wudu is clear, the intention will not be required. But those who consider that the form of the Wudu is not understood, the intention would be required.

While the declaration of the intention that a certain act is for the sake of Allah may not be required for Allah’s acceptance, declaring the intention draws the person closer to Allah and increases the reward for that act. Train yourself to use the intention as anchor for all your actions. This can only be achieved by continuous practice. So, whether you are going to work, going to school, preparing a meal for your family, going shopping, visiting a friend, etc. you need to train yourself to say that I am doing this for the sake of Allah. After a while it will be a second nature and your heart will be making the declaration automatically. Obviously, when you train yourself to declare your intention prior to starting any act, you will be self-conscious about the nature of any act and thus you will be inhibited from engaging in any act that violates Allah’s commands.

This principle, deeds are judged by intentions, has impact on business affairs such as contracts. For example, if someone sells a sword or a knife to a person who intended to use it to kill an innocent person, the seller is considered sinful.

2. Certainty is not removed by doubt

Allah says in Surah Yunis:

وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ إِلَّا ظَنًّا إِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا

“But most of them follow nothing but doubts; truly doubts can not avail against truth”. (Younes 10:36)

Also, when the Prophet (PBUH) was asked about a person who does not remember how many rakka he has prayed, the Prophet said:

قال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام-: إذا صلى أحدكم وشك في صلاته فلم يدر كم صلى ثلاثًا، أم أربعًا فليطرح الشك وليبن على ما استيقن

“Base it on the number he is certain of”.

This principle has many applications in our daily life. It applies in the cases of doubts about a certain matter such as prayer or purity. For example, if a person is certain that he was pure and then he doubted whether he had broken his purity, his certainty of purity prevails and his doubt is ignored. Similarly, if a person is certain that he was not pure and then he doubted whether he has performed the Wudu, his certainty of lack of purity prevails and he needs to perform the Wudu.

Also, there are some differences regarding a person who is compulsive doubter in the prayer. Imam Malik considers that his doubt should be ignored. But for the normal person, the doubt should be resolved by basing the action on certainty.

This principle is very important in courts in placing the burden of proof. As an example, person A admitted that he borrowed the money but insists that he returned the money back; the burden of proof is on person A because the debt is certain and the return of the money is in doubt.

Based on the principle “certainty is not removed by doubt”, several related rules are derived. The key ones are:

1. The foundational condition for a human being is freedom.
2. A person is innocent until he incriminates himself.
3. The basis for a speech is the truth.
4. Penal code requires absolute certainty.
5. Things remain as they were in the past.
6. Purity is the foundational state of all things.

The rule of “purity is the foundational state of all things” affects the views regarding the purity of things that are not mentioned in the Quran or the Hadith as impure. For example, some scholars consider the fur of the dog to be pure based on this rule.

The rule of “certainty is not removed by doubt” has also implication regarding the purity of substances. For example, if someone is walking and some water splashed on him from the street, he should assume it is pure water unless there is a clear sign that it is impure water.

3. Hardship requires dispensation

Allah says:

يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ

“Allah wants things to be easy for you and does not want hardship for you” (Al-Baqara 2:185)

Also, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قَالَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاَةُ وَالسَّلاَمُ ( إِنَّ خَيْرَ دِينِكُم أَيْسَرُهُ ، إِنَّ خَيْرَ دِينِكُم أَيْسَرُهُ ، إِنَّ خَيْرَ دِينِكُم أَيْسَرُهُ ) . (رواه أحمد)

“The best in your religion is its easiest (repeated it three times),””. (Ahmad)

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ ( إِنَّمَا بُعِثْتُم مُيَسِّرِينَ ، وَلَمْ تُبْعَثُوا مُعَسِّرِينَ ) . (رواه البخاري ومسلم)

“You were sent to make things easy, and you were not sent to make things difficult.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

قَالَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاَةُ وَالسَّلاَمُ: “إن الله لم يبعثني معنتًا ولا متنعنتًا، ولكن بعثني معلمًا ميسرًا”

“Allah did not send me to be harsh or make things difficult, rather He sent me to be a teacher and make things easy.”

When the Prophet, (PBUH) sent Abu Musa and Mu’adh to Yemen, he said to them:

عن أبي موسى الأشعري أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بعثه ومعاذا إلى اليمن، فقال: «يسِّرا ولا تعسِّرا، وبشِّرا ولا تنفِّرا، وتطاوعا ولا تختلفا»

“Make things easy, and don’t make them difficult. Give people glad tiding and don’t alienate the people. Cooperate and do not differ.”

When someone complained about Mu’adh because he lengthened the prayer, the Prophet reprimanded him by saying: “O’ Mu’adh, are you trying to create fitnah (an uprising)”.

This principle is also expressed by different terms such as:

1. Necessities allow the prohibited. (الضرورات تبيح المحظورات)
2. Harm should be removed (الضرر يزال)
3. When the matter is constricted, it requires expansion. (إذا ضاق الأمر اتسع)

Scholars have also ranked prohibitions in two categories:

1. Prohibitions of aims (محرمات المقاصد). These are based on a clear text and are forbidden for in-itself.
2. Prohibition of means (محرمات الوسائل). These are based on a general text and are forbidden because they can lead to something that is forbidden.

This distinction between the prohibitions based on aims and those based on means is derived from the following Hadith:

عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّه عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : (( إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْجُلُوسَ فِي الطُّرُقَاتِ ))

“Never sit in the roads.”

The people: “O Messenger of Allah, we have a need to meet and talk. ”The Prophet said, “If the meeting is what you want, then give the road its right.” They said, “What is its right, O Messenger of Allah?” The Prophet said, “Lower the gaze, avoid harming others, return the greetings of peace, enjoin the good, and forbid the evil.” (Ahmad and Abu Daud)

In this case the prohibition of sitting in the road was not an aim in-itself but it was based on the fact that sitting in the road may lead to harming people or looking at things that are prohibited.

Based on this distinction, many scholars say that the prohibition of mean can be violated when there is a medium hardship or a need, while the prohibition of aim can only be violated when there is a large hardship or a necessity.

Scholars have divided hardships into three levels: 1) large hardship, 2) medium hardship, and 3) small hardship.

Large hardship is related to essential needs to protect life and avoid physical harm. This type of hardship makes the prohibitions of aims to be violated. As an example, the person who is choking and the only available liquid is Alcohol, he is allowed to drink it to save his life.

Medium hardship is related to normal needs. This type of hardship is generally associated with commerce and business transactions. In this case, the prohibition based on aims cannot be violated but the prohibition based on means can be violated. (ما حرم لذاته لا يباح إلا للضرورة، وما حرم لسد الذريعة يباح للحاجة)

For example, a Muslim is prohibited from setting in a place where Alcohol is present, but since this is prohibition based on mean (sitting with those who drink may lead to drinking), a person who is traveling and the only place to eat is a restaurant that serves Alcohol, he is allowed to eat there.

Scholars have also suggested that under certain conditions, a need can be elevated to medium hardship or even to a necessity.

Small hardships are related to inconvenience. Hardships that may result in some inconveniences such as wearing some heavy clothes for the prayer when it is hot or performing the Wudu when the water is considered small, and they do not remove obligations or allow prohibitions.

4. Customs are applied

This may be important rule particularly for Muslims who live in the west because they live in societies whose customs are different from the customs of the Muslim countries. Allah says in the Quran:

لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً ۚ وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ مَتَاعًا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ۖ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ

“It is no sin for you if you divorce women while you have not yet touched them, nor appointed for them a portion. But bestow on them (a gift), the wealthy according to his means, and the poor according to his means, a customary amount is due from those who wish to do the right thing”. (2:236)

In this verse, Allah did not specify the value of the gift but leaves it up to the customs of that society.

Upon the arrival of the Prophet (PBUH) to the Mosque in Madinah after his return from a trip, the Ethiopians were playing and dancing in the Mosque. The Prophet said: “They are the people of Bani Arfida (referring to their tribe in Africa) and this is their customs, so leave them”. We all know this story because Sayeda Aisha watched them and when she got tired, the Prophet (PBUH) left with her.

After the Prophet’s victorious return to Mecca, Hend bent Utba, the wife of Abu Sufian, came to him and complained that her husband is a stingy person and she asked whether she is allowed to take from his money without his knowledge. The Prophet said: “Take what satisfies you and your children based on the customs”. (Referring to the customary spending of someone in her status.)

In legal setting, customs can serve in lieu of two witnesses, as will be the case in distributing the furniture of the house between the husband and wife in case of divorce. The items that are customarily for the use of the husband will go to him and those for the use of the wife will go to her.

Customs can also allow for certain transactions that may have been prohibited in the past. As an example, selling the fruit of the tree before it is ripe was prohibited by the Prophet (PBUH), but since now the risk of the loss is minimal and the customs of the farmers allow it, it is considered acceptable.

However, when customs are considered, they must satisfy four conditions:

1. The custom cannot violate any textual ruling from the Quran, or authentic hadith.
2. The custom must be broadly recognized and followed by the majority.
3. The custom must be stable and unambiguous, as an example in the U.S the customary currency is a dollar.
4. The custom must be precedent and not recent. This is important in some legal ruling as in the case of dowry where the customary amount at the time of the contract should be applied.

5. Actions have Consequences

Allah commanded Muslim not to insult the idols of the polytheist because this may lead them to curse Allah:

وَلا تَسُبُّوا الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ فَيَسُبُّوا اللهَ عَدْوًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ ( الأنعام: 108 )

“Do not insult those whom they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah wrongfully without knowledge.” (6:108)

The following are examples on how the Prophet (PBUH) has always deliberated on the consequences of his actions before performing them:

1/ When the Prophet (PBUH) was asked by Omar (RA) to give him the permission to kill the leader of the hypocrites, the Prophet said: “No, lest the people say that Muhammad is killing his companions”.

وعن جابر بن عبد الله – رضي الله عنهما – يقول : كنا في غزاة ، فكسع رجل من المهاجرين رجلاً من الأنصار ، فقال الأنصاري : يا للأنصار ، وقال المهاجري : يا للمهاجرين ، فسمع ذلك رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – فقال : ” ما بال دعوى الجاهلية ” ، قالوا : يا رسول الله ، كسع رجل من المهاجرين رجلاً من الأنصار ، فقال : ” دعوها ؛ فإنها منتنة ” ، فسمع بذلك عبد الله بن أبي ، فقال : أقد فعلوها ؟ والله لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ، فبلغ النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – فقام عمر فقال : يا رسول الله ، دعني أضرب عنق هذا المنافق ، فقال النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : ” دعه لا يتحدث الناس أن محمداً يقتل أصحابه ” (رواه البخاري ومسلم)

2/ After the Prophet (PBUH) returned victorious to Mecca, he wanted to build the Kabba on the foundation of Ibrahim. He told Aisha: “If it was not because your people are new to Islam, I would have demolished the Kabba and rebuild it on the foundation of Ibrahim and made two doors for it”.

عن عبد الله بن الزبير يقول : حدثتني خالتي (يعني : عائشة) رضي الله عنها قالت : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يا عائشة لولا أن قومك حديثو عهد بشرك لهدمت الكعبة فألزقتها بالأرض وجعلت لها بابين باباً شرقياً وباباً غربياً وزدت فيها ستة أذرع من الحجر فإن قريشاً اقتصرتها حيث بنت الكعبة ) (رواه البخاري ومسلم)

So, here the Prophet (PBUH) was concerned about the impact of the confusion that may cause the people of Mecca who just entered Islam.

3/ The Prophet (PBUH) did not come to the Masjid on the third day of Ramadan for Taraweeh after he had prayed with the people for two days. He said: “I was afraid that it may become an obligation for you”.

Using this principle, Imam Malik made it a dislikable act for a person to fast the six in Shawaal if he is a scholar or a leader so that the people do not think it is an obligation.

This principle is important when considering the impact on our actions and behaviors, the way we dress, and the way we talk to people.

This foundational rule of Fiqh “Actions have Consequences” has been expressed using other phrases such as:

1. Removal of harm takes priority over brining benefits (إزالة الضرر فوق جلب المنفعة)
2. There should be no harm to yourself or to other (لا ضرر ولا ضرار)

Closure:

We have completed the discussion on Aqidah, Shariah and Fiqh. On Fiqh we discussed the main tools and sources and the foundational rules. The goal of this discussion was to achieve the following:

1. Appreciating that the key goals of Islamic shariah are protection of human rights, promoting mercy and achieving the benefits of the people.
2. Realizing the main reasons for the differences that may exist among jurists on the same issue.
3. Becoming tolerant to differing opinions.
4. Knowing how to frame a Fiqh question properly and understanding the basis for the received response.
5. Selecting the qualified person to ask a Fiqh question by realizing that the scholars of Fiqh are generally divided in three categories:
6. The creative jurist who has the knowledge and the intellectual capacity to derive the rules from the original sources.
7. The integrator jurist who studies the different schools of Fiqh and derive a ruling based on the one that is most applicable for the current time and place.
8. The follower jurist who is knowledgeable in a specific school of Fiqh and drive the opinion solely based on this school of Fiqh.

A good website for Fiqh that address issues of interest for people who live in the west can be found at: https://www.e-cfr.org/

title: The Dilemma of the Federal Reserve (November 6, 2022)
excerpt:
The Dilemma of the Federal Reserve (November 6, 2022)

content:
The Dilemma of the Federal Reserve (November 6, 2022)

This is a brief talk to initiate discussion on the US and world economy because we have been studying the subject of Fiq and we realized that the great Imams always wanted the Muslims to know the basics of their religion and to make their own assessments.  As examples:  Imam Malik said: “I am just a human being who can be right and can make mistakes, so investigate my opinion, if it is consistent with the Book and the Sunnah, then follow it and if it was not that way, you should leave it.” And Imam Ahmad said: “Don’t copy me, or Malik, or Al-Shafie, or Al-Awzaie or Al-Thouri, but take from what we have taken.”

So, when it comes to economy and business, we need to also understand some of the basics that are currently challenging the US Federal reserve and their potential impact.

The US federal reserve has two mandates:
1. Keep unemployment rate to between 4 and 5%
2. Hold the inflation to about 2%

The Current Challenge: the inflation is about 8.4%

So, the solution is to slow down the economy by increasing the interest rate.  This is what the Fed has been doing, they increased the interest rate for almost zero to 4% and it is expected that they will increase it to 5% by March 2023 and some analysts project that the Fed will increase the interest rate to 6%.

But here is the challenge that the Fed is facing, and this is that none of the increases they made are slowing down the economy.   There are six key economic indicators that show that the US economy is not impacted.  These are:
1. Unemployment rate continues to be low; it is now 3.5%
2. The growth rate of the economy continues to be high, in last quarter it was 2.6%
3. The capacity utilization of the US industry is 80%, the highest in 40 years (I.e., there is no spare capacity to increase production)
4. The percent of loan defaulters is very low, it is only 1.2%.
5. The difference in the interest rates the bank charges the US government and charges the risky companies (junk rate) is only 4%. During the coronavirus epidemic, the difference was 8%.
6. The volatility index of the stock market is only 26% while it was 80% during corona. The normal value is 20%.

So, all these indicators show that the increase in the interest rate is not slowing the US economy.  But this picture is not totally correct because all these indicators are lagging indicators about the past but not the future.

But when we look at possible leading indicators, they suggest that the economy will slow down.  Three of these leading indicators are:
1. The dollar index: the dollar compared to the other currencies is the highest in 40 years. This is expected to hurt the US export causing slow down.
2. The mortgage applications are the slowest in 35 years. This put pressure of the housing market slowing down construction.
3. The S&P is down 20%. This means that investors will slow down their purchasing capacity.

The US is raising the interest rate to slow down the economy and control the inflation.  Other countries need to do the same and increase their interest rate to avoid foreign currencies from leaving their banks to the US.   But if these countries do this, they will slow down their economies and their unemployment rate which is already high will get higher and this can cause social disturbances.  Therefore, they may politically decide not to increase the interest rate and instead float their currencies which will lead to devaluating their currencies.   This will help if the country is net exporter because their products will be cheaper, but for countries that are net importer, they will have major economic problems no matter what they do.

So, the decisions of the US federal reserve to increase interest rate may bring world-wide recession.

Another factor that is also interesting is the relationship between the chines Yuan and the Japanese yen.  A year ago, the Chinese Yuan was 15.7 Yen, now it is 20.4 yen.   This means that the Chinese goods will be more expense than the Japanese and this will slow down the economy of China unless they devaluate their currency.

content:
Basics of Islam: Fiqh (Jurisprudence)

Literally the term “Fiqh” means understanding and comprehension. In the religious context “Fiqh” refers to understanding the Quran and the authentic Hadith to transform them into laws and procedures for societal and individual applications considering the conditions under which the rulings are applied. Muslim Jurists describe the role of Fiqh as “Transferring the divine text into reality (تنزيل النص على الواقع)” (Tanzil Alnas Alaa Alwaqie).

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the importance of understanding the divine commands of the religion by saying:

[عن مُعَاوِيَةَ بن أبي سفيان رضي الله عنه قال: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ : (مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ).] البخاري (71) ، ومسلم (1037)

“If Allah wants to do good to a person, He makes him understand the religion.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

Imam Ibn Timiah (ابن تيمية) said:

” كُلُّ مَنْ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يُفَقِّهَهُ فِي الدِّينِ ، فَمَنْ لَمْ يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ ، لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا “

“Whoever Allah wants good in him; He will make him understand the religion. So, whoever Allah does not make him understand the religion, Allah does not want good for him.”

This suggests that Muslims are required to understand their religion by at least understanding the basis on which a Jurist would derive a ruling from the divine text.

The rules of Fiqh are the same rules that are mentioned under Shariah, and these are:

Rulings of Sacred Law

Prescribed/obligatory: P: rewarded, NP: punished
Recommended: P: rewarded, NP: not punished
Permissible: P: not rewarded, NP: not punished
Disliked: P: not punished, NP: rewarded
Unlawful/prohibited: P: punished, NP: rewarded

The interest in Fiqh started after the Prophet’s death to address the application of the divine text in the societal needs. For example, rulings in Madinah were made by what was known as the seven jurists of Madinah: Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Sayeda Aisha, Zayd Ibn Thabet, Abd Allah Ibn Omar and Ibn Abbas. As Islam spread, some of them left Madinah to serve as Jurists in other states. As an example, Ibn Masoud went to Iraq to serve as its jurist on the order of Khalifa Omar.

During that time, the Fiqh rulings were not documented formally. The formal documentation of Fiqh started in the second century after Hijrah. This resulted in establishing several schools of Fiqh. Each school of Fiqh was named after the Imam who established it. Each school has students who became teachers after completing their education and became qualified to derive rulings using the principles established by the Imam of the school. These rules were documented under the Imam’s names, though many were not his but his students. Therefore, you can find differences in opinions within the same school of Fiqh.

While there are many schools of Fiqh, the four that more widely known are:

1. Imam Abu Hanifa (80-150 after Higra) – Born in Kufa, Iraq
2. Imam Malik (93-179 AH) – Born In Madinah
3. Imam Al-Shafia (150-204 AH) – Born in Gaza, Palestine
4. Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal (164-241 AH) – Born in Baghdad, Iraq

As previously mentioned, while the schools refer to these Imams, they were developed mostly by their students and the student of their students. It is noteworthy, however, to mention that these four schools agree on approximately 75% of their legal conclusions.

In addition, there are other such the Imamia school (مذهب الامامية) that is mainly used by the Shai sect. This school is often referred to as Al-Jaafari school in reference to Imam Jaafar Al-Sadiq (80-148 AH). However, the main contributor to the Imamia school is Muhammad ibn Ishaq (محمد ابن يعقوب بن اسحاق الكليني الرازي) (d: 328 H) the author of the book (الكافي في علوم الدين) “The sufficient in the Knowledge of the Religion”.

Another school of Fiqh is the Zahiri school that was developed in Andalusia by Imam Daoud ibn Ali Al-Zahri (داود ابن علي الاصفهاني الظاهري) (270-202H) and promoted by Imam Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Sa`id ibn Hazm (384-456 AH).

In addition, there are some not well formalized schools of Fiqh that are based on the opinions of several Imams such as Al-Thawri, Ibn Abu-Laila, Al Awza’i, and Al-Laith. Also, Imam Ahmad ibn Abd Al-Haleem ibn Timeiah (born in 661 H) has also developed his own Fiqh.

It should always be understood that the founders of the different Fiqh schools had high respect for each other. As an example, Imam Al-Shafia described Imam Abu Hanifa by saying: "I have never seen anyone who is more knowledgeable than Abu-Hanifa". He also described Imam Malik by saying: “Malik is the proof that Allah will use His servants”.

Those great Imams were humble and unassuming, Imam Malik said: “I am just a human being who can be right and can make mistakes, so investigate my opinion, if it is consistent with the Book and the Sunnah, then follow it and if it was not that way, you should leave it.”

Imam Ahmad said: “Don’t copy me, or Malik, or Al-Shafie, or Al-Awzaie or Al-Thouri, but take from what we have taken.”

The Tools of Fiqh

While the primary sources for deriving religious laws in all schools for Fiqh are the Quran and the authentic hadith, the Imams of the schools and students adopted different tools of Fiqh were derived from the Quran and the hadith. The following are the main tools of Fiqh:

1. Consensus (Unanimity of Muslim scholars) “Al-jgmaa”
2. Direct or indirect analogical reasoning” Al-Qiyas”
3. General benefits to the community” Al-Masalehl-Al-Mustarsah”
4. Actions of people of Madinah.
5. Opinion of the companions of the Prophet
6. Juristic preference “Al-Istehsan”

Justifications for the Tools of Fiqh

1. Consensus: The concept of using the consensus of scholars as a source for Fiqh is based on the following verse in Surah Al-Nisaa:

وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ الرَّسُولَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ الْهُدَى وَيَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّى وَنُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا

“Anyone who opposes the messenger after guidance has been explained to him and follows some path other than that of the believers. We shall leave him in the path he has chosen and land him in Hell, what an evil refuge” (Al-Nisaa 4:115)

Some suggest that this the principle of consensus is also supported by the following hadith, though this hadith has been deemed weak based on the narrators (Sanad).

“لا تجتمع أمتي على ضلالة”. ]رواه ابن ماجه، والطبراني، وغيره[. ) ضعيف الإسناد(

“My nation will never unite on error.” (Ibn Majah and Al-Tabarani)

In spite of its ranking as weak, some scholars interpreted this hadith to mean that the Prophet’s nation will not unit on a condition of kufr or deviance.

2. Analogical Reasoning: This rule is based on many examples in which this principle was used by the Prophet (PBUH). As example, a woman asked the Prophet whether she can perform the Hajj on behalf of her father who cannot do it. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “If you father has a debt, would you pay it?” She said: yes.

He (PBUH) said: “The debt of Allah is more deserving to be paid”.

Also, a man came to the Prophet (PBUH) expressing doubt about fathering his child because the child has dark skin while he and his wife have light skins. The Prophet (PBUH) asked him: “Do you have camels?” The man said: yes.

The Prophet (PBUH) asked: “What is their color?” The man said: Yellow. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “Does any of them have gray color?” The man said: Yes. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “From where?” The man said: from previous ancestors. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “And it so for your child”. (i.e., recessive genes)

3. General Benefits: This tool is used in cases when there is no guidance in the Quran or the Sunnah. The most obvious example for the application of this rule is the assembly of the Quran. When Omar suggested to Khalifa Abu Bakr to collect the Quran and assemble it in one manuscript after the death of many of the companions who memorized the Quran, Abu Baker’s first reaction was to object because the Prophet did not do it. But Omar told him “In this, there are benefits”. Abu Baker was convinced of the general benefits and asked Zaid Ibn Harith to collect it.

4. Actions of People of Madinah: Imam Malik considered a widespread practice of the people of Madinah, such as the form of Azan should be a source for Fiqh because it would not have been done unless it is sanctioned by the Prophet and the thousands of the companions. He gave a preference to the actions of People of Madinah over a solitary Hadith (narrated by a single person).

Summary of Tools by School:

- Abu-Hanifa: Quran and sunnah + Consensus + analogical reasoning + juristic preference + customs
- Malik: Quran and Sunnah + Consensus + analogical reasoning + general benefits + actions of people of madinah + opinions of the companions
- Al-Shafie: Quran and Sunnah + Consensus + analogical reasoning. Reject: juristic preference, general benefits, actions of people of Madinah, and the opinions of the companions
- Ahmad Ibn Hanbal: Quran and Sunnah + the opinions of the Prophet’s companions. He uses a weak Hadith over analogical reasoning
- Al-Imamiah (Gaafar Al-Sadeq): Quran and the Sunnah (that is only derived from hadith narrated by sources accepted to the Shia) + the Consensus that is only derived for divine text+ Ijtihad (renewal of interpretation by the shiah Imams). Reject: analogical reasoning
- Al-Zahri (Ibn Hazm): Quran and Sunnah (only the apparent meaning unless there are other evidence to justify using the unapparent meaning) + Consensus of the Prophet’s companions only + proof. Reject: analogical reasoning and juristic preference
- Ibn Timiah: Quran and Sunnah + Ijtihad (renewal of interpretation by all who are qualified). Reject: the restriction of adopting a certain school of Fiqh.

In addition to the differences among the schools of Fiqh that may result due to the use of different tools, differences can also exist between Jurists even when considering the same verse from the Quran or the same hadith for two main reasons. These are:

1/ The use of different authentication criteria for the Prophet’s Hadith. Thus, one Jurist may accept a Hadith while another Jurist may reject it because he raises questions about the reliability of its transmission. As an example, while Imam Malik accepted a hadith that may not be continuous in transmission, Imam Shafie only accepted the hadith whose transmission is continuous.

2/ The use of different linguistic analysis factors even when considering the same text from the Quran and authentic hadith. The science of textual analysis and signification of a text is critical in deriving a legal ruling from a divine text. Scholars have developed about 40 linguistic factors that need to be considered as part of understanding the intent and the nature of the text. These rules assess whether the text is broad or limited, general or specific (العام والخاص), implicit or explicit (الحقيقة والمجاز), apparent or implied (الظاهر والمؤول), imperative or descriptive (المجمل والبيان), etc.

An example to illustrate how opinions can greatly differ while looking at the same text is related to the rights of the divorced woman that is described in the first verse of Surah Al-Talaq in which Allah says:

يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ لَا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخْرُجْنَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ لَا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمْرًا

“O Prophet, when you (men) divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed periods of Iddah and count the period of Iddah and fear Allah, your Lord. And do not expel them from their homes, nor should they leave unless they commit a clearly shameful act. These are the limits prescribed by Allah. And whosoever transgresses the limits prescribed by Allah does indeed wrong himself. You do not know if by chance, Allah will bring about a new situation. (Al-Talaq 65:1)

The application of this verse in a legal ruling was a subject of dispute between Khalifa Omar and a woman by the name Fatima Bent Quays (فاطمة بنت قيس). Khalifa Omar considered the command of giving a woman who was divorced for the third time, which is irrevocable divorce, the right for domestic habitation. But Fatima Bent Quays considered the command is specific and objected to Omar’s giving such a woman should not have domestic habitation rights. She argued that the command is specific because the ending of the verse indicates that such rights is given because Allah may bring a new situation, which is reconciliation, but in this case, there will be no chance for reconciliation because the divorce is irrevocable.

In this case Fatima Bent Quays considered the ruling in the verse as specific to the condition of possible reconciliation while Khalifa Omar considered the ruling in the verse as general, independent of the ending circumstance. When you examine the ruling of the different Imams in this matter, you will find that Imam Abu Hanifa followed Khalifa Omar ruling while the other three Imams (Malik, Shafie and Ahmad) followed the ruling of Fatima Quays.

In addition to the importance of this event in deriving a legal ruling, it provides an insight on how much influence early Muslim women had on our Fiqh and demonstrates the ability of early Muslim women to holding their ground and arguing with vigor their Fiqh position in front of anyone including one of the most powerful Khalifa. This event as well as many others that have been recorded in the Islamic history offer the clear proof that Islam offered women roles that would be envied by women in any other civilization. Unfortunately, there are Muslims who would rather revert back to the way women were treated in the dark ignorant (Jahelia) time rather than continuing to treat women in the way they were treated during the Prophet’s time and the magnificent Islamic era.

Many scholars recognize that new meanings can be drawn from the same text as time, place and people change. They consider that those who insist on freezing the meanings and, thus, stagnating the Fiqh are committing grave mistakes. As an example, Imam Al-Qarafi (القرافي) who is one of the great Maliki jurists said:

الجمود أبداً على النصوص ضلال وإضلال.

“The stagnation in interpreting the meanings of the text is misguided and leads to misguidance”.

Scholars have identified few foundational rules, principles, and axioms, on which the Fiqh is based. These rules are derived from the Quran and the Sunnah and are expressed by the following brief statements:

1. Deeds are judged by intentions.
2. Certainty is not removed by doubt
3. Hardship requires dispensation
4. Customs are applied
5. Actions have consequences.

We will inshallah discuss these rules next week to provide their justification and the relevance of their applications.
