content:
Basics of Islam: Aqidah and Shariah

The Sources of Knowledge about Religion
The knowledge about any religion is derived from two sources, the divine revelation to the Messenger of Allah and the teachings of that messenger to his people. In Islam these two sources are the Quran and the Hadith.

The Quran
The Quran is the primary source of knowledge about Islam. It has the exact words of Allah that were revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who transmitted them to us verbatim and complete. The Quran that we have today is the exact Quran that was memorized by massive number of the Prophet’s companions and documented in writing by several designated writers under the Prophet’s supervision.

Upon the Prophet’s death, the first Muslim ruler, Khalifa Abu-Bakr, ordered the assembly of the Quran in one manuscript. This task was assigned to the Prophet’s trusted companion Zayd in Thabit. Zayd was extremely careful to ensure that no single error, however slight or unintentional, should creep into the Quran. When Zayd completed his task, he gave the compiled manuscript with Khalifa Abu Bakr. Before his death, Abu Bakr gave the manuscript with Omar who in turn left it with his daughter Hafsah, who was one of the wives of the Prophet.

During the time of the third Muslim leader, Uthman, Islam spread far. To ensure that differences in reading the Quran do not materialize, Uthman obtained the manuscript of the Quran from Hafsah and again summoned Zayd ibn Thabit to lead a group of competent companions to make accurate copies of it. Uthman sent a copy to every Muslim province, kept a copy for himself and returned the original manuscript to Hafsah.

Two of Uthman’s prepared originals exit today, one in Istanbul, Turkey and the second in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. However, the original manuscripts of the Quran did not include markings (Tashkeel). The Tashkeel was added on the order of the 5th Umayyad Caliph, Abd Al-Malik Ibn Marwaan (66-86 H, 685-705 CE) to ensure that those who are not proficient in the Arabic language to read it properly. The Quran we have now is a copy of that Quran.

The Quran is the only divinely revealed book for which the following are known:
1. The person who documented it in one manuscript
2. When the documentation was done
3. How its authenticity was assured during the assembly of the first manuscript

In addition, the Quran is the only book who text includes the following:
1. The definition of its purpose.
2. Affirmation that the Quran was revealed by God.
3. The name of the messenger to whom the book was revealed.
4. Tests to verify that the book in hand is the revealed book by God
5. The guarantees that the Quran’s authenticity is preserved and that it is free from any error

The Purpose of the Quran as revealed in the Quran:
ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ‌ۛ فِيهِ‌ۛ هُدً۬ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٢)
“This Book has not doubt in it, a guidance for the righteous” (Al-Baqara 2:2).

وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّا لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ‌ۙ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٦٤)
“We have not sent down the book to you except to explain to them what they differed about, and as a guidance and mercy for a people who believe,” (Al-Nahl 16:64).

وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)
“We have sent the book down to you explaining all things, and guidance, mercy and glad tidings for the Muslims” (Al-Nahl 16:89).

Allah affirms that that the Quran is His revelation:
لَّـٰكِنِ ٱللَّهُ يَشۡہَدُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ إِلَيۡكَ‌ۖ أَنزَلَهُ ۥ بِعِلۡمِهِۦ‌ۖ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ يَشۡہَدُونَ‌ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَہِيدًا (١٦٦)
“Allah bears witness that what He has sent down to you, He has sent with His Knowledge and the angels bear witness: though Allah suffices as a Witness” (Al-Nisa 4:166).

The Quran states that it was revealed to Allah’s Messenger Muhammad (PBUH)
وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَءَامَنُواْ بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدٍ۬ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ‌ۙ كَفَّرَ عَنۡہُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ وَأَصۡلَحَ بَالَهُمۡ (٢)
“And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad, for it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them their sins and improve their condition.” (Muhammad 47:2).

Tests to assure that the book in hand is the revealed book by God
أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ‌ۚ وَلَوۡ كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ غَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخۡتِلَـٰفً۬ا كَثِيرً۬ا (٨٢)
“Have they not seriously examined the Quran? If it had been from any other source than Allah, they would surely have found in it many contradictions” (Al-Nisa 4:82).

وَإِن ڪُنتُمۡ فِى رَيۡبٍ۬ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةٍ۬ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (٢٣)
“If you are in any doubt about what We have revealed to our servant (Muhammad), then produce a chapter like it and call upon your witnesses besides Allah if you are truthful” (Al-Baqara 2:23).

The Quran’s includes the guarantees for its preservation and freedom from any error
إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ ۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ (٩)
“We (Allah) have, sent down the dhikr (the Quran) and We shall certainly preserve it (from corruption)” (Al-Hijr 15:9).

لَّا يَأۡتِيهِ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَلَا مِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ‌ۖ تَنزِيلٌ۬ مِّنۡ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ۬ (٤٢)
“No falsehood can approach it (the Quran) from neither from its front of it or behind it. It is a revelation from one who is All-Wise and Praiseworthy” (Fussilat 41:42).

The Quran has always been preserved in two ways, hard copies (in paper and digital forms) and memorization.

The Hadith
The hadith is the second source of knowledge about Islam. The hadith books are records of the Prophet’s words, actions, and approvals.

Because of the delay in documenting the hadith, Muslim scholars developed procedures to validate the authenticity of a hadith. The validation criteria include:
1. The chain of narrators is continuous to the Prophet (PBUH) without interruptions.
2. The consecutive narrators must have lived in the same time period.
3. The narrators satisfy certain criteria regarding the trustworthiness and good memory.

However, differences occurred in the authentication level of a hadith because scholars differed in the strictness of their criteria. In this talk, I will only discuss two types of hadith that are considered the most authentic. The two types are:
1. The honorable Hadith (الحديث العزيز).
This classification requires that two companions heard it directly from the Prophet (PBUH) and then from each of them, two narrators heard it until the hadith was documented in a book.
An example of this classification is the hadith that was heard by both Anas and Abu Hurryrah and they said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عَنْ أَنَس – رضي الله عنه – قال: قال النَّبِيُّ – صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم -: ((لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ، وَوَلَدِهِ، وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ))
“None of you believe until I am more loved by him than his father, his son, and all the people”. (Bukhari and Muslim).

This classification of requiring that two people heard the hadith from the Prophet (PBUH) was the rule used by Khalifa Omar ibn Al-Khattab.
عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال كنت في مجلس من مجلس الأنصار إذا جاء أبو موسى الأشعري كأنه مذعور فقال استأذنت على عمر ثلاثا فلم يؤذن لي فرجعت فقال ما منعك قلت استأذنت ثلاثا فلم يؤذن لي فرجعت وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا استأذن أحدكم ثلاثا فلم يؤذن له فليرجع فقال والله لتأتيني على ذلك بالبينة )والا أوجعتك( أمنكم أحد سمعه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أبي بن كعب والله لا يقوم معك إلا أصغر القوم فكنت أصغر القوم فقمت معه فأخبرت عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ذلك.
I was sitting in a company of people from Al-Ansar when (أبو موسى الأشعري) Abou Musa Al-Ashaari came looking scared. He said: I asked Omar for permission to enter three times and he did not give me permission, so I left. Omar sent for me and asked: why did you leave? I said: I asked for permission three times and I did not get it, and the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:
If any of you ask permission three times and do not get permission, you should leave.
Omar said: Either you find for me a proof from someone else of what you said, or I’ll hurt you; did any of you hear this from the Prophet? Ubai ibn Ka’ab said: Only the youngest among us will go with you. I (Abou Said) was the youngest, so I went and testified to Omar that the Prophet (PBUH) said that.

Another example of insisting on two independent sources is the hadith by Qabisah ibn Dhuwayb (قبيصة بن ذؤيب):
جاءت جدة إلى أبي بكر تطلب ميراثها. فقال أبو بكر: مالك في كتاب الله شيء، ما ذكر الله للجدة فرضاً وما علمت أن رسول الله قضى للجدة بشيء، وارجعي حتى أسأل الناس. فقام المغيرة بن شعبة وقال: يا خليفة رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام، حضرت النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام وقد أطعم الجدة السدس، فقال له أبو بكر: هل معك أحد؟ فقام محمد بن مسلمة فقال مثل ما قال المغيرة، فأنفذه لها أبو بكر.
A grandmother came to Abu Bakr asking him for her share of inheritance. He said: There is nothing prescribed for you in the book of Allah, and I do not know that the Messenger (PBUH) prescribed anything for the grandmother. Go back until I ask people. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah stood up and said: O khalifa of the Messenger (PBUH), I had been present when the Prophet (PBUH) gave the grandmother one sixth. Abu Bakr said: Is there anyone who can testify with you? Muhammad ibn Maslamah stood and said I can testify to that. Then Abu Bakr implemented the ruling.

2. The Massively Transmitted” (Mutawater) (متواتر) Hadith:
This classification is considered the highest level of authenticity of the Prophet’s hadith. Scholars differ on the minimum number of companions that heard the hadith directly from the Prophet (PBUH) to be classified as massively transmitted, but most agree it is at least ten.
Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (جلال الدين السيوطي) (849-911 H), in his book “Harvesting scattered flowers of massively transmitted hadith”, listed 113 such hadith.
An example of a massively transmitted hadith that was narrated by about 200 companions is. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
إن كذِبَاً عليَّ ليس ككذب على أحد، من كذب علي متعمدا فليتبوأ مقعده من النار )البخاري(
“Lying about me is as lying about others whoever invents a lie and attributes it to me intentionally, let him prepare for his place in hellfire” (Bukhari).

One needs to ensure that his words and practices are based on authentic information. The authentic information is the only way to protect one’s self on the Day of Judgment.
يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِى ڪُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ تُجَـٰدِلُ عَن نَّفۡسِہَا وَتُوَفَّىٰ ڪُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (١١١)
“(Remember) the Day when every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and they will not be wronged.” (Al-Nahl 16:111).

Also, Allah says:
وَلَقَدۡ جِئۡتُمُونَا فُرَٲدَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ۬ وَتَرَكۡتُم مَّا خَوَّلۡنَـٰكُمۡ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِكُمۡ‌ۖ (٩٤)
And truly you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time. You have left behind you all that which We had bestowed on you. (Al-Anaam 6:94).

وَكُلَّ إِنسَـٰنٍ أَلۡزَمۡنَـٰهُ طَـٰٓٮِٕرَهُ ۥ فِى عُنُقِهِۦ‌ۖ وَنُخۡرِجُ لَهُ ۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ كِتَـٰبً۬ا يَلۡقَٮٰهُ مَنشُورًا (١٣)
And We have tied up every man’s book of deeds to his neck, and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall bring out for him a book which he will find wide open. (Al-Israa 17:13).

Based on the Quran and the authentic hadith, scholars divided the knowledge of Islam the religion of God into two parts: Aqidah and Shariah.

Aqidah (عقيدة) (creed/belief/faith)
While the term Aqidah is not in the Quran or hadith, scholars derive it from the term i’tiqaad (belief/certainty). Aqidah is the theoretical part of Islam that deals with the belief system.
The articles of belief as provided in the Quran are the beliefs in Allah, his angels, his books, his messengers, the Day of Judgment, and destiny (Qadar).
Unlike followers of other religions who justify their beliefs based on feelings, Islamic beliefs must be based on knowledge (Certainty). Allah says:
فاعلم أنه لا إله إلا الله
“Know that there is no god but Allah” (Muhammad 47:19)

Therefore, any matter of Aqida must satisfy three conditions:
1. Firm Recognition (إدراك جازم) that one’s heart is certain about it without any wavering or doubt.
2. Consistent with Realities (مطابقة للواقع) (Example: it is the reality that a stone statue that it cannot hear or respond, so the belief that it is a god is not Aqidah).
3. Based on Proofs (الناشئ عن دليل) (example: Since everything that exists needs a maker, the presence of creation is the proof of the existence of the creator).

Muslim scholars consider the imitator whose belief is not based on proof is not a true believer. The imitation is forbidden in Aqidah.
The Aqidah in Islam has a practical component that is built on the belief that the Quran is the exact word of Allah and it is the source of laws (Shariah).

Shariah (شريعة)
Literally, Shariah means a direction to be followed. It is the practical side of Aqidah and it governs all aspects of life.
وَ لَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا
“Do not follow their desires and thus deviating from the truth that has come to you. To each among you, We have prescribed a law (Shariah) and a clear way (Minhaj).” (Al-Maida 5:48).

The shariah (الشريعة) is a set of divine laws that encompasses rituals (acts of worship) and legal rulings (legal code). Shariah is intended to provide mankind with the life that is based on goodness and fairness.
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ
“You who believe, Obey Allah and the Prophet because He invites you to what which gives you life” (Al-Anfal 8:24).

All laws in Islamic shariah are intended to protect the five essentials of safe living and these are: Religion, Life, Mind, Honor/Progeny, and Property.

Islamic Shariah also alleviates the hardships (رفع الحرج والمشقة) that was imposed on previous nations.
ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِىَّ ٱلۡأُمِّىَّ ٱلَّذِى يَجِدُونَهُ ۥ مَكۡتُوبًا عِندَهُمۡ فِى ٱلتَّوۡرَٮٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ يَأۡمُرُهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡہَٮٰهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنڪَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيۡہِمُ ٱلۡخَبَـٰٓٮِٕثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنۡہُمۡ إِصۡرَهُمۡ وَٱلۡأَغۡلَـٰلَ ٱلَّتِى كَانَتۡ عَلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۚ
“Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. He commands them to do what is right and forbids them from what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the foul things, and relieves them of their burdens and the shackles which were upon them.” (Al-Araf 7:157).

There are many verses in the Quran that promote the concept of ease and removal of hardship. Allah says:
يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ
“Allah wants things to be easy for you and does not want to impose hardship on you” (Al Baquara 2:185)

يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا
“Allah wants to lighten things for you, since man was created weak” (Al-Nisaa 4:28)

مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ حَرَجٍ وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
“Allah does not want to place any inconvenience on you, but He wants to purify you and complete his favor to you that you may be thankful” (Al-Maida 5:6).

However, removing of hardship does not mean removal of accountability. There will always be an element of effort and struggle.

The acceptance of the Shariah is a must for every Muslim as Allah says:
وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنٍ۬ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥۤ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡ‌ۗ
“It is not open for a believing man or a believing woman, once Allah and His messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice about their matter.” (Al-Ahzab 33:36).

فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا
“Yet by your Lord, they will never believe until they make you judge in the disputes between them and find within themselves no resistance to your decisions and submit wholeheartedly.” (Al-Nisa 4:65).

Because accepting the laws identified in the Shariah are essential element of Islamic Aqidah (belief in the Quran), the hadith plays three major roles regarding Shariah:
1. It illustrates the application of the rulings in the Qur’an.
2. It details some of the concepts, laws and practical matters which are briefly stated in the Qur’an (e.g., how to perform the five daily prayers).
3. It gives some rulings regarding matters not explicitly stated in the Qur’an (e.g., refraining from eating predators like lions or tigers).

Muslim scholars have divided Shariah to four categories.
1. Ibadah (العبادات) (rituals): It refers to the rules and procedures of performing the prescribed rituals.
2. Mu’amalat (لمعاملات) are laws and regulations related to buying, selling, renting, lending and borrowing, and other commercial and social interactions.
3. Munakahat are laws concerning marriage and divorce.
4. Jinayat, addresses the criminal code that concerns with court procedures and punishment of those who commit crimes.

Rulings of the Shariah
Scholars grouped the rulings of Shariah into five categories: prescribed, recommended, permissible, disliked, and unlawful. The distinction between these rulings is based on whether the performance (P) or non-performance (NP) is rewarded or punished.

Rulings of Sacred Law
- Prescribed: P: rewarded, NP: punished
- Recommended: P: rewarded, NP: not punished
- Permissible: P: not rewarded, NP: not punished
- Disliked: P: not punished, NP: rewarded
- Unlawful: P: punished, NP: rewarded

Understanding the Shariah
Shariah represents the divine guidance that is instituted to bring mercy, benefits, and facilitation to mankind.
Interpretation of Shariah to derive a legal ruling requires: 1) full knowledge of the Shariah (Quran and Sunnah) and its goals, 2) knowledge of the language of the Quran and Sunnah (Arabic), and 3) deep understanding of the conditions and the environment under which the ruling will be applied.

content:
Commitment to Knowledge

Our presence in the west imposes on us two major responsibilities:

1. Preservation of our Islamic identity for us and for the future generations.
2. Presenting the Islamic ideals to others not necessarily to convert them, though we hope so, but to share with our communities the great values of Islam.
3. Play a positive and engaging role in the society.

Fulfilling these two responsibilities require knowledge. Knowledge leads to wisdom and wisdom leads to actions. We should strive to demonstrate the moral values of Islam by our actions. Deeds speak louder than words.

Islam motivates its followers to seek knowledge. The first word that was revealed in the Quran was (اقْرَأْ) that means “Read” and “Study”. A whole chapter in the Quran (number 68) is entitled “The Pen” (الْقَلَمِ).

The Prophet (PBUH) taught us that: “Knowledge is the leader “Imam” of work and work is the follower of knowledge”. He also said: “One learned man is harder on Satan than a thousand ignorant worshippers.”

Therefore, it is important that Muslims strive to be renown in knowledge, Certainly, we should master the basic knowledge about the rules of Islam. This does not mean that you must become a jurist, but you should know the basics of Islam and be able to frame a question in a concise manner for a jurist.

Many Muslims act as if they have lost their ability to learn by themselves and thus, they put their full trust in others to guide them in all matters of religion. Those who blindly follow “scholars” without analyzing their opinions may be doing something that Allah has condemned. Allah says:

تَّخَذُوٓاْ أَحۡبَارَهُمۡ وَرُهۡبَـٰنَهُمۡ أَرۡبَابً۬ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ

“They take their Rabbis and their monks to be their lords besides Allah (by giving their Rabbis and monks the authority to declare things lawful or unlawful).” (Al-Tuba 9:31)

Muslims should never blindly follow anyone without clear understanding of and agreeing to the bases of the rulings. Imam Al-Shafie warned against the blind following of the opinion of scholars without understanding the basis of the rulings. He said: :

“مثل الذي يطلب العلم بلا حجة، كمثل حاطب ليل، يحمل حزمة حطب وفيه أفعى، تلدغه وهو لا يدري”.

“The example of the one who accepts knowledge without proof is just as one who gathers wood at night; he carries the bundle of wood while there is a snake in it and it will bite him without his knowledge.”

Imam Ibn Hazm considers blind imitation (التقليد) without understanding prohibited. He said:

(إن التقليد حرام، ولا يحل لأحد أن يأخذ قول أحد غير رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بلا برهان)

“It is prohibited follow the opinion of anyone without proof except the Prophet (PBUH)”

Allah gives glad tiding to those who listen to different opinions and follow the opinion that they consider the best. Allah said:

(فبشر عباد. الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب) (الزمر 39:17-18)

“Announce the Good News to My Servants who listen to a saying, and follow the best in it: those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the ones who have with understanding” (Al-Zumur 39:17-18)

You should never be afraid of making an honest mistake after you put the effort to seek the truth. Allah has already accepted our Dua in this matter:

ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ،

“Our Lord do not hold us accountable if we forget or make mistake. (Al-Baqara 2:286)

Also, the prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَضَعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي الْخَطَأَ وَالنِّسْيَانَ وَمَا اسْتُكْرِهُوا عَلَيْهِ (ابن ماجة)

“Allah has relieved my nation for things they commit by mistake or out of forgetfulness or being forced to do”. (ibn Majah)

There is nothing wrong with making mistakes. This is the way people grow and build confidence in their ability to study and think on your own. Allah does not mind us making mistakes as long we make our decisions based on sincere efforts to understand Allah’s instructions, and not based on malice in our hearts. Allah says:

وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم وكان الله غفورا رحيما) سورة الأحزاب(

“And there is no sin for you in the mistakes that you make unintentionally, but what your hearts deliberately intend. Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Ahzab 33:5)

Allah wants Muslims to be thinkers not a robot. The Prophet (PBUH) grew up in a very ignorant society where the majority didn’t know how to read or write. Yet, the Prophet (PBUH) empowered them and gave them the confidence to know the difference between right and wrong.

When the Prophet (PBUH) was asked by many of his companions about righteous and sinful deeds, he never responded by giving them a long list of what is Halal and what is Haram. He only said:

‏عن وابصة بن معبد صاحب النبي ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏قال ‏جئت إلى رسول الله ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏فقال جئت تسأل عن البر والإثم قلت نعم قال استفت قلبك البر ما اطمأنت إليه النفس واطمأن إليه القلب والإثم ما حاك في النفس وتردد في الصدر وإن أفتاك الناس وأفتوك. (رواه الإمام أحمد والدامي)

قال ‏ ‏زيد بن الحباب الأنصاري) مسند أحمد( ‏‏قال ‏ ‏النواس بن سمعان الأنصاري) صحيح مسلم(

‏قال أبي ثعلبة الخشني ‏ ‏قلت يا رسول الله أخبرني بما يحل لي ويحرم علي فقال النبي ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏البر ما سكنت إليه النفس واطمأن إليه القلب والإثم ما لم تسكن إليه النفس ولم يطمئن إليه القلب وإن أفتاك المفتون. (مسند أحمد)

“Righteous deeds are those that make your soul feels calm, and your heart feels comfortable, and sinful deeds are those that make your soul feels restless, and you feel hesitation in your chest, even if people give you multiple different opinions.”

Also, Allah emphasized that Muslims should be thinkers, He said:

وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلذِّڪۡرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيۡہِمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

“And We have also sent down unto you (O Muhammad SAW) the Dhikr (the Quran), that you may explain clearly to men what is sent down to them, and that they may think.” (Al-Nahl 16:44)

This verse states that the Prophet’s role is to convey the revelations, and our responsibility is to think. Allah did not say “that they may follow”, Allah said “that they may think”. Allah wants us to think, study and understand.

Allah’s words and the Prophet ‘s actions gave early Muslims the confidence to learn the principles of Islam and they became leaders of the world. After few hundred years, Muslims abandoned thinking and decided to blindly follow others and that was the beginning of the decline of Muslims as a civilization.

We need to understand the various opinions and the reasons for such differences. Muslims should not run away from making their own choices after they study the issues.

The right to choose is a divine given right, no one can take it from you. The Prophet (PBUH) commanded us to inform others even if it is only one verse. This is how early Muslims spread the message of Islam all over the world.

Some Muslims may get discouraged from making their own decisions because they get overwhelmed with the amount of information about Islam. They think that they must know everything about Islam before they can make any decision.

A Bedouin (لأعرابي) came to the Prophet (PBUH) and told him: “O Mohammad Advise me but be brief” (يا محمد عظني وأوجز)

The Prophet (PBUH) recited for him two verses:

فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ * وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرّاً يَرَهُ) سورة الزلزلة(

And whosoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it then, and whosoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it then. (Al-Zalzalah 99:7-8)

The Bedouin said: (كُفيت) “That is enough.”

The Prophet (PBUH) said: (فقُهَ الرجل) “The man has full understanding”.

One verse was sufficient for this Bedouin! How about us, would one verse be sufficient for us. Here are some short verses that should be enough for us:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ رَقِيبً۬ا )النساء(
“Surely, Allah is watchful over you.” (Al-Nisa 4:1)

مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَـٰلِحً۬ا مِّن ذَڪَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنٌ۬ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُ ۥ حَيَوٰةً۬ طَيِّبَةً۬‌ۖ (النحل)
“Whoever works righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We shall certainly give him a good life.” (Al-Nahl 16:97)

فَمَنْ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلا يَضِلُّ وَلا يَشْقَى) طه(
“Whoever follows My Guidance shall neither go astray, nor shall be distressed.” (Taha 20:123)

Information overload is dangerous because it can lead to focusing on secondary issues in Islam on the expense of the core principles of Islam. The core principles of Islam are common to all Muslims, and they are the foundation of our unity.

إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِۦۤ أُمَّتُكُمۡ أُمَّةً۬ وَٲحِدَةً۬ وَأَنَا۟ رَبُّڪُمۡ فَٱعۡبُدُونِ
“Surely, this community of yours is one and I am your Lord, so worship me. (Al-Anbiyaa 21: 92)

وإن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاتقون )المؤمنون(
“Surely, this community of yours is one and I am your Lord, so have Taqwa (Al-Mu’minun 23: 52)

Allah lays great emphasis on the importance of unity among us and clearly condemns divisions, as He said:

وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلا تَنَازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ )الأنفال(
“Obey Allah and His Messenger; and do not fall into disputes, lest you fail and lose your power; and be patient. Surely Allah is with those who are patient.” (Al-Anfal 8: 46)

وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا )آل عمران(
“And hold fast, all together, by the Rope which Allah and do not be divided.” (Al-Imran 3: 103).

وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا وَاخْتَلَفُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ وَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ )آل عمران(
“Be not like those who are divided amongst themselves and fall into disputations after receiving Clear Signs: For them is a dreadful penalty.” (Al-Imran 3: 105)

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (الأنعام)
“As for those who divide their religion and break up into sects, you have no part in them in the least: their affair is with Allah: He will in the end tell them the truth of all that they did. (Al-Ana’am 6:159)

Our diversity should never be a cause for barriers, divisions, and animosities, if we have pure hearts and we truly love for each other what we love for ourselves.

عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه ) رواه البخاري ومسلم
“‘None of you will believe until your love for your brother what you love for yourself.’”

Our community is diverse in nature, our members follow different schools of Fiqh and have different cultures and languages. If we allow this diversity to be a source of divisions, then we will be weak and ineffective.

In his book: “Going to extreme, how like mind unite and divide”, Harvard law professor Cass Sunstein writes: “It is well known that when like-minded people get together, they end up more extreme in their views than they were before they got together. This is because they only hear one side of the argument and they are not challenged by other views.”

Every Muslim knows that believing in Allah, doing good deeds, purity of the heart and the mercy of Allah are the keys for success in eternity. Why then do we find Muslims fighting over secondary issues and differences in interpretations?

Allah intentionally constructed the divine texts that allowed for broad interpretations, and this is a mercy for us. It allows us to apply the principles of Islam in different cultures and times.

When Khalifa Al-Mansour told Imam Malik that he plans to use his book Al-Muwata (“الموطأ”) as the base for the legal system of the Islamic State and to force everyone to follow it, Imam Malik strongly rejected this and told him: “Don’t do that, because the companions of the Prophet (PBUH) have spread all over the world and each one of them had some knowledge that others didn’t have, and people in each region followed what they received from the companions who lived among them.”

To secure proper information and avoid confusion, it is important to understand the definitions and roles of the key figures in our community:

The preacher (داعية) role is to promote general topics that address special needs and weaknesses in a Muslim community. The preacher is not a scholar and should never be asked to give Fatwa on complex issues.

وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلاً مِمَّنْ دَعَا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ [ سورة فصلت]
““Who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, “I am of those who have surrendered themselves to Him?” [Fussilat 41:33]

قُلْ هَذِهِ سَبِيلِي أَدْعُو إِلَى اللَّهِ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي] سورة يوسف الآية 108]
“Say: “This is my way: I invite to Allah with sure knowledge, I and those who follow me.” (Yousef 12:108)

The Dawah is the responsibility of every Muslim using only the revelations that is knows. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي وَلَوْ آيَةً (البخاري)
“Convey from me, even a single verse”. (Bukhari)

The Scholar (فقيه) is an intelligent person who studied all the rules of Fiqh and understand the opinions of the different schools of thought. A scholar can be asked about the rules of Islam and the different interpretations.

The Jurist (مفتى) is a very intelligent person who understands the opinions of past jurists and can select the proper opinion that fits the specific circumstances and needs of a community.

The problem that we face in the west is that most of those who can be classified as preachers (داعية) are acting as scholars and jurists. They give Fatwas on complex issues without having the proper knowledge and understanding.

Accepting different opinions on the same issue is not an act of being overly accommodative, as some might think. It is the core of Islamic scholarship.

All opinions are based on divine revelations.
Interpretation of a divine revelation is only a human’s best effort because no one knows the assured meaning of a word in a divine text except Allah.
If Allah wanted to ensure a single interpretation, He would have used words that do not allow for multiple meanings.

Let me highlight a reason for why scholars differed. When scholars look at a command, they differ in whether it is a general command or a specific command.

Allah says:
خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها
“Take Sadaqat (alms) from their wealth in order to purify them and sanctify them with it” (Al-Tuba 9:103)

While this command seems general in nature because it does not specify the type of wealth. But scholars differ in whether it applies to all types of wealth or only to specific types of wealth.

Another example is the command:
وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٲلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَـٰنًا‌ۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ۬ وَلَا تَنۡہَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلاً۬ كَرِيمًا
“Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. If any one of them or both of them reach old age, do not say to them: “uff” (a word of disrespect) nor shout at them but address them in terms of honor.” (Al-Isra 17:23)

Does this mean that you can say other bad words as long as you don’t say “uff”? Although this is a specific command, it is treated by all scholars to represent a general command of being kind and respectful to parents.

Let me give you an example from the Quran that states a command, but it is always treated to represent a permission:

وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ
Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appear to you distinct from its black thread (Al-Baqarah 2:187)

If you treat this verse as command, it will mean that you should continuously eat and drink from dawn until sunset. But all scholars agree that it is a permission to eat and drink during the night of Ramadan.

Let me give examples of commands from the Prophet (PBUH) whose applications are considered cultural:

روى أبو داود أيضا عن يعلى بن شداد بن أوس عن أبيه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
خالفوا اليهود فإنهم لا يصلون في نعالهم ولا خفافهم
“Be different from the Jews, who do not pray in their shoes or in their leather slippers.” (Abu Dawood)

The Prophet (PBUH) also said:
( إذا جاء أحدكم إلى المسجد فلينظر ، فإن رأى في نعليه قذراً أو أذى فليمسحه وليصل فيهما )
“When any one of you comes to the Masjid, let him look if he sees any dirt on his shoes, let him wipe it and then pray in them.”

Although the command of praying in shoes is general, its application was specific to Masjids similar to those in the time of the Prophet (PBUH) where the floor was made of sand or pebbles. In today’s Masjids where the floor is covered with carpets, praying in shoes would be a sign of disrespect and lack of cleanliness.

Another example of commands that are only applicable to certain cultures. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن ابن عباس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ” اكتحلوا بالإثمد فإنه يجلو البصر وينبت الشعر “ [رواه الترمذي وابن ماجة]
“Put eye liner (Kohl) on our eyes using antimony; it clarifies the sight and grows the eye lashes”.

عن عبدالله بن عمر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:” عليكم بالإثمد, فإنه يجلو البصر, وينبت الشعر”) ابن ماجة(
“Stick to applying the antimony, as it clarifies the sight and grows the eye lashes “. [Ibn Majah]

عن ابن عباس كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا اكتحل يكتحل في اليمنى ثلاثة يبتدئ بها ويختم بها وفي اليسرى ثنتين (ابن ماجة)
The Prophet (PBUH) used to apply kohl to his right eye three times and to his left eye twice.

What would you think when today you see a Muslim boy with eyeliner (kohl) on his eyes? In today’s culture, this would be seen as a sign of being feminine and not masculine. Yet, at the time of the Prophet (PBUH), it was a common practice for men and women.

Even the companions of the Prophet (PBUH) treated some of the Prophet’s commands as recommended or even as cultural practices.

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن اليهود والنصارى لا يصبغون فخالفوهم
“The Jews and Christians do not dye (their grey hair), so do the opposite of what they do.” (Bukhari)

Several companions such as Ali, Abi Kaab, Salamah ibn Al-Aqwa, Anas and others (علي وأبي بن كعب وسلمة بن الأكوع وأنس وغيرهم) did not dye their grey hair. They treated the command as a recommendation and not as an obligation.

الدليل اذا تطرق اليه الاحتمال سقط به الاستدلال
“If the evidence is subject to probability, its inference becomes invalid.”

Many of the hadith in which the Prophet (PBUH) commanded Muslims to differentiate themselves from the Jews and Christians were specific to the circumstances of that time where there was a need to build a distinct Islamic identity.

Therefore, we must be careful and should never insist that one’s opinion or one’s way of practicing Islam is the only correct way.

The religion that Allah blessed us with and that he Prophet (PBUH) demonstrated was made easy and clear.

يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ
“Allah wants things to be easy for you and does not want to impose hardship on you” (Al Baqarah 2:185)

Prohibitions should be limited to the divine limits and should not be transgressed beyond them whether by adding more prohibitions or by making the application of the existing rules very rigid.

(تلك حدود الله فلا تعتدوها) [سورة البقرة:229].
“These are the limits imposed by Allah, do not transgress them.” (Al-Baqarah 2:229)

“Cutting Pretext” (سد الذرائع) should not be uses as an excuse to add prohibitions that Allah did not intend.

It is unfortunate that some people create conflicts by insisting that everyone should follow their specific interpretations of Islam. This is against the spirit of Islam and it only leads to divisions and weakness.

وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ هَذَا حَالَالٌ وَهَذَا حَرَامٌ لِتَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ (النحل)
“And do not let your tongues utter lies by saying: “This is lawful (Halal) and this is forbidden (Haram)” in order to invent lies about Allah. Surely those who invent lies about Allah will not succeed.” (Al-Nahl 16:116)

The next talks on the same subject will, inshallah, address the key terms in Islam such as Aqidah (creed), Shari`ah (sacred law) and its goals and Fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and its rules.
