content:
The Only True Role Model

Yesterday Muslims remembered the birthday of the Prophet (PBUH). On this occasion, I want to reflect on our relationship with the Prophet (PBUH). This relationship is important because I believe that the dire position of Muslims is not due to lack of knowledge about Islam but rather due to our improper relationship with the Prophet (PBUH). The only proper relationship with the prophet (PBUH) is based on us taking him as a role model.

Why Studying the Memoirs of the Prophet (PBUH)

Allah says:
لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِمَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا (الأحزاب)

You have indeed in the Messenger of Allah a good role model for anyone who has hope is in Allah and the Last Day, and who remembers Allah frequently. (Al-Ahzab 33: 21)

Allah also says:
قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (آل عمران)

Say: “If you really love Allah, follow me: Allah will love you and forgive you your sins; for Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al- Imran 3:31)

The Prophet’s Mission is Mercy

Following the Prophet (PBUH) means making his primary mission our mission, and Allah identified his mission by saying:
” وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلا رَحْمَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ” (الأنبياء 107)

We have not sent you but as mercy for all creatures. (Al-Anbi’a 21:107)

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the importance of mercy by saying:
الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمْ الرَّحْمَنُ ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on the earth and the One in the heaven will have mercy upon you”. (Al-Tirmidhī)

The Prophet (PBUH) was always concerned about the weak of the society and wanted to ensure that they are treatment honorably and fairly. Abu Dhar reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
فعن المعرور بن سويد قال: لقيت أبا ذر بِالرَّبَذَةِ وعليه حلة وعلى غلامه حلة، فسألته عن ذلك فقال: قال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن إخوانكم خولكم جعلهم الله تحت أيديكم، فمن كان أخوه تحت يده فليطعمه مما يأكل، وليلبسه مما يلبس، ولا تكلفوهم ما يغلبهم، فإن كلفتموهم فأعينوهم.

“Your slaves/servants are your brethren upon whom Allah has given you authority. So, if one has brothers under his control, he should feed them with the like of what he eats and clothe them with the like of what he wears. You should not overburden them with what they cannot bear, and if there is a difficult task he should help them (in their hard job).”

It is narrated by Umm Salamah (RA) and Anas Ibn Malik (RA) that the last advice the Prophet (PBUH) offered to his followers while he was on the death bed was:
أخر وصاياه وهو على فراش الموت: الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم، الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم، فجعل يرددها حتى ما يفيض بها لسانه. رواه أحمد والنسائي وابن ماجه وابن حبان عن أنس

“Guard your prayers and watch over whom you have control (your servants and others whom you have authority over them).” He continued to repeat these words until he was unable to talk.” (Ibn Maajah).

The Perfect Character

Also, taking the Prophet (PBUH) as a role model means striving to possess the key attribute that Allah identified him with by saying:
” وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ” (القلم 4)

And you have an exalted standard of character (Al-Qalam 68:4)

The Prophet (PBUH) summarized the purpose of his teaching by saying:
“إنّما بُعثت لأُتمم مكارم الأخلاق”.

“I haven’t been sent except to perfect the good manners.”

The Prophet (PBUH) is saying that his mission is not promote a good character but rather to perfect the good character. To delineate elements of the Prophet’s character to ensure that we emulate it, we need to study what his companions said about him. Abdullah ibn Amr described the character of the Prophet (PBUH) by saying:
عن عبد الله ابن عمرو قال: لم يكن فاحشا ولا متفحشا وقال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من أخيركم أحسنكم خلقا (البخاري)

The Prophet never said anything that is obscene or even joked by saying anything that is obscene” and said that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: “The best of you is the best in character”. (Bukhari)

Ibn Mas’ud reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:
لَيْسَ الْمُؤْمِنُ بِالطَّعَّانِ وَلَا اللَّعَّانِ وَلَا الْفَاحِشِ وَلَا الْبَذِيءِ
The believer does not insult others, does not curse others, he is not vulgar, and he is not shameless. (Al-Tirmidhī)

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the importance of good character in many of his saying. As examples:

Aisha (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), said:
إِنَّ مِنْ أَكْمَلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِيمَانًا أَحْسَنُهُمْ خُلُقًا وَأَلْطَفُهُمْ بِأَهْلِهِ
“Verily, the most complete of believers in faith are those with the best character and who are most kind to their families”. (Al-Tirmidhī)

Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
(أكمل المؤمنين أحسنهم خُلُقاً) [أبو داود وأحمد عن أبي هريرة]
“The best believer is the one who has good manners”. (Ahmad and Abu Dawud)

Ibn Omar (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), said:
(إن خياركم أحاسنكم أخلاقاً) [البخاري ومسلم عن ابن عمر]
“The best of you is the best in character”. (Bukhari and Muslim)

Ibn Omar (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), said:
(أفضل المؤمنين أحسنهم خُلُقاً) [الحاكم عن ابن عمر]
“The best among the believers is the best in manners,” (Al-Hakim)

(أحب عباد الله إلى الله أحسنهم خلُقاً) [الطبراني]
“The most beloved servant to Allah is the one who has the best manners”. (Al-Tabarani)

Aisha (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), said:
(إن الرجل ليُدرك بحسن خُلُقه درجات قائم الليل صائم النهار) [أبو داود والحاكم عن عائشة]
“A man reaches with his good manner the degree of the one who perform prayers all night and fasts all day”. (Abu Dawud and Al-Hakim)

Jaber (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), said:
(إن من أحبِّكم وأقربكم منّي مجلساً يوم القيامة: أحاسنكم أخلاقاً). [الترمذي عن جابر]
“The most beloved to me and nearest to me on the Day of Judgment is the one who has the best manners”. (Al-Tirmidhī)

Osama ibn Shareek (RA) said that while we are sitting with the messenger of Allah (PBUH) some people came as asked: Who are the most beloved people to Allah? The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن أسامة بن شريك رضي الله عنه قال: كنا جلوسًا عند النَّبيِّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ إذ جاءه أناسٌ فقالوا: من أحبُّ عبادِ اللهِ إلى اللهِ تعالى؟ قال: «أحسنُهم خُلُقًا». (أخرجه ابن ماجه، وأحمد)
“Those who have the best manners” (Ahmad and Ibn Majah)

Islam and Muslims in One word

The whole mission of the prophet (PBUH) was to perfect the character of people and this perfect character is founded on mercy. So, if you want to define Islam in one word it will be mercy. And if you want to identify a Muslims in one word, it will be perfect character. If you keep these two words, mercy and perfect character, in your mind all the time, you don’t need to ask anyone about what is Halal and what is Haram. You will know them on your own.

Now let us look at examples of the perfect character of the Prophet (PBUH) that we need emulate.

Tolerance, forbearance, clemency of the Prophet (PBUH)

While the Prophet (PBUH) was sitting with his companions, the Rabbi, Zayd bin Sa’nah (زيد بن سعنه) grabbed the Prophet (PBUH) aggressively and said: “Mohammad, return your debt that you ow me; indeed, you people of Bani Hashim are procrastinators (إنكم بني هاشم قوم تماطلون) (in repaying debts).”

The Prophet’s companion Omar Ibn Al-Khataab pulled his sword and said: O messenger pf Allah give me permission to cut his head. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
“O ‘Omar! (مره بحسن الطلب ومرني بحسن الأداء ) you should have told him to make his request in an appropriate manner and you should have told me to repay him on time and”. Yet there are still three days left before his debt is due.”

On hearing this the Rabbi said:
فقال اليهودي : والذي بعثك بالحق يا محمد ما جئت لأطلب منك دينا إنما جئت لأختبر أخلاقك ..فأنا أعلم أن موعد الدين لم يحن بعد ولكني قرأت جميع أوصافك في التوراة فرأيتها كلها متحققة فيك إلا صفة واحدة لم أجربها معك ..وهي أنك حليم عند الغضب .. وأن شدة الجهالة لا تزيدك إلا حلما .. ولقد رأيتها اليوم فيك ..أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله .. وأنك محمد رسول الله أما الدين الذي عندك فقد جعلته صدقة على فقراء المسلمين.

“By the One who sent you with the truth, I did not come to ask you for the debt because I know that it is not yet due, but I came to check your manners. I read all your signs in the Torah, and I confirmed that all of them in you except two signs left for me to confirm that you are indeed the awaited Prophet: these are that you react forbearing when you are transgressed against, and when someone increases his aggression against you, you increase in forbearance. And I have seen them in you, and I testify that there is no God, but Allah and you are Mohammad, His Messenger. As far as the debt, I offer it as charity for the poor among the Muslins” (Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim and others)

The Forgiveness of The Prophet (PBUH):

Forgiveness is when someone refrains from retaliating, although he can do so. This is a quality that reflects the nobility of character. Aisha (RA) Said:
عن عائشة قالت ما لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مسلما من لعنة تذكر ولا انتقم لنفسه شيئا يؤتى إليه قط إلا أن تنتهك حرمات الله عز وجل ولا ضرب بيده شيئا قط إلا أن يضرب بها في سبيل الله ولا سئل شيئا قط فمنعه إلا أن يسأل مأثما فإنه كان أبعد الناس منه ولا خير بين أمرين قط إلا اختار أيسرهما (مسند أحمد)

The messenger of Allah (PBUH) never cursed and never took revenge for himself and never hit anyone with his hand except in a battle for the sake of Allah and he has never been asked for something and held it except if it is a sin and he has never been given options between two matters but selected the easiest of them. (Ahmad)

Jabir narrated:
عن جابر أنه غزا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غزوة ناحية بلاد «نجد» من أرض الحجاز، وفى طريق عودته مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وقت الظهيرة، فأمر بالتوقف في هذا المكان لينالوا قسطاً من الراحة، فنام الجيش، ونام صلى الله عليه وسلم تحت ظل شجرة كثيرة الأوراق وقد علق بها سيفه، وبعد فترة نادى على المسلمين فتجمعوا حوله، فإذا بأعرابي يجلس أمامه، فقال رسول الله: «إن هذا الرجل أخذ سيفي وأنا نائم، فاستيقظت وسيفي في يده، فقال لي: من يمنعك مني؟، «أي من يمنعني من قتلك الآن»، فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في ثبات وثقة وإيمان: «الله»، فارتعد الأعرابي بشدة، ووقع السيف من يده، فأخذه رسول الله وقال له: من يمنعك مني؟، فقال الرجل لا أحد، ولم يقابل النبي الكريم إساءة الأعرابي له بمثلها، بل عفا عنه.

“We accompanied the Messenger of Allah in the campaign near Najd and in our return near the mid-day, the Prophet ordered us to stop and take rest. The Prophet (PBUH) took cover under a shade tree and hanged his sword. One of the polytheists came quietly and drew the sword of the Messenger of Allah and said standing over the Messenger “Who will protect you from me?” The Messenger of Allah replied: “Allah.” As soon as he said this, the sword fell from the polytheist’s hand and the Messenger of Allah, catching the sword, asked the man: “Now, who will protect you from me?” The polytheist said: “No one.” The Messenger of Allah said: “I’ll forgive you on the condition that you promise that you shall not fight against me, nor shall you fight with those who fight me.” The man agreed and the Prophet let him go. The man then went back to his associates and said: “I have come to you from one of the best of humanity”

Humility of the Prophet (PBUH)

There are many examples demonstrating the degree of humility for the Prophet (PBUH) and that in spite of his position, he never sought any preference and wanted any special treatments,

During one of the outings, the Prophet (PBUH) and a group of his companions wanted to slaughter a sheep (شاة). One of the companions said (علي ذبحها ) my responsibility is to slaughter it, the second said: (علي سلخها) my responsibility is to skin it, and the third said: (وعلي طبخها) and my responsibility to cook it. The Prophet (PBUH) said (وعلي جمع الحطب) and my responsibility is to collect the wood. The companions said: (نكفيك يا رسول الله) No, we suffice you and take care of this, Messenger of Allah. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
أعرف أنكم تكفونني ، ولكن الله يكره أن يرى عبده متميزاً على أقرانه .

“I know that you can do it instead of me but Allah hates to see one of his servants is given preference over his companions”.

Going to the battle of Badr to meet the army of Quraysh, Muslims did not have enough camels to carry everyone. The Prophet (PBUH) who is the leader of the army did not grant himself any preference. He (PBUH) shared a camel with two companions: Ali and Abu Lubabah (أبو لبابه). The Prophet (PBUH) rode for a while and when it was his time to walk, his companions begged him to keep riding and they walk instead of him. But the Prophet (PBUH) refused and said:
ما أنتما بأقوى مني على السير ، ولا أنا بأغنى منكما عن الأجر
“You are not stronger than me to walk and I am not richer than you for the rewards of Allah”.

The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) stopped people from standing up when he entered a place and did not seek to sit in a special place. He did not wear special cloths. He just looked like anyone of them at the extent that a Bedouin who never met him before entered the Masjid and asked who among you is Mohammed (أيكم محمد ؟)

The Prophet (PBUH) said in the Hadeath that was narrated by Omar
لا تُطْرُونِي كَمَا أَطْرَتِ النَّصَارَى عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ , فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ ) رواه البخاري
“Do not praise me as the Christians praised Jesus the son of Mary. I am only Allah’s slave and messenger.” (Bukhari)

When we read about Khalifa Omar and admire his humility even though he was the ruler over almost all the civilized world at that time; we should not be surprised because he had a great teacher. But when we compare the teaching of the Prophet (PBUH) and the practices of his companions with the practices of any leader of today’s Muslim world we see great contradictions.

The Prophet’s Teaching Approach

One important thing that we need to learn from the Prophet (PBUH) is that he did not focus on giving the companions lists of Halal (lawful) and Haram (prohibited). Rather he focused on teaching them wisdom to be able to identify the Halal and Haram on their own. On many occasions, the companions asked him about the righteous deeds and the sinful deeds. Rather than reciting for them a list, he taught them the way to derive the list on their own. The following are some examples. The Prophet (PBUH) was asked about righteous and sinful deeds and He said:

عن وابصة بن معبد صاحب النبي ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏قال ‏جئت إلى رسول الله ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏أسأله عن البر والإثم فقال جئت تسأل عن البر والإثم فقلت والذي بعثك بالحق ما جئت أسألك عن غيره فقال البر ما انشرح له صدرك والإثم ما حاك في صدرك وإن أفتاك عنه الناس) مسند أحمد

قال ‏ ‏زيد بن الحباب الأنصاري سألت النبي ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏عن البر والإثم فقال البر حسن الخلق والإثم ما حاك في صدرك وكرهت أن يطلع الناس عليه ) مسند أحمد

قال ‏ ‏النواس بن سمعان الأنصاري ‏ ‏ سألت رسول الله ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏عن البر والإثم فقال البر حسن الخلق والإثم ما حاك في صدرك وكرهت أن يطلع عليه الناس ) صحيح مسلم

قال أبي ثعلبة الخشني ‏ ‏قلت يا رسول الله أخبرني بما يحل لي ويحرم علي قال فصعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في النظر فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم البر ما سكنت إليه النفس واطمأن إليه القلب والإثم ما لم تسكن إليه النفس ولم يطمئن إليه القلب وإن أفتاك المفتون ) مسند أحمد

“Righteous deeds are those that make your soul feels calm, and your heart feels comfortable, and sinful deeds are the ones that make your soul feels hesitant and your heart feels agitated, and you will feel embarrassed if people know about them. This is how you know no matter what opinion you get on the matter.

Allah has given us the ability to differentiate between the right from wrong, Allah said:
(وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ دَسَّاهَا) الشمس 91:7-10

“By the Soul, and the proportion and order given to it; and its enlightenment as to its wrong and its right; truly he succeeds who purifies it, and he fails who corrupts it!” (Al-Shams 91:7-10)

The corruption we see in today’s world is instigated by people whose souls are corrupted. The only way to rid of corruption and bring justice and peace is to purify the souls of the people. This can be done by following the strategy of the Prophet (PBUH). The Prophet (PBUH) was able within 23 years to transform the most backward and corrupt tribes of Arabia to be the world leaders in knowledge, morality, spirituality, human brotherhood, freedom, and equality.

When Muslims do wrong, it is not because they don’t know what Halal and Haram. The way to avoid the haram is to purify one’s soul to know what is Halal is and what is Haram on its own? Let us look to example of the approach that the Prophet (PBUH) took to achieve that

حدثنا سليم بن عامر عن أبي أمامة قال إن فتى شابا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله ائذن لي بالزنا فأقبل القوم عليه فزجروه قالوا مه مه فقال ادنه فدنا منه قريبا قال فجلس قال أتحبه لأمك قال لا والله جعلني الله فداءك قال ولا الناس يحبونه لأمهاتهم قال أفتحبه لابنتك قال لا والله يا رسول الله جعلني الله فداءك قال ولا الناس يحبونه لبناتهم قال أفتحبه لأختك قال لا والله جعلني الله فداءك قال ولا الناس يحبونه لأخواتهم قال أفتحبه لعمتك قال لا والله جعلني الله فداءك قال ولا الناس يحبونه لعماتهم قال أفتحبه لخالتك قال لا والله جعلني الله فداءك قال ولا الناس يحبونه لخالاتهم قال فوضع يده عليه وقال اللهم اغفر ذنبه وطهر قلبه وحصن فرجه فلم يكن بعد ذلك الفتى يلتفت إلى شيء)) مسند أحمد

A youth came to the Prophet (PBUH) and asked for permission to commit fornication (zina). The companions who were setting with the Prophet (PBUH) got very angry of the youth and how he dares to ask for something like this. But the Prophet (PBUH) ordered them to stop and asked the youth to come and sit close to him. Them the asked him in a very soft and kind voice: would you accept this for your mother? The youth said: May Allah make me a sacrifice for you, no. The Prophet (PBUH) said: and so people don’t want this for their mothers.

Then he asked: would you accept this for your sister? The youth said: No, may Allah make me a sacrifice for you. The Prophet (PBUH) said: and so, people don’t like this for their sisters.

Then the Prophet (PBUH) asked: would you accept this for your aunt? The youth said: No, may Allah make me a sacrifice for you and the Prophet (PBUH) said: and so, people don’t like this for their aunts.

Then the Prophet put his hand with kindness on the youth and said: O’ Allah forgive his sins, purify his heart and preserve his chastity.

The youth was moved by what the Prophet did and said: The thought of fornication will never come to my mind again.

This is an example on how to teach others. No anger, no threats, but we should teach by moving the soul to its pure state, and making the mind differentiate between good and evil on its own. This training should lead the heart to feel disturbed by what is sinful and feel comfortable by what is good.

We are so fortunate that the Prophet (PBUH) has faced all these situations and his actions are well documented for us to learn and follow.

title: Greeting – Even a Marking (Tashkeel) Makes a Difference
excerpt:
Allah established for us a protocol for greeting by saying:

وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ۬ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحۡسَنَ مِنۡہَآ أَوۡ رُدُّوهَآ‌ۗٓ

“When you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return…
content:
Allah established for us a protocol for greeting by saying:

وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ۬ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحۡسَنَ مِنۡہَآ أَوۡ رُدُّوهَآ‌ۗٓ

“When you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or return the same.” (Al-Nisa 4:86)

In verse 25 in Surat Al-Dhariat, Allah relates to us a visit by some angels to prophet Ibrahim to give him the good news that he will have a son Isaac and that Isaac will have a son whose name will be Jacob. They will also inform him of their mission to destroy the people of Prophet Lot.

The verse we are discussing presents the scene of the first meeting between the angels and Prophet Ibrahim and the exchange of greetings:

إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلَـٰمً۬ا‌ۖ قَالَ سَلَـٰمٌ۬ قَوۡمٌ۬ مُّنكَرُونَ (الذّاریَات )

“When they (the angels) entered unto him and they said: Peace! he answered, Peace! (He said to himself): They are unknown people.” (Al-Dhariat 51:25)

The English translation of the verse suggest that both the angels and Prophet Ibrahim exchanged the same greeting. The angels greeted Prophet Ibrahim by saying Salaam” Peace” and he replied to them by saying Salaam “Peace”.

Allah commands that we should respond to a greeting with a better than it or the same, so the question is: Did Prophet Ibrahim responded with better greeting or with an equal one? Based on the English translation, he responded with equal greeting.

However, a closer look at the Arabic version reveals a difference between the greeting of the angels and the greeting of Prophet Ibrahim and the difference is in the Tashkeel (i.e., marking) of the that last letter (م) “meem” in Salaam.

1. The ending of the angels’ greeting has a “Fatha with tanween” that sounds as “Salam’an”
2. The ending of prophet Ibrahim’s greeting has “Dhamma with tanween” that sounds as “Salam’on”

In the Arabic language there are two types of sentences:

1. The verb-type sentence (verb, subject, and object) is associated with time: past, present, and future and thus temporary.
2. The noun-type sentence [noun (مبتدأ) and adjective (خبر)] has no time restriction and thus perpetual.

The difference between the two Tashkeels signified the two types of sentence structures:

1. The greeting by the angels is in the form of verb-type sentence in the form: “We greet you with peace”. (نسلم سلاماً)
2. The greeting by prophet Ibrahim is in the form of noun-type sentence in the form: ‘Peace on you” (سلامٌ عليكم).

The verb-type sentence is associated with time: past, present, and future and thus temporary. While the noun-type sentence has no time restriction and thus perpetual.

This means that the angels offered prophet Ibrahim a peace for the present time. But prophet Ibrahim greeted them with continuous peace, for all the time, now and forever. This means that Prophet Ibrahim responded to the angels’ greeting with a better greeting in fulfillment of Allah’s command.

Now, you may ask why the angels did not use a noun-type sentence in their greeting? Perhaps because the angels are like soldiers. They only follow strict commands. The command they received from Allah was to go to Ibrahim for a specific mission and give him a greeting of peace. Therefore, they could not offer him a perpetual greeting of Peace that involves the future.

Angels could not speculate regarding what future commands regarding Ibrahim. But Prophet Ibrahim had the choice to either respond to them with a temporary greeting of peace or with a perpetual greeting peace. He chose the latter because he has free will to make his own decisions and he wanted to follow Allah’s command to greet them with better greeting.

title: 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics and Prophet Solomon (Surah Al-Naml)
excerpt: Recently, the Noble prize committee announced the 2022 winners of the noble prize in Physics.   The winners were John Clauser (American), Alain Aspect (French) and Anton Zellinger (Austrian). They…
content:
Recently, the Noble prize committee announced the 2022 winners of the noble prize in Physics.   The winners were John Clauser (American), Alain Aspect (French) and Anton Zellinger (Austrian). They won the prize for their experimental work on Quantum Entanglement. Their experiments showed that two particles behave like a single unit even when they are separated. Their results have cleared the way for new quantum information science that is creating a large field of research that includes quantum computers, quantum Internet and quantum encrypted technology.

(Definition: A quantum (plural: quanta is the smallest discrete unit of a phenomenon. For example, a quantum of light is a photon, and a quantum of electricity is an electron,

Quantum entanglement is when two particles link together in a certain way no matter how far apart, they are in space.)

The importance of quantum entanglement science is that it showed that there are speeds far higher than the speed of light. At this very high speed, information transfers between distant locations instantaneously at zero time. This is called Quantum teleportation. This new knowledge may offer some explanation regarding the perplexing issue of how Archangel Jibril communicated with the Prophet (PBUH) during the revelation of the Quran. Let me explain.

We now know that the radius of the observable universe is 13.8 billion light years. Since Jibril is made of light, it would take him 13.8 billion years to go from delivering the revelation to the prophet (PBUH) to merely the edge of our universe, providing his travel according to laws of physics without special divine intervention. Of course, if he goes beyond that to the 7th heaven, it will take exceedingly far longer. This may allow us to speculate on how Jibril was communicating with the Prophet (PBUH). However, I’ll leave this speculation to you after you read more about quantum entanglement.

On today’s talk, I will, inshallah, discuss the theme of Surat Al-Naml because it is relevant to the introduction I just made. The theme of Surat An-Naml is emphasizing the importance of technological advances in supporting the propagation of Allah’s message. The propagation of Allah’s message to others is only possible if Muslims are leaders in science and technology. Nations that are leaders in science and technology will also have financial and military supremacy that provide them with the capacity to influence the cultures of other nations including their morals and belief. The example of civilization excellence and technological advancement in Surat Al-Naml is Prophet Sulieman (Solomon) and his kingdom.

The Surat highlights that Allah favored Prophet Dawud and Sulieman with knowledge. It is knowledge that was the key to their preference over others. Allah says:

وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ عِلْمًا ۖ وَقَالَا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّنْ عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (15)

And indeed, We gave knowledge to Dawud (David) and Suleiman (Solomon), and they both said: “All the praises and thanks are to Allah, Who has favored us over many of His believing slaves!” (Al-Naml 27:15)

The Surat implies the importance of learning different languages because mastering foreign languages is key in advancing knowledge and facilitating interaction with other civilizations. Allah says:

وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُودَ ۖ وَقَالَ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ الطَّيْرِ وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْمُبِينُ (16)

And Suleiman (Solomon) inherited (the knowledge of) Dawud (David). He said: “O mankind! We have been taught the language of birds, and we have been of all things. This, verily, is an evident grace (from Allah).” (Al-Naml 27:16)

The value of knowing the different languages is to ensure the unintended harm to others. An example is in this account:

وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمَانَ جُنُودُهُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنسِ وَالطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ (17) حَتَّىٰ إِذَا أَتَوْا عَلَىٰ وَادِ النَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (18) فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًا مِّن قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ (19)

And mustered for Suleiman (Solomon) his forces among the jinn, the men, and the birds. All of them are kept under (his) control (17) When they came to the valley of the ants, one of the ants said: “O ants! enter your dwellings, lest Suleiman and his army crush you unknowingly.” (18) So, he (Solomon) smiled, amused at her speech, and said: “My Lord! Enable me to be grateful for Your favors that You have bestowed on me and on my parents, and that I do righteous good deeds that will please You, and admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous slaves.” (Al-Naml 27:18-19)

These verses illustrate the importance of the technologies of communications and sound transmission. In the past we discussed this issue when trying to address the question how Allah translated to Arabic the speeches of many creations who do not speak Arabic, including in this case the ants. You can review the presentation entitled: “The Straight Path to Richness – The Quran’s Multi-Billion Dollar Ideas”, Both the text and the YouTube presentation can be found at: https://successineternity.com/ .

The Surat also addresses an episode between Prophet Suleiman and the Hoopoe. This episode implies several scientific knowledge about the Hoopoe that are still undiscovered. We note that immediately after Prophet Suleiman heard the warning of the ant, he asked about the Hoopoe. When he discovered its absence, he made a serious threat against it.

وَتَفَقَّدَ الطَّيْرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِيَ لَا أَرَى الْهُدْهُدَ أَمْ كَانَ مِنَ الْغَائِبِينَ (20) لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا أَوْ لَأَذْبَحَنَّهُ أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّي بِسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ (21)

And he checked the birds, and said: “What is the matter that I do not see the hoopoe? Or has he disappeared. (20) “I will surely punish him with a severe torment, or slaughter him, unless he brings to me a plain excuse.” (Al-Naml 27:20-21)

This raises a question regarding the role of the Hoopoe and whether his absence has relevance to the warning of the ant that made prophet Sulieman punishing it with death. This requires a study on the characteristics of the Hoopoe. One could speculate that the Hoopoe’s role is reconnaissance to provide advanced warnings on the presence of any colony of ants and other creations that the army should avoid destroying them. Therefore, as soon as prophet Sulieman heard the warning of the ants and did not hear the early warning from the Hoopoe, he realized his absence. Although the hoopoe is a tiny soldier; this account shows that everyone in the army is important.

The Surat continues to give us a demonstration that everything in the universe is conscious of Allah and worships Him. In this account, we realize that even this tiny bird is committed to the mission of Prophet Sulieman. This mission was to search for those whom Allah’s message has not yet reached to deliver it to them. The Hoopoe went from Palestine to Yemen to check on the people there. It appears that the Hoopoe made this trip on his own and was planning to join the army when he returns. But it seems that he was delayed a little and thus his return was not long from the time his absence was noted. As soon as the Hoopoe returned after travelling the long-distance from Palestine to Yemen and back, he went to Prophet Suleiman and addressed him in what appears a bold tone saying:

فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ (22)

But the hoopoe did not take long, he said (to Sulieman): “I have discovered what you did not know, and I have come to you from Saba’ (Sheba) with sure information. (22)

The Hoopoe appears to have resilience and high level of observation and intelligence that he travelled this long distance and studied the situation very well and brought accurate information on that nation’s belief and economic power. He also showed his belief by being upset about their disbelief. He said:

إِنِّي وَجَدتُّ امْرَأَةً تَمْلِكُهُمْ وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ عَظِيمٌ (23) وَجَدتُّهَا وَقَوْمَهَا يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ (24) أَلَّا يَسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي يُخْرِجُ الْخَبْءَ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُخْفُونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ (25) اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ ۩ (26)

“I found a woman ruling over them”, all sorts of things are given to her, and she has a great throne. (23) “I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has beautified their deeds to them, and has prevented them from (Allah’s) Way, so they have no guidance,” (24) How can they not prostrate to Allah, Who brings to light what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal and what you reveal. (25) Allah, there is no God but He, the Lord of the Supreme Throne! (Al-Naml 27:22-26)

The Surat continues with communications between Prophet Suleiman and the Queen of Sheba and then highlights the importance of technology. This technology has been demonstrated by the transfer of the Queen’s throne form Yemen to Palestine in a blink of an eye. The importance of knowledge is highlighted by this exchange in Prophet Sulieman’s court:

قَالَ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِي بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ (38) قَالَ عِفْرِيتٌ مِّنَ الْجِنِّ أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ ۖ وَإِنِّي عَلَيْهِ لَقَوِيٌّ أَمِينٌ (39) قَالَ الَّذِي عِندَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِندَهُ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّي (40)

He (Suleiman) said: “O chiefs! Which one of you can bring me her throne before they come to me submissively?” (38) A strong one from the jinn said: “I will bring it to you before you rise up from your place; and I am indeed powerful, and reliable.” (39) The one who has the knowledge of the Book said: “I will bring it to you before your glance return to you.” Then when he (Solomon) saw it (the throne) well placed before him, he said: “This is by the grace of my Lord.” (Al-Naml 27:38-40)

These verses clearly show the benefits of technology, and this technology is possessed by a man and not by the strongest of the Jinn. The verses also show that teleportation is feasible and the research on quantum entanglement suggests that it is possible. Though the technology of teleportation is still to be developed, Muslim researchers should seek to develop it because they should be confident that it is feasible.

The Surat presented another important technology that Prophet Suleiman demonstrated to the Queen that made her believe in Allah. The verses of this scene are as follows:

فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْ قِيلَ أَهَٰكَذَا عَرْشُكِ ۖ قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ ۚ وَأُوتِينَا الْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ (42) وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ (43) قِيلَ لَهَا ادْخُلِي الصَّرْحَ ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُ صَرْحٌ مُّمَرَّدٌ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ ۚ قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (44)

So, when she came, it was said (to her): “Is your throne like this?” She said: “It seems to be the same as it.” And (Suleiman) said: “We have been given Knowledge before her and we were Muslims.” (42) And was prevented (from submitting to Allah) by that which she used to worship instead of Allah. Indeed, she was of a disbelieving people. (43) It was said to her: “Enter the “Sarh” (palace, hall) but when she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her legs. He (Suleiman) said: “it is a “Sarah” (palace, hall) made of glass placed over glasses.” She said: “My Lord! I had surely wronged myself, and I submit with Suleiman (Solomon), to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.” (Al-Naml 27:40-44)

In these verses, most interpreters suggested that the queen was amazed by the use of transparent glass in the construction of the hall in which the throne was placed, and this made her embrace Islam. This interpretation seems unconvincing for two reasons:
1. Even after she saw her thrown, the verse states that what she used to worship prevented her from the worship of Allah (وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ)
2. Just be being impressed by a construction of a building would not make people change their religion, let alone a powerful Queen.

Perhaps, the key to her conversion is related to entering the “Sarh” whose definition is not clear from these verses. We need to examine the use of the term in other verses. The term “Sarh” came in reference to Pharaoh in both Surat Al-Qasas (28:38) and Surat Ghafer (40:36).

وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِي فَأَوْقِدْ لِي يَا هَامَانُ عَلَى الطِّينِ فَاجْعَل لِّي صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّي أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ (38)

The Pharaoh said: “O Chiefs! I do not know any god for you other than myself. O’ Haman! Fire on the clay and build for me a “Sarh” (tower) so that I may look on to the God of Musa (Moses). Though I think that he is among the liars.” (Al-Qasas 28:38)

وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَا هَامَانُ ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ الْأَسْبَابَ (36) أَسْبَابَ السَّمَاوَاتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ كَاذِبًا ۚ (37)

And Pharaoh said: O Haman! Build a “Sarh” (tower) for me, perhaps I could reach the ways. (36) The ways to the heavens, and may look upon the God of Moses, though I think that he is a liar. (Ghafer 40:36-37)

In these two verses the term “Sarh” was translated as tower because the goal of Pharaoh is to see the God of Moses in heaven. But would building a tower really allow Pharaoh to penetrate the sky to see the God of Moses. And why he needs a tower, he could have gone on the top of the great Pyramid which is 480 ft.

(Note: The Great Pyramid of Khufu began construction was completed around 2560 BC. Prophet Yaqoub (Jacob) was born 1790 BC, which is over 700 years after the pyramid was constructed. And Prophet Moses was born 1400 BC which is over 1000 years after the pyramid was constructed. This should refute the Jews claim that they built the pyramids)

If one is to investigate the sky, he would likely be using a telescope. It would seem reasonable that the term “Sarh” refers to an observatory that contains a telescope. The reference to pure glass in the construction of the “Sarh” of Prophet Sulieman reinforces this idea. The lens of a telescope is made from a very pure glass, optical glass. This may also explain why the Queen of Sheba believed in Allah and overcame her worship of the sun when she looked and saw the existence of many stars that are like the sun and even bigger than it.

The Surat reference to other scientific issues that are related to the knowledge of the planets and stars and implying the movements of the earth and the existence of life outer space. In verse 86, Allah says:

أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (86)

Did they not see that We have made the night for them to rest therein, and the day to make them see? Surely, in this there are signs for the people who believe. (27:86)

The verse refers to the day and the night that occur due to the Earth rotating on its axis.

Verse 87 may shed some light on the debate regarding the existence of extraterrestrial beings, Allah says:

وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا مَن شَاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ (87)

And (remember) the Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will be terrified except those whom Allah wills. And all shall come to Him humbled. (27:87)

The verse refers to the presence of intelligent life outside our planet, the earth. These beings will return to Allah on the day of judgement for accountability. This verse Is not the only verse in the Quran that talks about the existence of intelligent beings in other places in the universe. For Muslims the mention of extraterrestrial beings in the Quran is sufficient evidence to resolve Fermi paradox that refers to the conflict between the lack of evidence for intelligent extraterrestrial beings and the various high estimates for their existence as suggested by Drake Equation that has the following form and estimates that there are at least 36 intelligent civilizations in our Galaxy.
N = R* fp ne fl fi fc L.

In verse 88, Allah says:

وَتَرَى الْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحَابِ ۚ صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۚ إِنَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَفْعَلُونَ (88)

And you will see the mountains and think that they are stationary, but they pass away as the passing away of the clouds. The work of Allah, Who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Well-Acquainted with what you do. (Al-Naml 27:88)

The scientific knowledge embedded in this verse refers to the movements of the mountain that is quite complex and its speed is relative for us and only absolute for Allah. The speed is relative because we cannot measure it from a fixed place since everything in the universe is moving. The earth rotates around its axis at 1000 miles/hr and rotates around the sun at 67,000 miles/hr, and rotates with others in the solar system around the center of the galaxy at 490,000 miles/hr, and moves with the galaxy at 2.24 million miles/hr and so on. Even the edge of the universe that is located 13.8 billion light year away from us is also moving at over 150,000 miles/hr, Only Allah knows the exact location and the true speed of everything.

After demonstrating the importance of the technological excellence, Surah Al-Naml shifts to displaying Allah’s power in the universe so that man may not be lured by civilization and forgets his God. Thus, a balance is established between civilization and faith in Allah, who has indeed power and authority over everything.

Say: Praise belongs to Allah, and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better or that which they associate with Him?
قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَىٰ ۗ آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (59)

Is not He (best) Who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky wherewith We cause to grow glamourous gardens. It was not within your ability to grow their trees. Is there any God along with Allah? No, but they are people who ascribe equals (to Allah).
أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ حَدَائِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍ مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنبِتُوا شَجَرَهَا ۗ أَإِلَٰهٌ مَّعَ اللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ (60)

Or, who has made the earth firm to live in; made rivers in its midst; set thereon mountains for making it firm; and made a barrier between the two seas? Is there any God along with Allah? No, but most of them do not have knowledge.
أَمَّن جَعَلَ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَجَعَلَ خِلَالَهَا أَنْهَارًا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا ۗ أَإِلَٰهٌ مَّعَ اللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (61)

Or, the One who responds to the distressed when he calls on Him and removes the distress, and Who makes you (mankind) vicegerents of the earth? Is there any God along with Allah? No, but little of you heed to advice.
أَمَّن يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ السُّوءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ الْأَرْضِ ۗ أَإِلَٰهٌ مَّعَ اللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ (62)

Or, the One who guides you through the depths of darkness on land and sea, and who sends the winds as bearing good news before His mercy? Is there any God along with Allah? No, Allah is far greater than the partners they ascribe to Him.
أَمَّن يَهْدِيكُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ وَمَن يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ ۗ أَإِلَٰهٌ مَّعَ اللَّهِ ۚ تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (63)

Or the One who originates Creation, then will reproduce it and who gives you provisions from the sky and the earth? Is there any God along with Allah? Say “Bring your proof if you are telling the truth!”
أَمَّن يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَمَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۗ أَإِلَٰهٌ مَّعَ اللَّهِ ۚ قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (64)

Say: None in the heavens or on the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah. And they do not even know when they shall be raised up (for Judgment).
قُل لَّا يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ ۚ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ (65)

Rather their knowledge has failed to comprehend the Hereafter. Rather they are in doubt about it and they are blind to it. (Al-Naml 27:59-66)
بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهَا ۖ بَلْ هُم مِّنْهَا عَمُونَ (66)

Surat Al-Naml ends as it starts by reference to the Quran. It started with:
طس ۚ تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْقُرْآنِ وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ (1) هُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (2)
Tâ Sîn; these are the Verses of the Qur’an, an enlightening book. (1) A guidance and good news for the believers. (Al-Naml 27:1-2)

And it ended with:
وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَ الْقُرْآنَ ۖ فَمَنِ اهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَقُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُنذِرِينَ (92) وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا ۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (93)
And that I should recite the Qur’an, so whoever is guided, he is guided for his own good, and whoever goes astray, say (to him): “I am only one of the warners.” (92) And say: “All the praises belong are to Allah. He will show you His signs, then you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.” (Al-Ahzab 27:92-93) [Note: Quran 27:92-93 is indeed in Surah Al-Naml, though the text mentions Al-Ahzab likely as a typo in the original source].

content:
The Trust and Human Resources

At least 17 times every day, we make a Dua to Allah asking him to guide us to the straight path by saying:

ٱهۡدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٲطَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ (٦)

Guide us to the Straight Way. (Al-Fatiha 1: 6)

Allah responded to our Dua immediately by saying here is the book that will give you the guidance to the straight path, as He said regarding the Quran:

ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ‌ۛ فِيهِ‌ۛ هُدً۬ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٢)

This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance to those who have Taqwa. (Al-Baqara 1-2)

This means that every verse in the Quran is intended to provide us with divine guidance but for us to get such guidance, we must follow Allah’s command not to just read the Quran but to do the Tadabour of it as He said:

كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (Sad 38:29)

“(This is) a Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings that they should ponder over its Verses, and those endowed with understanding may remember. “(Sad 38:29)

It is unfortunate that many Muslims who have proven their intellectual capacity by excelling in many difficult subjects like all of you claim that they are not qualified to understand this guidance of Allah by doing the tadboour of the Quran on their own and thus always rely on others.

I’ll, inshallah, nullify this excuse by seeking guidance from the last two verses in Surat Al-Ahzab (33:72-73); Allah says:

إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَہَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡہَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومً۬ا جَهُولاً۬ (٧٢) لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقَـٰتِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِڪِينَ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكَـٰتِ وَيَتُوبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ‌ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ا (٧٣)

The common English translation goes as follows:

“Indeed, We offered the Trust to the Heavens and the Earth and the Mountains; but they refused to undertake it and were afraid of it: but man undertook it; he was indeed unjust and foolish. (72)

So that Allah punishes the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the idolatrous men and the idolatrous women. And Allah pardons the believing men and the believing women, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. “(Al-Ahzab 33: 73)

This translation that I just read is based on a superficial interpretation of the individual words and lack the use of Tadabour to get the true and deeper meaning and the guidance of the verses. This translation suggests that:

Man, whom Allah described as unjust and ignorant, foolishly accepted to carry that trust and Allah allowed it for the purpose that Allah punishes the hypocrites and the idolators and to reward the believers.

Obviously, this suggestion cannot be correct because it violates a basic principle in understanding the Quran and this is that any interpretation of the Quran and the guidance, we derive from it must be consistent with Allah’s glorious names. No interpretation can be acceptable if it contradicts names such as: Al-`Adl (العدل) “The Just”, Ar-Rahim (الرحيم) “The All-Merciful”, Al-Ghaffar (الغفار) “The Forgiving”, Al-`Alim (العليم) “The All-Knowing”., Al-Khabir (الخبير) “The All-Aware” Al-Hakim (الحكيم) “The Perfectly Wise. Al-Hadi (الهادي) “The Guide.

So, in order to understand these verses and draw the guidance that we can apply, we need to answer three questions:

1. What is this (أمانة) that we translate as trust?
2. Did Allah offer this (أمانة) to man, and the stupidity of man let him commit injustice by accepting it and Allah allowed it?
3. Were the heavens, the earth and the mountains offered this (أمانة) and they decided on their own free will to reject it?

First, what is meant by (ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ) which is translated as trust? A trust means giving something to someone to preserve and then return to the owner later. We can seek the answer about the trust from Surat Al-Baqara when Allah announced His decision to create man to be His vicegerent in earth, Allah said:

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً

“And when your Lord told the angels: I am placing a vicegerent (Khalifa) in the earth,” (Al-Baqara 2:30)

This verse suggests that the trust (الامانة) that Allah is referring to in Surat Al-Ahzab is to serve as Allah’s khalifa on earth and have the guardianship over the earth according Allah’s guidance and decrees.

In order for man to fulfill this responsibility, Allah created for him all what he needs, subjugated many things to him, taught him information about all things, and equipped him with the capacity to learn on his own. Allah said:

وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعً۬ا مِّنۡهُ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١٣)

“And He has subjugated for you all that is in the heavens and in earth, all on His own. Surely, in this there are Signs indeed for those who reflect.” (Al-Jathiya 45:13)

وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا

“And He (Allah) taught Adam the names of all things” (Al-Baqara 2:31)

We can consider the knowledge that Allah taught Adam in the same way as we discussed verses are 1 to 4 of Surat Al-Rahman in a previous talk entitled “The Secret of Remembering the Quran without Memorizing it” (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zikcn-HWlqQ&t=7s ). Allah says:

ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ (١) عَلَّمَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ (٢) خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ (٣) عَلَّمَهُ ٱلۡبَيَانَ (٤)

Ar-Rahman. He taught the Qur’an. He created man. He taught him how to express himself. (Al-Rahman 55:1-4)

In that talk we made the hypothesis that Allah taught the Quran to the single soul (Nafs) form which all mankind were created. The same suggestion can be made regarding all the knowledge that Allah taught Adam. We all have this knowledge in our soul. This means that all the knowledge that man is developing is merely a recall of what Allah taught the soul. But to recall this knowledge you need to seek it and the quickest way to seek this knowledge is to have Taqwa of Allah and Allah will reconnect your materialistic brain with the knowledge in the soul. Allah says:

وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۖ وَيُعَلِّمُڪُمُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ۬

“Have Taqwa of Allah and Allah will teach you and Allah is all knowing of all things”. (Al-Baqara 2:282)

This suggests that we have in our soul all the knowledge. This in some way understood by Albert Einstein who said: “The most incomprehensible thing about the Universe is that it is comprehensible.” This means that we don’t know how we are able to understand the complexity of the universe, but this should not surprising when we read the many verses in the Quran in which Allah demands to study the universe because Allah embedded in us in the ability to understand it.

You may recall that in a previous talk entitled “The Journey of the Soul”, (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_uc1QqRz_wk&t=368s ) I proposed that our soul is like a hologram of our physical body, and it is unified with it as long as we are alive. When we die, the hologram leaves with all the information and get merged with another body in the hereafter. Our hologram has all the knowledge that Allah have taught it and all our knowledge is merely a retrieval process of this knowledge.

This concept of hologram may not be that strange because Richard Feynman who won 1965 Nobel prize in physics proposed that the universe is a hologram of another universe. The concept was proposed to refute Stephen Hawking’s idea that whatever enters the back hole is lost. Feynman says that an image of all the data still exist at the edge of the black hole. I am simplifying these concepts, but the key point is that Allah taught us all the knowledge we need to fulfill our role as His Khalifa and undertake the trust.

Therefore, man was never offered the option to carry the trust, man was created solely for this purpose. This is clear because the verse says:

وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُۖ ۬ (٧٢)

“And man undertook it. (Al-Ahzab 33:72)

You may ask whether assigning this trust was difficult for man to protect? Obviously, not because Allah said.

لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا‌ۚ

“Allah does not obligate anyone beyond his capacity.” (Al-Baqarah 2:286)

Then why did Allah describe man as (ظَلُومً۬ا جَهُولاً) (unjust and foolish)?

The description of man being unjust and foolish has nothing to do with his ability to undertake the trust. It is in reference to the grave injustice that man commits against himself and acts foolishly by not recognizing and not appreciating all the resources and the capabilities that Allah endowed him with.

Also, man becomes unjust and foolish because he does not appreciate the degree of honor that Allah granted him over many of the creations by choosing him to be His Khalifa. Allah says:

وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي آدَمَ وَحَمَلْنَاهُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِنْ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلًا (الإسراء 17:70)

“Verily we have honored the children of Adam. We carry them on the land and the sea, and have made provision of good things for them, and have preferred them above many of those whom We created with a marked preference. (Al-Isra 17:70)

So, now we know why Allah says than man is unjust and foolish, not because he is carrying the trust, but because he does not appreciate all what Allah has given him to fulfill his honorable responsibility on earth. The question for every one of us: Are we unjust to ourselves and foolish by not recognizing and appreciating all that what Allah has created for us and within us to serve as His vicegerent by protecting the trust of being guardian on the earth according to Allah’s guidance?

So, we now understand the context in which man could be described as ignorant and foolish. This can then explain the 2nd verse:

لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقَـٰتِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِڪِينَ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكَـٰتِ وَيَتُوبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ‌ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ا (٧٣)

So that Allah punishes the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the idolatrous men and the idolatrous women. And Allah pardons the believing men and the believing women, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. “(Al-Ahzab 33: 73)

In this verse, the hypocrites and the idolators are examples of those who do not protect the trust of being Khalifa and guardians over earth because they squander all the capabilities that Allah created in them and for them. But for those who guard the trust (i.e., the believers), Allah will reward them because they recognized and properly utilized the resources and capabilities that Allah granted them and fulfilled the terms of the trust following Allah’s commands.

But we still need to explain the beginning of verse 72 to understand the relevance of mentioning the heavens, the earth and the mountains.

إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَہَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡہَا (٧٢)

“Indeed, We offered the Trust to the Heavens and the Earth and the Mountains; but they refused to undertake it and were afraid of it. (Al-Ahzab 33:72)

Allah informed us in several verses in the Quran that everything in the universe praise Him and supplicate to Him as Allah says:

تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَن فِيہِنَّ‌ۚ وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورً۬ا (٤٤)

The seven heavens and the earth and all whosoever is in them praise Him, and there is not a thing but hymns His praise; but you do not understand their praise. Truly, He is Ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving (Al-Isra 17:44)

This means that everything in the universe has conscious and this has been proven experimentally using the “Double Slits Experiment”. This led Eugene P Wagner, the 1963 Nobel Prize winner in Physics. To say: ” It will remain remarkable that the very study of the external world led to the scientific conclusion that the content of the consciousness is the ultimate universal reality.”

But having conscious and having free will are different things, therefore, we need to re-interpret the meaning of 3 terms with meaning that the language allows and give us a clear insight to the verse. The three terms are:

1. the term (عَرَضۡ) in (عَرَضۡنَا), it does not necessarily mean “offer” but it can mean “show or expose”
2. the term (أَبَيۡ) in (فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَہَا) and it does not necessarily mean “refuse”, but it can mean “have no capability”.
3. the term (أَشۡفَقۡ) in (وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡہَا), it does not necessarily mean “to be afraid of”, but it can mean “they are soft”.

I’ll concluding by translating the meaning of the two verses and I sincerely hope that you study them more on your own to develop self-confidence and show real gratitude to Allah for all the great honor that He granted you to serve as His khalifa on earth:

إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَہَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡہَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومً۬ا جَهُولاً۬ (٧٢) لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقَـٰتِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِڪِينَ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكَـٰتِ وَيَتُوبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ‌ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ا (٧٣)

“(To demonstrate to man his unique capabilities compared to other creation) Allah projected the Trust (the guardianship on earth following His guidance) to the Heavens and the Earth and the Mountains; but they were unable to bear it because of their limited capacity and softness. But man (whom Allah equipped with special capabilities) was given the trust. (But if man does not recognize the capabilities and the talents that Allah endowed him with) He will be truly unjust and foolish. (72)

(Therefore ) Allah punishes the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the idolatrous men and the idolatrous women (those who commit injustice against themselves and do not protect the trust). And Allah pardons the believing men and the believing women (those who acknowledge the resources that Allah endowed them with and protect the trust), and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. “(Al-Ahzab 33: 72-73)

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom to appreciate and take full advantage all the capabilities that Allah placed in us and the resources that He made available to us to serve as His righteous vicegerent by protecting the trust of being guardian over the earth accordance to His guidance that He revealed to us in the Quran which a book that can be typed in 250 pages and the authentic Sunnah that can be typed in a book of less than 150 pages. I am sure that you have read and passed exams in many books that far exceed this number of pages. So, none of us has any excuse not to know firsthand Allah’s guidance to protect the trust.

## Allah’s Names Al-Ghaffar, Al-Ghafour and Al-Afwuu

Allah’s names Al-Ghaffar (ٱلْغَفَّارُ), Al-Ghafour (ٱلْغَفُورُ) and Al-Afuww (العفو) are similar but have subtle differences. Al-Ghaffar (ٱلْغَفَّارُ) and Al-Ghafour (ٱلْغَفُورُ) are derived from the root (ghafar) (غفر) that means to pardon, to forgive, to cover and to conceal. Al-Afuww (العفو) is derived from the root (عفا) that means to erase and remove.

Both the names Al-Ghaffar (ٱلْغَفَّارُ) and Al-Ghafour (ٱلْغَفُورُ) refer to Allah’s attribute of forgiving sins and concealing them to protect the person even from any embarrassment. Both names infer exaggeration of the attributes.

Al-Ghaffar (ٱلْغَفَّارُ) infers forgiveness regardless of the type of sins (i.e., the quality of the sin).
Al-Ghafour (ٱلْغَفُورُ) infers forgiveness regardless of the frequency of the sins (i.e., quantity of the sins).

Allah’s name Al-Afuww (العفو) infers erasing and wiping out the sin completely from the records as if the sin has never been committed.

Because of the similarities of the three names, they are translated in English as the “Most Forgiving”, therefore, let us elaborate on each name separately.

Allah’s name Al-Ghaffar (ٱلْغَفَّارُ):
It is mentioned in the Quran 3 times, and it always associated with Allah’s name Al-Aziz (The Mighty). Allah says:

رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفَّـٰرُ (٦٦)
“The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Mighty, the Most Forgiving.” (Sad 38:66)

خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۖ يُكَوِّرُ ٱلَّيۡلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّہَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّہَارَ عَلَى ٱلَّيۡلِ‌ۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ‌ۖ كُلٌّ۬ يَجۡرِى لِأَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّى‌ۗ أَلَا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفَّـٰرُ (٥)
“He created the heavens and the earth for just purpose. He wraps the night over the day, and He wraps the day over the night: He has subjected the sun and the moon (to His law), each one moving for an appointed term. Is not He the Mighty, the Most Forgiving?” (Al-Zumar 39:5)

وَيَـٰقَوۡمِ مَا لِىٓ أَدۡعُوڪُمۡ إِلَى ٱلنَّجَوٰةِ وَتَدۡعُونَنِىٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ (٤١) تَدۡعُونَنِى لِأَڪۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَأُشۡرِكَ بِهِۦ مَا لَيۡسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ۬ وَأَنَا۟ أَدۡعُوڪُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡغَفَّـٰرِ (٤٢)
“O my people! Why shouldn’t I call you salvation while you are calling me to the Fire? (41) You call me to disbelieve in Allah and ascribe to Him partners about whom I have no knowledge, while I call you to the Mighty, the Most-Forgiving.” (Ghafir 40:41-42)

Allah’s name Al-Ghafour (ٱلْغَفُورُ):
It is mentioned in the Quran 11 times
* 9 times associated with Allah’s name Al-Rahime (The Most Merciful)
* 1 time associated with Allah’s name Al-Aziz (The Mighty)
* 1 time associated with Allah’s name Al-Wadud (The Most Loving).

Allah says:
نَبِّئۡ عِبَادِىٓ أَنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٤٩)
“Tell My slaves that I am the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful” (Al-Hijr 15:49)

قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
“Say: “O my Servants who have transgressed against their souls! Despair not of the Mercy of Allah: for Allah forgives all sins: for He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Zumur 39:53)

تَبَـٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ (١) ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلاً۬‌ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ (٢)
“Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Kingdom: and He is powerful over everything (1) He Who created Death and Life, that He may test you as of which is better in his deeds: and He is the All-Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving” (Al-Mulk 67:1-2)

إِنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ يُبۡدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ (١٣) وَهُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلۡوَدُودُ (١٤) ذُو ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡمَجِيدُ (١٥) فَعَّالٌ۬ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ (١٦)
“Surely, He begins (creation) and restores it (13) And He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most-Loving, (14) The Master of the Throne of Glory, (15) The Doer of all that He intends.” (Al-Burooj 85:13-16)

There are other forms that are related to Allah’s names Al-Ghaffar and Al-Ghafour. These are Ghaffar (غَفَّارً), Ghafer (غَافِر) and Ghafour (غَفُور). Allah says:

فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ غَفَّارً۬ا (١٠) يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارً۬ا (١١) وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٲلٍ۬ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡہَـٰرً۬ا (١٢)
“I (Nuh) said, `ask forgiveness from your Lord; for He is Oft-Forgiving. (10) ‘He will send abundant rain from the sky upon you, (11) and will provide you with wealth and children, and will bestow gardens on you and bestow rivers on you.” (Nuh 71:10-12)

غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ الْعِقَابِ ذِي الطَّوْلِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ إِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ
“The Forgiver of sin who accepts repentance, who is strict in punishment, and who has a Long Reach (of power). There is no god but He. To Him is the final return.” (Ghafir 40:3)

قُلۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى يُحۡبِبۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ۬ (٣١)
Say: “If you really love Allah, follow me: Allah will love you and forgive you your sins; for Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Imran 3:31)

Allah’s name Al-Afuww (العفو):
It is mentioned in the Quran in 5 verses.
* 4 times associated with Allah’s name Al-Ghafour
* 1 time associated with Allah’s name Al-Qader (القادر) *The All-Powerful”.

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَفَّٮٰهُمُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ ظَالِمِىٓ أَنفُسِہِمۡ قَالُواْ فِيمَ كُنتُمۡ‌ۖ قَالُواْ كُنَّا مُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ ... فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَعۡفُوَعَنۡہُمۡ‌ۚ وَڪَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورً۬ا (٩٧-٩٩)
“When angels take the souls of those who die while transgressing against themselves (i.e., committing sins)... For these, there is hope that Allah will forgive them: for Allah is Oft-Pardoning, Oft-Forgiving.” (Al-Nisa 4:97-99)

إِنْ تُبْدُوا خَيْرًا أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ أَوْ تَعْفُوا عَنْ سُوءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا قَدِيرًا
“Whether you disclose a good deed, or conceal it, or pardon an evil, verily, Allah is Most-forgiving, All-Powerful” (Al-Nisa 4:149)

Allah’s name Al-Afuww was the name that the Prophet (PBUH) said to his wife Aisha (RA) to invoke if she witnessed the night of power. Aisha (RA) asked:
يا رسولَ الله إِنْ وَافَقْتُ ليلةَ القَدْرِ ، ما أَدْعُو به ؟
“If I witnesses the night of power (ليلةَ القَدْرِ), what supplication should I make?
The Prophet (PBUH) told her to say:
اللهم إنك عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُ الْعَفْوَ فاعْفُ عَنِّي
Say: O’ Allah you are the most forgiving, You love forgiveness, forgive me.”

In reading the Quran, one notes that the Al-Afwu (العفو) is associated with erasing major sins. An example is the sin of worshipping the calf:
وَإِذۡ وَٲعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةً۬ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَـٰلِمُونَ (٥١) ثُمَّ عَفَيۡنَا عَنڪُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ (٥٢)
“And remember when We appointed forty nights for Moses and (in his absence) you took the calf (for worship), and you were transgressors. (51) Then, even after that, We forgave (Afuwna) you, so that you might be grateful.” (Al-Baqarah 2:51-52)

Also, when some Muslims committed major sin and ran away in the Battle of Uhud:
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسۡتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ بِبَعۡضِ مَا كَسَبُواْ‌ۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡہُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ۬ (١٥٥)
“Those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met (i.e. the battle of Uhud), it was Satan who caused them to backslide because of some of their (past) deeds. But Allah has already forgiven (Afa’a) them. Surely, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Forbearing.” (Al-Imran 3:155)

Comparison
Scholars have differed regarding which of Allah’s names Al-Ghafour and the Al-Afuww has broader implication. Some said that Al-Ghafour is broader since it includes the meaning of Al-Afuww plus concealment of the sins. However, the majority of scholars believe that Al-Afuww has broader meaning since it refers to total erasing and removal of the sins from the person’s records, while Al-Ghafour refers to covering and concealing the sins without necessarily erasing them from the record.

Furthermore, Al-Afuww includes the meaning of transforming the sins into good deeds. Allah says:
وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَ‌ۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٲلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامً۬ا (٦٨) يُضَـٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا (٦٩) إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلاً۬ صَـٰلِحً۬ا فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِہِمۡ حَسَنَـٰتٍ۬‌ۗ وَڪَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ (٧٠)
“(The faithful slaves of Allah) Those who do not invoke with Allah, any other god, and do not kill any person whom Allah has forbidden, except for just cause, and do not commit adultery. Anyone who does this will meet the penalty. (68) Doubled for him will be the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in disgrace. (69) Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, for them Allah will change their sins into good deeds, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Furqan 25:68-70)

Note that the verses specify that transforming the sins to good deeds is conditional on four conditions:
1. Turning to Allah in repentance (Tawba)
2. Firm belief in Allah (Iman)
3. Doing righteous deeds (Amal Salih)
4. Insisting on goodness.

To ensure total forgiveness, wiping out of our sins and replacing them with good deeds, we should invoke Allah with Al-Afuww (العفو).

Exceptions to Securing Allah’s Forgiveness
1/ Associating anyone with Allah in worship. Allah said:
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ افْتَرَى إِثْمًا عَظِيمًا
“Allah does not forgive ascribing a partner to Him, but He forgives anything else for whomsoever He wills. And whoever ascribes partners to Allah has indeed invented a tremendous sin.” (Al-Nisa 4:48)

2/ Insisting on Allah’s disobedience knowingly
وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَنْ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلَى مَا فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
“And those who commit shameful deeds or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins – and who can forgive sins except Allah? – and they don’t knowingly persist on whatever they have been doing.” (Al-Imran 3:135)

## Elements to Adopt in our Character

1/ Always call upon Al-Ghaffar, Al-Ghafoor and Al-Afuww regardless of the nature and the frequency of your sins.
2/ Never despair from the mercy of Allah to forgive you. Abu Hurairah (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
قال الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: والذي نفسي بيده لو لم تذنبوا لذهب الله بكم ولجاء بقوم غيركم يذنبون فيستغفرون الله فيغفر لهم
“By the One in Whose Hand my soul is, if you were you not to commit sins, Allah would replace you with another people who would commit sins and ask for Allah’s forgiveness, and He would forgive them.” (Muslim)

Similar Hadith was reported Abu Ayyub Khalid bin Zaid (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
حديث أبي أيوب، خالد بن زيد  قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: لولا أنكم تذنبون لخلق الله خلقًا يذنبون، فيستغفرون فيغفر لهم
“Were you not to commit sins, Allah would create people who would commit sins and ask for forgiveness and He would forgive them.” (Muslim)

These hadith are not intended to encourage people to sin, but rather to ensure that they never get despaired from Allah’s mercy.

3/ Forgive and cleanse your heart from grudges and anger towards anyone. Allah’s forgiveness belongs to those who forgive others.
وَلْيَعْفُوا وَلْيَصْفَحُوا أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ
“Let them forgive and show tolerance, do you not want Allah to forgive you? Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Nur 24:22)

While Muslims are not prohibited from punishing those who transgress against them with equal punishment, it is much better to forgive. Allah said:
وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَهُمْ الْبَغْيُ هُمْ يَنْتَصِرُونَ (٣٩) وَجَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُهَا فَمَنْ عَفَا وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ
“And those who, when an oppression inflicts them, they defend themselves. The recompense for an injury is an injury equal to it (in degree): but if a person forgives and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from Allah: for (Allah) loves not those who do wrong.” (Al-Shura 42:39-40)

وَسَارِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةٍ۬ مِّن رَّبِّڪُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ (١٣٣)
And race with one with another towards forgiveness from your Lord, and towards a paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. (Al-Imran 3:133)

4/ Commit yourself to conceal others’ faults and sins. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( —- ومن ستر مؤمنا ستره الله في الدنيا والآخرة )
“Whoever conceals the sins of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his sins in this world and the Hereafter”. (Muslim)

5/ Never spread the news about your sins. Repent and keep them to yourself. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
في الصحيحين من حديث أبي هريرة ـ رضي الله عنه ـ أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: كل أمتي معافى إلا المجاهرين
“Everyone from my nation will be forgiven except those who expose their wrongdoings. An example of this is that a person commits a sin at night which Allah has concealed, but in the morning, he goes and says: ‘O so-and-so, I did such and such last night.’ He spends the night concealed by his Lord, but in the morning, he removes Allah’s concealment from himself.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

6/ Be frequent in asking Allah for His forgiveness. Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) Said:
عن أبي هريرة – رضي الله عنه – قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : “والله إني لأستغفر الله وأتوب إليه في اليوم أكثر من سبعين مرة”
“By Allah, I ask Allah for forgiveness over than seventy times per day.” (Bukhari)

A man came to Imam Al-Hasan al-Basri and complained to him about the drought. The Imam said: “Seek Allah’s forgiveness”. Another man came and complained about poverty, another about lack of children, and another about a dry garden. To each of them, the Imam gave the same answer: “Seek Allah’s forgiveness”. When asked why he gave the same answer to different problems, he recited the following verses:
فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ غَفَّارً۬ا (١٠) يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارً۬ا (١١) وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٲلٍ۬ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡہَـٰرً۬ا (١٢)
“I (Nuh) said, `ask forgiveness from your Lord; for He is Oft-Forgiving. (10) ‘He will send abundant rain from the sky upon you, (11) and will provide you with wealth and children, and will bestow gardens on you and bestow rivers on you.” (Nuh 71:10-12)

Seeking Allah’s forgiveness at the pre-dawn hours is a great act of worship since Allah acknowledges these people:
وَٱلۡمُسۡتَغۡفِرِينَ بِٱلۡأَسۡحَارِ (١٧)
“Those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours” (Al-Emran 3:17)

وَبِٱلۡأَسۡحَارِ هُمۡ يَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ (١٨)
“And in the hours before dawn they (were found) asking (Allah) for forgiveness;” (Al-Dhariyat 51:18)
