# Allah’s Name Al-Aleem (العليم) – “The All-Knowing”

Allah’s name Al-Alim (العليم) is revealed in the Quran in more than 150 verses, and it came mostly in association with other names such as (الحكيم) The All-wise, (العزيز) The All-Mighty, (القدير) The All-Powerful, (الخبير) The All-Aware, (الخلاق) The Creator, and (السَّمِيعُ) The All-Hearer.

### The All-wise (الحكيم)
قَالُواْ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
“They (angels) said: “Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what you have taught us. Verily, it is You, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.”” (Al-Baqara 2:32)

### The All-Mighty (العزيز)
فَالِقُ ٱلۡإِصۡبَاحِ وَجَعَلَ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَكَنً۬ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ حُسۡبَانً۬ا‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
“(He is the) Cleaver of the daybreak. He has made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. This is a measure set by the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing” (Al-Anam 6:96)

### The All-Powerful (القدير)
وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّٮٰكُمۡ‌ۚ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرۡذَلِ ٱلۡعُمُرِ لِكَىۡ لَا يَعۡلَمَ بَعۡدَ عِلۡمٍ۬ شَيۡـًٔا‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬
“Allah has created you, then takes you back. And among you there are some who are sent back to a feeble age, so that they know nothing after having known (much): for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.” (Al-Nahl 16:70)

### The All-Aware (الخبير)
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ۬ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ شُعُوبً۬ا وَقَبَآٮِٕلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْ‌ۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَٮٰكُمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ۬
“O mankind! We have created you from a male and a female, and made you into nations and tribes, that you may know one another. Verily, the most honorable of you with Allah is the one with most Taqwa. Surely, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.” (Al-Hujurat 49:13)

### The Creator (الخلاق)
وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَأَتِيَةٌ۬‌ۖ فَٱصۡفَحِ ٱلصَّفۡحَ ٱلۡجَمِيلَ (٨٥) إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخَلَّـٰقُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ (٨٦)
“We have not created the heavens, the earth, and all that is in between them but for just purpose. The Hour is surely coming. So, overlook (any human faults) with gracious forgiveness. (85) Surely Your Lord is the Creator of all, the All-knowing” (Al-Hijr 15:85-86)

### The All-Hearer (السَّمِيعُ)
وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ نَزۡغٌ۬ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ ٱالسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
“And should an incitement from Satan strike you, seek refuge in Allah. He is the All-Hearer, the All-knowing.” (Fusselat 41:36)

Allah is the only one who can protect your from Satan’s incitements and thus you should refuge in Him from Satan. Abu Saed Al-Khudri (أبي سعيد الخدري) narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) taught the companion to say
(  أعوذُ بِاللهِ السَّميعِ العليمِ من الشَّيطان الرجيم ، مِنَ هَمْزِهِ ونَفْخِهِ ونَفْثِهِ ( أبو داود والترمذي والنسائي )
“I seek refuge in Allah the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, from the accursed Shaytan and his evil insinuations, breath and impurity.”

The construct of the name Al-Aleem (العليم) is of an exaggerated form (صيغ المبالغة) regarding both the extent (الكم) and the quality (النوع) of the knowledge being possessed. Allah’s name Al-Aleem (العليم) refers to Allah’s attribute of having infinite and perfect knowledge. The extent and perfection of Allah’s knowledge lies in comprehending everything whether it is manifest or hidden, small or large, and an inception or an outcome.

The perfection of Allah’s knowledge is not derived from things known, rather all things that are known are derived from Allah’s knowledge. Elements of Allah knowledge are revealed to mankind to ensure their survival, advances and serving their role in the earth as His vicegerent. But such knowledge, no matter how impressive they are, they are still infinitesimal compared to Allah’s knowledge. Allah says:
وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬
“And you are not given from the knowledge but a little” (Al-Isra 17:85)

In site the limited knowledge that man will ever acquire, still the title Aleem (عليم) (Knowledgeable) can be given to people. Such title was claimed by Prophet Yusuf when he said to the king:
( قَالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلَى خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ ﴾ 9يوسف
“He said: “Appoint me over the treasures of the land: I am indeed a knowledgeable custodian.” (Yusuf 12:55)

No matter how much knowledge man has, his knowledge is very limited because only Allah knows what is happening now, what happened in the past and what will happen in the future and what are the consequences of everything that happened or will happen. Also, Allah knows both the unseen (ٱلۡغَيۡبِ) and the seen (ٱلشَّہَـٰدَةِ) as He emphasized many times in the Quran such as:
وَقُلِ ٱعۡمَلُواْ فَسَيَرَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمۡ وَرَسُولُهُ ۥ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ‌ۖ وَسَتُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَـٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّہَـٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (١٠٥)
Say, “so whatever you do, Allah will see your deed, as will His messenger and the believers, and you shall be returned to the Knower of the seen and the unseen, then He will tell you what you used to do. (Al-Tawba 9:105)

هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ (سورة الحشر الآية: 22)
“He is Allah, there is no god but He― He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen; He is the Merciful Rahman” (Al-Hashr 59:22)

It is interesting that Allah states that He knows the unseen (invisible/ past/ future) first and the seen (visible/present) second. This suggested that knowing the seen which is listed second is more compelling than the unseen that is listed first. [To clarify, you would say that a student passed the exam, and he was the top of the class. The sequence is relevant because being the top of the class is more impressive than passing the exam. But saying the student was the top of the class and passed the exam does not make sense.]

One may argue that Allah is unseen and thus Him knowing the unseen is easier than knowing the seen. But this is not correct when we realize that we, ourselves, know the unseen (the invisible past) and do not have any knowledge about the seen (what is presently visible). This needs explanation to show that it is impossible for us to know the present? The process of human vision involves the following steps:

1. The light is reflected off the object and travels in a straight line into the eye through the cornea that focuses it on the back of the eye that projects it on the retina.
2. The photoreceptors in the retina translate the image into electrical impulses that travel along the optical nerve and into the brain.
3. The brain makes sense of the signals and tells us what we are seeing.

Obviously, these steps take time, so by the time our brain deciphers what is there, the object is no longer there and all what you think we are seeing is the object in past time and not in the present time. Because the speed of light is 670 million miles per hour, if I am standing 10 feet in front of you; it takes 1.0×10^-8 seconds (10 billionth of a second) (10 million femtoseconds) for you to see me. So, what you saw is what you were doing 10 million femtoseconds ago and not now. (Recall that Dr. Ahmad Zewail won noble prize in chemistry for his work in developing pulsed laser microscope that can measure chemical reaction that occurs at 1 femtosecond).

It is the mercy of Allah that our eyes and brain cannot differentiate between images that fast, otherwise, we would always see discrete pictures that come one after another because objects located at different distances would be seen at different times. So, things that are close to us we will see them in the past but within billionth of seconds from their occurrence. But there are objects that are very far away, and the light takes many years to arrive to us.

Based on images from the James Webb telescope, astronomers identified that the farthest star to earth lies 13.6 billion light years away. So, we are seeing this star when it was 13.6 billion years ago, where is it now, no one knows but Allah. Using Hubble law on the accelerating expansion of the universe, astronomers suggest that this star is now over 30 billion light years from where it was when we saw it. To appreciate the distances that we are discussing; the light travels at a speed of 670 million miles per hour, the distance between earth and this star that is at 13.6 billion light years which is 80 x 10^21 miles (80 sextillion miles) away from us.
Note: [Million (10^6), Billion (10^9), Trillion (10^12), Quadrillion (10^15), Quintillion (10^18) Sextillion (10^21)]

This should give us more appreciation of Allah’s knowledge. He is the only one who knows everything that exist in the universe all the time. Allah says:
لَا يَعۡزُبُ عَنۡهُ مِثۡقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ۬ فِى ٱالسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَآ أَصۡغَرُ مِن ذَٲلِكَ وَلَآ أَكۡبَرُ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَآ أَصۡغَرُ مِن ذَٲلِكَ وَلَآ أَكۡبَرُ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬
“Not an atom or less or greater than that whether in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him.” (Saba 34:3)

Allah does not only know where every star in this vast universe is and what every human being is doing or thinking, but He also even knows when a leaf falls from a tree and where it falls. Allah says:
وَعِندَهُ ۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ‌ۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبٍ۬ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٥٩)
“And with Him are the keys of the Unseen. No One knows them but He. He knows what is in the land and the sea. No leaf ever falls but that He knows about it, and there is no grain in the darkness of the earth, or anything fresh or dry that is not in a clear record.” (Al-Anaam 6:59)

Allah knowledge of every minute detail that happens in the universe is so critical because of the dynamic nature of the universe. Things you may consider minor can have major effect; this is known as the Butterfly effect. In 1963 Edward Lorenz, a meteorologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, published an article on “Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow,” that became a classic in the field of chaos research that is popularly known as the “Butterfly effect.” The theory suggests that a very small change in the initial conditions of some physical system can result in very large effects later in time. The example is that the fluttering of a butterfly’s wing in China can have cascading effect that produces a thunderstorm in New York.

Everything, small or large, is known to Allah, He says:
يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡہَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱالسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيہَا‌ۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ ( الحديد : 4 )
“He knows all that enters the earth and all that emerges from it, and all that comes down from the sky and all that ascends from it; and He is with you wheresoever you may be. And Allah is Seer of what you do.” (Al-Hadeed 57:4)

وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ {ق:16}
“We verily created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein” (Qaf 50:16)

ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَحۡمِلُ ڪُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامُ وَمَا تَزۡدَادُ‌ۖ وَڪُلُّ شَىۡءٍ عِندَهُ ۥ بِمِقۡدَارٍ (٨) عَالِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّہَـٰدَةِ ٱلۡڪَبِيرُ ٱلۡمُتَعَالِ (٩)
“Allah knows what every female bears, and by how much the wombs fall short (of their time or number) or exceed. Everything with Him is in (due) proportion. (8) He is the All-Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Great, the Most- High.” (Ar Ra'd 13:8-9)

While Allah knows what is happening at distances that we can estimate, He also knows what exists at the very minute distance that we cannot even comprehend. The smallest distance that scientists assume to exist is what is known as the Planck length which is the distance that it is impossible to determine the difference between two locations less than it apart. This Planck distance is about (1.6×10^-32 mm) (1.6×10^-12 X 10^-12 x 10^-9 mm) (i.e., take one mm and divide it trillion times and then take one of these parts and divide it trillion time and then take one of these parts and divide it again billion times).

Allah does not only know what exists within the Planck length, but He also knows all the changes that happen with the Planck time. The Planck time is the time it would take a photon traveling at the speed of light to cross a distance equal to one Planck length and this time is roughly 10^-43 seconds. (Note that the femtosecond (10^-15 of a second) that resulted in Ahmed H. Zewail winning noble prize is 10^28 times larger than the Planck time (i.e 10 octillion times).
Note: [Million (10^6), Billion (10^9), Trillion (10^12), Quadrillion (10^15), Quintillion (10^18), Sextillion (10^21), Septillion (10^24), Octillion (10^27)]

Reflecting on the above verses open to us a window to some level of Allah knowledge to encourage us to study in detail everything around us whether it is small or large. This can only be done by true Tadabour of the Ayat (signs) identified to us in the Quran. The extent of Allah’s knowledge should teach us the importance of big data and data analytics to help us identify Allah’s rules in the universe because they have impact on our lives.

## Elements to Adopt in our Character
4. Strive to be Aleem in your field by expanding your knowledge in all the critical elements in both depth and breadth.
5. Learn not to marginalize small factors (Allah known even when and where a leaf is falling) and appreciate the significance of big data.
6. Have a true appreciation of Allah’s knowledge to strengthen your belief in Him and thus have an awe of Him that gives you a compelling incentive to follow His commands.
7. Seek Allah’s knowledge by improving your Taqwa as He said:
وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ‌ۖ وَيُعَلِّمُڪُمُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ۬
“Have Taqwa of Allah and Allah will teach you and Allah is all knowing of all things”. (Al-Baqara 2:282)
5. Study all the verses in the Quran that speak about the creations of Allah and commit to study and excel in natural sciences. Allah commands us to study these subjects as He said:
إِنَّ فِى خَلۡقِ ٱالسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخْتِلَـٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهارِ وَٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلَّتِي تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱالسَّمَآءِ مِن مَّآءٍ۬ فَأَحۡيَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن ڪُلِّ دَآبَّةٍ۬ وَتَصۡرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَـٰحِ وَٱالسَّحَابِ ٱلۡمُسَخَّرِ بَيۡنَ ٱالسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوْمٍ۬ يَعۡقِلُونَ
“Verily! In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which is of use to mankind, and the water (rain) which Allah sends down from the sky and makes the earth alive therewith after its death, and the moving (living) creatures of all kinds that He has scattered therein, and in the veering of winds and clouds which are held between the sky and the earth, are indeed ayat (proofs, evidences, signs, etc.) for people of understanding.” (Al-Baqara 2:164)
إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ لَآَيَاتٍ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ (190)
“Verily! In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, there are indeed signs for those who endowed with understanding.” (Al-Imran 3:190)
6. Heed the advice of Imam Badi Al-Zaman (الإمام بديع الزمان سعيد النورسي), the great Turkish scholar who was born in 1873 who said that the miracles that Allah reported in the Quran and done by other than prophets are a promise by Allah that He, as part of His blessing and mercy, will allow people to achieve them through knowledge and understanding. (المعجزات في كتاب الله هي وعد للبشر سيبلغون مثلها بالاسباب و العلم). The Quran includes several miracles that was even done on the hand of people such as the teleportation of the throne of the Queen of Sheba. This is a technology that Muslim researchers should seek to develop because they are confident that it will happen one day, so let them be the ones who make it happen. Also, many verses in the Quran suggest that the universe has intelligent beings who may even have more advanced civilizations than ours. Muslims scientists should seek to develop means to communicate with them. The Prophet (PBUH) said that for every disease, Allah created a remedy. Muslims scientists ought to seek to find treatment to all currently untreatable diseases since they are confident that treatments exist.

content:
Atheism between Arrogance and Stupidity or Confusion

Today, I will, inshallah, revisit the subject of atheism among Muslims. In the past I presented eight proofs that Allah exist in a talk entitled “A Muslim can never be atheist”.  You can review this talk and its YouTube video at (https://successineternity.com/) and  (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OmS_xgAn8r4). The eight proofs were:

1. The Claimant Proof
2. The Language Proof
3. The Unique Name Proof
4. The Philosophers’ Proof
5. The legal System Proof
6. The Progressive Superiority Proof
7. The Hope Proof
8. The Fairness Resolution Proof

In this talk, I intend to, inshallah, show that atheism results from arrogance or stupidity or confusion and discuss how you respond to each cause.

Some Muslims who claim to be atheists fall in the stupid category because they blindly follow the opinion of others who may be arrogant scientists or individuals who refuse to live under the moral code of religion. You cannot change their mind because they refuse to listen to any logical argument that is religiously related.

However, one possible argument that you may offer them is the simple decision tree, shown in Figure 1. This decision tree is used to identify the scenario that can achieve the highest potential positive outcome.  As shown in Figure 1, deciding that God does not exist can results in the tremendous loss of eternal condemnation in Hell.  But deciding that God exists can lead to the outcome of eternal happiness in paradise.  By default, if God exists, He will inform us about the consequences of believing or rejecting Him and His expectations from us, and this can be derived from His revealed religions.

Figure 1. Decision Tree

Also, the mere existence of the word God proves that God exists. Words are identified by man after a concept is conceived, not before it. A word is identified to allow people to communicate about the concept or the idea. The word God exists in all cultures and in the writing of man from the beginning of civilizations. The word would not have existed if people did not know that there is a creator for the universe and His title is God.

If these two simple arguments did not convince, ignoring those people is more appropriate as Allah advised us by saying:

خُذِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡعُرۡفِ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِينَ (١٩٩)
“Hold to forgiveness; command what is right; but turn away from the ignorant.” (Al-Araf 7:199)

Another group of Muslims claim to be atheists because of their confusion about the nature of God. This group denies God’s existence because of what they consider a contradiction between the Merciful God who controls everything in the universe and Him allowing the suffering in the world even children. The confusion results from attempting to put God under the same constrains that apply on people. People are constrained by four dimensions: three spatial dimensions (width, height, and length) and one time dimension. God is not constrained by any. Since God is not constrained by the time dimension, we cannot discuss His actions using past, present and futures tenses.

We must admit our limitations and be confident that God is merciful and just even if we cannot truly comprehend certain things that happen around us. Also, God informs us that anything bad happens, it is because of what we have done. So, people should stop blaming God for their problems as He clearly says:

ظَهَرَ ٱلۡفَسَادُ فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِى ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِى عَمِلُواْ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ (٤١) (الرُّوم)
“Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so that He (Allah) makes them taste some of what they have done, in order that they may return (to the right way).” (Al-Rome 30:41)

وَمَآ أَصَـٰبَڪُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ۬ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِيكُمۡ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَن كَثِيرٍ۬ (الشورى)
“And whatever a disaster befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned. And He overlooks many (of your evil deeds).” (Al-Shura 42:30)

There is another group who claim to be atheist because of their confusion about the religious laws. Those people are generally disenfranchised by zealous parents or corrupt religious teachers or stubborn religious teachers who promote illogical ideas just because some scholar in the past have proposed them. Those need to remove their confusion by studying the religion of Islam from its authentic sources: the Quran and the few authentic hadith, not on everything that they hear.

It is unfortunate that some accomplished scientists claim that they do not believe in God, though they have shown the intricate nature of the universe that relies on extremely tight tolerance of the fundamental cosmological parameters for it to exist. An example of those accomplished scientists is Dr. Martin Rees, the renowned British cosmologist and astrophysicist.

One of Rees’s books is the book entitled: “Just Six numbers’ that govern the universe”. This book discusses the necessary degree of exactness of the cosmological numbers for the universe to exist. These six cosmological numbers are classified as follows:

1. Two numbers are related to basic forces: M and €
2. Two numbers control the size of the universe: Ɣ and λ
3. Two numbers govern the properties of the space: Q and D

For the universe to exist, these numbers must be extremely concise. The term that scientists often use to express the degree of conciseness of the universe’s cosmological numbers is “fine tuning”.

As example of the required degree of conciseness for the universe to exist is the exactness of value of the number N. Number N represents the strength of the electrical forces holding atoms together divided by the force of the gravity between them. This value of number N is 10^36 (billion billion billion billion). The analysis by many accomplished scientists has shown that if the Number N changes by 1 every 10 Decillion (change by 10^-34), only a short-lived miniature universe could exist, and no creatures could grow larger than insects.

Note: [Million (10^6), Billion (10^9), Trillion (10^12), Quadrillion (10^15), Quintillion (10^18), Sextillion (10^21), Septillion (10^24), Octillion (10^27), Nonillion (10^30), Decillion (10^33), Undecillion (10^36)]

Another atheist who is well-known cosmologist and theoretical physicist is Stephen Hawking who concluded, based on rigorous mathematical derivation, that if the expansion rate of the universe was different by one part of a thousand, million, million a second (10^-15 per second) after the big bang, the universe would have collapsed back to itself and never developed galaxies. Scientists have estimated that the age of the universe is 13.7 billion years that corresponds to 4.3X10^17 seconds. Based on Hawking’s prediction the existence of the universe would collapse is the expansion occurred in 1.2 hrs less than the current age of 13.7 billion years.

To appreciate the necessary level of accuracy for the universe to exist, consider

A person that weights 70 kg (154 lb). The body of such as person is composed of 6.5 x 10^27 atoms. If the degree of accuracy in the cosmological number N applies to man, we can say that the person will not survive if his number of atoms is reduced by less than 0.5×10^-6 atom (i.e 1 atom from every two million atoms), or in other words if the person loses ¼ gm of his weight. Man loses kilograms not grams and he still survive. This means that the existence of the universe requires far more accuracy, and this cannot not logically achieved except by an infinitely knowledgeable creator.

Allah has informed us in the Quran that He created the universe (the heavens and the earth) with very high accuracy and following strict rules. The word Allah used to describe the condition for creating the universe is (بِالْحَقِّ) that means with justice, in truth, according to strict rules, just laws, proper rules, etc. Allah says:

وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۖ وَيَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ڪُن فَيَڪُونُ‌ۚ قَوۡلُهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ‌ۚ (الأنعام)
“He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth with strict rules. On the day He says: “Be” it will become to be, His Word is the truth.” (Al-Anaam 6:73)

خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (العنكبوت)
“Allah created the heavens and the earth with strict rules. Surely in this there is a sign for the believers” (Al-Ankaboot 29:44)

Because Allah knew that some intelligent people will not believe, He directed them to study themselves to know that He is their Creator, and the Creator the universe. Allah says:

أَوَلَمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ فِىٓ أَنفُسِہِم‌ۗ مَّا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّى‌ۗ وَإِنَّ ڪَثِيرً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّہِمۡ لَكَـٰفِرُونَ (٨) (الرُّوم)
“Do they not reflect in their own selves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them but with strict rules, and for an appointed time. Yes, many of the people are disbelieves in the meeting with their Lord (at the Resurrection)!” (Al-Room 30:8)

Allah also directs those people to humble themselves by realizing their origin which is a drop of fluid. But Allah points out that there will be some people who when they grow, they will have the audacity to become open adversaries to Allah to the point of denying His existence or associating others with Him. Allah says:

خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ تَعَـٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٣) خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةٍ۬ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (٤) (النحل)
He (Allah) created the heavens and the earth with strict rules. He is above ascribing partners to Him. (3) He created man from a drop of fluid, and soon man becomes an open adversary (to Allah) (Al-Nahl 16:3-4)

أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقۡنَـٰهُ مِن نُّطۡفَةٍ۬ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (٧٧) (يس)
“Doesn’t man see that We have created him from a drop of fluid? and soon man becomes an open adversary (to Allah) (Yaseen 37:77)

Humility can come when man recognizes that he is made from mainly hydrogen, oxygen and carbon atoms as shown in Table 1.  It is interesting that the composition of man needs to be extremely accurate to survive.  We know that iron is very important to our existence, but its number atoms are 100,000 less than the number of hydrogen atoms, but even this extremely small number must exist.  So, if we lose only 0.0007% of our atoms, we will die.

Table 1 Atomic Composition of a 70-kg Man

zinc | 2.1 x 10^22
rubidium | 2.2 x 10^21
strontium | 2.2 x 10^21
bromine | 2 x 10^21
aluminum | 1 x 10^21
copper | 7 x 10^20
lead | 3 x 10^20
cadmium | 3 x 10^20
boron | 2 x 10^20
manganese | 1 x 10^20
nickel | 1 x 10^20
lithium | 1 x 10^20
barium | 8 x 10^19
iodine | 5 x 10^19
tin | 4 x 10^19
gold | 2 x 10^19
zirconium | 2 x 10^19
cobalt | 2 x 10^19
cesium | 7 x 10^18
mercury | 6 x 10^18
arsenic | 6 x 10^18
chromium | 6 x 10^18
molybdenum | 3 x 10^18
selenium | 3 x 10^18
beryllium | 3 x 10^18
vanadium | 8 x 10^17

With these compelling numbers that scientists have developed regarding the extreme accuracy that are required to create the universe, what are their justifications to deny the presence of God? Their justification of denying God’s existence may be summarized in two main reasons:

1. They cannot derive the presence of God from a mathematical model.
2. They claim that they may be able to identify other values for the cosmological numbers that will allow the universe to exist with larger variations the currently derived numbers. They are basically claiming that they may be able to design the universe better than God.

Regarding the first reason, the justification is not even scientific because mathematical models start by basing them on axioms. Axioms, also called postulates, are assumptions that are designated as self-evidently true and thus needing no proof. So, suggesting that every truth must be incorporated in equation is not correct. As example of postulate in the general relativity theory is the presence of matter “curves” spacetime, and this curvature affects the path of free particles. Other example of axions: “things that are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another”.

The second reason is a clear demonstration of despised arrogance for the simple reason that there is no absolute proof that the current theories are correct and that there are no more than the six cosmological numbers in play. Also, history tells us that knowledge keeps advancing and theories of physics change. In fact, even the number of forces that exist in the universe is now being questioned. Current theories are based on the understanding that there are only 4 fundamental forces in the universe, and these are: 1) the strong nuclear force, 2) the electromagnetic force, 3) the weak nuclear force, and 4) gravity. But recent analysis of data on the elementary particle W bosons has shown that the particle is heavier than the prediction of the Standard Model of particle physics. The measurement was reported in the journal Science (April 2022) comes from the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory. Such measurements could result in a huge shift in fundamental physics.

Scientists who think that they have discovered all the rules of creation need to have some humility because no matter how much knowledge man will ever have, it is infinitesimal compared to Allah’s knowledge as He said:

وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬
“And you are not given from the knowledge but a little” (Al-Isra 17:85)

For those scientists whose arrogance are clear from their basis for denying God’s existence, Allah, has identified for them the one condition that must exist for them to believe in Him. This condition is seeing the painful punishment of Hell, Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّتۡ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ڪَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٩٦) وَلَوۡ جَآءَتۡہُمۡ ڪُلُّ ءَايَةٍ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ (٩٧) (يونس)
“Surely, those against whom the Word of Your Lord has been verified would not believe (96) Even though every sign comes to them unless they see (for themselves) the painful punishment.” (Yunus 10:96-97)

كَذَٲلِكَ سَلَكۡنَـٰهُ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ (٢٠٠) لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ (٢٠١) فَيَأۡتِيَہُم بَغۡتَةً۬ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ (الشعراء)
“Thus, have We caused it pass through the hearts of the sinners. (200) They will not believe in it (the Quran) until they see the painful punishment; (201) But the (Penalty) will come to them suddenly while they will not be anticipating.” (Al-Shuara 26:201)

Is it surprising that several well recognized scientists deny the presence of God? Not really, because arrogance can blind the heart and the mind of any person.

Satan is a good example. His arrogance made him believe that he can make better decisions than God. This sounds similar to those scientists who claim that they can identify better cosmological constants for the universe than God.

Arrogance is a very dangerous disease that can lead man to misguidance and thus the Prophet warned from it by saying:

عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من كبر ( رواه مسلم وأحمد وغيرهما)
“No one will enter Paradise if he has in his heart an atom weight of arrogance”.

Also, Allah assured Hell for those who are arrogant, He said:

سَأَصۡرِفُ عَنۡ ءَايَـٰتِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ ڪُلَّ ءَايَةٍ۬ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِہَا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرُّشۡدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً۬ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡغَىِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّہُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا وَڪَانُواْ عَنۡہَا غَـٰفِلِينَ (الأعراف)
“I shall turn away from My revelations those who show arrogance in the earth with no right to do so and if they were to see every sign, they would not believe in it; and if they see the Path of guidance, they do not take it as their way; and if they see the path of misguidance, they would take it as their way. That is because they have rejected Our signs, and have been disregarding them.” (Al-Araf 7:146)

وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ تَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُم مُّسۡوَدَّةٌ‌ۚ أَلَيۡسَ فِى جَهَنَّمَ مَثۡوًى لِّلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ (٦٠) (الزمر)
“And on the Day of Judgment, you will see those who lied against Allah— their faces are turned black. Is it not that Hell is an abode for the arrogant?” (Al-Zumur 39:60)

Satan rejected God’s commands on the basis that he knows better than God and this resulted in him being condemned for eternity. And instead of Satan apologizing for his transgression and asking for Allah’s forgiveness he continued his transgression by committing to lead many people to reject God and thus leading them to eternal punishment. Allah says:

وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَـٰڪُمۡ ثُمَّ صَوَّرۡنَـٰكُمۡ ثُمَّ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ لَمۡ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّـٰجِدِينَ (١١) قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسۡجُدَ إِذۡ أَمَرۡتُكَ‌ۖ قَالَ أَنَا۟ خَيۡرٌ۬ مِّنۡهُ خَلَقۡتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ۬ وَخَلَقۡتَهُ ۥ مِن طِينٍ (١٢) قَالَ فَٱهۡبِطۡ مِنۡہَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيہَا فَٱخۡرُجۡ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰغِرِينَ (١٣) قَالَ أَنظِرۡنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ (١٤) قَالَ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنظَرِينَ (١٥) قَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغۡوَيۡتَنِى لَأَقۡعُدَنَّ لَهُمۡ صِرَٲطَكَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ (١٦) ثُمَّ لَأَتِيَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيہِمۡ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ وَعَنۡ أَيۡمَـٰنِہِمۡ وَعَن شَمَآٮِٕلِهِمۡ‌ۖ وَلَا تَجِدُ أَڪۡثَرَهُمۡ شَـٰڪِرِينَ (١٧) قَالَ ٱخۡرُجۡ مِنۡہَا مَذۡءُومً۬ا مُّدۡحُورً۬ا‌ۖ لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡہُمۡ لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنڪُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ (الأعراف)
“And surely, We created you and shaped you and then We told the angels, “Prostrate to Adam”, and they prostrated except Iblis (Satan, who was a Jinn), he refused to be of those who prostrated. (Allah) said: “What prevented you (O Iblis) from prostrating when I commanded you?” Iblis said: “I am better than him, You created me from fire, and You created him from clay.” (Allah) said: “(O Iblis) get down from this (Paradise), it is not for you to be arrogant here. Get out, you are among those who are humiliated and disgraced.” (Iblis) said: “Allow me respite till the Day when they (mankind) are raised up. (Allah) said: “You are of those respited.” (Iblis) said: “Because You have allowed me to go astray, I will, surely, sit in wait against them (mankind) on Your Straight Path (16) Then I will come to them from before them and behind them, from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them as thankful ones.” (17) (Allah) said (to Iblis) “Get out from this (Paradise) disgraced and expelled. Whoever of them (mankind) will follow you, then surely, I will fill Hell with you all.” (Al-Araf 7:11-18)

Therefore, there are certain people who can easily fall in the net of Satan by possessing his main character of arrogance, Allah said regarding them:

ٱسۡتَحۡوَذَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ فَأَنسَٮٰهُمۡ ذِكۡرَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ حِزۡبُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ‌ۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ هُمُ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرُونَ (المجادلة)
“The devil (Satan) has prevailed upon them, so caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan, Be assured that Satan’s party are the losers? (Al-Mujadalah 58:19)

Allah gives those people a grave warning that those who deny His existence, He will give up on them and will appoint for them a devil to continue to mislead them. Allah says:

وَمَن يَعۡشُ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ نُقَيِّضۡ لَهُ ۥ شَيۡطَـٰنً۬ا فَهو لَهُ ۥ قَرِينٌ۬ (٣٦) وَإِنَّہُمۡ لَيَصُدُّونَہُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّہُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ (٣٧) (الزخرف)
“And anyone who makes himself blind from remembrance of Al-Rahman (the Majestic Creator and Ruler over the universe), We (Allah) will appoint for him a devil as his intimate companion. (36) And they (the devils) prevent such people from the right path, while they think that they are rightly guided.” (Al-Zughrouf 43:36-73)

I’ll finish with verses from Surat Al-Naml (27) in which Allah raises several rhetorical questions to encourage those who deny His existence or associate others with Him to think. Allah says:

Say: Praise belongs to Allah, and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better or that which they associate with Him?
قُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَـٰمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰٓ‌ۗ ءَآللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ أَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٥٩)

Is not He (best) Who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky wherewith We cause to grow glamourous gardens. It was not within your ability to grow their trees. Is there any God along with Allah? No, but they are people who ascribe equals (to Allah).
أَمَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآٮِٕقَ ذَاتَ بَهۡجَةٍ۬ مَّا ڪَانَ لَكُمۡ أَن تُنۢبِتُواْ شَجَرَهَآ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ۬ يَعۡدِلُونَ (٦٠)

Or, who has made the earth firm to live in; made rivers in its midst; set thereon mountains for making it firm; and made a barrier between the two seas? Is there any God along with Allah? No, but most of them do not have knowledge.
أَمَّن جَعَلَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ قَرَارً۬ا وَجَعَلَ خِلَـٰلَهَآ أَنْہَـٰرً۬ا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَٲسِىَ وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ حَاجِزًا‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ بَلۡ أَڪۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (٦١)

Or, the One who responds to the distressed when he calls on Him and removes the distress, and Who makes you (mankind) vicegerents of the earth? Is there any God along with Allah? No, but little of you heed to advice.
أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلۡمُضۡطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكۡشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجۡعَلُكُمۡ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ قَلِيلاً۬ مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٦٢)

Or, the One who guides you through the depths of darkness on land and sea, and who sends the winds as bearing good news before His mercy? Is there any God along with Allah? No, Allah is far greater than the partners they ascribe to Him.
أَمَّن يَہۡدِيڪُمۡ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَمَن يُرۡسِلُ ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ بُشۡرَۢا بَيۡنَ يَدَىۡ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۤ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ تَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٦٣)

Or the One who originates Creation, then will reproduce it and who gives you provisions from the sky and the earth? Is there any God along with Allah? Say “Bring your proof if you are telling the truth!”
أَمَّن يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ۥ وَمَن يَرۡزُقُڪُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ۬ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ قُلۡ هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَـٰنَڪُمۡ إِن ڪُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (٦٤)

Say: None in the heavens or on the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah. And they do not even know when they shall be raised up (for Judgment).
قُل لَّا يَعۡلَمُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبۡعَثُونَ (٦٥)

Rather their knowledge has failed to comprehend the Hereafter. Rather they are in doubt about it and they are blind to it. (Al-Naml 27:59-66)

content:
Prophet David’s Story of the 99 and the One (Surat Sad)

The stories in the Quran are not intended for entertainment.  Rather, they serve several purposes including: teaching lessons and moral values and also expanding the readers’ cognitive capacity because they require analysis and creativity to connect the key events of the story together. The Quran reveals key events that serve as scenes in the story that require the reader to develop a realistic scenario of the story by connecting the key scenes.  Therefore, each time a serious reader reads the same story, he/she can develop a different scenario and derive new lessons. The only time we would know the exact scenario is when we meet the key righteous participants in the story and those in almost all the stories are Prophets.  This should motivate us to do our utmost to be with them in Paradise.

Verses 17 to 26 Surat Sad (38) describes a story involving Prophet Dawud (David).  These verses present an introduction to a story involving Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), followed by four scenes involving Prophet Dawud and then an ending with a command form Allah to Prophet Dawud.

The story starts with Allah advising Prophet Mohammad to be patient and informing him about Prophet Dawud’s kingdom and superior logic that Allah granted to him. The introduction is given in verses 17-20

ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُ ۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥۤ أَوَّابٌ (١٧) إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُ ۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِىِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ (١٨) وَٱلطَّيۡرَ مَحۡشُورَةً۬‌ۖ كُلٌّ۬ لَّهُ ۥۤ أَوَّابٌ (١٩) وَشَدَدۡنَا مُلۡكَهُ ۥ وَءَاتَيۡنَـٰهُ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَفَصۡلَ ٱلۡخِطَابِ (٢٠)

(O Mohammad) have patience at what they say, and remember Our slave Dawud (David), endued with power. Surely, he was ever turning to Allah. (17) We subjugated the mountains to glorify Our Praises with him at evenings and sunrise. (18) And the birds as well, assembled, all were turning to Allah with him. (19) And We made his kingdom strong and gave him the wisdom and decisive speech. (20)

The first scene describes Prophet Dawud in his sanctuary which was not accessible to the public. Two men broke in the sanctuary scaring him but they gave him the excuse that they wanted him to judge between them in a dispute. This scene is presented in verses 21 and 22.

وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ (٢١) إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنۡہُمۡ‌ۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡ‌ۖ خَصۡمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعۡضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تُشۡطِطۡ وَٱهۡدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ (٢٢)

Has the story of the litigants reached you? When they climbed over the wall of the sanctuary (21) When they entered in upon Dawud, he was scared of them. They said: “Don’t be scared, (we are) two litigants, one has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, and do not cross the limits, and guide us to the Right path. (22)

The second scene is a presentation of the dispute that involved their ewes. One of them owned 99 ewes and the other owned only one ewe. The one who owned the one ewe made the presentation regarding how he one who owned the 99 ewes kept pushing him to give him his one ewe to raise it with his ewes. This scene is presented in verse 23.

إِنَّ هَـٰذَآ أَخِى لَهُ ۥ تِسۡعٌ۬ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةً۬ وَلِىَ نَعۡجَةٌ۬ وَٲحِدَةٌ۬ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيِهَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلۡخِطَابِ (٢٣)

This is my brother, has ninety-nine ewes (female sheep), while I have a single ewe. He said: “Entrust it to me, and he overpowered me in speech.” (23)

The third scene shows Prophet Dawud listening only to the one who has the one ewe and, on that basis, he made a ruling siding with that man. This scene is presented in verse 24

قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦ‌ۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِى بَعۡضُہُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمۡۗ

[Dawud] said: “He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe to be added to his ewes. Indeed, many partners oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous good deeds, and they are few.” (24)

The fourth scene is of Prophet Dawud apparently feeling bad for some reason and thus asked Allah for forgiveness and Allah forgave him. This scene presented in verses 24 and 25.

وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّـٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعً۬ا وَأَنَابَ ۩ (٢٤) فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ‌ۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابٍ (٢٥)

And Dawud realized that We have tested him, so he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down prostrating and turning (to Allah) in repentance. (24) So, We forgave him that, and surely, he had access to Our presence, and a beautiful place of (final) return (Paradise). (25)

The ending of the story involves commands from Allah to Prophet Dawud.  This ending is presented in verse 26.

يَـٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَـٰكَ خَلِيفَةً۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡہَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ (٢٦)

O Dawud! We have indeed made you a vicegerent on earth, so judge between the people with truth and do not follow your desire for it will mislead you from the path of Allah. Surely, those who deviate from the Path of Allah shall have a severe torment, because they had forgotten the Day of Judgment. (Sad 38:26)

Analysis of the Story

In interpreting this story, an important question to ask is whether the ewes (female sheep) are real or metaphors for something else. In this talk I’ll, inshallah, present four scenarios and the lessons drawn from each one and it is up to you, the reader, to decide which one is the more likely. And obviously, you may identify another scenario for the story as you study it further.

The first scenario is unfortunate, and it is copied from the Israelite accounts (الإسرائيليات) in the Old Testament.  This scenario attributed to Prophet Dawud grave sin by assuming that the ewe is a metaphor for woman and that he has 99 wives and decided to acquire a wife that was married to one of his army commanders. This scenario can be rejected because 1) it is totally inconsistent with the account in the Quran, 2) it does offer any moral lesson and 3) it is not befitting for a great prophet of Allah.

The second scenario assumes that the ewes were real animals and the reason that Prophet Dawud asked Allah for forgiveness was due to his mistake of listening to only one claimant and not both before announcing his judgment. Based on this scenario the lesson is that a judge should listen to all claimants before ruling.  It is hard to accept that Prophet Dawud would make such a naive mistake because Allah granted him wisdom and sound speech (وَعَاتَيْنَاهُ الْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ الْخِطَابِ) as in verse 20.

The third scenario also assumes that the ewes were real.  As soon as Prophet Dawud listened to the first claimant who owned only one ewe, he recognized that the conflict occurred because the agreement was not clear to him.  The dispute may have resulted after that one ewe delivered a baby sheep and the question became who owns it. Prophet Dawud felt that the blame should fall on the one who had more business experience by the virtue of owning 99 ewes. Therefore, he said:

وَإِنَّ كَثِيرً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِى بَعۡضُہُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمۡۗ

Many partners oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous good deeds, and they are few.” (Sad 38:24)

The lesson to be drawn here is to always establish a clear agreement among the partners on all possible outcomes before entering into a business.  The lesson also could be that the responsibility of the more experienced partner is to identify all the possible issues that may arise regarding splitting the gains or losses to avoid any future conflict.

While this scenario is possible, it does not explain why prophet Dawud needed to repent and ask Allah for forgiveness.  Here a possible justification for Prophet’s Dawud’s need to repent.

1. Verse 21 presents a scene that implies desperate:

وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ (٢١)

“Has the story of the litigants reached you? When they climbed over the wall of the sanctuary.” (Sad 38:21)

1. We have a situation in which the claimants had an urgent issue. They needed Prophet Dawud, who was their king and their judge, to settle their dispute.  However, they did not have access to him. One can imagine that he instructed his guards to prevent anyone from disturbing him.

2. Therefore, the claimants had no choice but to climb up the walls of the sanctuary to reach him. Probably, the risk they took in forcing their way in, made Prophet Dawud feel that he failed in serving his people when they urgently needed him.

3. His desire to spend a lot of time in the sanctuary in worship made him fail in his responsibility of handling the affairs of his subjects. This incident made him recognize his unfairness to his subjects and thus he fell in prostration, repenting to Allah and seeking His forgiveness. Allah accepted His repentance and reminded him of his prime responsibility as Khalifa on earth.

يَـٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَـٰكَ خَلِيفَةً۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡہَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ

“O Dawud! We have indeed made you a vicegerent on earth, so judge between the people with truth and do not follow your (Hawa) desires for it will mislead you from the path of Allah.” (Sad 38:26)

Allah is emphasizing that the prime responsibility of a ruler/khalifah is to establish justice and peace. Allah is forewarning against getting distracted from this prime responsibility by any desire. Even if the desire is to spend most of his time in worshiping if this results in neglecting his responsibilities towards the people. Those who fail to fulfill their responsibility using the excuse of spending time in worshipping Allah should remember what Prophet Mohammed (PBUH) said:

عن ابن عمر: أن رجلًا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: يا رسول الله، أي الناس أحب إلى الله؟ وأي الأعمال أحب إلى الله؟ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أحب الناس إلى الله أنفعهم للناس، وأحب الأعمال إلى الله سرور تدخله على مسلم، أو تكشف عنه كربة، أو تقضي عنه دينًا، أو تطرد عنه جوعًا، ولأن أمشي مع أخ لي في حاجة أحب إلي من أن أعتكف في هذا المسجد، يعني مسجد المدينة، شهرًا، ومن مشى مع أخيه في حاجة حتى أثبتها له، أثبت الله عز وجل قدمه على الصراط يوم تزل فيه الأقدام» ( المعجم الأوسط للطبراني)

“The most beloved person to Allah is the one who is most beneficial to people. The most beloved deed to Allah is to bring happiness to a Muslim, or to remove one of his difficulties, or to forgive his debt, or to feed his hunger.

If I would walk with a brother regarding a need is more beloved to me than secluding myself in this mosque (in Medina) for a month. Whoever walks with his brother regarding a need until he secures it for him, Allah Almighty will make his footing firm across the bridge on the day when the footings are shaken.” (Al-Tabarani).

This interpretation is quite logical, and the lesson form it is compelling. However, how does it comfort Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and encourages him to be patient since Verse 17 states:

ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِ‌ۖ إِنَّهُۥۤ أَوَّابٌ (١٧)

(O Mohammad) have patience at what they say, and remember Our slave Dawud (David), endued with power. Surely, he was ever turning to Allah. (Sad 38:17)

This suggests that the story of prophet Dawud was intended to offer some comfort to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) regarding the rejection he was facing from the people of Mecca. Allah informs us of this situation in the start of Surat Sad that the people of Mecca were rejecting prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and giving lame excuses for their rejection:

وَعَجِبُوٓاْ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرٌ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ‌ۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرُونَ هَـٰذَا سَـٰحِرٌ۬ كَذَّابٌ (٤) أَجَعَلَ ٱلۡأَلِهَةَ إِلَـٰهً۬ا وَٲحِدًا‌ۖ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَشَىۡءٌ عُجَابٌ (٥) وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِنۡہُمۡ أَنِ ٱمۡشُواْ وَٱصۡبِرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِڪُمۡ‌ۖ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَشَىۡءٌ۬ يُرَادُ (٦) مَا سَمِعۡنَا بِہَـٰذَا فِى ٱلۡمِلَّةِ ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ إِنۡ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّا ٱخۡتِلَـٰقٌ (٧) أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلذِّڪۡرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا‌ۚ

“So, they (the idolators) wonder that a Warner has come to them from among themselves! And the disbelievers say: This is a sorcerer, a sheer liar. (4) “Has he made all the gods into one God? Truly this is a strange thing! (5) And the leaders among them walked out (saying) “Walk away (from the prophet) and remain firm on (adhering to) your gods! For this is truly a plot (against your gods). (6) We never heard of this in the last religion, this is nothing but an invention. (7) What! Has the Message been sent to him (of all people) among us?” (Sad 38:4-8)

After this, Allah told Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) to be patient and to remember the story of Prophet Dawud (David). Therefore, we need to reexamine the story and develop a fourth Scenario to identify what part of the story offered such comfort.  By reexamining the story, you may notice the following:

1. his was the last story in which Prophet Dawud’s name was mentioned in the Quran. This may suggest that it occurred at the end of his reign as a king and prophet.

2. Prophet Dawud was a king and thus his sanctuary would have been in a fortified place that would not be easily accessible. Probably, this is the reason that the verse used the term “Mehrab” (مِحْرَاب) which is derived from the word “Harb” (حرب) “war”, indicating that this place was fortified.

3. Prophet Dawud was a strong and courageous man. In his youth, he killed one of the fiercest fighters, Goliath. So, he would not be easily threatened or get scared. But verse 21 states that he was scared, and those two men comforted him by saying “do not be scared” (فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ). This may suggest that the two who entered were not common subjects, maybe they were angels sent by Allah to teach Prophet Dawud an important lesson.

4. The person who owned the one ewe stated that his brother overpowered him by his reasoning (وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ). This may imply that he was forceful and not offering him choices. Prophet Dawud immediately recognized the problem and thus reached the conclusion quickly.  But what did he understand?

May be the ewes were a metaphor for people who are under the governance of Prophet Dawud. While 99% of the people were Muslims, following the religion of Prophet Dawud, there were still 1% of his subjects refusing to accept his religion. Prophet Dawud was not satisfied with the 99% who followed his religion and thus could not tolerate the rejection by this minority. Therefore, he started using his authority and power of persuasion to convince them, but they were feeling as being forced to accept his religion.

As soon as the issue of the one ewe was mentioned and the commitment of the one who already owned 99 ewes to acquire it, Prophet Dawud recognized the message that was being sent to him. He recognized that his relationship with his subjects is a relation of partnership. Yes, Allah has granted him power, knowledge, and wisdom that he was able to use to convince the majority of his subjects to follow his religion. But accepting the religion of Allah is a matter of free choice by everyone and thus he cannot use the power and wisdom that Allah granted him to force the remaining minority to follow his religion.

As soon Prophet Dawud recognized his mistake of trying to compel people to become believers contrary to the commands of Allah, he fell prostrating, repenting, and seeking Allah’s forgiveness.

From this story Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) realized that he needs to be patient, his role is only to deliver the message and not to be so concerned about those who reject his message. The Prophet (PBUH) also learnt that even though Dawud was a Prophet whom Allah gave him wisdom and convincing speech and he was also a king who ruled over a powerful kingdom, there were still some people under his rule who remained rejecting his message.

So, the story comforted the Prophet (PBUH) by informing his that he is in the early stages of delivering the message and that he still has no governance power. Therefore, He should not be concerned and depressed about those who reject his message. This story supports the commands that Allah gave to him not be saddened by people’s rejection, as Allah pointed out in several verses such as:

لَعَلَّكَ بَـٰخِعٌ۬ نَّفۡسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ (الشُّعَرَاء )

“(O Prophet) It may be that you are tormenting yourself with grief, because they do believe” (Al-Shuara 26:3)

Ignoring the first scenario, I offered three possible scenarios for the story that to different degrees seem possible. I hope that as you study this story further, you may be able to come with others that will enrich the lessons that we can learn from the story.

content:
Allah’s Names Al-Wahed and Al-Ahad _The One and Only One

Allah’s names Al-Wahed and Al-Ahad are the cornerstone of monotheistic religions. These two names of Allah nullify any partners with Him including His Self and His Attributes. He is the Only One without any equal. The combination of the two names when referring to Allah as Al-Wahed Al-Ahad means that:

1. He is singular that has no double
2. He is One who can neither be divided nor duplicated
3. He is unique that nothing can be like Him
4. His names and attributes are limitless, and no one can fully comprehend their majesty and glory except Him.

Allah’s name Al-Ahad came only once in the Quran, in Surat Al-Ikhlas (The Sincerity)

قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (١) ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ (٢) لَمۡ يَلِدۡ وَلَمۡ يُولَدۡ (٣) وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (٤)

“Say: He is Allah the Only One; (1) Allah, the Besought of all, needing none; (2) He neither begot nor was He begotten; (3) And there is none like unto Him”. (Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4)

Allah’s name Al-Wahed (الواحد) (The One) is mentioned in the Quran 6 times, and always associated with Allah’s name Al-Qahar (ٱلۡقَهَّـٰرُ) (The Dominant, The Subduer, The All-Prevailing One, The Irresistible, the One who holds absolute sway over all that exists). As examples:

قُلِ ٱللَّهُ خَـٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَٲحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّـٰرُ (١٦)

“Say, Allah is the Creator of everything, He is the One, the All-Dominant”. (Al-Rad 13;16)

قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۟ مُنذِرٌ۬‌ۖ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٲحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ (٦٥) رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفَّـٰرُ

“Say: “I am only a Warner: there is no god but Allah, the One, the All-Dominant. (65) “The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and what is between them, the Mighty, the All-Forgiving.” (Sad 38:65-65)

لَّوۡ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدً۬ا لَّاصۡطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ‌ۚ سُبۡحَـٰنَهُۥ‌ۖ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٲحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ (٤)

“If Allah had willed to choose a son, He could have chosen anyone He wanted out of what He has created. Glorified is He, He is Allah, the One, the All-Dominant.” (Al-Zumur 39:4)

The associating of the Al-Qahar with Allah’s name Al-Wahed suggests that Allah is giving an ultimatum to all those who do not acknowledge His oneness and associate any other with Him. This is noted in several verses where Allah’s attribute Wahed (One) is used as in the following examples:

يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ لَا تَغۡلُواْ فِى دِينِڪُمۡ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّ‌ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُۥٓ أَلۡقَىٰہَآ إِلَىٰ مَرۡيَمَ وَرُوحٌ۬ مِّنۡهُ‌ۖ فَـَٔامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦ‌ۖ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ ثَلَـٰثَةٌ‌ۚ ٱنتَهُواْ خَيۡرً۬ا لَّڪُمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ وَٲحِدٌ۬‌ۖ سُبۡحَـٰنَهُۥٓ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌ۬‌ۘ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلاً۬ (١٧١)

“O People of the Book do not exaggerate in your religion and do not say about Allah anything but the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, is only a messenger of Allah, and His word that He delivered to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So, believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say “Three” – stop it, that is better for you! – Allah is only One God. He is far pure to have a son. To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs.” (Al-Nisa 4:171)

لَّقَدۡ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَـٰثَةٍ۬‌ۘ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلَّآ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ وَٲحِدٌ۬‌ۚ وَإِن لَّمۡ يَنتَهُواْ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡہُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٧٣)

“Surely, the disbelievers are those who say: “Allah is the third of the three.” But there is no god but One God. If they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment shall certainly befall all disbelievers” (Al-Maeda 5:73)

The concept of believing in the Oneness of Allah is so critical because Allah makes it clear in the Quran that rejecting it is the gravest sin that man can ever commit, and it is the only sin that Allah will never forgive for any person who dies while committing it. Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٲلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ‌ۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا (٤٨)

“Surely, Allah does not forgive that a partner is ascribed to Him, and He forgives anything short of that to whomsoever He wills, whoever ascribes a partner to Allah has indeed invented a tremendous sin.”. (Al-Nisa 4:48)

مَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَمَأۡوَٮٰهُ ٱلنَّارُ‌ۖ وَمَا لِلظَّـٰلِمِينَ مِنۡ أَنصَارٍ۬

“Whoever ascribes ant partner to Allah, Allah has forbidden paradise for him. His abode is the Fire and there is no supporters for the unjust.” (Al-Maeda 5:72)

Believing in the Oneness of Allah is the most liberating because it removes from our heart all fears from anyone and eliminates our undue reliance on anyone. Believing in the Oneness of Allah is a source of peace and security, after all everything is under His control and no one else. Allah says:

وَلِلَّهِ غَيۡبُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ كُلُّهُۥ فَٱعۡبُدۡهُ وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَيۡهِ‌ۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَـٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ [هود:123]

“To Allah belong the secrets of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter (decision, affair) is returned. So, worship Him and put thy trust in Hi. Your Lord is not unaware of what you do.” (Hud 11:123)

The lack of belief in the oneness of God is the source of insecurity, suffering and loss in this life and in the hereafter. Allah says:

فَلَا تَدۡعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُعَذَّبِينَ (الشُّعَرَاء)

“Therefor do not invoke with Allah another god, otherwise you will be among those who are doomed.” (Al-Shuara 26:213)

Elements to Adopt in our Character

1/ Allah created you unique and has gifted you with special talents and capabilities to complement others, do not squander your unique talents. You should strive to develop your uniqueness, to be recognized for your knowledge, morality, spirituality, human brotherhood, generosity, kindness, and honesty.

2/ Examine your belief in Allah regularly to ensure that you do not unintentionally ascribing partners to Him by acting as if your future and your livelihood are in the hands of others and by compromising your faith for the sake of pleasing others. Allah warns the believers to beware of shirk, He said:

وَمَا يُؤۡمِنُ أَڪۡثَرُهُم بِٱللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُم مُّشۡرِكُونَ (١٠٦)

“And most of them do not believe in Allah without associating partners with Him” (Yusuf 106)

The Prophet (PBUH) warned us by saying:

(عن محمود بن لبيد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم الشرك الأصغر. قالوا: وما الشرك الأصغر يا رسول الله؟ قال: الرياء. (رواه أحمد))

“The one I most fear about you is falling in the minor shirk”. The companions asked: What is the minor shirk, He (PBUH) said: “Al-Riyaa” Showing off, insincerity.

3/ Realize that maintaining a state of pure monotheism requires serious study of both the Quran and Allah’s creations until you reach the point of visualizing Allah’s power and authority. You realize the power and authority of people by your physical eye, but You will only be realizing the power and authority of Allah by investing serious efforts to visualize them by the eyes and heart, Allah says regarding the disbelievers:

فَإِنَّہَا لَا تَعۡمَى ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ وَلَـٰكِن تَعۡمَى ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِى فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ (٤٦)

“Verily, it is not the eyes that turn blind, but it is the hearts that are in the chests that turns blind.” (Al-Hajj 22:46)

4/ Since initiating discussion on religion with non-Muslims is not easy, it is important that you should, if asked, be very honest about your belief regarding the oneness of God and the rejection of any form of having partners with Him.

5/ Because the criticality of believing in One God, Muslim scholars have argued that the belief of a Muslim cannot be based on imitation (إن عقيدة المسلم لا تقبل التقليد) because imitating others and blindly following anyone can only lead to misguidance. The belief of Muslims must be based on verification and confirmation (لا تقبل العقيدة إلا تحقيقاً) as Allah said:

فَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لِذَنۢبِكَ

“So, know that there is no God but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin.” (Muhammad 47:19)

The verse implies that if you know that there is no God but Allah and if something annoyed you, know that you must be the cause of it.

Also, Allah considers blind obedience to anyone is an act of worship and thus a form of associating other gods with Allah (i.e. shirk), Allah says:

ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَحۡبَارَهُمۡ وَرُهۡبَـٰنَهُمۡ أَرۡبَابً۬ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَسِيحَ ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَـٰهً۬ا وَٲحِدً۬ا‌ۖ لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ سُبۡحَـٰنَهُۥ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٣١)

“They have taken their rabbis and their monks as gods besides Allah, and (have also taken) the Messiah, son of Mary (as god). And they were not commanded but to worship only One God, there is no god but He. Pure is He from what they associate with Him.” (Al-Tawba 9:31)

When Uday Ibn Hatim (عَدِيّ بْن حَاتِم ) who was a Christian at that time, heard the Prophet (PBUH) reciting this verse, he said: They do not worship them (إنَّهُمْ لَمْ يَعْبُدُوهُمْ). The Prophet (PBUH) replied: (بَلَى إِنَّهُمْ حَرَّمُوا عَلَيْهِمْ الْحَلَال وَأَحَلُّوا لَهُمْ الْحَرَام فَاتَّبَعُوهُمْ فَذَلِكَ عِبَادَتُهُمْ إِيَّاهُمْ) No, they do because they designate for them what is Hallal and what is Haram, and they blindly follow them and this is their worship of them.

Imam Ibn Hazm emphasized that blind imitation (التقليد) without understanding is not acceptable in Islam:

فقيه قوي الحجة كابن حزم حيث قال: (إن التقليد حرام، ولا يحل لأحد أن يأخذ قول أحد غير رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بلا برهان)

“It is prohibited follow the opinion of anyone without a proof except the Prophet (PBUH)”

Allah praises those who think and only follow what they consider best by saying:

(الزمر: 17، 18) (فبشر عباد. الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب)

“Announce the Good News to My Servants who listen to the Word, and follow the best in it: those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the ones endued with understanding” (Al-Zumur 39:17-18)

Allah also, wanted the Muslims to be thinkers and not just followers without thinking because the role of the Prophet is to mainly explain the message and everyone has to think about it, as Allah sys in Surat Al-Nahl:

وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلذِّڪۡرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيۡہِمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

“And We have also sent down the reminder (the Quran) to you (O Muhammad) to explain to the people what is sent down to them, and that they may give it their thought” (Al-Nahl 16:44)

Imam Al-Shafie said:

فقال الشافعي: “مثل الذي يطلب العلم بلا حجة، كمثل حاطب ليل، يحمل حزمة حطب وفيه أفعى، تلدغه وهو لا يدري.”

The example of the one who accepts knowledge without proof is just as one who gathers wood at night and carries the bundle of wood while there is a snake in it and it will bite him without his knowledge.”

6/ You need to strive to read Surat Al-Ikhlas (The Sincerity), the Prophet (PBUH) assessed it to be equivalent to 1/3 of the Quran.

قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (١) ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ (٢) لَمۡ يَلِدۡ وَلَمۡ يُولَدۡ (٣) وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (٤)

“Say: He is Allah the Only One; (1) Allah, the Besought of all, needing none; (2) He neither begot nor was He begotten; (3) And there is none like unto Him”. (Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4)

Ibn Saeed Al-Khudry (أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ) said the Prophet (PBUH) asked: his companions:

(عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: «قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه: أيعجز أحدكم أن يقرأ ثلث القرآن في ليلة، فشق ذلك عليهم وقالوا: أينا يطيق ذلك يا رسول الله؟ فقال: الله الواحد الصمد ثلث القرآن»..) البخاري

“Is any of you unable to read a third of the Qur’an in a single night. This considered that this is difficult for them, so they said: “Who of us can do this, O messenger of Allah.”

The Prophet (PBUH) replied: “Allah is the One, the Besought of all, needing none” is third the Quran. (Bukhari)

A similar hadith is reported by Abu Al-Darda (أبي الدرداء) who said that the Prophet (PBUH) said to his companions:

(حديث أبي الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أيعجز أحدكم أن يقرأ في ليلة ثلث القرآن؟ قالوا: كيف يقرأ ثلث القرآن؟ قال: (قل هو الله أحد) تعدل ثلث القرآن.) مسلم

“Is any of you unable to read a third of the Qur’an in a single night? They said: How can we read the third of the Quran? He (PBUH) said: “Say: He is Allah the Only One” is equivalent to third the Quran. (Muslim)

The content of the Quran can be classified in three categorifies: Jurisprudence (أحكامٌ), News (أخبارٌ) and Monotheism (توحيدٌ). Surat Al-Ikhals (112) summarizes all elements of monotheism. So, whoever reads this Surat with full conviction and sincerity three rimes will receive from Allah the reward of reading the whole Quran.

Anas ibn Malik (أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ) said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قَالَ أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ , أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ , قَالَ:: ” أسست السماوات السبع والأرضون السبع على قل هو الله أحد “

“The seven heavens and the seven earth are founded upon (قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ) – Say, He is Allah, the Only One”.

The hadith implies that as long as there are inhabitants of the heavens and the earths who are declaring the Oneness of Allah, the heavens and Earths are to continue in existence, otherwise they all will be destroyed because this sole reason for the creations of people and the Jinn as Allah says:

وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ (الذّاریَات)

“I did not create the Jinns and the Humans except that they worship Me.” (Al-Dhariat 51:56)

7/ While Surat Al-Ikhlas summarizes the concept of monotheism, you need to keep in your mind the two key elements of the message of the Quran and these are no associating anything with Allah and doing righteous deeds as Allah says:

قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۟ بَشَرٌ۬ مِّثۡلُكُمۡ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمۡ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ وَٲحِدٌ۬‌ۖ فَمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلۡيَعۡمَلۡ عَمَلاً۬ صَـٰلِحً۬ا وَلَا يُشۡرِكۡ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدً۬ا [الكهف:110]

Say (O Mohammad): I am, indeed, just a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is only One God. So, however hopes to meet his Lord must do righteous deeds and must not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord. (Al-Kahf 18:110)

title: Your Character in the Shade of Allah’s Name Al-Wadud
