title: Your Character in the Shade of Allah’s Names Al-Bari’ and Al-Musawwir
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

We are continuing in this talk with the study of the names of Allah as part of our answer to the fourth question in the series of the topic entitled:” Your Life in Light of Eternity”, as a reminder, this topic addresses the following four questions:

1. What is the purpose of our lives on earth?
2. What is the nature of this life on earth?
3. What is our role on earth to fulfil the purpose of our lives on it?
4. What are the traits and qualities that we must possess to fulfill our role and achieve our purpose on earth?

We already addressed the first three questions, and we started the answer to the fourth question which is adopting in our character elements of the Names/Attributes of Allah. We already discussed 12 names and today, we will Insha’Allah discuss Allah’s names Al-Bari and Al-Musawwir.

## 13 Al-Bari’ (البارئ) – The Producer

Allah’s name Al-Bari’ (البـارئ) came in the Quran once in combination with the names Al-Khaliq (الخالق) and Al-Musawwir (المصور) in verse 24 of Surat Al-Hashr. Allah says:

(هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُ‌ ۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ‌ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ )٢٤(

“He is Allah, the Creator, the Producer, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorify Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. (Al-Hashr 59:24)

In the discussion on Allah’s name Al-Khaliq, we highlighted that while the three names Al-Khaliq (الخالق), Al-Bari’ (البارئ) and Al-Musawwir (المصور) refer to Allah’s power of creation, having them together means that there are some differences in their role in the process of creation. We suggested that Al-Khaliq is the planner, Al-Bari is the executor of the plan, and the Al-Musawwir is the attribute associated with the final and delicate finishes. But if any of the names come by itself, it will refer to the One responsible for the whole creation process. Therefore, when Allah says:

{مَا أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّبْرَأَهَا ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ} [الحديد:22].

“No disaster befalls the earth or yourselves, but it is in a Book before we bring it into being – Indeed that is easy for Allah” (Al-Hadid 57:22)

The term (نَّبْرَأَهَا) in this verse is related to Allah’s name Al-Bari’ (البارئ) emphasizing the role of Al-Bari’ (البارئ) as the executer of the plan that already existed. This verse infers that serious events such as hurricanes and earthquakes are not haphazard but occur according to divine plans of the conditions that are necessary to bring them to reality when these conditions are met.

But when Allah says:

{فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ} [البقرة من الآية:54].

“So, turn in repentance to your (Bari’okum) Creator” (Al-Baqara 2:54)

In this verse Allah’s attribute as Al-Bari’ (البارئ) refers Al-Bari’ (البارئ) as responsible for the whole process of creation. Therefore, the role of Allah’s attribute Al-Bari’ (البارئ) in this case includes the roles of Allah’s attributes Al-Khaliq (الخالق), and Al-Musawwir (المصور).

Also, derived from Allah’s name Al-Bari, the word referring to His creations, Allah says:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ‌ۚ أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمۡ شَرُّ ٱلۡبَرِيَّةِ (٦) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمۡ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡبَرِيَّةِ (٧)

“Those who disbelieved from among the People of the Book and the Polytheists, will be in Hellfire, to dwell in it forever. They are the worst of (bari’ah) creations. (6) As for those who believed and did righteous deeds— they are the best of (bari’ah) creatures.” (Al-Bayyina 98:6-7)

Allah’s name Al-Bari’ (البارئ) references other attributes that are derived from the root of the name and have the following classical Arabic connotations:

* to create something of value out of nothing
* to be free from fault or blemish
* to cure and heal from illnesses
* to be free of a claim put forth by others,
* to cut and sharpen something

The root is used in the common Arabic words such as: patent (برأة الاختراع), innocent (برئ), sharpen the pen (برى القلم), and cured from illness (برأ من المرض).

Allah’s name Al-Bara’a (البارئ) implies the following key attributes:

1. Allah, Al-Bari, brings about something out of nothing and this involves creating the basic materials, that are used to create all things without precedent (i.e. no previous model).

Allah informs us that everything was created from water.

أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ ڪَانَتَا رَتۡقً۬ا فَفَتَقۡنَـٰهُمَا‌ۖ وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ حَىٍّ‌ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ [الأنبياء من الآية:30]

“Have The disbelievers not recognized that the heavens and the earth were one united piece, then We parted them? And We created from water every living thing. Would they still not believe.” (Al-Anbiya 21:30)

Therefore, Allah’s attribute Al-Bari creates the basic components of the water that are Hydrogen and Oxygen and use them to create water and then all creations. Note that even Oxygen was created from Hydrogen, which was with Helium, the first atoms that were created by Allah, Al- Bari, based on the plan that was set by Allah, Al-Khaliq.

Also, Allah, Al-Bari, created all the elements that are required to form the dust from which mankind were created, Allah says:

وَمِنۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦۤ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابٍ۬ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرٌ۬ تَنتَشِرُونَ [الروم الآية:20]

“And among His signs that He created you of dust, then soon you are humans being scattered around.” (Al-Rome 30:20)

2. Allah’s attribute, Al-Bari, is responsible for curing or healing of individuals.

Allah quoted to us the declaration made by Prophet Ibrahim who said regarding Allah:

وَإِذَا مَرِضۡتُ فَهُوَ يَشۡفِينِ (٨٠)

“And when I become sick, He heals me.” (Al-Shuara 26:80)

3. Allah, Al Bari is the defender of the believers against the claims and action of the transgressors as He said:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٲفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ۬ كَفُورٍ (٣٨)

“Surely, Allah defends those who believe.  Allah does not love anyone treacherous, ungrateful.” (Al-Hajj 22:38)

4. Allah’s attribute, Al-Bari, is responsible for purifying societies from evil by first giving them warning before imposing punishment.

Allah does not cleanse them by subjecting the transgressors among them to severe punishment except after giving sufficient warning. As example, Allah gave warning to the idolators by saying:

بَرَآءَةٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۤ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ عَـٰهَدتُّم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ [التوبة من الآية:1]

“Freedom from obligation (is proclaimed) from Allah and His messenger towards those of the idolators with whom you made a treaty.” (Al-Tawba 9:1)

مَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّ۬ى‌ۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَمَّآ أُنذِرُواْ مُعۡرِضُونَ (٣)

“We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them but for true purpose and for a specified term but those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of.’ (Al-Ahqaf 46:3)

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the point that Allah always gives warning before punishment by saying:

عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا شخصٌ أحبَّ إليه العذرُ من الله، منْ أجلِ ذلك بعثَ الله المرسلين مبشرين ومنذرين» (صحيح البخاري، وصحيح مسلم).

“No one love accepting excuses other than Allah and this is why He sent Messengers to deliver good news and warnings.”

Allah does not punish immediately but gives many warnings to eliminate the excuse from anyone.

5. Allah, Al-Bari exercises His power to eliminate and remove elements of a society to free the society from evil

When transgressors in a society reach the point that there is no hope in their rehabilitation, Allah cuts them off. History presents us with many examples including the people of Nuh. Allah drowned all the transgressor after Prophet Nuh exhausted all means to guide them.

وَقَالَ نُوحٌ۬ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا (٢٦) إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرۡهُمۡ يُضِلُّواْ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓاْ إِلَّا فَاجِرً۬ا كَفَّارً۬ا (٢٧)

“And Nuh (Noah) said: “My Lord, do not leave on earth a single one of the disbelievers (26) “If You leave them, they will mislead Your slaves, and they will beget none but wicked disbelievers.” (Nuh 71:26-27)

## Elements to Adopt in our Character

Muslims need to adopt the following elements of character from Allah’s name Al-Bari

1/ Since Allah’s Al-Bari’ (البارئ) is the executer of the plan that already exists and brings the plan to reality when the conditions for it are met, this should encourage Muslims to study the conditions that need to exist for disasters to occur and thus be able to predict their happening to protect themselves against their effects

2/ When a plan for any project is established, a Muslim who becomes responsible for executing the plan needs to establish the best procedure and select the optimum materials to implement the plan to its fullest.

3/ A Muslim needs to purify himself from any wrong practices and to dissociate himself from any relationship that can lead to his disobedience or tolerating evils.

4/ A Muslim must always give excuses to others when mistakes are made and give advice before imposing penalties. Imam Gafar Al-Sadiq said:

روى البيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن جعفر الصادق رحمه الله قال: “إذا بلغَكَ عن أخيكَ الشيءُ تُنْكِرُه فالتَمِسْ له عذرًا واحدًا إلى سبعين عذرًا، فإن أصبتَه وإلا قُلْ: لعلَّ له عذرًا لا أعرفُه.”

“If you hear something about your brother that you do not like, find for him excuses up to seventy ones and if you cannot come with any excuse for him say, may be he has an excuse that I just do not know.”

5/ One must realize that he is created from soil and thus he should always be humble and never act arrogantly.

6/ Muslims should always show gratitude towards Allah who is the healer and thus they also need to be a source of comfort and healing to others.

The next name that we will discuss is Al-Musawwir (المصور)

## 14 Al-Musawwir (المصور) – The Fashioner

Allah’s name Al-Musawwir (المصور) came in the Quran once in combination with the names Al-Khaliq (الخالق) and Al-Musawwir (المصور) in verse 24 of Surat Al-Hashr. Allah says:

(هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُ‌ ۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ‌ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ )٢٤(

“He is Allah, the Creator, the Producer, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorify Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. (Al-Hashr 59:24)

In the discussion on Allah’s names Al-Khaliq and Al-Bari, we highlighted that while the three names Al-Khaliq (الخالق), Al-Bari’ (البارئ) and Al-Musawwir (المصور) refer to Allah’s power of creation, having them together means that there are some differences in their role in the process of creation. We suggested that Al-Khaliq is the planner, the Bari is the executor of the plan, and the Al-Musawwir is the attribute responsible for the final and delicate finishes to ensure uniqueness for every creation. Allah says:

وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَـٰڪُمۡ ثُمَّ صَوَّرۡنَـٰكُمۡ ثُمَّ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ [الأعراف من الآية:11]

“We have created you then gave you a shape, then We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam.” (Al-Araf 7:11)

The verse suggests that the creation (Khalq) is a step that precedes the step of making the final shape (Tasweer) which is derived from Allah’s name, Al-Musawwir. In this verse Allah is speaking about the creation (Khalq) and the shaping (Tasweer) of human beings and this may highlight the emphasis on the vast variations of shapes among human being than any other creation. When you look at animals such as lions, you note the similarity among them, but even children from the same father and mother look different to be easily distinguished.

The word Musawwir comes from the root letters ṣa wa ra (ص و ر) and it has the following Arabic connotations:

* to form, fashion, sculpt, imagine, or picture something
* to have an inclination or desire towards something

From this we can conclude that the attributes of Allah as Al-Musawwir include:

* Being responsible for bestowing the form and the shape of all creations.
* Ensuring that everything is in perfect harmony and proportion, without blemish or fault.
* Giving everything its uniqueness and special features.

Allah says regarding His attribute as Al-Musawwir:

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَوِّرُڪُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُ‌ۚ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ (٦)

“He it is the One who shapes you in the wombs as He likes. There is no God but He, the Almighty, the Wise” (Al-Emran 3:6)

ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَڪُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ قَرَارً۬ا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءً۬ وَصَوَّرَڪُمۡ فَأَحۡسَنَ صُوَرَڪُمۡ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ (٦٤)

“Allah is the One who has made for you the earth as a dwelling place, and the sky as a canopy, and shaped you and made your shape beautiful.” (Ghafer 40:64)

خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمۡ فَأَحۡسَنَ صُوَرَكُمۡ‌ۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ (٣)

“He created the heavens and the earth in just proportions, and He shaped you and made your shape beautiful and to Him is the final return.” (Al-Taghabun 64:3)

Allah’s attribute Al-Musawwir ensures the perfection of the creation as He said:

ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَـٰوَٲتٍ۬ طِبَاقً۬ا‌ۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِى خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ مِن تَفَـٰوُتٍ۬‌ۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٍ۬ (٣) ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئً۬ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ۬ (٤)

“He is Who has created the seven heavens one above the other, you can see nothing out of proportion in the creation of the Rahman (the encompassing all the glorious names). Then look again: “Can you see any rifts?” (3) Then look again and yet again, your sight will return to you abased and in a state of weariness.” (Al-Mulk 67:3-4)

## Elements to Adopt in our Character

Some elements from Allah’s name Al-Musawwir to adopt in our character

1/ Ponder on Allah’s creation and express your gratitude by enjoying the beauties of the birds, flowers, trees, fruits, lakes, and mountains that Allah created to please you. Honor and respect all of Allah’s creations and look at the differences as manifestation of Allah’s attribute as Al-Musawwir.

2/ Be assured that Allah created you in the best form, be content with your appearance and trust Allah’s wisdom. Beware that if we were as beautiful as the Prophet Yusuf, we would not be able to withstand the temptations he faced.

3/ When you look at yourself in the mirror, thank Allah for making you the way you are but when you look at the mirror look at the personality and character of the person you see and ask Allah to beautify them as He beautified the look.

4/ Live up to your Potential, after all Allah created you in the best form as He said:

لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ فِىٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٍ۬ (٤)

“Indeed, We have created the human being in the best of forms.” (Al-Teen 95:4)

Allah gave you brain, limbs, skills, and knowledge, now it is up to you on how to use them. Always strive to perfect any task assigned to you and always focus your efforts on only what is important. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ” إن الله يحب إذا عمل أحدكم عملاً أن يتقنه.” (أخرجه أبو يعلى والطبراني)

“Allah loves that whenever anyone does something should perfect it.”

إنَّ اللهَ تعالى يُحِبُّ مَعاليَ الأُمورِ ، و أَشرافَها ، و يَكرَهُ سَفْسافَها ) أخرجه الطبراني عن الحسين بن علي أمير المؤمنين

“Allah loves the serious matters and hates the trivial ones”.

Note:  A question may be raised, how can we claim that everything Allah created is perfect while we see some deficiencies in some creations? This question is improper because Allah says:

{لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ} [الأنبياء:23]،

He is not questioned of what He does, but they are questioned. (Al-Anbiya 21:23)

But we must know that anything that appears to us imperfect has wisdom behind and our lack of understanding the wisdom should not negate the perfection of Allah’s creations. As example, Allah may create a person blind because Allah wants to guarantee such a person paradise if the person accepts Allah’s will: The Prophet (PBUH) said:

«من فقد حبيبتيه فإن الله عز وجل يبدله بهما الجنة يصبر على ذلك» (مسند أحمد بن حنبل)،

“If a person loses his eyes, Allah, All Mighty, will grant him paradise if he is patient about his loss”.

In the next talk, we will, inshallah, discuss Allah’s name Al-Kakeem (The Wise).

(هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُ‌ ۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ‌ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ )٢٤(

“He is Allah, the Creator, the Producer, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorify Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. (Al-Hashr 59:24)

DUA

title: Your Character in the Shade of Allah’s Name Al-Muhaymin
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

We will continue in this talk by studying the names of Allah as part of our answer to the fourth question in the series of the topic entitled: ”Your Life in Light of Eternity”, as a reminder, this topic addresses the following four questions:

1. What is the purpose of our lives on earth?
2. What is the nature of this life on earth?
3. What is our role on earth to fulfil the purpose of our lives on it?
4. What are the traits and qualities that we must possess to fulfill our role and achieve our purpose on earth?

We already addressed the first three questions, and we started the answer to the fourth question which is adopting in our character elements of the Names/Attributes of Allah, and we started with discussing the names, Allah, Al-Rahman, and Al-Rahime. Then we proceeded with discussing the names in the last two verses of Surat Al-Hashr (59) and we discussed the names Al-Malik and Al-Quddus, Al-Salaam and Al-Mu’min and now we will Insha’Allah discuss the name Al-Muhaymin.

## 8 Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) – The Guardian

Allah’s name, Al-Muhaymin, is only mentioned once in the Quran in Surah Al-Hashr (59:23)

هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ

“He is Allah, there is no god but He, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Inspirer of faith, the Guardian, the Eminent, the Compeller, the Proud, glory to Allah above the partners they attribute to Him.” (Al-Hashr 59:23)

The interpreters offered several translations for Allah’s name Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) including: the Guardian, the Guardian over all creations, the Dominator, the Protector, the Watcher over His creatures, the Preserver of Safety, and the One who determines what is true and false. The different translation illustrates the difficulty of selecting one word to represent the different attributes implied by the name. Allah’s name Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) implies three main attributes: perfect knowledge, infinite power and full control, and these attributes are constant and eternal and are manifested by mercy and kindness. These three elements involve:

### 1. Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) has perfect knowledge:

Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) knows all things that exist in the universe whether they are open or secret and whether they are current or future. Allah says in the Quran:

أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَاهُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ

“Don’t they Know that Allah knows their secret (thoughts) and their secret counsels, and that Allah knows well all things unseen.” (Al-Tauba 9:78)

وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِنْ وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْأَرْضِ وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ

“With Him are the keys of the Unseen, the treasures that none knows but He. He knows whatever is in the earth and the sea. Not a leaf does fall but He Knows it.” (Al-Ana'am 6:59)

يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا (١)

“O mankind! Be fully aware of your Lord Who created you from a single soul and from it created its mate and from them spread many men and women; fear Allah, in Whom you demand your (rights) and (honor) your kinship. Surely, Allah is watchful over you.” (Al-Nisa 4:1)

### 1. Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) has infinite power and full control:

Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) has infinite power and full control over everything that exist in the universe. Allah says:

وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

“To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and Allah has power over all things. “(Al-Imran 3:189)

قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٦)

“Say: “O Allah, The Possessor of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will, and You take the kingdom from whom You will, and You bestow honor on whom You will, and You humiliate whom You will. In Your Hand is the good (of everything). Indeed, You are powerful over everything.” (Al-Imran 3: 26)

تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (١)

“Glorious in the One in Whose hands is the kingdom: and He is powerful over everything,” (Al-Muluk 67:1)

Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) means that Allah has the both the perfect knowledge and full control, Allah says:

قُلْ إِنْ تُخْفُوا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٩)

“Say: “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, Allah knows it. He knows what is in the heavens, and what is on earth. And Allah has power over all things.” (Al-Imran 3:29)

### 1. Allah’s knowledge and power and control are constant and eternal and are manifested by Mercy.

The knowledge and power of Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) are not subject to changes because Allah does not operate within the constraints of time and space as we do.

However, unlike people, who get authority over others, Allah’s infinite power and full control are used as manifestation of His mercy, kindness, and love.

The Mercy of Allah is discussed in more details under Allah’s name Al-Rahime. But the following Hadith provides a practical illustration of Allah’s mercy. On one occasion, the Prophet saw a woman holding her child and breast feeding him, so he asked his companions:

عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: (، فإذا امرأةٌ وجدَتْ صبيًّها فأخذَتْه، فألصقَتْه ببَطنِها وأرضعته، فقال لنا النبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: أتَرَون هذه طارحةً ولدَها في النار؟ قُلنا: لا، فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: للهُ أرحمُ بعباده من هذه بولدِها) رواه البخاري

Can you ever imagine that this woman will ever throw her child in the fire?

They said: No.

He (PBUH) said: “Allah is more merciful with his slaves than this woman with her child.” (Bukhari)

Allah is the Muhaymin when He protected Moses from the Pharaoh and his army, when He protected prophet Ibrahim from the fire, when He protected Prophet Younes while he was in the belly of the whale, and protected Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) from the many plots that were made against him.

Out of Mercy as an exercise of His perfect knowledge and total control, Allah Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن) sent to mankind his final guidance, the Quran, to include comprehensive knowledge beyond those in all past revelations such as Torah, Injeel, Zabour, etc., and to serve as controller, verifier and corrector of the information that reached us from past revelations, and thus Allah assigned to the Quran a role that is derivative of His name Al-Muhaymin (المهيمن). Allah says:

وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ

“And We have sent down to you (O Muhammad) the Book (this Qur’an) in truth, confirming those before it and Muhaymin (dominant, watcher, witness, verifier) over them.” (Al-Maeda 5:48)

The Prophet (PBUH) knew that Allah was the Muhaymin when he was promising his companions victory over the two great powers of his time, the Romans, and the Persians, at the time when Muslims were in their direst and most frightful situation during the Battle of the Trench. This is the battle when all the tribes in Arabia gathered to eliminate the Muslims and to complicate the situation the Muslims’ back was exposed by the betrayal of the Jewish tribe, Bani Quriza. At that time, the hypocrites who never knew Allah, the Muhaymin, said: How can Muhammad promise us victory over Kaiser and Cesar when none of us feels safe to go to satisfy his call of nature. But the Muhaymin was in full control and defeated all the confederates without the Prophet and His companions engaging them in a battle. The Muhaymin possesses all sources of power, and no one knows them except He, as He said:

وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا

“To Allah belongs the Forces of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is Exalted in Power, Full of Wisdom.” (Al-Fat’h 48:4 and 7)

وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ

“No One knows the forces of your Lord, except Him. “ (Al-Moudather 74:31)

## Elements to Adopt in our Character

Knowing that Allah is the Muhaymin, we must incorporate in our character at least the following traits:

1. Having full confident that Allah is the only One who has the power to protect and support us against all enemies
2. Having full confident that every statement made in the Quran is true and every promise Allah made to us, the believers, will be fulfilled.
3. Having complete reliance on the Muhaymin who controls everything and thus having full trust in the bright future and your ultimate success as long as you are in His obedience.
4. Paying no attention to anyone other than Allah, the Muhaymin, and having no fear from anyone but Him.
5. Seek knowledge to purify our heart from all diseases that reduces our love for Allah, the Muhaymin, our mind from falsehood and our senses from His disobedience.
6. Being fully aware that Allah the Muhaymin knows everything we think of, and what we do, therefore we should have a feeling of shame when we think about disobeying Him and we should hasten to repentance if we fall in the sin of His disobedience.

In the next talk, we will Insha’Allah discuss Allah’s name Al-Aziz.

هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ

(DUA)

### EXTRA (THE Quran is Muhaymin over all previous revelations)

When Allah sends new Messenger while a previously sent messenger is still alive, this previous messenger must follow the new Messenger and this command must have been made clear in the revelation received by the previous messenger. This was a covenant that Allah took from all those whom He designated as prophets to mankind before they were even assigned. This point is clear in verse 81 of Surat Al-Imran:

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنْصُرُنَّهُ قَالَ أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ إِصْرِي قَالُوا أَقْرَرْنَا قَالَ فَاشْهَدُوا وَأَنَا مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ (٨١) فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ (٨٢)

“And (recall) when Allah took the Covenant of the Prophets, saying: “If I give you a book and wisdom then comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you; you must believe in him and support him.” Allah said: “Do you affirm and accept My Covenant in this respect?” They said: “We affirm.” He said: “Then bear witness; and I am with you among the witnesses.” (81) Then whoever turns back after this, they are the rebellious.” (Al-Imran 3:81-82)

Regarding Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), these verses state in a very clear language, that Allah took the covenant from all prophets, from Adam to Jesus (peace by upon them all) that when He sends a messenger conforming what they have received, they should believe in him and support him and anyone who does not fulfill this covenant is rebellious and sinful. Allah also tells us that they all agreed to this covenant and Allah confirmed that as their witness.

If all the Prophets agreed to follow Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), anyone who does not follow him after hearing about him, is declared by Allah as rebellious. But for this to be just, previous revelations must have clear description of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) to leave no ambiguity that he is the one designated by Allah as the seal of the Prophets.

Allah affirms in the Quran that the nature of the mission and the attributes of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) are clearly identified in both the Torah and the gospel (in the new and Old Testament) and this should remove any doubt about the legitimacy of His prophethood. Allah says:

الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبَائِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (١٥٧)

“Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Injeel (Gospel), he commands them with goodness and forbids them from indecency; he makes lawful for them all that is good, and prohibits them all that is foul, he relieves them from their heavy burdens and from the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor him, help him, and follow the light that has been sent down with him, it is they who are successful”. (Al-Araf 7:157)

Note that this command is addressed to the Jews and Christians, and it clearly states that the attributes of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is revealed to them in their books. So, when they reject him, they are actually rejecting part of their own religion and anyone who does this is condemned to Hell.

title: Your Character in the Shade of Allah’s Name Al-Mu’min
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

We will continue in this talk by studying the names of Allah as part of our answer to the fourth question in the series of the topic entitled: ” Your Life in Light of Eternity”, as a reminder, this topic addresses the following four questions:

1. What is the purpose of our lives on earth?
2. What is the nature of this life on earth?
3. What is our role on earth to fulfil the purpose of our lives on it?
4. What are the traits and qualities that we must possess to fulfill our role and achieve our purpose on earth?

We already addressed the first three questions, and we started the answer to the fourth question which is adopting in our character elements of the Names/Attributes of Allah, and we started with discussing the names, Allah, Al-Rahman, and Al-Rahime.  Then we proceeded with discussing the names in the last two verses of Surat Al-Hashr (59) and we discussed the names Al-Malik and Al-Quddus and Al-Salaam and today, we will Insha’Allah discuss the name Al-Mu’min.

## 7 Al-Mu’min (المؤمن) –  The Inspirer of Faith

Allah’s name “Al-Mu’min” was revealed once in the Quran in Surah Al-Hashr (59:23)

هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ

“He is Allah, there is no god but He, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Inspirer of faith, the Guardian, the Eminent, the Compeller, the Proud, glory to Allah above the partners they attribute to Him.” (Al-Hashr 59:23)

The interpreters offered several translations of Allah’s name Al-Mu’min (الْمُؤْمِنُ) including: the Inspirer of faith, the Infuser of faith, the Giver of faith, the Guardian of faith, the Keeper of faith, and the supreme Believer.

The challenge in translating this name is that the attribute Mu’min (مُؤْمِنُ) is used referring to a good Muslim as “believer”.  Thus, the simple translation of Allah’s name Al-Mu’min (الْمُؤْمِنُ) should be “The Believer”.  But if Allah is described as the Believer, the question is: believe in what?

Because this name came only once in the Quran, we don’t have other verses to give us additional meaning of the name.  Therefore, we can seek the Arabic Lexicon to give us the root of the name of its meanings.  The name Al-Mumin (الْمُؤْمِنُ) is derived from the root [أ م ن] “Amena” which means: to trust, to believe, to bring security.  Examples of the use of words used in the Quran and derived from the root include:

وَمَا أَنْتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَادِقِينَ
“And you will not believe us even if we are truthful”. (Yusuf 12:17)

الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ
“He is the one who fed them after being hungry and gave them security after being fearful.”( Quraish 106:4)

وَمِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ مَنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِقِنطَارٍ۬ يُؤَدِّهِۦۤ إِلَيۡكَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِدِينَارٍ۬ لَّا يُؤَدِّهِۦۤ إِلَيۡكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ قَآٮِٕمً۬ا‌ۗ
“Among the People of the Book are some who, if entrusted with a ton of gold, will (readily) pay it back; others, who if entrusted with a single silver coin, will not repay it unless you keep demanding it.” (Al-Emran 3:75)

وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ۬ مُّؤۡمِنٌ۬ مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَكۡتُمُ إِيمَـٰنَهُۥۤ أَتَقۡتُلُونَ رَجُلاً أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
“And said a believer, a man from among the people of Pharaoh, who had concealed his belief, “Will you kill a man because he says `My Lord is Allah’?’ (Ghafer 40:28)

So, when the name Al-Mu’min (الْمُؤْمِنُ)is used to represent the attribute of Allah, it implies the following meanings:

Allah fully believes in Himself, in His authority and His power and accepts all His glorious names and attributes.
In surah Al-Imran, Allah testifies that He is the only God:

شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ
“Allah testifies that there is no God but He.” (3:18)

To make this matter clear, we know that a person gets in deep trouble if he does not know himself and his limits.  If a person believes he can do something which he cannot really do, he will fail and bring harm to himself.  This is not applicable to Allah.  Allah knows His unlimited power and His unlimited ability, and He believes in them and what He says about them is the absolute truth.  Allah says:

وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَلِيمًا قَدِيرًا
“There is nothing in the heavens or on earth that is difficult for Allah.” (Fatir 35:44)

وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرًا
“Allah is always able to do everything. “(Al-Fath 48:21)

Allah believes in His messengers and their message that He revealed to them.
Allah expresses His belief in the truthfulness of the message of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by saying:

لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ أَنْزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا
“Allah bears witness that what He has sent down to you (Muhammad), He has sent with His (Own full) Knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And Allah is sufficient as a Witness. (Al-Nisa 4:166)

When Allah makes it clear that He believes in the truth of the revelations given to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), it means that Allah’s promise to those who believe in this message is true and Allah will fulfill it.

وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا
“Allah’s promise is the truth and whose word can be truer than Allah’s. (Al-Nisa 4:122)

وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ
“The promise is from Allah and Allah never fails to fulfill His promise” (Al-Rome 30:6)

Thus, Allah’s name Al-Mu’min means that Allah’s actions will be consistent with every statement and every promise He made.

Allah is the provider of security and safety to the world.
Allah, Al-Mu’min, means that security and safety emanates from Him and to Him security and safety are attributed.  Al-Mu’min is the one who provides security and safety and removes fear.

If you examine Allah’s creations, you cannot help but be overwhelmed by how Allah ensured our safety and security.  If the earth did not have the exact gravitational force, we have, we would have not been able to walk on it.  If the ozone layer was not at its height or its thickness, the sun’s rays would have burned us.

Allah made the rotational speed of all stars and galaxies are so accurate to maintain positions that ensure safety and security of the whole universe.

When we examine our own bodies, we note that Allah designed all the systems to ensure our safety and security.  For example, the immune system detects any intruding virus or bacteria and destroys them before they can harm us.

But a fair question would be, if Allah is the Mu’min from whom security and safety emanates, why do we see so much suffering and lack of safety and security in the world.  The answer is that Allah created the world and established its laws to ensure safety and security, but when people violate these laws, they bring suffering upon themselves.

Examples of the Manifestation of Allah’s Name Al-Mu’min in the Character of the Prophet (PBUH):

When we study history of the Prophet (PBUH) we realize that he manifested this name. Al-Mu’min, in his character.  He believed in Allah and in his message, and he was the source of security and safety for all around him, including non-Muslims who lived in the Islamic state.  He made it clear that those non-Muslims are entitled to security and safety.

عَنْ عَبْدِاللَّهِ بْنِ عمر رضي الله عنهما، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: مَنْ قَتَلَ مُعَاهَدًا لَمْ يَرِحْ رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ، وَإِنَّ رِيحَهَا تُوجَدُ مِنْ مَسِيرَةِ أَرْبَعِينَ عَامًا. [ رواه البخاري]
“Whoever kill a Mu‘āhad (non-Muslim citizen and any person protected by a treaty) will never smell the fragrance of Paradise, although its fragrance can be detected from a distance of forty years.” [Sahih Bukhari]

عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: ألا من ظلم معاهدًا أو انتقصه أو كلفه فوق طاقته أو أخذ منه شيئا بغير طيب نفس منه فأنا حجيجه يوم القيامة. [ سنن أبي داود]
“Indeed, whoever wrongs a Mu‘āhad (non-Muslim citizen and any person protected by a treaty) or violates his rights or burdens him with more than he can bear or takes anything from him without his consent, I shall be his adversary on the Day of Judgment.” [Sunan Abu-Dawud]

حديث صحيح عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: “. من عادى ذميًا فقد عاداني
“Whoever harms a dhimmī (a non-Muslim citizen), he harms me.”

In addition, the Prophet (PBUH) was fully aware of his superior role and status among the people which was assigned to him by Allah, and he believed in it.

Regarding believing in special position, Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said,

عن أَبُي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : ” أَنَا سَيِّدُ وَلَدِ آدَمَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ، وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ يَنْشَقُّ عَنْهُ الْقَبْرُ ، وَأَوَّلُ شَافِعٍ ، وَأَوَّلُ مُشَفَّعٍ “. [صحيح مسلم]
“I am the master of the children of Adam on the he Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to emerge from the grave, and I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession will be accepted.” [Sahih Muslim]

Abu Abu Sa’id reported a similar hadith in which the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أَبِي سَعِيدٍ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَا سَيِّدُ وَلَدِ آدَمَ وَلَا فَخْرَ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ مَنْ تَنْشَقُّ عَنْهُ الْأَرْضُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا فَخْرَ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ شَافِعٍ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ مُشَفَّعٍ وَلَا فَخْرَ وَلِوَاءُ الْحَمْدِ بِيَدِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا فَخْرَ. [ سنن ابن ماجه]
“I am the master of the children of Adam, and it is no boast. I will be the first for whom the earth will split open on the Day of Resurrection, and it is no boast. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession will be accepted, and it is no boast. And the Banner of Praise will be in my hand on the Day of Resurrection, and it is no boast.” [Sunan Ibn-Majah]

While the Prophet realized his superior status and believed in it, this did not cause him to lose his humility or act as a king.  He maintained his character as the son of a humble woman.

Once, a man came to the Prophet (PBUH) shaking with fear. Upon seeing him the Prophet (PBUH) smiled and said to him:

عن قيس بن أبي حازم : أن رجلاً أتي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقام بين يديه فأخذته رعدة فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (هون عليك فإني لست بملك إنما أنا ابن امرأة من قريش كانت تأكل القديد)
“Be at ease. I am not a king, but I am the son of a woman from Quraish who used to eat dried meat.” [Ibn-Majah]

Both Abu Dhar and Abu Hurairah said:

عن أبي ذرٍّ وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما قالا: “كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس بين ظهري أصحابه فيجيء الغريب فلا يدري أيُّهم هو حتى يسأل”.
“The Prophet would sit with his companions in any vacant spot, So, when a stranger come would not distinguish him from them until he asks who is the Prophet.”

The Prophet (PBUH) prohibited his companions from standing up when he enters their gathering and said:

(من أحب أن يتمثل له الرجال قياماً فليتبوأ مقعده من النار) رواه أحمد والترمذي و أبو داوود.
“Let him who likes people to stand up before him prepare his place in Hell.” [Abu-Dawud]

## Elements to Adopt in our Character

When the name Mu’min (مُؤْمِنُ) is applied to us, it does not only mean the belief in Allah, the prophets, the revelations, the Day of Judgment and destiny.  It has other meanings that should be adopted in our character:

To be a Mu’min, you should believe in yourself that you have been placed by Allah on this earth to fulfill a role and achieve a purpose.  You should be confident in your ability to fulfill your role and achieve your purpose because Allah would have not given you the role and the purpose without giving you the ability to fulfill them.  You must know your strengths and your weaknesses.
To be a Mu’min, you must serve as source of security and safety to all who are around you.  A Mu’min is someone who people feel safe around them. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أَبي هريرة : أَن النَّبيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: واللَّهِ لا يُؤْمِنُ، واللَّهِ لا يُؤْمِنُ، واللَّهِ لا يُؤْمِنُ.
“By Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe.”

So, the people asked:  O’ Messenger of Allah, who is that? He said: “He is the one whose neighbor is not safe from his evils.”

This is why you will find that Allah, in the Quran, always says those who believe do righteous deeds.  Righteous deeds are those that bring benefit and ensure safety and security of the people and the society.

In the next talk, we will Insha’Allah discuss Allah’s name Al-Muhaymin.

هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
“He is Allah, there is no god but He, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Inspirer of faith, the Guardian, the Eminent, the Compeller, the Proud, glory to Allah above the partners they attribute to Him.” (Al-Hashr 59:23)

(DUA)

title: Your Character in the Shade of Allah’s Name Al-Salaam -The Peace
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

We are continuing with the study on the names of Allah as part of our answer to the fourth question in the series of the topic entitled: ” Your Life in Light of Eternity”. As a reminder this topic addresses the following four questions:

1. What is the purpose of our lives on earth?
2. What is the nature of this life on earth?
3. What is our role on earth to fulfil the purpose of our lives on it?
4. What are the traits and qualities that we must possess to fulfill our role and achieve our purpose on earth?

We already addressed the first three questions, and we started the answer to the fourth question which is adopting in our character elements of the Names/Attributes of Allah. We discussed the names, Allah, Al-Rahman, Al-Rahime, Al-Malik and Al-Quddus and today we will, inshallah, discuss the name Al-Salaam.

Allah’s name As-Salaam (السلام) “The Peace” is mentioned once in the Quran and this is in verse 23 in Surat Al-Hashr:

(هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ) الحشر

“He is Allah, there is no god but He, the King, the Holy, the Peace, The Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Eminent, the Compeller, the Proud, glory to Allah above the partners they attribute to Him.” (Al-Hashr 59:23)

Abu-Hurairah (أبي هريرة) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
إن اسم السلام من أسماء الله تعالى فأفشوه بينكم (الطبراني)
“The name Al-Salaam (The Peace) is among the names of Allah, the Most-High, so spread it among yourselves”. (Al-Tabarani)

It is reported that both Thouban (ثوبان) and Aisha (عَائِشَةَ) said that the Prophet (PBUH) used to say after ending his prayers:
اللَّهم أنْتَ السَّلامُ، ومِنكَ السَّلامُ، تَبَاركتَ يا ذَا الجلالِ والإكرَام(صحيح مسلم)
“O Allah, you are The Peace and from you is peace. Blessed are you, the Majestic and Generous.” (Muslim)

The name Al-Salaam is derived from the root s-l-m (سلم) which has the following classical Arabic connotations:
1. A source of peace, peaceful, quiet, tranquil, content, secure, healthy and prosperous
2. Free from imperfections, free from faults, complete, pure, whole, and sound

Allah’s name Al-Salaam involves three elements:
1. Allah’s character and attributes are perfect and pure from any impurity.
2. Allah is the source of peace, safety, and security for all creations.
3. Allah’s actions are free from any evil and harm.

Allah’s name Al-Salaam (The Peace) implies that He is the source of all safety, security and peace in the world. To appreciate that Allah is the source of all the safety and security that we enjoy, let us examine few things that Allah has provided to ensure our safety.

1. When you examine your own body, you realize that the locations and mechanisms that Allah selected for the different body parts are intended to make us safe. For example:
- Your blood filtration organ, the kidney, is designed with redundancy; we can survive normal life with only kidney.
- The location of the vessels that carry your blood from and to the heart is selected with our safety in mind. The arteries that carry the blood from the heart to the rest of the organs under high pressure are located deep under the skin while the veins that carry the blood to the heart under low pressure are near the skin allowing to take blood samples. If arteries were to be located near the skin, any cut to the skin could have caused cut to them resulting in great loss of blood because of the high pressure and this can lead to death.
- Even as we grow, Allah accommodates the changes in your functions. As an example, the nose of an infant is stiff so it would not bend and close when the infant is being breast fed; otherwise, the child will suffocate.
2. When you study water which is the source of life for all living beings on Earth. You find that Allah designed it with special properties to secure it forever. When it reaches the freezing point, unlike other matters, it expands. That is why ice is lighter than water and thus floats and acts as thermal insulation to protect the water under it from subfreezing air temperatures. If it did not, all oceans would be frozen.

The use of the word Al-Salaam and its derivates are very common in the Islamic vocabulary.
1/ It is used in the common greeting among Muslims which is “As-Salaamu Alaykum” (السلام عليكم) “Peace be unto you”. In fact, this greeting is not only for Muslims, but it is rather a greeting from all humanity since it is the greeting that Allah taught Prophet Adam to say. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن أبي هريرة -رضي الله عنه- عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: «لما خلق الله آدم -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: اذهب فسلّم على أولئك -نفر من الملائكة جلوس- فاستمع ما يحيّونك؛ فإنها تحيتك وتحية ذريتك. فقال: السلام عليكم، فقالوا: السلام عليك ورحمة الله، فزادوه: ورحمة الله». [متفق عليه.]
After Allah created Adam, He told him to and greet this group of angels who are there and listen to how they will greet you because it is your greeting and the greeting of your descendants. Adam went and said “Asalaam Alukum” (Peace be unto you”. They answered, “Alyk Asalaam Wa Rahmat Allah” (Peace and Mercy of Allah be unto you), they added Mercy of Allah. (Bukhari and Muslim)

2/ it is used by the righteous people when responding to evil people, Allah says:
وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنً۬ا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلَـٰمً۬ا (الفرقان)
“The righteous slaves of Allah are those who walk on the earth in humility, and when the ignorant or the belligerent address them, they respond by saying: Peace.” (Al-Fourqan 25:63)

3/ It used as a name for paradise, “Dar Al-Salaam” (دَارِ السَّلَامِ) “abode of peace” because it is a place that is safe, tranquil, secure, prosperous, perfect, and free from any flaw. Allah says:
وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو إِلَى دَارِ السَّلَامِ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ
“Allah invites to the abode of peace and guides whomsoever he wants to the straight Path.” (Yunus 10:25)

4/ Real peace will only be achieved when people enter paradise where they will enter in peace and live in peace because all the causes of conflicts and pain will be eliminated. Allah says:
إِنَّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَعُيُونٍ (٤٥) ٱدۡخُلُوهَا بِسَلَـٰمٍ ءَامِنِينَ (٤٦) وَنَزَعۡنَا مَا فِى صُدُورِهِم مِّنۡ غِلٍّ إِخۡوَٰنًا عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ۬ مُّتَقَـٰبِلِينَ (٤٧) لَا يَمَسُّهُمۡ فِيهَا نَصَبٌ۬ وَما هُم مِّنۡہَا بِمُخۡرَجِينَ (٤٨)
“The righteous will be in gardens that have springs. (45) (They will be told): “Enter here in Peace and Security.” (46) And We shall remove any grudge from their hearts: (they will be) brothers (joyfully) sitting on couches, facing each other. (47) No fatigue shall touch them, nor will they be asked to leave from there.” (Al-Hijr 15:45-48)

Those who will enter paradise will be in total peace because all they can imagine of pleasures and luxury will be there at their fingertips. In a Hadeath Qudsi, the Prophet (PBUH) reported that Allah said about Paradise:
أعْدَدْتُ لعباديَ الصالحين ما لا عين رأتْ ولا أذن سمعتْ، ولا خطَر على قلبِ بَشَرْ (البخاري ومسلم والترمذي)
‘I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, and no ear has heard, nor has it occurred to the human heart.” (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

5/ The greeting in paradise is Salaam (peace), Allah says:
وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّہِمۡ‌ۖ تَحِيَّتُہُمۡ فِيهَا سَلَـٰمٌ (٢٣)
“And those who believed and did good deeds shall be admitted to Gardens underneath which rivers flow, living there forever by the will of their Lord. There their greeting is Peace.” (Ibrahim 14:23)

6/ The Quran is the book that guides to the path of peace (سبل السلام), Allah says:
قَدۡ جَآءَڪُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ نُورٌ۬ وَڪِتَـٰبٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (١٥) يَهۡدِى بِهِ ٱللَّهُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضۡوَٰنَهُ ۥ سُبُلَ ٱلسَّلَـٰمِ
“There has come to you from Allah, a light and clear book (15) With it Allah guides who seeks His pleasure to the path of Peace.” (Al-Maeda 5:15-16)

7/ The salutation received by the successful people who will, on the day of judgment, receive their book of deeds in their right hand will be Salaam (Peace) is for you: Allah says:
وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ فَسَلَامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ
“And if he is from among the people of the right, (90) (it will be said to them) “Peace to you,” as you are one of the people of the Right. ” (Al-Waqia 56: 90-91)

8/ The whole message of Islam can be summarized around Allah’s name Al-Salaam (The Peace) in one sentence: “Allah is the Peace (Al-Salaam) and He revealed the Quran to guide mankind to the path of peace (سبل السلام) to ensure that they live in peace (في سلم) and this leads them to the final destination which is the abode of peace (دار السلام) where they will enter it in peace (بسلّم) and they will greet each other with peace (سلام) greetings..

9/ The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized that to enter paradise in peace, we must spread peace, he (PBUH) said:
عن عبدِاللَّهِ بنِ سَلاَمٍ ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قالَ: أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَفْشوا السَّلامَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا باللَّيْل وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ بِسَلامٍ رواه أحمد والترمذي والحاكم
“O people, spread peace, offer the food and pray at night while people are sleeping, you will enter paradise in peace. (Ahmad, Tirmidhi)

The Prophet (PBUH) also said:
عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (لا تدخلون الجنة حتى تؤمنوا، ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا، أولا أدلكم على شيء إذا فعلتموه تحاببتم: أفشوا السلام بينكم) رواه مسلم
“You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love each other. Shall I tell you something which if you did, you would love each other? Spread peace among yourselves” (Muslim)

Throughout his life, the prophet (PBUH) demonstrated his keen desire for peace, and this is best demonstrated by two examples.

The first is Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (صَلَح ٱلْحُدَيْبِيَّة): This is the unfair treaty that the Prophet (PBUH) signed with his archenemy, the people of Mecca, to ensure peace and stop all conflicts. The terms of this agreement were as follows:

“In the name of almighty Allah. These are the conditions of Peace between Muhammad, son of Abdullah, and Suhayl ibn Amr, the envoy of Mecca. The conditions of this agreement are as follows:
1. There will be no fighting for ten years.
2. Anyone who wishes to join Muhammad and to enter into any agreement with him is free to do so and should abide by this agreement. Anyone who wishes to join the Quraish and to enter into any agreement with them is free to do so and should abide by this agreement.
3. If a young man, or one whose father is alive, converts to Islam and joins Muhammad without permission from his father or guardian, will be returned to his father or guardian. But if Muslin reverts from Islam and goes to the Quraish, he will not be returned.

Most of the Prophet’s companions were distressed by the 3rd term of the agreement, but still the Prophet (PBUH) signed it, just to secure the 10 years of peace.

The second was related the outcome of the violation of the agreement by the people of Mecca. The People of Mecca violated this agreement when they supported a tribe that joined the agreement as their ally in their attack of one of the tribes that joined the agreement as allies of the Prophet. The Prophet wrote to the people of Mecca and offered them the option to resolve the violation by 1) Paying blood money for the victims of the victimized tribe that was an ally of the Prophet, and 2) The people of Mecca terminate their alliance with the tribe that violated the agreement.

The Prophet (PBUH) informed them that the treaty is considered nullified if they reject these two conditions. When the people of Mecca refused the conditions, the Prophet (PBUH) went to Mecca with an army and gained victory over them. When the people of Mecca from whom the Prophet (PBUH) suffered for over 20 years and were responsible of nullifying the peace treaty asked him what he is going to do with them. He said:
(‏فإني أقول لكم كما قال يوسف لإخوته‏:‏ ‏{‏لاَ تَثْرَيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ‏}‏ اذهبوا فأنتم الطلقاء‏)‏‏.‏
“I only tell you what Yusuf (Joseph) told his brothers: “No reproach you”, you are all free.”

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized to Muslims that the believer is the one from whom people around him are totally safe and secure. It is reported in Bukhari (البخاري) that the Prophet (PBUH) said: “By Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe.” (والله لا يؤمن، والله لا يؤمن، والله لا يؤمن)
The people asked: O’ Messenger of Allah, who is that? (مَن يا رسول الله ؟)
He said:
(الذي لا يأمَن جارُه بَوائِقَهُ) He is the one whose neighbor is not safe from his evils.”

Since Allah’s name of Al-Salaam implies that all His actions are free from evil and are intended to ensure peace, safety, and security for mankind, how can we reconcile seeing evil, wars and suffering in this world that is under Allah’s control and authority?

If you examine the world, we can say with certainty that there is no absolute evil which is evil of no purpose other than evil itself. But this does not mean that Allah will never allow evil to occur, because He will allow relative evil to occur so that it will result in something good. As example, Allah allowed knives to exist. Using a knife to cut the flesh of an innocent person is perceived to be evil, but if the person doing the cutting is a surgeon to remove an inflamed appendix, it will have a good outcome. This point is clearly demonstrated in surah Al-Kahf in the encounter between Prophet Moses and Al Khidr, the man whom Allah has provided with secret knowledge of the future. Prophet Moses interpreted Al Khidr’s actions, e.g., drilling a hole in the ship, as evil but when he was told the reason was to force its owners to return to shore to avoid the attacks by the pirates, he understood that the apparent evil act led to good consequence.

Allah may inflict a person with pain and suffering to force him to change the path from one leading him to Hell to a path that leads to the abode of peace, Paradise. No loving father would leave his son or daughter uncorrected if he sees them doing something wrong! Obviously, from the child’s viewpoint, the father’s actions are unjust and even abusive. Only when the child grows, he will realize that his father’s actions were the best for his success, and they were all motivated by love.

We must realize that the absolute evil has no place in the actions of Allah, and that all the evil may exist are consequences of people actions. Allah confirms this point in the following verses:
ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
“Mischief has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned; so (Allah) may give them a taste of some of their deeds, in order that they may turn back (from Evil).” (Al-Rom 30:41)

وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ
“Whatever misfortune happens to you, it is because of the things your hands have brought, and for many (of them) He grants forgiveness.” (Al-Shura 42:30)

Even when Allah allows wars to happen, they are done as a demonstration of His name Al-Salaam, The Peace, if only people follow His commands. Allah forbids all wars for unjust gain and oppression, but He does not ignore the reality that this life is a test and thus evil men who wish to do evil will exist and thus it would be self-defeating for believers to tolerate oppression and injustice. Fighting was sanctioned by Allah for three reasons: 1) self-defense, 2) repulsion of aggression and 3) protecting freedom of belief. The following verses from the holy Quran present the conditions under which fighting is permissible:
أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَقُولُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَاتٌ وَمَسَاجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا وَلَيَنْصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ
“Permission to fight is given to those against whom fighting is launched, because they have been wronged, and Allah is powerful to give them victory. Those who have been driven from their home unjustly just because they said: Our Lord is Allah, and Allah is indeed able to give them victory. If it were not because Allah repels some men by means of others, cloisters, churches, synagogues and mosques, where Allah’s name is frequently mentioned, would have been demolished. Allah supports those who support Him – Allah is Strong, Powerful. We (God) will give victory to those who, if we give them power in the land, would establish worship and pay the welfare tax and enjoin kindness and forbid iniquity” (Al-Hajj 22:39-41)

The same point that emphasizes that Muslims are only allowed to engage in war if provoked is given in the following verse:
وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ
“Fight in the cause of Allah those who fight you, but do not initiate hostilities; Allah does not love aggressors.” (Al-Baqara 2:190).

Maybe the most revealing command about the restrictions imposed on Muslims during a war is illustrated by the following verse in Surah Al-Anfal which commands Muslims to go against their self-interest by stopping the fight even when they are victorious as soon as the enemy asks to negotiate peace. This is even though Muslims may be suspicious that the enemy is only asking for negotiation as a tactical move to deceive the Muslim army and deprive it from securing the victory: Allah says:
وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا أَنْ يَخْدَعُوكَ فَإِنَّ حَسْبَكَ اللَّهُ هُوَ الَّذِي أَيَّدَكَ بِنَصْرِهِ وَبِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ
“And if they incline to peace, then incline to it also, and rely on Allah, He is Alert, Aware. Should they intend to deceive you, let Allah serve as your protector.” (Al-Anfal 8:61-62).

Elements to Adopt in our Character
In order for Muslims to possess part of Allah’s name, As-Salaam, they need to strive to fulfill four elements:

1. Muslims must always feel confident that each time they mention Allah; they are safe and secure. Allah says:
أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
“Without a doubt, by the mention of Allah’s name, the hearts feel secure” (Al-Raad 13:28)

2. Muslims should strive to have a flawless heart that is free from all forms of evil such as deceit, hatred, envy, jealousy, etc. The purity of the heart is a prerequisite for success in the Hereafter, Allah says:
يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
“At that day neither wealth nor progeny shall be of benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a pure heart.” (Al-Shuara 26:88-89)

3. Achieve internal peace by ensuring that all your actions are free from any violation of Allah’s rules. Muslims should strive to ensure that their limbs that Allah put under their control are pleased and at peace by only using them on what is pleasing to Allah. Muslims know that if they distress their limbs by engaging them in sins, they will testify against their own person on the first opportunity they are allowed to speak. Allah says:
وَيَوۡمَ يُحۡشَرُ أَعۡدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ (١٩) حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَـٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٠) وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَا‌ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ۬ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ (٢١) وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡهَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَـٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَـٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرً۬ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٢) وَذَٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمۡ أَرْدَاكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٢٣)
“Remind them of the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered unto the Fire, they will be driven on. (19) Until when they will come to it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against about what they used to do. (20) They will say to their skins: “Why did you testify against us?” They will say: “Allah made us speak— (He) Who made everything speak: He created you for the first time, and to Him were you to return. (21) “You did not seek to hide yourselves from your hearing, your sight, and your skins that they would bear witness against you! But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you used to do! (22) But this thought of yours which you conceived about your Lord brought you to ruin and (now) you become among the losers.” (Fussilat 41:19-21)

4. Muslims should always be the source of peace and security for everyone. People must feel safe from our tongue and our hand. The Prophet (PBUH) defined the Muslim and the believer by saying:
[ عن أبو هريرة ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قالَ المسلم من سلم الناس من لسانه ويده، والمؤمن من أمنه الناس على دمائهم وأموالهم. ] الترمذي والنسائي وأحمد
“The Muslim is the one people are safe from his tongue and his hand and the believer is the one people feel secure from him about their lives and their money”.

Any Muslim who believes in Allah, Al-Salaam, he/she would live in peace and be a source of peace and security for all people.

We pray to Allah to help us to live in total peace and to be a source of peace to all.
