Another key aspect of Allah’s mercy is that He rewards ten folds the value of each good deed but only accounts one time for the impact of each evil deed. Allah said:

مَن جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وَمَن جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَى إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ ) الأنعام (
“Whoever comes (to the day of Judgment) with a good deed shall have ten times the like of it in reward and whoever comes with bad deed he will only be requited with no more than the like of it and they shall not be wronged”. (Al-An’am 6: 160)

But it even goes beyond this generous reward system, when we do a bad deed and follow it with a good deed, the bad deed will be erased as Allah says:

وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ ذَلِكَ ذِكْرَى لِلذَّاكِرِينَ) هود (
“And establish prayers at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night.  Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds. That is a reminder or those who remember.” (Hud 11:114)

But it even goes more than that, actually our bad deed can be replaced with good deeds. In Surah Al-Fourqan, Allah says following his description of “وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ” The righteous slaves of Al-Rahman”:

فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَـٰتٍ۬‌ۗ
Allah will substitute their evil deeds with good deeds.” (Al-Furqan 25:70)

So, Allah tells us that when one does a good deed, it will be accounted as 10. In addition, it will either erase his bad deed or will cause the bad deed to be substituted with a good deed.

But we must be careful of two actions that can erase the rewards of good deeds. These two actions are the (منّ) which is boasting about the good deed or harming the person to whom you have done the good deed. Allah says:

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقَاتِكُمْ بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذَى)  البقرة(
“O you who believe, do not nullify your charity with boastful reminders and harm (Al-Baqara 2:264)

Another important element of Allah’s mercy that goes beyond the ten-time rewards is that He rewards for the intention. If one is intending to commit a bad deed but did not do it, Allah rewards him for not doing it. And if one is intending to do a good deed but was not able to do it, Allah will reward him for his intention as if he did it. In a divine (Qudsi) hadith, the prophet (PBUH) narrated on behalf of Allah who said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : قال الله عز وجل : ( إذا تحدث عبدي بأن يعمل حسنة فأنا أكتبها له حسنة ما لم يعمل ، فإذا عملها فأنا أكتبها بعشر أمثالها ، وإذا تحدث بأن يعمل سيئة فأنا أغفرها له ما لم يعملها ، فإذا عملها فأنا أكتبها له بمثلها ، وقال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – قالت الملائكة : رب ذاك عبدك يريد أن يعمل سيئة وهو أبصر به ، فقال : ارقبوه ، فإن عملها فاكتبوها له بمثلها ، وإن تركها فاكتبوها له حسنة ، فإنما تركها من جراي ) [رواه الشيخان ، وهذه رواية مسلم]

If My slave intended to do a good deed but he does not do it, I will record it for him as one good, but if he does it, I will record it or him as ten good deeds. And if he intended to do an evil deed, but he does not commit it, I will forgive that. But if he commits it, I will record it against him as one evil.

The angels said: Our Lord, your slave was intending to commit the evil, but obviously Allah is more aware than them. Allah said: Watch him; if he commits it (evil), write it against him by its equivalent but if he refrains from doing it for My sake, write it for him as one good deed. [Bukhari and Muslim]

This hadith represents a great gift from Allah if we take advantage of it with pure intention. You may say, if Allah grants me this money, I’ll give half of it as charity. Even if you do not get the money Allah will grant you the reward for spending the money, though in reality you did not. The same thing for any good deed whether it is fasting, memorizing the Quran, helping people, etc. The important issue is the sincere intention to do these good deeds.

The same principle has been reported in the record of past prophets. The following has been reported in records from the time of Prophet Musa (Moses) (PBUH)

قد جاء في الأثر أنه قد أصاب بني إسرائيل زمن موسى عليه السلام فاقة ومجاعة، وأنَّ راعياً بسيطاً نظرَ إلى الجبال حيث يرعى غنم النَّاس، وقال: اللهم إنَّك تعلَمُ أنه لو كان لي مثل هذه الجبال ذهباً لتصدَّقتُ بها على عبادك! فأوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى عليه السلام أن يا موسى قُلْ لعبدي أني قبلتُ منه صدقته

“During the time of Prophet Musa (Moses), the children of Bani Israel suffered poverty and famine. A simple shepherd looked at the mountains where he was grazing the sheep of the people, and said: O Allah, You know that if I had such mountains of gold, I would have given it all as charity to help Your slaves. Allah revealed to Musa (PBUH) to tell this slave (the Shepard) that Allah accepted his charity.”

Mercy is the hallmark of Islam; Allah described the mission of the Prophet (PBUH) by saying:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ إِلَّا رَحۡمَةً۬ لِّلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٠٧)
“We have not sent you, but as a mercy for all creatures.” (Al-Anbia  (21:107)

And the Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the importance of mercy in many of his sayings, as example, He (PBUH) said:

حديث أبي هريرة  قال رسول الله ﷺ يا أيُّها النَّاسُ إنَّما أنا رحمةٌ مُهداةٌ]   البخاري[
“O People, I am but a guided Mercy” (Bukhari)

حديث أبي هريرة  قال رسول الله ﷺ من لا يَرحم لا يُرحم [أخرجه البخاري، ومسلم.]
“Who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy (by Allah).”

But more that sayings, the Prophet (PBUH) demonstrated by actions throughout his life that he (PBUH) is a walking mercy. A clear example is what the Prophet (PBUH) said after the battle of Uhud when the army from Quraysh came to attack him and his followers in Madina, During the battle several of his companions were killed including his uncle and major supporter Hamza and he was severely injured including breaking his lower Jaw. The companions asked him to supplicate to Allah against the people of Quraysh. Instead, he (PBUH) said: (اللَّهمَّ اغفر لقومي فإنَّهم لا يعلمونَ) “O Allah forgive my people, they just do not know”. Also, when he (PBUH) gained major victory against the people of Quraysh, instead of taking revenge from them for all the harm and the suffering they caused him and Him companions for 20 years, instead he (PBUH) forgave all of them.

There are many examples of the applications of Allah’s name Al-Rahime (The Most Merciful). If we are to incorporate Allah’s name Al-Rahime in our character, our share of this name needs to at least include the following three elements:

1. Anchoring our action with mercy even when someone do injustice to us.
2. Showing mercy to the negligent and disobedient by demonstrating commitment to help them eliminate their negligence towards Allah to secure His mercy.
3. Never turning away from any needy person and committing to meet his/her needs to the extent of our ability. Even if we cannot offer the needed help, we should show sympathy and love and assist them by our prayers to Allah to satisfy their needs.

We pray to Allah to help us incorporate Mercy in all our actions and thoughts.

Next time, we will inshallah cover other names of Allah staring with the names given at the end of Surah Al-Hashr (59) in verses 23 and 24. These two verses provide a list of 11 names.

DUA

title: Your Life in Light of Eternity – Worship’s Trust, Quality Metric and Barriers
excerpt:
Your Life in Light of Eternity – Worship’s Trust, Quality Metric and Barriers

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك…
content:
Your Life in Light of Eternity – Worship’s Trust, Quality Metric and Barriers

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

This is the 6th talk on the topic entitled:” Your Life in Light of Eternity”, as a reminder, this topic addresses the following four questions:

1. What is the purpose of our lives on earth? And answer was to prepare us for eternity when we return to Allah who will assess whether we are worthy of being in His company in Paradise forever or He will send us to another place as punishment for our failure
2. What is the nature of this life on earth? And the answer was that our life on earth is a temporary assignment, it is a test, and it is a trust.
3. What is our role on earth to fulfil the purpose of our lives on it? And the answer was to worship Allah and we defined worship as total obedience to Allah’s commands motivated by our love and gratitude to Him and by our trust in Him that all His commands are intended for our benefits.
4. What are the traits and qualities that we must possess to fulfill our role and achieve our purpose on earth?

In the last talk, we discussed the worship’s elements of love and gratitude, and Inshallah, today, I plan to discuss the element of trust and then move to discuss quality metrics for worship and barriers to proper worship.

1. Trust in Allah

Complete trust in Allah means that you should have faith that He knows what is best for you.  You should have no doubt that He will help you when you face problems, and He will never impose on you something that you cannot bear. Therefore, we demonstrate our trust in Allah by how we react to misfortunes. Allah taught every Muslim what to say when they face misfortunes:

قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا هُوَ مَوْلَانَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ

“Say, nothing will ever happen to us except what Allah has prescribed for us.  He is our protector and on Allah alone the believers should put their trust” (Al-Tawba 9:51).

(Note:  The Quranic expression “Katab Allah Lana” meaning “what Allah prescribed for us”, and not “Katab Allah Alaina” meaning “what Allah prescribed against us”.)

We must have full trust that whatever Allah prescribes for us must be for our own good, no matter how much it may appear to us at the time as a misfortune or a tragedy, Allah says:

فَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا

“It may be that you dislike something in which Allah has placed a great deal of good” (Al-Nisaa 4:19).

Also, we have to trust that Allah knows what is better for us more than our own selves, Allah says:

وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَعَسَى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

“It is possible that you dislike something which is good for you; while you love something, which is bad for you. Allah knows, and you do not know.” (Al-Baqara 2:216).

Having trust in Allah that any setback and hardship must be good for us, makes us face them not with anger and frustration, but with patience and the positive anticipation of Allah’s rewards.  Allah says:

وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ وَالْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَنْفُسِ وَالثَّمَرَاتِ وَبَشِّرِ الصَّابِرِينَ (155) الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (156)

“We will surely test you with some fear and hunger, and some loss in wealth, lives and the fruits of your toil. But give good news to those who are patient. (155) Those who, when a misfortune befalls them, say: ‘To Allah we belong and to Him we shall return’. (156)” (Al-Baqara 2:155-156).

The Prophet (PBUH) directed Muslims to face any misfortune by saying:

ثبت عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال: ما من عبد يصاب بمصيبة فيقول: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون، اللهم آجرني في مصيبتي، وأخلف لي خيرا منها، إلا آجره الله في مصيبته، وأخلف له خيرا منها.

“Verily, we belong to Allah and verily, unto Him shall we return. O Allah! Reward me for the calamity that has befallen me and grant me something better than it in exchange for it.”

A test that Allah has instituted to evaluate our trust in Him is the money. For many people money is their security, and thus they fear losing it.

Allah made money as a key test for every Muslim by making it the third pillar of Islam (zakat).  How you manage your worldly wealth and your level of charity demonstrate the level of your trust in Allah. Allah says:

وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلَا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ

“Spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he would say: ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short while so that I could give charity and be among the righteous’.” (Al-Munafiqun 63:10).

When an opportunity arises to spend your money in charity and you withhold, it will be to your loss and not Allah’s, as He says:

هَا أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يَبْخَلُ وَمَنْ يَبْخَلْ فَإِنَّمَا يَبْخَلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ

“Here you are being invited to spend in the way of Allah, among you are some who are miser. But anyone who is miser is only miser to his own self.  Allah is the Rich (Self-Sufficient) and you are the poor.” (Mohammad 47:38).

Allah has warned us about Satan’s trickery of using the fear of poverty to make us fail in demonstrating our trust in Allah.  Allah says:

الشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْفَحْشَاءِ وَاللَّهُ يَعِدُكُمْ مَغْفِرَةً مِنْهُ وَفَضْلًا وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ

“Satan threatens you with poverty and bids you to commit indecency.  But Allah promises you His forgiveness and bounty.  Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.” (Al-Baqara 2:268).

Because Allah knows that Satan will use poverty to convince us to be miser, Allah emphasized His promise of the great rewards for those who spend.  Allah says:

وَسَارِعُوا إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (133) الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ

“Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and for a garden that expands the heavens and the earth prepared for the righteous. (133) Those who spend (in the way of Allah) in time of prosperity and in time of adversity.” (Al-Imran 3:133-134).

The money we will be spending is an investment with huge return as Allah said:

مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ

“The parable of those who spend their money in the way of Allah is that of a grain that produces seven ears and in every ear there are a hundred grains.  Allah gives manifold increase to whoever He wills.  Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.” (Al-Baqara 2:261).

If you withhold because all you have can barely satisfy my needs, Allah addressed your concern by saying:

وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا (2) وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ

“Whoever has Taqwa of Allah, He will grant him a way-out and will provide for him from sources that he could never imagine. And whoever puts his trust in Allah, He will be enough for him.” (Al-Talaq 65:2-3).

You will surely be provided with wealth from completely unexpected sources, if you just trust Allah and give from the little you have. The Prophet (PBUH) confirmed this when he said:

عن أبي كبشة عمرو بن سعد الأنمارى رضي الله عنه أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ثلاثة أقسم عليهن، وأحدثكم حديثاً فاحفظوه: ما نقص مال عبد من صدقة، ولا ظلم عبد مظلمة فصبر عليها إلا زاده الله عزاً، ولا فتح عبد باب مسألة إلا فتح الله عليه باب فقر".

“Three things, I swear by Allah for them, and I am going to tell you about them, so you should remember them: (1) Charity does not decrease wealth, (2) No one suffers an injustice and is patient with it, except that Allah will increase him in honor, and (3) No one opens a door of begging except that Allah opens for him a door of poverty.”

The Quality Metrics for Proper Worship

Proper worship must fulfill two requirements: sincerity and accuracy and thus proper worship requires a pure heart and correct knowledge.

1/ Sincerity:

Worship must be sincere and genuine, it is not just a matter of saying the right words, but you must mean them from the bottom of your heart.

The Prophet (PBUH) pointed to the heart and said: (التقوى ها هنا) “righteousness is here, righteous is here.”

Allah also teaches us that without a pure and sound heart, all we do are in vain as He said regarding the Day of Judgment:

يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ (88) إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ (89)

“At that day neither wealth nor progeny shall be of benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.” (Al-Shu'ara 26:88-89).

2/ Accuracy:

Your Worship must be as Allah commanded, not as you wish.  We cannot just create our own comfortable way of worship; we must follow the way that Allah has prescribed.

Islam sets high priority on seeking knowledge before actions and deeds.  In his Book of Knowledge (Kitab al-Ilm), Imam al-Bukhari wrote a chapter entitled: “Knowledge comes before words and deeds”.

Allah says:

يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ

“Allah raises in ranks those of you who believe and have knowledge. And Allah is Well-Acquainted with all that you do.” (Al-Mujadila 58:11).

The prophet (PBUH) said,

وَإِنَّ فَضْلَ الْعَالِمِ عَلَى الْعَابِدِ كَفَضْلِ الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ عَلَى سَائِرِ الْكَوَاكِبِ

“An ‘Alim (learned person) is as much superior to an ‘Abid (Worshiper) as the full moon is superior to all the stars.”

The companions and those who came behind them understood the value of knowledge.  The Prophet’s companion, Muadh bin Jabal, said:

عن معاذ بن جبل أنه قال :” تَعَلَّمُوا الْعِلْمَ ، فَإِنَّ تَعَلُّمَهُ لِلَّهِ خَشْيَةٌ ، وَطَلَبَهُ عِبَادَةٌ ، وَمُذَاكَرَتَهُ تَسْبِيحٌ ، وَالْبَحْثَ عَنْهُ جِهَادٌ ، وَتَعْلِيمَهُ لِمَنْ لا يَعْلَمُهُ صَدَقَةٌ ، وَبَذْلَهُ لأَهْلِهِ قُرْبَةٌ “.

“Seek the knowledge, in learning it, there is awareness of Allah and seeking it is worship and searching for it is Jihad and teaching it to those who do not know is charity and giving it to those who are worthy of it is a means of drawing closer to Allah.”

Imam Al-Hassan Al-Basri warned of getting too deep into the area of actions before having knowledge. He said:

قال الحسن البصري رحمه الله تعالى: (العامل على غير علم كالسالك على غير طريق، والعامل على غير علم يفسد أكثر مما يصلح، فاطلبوا العلم طلبا لا يضر بالعبادة، واطلبوا العبادة طلبا لا يضر بالعلم).

“The one who does anything without knowledge is like the one who is not on any road, he causes more harm than good. So, seek knowledge in a way that does not harm your worship, and seek worship in a way that does not harm your knowledge.”

Unfortunately, past, and current history has shown that there are those who do not lack righteousness and sincerity, but they lack knowledge and thus they were led to commit heinous crimes in the name of Islam. Regarding those, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: سيخرج في آخر الزمان قوم أحداث الأسنان، أحلاء الأحلام، يقولون من خير قول البرية، يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم، يمرقون من الدين كما يمرق السهم من الرمية.

“In the end of time there will come a people young in years, foolish in minds, quote the sayings of the best of people, they recite the Quran but it does not go beyond their throats. They go out of the religion as an arrow goes through its target.”

Barriers to Proper Worship

There are four main barriers for proper worship of Allah. These are arrogance, fear, lack of commitment and confusion/ignorance.

1/ Arrogance:

Arrogance is the most dangerous barrier to worship; it is the barrier that prevented Satan from obeying Allah’s command. Allah says:

وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبَى وَاسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ

“And when We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they prostrated, all but Iblis (Satan), he refused and was arrogant and was one of the disbelievers.” (Al-Baqara 2:34).

Arrogance is the most dangerous disease of the heart, and its impact is dire in the Hereafter, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من كبر.

“No one will enter Paradise if he has in his heart an atom weight of arrogance.”

Arrogance comes when the person desires to be like God, but no one is like God and will never be. Only through humility, will you be able to open your heart to worship Allah.

2/ Fear: While fear of the unknown is a natural human emotion, fear that makes the person disobeys the commands of Allah is a barrier for worship.

Some people may fear poverty and ignore that Allah says:

وَفِي السَّمَاءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ (22) فَوَرَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِثْلَ مَا أَنَّكُمْ تَنْطِقُونَ (23)

“And in Heaven is your fortunes and whatever you have been promised. (22) By the Lord of the heavens and the earth, it is certainly true, as true as your ability to speak. (23)” (Al-Dhariyat 51:22-23).

We also fear the future of our children, but this fear may drive some people to violate Allah’s commands to secure the children’s future. To them Allah says:

وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا

“Let those who fear to leave behind helpless children to have Taqwa of Allah and only say what is right.” (Al-Nisaa 4:9).

Allah revealed in the Quran two examples on how He protected the children of righteous people who passed away (the boy in Surat al-Kahf and the two orphans in the same Surat).

This concept of ensuring the security of children through righteousness was well understood by early Muslims. It was said to Mohammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi: “Why don’t you save some of your money for your children after you die?” He replied:

وروي أن محمد بن كعب القرظي أصاب مالاً كثيراً فقيل له‏:‏ لو ادخرته لولدك من بعدك قال‏:‏ لا ولكني أدخره لنفسي عند ربي وأدخر ربي لولدي.

“No, I save this money for myself with my Lord, and I save my Lord for my Children.”

Only through trusting Allah, will you be able to overcome fear of the future and experience peace, which is the key to proper worship.

3/ Lack of Commitment: Most Muslims want to perfect their worship of Allah but is everyone willing to do whatever it takes? Lack of commitment and procrastination are major barriers. Allah says:

أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ

“Has the time not yet come for those who believe that their hearts should be humbled by the remembrance of Allah and by the Truth which has been revealed?” (Al-Hadid 57:16).

The Prophet (PBUH) warned us of procrastination and advised us by saying:

وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلي الله علية وسلم لرجل وهو يعظه : " اغتنم خمساً قبل خمس : شبابك قبل هرمك ، وصحتك قبل سقمك ، وغناك قبل فقرك ، وفراغك قبل شغلك ، وحياتك قبل موتك ".

“Make use of five before five: your youth before old age, your health before sickness, your wealth before poverty, your free time before becoming busy, and your life before death.”

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : سمعت رسول الله صلي الله علية وسلم يقول : " لا يزال قلب الكبير شاباً في اثنتين : في حب الدنيا ، وطول الأمل ".

“The heart of the old person is always young in two things: the love of this life and the hope for a long life.”

Ibn Omar used to say:

كان ابن عمر يقول : " إذا أمسيت فلا تنتظر الصباح وإذا أصبحت فلا تنتظر المساء ، وخذ من صحتك لمرضك ، ومن حياتك لموتك ".

“If the night comes don’t wait for the morning and if the morning comes do not wait for night, take from your health for your sickness and from your life for your death.”

4/ Confusion/Ignorance:

Proper worship requires knowledge and people often fail because of their confusion that is manifested in following things without knowledge.  Allah says:

وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا

“Do not follow anything about which you have no knowledge. Surely, the hearing, the sight, and the heart, all of those will be questioned.” (Al-Israa 17:36).

Since everyone will be held accountable for his actions, one must have knowledge to be able to defend his actions on the Day of Judgment. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من سلك طريقاً يطلب فيه علماً سهل الله له طريقاً إلى الجنة ).

“Whoever seeks a path to acquire knowledge, Allah will make an easy path for him to paradise.”

There may other barriers to worship, but they will most likely be subsets of these 4 barriers.

I’ll stop here and inshallah next time, we can start addressing the 4th question which is: What are the traits and qualities that we must possess to fulfill our role and achieve our purpose on earth?

DUA
