content:
Your Life in Light of Eternity

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

This talk and may be the next few ones will, inshallah, discuss talks that I gave few years back, but I want to repeat as means of review and update. The theme of the talks is: “Your Life in Light of Eternity”

We and the rest of Muslims have been reading the Quran, studying the life of the Prophet, listening to lectures, and witnessing the coming and the passing of many of the blessed months of Ramadan. We fast, give charity, and perform many voluntary prayers, but it seems that our undesirable condition remains at a standstill and thus everyone must ask himself/herself the following questions:

1. How do all these activities impact my life?
2. Does the approach I chose to live my life change or remain the same?
3. Is my life driven by guilt, regrets, resentment, anger, fear, unrealistic expectations, materialism or need for approval, or is my life driven by something else that is nobler and greater?
4. Do I know the eternal truths based on which I should build my life?
5. Do I have clarity regarding the purpose of my life?
6. Do I use Allah for the fulfillment of my purpose, or do I use my life for the fulfillment of Allah’s purpose?
7. Even if I have noble goals for my life and know the true purpose of my life, do I have the proper traits and attributes to live my life?

The proper answer to all these questions can only be found in Allah’s revealed words, as documented in the Quran and the authentic statements of the Prophet (PBUH). In order to see the real change in our lives, we need to be serious and sincere about learning and living our religion and not just going through the motion of performing its rituals.

The one reason that the Quran and the Sunnah do not transform many Muslims is that most people are not willing to take the time to seriously consider and apply what they read or listen to. We often focus on the quantity rather than the Quality of what we do. We want to finish reading the Quran in a month or less, we want the Imam to finish the prayer in two minutes or less, and we want the speaker to finish his talk in ten minutes or less. Obviously, this was not the attitude of the early Muslims whose lives were fully transformed by hearing far less than what we have heard or read about Islam.

Equipped with the same teachings that we have, the most backward tribes of Arabia were transformed to be the world leaders in knowledge, morality, spirituality, human brotherhood, and equality. Khalifa Omar said that we did not move from one verse in the Quran to another unless we understood what it meant for us and how we could apply it. In order to get value from the Quran, you don’t just read it, but you must learn the message to apply it.

Equipped with the same information that we have, early Muslims succeeded in few years in establishing the greatest civilization history has ever known. Let us start by affirming that our responsibility as Muslims has been assigned to us by Allah Who said in His Holy Book:

كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ

“You are the best nation that has been raised for mankind. You enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong and you believe in Allah” (Al-Imran 3-110).

وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا

“And thus, we have made you a moderate nation, so that you will be witnesses over the people and the prophet will be a witness over you.” (Al-Baqara 2:143).

The responsibility of Muslims is to take the Prophet (PBUH) as their role model and to set the example for others. This responsibility is emphasized by the Prophet’s saying: “Be the best, be the most virtuous among all people.”

Every Muslim has been honored by the responsibility to be the best among all people, so he/she can be worthy of setting the right example for them. This responsibility sets the ultimate test and the absolute criterion to evaluate the Muslim’s actions. You are the only one who can answer this question: Am I worthy of being a role model for others?

If you are going to call yourself a true Muslim and meet the responsibility that Allah has assigned to you, you must be a leader, not a follower; you must be a teacher, not a student; you must be strong, not weak; you must be a winner, not a loser; you must be a giver, not a receiver; you must be knowledgeable, not ignorant; you must be kind, not cruel; you must be generous, not greedy; you must be the best, not an average; and you must be successful, not a failure. However, Muslims cannot achieve their God given role on this earth unless they have clarity regarding the purpose of this life, its nature, and its requirements as well as the qualities that they must develop to serve as role models. The main objective of these talks is to present a modest attempt to answer four fundamental questions that are pre-requisites for Muslims’ ability to advance and fulfill their obligations. These questions are:

1. What is the purpose of our lives on earth?
2. What is the nature of this life?
3. What is required to fulfill this purpose?
4. What are the traits and qualities that we must possess in order to fulfill these requirements?

As an analogy to these questions, you can ask a student who is in college:

1. What is your purpose for going to college? The answer will likely be to prepare myself for the job market.
2. What is the nature of life in college? The answer may be testing of my competency in the subjects on my specialty.
3. What do you need to do to fulfill this purpose? The answer may include actions such as attending classes and studying.
4. What are the traits and qualities that you must possess to be successful student? The answer may be intelligence, diligence, promptness, honesty, etc.

The Purpose of Life

Having a clarity regarding the purpose of our life is extremely important because knowing the purpose of our life gives it meaning, simplicity, focus and motivation. Understanding the meaning of our life allows us to cope with its difficulties, gives us the foundation on which we can make decisions, allows us to concentrate our efforts and energy on what is important, and makes us avoid being distracted by minor issues. Without knowing the purpose of our life, life becomes trivial, confusing, and pointless.

It is unfortunate that most Muslims have no clarity regarding their purpose in life and unfortunately, they impose the same lack of clarity on their children at a young age because they begin at the wrong starting point by asking them self-centered questions like:

What do you want to be?
What should you do with your life?
What are your goals and your dreams?

Focusing on ourselves will never reveal the purpose of our life. If we want to know why we were placed on this planet, we must begin with the Creator, Allah.

We must know that we are not an accident, our parents may not have planned us, but Allah did. Long before we were conceived in our mothers’ womb, we were conceived by Allah. Allah created us many thousands of years ago. Allah tells us about our first creation during the time of Adam, as He said in Surah Al-Araf:

وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ

“We created you and shaped you, then We said to the angels: prostrate before Adam” (Al-Araf 7:11)

Also, in Surah Al-Araf, Allah presents to us another scene for our original birth as He said:

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ

“(Recall) when your Lord brought the descendants of the children of Adam (meaning you and I) from their loins and made them bear witness about themselves (by asking them) Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, indeed, we bear witness.” (Al-Araf 7:172)

In Surah Al-Kahf, Allah describes a similar scene to that of the first creation when we will stand in front of Him again in the Day of Judgment as He says:

وَعُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا

“And they will be presented lined-up before your Lord, (with the announcement), “Now you have come back to Us as We created you the first time; yet you thought We would not make any appointed time for you.” (Al-Kahf 18:48)

How were we brought to a life from lions to stand in front of Allah and testify that He is our Lord is not the subject here, but what we need to know is that at that time Allah had already prescribed every single detail about every one of us. He deliberately chose your race, the color of your skin and every other feature of your body. Allah chose your parents with the right genetic makeup to custom make you. He also determined the natural talents you would possess and the uniqueness of your personality. He even created the world with great precision to be uniquely suited for your existence, to make your life possible.

Allah has a reason for everything and because of that reason, He decided the exact time and place of your birth and your death, and He planned how long and where you would live on earth. Nothing in your life is arbitrary, it is all for a purpose. Allah did not create you because He was lonely, but he wanted to make you because He has a purpose for you. Allah made you for a reason; Allah says in Surah Al-Mu’minun:

أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ عَبَثًا وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا تُرْجَعُونَ

“Do you think We created you for nothing, and that you would not be returned to us.” (Al-Mu’minun 23:115)

So, when we ask what is the purpose of our life on earth? The answer will be to prepare ourselves for the eternal life when we return to the Creator. This point is emphasized in many verses in the Quran as Allah said that when we return to Him again after our short stay on earth, He will ask:

يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا قَالُوا شَهِدْنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا

“O you assembly of Jinn and humankind, haven’t you received Messengers from amongst yourselves who used to relate My verses to you, and used to warn you of the meeting of this Day?” They will say: “We testify against ourselves.” (Al-Anaam 6:130)

The purpose of this life on Earth is to prepare ourselves for this return and this preparation is very important because while on earth we have many options, in the eternal life we will have only two options: Heaven or Hell. The purpose of preparing for eternity should be far greater than our personal fulfillment and happiness. Being successful and fulfilling your life purpose are not the same. You could reach all your personal goals, becoming a raving success by the world’s standard and still miss the purpose for which you were created by Allah.

Life on earth is just a dress rehearsal before the real production. Just as the nine months you spend in your mother’s womb were not the end in themselves but preparation for your life, this life is a preparation for the next. Tragically, many people will have to endure eternity without the company of Allah because they chose to live without Him on Earth.

While a person’s life on earth seems long, it is actually extremely short, when compared to a single day in the hereafter, as Allah says:

وَإِنَّ يَوْمًا عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِمَّا تَعُدُّونَ

“Verily a day with your Lord is like a thousand years from what you count (on Earth).” (Al-Hajj 22:47)

So, even if you live on Earth 100 years, they are merely equivalent to about 2 hrs of one of the days in eternity. And Allah emphasizes this point in many places in the Quran, as He says:

كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ مَا يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ

“On the Day when they see what had been promised them, they will realize that their life on Earth has only been a mere one hour of day. (Al-Ahqaf 46:35)

The purpose of your life on Earth is to prepare for eternity. Recognizing that you live on Earth in the light of eternity, your values will be noble, your use of time and money will be wiser, and you will place a higher premium on character instead of wealth and fame. Living in the light of eternity, many of your problems will appear to be trivial.

To make the most of your life, you must keep the vision of eternity continuously in your mind and the value of it in your heart. If you have this vision, you will never fear death because you will know that death is not the end of life, but it is the birthday into an eternal life. While the capacity of our brains cannot handle the wonders and greatness of heaven, Allah has given us in the Quran glimpses of eternity in words that we can understand.

The Nature of this Life

The way we see our life shapes our life. If you ask someone, how do you picture your life? It is most likely that he will express his life in a metaphor, and you will note this metaphor has far more influence on his life than he thinks. As an example:

1. If a person sees his life as a party, you will find that his primary value is to have fun.
2. If a person sees his life as a race, you will note that he values speed and he is always in a hurry.
3. If a person views his life as a marathon, you will note that he values endurance.
4. If a person sees his life as a battle, you will note that winning is the most important thing in his life.

But for a Muslim, the Quran offers us three metaphors that represent the eternal truths about the nature of this life and they should be the foundation based on which we should live our lives. They will also allow us to explain everything happening around us. The three metaphors that should shape the life of every Muslim are:

1. Life is a temporary assignment
2. Life is a test
3. Life is a trust

We will stop here and continue next time, inshallah.

We pray to Allah that He makes us among those who hear and follow the best.

DUA

title: Prophet Nuh (Noah) – Where is the Ship
excerpt:
# Prophet Nuh (Noah) – Where is the Ship

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده…
content:
# Prophet Nuh (Noah) – Where is the Ship

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

This talk is a follow up of last week talk and here I will, inshallah address several issues and these are:

1. Clarify couple of points that I made last time regarding the time between Prophet Adam and Prophet Nuh and the nature of the messengers that were present with Prophet Nuh.
2. Explain the meaning of the sign that was established to start the loading the ship.
3. Address the issue of the nature of animals that were in the ship.
4. Speculate on the most likely location of the ship and whether the whole ship is still present or only parts of it.

Last week we highlighted the importance of stories in the Quran and that they serve two purposes, they provide key lessons and offer educational strategy to increase the analytical capabilities and cognitive capacity of the serious reader of the Quran.

We mentioned several key lessons and then discussed several elements of the Story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) as presented in the Quran and illustrated their differences from those in the Old Testaments and showed why the Old Testament accounts are not logical.

We illustrated that the flood of the whole earth is not justified by the Quran and that the flood may have been limited to the area in which Prophet Nuh was directly preaching and it is unlikely to cover the areas that are not inhabited by people and areas where the other messengers, who existed during the life of Prophet Nuh were preaching.

In last week talk, I suggested that the likely average age in prophet Adam time was 5,000 years by extrapolating from the age of prophet Ibrahim to the age of prophet Nuh. However, I was reminded there is a hadith reported by Imam Ahmad that mentioned that Prophet Adam’s age was 960 years. However, there is another very similar hadith that was reported by Imam Al-Tirmidhi and does not mention Prophet Adam's age. The hadith by Imam Ahmad that mentions the age and was narrated by Ibn Abbas is as follows:

عن عبدالله بن عباس قال قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : إن الله عز وجل لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره فأخرج منه ما هو من ذراري إلى يوم القيامة، فجعل يعرض ذريته عليه فرأى فيهم رجلاً يزهر، فقال: أي رب من هذا؟ قال: هذا ابنك داود، قال: أي رب كم عمره؟ قال: ستون عاماً، قال رب: زد في عمره. قال: لا ، إلا أن أزيده من عمرك، وكان عمر آدم ألف عام. فزاده أربعين عاما، فكتب الله عز وجل عليه بذلك كتاباً وأشهد عليه الملائكة، فلما احتضر آدم وأتته الملائكة لتقبضه قال: إنه قد بقي من عمري أربعون عاماً، فقيل إنك قد وهبتها لابنك داود قال: ما فعلت، وأبرز الله عز وجل عليه الكتاب وشهدت عليه الملائكة. (رواه أحمد)

“When Allah created Adam, He wiped over his back and came out of it all his offspring that Allah will create until the Day of Judgement. Allah showed Adam his offspring. Adam saw one of them shining with light. Adam asked: “My Lord who are they? Allah said: he is your son Dawoud (David). Adam asked: My Lord, what is his age? Allah said: sixty years. Adam said: My Lord increase his age. Allah said: No, unless I increase his age from your age. Adam knew that his age is 1000 years. So, Allah increased Daud age 40 years. Allah wrote with this a book that is witnessed by the angels.

When the angel of death came to Adam, he said there are forty years remaining. He is told, you have granted them to your son Dawoud (David).

Adam said: I did not. Allah produced for him the book and the angels testified about in the book. “(Reported by Ahmad)

The Hadith by Imam Al-Tirmidhi that does not mention the age and was narrated by Abu Hurrirah is as follows:

عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره فسقط عن ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة ، وجعل بين عيني كل إنسان منهم وبيصا من نور ، ثم عرضهم على آدم ، فقال أي رب ! من هؤلاء ؟ فقال ذريتك . فرأى رجلا منهم فأعجبه ، وبيص ما بين عينيه ، قال : أي رب ! من هذا ؟ قال : داود . فقال : رب ! كم جعلت عمره ؟ قال : ستين سنة . قال : رب زده من عمري أربعين سنة ) . قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : ( فلما انقضى عمر آدم إلا أربعين جاءه ملك الموت ، فقال آدم ) : أولم يبق من عمري أربعون سنة ؟ قال : أولم تعطها ابنك داود ؟ ! فجحد آدم ، فجحدت ذريته ، ونسي آدم فأكل من الشجرة ، فنسيت ذريته ، وخطأ آدم وخطأت ذريته ) رواه الترمذي

“When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back brought from it every soul of his offspring that Allah will create until the Day of Judgement. Allah put on the forehead of every one of them a flash of light, then showed them to Adam. Adam asked: “My Lord who are they? Allah said: They are your offspring.

Adam saw one of them and he was charmed by a bright flash between his eyes. He asked: My Lord, who is this? Allah said: he is Dawoud (David).

Adam asked: My Lord, what is his age? Allah said: sixty years.

Adam said: My Lord give him from my age 40 years.

When the age of Adam ended minus the 40 years. The angel of death came to him

Adam said: Is it not that I still have 40 years. The angel said: didn’t you give it to your son Dawoud (David).

The Prophet said: Adam denied it and his offspring will deny. Adam forgot and ate from the tree and his offspringg will forget. Adam made mistake and his offspring will make mistakes. (Reported by Al-Tirmidhi)

The second issue is existence of messengers during the time of Prophet Nuh, in some books of Tafseer, it is suggested that these messengers were send by Prophet Nuh and not by Allah. But there is nothing to justify that the messengers that are mentioned in the following verses were not sent by Allah. The important point that remains is that Prophet Nuh was the first messenger, but he was not the only messenger at that time as Allah says:

وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ آيَةً (٣٧)

“And for the people of Nuh (Noah), when they rejected the Messengers, We drowned them and made them as a sign for mankind.” (Al-Furqan 25:37)

كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (١٠٥)

“The people of Nuh (Noah) rejected the Messengers.” (Al-Shura 26:105)

Now, let us address the question that has created confusion because what is included in the Old Testament regarding the numbers of animals that Prophet Nuh carried with him in the Ship. The Quran suggests that not all the earth was flooded and thus the only animals to be saved are those in the area where the flood occurred. The command to Prophet Nuh that ended with last week was as follows:

حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ آمَنَ ۚ وَمَا آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ (٤٠)

When Our command came to pass and “Al Tanour” gushed, We said: Load in it from every pair two and your family, except those against whom the word already been pronounced, and take those who have believed. And there were only few who believed with him.” (Hud 11:40)

In the last week talk, I suggested that there are two phrases that need explanations, the first is the phrase “gushing or overflowing of Al-Tanour” (وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ) which was the sign to start loading the Ship and the second phrase is “from every pair two” (مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ). In the first phrase, what is “Al-Tanour” and in the second phrase what does “from every pair two” mean.

In the first phrase, what is the meaning of “Al-Tanour”? Interpreters of the Quran suggested many different meanings for this “Al-Tanour” that will overflow and become a sign to all who see it to come to the Ship. However, the most logical interpretation seems that this sign refers to a volcano that will be erupted and all those who are intended to be with Prophet Nuh on the Ship will be able to see it and start travelling towards the ship.

However, there is one very interesting interpretation and that Al-Tanour” is a steam engine that Allah taught Prophet Nuh how to build as He taught him how to build the ship as Allah said:

وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا (٣٧)

“And construct the ship under Our Eyes and according to Our Revelation.” (Hud 11:37)

So, since Allah taught Prophet Nuh how to build the ship, it is possible that Allah also taught him how to build the steam engine. The sign for those who are intended to ride on the ship is when the engine is fired, and the steam gushed out of it. Obviously, the only way to verify the steam engine interpretation is to find the Ship. Until the ship is found, the idea of an erupted volcano seems to be the most logical.

The phrase “from every pair two (مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ) does not imply that all the kinds of animals were taken in the ship because as we have discussed previously in the discussion on the concept of Biddah, the word (كل) which is translated as every or all, does not mean everything. In the talk on Biddah, I referenced a book that has been dedicated to this word “Kul”. Therefore, the objection to the idea that the ship of Prophet Nuh cannot carry all the species that exist is not relevant to the account in the Quran.

The other words in the phrase are (زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ) (a pair of two). This means that the command is to carry 4 animals of each type that Prophet Nuh wanted to save, two females and two males and this is to ensure redundancy.

The remaining and probably the most intriguing question is where did the ship land whether it still exists since Allah is said that He left it as sign for mankind. Allah said:

وَحَمَلْنَاهُ عَلَىٰ ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ (١٣) تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَاءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ (١٤) وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَاهَا آيَةً فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ (١٥)

“And We carried him upon the ship of planks and nails, (13) That sailed under Our Sight, as a reward for him who was rejected. (14) And Indeed, We left it (the ship) as a sign. So, is there anyone to remember?” (Al-Qamar 54: 13-15)

In this verse Allah provided specific details about the construction materials of the ship and these are the planks and the nails. Does this mean that these two items are the only things that are remaining as a sign or is the whole ship remains as sign? The Quran does not give us a firm answer beyond affirming that the ship's two key building materials (أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ) remain until now.

Note that the term “Alwaah” (أَلْوَاحٍ) is translated as “wood planks” and the term “Dusur” (دُسُرٍ) is translated as nails. This may make finding the ship easier using metal detectors. However, the record shows that metal nails were used in ancient Egypt around 3500 BC and we estimated that Prophet Noah was around 7500 BC. This, Allah must have taught him how to make them. However, the term (دُسُرٍ) can also mean ropes that were available and can be used to assemble the ship.

Also, the verb related to the term “Dusur” is “Dasar” (دَسَرَ) that means push hard. Could the term “Dusur” (دُسُرٍ) be referring to the engine that pushed the ship in the water and not merely the materials that held the planks of the ship tightly together, Allah knows best. Only, when we find the ship, will we really know.

This point of having specific elements of the ship remaining as a sign for mankind and not the whole ship is noted because Allah used two other terms when referring to the ship of Prophet Nuh. One term is Fulk (فلك) and the second term is Safina (سفينة) and both are translated as ship.

The term Fulk (فلك) is used in the Quran 23 times with 8 related to the ship of Prophet Nuh and in none of these verses, Allah mentioned that it is remaining as a sign for mankind.

The term Safina (سفينة) came in the Quran 3 times with one related to the ship of Prophet Nuh and in this case, Allah says:

فَأَنجَيْنَاهُ وَأَصْحَابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِّلْعَالَمِينَ (١٥)

“And We saved him and the people of the ship and made of it a sign for the worlds.” (Al-Ankabout 29:15)

In this verse, is the sign the ship or is the sign the saving of Prophet Nuh and the people of the ship. The verse can be interpreted to mean either. Therefore, this verse is not as clear as the verse in Surat Al-Qamar that specifies the materials of constriction, the planks and the nails (أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ), as the ones that are saved as a sign for mankind.

The key question is where the ship landed for explorers to look for it. Although there are reports that the ship was found at different places, none of these reports has been proven true so far. One of the problems in validating what people find is when was Prophet Noah. People think that the flood occurred 4,400 years ago based on the Bible, but in my talk last time, I proposed that it was about 10,000 years ago based on a hadith by the Prophet (PBUH). Also, note that in my previous talk, I presented population studies that suggested that the earth was inhabited by one million people 12,000 years ago.

Regarding where the ship could be found, the Quran informs us that the ship landed on Al-Judi, as Allah says:

وَقِيلَ يَا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي مَاءَكِ وَيَا سَمَاءُ أَقْلِعِي وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ ۖ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ (٤٤)

“And it was said: “O earth! Swallow your water and, O sky! stop! And the water subsided. And the matter was fulfilled. And it (the ship) came to rest upon Al-Judi and it was said: Away with the wrongdoers!” (Hud 11:44)

As we mentioned in the previous talk, the Epic of Gilgamesh (ملحمة جلجامش) stated that the ship landed on the mountain of Naseer (جبل نصير) and the Old Testament stated that it landed on the mountain of Ararat (جبل أرارات). The mountain of Naseer (جبل نصير) is located in Iraq near the city Al-Sulaymaniyah (بالقرب من المدينة السليمانية في كردستان), and the mountain of Ararat (جبل أرارات) is located in the extreme east of Turkey. Also, the mountain of Al-Judi (الجودى) is located in North Iraq near the city of Mosel (الموصل).

The question is whether the names of these mountains existed before these documents existed or the names of the mountains were given by the people to justify what is in the documents? But it would be hard to suggest that these names were merely invented by the writers of the legend of Gilgamesh or the Old Testament because it will be easy to prove the inaccuracy of the names since there exist mountains with these names.

The question is whether these names refer to names of specific mountains or do they refer to a description of the one mountain on which the ship landed. Supporting that the name is related to a description is the change of the name of the mountain in the Old Testament to Ararat from the name Naseer in the Epic of Gilgamesh (ملحمة جلجامش) from which the story in the Old Testament was copied.

If the name is a description, these three names, Naseer, Ararat and Al-Judi, must be related to each other.

1. The mountain name Naseer (جبل نصير) could mean the mountain on which victory and help is granted. Note that one of Allah’s glorious names is Al-Naseer (النصير) that means “The Helper and the Granter of Victory”.
2. The mountain name Ararat (جبل أرارات) needs to be resolved by knowing what the word Ararat mean in Hebrew. In Hebrew, the word “Ar” means city” and the “Arat: means “to grab”. Could the name Ararat mean “the place that grabbed the ship”
3. The name Al-Judi (الجودى) means the blessings. This means that ship is landed in the mountain of blessings.

Therefore, it seems that all the three names of the mountain where the ship landed are related. They imply that the mountain on which the ship landed is a blessed location that grabbed the ship, and this was done by the help of Allah. This does not help us identify the mountain until we examine where Prophet Nuh lived.

We can justify the Prophet Nuh lived in Arabia based on some observations:

1. Prophet Adam lived in Arabia where the angels built for him the first place of worship in the earth in Mecca and most likely his descendants lived there.
2. The two prophets who came after Prophet Nuh are Hud and Saleh and they lived in Arabia where they were prophets to the people of Ad and the people of Thamud.
3. The names of the Idols that were worshipped by Prophet Nuh’s people (ود و سواعا و يغوث ويعوق ونسر) are names of idols that were worshipped in Arabia until Islam came.
4. Since we suggested that an erupted volcano could have been the sign for Prophet Nuh to start loading the ship, there are at least 13 main volcanos that have erupted in Arabia long time ago.

If Prophet Nuh was in Arabia and the flood occurred in Arabia, the mountain on which the ship landed is most likely be also in Arabia. There is one recent Islamic scholar who suggested that prophet Nuh’s ship landed in the mountain of Shamonaseer (جبل شمنصير) which is located about 100 km northeast of Mecca. In general, I don’t give references because I don’t want you to make your decision to accept or reject an idea based on the person who is saying it, but I want you to make your decision based on the merit of the idea itself. After all, you are not obligated to accept any idea unless it makes sense to you. But here, I am going to give the reference because of the uniqueness of the identified location, he is the Palestinian religious scholar Dr. Mohammad Al-Mubayad (محمد المبيض).

Obviously, most people will justifiably question the relevance of this mountain, Shamonaseer (جبل شمنصير), because its name appears to have no relationship to the meaning of the other names Al-Judi (الجودى), Naseer (جبل نصير) and Ararat (جبل أرارات). But this may be resolved by noting that this name is very odd name in the structure of Arabic language, and it is most likely a combination of two names: “Shamon” and “Naseer”. The word “Naseer” has a meaning of victory and help as we have discussed, and its meaning is related to the meaning of the name Al-Judi.

But what does “Shamon” mean? The word “Shamon” in Hebrew means the number eighty. Number 80 in Hebrew sounds in English as “shmoneem”. We previously discussed that the number of people who were saved with Prophet Nuh in the ship is 80. So, one can say that the name of the mountain Shamonaseer (جبل شمنصير) means the mountain on which 80 people were saved by Allah. And thus, this mountain could have been named after the victorious eighty people who were with Prophet Nuh on the ship.

In fact, at the bottom of the mountain a village called the village of Shamon (قرية شمن قرب جبل شمنصير) meaning the village of the eighty. And west of the mountain is the village of Rahat (قرية رهاط). Note the similarity in the sounding of the Old Testament’s name Ara-Arat (أرارات) which means the city of Arat with the sound of the village of Rahat.

It is interesting that this mountain Shamonaseer (جبل شمنصير) is blessed in that it can hold rainwater and thus plants grow on it and the water in it transforms into perpetual springs from which water flows down to the villages at its bottom.

I’ll stop here and I’ll leave it up to you to study the subject further if interested. Hope, this presentation increases your curiosity to take a trip to this mountain when you go to Saudi Arabia in Ummrah or Hajj. You may be that explorer who will be blessed and find the planks and the nails, if not the ship.

DUA

title: The Truth and Legend about Prophet Nuh (Noah)
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

Today, I plan inshallah to discuss the story that all of you know which is the story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) as revealed to us in the Quran and the hadith of the Prophet (PBUH). We realize that the stories of the Quran are intended to provide key lessons for us. When we study the story of Prophet Nuh, we can derive several lessons that include:

1. Success in this life and in the hereafter require following the messenger of Allah.
2. Patience and sincerity are keys to fulfilling the commands of Allah.
3. Patience is a prerequisite when facing the ignorant and fools.
4. Patience and not rushing for the results are essential because the results are controlled by Allah.
5. Seek to apply different approaches when giving advice and guidance to people.
6. Success will always be the outcome for the righteous.
7. Always rely on Allah in all matters and supplicate to Him for help is a key tool.
8. Your responsibility is only to do your best with your family, you are not responsible for their response.
9. Linage alone does not maintain family relationship, association in belief is essential.

But the value of the stories in the Quran goes beyond teaching valuable lessons.  The way the story is narrated in the Quran serves as an educational tool to help expanding the analytical capability and the cognitive capacity of the serious readers.  The process to understand the story is to assemble all the verses related to the key figure in the story and harmonize the verses to derive a coherent story.

The name of Prophet Nuh (Noah) came in the Quran 43 times in 28 Surat.  It came by itself 30 times and came associated with his people 11 times and with his wife 1 time.

For those who enjoy the analytical models in the Quran, we note that Nuh name is mentioned 43 times.
1. Surat Nuh is number 71 and it has 28 verses, the difference is 43
2. The last time Nuh’s name was mentioned is in Surat number 71 (Surat Nuh). The Quran has 114 Surat, so Nuh was not mentioned is 43 Surat after his last mention in Surat 71.
3. The name Nuh was not mentioned in 43 Surat that are before his last mention in Surat 71.
4. The Name Nuh was not mentioned in 86 Surat which 2 times 43.

The story of the great flood that devastated earlier civilizations is mentioned in many of the world’s cultures. Nearly all these stories indicate that God or the gods sent the flood to destroy the civilization as an act of divine retribution and only a small number of humans survived by being on a ship, and they repopulated humankind. The widespread of the story among many cultures suggests that the flood happened, through the details reported in every culture has differed and this is attributed to the mix between truth and fables.

There are widespread differences among the accounts regarding where the survivals landed.  An account says that the survivals were the first inhabitants of Ireland, another says that they landed in Hawaii, a third suggests that they landed in South America, a fourth says that they landed in North America and a fifth says that they landed in Australia. In addition, there are accounts that say they landed in Europe, in Africa and in the Middle East. In the Middle East, countries such as Iraq, Turkey and Saudi Arabia are mentioned.

Both the Old Testament and the Quran provide accounts of this great flood and mention Noah as the one who built the ship (generally called Noah’s Ark). There are however key differences between the Old Testament and the Quran. For example, in the Old Testament Noah was a preacher while he was a Messenger and a prophet in the Quran. The story in the Old Testament borrowed heavily from the story in the Epic of Gilgamesh (ملحمة جلجامش) which was a well-known story in Iraq where many sections of Old Testament were written over 500 years after Prophet Moses. Other parts of the Old Testament were written later in Jerusalem.

Most people are interested in knowing where the Ship landed.
1. The Epic of Gilgamesh (ملحمة جلجامش) says that it landed in the mountain of Nasir (جبل نصير) which is a mountain in Iraq near the city Al-Sulaymaniyah (القرب من المدينة السليمانية في كردستان).
2. The Old Testament says that it landed on the mountain of Ararat (جبل أرارات) which is a mountain located in the extreme east of Turkey.
3. The Quran says that it is landed on the mountain of Judi (الجودى) which is a mountain located in North Iraq near the city of Mosel (الموصل).

However, despite many expeditions, this ship, Noah’s Ark, has not been found and many suggest that it is unlikely to be found because its wood must have been deteriorated.

There are many elements of Nuh’s account in the Old Testament that are used by those who want to discredit the Bible as fables. Unfortunately, some elements of the biblical account creeped into some books of Tafseer of the Quran. People who don’t study the Quran try to discredit the Quran on the assumption that it says the same thing as what exists in the Old Testament, and this is completely wrong.

Some of the elements in the story of Nuh (Noah) in the Old Testament that have been justifiably discredited include:
1. The whole earth was flooded and everything on earth perished except those who were in Noah’s Ark who consisted of only 8 people.
2. The ship has a pair of all clean and unclean animals, of birds and of all creatures that move along the ground.
3. The biblical story states that only 8 people survived, and they were Noah and his wife and their three sons and their wives.

(Note that it took 12,000 years for the population to grow from 1 million to 8 billion)
The attached chart shows the world population from the year 10,000 BC (i.e.,12,020 years ago) when it was 1 million to reach the 8 billion level in the year 2020.

In order to understand the true story of Prophet Nuh, we need to only focus on the related verses in the Quran and the Hadith of the prophet (PBUH) to answer the following questions:
1. When did this event occur relative to Prophet Adam?
2. Did the flood cover the whole earth?
3. Did Prophet Noah take all the animals on the earth with him in the Ship?
4. Did all people drown, and the only survivors were the people with Prophet Noah?
5. Does the ship still exist and if it does, where it is most likely to be located?

Regarding the time between Prophet Adam and Prophet Noah, the Prophet (PBUH) was asked about this time.
ويذكر الطبراني أن رجلا قال: “يا رسول الله، أنبيّ كان آدم؟” قال: ((نعم))، قال: كم بينه وبين نوح؟” قال: ((عشرة قرون))
He (PBUH) said: “Between Adam and Nuh was 10 Qoroun”
And He was asked about the time between Noah and Ibrahim.
He (PBUH) said: Between Nuh and Ibrahim was 10 Qoroun
Then he was asked about the number of messengers.
He (PBUH) said: The number of messengers was 315.

Quroun (قرون) means generations as in the following verse:
أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ أَنَّہُمۡ إِلَيۡہِمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ (يس ٣١)
“Have they not seen how many (Quroun) generations We destroyed before them who will not return to them.” (Ya-Sin 36:31)

The confusion that some people make is thinking that the “Qarn” (قرن) is 100 years as we commonly call a century. But in Arabic language, “Qarn” refers to people of similar age or contemporaries.
The Qarn is the likely time two people who are born at the same time to be companions because it is derived from the word “Qareen” (قرين) meaning companion. Allah said:
وَمَن يَعۡشُ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ نُقَيِّضۡ لَهُ ۥ شَيۡطَـٰنً۬ا فَهُوَ لَهُ ۥ قَرِينٌ۬ (الزّخرُف)
“And whosoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Gracious, We appoint for him a devil to be an intimate companion to him” (Az-Zukhruf 43:36)

It appears that at the beginning on mankind on earth the average life of humans was far longer than what it is now. We know that Prophet Nuh’s stayed with his people 950 years.
So, if we assume that the average Qarn between Prophet Adam and Prophet Noah is 2.500 years, we can conclude that the time between prophet Adam and Prophet Noah is about 25,000 years.  One would expect that during this time people would have spread far beyond the area in which Prophet Noah was present.
(Note: The Hebrew Text of the Torah indicates that the time between Adam and Noah was only 1000 years and the flood occurred in the year 2348 BC)

Regarding the relevant question of whether all the earth was flooded and thus only those who were in the ship survived. Allah said:
وَقَوۡمَ نُوحٍ۬ لَّمَّا ڪَذَّبُواْ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغۡرَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ لِلنَّاسِ ءَايَةً۬‌ۖ (الفرقان ٣٧)
“And for the people of Nuh (Noah), when they rejected the Messengers, We drowned them and made them as a sign for mankind.” (Al-Furqan 25:37)
كَذَّبَتۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحٍ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (الشعراء ١٠٥)
“The people of Nuh (Noah) rejected the Messengers.” (Al-Shura 26:105)

The presence of multiple messengers during the time of Prophet Nuh suggests that.  the people were spread over a wide area and that is why multiple messengers were sent to them. Allah says:
وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلاً أَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ إِذۡ جَآءَهَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ (١٣) إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡہِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثٍ۬ (يس)
“And cite for them the example of the people of the village, when the messengers came to them. (13) When We sent to them two, they rejected them, so We reinforced them with a third.” (Ya-Sin 36:13-14)

We also know that prophet Ibrahim and Prophet Lut as well as Prophets Ishaq (Isaac) and Ismael were all contemporaries.
Calling all people as that time “the people of Nuh” (قوم نوح) is reasonable since Nuh was the first of the messengers. But then one should ask the following questions:
1. Did the other messengers face the same rejection as Prophet Nuh?
2. If there were followers with the other messengers, were they also in the ship that Nuh built?
3. Did the areas in which the other messengers were present also suffer flood and thus all the area where people spread were flooded?

There is nothing in the Quran that suggest that whole earth was flooded specifically the areas where other messengers were present.
Let us see what the Quran says regarding whether the flood covered the whole earth.  Allah says:
وَقَالَ نُوحٌ۬ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا (نوح ٢٦)
“And Nuh (Noah) said: My Lord! Do not leave on the earth even a single disbeliever.” (Nuh 71:26)

The verse suggests that only the disbelievers were destroyed by the flood and thus there is no reason to flood the areas where believers were present. The word “The Earth” (الأرض) in Arabic doesn’t only refer to the whole globe but it can also refer to a certain land as in the following verses about Prophet Yusuf:
وَكَذَٲلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنۡہَا حَيۡثُ يَشَآءُ‌ۚ
“And thus, We gave Yusuf the power in the earth.  He could settle in it wherever he wished.” (Yusuf 12: 56)
قَالَ ڪَبِيرُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمۡ قَدۡ أَخَذَ عَلَيۡكُم مَّوۡثِقً۬ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبۡلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمۡ فِى يُوسُفَ‌ۖ فَلَنۡ أَبۡرَحَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡذَنَ لِىٓ أَبِىٓ أَوۡ يَحۡكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِى‌ۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡحَـٰكِمِينَ (٨٠)
“The eldest among them said: “Do you not know that your father has taken an oath from you in the name of Allah, and before this you failed in your duty with Yusuf. I will never leave the earth until my father permits me, or Allah decides my case and He is the Best of the judges.” (Yusuf 12: 80)

Conclusion 1: Therefore, there is no suggestion in the Quran that the flood covered the whole earth and any claim otherwise is based on the account in the Old Testament.

Someone may argue that that there appears to be an indication that the whole earth was covered with water when Allah created the earth based on the following Hadith:
“كانت الكعبة خشعة على الماء فدحيت منها الأرض “‏ والحديث ذكره الهروي في غريب لحديث‏(3/362) ,‏ وذكره الزمخشري في الفائق‏(1/371)‏
“The Kaaba emerged from beneath the water as a small hill, and then land formed around it.”
This Hadith is supported by another Hadith in which the prophet (PBUH) said:
وهذا الحديث النبوي الشريف يدعمه حديث آخر أخرجه كل من الطبراني والبيهقي في الشعب عن ابن عمر‏ (رضي الله عنهما‏)‏ عن النبي‏ (صلي الله عليه وسلم‏)‏ إنه قال‏:‏
إنه‏ (أي بيت الله الحرام‏)‏ كان أول ما ظهر على وجه الماء عند خلق السماوات والأرض زبدة‏ (بفتح الزاي‏)‏ بيضاء فدحيت الأرض من تحته‏.‏
“It (the Sanctified House) was the first thing to come out over the surface of the water in the time of the creation of the heavens and the earth as a white froth, and then the earth was formed around it.”
[Source: Akhbar Makkah by Al-Azraqi (1/64) and Al-Fakihi (2/230)]

The other main question is whether all the earth population were destroyed by the flood except those who were in the ship. Allah said:
وَلَقَدۡ نَادَٮٰنَا نُوحٌ۬ فَلَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمُجِيبُونَ (٧٥) وَنَجَّيۡنَـٰهُ وَأَهۡلَهُ ۥ مِنَ ٱلۡكَرۡبِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ (٧٦) وَجَعَلۡنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ ۥ هُمُ ٱلۡبَاقِينَ (٧٧)
“And Nuh (Noah) invoked Us, and We are the best to respond. (75) And We saved him and his family from the great distress. (76) And, made his progeny, the survivors.” (As-Saffat 37: 75-77)

If we assume that the verse implies that only those with prophet Nuh in the ship survived, this will raise many questions regarding the fate of the other messengers and their followers who were spread over the earth.
If only those in the ship survived and were responsible for repopulating the earth, how many people were in the ship?

Many interpreters of verse 77 in Surat Al-saffat (وَجَعَلۡنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ ۥ هُمُ ٱلۡبَاقِينَ) (And, made his progeny, the survivors) suggest that all the world population came from the 3 sons of Prophet Nuh.  But, how about the other followers who were in the ship? Didn’t they also have children and thus progeny?
Since the Quran did not provide clear answer to this question of who repopulated the earth after the flood, we should apply the following command of Allah:
قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ ڪَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ‌ۚ
Say: “Travel in the land and see how He (Allah) originated the creation.” (Al-Ankaboot 29:20)

The question that creates confusion because what is included in the Old Testament regarding the number of animals that Prophet Nuh was commanded to take in the ship. Allah says:
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلۡنَا ٱحۡمِلۡ فِيہَا مِن ڪُلٍّ۬ زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَأَهۡلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ وَمَنۡ ءَامَنَ‌ۚ (هود ٤٠)
When Our command came to pass and “Al Tanour” gushed, We said: Load in it from every pair two and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe.” (Hud 11:40)

In this verse there are two phrases that need explanations, the first is the phrase “gushing or overflowing of Al-Tanour” (وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ) which was the sign to start loading the ark and the second phrase is “from every pair two (مِن ڪُلٍّ۬ زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ).”

In the first phrase, what is the meaning of Al-Tanour” and in the second phrase what does it mean for every pair two. Does it mean a pair of every animal species on earth?
I am going to stop here and will continue Inshallah next time because in addition to explaining this, we will discuss where the ship is most likely located.

DUA

title: A Muslim Can Never be Atheist
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

My focus in this talk will be, Insha’Allah, on providing rational proofs of God’s existence to ensure that this fundamental article of belief is engrained in the mind and thus help those Muslims who are shown by some surveys as becoming atheists.

Some published surveys suggest that atheism is appearing among Muslims, particularly, the youth and such a phenomenon is occurring even in Muslim Countries. According to a 2012 poll by WIN/Gallup International, 5 percent of the citizens of Saudi Arabia described themselves as “convinced atheist”—the same percentage as in the United States. In addition, 19 percent self-identified as “non-religious.” But these statistics are not totally accurate because it classifies anyone who is born to Muslim parents as a Muslim. But are those people really know what the fundamentals of Islam are to be classified as true Muslims.

As similitude to this situation, it is the tradition that people, particularly in Muslim countries, call any student who enters an engineering school an engineer while he has not graduated yet. If a student leaves the school without graduation and becomes factory worker, is it proper to say some engineers became factory workers. Similarly, a person is called Muslim just because he/she is born to a Muslim family. If such persons are not vested in the fundamental article of Islam and leave Islam, is it proper to say some Muslims are deserting Islam?

Let us start by defining what Islam is and when a person should be counted as true Muslim. Islam is a religion that demands belief based on knowledge and convection and not on cultural norm. After all, the first word that was revealed in Islam was (اِقْرَأْ) “Read” which is the mean to acquire knowledge and, the Quran, has a whole chapter that is entitled “The Pen” (Surat no. 68). which is the mean by which knowledge is recorded and transferred.

The Religion of Islam is based on three pillars: Aqedah (العقيدة) (faith, belief), Shari’ah (divine rules) and Fiqh (human interpretation of the divine rules). The Aqedah is s the most important pillar and it involves six elements of beliefs: belief in Allah, his angels, his books, his messengers, the last day (the Day of Judgement), and the decree good and bad (الإيمان بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر والقدر خيره وشره).

The key element in Aqedah is the belief in Allah as the sovereign creator of the Universe. Therefore, no person can be considered a Muslim if this element is not already part of his/her Aqedah. A person who has any doubt about the existance and absolute authority of Allah cannot be counted as a true Muslim.

The term Aqedah is derivative of the word Aqd (عقد) (contract) and the word Uqdah (عقدة) (knot) that cannot be untied. The Aqedah is related to the belief in unseen matters that cannot be defined by human senses because they are not materialistic. Materialistic matters that can be defined by our senses are not Aqedah (belief). When you sit on chair working on a computer, you don’t say I believe that I am sitting on a chair or say I believe I have computer in front of me. You say I believe when you address issues that could not be verified by the five senses. Since belief in Allah is an unseen matter, it cannot be proven by human senses but only by intellectual analysis of the the effects of this belief.

A certain belief becomes Aqedah when the belief has been discussed, logically examined by the mind, its truthfulness has engrained in the mind, doubts have been totally cleared, and the belief has strongly settled in the heart.

If the person still has doubts about any unseen element, this element cannot be considered Aqedah, but it is an idea of unseen matter that is still being evaluated. Only after the person seriously evaluates this unseen matter and develops firm belief in it with no doubt ever, it become Aqedah.

Islamic scholars consider that any matter of Aqedah must satisfy three conditions:
1. Certainty of recognition (إدراك جازم) that one’s heart and mind are fixed upon without any wavering or doubt.
2. Consistency with realities (مطابقة للواقع) that it makes rational sense.
3. Based on relevant proofs (الناشئ عن دليل)

Scholars consider any person whose belief is not based on proof is not a believer. Even the uneducated layman must at least to rationalize that Allah exists because everything that exist need a maker and He is the maker of the universe and have also to recognize that the maker of the universe is needed by every creation to survive but He is in need of none.

Why the belief of some born Muslim does not rise to the level of Aqedah because the focus in teaching Muslim children starts with the list of what is Halal and what is Haram and neglect the build the Aqedah by providing logical proofs of the existence and sovereignty of Allah.

The basic element of Aqedah for any true Muslim is unshaken belief that God (Allah) is the sovereign creator and sustainer of the Universe.

In this talk, I plan to Inshallah, provide several rational proofs to prove God’s existence that can elevate the belief of any person to the level of Aqedah that can never be broken.

In a previous talk, I presented six logical arguments that God exists. These included discussions on the First Cause, Design, Fine-Tuning, Moral, and Consciousness. Today, I will offer eight additional rational arguments.

1. The Claimant Proof
Legally, a claimant means a person who is entitled to something that belongs to him. Other than God, many humans claimed greatness, but no human being ever claimed to be the creator of the universe or even a creator of any small part of the universe.

Since man came to earth, only God claimed that He is the creator and the controller all that exist and no one else ever challenged Him. If God were not the creator, the real creator would have made his claim. Since no one else ever made a claim, it is logically correct to accept the claim of the only claimant, who is God.

2. The Language Proof
There are many spoken languages in the world and the words in each language are used to define an action or an entity (item). For example, in English we use the word “Tree” to define an entity and the word “Walk” to define an action. If you don’t have an entity or an action, you don’t need a word for it.

If you ask the linguistics what comes first the word or the concept, they tell you the concept come first then a word is used to describe it. If you have no concept, you don’t have a word.

Every culture and language have a word for an entity of some unseen being who is bigger and more powerful than humans. In English, we call Him God, in French Dieu, in Spanish Dios, in Arabic Allah, and so on.

This suggests that God made Himself known to the soul of everyone. The roles of the prophets were to define who this God is and how he wants us to live. This is what we call Fitra (فطرة) (the natural instinct) which is the intuition by which humans can recognize the existence of God.

3. The Unique Name Proof
This proof may be driven from a religious text, but it comes as a challenge to anyone who claims that God does not exist. Allah challenged mankind in the Quran (Surah Maryam 19:65):

رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَہُمَا فَٱعۡبُدۡهُ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ لِعِبَـٰدَتِهِۦ‌ۚ هَلۡ تَعۡلَمُ لَهُ ۥ سَمِيًّ۬ا
“The Lord of the Heavens and the earth and all that is in between. So, worship Him and remain steadfast in His worship; do you know of anyone who has the same name (as He)?”

Since man first roamed the earth, no human being was ever named Allah. So, anyone who does not believe in Allah needs to answer, how come that throughout history no human being was ever named Allah? The only logical answer is that Allah protected His name so it remains unique to Him.

By the way, God’s name Allah is not only known to Muslims, but all Christians and Jews who read the bible in Arabic also use the name Allah for God.

4. The Philosophers’ Proof
Philosophy is the study of the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence. The two major branches of philosophy are metaphysics (the study of existence and reality) and epistemology (the study of knowledge).

The physical branch in philosophy continued to prosper and expand because of the value it created. The metaphysical branch remained stagnant because philosophers attempted to use the physical tools of the five senses to describe God who is non-materialistic.

The confusion regarding God occurs when people try to describe God using materialist images that the mind can perceive through the five senses. Since the mind cannot visualize anything it has not seen, people who wanted to visualize God created idols or used elements of nature like the sun or moon as their gods.

While the idea of not able to create an image for God is confusing to some people, surprisingly, they don’t find it confusing when they are being unable to put image for their own soul/spirt.

We can only rationalize God’s existence, but we will never be able to develop a true image for Him and thus we will never agree on one. If we cannot ever agree on visual image of the soul that is inside us, how can we transgress to create a visual image for the One who created and controls our souls and the universe!

5. The Legal System Proof
Every society have developed a system and established rules to ensure the safety of its members. They have defined what acts are lawful and what acts are criminal and deserve punishment. If the people in authority are perfect, they should be able to identify any person who commits a crime to enforce justice. But no authority in the world is that perfect, particularly, if the crime is committed by those people in authority or by someone who can hide from the authority. Therefore, absolute justice will never exist, and people will always be seeking an authority that no criminal can hide from, and such authority will be more powerful than any authority on earth. Such authority is God.

So, anyone who denies the existence of such authority must respond to the question, should those who commit crimes go unpunished since we never have perfect system to punish all.

6. The Progressive Superiority Proof
We don’t have any doubt about our existence, and we also have no doubt about the existence of the universe. We consider ourselves the master of the universe and the most superior because we receive benefits from everything else. The second level of superiority is the animals, and they are inferior to us in intelligence. Then comes the third level of superiority which is the plants, and they are inferior to animals regarding emotion and motion. Then comes the fourth level in superiority which is solids, and they are inferior to the plants regarding growth.

Note that the lower level in superiority serves the higher levels of superiority. Solids directly serve plants by providing them with water and the minerals, and they also serve animals and man. Plants service animals and man. The animals serve man. So, man is the master of these three entities because they are at his service, and he takes benefits from all of them.

Since we recognize that everything below us has a function to perform because of its existence, we should also have a function. If our life has any meaning, the concept of progressive superiority demands that we exist to serve an entity that has higher superiority than us. Since we have not created the entities that serves us, we must look for who created them and placed them in our service. While we may claim that these things serve us because we control them, there are others such as the sun, the moon, the wind, the rain and the air, etc that serve us, and we have no control over them. No one can make something beneficial to others unless it belongs to him.

So, an atheist needs to answer, to whom these things belong to make them available for you to benefit from them. There must be an entity that is superior to man and to whom everything belongs, and that is God.

It is reported that someone asked a wise man: have you known the prophet by God or have known God by the prophet? He said: I have known God by God and if it were not for God, I would have not known the prophet.

7. The Hope Proof
At some point in a person’s life, he/she will a face situation that is beyond one’s ability and comfort. In such a situation, a person will seek help from a power that is greater than his/her own power. This power is God. The hope that God will help is what keeps a person going.

How miserable a person will be if he does not have such hope, this will be the life of the atheist. When he faces a problem he cannot solve, he will lose hope and may end his life. This is why the suicide rate among atheists is higher than among believers.

وَلَا تَاْيۡـَٔسُواْ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ لَا يَاْيۡـَٔسُ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرُونَ
“Never give up hope of Allah’s Mercy. Certainly no one despairs of Allah’s Mercy, except the disbelieving people.” (12:87)

8. The Fairness Resolution Proof
Since the beginning of time when communities started forming, people have been facing four conflicts:
1. Social conflict between men and women: men favor men and women favor women.
2. Economic conflict between capital and labor: capital wants labor to work more and be paid less and labor wants to work less and be paid more.
3. Political conflict between government and people: government wants more control and people to pay more taxes, people want freedom and pay less taxes.
4. Internal conflict between body and soul: body wants physical pleasures; soul wants self-restraint.

Whom should we seek guidance from to fairly solve these conflicts without the judge being a beneficiary of the solution? The entity to give fair answer cannot be man or woman, cannot be business owner or labor, cannot be government or citizen and cannot be body or soul. The atheist needs to answer, if it is not God, who?

We pray to Allah to strength of faith, increase our knowledge and make us benefit form He has taught us.

DUA
