content:
The Unfolding of the Foretold Tribulations Facing Muslims

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In the 10th year of Hijra, The Prophet (PBUH) went to Hajj and that was his only Hajj, During the Hajj on the 9th day of Dhul-Hijjah, the Prophet (PBUH) left Mina after sunrise and went the mountain of Arafat (عرفة). When the sun went down (زالت الشمس), he went down the valley where over hundred and twenty thousand (over 120,000) Muslims gathered. There he stood up and delivered his last sermon while Rabi’a bin Omaiyah bin Khalaf (ربيعة بن أمية ابن خلف) repeated the Prophet’s (PBUH) statements loudly. Some elements of this sermon are as follows:

أيها الناس إن دماءكم وأموالكم حرام عليكم كحرمة يومكم هذا، في شهركم هذا، في بلدكم هذا.

“O People! just as you regard this month, this day, this city as sacred, so regard the life and property of every Muslim a sacred trust.

أيها الناس، إنما المؤمنون إخوة، ولا يَحلُّ لامرئٍ مالُ أخيه إلا عن طيب نفسٍ منه، ألا هل بلغت، اللهم فاشهد، فلا ترجعوا بعدي كفَّارًا يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض، فإني قد تركتُ فيكم ما إن تمسكتم به لن تضلوا بعده؛ كتاب الله.

O People, the believers are brothers, it Is not allowed for anyone to take any money of his brother without his permission. Do not return after me idolators (kufar) killing each other. I leave for you the Book of Allah which if you hold fast, you shall never go astray.”

أيها الناس، إن ربَّكم واحدٌ، وإن أباكم واحد، كلكم لآدمَ، وآدمُ من تراب، أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم، ليس لعربي فضل على عجمي إلا بالتقوى، ألا هل بلغت، اللهم فاشهد.

O People, your God is One and your father (Adam) is One and you are all from Adam and Adam is from dust, the most honorable among you with Allah is the most righteous. There is no preference between an Arab and a no-Arab expect by righteousness. O’ Allah, I have delivered the message, O Allah be my Witness.

Then the Prophet (PBUH) directed a question to the attendees by saying

وبعد الانتهاء من خطبة الوداع سأل رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- الناس فقال: (وَأَنْتُمْ تُسْأَلُونَ عَنِّي، فَمَا أَنْتُمْ قَائِلُونَ؟ قَالُوا: نَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ وَأَدَّيْتَ وَنَصَحْتَ، فَقَالَ: بِإِصْبُعِهِ السَّبَّابَةِ، يَرْفَعُهَا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَيَنْكُتُهَا إِلَى النَّاسِ اللَّهُمَّ، اشْهَدْ، اللَّهُمَّ، اشْهَدْ، اللَّهُمَّ، اشْهَدْ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ)

You will be asked about me, what will you say?

The people replied: “We bear witness that you have conveyed the message and gave us complete advise.”

He (PBUH) then raised his fore finger skywards and said: “O Allah, be my witness, that I have conveyed your message to Your people.” He said this phrase thrice.

The emphasizes in the Prophet’s sermon was on the unity of Muslims and warning them of returning to the time of ignorance and the worship of idols by killing each other. Worshiping idols does not only mean worshipping statutes but worshipping leaders who mislead them and create dissent among them. Following any person blindly implies worshipping that person as the Prophet (PBUH) explained the following verse in Surat Al-Tawba:

ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَحۡبَارَهُمۡ وَرُهۡبَـٰنَهُمۡ أَرۡبَابً۬ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ

“They take their Rabbis and their monks to be their lords besides Allah (by obeying them in things which they made lawful or unlawful according to their own desires).” (Al-Tawba 9:31)

One of the major concerns of the Prophet (PBUH) was the division among Muslims and he warned against this in many of His sayings such as this one reported in both Bukhari and Muslim:

روى البخاري ومسلم عن أبي بكرة أن النبي ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قال: “إذا التقى المسلمانِ بسيفَيْهما فالقاتلُ والمقتولُ في النار” قُلتُ: يا رسول الله هذا القاتل فما بالُ المقتول؟ قال: “إنه كان حريصًا على قتلِ صاحبه”

If two Muslims met raising their swords against each other, both the killer and the own who is killed in the hellfire.

The companions asked, this can be for the killer but why the one being killed.

The Prophet (PBUH) said: because he was keen to kill his companion.

This hadith is reinforcement of Allah’s grave waring:

وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِداً فِيهَا وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذَاباً عَظِيماً) [النساء (93)]

“Whoever kills a Believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, to abide therein forever: and the wrath and the curse of Allah are upon him, and a dreadful penalty is prepared for him.” (Al-Nisa 4:93)

Because of this concern, the Prophet (PBUH) repeatedly warned the Muslims from what will happen to them in the future to make sure that they heed his warnings. The sad part is that Muslims continue until today to walk blind and fall in every trap that the Prophet (PBUH) identified for them. When you read what the prophet (PBUH) said, you will be perplexed regarding how Muslims can be that blind that they continue to exactly create the conditions that the Prophet (PBUH) warned them from.

As we read the hadith of the Prophet (PBUH), we realize that he (PBUH) was reading to us from the book of the future that Allah revealed to him because what he said happened and is happening even today. This may bring the argument that are often made when discussing future events that are mentioned by the Prophet (PBUH) and are materialized. The argument goes as follows: since the Prophet (PBUH) told us what will happen and he does not say anything that is not a revelation, why should we blame Muslims for falling in the foretold disasters since what he said must happen because it is a decree by Allah. This argument about the divine decree is old one and it can be addressed on several grounds such as:

1. Is the decree of Allah based on His command or based on His pre-knowledge of the consequences of the divine system that He established of the cause-effect relationship?

2. Arguing that Allah’s decree is predestined and thus must happen imposes a time constraint on Allah and we know that Allah does not live under time constraint. Therefore, you cannot speak of past, present, and future regarding Allah’s actions because all these are time dependent elements. Allah gave us the experience of not living under time constraint through our dreams that may last only for a minute but in our dream, it appears to last for years.

3. We also realize that the divine decree can be avoided since the Prophet (PBUH) said:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يرد القضاء إلا الدعاء ولا يزيد في العمر إلا البر. )رواه أحمد والترمذي وابن ماجه والحاكم(

“Nothing repels Divine Decree except Du’a, and nothing increases one’s life-span except righteousness (good deeds)” [Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim]

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : (لا يزال القضاء والدعاء يعتلجان ما بين الأرض والسماء فأيهما غلب أصاب ). ومعنى (يعتلجان) أي: يتصارعان.

“The Dua and the divine decree meet each other between heaven and earth and continue preventing each other from moving until one of them wins and whoever wins, its impact will happen.”

There are verses in the Quran that suggest that the divine decree can change based on certain divine rules and these include Dua and Charity. Allah says:

يَمۡحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثۡبِتُ‌ۖ وَعِندَهُ ۥۤ أُمُّ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ (٣٩)

“Allah erases what He wills and affirms what He wills and with Him is the Mother Book.” (Al-Rad 13:39)

هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَى أَجَلًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ) الأنعام(

He is the One Who created you from clay, and then decreed a stated term (for you). And there is another determined term with Him; yet you are in doubt.” (Al-An’am 6:2)

These verses suggest that Allah decreed two things depending on the people’s behavior.

Also, Allah refuted the claim by anyone that the problem he faced is a decree from Allah, as He said:

وَقَالُوا لَوْ شَاءَ الرَّحْمَنُ مَا عَبَدْنَاهُمْ مَا لَهُمْ بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ ) سورة الزخرف (

“And they said: “Had the Rahman so willed, we should not have worshipped them (the false deities).” They have no knowledge whatsoever of that. They do nothing but lie.” (Al-Zughruf 43:20)

4. One of the challenges with the divine decree is that we ignore that Allah’s knowledge, power and authority are infinite and thus argument that are made for finite properties do not hold. As example, If I say that X + Y = X +Z, you will directly expect that Y =Z but this is only true if the value of X is finite. But if X is infinite, there is no reason for Y to be equal to Z. Therefore, any analytical model will fail when it involves Allah’s infinite attributes. So, if I say:

Divine authority + Decree = Divine authority + Fulfillment

We cannot conclude that decree equals fulfillment because the divine authority is infinite.

5. But a key issue that we must keep in mind is that when Allah or the Prophet (PBUH) warns us of a disaster that will happen in the future, it must be for our benefit to either make plans and take actions to avoid it or at least to not participant in creating the disaster or suffering from it.

Now, let us examine some of the foretold history that the Prophet (PBUH) warned the companion from. It is reported by Imam Ahmad that Hud hifa said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

روى الإمام أحمد عن حذيفة: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: تكون النبوة فيكم ما شاء الله أن تكون، ثم يرفعها الله إذا شاء أن يرفعها، ثم تكون خلافة على منهاج النبوة فتكون ما شاء الله أن تكون، ثم يرفعها الله إذا شاء أن يرفعها، ثم تكون ملكًا عاضًا فيكون ما شاء الله أن يكون، ثم يرفعها إذا شاء الله أن يرفعها، ثم تكون ملكًا جبرية فتكون ما شاء الله أن تكون، ثم يرفعها الله إذا شاء أن يرفعها، ثم تكون خلافة على منهاج النبوة، ثم سكت) وروى الحديث أيضًا الطيالسي والبيهقي، والطبري(

“Prophethood will be among you as long as Allah intends, and then Allah will take it away if He so wills.

Then there will be a caliphate according to the prophetic method. It will be among you as long as Allah intends, and then Allah will take it away if He so wills.

Then there will be a mordacious monarchy (taken by corrosive style). It will be among you as long as Allah intends, and then Allah will take it away if He so wills.

Then there will be a tyrannical monarchy. It will be among you as long as Allah intends, and then Allah will take it away if He so wills.

Then there will be a caliphate in accordance with the prophetic method. And the Prophet stopped” (Ahmad, Baihaqi and Tabari)

According to this hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) specified the four governing phases for Muslims after he passes away. Two of these phases are good and Muslims must always seek to preserve them and two are bad and Muslims must seek to prevent them and get rid of them if they occur.

The first good governing phase is the one that follows the death of the Prophet (PBUH), and this is something that early Muslims should have directed their efforts to protect it. But this just system failed because of Muslims’ division and in-fighting, The following two systems will be monarchy form of government with progressive tyranny. Muslims who live during these two phases must work hard to minimize their rein to allow for the fourth phase to come.

To give the Muslims even greater warning, the Prophet (PBUH) informed them of the time at which they should be doubly careful because it is the time at which they are at the highest risk of destroying the prophetically based system of government. This time will be near the 30th year after the death of the Prophet (PBUH). The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن سَفِينَةُ رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: الْخِلاَفَةُ فِي أُمّتِي ثَلاَثُونَ سَنَةً، ثُمّ مُلْكٌ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ.. )رواه أحمد (

“The Caliphate according to the Prophetic method will last 30 years and after it will be monarchy”. (Ahmad)

In the previous hadith, the Prophet warned of the monarchy that will be obtained by force and it will progressively get tyrannical. When we examine what happens, we note that Umayyad rule started exactly on the 30th year after the death of the Prophet (PBUH) and it was monarchy that was obtained by force. It continued since then and we may be now living under tyrannically systems of government.

The 30 years of prophetic based system of government was as follows:

Abu Bakr ruled over the righteous Caliphate from 632-634 CE (2 years) (11-13H)
Omar ruled over the righteous Caliphate from 634 to 644 (10 years) (13-23 H)
Uthman ibn Affan ruled over the righteous Caliphate from 644-656 CE. (12 years) (23-35 H)
Ali ruled over the righteous Caliphate from 656 to 661 CE (5 years) (35-40H)
Hasan was the caliph for 7 months before he surrendered his control of Iraq in Rabi II 41 (August 661) to Muawiya who transformed the system into a monarchy system.

The Umayyad ruled from 661 to 750 CE (89 years), (41 – 132H)
The Abbasid ruled from 750 – 1258 CE (508 years) (132 – 656 H)
The Ottomans ruled from 1299 to 1922 (623 years) and the Khalifa ended in 1924. This followed by the occupation of all the Muslim world in the Middle East and establishing dictatorships that continue until now.

There are several other hadith that gave more details about specific conflicts that led to the assignation of Khalifa Omar, Uthman, and Ali.

There is another Hadith that gives details on the great tribulation that will face the Muslims and thus we must heed since these tribulations may be in our time now. The hadith is narrated by Abdullah ibn Omar who said:

روى أبو داود وأحمد عن عبد الله بن عمر يقول: كُنَّا قُعُودًا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ فَذَكَرَ الْفِتَنَ فَأَكْثَرَ فِي ذِكْرِهَا حَتَّى ذَكَرَ فِتْنَةَ الْأَحْلَاسِ فَقَالَ قَائِلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا فِتْنَةُ الْأَحْلَاسِ قَالَ هِيَ هَرَبٌ وَحَرْبٌ ثُمَّ فِتْنَةُ السَّرَّاءِ دَخَنُهَا مِنْ تَحْتِ قَدَمَيْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ مِنِّي وَلَيْسَ مِنِّي وَإِنَّمَا أَوْلِيَائِي الْمُتَّقُونَ ثُمَّ يَصْطَلِحُ النَّاسُ عَلَى رَجُلٍ كَوَرِكٍ عَلَى ضِلَعٍ ثُمَّ فِتْنَةُ الدُّهَيْمَاءِ لَا تَدَعُ أَحَدًا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ إِلَّا لَطَمَتْهُ لَطْمَةً فَإِذَا قِيلَ انْقَضَتْ تَمَادَتْ يُصْبِحُ الرَّجُلُ فِيهَا مُؤْمِنًا وَيُمْسِي كَافِرًا حَتَّى يَصِيرَ النَّاسُ إِلَى فُسْطَاطَيْنِ فُسْطَاطِ إِيمَانٍ لَا نِفَاقَ فِيهِ وَفُسْطَاطِ نِفَاقٍ لَا إِيمَانَ فِيهِ فَإِذَا كَانَ ذَاكُمْ فَانْتَظِرُوا الدَّجَّالَ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ أَوْ مِنْ غَدِهِ

When we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he talked about periods of tribulations (fitan), mentioning many of them. Of what he mentioned is “Fitnat Al-Ahlas” (فِتْنَةَ الْأَحْلَاسِ).

Some asked him: Messenger of Allah, what is “Fitnat Al-Ahlas”

The Prophet (PBUH) said: It will be fight and flight.

Then there will come “Fitnat Al-Sara’a (فِتْنَةُ السَّرَّاءِ). Its murkiness is due to the fact that it is produced by a man from the people of my house (Ahl Al-Bayt), who will assert that he belongs to me, whereas he does not, for my ahl (family) are only those who have Taqwa (God-fearing).

Then the people will unite under a man who will be like a hipbone on a rib (unfit).

Then there will be “Fitanat Al-Duhima’a” (فِتْنَةُ الدُّهَيْمَاءِ) which will leave none of this community without impacting (giving him a slap), and when people say that it is finished, it will be extended. During it a man will be a believer in the morning and an infidel in the evening, so that the people will be in two camps: the camp of the faithful who have no hypocrisy, and the camp of hypocrites who have no faith. When this ends, expect the Antichrist (Dajjal) in a day or two.

The first Fitnah “Fitnat Al-Ahlas” (فِتْنَةَ الْأَحْلَاسِ) has apparently passed with the conflicts in history between Ali and Muawiya and between the Ummayd and the Abassi and all the other wars in between until the Ottoman rule.

The second Fitnat: Fitnat Al-Sara’a (ثفِتْنَةُ السَّرَّاءِ) is one that started by one of the people from the house of the Prophet. From the name this fitnah it was deceiving because it was led by a man from the house of the Prophet on the promise of that it will bring happiness to the Muslims. But is resulted in an evil outcome, The Prophet (PBUH) rejected the relationship with this man and asserted that the people of his house are only the righteous and not merely because of lineage. This fitnah has apparently passed because it started by one from the house of the Prophet and it led to the destruction of the Ottoman khilafa and the occupation of many Muslim countries.

This fitnah was led by Sharif Hussein ibn Ali who was plotting with the British to break the Ottoman rule on the Arab world on the promise that he will be declared as the khalifa. This fitnah became apparent with the Arab Revolt that began in June 1916 when Sharif Hussein publicly proclaimed the revolt in Mecca. His forces seized the city defeating the Ottoman garrison and one of his sons besieged the town of Ta’if and his other two sons attacked the Ottoman garrison in Medina.

The plot to break the Ottoman rule started when Lieutenant Colonel Sir Henry McMahon (مكماهون), the British High Commissioner to Egypt started sending letters to Sharif Hussein informing him that the king of England wants the Khliafa to return to a pure Arab from the blessed house of the Prophet. Obviously, none of the promises that McMahon made to the naïve Sharif Hussein was fulfilled. In fact the opposite happened through the Sykes–Picot Agreement between the British and the French and the Balfour Declaration that granted the Jews Palestine. While the Arabs lost everything, the British gained victory over the Ottoman because the Arabs refused to support the Ottoman army in the first world war and started campaigns against it. This led to the defeat of the Ottoman army and the destruction of the Ottoman khilafa and deposing the khalifa and replacing him with the Turkish field marshal Kamal Atatürk who served as Turkey’s president from 1923 to 1938. During his rule, Turkey was transformed into a secular republic.

All this is history, what is of concern to us now in the third Fitnah, “Fitanat Al-Duhima’a” (فِتْنَةُ الدُّهَيْمَاءِ) that we appear to be in its midst. This Fitnah will be widespread. It will leave no one but impacts him. This fitnah will not end until people’ belief is fully tested and will split the Muslims into two groups, a group of hypocrites who have no belief and a group of believers who have no hypocrisy.

When this Fitnah ends, the anti-Christ will rise.

We pray to Allah to protect us from this tribulation and help us strengthening our belief that we remain steadfast on our belief.

DUa

The One Lesson from the Story of Prophet Ibrahim

content:
The One Lesson from the Story of Prophet Ibrahim

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

The story of Prophet Ibrahim is probably the most important story in the Quran because based on it we can derive the most important attribute in our religion. Allah emphasized in seven verses in the Quran that Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and us follow the religion of Ibrahim (مِّلَّةِ إِبۡرَٲهِـۧمَ). This emphasis is in verse 130 and 135 of Surat Al-Baqarah, verse 95 in Surat Al-Emran, verse 125 in Surat Al-Nisa, verse 161 in Surat Al-An'am, verse 123 in Surat Al-Nahl and in verse 78 in Surat Al-Hajj. As examples, Allah says:

وَقَالُواْ ڪُونُواْ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَـٰرَىٰ تَہۡتَدُواْ‌ۗ قُلۡ بَلۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٲهِـۧمَ حَنِيفً۬ا‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِڪِينَ (١٣٥)

“They say: “Become Jews or Christians and you will be guided.” Say: “Nay! but (we follow) the religion of Ibrahim, the upright, and he was not of the idolators.” (Al-Baqara 2:135)

ثُمَّ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ أَنِ ٱتَّبِعۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ حَنِيفً۬ا‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِڪِينَ (١٢٣)

“And We revealed to you; follow the religion of Ibrahim, the upright, and he was not of the idolaters.” (Al-Nahl 16:123)

When we study the story of Prophet Ibrahim in the Quran, we realize the dominant theme which is his total submission to the commands of Allah even when they are beyond any human comprehension. Every day we make at least 17 times a specific declaration to Allah that “we worship no one but Him” (إِيَّاكَ نَعۡبُدُ) as we read Surat Al-Fatiha.

What is the most dominant feature of worshiping Allah? It should be the most dominant feature of the actions of Prophet Ibrahim which is complete obedience to Allah, and this is the religion of Ibrahim, and this is the essence of our declaration that “we worship no one but Allah”.

Obeying the command of anyone including your own self, over Allah’s command is not only an act of shirk but it is also an act of kufr. Kufr does not necessarily mean being atheist or agnostic, it means rejecting Allah’s command because it does not suit your own desires or interests. The best example of a person who never associated anything with Allah, but Allah declared him a kafir, a disbeliever, is Iblis (Satan). All Satan did is to reject a command from Allah because he did not like it. Allah says:

فَسَجَدَ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ ڪُلُّهُمۡ أَجۡمَعُونَ (٧٣) إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ (٧٤)

“The angels prostrated themselves, everyone, (73) Except Iblis (Satan); he showed arrogance and became one of the disbelievers.” (Sad 38:73-74)

Allah also warned us from worshipping Satan, as He said:

أَلَمۡ أَعۡهَدۡ إِلَيۡكُمۡ يَـٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ أَن لَّا تَعۡبُدُواْ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنَ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوٌّ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (٦٠) وَأَنِ ٱعۡبُدُونِى‌ۚ هَـٰذَا صِرَٲطٌ۬ مُّسۡتَقِيمٌ۬ (٦١)

“Did I not order on you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan; for that he is an open enemy for you? (60) “And that you should worship Me, (because) this is the straight path?” (Yasin 36:60-61)

Worshiping Iblis does not mean that we will consider him as the creator, but our worshiping him is by obeying his commands.

In this talk, I plan to inshallah remind us of the nature of Allah’s obedience that He expects from us and provided for us the story of Prophet Ibrahim as a living example of true worship that we need to follow.

When Allah saved Ibrahim from the fire and from the King in Iraq, he emigrated from Iraq to Syria (الشام) and said: “ إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ”، “I am going to my Lord and He will guide me” (Al-Saffat 37:99). Since he grew old and did not have any children, he supplicated to Allah to grant him a son by saying: “رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ” “God gave me from the righteous” (Al-Saffat 37:100), Allah answered his prayers and “gave him the good news that he will have a forbearing son” “فَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِغُلَامٍ حَلِيمٍ” (Al-Saffat 37:101).

This boy was Prophet Ibrahim’s first born from his wife Hajar and he named him Ismael that means “God hears my Dua”. You can imagine the degree of happiness of Prophet Ibrahim with his son. But, soon after the birth of the child, Allah subjected Prophet Ibrahim to very severe trial to test his level of obedience and to set him as an example to all who will follow him on what is expected from them when they hear a command from Allah. Yes, Prophet Ibrahim faced several trials before when he was young, but anyone who has children realizes that the worst of the trials is when it impacts the children, particularly for a person who was blessed with a child at very old age. Allah commanded Prophet Ibrahim to take his only and infant son and his mother (Hajr) and leave them in the desert of Arabia, a place that is far away from where he lives; a place where there are no people, no water, and no food.

Can you imagine the emotion of prophet Ibrahim and the level of sadness and fear when he was leaving his son and his wife after he placed them in this place, Mecca? You need to measure your best level of trust in Allah with the level of trust of the wife, Sayeda Hajar, when she said: “If Allah commanded you, Allah will not cause us to be lost.” By these words, she was comforting her husband by saying “don’t worry about us, we will be fine”; obviously her heart must have been full of fear and worry if not for herself but at least for her infant son.

As the time passed, prophet Ibrahim used to visit his wife and his son Ismael in Mecca. Ismael was growing to become a handsome boy. When Ismael was at the age of say 10 to 12 that his father can walk with him and have meaningful discussion with him, Allah subjected Prophet Ibrahim to the most difficult trial that no human being can bear to demonstrate to us by real example the level of obedience that Allah expects from his slaves.

The test of obedience was to command Ibrahim to slaughter his only son and not only that, but Allah sent the command as a vision and not as a direct communication with Prophet Ibrahim. Yes, Prophet Ibrahim knew that the vision of the Prophets represents a revelation. But this vision of him slaughtering his son is very distressing. We can speculate on what was going in his mind, is this really a command from Allah or just a dream. While he knew that a vision of Prophets is revelations from Allah, doubts can come, and Satan surely would have been playing on Prophet’s Ibrahim emotion to reject the vision. Prophet Ibrahim had no choice but to tell his young son Ismael whom Allah described as (غلام حليم) (Al-Saffat 37:101); this attribute “Haleem” means sweat, soft patient, gentle, tolerant, and forbearing. With these beautiful attributes of Ismael, you can imagine the level of love prophet Ibrahim has for him.

So, Prophet Ibrahim told his son of his vison by saying:

قَالَ يَـٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ‌ۚ

“O my son! I have seen in my sleep that I am slaughtering you, so look what you think!” (Al-Saffat 37:102)

It may be that Prophet Ibrahim was hoping that his son may offer different interpretation of the vision or question whether this vision is a real command from Allah, but Ismael who is all aware that a vison of a prophet is a revelation from Allah, instantly understood that it is a command from Allah and without any hesitation he told his father “ O my dear father, do what you have been commanded and by the will of Allah I’ll be patient.” (يَـٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُ‌ۖ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ) (Al-Saffat 37:102)

Even at his young age, Ismael felt that his father is tormented by what he is commanded to do, therefore his response was comforting and firm. He addressed his father by my dear father and assured him that his vison is a command from Allah and comforted him that he will be patient.

We know what happened next, Allah acknowledged Ibrahim’s fulfillment of the command that Allah classified as major trial and then ransomed Ismael with an animal sacrifice as Allah informed us in Surat Al-Saffat

قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآ‌ۚ إِنَّا كَذَٲلِكَ نَجۡزِى ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (١٠٥) إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلۡبَلَـٰٓؤُاْ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (١٠٦) وَفَدَيۡنَـٰهُ بِذِبۡحٍ عَظِيمٍ۬ (١٠٧) وَتَرَڪۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرِينَ (١٠٨)

You have fulfilled the dream!” This is how we reward the good doers. (105) Indeed, this was a manifest trial. (106) And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice; (107) And We left for him (a word of praise) among the later generations. (Al-Saffat 37:104-108)

The last verse (وَتَرَڪۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرِينَ) gave the good news to Prophet Ibrahim that his obedience to Allah’s command will bring great praise for him by later generation. This promise is being fulfilled by Muslims all over the world each time, they say:

اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم ، اللهم بارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم

O Allah, pray on Muhammad and the “A’al” (آل) of Mohammad” as You prayed on Ibrahim and the ‘A’al” of Ibrahim. And grant Blessings to Muhammad and the “A’al” of Mohammad as You granted blessings to Ibrahim and the “A’al” of Ibrahim.

It is interesting to note the attribute that Allah emphasized for the two sons of Prophet Ibrahim, Ismael and Ishaq.

* For Ismael, Allah said:” فَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهُ بِغُلَـٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ۬ (١٠١) “We gave him the good news of a (Haleem) forbearing son” (Al-Saffat 37:101).
* For Ishaq, Allah said: (قَالُواْ لَا تَوۡجَلۡ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَـٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ۬ (٥٣)) “They said: “Have no fear, we give the give the good news of a (Aleamm) knowledgeable boy.” (Al-Hijr 15:53)

Note the difference, the trial of sacrifice needed a son who is Haleem, sweat, soft patient, gentle, tolerant, and forbearing more than a son who is knowledgeable and wise because Allah’s commands don’t require technical analysis on why, but they require obedience whether the purpose is understood or not.

True belief in Allah means surrendering to His authority as our Master and acknowledging that we are His slaves, and this can only be demonstrated by full obedience. Surrender to Allah means that you obey Allah’s command even if it does not make sense to you. There is no way that you call Allah your Lord when you refuse to obey Him. Allah is not interested in half-hearted commitment or partial obedience.

Although the commands given to Prophet Ibrahim, were very difficult to imagine, at the end no harm was done to him, his wife, and his son. Rather, they received great blessings from Allah. As a result of the command of taking Hajar and the infant Ismael to Mecca a new nation was formed whose members are the only ones today who declare the oneness and glory of Allah and pray for Prophet Ibrahim at least 5 times every day. Out of the command to sacrifice his only son Ismael comes the greatest annual ritual that the world witness which is the Hajj in Mecca and the Eid of Sacrifice commemorating the whole episode of the sacrifice. Also, the ritual of Hajj involves an enactment of what Prophet Ibrahim did to Satan by stoning him when he tried his best to prevent Prophet Ibrahim from following the command of Allah to perform the sacrifice.

In addition, after Prophet Ibrahim passed the test of the major command of sacrificing his son Ismael, Allah gave him the great news that his second wife Sarah will have for him a second son and his name will be Ishaq (Isaac) and Allah will appoint him as prophet. Allah said after the account of the episode of the sacrifice:

وَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهُ بِإِسۡحَـٰقَ نَبِيًّ۬ا مِّنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (١١٢)

And We gave him the good news of Ishaq (Isaac) a Prophet from among the righteous.” (Al-Saffat 37:112)

Not only that but this new son whose name Ishaq (Isaac) will live and get married and will have a son whose name will be Yaqoob (Jacob). So, prophet Ibrahim was not only given the good news that he will have a second son, but he was also given the good news that he will be a grandfather as Allah says in Surat Hud:

فَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهَا بِإِسۡحَـٰقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسۡحَـٰقَ يَعۡقُوبَ (٧١)

“We gave her (Sarah) the good news (of the birth) of Ishaq (Isaac), and Yaqub (Jacob) after Ishaq.” (Hud 11:71)

The Quran gives us many examples of the full obedience that Allah expects from His prophets and their followers. But the most compelling example is that of Prophet Ibrahim. Not only him but the submission of his wife Hajar and his young son Ismael to Allah’s commands are clear examples for us. The story of Prophet Ibrahim gives us a very important lesson that we must learn. By the grace of Allah, none of Allah’s commands to us rise to the level of the commands that Prophet Ibrahim received but his story should remain in our mind each time we become lax in fulfilling one of Allah’s commands.

The story of Prophet Ibrahim should also serve as lessons to the wives and the children that they should be a source of help to the father to fulfill Allah’s command and not be a hindrance. They need to heed Allah’s warning that even your family members can be enemies when they try to hinder your state of full obedience to Allah, Allah says:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٲجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَـٰدِڪُمۡ عَدُوًّ۬ا لَّڪُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡ‌ۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ (١٤) إِنَّمَآ أَمۡوَٲلُڪُمۡ وَأَوۡلَـٰدُڪُمۡ فِتۡنَةٌ۬‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُ ۥۤ أَجۡرٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١٥)

“O you who believe! Truly, among your wives and your children are (some that are) enemies to yourselves: So, beware of them! But if ye forgive and overlook and cover up (their faults), verily Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (14) Your riches and your children may be but a trial: but in the Presence of Allah is the highest Reward.” (Al-Taghabun 64:14-15)

It should be settled based on the Quran and the seerah and the rituals of Hajj that are performed in Mecca by the Arabs before Islam and by all Muslims after Islam for thousands of years that the son whom Allah commanded prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice is the first-born son, Ismael. Unfortunately, some early interpreters used a confusing statement in the Old Testament to suggest that the one who was intended for the sacrifice is the 2nd son Ishaq. This account was introduced by a chief Rabbi from Yemen who became Muslim after the Prophet’s death and moved to Madina during the rule of Khalifa Omar and became very influential, his name is Ka’b al-Aḥbār (كعب الأحبار). The account that mentions Isaaq is in Genesis 22:

“Sometime later God tested Abraham. He said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he replied. 2 Then God said, “Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you.” (Genesis 22:1-2)

You don’t need any serious analysis to know that the name Isaac was just added, so the Jews can take credit for the account, though it is very clear that Isaac was never the only son of Prophet Ibrahim by simple review of other statements in Old Testament. The following are relevant ones:

1. Ishmael was born to Prophet Ibrahim when he was 86 years Old: “And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne. Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael. (Genesis 16:15-16))
2. Isaac was born when Prophet Ibrahim was 100 years old and thus Ishmael was 14 years old: “Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him”. (Genesis 21:5)
3. For 14 years, Ishmael was the only son that Prophet Ibrahim has. So, Isaac cannot be the only son for Prophet Ibrahim unless Ishmael died before Prophet Ibrahim. But this did not happen because according to the Old Testament, Prophet Ibrahim died at the age of 175 years, and he was buried by his two sons Ishmael and Isaac: “Abraham lived a hundred and seventy-five years. Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man and full of years; and he was gathered to his people. His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him”. (Genesis 25:7-9) according to the bible Ishmael died at the age of 137 years, i.e., 48 years after his father)

So, based on the Old Testament’s historical accounts of ages, it is impossible that the command of sacrifice be applied to Isaac because he was never the only son. The sequence of events that I presented clearly indicate that the sacrifice can only be applied to Ishmael because Isaac was not even born.

To merely justify that Isaac is the one intended for sacrifice, it is unfortunate that some interpreters were willing to suggested that after Prophet Ibrahim made his supplication to Allah for a son, the series of verses in Surat Al-Saffat went as follows:

1. Verse 101: So, We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy (فَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهُ بِغُلَـٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ۬).
2. Verses 102 to 111 give the account of the sacrifice and the praise of Ibrahim.
3. Verse 112: And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet (وَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهُ بِإِسۡحَـٰقَ نَبِيًّ۬ا).

They suggest that verse 101 and verse 112 refer to the same child. This is absolutely wrong for several reasons:

1. It attributes to the Quran redundancy and poor style that is not befitting for the divine speech of the Quran.
2. The first good news in verse 101 refers to the first son in fulfillment of Prophet Ibrahim Dua in verse 100 (رَبِّ هَبۡ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ)
3. The first good news was for a son whose attribute is Haleem (حَلِيمٍ۬) and this is the key attribute of Ishmael, while the key attribute of Ishaq was Knowledgeable (عَلِيمٍ۬).
4. Linguistically the use of “and” in verse 112 (And We gave him the good news) directly means that this good news is different from the first one in verse 101. In addition, since Allah gave the good news that Ishaq will be a prophet, it would make no sense that Ibrahim will be ordered to sacrifice him.
5. This last point is emphasized in Surat Hud, when Allah gave the good news that Sarah will have son whose name is Ishaq and Ishaq will have a son who name is Yaqub (Jacob). So, it makes no sense that Allah will ask Ibrahim to sacrifice him, when Ibrahim already knew that he would have to live and get married and have a son called Jacob.

Someone may say but why Allah did not mention Ismael in this account, the reason is simple, the Quran is a book that requires you to think and when the information is obvious, it is not mentioned. Also, the Quran is not a linear book as humans write, it requires Tadabour by assembling all the verses related to the topic of interest and harmonizing them to gain a clear understanding.

There are several other proofs that Prophet Ismael who was the one intended for the sacrifice. As example, the horns of the ram that Allah sent to Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice were always hung in the Kabba. It was Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) who ordered them to be removed to avoid them from distracting the worshipper. And it is clear that Prophet Ibrahim and Ismael were the ones who built the Kabba in Mecca while Ishaq was in Syria.

We mentioned that many rituals of the Hajj in Mecca are an enactment of the sacrifice account, and these rituals are not only done by Muslims, but they were done by the Arabs before Islam. If it was Ishaq, don’t you think that the Jews would have made this a great ritual for them.

Another account that is reported in Al-Hakim that was narrated by Muawiya:

حديث الحاكم عن معاوية بعدم إنكار الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على من ناداه بابن الذبيحين ، كما يؤيدها ما روى عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم من قوله ” أنا ابن الذبيحين “.

The Prophet (PBUH) did not object when people called him the son of the two sacrifices. And in another account that the Prophet (PBUH) called himself with that name. (This was referring the sacrifice of prophet Ismael who was ransomed by a heavenly ram and the sacrifice of the Prophet’s father Abdullah who was ransomed with 100 camels).

Ataa ibn Abu Rabbah (عطاء بن أبي رباح) reported that Ibn Abbas said:

عن عطاء بن أبي رباح ، عن ابن عباس أنه قال : المفدي إسماعيل ، وزعمت اليهود أنه إسحاق وكذبت اليهود

“The one who is intended for the sacrifice is Ismael and the Jews claim that he is Ishaq but the Jews are lying”.

Also, Abu Amr ibn Al-Alaa (أبو عمرو بن العلاء) (D: 154H) who is one the seven primary transmitters of the chain of reciters of the Quran and a great Arabic linguist, was asked by a person about the one who was sacrificed, and his response was:

وكان أبو عمرو بن العلاء قد سأله عبد الملك بن قريب الأصمعى عن الذبيح، فقال له: أين ذهب عقلك ؟ متى كان إسحاق بمكة؟ إنما كان إسماعيل بمكة وهو الذى بنى البيت مع أبيه والمنحر بمكة.

How can you ask such a question! Ismael was in Mecca, and he is the one who built the Kabba with his father and the place of sacrifice is in Mecca. When was Ishaq ever in Mecca!

There are 7 mutawatir qira’at Nafi’ (d. 169/785), Ibn Kathir (d. 120/737), Abu ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ala’ (d. 154/762), Ibn ‘Amir (d. 154/762), ‘Asim (d. 127/744), Hamza (d. 156/772), al-Kisa’i (d. 189/904)

There is another issue that is also false due to misinterpreting the verse in the Quran when using the biblical account that prophet Ibrahim prayed for the people of Lot because he had compassion for them. Allah says in Surat Hud:

فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنۡ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ ٱلرَّوۡعُ وَجَآءَتۡهُ ٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰ يُجَـٰدِلُنَا فِى قَوۡمِ لُوطٍ (٧٤) إِنَّ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّٲهٌ۬ مُّنِيبٌ۬ (٧٥) يَـٰٓإِبۡرَٲهِيمُ أَعۡرِضۡ عَنۡ هَـٰذَاۤ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥ قَدۡ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ رَبِّكَ‌ۖ وَإِنَّہُمۡ ءَاتِيهِمۡ عَذَابٌ غَيۡرُ مَرۡدُودٍ۬ (٧٦)

“And when the fear left Abraham, and the good news came to him (about the birth of Ishaq), he started disputing with Us for the people of Lot. (74) Indeed, Ibrahim is forbearing very penitent, ever turning to Allah. (75) (It was said) O Abraham! Leave it. The command of your Lord has come to pass, and there has to come upon them a punishment that cannot be averted.” (Hud 11:74-76)

The question is: what was prophet Ibrahim disputing with the angels about regarding the people of Lot? Prophet Ibrahim had no objection for Allah’s decree to destroy the people who were committing the great sin among the people of Prophet Lot, he was only concerned about the believers among them. Accusing Prophet Ibrahim of praying for the people who committed that grave sin results from misinterpretation of Genesis 18:16-33 in the Old Testament. Even the biblical interpreters write that Abraham’s prayer was only for Lot and his family.

This account of Prophet’s Ibrahim dispute with the angels is presented as follows by many early interpreters such as: Qatada (d. 118 H), Al-Sady (127 H), Ibn Ishaq (d. 150 H), Ibn Jurayi (150H)

عن قتادة و عن السدي و عن ابن إسحاق و ابن جريج و أبو المثنى ومسلم أبو الحبيل الأشجعي

When the angles told Ibrahim that they are going to destroy the people of lot, he said: How can you destroy them and there are 100 believers among them.

The angels said: if there are 100 believers they will not be destroyed.

So, Prophet Ibrahim realized that they must be less than 100, so he said: How can you destroy them if there are 50 believers among them.

They said, if there 50 believers among them, they will not be destroyed.

He said: How can you destroy them if there are 10 believers among them.

They said, if there 10 believers among them, they will not be destroyed.

Then they said: Ibrahim, stop the argument, a city that does not even have 10 righteous people is not worthy of being saved from Allah’s wrath. Ibrahim, there are only 3 believers in only one family, and they will be saved.

To Conclude, let us focus on the main lesson from the story of Prophet Ibrahim that represents the foundation of our religion which is complete obedience of Allah’s commands even if we don’t understand their purpose.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom and to help us with the commitment to follow all His command without any hesitation or procrastination.

DUA

title: If You Are Insect and Tree; Which Ones would you Be?
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In past talks, I proposed that the reason for the “Decline of Muslims” is their failure to taken advantage of the outstanding teaching tool that Allah embedded in the Quran to expand the cognitive capacity of the Muslims.

In one of these talks, I discussed a metric that Allah has set in the Quran to assess our level of knowledge and the ability to use our brain. This metric is based on measuring the level of understanding of the “Amthal” which can be translated as similitudes, parables, and metaphors. Allah says regarding the use of these Amthal:

وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ ۖ وَمَا يَعْقِلُهَا إِلَّا الْعَالِمُونَ (٤٣)
“And these “Amthal” We put forward for mankind, but none understands them except the knowledgeable.” (Al-Ankabut 29:43)

وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّـهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
“Allah sets forth “Amthal” for the people in order that they may take lesson.” (Ibrahim 14:25)

وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٢١)
“Such are “Amthal” that We set forth to the people so that they may reflect.” (Al-Hashr 59:21)

In the process of developing the character of early Muslims, the Prophet (PBUH) also used the Amthal, the similitudes, to teach his companions the character of a true believer. In this talk, I'll inshallah present two of these similitudes. In one similitude the prophet (PBUH) compared the true believer with a specific insect and in the second he compared him with a specific tree.

I encourage you to measure your character against these two similitudes. This is important because many Muslims just slog through life without examining their level of belief which is the engine that drives their behavior and shapes their character. Auditing our own belief to identify the needed improvements should be an essential part of our journey to attain the higher level of belief and to develop the most perfect character. After all, the Prophet (PBUH) summarized the exclusive purpose of his mission by saying:

“إنّما بُعثت لأُتمم مكارم الأخلاق”
“I haven’t been sent except to perfect the noble manners.”

Understanding this key purpose of the religion of Islam, the great Hanbali Imam “Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (ابن قيم الجوزية) (1292 CE – 1350 CE / 691 AH – 751 AH) summarized the religion of Islam by saying:

الدّين كله خُلق ، فمن فاقَك في الخلق ،فاقَك في الدّين.
All the religion is good character, so whoever surpasses you in good character surpasses you in religion.

To teach the companions an example of good character, the Prophet gave the similitude of a perfect believer with a bee. Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

في مسند الإمام أحمد عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : “وَالَّذِي نَفْسُ ‏ ‏مُحَمَّدٍ ‏ ‏بِيَدِهِ إِنَّ مَثَلَ الْمُؤْمِنِ ‏ ‏لَكَمَثَلِ النَّحْلَةِ أَكَلَتْ طَيِّبًا وَوَضَعَتْ طَيِّبًا وَإِنْ وَقَعَتْ عَلَى عُودٍ نَخِرٍ لَمْ تَكْسِرْهُ .”
“By the One in whose hand is my soul, the believer is like a bee that only eats that which is pure and wholesome and produces that which is pure and wholesome, and when it lands on a weak branch it does not break it.” [Ahmad, Al-Baihaqi]

The Prophet (PBUH) mentioned three qualities of the Bee that should be key qualities of the true believer.

1/ The first quality is that the bees don’t land on anything they find, they are very selective and only land and eat from the best flowers. They pick the best flower by sensing its sweetness and scent. A true believer does not engage in any business, he only chooses businesses that are pure, lawful, and legal. He is very careful not to feed himself and his family except of what is pure and healthy. For the true believer, everything he takes as sustenance for his body and mind; the food he eats, the money he earns, the books he reads, the sounds he listens, are pure and wholesome. Abu Huraira (RA) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

فعَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: ” أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، إِنَّ اللهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا، وَإِنَّ اللهَ أَمَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ، فَقَالَ: {يَا أَيُّهَا الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا، إِنِّي بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ} [المؤمنون: 51] وَقَالَ: {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ} [البقرة: 172] ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ الرَّجُلَ يُطِيلُ السَّفَرَ أَشْعَثَ أَغْبَرَ، يَمُدُّ يَدَيْهِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ، يَا رَبِّ، يَا رَبِّ، وَمَطْعَمُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَشْرَبُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَلْبَسُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَغُذِيَ بِالْحَرَامِ، فَأَنَّى يُسْتَجَابُ لِذَلِكَ؟ ” رواه مسلم
“O people, Allah is pure, and He only accepts what is pure. Verily, Allah has commanded the believers as He has commanded His Messengers. Allah said: “O Messengers, eat from wholesome foods and act righteously, for I know what you do (Al-Munenoon 23:51). And Allah said: “O you who believe, eat from wholesome food We have provided for you,” (A-Baqara 2:172). Then, the Prophet (PBUH) mentioned a man who traveled far, becoming unruly and dusty and he raises his hands to the sky, saying, “O Lord! O Lord!” Yet his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished by the unlawful, so how can he be answered?” (Muslim)

2/ The second quality that the Prophet (PBUH) identified for the bee is that whatever it produces is good and the bee produces two things, both are very beneficial.

First, a bee excretes honey that is very beneficial for mankind as Allah said regarding bees:

ثُمَّ كُلِي مِن كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ فَاسْلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا ۚ يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِّلنَّاسِ ۗ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٦٩)
“Then eat from all the fruits and go along the pathways of your Lord that are made easy for you. There comes forth from their bellies a drink of various colors in which there is healing for mankind. Surely, in that there is assign for people who reflect.” (Al-Nahl 16:69)

A true believer must always be evaluating his contributions to the society and that he should always seek and engage in activities that produce something beneficial for the mankind. Whatever comes from a believer must be good, even when he speaks, his speech must be good and beneficial. Abu Hurairah narrated that the messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

روى الشيخان عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ
“Let him who believes in Allah and the Last Day either speak good or keep silent and let him who believes in Allah and the Last Day be generous to his neighbor and let him who believes in Allah and the Last Day be generous to his guest.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

Second, when a bee lands on the flowers to eat, it gives more than it takes. It transfers the pollen from one flower to another and this is how most plants have been capable of reproducing for millions of years. Therefore, a believer must always bring benefits and adds values to places where he gains some benefits. He must give more than he takes, and he must ensure the survival and growth of companies he is associated with.

A true believer will always be beneficial to others. Ibn Omar reported that a man came to the Prophet (PBUH) and asked: Who is the person most beloved to Allah and what deed is most beloved to Allah? The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن ابن عمر: أن رجلًا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: يا رسول الله، أي الناس أحب إلى الله؟ وأي الأعمال أحب إلى الله؟ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَحَبُّ النَّاسِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ، وَأَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ سُرُورٌ تُدْخِلُهُ عَلَى مُسْلِمٍ، أَوْ تَكْشِفُ عَنْهُ كُرْبَةً، أَوْ تَقْضِي عَنْهُ دَيْنًا، أَوْ تَطْرُدُ عَنْهُ جُوعًا، وَلَأَنْ أَمْشِيَ مَعَ أَخٍ لِي فِي حَاجَةٍ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أَعْتَكِفَ فِي هَذَا الْمَسْجِدِ، يَعْنِي مَسْجِدَ الْمَدِينَةِ، شَهْرًا، وَمَنْ كَفَّ غَضَبَهُ سَتَرَ اللَّهُ عَوْرَتَهُ، وَمَنْ كَظَمَ غَيْظَهُ، وَلَوْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُمْضِيَهُ أَمْضَاهُ مَلأَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ أَمْنًا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَمَنْ مَشَى مَعَ أَخِيهِ فِي حَاجَةٍ حَتَّى يُثْبِتَهَا لَهُ أَثْبَتَ اللَّهُ قَدَمَهُ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ يَوْمَ تَزِلُّ فِيهِ الْأَقْدَامُ» المعجم الأوسط للطبراني
“The most beloved person to Allah is the one who is most beneficial to people. The most beloved deed to Allah is to bring happiness to a Muslim, or to remove one of his difficulties, or to forgive his debt, or to feed his hunger. If I would walk with a brother regarding a need is more beloved to me than secluding myself in this mosque (in Medina) for a month. Whoever swallows his anger, Allah will conceal his faults. Whoever suppresses his rage, even though he could fulfill his anger if he wished, Allah will secure his heart on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever walks with his brother regarding a need until he secures it for him, Allah Almighty will make his footing firm across the bridge on the day when the footings are shaken.” (Al-Tabarani)

3/ The third quality of the bee is that when it lands on a branch, no matter how weak, it will never break it. The bee is light and nimble and does not harm the delicate petals of the flower. True believer should be gentle and kind in all his dealings, he does not harm or destroy any human, animal, or plant that he interacts with. Allah says regarding true believers:

وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا [سورة الفرقان:63]
“The slaves of the Beneficent are those who walk upon the earth humbly, and when the foolish ones address them, they reply: Peace” (Al-Furqan 25:63)

Like a bee, a true believer never hurt those whom he is associated with. Abdullah ibn Omar (عبد الله بن عمر) reported that Prophet (PBUH) said:

يقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما في الحديث الصحيح: «المُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ المُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ»
“The Muslim is the one Muslims are safe from his tongue and his hand”. (Bukhari)

This hadith is often interpreted to mean that a Muslim should not hurt or abuse other Muslims. But this is a narrow interpretation. The hadith means that a Muslim should never tarnish the honor or credibility of other Muslims even if he does not hurt them directly. If a Muslim hurts non-Muslims, his actions will implicate all Muslims and even implicate the religion of Islam and by this no Muslim will be safe from his actions. Therefore, the Prophet (PBUH) warned every Muslim about his responsibility to protect the image of Islam by saying:

أنت على ثغرة من ثغر الإسلام فلا يؤتين من قبلك ) ورد في الأثر(
“You are a guard at a gate in the fort of Islam don’t let Islam be attacked through your gate”.

Also, the bee is a light visitor at any flower, when the believer visits a friend, he should be light in his visits and never cause the host any burden or embarrassment. A believer always informs in advance whom he is visiting and select the time convenient for the person being visited and to never stretch his welcome. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ” زر غباً ، تزدد حباً ” [رواه الطبراني]
“Visit infrequently to be loved more.” (Tabarani)

There are many traits a believer can learn from the bee such as the dedication in her job. A bee flies tens of miles every day to fulfill its responsibility in the most perfect and efficient manner. But one very important trait of bees that is very essential for any Muslim community is unity.

A typical bee colony is made up of 30,000 – 50,000 honeybees living inside a self-constructed enclosure, every bee within the colony works for the good of the hive to help it function perfectly. Honeybees are interdependent, they rely on each other to create a working hive. Therefore, the unity of the bees is something that Muslims can learn from because it is an essential command from Allah who said:

(وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا) [آل عمران:103]
(وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا وَاخْتَلَفُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ ۚ وَأُولَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ) [آل عمران:105]
“And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of Allah, and do not be divided.” (Al-Emran 3: 103)
“And not be like those who became divided and fell int disputes after the clear proofs had come unto them. For such there is a grave punishment.” (Al-Emran 3:105)

Unity was something that the Prophet (PBUH) emphasized to his companions in many of his saying and informed then that the only mean for destroying the Muslim nation is the division within. The Prophet (PBUH) who said:

حديث ثوبان رضي الله عنه رواه الترمذي والنسائي و مسلم: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل ربه عزَّ وجلَّ ثلاث مسائل لأمته: الأولى: ألا يهلكهم بما أهلك به الأمم من الغرق والريح والرجفة وإلقاء الحجارة من السماء وغير ذلك من أنواع العذاب العظيم العام. والثانية: عدم ظهور عدو عليهم من غيرهم فيستبيح بيضتهم. والثالثة: عدم لبسهم الاختلاط والاختلاف بالأهواء، وقد أخبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ربه عزَّ وجلَّ تفضل عليه واستجاب له في الأوليين ومنعه الثالثة؛ لحكمة يعلمها تبارك وتعالى.
“I asked of my Lord, the Glorified and Exalted, three things; He granted me two, but refused me one. I asked my Lord not to destroy my nation with that with which He destroyed the nations before us, and He granted me this to me. I asked my Lord, the Glorified and Exalted, not to destroy my nation by an external enemy who will triumph over them, and He granted this to me. And I asked my Lord not to destroy my nation by division among themselves through confusion and warring sects, but He refused me this. (Muslim, Tormidhi and Nisa’i)

This hadith is quite interesting because it refutes any claim of conspiracy against Muslims as cause of the disintegration among Muslim countries and it places the complete responsibility on them.

Pointing out the bee as an example for the true believer is a truly insightful similitude that unfortunately is ignored by Muslims. Before proceeding to the other similitude of the believer as a tree, there are interesting statistics in the verse in which the bee was mentioned in the Quran. The only verse in which the word bee was mentioned is verse 68 is Surat Al-Nahl. Allah said:

وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى النَّحْلِ أَنِ اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا وَمِنَ الشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ (٦٨)
And your Lord inspired the bee, saying: Choose thou habitations in the hills and in the trees and in that which they thatch.” (Al-Nahl 16:68)

The only Surat in which the bee is mentioned is number 16. Number 16 is the number of chromosomes in the queen’s egg, and it is also the number of chromosomes in the drone sperm is 16.

A drone, male bee, hatches from unfertilized eggs and thus it only has 16 chromosomes. The female bee hatches from fertilized egg and thus it has pair of 16 chromosomes.

The number of the words in verse 68 in which the word bee is mentioned is 16 words. Also, the number of the unique Arabic Alphabet used in this verse is only 16 (out of the 28 letter is the Arabic alphabet).

For those who are interested in the mathematical structure in the Quran, there are other features that are related to number 16:
The number of verses in the Surat are 128 which is multiple of 16 (16 x 8).
The number of words in the Surat are 2080 words which is also multiple of 16 (16 x 130).
The number of words from the beginning of the Surat to the word bee is 992 which is multiple of 16 (16 x 62)
The number of words from the word bee to the end of the Surat is 1088 which is also multiple of 16 (16 x 68) and 68 is the number of the verse that includes the term bee.

Is there an intentional linkage between the number of chromosomes of 16 and these relationships or is this just coincidental, Allah knows best? But it seems that the connection is amazing.

The Prophet (PBUH) used another similitude to teach the companions the required traits of the believer, but in this case the prophet (PBUH) used the strategy of asking a question. Abdullah bin`Umar said, “We were with the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) when he said:

عن ابن عمر قال كنت عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنَّ مِنَ الشَّجَرِ شَجَرَةً لا يَسْقُطُ وَرَقُهَا، وَهِيَ مَثَلُ الْمُسْلِمِ، حَدِّثُونِي مَا هِيَ؟ فَوَقَعَ النَّاسُ فِي شَجَرِ الْبَادِيَةِ، وَوَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِي أَنَّهَا النَّخْلَةُ، ..قَالَ عَبْدُ اللهِ: فَاسْتَحْيَيْتُ، فَقَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، أَخْبِرْنَا بِهَا؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: هِيَ النَّخْلَةُ قَالَ عَبْدُ اللهِ: فَحَدَّثْتُ أَبِي بِمَا وَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِي، فَقَالَ: لأَنْ تَكُونَ قُلْتَهَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِي كَذَا وَكَذَا
‘Among the trees, there is a tree whose leaves do not fall in summer, and it resembles the Muslim, tell me about it. The people started talking about the ever-green tree, but I thought of the date palm tree, but felt shy to answer when I saw that Abu Bakr and my father did not talk. The companions said: tell us about it, O messenger of Allah.
The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: ‘It is the date palm tree.
When we departed, I said to my father: `My father, by Allah! I thought that it was the date tree.’ He said, `Why did you not speak then.’
I said, `I saw you were silent, and I felt shy to say anything.’ Omar said, `Had you said it, it would have been more precious to me than anything else.’” (Sahih al Bukhari)

Unlike the similitude of the bee in which the Prophet (PBUH) spelled out three attributes of the bee that Muslims must possess, here the (PBUH) left it to companions to analyze the properties of the date palm tree that makes it a good similitude of a Muslim. Let me mention a few and I am sure you can come with more to calibrate your character to the qualities of this tree.

1/ The roots of the date palm are very deep in earth. The deeper the root, the taller it rises. Similarly, in a believer, the deeper his Eman, the higher his actions that rise to Allah for acceptance. Allah says:

مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ ۚ (١٠)
“Whosoever desires honor, all honor lies with Allah alone. To Him ascend (all) the goodly words and He uplifts the righteous deed.” (Fater 35:10).

Also, while the root of the believer is on this Earth, he takes his Divine Guidance from the high heavens.

2/ Although the trunk of the date palm is straight and tall, the leaves are bent. A believer may be upright and principled, yet he is humble and never arrogant at the same time. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من كبر»
“No one will enter paradise if he has in his heart an atom weight of arrogance.” (Muslim)

3/ The date palm is an ever-green tree, and it is unaffected by seasonal changes. Similarly, a believer is not seasonal. He doesn’t do good only in the month of Ramadan, but he does good all the 12 months that Allah established as He said:

إِنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِندَ اللَّهِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَأوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ
“Indeed, the number of the months according to Allah is twelve months in the book of Allah since the day He created the heavens and the earth.” (Al-Tawba 9:36)

4/ The fruit of the palm tree is dates that are very sweet whether they are fresh or ripe or dried. They have many health benefits. A believer is a beneficial person, he is sweet in his actions and in his speech and his contribution are continuous throughout his life cycle whether he is youth, adult, or elderly. Believer days are never copy paste. Imam Al-Hasan Al-Basri said:

قال الحسن البصري رحمه الله: ’ما من يوم ينشق فجره، إلا وينادى: يا ابن آدم أنا خلق جديد، وعلى عملك شهيد، فتزود مني، فإني إذا مضيت لا أعود إلى يوم القيامة
‘No day breaks his dawn, but it will call: O son of Adam, I am a new creation, and a witness over your deeds, so take full benefits of me because when I go, I will not return until to the Day of Resurrection.”.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom to learn from these two similitudes of the bee and the date palm tree to prefect our character.

DUA

title: The Best Supplication Ever for Yourself
excerpt:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله .
