content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله .

On September 8, 2019, I gave a talk entitled “The Ultimate Dua while in the Best Position at the Perfect Time.”  In that talk, I highlighted the interesting observation that contrary to the common practice of starting with the greeting when we meet someone important to ask for favors, when we perform our Salat (prayer), we do not greet Allah in the beginning of the prayer but rather at the end when we sit down for the Tashahud (التشهد) that starts with (التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات) “All greetings, prayers and good deeds to Allah”. After the greeting, we end by making our request in the form of supplication (Dua).   All the steps before the Tashahud serve as prerequisites to purify ourselves to be worthy of greeting Allah to make our request.

In this state of purity while you are sitting in the divine presence, you want to make the most comprehensive request that is worthy of the opportunity.  What would you ask for?

It is reported in Bukhari and Muslim that Abdullah ibn Masoud (عبدالله بن مسعود) (RA) said that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:
عن عبدالله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: التفَت إلينا رسولُ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: ((إذا صلَّى أحدُكم، فليَقُل: التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدًا عبده ورسوله. ثم ليتخيَّر من الدعاء أعجبَه إليه، فيدعو))؛ متفق عليه، واللفظ للبخاري.

When one of you prays, he should say: "All greetings, prayers and good deeds are to Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be on us and on the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and His messenger.” And then you choose from the Dua (الدعاء) the most wonderous to you and make Dua with it. "

So, the Tashahud has two parts, the first part is greeting Allah and confessing our faith and the second part is Dua. The Question is what the best Dua is, and what is the most concise form that one can make in the Tashahud.    It is the one that we all know and say which is:
اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم ، اللهم بارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم

O Allah, pray on Muhammad and the “A’al” (آل) of Mohammad” as You prayed on Ibrahim and the ‘A’al” of Ibrahim. And grant Blessings to Muhammad and the “A’al” of Mohammad as You granted blessings to Ibrahim and the “A’al” of Ibrahim.  

This is the best dua that you will ever make for yourself.  You may ask where in this Dua, is a dua for me?   This is often missed by the way we translate “A’al” Mohammad (آل محمد), it is often translated as the family of Mohammad, but the Arabic word for family is ‘Ahl” (أهل) and is not “A’al” (آل)   

The only way to find the meanings of the term A’al” (آل) and the term Ahl” (أهل) is to study their use in the Quran.   When you search the Quran for the term A’al” (آل), you will find that it came 26 times with more than half (14 times) as “A’al Feruan” (ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ) and the second most frequently mentioned is “A’al” Lut, it came 4 times.  Let us look to examples showing that the “A’al” of a person does not mean his family but it means the people who follow that person.  Allah says regarding the people who follow Feruan: 

وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَـٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ
And [remember the time] when We saved you (Bani Israel) from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with cruel suffering, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women.  In this, there was great trial from your Lord.” (Al-Baqara 2:49) 

وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقْصٍ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
“And most certainly We overwhelmed the people of Pharaoh with drought and scarcity of fruits, so that they learn a lesson.” (Al-Araf 7:130)

كَدَأْبِ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَـٰهُم بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَكُلٌّ كَانُوا۟ ظَـٰلِمِينَ
Their practice (the sinners) is like the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they rejected the signs of their Lord.  So, We destroyed them for their sins, and drowned the people of Pharaoh: for all of them were evildoers. (Al-Anfal 8:54) 

أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ فَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ ءَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُم مُّلْكًا عَظِيمًا
Or is it that they are jealous of the people over what Allah has given them of His bounty?  While, We have given to the People of Abraham, the book and the wisdom and We have given them a great kingdom.”  (Al-Nisa 4:54)

Who are ‘A’al Ibrahim’ (ءَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ) whom Allah gave the book, the wisdom and great kingdom?  They are the prophets and messengers who followed Prophet Ibrahim.  They are Prophets Ishaq, Ismail, Yaqoub, Yusuf, Musa, Daud, Suliaman, Yunus, Zakaria, Isa, and others. 

So, the term “A’al” (آل) does not refer to family members but to the followers, obviously if the family members are followers, they are included in the term “A’al”.  This mean that “A’al Mohammad (PBUH)” (آل محمد) are you and I and anyone else who follows Him. 

So, when we supplicate to Allah in the Tashahud, we are asking Him to pray and bless Mohammad (PBUH) and His followers who are “A’al Mohammad” as He have prayed and blessed Ibrahim (PBUH) and His followers who are the prophets and messenger who followed him.  So you are asking Allah to pray and bless you, as one of the true followers of Mohammad (PBUH). as He prayed and blessed Prophets Ishaq, Ismail, Yaqoub, Yusuf, Musa, Daud, Suliaman, Yunus, Zakaria, Isa, and others. 

What is a better Dua for you than what Allah granted all those prophets! 

Now let us look to the term ‘Ahl” (أهل) that came often in the Quran, but it is most frequently mentioned as “Ahl Al-Kitab” (أهل الكتاب) which we translate as people of the book, it came 31 times.  The term “Ahl Al Bayt” (أهل البيت) came twice in the Quran.  Once related to Prophet Ibrahim and once related to Prophet Mohammed (PBUH) and in both cases it was referring to their wives.
Allah says regarding Sarah, the wife of Prophet Ibrahim who expressed her astonishment when the angels gave her the glad tiding that she will have a child: 

قَالُوٓاْ أَتَعۡجَبِينَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ رَحۡمَتُ ٱللَّهِ وَبَرَكَـٰتُهُ ۥ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ حَمِيدٌ۬ مَّجِيدٌ۬ (٧٣)
“They said: "Do you marvel at the Decree of Allah? Allah’s Mercy and His Blessings have always been upon you, O family (members) of the house. Surely, He (Allah) is Praiseworthy, All-Glorious.” (Hud 11:73)

Referring to the wives of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), Allah gave them the following Command:
وَقَرۡنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَأَقِمۡنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّڪَوٰةَ وَأَطِعۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۚ ۥۤ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنڪُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرً۬ا (٣٣)
“And stay in your houses, and do not display yourselves as it used to be displayed in the days of earlier ignorance, and establish the prayers, give the Zakat and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to keep away all sorts of evil from you, O family (members) of the house, and to purify you with a thorough purification.” (Al-Ahzab 33:33)

So, the term “Ahl” Al-Bayt (أهل البيت) of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) refers to his wives.  But even if what we say in the Tashahud refers to “Ahl” Mohammad (PBUH) and that the terms “A’al and “Ahl” are the same, though the equivalency of the two terms is not supported by the Quran, you and I who are the true followers of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) are “Ahl” Mohammad (PBUH).  Since “Ahl Al Bayt” of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) are his wives, we are from Ahl al-Bayt because the wives of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) are our mothers as Allah says:
ٱلنَّبِىُّ أَوۡلَىٰ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡ أَنفُسِہِمۡ‌ۖ وَأَزۡوَٲجُهُ ۥۤ أُمَّهَـٰتُہُمۡ‌ۗ
“The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers.” (Al-Ahzab 33:6)

So, we need to recognize that the supplication (Dua) in the Tashahud is not only supplication for Prophet Mohammad, but it is also supplication to us.  In it you are asking Allah for two things: 1) to pray on you. and 2) to grant you blessings similar to what He has granted to the Prophets who followed Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH).

Before we examine what are we expecting when we ask Allah to pray on us, let us realize that we are making this Dua after we have completed at the elements of the prayers from recitation of the Quran, Ruko and sujood. Perfecting these steps are critical to make us ready to greet Allah and ask him for the greatest blessings.  This is why Khosho in the prayer is very important because if we don’t, we are not pure enough to greet Allah and ask him.  This is, unfortunately, the biggest challenge we face because Satan is very keen to make you forfeit these blessings that he knew you would receive if you perfected your prayer.  Therefore, he will never leave you alone when you enter in the prayers.

This also means that prayers are the greatest gift that Allah granted to prophet Mohmmad (PBUH) and his followers, who are us.  Why prayers are the greatest gift; because unlike all the commands including the Quran that were delivered to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) through the holy spirit, the archangel Gibreel, only prayers were delivered to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) by Allah Himself.   But to be accurate the last two verses from Surat Al-Baqara were also delivered by Allah as we have discussed in previous talk.  Think about it, if the president of your company wants to give you an award, he can send it to you by mail, or give it to the senior vice president to give to you or give it to the manager to give to you.  But if the award is very valuable, he will call you to his office to give it to you in person.  This is the way that Allah used to send us the gift of prayers.  He arranged to have Prophet (PBUH) go beyond the seventh heaven to a place where no angel could even approach to grant him the prayers.

As I reflect on what I am saying, I really wonder if any Muslim who does not pray can really claim that he believes in Allah and is a follower of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH).  To Allah is the greatest examples, but this will be like the president of your company gives you an award and you tell him I don’t want it or take it and threw it away.  This may explain the Prophet’s (PBUH) saying:
عن بريدة بن الحصيب قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : بيننا وبينهم ترك الصلاة فمن تركها فقد كفر )رواه الترمذي ، والنسائي وابن ماجه وابن حبان والحاكم(
"The covenant between us and them is the Salat (prayer), so whoever abandons it has disbelieved."
The Prophet (PBUH) also said:
روى مسلم في صحيحه من حديث جابر قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : بين الرجل وبين الشرك ، والكفر ترك الصلاة .
“Between man and the polytheism (shirk) and the disbelief (kufr) is the abandonment of the salat (prayer).”

Jurists debated whether the person who does not pray out of laziness committed practice-based Kufr or belief-based Kufr.  This differentiation is very critical because if leaving prayers is equivalent to belief-based kufr, there will be major implications related to inheritance, marriage and praying on the person after his death.   But this subject is not our focus in this talk other than to highlight that prayers are very critical ritual in Islam.

We mentioned that all the activities that we perform during the prayers are requirements to make us deserve to sit in front of Allah to greet Him and make our request and thus these elements must be done when we are in a state of Khoshoo.  Allah says in the beginning of surah Al-Muminoon (المؤمنون):
قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ
“The Believers are surely successful.  Those who are reverent (have Khoshoo) in their prayers; (Al-Muminoon 23: 1-2)

Let us now look at the Dua that you will be making for yourself after you perfected all the elements of the prayer and sat down and greeted Allah. You will be asking Allah to pray on you and to grant you similar blessings as those that He granted to all the prophets who followed Prophet Ibrahim. What does it mean that Allah prays on us?   Allah revealed in Surat Al-Ahzab that He and His angels pray of us, the believers. Allah says:
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ ذِكۡرً۬ا كَثِيرً۬ا (٤١) وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكۡرَةً۬ وَأَصِيلاً (٤٢) هُوَ ٱلdouble_quoteى يُصَلِّى عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَتُهُ ۥ لِيُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَڪَانَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَحِيمً۬ا (٤٣)
"O you who believe! Remember Allah with much remembrance (41) And glorify Him morning and evening. (42)            He is the One Who prays on you, as do His angels, that He may bring you out from the darkness into light: and He is Full of Mercy to the Believers." (Ahzab 33:41:43)

Allah also revealed that He and His angels pray on the Prophet and commanded us to do the same, which we do as part of our payers for ourselves in the Dua of Tashahud.  Allah says:
إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا َسْلِيمًا )  الأحزاب(
Allah and His Angels pray on the Prophet: O you that believe! pray on him, and salute him with all respect.  (Al-Azab 33:56)

The Prophet (PBUH) was asked:  How is the prayer of Allah on his slaves.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:
قال ابن عطية : وروت فرقة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل له : يا رسول الله ، كيف صلاة الله على عباده . قال : ( سبوح قدوس - رحمتي سبقت غضبي )
“Glory, Holy, Perfect, My Mercy overcomes my wrath.“ ( سبوح قدوس - رحمتي سبقت غضبي)
Interpreters differed on whether this statement is by Allah on how He prays on His slaves or by the Prophet who started by prefacing his answer by saying (سبوح قدوس) “Glory and Holy” followed by the answer on the nature of Allah’s payers which is “My Mercy overcomes my wrath”  (رحمتي سبقت غضبي), meaning that the prayers of Allah on His slaves is to forgive them and grant them His Mercy in this life and in the Hereafter.

The prayers of the angels on us are their Dua to Allah for our forgiveness as Allah says:
يَحۡمِلُونَ ٱلۡعَرۡشَ وَمَنۡ حَوۡلَهُ ۥ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّہِمۡ وَيُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦ وَيَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ رَبَّنَا وَسِعۡتَ ڪُلَّ شَىۡءٍ۬ رَّحۡمَةً۬ وَعِلۡمً۬ا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ (٧)
“Those (angels) who bear the Throne (of Allah) and those around it glorify the praises of their Lord, and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe (saying): "Our Lord! You have embraced all things in Your mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and have followed Your Way and save them from the torment of the blazing Fire! (Ghafir 40:7)

رَبَّنَا وَأَدۡخِلۡهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتِ عَدۡنٍ ٱلَّتِى وَعَدتَّهُمۡ وَمَن صَلَحَ مِنۡ ءَابَآٮِٕهِمۡ وَأَزۡوَٲجِهِمۡ وَذُرِّيَّـٰتِهِمۡۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ (٨) وَقِهِمُ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِۚ وَمَن تَقِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ فَقَدۡ رَحِمۡتَهُ ۥۚ وَذَٲلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ (٩)
"Our Lord! admit them to the gardens of Adn (Eden) which you have promised them, together with whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring! Indeed, You are the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. (8)  And save them from the evil of their misdeeds, and whomsoever You save that Day from the consequence of their misdeeds, most surely You have shown him mercy." And that is the supreme success. (Ghafir 40:8-9)

Back to the Dua that we say in the Tashahud, we start by asking Allah to pray on the Prophet before we ask Him to pry on us.  Even in this, there is a great reward for us because the Prophet (PBUH) said as narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr (عن عبد الله بن عمرو):
فعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : (مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بِهَا عَشْرًا) رواه مسلم [.
“Whosoever prays on me one prayer, Allah will pray on him ten times”.

How do we pray on the Prophet (PBUH)?  We pray by saying the Dua in the Tashahud, so if you think about, we start by Ask Allah to pray on the Prophet and Allah will pray on us 10 times and then we ask Allah to pray on us and Allah will pray on us another time and the same thing for asking Allah to bless the Prophet (PBUH) and bless us.   This is why the Prophet (PBUH) said according to the account narrated by Ubai bin Ka’ab (أبي بن كعب) that saying this Dua of Tashahud will result in having (تُكْفَى همَّكَ ويغفرْ لكَ ذنبُكَ) “your needs satisfied, and your sins forgiven” (reported by Al-Tirmidhi)

Hope I have presented the case that if you fulfill the khoshoo in the prayers and sit down to greet Allah, the best dua you will ever make for yourself is:
اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم ، اللهم بارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم

The second important point that I hope I have justified is that you, as a true follower of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is of “A’al Al-Bayt and “Ahl Al-Bayt of Mohammad (PBUH).  So, don’t let anyone deprive you from this honor.  If it is a tradition to call Ahl Al-Bayt of Mohammad (PBUH) ‘Sayed”, then we should call each other “Sayed”.  But keep in mind that being a true follower is Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is not just by being Muslim but by being committed to follow his footsteps to deliver the message that was revealed to him.  I have discussed this role in previous talks. 

DUA

title: Accountabilities: Individual and Societal?
excerpt:

content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله .

Inshallah today, we will try to address an important subject which is related to our accountabilities on the day of judgment. Are we only accountable for our own actions or will we also be held accountable for the actions of our community? And if we are accountable for actions of our community, what is our responsibility towards it?

If you consider this life like being in school, your graduation grade will depend on the nature of the assignment given to you by the professors. If the assignment is an individual exam, your grade will be based on your answers in the exam. But, if the assignment is a team project, your grade will depend on the grade of the team project, but it is possible that your grade will be based on a combination of the team grade as well as a grade of your own contribution to the team.

We can take a survey to assess how many of you believe that they will be judged by Allah solely based on their level of righteousness; and how many believe that they will be judged based on a combination of their own righteousness as well as the righteousness of the community they live in.

Only if you believe that the righteousness of the community you live in has an impact on your rating in the hereafter, you will be committed to help the community achieve the highest level of righteousness. But, if you believe that the status of your community has no impact on your rating in the hereafter, you will not care about whether they are righteous or not as long as you are righteous.

To understand how Allah will judge us, we need to understand our role in this life. Does Islam only emphasize the righteousness of the individual or does it emphasize the righteousness of the society? If it emphasizes the righteousness of the society, one would expect that each member of the society will have some accountability of the actions of the society.

The answer to these issues must be derived from relevant verses in the Quran and the authentic hadith.

First, we find that there are many verses in the Quran that emphasize the individual responsibility and that each one of us will have a book that includes records of all what he did in this life. As example, Allah says in Surat Al-Isra:

وَكُلَّ إِنسَـٰنٍ أَلۡزَمۡنَـٰهُ طَـٰٓٮِٕرَهُ ۥ فِى عُنُقِهِۦ‌ۖ وَنُخۡرِجُ لَهُ ۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ كِتَـٰبً۬ا يَلۡقَٮٰهُ مَنشُورًا (١٣) ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَـٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبً۬ا (١٤)

“And We have tied the destiny of every human being to his neck; and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall bring forth a book for him that he will find wide open; (13) [and he will be told:] ‘Read your book.” Enough for you today that your own self to hold you accountable!” (Al-Isra 17:13-14)

These verses imply that every person will have his own book, but we note that another verse that talks about the transgressors and it implies that they will have a single book, as Allah says in Surat Al-Kahf:

وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَـٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَـٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً۬ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَٮٰهَا‌ۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرً۬ا‌ۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدً۬ا (٤٩)

“And the book will be placed (before them), then you will see the the guilty scared of its content and say: “Woe to us! What a book is this! It leaves out nothing, be it small or great, but takes everything into account!’ Thus, they will find all that they did facing them, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.” (Al-Kahf 18:49)

The verse implies that the guilty ones will be treated as a group and will have one book. This may indicate that there will be a community trial. This suggestion can be justified by the following verses form Surat Al-Jathiya:

وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ۬ جَاثِيَةً۬‌ۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ۬ تُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَـٰبِہَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٨) هَـٰذَا كِتَـٰبُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيۡكُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسۡتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٩)

“And you will see every community kneeling, every community will be called to its book. This Day you shall be recompensed for all that you used to do. (28) This is Our book that speaks against you with truth. Verily, We used to record all that you used to do.” (Al-Jathiya 45:28-29)

The verses indicate that the whole community apparently will be presented with one book, but then they will be divided in two groups, a group of the righteous and a group of the criminals as Allah says:

فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ فَيُدۡخِلُهُمۡ رَبُّہُمۡ فِى رَحۡمَتِهِۦ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (٣٠) وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ أَفَلَمۡ تَكُنۡ ءَايَـٰتِى تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرۡتُمۡ وَكُنتُمۡ قَوۡمً۬ا مُّجۡرِمِينَ (٣١)

“Then, as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them to His mercy. That is the evident triumph. (30) And as for those who disbelieved (it will be said to them): Were Our revelations not recited to you? But you showed arrogance and were a guilty people.” (Al-Jathiya 45:30-31)

This apparent group trial, does not contradict our standing in front of Allah as individuals as Allah says:

وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَٰدَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقْنَـٰكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ

“And you have come to Us as individuals, just as We created you in the first time.” (Al-Ana’am 6:94)

وَكُلُّهُمۡ ءَاتِيهِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ فَرۡدًا (٩٥)

“And every one of them will come to Him (Allah) alone on the Day of Judgement.” (Maryam 19:95)

These verses imply that when we stand as individuals, no one will have a defender to argue on his behalf. But if you are being judged in a group, you can argue for yourself to absolve yourself from their crimes. But you will only be justified to claim that you should not be judged based on the group action if you had advised them and they did not listen. Only then you have an excuse. This point is clear from the following verse in Surat Al-Araf:

وَإِذۡ قَالَتۡ أُمَّةٌ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوۡمًا‌ۙ ٱللَّهُ مُهۡلِكُهُمۡ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُہُمۡ عَذَابً۬ا شَدِيدً۬ا‌ۖ قَالُواْ مَعۡذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ (١٦٤)

“And when a group among them said: Why do you preach to a people whom Allah is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment, they said: In order to absolve ourselves (to be free from guilt) before your Lord, and perhaps they may fear Allah.” (Al-Araf 7:164)

This verse addresses a key point that one often uses as excuse for not advising people when you know they are committing a clear violation of Allah. The excuse would be that your advice will not help. This verse gives two important reasons why you should advise: First is that you don’t know whether they will heed your advice or not, only Allah knows. Second is that this will be your excuse in front of Allah not to judge you among them. If you stay silent when you see grave violation of Allah’s commands being committed, you will be judged among the guilty group. This warning is clear from these verses in Surat Al-Maeda:

لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُۥدَ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ (٧٨) كَانُواْ لَا يَتَنَاهَوۡنَ عَن مُّنكَرٍ۬ فَعَلُوهُ‌ۚ لَبِئۡسَ مَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ (٧٩)

“Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed by the tongue of David, and of Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and used to transgress. (78) They did not forbid each other from the wickedness they did. Indeed, evil was what they have been doing!” (Al-Maeda 5:78-79)

The Quran is clear that a righteous person has the responsibility of giving advice to his community to promote goodness and prevent evil. Many verses in the Quran emphasize this responsibility. As an example, Allah says:

كُنتُمۡ خَيۡرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخۡرِجَتۡ لِلنَّاسِ تَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنڪَرِ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ‌ۗ

“You are the best Ummah (nation, community, society) ever raised up for mankind; you enjoin goodness and forbid evil and believe in Allah.” (Al-Emran 3:110)

The interesting observation about this verse is that Allah made the obligation to command goodness and forbid evil ahead of the belief in Him to emphasize the criticality of this obligatory command on every Muslim. When Allah commands us to enjoin goodness and forbid evil, Allah is speaking of something that any fair-minded and decent person will rate as good or evil and He is not talking about some issues on which Muslim scholars have differed. After all Allah embedded in every human being what is good and what is bad.

Because commanding goodness and forbidding evil is a major responsibility, every Muslim must be trained to be qualified to give advice regarding what is right and warn of what is wrong, To be qualified you must meet three qualifications. In his book “The Certified” (المعتمد), Al-Qadi Abou Yaala (القاضي أبو يعلى) the great Hanbali scholar (380- 458H) wrote:

“It is not permitted for anyone to command what is good and forbid what is evil unless he is knowledgeable about what he commands and forbids, kind to whom he commands and forbids, and wise in the way he commands and forbids.”

If you commit to give advice based on clear knowledge and using the best approach and you are rejected, then you can claim that you are a community by yourself similar to Prophet Ibrahim regarding him, Allah says:

إِنَّ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً۬ قَانِتً۬ا لِّلَّهِ حَنِيفً۬ا (١٢٠)

“Surely, Ibrahim was a community (by himself), devoted to Allah, a man of pure faith.” (Al-Nahl 16:120)

Commanding goodness and forbidding evil is so important that need to be taught to our children as Luqman did with his young son when he said to him:

يَا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا أَصَابَكَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ

“O my dear son! establish regular prayer, enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong; and be patient in facing whatever happens to you; for this is firmness in (the conduct of) all matters. (Luqman 31:17)

After Luqman advised his son is to establish prayers which is the key to building the child’s connection with Allah, he advised him of commanding good and forbidding evil. This gives the child a sense of his social responsibility toward others who will be mainly his friends. Then the child was told to be aware that standing for what is good and against what is evil requires patience because he should expect to face difficulties, and this requires firmness of his character (إن ذلك من عزم الأمور).

The question is whether the responsibility of advising with goodness and warning about evil is obligatory upon everyone (فرض عين) or the responsibility is removed if a group of people in the community is doing it (فرض كفاية). The following verse in Surat Al-Emran may imply that the obligation can be satisfied by a group from among the community:

وَلۡتَكُن مِّنكُمۡ أُمَّةٌ۬ يَدۡعُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡخَيۡرِ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنڪَرِ‌ۚ وَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ (١٠٤)

“There has to be a group from among you who invite to goodness and enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency. And they are the successful.” (Al-Emran 3:104)

But the general opinion is that this obligation is upon every individual (فرض عين) unless you are sure that this group will reach your own friends and associates. This opinion is logical for two reasons. First the verse states that this group are the successful which can imply that those who are not part of this group are not successful. Second, Allah will designate you as witness against those people who committed the evil, verifying that you have delivered to them His command. How are you going to be a witness against others if you haven’t given them any advice? Your role as witness is stated in verses such as:

وَكَذَٲلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةً۬ وَسَطً۬ا لِّتَڪُونُواْ شُہَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدً۬ا‌ۗ

“Thus, We have made you a moderate (balanced, middle) nation, so that you should be witnesses against the people, and the messenger a witness against you.” (Al-Baqara 2:143)

وَجَـٰهِدُواْ فِى ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦ‌ۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَٮٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجٍ۬‌ۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ‌ۚ هُوَ سَمَّٮٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِى هَـٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُہَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۚ

“And strive hard in Allah’s Cause as you ought to strive. He has chosen you (to convey His Message) and has not imposed in the religion any hardship on you. It is the faith of your father Ibrahim (Abraham). He (Allah) named you Muslims earlier and in this (the Qur’an), so that the Messenger becomes a witness over you and you be witness over (other) people.” (Al-Hajj 22:78)

The support of the opinion that the responsibility is upon every Muslim can be justified by the example of the man mentioned in Surat Yasin who risked his life to give advice to the people even though there were three prophets assigned to this community, Allah says:

وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ۬ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَـٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (٢٠) ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَن لَّا يَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ أَجۡرً۬ا وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ (٢١)

“And there came rushing from the farthest part of the city. He said: O my people! Follow the messengers. (20) Follow those who do not ask for a reward from you and who are rightly guided.” (Yaseen 36:20-21)

To emphasize this responsibility, the Prophet (PBUH) gave the example of people on the ship: Nu’man bin Bashir reported that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said:

عن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( مثل القائم على حدود الله والواقع فيها ، كمثل قوم استهموا على سفينة ، فأصاب بعضهم أعلاها وبعضهم أسفلها ، فكان الذين في أسفلها إذا استقوا من الماء مروا على من فوقهم ، فقالوا : لو أنا خرقنا في نصيبنا خرقا ولم نؤذ من فوقنا ، فإن يتركوهم وما أرادوا هلكوا جميعا ، وإن أخذوا على أيديهم نجوا ونجوا جميعا ) رواه البخاري

“The example of the person abiding by Allah’s order and restrictions in comparison to those who violate them is like the example of those persons who drew lots for their position in a boat. Some of them got positions in the upper deck, and the others in the lower deck. When the latter needed water, they had to go up to bring water from the top deck. Concerning that they are troubling the passengers on the upper deck, they said, ‘Let us make a hole in the bottom of the ship (and get water) so that we do not trouble the upper deck passengers.’ If the people in the upper deck left the lower deck passengers to do what they had suggested; then all the people of the ship would be destroyed, but if they had prevented them, then both parties would be safe.” (Bukhari)

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized that Allah’s punishment does not only befall those who commit evil, but it befalls everyone in the community who does not stand against it: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yamān RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

عن حذيفة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال { والذي نفسي بيده لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليوشكن الله عز وجل أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من عنده ثم تدعونه فلا يستجاب لكم } رواه الترمذي

“By the One in Whose Hand my soul is! Either you command good and forbid evil, or Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will pray to Him but He will not respond to you.” [At-Tirmidhi – Ahmad]

Sayeda Aiysha said that the Prophet (PBUH) stood on the minbar and said:

عن عائشة ، قالت : دخل علي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فعرفت في وجهه أن قد حضره شيء ، فتوضأ ، وما كلم أحدا ، فلصقت بالحجرة أسمع ما يقول ، فقعد على المنبر ، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه ، ثم قال : ( يا أيها الناس ، إن الله تبارك وتعالى يقول لكم : مروا بالمعروف ، وانهوا عن المنكر ، قبل أن تدعوني ، فلا أجيبكم ، وتسألوني فلا أعطيكم ، وتستنصروني فلا أنصركم )،صحيح ابن حبان

“Allah the exalted is telling you: Enjoin good and forbid evil before you supplicate to Me and I will not answer you and before you ask Me and I will not give you and before you seek My help and I will not help you.” (ibn Hibban)

The companions clearly understood the criticality of this command. Khalifa Abu Bakr (RA) said in one of his sermons:

ثبت أنّ أبا بكر الصديق t قال في خطبته: (أيّها الناس إنّكم تقرؤون هذه الآية {يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضلّ إذا اهتديتم} [سورة المائدة: آية 105] وإنّكم تضعونها على غير موضعها، وإنّي t سمعت النبي ﷺيقول: ((إنّ النّاس إذا رأوا المنكر فلم يغيّروه أوشك أن يعمهم الله بعقاب منه))[] أخرجه الترمذيّ، و أحمد وابن ماجه

“O People, you read this verse

{يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضلّ إذا اهتديتم} [سورة المائدة: آية 105]

“O Who you believe, take care of yourselves. The one who goes astray cannot harm you, if you are rightly guided”, but you do not properly apply it, because I heard the Prophet (PBUH) saying: If people see evil and do not forbid it, they will be on the verge of being overtaken by punishment from Allah.”

We often use the excuse that we cannot openly express our views about the evil in the society for fear of the potential harm that can befall us and we justify our position by quoting:

وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَلَدَيْنَا كِتَـٰبٌ يَنطِقُ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ

“And We do not task any human being with more than what he is able to bear:” (Al-Muminum 23:62)

Obviously, this is correct, but who decides what you can bear, is it you or Allah who has full knowledge of your abilities. The complete verse reads:

وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَلَدَيْنَا كِتَـٰبٌ يَنطِقُ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ

“And We do not task any human being with more than what he is able to bear. With Us there is a book that speaks with truth [about the person’s abilities]; and they shall not be wronged” (Al-Muminum 23:62)

The honesty of assessing our abilities must be considered when applying the following hadith. Abu Sa`eed al-Khudree (RA) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:

عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( من رأى منكم منكرا فليغيره بيده ، فإن لم يستطع فبلسانه ، فإن لم يستطع فبقلبه ، وذلك أضعف الإيمان ) رواه مسلم

“Whosoever of you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; and if he is not able to do so, then [let him change it] with his tongue; and if he is not able to do so, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith.” [Muslim]

The problem that we see these days is that issues that are very clear in our religion and in fact in all religions as evil, Muslims are now tolerating it and many of those who are in leadership positions give watered down answer when they are asked about them. And worse, this will confuse our youth.

I hope that I presented the case that we will be held accountable for the evil others commit if we don’t absolve ourselves from this evil by clearly speaking against it and supporting those who speak against it. If you are still not convinced of your responsibility towards the society you live in, you need to answer on whose behalf you are making the following declarations at least 17 time per day:

إِيَّاكَ نَعۡبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسۡتَعِينُ (٥)

You alone we worship and You alone we seek help (5). (Al-Fatiha 1:5)

Who are the “we” you are speaking on their behalf when you are praying alone?

Allah made an oath in Surat Al-Asr that we often recite that people are at loss if they don’t exhort each other to the truth, so if you don’t, who else is to save your community from the state of loss:

وَٱلۡعَصۡرِ (١) إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ لَفِى خُسۡرٍ (٢) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ (٣)

By the time, (1) Man is indeed in a state of loss, (2) Except those who believe and do good deeds and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to observe patience. (Al-Asr 103:1-3)

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom to always invite people to goodness and warn them of evil. We pray to Allah to give us the courage to always tell the truth and not make us of those who are willing to compromise in the truth for the sake of political correctness or for personal benefits.

DUA

title: Islam in Two Words: Knowledge and Accountability
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

To identify the most important issues in Islam, you need to look at the first revelation and the last one because any revelation in between will mainly be to support and expand their key commands of the first revealed verses and the last revelated verse.

The first reveled verses are
ٱقۡرَأۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ (١) خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِنۡ عَلَقٍ (٢) ٱقۡرَأۡ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡأَڪۡرَمُ (٣) ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلۡقَلَمِ (٤) عَلَّمَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ (٥)

“Read! In the Name of your Lord, Who created (all that exists), (1)
He created man from a clinging clot (2) Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous, (3) Who taught by the pen. (4) He taught man what he did not know. (Al-Alaq 96:1-5)

The last revealed verse after 23 years from the first revelation is
وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمً۬ا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّا ڪَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (٢٨١)

“And be fully conscious of a day when you shall be brought back to Allah. Then every soul shall be paid in full what he has earned, and they shall not be wronged.” (Al-Baqara 2:281)

The first revelation that starts with the command ‘Read” clearly highlights the importance of literacy for Muslims. Reading, obviously with tadabour, is the means by which one can acquire knowledge. The significance of acquiring knowledge and the emphasizes on its value are clearly expounded in many verses in the Quran. Let us look at few examples.

In Surat Al-Baqara, Allah informs us that it was the ability to learn and to retain knowledge are the reason why man was preferred over all creations, including the angels. Allah says:

وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةً۬‌ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيہَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيہَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ‌ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ (٣٠) وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّہَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَہُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبُِٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (٣١) قَالُواْ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ (٣٢) قَالَ يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآٮِٕہِمۡ‌ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآٮِٕہِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّىٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ (٣٣) وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ (٣٤)

“And (recall) when your Lord told the angels: I am placing a vicegerent (Khalifa) in the earth. They said: will You place in it someone who will make mischief in it and shed blood, while we, we hymn Your praise and glorify Your holiness? He said: I know that which you do not know.” (30)

“And He taught Adam the names of all things; then He placed them before the angels and said: Tell me their names if you are truthful. (31) They said: Glory to You: we have no knowledge beyond what You have taught us, You are the all-knowing, the all Wise” (32)

“He said: o Adam, tell them their names. When he told them their names, Allah said: Didn’t I tell you that I know what is unseen in the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.” (2:33)

“And behold, We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated down, except Iblis who refused and was arrogant and was of the disbelievers (disobedient to Allah)”. (Al-Baqara 2:30-34)

Another example of the importance of knowledge is associated with Prophet Suliman and the throne of queen of Sheba. It was the man who has the knowledge who was able to teleport the throne of the queen from Yemen to Jerusalem in a blink of an eye and it was not the Jinn who has superpower. This emphasizes the importance of knowledge over power, and this is logical because it is knowledge that will allow any nation to develop the sources of power. Allah reports to us this account by saying:

قَالَ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمَلَؤُاْ أَيُّكُمۡ يَأۡتِينِى بِعَرۡشِہَا قَبۡلَ أَن يَأۡتُونِى مُسۡلِمِينَ (٣٨) قَالَ عِفۡرِيتٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ أَنَا۟ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ‌ۖ وَإِنِّى عَلَيۡهِ لَقَوِىٌّ أَمِينٌ۬ (٣٩) قَالَ ٱلَّذِى عِندَهُ ۥ عِلۡمٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ أَنَا۟ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَرۡتَدَّ إِلَيۡكَ طَرۡفُكَ‌ۚ فَلَمَّا رَأَهُ مُسۡتَقِرًّا عِندَهُ ۥ قَالَ هَـٰذَا مِن فَضۡلِ رَبِّى لِيَبۡلُوَنِىٓ ءَأَشۡكُرُ أَمۡ أَكۡفُرُ‌ۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦ‌ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّى غَنِىٌّ۬ كَرِيمٌ۬ (٤٠)

“ He Suleiman (Solomon) said: “O chiefs! Which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me submissively?” (38) A strong one from the jinn said: “I will bring it to you before you rise up from your place (council). And I am indeed strong, and trustworthy for this task.” (39)

But the one who has knowledge of the book said: “I will bring it to you before you glance returns to you!” Then when he (Solomon) saw it well placed before him, he said: “This is by the Grace of my Lord – to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful! And whoever is grateful, truly, his gratitude is for his own benefit, and whoever is ungrateful, certainly! my Lord is Free of all wants, Bountiful.” (Al-Naml 27:38-40)

The Quran has many verses that challenges the believers who are expected to serve as Allah’s vicegerent on earth to seek knowledge in all subjects that allow them to take advantage of what Allah created for them on earth. After all, a key responsibility of man is to build and develop the earth as a place for his settlement, Allah says:

هو أنشأكم من الأرض واستعمركم فيها
“He brought you forth from the earth and made you settle in it.” (Hud 11:61)

Settling in earth requires all kinds of knowledge to support farming, industry, construction, communication, business, health, defense, government as well moral and legal. All the blessings that Allah created in earth for the benefit of man have keys and it is a moral obligation to search for these keys to take advantage of these blessings and prevent any harm that come from them. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن سهل بن سعد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن هذا الخير خزائن ولتلك الخزائن مفاتيح فطوبى لعبد جعله الله مفتاحا للخير مغلاقا للشر وويل لعبد جعله الله مفتاحا للشر مغلاقا للخير ( ابن ماجه)
“The goodness has been stored in vaults, and those vaults have keys, blessed be the servant whom Allah made a key for the blessings and a lock for the evil and woe to a slave whom Allah made a key to evil and lock for the good.” (Ibn Majah)

Seeking knowledge that unlocks the sources of benefits for mankind is a religious obligation, Allah said:

قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِى ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ‌ۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَـٰبِ (الزمر/9)
“Say: “Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” It is only the people of understanding who are receptive.” (Al-Zumur 39: 9)

رَفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ دَرَجَـٰتٍ۬‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ۬ (المجادلة/11)
“Allah raises in ranks those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge and Allah is well aware of what you do” (Al-Mujadala 58:11)

The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن أبي الدرداء -رضي الله عنه- عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: «مَنْ سَلَكَ طَريقا يَبْتَغي فيه عِلْماً سَهَّلَ الله له طَريقاً إلى الجنة، وإنَّ المَلائِكَةَ لَتَضَعُ أَجْنِحَتَهَا لِطالِبِ العِلْمِ رِضاً بما يَصْنَعُ،» (رواه البخاري)
“Whoever follows a path in pursuit of knowledge, Allah will facilitate for him a path to Paradise. Indeed, the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, out of pleasure for what he does.” (Bukhari)

The Quran discusses many natural sciences to encourage Muslims to study them. Allah praises those who study these subjects as the thinkers and as people of intellect. The following are some examples:

1/ Pointing to the science of botany, Allah say:
يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرْعَ وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلْأَعْنَـٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
“He causes crops to grow for you, and olive trees, and date palms, and grapes, and all [other] kinds of fruit: in this, behold, there is a message indeed for people who think!” (Al-Nahl 16:11)

2/ Pointing to sciences related to bees, honey, and medicine, Allah says:
ثُمَّ كُلِى مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ فَٱسْلُكِى سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا ۚ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَٰنُهُۥ فِيهِ شِفَآءٌ لِّلنَّاسِ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
“Then, (O bees) eat from all the fruits and follow the pathways that your Lord made easy for you. From their bellies come out a drink of various colors in which there is cure for people. Surely, in that there is a sign for people who think! (Al-Nahl 16:69)

3/ Pointing to the sciences of languages and the exploration for in-earth and outer-space creations, Allah says:
تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ ٱالسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيہِنَّ‌ۚ وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورً۬ا (٤٤)
“The seven heavens and the earth and all those therein praise Him, and there is not a single thing but hymns His praise; but you do not understand their praise. Surely, He is Forbearing, Most Forgiving.” (Al-Isra 17:44)

4/ Pointing to the science of physical cosmology to study the creation of the universe, Allah says:
ٱلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَـٰمًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَـٰذَا بَـٰطِلًا سُبْحَـٰنَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
“Who remember Allah standing and sitting and (lying) on their sides and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth (and say): “Our Lord! You have not created all of this in vain. We proclaim Your perfection, so save us from the punishment of the fire! (Al-Imran 3:191)

5/ Pointing at the importance of the science of meteorology, Allah says:
أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزۡجِى سَحَابً۬ا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيۡنَهُ ۥ ثُمَّ يَجۡعَلُهُ ۥ رُكَامً۬ا فَتَرَى ٱلۡوَدۡقَ يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡ خِلَـٰلِهِۦ وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍ۬ فِيہَا مِنۢ بَرَدٍ۬ فَيُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَصۡرِفُهُ ۥ عَن مَّن يَشَآءُ‌ۖ يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرۡقِهِۦ يَذۡهَبُ بِٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرِ (٤٣)
“Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds gently, then joins them together, then makes them into a heap of layers, and you see the rain comes out from their midst. And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail, that He afflicts with it whomsoever He wills, and averts it from whomsoever He wills. The vivid flash of its lightning nearly blinds the sight.” (Al-Noor 24:43)

6/ Pointing to embryology, Allah says:
ثُمَّ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلنُّطۡفَةَ عَلَقَةً۬ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡعَلَقَةَ مُضۡغَةً۬ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡمُضۡغَةَ عِظَـٰمً۬ا فَكَسَوۡنَا ٱلۡعِظَـٰمَ لَحۡمً۬ا ثُمَّ أَنشَأۡنَـٰهُ خَلۡقًا ءَاخَرَ‌ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحۡسَنُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقِينَ (١٤) ثُمَّ إِنَّڪُم بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ (١٥) ثُمَّ إِنَّڪُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ تُبۡعَثُونَ (١٦)
“Then We made the Nutfah into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a little lump of flesh, then We made out of that little lump of flesh bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh, and then We brought it forth as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the Best of creators. (14) After that, surely, you will die. (15) Then (again), surely, you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.” (Al-Mouminoun 23:14-16)

7/ Pointing to a very important principle to anyone who seeks knowledge, and this is to be honest and fair and always say the truth. While Allah has clearly prohibited gambling and intoxicants and identified them as evil, Allah did not say that they do not have any benefits, Allah said that they have some benefits. Allah says:

يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ ۖ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَـٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثْمُهُمَآ أَكْبَرُ مِن نَّفْعِهِمَا ۗ
They ask you about intoxicants and gambling. Say: ‘In both there is great evil as well as some benefits for people; but their evil is greater than the benefits.’ (Al-Baqara 2:219)

These are just few examples, and the Quran includes far more. Both Imam Abu Hamed Al-Ghazali (ابو حامد محمد الغزالي) and Imam Abu Bakr al-Arabi (ابو بكر العربي) said that the Quran includes over 77,000 forms of knowledge. So, it clear that seeking knowledge is a foundational principle in Islam. Without knowledge, man does not deserve the honor that Allah bestowed upon him by being His vicegerent.

The second foundational principle in Islam is accountability which is summarized by the last revealed verse:

وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمً۬ا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّا ڪَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (٢٨١)

“And fully conscious of a day when you shall be brought back to Allah. Then every person shall be paid in full what he has earned, and they shall not be wronged.” (Al-Baqara 2:281)

While the verse refers to general accountability for all what man does, the context of this last revealed verse gives focus on financial accountability and gives special emphasis on the charity part of the financial accountability because the verse before this last revealed verse reads:

وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسۡرَةٍ۬ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيۡسَرَةٍ۬‌ۚ وَأَن تَصَدَّقُواْ خَيۡرٌ۬ لَّڪُمۡ‌ۖ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ (٢٨٠)

“And if the debtor is in financial difficulty, grant him a delay until a time of ease; and if you forgo the debt as charity, it would be better for you if you really know”. (Al-Baqara 2:280)

Acquiring money and other forms of wealth is encouraged in Islam because they are required to fulfill two of the five pillars on which the religion of Islam is built. These 5 pillars are: confessing the faith, prayers, Zakat (obligatory charity), fasting and Hajj. A Muslim cannot fulfill the third and the fifth pillars of paying Zakat and going to Hajj unless he has sufficient money that exceeds his needs.

Accountability of money is also two of the five questions that every person will be asked to address on the day of Judgment. Ibn Mas’ud reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ لَا تَزُولُ قَدَمُ ابْنِ آدَمَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّهِ حَتَّى يُسْأَلَ عَنْ خَمْسٍ عَنْ عُمْرِهِ فِيمَ أَفْنَاهُ وَعَنْ شَبَابِهِ فِيمَ أَبْلَاهُ وَمَالِهِ مِنْ أَيْنَ اكْتَسَبَهُ وَفِيمَ أَنْفَقَهُ وَمَاذَا عَمِلَ فِيمَا عَلِمَ

“On the Day of Resurrection, the son of Adam will not be dismissed from (the court of) his Lord until he is asked about five issues:
1. His life and how he lived it
2. His youth and how he used it
3. His wealth and how he earned it
4. His Wealth how he spent it
5. His knowledge and how he acted upon it.” (Al-Tirmidhi)

Allah made money as a foundational test for every Muslim because it a measure of the person’s belief and trust in Allah. A Muslim should have no doubt in his mind of the following:

1. The wealth he has is granted to him by Allah as a trust (the skills and the opportunities that you have that allowed you to obtain your wealth are from Allah and He can take it away from you at any time)
2. The resources from which our wealth comes will never run out.
3. When you spend your money for the sake of Allah, your wealth will never diminish but rather it will increase in this life, and you will have great rewards in the hereafter.
4. Being poor is not a justification for being a miser.
5. Be charitable now because the time will come when we will regret the opportunities, we have missed by not giving in the way of Allah, but it will be too late. Allah says:

وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِىَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنِىٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ قَرِيبٍ۬ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (١٠) وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُہَا‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ (١١)

“Spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he would say: ‘My Lord, if You would only delay things for me for a short time, then I will give in charity and become one of the doers of good. (10) But Allah will never give respite to anyone, once his appointed time comes. Allah is All-Aware of what you do.” (Al-Munafeqoun 63:10-11)

By being a miser, you are not hurting anyone but yourself, Allah says:
هَا أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يَبْخَلُ ۖ وَمَنْ يَبْخَلْ فَإِنَّمَا يَبْخَلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ ۚ

“Here you are being invited to spend in the way of Allah, but among you are some who are miser. But anyone who is miser, his miserliness is only at the expense of his soul. Allah is rich, and you are poor.” (Mohammad 47:38)

Because Allah uses money as a test to validate our claims of trusting Him, Satan also uses money to show that we don’t really trust Allah. Allah has warned us about Satan’s trickery of using the fear of poverty to make us fail in demonstrating our trust in Allah. Allah said:
الشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْفَحْشَاءِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ يَعِدُكُمْ مَغْفِرَةً مِنْهُ وَفَضْلًا ۗ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ

“Satan threatens you with poverty and bids you to conduct unseemly. Allah promises you His forgiveness and bounties and Allah cares for all and He knows all things.” (Al-Baqara 2: 268)

Because Allah knows that Satan will use poverty as an excuse for convincing us to be a miser, Allah emphasized His promise of goodness and prosperity in this life and the hereafter to those who spend their money in Allah’s sake as He said:
وَسَارِعُوا إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ

“Hasten (rush, compete) to forgiveness from your Lord and for a garden that expands the heavens and the earth prepared for the righteous who spend (in cause of Allah) in prosperity and in adversity.” (Al-Imran 3:133-134)

We should rush, because the money we will be spending is an investment with huge return as Allah said:
مَّثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ

“The parable of those who spend their money in the way of Allah is that of a grain that produces seven ears and each ear has a hundred grains. Allah gives manifold increase to whom He pleases; and Allah is All-Embracing and All-Knowing, “(2:261).

Spending of our wealth in charity does not only offer protection but it also increases the wealth in this life and the hereafter. Be assured that your generosity will be answered by Allah Who said:
الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

“Those who spend (in charity) of their goods by night and by day in secret and in public have their reward with their Lord: on them shall be no fear nor shall they grieve,” (Al-Baqara 2:274).

Since the wealth we own belongs to Allah, He uses it as a metric to measure of our level of righteousness, He said
لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ ۚ وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ

“By no means shall you attain righteousness unless you give (freely) of that which you love; and whatever you give, Allah knows it well,” (Al-Imran 3:92).

Asama bnt Aby Bakr said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق -رضي الله عنهما- قالت: قال لي رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: «لا تُوكِي فَيُوكى عليك»، وفي رواية: «أَنْفِقي أو انْفَحي، أو انْضَحي، ولا تُحْصي فَيُحْصي الله عليك، ولا تُوعي فَيُوعي الله عليك». ) البخاري. مسلم (
شرح الحديث : لَا تَدَّخِرِي وَتَشُدِّي مَا عِنْدَكِ وَتَمْنَعِي مَا فِي يدك، فتنقطع مَادَّة الرزق عَنْكِ، ولا تحسبي خوفًا من انقطاع الرزق، فيكون سببًا لانقطاع إنفاقك، قوله: (فيحصي الله عليك)، ولا تمنعي فضل المال عن الفقير فيمنع الله عنك فضله ويسده عليك.

“Give (in charity) and do not give reluctantly lest Allah should give you in a limited amount; and do not withhold your money lest Allah should withhold it from you.”(Bukhari and Muslim)

The bottom line is that the money we acquire is a test to demonstrate the nature and level of your trust in Allah and thus we will be held accountable for how we acquired and how we spend it. In conclusion if you want to summarize Islam in two words, they will be knowledge and accountability with emphasis on financial accountability.

We pray to Allah to grant us the wisdom to be source of knowledge and to be generous with the financial resources that He trusted us with.
DUA

title: The Root of All Virtues
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In my last talk, I discussed “The Key for the Most Valuable Treasure” and in it I indicated that about 2/3 of the Quran emphasizes moral conduct and that the Prophet (PBUH) spent more time teaching moral conduct than he spent explaining the Quran. I also presented 6 strategies that the prophet (PBUH) used for teaching his followers morality and virtues and these included: role model, competition for his love, stories, dialogue, him asking questions, and response to questions.

I also presented the two axes of Islam to define the status of a Muslim in the metrics of monotheism and morality.

Out of all moral conducts, we note that Allah in the Quran and the Prophet (PBUH) in his teachings placed major emphasis on the importance of “truthfulness” and warning of the evil of “lying”. The verses that you listened to are from Surat Al-Emran and they set an easy solution to any dispute in a fundamental matter of belief. Rather than keep going back and forth in argument, the issue can be easily settled by proposing that to prove whether he or you are telling the truth is for you and him to make sincere supplication to Allah, the creator of the universe, to curse the one and the family of him who is lying. Allah sets this truth test by saying:

فَمَنۡ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ فَقُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ نَدۡعُ أَبۡنَآءَنَا وَأَبۡنَآءَڪُمۡ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَڪُمۡ وَأَنفُسَنَا وَأَنفُسَكُمۡ ثُمَّ نَبۡتَہِلۡ فَنَجۡعَل لَّعۡنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَـٰذِبِينَ (٦١)

“If someone argues with you over this matter after the knowledge has come to you, say (to him): Come! Let us call our children and your children, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves, then let us pray humbly that the curse of Allah be upon the liars.” (Al-Emran 3:61)

Allah gives severe warning to those who utter lies about Allah, He says:

فَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن ڪَذَبَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلصِّدۡقِ إِذۡ جَآءَهُ ۥۤ‌ۚ أَلَيۡسَ فِى جَهَنَّمَ مَثۡوًى لِّلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ (٣٢)

“Who is more unjust than the one who forges a lie against Allah and rejects the truth when it comes to him? Is there not a home in Hell for the disbelievers?” (Al-Zumar 39:32)

On the other hand Allah promises great rewards for those who are truthful and accept the truth, Allah says:

وَٱلَّذِى جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدۡقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِۦۤ‌ۙ أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ (٣٣) لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (٣٤)

“And for the one who has come with the truth and believed in the truth, such people are the ones who are God-fearing. (33) They shall have from their Lord whatever they desire. That is the reward of the good-doers.” (Al-Zumar 39:33-34)

Truthfulness is the root of all virtues and lying is the root of all evils in the world. How many problems in the world, whether on a personal level, family level, or global level are based on lies?

وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدۡقً۬ا وَعَدۡلاً۬‌ۚ لَّا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَـٰتِهِۦ‌ۚ وَهُوَ ٱالسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ (١١٥)

“And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can change His Words. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.” (Al-An’am 6:115).

Truthfulness comes ahead of justice because there will be no justice until true information is available.

Allah describes His Prophets as being men of truth:

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقً۬ا نَّبِيًّا (٤١)

“And mention in the Book, Abraham: surely, he was a man of truth, a Prophet.” (Maryam 19:41)

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ إِسۡمَـٰعِيلَ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ صَادِقَ ٱلۡوَعۡدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولاً۬ نَّبِيًّا (٥٤)

“And mention in the Book Ismail (Ishmael): surely, he was true to his promise, and was a Messenger, a Prophet.” (Maryam 19:54)

وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ إِدۡرِيسَ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقً۬ا نَّبِيًّ۬ا (٥٦)

“And mention in the Book, Idris (Enoch): surely, he was a man of truth, a Prophet.” (Maryam 19:56)

Allah emphasizes to the believers the importance of not only abiding by truth but also by being in the company of the truthful:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَكُونُواْ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ (١١٩)

“O you who have believed, fear Allah and be in the company of the truthful.” (At-Tawbah 9: 119).

Allah associates those who are truthful with those whom He has blessed, Allah says:

وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ معَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡہِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَٱلصِّدِّيقِينَ وَٱلشُّهَدَآءِ وَٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ‌ۚ وَحَسُنَ أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ رَفِيقًا (٦٩)

“And whosoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, such will be in the company of those whom Allah has blessed: the Prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous. And how excellent these companions are!” (An-Nisa 4:69)

Note that every Muslim should be reading Surat Al-Fatiha at least 17 times every day and every time he/she says:

ٱهۡدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٲطَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ (٦) صِرَٲطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ

“Guide us to the straight path. (6) The path of those on whom You have blessed.” (Al-Fatiha 1:6-7)

Who are those whom Allah has blessed? They are the ones whom we just mentioned, they are the Prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous.

The Prophet (PBUH) took every opportunity to emphasize to his followers the importance of truthfulness:

وعَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَمَا يَزَالُ الرَّجُلُ يَصْدُقُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الصِّدْقَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ صِدِّيقًا وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ وَإِنَّ الْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ وَمَا يَزَالُ الرَّجُلُ يَكْذِبُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الْكَذِبَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَذَّابًا. (رواه مسلم)

“Adhere to truthfulness, for indeed truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth and strives to be truthful until he is written with Allah as a truthful man. And beware of lying, for indeed lying leads to sinning, and sinning leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and strives to lie until he is written with Allah as a liar.” (Saheeh Muslim)

The emphasis by the Prophet (PBUH) that truthfulness is the most important virtue can be understood from the following hadith:

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَرَادٍ ، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ : يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ ، هَلْ يَزْنِي الْمُؤْمِنُ ؟ قَالَ : " قَدْ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ " ، قَالَ : هَلْ يَسْرِقُ الْمُؤْمِنُ ؟ قَالَ : " قَدْ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ " ، قَالَ : هَلْ يَكْذِبُ الْمُؤْمِنُ ؟ قَالَ : " لا " ، ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : ( إِنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي الْكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ ).

I asked the Prophet (PBUH): O Prophet of Allah, would a believer ever commit fornication?
The Prophet (PBUH) said: This may happen.
So, I said: O Messenger of Allah, would a believer ever steal.
The Prophet (PBUH) replied: This may happen.
Then I said: O Prophet of Allah, would the believer ever lie
The Prophet (PBUH) replied: No and recited a verse of Surat Al-Nahl:
“Only those who do not believe invent lies.” (إِنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي الْكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (Al-Nahl 16:105)

In another hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) was asked: Whether a believer will ever lie, and he said:

عن عبد الله بن جراد قال : قال أبو الدرداء : يا رسول الله، هل يكذب المؤمن؟ قال : ” لا يؤمن بالله ولا باليوم الآخر من إذا حدث كذب ” .

“None believes in Allah and in the day of judgment who when he speaks lies.”

The Prophet (PBUH) also emphasized the criticality of truthfulness in business dealings and that it brings blessings to the business:

وعن حكيم بن حزام رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ” البيعان بالخيار ما لم يتفرقا، فإن صدقا وبينا بورك لهما في بيعهما، وإن كذبا وكتما محقت بركة بيعهما ” (متفق عليه)

The seller and the buyer have the right to negotiate as long as they have not settled the deal. If they are truthful and clear (about the product), Allah will bless their deal. But if they lie and hide (defects of the product), the blessings of their deal will be wiped out. (Bukhari & Muslim)

Abdallah Ibn Omar reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبدالله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: “أربع إذا كن فيك فلا عليك ما فاتك من الدنيا: حفظ أمانة، وصدق حديث، وحسن خليقة، وعفة في طعمة” (رواه أحمد)

“There are four things, which if you possess, you should not regret whatever you miss from this world: keeping the trust, truthful speech, good character, and abstaining from prohibited food.” (Ahmad)

Ubadah Ibn Al-Samit narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: « اضْمَنُوا لِي سِتًّا مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَضْمَنْ لَكُمُ الْجَنَّةَ: اصْدُقُوا إِذَا حَدَّثْتُمْ، وَأَوْفُوا إِذَا وَعَدْتُمْ، وَأَدُّوا إِذَا اؤْتُمِنْتُمْ، وَاحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَكُمْ، وَغُضُّوا أَبْصَارَكُمْ، وَكُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ »

“Guarantee for me six things and I will guarantee Paradise for you: 1) tell the truth when you speak, 2) fulfill your promise, 3) return the trust to its owner, 4) guard your private parts, 5) lower your gaze, and 6) restrain your hands (from hurting others).”

Key Divisions of Truthfulness:

Verbal-based truth (الصدق بالقول): When you speak, you should only speak the truth with no addition or subtraction. Also, you should never speak except when you are certain of what you say. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “كَفَى بِالْمَرْءِ كَذِبًا أَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ”, “It is enough lies of a person that he speaks everything he hears”.

Action-based truth (الصدق بالفعل) : Your actions and words must be consistent, you should never deceive others by your actions.

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (٢) ڪَبُرَ مَقۡتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (٣)

“O you who believe! Why do you say what you do not do? (2) It is most hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do.” (As-Saff 61:2-3)

Intention-based truth (الصدق بالنية): Your intention for all what you say and do must be sincerely for the sake of Allah.

[وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ]

“They have not been ordered but to worship Allah with full sincerity.” (Al-Bayyina 98:5)

A legend that represents the condition of the world today:

According to a 19th century legend, the Truth and the Lie meet one day. The Lie said to the Truth: “It is a wonderful day today!” The Truth looked at the sky and sighed, for the day was really beautiful. They spent a lot of time together, ultimately arriving alongside a well. The Lie said to the Truth: “The water is very nice, let’s take a bath together!” The Truth, once again suspicious, tested the water and discovered that it indeed was very nice. They undressed and started bathing.

Suddenly, the Lie comes out of the water, puts on the clothes of the Truth and runs away. The furious Truth comes out of the well and runs everywhere to find the Lie and to get her clothes back. The World, seeing the Truth naked, turns its gaze away, with contempt and rage.

The poor Truth returns to the river and disappears, hiding therein. Since then, the Lie travels around the world, dressed as the Truth, satisfying the needs of society, because, the World, in any case, has no wish at all to meet the naked Truth.

The Misunderstood concept of “taqiyya”:

Unfortunately lying is the common practice of the Islamophobes who pick something out of context and use it against Muslims. They quote the following verse:

لَّا يَتَّخِذِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ‌ۖ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٲلِكَ فَلَيۡسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِى شَىۡءٍ إِلَّآ أَن تَتَّقُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ تُقَٮٰةً۬ ‌ۗ

“Let not the believers take unbelievers for their guardians instead of the believers and whoever does this shall have no help from Allah, unless you guard yourselves against them (as a precaution).” (Al-Imran 3:28)

Those Islamophobes completely corrupt the meaning of the Arabic “taqiyya” which is derived from the Arabic root “waqa” (وقى) which means “guarding or protecting”. This root is also the origin of the word “Taqwa” (God-consciousness or fearing Allah).

فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَٱعۡتَدُواْ عَلَيۡهِ بِمِثۡلِ مَا ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ‌ۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ (١٩٤)

“Then whoever transgresses against you, you transgress likewise against him. And fear Allah and know that Allah is with the God-fearing.” (Al-Baqara 2:194)

The verse that they quote mainly suggests that a person who faces religious persecution can withhold the fact that he is a Muslim to save his life.

Yes, it is permissible to hide the fact that you are Muslim if you are under threat, as long as it does not involve hurting anyone else. The definition of Taqiyya by scholars is:

“taqiyya is dissimulation when one is being oppressed or tortured or having one’s views banned, a believer can then hide his faith, but the condition is that his heart must remain firm in belief.”

There is no allowance in Islam that would permit a Muslim to lie to pursue any materialistic gains or to deceive others.

In Islam, truthfulness is something which is so cultivated that it became implanted in a Muslim’s soul.

Abu Bakr (RA) said:
قال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه: الصدق أمانة، والكذب خيانة.
“Truthfulness is trust and lying is betrayal”

Omar Ibn Al-Khattab (RA) said:
قال عمر بن خطاب رضي الله عنه: “لا تنظروا إلى صيام أحد ولا إلى صلاته ولكن انظروا من إذا حدث صدق”.
“Do not look at the person extent of fasting or prayers but only look to whether when he speaks, he tells the truth.”

Omar Ibn Al-Khattab (RA) also said:
عليك بالصدق وان قتلك, ولأن يضعني الصدق – وقلما يضع- أحب الي من ان يرفعني الكذب- وقلما يفعل-
“Be steadfast on truth even if it ruins you, and even if the truth ruins me, and it rarely does, it is better for me than if the lie raises me, and it rarely does.”

While lying to the enemies is permitted during the war, The prophet (PBUH) never lied even during the war. Once an old man came to him during a battle and asked: where are you from? The prophet (PBUH) replied: “We are from water”. The man went back thinking that there is a tribe called “Water”, while the prophet (PBUH) meant that:
We created from water every living thing. (وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ حَىٍّ‌ۖ) (Al-Anbiya 21:30)

The Prophet (PBUH) warned against lying to one’s children. Abdullah ibn Amir said:

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ دَعَتْنِي أُمِّي يَوْمًا، وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قَاعِدٌ فِي بَيْتِنَا، فَقَالَتْ: هَا تَعَالَ أُعْطِكَ. فَقَالَ لَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: « مَا أَرَدْتِ أَنْ تُعْطِيَهُ؟ ». قَالَتْ: أُعْطِيهِ تَمْرًا. فَقَالَ لَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: « أَمَا إِنَّكِ لَوْ لَمْ تُعْطِهِ شَيْئًا كُتِبَتْ عَلَيْكِ كِذْبَةٌ »

“My mother called me while the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) was visiting us, and she said: come here and I will give you something. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: what did you want to give him? She said: a date. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: If you would not have given him something, this would have been written for you as a lie.”

Unfortunately, parents may take it lightly and lie to their children so they would stop nagging them, not realizing that they are teaching their children how to lie.

This impeccable character of early Muslim by always speaking the truth was a key for them being trusted by others and thus spreading Islam to the end of the world.

While it is not based on confirmed saying of the Prophet (PBUH), Islamic scholars suggested that the root of all virtues is truthfulness and the root of all evils is lying.

We pray to Allah to make us of the truthful and resurrect us with the truthful and to make our tongues only speak the truth.

DUA

title: Are You Ready for the Eight Questions at the End of the Bridge?
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

This worldly life is our bridge to our destination which is the Hereafter. This destination is either eternal happiness or eternal suffering. At the end of the bridge, everyone will be given an oral exam of 8 questions. Depending on the person’s answers, he may be subjected to a trial that can last for 50,000 years while the person is standing with the sun over his head.

Three of the questions are given to the person after he is buried in the grave. The other 5 questions will be given to him in the beginning of the person’s trial after the resurrection on the day of judgement.

The person must answer the first three questions correctly to get full score, any wrong answer will give a failing grade and his answer to the other questions will not change the failing grade. If the person passes the first three questions, he can take partial credit for his answers to the other 5 question. The first 3 question that everyone will be asked in the grave are recorded for us in this account:

The Prophet (PBUH) attended the burial of one person and after the person was put in the ground and he was covered, he (PBUH) said:

عن البراء بن عازب قال: خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جَنَازَةِ رَجُلِ مِنَ الأنْصَارِ فَانْتَهَيْنَا إِلَى الْقَبْرِ وَلَمَّا يُلْحَدْ فَجَلَسَ رَسُولُ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَلَسْنَا حَوْلَهُ كَأَنَّمَا عَلَى رُؤُوسِنَا الطَّيْرُ وَفِي يَدِهِ عُودٌ يَنْكُتُ بِهِ فِي الأَرْضِ، فَرَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ فَقَالَ: اسْتَعِيذُوا بِالله مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ مَرَّتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثاً، وَقَالَ: وَإِنَّهُ لَيَسْمَعُ خَفْقَ نِعَالِهِمْ إِذَا وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ حِينَ يُقَالُ لَهُ: يَا هَذَا مَنْ رَبُّكَ وَمَا دِينُكَ وَمَنْ نَبِيُّكَ

The buried person is being asked about three things:
1. Who is your God? (من ربك)
2. What is your religion? (ما دينك)
3. What do you say about the man who was sent by God to you? (ما هذا الرجل الذي بعث فيكم) (Sunan Abi Dawud)

These questions may seem simple and easy to answer, however imagine you just died, in the grave in a state of confusion and voices of the angels ask you these questions. Do you really believe that you can answer these questions in such a state without the answers being truly embedded in your soul!

Regarding the other five questions a person will be asked on the day of judgement, Ibn Mas’ud reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ لَا تَزُولُ قَدَمُ ابْنِ آدَمَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّهِ حَتَّى يُسْأَلَ عَنْ خَمْسٍ عَنْ عُمْرِهِ فِيمَ أَفْنَاهُ وَعَنْ شَبَابِهِ فِيمَ أَبْلَاهُ وَمَالِهِ مِنْ أَيْنَ اكْتَسَبَهُ وَفِيمَ أَنْفَقَهُ وَمَاذَا عَمِلَ فِيمَا عَلِمَ

عن أبي برزة نضلة بن عبيد الأسلمي قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: لا تزول قدما عبد يوم القيامة حتى يسأل عن عمره فيم أفناه؟ وعن علمه فيم فعل فيه؟ وعن ماله من أين اكتسبه؟ وفيم أنفقه؟ وعن جسمه فيم أبلاه؟

“On the Day of Resurrection, the son of Adam will not be dismissed from (the court of) his Lord until he is asked about five issues:
1. His life and how he lived it
2. His youth and how he used it
3. His wealth and how he earned it
4. His Wealth how he spent it
5. His knowledge and how he acted upon it.” (Al-Tirmidhi)

Our focus in the worldly life should be on preparation to give concise answers to these questions.
