While you may think that answering the first 3 questions is easy, your ability to answer them correctly will depend on your preparation for answering the other 5 questions. Keep in mind that at the end of the bridge of your life on earth, you need the divine support to answer the three questions properly, Allah says:

يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الآخِرَةِ وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاء

“Allah reinforces those who believe with the firm word (response) in this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah will let the wrongdoers go astray. And Allah does whatever He so wills.” (Ibrahim 14: 27)

During the trial of every person, Allah will produce for him three books of records. Sayeda Aisha said that the Prophet (PBUH) Said:

عن عائشة قالت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم” الدواوين عند الله عز وجل ثلاثة ديوان لا يعبأ الله به شيئا وديوان لا يترك الله منه شيئا وديوان لا يغفره الله) أخرجه الإمام أحمد في المسند و الحاكم في المستدرك و البيهقي في شعب الإيمان . فأما الديوان الذي لا يغفره الله فالشرك بالله قال الله عز وجل إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة

وأما الديوان الذي لا يعبأ الله به شيئا فظلم العبد نفسه فيما بينه وبين ربه من صوم يوم تركه أو صلاة تركها فإن الله عز وجل يغفر ذلك ويتجاوز ان شاء. وأما الديوان الذي لا يترك الله منه شيئا فظلم العباد بعضهم بعضا القصاص لا محالة) أخرجه احمد من حديث عائشه فيه صدقه بن موسى وقال مسلم بن ابراهيم صدوق وبقية رجال الحديث ثقات

Allah will produce for every person three books of records: For one book of records, Allah does not give it attention and forgives to whom He will, what is in it. For the second book of records, Allah does not ignore any thing in it. And for the third book of records Allah does not forgive anything in it.

The book of records that Allah does not forgive what is in it is the book that records the shirk (taking associates with Him) as Allah said: Whoever associate others with Allah, Allah prohibited him from Paradise (من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة).

The book of records that Allah does not give it attention is the book that includes the injustices that a person committed against himself in his relationship with Allah from missing fasting or prayers, Allah forgives and overlooks these deficiencies for whom he wishes.

But the book of records that Allah does not ignore anything in it is the book that includes records of the injustices the person committed against others, there must be retribution, no doubt about it.

In a similar hadith, Salaman Al-Farisi said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن سلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :“ذنب لا يغفر وذنب لا يترك وذنب يغفر فأما الذنب الذي لا يغفر فالإشراك بالله وأما الذنب الذي لا يترك فظلم العباد بعضهم بعضا وأما الذنب الذي يغفر فذنب العبد بينه وبين الله تعالى”) حديث سلمان رواه البزار و اخرجه الطبراني

Sins are of three types; sin that is not forgiven, sin that will not be ignored and sin that is forgiven. The sin that is not forgiven is the Shirk, the sin that is not ignored is the oppression people commit against each other and the sin that is forgiven is the one between the servant and His Lord.

The same point is emphasized in another hadith narrated by Anas ibn Malik who said that the prophet (PBUH) said:

حدثنا الربيع عن يزيد عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : “الظلم ثلاثة: فظلم لا يتركه الله وظلم يغفر وظلم لا يغفر فأما الظلم الذي لا يغفر فالشرك لا يغفره الله وأما الظلم الذي يغفر فظلم العبد فيما بينه وبين ربه وأما الظلم الذي لا يتركه فيقص الله بعضهم من بعض”

Injustice is of three types; injustice that Allah will not neglect, injustice that is forgiven and injustice that is never be forgiven. The injustice that Allah will never forgive is the shirk, the injustice that is forgiven is the injustice that the servant commits between himself and His Lord, and the injustice that Allah does not neglect is the injustice among one another until retribution is done. [At-Tirmidhi]

The greatest danger for any person who truly believes in Allah and never associate anything or anyone with Him in worship, comes from his relationship with other human beings. Any injustice done against any person, no matter how small, should be a cause of concern because you will be held accountable for it unless the person whom you hurt forgives. Worst that you commit injustice against someone whom you don’t even know. This can happen when you transmit a rumor about someone that causes him hurt. Treating other people with the greatest respect and honor is something that should be ingrained in a Muslim’s nature.

There are many sayings of the Prophet (PBUH) that make this point abundantly clear. On several occasions, the Prophet (PBUH) was told about a woman who spends all nights praying, and all days fasting, and spends much money in charity but she hurts her neighbors with her tongue. Without hesitations, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قيلَ للنَّبيِّ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ و سلَّمَ : يا رَسولَ اللهِ ! إنَّ فلانةَ تقومُ اللَّيلَ و تَصومُ النَّهارَ و تفعلُ ، و تصدَّقُ ، و تُؤذي جيرانَها بلسانِها ؟ فقالَ رسولُ اللَّهِ صلَّى اللَّهُ عليهِ و سلَّمَ لا خيرَ فيها ، هيَ من أهلِ النَّارِ . قالوا : و فلانةٌ تصلِّي المكتوبةَ ، و تصدَّقُ بأثوارٍ ، و لا تُؤذي أحدًا ؟ فقالَ رسولُ اللَّهِ : هيَ من أهلِ الجنَّةِ) الراوي : أبو هريرة – المصدر : صحيح الأدب المفرد

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رجل: يا رسول الله إن فلانة يُذكر من كثرة صلاتها وصيامها وصدقتها غير أنها تؤذي جيرانها بلسانها، قال: هي في النار، قال: يا رسول الله فإن فلانة يُذكر من قلة صيامها وصدقتها وصلاتها، وإنها تصدق بالأثوار من الأقط، ولا تؤذي جيرانها بلسانها، قال: هي في الجنة. )( الإمام أحمد وغيره

“There is no good in her, she will be in the hellfire”. Then the people said but there is another woman who only performs the obligatory payers and gives minimum charity, but she does not hurt anyone. The Prophet (PBUH) said: “She will be in paradise”.

Even hurting animals is a cause for a Muslim to be in the Hellfire. Abdullah ibn Omar said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

وفي الصحيحين أيضاً من حديث عبد الله بن عمر ر ضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: عذبت امرأة في هرة سجنتها حتى ماتت فدخلت فيها النار، لا هي أطعمتها ولا سقتها إذ حبستها، ولا هي تركتها تأكل من خشاش الأرض.

“There was a woman who punished her cat by depriving it from food and water until the cat died, and this woman entered the hellfire because of what she did. She did not feed the cat, nor she let it go to eat from what is outside”.

People often take Allah’s mercy for granted and don’t expect that He will punish them for the injustices they commit against others. Those people ignore the truth that Allah said about Himself:

نَبِّئْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ * وَأَنَّ عَذَابِي هُوَ الْعَذَابُ الْأَلِيمُ {الحجر:49-50}

“Tell My servants that I am indeed the Forgiving, the Merciful; (49) And that My punishment is indeed the most painful punishment.” (Al-Hijr 15:49-50)

غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ الْعِقَابِ ذِي الطَّوْلِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ إِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ. {غافر: 3}

“The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the One who is the source of power. There is no God but He. To Him is the final return.” (Ghafir 40:3)

The ultimate truth is that we all will be returning to Allah to be held accountable for what we have done in this life. This life is our bridge to the Hereafter. This bridge is full of temptations and the problem arises when Muslims get so distracted and attached to all the adornments on the bridge and don’t focus on the destination.

The adornment on the bridge is part of the divine plan to assess who is getting distracted and who is firm. Allah says:

إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ زِينَةً۬ لَّهَا لِنَبۡلُوَهُمۡ أَيُّہُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلاً۬ (٧)

“Surely, We have made what is on earth an adornment for it, so that We test them as who among them is best in conduct/deeds.” (Al-Kahf 18:7)

The imbalance happens when we focus on the adornment of this life for the expense of the adornment of the hereafter. Yes, we can enjoy our life here and all the beauty that Allah made available to us in it but that should never be at the expense of the pleasure of the adornment of the hereafter. All the enjoyment of this life is no comparison to the enjoyment of the hereafter. Similarly, all the suffering in this life has no comparison to the suffering of the hereafter.

The challenge in keeping the balance between this life and the hereafter is our difficulty in imaging the pleasures and the beauty of the hereafter because they are still described to us in terms of pleasures that we have here on earth. Yes, Allah provided to us many descriptions of the pleasures of the paradise in the Quran, but it will be nice to have the descriptions made by someone who physically saw it. Since the Prophet (PBUH) saw both heaven and hell in his ascension trip, he tried to draw a picture for us by making comparison. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن المُسْتَوْرِد بن شَدَّاد -رضي الله عنه- قال: قال رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: «ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا مِثْل ما يجعل أحدكم أصْبُعَه في اليَمِّ، فلينظر بِمَ يَرْجِع» [رواه مسلم.]

“The life of this world compared to the hereafter is as if one of you were to put his finger in the ocean and take it out then compare the water that remains on his finger to the water that remains in the ocean” [Sahih Muslim].

All the pleasures and enjoyments that anyone can accumulate in this life from palaces, yachts, airplanes, treasures, companions, etc. compared to the those in the hereafter are like the amount of water that your finger holds when you stick it in an ocean compared to the water in the ocean. So, what is the ratio between them. Obviously, there is no comparison between them.

To assess that the most adornment in this life has no comparison to the ones in the hereafter, Allah revealed an interesting verse that states what Allah could have done but he did not. Allah says in Surat Az-Zukhruf:

وَلَوۡلَآ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً۬ وَٲحِدَةً۬ لَّجَعَلۡنَا لِمَن يَكۡفُرُ بِٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِہِمۡ سُقُفً۬ا مِّن فَضَّةٍ۬ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيۡہَا يَظۡهَرُونَ (٣٣) وَلِبُيُوتِہِمۡ أَبۡوَٲبً۬ا وَسُرُرًا عَلَيۡہَا يَتَّكِـُٔونَ (٣٤) وَزُخۡرُفً۬ا‌ۚ وَإِن كُلُّ ذَٲلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَـٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا‌ۚ وَٱلۡأَخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٣٥)

“And were it not that mankind would have become one community, We would have provided for those who disbelieve in Al-Rahman “the Beneficent” silver roofs for their houses, and (silver) stairs whereby they ascend, (33) And also for their houses, doors (of silver), and couches (of silver) on which they could recline, (34) And ornaments of gold. Yet all this is nothing but an enjoyment of this world. And the Hereafter with your Lord is (only) for the righteous.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:33-35).

These verses say that if all people would have been disbelievers, Allah would have showered them with materialistic pleasures but because there will be believers who may be tempted and confused by what the disbelievers have, Allah did not make this happen. But Allah ends the verses by saying, all these worldly pleasures are nothing compared to what the believers will have in the hereafter.

Then Allah described some of the pleasures that He has in store for the believers in paradise by saying:

ٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ أَنتُمۡ وَأَزۡوَٲجُكُمۡ تُحۡبَرُونَ (٧٠) يُطَافُ عَلَيۡہِم بِصِحَافٍ۬ مِّن ذَهَبٍ۬ وَأَكۡوَابٍ۬‌ۖ وَفِيهَا مَا تَشۡتَهِيهِ ٱلۡأَنفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ ٱلۡأَعۡيُنُ‌ۖ وَأَنتُمۡ فِيهَا خَلِدُونَ (٧١) وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡجَنَّةُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُورِثۡتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ (٧٢)

“Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, showered with bliss. (70) circulated among them will be trays and cups of gold. And there will be whatever the souls desire, and all what eyes could enjoy, and you will be living in it forever. (71) This is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do. (Al-Zukhruf 43:70-72)

While Allah describes the adornment in paradise in physical terms that we can relate to, He emphasizes one attribute that no one will get in this life no matter how much pleasures one can have, and this is eternity. No matter how much wealth and pleasures a person may have, still he will die and leave them. Therefore, there is no comparison between eternal pleasures and transient pleasures.

Even when Allah uses terms that we relate to, He tells us that you will never imagine the pleasure in paradise, as He said in Hadith Qudsi:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم-: قال الله تعالى: أعددت لعبادي الصالحين ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر.)البخاري ومسلم(

“I have prepared for My righteous slaves (such excellent things) as no eye has ever seen, nor an ear has ever heard, nor a human heart has ever perceived.’ (Bukhari and Muslim)

This tells us that the pleasures in paradise are indescribable by our human language. So, if you want to get some image of any house in paradise, search the internet for pictures of the most luxurious and enchanting palace in the world and realize that this is what man can build and imagine what Allah has built for you if you are smart enough to balance the equation of success whose terms are enjoyment of this life versus enjoyment of the hereafter. Allah says regarding all the pleasure in this life relative to the pleasures in the Hereafter:

فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

“So (remember that) the enjoyment of this worldly life is but trivial in comparison to the Hereafter.” (Al-Tawba 9:38)

To bring the image of paradise close to our mind, the Prophet (PBUH) described the construction materials and the covering of the land in paradise as materials that we extremely value in this life, but they are of no major value since they are equivalent to the construction material and the covering of the land in this earth that are mainly sand or soil. The prophet (PBUH) said:

حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنَّ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ : الْجَنَّةُ بِنَاؤُهَا لَبِنَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلَبِنَةٌ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَمِلاطُهَا الْمِسْكُ الأَذْفَرُ وَحَصْبَاؤُهَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْيَاقُوتُ وَتُرْبَتُهَا الزَّعْفَرَانُ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا يَنْعَمُ لا يَبْأَسُ وَيُخْلَدُ لا يَمُوتُ لا تَبْلَى ثِيَابُهُمْ وَلا يَفْنَى شَبَابُهُمْ )(الترمذي )

“The buildings in paradise are made of gold and silver bricks and the mortar between the bricks is musk. Its sand is pearl and ruby, and its soil is the saffron. The one who enters it will have bliss and never feels discomfort and lives for eternity and his youth will never age”. (Al-Tirmidhi)

Are people stupid enough to sacrifice all these pleasures for some temporary enjoyment in this earth! Even if one lives in this earth for 100 years with life full of enjoyment and pleasures and do not even suffer one moment of discomfort, all this will be erased by one minute in the Hellfire. Also, if one lives in this earth for 100 years subjected to the worst kind of suffering and injustices, all of this would be erased by the pleasure of one minute in paradise. Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أنس بن مالك -رضي الله عنه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يُؤْتَى بِأَنْعَمِ أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَيُصْبَغُ فِي النَّارِ صَبْغَةً ثُمَّ يُقَالُ: يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ خَيْرًا قَطُّ؟ هَلْ مَرَّ بِكَ نَعِيمٌ قَطُّ؟ فَيَقُولُ: لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَبِّ وَيُؤْتَى بِأَشَدِّ النَّاسِ بُؤْسًا فِي الدُّنْيَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ فَيُصْبَغُ صَبْغَةً فِي الْجَنَّةِ فَيُقَالُ لَهُ: يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ بُؤْسًا قَطُّ؟ هَلْ مَرَّ بِكَ شِدَّةٌ قَطُّ؟ فَيَقُولُ لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَبِّ مَا مَرَّ بِي بُؤْسٌ قَطُّ وَلَا رَأَيْتُ شِدَّةً قَطُّ». (رواه مسلم).

“The one who had the most enjoyable and comfort life in this world who is destined for the Hellfire will be brough on the day of judgment and dipped once in the Fire then he will be asked: O son of Adam, have you ever witnessed any goodness? Have you ever experienced any bliss? He will say: O Lord, by Allah I have not.

Then, the one who has the most miserable life in his world who is destined for Paradise, and will be dipped once in Paradise then he will be asked: O son of Adam, have you ever witnessed any misery? Have you ever experienced any hardship? He will say: No by Allah, I have never witnessed any misery, nor have I experienced any hardship.”

This is the equation that we need to balance: 100% enjoyments in this life versus one dip in hell in the hereafter or major suffering in this life versus one dip in paradise the hereafter. But there will be no one dip; it is an eternal immersion. You set your own priority and act accordingly.

This does in no way mean that believers should not seek the pleasures of this life, but it depends on how they are seeking it. It should be sought through justice, honesty, and fairness and never through injustice and greed. Allah wants the believers to enjoy His blessings in this life too. Allah says:

قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِ‌ۚ قُلۡ هِىَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِى ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةً۬ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ

” Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the wholesome things of provisions? Say: “They are for the believers during this worldly life (though shared by others), but they are exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.” (Al-Araf 7:32)

The main difference between the companions of the Prophet (PBUH) and the majority of the following generations is that the companions had the adornment of this worldly life in their hands but never in their hearts. Ibn Masoud said to the following generation:

قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه لأصحابه : أنتم أكثر صلاة و صياما من أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه و سلم و هم كانوا خيرا منكم قالوا : و لم يا أبا عبد الرحمن ؟ قال : كانوا أزهد منكم في الدنيا و أرغب في الآخرة

“You perform more prayers and fasting than the companions of Mohmmad (PBUH), but they were better than you. The people said: why? He said: “They were more dismissive of the pleasures of this life and more desirable for what is in the Hereafter.”

Many people have concocted ideas to convince themselves that they will enter paradise independent of their work and behavior in this life. Some suggested that they are guaranteed paradise because of their race, others believe that they are guaranteed paradise because someone else sacrificed on their behalf. Even Muslims suggest that if they say that “there is no god but Allah” they are fine independent of the sins they commit because they don’t commit shirk. Those Muslims are naïve because they ignore two things:

First, Allah has always associated the belief in Him with righteous deeds because it does not make sense that someone claims that he believes in Allah and continuously disobeys his commands.

Second, they ignore Satan’s example and that Allah cursed him and condemned him to Hell for eternity not because he associated any other god with Allah, he had full belief in the oneness of Allah, but because of his intentional rejection of Allah’s command. Satan’s shirk was not associating someone else with Allah, but his shirk was merely following his own desires ahead of Allah’s commands and this is a form of shirk as Allah defined by saying:

أَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ ۥ هَوَٮٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِ وَڪِيلاً (٤٣)

“Have you seen the one who takes his desires as his god.? Would you then be guardian for him?” (Al-Furqan 25:43)

So, a person who commits shirk is not only the one who associates other deities with Allah but is also the one who puts his own desires ahead of Allah’s commands. This is all what Satan did to deserve Allah’s curse, he chose his own desires over Allah’s commands. So, we should be fully aware of this type of shirk that is classified by Allah as disbelief (kufr) that will not be forgiven.

Muslims must be careful with statements such as this command of Allah is not suitable for our time, or this command of Allah is not necessary. There is a big difference between a person who rejects a command of Allah because his logic tells him so, and the person who do not obey a command of Allah because of his weakness or laziness but keeps repenting to Allah for his shortcomings. The person in the first case is a disbeliever of the satanic disbelief type. The second person is sinful, but he has not been deprived from the mercy and forgiveness of Allah.

We pray to Allah to cleanse our hearts from all forms of shirk and purify our deeds from any form of injustice or ill treatment of anyone.

DUA

The Motivating Inner Driver for All virtues – (حياء) “Haya’a”

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In the past two talks, I discussed the Prophet’s major effort to make the companions worthy to be messengers of Allah to deliver His message, the Quran, to all those whom the Prophet (PBUH) did not reach. In the talk entitled “The Key for the Most Valuable Treasure” I indicated that about 2/3 of the Quran emphasizes moral conduct and that the Prophet (PBUH) spent more time teaching moral conduct than he spent explaining the Quran. In the last week talk entitled “The Root of all Virtues”, I identified truthfulness as the root of all virtues. Truthfulness and all other associated moral behaviors are reflected as outward behavior that people will note.

Today, I plan to inshallah focus on the motivating inner driver of all virtues.  This internal driver is called (حياء) “Haya’a’. This human attribute (حياء) “Haya’a’ refers to the internal constraint that prevents the person from doing anything that embarrasses him, not out of fear from someone but out of respect to himself and honor to anyone who sees or hears him. So, (حياء) “Haya’a” is the noble attitude that always motivates the person to behave in the most honorable manner and refrain from doing or engaging in any bad deed and even prevents him from failing in his duties towards himself and those who have rights over him.

The key difference between humans and animals is (حياء) “Haya’a”, animals do not have this trait and thus you see animals relieve themselves and mate in public without feeling any sense of embarrassment. Any human being who loses this trait of (حياء) “Haya’a”, will behave like an animal or even worse. The antonym of (حياء) “Haya’a” in Arabic is “badha’a” (بذاءة,) immodesty or “fahisha” (فاحشة), lewdness or obscenity.

The term (حياء) “Haya’a” and the term (حياة) which is “life” are related and thus the person who does not have (حياء) “Haya’a” is a person who does not have a human life. The attribute of (حياء) “Haya’a resides in the soul and its effect is openly manifested by the noble actions of the human limbs

I struggled to come with an English term equivalent for the Arabic term (حياء) “Haya’a”. If you search for the translation of (حياء) “Haya’a”, you will find that the common translation is shyness. But shyness has negative connotations because it infers fear and being timid. Also, the American Psychological Association defines shyness as the tendency to feel awkward, worried, or tense during social encounters, especially with unfamiliar people. Severely shy people may have physical symptoms like blushing, sweating, a pounding heart, or upset stomach; self-consciousness, feelings of insecurity and a tendency to withdraw from social interactions.

If you search the Quran for verses that includes terms that have the same root as (حياء) “Haya’a”, you find for example in Surah Al-Qasas (28:25):

فَجَآءَتۡهُ إِحۡدَٮٰهُمَا تَمۡشِى عَلَى ٱسۡتِحۡيَآءٍ۬ قَالَتۡ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدۡعُوكَ لِيَجۡزِيَكَ أَجۡرَ مَا سَقَيۡتَ لَنَا‌ۚ

Then one of the two sisters came to him (Moses), walking shyly (bashfully). She said: “My father is calling you so that he may reward you for having watered our flock for us.”

She was not walking shyly because of fear, worry or lack of confidence but rather because of her decency and high moral character that she did not want to appear in front of a stranger unless there is a valid reason.

In many of his sayings, the Prophet (PBUH) stressed to the companions the importance of (حياء) “Haya’a”.

Muadh ibn Jabal (RA) narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن معاذ بن جبل – رضي الله عنهما – قال : قال النبي – صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم : ( إِنَّ لِكُلِّ دِينٍ خُلُقًا ، وَخُلُقُ الْإِسْلَامِ الْحَيَاءُ )

“For every religion there is character, and the character of Islam is (حياء) “Haya’a.”

Ibn Omar (RA) narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن ابن عمر – رضي الله عنه – قال : قال النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم «الحياء والإيمان قرنا جميعًا، فإذا رفع أحدهما رفع الآخر»

The (حياء) “Haya’a and Eman (faith) are companions of one another, if one of them is absent, the other is absent. [Baihaqi]

Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:
قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ؛ وَالإِيمَانُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَالْبَذَاءُ مِنَ الْجَفَاءِ؛ وَالْجَفَاءُ فِي النَّارِ» رواه الترمذي وابن ماجه

The Haya’a is from Eman ( faith), and faith is in Paradise. Obscenity is from insolence, and insolence is in the Hellfire.” (Tirmidhi)

Abu Huraira (RA) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
الإِيمَانُ بِضْعٌ وَسِتُّونَ شُعْبَةً، وَالْحَيَاءُ شُعْبَةٌ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ

“The faith (Eman) is sixty and odd branches―and Al Haya’a is a part of the faith.” (Bukhari)

Abdullah bin ‘Umar (RA) said: “Once Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) passed by an Ansārī man who was admonishing his brother for being too modest and shy. On that Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said:
وقد مَرَّ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ – وَهُوَ يَعِظُ أَخَاهُ فِي الْحَيَاءِ – فَقَالَ لَهُ: «دَعْهُ؛ فَإِنَّ الْحَيَاءَ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ» رواه البخاري ومسلم

“Leave him, for indeed Al-Haya’a is a part of Eman (faith).” (Bukhari)

(حياء) “Haya’a serves as internal restraint that helps the true believer to maintain correct behavior and uphold proper values and prevents him from doing anything that is unpleasant, unbecoming or unacceptable from the social or religious point of view.

The (حياء) “Haya’a is a source of all goodness, the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن عِمْرَانَ بْن حُصَيْنٍ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ: “الْحَيَاءُ لَا يَأْتِي إِلَّا بِخَيْرٍ” رواه البخاري ومسلم

“Haya’a does not bring anything except good.” (Bukhari and Muslim)

Anas bin Malik (RA) reported that the prophet (PBUH) said:
عَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا كَانَ الْفُحْشُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا شَانَهُ، وَمَا كَانَ الْحَيَاءُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا زَانَهُ» صحيح – رواه الترمذي وابن ماجه

Whenever lewdness is in anything, it will make it ugly; and whenever the Haya’a in anything, it will make it beautiful. (Tirmidhi)

Aby Masoud Al-Ansari (RA) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:
أبي مسعود عقبة بن عمرو الأنصاري رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن مما أدرك الناس من كلام النبوة الأولى : إذا لم تستح فاصنع ما شئت ) رواه البخاري

“From the sayings of the early Prophets that have reached the people is: ‘If you have no Haya’a, then do whatever you want.’” (Bukhari)

This proves that the one who loses his sense of (حياء) “Haya’a, will end up doing whatever he wants without any restraint from his conscience.

The Prophet (PBUH) warned his people to beware of losing the Haya’a and to always supplicate to Allah to keep it in their hearts.
عن أبي هريرة قال :قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أول ما يرفع من هذه الأمة الحياء والأمانة فسلوها الله عز وجل) رواه الطبراني

“Haya’s and Trustworthiness will be the first to go from this nation; therefore, keep asking Allah for them.”

If a person has Haya’a, he will never want others to see him in any compromising position not because he is afraid of them but because he honors himself. The companion Aktham ibn Al-Sify (RA) said:
“Whoever does something in secret that he will embarrassed to do it in public, he has no value for himself.”

Obviously, we are not talking about lawful things that one can only do in private.

The Haya’a of a person from his own self will make him conscious that he does not allow his reputation to be questioned even for a mistake that others may make in interpreting his action.
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لَمَّا خرج ليلاً؛ لِيوصِلَ إحدى زوجاته إلى دارها فمر به رجلان فأسرعا، فناداهما، وقال: «عَلَى رِسْلِكُمَا، إِنَّهَا صَفِيَّةُ بِنْتُ حُيَيٍّ»

On one night, the Prophet (PBUH) was walking with his wife Safiya.  Two Ansari men met him, and they started walking fast to pass the Prophet (PBUH). He called them: “Stop, this is my wife Safiya bint Huyay.”
“Glory to Allah, O Allah’s messenger (this is an expression to mean that how dare we ever think anything bad about you),” they said.

The Prophet (PBUH) replied: “
Satan circulates in the human being as blood circulates in the body, and I was afraid that Satan may whisper something in your hearts.”

The (حياء) “Haya’a is very important trait for Muslims because it is related to one of Allah’s glorified attributes.
عن عبدالله بن عمر قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ، يَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْرًا»

“Verily your Lord is Generously Shy to return the hands of His servant who raises them to Him (in supplication) empty.”
[Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah]

Obviously, the shyness of Allah from His slave is the shyness of generosity, bounty, goodness, and majesty.

Any moral person should have Haya’a from four entities:  Haya’a from Allah (الحياء من الله), Haya’a from the Angels (الحياء من الملائكة), Haya’a from people (الحياء من الناس) and Haya’a from one’s own self (الحياء من النفس).

It is an essential part of a Muslim’s belief that Allah is seeing and hearing everything he does or say and even what is in his heart.
وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعۡلَمُ مَا تُوَسۡوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفۡسُهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ حَبۡلِ ٱلۡوَرِيدِ

“And indeed, We have created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him. And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.” (Qaf 50:16)

Allah also says:
أَرَءَيۡتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰٓ (١٣) أَلَمۡ يَعۡلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ (العلق)

“Have you noted the one who denies (the Quran) and turns away? (13) Is he not aware that Allah sees?” (Al-Alaq 96:13-14)

A true believer will be shy from Allah and does not want to do anything that will cause him embarrassment when he meets Allah.

Having Haya’a from Allah is very broad, as the Prophet (PBUH) explained.  Ibn Masoud (RA) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:
عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «استحيوا من الله حق الحياء». فقالوا: يا رسول الله، إنا نستحيي والحمد لله. قال: «ليس ذاك، ولكن الاستحياء من الله حق الحياء: أن تحفظ الرأس وما وعى، والبطن وما حوى، ولتذكر الموت والبلى، ومن أراد الآخرة ترك زينة الدنيا، فمن فعل ذلك فقد استحيا من الله حق الحياء»

“Be shy from Allah as you should truly be shy from Him”
The companions said,
‘O Messenger of Allah, indeed, we are shy from Him.’
The Prophet (PBUH) said:
‘It is not that I mean. Being truly shy from Allah means that you preserve your head and what it contains (thoughts, eyes, ears, tongue), and preserve your belly and what it encompasses (lawful food, and the private parts), and you remember death and the decay in the grave. And whoever desires the Hereafter, let him leave the adornments of the world. Whoever does that has been shy from Allah as he should truly be shy from Him.’
[Al-Tirmidhi]

Saeed ibn Yazeed (RA) said: I told the Prophet (PBUH) give me advice. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
وعَنْ سَعِيدِ بنِ يَزِيدَ الأَزْدِيِّ؛ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: أَوْصِنِي، قَالَ: “أُوصِيكَ أَنْ تَسْتَحِيَ مِنَ اللَّهِ كَمَا تَسْتَحِي مِنَ الرَّجُلِ الصَّالِحِ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ”

“Be shy from Allah as you are shy from the most righteous man among your people”.

Part of Al-Haya’s is covering not exposing your naked body.   Ya’ala ibn Ummaiyah (RA) said that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) saw a man bathing in an open place without a lower garment. So, he (the Prophet) ascended the pulpit, praised and extolled Allah and said:
عن يعلى بن أمية -رضي الله عنه- أنَّ رسولَ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلًا يغتسل بلا إزار، فصعِد المنبرَ، فحمِد اللهَ وأثنى عليه، ثم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: “إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَيِيٌّ سِتِّيرٌ، يُحِبُّ الْحَيَاءَ وَالسِّتْرَ، فَإِذَا اغْتَسَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَسْتَتِرْ”

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is (حَيِيٌّ) shy and concealing, and He loves shyness and concealment. So, when any of you bathes, let him conceal himself (i.e., from the sight of people).
[Abu Dawud, An-Nasaa’ee]

Unfortunately, we often see the loss of this form of Haya’a. One of the clear signs of the loss of Haya’a is when people dress in a provocative way.
يَـٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ لَا يَفۡتِنَنَّڪُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَ أَبَوَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ يَنزِعُ عَنۡہُمَا لِبَاسَہُمَا لِيُرِيَہُمَا سَوۡءَٲتِهِمَآ‌

O Children of Adam! Let not Satan deceive you, as he got your parents out of the garden, stripping them of their clothing, to show them their private parts. (Al-Araf 7:27)

A noble person should also have Haya’s from the angels who are accompanying him all the time and recording all his actions.
وَإِنَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَحَـٰفِظِينَ (١٠) كِرَامً۬ا كَـٰتِبِينَ (١١) يَعۡلَمُونَ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ

“We appointed over you watchers (Angels), (10) who are noble and writers (of all your deeds), (11) they know all that you do.” (Al-Infitar 82:10-12)

Some of the companions of the Prophet (PBUH) used to tell each other: “you have with you those who never leave alone, so don’t embarrass yourself in front of them, and be generous with them that they don’t see from you except what is good “.

The trait of Haya’a is the internal compass in every person that restrains him from doing anything that is immoral and repulsive and there is no value of any person who loses his Haya’a. Our youth, specifically, should be careful with what they post on social media. They should never post anything that causes an embarrassment to themselves or to others.

We pray to Allah to purify our heart and cleanse our soul and strengthen our internal compass of Haya’a that He does not see or hear us doing anything that is displeasing to Him.

DUA

title: The Relevance and the Myth of Number 3
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

There are certain numbers that appear to have significance in almost all religions, and one of these number is number 3. For many religions, this number created major confusion that caused changing the fundamental message of all Messengers which is the belief in one God. Allah says:

وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيۡهِ أَنَّهُ ۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۟ فَٱعۡبُدُونِ (٢٥)

“And We sent no messenger before you, but We revealed to him that there is no God but I, so worship Me.” (Al-Anbia 21:25)

Sometimes, it is hard to understand the cause of the confusion in some religions since their text includes many verses that clearly state that God is one. As example in the Bible, there are several verses that without a doubt state that God is One. As examples:

“Hear, O Israel! The Lord is our God, the Lord is one! (Deuteronomy 6:4)

Jesus answered, “The foremost is, ‘Hear, O Israel! The Lord our God is one Lord. (Mark 12:29)

The scribe said to Him, “Right, Teacher; You have truly stated that He is One, and there is no one else besides Him. (Mark 12:33)

When we examine the Quran and the sayings (hadith) of the Prophet (PBUH), we note that number 3 is frequently mentioned and thus it seems to have significance.

Number 3 came in the Quran 19 times in 19 Ayat in 15 Surat.   The derivates of the number 3 also came in the Quran, as example:
- Number 30 came 2 times
- Number 300 came 1 time.
- Number 3000 came 1 time
- 2/3 came 2 times
- 1/3 came 3 times

We also note several interesting statistics of the Quran related to the multiples of 3. As example:
The Quran includes 114 Surat which is 38 multiplied by 3.
The Quran includes 30 parts (أجزاء) which is 10 multiplied by 3
The Quran includes 6237 Ayat which is 703 multiplied by 3 times 3.

The following are some example of verses in the Quran that specify number 3:

1/ Allah says regarding the sign He gave to Prophet Zachariah when he was informed that he will have a son at both his and his wife old age; it was to stop speaking for 3 days:

قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آَيَةً قَالَ آَيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمْزًا (آل عمران 41)

“He [Zachariah] said ‘O my Lord! Make for me a sign!’ He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to the people for three days except through gestures.” (Al-Emran 3:41)

The same sign was repeated in surah Maryam with an additional information that his not speaking was involuntary.

قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً۬‌ۚ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَـٰثَ لَيَالٍ۬ سَوِيًّ۬ا (١٠)

“He (Zachariah) said: “My Lord! Make for me a sign.” He said: “Your sign is that you shall not speak to the people for three nights, though you will be sound.” (Maryam 19: 10)

So, his sign was not to speak to the people for 3 days, but this was not voluntarily rather it was involuntary; he just cannot speak although he was sound; meaning that he has no sickness of any form.

2/ For those who cannot afford making an offering during the Hajj, they have to fast three days while they are there:

فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَـٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِى ٱلْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ (البقرة 196)

“Whoever takes advantage of the Ummrah with the Hajj shall make an offering of whatever animal he can easily afford; however, he who cannot afford any shall fast for three days during the Hajj and for seven days after your return: they are ten in all.” (Al-Baqara 2:196)

3/ The expiation of an oath (كفارة الحنث باليمين) is fasting 3 days.

لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِىٓ أَيْمَـٰنِكُمْ وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلْأَيْمَـٰنَ فَكَفَّـٰرَتُهُۥ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَـٰكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَـٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّـٰرَةُ أَيْمَـٰنِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ وَٱحْفَظُوٓا۟ أَيْمَـٰنَكُمْ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (المائدة 89)

“Allah does not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, but He will hold you accountable for oaths that you have sworn in earnest, its expiation feeding ten needy persons at an average of what you feed your family with, or by clothing them, or by freeing a slave. However, if one cannot afford such, he has to fast for three days. This is expiation for the oaths that have sworn. Be mindful of your oaths!’ That is how Allah makes His revelation clear to you, so that you may be grateful.” (Al-Maeda 5:89)

4/ The divorced women cannot marry except after three monthly courses

وَالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ (البقرة 228)

“And the divorced women shall wait (without remarrying) for three (monthly) courses:” (Al-Baqara 2:228)

5/ After 3 announcements of divorce, the divorce is final, and the woman must marry someone else before she can remarry her first husband.

الطَّلَاقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسَانٍ (229)……

“Divorce is pronounced twice and then to return in all fairness ….” (Al-Baqara 2:229)

فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدُ حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُ فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا إِنْ ظَنَّا أَنْ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ (230) (البقرة 230)

“And if he divorces her (the third time), she is not lawful for him unless she marries another man. Should he too divorce her, it is no sin for them that they return to each other, if they are able to observe the limits set by Allah”. (Al-Baqara 2:230)

6/ Prophet Saleh gave a 3-day warning to his people before their destruction after they slaughtered the she-camel

وَيَـٰقَوۡمِ هَـٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَڪُمۡ ءَايَةً۬ فَذَرُوهَا تَأۡڪُلۡ فِىٓ أَرۡضِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءٍ۬ فَيَأۡخُذَكُمۡ عَذَابٌ۬ قَرِيبٌ۬ (٦٤) فَعَقَرُوهَا فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُواْ فِى دَارِكُمۡ ثَلَـٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ۬ ذَٲلِكَ وَعۡدٌ غَيۡرُ مَكۡذُوبٍ۬ (هود)

‘’ O my people! this she-camel of Allah, it is a sign to you, leave her free to eat in in the land of Allah and do not touch her with evil, lest a near punishment should seize you.” (64) But they killed her. So, he said: “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. This is a promise that will not be belied.” (Hud 11:64-65)

7/ We are protected in our mothers’ wombs with 3 veils.

يَخۡلُقُكُمۡ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِڪُمۡ خَلۡقً۬ا مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَلۡقٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتٍ۬ ثَلَـٰثٍ۬ ذَٲلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصۡرَفُونَ (٦)

“He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation in three veils of darkness, such is Allah your Lord. His is the kingdom. There is no God but He. To where are you turning away?” (Al-Zumur 39:6)

8/ We have 3 periods of full privacy in our homes

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَـٰنُكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَبۡلُغُواْ ٱلۡحُلُمَ مِنكُمۡ ثَلَـٰثَ مَرَّٲتٍ۬ مِّن قَبۡلِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡعِشَآءِ ثَلَـٰثُ عَوۡرَٲتٍ۬ لَّكُمۡ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ جُنَاحُۢ بَعۡدَهُنَّ

“O you who believe! Let those whom your hands possess, and the children among you who have not come to the age of puberty ask your permission (before entering in your room) on three occasions; before Fajr prayer, and while you take off your clothes at noon, and after the ‘Ishâ’ prayer. (These) three times are of privacy for you, other than these times there is no harm on you or on them.” (Al-Noor 24: 58)

These are example for few verses in the Quran where the number 3 has been specified. Also, many of the sayings of the Prophet (PBUH) specify the number 3.

As examples of hadith that specified number 3:

1/ Three things make the person feels the sweetness of Eman. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ثلاث من كن فيه وجد حلاوة الإيمان أن يكون الله ورسوله أحب إليه مما سواهما وأن يحب المرء لا يحبه إلا لله وأن يكره أن يعود في الكفر كما يكره أن يقذف في النار (البخاري)

“Whoever possesses the following three qualities will have the sweetness of Eman: 1) that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else., 2) that he loves a person, and he does not love him except for Allah’s sake.2) that he hates to revert to Atheism (disbelief) as he hates to be thrown into the fire. (Bukhari)

2/ Three things that confirm hypocrisy; The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث إذا كن في الرجل فهو المنافق الخالص إن حدث كذب وإن وعد أخلف وإن اؤتمن خان (مسند الإمام أحمد)

Anyone who has these three traits is a hypocrite: 1) Whenever he speaks, he lies. 2) whenever he makes a promise, he does not fulfill it, and 3) Whenever he is entrusted, he breaks the trust.

3/ Three Things that prevent a person from entering in Hell. The Messenger (ﷺ) said

عن أنس بن مالك – قال : سمعت رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – يقول : ” ثلاث من كن فيه حرم على النار وحرمت النار عليه : إيمان بالله ، وحب الله – تبارك وتعالى – وأن يلقى في النار فيحترق أحب إليه من أن يرجع إلى الكفر ” . (رواه أحمد)

Whoever has these three traits won’t burn in Hell: 1) Belief in Allah, 2) Loves Allah, and 3) Being thrown into the fire and burnt is more beloved to him than to disbelief.

4/ Allah is pleased with 3 things, and He hates 3 things from you. The Messenger of Allah [ ﷺ], said,

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْضَى لَكُمْ ثَلاثًا، وَيَسْخَطُ لَكُمْ ثَلاثًا، فَيَرْضَى لَكُمْ أَنْ تَعْبُدُوهُ وَلا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَأَنْ تَعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا، وَأَنْ تُنَاصِحُوا مَنْ وَلَّى اللَّهُ أَمْرَكُمْ، وَيَسْخَطُ لَكُمْ: قِيلَ وَقَالَ، وَإِضَاعَةَ الْمَالِ، وَكَثْرَةَ السُّؤَالِ. (مُسْلِمٌ)

“Allah is pleased with three things from you, and He is hates three things from you. He is pleased that: 1) you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, 2) that you, all together, take hold of the rope of Allah, and 3) that you give good counsel to the one to whom Allah gives command over you.

He is angry with you for 1) gossiping, 2) wasting your money, and 3) asking too many questions.

5/ There are 3 kinds of Judges. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

عَنْ بُرَيْدَةَ  قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: الْقُضَاةُ ثَلَاثَةٌ: اثْنَانِ فِي النَّارِ، وَوَاحِدٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ: رَجُلٌ عَرَفَ الْحَقَّ فَقَضَى بِهِ، فَهُوَ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَرَجُلٌ عَرَفَ الْحَقَّ فَلَمْ يَقْضِ بِهِ، وَجَارَ فِي الْحُكْمِ، فَهُوَ فِي النَّارِ، وَرَجُلٌ لَمْ يَعْرِفِ الْحَقَّ، فَقَضَى لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى جَهْلٍ، فَهُوَ فِي النَّارِ. (رَوَاهُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ)

The judges are three: Two judges are in the Fire, and a judge in Paradise. 1) A man who judges with the truth, and he knows that. This one is in the Fire. 2) A judge who judges while not knowing and thus ruins the rights of the people. He is in the Fire. 3) A judge who judges with the truth, that is the one in Paradise. “

6/ The 3 requests that the Prophet (PBUH) asked for. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

عن عامر بن سعد، عن أبيه، أن رسول قَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏ سَأَلْتُ رَبِّي ثَلاَثًا فَأَعْطَانِي ثِنْتَيْنِ وَمَنَعَنِي وَاحِدَةً سَأَلْتُ رَبِّي أَنْ لاَ يُهْلِكَ أُمَّتِي بِالسَّنَةِ فَأَعْطَانِيَهَا وَسَأَلْتُهُ أَنْ لاَ يُهْلِكَ أُمَّتِي بِالْغَرَقِ فَأَعْطَانِيَهَا وَسَأَلْتُهُ أَنْ لاَ يَجْعَلَ بَأْسَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ فَمَنَعَنِيهَا ” . أخرجه مسلم

“I asked my Lord three things, and He has granted me two and withheld one. I asked my Lord that my nation should not be destroyed because of famine, and He granted me this. And I asked Him that my nation should not be destroyed by drowning (by deluge) and He granted me this. And I asked Him that there will be no transgression between them., but He did not grant it.

7/ There are only three Masjids that you are allowed to make a special trip to pray in them. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ (لا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد: المسجد الحرام، ومسجد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومسجد الأقصى). صحيح مسلم

“Only three masjids you can take a special trip to visit (for prayers): the Sacred Mosque of Makkah, this mosque of mine (in Madinah), and Al-Aqsa Mosque (in Jerusalem).” (Bukhari and Muslim).

8/ The 3 person whose actions are not recorded. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ عَلِيٍّ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ رُفِعَ الْقَلَمُ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ عَنْ النَّائِمِ حَتَّى يَسْتَيْقِظَ وَعَنْ الصَّبِيِّ حَتَّى يَحْتَلِمَ وَعَنْ الْمَعْتُوهِ حَتَّى يَعْقِلَ – صحيح البخاري

“There are three (persons) whose actions are not recorded: the sleeper until he awakes, the boy till he reaches puberty, and the insane until he comes to reason,

9/ The 3 things that follow the deceased. The Messenger of Allah said:

عن أنس  عن رسولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: يتْبعُ الميْتَ ثلاثَةٌ: أهلُهُ ومالُه وعمَلُه، فيرْجِع اثنانِ ويبْقَى واحدٌ: يرجعُ أهلُهُ ومالُه، ويبْقَى عملُه (متفقٌ عليه).

“The dead person is followed by three: His family, his wealth and his deeds. Two of them return: his family and his wealth, and only one remains, his deeds. “[8]

10/ There are 3 forms of legacy for a person. The Prophet ({BUH) said:

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ إِذَا مَاتَ الْإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ (مسلم)

When the person dies, his deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.” (Muslim)

All what we have heard so far are revelations that involve the number 3. They address certain legal rules, encouragements, and warnings. But none of this impacts the key article of belief in the oneness of Allah. However, it is unfortunate that this number 3 created confusion in the doctrine of several religions. Allah provided a general warning for all those who suggest there are three gods by saying:

لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَـٰثَةٍ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلَّآ إِلَـٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ وَإِن لَّمْ يَنتَهُوا۟ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

“Indeed, the disbelievers are those who say, ‘Allah is the third of three’ – while there is no god but One God. If they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment shall certainly befall such disbelievers.” (Al-Maeda 5:73)

While we may think that only Christians believe in the trinity, this belief exists in several other traditions.

The Greek Mythology suggests three gods: 1) Zeus – ruler of the sky, 2) Poseidon – ruler of the sea, and 3) Hades – ruler of the underworld

The Roman Mythology suggests three equivalent gods: Jupiter, Neptune, and Pluto.

The same concept is in Hinduism, they believe in three gods: Brahma is the Creator, Vishnu is the Preserver, and Mahesh/shive is the Destroyer. They believe that Lord Mahesh, the third divine godhead in the Trinity, is the supreme and has ultimate power.

While there no three gods in the Jewish tradition, but number 3 is considered important. In the Jewish tradition of the Kabbalah, it is believed that the soul consists of three parts, with the highest being neshamah (“breath”), the middle being ruach (“wind” or “spirit”) and the lowest being nefesh (“repose”).

It interesting and may be even unfortunate, that even Muslim scholars were not immune from introducing number 3 in the belief of Muslims including the corner stone of Islam which is Tawheed (Monotheism), Oneness of Allah. They proposed that the concept of Tawhid involves 3 elements:

1. Tawheed al-Ruboobeeyah (توحيد الربوبية) (The unity of Lordship over all creations)
2. Tawheed al-Uluhiah (وتوحيد الألوهية) (The unity of Godship or Unity of worship).
3. Tawheed al-Asmaa-was-sifaat (توحيد الأسماء والصفات) (The unity of Allah’s name and attributes).

Keep in mind that the Prophet (PBUH) never made this distinction, and this was merely an effort by some scholars, mainly ibn Taymiyyah (born in 661 H) to explain the concept of Tawhid. Although this appears to be an innocent explanation of the concept of Tawheed, division occurred among Muslim scholars regarding making such divisions.

In addition, Muslim scholars have also given significance to number three by classifying Allah’s glorious names is 3 categories.

1. Perfection attributes (صفات الكمال) such as The Creator (الخالق), The Provider (الرزاق) the eternal (الصمد) The First, The Last,
2. Majestic and imposing attributes (صفات الجلال) such as Compeller (الجبار) and the Avenger (المنتقم)
3. Magnificent and Beautiful attributes (صفات الجمال) such as the Merciful (الرحمن), the Forgiver (الغفار), The Gentle (اللطيف)

While number 3 appears to be important for certain legal rulings, its real danger arises when it creeps in the pure belief in Allah. Therefore, we should only keep its relevance to elements of guidance as we quoted from the Quran and the hadith that mentioned the number.

In Islam, accomplishing certain tasks in odd numbers is preferred and the first odd number after 1 is 3.

It is interesting to note that number 3 surrounds us and serves as important part in our lives: As examples:
- The first number that denotes summation is number 3, it is the summation of 1 plus 2.
- We establish the location of any point in the space by 3 dimensions.
- Time passes through 3 stages: past, present, and future
- Three is the first number that forms a geometrical figure: the triangle.
- Water is the source of all lives is formed of 3 atoms, two hydron and one oxygen (H2O)
- There are three key components of each atom, electron, proton, and neutron.
- There are three valence quarks: in a Proton: two up quarks and one down quark,
- All matters have 3 forms: gas, liquid, and solids.
- There are three primary colors: red, yellow, and blue and the other colors come by mixing them.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom to appreciate the relevance of number 3 in nature and some Islamic rulings and protect us from confusing our basic belief with this number and cleanse the heart of those who are confused to return to the pure belief in Allah

DUA

content:
The Key for the Most Valuable Treasure

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه  ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

As you know, after the weekend Fajr prayer and the lecture, we go to the Masjid’s club and have breakfast and engage in general discussions. Yesterday, the question was raised on how did the poor tribes of Arabia, who were backward in culture and morality relative to the Roman and Persian empires, in less than 30 years be transformed by nothing other than the teaching of Islam to become the world leaders in knowledge, morality, spirituality, human brotherhood, freedom and equality that helped them establish a new civilization.  While the Muslim world today has the same Islam and have access to wealth, knowledge and natural resources but they are the most backward and corrupt among the civilized world.

I thought that a good subject for today is to try to uncover the key to the treasure of Islam that was responsible for helping early Muslims to establish this great civilization in a very short time.  Hopefully, if we can find the key, we can transform at least ourselves to contribute to enhancing and purifying the civilization that we live under here.

I gave two talks previously in which I discussed why the Quran is the most valuable blessing that Allah granted to mankind and why we need to set a strategy to share this blessing with our fellow citizens otherwise we will be responsible in front of Allah for concealing this great blessing from all those who haven’t heard of it other than the distorted image.  Some suggestions on how to share the Quran with others included:  distributing copies of the Quran, sponsoring a radio program to present recitation of the Quran, holding lectures and inviting non-Muslims to them, taking advantage of social media, and expanding our interfaith program.

These are all good ideas, but do we have any experience that these approaches were successful in broader scale.  The answer is no; yes, we may identify individual cases, but these are all unique.  However, there is a clue given in the Quran that help us understand why the Prophet (PBUH) was successful and why the early Muslims were successful after him in spreading the message of Islam.  Allah says in the beginning of Surat Al-Bayyina (Surah 98):

لَمۡ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأۡتِيَہُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَةُ (١)

“Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Book and the polytheists were not to be untied (from their wrong belief) until there comes to them clear evidence.” (Al-Bayyina 98:1)

This verse clearly states that the disbelievers will not leave and untie themselves from their disbelief and shirk unless clear evidence comes to them.  The question is what is this clear evidence that they need to abandon their disbelief and associating other entities with Allah.  Allah answers this question by saying:

رَسُولٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتۡلُواْ صُحُفً۬ا مُّطَهَّرَةً۬ (٢) فِيہَا كُتُبٌ۬ قَيِّمَةٌ۬ (٣)

“A Messenger from Allah, reciting (the Qur’an) purified scrolls (2) Containing valuable books.” (Al-Bayyina 98:2-3)

Allah identified the clear evidence as involving two things: 1) a messenger from Allah and 2) a revelation from Allah in the form of pure and valuable scripture.  So, scripture alone is not sufficient to change people’s disbelief, they also need a messenger who is qualified to deliver the message. Only then, people will be held accountable for rejecting the revelation.

Allah reinforces this point by emphasizing that people will only be punished for their disbelief if Allah sends them a messenger and they reject the message that was delivered to them by the chosen messenger, Allah says Surat Al-Isra: 

مَّنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَہۡتَدِى لِنَفۡسِهِۦ‌ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ۬ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰ‌ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبۡعَثَ رَسُولاً۬ (١٥)

“Whoever accepts guidance, he is guided for his own benefit. And whoever goes astray, he goes astray to his own loss. No bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another. And it is befitting for Us to punish until We send a Messenger.” (Al-Isra 17:15)

The Quran is the last message that Allah sent to mankind and Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is the last messenger.  Allah informed us that He will preserve the Quran as He said:

إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ ۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ (٩)

“Verily We: Ourselves, have sent down the Dhikr (the Quran) and surely, We will guard it.” (Al-Hijr 15:9)

So, the final divine book that Allah sent to mankind is guaranteed to be guarded by Allah from any alteration and thus it is available to everyone.   But will its availability make the disbelievers responsible for their disbelief by rejecting it.  Not likely, because Allah says that they need two things a divine book and a messenger assigned by Allah who is qualified to deliver the divine book.

Now, we are facing a challenge because Prophet Mohmmad (PBUH) is the last messenger and he has already passed away, does this mean that all the disbelievers now have a pass since they will not have a messenger from Allah. Not quite, because Allah has already assigned so many people to serve as Messengers from Him to deliver the Quran as Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) did. Who are those messengers?  Did Allah specify them in the Quran, the answer is yes:  Allah says:

قُلۡ هَـٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۟ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى‌ۖ وَسُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۟ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ (١٠٨)

“Say: “This is my way; I invite unto Allah with sure knowledge, I and whosoever follows me. And Glorified and Exalted is Allah and I am not of the idolaters.” (Yusuf 12:108)

So, after the death of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), the messengers become all those who claim to be his followers.  Since Allah guaranteed to guard the Quran, does Allah guard those followers who are committed to deliver His book to the disbelievers? The answer is there in the Quran too.  Allah makes a declaration and promise to all those followers of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) who will continue his legacy by delivering the Quran to all those whom Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) did not meet; Allah says to everyone of them:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغۡ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ‌ۖ وَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلۡ فَمَا بَلَّغۡتَ رِسَالَتَهُ ۥ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡصِمُكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَہۡدِى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ (٦٧)

“O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His Message. And Allah will protect you from mankind. Verily, Allah does not guide the people who disbelieve.” (Al-Maeda 5:67)

So, now we know that Allah guaranteed to protect the Quran and protect the followers of Prophet Mahammad who take the responsibility to deliver the Quran to others.

The question, now, is whether anyone who claims to be a follower of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) should serve as a messenger to deliver the final message of Allah to all those who haven’t received it. It seems that the verse in Surat Yusuf does not give any exceptions.

قُلۡ هَـٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۟ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى‌ۖ وَسُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۟ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ (١٠٨)

“Say: “This is my way; I (Mohammad) invite unto Allah with sure knowledge, I and whosoever follows me.  And Glorified and Exalted is Allah and I am not of the idolaters.” (Yusuf 12:108)

Since we claim to be followers of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), we have been designated as messengers by Allah to deliver the Quran which is Allah’s final message to mankind.  If anyone of us feels that this is not his obligation, he may need to question whether he is really a true follower of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH).  This may a harsh reality for almost all of us but unless someone finds out that there are exceptions that make us not responsible, this reality remains.

And if you are still in doubt that this is your responsibility, justify then how are you going to be a witness over other people as Allah expects from you as He said:

وَكَذَٲلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةً۬ وَسَطً۬ا لِّتَڪُونُواْ شُہَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدً۬ا‌ۗ

Thus, have We made of you a justly balanced nation, so that you be witnesses over the people and the Messenger be a witness against you.” (Al-Baqara 2:143)

Someone may ask whether this responsibly is obligatory on everyone (فرض عين) who claims to be a follower of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) or the obligation is removed if a group of Muslims in the community perform this obligation (فرض كفاية).  This question may not be relevant for a Muslim who lives in the west, because who will be able to reach your own non-Muslim friends, colleagues, neighbors, service providers, etc., other than you. If you are convinced that others will reach them, then your responsibility will be at least to support those who are fulfilling this task on your behalf.

This responsibility of delivering the Quran is not simple, and thus it must have qualification requirements because if we don’t have the proper qualifications, we may be misleading the disbelievers instead of guiding them.  Therefore, Allah teaches us a Dua to say to ensure that we are not a cause for misleading others, the Dua is:

رَبَّنَا لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا فِتۡنَةً۬ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا رَبَّنَآ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ (٥)

“Our Lord! Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord! Lo! You and only You, are the All-Mighty, the All-Wise” (Al-Mumtahina 60:5)

Now, what are the Qualifications that Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) was emphasizing and training His companions to make them qualified to deliver Allah’s final message to others.

If we examine the nature of the message of Islam, we note that it is defined by two key axes. One axis is Monotheism (التوحيد) and the second axis is values (القيم) and Morals (الاخلاق).  This second axis of moral and values is the one on which the Prophet (PBUH) spent his major efforts to develop in the companions because without achieving the most exalted character they will not be qualified to deliver the message.

The level of transformation that the Prophet (PBUH) was able to achieve in the character of his companions is quite amazing.  This transformation was the key for the success of the companions in spreading the message of Islam all over the world in a very short time and in achieving all the miraculous success that we know of.  So, if we claim to be followers of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), we need to start by looking at our character.   If we assess that our character is the most honorable, then we are qualified to deliver the Quran to others, otherwise, we need to work on purifying our character. 

Where is the justification that the 2nd axis of defining a Muslim is his character and not the extent of his prayers and fasting?  We note that when Allah praised the Prophet (PBUH) in the Quran, He selected the most important attribute, and this attribute was not his devotion in prayer or his continuous fast or even his courage.  No, it was his character, Allah said:

وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ۬ (٤)

“And you are surely on an exalted character.” (Al-Qalam 68:4)

And the Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the primary purpose of his mission by saying:

إنّما بُعثت لأُتمم مكارم الأخلاق”.

“I have not been sent except to perfect the good manners.”

Allah also emphasized that the role of the Prophet (PBUH) is not only to recite the Quran but to purify the heart of the companions before even teaching them the Quran, Allah says:

هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي الأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولاً مِنْهُمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِهِ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمْ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَإِنْ كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ [الجمعة:2].

“It is He Who has sent amongst the Unlettered a Messenger from among themselves, to rehearse to them His Signs, sanctify them, and teach them the book (Quran) and wisdom, – while before, that they were in manifest error.”  (Al-Juma’a 62:2)

لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِهِ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمْ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَإِنْ كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ(164).آل عمران.

Allah did confer a great favor on the believers when He sent them a Messenger from among themselves, rehearse to them His Signs, sanctify them, and teach them the book (Quran) and wisdom, while before that, they were in manifest error. (Al-Imran 3:164)

How did the Prophet (PBUH) develop the upstanding moral character in the companions within a very short time to make them qualified to serve as Messengers of Allah to deliver Allah’s final message to mankind? We note that the Prophet (PBUH) dedicated most of his time for this task, and he used multiple approaches.  In this talk, I plan to identify 6 approaches but hope that you can identify others as you study the subject.

1/ He used himself as example of morality and superior character by always demonstrating his humility, mercy, kindness, patience, generosity, etc.  The Prophet’s character is well recorded and available for us to study and imitate.

2/ The Prophet (PBUH) took advantage of the companions’ love of him to create a competition between them regarding who is more beloved to him. As example, He said to them:  عن جابرٍ بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن من أحبكم إلي وأقربكم مني مجلسا يوم القيامة أحاسنكم أخلاقا، وإن من أبغضكم إلي وأبعدكم مني يوم القيامة الثرثارون والمتشدقون والمتفيهقون». قالوا: يا رسول الله قد علمنا الثرثارين والمتشدقين فما المتفيهقون؟ قال: «المتكبرون» (رواه الترمذي

“The most beloved to me and nearest to me on the Day of Judgment is the one who has the best manners and the most hated by me and the farthest away from me on the day of judgment are those who speak too much and those who are showing off and those who are arrogant”.

At every opportunity, he would remind them about the importance of good character, as example, He (PBUH) said:

(إن الرجل ليُدرك بحسن خُلُقه درجات قائم الليل صائم النهار] أبو داود والحاكم عن عائشة [

A man reaches with his good character the degree of the one who stand in prayers all night and fasts all day”.

3/ The Prophet (PBUH) used the stories to engrain morality and good character in the companions.  There are many stories that most of you have heard before and therefore I am not going to give their details but only highlight the moral character in some of them.

As example of the stories, he (PBUH) told the companions about the three men who were trapped in a cave by a big rock and how their good characters of kindness to the parents, avoiding shameful deeds and protecting people’s rights were the reason why Allah made the rock move to save them.  This emphasizes that only through good character Muslims will be saved in this life and in the Hereafter.

Another example is the story of the leper, the bald-man by skin disease, and the blind-man.  The story is intended to emphasize the moral character of gratitude

Another story is of the man who borrowed 1000 dinars that the Prophet (PBUH) told the companions to emphasize the moral character of honesty and fulfilling commitment.

There are other stories such as the Prostitute who was forgiven by Allah to emphasize the importance of mercy and kindness even towards animals.

4/ Another approach that the Prophet (PBUH) used to teach morality and honorable character is through dialogue.   An example is the account of the youth who came to the Prophet (PBUH) and asked to give him permission to commit fornication. Instead of the Prophet (PBUH) getting angry from him and warning him of the punishment that he will receive, he (PBUH) instead had a dialogue with the youth to convince him that this act is improper because a believer loves for others what he loves for himself.   In this account, the Prophet (PBUH) was also teaching the companions the wisdom in handling the youth.

The lesson for the companions was to have them compare their reaction versus the prophet’s.  When the youth made to the request to the prophet (PBUH) the companions who were setting with the Prophet (PBUH) got very angry of the youth and started to reprimand him on how he dares to ask for something like this.  But the Prophet (PBUH) asked them to stop and asked the youth to come and sit close to him and thru dialogue, he taught the youth how to differentiate between good and evil on his own.

5/ The Prophet (PBUH) also used to emphasize honorable character by raising an issue as a question.  As an example, Abu Bakrah (أبي بَكْرة) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) was sitting with the companions, and he said three times:

عن أبي بَكْرة قال: كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ((ألا أنبئكم بأكبرِ الكبائر؟ ثلاثًا: الإشراك بالله، وعقوق الوالدين، وشهادة الزور، أو قول الزور))، وكان رسول الله متكئًا فجلس، فما زال يكررها حتى قلنا: ليته سكت!

وفي الصحيحين عن أنس بنحوه وزاد فيه: ((وقتل النفس)).وورد نحوه عند البخاري من حديث الشعبي عن عبدالله بن عمرو، وزاد فيه: ((اليمين الغَموس))،قلت: وما اليمين الغموس؟ قال: ((الذي يقتطع مال امرئٍ مسلم هو فيها كاذب))

“Shall I not tell you about the worst of major sins?”

They said, “Of course, O Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet said, “They are: 1) associating partners with Allah and 2) disrespecting one’s parents.”

Abu Bakrah (أبي بَكْرة) said, the Prophet (PBUH) was reclining, and he sat up and said:  3) “And false speech.” Abu Bakrah (أبي بَكْرة) said that the Prophet (PBUH) continued to repeat “And false speech” so many times until we wished he would stop.  [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Muslim]

Another example, Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH was sitting with his companions and said to them:   جلس معهم ذات يوم فسألهم “كما روى مسلم في صحيحه عن أبي هريرة”: [أتدرون ما المفلِسُ؟ قالوا: المفلِسُ فينا من لا درهمَ له ولا متاعَ. فقال: إنَّ المفلسَ من أمَّتي، يأتي يومَ القيامةِ بصلاةٍ وصيامٍ وزكاةٍ، ويأتي قد شتم هذا، وقذف هذا، وأكل مالَ هذا، وسفك دمَ هذا، وضرب هذا. فيُعطَى هذا من حسناتِه وهذا من حسناتِه. فإن فَنِيَتْ حسناتُه قبل أن يقضيَ ما عليه، أخذ من خطاياهم فطُرِحت عليه ثمَّ طُرِح في النَّارِ] (رواه مسلم).

“Do you know who the bankrupt is?” They said: The bankrupt among us is the one who has no Dirham nor property.”

The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: “The bankrupt in my nation is the one who comes with prayers, fasting and Zakat on the Day of Judgement, but he comes having abused this one, falsely accusing that one, wrongfully consuming the wealth of this one, spilling the blood of that one, and beating this one. So, he is seated, and they will be requited from his rewards. If his rewards are exhausted before the sins that he committed are requited, then some of their sins will be taken and cast upon him, then he will be cast into the Fire.” [Muslim]

6/ Another approach that the Prophet (PBUH) used to teach honorable character is to take advantage of those who ask him for advice.   He used to give different advice depending on the person who is asking.  He would say to one, be patient and to another be kind to your parents and to a third be humble and to a fourth don’t get angry, and so on.

If you study the hadith of the Prophet (PBUH) you will note that he spent most of the time emphasizing morality and the noble characters far more than he spent teaching them the Quran.  The reason is obvious, without morality, the Quran has no influence on them and without morality, they will not be able to transmit it to others. But with morality, the Quran will be very simple for them to understand and easy for them to apply its commands.  When you examine the Quran, you will note that almost 2/3 of it teaches honorable characters and condemn immorality and evil characters.

The key to the treasure of Islam that the companions were able to own is morality and honorable charter.  Without them, the key is lost, and Muslims will gain absolutely nothing form spending all day and night reading the Quran, praying, and fasting.   These are not aims for themselves, but they are means to help Muslims to achieve the highest level of morality and honorable character to make them embody the final message of Allah to live according to it and transmit it to others.

Without Muslims achieving the highest level of morality and the most noble character, you cannot expect any change in their status and all the materialistic blessings that Allah is granting them are merely tests for them.

If there is one subject that Muslims need to focus on in all their talks is this subject of the prerequisite honorable characters that the Prophet (PBUH) was able to embed in the companions.   As an example, you can see the transformation of the character of a companion such as Omar ibn Al-Kataab by contrasting his character before Islam and his character after Islam to realize the dramatic change.  You will see how this man who was known for his arrogance and rudeness became the humblest and most kind person.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom and the commitment to cleanse our heart and to purify our character to be worthy of being called followers of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and messengers of Allah’s final message to all mankind.

DUA

title: The Key for the Most Valuable Treasure
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه  ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

As you know, after the weekend Fajr prayer and the lecture, we go to the Masjid’s club and have breakfast and engage in general discussions. Yesterday, the question was raised on how did the poor tribes of Arabia, who were backward in culture and morality relative to the Roman and Persian empires, in less than 30 years be transformed by nothing other than the teaching of Islam to become the world leaders in knowledge, morality, spirituality, human brotherhood, freedom and equality that helped them establish a new civilization.  While the Muslim world today has the same Islam and have access to wealth, knowledge and natural resources but they are the most backward and corrupt among the civilized world.

I thought that a good subject for today is to try to uncover the key to the treasure of Islam that was responsible for helping early Muslims to establish this great civilization in a very short time.  Hopefully, if we can find the key, we can transform at least ourselves to contribute to enhancing and purifying the civilization that we live under here.

I gave two talks previously in which I discussed why the Quran is the most valuable blessing that Allah granted to mankind and why we need to set a strategy to share this blessing with our fellow citizens otherwise we will be responsible in front of Allah for concealing this great blessing from all those who haven’t heard of it other than the distorted image.  Some suggestions on how to share the Quran with others included:  distributing copies of the Quran, sponsoring a radio program to present recitation of the Quran, holding lectures and inviting non-Muslims to them, taking advantage of social media, and expanding our interfaith program.

These are all good ideas, but do we have any experience that these approaches were successful in broader scale.  The answer is no; yes, we may identify individual cases, but these are all unique.   However, there is a clue given in the Quran that help us understand why the Prophet (PBUH) was successful and why the early Muslims were successful after him in spreading the message of Islam.   Allah says in the beginning of Surat Al-Bayyina (Surah 98):

لَمۡ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأۡتِيَہُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَةُ (١)

“Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Book and the polytheists were not to be untied (from their wrong belief) until there comes to them clear evidence.” (Al-Bayyina 98:1)

This verse clearly states that the disbelievers will not leave and untie themselves from their disbelief and shirk unless clear evidence comes to them.  The question is what is this clear evidence that they need to abandon their disbelief and associating other entities with Allah.  Allah answers this question by saying:

رَسُولٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتۡلُواْ صُحُفً۬ا مُّطَهَّرَةً۬ (٢) فِيہَا كُتُبٌ۬ قَيِّمَةٌ۬ (٣)

“A Messenger from Allah, reciting (the Qur’an) purified scrolls (2) Containing valuable books.” (Al-Bayyina 98:2-3)

Allah identified the clear evidence as involving two things: 1) a messenger from Allah and 2) a revelation from Allah in the form of pure and valuable scripture.  So, scripture alone is not sufficient to change people’s disbelief, they also need a messenger who is qualified to deliver the message. Only then, people will be held accountable for rejecting the revelation.

Allah reinforces this point by emphasizing that people will only be punished for their disbelief if Allah sends them a messenger and they reject the message that was delivered to them by the chosen messenger, Allah says Surat Al-Isra:

مَّنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَہۡتَدِى لِنَفۡسِهِۦ‌ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ۬ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰ‌ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبۡعَثَ رَسُولاً۬ (١٥)

“Whoever accepts guidance, he is guided for his own benefit. And whoever goes astray, he goes astray to his own loss. No bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another. And it is befitting for Us to punish until We send a Messenger.” (Al-Isra 17:15)

The Quran is the last message that Allah sent to mankind and Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) is the last messenger.  Allah informed us that He will preserve the Quran as He said:

إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ ۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ (٩)

“Verily We: Ourselves, have sent down the Dhikr (the Quran) and surely, We will guard it.” (Al-Hijr 15:9)

So, the final divine book that Allah sent to mankind is guaranteed to be guarded by Allah from any alteration and thus it is available to everyone.   But will its availability make the disbelievers responsible for their disbelief by rejecting it.
