content:
The Quran and its Strategy to Develop Super Cognitive Capacity

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

As preference to this talk, I am not discussing the use of science to explain to the Quran, but I am proposing to use the Quran to promote studying and excelling in all branches of sciences.

In a previous talk, I discussed “The reason for the Decline of the Muslims” and stated that the reason for the decline of Muslims is that we have failed to properly teach the Quran and thus we have not taken advantage of outstanding teaching tool that Allah embedded in it to expand the cognitive Capacity of the Muslim youth. Having superior cognitive capacity is essential to truly serve Allah by being true guardians over the universe that He created for us. We cannot be true guardian over the universe unless we can identify all the laws of the universe that Allah established and these laws don’t change, as Allah said:

فَهَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَۚ فَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلاً۬ۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ ٱللَّهِ تَحۡوِيلاً۬ (٤٣)

“Haven’t they looked at by the Sunnah with earlier people? So, you never find in Allah’s Sunnah any change, and you will never find in Allah’s sunnah any diversion.” (Fatir 35:43)

The Quran has about 77,000 words, the whole Quran can be written in about 300 pages. within these 300 pages, Allah presented many serious topics such as Aqida (creed/beliefs), Sharia (laws), history, social science, natural science, etc. Imam Abu Hamed Al-Ghazali (ابو حامد محمد الغزالي) as well as Imam Abu Bakr al-Arabi (ابو بكر العربى), the Maliki Imam suggested that the Quran encompasses over 70,000 forms of knowledge. To achieve this extent of knowledge in few pages, Allah uses words whose meaning and the information derived from them depend on the seriousness of the reader, level of education and the knowledge available at the time. As the human knowledge expand, the meaning of the verses of the Quran expands. The Prophet (PBUH) described the attributes of Quran by saying:

وَلاَ يَشْبَعُ مِنْهُ الْعُلَمَاءُ، وَلاَ يَخْلُقُ عَلى كَثْرَةِ الرّدّ، وَلاَ تَنْقَضَي عَجَائِبُهُ

“The scholars will always be hungry to study it. Its responses do not need replenishment and its wonders do not end.”

Excluding the verses that discuss Islamic Aqida and basis Shariah for which the Quran uses very concise and precise words, most of the other verses are descriptive and use terminology that can accommodate the increase in human knowledge.

Let me give an example to illustrate how the words of the Quran can be used to derive scientific knowledge:

وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيۡنَـٰهَا بِأَيۡيْدٍ۬ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ (٤٧)

“We have built the heaven (universe) with might, and indeed We are expanding it.” (Al-Dhariyat 51:47)

In 1922, Einstein developed the general relativity field equations that describe a homogeneous and isotropic universe. Since he believed that the universe is static, he introduced a constant that he called “Cosmological Constant” to allow for a static universe solution. However, Alexander Friedmann, a Russian physicist and mathematician, showed that Einstein’s equations without the cosmological constant allow for an expanding universe. Edwin Hubble in 1929 confirmed that the universe is indeed expanding. So, the word “expanding” (مُوسِعُونَ) in the verse was verified by scientists 1300 years later.

The secret of the Quran lies in its methodology that can only be gained by those who bonder and reflect on its verses. Allah said:

كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ

“(This is) a Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings that they should ponder over its verses, and that men of understanding may remember.” (Saad 38:29)

The Quran challenges Muslims to think, reflect and analyze because only through thinking, reflection and analysis one can expand the capacity of the brain and develop superior cognitive capacity.

In this talk, I plan to, inshallah, present certain verses from the Quran and suggest that you challenge our youth to interpret them using the latest human knowledge.

In this talk, I plan to only present 11 verse but with your help, we need to develop at least 100 verses. The goal is not to give the answer but for our youth to read and analyze the different knowledge to understand the basis for the answer whether the basis is analytical or experimental. This should help them grow new brain cells and make new neural connections and as important develop high cognitive capacity.

## 1. Verse 1
أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ ڪَانَتَا رَتۡقً۬ا فَفَتَقۡنَـٰهُمَا‌ۖ (٣٠)
“Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were one united piece, then We ruptured them apart?” (Al-Anbiya 21:30)

Question: interpret the verse seeking data at the time of the rupture of the first matter from which the whole universe was created.
Hints:
Study the Big Bang theory and its Planck parameters constraints.
Planck length: equal to 1.6 x10⁻³⁵ m, it is expected to be the shortest measurable distance.
Planck temperature: it equals about 10³² Kelvin, at which you start producing miniature Planck-mass black holes, which are the hottest black holes possible.
Planck Time: is 10⁻⁴³ seconds, it is the time it would take a photon travelling at the speed of light to across a distance equal to the Planck length.
Scientist have estimated the outcome of the Big Bang after the time is 10⁻³³ seconds which is far longer than the Plank time and thus at temperatures of 10²⁷ to 10²⁸ K which is far lower than the Plank temperature.

## 2. Verse 2
وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيۡنَـٰهَا بِأَيۡيْدٍ۬ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ (٤٧)
“We have built the heaven (universe) with might, and indeed We are expanding it.” (Al-Dhariyat 51:47)

Question:
The verse implies that the universe is expanding. What is the expansion rate? Does this expansion continue forever or will it reach a maximum point and then start shrinking?
Hint: study Hubble’s Law and the expanding universe and the correction made by Alexander Friedmann (Russian Physicist) and Georges Lemaître (Belgian Astronomer) to Einstein’s general relativity field equations.

## 3. Verse 3
يَوۡمَ نَطۡوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ ڪَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلۡڪُتُبِ‌ۚ (١٠٤)
“The Day when We shall roll up the heaven (universe) as the rolling of the scroll with the records.” (Al-Anbiya 21:104)

Question: Does the verse imply that the universe will collapse at some point to the point of its start and then recreate it?
Hint:
Study the concept of the universe shrinkage after expansion. Which of the Friedmann curvature models suggests this scenario?

وقال ابن أبي حاتم : عن ابن عباس قال : يطوي الله السماوات السبع بما فيها من الخليقة والأرضين السبع بما فيها من الخليقة، يطوي ذلك كله بيمينه، يكون ذلك كله في يده بمنزلة خردلة .
“Allah folds the seven heavens and all what is in them and the seven earths and all what is in them, he folds all of this by His right, and all of this will be in His hand as a small seed.”

## 4. Verse 4
كَمَا بَدَأۡنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلۡقٍ۬ نُّعِيدُهُ ۥ‌ۚ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡنَآ‌ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَـٰعِلِينَ (١٠٤)
“Just as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it. (It is) a promise (binding) upon Us. Truly, We shall do it.” (Al-Anbiya 21:104)

Question: Allah emphasizes in this verse as well as several verses (Yunus 10:4 and 34, Al-Naml 27:64 , Al-Ankabout 29:19, Al-Rome 30:11 and 27, Yaseen 36: 79, and Nuh 71:18) that He will recreate the universe. Why this is relevant to proving the concept of creation and refuting any argument regarding the creation by chance.
Hint: Study the 2nd law of thermodynamics and the concept of entropy for reversible vs irreversible systems.

## 5. Verse 5
اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا
“Allah is the One Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof (i.e. seven). His Command descends between them, that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah surrounds (comprehends) all things in (His) Knowledge. (Al-Talaq 65:12)

Question: What is meant by seven earths and why Allah is saying that the information in the verse is a proof that Allah has power over all things.
Hint: Study the string theory and its impact on resolving the singularity of the equation of the big bang theory. Also study the concept of the parallel universe. You may also consider the following hadith that is reported by Abu Hatem (أبي حاتم) and Al-Hakim (الحاكم) and Al-Bayhaqi (البيهقي) that Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس) who said:

رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره والحاكم في مستدركه، و رواه البيهقي ، عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: سبع أرضين في كل أرض نبي كنبيكم، وآدم كآدم، ونوح كنوح، وإبراهيم كإبراهيم، وعيسى كعيسى
“There are Seven earths: In every earth there is a prophet like your Prophet, Adam like your Adam, Noah like your Noah, Ibrahim like your Ibrahim, and Isa like your Isa.”

## 6. Verse 6
قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَىَّ هَـٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِى ثَمَـٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ۬‌ۖ فَإِنۡ أَتۡمَمۡتَ عَشۡرً۬ا فَمِنۡ عِندِكَ‌ۖ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أَشُقَّ عَلَيۡكَ‌ۚ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (٢٧) قَالَ ذَٲلِكَ بَيۡنِى وَبَيۡنَكَ‌ۖ أَيَّمَا ٱلۡأَجَلَيۡنِ قَضَيۡتُ فَلَا عُدۡوَٲنَ عَلَىَّ‌ۖ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَڪِيلٌ۬ (٢٨) فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهۡلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارً۬ا قَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارً۬ا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيڪُم مِّنۡہَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوۡ جَذۡوَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَصۡطَلُونَ (٢٩)

“He said: “I wish to wed one of my two daughters to you, on condition that you serve me for eight years, but if you complete ten years, it will be of your accord. And I do not intend to place you under any difficulty. If Allah wills, you will find me one of the righteous.” (27) He [Musa (Moses)] said: “This (is settled) between me and you whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no excess against me, and Allah is witness to what we are saying.” (28) Then, when Musa completed the term, and was travelling with his family, he noticed a fire from the direction of Tur (Mount). He said to his wife: “Stay here, I have noticed a fire; perhaps I may bring to you from there some information, or a burning fire-brand that you may warm yourself.” (Al-Qasas 28:27-29)

Question: How long did Prophet Musa serve his father-in-law 8 or 10 years and why he needed to wait that long to return to Egypt.
Hint: Study the criminal law in Egypt at that time to understand why Prophet Musa was willing to return to Egypt though he was accused of killing an Egyptian. Study the statute of limitations guidelines.

## 7. Verse 7
وَٱلشَّمۡسِ وَضُحَٮٰهَا (١) وَٱلۡقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَٮٰهَا (٢) وَٱلنَّہَارِ إِذَا جَلَّٮٰهَا (٣) وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَغۡشَٮٰهَا (٤) [ سورة الشمس]
“By the sun in its morning brightness; (1) By the moon as it follows it; (2) By the day as it reveals it (the sun); (3) By the night as it conceals it (the sun).” (Al-Shams 91:1-4)

Question: Verse 3 suggests that the daylight is the one that reveals the sun and not vice versa, why? Verse 4 states that the night conceals the sun, how can night conceal the sun?
Hint: Study the space beyond the earth atmosphere. You may also study the subject of dark matter. Also consider the following verse to understand why the day is the skin of the night and when the skin is removed, darkness will be overwhelming.

وَءَايَةٌ۬ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيۡلُ نَسۡلَخُ مِنۡهُ ٱلنَّہَارَ فَإِذَا هُم مُّظۡلِمُونَ (٣٧)
And a sign for them is the night that we skin from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. (Yaseen 36:37)

## 8. Verse 8
كَذَّبَتۡ عَادٌ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (١٢٣) إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ أَخُوهُمۡ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ (١٢٤) إِنِّى لَڪُمۡ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ۬ (١٢٥) فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ (١٢٦) [ سورة الشعراء]
“The (people of) Ad rejected the Messengers. (123) When their brother Hud said to them: “Will you not fear Allah? (124) I am a trustworthy Messenger to you. (125) So fear Allah and obey me.” (Al-Shu’ara 26:123-126)

أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ (٦) إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلۡعِمَادِ (٧) ٱلَّتِى لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِى ٱلۡبِلَـٰدِ (٨) [ سورة الفجر]
“Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with (the people of) Ad (6) Of Iram that have the (lofty) pillars, (7) The like of which were not created in the lands.” (Al-Fajr 89:6-8)

Question: Until now there is no archaeological find of the civilization of the people of Ad whom Allah provided them with advanced knowledge and power that was not equaled by others. Where should we look for them?
Hint: Read the other verses that describe the attributes of the people of Ad to help narrowing your selection for the place of their existence. You may use satellite imagery technology and search for a site under the sand.

## 9. Verse 9
وَتَرَى ٱلۡجِبَالَ تَحۡسَبُہَا جَامِدَةً۬ وَهِىَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِ‌ۚ صُنۡعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتۡقَنَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (٨٨) [ سورة النمل]
“And you will see the mountains and think them still, while they pass away as the passing away of the clouds. (This is) the work of Allah Who perfected all things. Truly, He is All-Aware of what you do.” (Al-Naml 27:88)

وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ جُدَدُۢ بِيضٌ۬ وَحُمۡرٌ۬ مُّخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٲنُہَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودٌ۬ (٢٧)
“And among the mountains are streaks white and red, of varying colors and (others) very black” (Fatir 35:27)

Question: What is the nature of the movement of the mountains, how fast are the different movements? How does the verse 27 relate to the movement of the mountains?
Hint: Read about plate tectonics and mid oceanic ridge. Study the three motions of the earth, 1) rotation on its axis, 2) revolving around the sun and 3) the solar system rotation around the center of the galaxy. Calculate the speed of each movement to identify the movement described in the verse.

## 10. Verse 10
تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيہِنَّ‌ۚ وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورً۬ا (٤٤)
The seven heavens and the earth and all whosoever is in them praise Him, and there is not a thing but celebrates His praise, but you do not understand their praise. Truly, He is All-Forbearing, All-Forgiving. (Al-Isra 17:44)

Question: Are there ways to demonstrate that all that exist have conscious to know Allah and thus praise Him?
Hint: Study Thomas Young’s “Double Slits Experiment” and the different explanations for it. Search for the explanation that suggests that the sub-atomic particles have conscious to observe and react to being observed. Also consider the following hadith:

وعن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: كان جذع يقوم إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، يعني في الخطبة. فلما وضع المنبر، سمعنا للجذع مثل صوت العشار، حتى نزل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فوضع يده عليه فسكن. وفي رواية: فلما كان يوم الجمعة قعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على المنبر، فصاحت النخلة التي كان يخطب عندها حتى كادت أن تنشق. وفي رواية: فصاحت صياح الصبي، فنزل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أخذها فالتزمها، فجعلت تئن أنين الصبي الذي يسكن، حتى استقرت. قال: بكت على ما كانت تسمع من الذكر. رواه البخاري.
There was a trunk of a date-palm tree upon which the Prophet (PBUH) used to recline while delivering the Khutbah (sermon). When the pulpit was placed, we heard the trunk crying like a pregnant camel till the Prophet (PBUH) came down and placed his hand over it and it became quiet. Another narration: On a Friday, the Prophet (PBUH) sat on the pulpit and the palm trunk where he used to deliver the Khutbah cried so loudly that it was about to burst. Another narration: It cried like a child. The Prophet (PBUH) came down from the pulpit and took it and embraced it, and it started moaning like a child who is being quieted till it became calm. He said: “It cried for the remembrance of Allah which it used to hear.” (Reported by Al-Bukhari)

## 11. Verse 11
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَرَجَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ هَـٰذَا عَذۡبٌ۬ فُرَاتٌ۬ وَهَـٰذَا مِلۡحٌ أُجَاجٌ۬ وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَہُمَا بَرۡزَخً۬ا وَحِجۡرً۬ا مَّحۡجُورً۬ا (٥٣)
“And He is the One who has let free the two seas, one palatable and sweet, and the other salt and bitter, and He has made between them a barrier and a prohibited partition.” (Al-Furqan 25:53)

مَرَجَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ يَلۡتَقِيَانِ (١٩) بَيۡنَہُمَا بَرۡزَخٌ۬ لَّا يَبۡغِيَانِ (٢٠)
“He has let loose the two seas meeting together. (19) Between them is a barrier, they do not encroach (one upon the other).” (Al-Rahman 55:19-20)

Question: why the fresh water and the ocean water do not mix?
Hint: Study the effect of the difference in the salinity and densities of these two water bodies on them and how it prevents them from mixing. Good references to study are: Advances in water desalination, edited by Noam Lior, and Reserve Osmosis by Wes Byrne

I am ending this talk as I started it, I am not proposing to use of science to explain to the Quran, but I am proposing to use the Quran to encourage our youth to study and excel in all branches of sciences as a religious obligation and essential form of worship of Allah to develop the like of Ibn Sina, Ibn Rushd, Ibn Al-Haytham, Ibn Khaldun and other greats.

We pay to Allah to guide us to develop a proper system for our youth to study the Quran to help them become the leaders of the world in all branches or natural and social sciences and have contributions worthy of them as true servants of Allah as their ancestors had done.

DUA

Appendix 1.
Example of the Breadth of Knowledge of Those who Built Islamic Civilization

Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
work was motivated by the belief that all natural phenomena occur following laws that Allah established. In order to predict what will happen and take advantage of the system that Allah established; one must discover the divine laws in the universe. This inspired him to study and write on: mathematics, medicine, astronomy, physics, mechanics, logic, geography, philosophy, psychology, classical music theory, theology, and Islamic jurisprudence.

Ibn Sina (ابن سینا) (Avicenna)
studied and memorized the entire Quran by the age of 10. Of the 450 works that is believed that he has written, around 240 have survived and they are in the areas of: philosophy, medicine, astronomy, alchemy, geography and geology, psychology, Islamic theology, logic, mathematics, physics and works of poetry.

Others:
Abu Nasr Al-Farabi (Alpharabius)
Muhammad ibn Musa Al-Khwarizmi
Abu Bakr Al-Razi
Jabir Ibn Haiyan
Ibn Al-Haytham (Alhazen)
Ibn Khaldun; Ibn Al-Nafis, Jaʿfar aṣ-Ṣādiq

title: Covid19, Floods, Fires .. Where Are We Going?
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

People have been witnessing major undesirable changes in their lives, started with the Covid19 epidemic that seems not going away and now they are facing the worsening of the environment that is causing unexpected major floods in many countries, widespread fires all over the world, heat waves causing the death of many. People are even expecting stronger and more intense hurricanes and long freezing wave in the winter. Some people attributed these disasters to several conspiracy theories and others attributed them to human activities such as genetic modification of the virus and greenhouse gases.

Allah informs us that the Quran includes information on all things by saying:

وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)
We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur’an) as an exposition of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and glad tidings for the Muslims. (Al-Nahl 16:89)

مَا فَرَّطْنَا فِي الْكِتَابِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ )الأنعام(
We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered. (Al-Ana’am 6:38)

Also, the Prophet (PBUH) emphasized this point of the comprehensive nature of the Quran by giving certain attributes to the Quran that included as he (PBUH) said:

فِيهِ نَبَأُ مَا كان قَبْلَكُمْ، وَخَبَرُ مَا بَعْدَكُمْ
In it there is the true account of those before you, the news of those who will follow you.

وَهُوَ الفَصْلُ لَيْسَ بِالْهَزْلِ مَنْ ابَتَغَى الهُدَى فِي غَيْرِهِ أَضَلّهُ الله
It is the serious judgment and not the lighthearted amusement, whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will misguide him.

وَهُوَ حَبْلُ الله المَتِينُ، وَهُوَ الذّكْرُ الْحَكِيمُ، وَهُوَ الصّرَاطُ المُسْتَقِيمُ، هُوَ الّذِي لاَ تَزِيغُ بِهِ الأَهْوَاءُ، وَلاَ يَلْتَبِسُ مِنْهُ الأَلْسِنَةُ، وَلاَ يَشْبَعُ مِنْهُ الْعُلَمَاءُ، وَلاَ يَخْلُقُ عَلَى كَثْرَةِ الرّدّ، وَلاَ تَنْقَضِي عَجَائِبُهُ
It is the mighty rope of Allah. It is the wise remembrance. It is the straight path. It is the one that will not make the whims deviates, and scholars will always be hungry to study it. Its responses do not need replenishment and its wonders will never cease.

Therefore, we should expect that the Quran gives information regarding major disasters that mankind will face at any time. While we cannot expect the Quran to give us the details and timing of every event, we can expect that it will identify certain principles and provide examples by which we can rationalize the reasons for the disasters and how to avoid them.

This view is supported by several scholars. As example, Ibn Masoud (ابن مسعود) said:

مَنْ أَرَادَ الْعِلْمَ فَلْيُثَوِّرِ الْقُرْآنَ ، فَإِنَّ فِيهِ عِلْمَ الأَوَّلِينَ وَالآخِرِينَ ) الطبراني في ” الكبير” ابن المبارك في ” الزهد ” ( ثَوِّرِ الْقُرْآنَ: بَحَثَ عن معانيه
“Who wanted the knowledge should study the Quran, it has the knowledge of the earlier and the later civilizations.” (Al-Tabarani)

Also, Imam Abu Hamed Al-Ghazali (ابو حامد محمد الغزالي‎) as well as Imam Abu Bakr al-Arabi (ابو بكر العربي), the Maliki Imam claimed that the Quran encompasses over 70,000 forms of knowledge.

It would be reasonable that we would expect that the changes in the environment and the spread of diseases be part of these knowledge in the Quran. Therefore, studying the Quran is very important because it will help us identify the key factors that come to play in these disasters, which as we see it now being completely ignored and instead people are focusing on the side effect rather than the main cause.

Studying the Quran will lead us to identify several principles that Allah have established, to help us explain the causes of disasters and in which direction are they going. In this talk, I’ll, inshallah, identify three relevant principles addressing natural disasters that man faces. I hope that, as you study the Quran on your own, you can identify others.

The first principle states that while Allah allows disasters to happen to mankind, He is not the cause of them. People are responsible for the disasters that happen to them So, people should stop blaming Allah’s decree for their problems. Allah clearly says:

ظَهَرَ ٱلۡفَسَادُ فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِى ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِى عَمِلُواْ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ (٤١) قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَـٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ‌ۚ كَانَ أَڪۡثَرُهُم مُّشۡرِڪِينَ (الرُّوم)
“Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so that He (Allah) makes them taste some of what they have done, in order that they may return (to the right way). (41) Say: “Travel in the land and see the consequence of actions of those before (you)! Most of them were idolaters.” (Al-Rome 30:41-42)

وَمَآ أَصَـٰبَڪُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ۬ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِيكُمۡ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَن كَثِيرٍ۬ (الشورى)
“And whatever a disaster befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned. And He overlooks many (of your evil deeds).” (Al-Shura 42:30)

أَوَلَمَّآ أَصَـٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةٌ۬ قَدۡ أَصَبۡتُم مِّثۡلَيۡہَا قُلۡتُمۡ أَنَّىٰ هَـٰذَا‌ۖ قُلۡ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ أَنفُسِكُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬ (آل عمران)
“(What is the matter with you?) When you suffer a disaster twice of which you caused (your enemies), you say: “From where does this come to us?” Say, “It is from your own selves.” And Allah is surely powerful over everything.” (Al-Imran 3:165)

It is interesting that Allah applies the same principle on the Prophet (PBUH). Allah says:

مَّآ أَصَابَكَ مِنۡ حَسَنَةٍ۬ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ وَمَآ أَصَابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ۬ فَمِن نَّفۡسِكَ‌ۚ وَأَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولاً۬‌ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَہِيدً۬ا (النساء)
“Whatever of good reaches you, it is from Allah, but whatever of iniquity befalls you, is from your own self. We have sent you as a Messenger to mankind, and Allah is Sufficient as a Witness.” (Al-Nisa 4:79)

This verse causes problems to those who believe that all actions of the Prophet (PBUH) were based on revelation and thus he cannot take any action that result in causing him harm. This opinion appears to be unrealistic because the Prophet, as human being took initiatives on his own to deliver the message such as the case of going to the Taif and when he found that this approach did not bring the desirable results, he changed his strategy. Also, the prophet (PBUH) made the decision on his own to reconcile the heart of the Jews of Khybar by accepting the invitation of a Jewish woman and eating her food that turned out to be poisonous. This poison affected the Prophet’s health as reported in the seerah books. But this issue is not the subject here, it is just to emphasize that no human being is immune form this principle.

However, we note that when Allah addressed the people regarding the harm that will befall them because what they are doing, he used the term (مُّصِيبَةٍ) which can be translated as calamity, disaster, misfortune. But, when Allah addressed the Prophet (PBUH), He used the term (سَيِّئَةٍ) which is translated as iniquity or bad thing.

Someone may suggest that there is contradiction between this principle and the following verses that suggest that every calamity occurs but by the permission of Allah:

مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ (التغابن)
“No calamity befalls, but by the command of Allah” (Al-Taghabun 64: 11)

مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ إِلَّا فِى ڪِتَـٰبٍ۬ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن نَّبۡرَأَهَآ‌ۚ إِنَّ ذَٲلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ۬ (الحديد)
“No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but is recorded in a book before We bring it into existence: that is truly easy for Allah” (Al-Hadid 57:22)

But there is really no contradiction because of the second principle that states that Allah has established the rules regarding the cause-effect relationship between man’s actions and the universe response to these actions which can be in the form of natural disasters.

This second principle suggest that Allah has established a balanced Balance that govern man’s behavior and another balanced Balance that controls the operation of the universe. If man caused imbalance to his Divine Balance, an imbalance would occur to the universe divine Balance. Therefore, certain operations of the universe can change and instead of giving protection to mankind, it will cause harm to them.

Yes, Allah is the One who established the cause-effect rule, but we are completely free to either positively or negatively manage our behavior in relation to this divine rule and face the consequence because nothing will ever diminish the application of the divine rule.

The cause-effect relationship between Man’s behavior and the universe stability are called the Sunnan of Allah that will never change and are always applied since Allah created this universe. Allah provided in the Quran many examples of past nations to emphasize to us these cause-effect relationship between the imbalance of the human Balance and that of the universe Balance. Let us look at several verses to support this principle.

Regarding the divine Balance of the universe, Allah says:

وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ (٧) أَلَّا تَطۡغَوۡاْ فِى ٱلۡمِيزَانِ (٨)
“And He raised the heaven high, and He has set up the Balance. (7) Do not cause imbalance in the Balance.” (Al-Rahman 55:7-8)

Regarding the man’s divine Balance, Allah says:

ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ‌ۗ وَمَا يُدۡرِيكَ لَعَلَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ۬ (الشورى)
Allah is the One Who has sent down the Book in truth, and the Balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.? (Al-Shua 42:17)

لَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۖ
“We sent our messengers with Clear Signs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance that people may uphold equity.” (Al-Hadid 57:25)

Regarding the consistency of the rules that govern the cause-effect relationships between the man’s Balance and the universe Balance (i.e. Sunnan of Allah), Allah says:

سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِى ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ lسُنَّةِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلاً۬ (الأحزاب)
“That was the Sunnah (rule, way, practice) of Allah in the matter of those who have gone before, and you never find in Allah’s Sunnah any change.” (Al-Ahzab 33:62)

سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلُ‌ۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلاً۬ (الفتح)
“That is the Sunnah of Allah in the matter of those who have gone before, and you never find in Allah’s Sunnah any change.” (Al-Fath 48:23)

فَهَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَۚ فَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلاً۬ۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ ٱللَّهِ تَحۡوِيلاً۬ (٤٣)
“Haven’t they looked at by the Sunnah with earlier people? So, you never find in Allah’s Sunnah any change, and you will never find in Allah’s sunnah any diversion.” (Fatir 35:43)

Therefore, one can conclude that all the disasters that people are facing and will be facing are caused by the imbalance to their Balance that Allah established to govern their activities behaviors and relationships. Violating Allah commands will cause an imbalance to the universe’s divine Balance and thus natural disasters will happen. People can stop these disasters by working on balancing their divine Balance, otherwise things will get worst.

Allah informs us of six types of disasters that people faced in the past and these were: 1) heavy rains causing major floods, 2) instability of the earth causing major sink holes, 3) sky quake causing blast deafening sound, 4) tornados, 5) hurricane wind filled with stone, and 6) earthquake. None of those people had done virus manipulation or caused green gas climate change, but they faced these disasters because of the imbalance they caused to the divine Balance by their sins and transgression against Allah’s commands.

Allah says regarding some of these disasters:

فَكُلاًّ أَخَذۡنَا بِذَنۢبِهِۦ‌ۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ حَاصِبً۬ا وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ خَسَفۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ أَغۡرَقۡنَا‌ۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظۡلِمَهُمۡ وَلَـٰڪِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ (٤٠)
“So, We punished every one of them with his sins; against some We sent a hurricane wind with shower of stones, and some were overtaken by an (Awful) acoustic blast, and some We caused to sink in the earth, and some We drowned. It was not for Allah to wrong them, but they wronged themselves.” (Al-Ankabout 29: 40)

Interesting in this verse is the sequence of the different disasters, the hurricane shower with stones referring to the people of Prophet Lut was the listed first while it was last in the chronological sequence of occurrence while the drowning referring the people of prophet Noah was listed last while it was the first in the chronological sequence. The reason appears that Allah is emphasizing the punishment for the worst violation first. So, now you can judge where are we stand regarding the nature of the imbalance er are causing to our divine Balance. are we like the people of Prophet Noah, or Prophet Saleh, or Prophet Hud, or Prophet Shoaib or Prophet Moses or Prophet Lot, or are we as all of them together?

To know the primary causes of what is happening to us, you need to compare our actions with those of past nations that were destroyed to see whether we are committing more of less than their transgressions. Frankly, there should be no surprises regarding what we see now. Allah says at the end of Surat Fater after giving many advice to mankind and identifying many of His blessings:

ٱسۡتِكۡبَارً۬ا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَكۡرَ ٱلسَّيِّىِٕۚ وَلَا يَحِيقُ ٱلۡمَكۡرُ ٱلسَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهۡلِهِۦ‌ۚ فَهَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَۚ فَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلاً۬ۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ ٱللَّهِ تَحۡوِيلاً۬ (٤٣) أَوَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَـٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِہِمۡ وَكَانُوٓاْ أَشَدَّ مِنۡہُمۡ قُوَّةً۬‌ۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعۡجِزَهُۥ مِن شَىۡءٍ۬ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَلِيمً۬ا قَدِيرً۬ا (٤٤) وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُواْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهۡرِهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ۬ وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّى‌ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ بَصِيرً۬ا (٤٥)
“Because of their showing arrogance in the land and plotting of evil. But the evil plot encompasses none but those who make it. Do they expect anything (else), but the divine Sunnah (rules) with the earlier peoples? So, you will never find in Allah’s Sunnah any change, and you will never find in Allah’s sunnah any diversion. (43) Have they not travelled in the land, and seen what was the end of those before them who were stronger than them in power? Allah is not such that anything in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him. Surely, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful. (44) If Allah were to take mankind to task for what they deserve, He would not leave a living creature on the surface of the earth, but He gives them respite to an appointed time, and when their time comes, then Allah is the Ever Seer of His slaves.” (Fatir 35:43-45)

The response of the universe to man’s actions according Sunnan Allah is not always negative, it can be positive if man continuously maintains the balance of his divine Balance by always being steadfast on the state of belief and Taqwa. Allah says:

وَلَوۡ أَنَّ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّقَوۡاْ لَفَتَحۡنَا عَلَيۡہِم بَرَكَـٰتٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَـٰڪِن كَذَّبُواْ فَأَخَذۡنَـٰهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ (٩٦)
“If the people of the towns believed and have Taqwa, We would have opened for them blessings from heaven and earth; but they rejected (the truth), so We seized them on account of what they have been earning (of misdeeds)” (Al-Araf 7:96)

The third principle is that the effect of imbalance in the universe Balance due to man’s action is progressive and thus the severity of the disasters will keep increasing unless man heeds the warning and start changing.

وَمَا نُرِيهِم مِّنۡ ءَايَةٍ إِلَّا هِىَ أَڪۡبَرُ مِنۡ أُخۡتِهَا‌ۖ وَأَخَذۡنَـٰهُم بِٱلۡعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ (٤٨)
“And We did not show them a sign, but it was greater than the one that preceded it. And We seized them with punishment, so that they may heed.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:48)

An example of the progressive punishment is that on Pharaoh and his people:

فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡہِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلۡجَرَادَ وَٱلۡقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَـٰتٍ۬ مُّفَصَّلَـٰتٍ۬ فَٱسۡتَڪۡبَرُواْ وَكَانُواْ قَوۡمً۬ا مُّجۡرِمِينَ (١٣٣) وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيۡہِمُ ٱلرِّجۡزُ قَالُواْ يَـٰمُوسَى ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ‌ۖ لَٮِٕن كَشَفۡتَ عَنَّا ٱلرِّجۡزَ لَنُؤۡمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرۡسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ (١٣٤) فَلَمَّا كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡہُمُ ٱلرِّجۡزَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ هُم بَـٰلِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمۡ يَنكُثُونَ (١٣٥) فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡہُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡيَمِّ بِأَنَّہُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡہَا غَـٰفِلِينَ (١٣٦)
“So, We sent on them: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood: a succession of clear signs. Yet they remained arrogant, and they were guilty people. (133) and when the terror fell on them, they said: “O Musa (Moses)! Pray to your Lord for us because of His covenant with you. If you remove the terror from us, we indeed shall believe in you, and we will let the Children of Israel go with you.” (134) But when We removed the punishment from them for a term, which they had to reach, in no time, they broke their promise! (135) So, We took retribution from them. We drowned them in the sea, because they rejected Our signs and were heedless of them” (Al-Araf 7:133)

The Prophet (PBUH) also spelled our several punishments that will impact Muslims; unfortunately, we see some of them happening now. Abdullah bin ‘Umar said: “The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to us and said:

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ فَقَالَ ‏ “‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ خَمْسٌ إِذَا ابْتُلِيتُمْ بِهِنَّ وَأَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ تُدْرِكُوهُنَّ لَمْ تَظْهَرِ الْفَاحِشَةُ فِي قَوْمٍ قَطُّ حَتَّى يُعْلِنُوا بِهَا إِلاَّ فَشَا فِيهِمُ الطَّاعُونُ وَالأَوْجَاعُ الَّتِي لَمْ تَكُنْ مَضَتْ فِي أَسْلاَفِهِمُ الَّذِينَ مَضَوْا‏.‏ وَلَمْ يَنْقُصُوا الْمِكْيَالَ وَالْمِيزَانَ إِلاَّ أُخِذُوا بِالسِّنِينَ وَشِدَّةِ الْمَؤُنَةِ وَجَوْرِ السُّلْطَانِ عَلَيْهِمْ‏.‏ وَلَمْ يَمْنَعُوا زَكَاةَ أَمْوَالِهِمْ إِلاَّ مُنِعُوا الْقَطْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَلَوْلاَ الْبَهَائِمُ لَمْ يُمْطَرُوا وَلَمْ يَنْقُضُوا عَهْدَ اللَّهِ وَعَهْدَ رَسُولِهِ إِلاَّ سَلَّطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ عَدُوًّا مِنْ غَيْرِهِمْ فَأَخَذُوا بَعْضَ مَا فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ‏.‏ وَمَا لَمْ تَحْكُمْ أَئِمَّتُهُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَيَتَخَيَّرُوا مِمَّا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلاَّ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ بَأْسَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ ‏”‏ ‏.‏
“O Muhajirun, there are five things with which you may witness, and I seek refuge with Allah that you witness them:

• Immorality never appears among a people to such an extent that they commit it openly, but plagues and diseases that were never known among the predecessors will spread among them.
• They do not cheat in weights and measures, but they will be stricken with famine, severe disasters, and the oppression of their rulers.
• They do not withhold the Zakah of their wealth, but rain will be withheld from the sky, and were it not for the animals, no rain would fall on them.
• They do not break their covenant with Allah and His Messenger, but Allah will enable their enemies to overpower them and take some of what is in their hands.
• Unless their leaders rule according to the Book of Allah and seek all good from that which Allah has revealed, Allah will cause them to fight one another.’”

The critical question is where we are going from here; are moving towards escalation of the natural disasters or towards reducing them. The answer is quite simple because it should be available in the mass media for anyone to know. Are we doing less or more than what the nations that were destroyed have done as provided to us in the Quran? Are we trying to rebalance our divine Balance or are we proceeding to causing more imbalance and thus cause more imbalance to the divine Balance of the universe?

Frankly, there should be no surprises regarding the future. It will get worst if the people of the world stay heedless and continue in their transgression, arrogance, and intransigence. How worst? There is one disaster that is mentioned 5 times in the Quran, but it did not happen yet and thus it can happen to us if we are not careful. This disaster is falling stars of earth (كِسَفًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ). This is a warning that the Prophet (PBUH) threatened the disbelievers of Mecca with, as Allah recorded for us what they said; they said:

أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنا كِسَفًا (الإسراء)
“Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have said.” (Al-Isra 17: 92)

If this disaster happens, it may be the first of the ten major signs of the day of Judgment This disaster is a smoke that will engulf the earth for long time. Allah named a whole Surat after it, it is surat Al-Dukhan 44). This can be subject of another talk. Allah says:

فَٱرۡتَقِبۡ يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِى ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (١٠) يَغۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ‌ۖ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ۬ (١١)
“So, wait for the Day when the sky will come up with a visible smoke. (10) That will envelop the people? this will be a painful torment.” (Al-Dukhan 44:10-11)

We pray to Allah to Allah to grant us the wisdom and the commitment to study the Quran and discover Allah’s system to help us have concise picture of the changes that we are seeing in the world.

We pray to Allah to give mankind the wisdom to stop transgressing and causing greater imbalance on their divine Balance that Allah and to protect us from any disasters that will happen as a result of the heedless on many of mankind.

DUA

title: The Journey from Belief (إيمان) to Certainty (يقين)
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

The Quan starts by setting its purpose and giving concise description of the believers by saying:

ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ‌ۛ فِيهِ‌ۛ هُدً۬ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٢) ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ (٣) وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ وَبِٱلۡأَخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ (٤) أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ عَلَىٰ هُدً۬ى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ‌ۖ وَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ (٥)

“This is the Book whereof there is no doubt, a guidance to those who are God-conscious. (2) Who believe in the unseen and steadfast in the prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them (3) And who believe in what has been send down to you and in what has been sent down before you and they have certainty in the Hereafter. (4) They are on guidance from their Lord, and they are the successful”. (Al-Baqara 2:2-5)

In describing those who are standing on true guidance, Allah stated that they believe (يُؤۡمِنُونَ) in the unsees and the revelations to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and to previous messengers. But when it came to the day of judgment, Allah stated that they have certainty (يُوقِنُونَ) about it. The emphasis on having certainty regarding the day of judgement is also emphasized in both Surat Al-Naml (27: 3) and Surat Luqman (31:4):

طسٓ‌ۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَڪِتَابٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ (١) هُدً۬ى وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٢) ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلۡأَخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ (٣) (النمل)

“Tâ-Sîn. These are the Verses of the Qur’an, and a clear Book; (1) A guide and glad tidings for the believers (2) Those who are steadfast in the prayers and pay Zakat and they have certainty in the Hereafter”. (Al-Naml 27:1-3)

الٓمٓ (١) تِلۡكَ ءَايَـٰتُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ (٢) هُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ لِّلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (٣) ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلۡأَخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ (٤) (لقمان)

Alif-Lâm-Mîm (1) These are Verses of the Wise Book. (2) A guide and a mercy for the good-doers (3) Those who are steadfast in the prayers and pay Zakat and they have certainty in the Hereafter”. (Luqman 31:1-4)

In this talk, I plan to, insha’Allah, discuss the issues of belief (إيمان) and certainty (يقين) and their differences. Why the subject is important because we are not expected to stay on the state of belief if we are to ensure success. But we have to progress to the state of certainty. To appreciate the reason for the distinction is to look at the reverse position for both. The reverse position for the belief if doubts creep in the mind of the believer is disbelief which is kufr. But the reverse position for certainty is limited to doubt to which the person has strong resistance because he can easily address them and thus, they will have no effect on the certainty of his belief.

To highlight the difference between belief and certainty, let us consider a physical illustration of a person who is standing on the shore of a stormy ocean. This person is in a safe position that we use to represent the state of belief. But if the waves that represents doubts gets worst, it can reach the shoreline and can draw the person in the ocean to drown. Thus, this person who is standing on the shoreline moved from the state of safety which is belief to state of danger which is Kufr by the storm which is the doubts. But if this person moves away from the shoreline deeper to stand on a mountain which will be a state of certainty, even if the waves move to the shoreline, he will remain safe and in state of belief.

Therefore, there is important difference between belief (إيمان) to certainty (يقين). Doubts creeps into the belief and if they are not resisted and properly addressed, they can lead to kufr and unfortunately this is a dilemma that some Muslims fall into. In a study that was published by the Pew Research center in 2018 shows that about a quarter of adults who were raised Muslims (23%) no longer identify as members of Islam.

The Prophet (PBUH) warned us of the risk of changing from the state of belief to kufr and therefore, this danger cannot be taken lightly. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said

عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بادروا بالأعمال فتنا كقطع الليل المظلم يصبح الرجل مؤمنا ويمسي كافرا أو يمسي مؤمنا ويصبح كافرا يبيع دينه بعرض من الدنيا (رواه مسلم)

“ Rush to doing good deeds (before you are overtaken) by a fitnah (turbulence) which would be like a part of the dark night. A man would be a believer in the morning and turn to disbelief in the evening, or he would be a believer in the evening and turn disbeliever in the morning and would sell his religion for worldly goods.”

أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله، لا يلقى الله بهما عبد مستيقناً بهما غير شاك إلا دخل الجنة

“Witnessing that there is no God but Allah, whosoever meets Allah on it with certainty with no doubt in it will enter paradise”.

من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله موقناً بها من قلبه دخل الجنة

“Whoever witnesses that there no God but Allah with certainty in his heart will enter paradise”.

حرم على النار من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله موقناً بها من قلبه

“Allah has prohibited the fire on anyone who witnesses that there no God but Allah with certainty in his heart”.

أحب الأعمال إلى الله عز وجل، إيمان لا ريب فيه أو لا شك فيه

“The best deed to Allah Almighty is Belief that has no skepticism nor doubt”.

Khalifa Abu Bakr said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

أبا بكر الصديق -رضي الله عنه- خطب الناس؛ فقال: قال رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: “يا أيها الناس: إن الناس لم يعطوا في الدنيا خيرًا من اليقين والمعافاة، فسلوهما الله عز وجل”(رواه أحمد)

“People have not been given in this world anything better than certainty and well-being, so ask Allah almighty for them.”

Imam Hassan Al-Basri said:

ويقول الحسن البصري: “ما طُلبت الجنة إلا باليقين، ولا هرب من النار إلا باليقين، ولا صبر على الحق إلا باليقين.”

“Paradise is only secured by certainty, and the fire is only avoided by certainty, and there is no patience on the truth except by certainty.”

Imam Ja’afr Al-Sadiq said:

فعن الاِمام الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال: (الاِسلام درجة والاِيمان عن الاِسلام درجة. واليقين على الاِيمان درجة)

“Islam is a degree and belief is higher degree than Islam and certainty is higher degree that belief.”

Abdullah Ibn Masoud (عبد الله بن مسعود) said:

الصبر شطر الإيمان، واليقين الإيمان كله

Patience is part of the belief and certainty is the whole belief.

The reason that Abdullah Ibn Masoud said that patience is only part of belief (الصبر شطر الإيمان) but certainty is the whole belief (اليقين الإيمان كله) because patience requires full trust and reliance in Allah and this cannot be attained except through certainty.

Certainty is a status beyond’ belief. This is why Prophet Ibrahim asked Allah to show him how He raises the dead to move his belief to this higher state of certainty, as Allah informs us:

وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٲهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى ڪَيۡفَ تُحۡىِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ‌ۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِن‌ۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَٮِٕنَّ قَلۡبِى‌ۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةً۬ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ۬ مِّنۡہُنَّ جُزۡءً۬ ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيًا‌ۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٢٦٠)

“And when Ibrahim (Abraham) said, “My Lord! Show me how You give life to the dead.” He (Allah) said: “Do you not believe?” He (Ibrahim) said: “No. (I believe), but It is just to make my heart at peace.” He (Allah) said: “Take four birds and make them incline towards you, and then put a portion of them on every mountain, and call them, they will come to you in haste. And know that Allah is All-Might, All-Wise.” (Al-Baqara 2:260)

We discussed this verse before in attempt to explain how Allah gives life to the dead. This is not the subject here, but I want to highlight that Prophet Ibrahim has belief, but he was seeking certainty. Allah confirms this certainty by saying in Surat Al-Ana’am regarding Prophet Ibrahim:

وَكَذَٲلِكَ نُرِىٓ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُوقِنِينَ (٧٥)

“Thus, we showed Ibrahim the kingdom of the heavens and the earth so that he be one of those who have certainty” (Al-An’am 6:75)

This introduction on the importance of advancing from the state of belief to the state of certainty even for Prophets, requires us to address at least four issues:

1. What is the nature of certainty that we want to achieve?
2. How can we achieve the proper level certainty since we are not Prophets?
3. What are the most common doubts that face Muslims and can shake their belief?
4. How do we address these common doubts?
5. What is Certainty (يقين)

The subject of certainty has been addressed by both philosophers and religious scholars, but they never reached consensus. Some argue that there is nothing called certainty because our knowledge is finite and always limited and thus any claim to certainty is arrogant and merely used by those who conceal their unjustifiable beliefs. Those who hold this view are obviously wrong because they themselves are claiming certainty by their claim that there is no certainty and thus such claim is self-refuting. The proper way to address certainty is to ask is: what is certainty?

A skeptic might say that certainty refers to the rigorous assurance that something we believe is totally true. The requirement of rigorous assurance is unrealistic because on what grounds do anyone of us believe that when he goes to the garage to use his car, it will not turn into a horse. One can claim certainty because many times in the past his car has not turned into a horse. But if one is truly pressed, he could not really claim that he had rigorous certainty if he is perfectly honest.

Thus, certainty is only achieved from an assumption of the continued regularity of the laws of nature. But this belief would be an assumption. In addition, even our belief that the universe actually exists and is not some kind of illusion, a figment of our imagination, or a computer simulation like the Matrix is an assumption without any rigorous evidence.

Chuang Chou (Zhuangzi, Zhuang Zhou) who was a Chinese philosopher between 369 BC and 286 BC said: “Once upon a time, I, Chuang Chou, dreamt I was a butterfly, fluttering here and there, to all intents and purposes a butterfly. I was conscious only of my happiness as a butterfly, unaware that I was Chou. Soon I awaked, and there I was, myself again. Now I do not know whether I was then a man dreaming I was a butterfly, or whether I am now a butterfly, dreaming I am a man.”

If the existence of the universe is not certain, any subsequent reasoning derived from scientific observation of the universe will be equally uncertain. If we demand rigorous certainty of even the most basic truths of mathematics or science, we are left completely empty-handed. All truth is ultimately derived from the assumption of certain axioms, about which we can have no rigorous certainty.

Therefore, we need to differentiate between “rigorous certainty” and “pragmatic certainty.” We, as human beings, cannot be “rigorously certain” about anything at all. However, my may claim “pragmatic certainty”, that is, the subjective assurance that our beliefs and our assumptions are true. Even the skeptics will act upon pragmatic certainty on a daily basis.

In general philosophers classify certainty as follows:

1. Psychological certainty: A belief is psychologically certain when the person who has it is completely convinced of its truth.
2. Epistemic certainty: The certainty based on knowledge that has a degree of validation.
3. Moral certainty: A certainty, which is sufficient to regulate our behavior,
4. Systematic certainty: It is certainty that is evident and difficult e to fully doubt.
5. Human certainty: Certainty that is mixed with doubts.

Instead of studying the views of others on the classes of certainty, let us look at what Allah says. Allah identified for us three levels of certainty, and these are:

1. Knowledge-Based Certainty (عِلۡمَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ)
2. Sight-Based Certainty (عَيۡنَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ)
3. True Certainty (حَقُّ ٱلۡيَقِينِ)

These are identified in the following verses that are related to the certainty about the hellfire.

كَلَّا لَوۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ عِلۡمَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٥) لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلۡجَحِيمَ (٦) ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّہَا عَيۡنَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٧) (التكاثر)

“If you know with knowledge-based certainty, (5) You will certainly see hell-fire! (5) Again, you shall see it with Sight-based certainty! (Al-Takathur 102:5-7)

وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ (٩٢) فَنُزُلٌ۬ مِّنۡ حَمِيمٍ۬ (٩٣) وَتَصۡلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ (٩٤) إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ ٱلۡيَقِينِ (٩٥) (الواقِعَة)

“However, if he is one of the deniers and goes astray, (92) for him is a welcome of scalding water, (93) and roasting in hell-fire. (94) This is the true certainty. (Al-Waqia 56:92-95).

We accept the certainty of a specific knowledge based on a reference that we trust its reliability. But our level of certainty regarding the same knowledge will increase if we were witnesses of this knowledge. The only true certainty regarding the same knowledge when we are part of this knowledge.

To illustrate these three levels of certainty, let us assume that you were told by a family member that a helicopter is in your driveway. You can believe with knowledge-based certainty that a helicopter is in your driveway. But this knowledge-based certainty cannot be based on blind trust. It should be based on your intellectual assessment of the truthfulness of the source of the knowledge.

A higher level of certainty can be achieved if you went outside and saw a helicopter in your driveway. This will be a sight-based certainty which is obviously higher level than the knowledge-based certainty.

The highest level of certainty can only be realized if you go out, open the door of the helicopter, and sit on the pilot seat. This may represent the true certainty, and it is the maximum level than one can achieve in this life since even this level of certainty may be an illusion.

This a very concise classification of certainties. In fact, it addresses the objections of the skeptics that there is nothing called rigorous certainty in this life. The Quran teaches us that the only true certainty is the one in the day of Judgement.

Since the only true certainty is the certainty we face in the day of judgment, has the Quran identified another term to reflect that what we call certainty in this life is not 100% certain. The term used in the Quran is “Dhann” (ظن) which can be translated as supposition which is reflects that the truthfulness of the knowledge is over 50%. As the person progresses from belief to certainty, his “Dhann” (ظن) regarding the truthfulness of certain belief can reach 99% but never 100%. Allah uses this term Dhann (ظن) in describing what the submissive believers (Al-Khasheen) who are firm in their patience and prayers think regarding meeting Allah. Allah says:

وَٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ‌ۚ وَإِنَّہَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلۡخَـٰشِعِينَ (٤٥) ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّہُم مُّلَـٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ رَٲجِعُونَ (٤٦) (البقرة)

“Seek help with patience and prayer; it is indeed hard except for (Al-Khashieen) the submissive. (45) Who realize (think, bear in mind) that they shall meet their Lord and shall return to Him. (Al-Baqara 2:45-46)

Examining different translations of verse 46 one notes that the translators are struggling with translating the term (يَظُنُّونَ). The translations included: 1) bear in mind, 2) bear in mind the certainty, 3) certain, 4) believe, 5) seriously believe, 6) realize, 7) assume, and 8) know.

The problem is that the same term (يَظُنُّونَ) is used in 3 other verses and the same translators translate it as conjecture, guess and think without inferring certainty, such as in:

وَمِنۡہُمۡ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّآ أَمَانِىَّ وَإِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ (٧٨)

“And there are among them (Jews) unlettered people, who do not know the Book, but as fancies and they but guess (conjecture).” (Al-Baqara 2: 78)

وَطَآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡہُمۡ أَنفُسُہُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ‌ۖ

“And another group was thinking about themselves and thought wrongly of Allah – the thought of ignorance.” (Al-Imran 3: 154)

وَقَالُواْ مَا هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنۡيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحۡيَا وَمَا يُہۡلِكُنَآ إِلَّا ٱلدَّهۡرُ‌ۚ وَمَا لَهُم بِذَٲلِكَ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍ‌ۖ إِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ (٢٤)

“And they say: “There is nothing but our worldly life, we die, and we live and nothing destroys us except time. They have no knowledge about that, they do nothing but conjecture (guess).” (Al-Jathia 45: 24)

But we need to accept the reality that only 100% certainty (يقين) is in the hereafter and everything in this life is certainty that is higher than 50% but less than 100. Therefore, the choice of the term “Dhann” (ظن) that implies some degree of assumption is very appropriate. In this case, we are required not to remain stationary at one level of certainty but continue to improve to move as close to the 100% certainty as possible.

2. How can we increase our level of certainty?

The improvement in our level of certainty can only secured with help from Allah. Allah is the One who brought the level of certainty of the Prophets to the perfect level. This is done by revelation and by exposing to them the secrets of the universe as Allah says regarding Prophet Ibrahim:

وَكَذَٲلِكَ نُرِىٓ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُوقِنِينَ (٧٥)

“Thus, we showed Ibrahim the kingdom of the heavens and the earth so that he be one of those who have certainty” (Al-An’am 6:75)

Similar thing happened to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) when he saw the reality of the unseen during his ascension trip to the heavens. For us, we can progress our level of certainty through continuous worship as Allah says Surat Al-Hijr:

وَٱعۡبُدۡ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَكَ ٱلۡيَقِينُ (الحجر – الآية 99)

“And worship your Lord until there comes unto you the certainty.” (Al-Hijr 15:99)

Almost all books of Tafseer, consider the certainty (ٱلۡيَقِينُ) here refers to death though Allah did not use the term death. In fact, the context cannot mean that certainty is death of the Prophet but rather the certainty of him achieving victory and triumph over all his enemies and thus a fulfillment of Allah’s promises as in Surat Al-Rom:

وَكَانَ حَقًّا عَلَيۡنَا نَصۡرُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٤٧)

“And it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers.” (Rome 30:47)

A mean by which Allah increases our level of certainty is the fulfillment of his promises in our lives. Also desires to increase our state of certainty require our commitment to intellectually address all issues that can create doubt in the mind of the believers and Allah promises to help those who are serious as He said:

وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَہۡدِيَنَّہُمۡ سُبُلَنَا‌ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (٦٩)

“As for those who strive hard in Our way, We will surely guide them to Our Paths. And indeed, Allah is with the good doers.” (Al-Ankaboot 29:69)

As a note, almost all religions require beliefs in the unseen, and we rely for this on books that are claimed to be divine. Therefore, all the information is derived based on Knowledge-Based Certainty (عِلۡمَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ). The focus of any person who follows any of these books is to convince himself of the reliability of the text. As a minimum, the reference used to derive Knowledge-Based Certainty (عِلۡمَ ٱلۡيَقِينِ) must be examined regarding at least six issues:

1. Clear statement in the reference that it is revealed by God.
2. The purpose of the book as defined in the book.
3. The name of the person (Prophet) to who the revelation is attributed.
4. Information on the character of the claimed Prophet.
5. The name of the writers of the reference in hand.
6. Assurance that the copy we have is an exact original.

I’ll stop here but there are two remaining issues to discuss in the future, inshallah, and these are:

1. What are the most common doubts that face Muslims and can shake the status of their belief?
2. How do we address these common doubts?

DUA

content:
Protection from the Most Critical Danger (Surah Al-Anas)

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In this talk, I plan, inshallah, to focus on Surat Al-Nas which is the last Surat in the Quran, it is number 114. Generally, the last chapter in any book is very important. This last Surat in the Quran is very critical because it identifies the greatest danger that can make the reader forfeits all the benefits, he/she has gained from the Quran. Although this Surat is quite short and it is memorized by almost, if not all, Muslims, it may not have been given the attention it deserves. Allah ends the Quran with this Surat

قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ (١) مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٢) إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٣) مِن شَرِّ ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ (٤) ٱلَّذِى يُوَسۡوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٥) مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ (٦)

Before giving the translation, let us first define the key Arabic terms that are used in the Surat:

The term Rab (رب) which is often translated as Lord though some translated it as sustainer and cherisher. But the definition of Rab means the one who changes the condition of people to the opposite. In the case of Allah, He as Rab changes the undesirable condition of people to the desirable condition. This means that 1) when people are hungry, Allah as Rab is the one who gives them food, 2) when the people are misguided, Allah as Rab is the one who gives them guidance, 3) when the people are homeless, Allah as Rab is the one who gives them shelter, 4) when the people are afraid, Allah as Rab is the one who grants them security, 5) when the people are sick, Allah as Rab is the one who gives them health, 6) when the people are violent, Allah as the Rab is the one who forces them to be subdued, and so on. Therefore, it is difficult to pick one word to use as translation for Rab, may be the translation as cherisher and sustainer is better than the term Lord.

In this regard a father is Rab for his family because he is the one responsible for providing food, shelter and security to his family and he is the one responsible for disciplining his kids when they don’t behave. But there are limitations for any person who is serving in the role of Rab due to limitations of resources, authorities, and knowledge to ensure that what he is providing is the optimum and that he can enforce the implementation of what he wants to change. But for Allah, He is not only Rab but He is also King (مَلِكِ) but unlike the kings among men, Allah as king has four integrated elements that are unique to Him: 1) He is the owner of everything that exist, 2) He has full control and authority over everything that exist. 3) He has no need for anything that exists, and 4) Everything that exist is in need of Him.

With these attributes of Allah as Rab and as King, He will be the only One who deserves to be worshipped and thus He is the only Ilah. So, the term “Ilah” (إِلَـٰهِ) means the One who is worthy of being worshipped. In this case, the translation of Ilah as God seems reasonable through it is still limited.

When we invoke the names of Allah as Rab and as King, we are invoking His actions towards us but when we invoke Allah’s name as Ilah we are invoking our actions towards Him.

The term “Wis’Was” (وسواس) means the one creating whispers, not one time but repeated times. When the Arabic verb includes two similar sections, it means repetition of the action. In this case the verb is Was’was (وسوس) and it has the letters Waw and Seen repeated meaning the process of whispering is repeated. Similarly, the verb Zal’zal (زلزل) in which the letters Z and lam are repeated means repeated vibration and derived from it the term Zilzal (زلزال) which is earthquake. Als, the term Tam’tam (تمتم) in which the letters “Ta” and “Meem” are repeated; meaning repeated uttering that cannot be understood which is mumbling.

The term Al-Khanas (ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ) means the one who engages in a process and when discovered he shrinks and retreats. Since this terrn is associated with term “Wis’Was” (ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ), this means that when the one who causes the repeated whispers is discovered, he will shrink and retreat and to get ready to come again and again to deliver the whisper.

The last term is Al-Jinnat (ٱلۡجِنَّةِ) which is often translated as Jinns but it is also translated as “invisible forces”. The translation invisible forces is more appropriate because the term Jinn refers to anything that is invisible. Since we don’t see the Jinn, the term refers to them. Even the term Jannah (جنة) which is translated as Garden or paradise is derived from the same root because it refers to a garden that is full of trees and vegetations in which everything is invisible. The term Magnoon (مجنون) which is translated as mad or insane is derived from the same root because his brain function is invisible. In this regard, anything that is invisible can be named Jinn. Based solely on linguistic understanding, even the angels can be called Jinn because they are invisible to us.

As aside note, the Quran uses two terms that refer to mankind: the term “Inns” (إنس) and the term “Na’as” (ناس) and two terms that refer to Jinn: the term Jan (جان) and its plural Jinn (جن) and the term “Jinnat” (جنة).

1. You will note that the term “Inns” (إنس) always comes associated with the term Jan (جان) and its plural Jinn (جن) and,
2. the term “Na’as” (ناس) always comes associated with the term “Jinnat” (جنة).

Note that the roots for the terms “Inns” (إنس) and the term “Na’as” (ناس) are different.
The root for the term “Inns” (إنس) is (أنَسَ يَأنِس), while
the root for the term “Na’as” (ناس) is (يَنُوس).

To understand the key difference, you need to read their use in the Quran.
Based on this discussion, we can translate the Surat as follows:

قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ (١) مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٢) إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٣) مِن شَرِّ ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ (٤) ٱلَّذِى يُوَسۡوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٥) مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ (٦)

Say: I seek refuge in the cherisher and sustainer (e.g, Lord) of mankind, (1) The King of mankind, (2) The God of mankind, (3) From the evil of the relenting sneaking whisperer, (4) Who whispers into the hearts of mankind, (5) From among Jinn and among mankind (6).

Last week I discussed Surat Al-Falq (the cleavage) which is number 113 and both Suart Al-Falq and Surat Al-Nas were revealed at the same time and are called “Al-Mu’awwidhatayn” (the two surahs for seeking refuge).

In Surat Al-Falaq, we are asked to invoke only one glorious name of Allah (رَبِّ ٱلۡفَلَق) that we can translate as:
“Lord of the system of creations”
to protect us from four dangers:
مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَـٰتِ فِى ٱلۡعُقَدِ وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
1) From the evil of that which He create, 2) From the evil of something that is in darkness when it spreads, 3) From the evil of those who blow on knots (e.g. magic), and 4) From the evil of the envier when he envies.

But in this surat, Surat Al-Nas, we are asked to invoke three glorious names of Allah (رَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ، مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ، إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ):
“1) the Lord of mankind, 2) the king of mankind and 3) the God of mankind”
from only one danger which is: (ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ)
“the relenting sneaking whisperer”.

The reason for ending the Quran with this Surat may be that Allah knows full well that there are many external dangers that can affect our lives, but there is one unique force that can destroy everything we have worked for in our life including our afterlife. This force can penetrate our emotional center which is our heart and confuse our brain with doubts and desires that eventually lead to our ruin. This force is the relenting sneaking whisperer (ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ).

Because of this most damaging and unique danger, Allah placed this very critical surah as closing of the Quran. Allah is asking us to seek His refuge from it by invoking all His key attributes as 1) Lord (رَبِّ), 2) King (مَلِكِ), and 3) God (إِلَـٰهِ) against the evil of the relenting sneaking whisperer (مِن شَرِّ ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ).

We are asking Allah to protect us from both the entity that is sending us the evil whisper and from the message itself that is being whispered. To make the sources of these whispered messages even more dangerous is that they are relentless, they keep coming back whenever they see a chance.

This danger should not be taken lightly because it was this sneaking whisper that made Prophet Adam (AS) eats from the forbidden tree:
فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ قَالَ يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكٍ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ (طه 120)
Then, Satan whispered to him, saying: “O Adam! Shall I lead you to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that will never decay?” (Taha 20:120)

The sneaking whisper do not only come to us from external sources, but it can also come to us from our own selves:
وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعۡلَمُ مَا تُوَسۡوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفۡسُهُ ۥ‌
“Indeed, We have created man, and We know what his own self whispers to him.” (Qaf 50:16)

Allah identified to us that whispers can come to us from two sources, from invisible sources such as Jinn and from visible sources such as human beings. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) cautioned us about the danger of the whispering that comes from human beings by saying:
يا أبا ذر هل تعوذت بالله من شر شياطين الإنس والجن؟ قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، وهل للإنس من شياطين؟ قال: نعم، هم شر من شياطين الجن
O Aba-Dhar: seek refuge in Allah from the devils of men and Jinn. Aba Dhar said: O Messenger of Allah: Are there devils from mankind. The Prophet (PBUH) said: Yes, and they are even more dangerous than the devils of Jinn.

All the devils of Jinn can do is to whisper, and they retreat when you say: “I seek refuge in Allah from the cursed Satan” (أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم). But the human Satans go beyond whispering, they keep working on convincing you to commit the sins until they succeed.

But the devils among humans have discovered many ways to sneak the whisper to the righteous through innocent media. People have perfected methods to send subliminal messages that may have started as commercial tool such as the logo of the FedEx company that includes an arrow formed by the space between the “E” and the “x.”. The hidden message behind the arrow is that FedEx is moving and delivered fast.

Unfortunately, the same technique of sending subliminal messages through an appearing innocent medium is being used today to whisper many wrong ideas and concepts to our kids through cartoons, movies, songs, etc. We also start seeing relenting invisible whispers that keep coming using the idea of enlightenment, human rights, personal freedom, etc. to whisper doubt in the message of the Quran.

In additions, the devils among the people have been developing methods for thought control to reduce our choices to only the options they have selected for us. Even if you shut off all sources of media which is practically impossible, you will still get these whispers from people around you.

While the devil among men whispers to us through our senses, the devils among the Jinn have the capacity to go inside our heart to deliver the whispers and even make us forget:
اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ فَأَنْسَاهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ (المجادلة)
“Satan has prevailed upon them. So, he has made them forget the remembrance of Allah.” (Al-Mugadalah 58:19)

Also, Allah identifies to us the tactics of Satan by saying:
إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ وَيَصُدَّكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلَاةِ ۖ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ
“Satan wishes to plant enmity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling, and to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. Will you not then desist?” (Al-Maida 5:91)

To avoid blaming Satan for all our wrong actions, Allah informs us that Satan has really no influence on us other than the whispering and we are the ones who make the decision to follow it:
وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ لَمَّا قُضِىَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَڪُمۡ وَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُكُمۡ‌ۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِىَ عَلَيۡڪُم مِّن سُلۡطَـٰنٍ إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوْتُڪُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡتُمۡ لِى‌ۖ فَلَا تَلُومُونِى وَلُومُوٓاْ أَنفُسَڪُم
“And Satan says when the matter has been decided: “Surely, Allah promised you a promise of truth. And I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves.” (Ibrahim 14:22)

While the surat focuses on providing us with a dua to say to protect us from the evil whispers from the devils, you should know that you also receive whispers from the angels:
عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله ﷺ: «إِنَّ لِلْمَلَكِ لَـمَّةً وَإِنَّ لِلشَّيْطَانِ لَـمَّةً، فَأَمَّا لَـمَّةُ الْـمَلَكِ فَإِيعَادٌ بِالْـخَيْرِ وَتَصْدِيقٌ بِالْـحَقِّ، وَأَمَّا لَـمَّةُ الشَّيْطَانِ فَإِيعَادٌ بِالشَّرِّ وَتَكْذِيبٌ بِالْـحَقِّ»
“The angels whispers and the devil whispers. The whisper of the angel is affirming the truth and promising good, and the whisper of the devil is denying the truth and promising evil.”

As a final comment, you can note the feature of the ring structure in the Quran by comparing the last Surat in the Quran with the first Surat (Al-Fatiha):
قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ (١) <=> ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٢)
مَلِكِ الناس (٢) <=> مَـٰلِكِ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ (٤)
إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ (٣) <=> إِيَّاكَ نَعۡبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسۡتَعِينُ (٥)

We pray to Allah to protect us from all the visible and invisible evil whispers.

Appendix 1: Background on the Revelation of the Surat
It is the consensus that the both Surat Al-Falaq and Surat Al-Nas ‘ were revealed at the same time. While it is certain that they were revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in Medina, there are some scholars who suggested that they were revealed in Makkah and some even suggest that they were revealed to previous messengers as well.

One of those people who suggests that these Starts were revealed to previous messengers is Abdullah Ibn Abbas (RA).

Regarding whether part of the Quran was revealed to previous Messengers, the Prophet (PBUH) said regarding Prophet David (AS):
خُفِّفَ عَلَى دَاوُدَ الْقُرْآنُ ، فَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ بِدَوَابِّهِ تُسْرَجُ ، فَكَانَ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُسْرَجَ دَوَابُّهُ ، وَلَا يَأْكُلُ إِلَّا مِنْ عَمَلِ يَدِهِ
“The Quran was lightened on David that he would order for his horse to saddled and would be able to read the Quran (e.g. sections revealed to him) before the horse is saddled.”

Allah also states that part of the Quran is included in previous messages as He says:
وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (١٩٢) نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلۡأَمِينُ (١٩٣) عَلَىٰ قَلۡبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنذِرِينَ (١٩٤) بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّ مُّبِينٍ (١٩٥) وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ (الشعراء)
“And truly, it is a revelation of the Lord of the Worlds, (192) Which the Trusted Spirit has brought down (193) Upon your heart that you may be of the warners, (194) In a plain Arabic language. (195) And indeed, it is in the former scriptures.” (Ash-Shu'ara 26:192-196)

Having sections of the Quran revealed to other Prophets is also clear from the letter that Prophet Sulaiman (AS) sent to the Queen of Saba:
إِنَّهُ مِنْ سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ (النمل)
“It is from Sulaiman, and it is (as follows): `In the name of Allah, Most Gracious, Most Merciful.” (An-Naml 27:30)

إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ (١٨) صُحُفِ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ (١٩) (الأعلى)
Indeed, this is in (has been mentioned in) the former scriptures 19) The scriptures of Abraham and Moses. (Al-A'la 87:18-19)

وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِي الزَّبُورِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ (الأنبياء)
“And we have written in the “Zabour” Psalms, after the Reminder that the land will be inherited by My righteous servants.” (Al-Anbiya 21:105)

This verse challenges some interpreters regarding what is that Dhikr (الذِّكْرِ) that was there before the Psalms.

These verses suggest that only small sections of the Quran were revealed to previous messengers, but the complete Quran was revealed only to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

Appendix 2. The limitation of what we See
Everything we hear, see, smell, taste or touch are converted to electromagnetic waves recognized through our brain. But our senses are limited to only a very small part of the electromagnetic spectrum. For example, the visible light we see is only a very tiny section of the full spectrum of light. We don’t see Infrared, Ultraviolet, X-rays, Gamma rays, etc. Similarly, we don’t hear all frequencies.

We make equipment such as radios and Televisions that can see different parts of this spectrum that we don’t see and convert them to sections we can see or hear. So, the Jinn exists but we don’t have the senses to see them or hear them.

نَاسَ لُعَابُهُ : سَالَ، اِضْطَرَبَ
نَاسَ الْجِمَالَ : سَاقَهَا
