content:
The Mystery of the Cattle – Why they are the focus of Satan!

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

In Surat Al-Nisa (4), Allah exposed for us some of the threats that Satan made to mislead the children of Adam and one of these threats is not obvious and its interpretations in most books of tafsir are not convincing. The context of this threat is in verses 116 to 121 of Surat Al-NIsa (4). I am focusing in this talk on the threat in red. The translation I am providing here is the common one. These verses read:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٲلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ‌ۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَـٰلاًۢ بَعِيدًا (١١٦) إِن يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦۤ إِلَّآ إِنَـٰثً۬ا وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَـٰنً۬ا مَّرِيدً۬ا (١١٧) لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۘ وَقَالَ لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنۡ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيبً۬ا مَّفۡرُوضً۬ا (١١٨) وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمۡ وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمۡ وَلَأَمُرَنَّهُمۡ فَلَيُبَتِّڪُنَّ ءَاذَانَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ وَلَأَمُرَنَّهُمۡ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلۡقَ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ وَمَن يَتَّخِذِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنَ وَلِيًّ۬ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ خَسِرَ خُسۡرَانً۬ا مُّبِينً۬ا (١١٩) يَعِدُهُمۡ وَيُمَنِّيہِمۡ‌ۖ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا (١٢٠) أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ مَأۡوَٮٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ عَنۡہَا مَحِيصً۬ا (١٢١)

Indeed, Allah does not forgive that a partner is ascribed to Him and He forgives everything else for whom He wills; and whoever sets up partners with Allah, has indeed gone far astray. (116) They invoke nothing but female deities besides Him, and they invoke nothing but Satan, the rebel! (117) whom Allah has cursed. And he (Satan) said: “I will take control of an appointed portion of your slaves; (118) And I will lead they astray and tempt them with false hope and I will order them to slit the ears of the cattle, and I will command them to alter the creation of Allah.” But whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah, has surely incurred an obvious loss. (119) He (Satan)] makes promises to them and tempts them with false hopes; and Satan’s promises are nothing but deceptions. (120) For such people, their dwelling is Hell, and they will find no way of escape from it. (Al-Nisa 4:116-121)

Satan’s threat that is not clear is that he will order the children of Adam to (فَلَيُبَتِّڪُنَّ ءَاذَانَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ) which is translated in most English translations as (to slit the ears of cattle). This threat is not obvious because what is the big deal about making people slit the ear of a cow or a sheep as the purpose of marking them. In fact, some people even slit their own ears and almost all women do this to have earrings.

My guess is that most interpreters suggested that the threat refers to making a slit in the ear of cattle is to tie this Satan’s threat to one of the actions of the idolators in which they used to slit the ear of certain cattle for identification as being dedicated for the idols, so no one can take advantage of them. They called such animals “Bahirah”. This is stated in Surat al-Maeda:

مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنۢ بَحِيرَةٍ۬ وَلَا سَآٮِٕبَةٍ۬ وَلَا وَصِيلَةٍ۬ وَلَا حَامٍ۬‌ۙ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ‌ۖ وَأَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ (١٠٣)

“Allah has made no Bahirah or Sa’ibah or Wasilah or Hami, but those who disbelieve invent a lie against Allah. Most of them have no understanding.” (Al-Maeda 5:103)

The idolators used to dedicate four classes of animals to the idols and these are called Bahirah, a Sa’ibah, Wasilah or Hami.

1. Bahirah is the female camel that they stop taking advantage of it after it delivers five times, and it is marked by slitting its ear.
2. Sa’ibah is the animal that is dedicated for the idols from its birth.
3. Wasilah is the she sheep that delivers 7 times and after the 7th delivery, it will not be slaughtered but any future benefit from it will only be for man and not women.
4. Hami is the male of the cattle that was responsible for ten pregnancies, and it will be dedicated only for the idols.

Suggesting that term (يُبَتِّڪُنَّ) means making a “slit” to match it with the term Bahirah is forcing a meaning on a term just to have a link between two verses. The proper meaning of the term (يُبَتِّڪُنَّ) is to “cut off form the source” or to “completely tear off”. Therefore, Satan’s threat to make Adam’s children (فَلَيُبَتِّڪُنَّ ءَاذَانَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ) “to completely cut off the ears of the cattle” remains perplexing because we are not aware of this being done in any past or present culture. Therefore, this threat must mean something compelling that is being done by those people whom Satan has deceived.

In order to understand this verse, we need to apply two of the seven steps of studying the Quran that we previously discussed. The seven steps are reading, recitation, purification, Tarteel, Tadabour, recollection and Dirasah). The two steps to apply are Tarteel and Tadabour. The tarteel step involves the assembly of all the verses related to the subject. The Tadabour process requires studying the verses together to get better understanding of the subject.

The focus in this talk is on the term (ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ) which is “the Cattle” and this term came in the Quran 30 times. Some of these verses should give us the clue about the nature of the threat of Satan to ensure that we resist it.

First, let us identify form the Quran the animals that are designated as cattle (ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ). In verses 142 to 144 of Surat Al-An’am (The Cattle), Allah defines the cattle as the males an females of the sheep, goats, camels and cows. Allah says:

وَمِنَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ حَمُولَةً۬ وَفَرۡشً۬ا‌ۚ ڪُلُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٲتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ‌ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوٌّ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (١٤٢) ثَمَـٰنِيَةَ أَزۡوَٲجٍ۬‌ۖ مِّنَ ٱلضَّأۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَمِنَ ٱلۡمَعۡزِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ‌ۗ قُلۡ ءَآلذَّكَرَيۡنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِ أَمَّا ٱشۡتَمَلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَرۡحَامُ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيَيۡنِ‌ۖ نَبِّـُٔونِى بِعِلۡمٍ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ (١٤٣) وَمِنَ ٱلۡإِبِلِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَمِنَ ٱلۡبَقَرِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ‌ۗ قُلۡ ءَآلذَّكَرَيۡنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِ أَمَّا ٱشۡتَمَلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَرۡحَامُ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيَيۡنِ‌ۖ أَمۡ كُنتُمۡ شُهَدَآءَ إِذۡ وَصَّٮٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِهَـٰذَا‌ۚ فَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبً۬ا لِّيُضِلَّ ٱلنَّاسَ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (١٤٤)

And of the cattle are those fit for loading and those that are small. Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Surely, he is an open enemy to you.

(142) Eight pairs; of the sheep two (male and female), and of the goats two (male and female). Say: “Has He (Allah) forbidden the two males or the two females, or (the young) which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge if you are truthful.” (143)

And of the camels two (male and female), and of the cow two (male and female). Say: “Has He forbidden the two males or the two females or (the young) which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you present when Allah ordered you such a thing? Then who does more wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah, to lead people astray without knowledge. Certainly, Allah does not guide the people who are wrong-doers.” (Al-An’am 6: 142-144)

Before referring to another verse to clarify the nature of Satan’s threat, there is a verse related to the cattle whose relevance is not obvious unless we understand Satan’s threat. This is verse 17 of a Surat Al-Ghashiya (ٱلۡغَاشِيَةِ) “The Overwhelming” (88); which is the Surat that the Prophet (PBUH) often read in Friday and Eid prayers. This verse is (أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡإِبِلِ ڪَيۡفَ خُلِقَتۡ) “Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?” It is not clear what is the relevance of the camels in the context of the other verses that read.

أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡإِبِلِ ڪَيۡفَ خُلِقَتۡ (١٧) وَإِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ڪَيۡفَ رُفِعَتۡ (١٨) وَإِلَى ٱلۡجِبَالِ ڪَيۡفَ نُصِبَتۡ (١٩) وَإِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ڪَيۡفَ سُطِحَتۡ (٢٠)

Do they not look at the camels, how they are created? (17) And at the sky, how it is raised? (18) And at the mountains, how they are rooted (fixed firm)? (19) And at the earth, how it is spread out? (Al-Ghashiya 88:17-20)

In these verses, we note that the mountains, and the earth are related but how can the camels and the sky be related? Because of this disconnect, some interpreters suggested that the term (ٱلۡإِبِلِ) may not be referring to the clouds and not camels to achieve the relevance between clouds and sky. But others objected because the use of the term (ٱلۡإِبِلِ) to mean clouds has not been used in the Quran, Hadith, or poetry.

Therefore, considering that the term (ٱلۡإِبِلِ) refers to the camels which is part of the cattle preserves the accuracy of the verse, but we need to identify a link between the camels to the sky.

We do not have to search hard to find the link between the camels and the sky. There are two verses that give us insight on the nature of the creation of the cattle. These verses inform us that the creation of the cattle is very unique among all animals,, The cattle were created by Allah in Heaven and then sent down to earth which is unlike all other animals that have been created in earth and may have gone through certain evolution cycles. Allah says in Surat Yasin (36):

أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا خَلَقۡنَا لَهُم مِّمَّا عَمِلَتۡ أَيۡدِينَآ أَنۡعَـٰمً۬ا فَهُمۡ لَهَا مَـٰلِكُونَ (٧١) وَذَلَّلۡنَـٰهَا لَهُمۡ فَمِنۡہَا رَڪُوبُهُمۡ وَمِنۡہَا يَأۡكُلُونَ (٧٢) وَلَهُمۡ فِيہَا مَنَـٰفِعُ وَمَشَارِبُ‌ۖ أَفَلَا يَشۡكُرُونَ (٧٣)

“Have they not seen how We have created for them cattle, among the things that were made by Our hands and then they become their owners, (71) And We have subdued them unto them, so that some of them they have for riding and some for food? (72) And they have (other) benefits from them, and things to drink. So, will they not be grateful?” (Yasin 36:71-73)

In Suart Al-Zummur (39), Allah says:

خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٍ۬ وَٲحِدَةٍ۬ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنۡہَا زَوۡجَهَا وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ ثَمَـٰنِيَةَ أَزۡوَٲجٍ۬‌ۚ يَخۡلُقُكُمۡ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِڪُمۡ خَلۡقً۬ا مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَلۡقٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتٍ۬ ثَلَـٰثٍ۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ‌ۖ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصۡرَفُونَ (٦)

He created you (all) from a single soul; then made from him his mate. And He sent down for you eight pairs of cattle (these are the male and female pair of sheep, goat, cow, and camel). He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation in three veils of darkness; such is Allah your Lord. His is the kingdom; there is no God but He. Then, to where are you being turned away? (Al-Zumur 39:6)

These verses provide us special knowledge regarding the creation of the cattle and that they were not created in earth but were created in heaven and sent down to earth.

When we study the Quran, we note that Allah used the action verb Anz’al (sent down) 162 time referring to 6 things that He sent down to the earth, these are:

1. Revelations
2. angels
3. Rain
4. Blessings such as the table to Prophet Isa, the special food (ma’an and Salwa) to children of Israel, the tranquility on the heart of the believers.
5. Cattle
6. Iron

Interesting that Allah did not use the action verb Anz’al (أنزل) to refer to the process by which man came to earth, Allah used the verb (إهبط) (go down) and this mean that man came to earth through actions by himself.

Out of these 6 items, two require some study because they are not obvious, and these are the cattle and the iron. The other 4 are well understood. The revelation that iron was sent down to earth is given in verse 25 of Surat Al-Hadeed (57) that says:

لَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۖ وَأَنزَلۡنَا ٱلۡحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأۡسٌ۬ شَدِيدٌ۬ وَمَنَـٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥ وَرُسُلَهُۥ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ۬ (٢٥)

“We have indeed sent Our Messengers with clear proofs, and we sent down with them the Book and the Balance (justice) that mankind may stand up for justice. And We sent down the iron wherein is mighty power, as well as many benefits for mankind, that Allah knows who supports Him and His Messengers, though unseen. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, All-Mighty.” (Al-Hadeed 57:25)

Early Muslims gave superficial interpretation to this verse with some such as Ibn Abbas suggesting that Allah sent with Adam the anvil, the tongs and the sledgehammer.

أن ابن عباس قال : ثلاثة أشياء نزلت مع آدم : السندان ، والكلبتان ، والميقعة ، يعني المطرقة . رواه ابن أبي جرير ، وابن أبي حاتم .

But we now know that this verse reveals part of the mystery of the creation of the universe by identifying that iron came to earth from outside the solar system. The earth as well as all other planets and satellites in our solar system were separated from the sun. The production of iron by the nuclear fusion process requires a temperature that exceeds 4.7 billion °C.

But the surface temperature of the sun is about 6,000 °C, and its inner core temperature of about 15 million °C, that are far lower than the temperature to form iron; therefore, sources much hotter than the sun must be responsible for the generation of iron in the universe.

The theory is that when the earth was separated from the sun, it was a heap of ash, containing nothing heavier than the elements aluminum and silicon. Then this heap of ash was bombarded by a shower of iron meteorites from massive stars. This bombardment caused the heap of ash to heat up rapidly to a temperature that exceeded the melting point of iron (2000°C) causing iron and other heavy elements such as nickel to melt forming mega drops that penetrated the heap of ash, reaching its center to form its mainly iron-nickel core. This process has changed the Earth from a homogeneous heap of ash to a distinct body.

While the mystery of sending down iron to the earth has been resolved, the mystery of sending down cattle to the earth remains for someone to resolve. May be research needs to be done to identify:

• The uniqueness of cattle compared to other animals.
• When Cattle were first noted in earth.
• The importance of cattle to the survival of the family of Adam on earth.
• 

May be one of our students who is studying zoology or veterinarian will be successful in resolving this mystery. However, in a recent study by researchers at the Baylor College of Medicine, USDA’s Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Georgetown University and CSIRO Australia estimated that the genome of the cattle contains approximately 22,000 genes and shares about 80% of its genes with humans. The researchers also found that the organization of human chromosomes is closer to that of cattle than other animals.

So, we realize from the Quran that cattle were created in heaven and descended to earth for man to see, it was a clear declaration to the power and authority of Allah as well as His mercy on Mankind.

The confusion that is created regarding Satan’s threat (وَلَأَمُرَنَّهُمۡ فَلَيُبَتِّڪُنَّ ءَاذَانَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ) is caused by the interpretation that was made for the term Adhan (ءَاذَانَ). It was interpreted to mean ears, but the term Adhan can also mean announcement for something important. We use the term Adhan to refer to calling for prayers. So, if we assume that the Adhan of the cattle means the announcement of the cattle regarding Allah’s power of creation and His mercy on mankind. One can understand why Satan made the threat.

Satan threatened that he will cut off the children of Adam from the true message of the cattle and by this he cuts them off the connection to Allah, the creator of the cattle. Therefore, we can translate the verse as follows:

وَلَأَمُرَنَّهُمۡ فَلَيُبَتِّڪُنَّ ءَاذَانَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ

I will order them to cut off the announcement of the cattle (regarding Allah’s power of creation and His Mercy upon Mankind). (Al-Nisa 4:116-121)

Did Satan succeed in cutting people from the true message of the cattle’s creations? Obviously, he did because instead of learning the true message, many people started considering cattle as sacred. We notice that cattle played major roles in many religions, including those of ancient Egypt, ancient Greece, ancient Israel, ancient Rome, and ancient Germany. Even today, cattle are considered sacred in religions such as Hinduism, Jainism, Buddhism, and others. In Hinduism, the cow is considered as representative of the divine and should therefore be protected and venerated. The cow has also been associated with various deities, notably Shiva, Indra, Krishna, and goddesses in general.

Allah revealed to us all the secrets of Satan including this one, but people, even educated ones, are submitting to Satan’s deceit, and making him successful in carrying out his threats.

Allah may have instituted the obligatory command to sacrifice the cattle as part of certain obligatory rituals such as Hajj in order to counter Satan’s threat of making people confused about the true message of the creation of the cattle. The command to sacrifice the cattle should ensure that people do not give any degree of sanctity to the cattle. Allah emphasizes the importance of sacrificing the cattle in Surat Al-Hajj (22) and also in Surat Al-Baqara(2) . In surat Al-Hajj, Allah says:

وَلِڪُلِّ أُمَّةٍ۬ جَعَلۡنَا مَنسَكً۬ا لِّيَذۡكُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ‌ۗ فَإِلَـٰهُكُمۡ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ وَٲحِدٌ۬ فَلَهُۥۤ أَسۡلِمُواْ‌ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُخۡبِتِينَ (٣٤) ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡ وَٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَہُمۡ وَٱلۡمُقِيمِى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ (٣٥)

To every nation We prescribed the rites (of sacrifice), so that they mention the name of Allah over the sustenance He gave them from the cattle. Your God is one God: submit then your wills to Him and give Good News to those who turn to Him in humbleness. (34) Those whose hearts are filled with awe when Allah is mentioned and those who show patience against whatever befalls them, and who keep up regular prayer, and spend (in charity) out of what we have bestowed upon them. (35)

وَٱلۡبُدۡنَ جَعَلۡنَـٰهَا لَكُم مِّن شَعَـٰٓٮِٕرِ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمۡ فِيہَا خَيۡرٌ۬‌ۖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡہَا صَوَآفَّ‌ۖ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتۡ جُنُوبُہَا فَكُلُواْ مِنۡہَا وَأَطۡعِمُواْ ٱلۡقَانِعَ وَٱلۡمُعۡتَرَّ‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ سَخَّرۡنَـٰهَا لَكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ (٣٦) لَن يَنَالُ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَـٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ مِنكُمۡ‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمۡ لِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَٲكُمۡ‌ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (٣٧)

We appointed for you the sacrificial large animals (camels and cows) among the Symbols of Allah. In them there is much good for you: then pronounce the name of Allah over them as they are lined up (for sacrifice). Then when they are down on their sides (after slaughter), eat from them and feed those who are content, and those who ask with due humility. Thus, We have made them (the cattle) subjugated to you, that you may be grateful. (36) It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah: it is your piety that reaches Him. Thus, He has made them subjugated to you, that you may glorify Allah for the guidance He granted you: and proclaim the Good News to all who do good.” (Al-Hajj 22:32-37)

In addition to the animal sacrifice in Eid Al-Adha, there are other conditions in which a person is required to make animal sacrifices, these conditions are specified in verse 196 of Surat Al-Baqara as Allah says:

وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِ‌ۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡىِ‌ۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡىُ مَحِلَّهُۥ‌ۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦۤ أَذً۬ى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٌ۬ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٍ۬‌ۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡىِ‌ۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَـٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ۬ فِى ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡ‌ۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٌ۬ كَامِلَةٌ۬‌ۗ ذَٲلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ‌ۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ (١٩٦)

“And complete the Hajj and ‘Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented (from completing them), make an affordable offering of sacrifice, and do not shave your heads until the offering reaches it place (of sacrifice). And whosoever of you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp (preventing shaving), he must in compensation pay fast, feed the poor or offer sacrifice. And when you are in a comfortable condition again and wish to continue the Umrah in the months of Hajj, he must make an offering of sacrifice that he can afford, but if he cannot afford it, he should fast of three days during the Hajj and seven days after his return (to his home), making ten days in all. This is for him whose household is not present at Al Masjid-Al-Haram (i.e non-resident of Makkah) And fear Allah much and know that Allah is severe in punishment.” (Al-Baqara 2: 196)

Making animal sacrifice is very important and it is sign of the person’s Taqwa because it is a demonstration of honoring Allah’s signs and commands, as Allah says:

ذَٲلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمۡ شَعَـٰٓٮِٕرَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقۡوَى ٱلۡقُلُوبِ (٣٢) لَكُمۡ فِيہَا مَنَـٰفِعُ إِلَىٰۤ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّ۬ى ثُمَّ مَحِلُّہَآ إِلَى ٱلۡبَيۡتِ ٱلۡعَتِيقِ (٣٣)

“Such (is his state): and whoever holds in honor the rituals commanded by Allah, (in the sacrifice of animals), such (honor) emanates from the piety of heart. (32) In them (the cattle) you have benefits for a specified time: in the end their place of sacrifice is near the Ancient House. (Al-Hajj 22:33)

The term used to refer to animal sacrifice is (شَعَـٰٓٮِٕرَ ٱللَّهِ) which is translated as symbols of Allah, ceremonies of Allah, landmarks of Allah, symbols set up by Allah, the marks of Allah, the rites of Allah, the sacraments of Allah, the offering of Allah, the signs of Allah, the commands of Allah.

While sacrificing the cattle may have been instituted to counteract Satan’s threat, there are voices being raised, even among Muslims regarding the sacrificing the animals during Eid al-Adha (the feast of sacrifice) by suggesting that we should give the money to the poor instead of the meat because this will be more beneficial to them, and some raise the question of mercy towards the animals. These are false premises, the poor existed during the life of the Prophet (PBUH) and money would have been more beneficial to them and the Prophet (PBUH) made the sacrifice. Also, no one can have more mercy towards the animals than the Prophet (PBUH) and he made the sacrifices.

Sayeda Aisha said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عائشة – رضي الله عنها – قالت : قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – : ( ما عمل ابن آدم من عمل يوم النحر أحب إلى الله من إهراق الدم ، وإنه ليؤتى يوم القيامة ، بقرونها وأشعارها وأظلافها ، وإن الدم ليقع من الله بمكان قبل أن يقع بالأرض ، فطيبوا بها نفسا ) . رواه الترمذي ، وابن ماجه .

“No action done by the son of Adam on the day of sacrifice (Eid al-Aḍḥā) more beloved to Allah than spilling blood of the slaughtered animals. They will appear on the day of judgement with their horns, hair, and hooves. Indeed, the blood will be accepted by Allah from where it is received before it even falls on the ground, so let your heart delight with it.’ (Al-Timidhi and Ibn Majah)

Jaber reported that:

فقد روى الإمام أحمد وأبو يعلى في مسنديهما وغيرُهما بسند صحيح حديثَ جابر في حجة الوداع وفيه: وكان جماعة الهدي الذي أتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والذي أتى به عليُّ مائةٌ، فنحر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده ثلاثة وستين، وأعطى عليا فنحر ما غبر وأشركه في هديه.

“When the Prophet (PBUH) performed his farewell Hajj, he (PBUH) sacrificed 100 camels, he slaughtered 63 camels by himself, and asked Ali (RA) to slaughter the remaining camels.

(Observation: The Prophet (PBUH) slaughtered 63 camels and he lived 63 years)

The sacrifice of the cattle is very important ritual. Therefore, all the arguments that are being made to diminish the importance of making the animal sacrifice are very likely inspired by Satan to cut off the children of Adam form the wisdom of creating the cattle by Allah and sending them from heaven to earth.

Those who suggest that charity is more appropriately expressed in money in today’s conditions fail to understand both Islam as well as the ‘modern’ world. A study conducted by the Institute of Management Sciences, Peshawar in 2009 found that the sacrifice of animals on Eid Al-Adha constituted a direct transfer of money to rural households with fewer intermediaries and generated employment for thousands of opportunistic animal rearers, livestock traders, butchers and leather industry workers among others, who look to Eid for a small annual windfall.

We pray to Allah to grant us the opportunity to go for Hajj and to make the animal sacrifices that are please to Allah and to protect us from Satan and his trickery.

Dua

content:
The Importance of Ten Nights

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

In this talk I plan to focus, inshallah, on the beginning of Surat Al-Fajr and give more focus to one oath that is often mentioned in these 10 days of Dhul-Hijja (عشر ذي الحجة).

Surah Al-Fajr starts with 5 oaths and after the oaths Allah says that in these oaths are lessons for those who have brain to think. The Surat starts as follows; the English translation is one that is often used:

وَٱلۡفَجۡرِ (١) وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٍ۬ (٢) وَٱلشَّفۡعِ وَٱلۡوَتۡرِ (٣) وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَسۡرِ (٤) هَلۡ فِى ذَٲلِكَ قَسَمٌ۬ لِّذِى حِجۡرٍ (٥)

By the Dawn (1) And by ten nights, (2) And by the Even and the Odd, (3) And by the night when it moves away, (4) Aren’t these oaths enough for the one with sense. (Al-Fajr 89:1-5)

The oath that I want to give more attention to is the 2nd one which is (وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٍ۬) “By ten nights.”  While some interpreters consider that these ten nights refer to the last ten nights of Ramadan, many consider that they refer to the first ten days of Dhul-Hijja. Those who consider that the oath refers to the ten days of Dhul-Hijja justify their interpretation by a reference to the Prophet’s Hadith stating that these ten days of Dhul-Hijja are blessed days.

The hadith is the one narrated by Ibn Abbas and reported in Bukhari in which the Prophet (PBUH) said:

و روى الإمام البخاري -رحمه الله- في صحيحه  (عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ – صلى الله عليه وسلم – أَنَّهُ قَالَ « مَا الْعَمَلُ فِي أَيَّامٍ أَفْضَلَ مِنْهَا فِي هَذِهِ ». يَعْنِي أَيَّامَ الْعَشْرِ قَالُوا وَلاَ الْجِهَادُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قَالَ « وَلاَ الْجِهَادُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ رَجُلٌ خَرَجَ بِنَفْسِهِ وَمَالِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْجِعْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ. )

ما من أيَّامٍ العملُ الصَّالحُ فيهنَّ أحبُّ إلى اللهِ من هذه الأيَّامِ العشرِ . قالوا : يا رسولَ اللهِ ولا الجِهادُ في سبيلِ اللهِ ؟ فقال رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ : ولا الجِهادُ في سبيلِ اللهِ إلاَّ رجلٌ خرجَ بنفسِه ومالِه فلم يرجِعْ من ذلكَ بشيءٍ)المغني(

“There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these 10 days.” The people asked, “Not even Jihad for the sake of Allah?” He said, “Not even Jihad for the sake of Allah, except in the case of a man who went out to fight giving himself and his wealth up for the cause and came back with none of them.” (Bukhari).

The link between this hadith and the oath in Surat Al-Fajr is not convincing because the Surat mentions ten nights and the hadith mentions ten days (الأيَّامِ). But the argument used by those who suggest that the ten nights are referring to the ten days is that the term (Youm) (يوم) which is translated as day includes the night.

Here we can see how a confusion can result when you translate Arabic to English. In Arabic there are two terms, Nahar (نهار) and Youm (يوم); both are translated in English as day. While in Arabic the term Nahar (نهار) refers to the part of the Youm (يوم) from dawn to sunset. The term Youm (يوم) can be used to only refer to Nahar (dawn to sunset) or it can be used to refer to both the Nahar (dawn to sunset) and night “Layl” (ليل) (sunset to dawn). How can one know the difference in usage?

When the term Youm is intended to only refer to the Nahar, it will come in a verse that includes both Youm and Layl (night) or this can be understood form the context. Otherwise, the term Youm will be referring to both the Nahar (dawn to sunset) and night “Layl”, i.e. the 24 hrs.

The following is an example for the use of the term Youm to refer only to the Nahar (dawn to sunset) because it came associated with the term Layl: (night), Allah says:

سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيۡہِمۡ سَبۡعَ لَيَالٍ۬ وَثَمَـٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومً۬ا

“That He imposed on them (people of Ad) for seven nights and eight days in succession.” (Al-Haqqa 69:7)

Note that the terms Youm and Lyl are used, therefore the Youm here refers only to the Nahar (dawn to sunset).
The following is an example for the use of Youm referring only to the Nahar because of the context: Allah says:

فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَـٰثَةِ أَيۡمَـٰتٍ۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ كَفَّـٰرَةُ أَيۡمَـٰنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَلَفۡتُمۡ‌ۚ

“But whosoever cannot afford (that), he should fast for three days. That is the expiation for the oaths when you have sworn” (Al-Maeda 5:89)

Here the context is fasting, and we know that fasting is only from dawn to sunset, i.e. only during the Nahar.

In many other cases, the tern Youm is used to refer to both the Nahar and the Layl (night) as in:

لِّيَشۡهَدُواْ مَنَـٰفِعَ لَهُمۡ وَيَذۡڪُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ۬ مَّعۡلُومَـٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ‌ۖ

“So that they witness benefits for them, and mention the Name of Allah in specified days (i.e.10th, 11th, 12th, and 13th day of Dhul-Hijjah), over the provision He provided them form the cattle. (Al-Hajj 22:28)

Here the remembrance of Allah in a Youm is expected to be done during both the Nahar and the Layl.

So, the interpreters who say that the prophet’s Hadith and the oath in Surat Al-Fajr are related argue that the ten days in the Hadith include the ten nights referenced in surat Al-Fajr. But this argument is deficient because it ignores the counter argument that the oath in Suart Al-Fajr is referring only to Lyal (ليل) (night) and this is only limited to the time form sunset to dawn and it does not include the Nahar (dawn to sunset) which is included in the hadith.

Before discussing what the oath in Suart Al-Fajr could be referring to, let me clarify some elements of the righteous deeds in the hadith that are more valuable when done in these ten days of Dhul-Hijja than in any other time. Many people to consider that fasting in these days is very important. Obviously fasting is an important righteous deed at any time, but is the righteous deeds indicated in the Hadith refer to mainly to fasting. The answer is no for three reasons:

1. Note that the hadith mentions 10 days and those who want to fast, fast only 9 day and not 10.
2. While there is consensus that fasting the day of Arafah (the 9th day of Dhul Hijja) for those who are not at Arafat is a sure sunnah (سنة مؤكدة) of the Prophet (PBUH), there are conflicting accounts regarding whether the Prophet (PBUH) fasted the previous 8 days of Dhul-Hijja. A hadith narrated by Sayeda Aisha (عائشة رضي الله عنها) and reported in Muslim (مسلم) stated that the Prophet (PBUH) never fasted these days. But the hadith narrated by Sayeda Hafsa (حفصة رضي الله عنها) and reported in Sunnan Al-Nisaa (النسائي) and Abi Dawoud (أبي داود) stated that the Prophet (PBUH) fasted these days. The reason for the apparent conflict may be that Sayeda Aisha (عائشة رضي الله عنها) who had the right for two days with the Prophet (PBUH) every nine days did not notice that the Prophet (PBUH) ever fasted during that time when he was with her. But the Prophet (PBUH) fasted during the day of Sayeda Hafsa and thus she expected that he fasted all days. Therefore, fasting these days is not sure sunnah, however the fasting the day of Arafah is important because the Prophet (PBUH) said regarding it:

فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : (صِيَامُ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ أَحْتَسِبُ عَلَى اللَّهِ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ السَّنَةَ الَّتِي قَبْلَهُ وَالسَّنَةَ الَّتِي بَعْدَهُ وَصِيَامُ يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ أَحْتَسِبُ عَلَى اللَّهِ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ السَّنَةَ الَّتِي قَبْلَهُ ». [رواه مسلم]

“Fasting the day of `Arafah expiates the sins of two years: the past one and the coming one.” [Muslim]

3. The hadith refers to the immense value of doing righteous deeds during these days and the assumption that fasting is the best of the righteous deeds may not be totally accurate because the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألا أنبئكم بخير أعمالكم، وأزكاها عند مليككم، وأرفعها في درجاتكم، وخير لكم من إعطاء الذهب والورق، وخير لكم من أن تلقوا عدوكم فتضربوا أعناقهم ويضربوا أعناقكم؟ قالوا: وذلك ما هو يا رسول الله؟ قال: ذكر الله عز وجل. رواه أحمد والترمذي وغيرهما وصححه الألباني.

“Shall I tell you of the best of deeds and the purest in the sight of your Lord, which raises your rank to the highest order, and it is better for you than spending gold and silver, and better than meeting your enemy so that you strike at their necks, and they strike at yours?’ The companions said: ‘Yes, O messenger of Allah,’ He (PBUH) said: ‘It is Dhikr (the remembrance) of Allah.” (At-Tirmidhi)

So, the best righteous deeds to be done during all the ten days of Dhul-Hijja including the Eid day is Dhikr Allah and the best form of dhikr in these days is the Takbeer.  I really hope that no one interprets this analysis to suggest that I am saying that fasting is not important.

We can now go back to Surat Al-Fajr and try to understand what could the oath “by ten nights” (وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٍ۬) mean?

وَٱلۡفَجۡرِ (١) وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٍ۬ (٢) وَٱلشَّفۡعِ وَٱلۡوَتۡرِ (٣) وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَسۡرِ (٤) هَلۡ فِى ذَٲلِكَ قَسَمٌ۬ لِّذِى حِجۡرٍ (٥)

By the Dawn (1) And by ten nights, (2) And by the Even and the Odd, (3) And by the night when it moves away, (4) Aren’t these oaths enough for the one with sense. (Al-Fajr 89:1-5)

When Allah makes an oath, He makes an oath with something important and thus He expects us to give serious attention to this item. In this surah Allah ended the oaths with a unique statement (هَلۡ فِى ذَٲلِكَ قَسَمٌ۬ لِّذِى حِجۡرٍ) which is translated as: “Aren’t these oaths enough for the one with sense.”  While the term Dhi Hijr (ذِى حِجۡرٍ) is translated as “has sense, has brain, and has understanding,” it refers to additional meanings. The term Hijr gives reference to a stone wall that is built to set the boundary for a property. Therefore, the term Hijr does not only mean having a brain or sense or understanding but it also means having clear recognition of the boundaries to ensure that you never transgress beyond them.

When we examine these five oaths, we note that 4 of them are expressed in the definite form using the artic “Al” (The), the Fajr (الۡفَجۡرِ), the Shafa (ٱلشَّفۡعِ), the witr (ٱلۡوَتۡرِ) and the Layl (ٱلَّيۡلِ) but the second oath referring to ten nights (وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٍ۬) came indefinite without “Al” (the). Therefore, trying to make this oath definite by saying that it refers to specific ten nights is not justified. How are we going to figure out what is meant by them? We start by searching the Quran for the use of the two terms: the term night and the term ten.

We note that the term night often referred to the best time to connect with Allah and even the Quran was revealed during a night, as examples:

وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَتَهَجَّدۡ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةً۬ لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبۡعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامً۬ا مَّحۡمُودًا ( الإسراء – الآية 79 )

“And during the night wake up for Salat Al-Tahajjud, an additional prayer for you, it is likely that your Lord will raise you to a praised estate. (Al-Isra 17:79)

أَمَّنۡ هُوَ قَـٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ سَاجِدً۬ا وَقَآٮِٕمً۬ا يَحۡذَرُ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ وَيَرۡجُواْ رَحۡمَةَ رَبِّهِۦ‌ۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِى ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ‌ۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَـٰبِ ( الزمر – الآية 9 )

“Is one who worships during the hours of night, prostrating himself or standing, fearing the Hereafter, and having hopes in the Mercy of his Lord (like one who does not)? Say: “Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” It is only people with understanding who will remember” (Al-Zumar 39:9)

إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَـٰهُ فِى لَيۡلَةٍ۬ مُّبَـٰرَكَةٍ‌ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ (٣) فِيہَا يُفۡرَقُ كُلُّ أَمۡرٍ حَكِيمٍ ( الدخان – الآية 3 )

“We sent it (this Qur’an) down on a blessed night. Verily, We are ever warning. (3) In that (night) every wise matter is decreed.” (Al-Dukhan 44:3-4)

So, we realize that the best time to do the dhikr, pray and supplicate to Allah is at night when you will be the closest to Allah to purify your soul and grant you His blessings.

Then, we look for references to the number ten and we note a very interesting verse that gives us the clue, and this is related to Prophet Musa; Allah says:

وَوَٲعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلَـٰثِينَ لَيۡلَةً۬ وَأَتۡمَمۡنَـٰهَا بِعَشۡرٍ۬ فَتَمَّ مِيقَـٰتُ رَبِّهِۦۤ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةً۬‌ۚ ( الأعراف – الآية 142 )

“And We did appoint for Moses thirty nights (of solitude), and We supplemented them with another ten. So, he completed the term appointed by His Lord of forty nights.” (Al-Araf 7:142)

Here we note that for Prophet Musa to be ready to receive Allah’s blessings, he spent thirty nights which is three sets of 10s supplicating and praying to Allah and these, apparently, were not sufficient to ensure the total purity of his soul to receive the blessings, enlightenment, and revelations form Allah, so Allah added for him a fourth set of an additional ten nights.

Now, we may be able to make the connection to the oath of the indefinite ten nights (i.e., any ten nights). This oath may be referring to a divine law on how to achieve spiritual enlightenment. This law suggests that the purify of a person soul to receive enlightenment form Allah requires dedication of sets of ten consecutive nights to spend on supplication, dhikr and prayers.

In case of Prophet Musa, he needed four sets of ten nights each that are being devoted for prayers, dhikr and supplication to Allah to achieve the level of spiritual purity to be ready for Allah to communicate with him.

As I always repeat, it is up to you to accept this understanding that the oath refers to the divine law of ten nights to achieve spiritual enlightenment or to accept the opinions that the oath refers to the ten nights of Ramadan or the ten days of Dhul-Hijja.

Now, we can expand a little on the meaning the other oaths.

The first oath “by the Fajr” (وَٱلۡفَجۡرِ) and this refers to the well know natural phenomena of Al-Fajr which is the dawn which is the time when darkness starts to diminish, and the light starts coming up from among the darkness. The term Fajr infers to the process of tearing the darkness of the night to allow the light to come through it and thus the life begins. No matter how the condition appears to be dark, the Fajr will come and remove this darkness and brings light.

The second oath with ten nights (وَلَيَالٍ عَشۡرٍ۬) that we have already discussed.

The third Oath is “by the Shaf’a” (وَٱلشَّفۡعِ) which is translated as “even” which is multiple of two. We call the payer of two rakk as Shafa. But the term shafa does nor merely refer to any two items but refers to two items that are complementing to each other to give something coherent. If you look at all creations, they are Shafa. A husband and wife are Shafa, water is shafa because it has oxygen and hydrogen. So, this oath is far broader that limiting it to the Shafa prayer. The idea of shafa (شفاعة) (intercession) is to declare that someone is with you.

May be a better translation for the word Shaf’a (ٱلشَّفۡعِ) is “pair” to highlight the complementary nature of the elements. This will expand the meaning to many other examples such as this life and the hereafter, the oceans and the land, the day and the night. All the creations are created in pairs. So, the oath by the Shaf’a (ٱلشَّفۡعِ) is an oath by all the creations.

The fourth Oath is “by the Witr” (وَٱلۡوَتۡرِ). The only thing that stands alone without a pair is Allah (swt), He is the One and there is none like or comparable to Him. So, this Oath may suggest that Allah is making an oath “by Himself.” So, the oaths by (وَٱلشَّفۡعِ وَٱلۡوَتۡرِ) are oaths by the creation and the creator.

But there could also other interpretations for both oaths (وَٱلشَّفۡعِ وَٱلۡوَتۡرِ), you can look at the periodic table and say every element is witr and combining two elements to produce a matter is Shaffa’. You can consider the sun as witr and the earth and the moon as shaffa. You can also consider that the dunya and the akhira as shaffa and the Day of Resurrection as he witr. So, these two oaths are far broader than just oaths with Shafa and Witr prayers.

The fifth oath is by the night as it moves away (وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَسۡرِ). The translation of (وَٱلَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَسۡرِ) as “by the night as it moves away” or “by the night as it departs” may not reflect the exact meaning of the verb (يَسۡرِ) which does not just mean moving away but it means moving away or departing stealthily. When Allah asked Prophet Musa to escape with his followers from the Pharaoh, Allah used the term Asri by night, meaning to depart quietly during the night.

فَأَسۡرِ بِعِبَادِى لَيۡلاً إِنَّڪُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ (٢٣)

(Allah said): “Depart quietly with My slaves by night. Surely, you will be pursued.” (Al-Dukhan 44:23)

This oath can be related to the first one (By the Fajr). When the night starts to drift away it indicated that Fajr is on its way. So, while the darkness appears to slow in its movement, it is broken by the Fajr and the light will come quickly.

After the Oaths, Allah directs those who are intelligent to reflect on history. Allah gives three examples of nations that transgressed beyond bounds. While they were firm in their position and the darkness, they created appears to be hard to eliminate, when the command of Allah came, their destruction was swift bringing light as the Fajr breaks the night. These three nations are: the tribe of Ad (عَادٍ), the tribe of Thamud (ثَمُودَ) and the people of Fura’wn (فِرۡعَوۡنَ).

DUA

المائدة – الآية 89: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ الْأَيْمَانَ ۖ فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ ۖ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمَانِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ ۚ وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمَانَكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

الأنعام – الآية 160: مَن جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا ۖ وَمَن جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَىٰ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ..

القصص – الآية 27: قَالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ابْنَتَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ عَلَىٰ أَن تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ ۖ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِندِكَ ۖ وَمَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ ۚ سَتَجِدُنِي إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ

الفجر – الآية 2: وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ.

الإسراء – الآية 79: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَّكَ عَسَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا .

الزمر – الآية 9: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ سَاجِدًا وَقَائِمًا يَحْذَرُ الْآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُو رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ ۗ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ

الدخان – الآية 3: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ

ق – الآية 40: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ

الذاريات – الآية 17: كَانُوا قَلِيلًا مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ

الطور – الآية 49: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبَارَ النُّجُومِ

Hadith on Fasting

روى النسائي في سننه عن أم المؤمنين حفصة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله ﷺ كان لا يدع ثلاثًا: صيام العشر، وعشوراء، وصيام ثلاثة أيام من كل شهر، وركعتين قبل الغداة.

عن بعض أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رضي الله عن الجميع قالت: ” كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَصُومُ تِسْعَ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ وَيَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ وَثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ “، قال الشيخ الألباني رحمه الله: ” إسناده صحيح ” في ” صحيح سنن أبي داود “.

وروى مسلم في صحيحه عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها: ما رأيت رسول الله ﷺ صائمًا في العشر قط. وفي رواية: لم يصم العشر قط .

كان لعائشة يومان وليلتان من كل تسع

وظاهِرُ هذا الحَديثِ أنَّ هذه العَشَرةَ أفضَلُ مِن العَشرِ الأواخِرِ مِن رَمضانَ. وقيل: إنَّ عَشْرَ ذي الحِجَّةِ أفضَلُ أيَّامًا، وعَشْرَ رَمضانَ أفضَلُ لَياليَ؛ لوُجودِ لَيلةِ القَدْرِ فيها.

content:
The Original Sin that Never Happened!

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

This discussion focuses on the key episode in the human history, it is related to the life of Prophet Adam and Sayeda Hawa (Eve) when they were in the garden. The common understanding of this episode is that Allah ordered them not to approach a certain tree, but Satan tempted them, and they ate from it committing the first sin and thus they were punished by being sent to earth. While this account does not have any significant relevance to the articles of faith in Islam, it is very critical to the Christian faith because it is the primary basis for giving justification to divinity to Prophet Jesus (PBUH) to cleanse man form this original sin.

Personally, I believe that the major injustice that Muslims commit against the Quran and frankly against themselves is using the bible to explain many of the stories in the Quran including this one that I plan to discuss. Any story in the Quran must solely be explained using the Quran and the authentic Hadith and archaeological findings if they exist.

The Quran offers an important educational tool to develop the cognitive and analytical capacity of Muslims, and this will be lost if you just go and read the details of the story in the Bible. Frankly, how can we seek interpretation of the Quran from other religious books when the Prophet (PBUH) said regarding the Quran in a hadith that is narrated by Imam Ali (RA) and reported in Al-Tirmidhi (الترمذي):

مَنْ ابَتَغَى الهُدَى فِي غَيْرِهِ أَضَلّهُ الله
Whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will misguide him.

هُوَ الّذِي لاَ تَزِيعُ بِهِ الأَهْوَاءُ، وَلاَ يَشْبَعُ مِنْهُ الْعُلَمَاءُ، وَلاَ يَخْلُقُ عَلى كَثْرَةِ الرّدّ، وَلاَ تَنْقَضِي عَجَائِبُهُ.
It is the one that will not make the whims deviates, and scholars will always be hungry to study it. Its responses do not need replenishment. And its wonders will never cease.

Unfortunately, some of the false accounts in the Bible creeped into books of Tafseer which is clear from the various Hadith that have reached us and were included in Bukhari and Muslim.

عن جابر – رضي الله عنه – عن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – حين أتاه عمر فقال : إنا نسمع أحاديث من يهود تعجبنا ، أفترى أن نكتب بعضها ؟ فقال : ” أمتهوكون أنتم كما تهوكت اليهود والنصارى ؟ ! لقد جئتكم بها بيضاء نقية ، ولو كان موسى حيا ما وسعه إلا اتباعي “
“We hear talks from Jews that we like, do you agree that we write some of them.
The Prophet (PBUH) said:
“Do you want to be deceived as the Jews and the Christians have been deceived!” I came to you with it white and pure, and if Moses was alive, he would have no choice except following me.”

Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس) said:
عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله أن ابن عباس قال كيف تسألون أهل الكتاب عن شيء وكتابكم الذي أنزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحدث تقرءونه محضا لم يشب وقد حدثكم أن أهل الكتاب بدلوا كتاب الله وغيروه وكتبوا بأيديهم الكتاب وقالوا هو من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا ألا ينهاكم ما جاءكم من العلم عن مسألتهم فلا والله ما رأينا منهم رجلا يسألكم عن الذي أنزل عليكم
“How can you ask the people of the book for anything and the book that was revealed to the messenger of Allah (PBUH) is the most recent that you read purely and without being mixed? Allah informed you that the people of the book have changed the book of Allah and altered it and wrote the book with their own hands and said it is from Allah to buy with it a small price. Should not the knowledge that you have prevent you from asking them? No, by Allah, we never saw a man from them asking you about what was revealed to you.”

But why one needs any other source than the Quran to explain what is in it since Allah said:

وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)
We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur’an), an exposition of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and glad tidings for the Muslims. (Al-Nahl 16:89)

Frankly, how can any Muslim use the Bible to explain what is in the Quran when even the biblical scholars themselves don’t know who wrote it. In an article in the National Geographic magazine in December 2018, it states:
“Despite the Bible’s undeniable influence, mysteries continue to linger over its origins. Even after centuries of rigorous investigation by biblical scholars, we still don’t know with certainty who wrote its various texts, when they were written or under what circumstances”. If one is interested in more details about the origin of the bible, he may read the book written by Robert Huber and Stephen Miller.

If you really want to know what happened to our father Adam and our mother Hawa (Eve) when they were in the Garden and to derive valuable lessons, you need to cleanse your mind from anything that you have read or heard that is based on the Bible and focus on deriving the story from the Quran.

Before we start, let use briefly mention two topics that have discussed previously. The first topic is the 7 steps to study the Quran, and these are:

1. Reading (Qira’ah) (قراءة) (Uttering the words and sentences whether one may or may not understand the meanings of what is being read. This will give the reader a blessing from Allah, hasanah for each letter)
2. Recitation (Tilawah) (تلاوة) (Understanding the meaning of the words and the verses taking into account the context)
3. Purification (Tazkiah) (تزكية) (Purification of the Nafs)
4. Tarteel (ترتيل) (Assembly of all verses related to the same subject to allow comprehensive understanding of the subject)
5. Tadabour (تدبر) (This involves studying the verses related to the same subject that were assembled in the previous step of Tarteel to harmonize them to drive clear understating of the subject)
6. Recollection (Tadhakur) (تذكر) (Memorization and reminder of past learnings)
7. Study (Dirasah) (دراسة) (Continuous study to derive new knowledge and unlock the secrets of the Quran. The Prophet (PBUH) said regarding the Quran that “Its wonders will never cease”. (وَلَا تَنْقَضِي عَجَائِبُهُ).

The second topic is the scientific methodology that was developed by the Muslim scientist and scholar Abu-Ali al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham (أبو علي، الحسن بن الحسن بن الهيثم) whose Latinized name “Alhazen”. Ibn al-Haytham is considered the father of modern scientific methodology that involves 6 steps:

1. Make observations.
2. Think of questions.
3. Formulate hypothesis.
4. Developing testable predictions.
5. Collect data to test the prediction.
6. Develop a general theory if the data validates the hypothesis, otherwise repeat the process by redefining altering, expanding, or rejecting the hypothesis.

Both the 7 steps to study the Quran and the 6 steps of the scientific methodology are related. Through the recitation of the Quran, you make certain observation that brings e certain questions in your mind. And this leads you to make hypothesis regarding what happened in any of the events that are discussed in the Quran.

Then you go thru the process of testing the hypothesis based on all the verses in the Quran and any authentic Hadith.

If all elements of the hypothesis are validated, i.e., don’t contradict any of the data, you can assume that it is a valid hypothesis. However, one cannot assume that it is the only valid hypothesis because someone else many come with another hypothesis that is also valid. Also, even you may come with another more refined hypothesis as you read more and as you advance in knowledge, However, if the data contradicts the hypothesis, you will need to modify the hypothesis and repeat the process of validation.

The account of the story of Prophet Adam and Sayeda Hawa in the Garden came in the Quran in 22 verses in Surat Al-Baqara, Al-Araf and Taha. There are also 5 verses that are related to the study. In addition, there are 2 hadith that are relevant.

Direct Verses (22 verses): Surat Al-Baqara has 4 verses (2:34-38), Surat Al-Araf has 9 verses (7:19-27) and Surat Taha has 9 verses (20:115-123)
Related verses (5 verses): Al-Baqara 2: 30, Al-Arfat 7:11, 172, and 189) and Al-Isra 17:62

(I am not going to present the verses here because of the time, but I really suggest that you read them on your own). However, I’ll use them to implement the first step of the scientific methodology which is to make observations. When you read the account of Prophet Adam and Sayeda Hawa (Eve) in the Quran, you will most likely make several observations such as:

Observation 1: The stories in the Quran are intended as tools for teaching morality and wisdom, strengthening the emotional dimension, providing and knowledge and learning. In addition, the stories are educational tools to improve the cognitive capacity of the reader thru the use of reasoning for thinking about the overt and hidden points. This story should be no different.
Basis:
كَذَٲلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدۡ سَبَقَ‌ۚ وَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَـٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِڪۡرًا (٩٩)
Thus, We relate to you some information of what happened before. And We have given you from Us a Reminder. (Ta-Ha, 20:99)
لَقَدۡ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِہِمۡ عِبۡرَةٌ۬ لِّأُوْلِى ٱلۡأَرۡبَـٰبِ‌ۗ
Indeed, in their stories, there is a lesson for the people of understanding. (Yusuf 12:111)
وَكُلاًّ۬ نَّقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلرُّسُلِ مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ‌ۚ وَجَآءَكَ فِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرَى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٢٠)
And We relate to these accounts of the Messengers in order that We strengthen your heart and in these (stories) there has come to you the truth, as well as a good counsel and a reminder for the believers. (Hud 11:120)
فَٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١٧٦)
So, relate the stories, so that they may ponder (Al-Araf 7:176)

Observation 2: Even before the creation of Adam, Allah informed the angels that Adam will be a Khalifa (vicegerent) in earth and thus Adam was destined to be send to earth whether he ate from the tree or not.
Basis:
وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةً۬‌ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيہَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيہَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ‌ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ (٣٠)
And recall when your Lord said to the angels: verily I am going to create a vicegerent On the earth. They said: will you create therein one who will make mischief and shed blood while glorify You with praises and sanctify You! He (Allah) said: I know that which you do not know.” (Al-Baqara 2:30)
وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَـٰڪُمۡ ثُمَّ صَوَّرۡنَـٰكُمۡ ثُمَّ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ لَمۡ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّـٰجِدِينَ (١١)
And surely, We created you (all humans) and then gave you shape; then We told the angels, “Prostrate to Adam”, and they prostrated, except Iblîs (Satan), he refused to be of those who prostrated themselves. (Al-Arfat 7:11)
وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ ۖ قَالُوا بَلَىٰ ۛ شَهِدْنَا ۛ أَن تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَٰذَا غَافِلِينَ
“(Recall) when your Lord took from the children of Adam their descendants from the loins, and made them testify about themselves (by asking them,) “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Indeed, You are. We testify.” (We did so) just in case you may say on the Day of Judgment, “We were never unaware of this,” (Al-Araf 7:172)

Observation 3: Even before Allah asked the angels to prostrate to Adam, Allah exposed to Adam all his progeny and informed him of his and their life span. So, Adam knew that he would have descendants and thru them his legacy will remain.
Basis: It is reported by Imam Al-Tirmizi (الترمذي) that Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) said::
“ لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة وجعل بين عيني كل إنسان منهم وبيصا من نور ثم عرضهم على آدم فقال: أي ربي من هؤلاء؟ قال: هؤلاء ذريتك فرأى منهم فأعجبه وبيص ما بين عينيه فقال: يا رب من هذا؟ قال: هذا رجل من آخر الأمم من ذريتك يقال له: داود قال: يا رب كم عمره؟ قال: ستون سنة قال: أي رب أعطه من عمري أربعين فأخذ الله عليه الميثاق ”
“When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back and every soul of his offspring that Allah will create until the Day of judgement fell from his back. Allah put on the forehead of every one of them a flash of light, then showed them to Adam. Adam asked: “My Lord who are they? Allah said: They are your offspring. Adam saw one of them and he was charmed by a bright flash between his eyes. He asked: My Lord, who is this? Allah said: he is a man from the late nations from your descendants and his name is Dawoud (David). Adam asked: My Lord, what is his age? Allah said: sixty years. Adam said: My Lord give him 40 years from my age. Allah took the covenant from Adam that this is his demand.

Observation 4: When Allah rejected Satan form heaven because of his refusal to prostrate to Adam, Satan threatened to control Adam’s descendants. So, even before Adam was sent to earth Satan’s focus was on controlling Adam’s descendants and not even on Adam himself.
Basis:
قَالَ أَرَءَيۡتَكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِى ڪَرَّمۡتَ عَلَىَّ لَٮِٕنۡ أَخَّرۡتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ لَأَحۡتَنِڪَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ (٦٢)
“[Iblis (Satan)] said: “See this one whom You have honored above me, if You give me respite (keep me alive) to the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize and mislead his offspring except a few of them!” (Al-Isra 17:62)

Observation 5: When Adam violated Allah’s command and ate form the tree, Allah described the act as slip not as major sin. The word “azalla” (أَزَلَّ) means to cause one to lose his footing or his balance unintentionally and momentarily.
Basis:
فَأَزَلَّہُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ عَنۡہَا فَأَخۡرَجَہُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ‌ۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ۬‌ۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرٌّ۬ وَمَتَـٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ۬ (٣٦)
“But Satan caused them to slip and expelled them from the state in which they were. And We said: Go you all down. Some of you being the enemies of others, and on earth there will be your dwelling place and provision for a time. ” (Al-Baqara 2:36)

Observation 6: The slip that Adam did was forgiven and thus not important other than serving as important lesson for us, so we don’t repeat it.
Basis:
فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍ۬ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٣٧)
Then Adam received from his Lord words. And his Lord accepted his repentance. Verily, He is the One Who forgives, the Most Merciful (Al-Baqara 2:37)
ثُمَّ ٱجۡتَبَـٰهُ رَبُّهُ ۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ وَهَدَىٰ (١٢٢)
Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance, and gave him guidance (Taha 20:122)

Observation 7: Adam and Eve were dressed when they were in the Garden. This means that they were not naked. Thus, eating from the tree is not a cause for them being naked. Rather being naked is a prerequisite for eating from the tree.
Basis:
إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيہَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ (١١٨)
Here you will not be hungry, nor you will be naked. (Taha 20:118)

Observation 8: The one physical action that Satan did to Adam and Eve is stripping them form their clothing and thus making them naked. Allah warns the children of Adam not to allow Satan to do the same to them and make them naked.
Basis:
يَا بَنِي آدَمَ لَا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ كَمَا أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُم مِّنَ الْجَنَّةِ يَنزِعُ عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوْآتِهِمَا ۗ
O Children of Adam! Let not Satan deceive you, as he got your parents out of the garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. (Al-Araf 7:27)

Observation 9: Using his deception strategy, Satan guided Adam and Eve on how to taste the tree that led to their exposure and shame. So, neither Adam nor Evan knew how to eat form the tree before Satan showed them.
Basis:
فَدَلَّٮٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ۬‌ۚ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٲتُہُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡہِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ‌ۖ وَنَادَٮٰهُمَا رَبُّہُمَآ أَلَمۡ أَنۡہَكُمَا عَن تِلۡكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّڪُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (٢٢)
So, he (Satan) guided/showed them with deception. Then when they tasted of the tree, that which was hidden from them of their shame (private parts) became manifest to them and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Garden. And their Lord called out to them (saying): “Did I not forbid you that tree and tell you: Verily, Satan is an open enemy unto you?” (Al-Araf 7:22)

Observation 10: All the blame for eating from the tree was placed on Adam because he lacked firmness to resist the temptation that made him forget Allah’s command. Eve was merely a passive participant. Also, the joint act of eating for the tree lead to exposing their private parts.
Basis:
وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُ ۥ عَزۡمً۬ا (١١٥)
“We gave our command to Adam which he forgot and found that he lacks firmness.’ (Taha 20:115)
فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ ۚ وَعَصَىٰ آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَىٰ
“Then they both ate of the tree, and so their private parts became manifest to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Garden for their covering. Thus did Adam disobey his Lord, so he went astray” (Taha 20:121)

Observation 11: Hawa (Eve) was created as the wife for Adam from day one. And they know that they will have children thru a certain process.
Basis:
هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٍ۬ وَٲحِدَةٍ۬ وَجَعَلَ مِنۡہَا زَوۡجَہَا لِيَسۡكُنَ إِلَيۡہَا‌ۖ فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّٮٰهَا حَمَلَتۡ حَمۡلاً خَفِيفً۬ا فَمَرَّتۡ بِهِۦ‌ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَثۡقَلَت دَّعَوَا ٱللَّهَ رَبَّہُمَا لَٮِٕنۡ ءَاتَيۡتَنَا صَـٰلِحً۬ا لَّنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّـٰكِرِينَ (١٨٩)
It is He Who has created you from a single soul and out of him He has created from him his wife [Hawa (Eve)], so that he finds comfort in her. When he (Adam) covered her, she carried a light burden and moved about with it. Then when it became heavy, they both invoked Allah, their Lord (saying): “If You give us a a perfect child, we shall indeed be among the grateful.” (Al-Araf 7:189)

Observation 12: Both the Quran and the hadith use metaphors for terms that are embarrassing such as sextual intercourse.
Basis: Ibn Abbas said:
قال ابن عباس: (الدخول والتغشي والإفضاء والمباشرة والرفث واللمس هذا الجماع غير أن الله حَيِيٌّ كريم يكنى بما شاء شاء) .(المصنف، أبو بكر عبد الرزاق الصنعاني.)
“The terms entering, covering, access, confide, approach, and touching refer to intercourse, but Allah is shy and generous, He uses metaphores for what He wants.”

أُحِلَّ لَڪُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآٮِٕكُمۡ‌ۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ۬ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسٌ۬ لَّهُنَّ‌ۗ [البقرة: 187]
It is made lawful for you , on the night of the fast, is the approach to your wives. They are a garment onto you and you are a garment onto them. (Al-Baqara 2:187)
وَلَا تُبَـٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمۡ عَـٰكِفُونَ فِى ٱلۡمَسَـٰجِدِ‌ۗ [البقرة: 187]
And do not touch them when you are in seclusion in the mosques. (Al-Baqara 2:187)
{وَقَدْ أَفْضَى بَعْضُكُمْ إلَى بَعْضٍ} [النساء: 21].
“When you have had access to each other, (Al-Nisa 4:21)
{وَإن طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ} [البقرة: 237].
If you divorce them before you have touched them. (Al-Baqara 2:237)
{أَوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ} [النساء: 43].
“Or you have had contact with women” (Al-Nisa 4: 43)

Observation 13: A term such eat does not necessarily mean consuming food, it can be used to refer consuming other physical things or activities such as money, usury, good deeds.
Basis:
وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٲلَكُم بَيۡنَكُم بِٱلۡبَـٰطِلِ
“And do not eat each other property by false means.” (Al-Baqara 2:188)
ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡڪُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِى يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسِّ‌ۚ
“Those who eat Riba (usury) will not stand except like the standing of one whom the demon has driven to insanity by his touch.” (Al-Baqara 2:275)

The Prophet (PBUH) said:
[عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْحَسَدَ، فَإِنَّ الْحَسَدَ يَأْكُلُ الْحَسَنَاتِ] أَخْرَجَهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ. وَابْنُ مَاجَهْ
Beware of envy, indeed envy eats good deeds. (Abu Daud and Ibn Majah)

Observation 14: A term such as a tree that has been eaten from is used as metaphor for a woman that has been married before, i.e. not virgin because she has been engaged in sextual intercourse.
Basis: Both Bukhari and Muslim reported that Sayeda Aisha said that I said to the messenger of Allah (PBUH):
عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ – رضى الله عنها – قَالَتْ قُلتُ يا رَسولَ اللَّهِ، أرَأَيْتَ لَوْ نَزَلْتَ وادِيًا وفيهِ شَجَرَةٌ قدْ أُكِلَ مِنْها، ووَجَدْتَ شَجَرًا لَمْ يُؤْكَلْ مِنْها، في أيِّها كُنْتَ تُرْتِعُ بَعِيرَكَ؟ قالَ: في الذي لَمْ يُرْتَعْ مِنْها . تَعْنِي أنَّ رَسولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ لَمْ يَتَزَوَّجْ بكْرًا غَيْرَهَا.
“O Messenger of Allah: Suppose you landed in a valley where there is a tree of which something has been eaten from it and then you found trees of which nothing has been eaten from, of which tree would you let your camel graze?”
He said, “(I will let my camel graze) of the one of which nothing has been eaten before.”
(Aisha wanted to bring to the Prophet’s attention that he (PBUH) had not married a virgin besides herself.

يَـٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ لَا يَفۡتِنَنَّڪُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَ أَبَوَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ يَنزِعُ عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوْآتِهِمَا ۗ إِنَّهُ يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ ۗ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا الشَّيَاطِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (27)

Taha (20:115-123) (9 verses)
“We gave our command to Adam earlier, then he forgot and found that he lacks firm resolve. (115)
سُوۡرَةُ طٰه
وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُ ۥ عَزۡمً۬ا (١١٥)

When We said to the angels: “Prostrate yourselves to Adam.” They all prostrated themselves except Iblis (Satan) who refused. (116)
وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ (١١٦)

“We said: O’ Adam, this (Satan) is an enemy of you and your wife, so do not let him bring you out of the Garden so that you would suffer. (117)
فَقُلۡنَا يَـٰٓـٴَـادَمُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا عَدُوٌّ۬ لَّكَ وَلِزَوۡجِكَ فَلَا يُخۡرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ فَتَشۡقَىٰٓ (١١٧)

Here you have (a promise from Us) that you will not be hungry, nor you will be naked. (118)
إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيہَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ (١١٨)

And you will suffer not suffer from thirst nor will you be exposed top the sun’s heat. (119)
وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظۡمَؤُاْ فِيہَا وَلَا تَضۡحَىٰ (١١٩)

Then, Satan whispered to him, saying: “O Adam! Shall I lead you to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that will never decay?” (120)
فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ قَالَ يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكٍ۬ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ (١٢٠)

“Then they both ate of the tree, and so their private parts became manifest to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Garden for their covering. Thus did Adam disobey his Lord, so he went astray (121)
فَأَڪَلَا مِنۡہَا فَبَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٲتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡہِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ‌ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُ ۥ فَغَوَىٰ (١٢١)

Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance, and gave him guidance (122)
ثُمَّ ٱجۡتَبَـٰهُ رَبُّهُ ۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ وَهَدَىٰ (١٢٢)

He (Allah) said: “Get you down from here, all of you, some of you are an enemy to some others. Then should some guidance come to you from Me, whoever follows My Guidance he shall neither go astray, nor shall he be distressed. (123)
قَالَ ٱهۡبِطَا مِنۡهَا جَمِيعَۢا‌ۖ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ۬‌ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّڪُم مِّنِّى هُدً۬ى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشۡقَىٰ (١٢٣)

Related Verses
And recall when your Lord said to the angels: verily I am going to create a vicegerent On the earth. They said: will you create therein one who will mak mischief and shed blood While glorify You with praises and thanks and sanctify You! He (Allah) said: I know that which you do not knowt.” (Al-Baqara 2:30)
البقرة – وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةً۬‌ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيہَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيہَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ‌ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ (٣٠)

And surely, We created you (your father Adam) and then gave you shape (the noble shape of a human being); then We told the angels, “Prostrate yourselves to Adam”, and they prostrated themselves, except Iblîs (Satan), he refused to be of those who prostrated themselves. (Al-Arraf 7: 11)
الاٴعرَاف – – وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَـٰڪُمۡ ثُمَّ صَوَّرۡنَـٰكُمۡ ثُمَّ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ لَمۡ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّـٰجِدِينَ (١١)

“(Recall) when your Lord took from the children of Adam their descendants from the loins, and made them testify about themselves (by asking them,) “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Indeed, You are. We testify.” (We did so) just in case you may say on the Day of Judgment, “We were never unaware of this,” (Al-Araf 7:172)
سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف – وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَہُمۡ وَأَشۡہَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِہِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡ‌ۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ‌ۛ شَہِدۡنَآ‌ۛ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَـٰذَا غَـٰفِلِينَ (١٧٢)

It is He Who has created you from a single soul and out of him He has created from him his wife [Hawwa (Eve)], so that he may find comfort in her. When he covered her, she carried a light burden and moved about with it. Then when it became heavy, they both invoked Allah, their Lord (saying): “If You give us a a perfect child, we shall indeed be among the grateful.” (Al-Araf 7:189)
سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف – هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٍ۬ وَ\u0671حِدَةٍ۬ وَجَعَلَ مِنۡہَا زَوۡجَہَا لِيَسۡكُنَ إِلَيۡہَا‌ۖ فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّ\u0670ہَا حَمَلَتۡ حَمۡلاً خَفِيفً۬ا فَمَرَّتۡ بِهِۦ‌ۖ فَلَمَّ\u0670ٓ أَثۡقَلَت دَّعَوَا ٱللَّهَ رَبَّہُمَا لَ\u0671ئِنۡ ءَاتَيۡتَنَا صَ\u0640ٰلِحً۬ا لَّنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّ\u0640ٰكِرِينَ (١٨٩)

“[Iblis (Satan)] said: “See this one whom You have honored above me, if You give me respite (keep me alive) to the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize and mislead his offspring except a few of them!” (Al-Isra 17:62)
إسرَاء – قَالَ أَرَءَيۡتَكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِى ڪَرَّمۡتَ عَلَىَّ لَ\u0671ئِنۡ أَخَّرۡتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَ\u0640ٰمَةِ لَأَحۡتَنِڪَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ (٦٢)

Appendix 3. The Quran
It is reported in Al-Tirmidhi (الترمذي) that Imam Ali narrated that he heard the Prophet (PBUH) saying that there will be fitan (tribulations).
I said: مَا المَخْرَجُ مِنْهَا يَا رَسُولَ الله؟ “How can we save ourselves from them, O’ Messenger of Allah?
The Prophet (PBUH) replied: (كِتَابُ الله) the book of Allah, and the Prophet (PBUH) continued to give details about the Quran:
فِيهِ نَبَأُ مَا كان قَبْلَكُمْ، وَخَبَرُ مَا بَعْدَكُمْ وَحُكْمُ مَا بَيْنَكُمْ،
In it there is the true account of those before you, the news of those who will follow you; and the judgment on the case between you.

وَهُوَ الفَصْلُ لَيْسَ بِالْهَزْلِ مَنْ تَرَكَهُ مِنْ جَبّارٍ قَصَمَهُ الله، وَمَنْ ابَتَغَى الهُدَى فِي غَيْرِهِ أَضَلّهُ الله،
It is the serious judgment and not the lighthearted amusement. Any tyrant who discards it, Allah will crush him. Whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will misguide him.

وَهُوَ حَبْلُ الله المَتِينُ، وَهُوَ الذّكْرُ الْحَكِيمُ، وَهُوَ الصّرَاطُ المُسْتَقِيمُ، هُوَ الّذِي لاَ تَزِيعُ بِهِ الأَهْوَاءُ، وَلاَ تَلْبَسُ بِهِ الأَلْسِنَةُ، وَلاَ يَشْبَعُ مِنْهُ الْعُلَمَاءُ، وَلاَ يَخْلُقُ عَلى كَثْرَةِ الرّدّ، وَلاَ تَنْقَضِي عَجَائِبُهُ.
It is the mighty rope of Allah. It is the noteworthy wise remembrance. It is the straight path. It is the one that will not make the whims deviates, nor will it make the tongue ambiguous, and scholars will always be hungry to study it. Its responses do not need replenishment. And its wonders will never cease.

وَهُوَ َ الّذِي لَمْ تَنْتَهِ الْجِنّ إِذْ سَمِعَتْهُ حَتّى قالُوا {إِنّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنَا عَجَبَا يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ فَآمَنَّا بِهِ}
It is the one the Jinn said about it as soon they heard it: We have heard wondrous Quran. It guides to the right path and so we believed in it.

مَنْ قالَ بِهِ صَدَقَ، وَمَنْ عَمِلَ بِهِ أُجِرَ، وَمَنْ حَكَمَ بِهِ عَدَلَ، وَمَنْ دَعَا إِلَيْهِ هُدِيَ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ.
Whoever quotes it is truthful and whoever applies it will have lofty rewards and whoever rules with it will always achieve Justice, and whoever calls to it will be guided to the straight path.

The Breadth Knowledge in the Quran
Some scholars say that the Quran contains all kinds of knowledge including every event that happens in the earth. It was reported that Ibn Masoud (ابن مسعود) said:
مَنْ أَرَادَ الْعِلْمَ فَلْيُثَوِّرِ الْقُرْآنَ ، فَإِنَّ فِيهِ عِلْمَ الأَوَّلِينَ وَالآخِرِينَ ) الزهد ” لابن المبارك في ” الزهد ” (الكبير) ابن المبارك في ” الزهد ” (الكبير) لبَحْث عَن معانيه
“Who wanted the knowledge should study the Quran, it has the knowledge of the earlier and the later civilizations.”
It is also reported that Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس) said: لو ضاع لي عقال بعير لوجدته في كتاب الله “If my camel’s rope is lost, I will find it in the book of Allah.”
Imam Abu Hamed Al-Ghazali (ابو حامد محمد الغزالي‎) in his books “Revival of Religious Sciences” (إحياء علوم الدين) and “Jewels of the Qur’an and its Pearls” (جواهر القرآن ودرره) said: The Quran encompasses seventy-seven thousand and two hundred (77,200) forms of knowledge.
Imam Abu Bakr al-Arabi (ابو بكر العربى), the Maliki Imam, claimed the Quran includes 77,450 types of knowledge.
While Imam Al-Fakhr Al-Razi (الفخرالرازى) said the Quran does not include except religious knowledge, in his tafseer he contradicted this view by explaining many verses using the science of astronomy. When he was asked of this contradiction, he said that in many verses in the Quran, Allah asks us to ponder and examine the creations of heavens and earth.
Note: The reason that some scholars objected to claim that the Quran includes science and other knowledge because changes in people’s understanding can create doubt about the Quran. But the problem is never in the Quran but in people’s interpretation of the verses of the Quran.

Appendix 4: Original Sin in Christianity
Original sin is the Christian doctrine that humans inherit a tainted nature and a proclivity to sin through the fact of birth. Original sin is the guilt of disobedience to God passed on from Adam and Eve to all subsequent generations. For Catholics, original sin is a state, implying that infants are guilty at birth; for Protestants, in contrast, sin is an act, and original sin implies merely a propensity to commit sinful acts. There is no doctrine of original sin in traditional or Orthodox Judaism. For Christian, original sin is the basis for divinity of Jesus so he can cleanse the humanity of this sin.
The doctrine of original sin began to emerge in the 3rd century but only became fully formed with the writings of Augustine of Hippo (354–430), who was the first author to use the phrase “original sin” (peccatum originale).
The Jansenist movement, which the Catholic Church declared heretical from 1653, also maintained that original sin rendered humans incapable of good without God’s grace.
The religion of Islam completely rejects the concept of inherited sin and declares that: non one can carry the burden of the sin of another. Also, Allah is the most Merciful and most Compassionate, so He accepted the repentance of Adam and Eve as soon as they turned away from their sins and reformed themselves, without punishing them or any other person on their behalf.
In numerous verses in the Quran and statements of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), it is mentioned that those who commit sin then seek the forgiveness of Allah and perform good deeds, Allah will forgive them and change their sins to good deeds.

قُلۡ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٥٣) وَأَنِيبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَأَسۡلِمُواْ لَهُ ۥ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ ثُمَّ لَا تُنصَرُونَ (٥٤)
“Say: O My slaves who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. (53) And return [in repentance] to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.” (Al-Zumur 39: 53-54)

وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَ‌ۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٲلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامً۬ا (٦٨) يُضَـٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا (٦٩) إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلاً صَـٰلِحً۬ا فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِہِمۡ حَسَنَـٰتٍ۬‌ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورً۬ا رَّحِيمً۬ا (٧٠)
“And those who do not invoke any other god along with Allah, nor take the life that Allah has given sanctity except for (course of) justice, nor commit adultery – and whoever does this shall pay the penalty; (68) The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained forever; (69) Except the one who repents and believes and does righteous deeds; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.” (Al-Furqan 25:68-70)
