content:
Islamic Approach to Ending Domestic Violence

إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

Since March is women history month, it will be good to address the major problem of domestic violence that has been facing women for centuries and continues until today and look how Islam addressed this issue. Islam addressed this issue in the year 620 CE which is over 1350 years before the west established laws against it. Also, Islam gave women rights that have not been attained by women in the west even today.

Modern attention to domestic violence in the west began with women’s movement of the 1970s. In 1994, The US congress passed the Violence Against Women Act (“VAWA”) and in 1996 domestic violence was designated as national crime. In fact, prior to the mid-1800s, most legal systems implicitly accepted wife beating as a valid exercise of a husband’s authority over his wife. Also, until the mid-19th century a man in the west and the US was allowed to sell his wife.

However, in spite the laws that have been established against domestic violence against women, this shocking crime remains to be a big problem even today. Here are some statistics in the US:
- 1 in 3 women have experienced some form of physical violence by an intimate partner.
- 1 in 4 women have been victims of severe physical violence (e.g. beating, burning, strangling) by an intimate partner in their lifetime.
- 1 in 7 women have been injured by an intimate partner.

So, domestic violence of a husband against his wife is a social disease that existed in the past and based on statistics, it continues to exist until now. The problem may have risen because some religions place the responsibility of the original sin on women. In addition to this social disease, another social disease that existed openly in the past is slavery and it continues to exist today informally in many societies.

It is interesting that Islam eliminated these two diseases over 1400 years ago without setting law against them. This is done by changing the morals of the people and correcting their false ideas.

I previously discussed Islamic approach to eliminating slavery in a talk entitled “Abolishing Slavery” on September 22, 2019; it is available on YouTube. Today, I will inshallah focus on the issue of violence of a husband against his wife.

Addressing this topic is important for several reasons:
1. There is major confusion in the west regarding Islam’s position on women and the issue of women rights in Islam is often raised to attack Islam.
2. Violence against wives by so called Muslim husbands in the US remains to be a big problem. I heard some statistics that say about 20% of Muslim women in the US are experiencing domestic abuse and unfortunately this even happens to members of our community.
3. Some Muslims have no clue about Islamic rules and thus continue to follow male based tribal and pagan customs.

In my talk today, I’ll focus on verse 34 of Surat Al-Nisa that is often used to justify the abuse of women because it may be understood as giving a husband the right to freely hit his wife which is in complete contradiction to the verse and to the practices of our beloved Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) who is the only one whom we are required to use as reference to understand the interpretation of the Quran through his actions.

In translating the verse, I’ll not translate three key words because I want to explain their meanings in detail before giving their proper translations, Allah says:

ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٲمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٲلِهِمۡ‌ۚ فَٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ قَـٰنِتَـٰتٌ حَـٰفِظَـٰتٌ۬ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ وَٱلَّـٰتِى تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِى ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌ۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَڪُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡہِنَّ سَبِيلاً‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّ۬ا ڪَبِيرً۬ا (٣٤)

“Men are (قَوَّٲمُونَ) “Qawamoon” of women by the virtue of Allah has favored some of them above others, and because of their spending from their money. The righteous women are devoutly obedient (to Allah), guarding the unsee (the family secrets) that Allah has guarded. As for those whom you fear (نُشُوزَهُنَّ) “Noushouzuhun”, advise them, then refuse to share their beds, then (ٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌) “Adribuhun”. if they return to obedience, seek not a way against them. Surely, Allah is Exalted, Most Great (Al-Nisa 4:34)

The three words that require serious clarification because their wrong interpretation can lead to complete misunderstanding of the pragmatic strategy that the Quran uses to eliminate the social disease of domestic violence against wives. These words are (قَوَّٲمُونَ), (نُشُوزَهُنَّ), and (ٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌).

Let me start with the first word (قَوَّٲمُونَ) because this word set the responsibility of the husband and the wife which if understood from the Quran and the sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH), it will solve all the problems between the husband and the wife. The relationship between the husband and the wife is based on certain Islamic fundamentals that must be understood:

First, man and woman are created form the same soul this was emphasized in many verses in the Quran such as:
يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا
“O mankind! Fear your Lord Who created you from a single soul and from it created its mate”. (Al-Nisaa 4:1)
Therefore, there should be no preference between man and woman in the sight of Allah, except by Taqwa, the level of their degree of conscious of Allah in all what they do.

Second: The term (قَوَّٲمُونَ) came in several times in the Quran to mean stand up for justice and stand up for prayers. It does not imply any form superiority; in fact it implies humility and service. As example, Allah says:
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٲمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُہَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٲلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَ‌ۚ (١٣٥)
“O you who believe! Stand out firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah, even though it be against yourselves, or your parents, or your kin.” (Al-Nisa 4:135)

Third: Allah attributed solely to Adam (the man) the disobedience to Allah’s command that He gave to both Adam and Hawa (Eve):
وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُ ۥ عَزۡمً۬ا (١١٥)
“And indeed, We gave directive to Adam earlier, but he forgot, and We did not find in him firm resolve.” (Taha 20:115)
Therefore, the blame of disobeying Allah and eating form the tree was placed solely on Adam and Eve (Hawa) has nothing to do with it, as Allah says:
فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ‌ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُ ۥ فَغَوَىٰ
“They both ate of the tree, and so their nakedness appeared to them: they began to sew together, for their covering, leaves from the Garden; thus Adam disobeyed his Lord, and allowed himself to be seduced. (Taha 20:121)

Fourth: Allah made it clear to Adam and not Hawa (Eve) that the disobedience to Allah’s command not to eat form the tree will result in Adam leaving heaven and suffering in earth:
فَقُلۡنَا يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا عَدُوٌّ۬ لَّكَ وَلِزَوۡجِكَ فَلَا يُخۡرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ فَتَشۡقَىٰٓ (١١٧)
Then We said: “O Adam! Verily, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not get you both out of Paradise, so that you (Adam) will be in hardship. (Taha 20:117)
Therefore, the hardship that people will face in the earth should be on the man only and the women should not suffer any hardship. Since man was the one responsible for getting the woman from heaven, he should face all hardship to make her life in earth closely similar to her life heaven.

This is why in the Islamic law, the wife has no responsibility in her house other than two things:
1. make herself attractive to her husband to have intimate relationship with him.
2. Do not allow anyone he dislikes to enter their house.
These are the only two obligations for the wife. How about cooking and cleaning and taking care of the children, none of these are her responsibilities.

It is the opinion of (المالكية والشافعية وجمهور الحنابلة والظاهرية) Malik, Al-Shafie, Ahmad and Ibn Hazm that the wife is not obligated to work in her husband house; she has no responsibility to cook, clean, wash clothing or do anything around the house and that the husband needs to hire her servants.
Imam Malik has an opinion that if the husband is poor, the wife may help with the housework and Imam Abu Hanifa says that if she did, it is not as obligation but rather as something that Allah will reward her for doing it.
The majority opinion is that the wife is not obligated even if the husband cannot afford a servant. Imam Ibn Hazm, says that the husband cannot bring to his wife uncooked food or bring for her fabric that is not sewed. He needs to bring her cooked food and sewed clothing.

The Jurists derived their ruling based on the verse in surat At-Talaq in which the man is required to pay his divorced wife for breast feeding their infant child.
{ فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ }،
“Then if they are suckling for you (breast feed a child), give them their due payment,” (Al-Talaq 65:6)
If the woman is paid to breast feed her child, it would be more reasonable to consider that doing other tasks is not obligatory.

Even the Khalifa Omar ibn Al-Khtaab was on the opinion that the wife is not obligated to work in the house. Once a man came to complain to Omar about his wife and he knocked on the door, he heard Omar’s wife shouting at him, so he left but Omar opened the door and called him and asked him why did you come? The man said: I came to complain about my wife who shouts at me and I found you in worst position. So, Omar told him:
يا أخي إني احتملتها لحقوق لها علي : إنها طباخة لطعامي خبازة لخبزي غسالة لثيابي مرضعة لولدي و ليس ذلك كله بواجب عليها
“My brother, how can I not tolerate her, and she has rights over me. She cooks my food and bakes my bread and wash my clothing and breast feed my child and she is not obligated to do any of these.

Therefore, when it comes to work around the house, it is the husband obligation and if the wife does it, it is out of kindness and love and the husband should be grateful rather than complaining when he sees certain things are not done. Our role model for treating his wives is our Prophet (PBUH) and as Sayeda Aisha said:
إذا دخل بيته قالت: كان يكون في مهنة أهله فإذا حضرت الصلاة قام فصلى
“As soon as the Prophet (PBUH) enters his house, he is always in the service of his family and only stops for prayers”. (Muslim)
Sayeda Aisha also said:
عَن عَائِشَة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالتْ: ما كان أحد أحسن خلقا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ما دعاه أحد من الصحابة ولا من أهل بيته إلا قال لبيك
“No one had a better character than the Prophet (PBUH), no one ever called him from his family, but he answered “لبيك”, I am at your service”.

With this background, we realize that the term (قَوَّٲمُونَ) in the verse (ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٲمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ) means that men are always standing up in support and service of women financially, physically and emotionally. Therefore.
ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٲمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٲلِهِمۡ‌ۚ
Can be translated as follows:
“Men are standing in support/service of women by the virtue that Allah has favored some of them above others, and because of spending from their wealth. (Al-Nisa 4:34)

Since the wife has no responsibly around the house, the remaining on verse 34 has nothing to do with the wife refusing to do anything around the house, but it focuses on the one key responsibility of the wife towards her husband which is the intimate relationship with him.
The middle part of the verse describes two classes of wives with respect to their appreciation of his support and service,
The first class is the wife who appreciates her husband’s support and service for her. Allah describes her attributes as follows:
فَٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ قَـٰنِتَـٰتٌ حَـٰفِظَـٰتٌ۬ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ (٣٤)
“The righteous women are devoutly obedient (to Allah), guarding the unseen (family secrets) that Allah has guarded.
The second class is the wife that is characterized by the following behavior:
وَٱلَّـٰتِى تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ (٣٤)
“As for those whom you fear (نُشُوزَهُنَّ)

Based on the previous discussion on the responsibility of the wives and that she is not responsible for any service around the house, the attribute of the word (نُشُوزَهُنَّ) cannot mean disobedience unless it related to her not allowing the husband to sleep with her.
In order to properly interpret the verse, you must understand two terms, the term (نشوز) and the only way to understand the meaning of the term is to see how it is consistently used in the Quran in other verses.
In addition to the verse we are discussing, the term (نشوز) is used in three additional verses. It is used in Surat Al-Baqara, in Surat al-Nisa, and in Surat Al-Mujadila
In Surat Al-Baqara, it is used in verse 259 referring to the resurrection of the donkey of the man whom Allah made him die for 100 years and Allah told him:
‌ۖوَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجۡعَلَكَ ءَايَةً۬ لِّلنَّاسِ‌ۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعِظَامِ ڪَيۡفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكۡسُوهَا لَحۡمً۬ا‌ۚ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ۥ قَالَ أَعۡلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ ڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬ (٢٥٩)
“And look at your donkey and We will make you a sign for mankind. Look at the bones, how We raise them (نُنشِزُهَا) and clothe them with flesh”. When it became clear to him, he said, “I know that Allah is Able to do all things.” (Al-Baqara 2:259)
Obviously, the meaning of term (نشوز) here has nothing to do with disobedience, but it refers to raising the bones up.
In Surat Al-Mujadila, verse 11 is often stated in the Jumma prayer when the Masjid gets full and the Khateeb wants the people to make room for others.
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمۡ تَفَسَّحُواْ فِى ٱلۡمَجَـٰلِسِ فَٱفۡسَحُواْ يَفۡسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ‌ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ ٱنشُزُواْ فَٱنشُزُواْ (١١المجَادلة)
“O you who believe! When you are told to make room in the assemblies, make room. Allah will make room for you. And when you are told to rise up, rise up..” (Al-Mujadila 58:11)
Here also the term (نشوز) means rise up. So, in the context of the relationship between the husband and wife, the term (نشوز) means the behavior of one party acting in a way that is interpreted by the other party as being arrogant, conceit and condescending. Because this is an interpretation of actions, the husband cannot be fully sure that the wife action is intended to put him down, but he may be afraid that this is her intention and thus the Quran uses the term (تَخَافُونَ) meaning that you are afraid of.

But this interpretation that certain actions by the wife are interpreted by the husband as signs of her condescending and putting him down, it can also happen when the wife interprets certain actions by the husband as signs of him condescending and putting her down.
Verse 128 in Surat Al-Nisa referring to this situation of the actions of the husband that are interpreted by the wife as signs of e arrogance and conceit that the wife hates and if not corrected can lead to divorce:
وَإِنِ ٱمرَأَةٌ خَافَتۡ مِنۢ بَعۡلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوۡ إِعۡرَاضً۬ا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡہِمَآ أَن يُصۡلِحَا بَيۡنَہُمَا صُلۡحً۬ا‌ۚ وَٱلصُّلۡحُ خَيۡرٌ۬ (١٢٨)
“And if a woman fears conceit (نُشُوزا) or desertion from her husband, there is no blame on them should they come to an accord; and making peace is better.” (Al-Nisa 4:128)
Note that in both verse 4:34 and verse 4:128, the term fear is used suggesting that the spouse interprets the behavior to be conceit and arrogance but there is some doubt because no one knows the exact intention of the person action. This is why in both cases the advice is required to validate the motive of the behavior.

We note that verse 128 and the end of verse 34 talks about improper treatment between the husband and the wife related to a sensitive subject which is the intimate relationship between them. When it comes to this type of relationship, the Quran uses a covert approach to discuss the issue in decent way. Therefore, we can take from verse 128 the indication of the problem by the word desertion (إِعۡرَاضً۬ا). In verse 34, this term was not used and only the term conceit (نُشُوزاً) was used. But as we discussed before, the key responsibility of the wife is to have an intimate relationship with her husband. If the wife refuses and the husband interprets her refusal as rejection of him because she looks down on him. What would you expect the husband should react in this case? If there is no divine guidance, the husband’s reaction will most likely be violence against his wife.

In fact, many of the currently reported domestic violence in the west are caused by the husband feeling resentment from his wife due to her lack of attention or respect and that he becomes his wife’s last priority. It is common that some men may act violently because they have difficulty controlling their emotions.

But, if the husband is following Allah’s commands, he must control his emotion and follow a 4-step process to resolve what he perceives as bad behavior of the wife.
The first step is for him to cool down and advice his wife about his dissatisfaction and verify the reason for her rejecting him. If this does not result in a change in her behavior, then he implements the 2nd step to affirm his dissatisfaction by showing her that he does not care about this relationship by refusing to sleep with her in the bed.
If this does not result in any change in the wife behavior, we come to the third step that some people object to it, ignoring all the past discussion and trying to change the meaning of this step and thus missing the restrictions imposed on it by the Prophet (PBUH). The three steps are presents as follows:
وَٱلَّـٰتِى تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِى ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌ۖ (٣٤)
“As for those whom you fear conceit (نُشُوزَهُنَّ), advise them, then refuse to share their beds, then (ٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌) hit them. (Al-Nisa 4:34)

The third step is the one that people have an issue with and some Muslims try to be apologist by interpreting it in a way that is not consistent with the verse.
All early scholars interpreted the word (ٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌) in this verse to mean strike or hit and they said:
وضَرْب النساء الوارِد في القرآن مَنْهِي عنه ابتداء ، ويُشْرَع بِقَدْر الحاجة ، وهو مضبوط بِضوابِطه ، بحيث لا يكون مُبَرِّحًا ، ولا يكسر ولا يجرح ، ولا يكون في الْوَجْه
Hitting women that is stated in the Quran is prohibited as first step and it is only used in necessity and it is governed by restrictions, that it cannot cause any physical harm and it cannot be on the face.

Ibn Abbas was asked about what is the hitting that cannot cause harm, he said:
قال عطاء : قلت لابن عباس : ما الضَّرْب غير الْمُبَرِّح ؟ قال : بالسِّواك ونحوه .
It is with the swiak (a short soft stick that is used as toothbrush) and something similar.
But if hitting, though minor, is allowed in the verse, why the scholars said that hitting a wife is generally prohibited and went thru the details to set restriction in case it happens. The reason is that the Prophet (PBUH) who understood the Quran more than any other human being prohibited hitting the wife by his example and by saying:
عَنْ إِيَاسِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي ذُبَابٍ قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : ( لَا تَضْرِبُوا إِمَاءَ اللَّهِ ) [سنن أبي داود سنن ابن ماجه صحيح ابن حبان السنن الكبرى للنسائي السنن الكبرى للبيهقي مسند الإمام الشافعي المعجم الكبير للطبراني]
“Do not hit the women (the female slaves of Allah)”.
The Prophet (PBUH) also said:
عن ‏ ‏أبي هريرة ‏ ‏قال ‏ قال رسول الله ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏أكمل المؤمنين إيمانا أحسنهم خلقا وخياركم خيارهم لنسائهم) مسند أحمد
“The most perfect believers are the best in conduct. And the best of you tare hose who are best to their wives.”

With the additions of the severe restriction on the third step, it is not allowed to be used for the cases when its use complicates step 4 which is counseling, and thus leads to divorce. Step 4 which is counseling is described as follows:
وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ شِقَاقَ بَيۡنِہِمَا فَٱبۡعَثُواْ حَكَمً۬ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهِۦ وَحَكَمً۬ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهَآ إِن يُرِيدَآ إِصۡلَـٰحً۬ا يُوَفِّقِ ٱللَّهُ بَيۡنَہُمَآ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيماً خَبِيراً (٣٥)
“If you fear a split between them (the spouses), appoint (two) arbitrators, one from his family and the other from her family; if they desire to set things right, Allah will cause their reconciliation. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing All-Aware”. (Al-Nisa 4:35)

Just to close the discussion on the 3rd step, some people try to interpret it to mean a continuation of the 2nd step, which is separation, but this obviously contradicts the Prophet’s hadith who prohibited it and was the basis for the restrictions imposed by all past scholars.
Those who want to suggest that the third step in response to the wife disrespecting and bullying her husband and refusing to have intimate relationship with him means “to separate, refer to the use of the root (ضرب) in the following verses in the Quran:
لِلْفُقَرَاء الَّذِينَ أُحصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللّهِ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْباً فِي الأَرْضِ } البقرة٢٧٣
“(Charity is) for the poor, who are confined in the way of Allah, and are unable to travel in the land (for trade or work).” (Al-Baqara 2:273)
قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورً۬ا فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَہُم بِسُورٍ۬ لَّهُ ۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُ ۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَـٰهِرُهُ ۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ ١٣ الحديد
“It will be said: “Go back to your rear and search for light!” Then a wall will be struck (placed) between them, with a gate therein. In it sinner side, there will be mercy, while the outside there will be torment.” (Al-Hadeed 57:13)

But, the root (ضرب) clearly means strike/hit in other verses such as:
فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنِ اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْبحرَ فَانفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَالطَّوْدِ الْعَظِيمِ} الشعراء ٦٣
“Then We revealed to Mua (Moses) (saying): “Strike the sea with your staff.” And it will be severed apart, and each part became like the huge mountain.” (Al-Shuara 26:63)
وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لَّا تَخَافُ دَرَكاً وَلَا تَخْشَى} طه ٧٧
“And indeed, We revealed to Musa (Moses): Travel by night with My slaves and strike for them (with your staff) a dry path in the sea, neither fearing to be overtaken, nor having any fear (of drowning).” Taha 20:77)

When you see a different use in the Quran for the same word, it is important to see how the companions understood the meaning of the word in this specific verse.
If you go back to verse 128 where the disrespect and the rejection is done by the husband, there is sonly one step before divorce, and this is counseling.

Based on this talk, I am proposing that the translation of verse 34 of Surat Al-NIsa that we studied today can be as follows.
ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٲمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٲلِهِمۡ‌ۚ فَٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ قَـٰنِتَـٰتٌ حَـٰفِظَـٰتٌ۬ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ وَٱلَّـٰتِى تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِى ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّ‌ۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَڪُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡہِنَّ سَبِيلاً‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّ۬ا ڪَبِيرً۬ا (٣٤)
“Men are standing in support and service of women by the virtue of Allah has favored some of them above others, and because of their spending from their money.
The righteous women are devoutly obedient (to Allah), guarding the unseen (family secrets) that Allah has guarded.
As for those whom you fear their conceit and refusal (of intimate relationship) advise them, then refuse to share their beds, then hit them (without causing any physical harm), but if they return to obedience, seek not a way against them. Surely, Allah is Exalted, Most Great (Al-Nisa 4:34)

DUA

title: The Most Important Woman in Islam
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

March is designated as the Women’s History Month, and it will be good opportunity for us to study the life of key women in Islam who were companions of the Prophet (PBUH). There are several books published under the title “Women around the Messenger” and they discuss the life and the contribution of many important women. But, out of this list everyone should at least study the life and contributions of the following four to Islam:
- Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
- Naseebah bint Ka’b
- Rufaydah al-Aslamiyah
- Al-Khasna

In this talk, I’ll inshallah focus on Khadijah, may Allah be please with her, but let me start by giving you very brief idea about the other three to encourage you to read more about them

Naseebah bint Ka’ab, known also as Umm Ammarah, was a great warrior and highly intelligent woman.  She travelled from Madina to Mecca and participated in the pledge of Aqaba.  She also participated in the pledge of Huaybiyah.  She participated in many battles including Uhud, Khybar, conquest of Mecca and the campaign of Hunayn.  The Prophet (PBUH) said regarding her role in the battle of Uhud:
قال رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم- “لمقام نسيبة بنت كعب اليوم خير من مقام فلان وفلان، ما التفت يميناً أو شمالاً إلا وأنا أراها تقاتل دوني
“The stand of Naseebeh on this day was superior than the stand of many men, wherever I turned left or right I always saw her fighting in my defense”.
During the leadership of Abu Bakr, she participated in the battle of Yamamah against Musaylamah the Liar and she was the one who killed Musaylamah after he was hit with a spear.  She was not only a courageous worrier, but she was also narrator of several hadith that have been used in Fiqh in several Islamic legal rules.

Rufaydah Al-Aslamiyah, was the physician and the surgeon whom the Prophet (PBUH) placed for her a tent as hospital in his masjid in Madina to treat the sick and the wounded and teach women.  She was expert in production and application of drugs and treatment of illness and wounds and fixing broken bones.  She never received wages or rewards for her work.  Rufaydah participated in all the battles and her tent was a field hospital that moved from one battlefield to another.  She trained several women to support her.  Her medical tent was always equipped with surgical and autopsy materials, drugs, gauze and bandage for dressing wounds and also special medicine.

Al-Khansa – (تماضر بنت عمرو ‎), Tumaḍir bint ʿAmr was a great poet  and the Prophet (PBUH) encouraged her to recite more poems in defense of Islam.  Keep in mind that at that time Poetry was the mass media, it would spread as wildfire throughout Arabia.
It is a consensus of the scholars of poetry that no woman neither before her nor after her ever attained the status of al-Khansa in poetry.  Al-Khansa’ strength and nobility reached its prominence on the day of the Battle of Qadisiyah which is the decisive battle between the Muslims and the Persian army.  This prominence revolved around both her super inspiration to her four sons before the battle; and her statement after the martyrdom of all of her sons.

In this talk, I plan to focus on one woman who played the most critical role in Islam.  In fact, she was the first ever person to believe in the prophethood of Mohammad (PBUH) even before he believed that he is a messenger of Allah.  This woman is Sayeda Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the mother of the believers.  Sayeda Khadija was a very successful business-women in her own right who controlled one of the most important caravan trade routes in the region.  She was well known for her intelligent, wisdom, and honor.  She was known with the nickname, Al-Tahera (الطاهرة), the Pure.
The Prophet (PBUH) married her when he was 25 years old, and she was a widow at the age of 40 years old and had 3 children from her previous marriages.  The difference in their ages of 15 years was never a factor in their complete love and devotion to each other.  She was related to the Prophet (PBUH) from both her father and mother side through the 5th and the 7th grand fathers.
She was the first and only wife of the Prophet (PBUH) for 25 years until her death.  Khadija and the Prophet (PBUH) had six children together: [Qasim dies at 3 yrs), Zainab (died at 30), Ruqayyah (died at 23), Umm Kulthum (died at 27), Fatimah (died at 27) and Abdullah (dies at 4 years).  The Prophet (PBUH) had only another child from his other marriages after Khadija’s death, he was Ibrahim who dies at the age of 2.
All of the Prophet’s three male children died while infant and his four-daughters died when they were 23 to 70 years old.  Fatimah (married to Ali ibn Abi Talib) Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum (married to Uthman) and Zainab (married to Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi’).
After the death of Sayeda Khadijah, the Prophet (PBUH) married other women, but he always expressed his most admiration and love for her, so much so that his youngest wife, Ayesha, stated that she was never as jealous of any other woman as she was of Khadijah.  When she asked the Prophet about his love for Khadijah his response was:
لا ما أبدلني الله خيرا منها قد آمنت بي إذ كفر الناس وصدقتني إذ كذبني الناس وواستني بمالها إذ حرمني الناس ورزقني الله ولدها إذ حرمني أولاد النساء
“She believed in me when the people disbelieved in me; she supported me with her money when the people denied me, and Allah blessed with children from her.”
Sayeda Khadija was a woman whose role went far beyond merely that of a dutiful wife and mother; she was an individual imbued with truly extraordinary characteristics.  Her intellect, wisdom, grace, love, and beyond all else, her faith, set her apart from the entire world.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:
روى البخاري بإسناده إلى علي رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: ((خير نسائها مريم بنت عمران، وخير نسائها خديجة بنت خويلد)) . وعند مسلم بلفظ: ((خير نسائها مريم وخير نسائها خديجة)).
“The best of women are Mary the daughter of Emran and Khadijah bint Khuwaild.” (Bukhari, Muslim)
In another hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) said:
روى البزار والطبراني من حديث عمار بن ياسر رفعه ((لقد فضلت خديجة على نساء أمتي كما فضلت مريم على نساء العالمين))
“Khadijah was preferred over the woman of my nation as Maryam was preferred over the women of the world.”
Khadija was the only women that Allah sent His greetings to her and gave her the good news of her place on paradise.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:
فقد روى الشيخان بإسنادهما إلى أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: ((أتى جبريل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، هذه خديجة قد أتت معها إناء فيه إدام أو طعام أو شراب فإذا هي أتتك فاقرأ عليها السلام من ربها ومني، وبشرها ببيت في الجنة من قصب لا صخب ولا نصب))
Jibril came to me and said O Messenger of Allah, here is Khadijah coming to you with a dish of stew, food and drink.  When she arrives, give her the greeting of peace from her Lord and from me.  Give her glad tidings of a palace in Paradise from pearl and rubies, wherein there will be no turbulence, nor fatigue.”

I am going to focus in this talk on the role of Sayeda Khadija around the time when the Prophet (PBUH) received the first revelation.
When the Prophet (PBUH) was 37 years old, he started the practice of spending the whole month of Ramadan in the cave of Hira (غار حراء), in Al-Nour mountain (جبل النور) that is located outside Mecca.  He would spend the whole month in seclusion praying to Allah to guide him and reflecting on the creations of the heaven and earth.  He was seeking to understand the secret of creation by reflecting an all that he can see from his cave.  This was his form of worship during this month.  Allah has sanctioned this approach of worship as He said in Surat Al-Emran:
إِنَّ فِى خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَـٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّہَارِ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّأُوْلِى ٱلۡأَلۡبَـٰبِ (١٩٠) ٱلَّذِينَ يَذۡكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَـٰمً۬ا وَقُعُودً۬ا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمۡ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِى خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقۡتَ هَـٰذَا بَـٰطِلاً۬ سُبۡحَـٰنَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ (سورة آل عمران)
Verily! In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, there are indeed signs for men of understanding (190). Those who are continuously remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying down, and think deeply about the creation of the heavens and the earth.” (Al-Imran 3:190-191)
Reflection on the creations such as the clouds, the mountains, the sun, the moon, the heaven and the earth is an important form of worship that is emphasized in many verses in the Quran.  This was what the Prophet (PBUH) doing during his time of seclusion in the month of Ramadan.  This form or worship is encouraged, particularly in Ramadan in the form of Iktkaf.
The Prophet ‘s custom was to take sufficient food and water with him to the cave and Sayeda Khadija used to send him additional provisions from time to time.  A day before the end of Ramadan, he would return to Mecca and go to the Kabba to perform the circumambulation around it and then return to his home.
On the year when the prophet (PBUH) was 40 years old, he went to the cave of Hira starting the month of Ramadan as his practice.  A day before his plan to return to Mecca (August 610 CE), he was surprised with a stranger entering the cave on him and without any form of greetings, said to him with a firm voice: Read.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:  I can’t read (ما أنا بقارئ).  The man squeezed the Prophet to the point that the Prophet thought that he is dying and then released him and repeated the same command: Read.  The Prophet answered the same and the man squeezed him again.  He repeated it for the third time.
On the fourth time when the man asked the Prophet (PBUH) to Read, the Prophet (PBUH) said:  what should I read.  The man said:
ٱقۡرَأۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ (١) خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِنۡ عَلَقٍ (٢) ٱقۡرَأۡ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡأَكۡرَمُ (٣) ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلۡقَلَمِ (٤) عَلَّمَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ (٥)
“Deduce (reason) guided with the name of your creator who created (1) He created man and kept him clinging (to Him for his continuous needs) (2) Deduce, and your Lord is the most generous, (3) Who teaches by the pen. (4) He taught man what he did not know.” (Al-Alaq 96:1-5)
The Prophet has been searching for three years for the creator and here he was being told about Him.  The man left but his words were engraved on the Prophet’s heart.  The Prophet (PBUH) became scared and left the cave, rushing down when he was at the middle of the mountain, he heard a loud voice coming from the sky saying: Mohammad, I am Jibril, and you are the messenger of Allah.  The Prophet looked up and saw this man covering the whole horizon and each direction the Prophet turned to avoid looking at him, he found him.  Then he vanished.  The Prophet started running down shaken and in great distress and each time he passed by a rock or a tree, he heard a voice saying: Asalamu Alykum O’ Messenger of Allah.  But when turned to see who is speaking, he found no one.  This made him more scared and thought he has surely gone mad.
At the same time, Sayeda Khadija got a feeling of great worry about the Prophet, particularly since she was expecting him to be at home after his return from the cave and circumambulation around the Kabba.  She sent her servants looking for him and they went all over Mecca and returned without finding him.  But after a short time, he arrived to the house and was shivering with all his body shaken and telling Khadija cover me, cover me (زملوني زملوني), I have been touched by Satan.
Sayeda Khadiga put the prophet’s head on her lap and covered him and when he was comforted a little and his fear subsided somewhat, she asked him what happened.  He told her and here you see the wisdom of the wife.  She could have told him this may be an imagination; you may have been tired and saw this in your sleep.  But instead, she addressed his main concern that he may have been touched by Satan and said:
أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا والله إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث وتحمل الكل وتكسب المعدوم وتقري الضيف وتعين على نوائب الحق
“Allah would never humiliate you, you are good to your relatives, you are true to your word, you help those who are in need, you support the weak, you feed the guest and you answer the call of those who are in distress.”
She kept comforting the Prophet (PBUH) until he went to sleep.  After he had gone to sleep, she left and went to see her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal.  Waraqah was an interesting person, he never accepted the worship of idols and was looking for a true religion to follow.  He Learnt form the Jews the expectation of a prophet to come but did not follow Judaism because he did not like the way they describe Allah.  He asked about the last known Prophet and he was told about Prophet Isa (Jesus) who lived 600 years ago.  He travelled to Syria to learn Christianity but after he was told about the trinity, he rejected it and decided to just worship Allah and hope that he could live to see the new Prophet who was foretold in previous revelations.
When Khadija arrived to Waraqa’s house and told him what happened to Mohammad: he comforted her and told: By Allah what Muhammad have seen is the same messenger that Allah sent to Prophet Musa (Moses).  Have the good news, Mohammad is the expected messenger of Allah that has been prophesied in the previous revelations.
She left and returned to her house and Mohammad was still sleeping.  When he woke up, she told him what Waraqa has said, and this comforted him more.  He gained his strength and left the house to perform the circumambulation around the Kabba.  In his way, he met Waraqa who was coming to see him.  The Prophet (PBUH) asked Waraqa about what he told Khadija and Waraqa told me:
هذا الناموس الذي نزله الله على موسى، يا ليتني فيها جَذَعا، ليتنى أكون حيًا إذ يخرجك قومك،
” Yes, the one who came to you is the heavenly messenger who came to Moses and you have been chosen as the Prophet of your people.  I wish I would be alive when your people force you out”.
The Prophet (PBUH) said: Will my people force me out? (أو مخرجيّ هم؟)
Waraqa said:  نعم، لم يأت رجل قط بمثل ما جئت به إلا عُودِىَ، وإن يدركنى يومك أنصرك نصرًا مؤزرًا
Yes, no one ever came with what you came with without his people declaring enmity against him, if I am alive, I’ll support you with all my might”.
As if Allah made Waraqa lives until this happens to comfort the Prophet (PBUH) because two days later, he died in 610 CE.
So, the Prophet (PBUH) has only his wife Khadija to believe in him that he is the messenger of Allah.  At this time, the Prophet (PBUH) did not even know what does being a messenger of Allah mean and what is expected form him.  The Prophet (PBUH) became anxious and distressed because Jibril did not come back to tell him what to do.  So, he used to go outside Mecca and walk wandering whether he will see the angel again.
While he was walking outside Mecca, a month after his first encounter with Jibril, he suddenly heard a voice from the sky, when he looked up, and surely enough, it was the same man who had visited him in the cave of Hira.  He was sitting on a chair between the earth and the sky.  The Prophet said regarding this encounter that I became very afraid and ran to my home shaking again and saying to Khadija cover me, cover me, and told her that he saw Gabriel again.  She covered him and placed his head on her lap to comfort him.  Suddenly he said to Khadija I see him now.  She said look at the other side, do you see him, he said yes.  Then she removed the cover from her head and said do you still see him now, he said no.  She said, he is an angel and not Satan because Satan would not have vanished when I exposed myself.  She covered herself and said do you see him now and he said yes.  Here, you also see the wisdom of Sayeda Khadija, she was setting a test even for Jibril to verify his nature.  Then Jibril revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) the following revelations:
يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّل قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا
‘O you enveloped (in garments)! Stand (to prayer) by night, but not all night, half of it, or a little less, Or a little more; and recite the Quran in slow, measured rhythmic tones.  Soon shall We send down to you a weighty Message. (Al-Muzammil 73:1-5)
With only few revelations, the Prophet spent almost all-night reflecting and reciting the few verses he received and expecting that other revelation will come.  But for another 5 months nothing came, and the prophet (PBUH) began again getting anxious and distressed but here also Sayeda Khadija was his comfort and supporter.  We are now entering in Rabi Al-Awal and the Prophet is now 41 years old.  Then Jibril came again to the Prophet (PBUH), with the command to invite others.
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمُدَّثِّرُ (١) قُمۡ فَأَنذِرۡ (٢) وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرۡ (٣) وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرۡ (٤) وَٱلرُّجۡزَ فَٱهۡجُرۡ (٥) وَلَا تَمۡنُن تَسۡتَكۡثِرُ (٦) وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصۡبِرۡ (٧)
“O you who are enveloped in garments! (1) Arise and warn! (2) Magnify your Lord (3) And purify your garments! (4) And keep away from impurities (the idols)! (5) And do not do a favor seeking more in return. (6) And be patient for the sake of your Lord.” (Al-Muddathir 74:1-7)
Following this, the Prophet started receiving revelation regarding to what he should invite people.  The Prophet (PBUH) spent 3 years inviting to Islam in secret with Khadija fully supporting him financially and spiritually.  Later when the Prophet (PBUH) started delivering the message openly, he faced major difficulties from the elites of Quryash who placed a sanction on the Prophet and his family causing a stoppage of Khadija’s business, but she continued steadfast in her support for the Prophet (PBUH).  During the boycott, Khadijah depleted her entire large fortune supporting the followers of Islam.  Her wealth was gone, and her health strained.  However, her spirits remained high, and her devotion never weakened.  Finally, the brave, honorable, and faithful Khadijah became ill and died on the year 619 CE at the age of 65 years leaving a huge gap in the life of the Prophet (PBUH).
The Prophet (PBUH) received the first revelation in Ramadan (the 9th month in the lunar calendar) but six months earlier when he reached the age of 40 in Rabi Al-Awal (the 3rd month in the lunar calendar), he started seeing visions at night and noted that all the things that he saw in his vision at night are materialized the next day.  This would have been preparation form him regarding the ability to receive information from the unseen world.
Through the Prophet’s life, he (PBUH) received revelation thru 7 and possibly eight different forms and these are:
The first form is clear vision, a dream, like what the Prophet (PBUH) used to see before him seeing Jibril form the first time to receive his first revelation.  It is this form with which Prophet Ibrahim received the revelation to slaughter his son.  A vison of a Prophet is a form or revelation that is acted upon.  But the vison of any other human being is not something to act upon, it is only a blessing from Allah to expose some of the unseen world to His righteous servants.
The second form is inspiration which is information that the holy angel Jibril places directly in the heart of the Prophet (PBUH) without coming to him.  Many of the ahadith of the Prophet were revealed this way.  In one hadith the Prophet (PBUH) said:
قال النبى صلّى الله عليه وسلم: «إن روح القدس نفث فى روعى أنه لن تموت نفس حتى تستكمل رزقها، وأجملوا فى الطلب، ولا يحملنكم استبطاء الرزق على أن تطلبوه بمعصية الله، فإن ما عند الله لا ينال إلا بطاعته». ] أخرجه أبو نعيم فى الحلية من حديث أبى أمامة، وأورده الهيتمى فى مجمع الزوائد، ونسبه للطبرانى فى الكبير[
Ruh Al-Qudus (the holy Spirit) breathed in my heart that no soul shall die until it finishes its set provisions and its term limit.  Therefore, have Taqwa of Allah and seek your sustenance in the best way and don’t let the delay in your provision make you try to get it through unlawful means.”
The third form of revelation is thru Jibril coming in a form of a man who is only seen by the Prophet but no one else who may be present will see him.
The fourth form of revelation is thru Jibril coming in a form of a man who is seen by the Prophet and everyone else in his company.  This was the case when he came and asked the Prophet (PBUH) about Islam, Eman, Ihsan, the hour and the signs for the hour.
The fifth form is when Jibril comes in his actual image as the case when the Prophet (PBUH) saw him in the sky during the first revelation at the cave of Hira and during the ascension (Miraj).
The sixth form is when Jibril is infused in the Prophet’s body and this was the hardest on the Prophet because the Prophet would hear ringing of a bell and would feel very weight on him and he would sweat heavily.  On one occasion, the Prophet received revelation this way while he was riding a camel and the camel could not stand and sat down.
The seventh form is a direct revelation from Allah but with a veil that the Prophet does not see Allah as the revelation the Prophet (PBUH) received during the trip of ascension, the Mia’rag.  The Prophet (PBUH) received the commands of the five prayers and the last two verses form Surat Al-Baqara directly from Allah.  This was also the form of revelation to Prophet Musa.  Allah says:
وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحۡيًا أَوۡ مِن وَرَآىِٕ حِجَابٍ أَوۡ يُرۡسِلَ رَسُولاً۬ فَيُوحِىَ بِإِذۡنِهِۦ مَا يَشَآءُ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ عَلِىٌّ حَكِيمٌ۬ (٥١)
“It is not possible for a human being that Allah should speak to him except by the way of revelation, or from behind a veil, or (that) He sends a Messenger to reveal what He wills with His permission.  Surely, He is Most High, Most Wise.” (Al-Shura 42:51)
The eight form is revelation from Allah directly without any barrier.  The account is not clear whether the Prophet (PBUH) received the revelation form Allah during ascension in this form or through a veil.
But we have the good news that those who will enter paradise will secure the most blessed joy they will ever witness, and this is seeing Allah directly without any veil as Allah said:
وُجُوهٌ۬ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ نَّاضِرَةٌ (٢٢) إِلَىٰ رَبِّہَا نَاظِرَةٌ۬ (٢٣)
“Some faces that Day shall be radiant (22) Looking at their Lord.” (Al-Qiyama 75:22-23)
But the disbelievers will never see Allah:
كَلَّآ إِنَّہُمۡ عَن رَّبِّہِمۡ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ لَّمَحۡجُوبُونَ (١٥) ثُمَّ إِنَّہُمۡ لَصَالُواْ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ (١٦)
“Nay! Surely, they will be veiled from seeing their Lord on that Day. (15) Then, they will indeed burn in Hell” (Al-Mutafffifn 83:15-16)
We pray to Allah to make us of those who will see Him without any veil or barrier in the Ferdaus Al-Ala.
DUA

title: Comprehensive Peace Requires Complete Submission
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

Allah (سبحانه و تعالى) said:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱدۡخُلُواْ فِى ٱلسِّلۡمِ ڪَآفَّةً۬ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٲتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ‌ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوٌّ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬ (٢٠٨) فَإِن زَلَلۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡكُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتُ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٢٠٩)

“O’ you who believe! Enter totally “Kafah” in “Al-Silm” and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Surely, he is an open enemy for you. (208) And if you slip “Zallaltum” after the clear proofs have come to you, then you must know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.” (Al-Baqara 2:208-209)

There are three key words in these two verses:

The first word is “al-Silm (ٱلسِّلۡمِ) and this refers to three interlinking terms: Islam (اسلام), submission (تسليم) and peace (سلام). In other term, this term means that religion of Islam is demands submission to Allah to achieve peace.

The second word is “Kafah” (ڪَآفَّةً۬) that means totally, completely, and whole-heartedly. So, the Command to the believers is to enter in Islam totally thru complete submission to ensure that they live in total peace.

The third word is “zallaltum (زَلَلۡتُم) that means slip and slide back and this suggests minor variation from the straight position. This emphasizes the deviation does not need to be large, any minor deviation in submission will negate that full peace.

So, the law of Allah is clear, if the believers want to achieve full peace and this involves peace with Allah, peace with themselves and peace with others, they must have complete submission to Allah. Any slight deviations from the complete submission will cause them to forfeit this comprehensive peace. This is the divine law; complete submission is prerequisite for full peace and Allah’s laws will not change for anyone.

In many verses, Allah makes it clear that His rules do not change; Allah says:

سُنَّةَ مَنْ قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنَا وَلا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلا) الإسراء)

“(This was Our) sunnah that we sent with the Messengers who came before you: you will not find any changes in our rules”. (Al-Israa 17:77)

سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلا) الفتح)

“These have been the rules of Allah, already demonstrated in the past: no change you will find in the rules of Allah”. (Al-Fath 48:23)

This law that any slight deviations from the complete submission to Allah will cause the forfeit of the complete peace was applied even when the Prophet (PBUH) was among the companions. We, all know of the violation of few in the battle of Uhud that resulted in the major loss of Muslims even though the Prophet (PBUH) was among them.

Partial obedience to Allah by cherry picking certain commands to obey and ignoring others is not full obedience and Allah gave serious warning to those who engage in this behavior as He said:

أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَى أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ

“Do you believe in part of the scripture and disbelieve in others? The reward for those who do so is shame in this life and the most grievous doom on the hereafter. For Allah is aware of what you do.” (Al-Baqara 2:85)

By accepting Islam, you will not achieve the total peace that Allah promised in this life and the hereafter unless you embrace and follow all the divine guidance. By accepting Islam, you no longer have the freedom to use your intellect, education, passion, or customs to debate issues on which Allah and his Prophet have already decided; Allah said:

وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلَا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا مُبِينًا

“It is not allowed for any believing man or believing woman to have a choice on any matter on which Allah and His Messenger have decided. Anyone who disobeys Allah, and His Messenger has indeed seriously gone astray (Al-Ahzab 33:36).

You will never achieve total peace unless you are completely encircled in Islam. Selective application of Islam can only lead to confusion and chaos. Even in manmade systems, if the whole society does not enter in the system in its totality, confusion and conflicts will result.

Complete submission to Allah leads to comprehensive peace with your three relationships: relationship with Allah, relationship with the self and relationship with others, and others includes people and objects. I discussed these three relationships in my talk on “The Self’ that I gave on February 28th.

Let us talk about internal peace with oneself. There is no way you can live in peace with others unless you, first, live in peace with yourself. Internal peace requires that the person’s actions and feelings be consistent with his ideas of certain truth. The person’s ideas of certain truth will lead to certain feelings and these feelings will drive certain actions. If the actions are consistent with the idea, he will internally feel happy and content. But if his actions are inconsistent with his idea, he will internally feel disturbed and distressed. A Muslim who knows that prayers are obligatory will be happy when he performs all prayers on time, but if he misses a prayer, he will have the feeling of guilt and discomfort.

While internal peace of a person occurs through the consistency of the action with the idea in his brain, this occurs whether this idea is proper or false. As example, a person who has the idea in his mind that smoking is good for him and engages in smoking feels at peace while a person whose mind tells him that smoking is bad for him and smokes, he is in a state of stress each time he smokes.

Therefore, it is important to ensure that the ideas we have in our brains are good. How do you judge whether the idea in your mind is good or bad? The idea is good if it is based on divine revelation and/or rational thinking, otherwise the idea is bad. The whole purpose of Islam is to correct the ideas people have regarding their relationships with Allah, with themselves and with others. These corrections resulted in moving the people from the age of ignorance “Jahiliah (جاهلية)” to the age of enlightenment.

The age of enlightenment refers to the age when the group practices are based on revelation and/or rational thinking. On the other hand, the age of Jahiliah (جاهلية), the age of ignorance and darkness refers to the age when the group practices are based on neither revelation nor rational thinking. What is a rational thinking? It is the thinking that leads to ideas that are beneficial and just to all.

The command to enter in total peace is directed to the believers who already have accepted the truthfulness of the commands of Allah, when they violate any of the commands, they will feel internal distress and lack of peace because of the conflict between what they know and what they do.

The Quran teaches us not to follow Satan’s example when he went to war within himself. Despite Satan’s total convection in the absolute power and authority of Allah, his actions reflected the opposite of this belief by refusing to obey Allah’s command to prostrate to Adam. Allah warned Muslims of this internal war, He said:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (٢) ڪَبُرَ مَقۡتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (٣)

“O’ you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? It is most hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do.” (Al-Saff 61:2-3)

The contradiction between the belief and the deed creates an internal conflict within the person and results in transforming man from the best of molds, to the lowest of the low. Allah said:

لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ فِىٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٍ۬ (٤) ثُمَّ رَدَدۡنَـٰهُ أَسۡفَلَ سَـٰفِلِينَ (٥) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ

“We have indeed created man in the best of stature (mold) (4) Then reduced him to the lowest of the low (5) except for those who believe and perform honorable deeds” (Al-Tin 95:4-6).

Current technology takes advantage of this internal conflict to identify the truth using the lie detector that measures the disturbance in man’s internal system when he tries to suppress the truth. Allah created us and programmed us to know that lying is bad and honesty is good. Therefore, it requires a lot of effort and energy for a person to lie. During interrogation, the approach used is to weaken the person physically, by lack of sleep and lack of food, to the point that he can no longer suppress the truth within himself.

Allah’s command is to enter in Islam in its totality to achieve all the promises that Allah granted to the believers of comprehensive peace and honor in this life and the hereafter. The importance of entering in Islam in totality can be illustrated by many stories from the seerah. I will mention one account related to the meeting between the Prophet (PBUH) and the leaders of the tribe Banu Shiban (شيبان). This tribe resided in Iraq between the Arabs and the Persian empire.

When Allah commanded the Prophet (PBUH) to spread the message of Islam among the Arab tribes, the Prophet used to look for opportunities to meet the representatives of the different tribes who came to Mecca to perform the Hajj. The Prophet (PBUH) always took Abu Bakr with him because Abu Bakr was well knowledgeable with the lineage of the different tribes and the key leaders in each tribe. (This teaches us that before you meet anyone to discuss an important matter, learn about his background).

At one time, the Prophet (PBUH) and Abu Bakr encountered a gathering of 4; and Abu Bakr asked them who are you. They introduced themselves as Mafrouq ibn Amr (مَفْرُوقُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو), Hani ibn Qabysah (هَانِئُ بْنُ قَبِيصَةَ), Al-Muthana ibn Harithah (الْمُثَنَّى بْنُ حَارِثَةَ) and Al-Noman ibn Shareik (النُّعْمَانُ بْنُ شَرِيكٍ) from Banu Shyban in Tha’labah (بَنِي شَيْبَانَ بْنِ ثَعْلَبَةَ). Abu Bakr turned to the Prophet (PBUH) and said: “There is no more honorable people than those in their tribe.”

The account of this meeting was narrated by Ali ibn Abi Taleb (على بن أبى طالب) who joined the Prophet and Abu Bakr in this meeting and it is reported by Ibn Hiban, Al-Biyhaqi and Ibn Asaker (حبان و البيهقي وابن عساكر).

Mafrouq (مَفْرُوقُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو) said: (لَعَلَّكَ أَخُو قُرَيْشٍ) would you happen to be the brother of Quraysh?

Abu Bakr said: (إِنْ كَانَ بَلَغَكُمْ أَنَّهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَهَا هُوَ هَذَا) If it has reached you that he is the messenger of Allah, yes, he is.

Mafrouq (مَفْرُوقٌ) said:
فَقَالَ مَفْرُوقٌ: قَدْ بَلَغَنَا أَنَّهُ يَذْكُرُ ذَلِكَ. ثمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ: إلَامَ تَدْعُو يَا أَخَا قُرَيْشٍ؟

“We heard that he makes such claim. Then he turned to the Prophet (PBUH) and said: to what you are inviting people, the brother of Quraysh.”

The Prophet (PBUH) sat down and sat next to him Abu Bakr and Ali and the Prophet (PBUH) said:
أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَنِّي رَسُولُ اللهِ، وَأَنْ تُؤْوُونِي، وَتَنْصُرُونِي حَتَّى أُؤَدِّيَ عَنِ اللهِ الَّذِي أَمَرَنِي بِهِ، فَإِنَّ قُرَيْشًا قَدْ تَظَاهَرَتْ عَلَى أَمْرِ اللهِ وَكَذَّبَتْ رَسُولَهُ، وَاسْتَغْنَتْ بِالْبَاطِلِ عَنِ الْحَقِّ، وَاللهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ.

“I invite you to the witness that there is god but Allah who has no partners and I am the messenger of Allah and I invite you to shelter me, protect me and support me to deliver the message of Allah as He commanded me because Quraysh has stood against Allah’s commands and has rejected me and preferred falsehood over the truth, and Allah is self-sufficient, and He is the worthy of all Praise”.

Mafrouq (مَفْرُوقٌ) said: (وَإِلَامَ تَدْعُو -أيضًا- يَا أَخَا قُرَيْشٍ؟) “To what else do you invite, the brother of Quraysh?”

The Prophet (PBUH) (فَتَلَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم) recited three verses (151-153) from Surat Al-A’am:

قُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ أَتۡلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّڪُمۡ عَلَيۡڪُمۡ‌ۖ أَلَّا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا‌ۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٲلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَـٰنً۬ا‌ۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوْلَـٰدَكُم مِّنۡ إِمۡلَـٰقٍ۬‌ۖ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكُمۡ وَإِيَّاهُمۡ‌ۖ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلۡفَوَٲحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ‌ۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۚ ذَٲلِڪُمۡ وَصَّٮٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ (١٥١) وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلۡيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحۡسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ‌ۖ وَأَوْفُواْ ٱلۡڪَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ‌ۖ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا‌ۖ وَإِذَا قُلۡتُمۡ فَٱعۡدِلُواْ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰ‌ۖ وَبِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْفُواْ‌ۚ ذَٲلِڪُمۡ وَصَّٮٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ (١٥٢) وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَٲطِى مُسۡتَقِيمً۬ا فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ‌ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلسُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِڪُمۡ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ‌ۚ ذَٲلِڪُمۡ وَصَّٮٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ (١٥٣)

Say: “Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited you from:
• Do not join anything in worship with Him, and
• Be good and dutiful to your parents, and
• Do not kill your children because of poverty – We provide sustenance for you and for them, and
• Do not come near to obscene acts whether committed openly or secretly, and
• Do not kill the life that Allah made sacred, except for justice.
This He has commanded you that you may understand, and
• Do not come near to the orphan’s property, except to improve it, until he (or she) attains the age of maturity, and
• Give full measure and full weight with justice. We do not burden any person except by what he can bear, and
• Whenever you give testimony say the truth even if a near relative is concerned, and
• Fulfill the Covenant of Allah.
This He commands you, that you may remember. “And verily, this is my Straight Path, so follow it, and
• Do not follow (other) paths, for they will separate you away from His Path.
This He has ordained for you that you may gain Taqwa.” (Al-An’am 6: 151-153)

Mafrouq (مَفْرُوقٌ) said:
فَقَالَ لَهُ مَفْرُوقٌ: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا هَذَا مِنْ كَلَامِ أَهْلِ الأَرْضِ، وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ كَلَامِهِمْ لَعَرَفْنَاهُ. وَإِلَامَ تَدْعُو -أَيْضًا- يَا أَخَا قُرَيْشٍ؟

By Allah, these words are not the words of the people of the earth, and if they were of their words, we could have surely recognized it. What else do you call for the brother of Quraysh?

The Prophet (PBUH) recited verse 90 from Surat Al-Nahl:
فَتَلَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَٱلۡإِحۡسَـٰنِ وَإِيتَآءِ ذِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱلۡبَغۡىِۚ يَعِظُكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ (٩٠) [النحل

Indeed, Allah commands justice and doing good to others, and supporting the kins, and He forbids all obscenity and shameful deeds and aggression, He admonishes you, that you may take heed. (Al-Nahl 16:90)

Mafrouq (مَفْرُوقٌ) said:
فَقَالَ لَهُ مَفْرُوقٌ: دَعَوْتَ وَاللهِ يَا قُرَشِيُّ إِلَى مَكَارِمِ الأَخْلَاقِ، وَمَحَاسِنِ الأَعْمَالِ، وَلَقَدْ أَفِكَ قَوْمٌ كَذَّبُوكَ، وَظَاهَرُوا عَلَيْكَ. وَكَانَ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَشْرَكَهُ فِي الْكَلَامِ هَانِئُ بْنُ قَبِيصَةَ- فَقَالَ: وَهَذَا هَانِئُ بْنُ قَبِيصَةَ شَيْخُنَا وَصَاحِبُ دِينِنَا

“By Allah, you, the man from Quraysh, has indeed called to the best morals and the most virtues deeds and your people of Quraysh have certainly lied about you. But you need to hear from our chief and our religious scholar Hani ibn Qabisa (هَانِئُ بْنُ قَبِيصَةَ).”

Hani (هَانِئُ بْنُ قَبِيصَةَ) said:
فَقَالَ لَهُ هَانِئٌ: قَدْ سَمِعْتُ مَقَالَتَكَ يَا أَخَا قُرَيْشٍ، وَصَدَّقْتُ قَوْلَكَ، وَإِنِّي أَرَى أَنْ تَرْكَنَا دِينَنَا وَاتِّبَاعَنَا إِيَّاكَ عَلَى دِينِكَ لِمَجْلِسٍ جَلَسْتَهُ إِلَيْنَا لَيْسَ لَهُ أَوَّلٌ وَلَا آخِرٌ، لَمْ نَتَفَكَّرْ فِي أَمْرِكَ وَنَنْظُرْ فِي عَاقِبَةِ مَا تَدْعُو إِلَيْهِ- زَلَّةٌ فِي الرَّأْيِ، وَطَيْشَةٌ فِي الْعَقْلِ، وَقِلَّةُ نَظَرٍ فِي الْعَاقِبَةِ، وَإِنَّمَا تَكُونُ الزَّلَّةُ مَعَ الْعَجَلَةِ، وَإِنَّ مِنْ وَرَائِنَا قَوْمًا نَكْرَهُ أَنْ نَعْقِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَقْدًا، وَلَكِنْ تَرْجِعُ وَنَرْجِعُ وَتَنْظُرُ وَنَنْظُرُ- وَكَأَنَّهُ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَشْرَكَهُ فِي الْكَلَامِ الْمُثَنَّى بْنُ حَارِثَةَ- فَقَالَ: وَهَذَا الْمُثَنَّى شَيْخُنَا وَصَاحِبُ حَرْبِنَا

“I have heard what you’ve said the brother of Quraysh, and I believed in what you said, but I see that if we leave our religion and follow you embracing your religion after one meeting without giving additional thought to this matter, this will be a hasty and unwise decision by us because we would not have considered the future consequences and there is always harm in hasty decisions. Also, we have people whom we hate to make decision without taking their advice. But, I want to hear the opinion of our military chief, Al-Mouthana ibn Haritha (الْمُثَنَّى بْنُ حَارِثَةَ).”

Al-Mouthana (الْمُثَنَّى) said:
فَقَالَ الْمُثَنَّى: قَدْ سَمِعْتُ مَقَالَتَكَ، وَاسْتَحْسَنْتُ قَوْلَكَ يَا أَخَا قُرَيْشٍ، وَأَعْجَبَنِي مَا تَكَلَّمْتَ بِهِ، وَالْجَوَابُ هُوَ جَوَابُ هَانِئِ بْنِ قَبِيصَةَ، وَتَرْكُنَا دِينَنَا وَاتِّبَاعَنَا إِيَّاكَ لِمَجْلِسٍ جَلَسْتَهُ إِلَيْنَا، وَإِنَّا إِنَّمَا نَزَلْنَا بَيْنَ صِيرَيْنِ: أَحَدُهُمَا الْيَمَامَةُ، وَالْآخَرُ السَّمَامَةُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وَمَا هَذَانِ الصِّيرَانِ؟» فَقَالَ لَهُ: أَمَّا أَحَدُهُمَا فَطُفُوفُ الْبَرِّ وَأَرْضُ الْعَرَبِ، وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ فَأَرْضُ فَارِسٍ وَأَنْهَارُ كِسْرَى، وَإِنَّمَا نَزَلْنَا عَلَى عَهْدٍ أَخَذَهُ عَلَيْنَا كِسْرَى أَنْ لَا نُحْدِثَ حَدَثًا وَلَا نُؤْوِيَ مُحْدِثًا، وَلَعَلَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ الَّذِي تَدْعُونَا إِلَيْهِ مِمَّا تَكْرَهُهُ الْمُلُوكُ، فَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِمَّا يَلِي بِلَادَ الْعَرَبِ فَذَنْبُ صَاحِبِهِ مَغْفُورٌ، وَعُذْرُهُ غَيْرُ مَقْبُولٍ، وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِمَّا يَلِي بِلَادَ فَارِسَ فَذَنْبُ صَاحِبِهِ غَيْرُ مَغْفُورٍ، وَعُذْرُهُ غَيْرُ مَقْبُولٍ، فَإِنْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ نَنْصُرَكَ وَنَمْنَعَكَ مِمَّا يَلِي الْعَرَبَ فَعَلْنَا

” The brother of Quraysh, I have heard what you said and I liked your talk and admired your speech but the answer is what Hani Ibn Qabisa (هَانِئُ بْنُ قَبِيصَةَ) gave you, if we leave our religion and follow you after our first meeting, we would have placed ourselves between two dangers. We are located between the land of the Arabs and land of Persia. And we have a treaty with Kisra (king of Persia) that we neither create innovation nor we harbor someone who brings new matters. And the matter that you are bringing is something that kings hate. So, if you agree, we will support you and protect form the Arabs but regarding the Persians, you will be on your own”.

The Prophet (PBUH) said:
فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مَا أَسَأْتُمُ الرَّدَّ إِذْ أَفْصَحْتُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ، إِنَّهُ لَا يَقُومُ بِدِينِ اللهِ إِلَّا مَنْ حَاطَهُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ جَوَانِبِهِ».

“You have not said anything improper, you only spoke the truth, but no one will prevail with this religion of Allah unless he fulfills its obligations from all sides.”

Then the Prophet (PBUH) said:
ثمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ لَمْ تَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا يَسِيرًا حَتَّى يَمْنَحَكُمُ اللهُ بِلَادَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ، وَيُفْرِشَكُمْ بَنَاتِهِمْ، أَتُسَبِّحُونَ اللهَ وَتُقَدِّسُونَهُ؟

“You will see that within only short time, Allah will grant you their land and their money and you will marry their women? But you have to give Glory to Allah and declare his purification”.

Nomam ibn Shurayk (النُّعْمَانُ بْنُ شَرِيكٍ) said: (اللَّهُمَّ وَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَكَ يَا أَخَا قُرَيْشٍ) May Allah grant you this, the brother of Quyrash

The Prophet (PBUH) recited two verses from Surat Al-Ahzab:
فَتَلَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: {إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا وَمُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا * وَدَاعِيًا إِلَى اللَّهِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا} [الأحزاب]

“O prophet, We sent you as a witness, and as a bearer of good news and a Warner, (45) And as caller to Allah with His permission, and as an illuminating lamp.” (Al-Ahzab 33:45-46)

Then, the Prophet (PBUH) stood holding Abu-Bakr’s hand and left.

There are at least two lessons that we can learn from his account.

The First lesson is that the Prophet (PBUH) introduced the religion of Islam by quoting the Quran. So, if anyone ask you about Islam, do not use your own words, use Allah’s words by quoting the relevant verses from Quran that are suitable for the situation.

The second lesson is that there are no compromises in Islam, you must enter in it with 100% commitment. Partial obedience will neither achieve victory nor even internal personal peace.

It must be clear that for us to fulfill our noble responsibility on this earth as Allah’s trustee, we must achieve comprehensive peace, and this includes achieving internal peace thru self-unity by ensuring the harmony between our revelation’s based values and our actions. Internal conflict starts when people attempt to rationalize and legitimize their inappropriate actions that are inconsistent with their basic values.

When you succeed in achieving this self-unity, you will experience the highest form of peace and harmony within yourself. However, this cannot be achieved unless the individual defines his values and identifies the actions that are consistent with these values. In order to achieve self-unity, you may want to consider implementing the following four steps:

1. Prepare a list of your values. Examples may include values such as: faith, family, leadership, honesty, intellect, dignity, and humility.
2. Prioritize your values and select the three highest priority values. Ensure that they are consistent with the divine truth. Let your conscience, not how you perform, determine your list.
3. Write a paragraph stating the actions you need to take to achieve each value. As example:
• Be humble: Free myself from boasting, arrogance, and egotism, and be willing to listen and learn from others. Minimize the value of your personal accomplishments and promote the value of others.
• Have dignity: Develop and maintain a strong sense of personal worth as I relate to myself and others.
• Be Honest: Free myself from any form of hypocrisy. Ensure that all my business dealings are fair, completely aboveboard, impeccable.
1. Bring your performance in line with your values: Set a period of solitude to audit your actions against your values and set goals to adjust your actions. Ensuring complete harmony between your values and your action is not easy, but it is rewarding and fulfilling. The life of the prophet’s companions gives us ample examples of those whose divinely guided values transformed them to build the best civilization known to man in extremely short time.

Let me conclude with what I started with which is that comprehensive peace can only be achieved if the believers enter Islam in its totality and any minor deviation will cause wars and chaos. Does this mean that the cause of all the evil in the world is the Muslims? I will leave you with this verse from Surat Al-Anfal to answer the question:

وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بَعۡضُہُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ بَعۡضٍ‌ۚ إِلَّا تَفۡعَلُوهُ تَكُن فِتۡنَةٌ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَفَسَادٌ۬ كَبِيرٌ (٧٣)

And those who disbelieve are allies of one another, if you (Muslims) do not do so [i.e., become allies], there will be Fitnah (disorder, wars, confusion, chaos) in the land, and a great corruption. (Al-Anfal 8:73)

Are Muslims allies of each other? Since they are not, they are the cause of all the chaos and corruption on the earth.

We pray to Allah to guide us to ensures that our actions are always consistent with our beliefs.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom to implement the rules of Islam in totality with no compromise or deviation.

DUA
Beware, not all believers are 100% believers:

وَمَا يُؤۡمِنُ أَڪۡثَرُهُم بِٱللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُم مُّشۡرِكُونَ (١٠٦)

“And most of them do not believe Allah without associating partners with Him.” (Yusuf 12: 106)
