content:
The Sure Road to Paradise in Two Words (Belief and Istiqamah)

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

One thing that should be very clear is that Islam is very simple and easy religion but for some reason we complicate it and then complain. The simplicity of Islam is obvious when we look at the responses given by the Prophet (PBUH) in response to questions by the companions. You will note that the Prophet (PBUH) responses are very brief, few words and in general they are verse or part of verse form the Quran.

As example, a Bedouin (لأعرابي) came to the Prophet (PBUH) and told him: (عظِني وأوْجِز) “Advise me but be brief”. The Prophet (PBUH) told him:

مَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ * وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرّاً يَرَه

Whosoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whosoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.

The Bedouin said: (كُفيت) “That is enough.”

The Prophet (PBUH) said: (فقُهَ الرجل) “The man has clear understanding”.

The Prophet’s answer was two verses from surat Al-Zalzala  (99:7-8):

﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ * وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرّاً يَرَهُ﴾

So, we don’t need more information, we need sincerity and action upon what we already know; two short verses are all that Bedouin needed to act according to Allah’s commands that Allah instilled in all of us. Is there anyone who really does not know what is good and what is evil; Allah created us with the compass to know it on our own.

Another example, the companion Sufyan Al-Thaqafy (سفيان بن عبد الله الثقفي) came to the Prophet (PBUH) and said:

جاءه سفيان بن عبد الله الثقفي ـ رضي الله عنه ـ يقول له: قل لي في الإسلام قولاً لا أسأل عنه أحداً غيرك ، فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( قل: آمنتُ بالله ثم استقم )( رواه مسلم)

“O Messenger of Allah. tell me a statement about Islam that is sufficient that I will not need to ask anyone else after you.

The Prophet (PBUH) said: Say, (آمنتُ بالله ثم استقم) I believe in Allah and then become upright (Stand firm). [Muslim]

The Prophet (PBUH) summarized Islam in two words belief and Istiqamah which can be translated as standing upright or standing firm. This hadith is rephrasing the two conditions that Allah affirmed as the guarantee for paradise. So, our winning ticket to paradise is these two words as Allah says in Surat Fussilat:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَقَـٰمُواْ تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ وَأَبۡشِرُواْ بِٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمۡ تُوعَدُونَ (٣٠) نَحۡنُ أَوۡلِيَآؤُڪُمۡ فِى ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَفِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ‌ۖ وَلَڪُمۡ فِيهَا مَا تَشۡتَہِىٓ أَنفُسُڪُمۡ وَلَڪُمۡ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ (٣١) نُزُلً۬ا مِّنۡ غَفُورٍ۬ رَّحِيمٍ۬ (٣٢) [فصلت]

“Surely, those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and then became upright (afterward stood firm) the angels descend on them, saying: “Do not fear, and do not grieve; and be happy with the good news of the Paradise that you had been promised.

We are your guardians in the worldly life, and in the Hereafter. And for you here is whatever your souls desire, and for you here is whatever you call for (31) A gift of welcome from the Most-forgiving, the Very-Merciful”. (Fussilat 41:30-32)

Belief in Allah and Istiqamah are not only a guarantee for paradise but they are also a guarantee for happiness in this life. The same promise for those who meet these two conditions is given in Surat Al-Ahqaf:

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَامُوا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ * أُوْلَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ } [الأحقاف: 13، 14]

“Surely, those who say, “Our Lord is Allah” and then became upright (afterward stood firm), they will have no fear, nor shall they grieve. (13) Those are the people of Paradise, who will live there forever as a reward for what they used to do.” (Al-Ahqaf 46:13-14)

Istiqamah is an important Islamic concept.  The literal meaning of “Istiqamah” is to stand straight into the right direction, to act rightly with no deviation. It is related to the terms “Qiyyam” (قيام), which implies standing up and the term (مستقيم) that means straight.

So istiqamah means traversing upon the Sirat al-Mustaqeem (الصِّرَاطَ المُستَقِيمَ), the Straight path of guidance and this is the Dua, supplication that we make at least 17 time each day as we recite Surah al-Fatihah by asking Allah (اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ المُستَقِيمَ) to guide us to the straight path.

Since Istiqamah means traversing upon the Sirat al-Mustaqeem, the Straight Path of guidance, it means that we should avoid swerving to the left or the right but we should always be in the middle, not going beyond the limits by neither being extreme nor being negligent.

The Shaitan Satan, senses the heart of the Muslim and puts it to the test. So, if he senses that it is lazy and careless when it come to the obedience of Allah, he encourages it further with laziness, ease and distance from the religion until the person disengages from the Religion and Satan will not stop until a person severs all his ties with the Religion.

But, if the Shaitan, Satan, sees that the Muslim is passionate about the Religion and knows that he is not able to block him from it, he encourages him with more and more striving, and with becoming strict upon himself and upon others, and going beyond bounds of balance. Here the person leaves Istiqamah, and the example of this is the Khawārij. The Prophet (PBUH) described their worship compared to the those who have istiqamah. The Prophet informed us that the prayer, fasting and the recital of the Quran of the people of istiqamah seem insignificant compared to the prayer, fasting and the recital of the Qur’an of those extremists. Yet, those extremists leave the religion of Islam just like an arrow that misses its target.

Both of these inclinations are blameworthy: the negligent group, and the extreme group. Both have exited the path of the Istiqamah. The first group left the Istiqamah to deviation of neglect and loss. The second group left the Istiqamah to the deviation of excess, extremism and exaggeration.

It has been said that true Istiqamah is a road whose beginning is dignity, its middle is safety and its end is paradise: “الاستقامة طريق أولها الكرامة، وأوسطها السلامة، وآخرها الجنة.”

The command of the Istiqamah is emphasized in several verses in the Qur’an, Allah says:

فَٱسۡتَقِمۡ كَمَآ أُمِرۡتَ وَمَن تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطۡغَوۡاْ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ۬ (١١٢)

“Therefore, stand firm as you are commanded and those who turn in repentance with you. And do not transgress, for He (Allah) sees well all that you do.” (Hud 11:112)

So, we see that the lack of Istiqmah is manifested by transgression. Allah points out in surat Al-Shura that the cause of the deviation from Istiqamah is allowing ourselves to follow or be misled by desires (whether it is our desires or the desires of others), Allah says:

فَلِذَٲلِكَ فَٱدۡعُ‌ۖ وَٱسۡتَقِمۡ ڪَمَآ أُمِرۡتَ‌ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡ‌ۖ (١٥)

“So, unto this (religion) invite (people), and be steadfast as you are commanded, and do not follow their desires,” (Al-Shura 42:15)

Ibn Abbas said that command to stand firm as Allah commanded is the hardest and most difficult command in Qur’an. The reason is that it is a difficult to achieve Istiqamah all the time and under all circumstances. It is inevitable that we will fall short in the steadfastness on the obligations, so we should make our shortcoming up by that by seeking forgiveness as Allah says in Surat Fussilat:

قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۟ بَشَرٌ۬ مِّثۡلُكُمۡ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمۡ إِلَـٰهٌ۬ وَٲحِدٌ۬ فَٱسۡتَقِيمُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُوهُ‌ۗ (٦)

“Say, “I am but a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your god is only One God. Therefore, be steadfast upon the Straight Path to Him, and seek forgiveness from Him.” (Fussilat 41:6)

In addition to repentance, we can compensate for our deficiencies by regular spending in charity as Allah says in Surat Al-Taghabun:

فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرً۬ا لِّأَنفُسِڪُمۡ‌ۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ (١٦)

“So, observe taqwa of Allah (awareness of Allah) as best as you can, and listen and obey, and spend, it being good for you. And those who are saved from the greed, such are the successful.” (Al-Taghabun 64:16)

When one feels that he is short in remaining steadfast on Allah’s straight path, there are two ways to compensate for the deficiencies, seeking Allah’s forgiveness and spending in Charity.

Appreciating the difficulties that we will face in maintaining our Istiqamah, the Prophet (PBUH) comforted us by saying:

( عن ثوبان – رضي الله عنه – قال : قال رسول – صلى الله عليه وسلم – “اسْتَقِيمُوا وَلَنْ تُحْصُوا وَاعْمَلُوا وَخَيْرُ أَعْمَالِكُمُ الصَّلاةُ وَلَا يُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْوُضُوءِ إِلَّا مُؤْمِنٌ”) رواه مالك وأحمد وابن ماجه ، والدارمي.

“Be steadfast, although you will not be able to attain perfection.  So, act, and the best of your actions is the prayer. And only a believer is constant in his ablution (wudū).”

In another narration, the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

سَدِّدُوا وَقَارِبُوا وَلاَ يُحَافِظُ عَلَى الصلاة إِلاَّ مُؤْمِنٌ

“Do your best in the good deeds with determination to reach what is correct. And only a believer is constant in his prayers.” [Musnad Ahmad, 21927]

Istiqamah means obeying the commands of Allah regarding the obligatory rituals that He prescribed and were demonstrated to us by the prophet (PBUH). Since we realize that we cannot perfect all our obligations, we can compensate by the sunnan, supererogatory rituals.

There are three basic elements for Istiqamah: Istiqamah of the heart, Istiqamah of the tongue and Istiqamah of the character.

The first element is the Istiqama of your heart to ensure that it is free from all forms of shirks by keeping our heart steadfast on doing everything for the pleasure of Allah and not for anyone else. Shirk is the worst injustice man can commit and for the one who commits it the road to Hell is guaranteed. Allah says:

مَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَمأۡوَٮٰهُ ٱلنَّارُ‌ۖ وَمَا لِلظَّـٰلِمِينَ مِنۡ أَنصَارٍ۬ (٧٢)

“Whosoever ascribes any partner to Allah, Allah has prohibited for him the Paradise, and his abode is the Fire, and for the unjust, there will be no helpers.” (Al-Maeda 5:72)

Freedom from all forms of shirk requires purifying our heart from hypocrisy, jealousy and arrogance, heedlessness, from being overwhelmed by self-interests and desires and from showing off seeking others’ appraisal. Purity of the heart is a perquisite for success in the Hereafter as Allah says:

وَلَا تُخۡزِنِى يَوۡمَ يُبۡعَثُونَ (٨٧) يَوۡمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ۬ وَلَا بَنُونَ (٨٨) إِلَّا مَنۡ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلۡبٍ۬ سَلِيمٍ۬ (٨٩)

“And do not disgrace me on the Day of resurrection (87) The Day when neither wealth nor sons will be of benefit. (88) Except to him who will come to Allah with pure heart.” (Al-Shura 26:87-89)

In order to purify our heart from all forms of shirk, we should always be aware of the final destination, i.e., the Day of Judgment. We should use this awareness as a motive to commit to do things in the right way and in the best way possible. This will require continuous checking and reviewing our deeds and being honest with ourselves so as not to give false excuses for failing to perfect our deeds or to fulfill a commitment.

Therefore, we need to hold self-accountability twice:

1. First, before we start doing something, ensuring that it pleases Allah, that we do it for His sake only, realizing the right way it should be done.
2. Second, after the action has been done, to check whether we have achieved what we aimed for, and to check for defects and shortcomings.

We should realize that no one is perfect except Allah and thus we should be always be seeking His forgiveness, guidance and support. We also need to make commitment to strive to make improvements in all that we do (daily activities, work, actions, good deeds, ibadah, etc.) as one of our objectives.

It is important that whatever deed we are engaged in should be done with the right intention for the sake of Allah alone (ikhlas) and should be done on the basis of knowledge and in the best way possible.

The second basic element of Istiqamah is the Istiqamah of our tongue by avoiding all forms of lying, profane language, backbiting and false accusation of others. There are many sayings for the prophet (PBUH) that warns about the tongue if it is used improperly.

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

– وعن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: “لا يستقيم إيمان عبدٍ حتى يستقيم قلبه، ولا يستقيم قلبه حتى يستقيم لسانه –

The belief of Allah’s slave is never firm until his heart is firm and his heart will never be firm until his tongue is firm.

The Prophet (PBUH) said to his uncle Al-Abbas: I love your beauty.

. ” قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمه العباس رضوان الله عليه: يعجبني جمالك. قال: وما جمال الرجل ؟ قال: لسانه

Al-Abbas said: What is the beauty in a Man. The Prophet (PBUH) said: His tongue.

Allah commands us that we should always speak not what is only good but what is best. Allah says:

وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلْإِنسَانِ عَدُوًّا مُّبِينًا

“And say to My servants to say that which is best, Indeed Satan sow discord (induce dissension) among them Indeed Satan is ever to mankind a clear enemy.” (Al-Isra 17:53)

Interesting that this command was revelaed in Mecca and it is reported that its revelation was on the occasion of an incident in which a man from Quraysh insulted Syedna Omar after he became Muslim and Syedna Omar (عمر بن الخطاب) responded to him with insults and curses and was on the verge of killing him and this would have created big conflict.

If this applies in this situation, would you really justify any situation that you would not say what is best when speaking to a family member or another Muslim. Allah gives us the warning that if we don’t say the best, we will be giving an opening to Satan to sow discord and dissention that will escalate the situation. So, you should always seek the best words to respond to even bad words. Don’t reward a bad person with bad behavior and don’t give Satan a chance to sow conflicts.

Even when someone says something that you consider evil, you should respond to it with goodness as Allah commands us by saying:

.وَلَا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ، ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ، فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ

“Good and evil are not equal. Repel (evil) with what is best, and you will see that the one with whom you have enmity will become a close friend.” (Fussilat 41:34)

In Surat Ibrahim, Allah alerts us of the importance of watching every word that we utter as He says:

أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً۬ كَلِمَةً۬ طَيِّبَةً۬ كَشَجَرَةٍ۬ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصۡلُهَا ثَابِتٌ۬ وَفَرۡعُهَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ (٢٤) [إبراهيم]

“Have you not considered how Allah sets forth a parable?  A good word as a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed, and its branches (reach) to the sky. (Ibrahim 14:24)

وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ۬ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ٱجۡتُثَّتۡ مِن فَوۡقِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ (٢٦) [إبراهيم]

And the parable of a bad word is that of a bad tree uprooted from the face of the earth, it has no stability.” (Ibrahim 14: 26)

The third element of Istiqamah is the Istiqamah of our character. We need to also ensure that our character reflects the highest moral standard. When Allah wanted to praise the Prophet (PBUH), He praised him by His character as He said:

﴿ وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ ﴾ [القلم: 4]

“And you have an exalted standard of character (Al-Qalam 68:4)

The Prophet (PBUH) summarized the purpose of his teachings by saying:

.” إنّما بُعثت لأُتمم مكارم الأخلاق “

“I haven’t been sent except to perfect the good manners.”

The Prophet (PBUH) emphasized the importance of good character in many of his sayings.  He (PBUH) said:

(أحب عباد الله إلى الله أحسنهم خلُقاً) [ الطبراني]

“The most beloved servant of Allah to Allah is the one who has the best manners”. “

(إن الرجل ليُدرك بحسن خُلُقه درجات قائم الليل صائم النهار] أبو داود والحاكم عن عائشة [

A man reaches with his good manner the degree of the one who perform prayers all night and fasts all day”.

(إن من أحبِّكم وأقربكم منّي مجلساً يوم القيامة: أحاسنكم أخلاقاً). [ الترمذي عن جابر]

“The most beloved to me and nearest to me on the Day of Judgment is the one who has the best manners”.

As final note, resilience is a key component of Istiqamah but even strong and resilient people make mistakes.  The Istiqamah is an exhausting journey and it is the nature of humans to stumble and make mistakes. Never feel ashamed that you are not achieving perfection which you will never achieve because the One who is perfect is Allah. Mistakes and shortcoming make you humble and encourages you to constantly seek Allah’s forgiveness and help to make things easy for you.

Imam Ibn Qayyim has beautiful comments on the story of Prophet Adam, he says:

“Satan rejoiced when Adam came out of paradise, but he (Satan) did not know that when a diver sinks into the sea, he collects pearls and then rises again.”

Even strong and resilient Muslims make mistakes. But part of the Istiqamah is for a Muslim to reflect on his mistakes and turn them into opportunity to return to Allah in a more meaningful way.

We need to note that in both the hadith and the verses that link belief to Istiqamah uses the conjunction letter (ثُمَّ) “قُلْ: آمَنْتُ”, “قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَامُوا” and this infers time delay between declaring belief and achieving the Istiqamah. This means that achieving the Istiqamah is a journey that will take time and not an immediate event. If Allah and the Prophet (PBUH) would have used the conjunction letter (ف) it would have meant that as soon as one declares his belief it would have required from him to achieve the Istiqamah. We note the conjunction (ف) is used with the command of prayers such as:

وَذَكَرَ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ

And remembers the Name of his Lord, and pray. (Al-Ala 87:15)

We pray to Allah to help us remain steadfast on our journey of the Istiqamah of our heart, our tongue and our character.

DUA

title: The Journey of the Soul
excerpt: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In my talk today, I plan, Insha’Allah, discuss the Soul (Ruh) and its journey. But let me first define terminologies. The Quran uses two terms: Ruh and Nafs. Some translators translate Ruh as Spirit and Nafs as Soul. In this talk, I am making the assumption that Ruh and Nafs are the same. Therefore, I am going to use Soul referring to the Ruh and will use the Arabic terms Ruh and Nafs when I am trying to provide distinction between them.

Obviously, we are talking here about knowledge of the unseen and thus my hypothesis regarding what is the Ruh and the Nafs cannot be taken as absolute truth because only Allah knows the truth. But it should only be considered an intellectual exercise to explain verses in the Quran and some sayings of the Prophet (PBUH) regarding them.

You may ask, why wasting time in speculating about something of the unseen for which we don’t have clear definition. My answer is for two reasons:

The first reason is that Allah revealed to us these terms in many verses in the Quran and the Prophet (PBUH) provided additional details and we are required to do Tadabour which in depth study of the Quran and this means analyzing every word in it. The in-depth study of the Quran through the process of Tadabour is a command from Allah to all of us, He said:

كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (ص)
(This is) a Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings that they should to the Tadabour of its Verses, and those who have understanding may heed/reflect (on its commands). “(Sad 38:29)

There are two forms of Tadabour: 1) heart-driven tadabour (تدبر قلبى) and 2) brain-driven tadabour (تدبر عقلى).

Regarding the heart-driven tadabour, Allah says that those who don’t do tadabour, their hearts are sealed:
أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ أَمْ عَلَى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَا (محمد)
Will they not do the tadabour of the Qur’an, or do they have locks on the hearts?” (Mohammad 47:24)
This means that the Tadabour is the tool to open the heart because without it the heart is sealed.

Regarding the brain driven Tadabour, Allah says:

أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ‌ۚ وَلَوۡ كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ غَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخۡتِلَـٰفً۬ا كَثِيرً۬ا (٨٢)
“Will they not do tadabour of the Quran? Had it been from other than Allah, they would surely have found therein much discrepancy.” (An-Nisa’ 4:82)
This implies that only thru Tadabour, a person will be truly convinced that the Quran is from Allah.

Through these two forms of Tadabour the person heart will be cured from any doubt and his limbs will be motivated to implement the Divine message:
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم مَّوۡعِظَةٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّڪُمۡ وَشِفَآءٌ۬ لِّمَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةٌ۬ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (٥٧)
“O mankind! There has come to you an advice from your Lord, a healing for the (diseases) of the hearts, and a guidance and a mercy for the believers.” (Yunus 10:57)

Through the engagement of the heart and the mind as we read the Quran, we will not be one of those whom the Prophet (PBUH) will complain about to Allah on the day of Judgment:
يَا رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا (الفرقان)
“O my Lord! my people deserted this Quran (of no account). (Al-Fourqan 25:30)

The second reason why spending time in analyzing and speculating about something of the unseen for which we don’t have clear definition is related to human nature.

Curiosity is the essence of human existence and without curiosity no progress will ever be achieved. Allah asked use to be curious and to analyze:
قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ ڪَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ‌ۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬ (٢٠)
Say: “Travel in the land and see how He originated the creation. Then Allah will bring forth the second creation (Resurrection). Truly Allah has power over all things.” (Al-Ankaboot 29:20)

The Quran promotes curiosity, analytical capability and logic of Muslims and these are important human traits. Einstein said: “I have no special talents. I am only passionately curious”. It has been said that “Old Age Starts Where Curiosity Ends” and obviously, Allah wants Muslims to always be young because without curiosity, Muslims will not be able to develop the logic and the critical thinking that are needed to manage the challenges that we will be facing in this life.

The subject of the Ruh (the Soul) is fascinating and its study can help use address several intriguing questions such as:
1. What is the nature of the Ruh (the Soul)?
2. Is there a difference between Ruh and Nafs?
3. Which one existed first the Ruh or the body?
4. Does the Ruh/Nafs die or death is only confined to the body?
5. Are the deceased aware of those who visit them at their grave site?
6. Do the souls of the deceased visit each other?
7. Do the souls of the living and the dead meet?
8. How do souls recognize one another after separating from the body?
9. Does the soul return to the deceased body after burial for interrogation?
10. Is the interrogation in the gave limited only to Muslims or it include everyone?
11. Where do souls settle between death and the day of judgement?

In this talk I am going to focus on addressing the first two questions” 1) What is the Ruh and 2) Is there a difference between Ruh and Nafs.

There is a good reference that discusses many of these questions and it is entitled “The Soul”, (الروح) and it was written by Ibn Al-Qayim, roughly 700 years ago.

Before presenting my hypothesis, I want to introduce two technologies that may help in justifying the proposed hypothesis regarding the Ruh.

The first technology related to holograms. A hologram is a three-dimensional projection of diffracted light that retains the depth of the original physical object it represents. If we have a hologram of a person, we will see his exact copy but in a form of energy (light).

The second technology is related to data storage. Currently data are stored in hard drive disks and solid-state storage but these systems are fast approaching their physical limits. Recently, researchers were able to store huge amount of data in DNA and a very small drop of DNA can store enough data for millions of years. This means that a lot of information regarding every person can be stored in a very small volume.

So, these two technologies suggest that an exact replica of us can be created using light and this copy can have a record of everything about us from birth to death.

We also need to keep in mind our own personal experiences with the dreams we see during our sleep during which our souls can see and talk while our physical body is resting in bed.

Regarding the Ruh (Soul), Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) was asked about it and the response came in the revealed verse:
وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ‌ۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّى وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ (٨٥)
And they will ask you about the Ruh (the Soul). Say: The Ruh (the Soul) is a command of my Lord, and of knowledge you have been given but little. (Al-Isra 17:85)

This verse suggest that the Ruh (Soul) is a command from the Creator, Allah. This means that is a creation that follows the rule of “Be” and “It is”:
إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُ ۥۤ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيۡـٴً۬ـا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُ ۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ (٨٢)
“But His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says unto it: Be! and it becomes.” (Yasin 36:82)

The verse also suggests that our knowledge regarding the Ruh will be limited but it soes not suggest that we should not explore and use logical reasoning to try to understand its nature.

The Prophet (PBUH) informs us in a hadith narrated by Sayeda Aysha and reported in Muslim of the materials from which different creations were made of:
عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت قال رسول الله : صلى الله عليه وسلم خلقت الملائكة من نور وخلق الجان من مارج من نار وخلق آدم مما وصف لكم
The angels have been created form light and the Jinn have been created from smokeless flame and you have been created from what has been described to you (i.e., the description in the Quran).

This means that both the angels and the Jinn are created form a class of energy. While we know many forms of energy such as electricity and magnetic waves, we don’t know much about the energy of light that angels are made of or the smokeless flame from which Jinn were created.

Since man is made of physical body of elements from earth and Ruh, one can assume that the Ruh is a form of energy that we are not aware of yet.

So, here is the hypothesis.

The Ruh of all human beings was created first from the same elements which is probably light and was stored in a repository as a mature person form, like a hologram. This hologram has all the records that define every person (color of eyes, personality, length etc.). These records are taught to the Ruh by the Creator, Allah. The Quran may be part of what the Ruh was taught.

The Ruh enters in the undifferentiated human cells with the Divinely taught records while in the womb of our mothers and this merging between the Ruh and the cells initiate the growth of the fetus with its distinct characteristics.

There is only one person whose Ruh in its mature age form merged with his body when the body was in its adult form and this was Prophet Adam. However, for all of us, the Ruh (the Hologram of our mature body) is squeezed into the small fetus as it develops in the womb.

As a crude analogy, you can consider the Ruh as the internal of a new computer (Mother board, CPU and its operating system) and the physical body is the keyboard, the screen and the mouse.

Please note that only Allah knows the truth and this proposed concept of the Ruh is a hypothesis to explain the related verses and the Prophetic sayings.

Let me test the possible validity of this hypothesis against the verses in the Quran and the related Prophetic sayings.

Allah says in Surat Al-A’raf (7:11):
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ (١١)
“We created you, then shaped you; then We said to the angels prostrate to Adam and they prostrated except Iblis who was not among those who prostrated.” (Al-Araf 7:11)

This verse implies that the creation of mankind was done in three sequential steps with some time delay as suggested by the Arabic word (ثُمَّ):
1. The first step is the creation of the Ruh of all human beings (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ).
2. The second step is shaping the Ruh of every one of us in his adult form (ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ) and you can think of it as creating the hologram copy of everyone.
3. The third step is Allah’s command to the angels to prostrate to prophet Adam. Based on the hypothesis, this step happened after the creation of the Ruh of all human beings.

This proposed intermediate step may be justified by verses 28 and 29 from Surat Al-Hijr, Allah says:
وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ إِنِّى خَـٰلِقُۢ بَشَرً۬ا مِّن صَلۡصَـٰلٍ۬ مِّنۡ حَمَإٍ۬ مَّسۡنُونٍ۬ (٢٨) فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُ ۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى فَقَعُواْ لَهُ ۥ سَـٰجِدِينَ (٢٩)
“Recall when your Lord said to the angels, “I am going to create a human being from a ringing clay of a dark mud. (28) When I have completed his shaping and I have blown in him from My Ruh, then fall prostrate to him.” (Al-Hijr 15:28-29)

These verses justify the hypothesis that the Ruh was created before forming Adam’s physical body. Also, note that Allah says: “Blow in him from My Ruh “وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى”. This may make some suggest that we human being have something from Allah which is the Ruh and this is logically impossible because Allah is the Creator and we are the created. The phrase “My Ruh” means the Ruh that I created and it is like saying “My House” or “My Car”.

While Allah was the One who merged the Ruh of Prophet Adam with his body, the Ruh of all us, as well as the Ruh of the children of Adam were merged with our bodies by an Angel as specified by the Prophet (PBUH).

This somewhat explains the hadeath that is reported in both Bukhari and Muslim, Abdullah ibn Masoud said:
عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ الصَّادِقُ الْمَصْدُوقُ: إنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ خَلْقُهُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا نُطْفَةً، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يُرْسَلُ إلَيْهِ الْمَلَكُ فَيَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ، وَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ: بِكَتْبِ رِزْقِهِ، وَأَجَلِهِ، وَعَمَلِهِ، وَشَقِيٍّ أَوْ سَعِيدٍ
Verily each one of you is brought together in his mother’s womb for forty days in the form of a drop of fluid (Nutfah), then it is a leech-like complex for a like period, then a morsel of flesh for a like period, then there is sent to him the angel who blows the Ruh into him and who is commanded with four matters: to write down his sustenance, his life span, his actions, and whether he will be happy or unhappy (in the Hereafter).

This concept of creation of the Ruh first and for it having the shape of our mature body in a hologram-type form may explain verse 172 of Surat Al-A’raf, where Allah says:
وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ (١٧٢)
“When your Lord brought the offspring from the lions of the children of Adam, and made them bear witness about themselves, (saying): “Am I not your Lord?” They said: “Yes, we bear witness.” (this was) lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: “We were unaware of this.” (Al-Araf 7:172)

I said that Allah may have taught the Ruh, the Quran because this may explain verses 1 to 3 of Surat Ar-Rahman, where Allah says:
ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ (١) عَلَّمَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ (٢) خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ (٣)
Ar-Rahman. He taught the Qur’an. He created man. (Ar-Rahman 55:1-3)
The verses suggest that Allah taught the Quran to something before He created man. Based in the Hypothesis, Allah taught the Ruh the Quran and then the Ruh merged with the body and became a man.

Because of time, I am not going to check the validity of the hypothesis against all the related verses but I will briefly mention the Nafs.

Since the hypothesis suggests that the Ruh is the hologram-type concept of the human body that has the record of all our physical attributes and all our actions, then the Ruh becomes the Nafs as it merges with the physical body and starts experiencing life. The Nafs is then the being that will taste death and will be judged on the Day of Judgment.

Allah says in the Quran:
وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ كِتَابًا مُؤَجَّلًا (آل عمران)
No (Nafs) soul can ever die except by Allah’s will and at a term appointed (Al-Imran 3:145)

كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ (آل عمران)
Every Nafs (soul) will taste of death. And you will be paid on the Day of Resurrection only that which you have fairly earned. (Al-Imran 3:185)

We also should expect that the Nafs will be the one to face the Judgement since it has the record of everything it did during this life:
وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلۡوَعِيدِ (٢٠) وَجَآءَتۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّعَهَا سَآٮِٕقٌ۬ وَشَہِيدٌ۬ (٢١)
“And the Trumpet will be blown — that will be the Day of the dreadful threat. (20) And every Nafs will come, along with a driver and a witness. (21)” (Qaf 50:20-21)

يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِى ڪُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ تُجَـٰدِلُ عَن نَّفۡسِہَا وَتُوَفَّىٰ ڪُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (١١١)
“(Remember) the Day when every Nafs will come up pleading for himself, and everyone will be paid in full for what he did, and they will not be wronged.” (An-Nahl 16:111)

Part of the hypothesis is that on the Day of Resurrection, every Nafs will be merged with a body that is different from the physical body we have today but it will be an exact copy of it. Allah says:
وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتۡ (سُوۡرَةُ التّکویر)
And when the Nafs (souls) are paired (with new bodies). (Al-Takwir 81:7)

We can close by justifying that part of the hypothesis that suggests that the Nafs can temporarily leave the body while the body is living and this happens during sleep. Allah says:
ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلۡأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوۡتِهَا وَٱلَّتِى لَمۡ تَمُتۡ فِى مَنَامِهَا‌ۖ فَيُمۡسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيۡہَا ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَيُرۡسِلُ ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّى‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَأَلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٤٢)
“Allah takes away the Nafs (the souls) at the time of their death, and those who do not die during their sleep; then He withholds those on whom He has passed the decree of death and sends the others back till an appointed term. Verily, in this are signs for people who reflect.” (Al-Zumar 39:42)

To close, I want to emphasize that the hypothesis I presented to you is just a human effort and an intellectual exercise to reflect on the verses in the Quran and the Prophetic sayings. Only Allah knows the truth.

As I have often repeated, if my explanations make sense to you and you want to share, please share. However, if they don’t make sense or if you disagree with them, just ignore them.

We pray to Allah to grant is to wisdom to expand our cognitive capacity through serious study of the Quran.

DUA
It is reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عن أم سلمة قالت دخل رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي سلمة وقد شق بصره فأغمضه ثم قال: إن الروح إذا قبض تبعه البصر (صحيح مسلم)
“When the Ruh is taken the sight follow it.”

The Prophet Also said as narrated by Abu Hurrirah:
عن أبي هريرة عند مسلم قال: (إذا خرجت روح المؤمن تلقاها ملكان – يُصعدانها ويقول أهل السماء: روح طيبة جاءت من قبل الأرض، صلى الله عليك وعلى جسد كنت تعمرينه – ثم يذهب به إلى ربه عز وجل ثم يقول: انطلقوا به إلى آخر الأجل، وإن الكافر إذا خرجت روحه يقول أهل السماء: روح خبيثة جاءت من قبل الأرض)
“When the Spirit (Ruh) of the believer exits, two angels receive her and ascend with it and the residents of Heaven will say: pleasant spirit came from the direction of the earth. And when the Spirit of the disbeliever exists, the residents of heaven will say, rotten spirit is coming from the direction of earth.”

This suggests that both the Ruh and the Nafs are the same

title: The Freedom of Choice and its Consequence
excerpt: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

In my last week talk I discussed the first 6 verses from Surat Yasin (36) and ended the talk by verse 6:

لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمً۬ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَـٰفِلُونَ (٦)
That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless.” (Yasin 36:6).

This verse informs the Prophet and in turn us that the purpose of the Quran is to warn any people whose fathers have not delivered to them Allah’s message. Obviously, when the message is delivered some people will heed the warning and accept it and others will reject it. Verses 7 to 10 address those who reject the divine message and give them grave warning, Allah says:

لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ (٧) إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِىٓ أَعۡنَـٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَـٰلاً۬ فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ (٨) وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيْدِيهِمۡ سَدًّ۬ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدًّ۬ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَـٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ (٩) وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ (١٠)

“The word had indeed come true against the majority of them, so they will not believe. (7) We have placed shackles on their necks and hands pulling them to their chins, and forcing their heads upward. (8) And We have placed a barrier in front of them and a barrier behind them, and (thus) they are covered by Us; so, they cannot see. (9) It is same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe.” (Yasin 36:7-10)

These verses raise two questions that deserve serious analysis and require linkage with other verses in the Quran to properly understand them.

First: The verses state that there are certain people, actually the majority, whom Allah has already written them off and will not allow them to believe by placing shackles and barriers on them. This raises the question, is fair that Allah prevents certain people from belief and then punishes them.

Second: The verses state that shackles and barriers are placed on those people to prevent them from believing. The question is whether these things are merely similitude to give us an idea of the constraints placed on them or are these are real physical constrains. In the Quran, when Allah wanted to present a similitude, He clearly states that their likeness is like such and such. As example, when Allah spoke of the Hypocrites, He said:

مَثَلُهُمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى ٱسۡتَوۡقَدَ نَارً۬ا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتۡ مَا حَوۡلَهُ ۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمۡ وَتَرَكَهُمۡ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتٍ۬ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ

“Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindles fire, and when it illuminates everything around him, Allah takes away their lights and leaves them in layers of darkness, so that they see nothing. (Al-Baqara 2:17)

In this verse it is clear that the fire was just a similitude and the hypocrites did not kindle real fire, but in these verses, Allah does not say that their likeness is as the those who have collars on their necks and barriers placed around them. Therefore, it is appropriate to interpret these verses as being real and that those people actually have collar around their necks and barriers around them to prevent them from believing. How can this be real?

In this talk, I plan, inshallah to address the first issue and inshallah in next week I’ll try to address the second one.

We must realize that believing in Allah is an honor and Allah will not grant such an honor to several people whose attributes are clearly identified in several verses in the Quran. One of these attributes is arrogance as Allah says in Suart Al-Araf:

سَأَصۡرِفُ عَنۡ ءَايَـٰتِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كُلَّ ءَايَةٍ۬ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِہَا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرُّشۡدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً۬ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡغَىِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡہَا غَـٰفِلِينَ (١٤٦)

“I shall turn away from My revelations those who show arrogance in the earth with no right to do so and If they were to see every sign, they would not believe in it; and if they see the Path of guidance, they do not take it as their way; and if they see the path of misguidance, they would take it as their way. That is because they have rejected Our signs, and have been disregarding them.” (Al-Araf 7:146)

When reading the Quran, you realize that there are people whom Allah will not guide because they have certain evil attributes. These attributes that are identified in the Quran include: arrogance (كبر), injustice (ظلم), rebellion (فسق), lying (كذب) and rejection of truth (كفر).

The question that may still be raised why Allah created people who will not believe and punish them. Any person who raises question regarding Allah’s actions must consider three key points:

1. The attributes of Allah that we know by studying His glorious names.
2. The questioner needs to have the humility to recognize his level with respect to Allah.
3. We should not mix between Allah having the knowledge and allowing certain actions to proceed and Him influencing people to act based on His knowledge and authority. This is a key point that must be kept in mind, let me state it in different way: “Allah has the knowledge of what every person will do from the time of Adam until the end of life, and He allows certain actions that is displeasing to Him to proceed but He does not influence the people to act based on His knowledge and authority.”

To help you understand this point, you must realize that Allah is not constrained of the time and space that constrain us. Therefore, you really cannot use past, present and future with Allah because all these terms are time dimensions that we are constrained with but Allah does not. I realize that it is hard to visualize things without the dimensions of time and space. But we get some experience with it during our dreams when the time and space dimensions are almost eliminated.

When discussing Allah’s actions, we must consider one of His glorious names Al-Adl (The Justice) and this directly means that there is no way Allah will ever create people with the intention that they will do wrong so He can punish them. Allah emphasized to anyone who is humble enough to read Allah’s message that He will never do injustice to anyone as He affirmed is so many verses. As example, Allah says in Surat Al-Nisa:

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ۬‌ۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً۬ يُضَـٰعِفۡهَا وَيُؤۡ مِن لَّدُنۡهُ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمً۬ا (٤٠)

“Indeed, Allah does not do injustice not even of the weight of an atom; and if there is a good deed, He will double it and will give (the doer) from His presence an immense reward” (Al-Nisa 4:40)

All what Allah does is to have complete record of what everyone has done and hold him accountable for it in a completely just way. Allah says in Surat Al-Kahf:

وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَـٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَـٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً۬ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَٮٰهَا‌ۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرً۬ا‌ۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدً۬ا (٤٩)

“And the book (of deeds) will be placed (before them), then you will see the guilty people scared of its contents and saying, “Woe to us! What a book is this! It has missed nothing, minor or major, but has taken it into account.” Thus, they will find whatever they did present before them, and your Lord will not wrong anyone.” (Al-Kahf 18: 49)

So, Allah’s justice cannot be questioned, but some people may still argue that since we cannot do anything without Allah allowing it, so He could have prevented us from committing the sins. Interesting that Allah knew that this false argument will be made and thus He responded to it in several verses. As example, Allah says in Surat Al-An’am:

سَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَآ أَشۡرَڪۡنَا وَلَآ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمۡنَا مِن شَىۡءٍ۬‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ حَتَّىٰ ذَاقُواْ بَأۡسَنَا‌ۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ عِندَڪُم مِّنۡ عِلۡمٍ۬ فَتُخۡرِجُوهُ لَنَآ‌ۖ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَخۡرُصُونَ (١٤٨)

“Those who associate partners with Allah will say, “Had Allah willed, we would have not associated (partners with Him), nor our fathers, nor would we have made anything prohibited.” In the same way those who went before them gave the lie to (the truth) until they tasted Our punishment. Say, “Do you have any sure knowledge that you may produce to us? You follow nothing but an opinion, and do nothing but make guesses.” (Al-An’am 6:148)

A similar response is given in Surat Al-Nahl:

وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا عَبَدۡنَا مِن دُونِهِۦ مِن شَىۡءٍ۬ نَّحۡنُ وَلَآ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمۡنَا مِن دُونِهِۦ مِن شَىۡءٍ۬‌ۚ كَذَٲلِكَ فَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ‌ۚ فَهَلۡ عَلَى ٱلرُّسُلِ إِلَّا ٱلۡبَلَـٰغُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ (٣٥)

“Those who associate partners with Allah said, “Had Allah willed, we would have not worshipped anything other than Him – neither we nor our forefathers – nor would we have made anything prohibited without (a command from) Him.” In the same way, this was what those who were before them did. Are the messengers charged with anything but to convey the clear message?” (Al-Nahl 16:35)

Also, Allah make it very clear that He does not want disbelief for anyone even though people’s disbelief has no impact on Him. Allah says:

إِن تَكۡفُرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنكُمۡ‌ۖ وَلَا يَرۡضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ‌ۖ وَإِن تَشۡكُرُواْ يَرۡضَهُ لَكُمۡ‌ۗ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ۬ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰ‌ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّڪُم مَّرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَيُنَبِّئُڪُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ (٧)

“If you disbelieve, then, Allah is not in need of you, however He does not like disbelief for His slaves; and if you are grateful, He will like it for you. No one will bear the burden of another. Then, to your Lord is your return; so He will tell you about what you used to do. He is aware of whatever is in the hearts.’ (Al-Zumur: 39:7)

Obviously, if Allah willed it, He could have not allowed people to be disbelievers as He said:

وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَآ أَشۡرَكُواْ‌ۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَـٰكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَفِيظً۬ا‌ۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيۡہِم بِوَڪِيلٍ۬ (١٠٧)

“Had Allah willed, they would not have taken associates (besides Allah). We have not appointed you as a guard over them, nor are you a trustee over them.” (Al-An’am 6:107)

But Allah did not, because He wanted to create the most honorable creation by granting them complete free will to worship Him or not and to obey Him or not. Allah affirmed that He has honored the children of Adam as He said:

وَلَقَدۡ كَرَّمۡنَا بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَرَزَقۡنَـٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ وَفَضَّلۡنَـٰهُمۡ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ۬ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقۡنَا تَفۡضِيلاً۬ (٧٠)

“Indeed, we have honored the children of Adam. We provided them with rides on the land and in the sea, and provided them with a variety of good things and have preferred them above many of those whom We have created with a marked preferment.’ (Al-Isra 17:70)

Interesting that the word (كَرَّمۡنَا) (Honored) came only once in the Quran and it is related to honoring mankind. As part of honoring mankind, Allah subjugated for them all that in heaven and earth as He said on Surat Al-Jathiya:

وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعً۬ا مِّنۡهُ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَـٰتٍ۬ لِّقَوۡمٍ۬ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١٣)

“He has subjugated for you whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, it all from Him. Surely in this there are signs for a people who reflect.” (Al-Jathiya 45:13)

Believing in Allah is instinct for any fair-minded human being because Allah actually have taught all mankind about Him at the time of their first creation. Allah introduced Himself to them and took the covenant from them to believe in Him and associate no one with Him, as He said:

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ

“When your Lord brought the offspring from the lions of the children of Adam, and made them bear witness about themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, indeed, we bear witness. Lest you might say on the Day of Resurrection: we were unaware of this. Or lest you say, it was our forefathers who were polytheists and we are their late offspring, will You destroy us for what futile men have done?” (Al-Araf 7:172-173)

To ensure that no one would claim that he does not remember, Allah sent messengers to every nation to inform them of this covenant and He still maintained for the people the freedom of choice to believe or not. Allah says:

وَلَقَدۡ بَعَثۡنَا فِى ڪُلِّ أُمَّةٍ۬ رَّسُولاً أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱجۡتَنِبُواْ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتَ‌ۖ (٣٦)

“And verily We raised in every nation a messenger, (proclaiming): “Worship Allah and stay away from false gods.” (Al-Nahl 16:36)

إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرً۬ا وَنَذِيرً۬اۚ وَإِن مِّنۡ أُمَّةٍ إِلَّا خَلَا فِيہَا نَذِيرٌ۬ (٢٤)

‘Surely We have sent you with truth as a bearer of good news and as a warner, and and there is not a nation but a warner has passed among them.’” (Fatir 35:24)

As part of Allah’s infinite justice, He said that in case some people do not hear of His message from anyone, He will not hold them accountable. He said:

مَّنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَہۡتَدِى لِنَفۡسِهِۦ‌ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ۬ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰ‌ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبۡعَثَ رَسُولاً۬ (١٥)

“Whoever adopts the right path does so for his own benefit, and whoever goes astray does so to his own detriment, and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another, and We never punish until we have sent a messenger.” (Al-Isra 17:15)

The role of the messengers is to deliver the message of Allah but not to force anyone to believe because Allah wanted to ensure the fulfillment of the honor that He granted to man by allowing him to have the freedom to believe or not to believe. Allah says:

وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡ‌ۖ فَمَن شَآءَ فَلۡيُؤۡمِن وَمَن شَآءَ فَلۡيَكۡفُرۡ

“Say the truth from your Lord. Then, whosoever will, let him believe, and whosoever will, let him disbelieve.” (Al-Kahf 18: 29)

While every human being has been granted the right of free will by Allah to believe or not, but Allah made it clear that there is consequence for each decision. Allah made the consequence of rejecting His signs and the advice of His messengers very clear. He also identified for everyone the attributes of those who disbelieve and these are: arrogance, injustice and deceit.

Allah also made it very clear that those people who possess these attributes and reject His message will not be granted the honor of being believers and thus places barriers for them. This should be a warning for anyone to be aware that his arrogance can lead him to this dangerous position. But someone may still say why, can’t Allah give them more time, they may repent and become believers. This argument shows lack of appreciation of Allah’s knowledge and wisdom because if Allah knew that they will repent, He would not have placed barriers on them. Allah informs us of this to serve as advance warning.

One thing that we must realize is that Allah knows the invisible, the unseen, the hidden and thus we cannot compare our knowledge with His at all. While to Allah is the greatest examples, let us consider an example of the case that you know for sure that the design and construction methods the responsible engineer are using will cause the building to collapse. So, you gave him many advices and rationalize to him his mistakes but he continues to dismiss your input. Then you give him many warnings about what will happen to him when the building collapses but he continues to ignore the warnings. At the final stages of construction, the building collapses and he gets arrested and put to jail. Would you have any sympathy for such a person whose arrogance led him to this miserable position.

Allah’s knowledge is infinite and when He decides to stop giving a person the opportunity to believe, it is based on His knowledge of the unseen and that such a person will just not accept any advice or head any warnings.

People often don’t appreciate the extent of Allah’s knowledge and this is a problem. Allah gives us a very interesting example in Surat Al-An’am to give us a glimpse of His knowledge, He says:

وَعِندَهُ ۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ‌ۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ۬ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبٍ۬ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (٥٩)

“With Him are the keys of Al Ghaib (all that is invisible, unseen, hidden). No one knows them but He. He knows what is in the land and the sea. No leaf ever falls but that He knows about it, and there is no grain in the darkness of the earth, or anything fresh or dry but is written in a clear record.” (Al-Anam 6:59)

An interesting element in this verse is that Allah says that He knows about every leaf that falls down, when will it fall and where it will fall. This is something visible for us, can we use the most powerful computer system and apply the most advanced mathematical model to predict where exactly a certain leaf will fall. The answer is no. We cannot because the parameters that influence the location of a fallen leaf are so vast and we have no way of knowing many of them.

As example, we know that the trajectory of the leaf as it falls will depend on the leaf’s shape, size and weight distribution, the air temperature, and humidity as well as its density of viscosity. Then we need to know all the time other things such as other leaves that are falling as well as birds and animals that may be moving and can impact the trajectory when the leaf is falling. Then we have to develop a transient mathematical model that accounts for all these parameters.

Allah tells us that He knows when each leaf will fall, what is its trajectory, where it will land, and what is going to happen to it after it lands. But interesting that the verse also implies that all these predictions are based on clear and concise system that Allah has established. So, why we want to question Allah regarding how does He know that such and such a person will never believe and thus writes him off and no longer gives him guidance.

While Allah tells us that knowing about the fallen leaf and where every grain is located are part of His knowledge of the unseen, He tells us that there are things that of the unseen that also follow specific mathematical models that we can drive to make predictions of the future, this is related to the movement of the sun and the moon. Allah says in Surat Al-Rahman:

ٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُ بِحُسۡبَانٍ۬

“The sun and the moon are (bound) by a mathematical calculation.” (Al-Rahman 55:5)

This is why you find that scientists are able to predict the time and place of the solar and lunar eclipses for many years in advance. In fact, NASA has predictions to the year 3000. But, no one can until now discover the proper model to predict earthquakes too far in advance, though they are also following certain divine laws that we don’t know, but Allah knows.

People need to have humility and stop questioning what Allah does. But everyone should know that anyone who remains arrogant, he would have decreed for himself Allah’s rejection in this life and eternal punishment in the Hereafter. People have to realize who is Allah and give Him His due honor. Unfortunately, most people don’t. Allah says in Surat Al-Zumur:

وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعً۬ا قَبۡضَتُهُ ۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ مَطۡوِيَّـٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦ‌ۚ سُبۡحَـٰنَهُ ۥ وَتَعَـٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ (٦٧) (الزُّمَر)

“They have not given Allah His true esteem that is due to Him. The whole of the earth is in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be folded in His Right Hand. Glorified is He, and High is He above all that they associate with Him! (Az-Zumur 39: 67).

People who don’t heeds Allah’s warnings and don’t give Allah his due honor are deluded and will face the consequence of this grave mistake. Allah says:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلۡڪَرِيمِ (٦) ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّٮٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ (٧) فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍ۬ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ (٨) كَلَّا بَلۡ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ (٩) وَإِنَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَحَـٰفِظِينَ (١٠) كِرَامً۬ا كَـٰتِبِينَ (١١) يَعۡلَمُونَ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (١٢) إِنَّ ٱلۡأَبۡرَارَ لَفِى نَعِيمٍ۬ (١٣) وَإِنَّ ٱلۡفُجَّارَ لَفِى جَحِيمٍ۬ (١٤) يَصۡلَوۡنَهَا يَوۡمَ ٱلدِّينِ (١٥) وَمَا هُمۡ عَنۡہَا بِغَآٮِٕبِينَ (١٦)

“O man! What has made you deluded about your Lord, the Most Generous? (6) Who created you, fashioned you perfectly, and gave you due proportion; (7) In whatever form He willed, He put you together. (8) Nay! But you deny the Day of Judgement. (9) While over you there are watchers, (10) Who are noble, writers (of the deeds), (11) Who know whatever you do. (12) Surely the righteous will be in bliss, (13) And the wicked will be in Hell, (14) In which they will enter on the Day of Judgement, (15) And they will never be absent from it.” (Al-Infitar 82:6-16)

The reason for the faulty logic that people who raise questions about Allah’s decisions is that they apply finite logic to Allah’s infinite attributes.

If X + Y = X + Z
Is Y = Z
Yes, if X is finite number
No, if X is infinity

We pray to Allah to grant us to wisdom to appreciate the honor that He granted us by giving us the freedom of choice and that we should take advantage of this honor by only doing what is pleasing to Him

We also pray to Allah to grant us the commitment to always give Him His due status and honor by all what we say and do.

DUA

title: Reflection on the beginning of Surat Ya-Seen (یسٓ) (36:1-5)

Reflection on the beginning of Surat Ya-Seen (یسٓ) (36:1-5)

01/03/2021

content:
Reflection on the beginning of Surat Ya-Seen (یسٓ) (36:1-5)

01/03/2021

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

This is typically the time for setting New Year resolutions. The mistake that most people make is to have a resolution related to substantial change of one predominant behavior but then find it difficult to achieve and stop trying. A better resolution is to focus on making minor changes in your routine.

Making changes is difficult and thus making small change that is sustainable is far better than trying to make big change that you cannot sustain. Prophet Mohammed (PBUH) always stressed the importance of consistency; he (PBUH) said:

( عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن أحب الأعمال إلى الله ما دام وإن قل» ) صحيح البخاري

“The most pleasing deeds to Allah are those that are done continuously, no matter how small.”

As example, instead of committing to read, say, one Juz of the Quran per day, commit to read only one verse with understanding per day. You may consider one verse is too little, but if you do this every day, by the end of the year you would have studied Surat Al-Kahf 110 verses (18), Surat Al-Furqan 77 verses (25), Surat Ysin 83 verses (36), and Surat Al-Waqia 96 verses (56).

Let me, inshallah in the next 10-12 minutes give you a head start by discussing the first 5 verses from one of these 4 Suarts, it is Surat Yasin, it is number 36 and it has 83 verses.

The first Verse in Surat Yasin is two Arabic letters (يسٓ), the letter Ya and the letter seen. There are several surat in the Quran that start with individual Arabic letters and many scholars suggested interpretations for them but all are speculations since the Prophet (PBUH) did not explain any of them. So, their meanings and relevance remain hidden secret in the Quran that you may be the one whom Allah guide to their meaning.

يسٓ (١) وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ (٢) إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (٣)

The second verse is an Oath by Allah and this is an Oath by the Quran itself. Allah says: ( وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ ) (By the Quran, full of wisdom). The Question is do we recognize the wisdom in the Quran. Obviously, one cannot identify the wisdom in the Quran without serious analysis and study of its verses. This is really important because this oath with the Quran affirms the third verse ( إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ ) “Truly, you (O Muhammad SAW) are one of the Messengers.”

Allah is making an oath by the Quran that Mohammad (PBUH) is one of His messengers. This means that the physical proof that Mohammad (PBUH) is a messenger of Allah is the Quran. Unless you truly understand the miraculous wisdom of the Quran, you would have no proof that Mohammad (PBUH) is a messenger of Allah. You will be only accepting him as messenger based on your lucky birth to Muslim parents but not based on conviction. You will be no different than the followers of any other religions who follows with no physical proof that whoever Messenger they claim following is a real Messenger of Allah.

When Prophet Musa came to the people and declared that he is Allah’s messenger they asked for a proof. His proof was changing his staff into a snake, changing the color of his hand and splitting the sea. These proofs are only relevant to those who saw them. But when Prophet Musa died his proof died with him and there is no poof now that he was a messenger of Allah or even the Torah is a revelation from Allah.

The same situation is with Prophet Isa (Jesus) when the people asked him for the proof that he is a messenger of Allah. His proof was raising the people from death and healing the blind and the leper. These proofs are only relevant to those who saw them. When he was raised to heaven, the proof left with him and there is no poof now that he was a messenger of Allah or even the Gospel is a revelation from Allah.

But When the people asked Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) for a proof that he is a messenger of Allah, he said to them that his proof is the Quran itself. Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) died but the proof of his Messenger-hood remains alive, it is the Quran that we have.

When you ask any Jew or Christian, how do you prove that Moses or Isa (Jesus) is a messenger of Allah, he will say it is by the belief and the belief is something that cannot be proven by intellectual examination. But this is what everyone who does not have a proof say, the Hindo says it, the Buddhist says it, and so everyone else who follows a religion. Only Muslims have physical proof that Mohammad (PBUH) is a messenger of Allah and that the Quran is the revelation of Allah.

يسٓ (١) وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ (٢) إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (٣) عَلَىٰ صِرَٲطٍ۬ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ۬ (٤) تَنزِيلَ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ (٥)

The fourth verse describes the nature of the Message that Allah revelaed in the Quran to Prophet Mohammed (PBUH) to deliver to mankind. Allah says:

إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (٣) عَلَىٰ صِرَٲطٍ۬ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ۬ (٤)

Truly, you are one of the Messengers, (3) On the Straight Path. (36: 3-4).

The translation of the term (صِرَٲطٍ۬) as path is not really proper, a better translation would be highway because the term (صِرَٲطٍ۬) means a road that is wide and clear that can be easily seen and travelled on and thus cannot be just any road. And not only that Islam is a wide and clear road that it is also straight (مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ۬).

So, this means that Islam, the last divine message to mankind is wide, clear and straight. It is wide and clear so it shouldn’t be a constraint on people. A person who perceives that the teaching of Islam is constraining is either not understanding Islam or such a person is adding to it constraints that are not part of it, or such a person is morally corrupt. I am saying that because unless a person feels that the prohibitions of injustice, betrayal, lying, stealing and backbiting are constraining, such a person shouldn’t feel constrained. All rules that Islam imposes are intended to achieve happiness and security for the whole society. All the restrictions in Islam are few and very beneficial.

Verse 5 affirms that the Quran was revelaed by Allah and the verse provides two of His glorious names it says:

تَنزِيلَ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ (٥)

(This is a Revelation) sent down by the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful,

You can spend some time studying the two names of Allah in this verse ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ, to know what are the attributes associated with these names and how you can adopt elements of these attributes in your own character. In the famous Hadeath narrated by Abu Hurriarah and reported in Al-Bukhari, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسمًا، مائةً إلا واحدًا، من أحصاها دخل الجنة

“Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one, whoever “Ahsaha” them will enter Paradise.”

This simple Hadeath represents the cornerstone of belief and the building blocks of the character of the believer. However, to understand its significance we need to understand the meaning of the Arabic word “احصى” “Ahsaha” that is often translated inaccurately as “count”. However, the term “احصى” is related to the word “Ihsaa” which is a branch of mathematics called “statistics” that involves data collection, organization, and analysis and not just counting.

Ibn Abbas said: The word “Ahsaha” involves two elements, the first is to learn the names from the Quran and the sunnah, and the second is to apply them.

The same idea of this definition is stated by Imam Al-Ghazali who said: “Whoever has no part of the meaning of the names of Allah other than understanding their meanings and believing in them is ill-fated and of lowly rank. Those of high rank are those who adopt share of the meaning of His names and have longing and passionate love to possess these attributes as much as humanly possible”.

So, studying this verse will allow you to identify the gaps in your character that prevents you from reaching higher ranks in being (عَزِيزِ رَّحِيمِ).

Verse 6 moves to inform the Prophet and in turn us that the purpose of the Quran is to warn people whose fathers were not warned to bring them this message. The verse reads:

لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمً۬ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَـٰفِلُونَ (٦)

That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless.” (36: 1-6).

Note that verse speaks of undefined people (قَوۡمً۬ا) meaning any people who are not aware of this message and not specific ones. Obviously, when the message is delivered some people will heed the warning and accept it and others will reject it.

The following verses will be addressing the two groups. We will address Inshallah next time, but next week we will have a special presentation by Justice Shazado that will start at 7:00

Asalamu Alykum WRAWB
