content:
The Divine System: Expect Rejection and Face with Patience

Friday 12/27/2020     mamdouh.salama@comcast.net

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه  ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

In my last talk on the role of the stories in the Quran I mentioned that stories in the Quran serve as very important tool for demonstrating Allah’s system and laws on earth.  They also serve as a tool to help Muslims at younger age to develop their cognitive capacity.

In this talk, I will, inshallah, attempt to identify a key divine law that seems to permeate throughout many of the stories in the Quran.   This divine law is: “Resistance of the truth is natural and the road of the believers is full with barriers and hurdles and success of believers is not measured by achieving materialistic victory but by the demonstration of their persistence and patience”.   Realizing this basic law makes it quite understandable and actually comforting that Islamophobia exists, otherwise we may need to question whether we are truly on the right path. Here, I am defining Islamophobia as hatred of and prejudice towards Muslims and Islam.

True believers whose role on earth is to deliver the truth must expect resistance and harm.  However, this harm no matter how extensive it may appear, it is not major as Allah says:
لَن يَضُرُّوڪُمۡ إِلَّآ أَذً۬ى‌ۖ (١١١)
“They will not harm you except a trifling hurt.” (Al-Imran 3:111)

True believers know that no harm will ever reach them unless Allah has decreed it for them.  Abdullah bin Abbas (عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِي) said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: “كُنْت خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَوْمًا، فَقَالَ: احْفَظْ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْك، احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَك، إذَا سَأَلْت فَاسْأَلْ اللَّهَ، وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْت فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاَللَّهِ،  وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْأُمَّةَ لَوْ اجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَى أَنْ يَنْفَعُوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَنْفَعُوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ لَك، وَإِنْ اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى أَنْ يَضُرُّوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَضُرُّوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْك؛ رُفِعَتْ الْأَقْلَامُ، وَجَفَّتْ الصُّحُفُ” . رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ
“Be mindful of Allah and Allah will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him in front of you. If you ask, then ask Allah [alone]; and if you seek help, then seek help from Allah [alone]. And know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with anything, they would not benefit you except with what Allah had already prescribed for you. And if they were to gather together to harm you with anything, they would not harm you except with what Allah had already prescribed against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.”  (whatever we face is already predestined)

In studying the life of all the Prophets in the Quran, we realize the common theme that all of them had been rejected and all of them faced major suffering and resistance.  In fact, all of them were not able to convince many of their communities. This in spite the fact that they were given divine message and were supported by Allah.   When you face ridicule of people who will look down at you and say: are you the one who will guide us to the truth, do not be surprised because the same was said to the Prophet (PBUH) as Allah reported to us:

وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ قَالُواْ هَـٰذَا سِحۡرٌ۬ وَإِنَّا بِهِۦ كَـٰفِرُونَ (٣٠) وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَتَيۡنِ عَظِيمٍ (٣١)
“But when the truth came to them, they said, “This is mere magic, and we totally disbelieve in it.” (30) They say, “Why was this Qur’an not revealed on a great man of the two towns?” (Al-Zukhruf 43:30-31) (They are basically saying, couldn’t God found someone better than you to send his message).

We read the story of Prophet Noah who spent 950 years preaching the message of Allah to his people and remained patient against their continuous ridicule and insults. 
وَيَصۡنَعُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ وَڪُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَأٌ۬ مِّن قَوۡمِهِۦ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُ‌ۚ (٣٨)
“And as he was constructing the ship; whenever the chiefs of his people passed by him, they mocked at him.” (Hud 11:38)

Ridicule and insults are common response against the believers, Allah says: 
إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ۬ مِّنۡ عِبَادِى يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَا وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٲحِمِينَ (١٠٩) فَٱتَّخَذۡتُمُوهُمۡ سِخۡرِيًّا حَتَّىٰٓ أَنسَوۡكُمۡ ذِكۡرِى وَكُنتُم مِّنۡہُمۡ تَضۡحَكُونَ (١١٠)
“There was indeed a group of My servants who used to say, ‘Our Lord, we believe, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of all the merciful.’ (109) But you took them for a laughing-stock until they caused you to forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them.” (Al-Munenoun 23:109-110)

When we study what happened to the Prophet (PBUH) and his early companions, we realize the amount of suffering and insults they have faced.   So, the human history as reported in the Quran is full with the accounts of insults against the people of Allah because the reality is that most people will remain disbelievers as Allah says:
وَمَآ أَڪۡثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَوۡ حَرَصۡتَ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ (١٠٣)
“Most of the people are not going to believe, no matter how much you try”. (Yusuf 12:103)

None of the ridicule and insults of Muslims and even Islam that sometimes we witness these days should be surprising because Allah gave us enough lessons from history of the ridicule, insults and the rejections that Prophets and their followers faced.   Allah says:

وَكَذَٲلِكَ جَعَلۡنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِىٍّ عَدُوًّ۬ا شَيَـٰطِينَ ٱلۡإِنسِ وَٱلۡجِنِّ يُوحِى بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ زُخۡرُفَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ غُرُورً۬ا‌ۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ‌ۖ فَذَرۡهُمۡ وَمَا يَفۡتَرُونَ (١١٢)
“That is the way, for every prophet, We have set up enemies, devils of mankind and jinn who seduce one another with alluring rhetoric in order to deceive.  Had Allah willed, they would have not done it. So, leave them alone with their false claims;” (Al-Ana’am 6:112)

It will be naïve for us after we learn about all these historical experiences to be surprised or even complain about what we call Islamophobia. If we don’t suffer as a result of being steadfast on Islam, we should question ourselves regarding the extent of the compromises that are making to Allah’s religion. 

The rule of Allah is that Muslims who promote the truth and wanted to remain on the path of Allah will have to face difficulties and this is not because the people who inflict harm on them are rejecting the truth of Islam, they actually are not.  But the important point is that we should be convinced that Islam is the truth because Allah assured us that we are on clear truth and all we need is to put our full trust on Him as He said:

فَتَوكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَى ٱلۡحَقِّ ٱلۡمُبِينِ (٧٩)
“So put trust in Allah. Surely you are on the clear/plain truth” (Al-Naml 27:97)

Exposing people to the truth and to what is logical and beneficial revelation and they accepting it are completely different. This paradox is a result of the freedom of choice that Allah granted human beings. This why you find a prophet whom Allah sent to his tripe or nation spent years preaching to them and only few accepts and in some case no one accepts. The Prophet (PBUH) reported on something he saw during his trip of ascension (Al-Miarag). He (PBUH) said:  
حدثنا ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال عرضت علي الأمم فرأيت النبي ومعه الرهيط والنبي ومعه الرجل والرجلان والنبي ليس معه أحد
“I saw a prophet coming with few followers and saw a prophet with him only one follower and saw a prophet and no one with him.”

So, you should never be disappointed or discouraged when you invite people to Islam and you face utter rejection.   Allah provided several reasons for such illogical rejection and these include:

First: Sheer injustice and arrogance, Allah says:
وَجَحَدُواْ بِہَا وَٱسۡتَيۡقَنَتۡهَآ أَنفُسُہُمۡ ظُلۡمً۬ا وَعُلُوًّ۬ا‌ۚ (١٤)
“And they denied them out of sheer injustice and arrogance, though their hearts believed them (to be true).” (Al-Naml 27:14)

Second: Fear of loss of their livelihood.  This may actually be the case for many Muslim rulers who know that Islam is the truth but they fight against it in fear of loss of their power, Allah says:
وَقَالُوٓاْ إِن نَّتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفۡ مِنۡ أَرۡضِنَآ‌ۚ (٥٧)
“And they say: If we were to follow the Guidance with you, we will be driven out of our land.” (Al-Qasa 28:57)

Third: Jealousy even though they know that you are following the truth, they will not only resist you but they will also try to force you to deviate from the truth to be like them. Knowing that, your reaction should not be anger and hate but rather forgiveness. Patience and tolerance of their negative behaviors. As Allah says:

وَدَّ ڪَثِيرٌ۬ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لَوۡ يَرُدُّونَكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ إِيمَـٰنِكُمۡ كُفَّارًا حَسَدً۬ا مِّنۡ عِندِ أَنفُسِهِم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا Tَـبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ‌ۖ فَٱعۡفُواْ وَٱصۡفَحُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِىَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۤ‌ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ ڪُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬ (١٠٩)
“Many among the people of the Book desire to make you disbelievers after your belief, all out of envy on their part, even after the truth has become clear to them. So, forgive and overlook till Allah brings out His command. Certainly, Allah is powerful over everything.” (Al-Baqara 2:109)

Fourth: People have hard time changing form the path of their forefathers even if the path is wrong and this was the excuse of many in the past. 

وَكَذَٲلِكَ مَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ فِى قَرۡيَةٍ۬ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتۡرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةٍ۬ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّقۡتَدُونَ (٢٣) ۞ قَـٰلَ أَوَلَوۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِأَهۡدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَكُمۡ‌ۖ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَـٰفِرُونَ (٢٤)
“That is the way, We did not send a warner to a town before you, but its affluent people said, “We have found our fathers on a certain way, and we are following their footprints.” (23) He said, “Even if I bring to you something better in guidance than that on which you have found your fathers?” They said, “We totally disbelieve in what you are sent with.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:23-24)

Allah informs us from the stories of the Prophets that no matter how much threats He inflicts on the disbelievers to stop hurting the believers, most of them will not heed Allah’s warnings and will renege on their commitment to believe if the harm is removed from them. This should temper our enthusiasm that the Coronavirus will change the people and bring them close to Allah.  Allah reminds us of this reality in the story of the People of Egypt: 

وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَقَالَ إِنِّى رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٤٦) فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنۡہَا يَضۡحَكُونَ (٤٧) وَمَا نُرِيهِم مِّنۡ ءَايَةٍ إِلَّا هِىَ أَڪۡبَرُ مِنۡ أُخۡتِهَا‌ۖ وَأَخَذۡنَـٰهُم بِٱلۡعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ (٤٨) وَقَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهۡتَدُونَ (٤٩) فَلَمَّا كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡہُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابَ إِذَا هُمۡ يَنكُثُونَ (٥٠)
“We sent Musa with Our signs to Fir’aun (Pharaoh) and his chiefs; so he said, “I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds.” (46) So, when he came to them with Our signs, they at once started laughing at them. (47) And We did not show them a sign, but it used to be greater than the one that preceded it. And We seized them with punishment, so that they may return. (48) And they said, “O magician, pray for us to your Lord by the covenant He has made with you; we will certainly come to guidance.” (49) Then, once We removed the punishment from them, in no time they broke their promise.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:46-50)

These accounts should make it clear that the rule of Allah in earth is that the believers are not engaged in a dash game where the runner do not expect any barrier in the track but they are engaged in a hurdling completion where the runners expect many barriers along the track.   Muslims should not expect a clear and easy road in front of them but they should be aware that they will be facing many hurdle and obstacles all the way.

When you study the Seerah, you note that the Prophet (PBUH) faced a lot of resistance and was attacked both physically and verbally.  These could have caused anyone who faces such barriers to at least compromise a little.  The thought of compromise may have actually came in the mind of the prophet (PBUH) and thus Allah gave the staunch warning to eliminate any hope of the disbelievers that the Prophet (PBUH) may compromise with them.  Allah says in Surat Al-Isra: 

وَإِن ڪَادُواْ لَيَفۡتِنُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ لِتَفۡتَرِىَ عَلَيۡنَا غَيۡرَهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَإِذً۬ا لَّٱتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلاً۬ (٧٣) وَلَوۡلَآ أَن ثَبَّتۡنَـٰكَ لَقَدۡ كِدتَّ تَرۡڪَنُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا قَلِيلاً (٧٤) إِذً۬ا لَّأَذَقۡنَـٰكَ ضِعۡفَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ وَضِعۡفَ ٱلۡمَمَاتِ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ عَلَيۡنَا نَصِيرً۬ا (٧٥)
“And they indeed were about to lure you away from what We have revealed (the Qur’ân) unto you, to forge something else against Us, and then they would certainly have taken you as a close friend! (73) And had We not made you firm you would have likely inclined to them a little. (74) In that case, We would have made you taste a double portion (of punishment) in this life and a double portion (of punishment) after death. And then you would not have found anyone to help you against Us”. (Al-Isra 17:73-75). 

These verses declaring this severe warning against compromising in the religion should not be interpreted as only relevant to the Prophet (PBUH) but it is for anyone who is committed to deliver the message of Islam.   The religion must be presented in its pure nature without any modification, even minor ones.

Why Muslims compromise in their religion?  Mainly for two reasons:
One reason is to avoid the discrimination and harm imposed by others
The second reason is trying to make Islam more acceptable to others. We probably see this is being done by some Islamic organizations to avoid being accused of being anti certain groups whose practices are clearly forbidden by Allah. 

Muslims who try to compromise to make Islam palatable to others fail to understand the system that Allah clearly identified for us in the Quran thru the stories of many prophets. 
First, the role of those whom Allah selected to deliver His message is not to convert people to believe in Allah.  Their sole role is only to deliver the message and be steadfast in delivering the true message even if no one accepts it.   Getting discouraged and quitting by assuming that those people are hopeless case is a crime in the sight of Allah that deserves punishment.  The punishment of Prophet Yunus  because he abandoned his role as messenger when he faced complete rejection from his people is clear demonstration of this divine law.
وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (١٣٩) إِذۡ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلۡمَشۡحُونِ (١٤٠) فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُدۡحَضِينَ (١٤١) فَٱلۡتَقَمَهُ ٱلۡحوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ۬ (١٤٢)
“And Indeed, Yunus (Jonah) was one of the Messengers (139) When he ran away to  the loaded ship, (140) And he participated in drawing lots and was among the losers; (141) Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. ” (Al-Saffat 37:139-142)
Second, achieving victory for the believers against their enemies is not part of the deal that Allah made with the believers. The only deal that Allah made with the believers is that if they made sacrifices and demonstrated clear patience against all temptations and difficulties, He will grant them paradise. If victory is achieved, it is a bonus from Allah but it is not part of the deal.  The nature of this agreement is clear in Surat Al-Saffat: 

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَـٰرَةٍ۬ تُنجِيكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ۬ (١٠) تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَـٰهِدُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٲلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكُمۡ خَيۡرٌ۬ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ (١١) يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡ وَيُدۡخِلۡكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡہَـٰرُ وَمَسَـٰكِنَ طَيِّبَةً۬ فِى جَنَّـٰتِ عَدۡنٍ۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ (١٢)
“O You who believe! Shall I tell you to a trade that saves you from a painful punishment? (10) That you believe in Allah and His Messenger, and that you should strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives, that will be better for you, if you but know! (11) (If you do so) He will forgive you your sins, and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden Paradise; that is indeed the supreme success.” (Al-Saffat 61:10-12)
This is the agreement, there is no victory in it, you want great success in the Hereafter, you need to believe and sacrifice with your wealth and life. This is the deal.  But then Allah added, out of his mercy, a bonus that is not part of the main agreement and thus many righteous generations never witnessed this bonus. The bonus which is not part of the deal is:
وَأُخۡرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَہَا‌ۖ نَصۡرٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَتۡحٌ۬ قَرِيبٌ۬‌ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ (١٣)
And another thing which you love, help from Allah and a victory, near at hand. And give glad tidings to the believers. (Al-Saffat 61:13)

But for this victory to come, the group must demonstrate their absolute belief in Allah in face of all difficulties and this is manifested by their clear patience and commitment to sacrifice their money and life. The criticality of patience is clearly demonstrated in the story of Talut who devised a test to remove from his army anyone who is not patient and willing to face hardships. This is contrary to the general practice of any leader of an army whose goal would be to preserve his forces not to reduce them by putting severe qualification test on them.  Allah presented to us this account:
“So, when Talut (Saul) set out with the army, he said: “Verily! Allah will try you by a river. Whosoever drinks from it, he is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, he is of me, except him who takes (thereof) in the hollow of his hand.” Yet, they drank from it except a few of them.
فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبۡتَلِيڪُم بِنَهَرٍ۬ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنۡهُ فَلَيۡسَ مِنِّى وَمَن لَّمۡ يَطۡعَمۡهُ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ مِنِّىٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغۡتَرَفَ غُرۡفَةَۢ بِيَدِهِۦ‌ۚ فَشَرِبُواْ مِنۡهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ مِّنۡهُمۡ‌ۚ
So, when he had crossed it (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: “We have no power this day against Jalut (Goliath) and his troops.” But those who knew with certainty that they were to meet their Lord, said: “How often a small group overcame a mighty army by the will of Allah?” And Allah is with those who remain patient.  (249) 
فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ ۥ هُوَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُ ۥ قَالُواْ لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ‌ۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَـٰقُواْ ٱللَّهِ ڪَم مِّن فِئَةٍ۬ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةً۬ ڪَثِيرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ (٢٤٩)
And when they faced Jalut (Goliath) and his forces, they said: “Our Lord! Bestow on us patience, and make firm our feet and make us victorious over the disbelieving people.” (250) So, they defeated them by the will of Allah”. (Al-Baqara 2:249-251)
وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرً۬ا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ (٢٥٠) فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ

This story is very important because it shows that Muslims do not gain victory by their numbers.  Islam is not a political party whose goal is the maximize the number of its members.  Tault wanted to have an elite team whose members have demonstrated extremely high level of patience. 
Islam is an elite system that only wants the best to join in. You can think of what Talut was doing is filtering his army to identify the SEALS among them.  As you know the U.S. Navy SEALs are an elite unit that is more exclusive and harder to be admitted to than the U.S. Marines. The US marines has about 250,000 marines, the seals among them are less than 2500 which is less than 1%.  If the 1.4 billion Muslims who are alive today are filtered to the same level, they will be less than 14 million in the whole world.

To summarize, true victory in this life is proportional to our level of patience in facing the barriers that will be placed in front of us and in our ability to resist the temptations of compromise. True Believers never get discouraged or complain about the barriers they face but they rather express their gratitude to Allah for giving them the strength to face these barriers and hardships.  The reward of this is paradise and may be some form of worldly victory but this is secondary. The ability to face difficulties should be the primary objective. If this is the system of Allah for his believers, why should we be complaining about Islamophobia, shouldn’t this be something natural and expected and may even be cherished instead of despised. 

The stories in the Quran and the Seerah of the Prophet (PBUH) inform us of groups who demonstrated ultimate patience but never witnessed materialistic victory.  The story of the believers who were burnt alive in the trench in Surat Al-Buroog (85) is an example.
Cursed were the People of the Trench, (4) of the fuel-fed fire, (5) When they sat by it, (6) And were witnessing what they were doing to the believers. (7)
قُتِلَ أَصۡحَـٰبُ ٱلۡأُخۡدُودِ (٤) ٱلنَّارِ ذَاتِ ٱلۡوَقُودِ (٥) إِذۡ هُمۡ عَلَيۡہَا قُعُودٌ۬ (٦) وَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفۡعَلُونَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ شُہُودٌ۬ (٧)
They punished them for nothing but that they believed in Allah, the All-Mighty, the Worthy of All Praise, (8) The One to whom belongs the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is witness over everything. (9)
وَمَا نَقَمُواْ مِنۡہُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَمِيدِ (٨) ٱلَّذِى لَهُ ۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ شَہِيدٌ (٩)
Surely, those who persecuted the believing men and the believing women and did not repent, for them there is the torment of Hell, and for them there is the torment of burning. (10) As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them there are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the Great Success. (Al-Burooj 85:4-11)
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَتَنُواْ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَتوبُواْ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ (١٠) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٌ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِہَا ٱلۡأَنۡہَـٰرُ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ (١١)

How about the early Muslims such as Sumiah (سمية), Yasir (ياسر), Mus’ab (مصعب), Hamza (حمزة) and many others who were killed without seeing the victory of Islam.   They made the ultimate sacrifice in the beginning of the road and did not enjoy the materialistic fruits of what they started but they are enjoying the fruits of the deal they made with Allah which is paradise.  

We should not worry about how far we are from the end of the road; all we should care about is being on the road and this is the road of patience and gratitude that leads to paradise.
We pray to Allah to grant us the wisdom and the ability to always be patient in facing all difficulties so we would not make any compromises in our religion.   

DUA

content:
The Role of the Stories in the Quran and the True Story of John the Baptist (Prophet Yahya)

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

When you study the Quran, you will note that almost 1/3 of the Quran is stories.   This means that the stories in the Quran offer major learning and development tools for Muslims.  The stories in the Quran are not intended for entertainment, though they will, but they are intended to achieve at least two objectives.

1. Demonstrate the divine laws, approach and methodology (منهج)
2. Develop the cognitive capacity of Muslims from younger age.

Therefore, the stories in the Quran are not based on imaginary events or fables but rather they are based on real human experiences that are mostly unknown, even to those who lived at that time of their occurrence.  Since many stories in the Quran present the application of the divine laws on nations that have vanished, they present some events that are only known to Allah.  Through these stories, Allah unveils to us certain events from the unseen world.

These events from the unseen world are either related to conditions that only Allah knows, or conditions that only those who were intimately associated with them know.  But others who even existed at that time are unaware of them.  This point is critical because you may find old books speak about stories in the Quran but from the hearsay point of view and thus includes many fabrications.  The only accurate account of any story is the presentation in the Quran.

Because of the importance of the stories in presenting Allah’s rules, Allah commanded Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) to relate the stories to Muslins to make them think, as He said in Surat Al-Araf:

فَاقْصُصِ الْقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١٧٦)
“So, relate the stories, perhaps they may think/ponder/reflect.” (Al-Araf 7:175-176)

We often give a writer or a speaker who impresses us the title (مفكر اسلامى) “Islamic Thinker or Islamic Intellectual”. But the truth is that Allah wanted every Muslim to be an Islamic thinker.  And the way to become an Islamic thinker is to study the stories in the Quran.

Since the stories in the Quran present the practical application of the divine laws, it is important that we study them seriously to identify the divine laws whether they are physical or social based on these fully accurate and relevant human experiences.  We can derive these divine laws using the induction approach of scientific studies.

As you know, there are mainly three scientific approaches for identifying laws in nature whether these laws are related to natural or social sciences. These three approaches are:

1. The Induction Approach: It involves the observation of many real events and identifying the common factors among them and thus you will be able to say if these conditions exist, the outcome should be as follows.
2. The Experimental Approach: It involves running large number of experiments to achieve certain results and when one of them succeed, this experiment is repeated several times to confirm the conclusion.
3. The Deduction Approach: It involves noting a relationship between certain initial conditions and a result and thus when a result is observed, the initial conditions are assumed to have been present.  This is often used in the court by saying since this happened and this happened and this happened, this must have happened.

The stories in the Quran offer us the ability to use the induction approach to derive the divine laws and then use the deduction approach to explain current conditions and predict future events.  But this requires serious analysis of the stories in the Quran.  Unfortunately, this is extremely lacking among the Islamic literature.  May be this gap remained, so everyone of us will have the opportunity to contribute to the advancement of Islamic thoughts.

Because the importance of the stories in the Quran, Allah says at the end of Surat Yusuf:

لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ۬ لِّأُوْلِى ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ‌ۗ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثً۬ا يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحْمَةً۬ لِّقَوْمٍ۬ يُؤْمِنُونَ (١١١)
“Indeed, in their stories, there is a lesson for the people of understanding. It is not a forged story but a confirmation of what existed before it (previous scripture) and a detailed explanation of everything and guidance and Mercy for the people who believe.” (Yusuf 12: 111)

This verse identifies four key values of the stories in the Quran as: 1) Lessons (عِبْرَةٌ۬), 2) explanation of everything (وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ۬), 3) guidance (وَهُدً۬ى) and 4) Mercy (وَرَحْمَةً۬).  But the verse also identifies the two attributes of those who will benefit from these stories and these are: 1) intellect (لِّأُوْلِى ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ) and 2) belief (لِّقَوْمٍ۬ يُؤْمِنُونَ).

Allah describes the stories in the Quran as the best stories that should elevate you to the state of Ihsam at which you will feel seeing Allah and if you have not reached the level of righteousness of this feeling, you are fully confidence that He is seeing you all the time.  Allah says:

نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلْغَـٰفِلِينَ (٣)
“We relate unto you the best of stories through Our Revelations unto you, of this Quran. And before this, you were among those who are unaware (of it).” (Yusuf 12: 3)

The challenge that we often face when studying the stories in the Quran is that books of Tafseer can actually cloud our understanding and shield the real knowledge that exists in the Quranic stories because of integrating in them false accounts from other books.  This is why it is so critical that you should not study the stories in the Quran from any other source other the Quran itself and the authentic sayings of the Prophet (PBUH).

The use of other sources such as the Old testament creates confusion and leads to misguidance.  In my previous talk I discussed Prophet Dawud and Prophet Suliman; unfortunately, some books of tafseer mixed some stories form the old testaments with the authentic account in the Quran to create false projections that is causing major geopolitical issue for Muslims in our current time.

The issue I am talking about is related to some of Islamic books that made the claim that the Prophet Solomon’s Temple (هيكل سليمان) was built in the same place where the Masjid Al-Aqsa is now built.  This wild speculation was unfortunately advanced by both Ibn Khaldun (عبد الرحمن ابن خلدون) and Ibn Al-Wardy (زين الدين ابن الوردي) and propagated by some later Muslim writers.

Ibn Khaldun (أبو زيد عبد الرحمن بن محمد بن خلدون الحضرمي‎) [born in 1332 AD (732 AH) and died in 1406 AD).
Ibn al-Wardī (عمر ابن مظفر ابن الوردي‎) [born in 1291 (691 AH) and died in 1348 AD]

There is absolutely no reference in the Quran or the Sunnah or even a statement in the Old Testament that places the two buildings at the same location.  The current archeological effort by Israel that involves digging under the Masjid Al-Aqsa in search for Solomon’s temple is based on the unfortunate account by Muslims.  This digging is continuing even when this speculation is rejected by many Muslim scholars and even by many archeologists.  But Israel continues to explore with the goal to destroy Al-Aqsa Masjid.

This is just one example to illustrate the danger that can happen when other books are used to give tafseer of accounts in the Quran.  The Quran is very clear that Prophet Sulaiman has a kingdom that no one has seen before and no one will ever see it after.

The Quran informs us of a unique castle/palace that Prophet Sulaiman had and that it was made of pure glass.

قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدْخُلِى ٱلصَّرْحَ‌ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً۬ وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا‌ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ صَرْحٌ۬ مُّمَرَّدٌ۬ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ‌ۗ قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَـٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ (٤٤)
“It was said to her, “Enter the castle (palace).” When she saw it, she thought it was flowing water, and uncovered her legs. He (Sulaiman) said, “This is a palace made of glasses.” She said, “My Lord, I had surely wronged myself, and now I submit, along with Sulaiman, to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.” (Al-Naml 27:44)

This castle as mentioned in the Quran is made of pure glass that is completely transparent and as we know glass does not degrade or decompose by time.  Also, it seems that it cannot break easily since many people used to enter this castle because it was the place of government for Prophet Sulaiman and it was also the place to meet the dignitaries and this is where Prophet Suliman met the queen of Yemen.  It is interesting that Archaeologists have been trying for years to uncover parts of the kingdom of Prophet Sulaiman but nothing has been discovered yet.

We know from the Quran that the first house of worship that was built on earth was the sacred Masjid in Mecca and based on an authentic hadeath the second masjid was Al-Aqsa masjid in Jerusalem and it was built 40 years after the Sacred Mosque.  This means that Al-Aqsa Masjid existed far before the time of Prophet Sulaiman and no way he would have built a place or castle on it.

Is what the Jews are searching for the glass castle or are they looking for another building that they call Solomon’s Temple (هيكل سليمان) in which the box that contains the remains of Prophet’s Musa and Haroun exists.  The Quran informs us of a sign that Allah offered to Bani Israel to convince them that Talut was selected as their king.  This sign was that the angles will bring to him the remains of Prophet’s Musa and Haroun in a box.  Allah says in Surat Al-Baqara:

وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ ءَايَةَ مُلْكِهِۦۤ أَن يَأْتِيَكُمُ ٱلتَّابُوتُ فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَبَقِيَّةٌ۬ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ءَالُ مُوسَىٰ وَءَالُ هَـٰرُونَ تَحْمِلُهُ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً۬ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (٢٤٨)
“Their prophet said to them (Bani Israel): “The sign of his kingship (kingship of Talut) is that the At-Tabut (a wooden box) (Ark) shall come to you having therein tranquility from your Lord, and the remains of what the House of Musa (Moses) and the House of Harun (Aaron) had left, carried by the angels, Surely, in it there is a sign for you, if you are believers.” (Al-Baqara 2:248)

This wooden chest, named in the Bible as the Ark of the Covenant, contains the Tablets of Torah and some remains of the prophets (A.S).  This Ark was taken away from Bani Israel by their enemies; so Allah declared that it would be a sign of the appointment of Talut as king that the Ark would come back to them carried by angels.  Where is this box now, no one knows, though there are indications that it exists in Ethiopia?  But the Jews are looking for it under the Al-Aqsa Masjid based on Muslims’ writings because as I said, unfortunately, Ibn Khaldun suggested that this castle of pure glass is where the Ark of Covenant was placed and this where the Aqsa Masjid is now.

Here we see that going beyond what the Quran says regarding authentic historical events can lead to problems.  This is why the Prophet (PBUH) prevented the companies from using the previous books to explain anything in the Quran since anything of relevance is already included in the Quran as Allah says:

وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ تِبْيَانًا لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً وَبُشْرَى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ (٨٩)
We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur’an) as an exposition/explanation of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and glad tidings for the Muslims. (Al-Nahl 16:89)

It is the responsibility of every Muslim who has intellect and believer to study these stories and derive the truth from them as Allah says:

لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ۬ لِّأُوْلِى ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ‌ۗ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثً۬ا يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحْمَةً۬ لِّقَوْمٍ۬ يُؤْمِنُونَ (١١١)
“Indeed, in their stories, there is a lesson for the people of understanding. It is not a forged story but a confirmation of what existed before it (previous scripture) and a detailed explanation of everything and guidance and Mercy for the people who believe.” (Yusuf 12: 111)

One of the stories in the Quran that have been infiltrated with references from the Old Testament in many books of Tafseer and thus lead to complete misunderstanding and even derogatory description of a Prophet of Allah is the story of Prophet Yahya (John the Baptist).

The first step in understanding the history of Prophet Yahya is to assemble all the verses related to him in the Quran and any authentic hadeath.  The name of Prophet Yahya (يحيى) was mentioned in the Quran 5 times, in surat Al-Imran, (39) آل عمران, Al-An’am (85) الأنعام, Maryam (7 and 12) مريم and Al-Anbia (90) الأنبياء. The main account about him came in Surat Maryam (مريم).

Let me highlight 4 key observations that one can note based on these verses:

First the name of Prophet Yaha was given to him by Allah and therefore the name must have significance.  Allah says:

يَـٰزَڪَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَـٰمٍ ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّ۬ا (٧)
“O Zakariya, We give you the good news of a boy whose name is Yahya. We did not create any one before him of the same name. (Maryam 19:7)

The name Yahya mean to “The one to Live”. If Allah is calling him the one to live, it will be hard to accept that he will be killed but rather that he is still alive.

But this assumption that Prophet Yahya was not killed may be challenged by someone who may say that if Prophet Yahya was killed by king Herod for refusing to compromise the divine laws as reported in the book of Tafseer based on the Old Testament, this makes him a martyr and the Quran states that the Martyrs are always alive as Allah says:

وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ يُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتٌ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ وَلَكِنْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ (١٥٤)
“Do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah that they are dead. Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive it.” (Al-Baqara 2:154)

وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ (١٦٩)
“Do not think of those who are killed in the way of Allah that they are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, well-provided,” (Al-Imran 2:169)

Therefore, being killed as Martyr does not violate the name that Allah gave him as Yahya (the one to live) because he would have remained alive with Allah.  But this suggestion can be easily rejected because it contradicts the other attribute that Allah stated in the verse that (لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّ۬ا) “no one before him have been given this attribute”.  There were, obviously, many people before him who died as Martyrs and thus, he would not be unique.

Second: When we study the hadeath of the Prophet’s ascension (المعراج) to heaven we note that he saw different Prophets with only one Prophet in each heaven except in the 2nd heaven where he saw both Prophet Jesus (Isa) and Prophet John (Yahya).

In the 1st heaven, the Prophet (PBUH) saw Prophet Adam
In the 3rd heaven, he saw Prophet Joseph (Yusuf).
In the 4th heaven, he saw Prophet Enoch (Idris).
In the 5th heaven, he saw Prophet Aaron (Harun)
In the 6th heaven, he saw Prophet Moses (Musa).
In the 7th heaven, he saw Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim).
In the 2nd heaven, the Prophet (PBUH) saw both Prophet Jesus (Isa) and Prophet John (Yahya).  This is the only heaven where there were two Prophets suggesting that there is clear connection between these two Prophets that is even more relevant than the connection between Prophets Musa and Haroun who were separated in Heaven.

Third:  In reading the Quran, we will note a very strong similarity and connection between Prophet Isa (Jesus) and Prophet Yahya (John the Baptist). The following are few examples:

Prophet Jesus (Isa)
قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَـٰمٌ۬ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ۬ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّ۬ا (٢٠) قَالَ كَذَٲلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ۬‌ۖ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُۥۤ ءَايَةً۬ لِّنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً۬ مِّنَّا‌ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرً۬ا مَّقْضِيًّ۬ا (٢١)
She said, “How shall I have a boy while no human has ever touched me, nor have I ever been unchaste?” (20) He said, “So it is; your Lord said, ‘It is easy for Me, and so that We make it a sign for people and a mercy from Us, and this is a matter already destined.’” (Maryam 20-21)

Prophet Yahya (John)
قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَـٰمٌ۬ وَڪَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرً۬ا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ ٱلْڪِبَرِ عِتِيًّ۬ا (٨) قَالَ كَذَٲلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ۬ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْـًٔ۬ا (٩)
He Said, “My Lord, how shall there be a boy for me while my wife is barren, and I have reached the extreme of old age?” (8) He said, “So it is; your Lord said ‘it is easy for Me, and I did create you before, when you were nothing.’” (Maryam 8-9)

Prophet Jesus (Isa)
فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْبَشَرِ أَحَدً۬ا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ صَوْمً۬ا فَلَنْ أُڪَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّ۬ا (٢٦)
If you see any human being, say (to him), “I have vowed a fast (of silence) for the Al-Rahman and therefore, I shall never speak to any human today.” (Maryam 26)

Prophet Yahya (John)
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً۬‌ۚ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَـٰثَ لَيَالٍ۬ سَوِيًّ۬ا (١٠)
He said, “My Lord, make for me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not (be able to) speak to the people for three (consecutive) nights, even though you will be sound in health.” (Maryam 10)

Prophet Jesus (Isa)
وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٲلِدَتِى وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِى جَبَّارً۬ا شَقِيًّ۬ا (٣٢) وَٱلسَّلَـٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوْمُ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّ۬ا (٣٣)
And (He has made me) good to my mother, and he did not make me oppressive (or) ill-fated. (32) And peace is upon me the day I was born, the day I shall die, and the day I shall be raised alive again.” (Maryam 32-33)

Prophet Yahya (John)
وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٲلِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّ۬ا (١٤) وَسَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّ۬ا (١٥)
And he was good to his parents; and he was not oppressive (or) disobedient. (14) Peace on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive. (Maryam 14-15)

Fourth: The Quran shows that Prophet Yahya will be accused of being oppressor and disobedient (جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا) and Allah refuted this claim.  But this means that the claim will be made and this cannot happen unless Prophet Yahya will be in a position of authority. Also, his description as master and seizer (وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا) in Surat Al-Imran:

أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَى مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٣٩)
“Allah gives you the good news of Yahya who shall come to confirm a word of Allah and shall be master (chief), Hasora (حَصُورًا) and a prophet among the righteous.” (Al-Imran 3:39)

Allah described Prophet Yahya as being (سَيِّدًا) that can be translated as master and chief and thus suggesting that he will be in position of authority.

Allah also described Prophet Yahya as being Hasora (حَصُورًا) and this term is derived from the root that means “put to siege” and the form of the term is what is known as the subjective name (اسم فاعل) means that he is the one who is putting others under siege.

This suggest that he must serve in a position of power and leadership to put his enemies under siege and this justifies his enemies accusing him of being oppressor and disobedient (جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا) that Allah refuted.

Unfortunately, many books of Tafseer made the interpretation that “Hasora” (حَصُورًا) means that he put his desires under siege and abstained from women.  Obviously, this is not something that Allah ever suggested as good.  But to understand the meaning of “Hasora” (حَصُورًا), we need to consider the other attributes that Allah attributed to him such as master/chief (سَيِّدًا) and also the attributes that he will be accused of as oppressor and disobedient (جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا).

We can understand that the people whom he will put under siege will accuse him of being oppressor (جَبَّارًا) but why they would accuse of him of being disobedient (عَصِيًّا).

Now we can make the hypothesis that Prophet Yaya did not die but similar to Prophet Isa was raised up alive and he will return back and rule for while and will die natural death.  In his return, he will be following the religion of Islam as revelae d to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH).  He will be accused of being disobedient because his enemies will tell him that is not following the example of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) who was kind even with his enemies and that the Quran teaches the kind treatment of the prisoners as Allah said:

وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا (٨) إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا (٩)
“And they (the righteous) feed, out of their love for Him (Allah), to the needy, and the orphan, and the prisoner, (8) (Saying) “We feed you only for the sake of Allah; We wish no reward nor thanks from you.” (Al-Insan 76:8-9)

So, the understanding that I am proposing based solely on the analysis of the verses in the Quran is that Prophet Yahya was not never killed but he may have been saved and raised to heaven as Prophet Isa (Jesus) and he will return to earth and rule to possibly prepare for the return of Prophet Isa (Jesus) and then he will die natural death.  This is obviously contradictory to the story in the Bible that was used as basis in many books of Tafseer.

But this is just a human effort and Allah knows best.

DUA
