about him. will acknowledge as  sis no and keeping away from sexual relations with women.  But some transgressed and claimed that the term means that Prophet Yahya does male organ; obviously this interpretation is not befitting for a Prophet of Allah.

But the proper interpretation of this term “Hasora” (حَصُورًا) must be considered with the other attribute of being (سَيِّدًا) “master or chief”.  The term “Hasora” (حَصُورًا) is derived from the root “Hasr” (حصر) which means restrict or take inventory.  The term “Hisar” (حصار) means siege.  The term “Mahsour” (محصور) means “being under siege or being confined”.  But the term “Hasora” (حَصُورًا) means “to restrict others by putting them under siege”.  Since the meaning of (سَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا) means that he will be master and powerful enough to put his enemies under siege, it will be logical to expect them to accuse him of being “oppressive and disobedient”.  This explains why Allah negated these descriptions form him.

حصور اسم فاعل
و محصور اسم مفعول

Let us test the Hypothesis that Prophet Yaha is still alive and he will return to earth and rule.

Let me stop here and leave it up to you to reflect on these 4 observations to derive the real story of Prophet Yahya and the lessons from it.

We pray to Allah to grant us the opportunity and wisdom to study the stories of the Quran as they should be studied.

We pray to Allah to grant us the wisdom to be regular reader of the Quran and grant us the ability to be true thinkers.

DUA

title: The Mystery of Prophets and Kings David and Solomon between Truth and Fables
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

Although the Quran can be typed in less than 300 pages, it addresses many broad subjects that include:
The basics of Aqida by providing very concise account of the articles of belief
1. The key elements of Shariah focusing on the fundamental laws
2. History of the rise and fall of past civilization
3. Information on future technologies and scientific discoveries
4. Account of the unseen such as the creation of the universes, the Hereafter
5. Accounts of past Prophets with focus on those prophets whose lives have been falsely presented and whose righteousness has been attacked in previous religious books such as the Old testament. Two of those Prophets are Prophet Dawud (David) and Prophet Suliman (Solomon) and they will be the subject of this talk, Insha'Allah.

Unfortunately, some of these false accounts in the Bible creeped into books of Tafseer which is unfortunate because it clearly violates the Prophet’s command. It is reported that Omar Ibn Al-Khattab said to the Prophet (PBUH):
عن جابر – رضي الله عنه – عن النبي – صلى الله عليه وسلم – حين أتاه عمر فقال : إنا نسمع أحاديث من يهود تعجبنا ، أفترى أن نكتب بعضها ؟ فقال : أمتهوكون أنتم كما تهوكت اليهود والنصارى ؟ ! لقد جئتكم بها بيضاء نقية ، ولو كان موسى حيا ما وسعه إلا اتباعي ” . ( أحمد ، والبيهقي)

“We hear talks from Jews that we like, do you agree that we write some of them.
The Prophet (PBUH) said: “Do you want to be the same as the Jews and Christians!” I came to you with a pure clear message, and if Moses was alive, he could not have done anything but to follow me”.

Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس) said:
عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله أن ابن عباس قال كيف تسألون أهل الكتاب عن شيء وكتابكم الذي أنزل على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أحدث تقرءونه محضا لم يشب وقد حدثكم أن أهل الكتاب بدلوا كتاب الله وغيروه وكتبوا بأيديهم الكتاب وقالوا هو من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا ألا ينهاكم ما جاءكم من العلم عن مسألتهم لا والله ما رأينا منهم رجلا يسألكم عن الذي أنزل عليكم) صحيح البخاري

“How can you ask the people of the book for anything and the book that was revealed to the messenger of Allah (PBUH) is the most recent and you read it pure without any alternation and it informed you that the people of the book substituted and changed the book of Allah and they wrote the book with their hands and said it is from Allah to gain trifling price. Didn’t the knowledge that came to you prohibited you from asking them”.

But why one needs any other source than the Quran to explain what is in it since Allah said:
وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)
We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur’an) as an exposition/explanation of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and glad tidings for the Muslims. (Al-Nahl 16:89)

However, in order to study any subject in the Quran we are required to assemble all the verses related to the subject and harmonize them to provide coherent understanding of the subject. We can include in this effort the authentic hadith of the Prophet (PBUH) to complement our understanding and fill any gaps

One of the important styles that the Quran uses is storytelling and the Prophet (PBUH) used to use it too by telling stories to reinforce certain moral concepts. But the Quran does not provide the story in details, may be the exception is the Story of prophet Yousef. The Quran’s strategy is to provide basic accounts that will require the reader to stitch them together to basically write the script of the story. This may be the reason why there no accurate tafseer of the Quran because different interpreters can write different scripts for the same story. However, all of them must honor the proper linguistic meaning and structure of the words and verses of the Quran.

This approach represents a fascinating teaching strategy of the Quran because it promotes curiosity, analytical capability and logic of Muslims and these are important human trait and key catalysts for all human advancement. Albert Einstein said: “I have no special talents. I am only passionately curious”. This passionate curiosity is what the Quran encourages Muslims to develop.

This approach of giving key elements of the story and encouraging the reader to write the script has the advantage of expanding the Muslim’s cognitive capacity from young age and this is essential if Muslims were to advance in all areas of sciences. This approach should be the one we use when teaching children the Quran because it expands their intellectual abilities and makes the study of the Quran enjoyable.

The Quran provides fascinating accounts of Prophet Dawud (David) and Soliman (Solomon) that corrects many false ideas that people has about them from their stories in the Bible. These two prophets were unique in three ways:
1. They were not only prophets but they were also kings.
2. Prophet Soliman is the only prophet who inherited both the prophethood and the kingdom from his father.
3. During their time, many amazing things happened that did not happen to other prophets and this may explain why many false accounts were made regarding them.

In the Quran the name of both Prophet Dawud (David) and Prophet Suliman (Solomon) came in 16 verses. Prophet Dawud came by itself in 9 verses and also Prophet Suliman came by itself in 9 verses. They came together in 7 verses.

In these 6 verses, The first to be mentioned was prophet Suliman, in verse 102 in Surat Al-Baqarah (2) and the he was also the last to be mentioned in verse 34 of Surat Sad (38). The First mention of Prophet Dawud in the Quran came in verse 251 in Surat Al-Baqara and the last mention came in verse 30 in Surat Sad (38).

So, Prophet Suliman (Solomon) came first to refute all the falsehoods that have been attributed to him that he ruled thru magic. Eliminating this evil accusation sets the stage for proper interpretation of all the next verses. The magic referenced in this context is not the sly-of-hand type but it is what being called back magic, sorcery that is intended to control and harm people. This is the type of magic that was falsely attributed to Prophet Suliman and therefore, Allah dismissed it in the beginning and explained its source and the main purpose of it.

Linguistically, the term magic (سِحر) is derived from the Arabic word (سَحَر) which is the time prior the Fajr which is between the darkness of the night and the light of the day when the person cannot see clearly. The secret of magic is to confuse the eye that it will see things that does not exist and confuse the mind to think of something that happened while it never happened.

Allah says in verse 102 of surat Al-Baqara: (that we heard un the beginning)
وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَا تَتۡلُواْ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلۡكِ سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ‌ۖ وَمَا ڪَفَرَ سُلَيۡمَـٰنُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينُ كَفَرُواْ يُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ ٱلسِّحۡرَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَكَيۡنِ بِبَابِلَ هَـٰرُوتَ وَمَـٰرُوتَ‌ۚ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنۡ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَآ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ فِتۡنَةٌ۬ فَلَا تَكۡفُرۡ‌ۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنۡهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِۦ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡمَرۡءِ وَزَوْجِهِۦ‌ۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَآرِّينَ بِهِۦ مِنۡ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمۡ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمۡ‌ۚ وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمُواْ لَمَنِ ٱشۡتَرَٮٰهُ مَا لَهُ ۥ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَـٰقٍ۬‌ۚ وَلَبِئۡسَ مَا شَرَوۡاْ بِهِۦٓ أَنفُسَهُمۡ‌ۚ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ (١٠٢)

“They (the disbelievers from the Jews) followed what Satans (devils of both Jinn and men) falsely related against the kingdom of Solomon. And Solomon never disbelieved but Satans disbelieved. They (Satans) taught the people magic and (also taught them) what was sent down to the angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut.

They (the angels) never taught anyone without saying: “We are only a temptation, therefore do not disbelieve.” They (the people) learned from them (the angels) the means to sow discord between husband and wife. But they could not cause harm to anyone except by Allah’s permission.

And they (the people) learned what would harm them, not what would benefit them. And they knew that whoever would buy it (magic) would have no share in the happiness of the Hereafter. And vile was the price for which they sold their souls, if they but knew! (Al-Baqara 2:102)

The verse clearly refutes all claims made by Satans and creeped in the knowledge of people in the past that prophet Suleiman practiced magic which is a major sin and act of disbelief “Kufr” and Allah reaffirms that Suleiman never practiced any acts of Kufr. But the Satans whether from the Jinn and men are the ones who are disbelievers and practiced Kufr because they are teaching the people magic and also teaching them what was sent down to the two angels Harout and Marout who were sent to the people of Babylon.

Because Magic (sorcery and witchcraft) was widespread in Babylon, Allah, out of His mercy, sent two angles to teach anyone who wants to learn not the knowledge of magic but the knowledge on the nature of magic and how to eliminate its influence. But like a pharmacist who is being taught how to neutralize the effect of a poison, he must also learn how to make poison and how it works. The angels taught the people how to neutralize the effect of magic and also how magic works. But before teaching anyone the essence of magic, they warned the person that he is now under test because he now knew both the remedy and how to do it and practicing magic is kufr.

The verse suggests that magic is based on knowledge that can be learnt. But Muslims are forbidden from studying this subject since it is the second most destructive sin after the shirk. The Prophet (PBUH) said: (اجتنبوا السبع الموبقات، قالوا: وما هن يا رسول الله؟) Avoid the seven great destructive sins.

The people inquired, ‘O Allah’s Messenger! What are they? The Prophet (PBUH) said:
Associating partners with Allah, 2) magic, 3) killing the life which Allah has forbidden except for a just cause, 4) consuming usury, 5) consuming an orphan’s wealth, 6) fleeing from the battlefield, and 7) accusing chaste believing women, who never even think of anything that would tarnish their chastity. (الشرك بالله، والسحر، وقتل النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق، وأكل الربا، وأكل مال اليتيم، والتولي يوم الزحف، وقذف المحصنات الغافلات المؤمنات. (حديث الصحيحين

Note that Allah did not send prophets to teach people the nature of magic but He sent angels and the reason is that no prophet should be associated with magic whether learning it or teaching it. The angels came in the form of normal human beings and we know that angels can come in the form of humans as happened when the holy spirit Jibreal came to the Prophet to ask him about Islam, Eman, Ihsan and the Hour.

The main function of magic is to create division between a husband and his wife by creating false images in their minds about each other. Creating division between married couples is the primary purpose of the chief Satan, Iblis. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
عَنْ جَابِرٍ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِنَّ إِبْلِيسَ يَضَعُ عَرْشَهُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُ سَرَايَاهُ فَأَدْنَاهُمْ مِنْهُ مَنْزِلَةً أَعْظَمُهُمْ فِتْنَةً يَجِيءُ أَحَدُهُمْ فَيَقُولُ فَعَلْتُ كَذَا وَكَذَا فَيَقُولُ مَا صَنَعْتَ شَيْئًا قَالَ ثُمَّ يَجِيءُ أَحَدُهُمْ فَيَقُولُ مَا تَرَكْتُهُ حَتَّى فَرَّقْتُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ امْرَأَتِهِ قَالَ فَيُدْنِيهِ مِنْهُ وَيَقُولُ نِعْمَ أَنْتَ (صحيح مسلم)

“Iblis (Satan) places his throne upon water and sends his troops. The closest to him are those who (tempt people to) commit the greatest sins. Some of them would approach him and say: we did such-and-such. Iblis would reply: You have done nothing. But one of them would approach him and say: I did not leave the man until I caused him to divorce his wife. Iblis would bring him close to his throne and would say: You are it, how great you are!”

Magic is merely imagining things than do not exist and therefore imaginary thoughts and suspicion comes to the mind of the husband or the wife and conflicts start between them. But, if the husband and wife are righteous, they will regularly be reading the Quran, particularly the Maudhtan (معوذتين) (chapters 113 and 114 of the Quran) and this will protect them from such harm. There an interesting hadeath narrated by Ibn Abbas and reported in Bukhari, the Prophet (PBUH) said in this hadith: :
عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ” يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مِنْ هَؤُلاءِ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ هُمْ الَّذِينَ لا يَسْتَرْقُونَ وَلا يَتَطَيَّرُونَ وَلا يَكْتَوُونَ وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ “. ( البخاري )

“ Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without being held for account. They are those who: Do not seek Ruqyaa (رقية) (healing invocation), do not use evil omens (not superstitious), do not treat themselves with branding (use fire to treat diseases) and on their Lord they put their full trust.”

This hadeath discourages people from seeking Ruqyaa from anyone because those who are regular reciter of the Quran will not need it from anyone because no harm will come to them. Reading the Quran as Ruqya for yourself and your young children is fine but going to a sheikh to do Ruqya on you is discouraged.

To close the discussion on magic (sorcery), we must realize that it cannot cause physical harm or influence a person’s destiny or fortune because Allah will never allow anyone to have control of such things; these are only in the hand of Allah. But all magic does is to create imagination and this can be avoided by regular recitation of the Quran.

The last verse in which Prophet Suliman name was mentioned is verse 34 in Surat Sad (38) and it is followed his famous Dua.
وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا عَلَىٰ كُرۡسِيِّهِۦ جَسَدً۬ا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ (٣٤) قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِى وَهَبۡ لِى مُلۡكً۬ا لَّا يَنۢبَغِى لِأَحَدٍ۬ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِىٓ‌ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ (٣٥)

“And indeed, We tested Suliman, We threw on his throne a body after which he turned (to Us). He said, “O my Lord, forgive me, and grant me a kingdom that shall not be available to anyone after me. Surely, You are the Bestower.” (Sad 38:34-35)

This verse has to be integrated with other verses to provide a clear scenario to understand what is this body that was put on Prophet Suliman’s throne as a test for him and also why he would make such a Dua to be granted a kingdom that will not be available to anyone else. The Dua appears to be selfish in nature but this obviously cannot be true because Suliman is a prophet and he cannot be selfish.

I’ll skip the discussion on this verse and other verses related to Prophet Suliman but will come back to them, inshallah, in future talks because I want to discuss Prophet Dawud (David) since it will help us in explaining this verse as well others. But I encourage you to try to develop a scenario on your own that is harmonized with other verses and consistent with the honorable character of Prophet Suliman.

Regarding Prophet Dawud his name was first mentioned in the Quran in verse 251 of Surat Al-Baqara (2) and it sets the stage for his prophethood and kingdom:
وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرً۬ا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ (٢٥٠) فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُ ۥدُ جَالُوتَ وَءَاتَٮٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ وَٱلۡحِڪۡمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُ ۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُ‌ۗ وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضٍ۬ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَـٰڪِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٢٥١)

“And when they faced Jalut (Goliath) and his troops, they (Bani Israel) said: “Our Lord, shower us with patience, make firm our foothold and make us victorious over the disbelieving people.” (250) So, they defeated them by the will of Allah, and Dawud (David) killed Jalut (Goliath) and Allah gave him the kingdom and the wisdom and taught him what He willed. Had Allah not been repelling some people by others, the earth would have been corrupted. But Allah is All-Gracious to all that exist.” (Al-Baqara 2:250-251)

This verse explains the reason for the rise of Dawud (David) and inform us of the blessings that Allah granted to him and these are 1) kingdom, 2) wisdom and 3) special knowledge (وَعَلَّمَهُ ۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُ). Note there is another entity in the Quran whom Allah taught special knowledge and this was Al-Khidr who demonstrated his unique knowledge to Prophet Musa (Moses).
فَوَجَدَا عَبۡدً۬ا مِّنۡ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَـٰهُ رَحۡمَةً۬ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمۡنَـٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلۡمً۬ا (٦٥)
“Then they found one of Our slaves, on whom We had bestowed mercy from Us, and whom We had taught knowledge from Us.” (Al-Kahf 18:65)

But before we discuss this special knowledge that Allah taught Prophet Dawud, let us reflect on several lesson from this account that started with verse 246 that mentioned the elite of Bani Israel who went to their Prophet and asked him to recommend for them a ruler, king to lead them to fight their enemies. The verses are Al-Baqara 2: 246-251:

أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَإِ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذۡ قَالُواْ لِنَبِىٍّ۬ لَّهُمُ ٱبۡعَثۡ لَنَا مَلِڪً۬ا نُّقَـٰتِلۡ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ قَالَ هَلۡ عَسَيۡتُمۡ إِن ڪُتِبَ عَلَيۡڪُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَـٰتِلُواْ‌ۖ قَالُواْ وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نُّقَـٰتِلَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَدۡ أُخۡرِجۡنَا مِن دِيَـٰرِنَا وَأَبۡنَآٮِٕنَا‌ۖ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوۡاْ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ مِّنۡهُمۡ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (٢٤٦) وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ نَبِيُّہُمۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قدۡ بَعَثَ لَڪُمۡ طَالُوتَ مَلِكً۬ا‌ۚ قَالُوٓاْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ عَلَيۡنَا وَنَحۡنُ أَحَقُّ بِٱلۡمُلۡكِ مِنۡهُ وَلَمۡ يُؤۡتَ سَعَةً۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَالِ‌ۚ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَٮٰهُ عَلَيۡڪُمۡ وَزَادَهُ ۥ بَسۡطَةً۬ فِى ٱلۡعِلۡمِ وَٱلۡجِسۡمِ‌ۖ وَٱللَّهُ يُؤۡتِى مُلۡڪَهُ ۥ مَن يَشَآءُ‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ۬ (٢٤٧) وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ نَبِيُّہُمۡ إِنَّ ءَايَةَ مُلۡكِهِۦٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلتَّابُوتُ فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّڪُمۡ وَبَقِيَّةٌ۬ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ءَالُ مُوسَىٰ وَءَالُ هَـٰرُونَ تَحۡمِلُهُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةُ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬ لَّڪُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ (٢٤٨) فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبۡتَلِيڪُم بِنَہَرٍ۬ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنۡهُ فَلَيۡسَ مِنِّى وَمَن لَّمۡ يَطۡعَمۡهُ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ مِنِّىٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغۡتَرَفَ غُرۡفَةَۢ بِيَدِهِۦ‌ۚ فَشَرِبُواْ مِنۡهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ مِّنۡهُمۡ‌ۚ فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ ۥ هُوَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُ ۥ قَالُواْ لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ‌ۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَـٰقُوا ٱللَّهِ ڪَم مِّن فِئَةٍ۬ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةً۬ ڪَثِيرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ (٢٤٩) وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرً۬ا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡڪَـٰفِرِينَ (٢٥٠) فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُدُ جَالُوتَ وَءَاتَٮٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ وَٱلۡحِڪۡمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُ ۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُ‌ۗ وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضٍ۬ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَـٰڪِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ (٢٥١)

I am not going to translate these verses but you can read them on your own. But I want to highlight four important lessons that we can derive from these verses:
1. The leader of a society does not need to be the religious scholar. Bani Israel had a Prophet with them and they went to him seeking recommendation for a leader.
2. A leader can exist within a society but he may not be given the opportunity to advance because of their wrong metrics. In the case of Bani Israel, their metric for leadership was financial success.
3. The key attributes of the leader are vast knowledge and physical strength and not wealth
4. Allah’s support only comes if the team is 100% pure and this requires displacing those who are not righteous from among them. The quantity is not important, it is the quality of the team that counts.

Allah informed us that He gave Dawud special knowledge from Him and Allah made him unique among all prophets. The Prophet (PBUH) stated a hadeath that clearly illustrates that prophet Dawud was very unique from the time of creation of Prophet Adam. The hadeath is reported by Imam Al-Tirmizi (الترمذي) and was narrated by Abu Hurayrah (أبي هريرة -رضي الله عنه) and I mentioned it in my talk on the unique creation of Adam on January 26, 2020 that you can find on YouTube. The Prophet (PBUH) said:
“ لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة وجعل بين عيني كل إنسان منهم وبيصا من نور ثم عرضهم على آدم فقال: أي ربي من هؤلاء؟ قال: هؤلاء ذريتك فرأى رجلا منهم فأعجبه وبيص ما بين عينيه فقال: يا رب من هذا؟ قال: هذا رجل من آخر الأمم من ذريتك يقال له: داود قال: يا رب كم عمره؟ قال: ستون سنة قال: أي رب أعطه من عمري أربعين فأخذ الله عليه الميثاق”

“When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back and every soul of his offspring that Allah will create until the Day of Judgement fell from his back. Allah put on the forehead of every one of them a flash of light, then showed them to Adam. Adam asked: “My Lord who are they? Allah said: They are your offspring.
Adam saw one of them and he was charmed by a bright flash between his eyes. He asked: My Lord, who is this? Allah said: he is a man from the late nations from your descendants and his name is Dawoud (David).
Adam asked: My Lord, what is his age? Allah said: sixty years.
Adam said: My Lord give him from my age 40 years. Allah took the covenant from Adam that this is his demand.

This hadeath illustrates the uniqueness of Prophet Dawud (David) and there are verses in the Quran that suggest that Prophet Dawud was given unique book, unlike any other revelation. This should raise our curiosity to understand what type of revelation prophet Dawud received that made him very unique because it may explain other verses in the Quran. Allah informs us that Prophet Dawud (David) received a book called Zabur and the term Zabour came three times in the Quran. Linguistically Zabour means a book but an engraved book, whether engraved on metal or rocks.

The term Zabour is mentioned in the Quran twice as the book given to prophet Dawud in the indefinite form, i.e., it does not have the definite article “the” (Arabic “Al”) to indicate its specificity. The way it is listed in these two verses indicate its uniqueness. Allah says in verse 163 in Surat Al-Nisa (4):
إِنَّآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ كَمَآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ۬ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ‌ۚ وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُورًا (١٦٣)
“Surely, We have revealed to you (Mohammad) as We have revealed to Nuh and to the prophets after him; and We have revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and to Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and as We gave to David Zabour.” (Al-Nisa 4:163)

Note that verse started with Allah affirming that He revealed to Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) as He revealed to other Prophets and listed their names but Allah made a specific mention of what is given to David which is Zabour. Note that Allah said We gave to David and did not say We revealed to David as He said for the other Prophets.

The specific mention of Zabur came again in verse 55 in Surat Al-Isra (17):
وَرَبُّكَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۗ وَلَقَدۡ فَضَّلۡنَا بَعۡضَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬‌ۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُ ۥدَ زَبُورًا (٥٥)
“Your Lord is fully aware of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. We have exalted some Prophets above the others in ranks, and We gave David Zabour”. (Al-Isra 17:55)

Here also we note the specific attention given to what Allah gave to Prophet David. Allah mentions that He exalted in ranks some Prophets over others and then Allah specifically mentions David and what was given to him. (As a side note: This verse addresses the Question whether there is intelligent life in space, it says Yes.)

We also note that there is no verse in the Quran in which Allah reveals what was the purpose of this book Zabour while Allah mentioned the purpose of the other revelations such as the Torah, the Injil and the Quran as books of guidance and laws. So, the question is what was in this book Zabour?

There one verse in the Quran in which the term Zabour came with the definite article “Al” (Al-Zabour) (The Zabour). This is verse 105 in Surat Al-Anbiya and it reads:
وَلَقَدۡ ڪَتَبۡنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلذِّكۡرِ أَنَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحُونَ (١٠٥) إِنَّ فِى هَـٰذَا لَبَلَـٰغً۬ا لِّقَوۡمٍ عَبِدِينَ (١٠٦)
“And We have certainly written in Al-Zabour after the Dhikr (reminder) that the land will be inherited by My righteous slaves. (105) Surely, in this there is a plain message to people who are worshippers (of Allah).” (Al-Anbiya 21:105-106)

Several interpreters suggest that Al-Zabour in this verse refers to all the revealed books such as the Taurât (Torah), the Injeel (Gospel), and the Qur’an, and the Dhikr is the book in “The Preserved Tablet” (اللوح المحفوظ). Thus, the verse means that we have written in all the revealed books from what was written in the preserved tablet that the land will be inherited by the righteous servants of Allah. Some interpreters say that Al-Zabour here is the book of David and the Dhikr is the book that was revealed before it which is the Torah. So, this verse does not clear for us what is included in Zabour that Allah uniquely gave to Prophet Dawud (David).

The confusion in the books of Tafseer came because almost all the interpretations considered the book Zabour is the Book of Psalms (سفر المزامير) in the Old Testament but the association is very difficult to justify for at least 4 reasons.
1. The mention of Zabour in the Quran indicates that is something very special.
2. The book of Psalms includes 150 individual psalms. However, Jewish and Christian scholars only attribute 73 psalms to David and there are even some highly critical modern scholars who don’t accept the authorship of David to any of the psalms.
3. The title Psalm is derived from the Greek translation, psalmoi, meaning “instrumental music” and, by extension the book of Psalms means, “the words accompanying the music” and this cannot be appropriate for Allah’s revelation.
4. Some of the Psalms in the book of Psalms is similar to the books of Tasbeeh and Dhikr that are used by many Sofi followers and does not not even rise in quality in either words or rhythms to what exist in Islamic tradition.

The following is an example form the Book Psalms that clearly show that it cannot be revealed by Allah:
Lord, how many are my foes! How many rise up against me!
Many are saying of me, “God will not deliver him.
But you, Lord, are a shield around me, my glory, the One who lifts my head high.
I call out to the Lord, and he answers me from his holy mountain.
I lie down and sleep; I wake again, because the Lord sustains me.
I will not fear though tens of thousands assail me on every side.
Arise, Lord! Deliver me, my God! Strike all my enemies on the jaw; break the teeth of the wicked.
From the Lord comes deliverance. May your blessing be on your people.

So, it is very reasonable to conclude that Zabour is not the book of Psalms but it is rather a very unique book that Allah gave especially to Prophet Dawud (David). Keep in mind of verse 251 in Surat Al-Baqara in which Allah said that He taught special knowledge to Dawud (وَعَلَّمَهُ ۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُ). The Intriguing question is what is in this book, Zabour. There is one clue that may lead us to speculate on the nature of this book.

You recall that before Prophet Adam was created, Allah told the angles about His plan to create Khalifa (Vicegerent/deputy/representative) in earth. This term khalifa came in the Quran only twice; the first in verse 30 in Surat al-Baqara (2) and the second in verse 26 in Surat Sad (38):
وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةً۬‌ۖ (٣٠)
And (remember) when your Lord said to the angels, “Verily, I am going to make khalifa (vicegerent/deputy/representative) in earth.” (Al-Baqara 2:30)

يَـٰدَاوُ ۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَـٰكَ خَلِيفَةً۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ
“O Dawud (David), Verily, We have made you khalifa (vicegerent /deputy/ representative) in earth.” (Sad 38:26)

Could this give us the clue on the nature of Zabour, it is the manual that Prophet Dawud (David) would need to fulfill his role as a deputy of Allah in earth. Being a deputy of Allah means that he must have the knowledge to control and communicate with everything in earth.

Let us make this hypothesis that the book Zabour that Allah gave to prophet Dawud is the book that includes the secrets to control everything in earth. To prove the validity of this hypothesis, we can use it to assess whether it will be able to explain all the other verses related to Prophet Dawud and his son Suliman (Solomon). I am including Suliman because it is very likely that some of the knowledge of this book Zabour was transmitted to him since he inherited both the prophethood and the kingdom from his father.

There is no time in this talk to perform this analysis but you can do it on your own. But, you must be curious about knowing some of what is this book. Let me make another speculation that the Quran contains all the information if we can only derive it. What is the basis for this hypothesis? It is the first verse that I read in this talk about the content of the Quran, Allah says:
وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)
We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur’an) as an exposition/explanation of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and glad tidings for the Muslims. (Al-Nahl 16:89)

Another support of this assumption is a hadith reported in Bukhari that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ ( خُفِّفَتْ عَلَى دَاوُدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ الْقُرْآنُ ، فَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ بِدَوَابِّهِ فَتُسْرَجُ ، فَيَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُسْرَجَ دَوَابُّهُ )البخاري
“The Quran was lightened on Dawud (David) peace upon him, he would order for his animals to be saddled and he would be able to read the Quran before they are saddled.”

This hadith imply that Prophet Dawud has only received part of the Quran that allow him to read in this relatively short time. Can this part have the content of Zabour, can we identify this part in the Quran? The answer is: it is possible but there is a prerequisite that we may be able to identify from verse 12 in Surat Al-Mugadala (58):

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نَـٰجَيۡتُمُ ٱلرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَىۡ نَجۡوَٮٰكُمۡ صَدَقَةً۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ خَيۡرٌ۬ لَّكُمۡ وَأَطۡهَرُ‌ۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَجِدُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ۬ رَّحِيمٌ (١٢)
“O you who believe! When you seek discourse privately with the Messenger, offer something in charity before your private discourse. That will be better and purer for you. But if you do not find the means, then Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” (Al-Mugadala 58:12)

The time had already run out on this talk, so I’ll stop here but I gave enough information to do research on your own. We pray to Allah to grant us the wisdom to be regular reader of the Quran and grant us the ability to understand it.

DUA

title: The Preferred Time for the Different Prayers (Supplication)
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين .

Before we start, let us define the Arabic term “Salat”. The term Salat is generally translated as prayers and the prayers are merely a form of Dua (supplication). The term Salat is related to the root meaning “to connect”. So, when we are doing Salat to Allah, we are connecting with Allah to ask Him for whatever we need and also for Him to correct any spiritual ailment that we may have.

Therefore, recognizing that the terms Salat, prayers, Dua, supplication are all referring to the same thing and all of these are only directed to Allah because He is the only One who can help us both spiritually and materialistically. This recognition should be clear since Muslims only Worship Allah by directing all their Dua (prayers, supplication) to Him. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم- أنه قال: الدعاء هو العبادة. ثم قرأ: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين” رواه أحمد وأصحاب السنن

The Dua (Supplication) is the worship, and then recited: “Your Lord has said, “Call Me (Supplicate to Me, Pray to Me, Invoke Me), I will respond to you. Definitely those who show arrogance against worshipping Me shall enter Hell in humiliation!” (Ghafir 40:60)

There is very important and subtle issue that we must realize as believers that asking anyone for help while we are believing that this person has the sole power to help us is a form of Shirk. Keep in mind that I am not saying that you should not ask people for help, I am saying if you ask them and you are convinced that they have the sole power to help you, this is the shirk. But if you ask while believing that Allah is the only One in His hand is your help and this person you are asking may be the one by whom Allah will deliver to you the help, this is fine.

This point is very important because we declare it at least 17 times per day in front of Allah by saying during our prayers: (إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ) “You alone we worship and from you alone we seek help”. This simple verse summarizes the whole essence of the religion of Islam. Scholars have said that the Fatihah is the secret of the Quran and the secret of the Fatihah is (إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ) “.

How do you know whether you have committed some form of shirk by asking someone for help? Assess your feeling if the person did not help, do you get mad from him or you maintain good relationship with him because you know that he has no power to help unless Allah wanted him to do so. If you get mad and angry from him, you need to question your state of belief, but if you maintain the same relationship with him whether he helped or not, you are a true believer.

So, now we realize that all our prayers which is our dua is directed only to Allah. While it is not allowed to do prayers to anyone other than Allah, it is quite acceptable that we do prayers on someone. The only difference in this statement of the proposition “to” and “on”. “We only perform Salat, Prayers to Allah but we perform Salat, Prayers on anyone”.

Note: Since Salat (prayers) are Dua (supplication), one can say perform prayer for someone instead of on someone. But I’ll be using on in the talk because this is what the Quran uses. Using on may actually be better choice because when someone is sick and you do Ruqya, you say I read the Quran on him/her and don’t say, I read the Quran for him/her.

We said performing salat, prayers to Allah means doing Dua to Allah for help. Performing salat, prayers on someone means that we are doing Dua for him.

Allah gives us a clear command to do Salat, Prayers on the prophet (PBUH) by saying:

(إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَتَهُ ۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّۚ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيۡهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمًا (٥٦)) الأحزاب

” Indeed, Allah and His Angels do the Salat (prayers) on the Prophet: O you who believe, do your Salat on him, and salute him with perfect salutation. (Al-Azab 33:56)

So, in this verse Allah and His angles are doing Salat, Prayers on the Prophet (PBUH). We understand that when the angels do Salat on the Prophet, they are supplicating to Allah to grant the Prophet (PBUH) forgiveness, blessings and high rank. The same thing when we do Salat on the Prophet (PBUH), we are asking Allah to grant the Prophet (PBUH) forgiveness, blessings and high rank.

But when Allah is doing the Salat on the Prophet (PBUH) what does not it mean? It means that Allah is committing Himself to forgive the Prophet (PBUH), to grant him blessings and to raise his rank. So, if you can reach the point that Allah will do salat on you, it will mean that Allah has committed to forgive you, to grant you His blessings and to raise your rank. This obviously should be the ultimate goal of anyone of us.

But this verse states that Allah and the angels are doing the Salat on the Prophet (PBUH) only, how about us? When this verse was revealed Ubay Ibn Ka’ab (أبي بن كعب) said to the Prophet (PBUH):

ما أنزل فيك خيراً إلا خلطنا به معك إلا هذه الآية

“O Messenger of Allah, whenever a revelation came declaring goodness for you, we were included in it, except in this verse.

The same concern was raised by both the immigrants and the helpers (المهاجرون والأنصار) who told the Prophet (PBUH) as was reported by Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس):

هذا لك يا رسول الله خاصة، وليس لنا فيه شيء

“This blessing exclusive for you, Messenger of Allah, and we have no share in it.”

The reason of this concern is that in other revelations, Allah included the believers with the Messenger (PBUH) such as:

ءَامَنَ ٱلرَّسُولُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡهِ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ‌ ۚ كُلٌّ ءَامَنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕكَتِهِۦ وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَرُسُلِهِۦ

“The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, as do the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His Angels, His Books, and His Messengers.” (Al-Baqara 2:285)

لَـٰكِنِ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُ ۥ جَـٰهَدُواْ بِأَمۡوَٲلِهِمۡ وَأَنفُسِهِمۡ‌ۚ وَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٲتُ‌ۖ وَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ) التوبة

“But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove and fought with their wealth and their lives. For them all the good things and it is they who will be successful” (Al-Tuba 9:88)

Shortly after the verse in question was revealed stating that Allah and His angels do Salat on the Prophet, Allah revealed:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ ذِكۡرً۬ا كَثِيرً۬ا – وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكۡرَةً۬ وَأَصِيلاً – هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَلِّى عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَتُهُ ۥ لِيُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَكَانَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَحِيمًا. ( سورة الأحزاب)

“O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance and glorify Him morning and evening.

He is One Who does “Salat” on you, as do His angels, that He may bring you out from the depths of Darkness into Light: and He is Most Merciful to the Believers. (Al-Ahzab 33:41:43)

So, if we want Allah and His angels to do salat on us, all we need to is do regular Dhikr and Tasbeeh.

While we were commanded to do salat on the Prophet, we should aspire to also have the Prophet (PBUH) do salat on us. This is possible, all we need to do is to give charity as Allah said:

خُذۡ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٲلِهِمۡ صَدَقَةً۬ تُطَهِّرُهُمۡ وَتُزَكِّيہِم بِہَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيۡهِمۡ‌ۖ إِنَّ صَلَوٰتَكَ سَكَنٌ۬ لَّهُمۡ‌ۗ وَٱللَّه سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١٠٣)

“Take Sadaqah (charity, alms) from their wealth by which you purify them and sanctify them with it, and do Salat (prayers) on them. Verily! Your prayers are a source of security for them, and Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower.” (Al-Tuba 9:103)

But how do we do the Salat on the Prophet (PBUH)? The Prophet (PBUH) was asked about this and He (PBUH) said, say (the ending of the Tahyyaat, the salat Al-Ibrahimia):

اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد، اللهم بارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد،

There are many rewards awaiting those who are regular in doing the Salat on the Prophet (PBUH), These include:

First: it is a fulfillment of an obligatory command from Allah and obeying Allah’s command brings great rewards.

Second: It is an expression of our love of the Prophet (PBUH) and a demonstration of our true belief. Al-Bukhari reported that Anas ibn Malik said, the messenger of Allah (PBUH) said

(لَا يُؤْمِنُ أحَدُكُمْ، حتَّى أكُونَ أحَبَّ إلَيْهِ مِن والِدِهِ ووَلَدِهِ والنَّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ). [رواه البخاري، عن أنس بن مالك].

“None of you will believe until I became more beloved to him than his parents, children and all the people.”

The best way to show our love of the Prophet (PBUH) is to prayer on him frequently.

If you love the Prophet (PBUH) and want to communicate with him (PBUH) do the salat on him, Abu Hurryrah said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: صلوا علي فإن صلاتكم تبلغني حيثما كنتم [خرجه أبو داود وأحمد]

“Pray on me, your prayers reach me no matter where you are.”

Abu Hurryrah also said that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة أنَّ رسُولَ اللَّه ﷺ قَالَ: مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يُسلِّمُ علَيَّ إلاَّ ردَّ اللَّه علَيَّ رُوحِي حتَّى أَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامَ.] أبو داود].

“Whenever someone salutes me, Allah will return my soul to me so that I will be able to reply to his salutation”.

Keep in mind that Allah is commanding us to do both Salat and Salaam on the Prophet as He said (صَلُّواْ عَلَيۡهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمًا) “do your Salat on him, and salute him with perfect salutation”.

If you love the Prophet (PBUH) and wanted to be near him on the day of Judgement pray often on him, Ibn Masuad (ابن مسعود) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

وعن ابن مسْعُودٍ أنَّ رسُول اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: أَوْلى النَّاسِ بِي يوْمَ الْقِيامةِ أَكْثَرُهُم عَليَّ صلاةً رواه الترمذي وقال: حديثٌ حسنٌ.

“Those who are the nearest to me on the day of judgement are those who are most frequent in doing salat on me.

Third: Each time you do one salat on the Prophet (PBUH), Allah will do ten on you. It is reported by Muslim that Abdullah ibn Amr (عن عبد الله بن عمرو) said, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : (مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بِهَا عَشْرًا) رواه مسلم ].

“Whosoever prays on me one prayer, Allah will pray on him ten times”.

In a similar hadeath, the Prophet (PBUH) also said:

عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً وَاحِدَةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَشْرَ صَلَوَاتٍ ، وَحُطَّتْ عَنْهُ عَشْرُ خَطِيئَاتٍ ، وَرُفِعَتْ لَهُ عَشْرُ دَرَجَاتٍ ) [رواه أحمد والبخاري والنسائي والحاكم].

“Whosoever prays on me one prayer, Allah will pray on him ten times and will erase ten of his sins and will raise him up ten ranks”.

We said when Allah does Salat on you, it means that Allah committed to forgive you, to grant you His blessings and to raise your rank.

The worst state for any Muslim is to hear the Prophet’s name mentioned and does not care to do salat on him. Abu Hurryrah said that the messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

وعنْ أَبي هُريْرةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رسُولُ اللَّه ﷺ: رَغِم أنْفُ رجُلٍ ذُكِرْتُ عِنْدَهُ فَلَمْ يُصَلِّ علَيَّ] رواه الترمذي].

“Humiliated be the one who hears my name mentioned and does not pray on me.

There a hadeath reported in Al-Tirmidhi (الترمذي) and others and it highlights the importance of doing prayers on the Prophet (PBUH). The hadeath is narrated by Ubay bin Ka’ab (أبي بن كعب) who said:

رُوي عن أبي بن كعب -رضي الله عنه- أنه قال: قلْتُ: يا رسولَ اللهِ، إِنَّي أُكْثِرُ الصلاةَ عليْكَ فكم أجعلُ لكَ من صلاتي؟ فقال: ما شِئْتَ، قال: قلْتُ: الربعَ؟ قال: ما شِئْتَ، فإِنْ زدتَّ فهو خيرٌ لكَ، قلْتُ: النصفَ؟ قال: ما شِئْتَ، فإِنْ زدتَّ فهو خيرٌ لكَ، قال: قلْتُ: فالثلثينِ؟ قال: ما شِئْتَ، فإِنْ زدتَّ فهو خيرٌ لكَ، قلْتُ: أجعلُ لكَ صلاتي كلَّها؟ قال: إِذاً تُكْفَى همَّكَ ويغفرْ لكَ ذنبُكَ).[ رواه الترمذي، حسن صحيح]

‘I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I pray on you often, so how much of my prayers should I devote on you?’ He replied, ‘as you desire’.

I said, ‘a quarter of it?’ He said ‘as you desire, but if you were to increase upon this, it would be better for you.’

I said, ‘half of it?’ He said, ‘as you desire, but if you were to increase upon this, it would be better for you.’

I said, ‘two-thirds of it?’ He said again, ‘as you desire, but if you were to increase upon this, it would be better for you.’

Finally, I said: Should I then dedicate the entirety of my prayers on you?’ He said, ‘this is sufficient for your worries to be alleviated and for sins to be forgiven”.

When we pray on the Prophet (PBUH) once, Allah will pray on us ten folds, and when Allah prays on us, He will shower us with His abundant blessings and mercy. When you make a specific Dua, you seek one specific thing, but when you pray on the Prophet, you are in fact doing Dua for all kinds of blessings in this life and the Hereafter.

In addition, the hadeath ends with given the ultimate benefit which is alleviating our worries and forgiving our sins and this assures our happiness in this life because no worries will ever come to us and assures our happiness in the hereafter because our sins would have been forgiven. These are all by doing the Salat on the Prophet (PBUH).

But this hadeath raises a critical question, should we then dedicate all our Dua and dhikr to saying prayers on the Prophet (PBUH)?

How can we reconcile this hadeath with many other commands by Allah and His messenger (PBUH) that suggest different kind of dhikr and Dua.

Examples:

The Prophet (PBUH) also said:

لأن أقول : سبحان الله و بحمده و الحمد لله و لا إله إلا الله و الله أكبر خير إلى مما تطلع عليه الشمس ] رواه مسلم]

To be able to say (سبحان الله و بحمده و الحمد لله و لا إله إلا الله و الله أكبر) “Glory and Praise be to Allah, all thanks belong to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest” are better for me than anything that exists under the sun.

The Prophet (PBUH) told Abu Dhar: “Should I tell about the most beloved words to Allah”. Abu Dhar said: yes, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

«ألا أخبرُك بأحبِّ الكلامِ إلى اللهِ؟» قلتُ: “يا رسولَ اللهِ! أخبرني بأحبِّ الكلامِ إلى اللهِ”، فقال: «إنَّ أحبَّ الكلامِ إلى اللهِ، سبحانَ اللهِ وبحمدِه» (صحيح) [رواه مسلم من حديث أبي ذر رضي الله عنه.]

“The most beloved words to Allah are (سبحانَ اللهِ وبحمدِه) “Glory and Praise be to Allah.”

Sayeda Aisha reported that the Prophet (PBUH) used to say often:

عن عائشة رضي الله عنها كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر من قول: «سبحان الله وبحمدِه أستغفر الله وأتوب إليه»، قالت فقلت : يا رسول الله! أراك تكثر من قول: “سبحان الله وبحمده أستغفر الله وأتوب إليه”؟، فقال: «خبرني ربي أني سأري علامة في أمتي، فإذا رأيتها أكثرت من قول: سبحان الله وبحمده أستغفر الله وأتوب إليه، فقد رأيتها»، {إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ (فتح مكة) وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا، فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا} [النصر:] (رواه مسلم)

(سبحان الله وبحمده أستغفر الله وأتوب إليه) “Glory and Praise be to Allah; I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.” So, she asked him (PBUH) why do you say these often. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

“Allah have informed me of a sign that I’ll see in my nation and if I see it, I should say: (سبحان الله وبحمده أستغفر الله وأتوب إليه) “Glory and Praise be to Allah; I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.” an I have seen it.” The Prophet was referring to the victory over Mecca and on whose occasion Allah revealed surat al-Nasr that says:

إِذَا جَآءَ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡفَتۡحُ (١) وَرَأَيۡتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدۡخُلُونَ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفۡوَاجً۬ا (٢) فَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡهُ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ تَوَّابً۬ا (٣)

When there comes Allah’s help and the Victory, (1) And you see people entering Allah’s religion in multitudes, (2) Then hymn the praises of Your Lord, and seek forgiveness of Him. Surely, He is ever ready to accept repentance.” (Al-Nasr 110:1-3)

The prophet (PBUH) also said:

عن أبي هريرة أنَّ رسُولَ اللَّه ﷺ قَالَ كلمتان خفيفتان على اللسان ثقيلتان في الميزان حبيبتان إلى الرحمن :سبحان الله و بحمده ، سبحان الله العظيم [متفق عليه]

“Two words that are very easy on the tongue, weigh heavily on the scale of good deeds on the Day of Judgment, and dear to the Most Generous (Al-Rahman): Glory be to Allah and to Him is all the praise, Glory to Allah the Most High.

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

من كان آخر كلامه من الدنيا لا إله إلا الله دخل الجنة

“Whosoever his last words in this life are: “There is no God but Allah” will enter paradise

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

أفضل الذكر لا إله إلاّ الله وأفضل الدعاء الحمد لله

The best Dhikr is saying: (لا إله إلا الله) (There is no God but Allah) and the best “Dua” supplication is saying: (الحمد لله) Praise be to Allah (All thanks belong to Allah)

The Prophet (PBUH) said: Increase from the lasting virtues (إستكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات) and these are: التسبيح و التهليل و التحميد و التكبير ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله (سبحان الله و لا إله إلا الله و الحمد لله و الله أكبر )

The Prophet (PBUH) Said:

The most beloved speeches to Allah are four (أحب الكلام إلى الله تعالى أربع):

سبحان الله و الحمد لله و لا إله إلا الله و الله أكبر

And it does not matter with which one you start. (لا يضرك بأيهن بدأت).

The Prophet (PBUH) also said:

التسبيح نصف الميزان و الحمد لله تملأ الميزان و لا إله إلا الله ليس لها دون الله حجاب حتى تخلص إليه

Praise Allah fills half of the scale and thanking Allah fills the wholescale and there is no God but Allah has no barrier between it and Allah until it reaches Him.

Allah also encouraged to ask for forgiveness as He said:

فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ غَفَّارً۬ا (١٠) يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّيۡدۡرَارً۬ا (١١) وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٲلٍ۬ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡہَـٰرً۬ا (١٢)

“And I have said: Seek forgives of your Lord. Indeed, He was ever Forgiving. (10)

He will cause the heavens to rain upon you in abundance, (11) And will help you with riches and sons, and will cause gardens to grow for you, and will cause rivers to flow for you.” (Nooh 71:10)

Also, we are commanding to read the Quran and it is considered the best form of dhikr.

So, we see that there are so many commands that provide many forms of dhikr that are different from performing prayers on the Prophet (PBUH). So, how are we going to resolve this apparent dichotomy with the Hadeath reported by Ubay bin Ka’ab (أبي بن كعب).

It is almost the consensus of the scholars that the solution is what they call (وظيفة الوقت) “The function of the Time”. What they are saying is that every form of Dkir has preferred time for it and during this time is not preferred to do any other dhikr. So, it is important to know the best time to make a specific Dhikr and this time is revealed to us either in the Quran or in a hadeath of the Prophet (PBUH).

The best time to do Tasbeeh is before the rising of the sun, and before its setting, and during some hours of the night, and at the ends of the day, Allah says for Surat Taha:

وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِہَا‌ۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآىِٕ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلنَّہَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ (١٣٠)

“And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, and before its setting, and during some hours of the night, and at the ends of the day that you may become pleased (with all the rewards)” (Taha 20:130).

The best time to do salat on the Prophet (PBUH) is on Friday, as the Prophet (PBUH) said:

– وعن أوس بن أوسٍ، قَالَ: قالَ رسولُ اللَّه ﷺ: إنَّ مِن أَفْضلِ أيَّامِكُمْ يَوْمَ الجُمُعةِ، فَأَكْثِرُوا عَلَيَّ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ فِيهِ، فَإِنَّ صَلاتَكُمْ مَعْرُوضَةٌ عَلَيَّ قالوا: يا رسول اللَّه، وَكَيْفَ تُعْرَضُ صلاتُنَا عليْكَ وقدْ أَرَمْتَ؟ قال: يقولُ: بَلِيتَ، قَالَ: إنَّ اللَّه حَرَّمَ عَلَى الأرْضِ أَجْسَادَ الأنْبِيَاءِ. رواهُ أَبو داود بإسنادٍ صحيحٍ

“Of your best days is Friday, therefore, increase in sending your Salat on me, for your Salat on me is presented to me.”

They said: “O Messenger of Allah, how will our Salat on you be presented to you after you have perished?”

He (PBUH) replied: “Allah has prohibited the earth from (decomposing) the bodies of the Prophets.” [Abu Dawud in his Sunan, Ibn Khuzaimah and Ibn Hibban, and Hakim]

Also, the designated time to do salat on the Prophet (PBUH) after the Adhan (call for payer) as the Prophet (PBUH):

ولقوله ﷺ: إذا سمعتم المؤذن فقولوا مثلما يقول، ثم صلوا علي فإنه من صلى علي واحدة صلى الله عليه بها عشراً، ثم سلوا الله لي الوسيلة فإنها منزلة في الجنة لا تنبغي إلا لعبد من عباد الله، وأرجو أن أكون أنا هو، فمن سأل لي الوسيلة حلت له الشفاعة[مسلم]

When you hear the Muadhin (caller for the prayer) , say what he says and then do salat on me, as for every Salat on me, Allah will do ten prayers on him. .

The best time to ask for forgiveness is after the prostrations and immediately after the prayer. Then after the Istighfar, the best action is to say

سبحان الله، والحمد لله، والله أكبر ثلاثة وثلاثين مرة ثم يختم فيها بقوله: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

Subhan Allah 33 time, Al-Hamdulillah 33 time and Allahu Akbr 34 times (or 33 and complete the 100 by saying “There is no god but Allah, He is alone who has no partner. All thanks to Him and He is powerful over all things” (لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير).

The best dhikr one can do after the Maghrib and Fajr prayers is to say the following dua 10 times:

لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٍ

“There is no god but Allah. He is Alone and has no partner. His is the Kingdom and to Him is all praise, in His hands is good, He gives and takes life (gives death) and He has power overall things”, because the Prophet (PBUH) said:

حديث عبد الرحمن بن غنم – رضي الله عنه – عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: من قال قبل أن ينصرف ويثني رجليه من صلاة المغرب والصبح: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو على كل شيء قدير – عشر مرات – كتب الله له بكل واحدة عشر حسنات، ومحا عنه عشر سيئات، ورفع له عشر درجات، وكانت له حرزًا من كل مكروه، وحرزًا من الشيطان الرجيم، ولم يحل للذنب أن يدركه إلا الشرك، وكان من أفضل الناس عملاً إلا رجلاً يفضله يقول أفضل مما قال. قال المنذري: رواه أحمد

“Whoever recites this dua 10 times while sitting in the Tashahudd position after the prayers of the Maghrib and the morning, Allah will grant him for each one ten rewards and erase for him ten sins and raise him up ten ranks and they will be protection for him form every harm and shield him from Satan the cursed and no other sin besides shirk will be able to reach him, and he will be superior in deeds to other people except for one who recites more”.

In addition to preferred times, there are also preferred places for saying certain Dua. As example, the best Dua to say while on Arafat is what the Prophet (PBUH) instructed us to say:

عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ خَيْرُ الدُّعَاءِ دُعَاءُ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ وَخَيْرُ مَا قُلْتُ أَنَا وَالنَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ قَبْلِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ))سنن الترمذي باب في دعاء يوم عرفة

“The best supplication is the one makes on the day of Arafat and the best of what I and all the Prophets before me said is:

لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

There is no god but Allah alone, without any partners, unto him belong the dominion and all the praise and He has power over all things.” (Sunan al-Tirmidhī)

While the Quran is the best dhikr because it the speech of Allah, engaging in other forms of dhikr in their recommended time that is specified by the Quran or the Sunnah will be preferred.

Obviously, there is more to be said on the subject, but hope this is enough to encourage you to search it more.

DUA
