content:
People Love the Righteous (الصالح) but Hate the Reformer (المصلح)

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

One of the important responsibilities of a Muslim is to command what is Mauroof (مَعۡرُوفِ) and forbid what is Munkar (مُنكَرِ) because our relationship with each other evolves around this responsibility. Because of the importance of this responsibility, Allah repeated it 7 times in the Quran (3 times in surat Al-Imran, 2 in Al-Tawba 1 in Hajj and 1 in Luqman). In surat al-Tuba, Allah says:

وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ بَعۡضٍ۬‌ۚ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ

“The believers, men and women are protectors of one another. They enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil,” (Al-Tawba 9:71).

The question is what is Mauroof (مَعۡرُوفِ). It is often translated as what is right, just, kind, good, right conduct. All these meanings are reflected in the term but a key element is that all these things must be of the nature that is well accepted to any normal human being. Mauroof (مَعۡرُوفِ) is not based on your opinion or something that you have read, it must be of something well known and broadly recognized as proper conduct.

On the other hand, Munkar (مُنكَرِ) which is often translated as iniquity, indecency, wrong, evil, is something that is well known and broadly recognized as improper conduct.

Having reformers in the community to command the good and forbid the evil is absolutely required to ensure the protection of Allah Who said:

وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ الْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُون ( هود)

“Your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers.” (Hud 11:117)

The Prophet emphasized the important of commanding the good and forbidding the evil on a community by saying:

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «والذي نفسي بيده لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليوشكن الله أن يبعث عليكم عقابا منه ثم تدعونه فلا يستجيب لكم» (رواه الترمذي وأحمد)

The Prophet (PBUH) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you better command the good and forbid the evil or Allah will be on the verge on sending on you a torment from him, and He will not respond to your supplications.

When you are engaging in advising people with what is right and helping them make correction when they are wrong, you must realize that the majority of people do not like those who try to correct them even if they know that such person is a righteous person.

While people like the righteous person because he is good for himself and to them, as soon as he comes reformer, he is hated because his advice creates conflict with their passions and personal interests. Many people reject any correction because of their ego and inflated sense-of-self. Those people consider admitting they made a mistake or that they were wrong is fundamentally too threatening for their egos to tolerate. Also, absorbing the reality that they were wrong would be so psychologically shattering.

The Quran gives us many examples of people who were well honored and liked by their communities but as soon as they become reformers and start advising the people to change their wrong practices, they were hated and ridiculed.

We know this from the history of the Prophet (PBUH). He was well respected and trusted by all people in Mecca until he started asking them to Worship Allah alone. Then, they changed 180 degrees, they started attacking him with the worst name calling. The response is not to be angry or sad but be patient. Allah says:

فَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِہَا‌ۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآىِ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلَّنَہَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرۡضَىٰ (١٣٠)

“Endure with patience what they say, and celebrate the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset, and some hours of the night and at glorify Him at the two ends of the day, so that you may be well pleased.” (Taha 20:130)

قَدۡ نَعۡلَمُ إِنَّهُ ۥ لَيَحۡزُنُكَ ٱلَّذِى يَقُولُونَ‌ۖ فَإِنَّہُمۡ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ يَجۡحَدُونَ (٣٣) وَلَقَدۡ كُذِّبَتۡ رُسُلٌ۬ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ فَصَبَرُواْ عَلَىٰ مَا كُذِّبُواْ وَأُوذُواْ حَتَّىٰٓ أَتَٮٰهُمۡ نَصۡرُنَا‌ۚ

“Surely, We know that what they say makes you sad, but it is not you whom they reject, the transgressors actually deny the signs of Allah. (33) Indeed, many messengers have been rejected before you, but they were patient against their rejection, and they were persecuted until Our help came to them.” (Al-Anaam 6:33-34)

The same thing happened to other Prophets such as Prophet Saleh.

قَالُواْ يَـٰصَـٰلِحُ قَدۡ كُنتَ فِينَا مَرۡجُوًّ۬ا قَبۡلَ هَـٰذَآ‌ۖ أَتَنۡهَٮٰنَآ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا

“They said, “O Salih, we had high hopes in you till this (we loved you and wished for you to be our leader), are you forbidding us to worship what our fathers used to worship?” (Hud 11:62)

Luqman, the wise, warned his son of this rejection when he becomes reformer and advised him to be patient. Allah says:

يَـٰبُنَىَّ أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَٱنۡهَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَكَ‌ۖ إِنَّ ذَٲلِكَ مِنۡ عَزۡمِ ٱلۡأُمُورِ

“My dear son, establish prayers, and enjoin the goodness and forbid the iniquity, and persevere with patience against what may befall you; surely this requires serious determination.” (Luqman 31:17)

You should realize that commanding the good and forbidding the evil is not easy and requires serious determination as mentioned in the above verse of Luqman.

When any serious person is given a responsibility, he studies it and ensures that he is qualified to fulfill it. Reformers are required to have knowledge of the subject and they must also have knowledge of the proper manner and etiquette for delivering the message.

Allah stressed in many verses the importance of using kind, polite, and nice words. Allah says:

وَقُلْ لِعِبَادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنْزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلإِنْسَانِ عَدُوًّا مُبِينًا

And say to My slaves that they should (only) say what is best. Surely, Satan sows conflict among them. Surely Satan is a manifest enemy to man. (Al-Isra 17:53)

Note that this verse includes two commands:
First, you should use the best words and deliver them in the best manner
Second, you should be aware of Satan to ensure that he does not manipulate your words or the way you deliver them to sow conflict.

Maintaining good manners and wisdom when advising people is emphasized in Surat al-Nahl:

ٱدۡعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلۡحِكۡمَةِ وَٱلۡمَوۡعِظَةِ ٱلۡحَسَنَةِ‌ۖ وَجَـٰدِلۡهُم بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحۡسَنُ‌ۚ

‘’Invite (people) to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel. And argue with them in the best manner.’’ (An-Nahl 16:125).

Regarding the manner you speak, Allah instructs us that we should speak in soft and kind tone otherwise people will reject us although we are giving them the truth. Allah says to the Prophet (PBUH):

فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لانْفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ

It is part of the Mercy of Allah that you deal gently with them. If you were rude or harsh-hearted, they would have broken away from you. (Al-Imran 3:159)

In this translation the Arabic word ‘fuz’ is translated as rude. This does not reflect the complete meaning of the word. ‘Fuz’ refers to someone who delivers the right message but in the wrong manner.

So, the word ‘fuz’ in the verse means that if you are rude, they will reject your advice although they know you are telling them the truth. This explains why many people, specifically children, reject the advice of their parents although they know that the parents are right. The problem is with the manner the parents give the advice.

When Allah sent Prophets Musa and Haroun to the Pharaoh, He instructed them to speak kindly to him:

ٱذۡهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّهُ ۥ طَغَىٰ (٤٣) فَقُولَا لَهُ ۥ قَوۡلاً۬ لَّيِّنً۬ا لَّعَلَّهُ ۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ (٤٤)

“Go, both of you, to the Pharaoh who has indeed transgressed, and speak to him gently, perhaps he may take heed or show fear of Allah.” (Taha 20:43-44)

Even if you are giving the best advice to your wife, your children, your friends, or anyone else, you should be kind and gentle because no one can be more transgressor than the Pharaoh and you are not better than Musa or Haroun.

Commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong is not an assignment for the unqualified and uninformed.

ذكر القاضي أبو يعلى في المعتمد- “لا يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر إلا من كان فقيها فيما يأمر به، فقيها فيما ينهى عنه، رفيقا فيما يأمر به، رفيقا فيما ينهى عنه، حليما فيما يأمر به، حليما فيما ينهى عنه”

“It is not permitted for anyone to command what is good and forbid what is evil unless he is knowledgeable in what he commands and what he forbids; and kind in what he commands and what he forbids; and forbearant in what he commands and what he forbids.”

Therefore, knowledge, kindness, forbearance and obviously forbearance includes wisdom and patience are the basic requirements for the job of reformer.

Another very important point, never advice anyone, particularly your spouse, children or friends when they are depressed, in grief or sick because it would be ineffective and counterproductive. Allah says:

وَلَا تَهِنُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ فَقَدْ مَسَّ الْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِثْلُهُ

“Do not fall in despair or be depressed: for you must gain mastery if you are true believers. If have suffered a wound, so have others.” (Al-Imran 3:139)

An important lesson that we should learn from the Prophet (PBUH) is not to dwell on the mistakes that someone has made. Anas ibn Malik (the servant of the Prophet) reported:

خدمت رسول الله ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏عشر سنين والله ما قال لي أفا قط ولا قال لي لشيء لم فعلت كذا وهلا فعلت كذا

“I served the prophet (PBUH) for 10 years and he never said to me “oof”, or said why you did such a thing or why didn’t you do such a thing.”

If this is the way the Prophet (PBUH) treated his servant, can you imagine his noble treatment of his family?

Can you imagine how happy the family would be if the husband and wife would follow the Prophet’s example of not dwelling on mistakes.

Can you imagine how happy the family would be if the husband and wife never lecture each other about what they should have done or should not have done after the event passed.

Kindness is a critical element in human interactions and is particularly essential when correcting others. The prophet (PBUH) emphasized the importance of kindness and gentleness in many of his hadith. Ibn Mas’ud reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِمَنْ يَحْرُمُ عَلَى النَّارِ أَوْ بِمَنْ تَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهِ النَّارُ عَلَى كُلِّ قَرِيبٍ هَيِّنٍ لَيِّنٍ سَهْلٍ

Shall I not tell you for whom the Hellfire is forbidden? It is for every person who is reachable, polite, gentle, and easy to deal with. (Sunan At-Tirmidhi)

Sayeda Aysha (عائِشةَ) reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said

عن عائِشةَ رضيَ اللَّه عنها قَالَتْ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﷺ: إِنَّ اللَّه رفيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ في الأَمْرِ كُلِّه

Allah is kind and He loves kindness in all matters.

In addition to kindness, wisdom, humility and patience, you should not give advice unless you are following it yourself.

The worst thing one can do is to correct someone in public; it is impolite, inconsiderate, insensitive and ineffective. Imam Al-Shafie wrote a poem on the etiquette of advice:

Shower me with your advice in private
and save me your advice in public

تعمدني بنصحك في انفرادي …..
وجنبني النصيحة في الجماعة

Advice among others is a form of rebuke
that I have no desire of hearing

فإن النصح بين الناس نوع …..
من التوبيخ لا أرضى استماعه

If you ignore and disobey my warning
Don’t be angry if your advice is disregarded

وإن خالفتني وعصيت قولي …..
فلا تجزع إذا لم تعط طاعه

We should learn from the kindness, wisdom and tolerance of the Prophet by his reaction to the man who urinated in the mosque and the reaction of the Sahaba and the Prophet’s command to them to let him finish and then talk to him with kindness.

We should follow the Prophet’s example when he wanted to point mistakes that someone has made. The Prophet (PBUH) used to address the public and say: “What is the matter with people who do such and such.” This way he points to the mistake without embarrassing the person.

Having patience cannot be over emphasized, it is essential if you are really sincere in trying to correct someone. When the command of warning the people was given to the Prophet (PBUH) in the beginning of the message, Allah linked the command of warning with the command of being patient:

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمُدَّثِّرُ (١) قُمۡ فَأَنذِرۡ (٢) وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرۡ (٣) وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرۡ (٤) وَٱلرُّجۡزَ فَٱهۡجُرۡ (٥) وَلَا تَمۡنُن تَسۡتَكۡثِرُ (٦) وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصۡبِرۡ (٧)

“You who are wrapped in a cloak. Stand up and warn the people, Magnify your Lord. Purify your clothes. Shun all filth. Do not give out in order to get more in return. And for the sake of your Lord, be patient. (Al-Mudather 74:1-7).

Even when advising your family to pray, you should be patient. Allah says:

وَأۡمُرۡ أَهۡلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۖ

“And enjoin prayers on your family and be patient on it.” (Ta-Ha 20:132)

The Prophet (PBUH) commanded us to be patient and apply our religion with ease as he (PBUH) said:

عن أَنَسُ – رضي الله عنه – أن رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: “إِنَّ هَذَا الدِّينَ مَتِينٌ، فَأَوْغِلُوا فِيهِ بِرِفْقٍ”

“This religion is strongly founded, enter in it with moderation.”

The Prophet (PBUH) also said:

عن أَبِي هريرة النَّبيّ ﷺ قَالَ: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، ولنْ يشادَّ الدِّينُ إلاَّ غَلَبه فسدِّدُوا وقَارِبُوا وَأَبْشِرُوا

“Indeed, this religion is easy, and no one will ever overburden himself in religion, except that it will overcome him. So follow the right course, and seek to be near to it, and receive the good news.” (Sahih Al-Bukhari)

Muslims used to recite when departing from a gathering the short chapter “Al Asr” as a reminder to each other of what is required to be saved from loss:

وَٱلۡعَصۡرِ (١) إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ لَفِى خُسۡرٍ (٢) إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ (٣)

“By the passage of Time, man is in loss. except for those who believe, perform righteous deeds, command each other with truth and command each other to preserve their patience,” (Al-Asr 103:1-3).

These attributes of knowledge, kindness, wisdom, tolerance and patience are so important when correcting people because every person thinks and acts based on how his brain is configured.

The outcome of any discussion depends on whether the configuration of these brains is rigid of flexible. If you sense rigidity, give up the discussion.

عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنا زعيم ببيت في ربض الجنة لمن ترك المراء وإن كان محقا، وببيت في وسط الجنة لمن ترك الكذب وإن كان مازحا، وببيت في أعلى الجنة لمن حسن خلقه

“I guarantee a palace in the outskirts of Paradise for the one who gives up disputing while he is right, and a palace in the middle of paradise for the one who abandons lies even when he is joking, and a palace in the highest part of paradise for the one who has excellent character.” (Abu Dawood)

Imam Al-Shafie used to say:

قال الامام الشافعي رحمه الله مَا نَاظَرْتُ أَحَدًا قَطُّ إِلا أَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ يُوَفَّقَ وَيُسَدَّدَ وَيُعَانَ وَيَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ رِعَايَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَحِفْظٌ

“I have never debated anyone but would love for him to be guided, directed, helped, and to be under the care and protection of Allah.”

He also said:

يقول الامام الشافعي رحمه الله* ما جادلت أحداً إلا تمنّيت أن يظهِر الله الحق على لسانه دوني

“I have never debated anyone but wished that Allah brings the truth on his tongue instead of mine”.

An obvious requirement for anyone who is giving advice is to be knowledgeable about the subject. When you are asked about something you don’t know, admit it.

As final point, don’t use religion to get your family members feel guilty in order to get your rights from them. Don’t use religion as a weapon to force your parents, your spouse, or your children to respect or obey you.

If you have to seek your rights from your family by invoking the Quran and the teaching of the Prophet, then something is seriously wrong with the family dynamics. Respect and obedience should come from love and not by force or fear of committing a sin.

وَإِذۡ قَالَ لُقۡمَـٰنُ لِٱبۡنِهِۦ وَهُوة يَعِظُهُ ۥ يَـٰبُنَىَّ لَا تُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ‌ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشِّرۡكَ لَظُلۡمٌ عَظِيمٌ۬ (١٣)

“And (remember) when Luqman said to his son, when he was advising him, “My dear son, do not ascribe any partner to Allah. Surely, ascribing partners to Him is a grave transgression.” (Luqman 31:13)

We note that Luqman advised his son not to have associates with Allah, but when it came to respecting parents, he did not advise his son; it was Allah who instructed the son.

As Allah directs your spouse and children to love, respect and obey you, you should give your parents the respect and kindness they deserve even after they pass away. A man asked the Prophet:

يا رسول الله هل بقي عليّ شيء مِن برِّ والديّ بعد موتهما ؟

“O Messenger of Allah, is there anything left from the goodness I owe my parents after their death?”

The Prophet (PBUH) replied:

نعم ، أربعة أشياء ، أن تدعُوَ لهما كل يوم خمس مرات ، رب اغفر لي ولوالديّ ، رب ارحمهما كما ربَّياني صغيرًا ، وإكرام صديقهما ، وإنفاذ عهدهما ، وصلة الرحم التي لا تُوصَل إلا من قِبلهما

“Yes, four things:
1) Pray and ask forgiveness for them five time per day by saying: (رب اغفر لي ولوالديّ ، رب ارحمهما كما ربَّياني صغيرًا) My Lord, forgive me, my parents, My Lord have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small.
2) Be kind to their friends.
3) Fulfill their pledges.
4) And maintain the ties of kinship that come only from their direction”.
(Ahmad, Abu Dawood &ibn Majah)

DUA

title: The Master of the Best Characters – Forbearance (الحلم)
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه  ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

The Quran informs us that Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) made four requests to Allah and Allah corrected them for him. Prophet Ibrahim asked Allah to make his offspring as religious leaders, but Allah corrected him by saying that only the righteous ones will be granted this honor but not the wrongdoers from your progeny.  Allah says:

وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٲهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُ ۥ بِكَلِمَـٰتٍ۬ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ‌ۖ قَالَ إِنِّى جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامً۬ا‌ۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى‌ۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ (١٢٤)

And (recall) when his Lord put Ibrahim to a test with certain commands, and he fulfilled them, He (Allah) said, “I am going to make you an Imam for the mankind.” He (Ibrahim) said, “And from among my offspring (to make leaders too)?” He (Allah) replied, “My covenant does not extend to the unjust (wrong-doers).” (Al-Baqara 2:124)

Prophet Ibrahim learnt the lesson and he made another request that Allah grants prosperity only to the believers from his progeny. Allah corrected him here too by saying even the disbelievers will be granted prosperity in this life but their account will be in the hereafter.  Allah says:

وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٲهِـۧمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَـٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنً۬ا وَٱرۡزُقۡ أَهۡلَهُ ۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٲتِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡہُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأَخِرِ‌ۖ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ ۥ قَلِيلاً۬ ثُمَّ أَضۡطَرُّهُ ۥۤ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِ‌ۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ (١٢٦)

“And (recall) when Ibrahim said, “My Lord, make this a city of peace, and provide its people with fruits – those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.” He (Allah) said, “As for the one who disbelieves, I shall let him enjoy a little, then I shall drag him to the punishment of the Fire. How evil an end it is!” (Al-Baqara 2:124)

Prophet Ibrahim asked Allah to grant the People a Prophet to teach them the Quran and wisdom and to purify them.  Allah corrected the role of the Prophet that he will first purifies them and then teaches them the Quran and wisdom.  Prophet Ibrahim said:

رَبَّنَا وَٱبۡعَثۡ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولاً۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ءَايَـٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيہِمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ (١٢٩)

“Our Lord, raise in their midst a Messenger from among them, who recites to them Your signs, and teaches them the Book and the wisdom, and purifies them. Indeed You, and You alone, are the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.” (Al-Baqara 2:129)

Allah’s response was:

لَقَدۡ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذۡ بَعَثَ فِيہِمۡ رَسُولاً۬ مِّنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡہِمۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَڪِّيہِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡحِڪۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِى ضَلَـٰلٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ (١٦٤)

“Allah has surely conferred favor on the believers when He raised in their midst a Messenger from among themselves who recites to them His signs and purifies than and teaches them the Book and the Wisdom, while earlier, they were in flagrant error.” (Al-Emran 3:164)

The fourth request that Prophet Ibrahim made was that Allah grants him a righteous son “a saleh son” but Allah told him that we are granting you a forbearing gentle (Haleem) son.  Allah says:

رَبِّ هَبۡ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحِينَ (١٠٠) فَبَشَّرۡنَـٰهُ بِغُلَـٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ۬ (١٠١)

“O my Lord, bless me with a righteous son.” (100) So, We gave him the glad tidings of a forbearing (gentle) son.” (Al-Saffat 37:100-101)

This means that one cannot be righteous and good unless he is first forbearing (Haleem).  Both the terms Hilm which refers to a certain human character and the term Haleem that refers to the one who possesses the character of Hilm are difficult to translate because they involve many attributes.  The closest English translation for Hilm is forbearance and Haleem as a forbearing person.

The attribute of forbearance (Hilm) encompasses all the good characters of wisdom, patience, maturity, tolerance, compassion, kindness, mercy, humility, dignity, forgiveness, strength, calm, optimism and so on.  This is why the Arabs used to say: “Forbearance “Hilm” is the master of all characters.” (الحلم سيد الأخلاق)

The person who possesses this attribute of forbearance (hilm) is the one who is not provoked by ignorance or disobedience, he is the one who is kind, merciful and quick to forgive though he is able to punish. The Forbearing ‘Haleem” person is who is quiet and peaceful, and who is in control of his lower nature.

This attribute of Hilm is the most critical for any Muslim.  In fact, Al-Haleem (The Most Forbearing) is one of the glorious names of Allah.

The first step in developing the character of Hilm (Forbearance) to learn how to control your anger. There are many hadith in which the Prophet (PBUH) gave the advice to the companions about the importance of controlling their anger. As example, Abu Hurayrah said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه: أن رجلًا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أوصني، قال: «لا تغضب» فردد مرارًا، قال: «لا تغضب» [أخرجه البخاري]

A man asked the Prophet (PBUH) for an advice and the Prophet (PBUH) said, “Do not get angry”. The man repeated that several times and the Prophet (PBUH) gave the same response “Do not get angry”. [Al-Bukhari].

Since controlling anger of the first step for achieving the character of Hilm, Allah emphasized it in the following verse from Al-Imran:

وَٱلۡڪَـٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (١٣٤)

“those who control anger and forgive people. And Allah loves those who are good doers.” (Al-Imran 3:134)

Allah commands us to imitate the character of the Prophet (PBUH) by taking him as our role model, as He says:

لَّقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِى رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ۬ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأَخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرً۬ا (٢١)

“There is indeed a good role model for you in the Messenger of Allah – for the one who has hope in (meeting) Allah and the Last Day, and remembers Allah much.” (Al-Ahzab 33:21)

So, if you are really serious about taking the Prophet (PBUH) as your role model, you should study his examples of forbearance “Hilm” and strive to imitate them.

Both before and after his prophethood, The Prophet (PBUH) was the gentlest of people. This is a quality that he carried throughout his life. Allah acknowledged this quality and highlighted its importance by saying:

فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡ‌ۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَ‌ۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡہُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ‌ۖ (١٥٩)

“And it is by the Mercy of Allah that you were gentle with them, and had you been rude and harsh-hearted, they would have scattered away from you; so overlook (their faults), and ask (Allah's) forgiveness for them; and consult them in the affairs.” (Al-Imran 3:159)

The Prophet never thought to avenge himself for wrongs done to his person. In addition, he was the hardest to anger, the easiest to please, and the most forgiving of all. When Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) began his prophetic mission, the disbelievers in Mecca leveled at him every kind of insult and indignity.

We know from the well recorded history that the disbelievers tried everything they could think of to anger the Prophet (PBUH), but he endured everything they did to him. He reacted to all their evil deeds with calm, patience, and tolerance and more than that when Jibril came to him and told him that Allah has granted him the authority to ask the angels of mountains to destroy the disbelievers, the Prophet (PBUH) refused and instead, he prayed to Allah by saying: (اللهم اغفر لقومي، فإنهم لا يعلمون) “O’ Allah guide my people; they just don’t know”.

While there are many accounts that clearly demonstrate the Prophet’s level of (Hilm), I’ll only mention few in this talk. I sincerely hope that you study this subject to learn how to develop this prophetic character in your character.

Example 1: The Prophet’s reaction to the Jewish scholar Zayd ibn Si’nah (زيد بن سعنة).

The Jewish scholar Zayd ibn Si’nah (زيد بن سعنة) wanted to test the attribute of forbearance “Hilm” on the Prophet (PBUH) because a key attribute of the upcoming Prophet that was prophesized in the Torat is his great level of forbearance (Hilm) and patience in face of ignorance.

So, Zayd took advantage of an opportunity when a man came asking the Prophet (PBUH) for financial help and the Prophet did not have any to give at that time, so he asked for a loan and Zayd was quick in lending the Prophet (PBUH) an amount of dates for a specified time. Three days before the designated date, Zayd came while the Prophet (PBUH) was standing with Omar ibn Al-Khattab and grabbed the Prophet (PBUH) by his robe around his neck and pulled it hard and in harsh and rude way he shouted at the Prophet (PBUH) saying:

وجاء زيد بن سعنة – قبل إسلامه – يطلب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بدين، فجبذ ثوبه عن منكبه وأخذ بمجامع ثيابه، وأغلظ له، ثم قال: إنكم يا بني عبدالمطلب قوم مطل

‘O Muhammad, pay me back. You sons of Abdul Muttalib are always delinquent in paying your debts.’”

Omar got so angry and pulled Zayd and holding him asked the Prophet for permission to cut his neck. But the Prophet (PBUH) stopped Omar and reprimanded him and said:

فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أنا وهو كنا إلى غير هذا أحوج منك يا عمر، تأمرني بحسن القضاء وتأمره بحسن التقاضي

“O Omar, both I and he expected better from you. You should have ordered me to pay what I owe him, and you should have asked him to asks for his money with courtesy.”

Then, the Prophet (PBUH) said to Zayd:

ثم قال: «لقد بقي من أجله ثلاث» وأمر عمر أن يقضيه ماله، ويزيده عشرين صاعًا لِمَا روَّعه. فكان سبب إسلامه

Zayd, there are still three days to the deadline. Then he told Omar: pay Zayd the amount and add more until he is pleased as recompense for the fear you caused him.

Omar took Zayd to pay him the dates and increased the amount until Zayd said that is enough. Then Zayd said: O’ Omar, I know that there are still three days for the payment, do you why I did this.

يقول زيد - وهو من اليهود -: ما بقي من علامات النبوة شيء إلا وقد عرفتها في محمد إلا اثنتين لم أخبرهما: يسبق حلمه جهله، ولا تزيده شدة الجهل إلا حلمًا. فاختبرته بهذا، فوجدته كما وُصِف] أخرجه البغوي في «الأنوار» وقال المحقق أخرجه الحاكم في المستدرك و أبو نعيم في الدلائل وذكره الهيتمي في مجمع الزوائد ونسبه للطبراني]

I did this because I have found in the Prophet (PBUH) all the characters of prophethood that are described to us in the Torah except for two that I wanted to check and they are he responds to ignorance with forbearance and the more the ignorance the more forbearance he shows (يسبق حلمه جهله، ولا تزيده شدة الجهل إلا حلمًا) and now I found both of them. The Messenger responded to my ignorant, harsh, rude manner only by increasing his own forbearance.

O Omar you be my witness, I donate all these dates to the poor Muslims, let us go back to the Prophet to declare my Shahadah.

They returned to the Prophet (PBUH) and Zayd declared his Islam.

The Prophet (PBUH) always responded to words and actions that were turned against him with maturity, compassion, and kindness. This is just one simple demonstration of the Prophet’s patience and gentleness that brought many people to Islam.

Ask yourself, how many people you may have discouraged from considering Islam by your rudeness or even derived a Muslim, particularly, a youth out Islam because of your anger and lack of forbearance (Hilm).

Ask yourself, do you demonstrate the character of Hilm with your wife, your children or your students.

Let us look at other examples of the level of Hilm of the Prophet (PBUH) with his family.

As would happen within any family, conflicts sometimes happen between the husband and the wife and the Prophet’s house was not immune from these conflicts. The lesson that we need to learn how the Prophet’s forbearance (Hilm) was demonstrated in these situations.

Example 2:  Conflict between the Prophet (PBUH) and his wife Aisha (RA)

Al-Hafez Al-Dimishqi (الحافظ الدمشقي) reported:

حدث خلاف بين النبي  وعائشة ـ رضي الله عنهما فقال لها من ترضين بيني وبينك .. أترضين بعمر؟ قالت: لا أرضي عمر قط "عمر غليظ". قال أترضين بأبيك بيني وبينك؟ قالت: نعم، فبعث رسول الله رسولاً إلى أبي بكر  فلما جاء قال الرسول : تتكلمين أم أتكلم؟ قالت: تكلم ولا تقل إلا حقاً، فرفع أبو بكر يده فلطم أنفها، فولت عائشة هاربة منه واحتمت بظهر النبي ، حتى قال له رسول الله: أقسمت عليك لما خرجت بأن لم ندعك لهذا. فلما خرج قامت عائشة فقال لها الرسول : ادني مني؛ فأبت؛ فتبسم وقال: لقد كنت من قبل شديدة اللزوق(اللصوق) بظهري – إيماءة إلى احتمائها بظهره  خوفاً من ضرب أبيها لها -، ولما عاد أبو بكر ووجدهما يضحكان قال: أشركاني في سلامكما، كما أشركتماني في حربكما". (رواه الحافظ الدمشقي في السمط الثمين)

One time, the Prophet (PBUH) and Sayeda Aisha had a conflict. The Prophet asked her whom does she want to come to judge between them.  Do you want Omar, she said: No. Do want your father; she said yes.

The Prophet (PBUH) send to Abu Bakr to come and when he came, The Prophet (PBUH) asked Aysha:  Do you want to speak first or do you want me to speak.

She said: You speak but don’t say anything other than the truth.

Abu Bakr, shouted at Aysha how dare you say that; who else will tell the truth other than the Prophet and stood going toward her to hit her.

So, she jumped and hid behind the Prophet (PBUH).

The Prophet (PBUH) said to Abu Bakr, please leave, we did not ask you to come to do this.

Abu Bakr, left.  The Prophet (PBUH) asked Aysha to come close to him but she refused.  The Prophet (PBUH) smiled and went toward her and said: you were sticking to me for protection form your father and now you don’t want to come close.  He went and kissed her and they started laughing.

When Abu Bakr heard their laugh from the outside the door, he knocked on the door.

When the Prophet (PBUH) opened the door, Abu Bakr said:  Get me involved in your peace as you involved me in your conflict.

Question: What would you have done if you faced the same situation and your wife told you to speak but don’t say anything but the truth. Would you get angry and create another conflict by saying how dare you are accusing me that I may not tell the truth? Your anger will only make the situation worse and change a simple conflict to a bigger one that can lead to bad consequence.

Example 3:  Sayeda Aysha (RA) Getting Angry and Breaking a Plate with Food

The Nisa’i (النسائي) reported

روى النسائي عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها أنها أتت بطعام في صفحة لها إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه فجاءت عائشة متزرة بكساء ومعها فهر "حجر" ففلقت به الصفحة، فجمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين فلقتي الصفحة ويقول: « كلوا، غارت أمكم » مرتين، ثم أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صفحة عائشة فبعث بها إلى أم سلمة، وأعطى صفحة أم سلمة عائشة .

One day the Prophet (PBUH) was in the house of Aysha and had some companions visiting his.  Umm Salamah came and knocked on the door and when the Prophet (PBUH) opened, she handed him a dish with food.  When The prophet (PBUH) put the plate on the floor so the companions can eat, Aysha came with a rock and throw it at the plate splitting it and spilling the food.  The prophet (PBUH) put the two pieces of the plate together with whatever food still there and looked at the companions smiling and Aysha and said: No worry, your mother Aysha is a little jealous. After the gathering, he took a plate from Aysha and gave it to Umm Salamah.

Question:  what would be you reaction if your wife did something similar or even something smaller such as accidently spilling the food that is being serving to your friends.

Example 3:  The Response of the Prophet (PBUH) to his Wife Maymunah (RA) Locking Him Out of the House

It is reported by Ibn Sa’d (ابن سعد)

عَنْ مَيْمُونَة بْنَت ٱلَحَارِث قَالَتْ : خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ عِنْدِي فَأَغْلَقْتُ دُونَهُ الْبَابَ فَجَاءَ يَسْتَفْتِحُ الْبَابَ فَأَبَيْتُ أَنْ أَفْتَحَ لَهُ ، فَقَالَ : " أَقْسَمْتُ إِلَّا فَتَحْتِهِ لِي " فَقُلْتُ لَهُ : تَذْهَبُ إِلَى أَزْوَاجِكَ فِي لَيْلَتِي هَذِهِ ، قَالَ : " مَا فَعَلْتُ وَلَكِنْ وَجَدْتُ حَقْنًا مِنْ بَوْلِي " . [ابن سعد في الطبقات الكبرى]

The Prophet (PBUH) was in the house of his wife Maymunah and after they went to sleep; the Prophet (PBUH) got up slowly from the bed and open the door and went outside. When Maymunah noticed what he did, she got up and locked the door. After short time, the Prophet (PBUH) came and tried to open the door but it was locked. He knocked on the door and Maymunah said, I was awake but I did not respond and did not open the door. The Prophet (PBUH) knocked on the door several times but I did respond. The Prophet then said: I make an oath by Allah that you open the door for me.  Only then she got up and opened the door.

As soon as the Prophet entered, she grabbed him from his clothing and said while angry: Where did you go, how can you leave me and go to one of your other wives.

In a clam voice, the Prophet (PBUH) said: I did not go anywhere, I felt pain in my stomach and did not want to wake you up, so I went outside to walk a little and when the pain subsided, I came back.  She apologized and they went back to sleep.

Question:  What would you have done, if you stayed late and your wife locked the door that you cannot enter and when you entered, she shouts at you where have been. The Prophet (PBUH) did not get angry, rather he responded to her in calm voice and comforted her and the matter ended.

Example 5:  The Prophets’ Reaction to the Youth Who Wanted Permission to Commit Adultery

Reported by Ahmad that Abu Umamah (أَبِي أُمَامَةَ) said:

عَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ قَالَ إِنَّ فَتًى شَابًّا أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ائْذَنْ لِي بِالزِّنَا فَأَقْبَلَ الْقَوْمُ عَلَيْهِ فَزَجَرُوهُ قَالُوا مَهْ مَهْ فَقَالَ ادْنُهْ فَدَنَا مِنْهُ قَرِيبًا قَالَ فَجَلَسَ قَالَ أَتُحِبُّهُ لِأُمِّكَ قَالَ لَا وَاللَّهِ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاءَكَ قَالَ وَلَا النَّاسُ يُحِبُّونَهُ لِأُمَّهَاتِهِمْ قَالَ أَفَتُحِبُّهُ لِابْنَتِكَ قَالَ لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاءَكَ قَالَ وَلَا النَّاسُ يُحِبُّونَهُ لِبَنَاتِهِمْ قَالَ أَفَتُحِبُّهُ لِأُخْتِكَ قَالَ لَا وَاللَّهِ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاءَكَ قَالَ وَلَا النَّاسُ يُحِبُّونَهُ لِأَخَوَاتِهِمْ قَالَ أَفَتُحِبُّهُ لِعَمَّتِكَ قَالَ لَا وَاللَّهِ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاءَكَ قَالَ وَلَا النَّاسُ يُحِبُّونَهُ لِعَمَّاتِهِمْ قَالَ أَفَتُحِبُّهُ لِخَالَتِكَ قَالَ لَا وَاللَّهِ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاءَكَ قَالَ وَلَا النَّاسُ يُحِبُّونَهُ لِخَالَاتِهِمْ قَالَ فَمَسَحَ يَدَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ ذَنْبَهُ وَطَهِّرْ قَلْبَهُ وَحَصِّنْ فَرْجَهُ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ بَعْدُ ذَلِكَ الْفَتَى يَلْتَفِتُ إِلَى شَيْءٍ ) مسند أحمد باقي مسند الأنصار)

A young man came to the Prophet (PBUH) and said, “O Messenger of Allah, give me permission to commit adultery.” The people shouted at him rebuking him, how date he can make such request.

But the Prophet (PBUH) asked them to stop and asked the young man to come and sit with him. When The young man came and sat down by the Prophet.

The Prophet said, “Would you like that for your mother?” The youth said, “No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you (لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاءَكَ).” The Prophet said, “Neither would people like it for their mothers.

Would you like that for your daughter?” The youth said, “No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you.” The Prophet said, “Neither would people like it for their daughters.

Would you like that for your sister?” The youth said, “No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you.” The Prophet said, “Neither would people like it for their sisters.

Would you like that for your aunts?” The youth said, “No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you.” And. said: Hate what Allah hates and love for your brother what you love for yourself.

The youth, asked the Prophet (PBUH) to pray for him.  The Prophet (PBUH) placed his hand on the youth’s heart and said, “O Allah, forgive his sins, purify his heart, and guard his chastity.” (اغْفِرْ ذَنْبَهُ وَطَهِّرْ قَلْبَهُ وَحَصِّنْ فَرْجَهُ)

The young man left the masjid saying, I came and the adultery was the most beloved to me and I am leaving with adultery the most despised act to me. (Musnad Ahmad)

I just gave few examples demonstrating the Prophet’ Forbearance (Hilm)  and this is why Allah selected the Prophet character as the one attribute to praise him with when He said: “And you have an exalted character” (Al-Qalam 68:4) (وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ۬ (٤))

Is the Prophet’s character hard to imitate?  Yes, it is hard unless you are one of those who really loved the Prophet (PBUH). Frankly, it is easy for anyone to claim loving the Prophet (PBUH) but unless the person strives to imitate the Prophet’s character, the claim will be just an empty talk.

Example 6: The Hilm of Ma’n ibn Za’ida (معن بن زائدة)

In the remaining few minutes, I’ll give one account of the behavior of one of the true Muslims who committed to follow the Prophet example in forbearance (Hilm) and this is Ma’n ibn Za’ida (معن بن زائدة) (died 70 H).  Ma’n ibn Za’ida was an army commander and  member of nobility of the Shayban tribe who was committed to imitate the Prophet (PBUH) in his forbearance (Hilm).

People wanted to test Ma’n’s “Hilm” him. They searched for the most obnoxious person and promised to give him 100 camels if he can get Ma’n (معن) angry.

So, the man slaughtered a sheep and wore its skin the bloody and dirty side of the skin  on the outside and walked to the house of Ma’n (معن) uninvited and without giving him any greeting and looked at Ma’n with disgust and said:  Do you remember Ma’n (معن) when your clothing were the skin of sheep and your sandals were from the skin of camels (أتذكر إذ لحافك جلد شاةٍ وإذ نعلاك من جلد البعيرِ؟).

Ma’n said: Yes, I remember that (أذكر ذلك)

The man said: glory to the one who gave you honor and make you know how to sit of these soft cushions (فسبحان الذي أعطاك ملكاً وعلّمك الجلوس على السريرِ)

Ma’n said:  Glory to Allah almighty (سبحانه وتعالى)

The man said: (فلست مُسَلِّماً ما عشتُ حياً علـى مـعـن بتسلـيـم الأمـيـرِ) You will never live as Muslim since you did not great me

Ma’n said: (إن سلَّمت رددنا عليك السلام، وإن تركت فلا ضير عليك) If you greeted us, we would have greeted you but if you did not greet us no blame be on you.

The man said: (سأرحل عن بلاد أنت فيهـا، ولو جار الزمان على الفقيرِ) I’ll depart any city you live in it even if this makes me poor.

Ma’n said: (إن أقمت بنا فعلى الرحب والسعة، وإن رحلت عنا فمصحوباً بالسّلامة) If you stay with us, you will be very welcomed and if you depart, we wish safety in your travel.

The man started getting desperate in getting Ma’n to be angry, so he said to him:

Then the son of the deprived (يابـن ناقـصـة) grant me some money since I decided to leave (فجـد لـي بالـقـلـيل أو الـكـثـيرِ).

Note: that Ma’n is called Ma’n ibn Za’ida (معن بن زائدة) Zaida is his mother name and it means the “proposer one”. So his name will be Ma’n the son of the proposer one. But the man called him Ma’n ibn Na’qsa meaning Ma’s the son of the deprived one.

Ma’n continued to tolerate the man’s continued insults and ordered his workers to give him  one thousand dinars.

When they gave it to him, the man said: This is too little, I am expecting more, you have plenty of money and whatever you have is accidental since you don’t deserve it and you have no intelligent and cannot make proper decisions.

قليـل مـا أتيـتَ بـه وإنـي لأطمع منك بالمال الكثيرِ فثنِّ فقد أتاك الملك عفواً بــلا عـقـل ولا رأي مـنـيرِ

Ma’n ordered his workers to give the man another 1000 dinars. (أعطوه ألفاً ثانياً)

At this time, the man came close to Ma’n (معن) and kissed his hands and feet and said: May Allah save you and give you long life, there is no one like you, your forbearance is unmatched and your generosity is overwhelming. If this is your character, how was the character of the Prophet whom you try to imitate.

Ma’n looked at his workers and said: We gave him 2000 dinars for insulting us. So, give him 4000 for honoring us.

The man said: (نفسي فداك، ما فعلت ذلك إلا لمئة بعير جُعِلَت على إغضابك). I offer my life as sacrifice for yours, I haven’t done this expect I was promised to get 100 camels if I can make you angry

Ma’n said: (لا خوف عليك، ثم أمر له بمئتي بعير، نصفها للّرهان والنصف الآخر له.) No fear be on you, and ordered to give him 200 camels, and said, one 100 for the bet that was made and 100 extras for you.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom to show our love for the Prophet (PBUH) by adopting his Hilm in our character. If Ma’n can demonstrate an element of the Prophet Hilm, we ask Allah to cleanse our soul to also demonstrate it.

DUA

title: Extending Your Life & The Eight Gates of Heaven
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله تعالى من شرور أنفسنا، وسيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين.

Imam Abu Musa Al-Madini (أبو موسى المدينى) (161 H -234 H) has book of hadeath that focused on the long hadeath. In his collection of hadeath book At-Targheen Al-Tarheeb (الترغيب والترهيب) (Inspiration and intimidation/ Instilling pleasure and Fear) , he reported that Abdurrahman ibn Samura (عبد الرحمن بن سمرة) said:

عن عبد الرحمن بن سمرة قال :خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ونحن في الصفة بالمدينة ، فقام علينا فقال :إني رأيت البارحة عجبا :رأيت رجلا من أمتي أتاه ملك الموت ليقبض روحه، فجاءه بر والديه فرد ملك الموت عنه .

While we were in Al-Sufa in Al-Madina (this is the place where the Prophet (PBUH) designated in his Masjid as shelter for the homeless among the Muslims to stay in it), the messenger of Allah (PBUH) came and said: I saw something astonishing last night: I saw a man from my nation who the angel of death came to seize his soul, but his good treatment of his parents prevented the angel of death and caused him to leave.

This hadeath is long and in it the Prophet (PBUH) talked about 17 people from his nation who were saved because of different good things that they used to do. You can find the English translation of the hadeath in the book entitled “The Soul” (الروح) by Imam ibn Al-Qyyem All-Jawziah (ابن قيم الجوزية).

I want to focus on this part because it may cause confusion regarding the belief that our life is predestined and when the time comes, there will be no delays as Allah says:

وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ۬‌ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَأۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةً۬‌ۖ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ (٣٤)

“For every people there is an appointed time. When their appointed time comes, they can neither delay it for an hour nor can they advance it.” (Al-A’raf 7:34)

قُل لَّآ أَمۡلِكُ لِنَفۡسِى ضَرًّ۬ا وَلَا نَفۡعًا إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۗ لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ‌ۚ إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ فَلَا يَسۡتَأۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةً۬‌ۖ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ (٤٩)

“Say: “I have no power to bring a harm or a benefit to myself except what Allah may will. For every people there is an appointed time. When their appointed time comes, they can neither delay it for an hour nor can they advance it.” (Yunus 10:49)

وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلۡمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيۡہَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ۬ وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ۬ مُّسَمًّ۬ى‌ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَأۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةً۬‌ۖ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ (٦١)

“If Allah were to seize the people for their injustice, He would have spared a single creature on earth, but He gives them respite until an appointed time. When their appointed time comes, they can neither delay it for an hour nor can they advance it.” (Al-Nahl 16:61)

وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهَا‌ۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ (١١)

“And Allah will never give respite to anyone once his appointed time comes. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.” (Al-Munafiqun 63:11)

If our lives are predestined, then how can our life be extended according to the Hadith. Does this mean that there is a contradiction? Not really, especially if we look at other hadeath:

عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ : سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ : مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ .

Whoever is pleased to have his provision expanded and his life span extended, let him keep good relations with his family. (Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

The question remains, do these two hadith contradict the predestination of our lives as we understand it from the Quran. The answer is found in Surat Al-Ra’d:

وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلاً۬ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُمۡ أَزۡوَٲجً۬ا وَذُرِّيَّةً۬‌ۚ وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأۡتِىَ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ۬ ڪِتَابٌ۬ (٣٨)

‘’And indeed, We sent Messengers before you, and granted them wives and offspring. And it is not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by Allah’s leave. For every appointed time there is a book.” (Al-Rad 13:38)

This verse suggests that the life of everyone of us is written not as one number or in one line, it is written in a book. This is further explained in the following verse:

يَمۡحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثۡبِتُ‌ۖ وَعِندَهُ ۥۤ أُمُّ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ (٣٩)

“Allah wipes off what He wills and affirms (what He wills), and with Him is the Mother Book. (Al-Lad 13:39)

So, we still have chance to extend our lives to do the right things to deserve to enter paradise. In paradise, there are 8 gates.

So, while the number of gates of Paradise is not given in the Quran, the number of gates of Hell is given:

وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمَوۡعِدُهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ (٤٣) لَهَا سَبۡعَةُ أَبۡوَٲبٍ۬ لِّكُلِّ بَابٍ۬ مِّنۡہُۡم جُزۡءٌ۬ مَّقۡسُومٌ (٤٤)

“”And surely, Hell is the promised place for them all. (43) “It (Hell) has seven gates, for each gate is a group of them assigned. (44)” (Al-Hijr 15:43-44)

But how the scholars derived that Paradise has eight gates. They inferred this number from the Quran itself from a linguistic analysis of certain verses.

This is an interesting analysis. Scholars identified three uses for the letter “Waw” (و) in the Arabic language:

First: It is used for an oath (واو القسم) such as:

وَ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَضُحَٮٰهَا (١) وَ ٱلۡقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَٮٰهَا (٢) وَ ٱلنَّہَارِ إِذَا جَلَّٮٰهَا (٣) وَ ٱللَّيۡلِ إِذَا يَغۡشَٮٰهَا (٤)

By the sun and its brightness; (1) By the moon as it follows it (the sun); (2) By the day as it shows its (the sun’s) glory; (3) By the night as it conceals it (the sun); (4) (Al-Shams 91:1-4)

وَ الضُّحَى * وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى ﴾ [الضحى: 1، 2].

By the forenoon (1) By the night when it becomes still. (Ad-Dhuha 93:1-2)

Second: It is used as the conjunction “and” (واو العطف) such as:

﴿ وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا وَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ﴾ [الحديد: 26]،

“Indeed, We sent Nuh and Ibrahim,” (Al-Hadid 57:26)

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱرۡڪَعُواْ وَٱسۡجُدُواْ وَ ٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ وَ ٱفۡعَلُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ (٧٧)

“O you who have believed! Bow down, and prostrate yourselves, and worship your Lord and do good that you may succeed.” (Al-Hajj 22:77)

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَ أَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ وَ امْسَحُوا بِرُؤوسِكُمْ وَ أَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ ﴾ [المائدة: 6].

“O you who believe! When you intend to offer the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows and rub your heads and (wash) your feet up to the ankles.” (Al-Maidah 5:6)

As a side issue, linguistics as well as Jurist differed regarding the use of this “waw”, whether it implies sequence or not.

These two uses of the letter “Waw” are obvious, the third use of the letter “Waw” is interesting:

Third: the letter “Waw” is used to refer to the number 8 (واو الثمانية). We note that in several verses in the Quran, when there is a list of items, the letter “Waw” is placed before the 8th item. The following are examples:

سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَـٰثَةٌ۬ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةٌ۬ سَادِسُہُمۡ كَلۡبُہُمۡ رَجۡمًۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ‌ۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةٌ۬ وَ ثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ‌ۚ

“Some will say, “(They were) three, the fourth is their dog,” and some will say, “Five, the sixth is their dog,” – guessing at the unseen; and some will say, “Seven, and the eighth is their dog.” (Al-Kahf 18:22)

ٱلتَّـٰٓٮِٕبُونَ ٱلۡعَـٰبِدُونَ ٱلۡحَـٰمِدُونَ ٱلسَّـٰٓٮِٕحُونَ ٱلرَّٲڪِعُونَ ٱلسَّـٰجِدُونَ ٱلۡأَمِرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَٱلنَّاهُونَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنڪَرِ وَ ٱلۡحَـٰفِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ (١١٢)

(The Triumphant) are 1) those who turn repentant (to Allah), 2) those who serve (Him), 3) those who praise (Him), 4) those who fast, 5) those who bow down, 6) those who fall prostrate, 7) those who enjoin the right and 8) forbid the wrong and those who keep the limits (set) by Allah. (Al-Tuba 9:112)

عَسَىٰ رَبُّهُ ۥۤ إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَن يُبۡدِلَهُ ۥۤ أَزۡوَٲجًا خَيۡرً۬ا مِّنكُنَّ مُسۡلِمَـٰتٍ۬ مُّؤۡمِنَـٰتٍ۬ قَـٰنِتَـٰتٍ۬ تَـٰٓٮِٕبَـٰتٍ۬ عupdate_todo_statusبِدَٲتٍ۬ سَـٰٓٮِٕحَـٰتٍ۬ ثَيِّبَـٰتٍ۬ وَ أَبۡكَارً۬ا (٥)

“It may be if he divorced you (all) that his Lord will give him instead of you, wives better than you: 1) submissive (to Allah), 2) believers, 3) obedient, 4) penitent, 5) adorers (of Allah), 6) given to fasting, 7) widows and 8) virgins.” (Al-Tahrim 66:5)

But, how is this application of the “Waw” used to derive the number of gates of Heaven. It is thru comparing two verses in Surat Al-Zumar:

وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا‌ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٲبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُہَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ رُسُلٌ۬ مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَـٰتِ رَبِّڪُمۡ … (٧١)

“And those who disbelieved are driven towards Jahannam (Hell) in groups, until when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say,” (Al-Zumur 39:71)

Note here that when the disbelievers were driven to Hell, the gates are opened with no “Waw” before it. This indicates that Hell has 7 gates.

وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّہُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًا‌ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَ فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٲبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُہَا سَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيۡڪُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَـٰلِدِينَ (٧٣)

“And those who maintained the Taqwa of their Lord are driven unto the Garden in troops when they reach it, and its gates are opened and its keepers will say” (Al-Zumur 39:73)

Note that here the letter “Waw came before the phrase “its gates are opened”. Based on the consideration that this is the “Waw of the eight”, the scholars concluded that Paradise has eight gates.

This inference is further supported by the hadeath:

عن عبادة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: “مَنْ قَالَ: أَشْهَدُ أَنّ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاّ الله وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَنّ مُحَمّداً عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، وَأَنّ عِيسَىَ عَبْدُ اللّهِ وَابْنُ أَمَتِهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا إِلَىَ مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ، وَأَنّ الْجَنّةَ حَقّ، وَأَنّ النّارَ حَقّ، أَدْخَلَهُ اللّهُ مِنْ أَيّ أَبْوَابِ الْجَنّةِ الثّمَانِيَةِ شَاءَ”.

“Whoever bears witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that ‘Isa is the servant of Allah and His Messenger and His Word which He bestowed on Maryam and a spirit created by Him, and that Paradise is true and Hell is true, Allah will admit him through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise he wishes.” (Bukhari 3180).

Someone may wonder what is the width of each of these eight gates to allow all those believers to enter?

قالﷺ: والذي نفس محمد بيده إن ما بين المصراعين من مصاريع الجنة كما بين مكة وهجر أوكما بين مكة وبصرى”

“By the one in whose Hands is my soul, the distance between the two doors of each gate of Heaven is as the distance between Makkah and Hajar, or between Makkah and Busra.” (Muslim)

This hadeath specifies the width of each gate of the eighth gates of Hevean. The three locations specified in this hadeath are: Makkah (in Saudi Arabia), Hajar (in Bahrain) and Busra (in Syria).

Distance between Makkah and Busra (Syria) is 793 miles (1273 KM).

But Hajar is a province located in the east of the Arabian Peninsula that includes Qatar and Bahrain. The distance between Makkah and Hajar is also about 794 miles.

Based on this hadeath the width of each gate in Heaven is 794 miles and this is verified by the two locations that the Prophet (PBUH) specified.

These eight gates have names indicating the attributes of the people who will be entering from them.

In a hadeath narrated by Abu Huryrah (أبي هريرة) and reported by Bukhari and Muslim the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من أنفق زوجين في سبيل الله نودي من أي أبواب الجنة يا عبد الله هذا خير، فمن كان من أهل الصلاة دعي من باب الصلاة، ومن كان من أهل الجهاد دعي من باب الجهاد، ومن كان من أهل الصدقة دعي من باب الصدقة، ومن كان من أهل الصيام دعي من باب الريان.

“Whoever gives two kinds (of things or property) in charity for Allah’s Cause, will be called from the gates of Paradise and will be addressed, ‘O slaves of Allah! Here is prosperity!’ So, whoever was among the people who used to offer their prayers, will be called from the gate of Prayer; and whoever was among the people who used to participate in Jihad, will be called from the gate of Jihad; and whoever was among the people who used to give charity, will be called from the gate of Charity; and whoever was among the people who used to fast, will be called from the gate of Ar-Rayyan.”

Sahl (RA) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

“In Paradise there is a gate called Al-Rayyaan, through which those who used to fast will enter on the Day of Resurrection, and no one but they will enter through it. It will be said: ‘Where are those who used to fast?’ They will stand up, and no one but they will enter through it. When they have entered, it will be closed and no one else will enter through it.” (Bukhari & Muslim)

Also, Abu Huryrah (أبي هريرة) and reported by Bukhari and Muslim the Prophet (PBUH) said:

أيضاً عن أبي هريرة في حديث شفاعة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيه: فيقال: يا محمد أدخل الجنة من أمتك من لا حساب عليه من الباب الأيمن من أبواب الجنة وهم شركاء الناس فيما سوى ذلك من الأبواب.

Allah Says: “O Muhammad! Let those of your followers who have no accounts, enter through the gate on the right (Baab Al-Ayman); and they are the partners with the people in the other gates.”

It is reported by Ahmad that Al-Hassan said:

عن الحسن مرسلاً: إن لله باباً في الجنة لا يدخله إلا من عفا عن مظلمة. ]رواه الإمام أحمد و الحافظ في الفتح (11/465)

“Allah has a door in paradise, no one enters from it except the one who forgave injustice.”

So, the names of these 8 gates are:

Bāb al-Ṣalāh (the gate of prayers): This gate is for those who were punctual and attentive in prayers.
Bāb al-Jihād (The gate of struggle): This gate is for those who sacrificed their lives while they are struggling for the sake of Allah.
Bāb al-Ṣadaqah (The gate of charity): This gate is for those who are frequent in giving charity.
Bāb al-Rayyān (The gate of fasting) This gate is for those who kept their fast with sincerity.
Bāb al-Ḥajj (The gate of pilgrimage): This gate is for those who participated in the annual pilgrimage (Hajj).
Baab Al-Kaazimeen Al-Ghaiz Wal Aafina Anin Naas: (The gate if those who suppress their anger and forgive people).
Baab Al-Ayman (The gate of the right): This gate is for those who were steadfast in their faith in Allah and put their trust in Him (Al-Tawakul).
Baab Al-Dhikr (The gate of Allah’s remembrance): This gate is for those who constantly in remembrance of Allah.
It is natural for Muslims to wonder what will happen to those people who have earned the privilege to enter from more than one gate. Abu Bakr asked the Prophet (PBUH):

“Will there be anyone who will be called from all these gates?”

The Prophet answered him,

“Yes. And I hope you will be one of them.”

We pray to Allah that we also be one of them. We still have time to earn this honor if we take responsibility for our actions and show kindness to others, especially our parents.

One of you may say, but the parents of someone of us have already died. How can we show kindness to them?

A man from among the companions asked Prophet Mohammad (PBUH):

يا رسول الله هل بقي عليّ شيء مِن برِّ والديّ بعد موتهما ؟

“O Messenger of Allah, is there anything left from the goodness I owe my parents after their death?”

The Prophet (PBUH) replied:

نعم ، أربعة أشياء ، أن تدعُوَ لهما كل يوم خمس مرات ، رب اغفر لي ولوالديّ ، رب ارحمهما كما ربَّياني صغيرًا ، وأن تستغفر لهما ، وأن تنفذ عهدهما ، وأن تُكرم صديقهما ، وأن تصل الرحم التي لا تُوصل إلا بهما.

“Yes, four things:

Pray and ask forgiveness for them five time per day by saying:
(رب اغفر لي ولوالديّ ، رب ارحمهما كما ربَّياني صغيرًا) My Lord, forgive me, my parents, My Lord have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.

2) Be kind to their friends.

3) Fulfill their pledges.

4) And maintain the ties of kinship that come only from their direction”.

(Ahmad, Abu Dawood &ibn Majah)

DUA
