content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا

وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله.

A question that any serious Muslim must always ask himself is whether he is truly presenting the true message of Islam to others because whether we like it or not, people will judge the religion of Islam based on the practices and behaviors of Muslims.

Every Muslim is carrying on his shoulders the responsibility of being the image of Islam.  The Prophet (PBUH) warned Muslims of this reality by saying:

قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (كل رجل من المسلمين على ثغرة من ثغر الإسلام، الله الله لا يؤتى الإسلام من قبلك). [السنة للمروزي رواه بسند صحيح عن الوضيع بن عطاء عن يزيد بن مرثد مرفوعاً]

“Every Muslim guards a gate of the gates of Islam, By Allah don’t let Islam be weakened from your side”.

You are a part in the picture or a section in the quilt of Islam, don’t make your part ruin the picture or the quilt.

Some Muslims are deceived by thinking that Allah will judge them based solely on their actions and not on the actions of others who are misguided by being directly or indirectly influenced by theirs.  Allah said:

لِيَحۡمِلُوٓاْ أَوۡزَارَهُمۡ كَامِلَةً۬ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ‌ۙ وَمِنۡ أَوۡزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُم بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍ‌ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ

” Let them carry all their own burdens on the Day of Judgement as well as the burdens of those whom they have misled without being aware of it.  Surely what they bear is evil” (Al-Nahl 16:25).

How many people turned away from knowing the true Islam by Muslims who do not project the true image of Islam?

In fact, even many Muslims may build their understanding of the religion on the behaviors and actions of those whom they consider are scholars and/or righteous.  It is even unfortunate that people often judge people righteousness and religiosity of a person based on how the person looks and how he dresses ignoring the hadeath of the Prophet (PBUH) who said:

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: إِنَّ اللَّه لا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَجْسَادِكُمْ و لا إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَشَارَ بِأَصَابِعِهِ إِلَى صَدْرِهِ ]متفق عليه ]

“Allah does not look at your figures, nor at your attire but He looks at your hearts and pointed out to his chest.”

And in a similar hadeath, the Prophet (PBUH) said;

أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : ” إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَإِنَّمَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ ” .] رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ [

“Allah does not look at your looks or your wealth but He looks at your hearts and accomplishments”.

The importance of the heart is emphasized in the Quran, Allah said

﴿ يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ (88) إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ (89)﴾ [ سورة الشعراء]

The Day when neither wealth nor children will avail, except he who comes to Allah with pure heart.” (Al-Shuara’a 26:88-89)

Since we cannot judge the hearth of people, we cannot judge their level of Taqwa and we cannot judge the authenticity of their religiosity (تدين).  All we can judge is the person’s deeds and based on it we say “we think he his righteous, but never make the statement with affirmation.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:

خرج البخاري في صحيحه من حديث أبي بكرة رضي الله عنه: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن كان أحدكم مادحا لا محالة فليقل أحسب كذا وكذا إن كان يرى أنه كذلك، والله حسيبه ولا يزكي على الله أحدا..”

“If it is necessary for one of you to praise someone knowing that what he is praising that person for to be true, he should say: ‘I believe him to be as such, and Allah is a judge over him, and I do not praise anyone over Allah.”

The same point is emphasized in surat Al-Najm, Allah says:

فَلاَ تُزَكُّوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ)  النجم(

“Do not ascribe purity to yourselves. He knows best him has Taqwa.” (Al-Najm 53:32)

It is a command from Allah that while we can acknowledge the good character based on what we observe, we should not ascribe purity of belief or taqwa to ourselves or anyone else because none of us knows what is in the heart; only Allah knows the state of Taqwa of anyone.

The point of not affirming purity and Taqwa and thus assurance of Allah’s acceptance to anyone can be clearly demonstrated from the account of Umm Al-Ala’aa (أُمُّ الْعَلاءِ الأَنْصَارِيَّةُ) on Uthman bin Maz’oon (عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ).

Uthman bin Maz’oon (عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ) was one of the close companions of the Prophet (PBUH), he was very early in converting to Islam, he led the first migration of Muslim to Ethiopia and he immigrated to Madina.  He was well known among the companions for his devotion by the extent of his night prayers and fasting.  He participated in the battle of Badr and was injured in it.  So, based on this record, he was very righteous man.  When he immigrated to Madina with his wife, he stayed in the house of Umm Al-Ala’aa (أُمُّ الْعَلاءِ الأَنْصَارِيَّةُ).

It is reported by Imam al-Boukhari and Ahmad that Umm Al-Ala’aa said: when Uthman bin Maz’oon (عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ) died, the Prophet (PBUH) came to my house and I said addressing the dead body:

رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَا السَّائِبِ , شَهَادَتِي عَلَيْكَ لَقَدْ أَكْرَمَكَ اللَّهُ ,

“May Allah’s Mercy be on you, O Aba As-Sa’ib (the nickname of Uthman bon Maz’oom), my testimony is that Allah has honored you.”

The Prophet (PBUH) said: ” وَمَا يُدْرِيكِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَكْرَمَهُ ؟ “, ‘How do you know that Allah has honored him?

I said: (لَا أَدْرِي , بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي) ‘I do not know, my beloved and respected.

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

أَمَّا هُوَ , فَقَدْ جَاءَهُ الْيَقِينُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ , وَإِنِّي لَأَرْجُو الْخَيْرَ له , وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي وَأَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلا بِكُمْ

‘As for him, death has come to him and I wish him all the goodness. But, by Allah, though I am Allah’s messenger, I do not know what will happen to me or to you.’ “

Umm Ala’aa (أُمُّ الْعَلاءِ الأَنْصَارِيَّةُ) said: (وَاللَّهِ لَا أُزَكِّي أَحَدًا بَعْدَهُ أَبَدًا) “By Allah, I will never attest the righteousness of anybody after that.”

This statement of the Prophet (PBUH) and the understanding of Umm Ala’aa is consistent with Allah revelation in Surat Al-Ahqaf, Allah says:

قُلۡ مَا كُنتُ بِدۡعً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدۡرِى مَا يُفۡعَلُ بِى وَلَا بِكُمۡ‌ۖ إِنۡ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۟ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬) الأحقاف(.

“Say (O Muhammad): I am not a novelty among the Messengers (of Allah); nor do I claim that I know what shall be done with me or with you.  I only follow what is revealed to me and I am but clear warner.” (Al-Ahqaf 46:9).

Umm Al-Ala’aa (أُمُّ الْعَلاءِ الأَنْصَارِيَّةُ) continued her account of the event by saying:

فَأَحْزَنَنِي ذَلِكَ , فَنِمْتُ فَأُرِيتُ لِعُثْمَانَ عَيْنًا تَجْرِي , فَجِئْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ , فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ ذَلِكَ

فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : ” ذَاكَ عَمَلُهُ ”   )مسند أحمد بن حنبل- أخرجه البخاري(

This saddened me, not knowing that Allah honored Uthman bin Maz’oon (عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ), but when I went to sleep, I saw in my dream, that Uthman has a flowing spring. So, I went to the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) and mentioned it to him.

He (PBUH) said, ‘That is (the symbol of) his good deeds.’ And this made me so happy”.

If this is what the Prophet (PBUH) taught Umm Al-Ala’aa regarding one of his greatest companions, how can we really be so definitive of judging anyone that he is a truly man of God and Wali of Allah.

Even when we witness a person doing outstanding deeds, we still cannot be definitive about his status with Allah, we just have to admit that we are not good judges on whom Allah will accept.   Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:إن أول الناس يُقضى يوم القيامة عليه رجلٌ استشهد فأُتيَ به فعرَّفه نعمَه فعرفها، قال فما عملت فيها؟ قال: قاتلت فيك حتى استشهدت، قال كذبت، ولكنك قاتلت لأن يقال هو جريء، فقد قيل، ثم أمر به فسُحبَ على وجهه حتى ألقي في النار، ورجلٌ تعلَّم العلم وعلَّمه وقرأ القرآن فأتي به فعرَّفه نعمَه فعرفها، قال فما عملت فيها؟ قال: تعلمت العلم وعلمته وقرأت فيك القرآن، قال كذبت، ولكنك تعلمت ليقال عالم وقرأت القرآن ليقال هو قارئ، فقد قيل ثم أمر به فسُحبَ على وجهه حتى ألقي في النار، ورجلٌ وسع الله عليه وأعطاه من أصناف المال فأتي به فعرفه نعمه فعرفها، قال فما عملت فيها؟ قال: ما تركت من سبيل تحب أن ينفق فيها إلا أنفقت فيها لك، قال كذبت، ولكنك فعلت ليقال هو جواد، فقد قيل ثم أمر به فسُحبَ على وجهه ثم ألقي في النار ) رواه مسلم.

The first to be judged on the Day of Judgement will be a man who had died as a martyr . He will be brought forward. Allah will remind him of the favors He had bestowed upon him and the man will acknowledge them. Then Allah will ask him: `What did you do to express gratitude for it?’ The man will reply: `I fought for Your Cause till I was martyred.’

Allah will say: `You have lied. You fought so that people might call you courageous; and they have done so.’ Command will then be issued about him and he will be dragged on his face and thrown into Hell.

Next a man who had acquired and imparted knowledge and read the Qur’an will be brought forward, Allah will remind him of the favors He had bestowed upon him and the man will acknowledge them. Then He will ask him: `What did you do to express gratitude for it?’ The man will reply: `I acquired knowledge and taught it, and read the Qur’an for Your sake.’ Allah will say to him: `You have lied. You acquired knowledge so that people might call you a learned (man), and you read the Qur’an so that they might call you a reciter, and they have done so.’ Command will then be issued about him, and he will be dragged on his face and thrown into Hell.

Next a man whom Allah had made affluent and to whom Allah had given plenty of wealth , will be brought forward, Allah will remind him of the favors He had bestowed upon him and the man will acknowledge them.

Allah will ask him: `What did you do to express gratitude for it?’ The man will reply: `I did not neglect any of the ways You liked wealth to be spend liberally for Your sake’. Allah will say to him: `You have lied. You did it so that people might call you generous, and they have done so.’ Command will then be issued about him and he will be dragged on his face and thrown into Hell . (Saheeh Muslim)

Why this point is important because one of the major causes of the misunderstanding about the religion of Islam, particularly in the west, results from not differentiating between the religion of Islam and the religiosity/practices of the Muslims.   When people judge a Muslim or group of Muslims as being religious, they directly interpret their actions and behaviors as representatives of the teaching of Islam.  This is complete incorrect.

It must be recognized that religion (الدين) of Islam and the religiosity (التدين) of Muslims are two different things. Religion is divine and thus perfect but religiosity is human and thus subjected to human imperfections.

The foundational principles of the Islamic religion are derived from two authentic sources:  The Quran the authentic hadeath (النصوص اليقينية الورود).   But one must not ignore that the texts in these sources have two classifications:

First : Texts that are concise and unambiguous that can only have single interpretation (القطعية الدلالة) and these interpretations are independent of time and place.  These are the texts on which the fundamentals of the religion regarding the belief and rules are based.  These are the texts that represent the religion of Islam for which Allah said:

إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ) آل عمران(

“Indeed, the only religion recognized by Allah is Islam” (Al-Imran 3:19),

Allah also says:

وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ) آل عمران(

And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him” (Al-Imran 3:85)

The second classification is the texts that are ambiguous and thus may have differing interpretation to accommodate the different times and place. (الظنية الدلالة).  However, these differing interpretations should not be source of conflict among Muslims but rather they are intended to accommodate the diversity of the human race. These texts are not part of the fundamentals of the religion but they are there as divine guide for the human race thru the ages.

These two classifications are clearly understood from the following verse from Surat Al-Imran:

“He is the (One) Who sent down to you the Book, in it there are verses that are concise and clear “Muhkamat” and they are the foundation (Literally: the Mother) of the Book, هُوَ ٱلَّذِى أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِنْهُ آيَـٰتٌ مُّحْكَمَـٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ and there are others that are ambiguous “Mutashabihat” (whose definite meanings are not entirely unclear). Those whose hearts are deviant follow the ambiguous parts “mutashabih,” seeking confusion and seeking its interpretation (“taiweleh”); while no one knows its interpretation “taiweleh” except Allah. و َأُخَرُ مُتَشَـٰبِهَـٰتٌ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فى قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَـٰبَهَ مِنْهُ ٱبْتِغَاء ٱلْفِتْنَةِ وَٱبْتِغَاء تَأْوِيلِهِ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلاَّ ٱلله And those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: “We have believed in it; all is from our Lord.” And no one can always be in state of awareness except those who are endowed with intellects.” (Al-Imran 3:7) وَٱلرسِخُونَ فِي ٱلْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ ءامَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مّنْ عِندِ رَبّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلاَّ أُوْلُواْ ٱلالْبَـٰبِ

It cannot be over emphasized that the religion of Islam is based on the “Muhkamat” the concise and clear verses. Knowing these Muhkamat” the concise and clear verses and becoming so grounded on them is so critical before you even discuss the religion with others who wants to confuse you by focusing on the “mutashabih,” the ambiguous verses. Allah clearly warned us of this point as He said that those whose hearts are deviant will be seeking confusion by trying to interpret them.  You cannot interpret them unless you reference them back to the “Muhkamat” the concise and clear verses.

This point is so critical because many of the Muslim youth get trapped in arguing about the “mutashabih,” the ambiguous verses without being grounded on the “Muhkamat” the concise and clear verses first.  Unfortunately, this leads them to confusion and doubt that may lead some of them to even rejecting the religion all together.

The religiosity of Muslims that is manifested by their practices is influenced by many personal factors such as level of education, cognitive capacity, character, emotion, psychology, personal sense of the divine, culture; and social and economic status.

The variations in religiosity among Muslims also results from the multi-dimensional nature of the religion of Islam that involve beliefs (لاعتقاد), rituals (العبادات), ethics (الأخلاق) and transactions (المعاملات).   People differ with respect to their selective focus on these dimensions and on their level of religious maturity that vary from Islam to Eman to Ihsan (الاسلام والأيمان والإحسان).

No one should learn the teaching of a religion based on the religiosity of their followers.  What is proper is to assess the religiosity of the followers based on their level of sincerity and application of the teachings of the religion. Religion is intended to provide the constraints around religiosity and not vice versa.

In Islam, the fundamental in religiosity starts with the innate human attribute (فطره) that Allah created in mankind as Allah says:

(فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفً۬ا‌ۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡہَا‌ۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَڪۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (٣٠)) (الروم : 30)

“So, set your face to the Faith uprightly, this (faith) being the nature designed by Allah on which He has created the mankind. There is no change in Allah’s creation. That is the straight faith, but most of the people do not know.” (Romans: 30:30)

The Prophet (PBUH) said: (ما من مولود إلا يولد على الفطرة، فأبواه يهودانه، أو ينصرانه، أو يمجسانه)

“No one is born except according to intrinsic nature, but their parents make them Jews, or Christians, or Magaians.”

This innate instinct is related to the belief in a creator and the basic moral principles that all normal people will ascribe to.

The practices of religion, which is religiosity is based on human application of the religion.  Because of the differences in religiosity among people, it can vary between in a scale between the two extremes, on one side is the genuine and proper religiosity and on the other is the negative and deficient religiosity.

Genuine and proper religiosity results from proper understanding of the religion’s morals and principles that are solely based on the divine revelations.

Negative and deficient religiosity occurs when the actions of the person do not fall under the quality control of the religion and are not carefully assessed against its revealed values and rules but rather it is greatly influenced by personal conditions and preferences.

In Islam, genuine/ proper religiosity (التدين الأصيل) of a Muslim is demonstrated by the accurate balance between the spiritual dimension of human existence that is necessary for the purification of man’s soul, and the materialistic dimension of human existence that is necessary for the survival and advancement of man in this life.  In Islam, the spiritual dimension does not eliminate the materialistic dimension but puts constrains around it to nourish it and complete it.  Allah says:

وَكَذَٲلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةً۬ وَسَطً۬ا

“Thus, We have made you, a justly balanced (middle) nation”. (Al-Baqara 2:143)

Allah also says regarding those who achieve balanced state:

وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمۡ يُسۡرِفُواْ وَلَمۡ يَقۡتُرُواْ وَڪَانَ بَيۡنَ ذَٲلِكَ قَوَامً۬ا

“And those when they spend, they are neither extravagant nor grudging and are in the middle between the extremes.” (Al-Furqan 25:67)

Genuine Religiosity (التدين الأصيل) is manifested when the foundations of the religion penetrate the circles of human knowledge, emotion and behavior.  Those who possess genuine religiosity have sufficient religious knowledge and deep religious passion to make their behaviors and cations always consistent with the principles and morals of the religion.

For those people, religion becomes the central engine that directs all their activities, both the external and the internal.  You will find their outward behavior is congruent with their inward feeling, and their actions are consistent with their words.

Those people are always devoted to serving others and never seek advantage from their religiosity.  When a person reaches this level of religiosity, he would achieve a high degree of psychological balance that makes him able to meet adversity with patience and satisfaction. If you meet such a person, you will find a person who is in total peace; he is always calm, tolerant, humble, satisfied and at ease.  You will find yourself communicating with him with ease and joy.

On the other hand, Negative religiosity occurs when it does not fall under the quality control of the religion and is not carefully assessed against its revealed values and rules but rather it is influenced by personal conditions and preferences.

Negative and deficient religiosity occurs when an imbalance occurs between the spiritual and materialistic dimensions.  Imam Ibn al-Qayyim (ابن القيم) said:

(ما أمر الله بأمر إلا وللشيطان فيه نزعتان: إما إلى تفريط وإضاعة، وإما إلى إفراط وغلو، ودين الله وسط بين الجافي عنه والغالي فيه، كالوادي بين الجبلين، والهدى بين الضلالتين، والوسط بين طرفين ذميمين) (مدارج السالكين: 2/496(.

“Whatever there is a command from Allah but Satan influences people regarding it in two ways:  either by negligence and waste, or by excess and hyperbole. But the religion of Allah is balanced between neglect and excess, it is as the valley between two mountains, a guidance between two deviations and as the center between two despicable ends”.

Deficient religiosity can take many forms but there are some common traits of those who practice it, and these traits may include:

Inflating the value of the outward manifestations of religion at the expense on the deep spiritual depth of the religion.

Accepting the contradictions between his outward religious appearance and the inward ideas and feelings and the concealed actions.

Amplification of oneself and the desire to control the thinking, feelings and behavior of others.

Stubborn rejection to the opinion of the others and the inability to engage in substantive discussion.

Over emphasis on certain practices of the religion on the expense of others that may even be more important.  As an example, one becomes so dedicated to spending much wealth to perform Umrah while ignoring obligations such as helping the needy.

Content with oneself and the tendency to be negative towards others.

When you examine religiosity today among Muslims, you may note several forms that fall short from being truly genuine because they suffer from some form of imbalance.  These forms include:

Opportunistic Religiosity (Utilitarian -Benefit based) التدين النفعي (المصلحي)

Fanatical Religiosity (Extremism) (التطرف)

Intellectual (Knowledge based) Religiosity (التدين المعرفي :الفكري)

Emotional Religiosity (enthusiastic) (التدين العاطفي) ( (التدين الحماسي(التدين الوجداني)

Ritualistic (Behavioral) Religiosity التدين السلوكي (تدين العبادة)

Reactive Religiosity التدين التفاعلي (تدين رد الفعل)

Defensive Religiosity (neurotic) التدين الدفاعي

Psychotic Religiosity التدين المرضى

Mystical Religiosity (التصوف)

Opportunistic religiosity (Utilitarian -Benefit based) التدين النفعي (المصلحي) (التدين التظاهري)

This is a deceptive form of religiosity when the person pretends to be serious about his religion but has no commitment to it and his sole purpose is to ensure materialistic gains. The person shows the appearance of commitment to many aspects of religion to reach high political, social and/or financial status.  People who have this type of religiosity exploit the trust they gain and the affection they receive from others to advance their personal objectives.  This type of religiosity is completely prohibited by Allah as He says:

وَلَا تَشۡتَرُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِى ثَمَنً۬ا قَلِيلاً۬. ( المائدة(

“And do not barter My revelations for a little gain”. (Al-Maeda 5:44).

The Prophet (PBUH) also discouraged even taking religious teaching as a full-time profession as He said:

إن الله يحب العبد يتخذ المهنة يستغني بها عن الناس، ويبغض العبد يتعلم العلم يتخذه مهنة

“Allah loves a person to take the profession to make him independent of people and hates the person learns the (religious) knowledge and takes it as profession.

Fanatical Religiosity (Extremism) ( التطرف)

This religiosity is characterized by the excess in certain aspects of the understanding of the religion beyond the acceptable limits that are sanctioned by religious scholars and in violations to Allah’s and His messengers’ warnings:

﴿ قُلۡ يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ لَا تَغۡلُواْ فِى دِينِڪُمۡ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَ قَوۡمٍ۬ قَدۡ ضَلُّواْ مِن قَبۡلُ وَأَضَلُّواْ ڪَثِيرً۬ا وَضَلُّواْ عَن سَوَآءِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ ﴾ (المائدة)

“Say: O People of the Book do not exceed the bounds of your religion and do not follow the vain desires of people who went astray before, and who misled many, and strayed from the Right Path.” (Al-Maeda 5:77)

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

(يا أيها الناس إياكم والغلو في الدين، فانه أهلك من قبلكم الغلو في الدين) (رواه أحمد والنسائي وابن ماجه).

“O people, beware of extremism in religion, it is extremism in religion that destroyed those who came before you.”

Allah says:

فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡ‌ۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَ‌ۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡہُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ‌ۖ

“And it is by the Mercy of Allah that you dealt with them gently, and had you been rude and harsh-hearted, they would have broken away from you; so overlook (their faults), and ask (Allah’s) Forgiveness for them; and consult them in the affairs.” (Al-Imran 3:159)

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

” أكلفوا من الأعمال ما تطيقون ” (البخاري(.

“Demand from yourself only what you can tolerate.”

(إن هذا الدين يسر ولن يشاد الدين أحد إلا غلبه ، فسددوا وقاربوا وابشروا واستعينوا بالغدوة والروحة وشيء من الدلجة ) رواه البخاري

“This religion is very easy and whoever overburdens himself in his religion will not be able to continue in that way. So you should not be extremists, but try to be near to perfection and receive the good tidings that you will be rewarded; and gain strength by worshipping during the day and part of the nights.”

Excess in religion can take three forms:

Intellectual extremism ( التطرف الفكري) :  This makes the person so narrow minded that he cannot accept any idea other than what he already knew.  It is impossible to have an intellectual discussion with such a person to present alternate views.

Emotional extremism ( التطرف العاطفي): In this case the person’s passion become totally concentrated on the religious aspects and becomes extremist in the expression of his emotion.

Behavioral Extremism ( التطرف السلوكي) : Here, the person exaggerates in the performance of the outward religious rites as if the whole purpose of the religion is these outward rituals devoid of spiritual meanings.  The danger of this type of extremism occurs when it extends beyond the person’s own actions and makes him transgress to demand and compel others to follow and behave like him by force, if necessary, which is in contrary to the fundamental teachings of Islam.    Allah warns of the heavy-handed style, and rudeness in dealing with others and prohibits the use of force to achieve the ends.  Rather, Allah demands mercy and gentleness and always thinking good about others.

I’ll finish here and inshallah in future talks we can discuss the other forms of religiosity.

Dua

title: Khoshoo (خشوع) the Prerequisite for Achieving Ecstasy in Prayers

content:
Khoshoo (خشوع) the Prerequisite for Achieving Ecstasy in Prayers

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله ، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

One question that is often asked is “how to achieve Khoshoo (خشوع) in our prayers”. First, we need to know why we need khoshoo in prayer and then how we can achieve it both psychologically and physically and this will lead us to know what is khoshoo.

Khoshoo in our prayers is so important because it is prerequisite to guaranteeing our success in this life and in the hereafter as Allah said in the beginning of surah (المؤمنون) that we just listened to. Allah says:

قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ
الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ

“The Believers are surely successful. Those who are reverent (have Khoshoo) in their prayers; (Al-Muminoon 23: 1-2)

Allah continued to describe five additional attributes of the successful believers, and these are:

Who avoid vain talk (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ)
Who are active in deeds of charity (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكَاةِ فَاعِلُونَ)
Who guard their private parts; except with their spouses and whomever their right hands may control, (in their case) they are free from blame; but those whose desires exceed those limits are transgressors (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ فَمَنِ ابْتَغَىٰ وَرَاءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْعَادُونَ)
Who faithfully observe their trusts and their covenants (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ)
And who carefully maintain their prayers (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَوَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ)

Allah finishes these attributes by giving his promise to those successful believers by saying:

أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْوَارِثُونَ الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ

These will be the heirs, who will inherit Paradise: they will dwell therein for eternity. (Al-Muminoon 23: 3-11)

We note that four of the attributes (avoiding vain talks, actively giving charity, guarding their private parts except on their spouses, and fulfilling their trusts and convents) are sandwiched between the Quality of the prayer which is khoshoo and the quantity of the prayers.

Starting with the quality of the prayer which is khosooh suggests that achieving these four honorable attributes plus satisfying the frequency of the prayers depend on achieving the first attribute which is the khoshoo in the prayer. A person who is able to achieve “khoshoo in the prayer will be the most honorable person because his prayer will perfect his character and will inhibit him from engaging in any improper behavior because Allah assures us of this outcome by saying in Surah Al-Ankabout:

وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَنْهَى عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ

“Establish Prayers: for Prayers restrains from shameful and unjust deeds” (Al-Ankabout 29:45)

Also, Allah tells us in Surah (المعارج) that the person who perfects his prayer will not suffer from depression and impatience:

إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ دَائِمُونَ

“We have created man very impatient, fretful when evil touches him and grudging when good reaches him, except for those who are constant at their prayers.” (Al-Maareg 70:23)

When we look at the state of Muslims, we note many deficiencies in their character while they may be praying regularly. This means that the payers are not achieving what Allah said that they will achieve. This can only mean that we do not perform the prayer properly, we go through the motion but we do not have khoshoo.

How do you know that you are in a state of Khoshoo. When you are in this state:
- You will be in state of happiness, serenity and tranquility that you don’t want to get out of it.
- Your body will be in state of complete stillness; you will as if you have out of body experience, your soul and mind are in different state.
- You will be totally focusing on what you are saying but feeling as if you are hearing them from outside.
- You will be in a state of sublime perfect happiness because you will be feeling the connection to the Divine.

Achieving this state of khoshooh in not easy, it a journey that every Muslim struggle to reach its end.

Anything a person does is expected to have benefit for someone. Who benefits from our prayers?
It is narrated by Abu Dharr Al-Ghafari (أبي ذر) and reported in Muslim that the Prophet (PBUH) said that Allah says in a Qudsi Hadeath:

يا عبادي إنكم لن تبلغوا ضري فتضروني ولن تبلغوا نفعي فتنفعوني ، يا عبادي لو أن أولكم وآخركم وإنسكم وجنكم كانوا على أتقى قلب رجل واحد منكم ما زاد ذلك في ملكي شيئاً ، يا عبادي لو أن أولكم وآخركم وإنسكم وجنكم كانوا على أفجر قلب رجل واحد منكم ما نقص ذلك من ملكي شيئاً...

“O My servants, you will not attain harming Me so as to harm Me, and you will not attain benefiting Me so as to benefit Me.
O my servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you become as the most God-fearing heart of any one man of you, that would not add anything to My Kingdom.
O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you to be as the most wicked heart of any one man of you, that would not decrease anything from My Kingdom.” Related by Muslim.

This means that Allah gains nothing from our prayers and loses nothing form our lack of prayers.

Do our friends, family and neighbors benefit from our prayers, the answer will depend on whether our prayers have an impact on us or not. Allah says:

قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ
الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ

“The Believers are surely successful. Those who are reverent in their prayers; (Al-Muminoon 23: 1-2)

So, unless the prayers benefit us by making us better people, no one will benefit from our prayers. The only way to secure benefits from the prayers for both us and for others is to have khoshoo in our prayers.

How can we start our journey of achieving khoshoo?

You may have heard some speakers say that to be in a state of khoshoo in the prayers you need to imagine heaven on your right and hell on your left and the Sirat is in front of you and the angle of death is standing over your head ready to take your soul.

I don’t know about you, but frankly for me if I thought that the angel of death is standing over my head, I will be distracted in the prayer and thinking about all things that I should have done before the angle of death takes my soul.

But we may seek the answer by asking: what are the situations in which we were involved in and made us in a state of complete happiness that we became unaware of anything around us except the situations we are in? You will note that the common feature in these situations is that they involve talking to someone whom you love too much.

So, the simple and frankly the only answer to achieving khoshoo in the payer is love Allah so much that you don’t even want the prayer to end since this means that meeting Him will end. Your degree of Khoshoo depends on your degree of the love and the Awe of Allah.

The problem is that we learnt from early age that the prayer is an obligatory ritual and we will be punished if we don’t perform it. So, we go thru the motion to avoid the punishment and thus our focus will be on just finishing this obligation. Think about it, if you are obligated to meet someone whom you fear, would you really enjoy this meeting; you will probably want this meeting to get over with as soon as possible.

When considering prayers, we should never look at them as obligations, but as honor that Allah granted us an opportunity to meet and speak to Him. If you look at prayers this way, your feelings will be completely different because you are now meeting a very powerful King who loves you and you love, honor and in Awe of Him. Prayers represent a great opportunity to communicate with Him and to ask Him for whatever you want.

The relationship that Allah wants to have with the believers is a relationship based on love and not fear. Allah makes this point very clear in verse 54 of Surat Al-Maeda (5:54)

يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ (المائدة ٥٤)

“O’ you who believe, if any of you turn back from his religion, Allah will bring forth people whom He loves and they love Him.” (Al-Maeda 5:54)

In fact, Allah expects our love for Him to be far more than anything else otherwise the person is considered a rebel (faseq):

“Say: If it be that your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your mates, your clans; the wealth that you have gained; the commerce in which you fear its decline; or the houses in which you delight –

قُلْ إِنْ كَانَ آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ وَإِخْوَانُكُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُكُمْ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمْ وَأَمْوالٌ اقْتَرَفْتُمُوهَا وَتِجَارَةٌ تَخْشَوْنَ كَسَادَهَا وَمَسَاكِنُ تَرْضَوْنَهَا

are more beloved to you than Allah, and His Messenger, and the striving in His cause – then wait until Allah brings about His decree: and Allah guides not the rebellious.” (Al-Tuba 9:24)

Allah also describes the believers that their love of Allah is beyond their love for anything:

وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْدَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ

“Yet there are people who take others as equals besides Allah, they love them as they love Allah, but the believers love Allah more than anything.” (Al-Baqarah 2:165)

The Prophet (PUH) informs us that the only way to find enjoyment in Eman is by loving Allah and His messenger more than anything:

ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ وَجَدَ حَلَاوَةَ الْإِيمَانِ: أَنْ يَكُونَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِمَّا سِوَاهُمَا

“There are three things that if one has, he will taste the sweetness of Eman (Faith); that Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to him than anything else...”

As soon as you say Allah Akbar to start the prayer, you will be given permission to enter in a personal communication with Allah. If you look at the prayers this way, you realize that you are entering into a dialogue with Allah.

Does Allah speak to you when you enter the prayer? Other than the time when you are asking Allah for things in your prayers Allah is speaking to you and you are repeating what He said.

When hearing or reading the Quran, there are those who will feel that they are hearing it from Allah. Iman Gaafar Al Sadeq, May Allah be pleased with him, said:

I wonder about the one who is distressed and is not alert to the words of Allah:
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
“There is no God but you, You are far exalted and above all weaknesses, and I was indeed a wrongdoer”; because I heard Allah says following it:
فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَكَذَلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
“Allah saved him from depression and thus we save those who have faith.” (Al-Anbiya 21:87-88)

I wonder about the one who is afraid of harm and is not alert to the words of Allah:
وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
“Allah is sufficient for us, He is the best guarantor”; because I heard Allah says following it:
فَانْقَلَبُوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوءٌ
“So they returned with grace and favor from Allah, and no harm touched them.” (Al-Emran 3:173-174)

I wonder about the one who is afraid to be tricked and is not alert to the words of Allah:
أُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ
“I entrust Allah with all my affairs because Allah watches over His servants”, because I heard Allah says following it:
فَوَقَاهُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِ مَا مَكَرُوا
“Allah saved him from the evils which they plotted against him” (Ghafir 40:44-45)

I wonder about the one who is inflicted with adversity and is not alert to the words of Allah:
أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
“Adversity afflicted me and You are the most merciful of all who are merciful”, because I heard Allah says following it:
فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِ مِنْ ضُرٍّ
“We heard his prayer and removed that adversity from which he suffered” (Al-Anbiya 21:83-84)

The 2nd proof that Allah is speaking to you in the prayers is the famous Qudsi Hadeath in which the Prophet (PBUH) reported that Allah said: “I have divided the prayer (Al-Fatiha) between Me and My servant in two halves”.

When my servant says “All praises and thanks are due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds”,
Allah says, ‘My servant has praised Me.’
When he says: The Beneficent, the Merciful.
Allah says: My servant has cherished me.
When he says: The Master of the Day of Judgment.
Allah says: My servant has glorified me.
When he says: You alone we worship and from You alone we seek help.
Allah says: This is between Me and My servant and to my servant all he asks.
When he says: Guide us to the straight path, the path of those on whom You have favored; Not the path of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray.
Allah says, ‘this is for My servant and My servant shall have what he asked for.’

Therefore, it is important when reading Al-Fatiha which is the most important part of the prayer that we stop after every verse to allow ourselves to hear Allah’s response.

We will never have khoshoo in prayers until we love Allah and we will never love Allah until we really know Him. Therefore, it is very critical that we should spend the time to know Allah. We can start by studying Allah’s glorious names. In the famous Hadeath that is reported in Al-Boukhari, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

إن لله تسعة و تسعين اسمًا، مائةً إلا واحدًا، من أحصاها دخل الجنة

“Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one, whoever “Ahsaha” (counts, analyze them and understand them) will enter Paradise.”

So, we should take the time to identify the 99 names and study them to really know Allah. This will be worthy theme that we can study in these after Fajr sessions.

To have khoshoo in the prayers, you need to reflect on how they were instituted. By instituting the prayers, Allah made the promise that He will make Himself available for us anytime we want to speak to Him and provided us with the protocol of coming to Him and this is thru the prayers. We should consider the prayers are the greatest gift that Allah has honored us with.

Imagine the degree of happiness and honor you would you feel if the president of a country or even a CEO of a company gave you permission to come to him any time you want. Would you consider this offer as obligation on you or the greatest gift you have received? But here we are not speaking about a president or king, we are speaking about the Lord of the universe.

As an illustration of why the prayers are the greatest gift that Allah granted to us, let us consider the case of the president of your company who wanted to give you an award. He may send it to you using the company mail, or give it to his secretary to hand it to you or give it to your manager to give to you. But, if the reward is extremely valuable, he will call you to his office to hand it to you in person.

Considering this example and to Allah the greatest examples, the prayers were the only thing in our religion that Allah asked the Prophet (PBUH) to come to the seventh heaven to give to Him. So, the prayers are the greatest gift that Allah can grant to any human being by giving him the permission to talk to Him, any time the person wants. Frankly, only the fools who squander this gift of having the opportunity to meet the Lord of the universe and to ask Him for whatever they need.

In addition to the role of the prayers of offering us the optimum opportunity to ask Allah for all our needs, a very valuable benefit that we gain during the prayer is to be treated by Allah from any spiritual ailment. Allah created us with an internal balance which is our “Nafs” or “soul” and this Nafs recognizes the right from wrong and directs us to always do what is right only if it is properly calibrated. Allah says:

وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا

“By the Soul, and the proportion and order given to it; and its enlightenment as to its wrong and its right; Truly he succeeds who purifies it.” (Al-Shams 91:7-9)

How can we keep this spiritual balance in perfect order; it is through prayers as Allah says:

قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى
وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى ( الأعلى ١٤)

Success is surely achieved by him who purifies himself, he glorifies the name of his Lord and prays. (Al-Ala 87:14)

When we stand in front of Allah in prayers, He will calibrate our spiritual balance and correct any deviation that we may have acquired during the time between the prayers as we were moving from one task to another. You want to be recalibrated by performing a prayer.

You may ask why we have to pray five times; can’t once a day be sufficient. To appreciate the reason, let us look at the scale of our values. Obviously, the frequency of calibrating a balance depends to the value of the material we are weighing.

If you are buying or selling gold that costs about $40/gm; you may want to ensure that the balance is calibrated every day.
But if you are using the balance to weigh Californium-252 that costs $27 million/gm, or the antimatter that costs $62.5 trillion/gm; you would want the balance calibrated before and after every weighing.

Now, you realize your value to Allah by the frequency He made Himself available for you so He can calibrate your spiritual balance. He wants you to be calibrated 5 times a day.

This is why prayers are so critical in our lives as it was very critical in the Prophet’s life that his last words before he left this world was “Al-Salah, Al-Salah” (the prayers, the prayers).

You may recall that originally, Allah instituted 50 prayers and then He reduced them to 5. If we had 50 prayers, then we would be praying about every 18 minutes. While you may not be able to go thru the formal prayer every 18 minutes, you need to do yourself a favor and do dhikr (remembrance of Allah). Allah says:

إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۟ فَٱعۡبُدۡنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِڪۡرِىٓ (طه ١٤)

“Surely, I am Allah. There is no god but Me, so worship Me, and establish Salah for My remembrance.” (Ta-Ha 20:14)

أَلَا بِذِڪۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَٮِٕنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ (٢٨)

“Indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.” (Al-Rad 13:28)

As aside note, it is interesting that the TED talks is limited to 18 minutes because 18 minutes is how long a listener could take in, digest, and understand the important information. May we should learn and limit these Fajr talks to 18 minutes, or may be to stop every 18 minutes and do dhikr.

Let me finish here but leave you with few Physical steps that may help you in having khoshoo in prayers:

1. After doing the Wudu, come to the prayer calm and sit for a minute doing dhikr.
2. When reading the Fatiha be sure to stop after every verse to listen to Allah’s response.
3. Try as much as you can do 2 rakka sunnah before each obligatory prayer to get in the mood. Since we do the obligatory prayer because of Allah’s command and we do the sunnah based on the practices of the Prophet (PBUH), consider the Sunnah as if it is your way of getting the Prophet (PBUH) to introduce you when you meet Allah during the obligatory prayer.
4. Think of the verses that you will read after the Fatiha ahead of the prayer.
5. Think of separate dua that you may want to say in the Sujood of every Rakka.
6. Think of a dua that you may want to make after the Tashahood before you end the prayer.

I am sure there are several others that you can also do to increase your level of khoshoo in the prayers.

DUA

title: The Mystery: Why Standing on Arafat is the Hajj
excerpt: الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمداً عبده ورسوله، اللهم صلِّ وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن تبعه إلى يوم الدين

We are now in the blessed 10 days of Dhu Al-Hijja and these days are important because they are concluded by the most important step in the Hajj which is standing on mountain of Arafat and then followed by the celebration of Eid Al-Adha.  We pray to Allah to grant us the opportunity to be on Arafat next year.

As a reminder before I discuss the main topic on the relevance of standing on Arafat during the Hajj, we need to be reminded of what the Prophet (PBUH) said regarding these days, the (PBUH) said:

ما من أيام العمل الصالح فيهن أحب إلى الله من هذه الأيام العشر

“There are no days on which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days.” [Bukhari]

The righteous deeds that we need to be engaged in these days may include:

1. Reading the Quran.
2. Increasing the voluntary (Nawaafil) ritulas such as prayers, giving charity, and fasting; in hadeath Qudsi, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

(وما تقرب إليّ عبدي بشيء أحب إليّ مما افترضته عليه….) رواه البخاري

My servant does not draw nearer to me by anything more than what I made obligatory upon him.

Fasting, particularly on the day of Arafat (this coming Thursday) is very valuable, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي قتادة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن صوم يوم عرفة فقال: (يكفّر السنة الماضية والباقية) رواه مسلم

“Fasting the day of Arafat expiates the sins of two years: the past one and the coming one.” [Muslim]

3. Making lots of dhikr, the Prophet (PBUH) said

ما من أيام أعظم عند الله ولا أحب إليه من العمل فيهن من هذه العشر، فأكثروا فيهن من التهليل والتكبير والتحميد

“There are no days that are greater before Allah or in which good deeds are more beloved to Him, than these ten days, so recite a great deal of tahleel, takbeer and tahmeed during them.” [Ahmad]

4. Making lots of Istighfar by seeking forgiveness for all our wrongdoings,
5. Increasing ties with kinship, regarding ties with kinship, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مَن سرَّه أن يُبسَط له في رزقه، وأن يُنسَأ له في أثره، فليَصِلْ رَحِمَه» رواه البخاري.

“Whoever would like his provision to be increased and his lifespan to be extended, should maintain the ties of kinship.” [Bukhari]

Hajj is one of the five foundational pillars on which Islam is built.  Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab reported that the Messenger of Allah, (PBUH) said:

عن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: (بني الإسلام على خمس: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمداً رسول الله، وإقام الصلاة، وإيتاء الزكاة، والحج، وصوم رمضان) رواه البخاري ومسلم.

“Islam has been built on five [pillars]: 1) testifying that there is no god but Allah and  except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, 2) performing the prayers, 3) paying the zakat, 4) making the pilgrimage (Hajj) to the House, and 5) fasting in Ramadan.” [Bukhari & Muslim]

While a Muslim is obligated to perform Hajj only once in his life and only if he can afford financially and physically, there are several hadeath that highlights the seriousness of not performing it even if you have the resources.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:

من ملك زاداً وراحلة تبلغه إلى بيت الله الحرام فلم يحج فلا عليه أن يموت يهودياً أو نصرانياً، وذلك أن الله يقول في كتابه: (ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا)

“Whoever has the resources to perform the Hajj and does not; let him die as Christian or a Jew because Allah says in his book:

وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ حِجُّ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَاعَ إِلَيۡهِ سَبِيلاً۬‌ۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ

As a right of Allah that the people perform the Hajj of the House on everyone who can afford it, and whoever disbelieves, then Allah is rich enough to be independent of the worlds. (Al-Imran 3:97)

(The verse ties the person who has the means but don’t perform Hajj with disbelief)

It is reported that Sayedna Omar said:

عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: لقد هممت أن أبعث رجالاً إلى هذه الأمصار فينظروا كل من له جدة ولم يحج فيضربوا عليهم الجزية، ما هم بمسلمين، ما هم بمسلمين

“I was on the verge of sending my men to all the states to check on those who have financial resources but did not perform Hajj to impose the Jizya tax on them, because they are not Muslims, they are not Muslims (repeating it twice)”

And in another narration, he said:

“Let him die as Jew or Christian (he repeated this 3 times), the man who dies without performing the Hajj when he has the resources.”

Obviously, it is too late to make the Hajj this year but as remainder for those who can afford it but keep delaying it.

I said Hajj may be the most important ritual in Islam because it is the one ritual that wipes the record of all sins.  Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said:

قَالَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ “‏ مَنْ حَجَّ لِلَّهِ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ ‏”‏‏.

“Whoever performs Hajj for Allah’s pleasure and abstain from sex, and does not commit evil, will return home free from sin as on the day his mother bore him.” [Bukhari]

Out of all the rituals that one performs in Hajj, the most important is standing on Arafat.  Abdu Rahman ibn Ya’mar reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ يَعْمَرَ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ فَمَنْ أَدْرَكَ لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ مِنْ لَيْلَةِ جَمْعٍ فَقَدْ تَمَّ حَجُّهُ

“The Hajj is Arafat. Whoever reaches the night of Arafat before the rising of the sun at dawn the next day, then his Hajj is complete.” (Sunan al-Nasā’ī)

The time for Standing on Arafat is from noon time of the 9th of the Dhu Al-Hijja to the Fajr time of the 10th).  If one misses standing on Arafat, his Hajj is invalid.

وزمن الوقوف ما بين زوال الشمس يوم عرفة يوم التاسع من ذي الحجة وهو يوم عرفة إلى طلوع الفجر من ليلة العاشر

Many of the rituals that we perform during the Hajj are enactment of events encountered by Prophet Ibrahim and his family.

We traverse between the mountains of Safa and Marwa as representation of what Sayeda Hajr did when she was looking for water for her infant son, Ismael.
We drink from the spring of Zamzam as she did when she went to rest after the traversing between the two hills.
We circle around the Kabba that was rebuilt by Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismael.
We go to Mina, cast the stones at Satan, go to the Muzdalifah as representation to the journey of Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son Ismael.

All rituals of the Hajj can be related to certain events in the history of Islam, mainly from the time of Prophet Ibrahim.

Since every ritual in the Hajj is an enactment of a transformational event impacting religious, historical or emotional lives of Muslims, the question is: “What is the relevance of Standing in Arafat?”  What event are we enacting?

There is no hadeath that gives us an explanation on the historical relevance of standing in Arafat.  Therefore, scholars offer several speculations.

قال القرطبي في التفسير وغيره: وقالوا في تسمية عرفة بهذا الاسم لأن الناس يتعارفون فيه، وقيل لأن جبريل عليه السلام طاف بإبراهيم فكان يريه المشاهد فيقول له: أَعَرَفْتَ؟ أَعَرَفْتَ؟ فيقول إبراهيم: عَرَفْتُ عَرَفْتُ. وقيل لأن آدم عليه السلام لما هبط من الجنة هو وحواء التقيا في ذلك الموضع فعرفها وعرفته.

The most popular speculation in books of Tafseer is that when Allah sent Adam and Hawa (Eve) to earth, they were separated and they first met and recognized each other at Arafat. (Thus the name Arafat, from the Arabic word ‘Arafa’ which means to know or meet).

Another speculation is that Jibreal took prophet Ibrahim around to show him places and when he took Ibrahim to Arafat, he asked him: “Do you recognize this place?” and he replied: “I recognize it”.

A third speculation is that Arafat is the place where people get introduced to each other during Hajj.

A fourth speculation is that the assembly at Arafat simulates the assembly during the day of Judgement.

Regarding the last speculation, I feel that a far better simulation of the assembly on the day of judgement is the state of Ihram and the gathering at the plains of Mina.  At Mina, millions of people stay in tents, and they look identical as they wear simple identical white pieces of cloths.

Unfortunately, you cannot get this feeling now, because of all the major construction and high-rise buildings and modern hotels and luxurious air-conditioned tents.

I realize that one of these speculations may be convincing to you and this is fine.  But I’ll offer you another one that is based on the Quran and supported by a Hadeath.

When we study the Quran, we read of only one event at which all the human race was assembled.  All humans from the first to the last were present.

Allah informs us of this assembly in Surat Al-Araf. Allah says:

وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَہُمۡ وَأَشۡہَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِہِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡ‌ۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ‌ۛ شَہِدۡنَآ‌ۛ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَـٰذَا غَـٰفِلِينَ (١٧٢) أَوۡ تَقُولُوٓاْ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡرَكَ ءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً۬ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ‌ۖ أَفَتُہۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلۡمُبۡطِلُونَ (١٧٣)

“(Recall) when your Lord took from the children of Adam their descendants from the loins, and made them testify as to themselves, saying, “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Yes, we testify.” (This was done) lest you should say on the Day of Judgment, “We were unaware of this.”

Or you would say, “It was our fathers who associated partners, and we are their descendants, would You destroy us for what the liars did?” (Al-Araf 7:172-173)

Regarding this first and very important assembly of human race, the Prophet (PBUH) provided more details.  Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال ابن عباس : إن الله لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره ، وأخرج ذريته كلهم كهيئة الذر ، فأنطقهم فتكلموا ، وأشهدهم على أنفسهم : ( ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا )

“When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back, and took out all his descendants in the size of ants (dhar, الذر) (so, they were in their natural look but small in size of ants) and made them speak and they spoke, and He made them testify on themselves, and he made light with some of them…”

A similar hadeath by reported by Ubay ibn Kaab (أبي بن كعب) who reported that he heard the Prophet (PBUH) saying:

عن أبي بن كعب في قوله : ( وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم ) قال : جمعهم ، فجعلهم أزواجا ، ثم صورهم ، ثم استنطقهم فتكلموا ، ثم أخذ عليهم العهد والميثاق ، وأشهدهم على أنفسهم : ( ألست بربكم ) ؟ قالوا : ( بلى شهدنا ) قال : فإني أشهد عليكم السماوات السبع ، والأرضين السبع ، وأشهد عليكم أباكم آدم ؛ لئلا تقولوا يوم القيامة : لم نعلم بهذا . اعلموا أنه لا إله غيري ، ولا رب غيري ، ولا تشركوا بي شيئا ، وإني سأرسل إليكم رسلي يذكرونكم عهدي وميثاقي ، وأنزل عليكم كتبي . قالوا : نشهد أنك ربنا وإلهنا ، لا رب لنا غيرك ، ولا إله لنا غيرك

Allah gathered all human beings, divided them into different groups, granted them human form and the power of speech.
He asked them: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They replied: ‘Indeed, you are Our Lord.’
Then Allah said: ‘I call upon the sky and the earth and your father, Adam, to be witness against you lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection that you had no knowledge of this.
You should know well that no one other than Me deserves to be worshipped and no one other than Me is the Lord.
I shall send to you My Messengers who will remind you of this covenant which you made with Me. I shall send down My Books to you.’
In reply all said: ‘We testify that You are Our Lord and our Deity. We have no Lord or deity other than You.’
Then Allah raised Adam to look at them and he saw the Prophets with sharp light over them and they made their own unique covenant:

وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِيثَـٰقَهُمۡ وَمِنكَ وَمِن نُّوحٍ۬ وَإِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَ‌ۖ وَأَخَذۡنَا مِنۡہُم مِّيثَـٰقًا غَلِيظً۬ا

“And We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you and from Nuh and Ibrahim and Musa and ‘Isa ibn Maryam; and We took from them a solemn covenant.” (Al-Ahzab 33:7)
(Ahmad)

This scene of having all the human race standing in front of Allah will be repeated again on the Day of Judgement.

وَعُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا

“And they will be marshaled before your Lord in lines, (with the announcement), “Now you have come to Us as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would never appoint a time for the fulfillment of the promise.” (Al-Kahf 18:48)

The standing in Arafat is  a simulation and reminder of this assembly and reaffirmation of our original covenant with Allah by making the ultimate proclamation:

لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

There is no god but Allah alone, without any partners, unto him belong the dominion and all praise and He has power over all things.

Amr ibn Shu’ayb (عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ) reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ خَيْرُ الدُّعَاءِ دُعَاءُ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ وَخَيْرُ مَا قُلْتُ أَنَا وَالنَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ قَبْلِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

“The best supplication is the one made on the day of Arafat and the best of what I and all the Prophets before me said is:

لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

There is no god but Allah alone, without any partners, unto him belong the dominion and all the praise and He has power over all things.” (Sunan al-Tirmidhī)

One may suggest that standing on Arafat is a reenactment of the human race assembly at the time of the original covenant (Mithaq).

عَنْ جَابِرٍ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مَا مِنْ يَوْمٍ أَفْضَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ يَنْزِلُ اللَّهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا فَيُبَاهِي بِأَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ أَهْلَ السَّمَاءِ

“No day is better to Allah than the day of Arafat. Allah descends to the lowest heaven and He boasts of the people of the earth to the people of heaven.” (Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Ḥibbān)

A similar hadeath was narrated by Sayeda Aisha (عَائِشَةُ) who reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ مَا مِنْ يَوْمٍ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَنْ يُعْتِقَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ عَبْدًا مِنْ النَّارِ مِنْ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ وَإِنَّهُ لَيَدْنُو ثُمَّ يُبَاهِي بِهِمْ الْمَلَائِكَةَ

“There is no day upon which Allah frees more of his servants from the Hellfire than the day of Arafat. He draws near and then He boasts of them to the angels.” (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)

So, all those people who will stand on Arafat will be forgiven and as the Prophet (PBUH) said:
(الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ) “The Hajj is Arafat”
and said
(مَنْ حَجَّ لِلَّهِ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ)  “Whoever performs Hajj for Allah’s pleasure… will return (from Hajj free from all sins) as if he was born anew.”

Those people who stood in Arafat will descent, from it as if they were born again by being completely purified from all sins.

Where was this first assembly held when people were in (عالم الذر) (the microscopic world) and their covenant was taken?

روى الإمام أحمد في (مسنده) بإسناد صحيح إلى ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ((أخذ الله الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان - يعني عرفة - فأخرج من صلبه كل ذرية ذرأها فنثرهم بين يديه كالذر، ثم كلمهم قبلاً قال: {أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ * أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ} )ورواه النسائي ، وابن جرير ، وابن أبي حاتم ، والحاكم في المستدرك(

“Allah took the covenant from the children of Adam at Na’maan (نعمان), meaning Arafat; Allah took form Adam’s lion all his descendants and spread them between His hands like ants, then he spoke to them face to face saying: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Indeed, we testify’…” (Ahmad)

The valley of Na’man is the largest valley in Makkah and it is on the south side of mountain of Arafat.

It is also quite interesting to note that the completion of the religion of Islam was declared by Allah on the day of Arafat.

عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ الْيَهُودِ قَالَ لَهُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ آيَةٌ فِي كِتَابِكُمْ تَقْرَؤُونَهَا لَوْ عَلَيْنَا مَعْشَرَ الْيَهُودِ نَزَلَتْ لَاتَّخَذْنَا ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ عِيدًا

“O leader of the believers, there is a verse you recite in your book, had it been revealed to us as a group of Jews, we would have taken that day as a holiday.”
Omar said, “Which verse is it?” The man said:

الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمْ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا

“Today I have completed your religion for you, perfected My favor upon you, and have chosen Islam as your religion.” (Al-Maeda 5:3)

Omar said, “I know the day and place in which this verse was revealed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. It was when he was standing on Arafat on a Friday.”

Finally, we note that we start the Hajj by answering Allah’s call by the proclamation;
لبيك اللهم لبيك.. لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك.. إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك. لا شريك لك
We are here to answer Your invitation and be completely obedient You. Praise, Blessings and the Kingdom are Yours. You have no partners.

And when we stand on Arafat, we make the ultimate proclamation:
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
There is no god but Allah alone, without any partners, unto Him belong the dominion and all praise and He has power over all things.

This proclamation that we make at Arafat is a reaffirmation of our covenant with Allah and a declaration of our readiness to fulfill our original commitment to Him.

We pray to Allah to grant us the opportunity to stand on Arafat next year and reaffirm our covenant with Him.

DUA

title: Elements of Proper Communication – Lessons from the Quran
excerpt:
