content:
Surat Al-Araf (7:187)
يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَٮٰهَا‌ۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى‌ۖ لَا يُجَلِّيہَا لِوَقۡتِہَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ لَا تَأۡتِيڪُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةً۬‌ۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِىٌّ عَنۡہَا‌ۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (١٨٧)

The 4th Element of Islam
The Pre-Hour Signs (الساعة عالمات)
Maryam Islamic Center
July 5th, 2020
Mamdouh.Salama@comcast.net

The 4 Elements of Religion
There is well known hadeath that was reported by Omar ibn Al-Khtaab (عمر رضي الله) who said:

عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال “بينما نحن جلوس عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم إذ طلع علينا رجل شديد بياض الثياب شديد سواد الشعر لا يرى عليه أثر السفر ولا يعرفه منا أحد حتى جلس إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأسند ركبتيه إلى ركبتيه ووضع كفيه على فخذيه وقال يا محمد أخبرني على الإسلام فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الإسلام أن تشهد أن لا إله إلا الله ورسول الله وتقيم الصلاة وتؤتي الزكاة وتصوم رمضان وتحج البيت إن استطعت إليه سبيلا قال صدقت قال فعجبنا له يسأله ويصدقه قال فأخبرني عن الإيمان قال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وتؤمن بالقدر خيره وشره قال صدقت قال فأخبرني عن الإحسان قال أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك قال فأخبرني عن الساعة قال ما المسؤول عنها بأعلم من السائل قال فأخبرني عن أماراتها قال أن تلد الأمة ربتها وأن ترى الحفاة العراة العالة رعاء الشاة يتطاولون في البنيان قال ثم انطلق فلبثت مليا ثم قال لي يا عمر أتدري من السائل قلت الله ورسوله أعلم قال فإنه جبريل أتآكم يعلمكم دينكم” (رواه مسلم)

One day, while we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), a man came whose clothes were exceedingly white and whose hair was exceedingly black. There were no signs of travel seen on him and none of us knew him. He approached and sat down by the Prophet (PBUH) resting his knees to his and placing the palms of his hands on his thighs.
Then he said: “O Muhammad, inform me about Islam.” The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said: “Islam is to testify that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to pay the Zakat, to fast in Ramadan, and to make the pilgrimage (Hajj) to the House if you are able to do so.”
The man said, “You have spoken the truth.” We were amazed that he was asking him and telling him and them affirming what the Messenger said.
Then the man said, “So inform me about Eman (Faith).” The Prophet (PBUH) said, “It is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in the Divine Decree (Qadr), both the good and the bad thereof.”
The man said: “You have spoken the truth. Then inform me about Ihsan.” The Prophet (PBUH) said, “It is to worship Allah as though you see Him and if you are not able to see Him then He sees you.”
The man said: “Then inform me about the Hour (i.e. the Day of Judgment).” The Prophet (PBUH) said: “The one being questioned is not more knowledgeable about it than the questioner.” The man said, “Then, inform me about its signs.”
The Prophet (PBUH) said, “That the maid gives birth to her Mistress and that you will see the barefooted, naked, destitute shepherds competing in construction of high buildings.”
Then the man departed and I stayed for a time. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) asked me: “do you know who the questioner was?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said, “He was Jibreel who came to teach you your religion.” (Related by Muslim)

I want to place special emphasis on the last statement that was made by the Prophet (PBUH) which is: “He was Jibreel who came to teach you your religion.”
This means that the religion of Islam involves four elements and these are: Islam, Eman, Ihsan and the Hour (the pre-Hour signs).
These 4 elements address all aspect of your life, current and future.
• The definition of Islam provides the physical rituals that are involved in your personal relationship with Allah.
• The definition of Eman provides the articles of belief that are settled in your heart.
• The definition of Ehsan provides the control of your relationship with all creations under the continuous monitoring by Allah.
• The fourth element provides some signs of the hour (day of judgment) and these represent future events that you, as a Muslim, need to know to be prepared for it and establish plans to face them when they arrive, particularly since most of these signs represent tribulation and challenges.

No one knows the time of the Hour (the day of Judgement) except Allah and this is clear in the Quran:

يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَٮٰهَا‌ۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى‌ۖ لَا يُجَلِّيہَا لِوَقۡتِہَآ إِلَّا هُوَ‌ۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۚ لَا تَأۡتِيڪُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةً۬‌ۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِىٌّ عَنۡہَا‌ۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (١٨٧)
“They ask you about the Hour, “When is it due to happen?” Say, “Its knowledge is only with my Lord. No one can unfold it except He at its time. It weighs heavy in the heavens and the earth. It shall not come upon you but suddenly.” They ask you as if you were aware of it. Say, “Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know.” (Al-Araf 7:187)

يَسۡــٴَـلُكَ ٱلنَّاسُ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَا يُدۡرِيكَ لَعَلَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيبًا (٦٣)
“People ask you about the Hour (i.e. the Day of Judgment). Say,” Its knowledge is only with Allah.” And what can let you know? Maybe, the Hour is near.” (Al-Ahzab 33:63)

Is knowing the Signs of the Hour important?
• The importance of the events that precede Hour for Muslims is demonstrated by Allah revealing several of them in the Quran and by the Prophet (PBUH) providing many additional details on his own.
• These events will have dramatic impact on how we live on earth and we, as Muslims, who have been told about them, should be the most prepared to face them.

Number of signs and their classification:
Based on the Quran and the authentic hadeath, scholars have identified more than eighty (80) signs of the Hour.
Scholars suggested two main methods for classification:
• Classify them as “minor signs” and “major signs.”
• Classify them as signs that have passed, signs that can be observed at present,” and “signs that have yet to occur.

Some of the Signs that have already been fulfilled:
The Prophet (PBUH) mentioned two signs in the hadeath we discussed:
1. The maid gives birth to her Mistress.
• Past explanation was that this is a metaphor (مجاز) for the disrespect of the daughter to her mother and treating her as a maid.
• Now we can interpret this sign literally (حقيقي) by the establishment of the womb for hire and the surrogate mother business. Poor women are paid to carry the child of rich couples.
2. The barefooted, naked, destitute shepherds competing in construction of high buildings.
• Now we are witnessing the fulfillment of this sign when we hear of the people in Arabia competing on who has the highest building.

List of some of the tallest buildings in the Arab League:
Rank | Name | City | Height
1 | Burj Khalifa | Dubai | 828 m (2,717 ft)
2 | Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower | Mecca | 601 m (1,972 ft)
3 | Marina 101 | Dubai | 425 m (1,394 ft)
3 | Princess Tower | Dubai | 414 m (1,358 ft)
4 | Al Hamra Tower | Kuwait City | 413 m (1,355 ft)
5 | 23 Marina | Dubai | 392.4 m (1,287 ft)
6 | Capital Market Authority Headquarters | Riyadh | 385 m (1,263 ft)
7 | Burj Mohammed Bin Rashid | Abu Dhabi | 381 m (1,250 ft)

Interesting pre-hour sign that has recently been fulfilled:
It is reported by Abi Saeed Al-Khudry (أبي سعيد الخدري) that the Prophet (PBUH) said:
قال أبي سعيد الخدري قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: “والذي نفسي بيده لا تقوم الساعة حتى تكلم الرجل عذبة سوطه وشراك نعله وتخبره بما أحدث أهله من بعده” (رواه أحمد والترمذي)
“By the One in Whose Hand is my soul! The Hour will not come until the tip of a man’s hip and the straps on his sandal (shoe) speak to him of what occurred with his family after he left.”
• Early Muslims accepted this pre-Hour event as real, but they were not able to interpret it.
• But we see its fulfillment now with the advent of cellphones and pagers (Speaking thru belt and Shoes).

Why knowing the Pre-Hour Signs is Important?
1. Focus on developing technologies that protect humanity in face of the expected calamities.
2. Allow for better understanding of certain Surat in the Quran that seem unclear without taking these signs into account.

Technology planning to allow survival when encountering some signs of the Hour:
• Dust Storm: It has been revealed that there will be a major dust storm that will engulf the earth and shield the sun. Shouldn’t we work on developing efficient air filtration systems and food production in the absence of the sun?
• Earthquakes: It has been revealed that after certain cosmic events, the number and the intensity of earthquakes will increase. Shouldn’t we start developing building codes that withstand them and minimize the impact of sinkholes?
• Random killing: It has been revealed that random killing will become so spread. Shouldn’t we plan on how to protect our society?
• Changes in the solar system: It has been revealed that the earth will be bombarded by stars or massive asteroids. Shouldn’t we plan for communication in the absence of satellites and keep paper copies of records?

All Messengers told their followers of the Signs of the Hour:
Because of the importance of the pre-hour signs, Allah revealed them to all His Messengers. Several of the signs revealed in the Quran and in the sayings of our Prophet (PBUH) also exist in the Torah and the Bible and even in far older religious books.
The question is not whether these signs will happen, the question is when will they happen. Since we don’t know when, we should always be prepared to face them when they happen.

The 2nd main benefit of studying the signs of the hour:
Knowing the signs allows for better understanding certain Surats in the Quran that seem unclear without taking these signs into account.
Many of the signs of the hour in the Quran are related to punishments that the Prophet (PBUH) threatened the disbelievers with but have not been fulfilled during his life and will be fulfilled after the Prophet’s death.
• The Prophet’s message was neither solely for Quraysh and the Arabs nor for the time of his mission.
• The Prophet’s message is for all people and for all times until the coming of the hour.

Warnings in the Quran extends beyond the life of the Prophet (PBUH):
وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِى نَعِدُهُمۡ أَوۡ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُهُمۡ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ شَہِيدٌ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفۡعَلُونَ (٤٦)
“No matter whether We show you (during your life) some of what We have promised to them, or We cause you to die (before it), still they have to return to Us. Then, Allah is witness over what they do.” (Yunus 10:46)

فَٱصۡبِرۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ۬ فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِى نَعِدُهُمۡ أَوۡ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيۡنَا يُرۡجَعُونَ (٧٧)
“Therefore, be patient. Surely, Allah’s promise is true. Then, (O Prophet,) whether We show you (in your life) a part of what We have promised to them, or make you die (before they are punished), in any case they have to be returned to Us.” (Ghafir 40:77)

Did the Prophet (PBUH) threatened the disbelievers with punishments and what were their nature?
وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفۡجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَنۢبُوعًا (٩٠) أَوۡ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ۬ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ۬ وَعِنَبٍ۬ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرَ خِلَـٰلَهَا تَفۡجِيرًا (٩١) أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفًا أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَةِ قَبِيلاً (٩٢)
“They said, “We shall never believe in you unless you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. (90) Or you have a garden of date palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth therein abundantly. (91) Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed, or you bring Allah and angels before us face to face.” (Al-Isra 17:90-92)

لَعَلَّكَ بَـٰخِعٌ۬ نَّفۡسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ (٣) إِن نَّشَأۡ نُنَزِّلۡ عَلَيۡہِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةً۬ فَظَلَّتۡ أَعۡنَـٰقُهُمۡ لَهَا خَـٰضِعِينَ (٤)
“It may be that thou tormenting yourself because they do not believe. (3) If We will, We can send down on them a sign from the sky on which their necks will stay in submission.” (Al-Shuara 26:3-4)

أَفَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِن نَّشَأۡ نَخۡسِفۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَوۡ نُسۡقِطۡ عَلَيۡہِمۡ كِسَفً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَأَيَةً۬ لِّكُلِّ عَبۡدٍ۬ مُّنِيبٍ۬ (٩)
“Have they not, then, looked to the sky and the earth that lies before them and behind them? If We so will, We would make the earth swallow them up, or cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them. Surely, in this there is a sign for a servant (of Allah) who turns to Him.“ (Saba 34:9)

بَلۡ هُمۡ فِى شَكٍّ۬ يَلۡعَبُونَ (٩) فَٱرۡتَقِبۡ يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِى ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬ (١٠) يَغۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ‌ۖ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ۬ (١١)
“But they, being in doubt, are playing around. (9) So, wait for a day when the sky will produce visible smoke (10) That will envelop people. This will be a painful punishment. (11)” (Al-Dukhan 44:9-11)

أَزِفَتِ ٱلۡأَزِفَةُ (٥٧) لَيۡسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ (٥٨)
“The Imminent (event) has approached. (57) There is no one, beside Allah, can disclose it (can remove it).” (Al-Najm 53:57-58)

وَإِن مِّن قَرۡيَةٍ إِلَّا نَحۡنُ مُهۡلِڪُوهَا قَبۡلَ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا‌ۚ كَانَ ذَٲلِكَ فِى ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ مَسۡطُورًا (٥٨)
“There is no town but We are to destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with severe punishment. That is set forth in the Book.” (Al-Isra 17:58)

Next week, Insha’Allah
Surat Al-Tariq (الطارق) (86)
I’ll stop here and next week, I plan, inshallah, to present the picture of the punishment from the verses of the Quran and use to give coherent meaning to Surat Al-Tariq (86).

DUA
O Allah, you said ”Ask me and I’ll respond to you,” O’ Allah, we are asking You as You have commanded us, O’ Allah accept our Dua.
اللهم صل وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين.
O’ Allah, spread your mercy upon us, shower us with Your blessings, increase our knowledge, grant us Your forgiveness, and reward us with the company of His prophets in the highest place in Heaven, Al-Ferdous Al-Aala.
O’ Allah, purify our heart, strengthen our faith, increase our knowledge and make us benefit from you have taught us.
O Allah, forgive our parents and all the believers, grant them your mercy, make their grave a garden from heaven and grant them the Ferdous Al-Ala.
O’ Allah remedy our sick and grant them full and speedy recovery,
O Allah, Grant us the ability to be grateful for Your Favors which You have bestowed upon us and upon our parents, and that we may do righteous deeds that are pleasing to you, O’ Allah guide our children, protect them and make them righteous.
O’ Allah, we seek from You all the good, whether we know it or we don’t, and we seek Your refuge from all the evil, whether we know it or we don’t.
O’ Allah, We ask with every name you have elected for yourself that none of us leave this gathering except with his pains are relieved, his worries are removed, his debts are paid, his weaknesses are concealed, his sins are forgiven and his needs is fulfilled.
وآخر دعوانا أن الحمد لله رب العالمين والصلاة والسلام على أشرف المرسلين سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين.
اللهم صل وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين.

excerpt:
The Divine Sunnah (Law) of Timing

content:
The Divine Sunnah (Law) of Timing

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا

وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله

After Surat Al-Fatiha, the first verse in the Quran gives us its purpose which is guidance to those who have Taqwa, Allah said:

الٓمٓ (١) ذَٲلِكَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ‌ۛ فِيهِ‌ۛ هُدً۬ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ (٢)

Alif-Lam-Mîm. (1) This is the Book where in which there is no doubt guidance for the Muttaqin (God conscious)”. (Al-Baqara 2:1-2)

Allah has also directed us on how to study the Quran to derive this guidance and this is thru the process of Tadabour, as Allah said:

كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ )ص(

(This is) a Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings that they should do the Tadabour of its Verses, and that those of understanding may remember (heed/reflect on its commands). “(Sad 38:29)

We have discussed in the past that there are 7 setep to unlock the knowledge of the Quran and these are:

1. Reading (Qira’ah) (قراءة) (Uttering the words and sentences whether one may or may not understand the meanings of what is being read)
2. Recitation (Tilawah) (تلاوة) (Understanding of the meanings and forward linkage)
3. Purification (Tazkiah) (تزكية) (purification of the Nafs)
4. Tarteel (ترتيل) (assembly of verse related to the same topic)
5. Tadabour (تدبر) (study the related verses to derive coherent understanding of the topic)
6. Recollection (Tadhakur) (تذكر) (memorization and reminder of past learnings)
7. Study (Dirasah) (دراسة) (continuity of the serious study)

Thru the process of Tadabour, you will be able achieve the guidance of identifying the universal laws that Allah established in this universe and these are called (سنن الله في الكون) “Allah’s laws in the universe”.  Some scholars suggest that the Quran includes abut 90 divine laws.  These divine laws don’t change as Allah emphasized by says in Surat Fatir:

فلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا

“… You will never find in the laws (sunan) of Allah any change, and you will never find in the laws of Allah any alteration.” (Fatir 35:43)

These laws govern many aspects on our lives from the cosmological to the social and from the materialistic to the spiritual. Almost all Muslims recognize the divine cosmic laws (سنن الله الكونية) that Allah identified in many verses such as:

لَا ٱلشَّمۡسُ يَنۢبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدۡرِكَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيۡلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّہَارِ‌ۚ وَكُلٌّ۬ فِى فَلَكٍ۬ يَسۡبَحُونَ (٤٠)

“Neither it is for the sun to overtake the moon, nor can the night outpace the day. Each one is floating in an orbit.” (Yaseen 35:40)

Also,

وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّہَارَ وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ‌ۖ كُلٌّ۬ فِى فَلَكٍ۬ يَسۡبَحُونَ (٣٣)

“And He is the One Who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit floating. (33)” (Al-Anbia 21:33)

In this talk, I plan inshallah to focus on one divine law that is often overlooked by most of us.   I believe that ignoring it is the cause of most of the anxiety and stress that we put ourselves under.  This is Allah’s law of timing (سنة التوقيت).   I am talking about the divine law of timing and not the divine law of time.

The divine law of time is part of the divine cosmic laws that we are familiar with because it is the basis for establishing the time during the day and for developing the yearly calendar.  The reference to this law of time came in several verses such as:

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ ضِيَآءً۬ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ نُورً۬ا وَقَدَّرَهُ ۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَ‌ۚ

“He is the One who has made the sun a glow, and the moon a light, and determined for it stages, so that you may learn the number of the years and the calculation (of time).” (Yunus 10:5)

Also,

وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّہَارَ ءَايَتَيۡنِ‌ۖ فَمَحَوۡنَآ ءَايَةَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَجَعَلۡنَآ ءَايَةَ ٱلنَّہَارِ مُبۡصِرَةً۬ لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلاً۬ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَلِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَ‌ۚ وَڪُلَّ شَىۡءٍ۬ فَصَّلۡنَـٰهُ تَفۡصِيلاً۬ (١٢)

“And We made the night and the day as two signs. Then, We obscured the sign of the night (with darkness) and We made the sign of the day bright, that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and that you may know the number of the years and the calculation (of time). And We have explained everything (in detail) with full explanation. (” (Al-Isra 17:12)

The divine law that I want to address is the law of timing.  This law requires infinite wisdom and ultimate knowledge, not only of the present but also of the future and of the interactive consequences of all associated events.  Obviously, the only One Who possesses this level of knowledge and wisdom is Allah.  Because of our limitations, Allah’s timing in very often different from our timing.

Our short-term interest and limited knowledge make us often rush and act in haste even if this action causes us harm. Allah warned us of our characteristic of haste and impatience by saying in Surat Al-Isra:

وَيَدۡعُ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُ ۥ بِٱلۡخَيۡرِ‌ۖ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ عَجُولاً۬ (١١)

“And man invokes (Allah) for evil as he invokes (Allah) for good and man is ever hasty (Al-Isra 17:11)

Because Allah’s law (Sunnah) of timing is very important, Allah provided us with many examples in the Quran to illustrate its relevance and to convince us that we should trust Allah’s timing because it is always better than ours.  Believing in the divine Law of Timing should help us develop the wisdom of being patient and avoid complaining and getting frustrated when things that we want are delayed.

Allah’s law of timing will not change for us, so we better accept its existence and learn how to live with it.

There are many examples in the Quran that we can use to study the impact of Allah’s timing but I’ll only present two to illustrate two points:

1. The negative consequence when a person acts on his timing instead of Allah’s timing.
2. The superior consequence when Allah grants the person what he wants on Allah’s timing instead of the person’s timing.

The Negative Consequence of Violating the Divine Timing

Avoiding haste does not mean that we should not plan and do everything possible to achieve our goals but we should not allow our desire for quick achievement to make us act in haste. Even haste in trying to please Allah can cause harm.

The example that Allah presented to us is of Prophet Musa.  Allah gave Prophet Musa an appointment for a specific time, but Prophet Musa was so anxious to talk to Allah, so he went earlier than Allah’s appointed time.   When he arrived to the designated place, Allah asked him why did you come early as revelated to us in Surat Taha:

وَمَآ أَعۡجَلَكَ عن قَوۡمِكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ (٨٣) قَالَ هُمۡ أُوْلَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ رَبِّ لِتَرۡضَىٰ (٨٤)

“What has caused you to hurry leaving your people, O Musa?” (83) He (Musa) said, “they are just behind me, and I hurried towards You, my Lord, so that You be pleased.” (Taha 20:83-84)

Prophet Musa’s reason for going early is obviously good, to please Allah. But, prophet Musa used his timing instead of Allah’s and Allah allowed it to happen may be to teach us a lesson.

What Prophet Musa did not know is that at the time when he did not have to leave, bad things will happen to his people and his presence for these few days until his appointment would have be necessary to prevent major sin from being committed by his people.  Allah provided us with this important lesson in Surat Taha.

Allah told Musa about what happened to his people when he left them early, Allah said:

قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَوۡمَكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ (٨٥) فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَـٰنَ أَسِفً۬ا‌ۚ (٨٦)

“He (Allah) said, “We have put your people to test after you (left them) and Al-Samiriy has misguided them.” (85) So, Musa went back to his people, angry and sad.” (Taha 20:85-86)

This account of Prophet Musa should teach us that we should always accept Allah’s timing when we face delays in doing something that is intended to bring us closer to Allah.  Those who were planning to go for Hajj this year and now they are not, should not be upset and express gratitude to Allah because Allah’s timing for them to go later is far better than their own timing to go this year.

This account of Prophet Musa should also teach us not rush even if we are making a decision that we know is good.  We may relate this account to our interest in opening the Masjid as early as we can.  The goal is noble, but if we rush and open early, it may represent the wrong timing and harm may com, so we should be patient.

The superior consequence of Allah’s timing vs ours – The Story of Prophet Yusuf

Let reflect on the story of Prophet Yusuf that is revealed to us in Surat Yousef (12) that we listened in the beginning to some of its verses.   The scene that Allah is presenting to us is in the prison when two prisoners came to him to interpret their dreams and he interpreted that one of them will be set free and will be working for the king.

So, Prophet Yusuf wanted to take advantage of this person and his future relationship with the king to explain his innocence to be granted his freedom.  But because the timing that Prophet Yusuf was far earlier than the timing that Allah set for Prophet Yusuf’s release from the prison, Allah allowed Satan to make the freed prisoner forget and thus prophet Yusuf stayed several more years in the prison, Allah says:

وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ۥ نَاجٍ۬ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱذۡڪُرۡنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَٮٰهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ ذِڪۡرَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجۡنِ بِضۡعَ سِنِينَ (٤٢)

“And he (Yusuf) said to the one whom he believed likely to be released, “Tell your lord about me.” But Satan made him forget to mention him to his lord. So, he (Yusuf) remained in prison for a few (more) years.”  (Yusuf 12: 42)

After few years, the king saw a strange dream for several days and he asked all people about its interpretation but no one was able to interpret it:  Allah relates to us this account:

وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبۡعَ بَقَرَٲتٍ۬ سِمَانٍ۬ يَأۡڪُلُهُنَّ سَبۡعٌ عِجَافٌ۬ وَسَبۡعَ سُنۢبُلَـٰتٍ خُضۡرٍ۬ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَـٰتٍ۬‌ۖ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡمَلَأُ أَفۡتُونِى فِى رُءۡيَـٰىَ إِن كُنتُمۡ لِلرُّءۡيَا تَعۡبُرُونَ (٤٣) قَالُوٓاْ أَضۡغَـٰثُ أَحۡلَـٰمٍ۬‌ۖ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِتَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحۡلَـٰمِ بِعَـٰلِمِينَ (٤٤)

“And (one day) the king said: “I have seen (in a dream) seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and (seven) others that are dry. O people, tell me about my dream, if you can interpret dreams.” (43)

They said: Jumbled dreams! And we do not know the interpretation of dreams.”  (Yusuf 12: 43-44)

Only then, the freed prisoner remembered Yusuf and this was the time that Allah wanted things to happen:  Allah said:

وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنۡہُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعۡدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۟ أُنَبِّئُڪُم بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرۡسِلُونِ (٤٥) يُوسُفُ أَيُّہَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفۡتِنَا فِى سَبۡعِ بَقَرَٲتٍ۬ سِمَانٍ۬ يَأۡڪُلُهُنَّ سَبۡعٌ عِجَافٌ۬ وَسَبۡعِ سُنۢبُلَـٰتٍ خُضۡرٍ۬ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَـٰتٍ۬ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرۡجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ (٤٦)

“Then the man who was released (from the prison) remembered after the long time and said: “I will tell you of its interpretation, so send me forth (to Yusuf).”  (45)   (He came to the prison and said to Yusuf), “Yusuf, O the truthful one, tell us about seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and (seven) others that are dry, so that I may go back to the people so that they may know (the interpretation of the dream.)”  (Yusuf 12: 42-46)

Here Prophet Yusuf, could have said, I’ll interpret the dream only after you tell the king about my story to release me.  But no, he now appreciates that he will be released when Allah wanted him to be released, so he did his job as a righteous person who is willing to help without expecting reward from anyone other than Allah.

He interpreted the dream without any pre-demand knowing that his interpretation will save the people of Egypt whose leaders have done great injustice to him. In fact, he did not only interpret the dream but he went beyond the dream and gave them technical advices to ensure Egypt’s long-term prosperity; he said:

قَالَ تَزۡرَعُونَ سَبۡعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبً۬ا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمۡ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦۤ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ مِّمَّا تَأۡكُلُونَ (٤٧) ثُمَّ يَأۡتِى مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ سَبۡعٌ۬ شِدَادٌ۬ يَأۡكُلۡنَ مَا قَدَّمۡتُمۡ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬ مِّمَّا تُحۡصِنُونَ (٤٨) ثُمَّ يَأۡتِى مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ عَامٌ۬ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعۡصِرُونَ (٤٩)

“He said, “You will grow crops for seven years consecutively. So, what you have harvested, leave it in its ears, except a little which you eat. (47) Then seven hard (drought) years shall come after that, which shall consume what you have stored in preparation for them, except a little which you need to preserve (to sow). (48) Then there shall come after that a year in which people will have rains and in which they will extract oils.” (Yusuf 12: 47-49)

When the freed prisoner told the king, the king asked for Yusuf to be released and brought to him.  But Yusuf refused to leave the prison until the king investigates his case.   The king did, and discovered the innocence of Prophet Yusuf.   So, the king declared Yusuf’s innocence and ordered his immediate release and offered him a job as his personal advisor. Yusuf suggested that the king appoints him as minister of finance and the king agreed.    Allah summarizes to us the account as follows:

وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱئۡتُونِى بِهِۦۤ أَسۡتَخۡلِصۡهُ لِنَفۡسِى‌ۖ فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ ۥ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَدَيۡنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ۬ (٥٤) قَالَ ٱجۡععلۡنِى عَلَىٰ خَزَآٮِٕنِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ‌ۖ إِنِّى حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ۬ (٥٥) وَكَذَٲلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنۡہَا حَيۡثُ يَشَآءُ‌ۚ نُصِيبُ بِرَحۡمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُ‌ۖ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ (٥٦)

“The king said, “Bring him to me, and I shall employ him purely for myself.” So, when he (the king) talked to him, he said (to Yusuf), “Today you are with us well-placed, fully trusted.” (54) He said, “Appoint me to (supervise) the treasures of the land. I am indeed a knowledgeable keeper.” (55) And this is the way, We gave Yusuf power in the land. He could settle in it wherever he wished. We extend Our mercy to whomsoever We will, and We do not let the reward of the righteous people to go to waste.” (Yusuf 12: 54:56)

Yusuf came out of the prison after all these years as freed man but as the minister of finance in the most powerful country in the world at that time.

Reflecting on this account, Prophet Yusuf was expecting that the released prisoner to tell the king as soon as he was released, so the king can pardon him.   But think about what would be outcome if this happened.  Prophet Yusuf would still be released as slave and still probably be hated by those who accused him in the first place. He would not have the chance to even interpret the dream for the king.  So, this early release wouldn’t have been good for Prophet Yusuf and Allah had a different timing that is far better for Yusuf’s.

Yes, Prophet Yusuf had to suffer more, but this delay and extended suffering was the best thing that happened to him.  He has now been released as innocent and free man and not only as free man but also as holder of the highest positions in Egypt.

This story is not intended for entertainment but to teach us the critical divine law that Allah’s timing is far better than our timing.  So, we should be patient even when facing difficulties and should remain steadfast on our righteous deeds.

The Quran has many other examples that illustrates Allah’s timing such as:

* The divine timing that brought Prophet Musa and Al-Khidr to a village to arrive at the time when a wall was just ready to fall down and they fixed it to protect the treasure of the two orphans. (Surat Al-Kahf)
* The Divine Timing from the Battle of Badr (Surat Al-Anfal)
* The Divine Timing for Prophet Musa to meet his future wife and her father Prophet Shu’ayb شعيب)). The divine timing of reaching the mount of Tur to receive his assignment as Messenger of Allah.  (Surat Al-Qasas and Taha)

You can study these on your own.

But before I end, I need to emphasize a cautionary note:

Recognizing the divine law of timing does not mean that we do nothing waiting for it.

Yes, we all want to see the results of our noble aims as soon as possible and we should seek to achieve them with good planning, hard work and thru moral means but we should not be impatient and we should never be discouraged because of delays.

We should accept that there is divine timing for everything and the results will come not at our timing but at Allah’s. Allah’s timing is based on his infinite knowledge and ultimate wisdom but our timing will always be based on limited knowledge and impatience.

Dua

The Conscious world– Quantum Physics

content:
The Conscious world– Quantum Physics

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا

وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله.

Before I talk about the subject that I was asked to discuss which is the double slits experiment, let me take advantage of having our middle and high school students here and clarify couple of important points related to the Quran.

The Quran contains about 6200 verses and out of these verses there are only 200 verses that address prohibitions and laws and out of these there is only 9 that focuses on the penal system.

But the Quran include more than 1000 verses discuss physical sciences.  This clearly illustrates the important of the different branches of natural sciences to understanding the Quran.  Therefore, you find that in the golden age of Islam the great scientists were also great theologians.

As example Ja’far as-Sadiq (جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ٱلصَّادِقُ‎‎; 702–765 CE) who developed the Ja’fari school of Fiqh and he is considered the sixth Shia Imam but he is also considered as a major figure in the Hanafi and Maliki schools of Sunni jurisprudence.  He wrote in the subjects of chemistry, mathematics, philosophy, astronomy, anatomy, and others.

It is interesting t know that Ja’far as-Sadiq was the chemistry teacher of Jābir ibn Hayyān who is known as the father of chemistry.  Jābir ibn Hayyān said: “My master Ja’far as-Sadiq taught me about evaporation, distillation and crystallization and everything I learned in alchemy was from him.”

Another example is Ibn Rush (Averroes) who wrote over 80 books on mathematics, medicine, astronomy, physics, celestial mechanics, logic, geography, philosophy, and psychology, in addition to writing on theology, Sharia, and Islamic jurisprudence.   In fact one the best books on comparative Fiqh was written by Ibn Rushd, its title is “Distinguished Jurist’s Primer” ( بداية المجتهد و نهاية المقتصد).

I am saying this because I want to emphasize to our youth that their study of physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics, history and so on are very important in truly knowing Allah.  This is why scholars say that Allah revealed two books.  A read book and perspective visual book (كتاب الله المقروء و كتاب الله المنظور).  The read book is the Quran and the visual book is the universe.  You will never fully know the power and wisdom of Allah by reading the Quran only, but you will see the reality of the power and wisdom of Allah by studying his creations and this requires excelling in the study of natural sciences.

This point is affirmed by the great Muslim scientist and scholar Ibn al-Haytham (بن الهيثم) whose name is Latinized as “Alhazen” who is recognized in the west as the father of modern scientific methodology. Ibn al-Haytham wrote: “I constantly sought knowledge and truth, and it became my belief that for gaining access to the glory and closeness to Allah, there is no better way than that of searching for truth and knowledge.”

Now, let me go to the topic I was asked to discuss.   Allah informs us in the Quran that everything in the universe sings His praise and prostrated to His glory but we just lack the knowledge to understand them.   As example, Allah says in Surat Al-Isra

تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيہِنَّ‌ۚ وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡ‌ۗ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورً۬ا (٤٤)

The seven heavens and the earth and all whosoever is in them praise Him, and there is not a thing but hymns His praise; but you do not understand their praise. Truly, He is Ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving (Al-Isra 17:44)

Similarly, Allah says in Surat Al-Noor:

أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلطَّيۡرُ صَـٰٓفَّـٰتٍ۬‌ۖ كُلٌّ۬ قَدۡ عَلِمَ صَلَاتَهُ ۥ وَتَسۡبِيحَهُ ۥ‌ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِمَا يَفۡعَلُونَ (٤١)

“Have you not seen that Allah is praised by whosoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds with wings out-spread in their flight? Everyone knows his prayer and his way of praise; and Allah is Aware of what they do (Al-Noor 24:41)

These verses and others like them tell us that every particle in the universe has conscious to know Allah and thus do Tasbeeh to Him.  If we believe in this, we must treat everything in the universe with respect because they have feelings.

This understanding is supported by a hadeath that has been reported by Imam Bukhari and narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah (جابر رضي الله عن) who said:

وعن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: كان جذع يقوم إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، يعني في الخطبة. فلما وضع المنبر، سمعنا للجذع مثل صوت العشار حتى نزل النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم، فوضع يده عليه فسكن”. ((رواه البخاري))

There was a trunk of a date-palm tree upon which the Prophet (PBUH) used to recline while delivering Khutbah. When a pulpit [Minbar] was placed in the Masjid, we heard the trunk crying out like a pregnant she-camel. the Prophet (PBUH) came down from the pulpit and put his hand on the trunk and it became quiet.

In another narration, it says that the Prophet (PBUH) stopped the khutbah, descended from the minbar and began to stroke the trunk of the palm tree and then he hugged it and told the companions who were gathered round the tree:

‘By Allah in whose hands rest my soul if I had not hugged it, it would have remained sobbing like this until the Day of Judgement.

Is there proof that all matters have conscious and they know what is happening around them?

In about the year 1800, an interesting experiment was conducted by Thomas Young and it became to be known by the “Double Slits Experiment” (1773–1829). Thomas’s experiment involved using a coherent light source, such as a laser beam, to illuminate a plate containing two parallel slits, and observed the light passing through the two slits on a screen behind the plate.

He noted that instead of having two bands corresponding the two slits, the light passing through the two slits interfered producing a diffraction (interference) pattern of bright and dark bands on the screen.  No big deal because at that time, scientists considered that light are waves and thus the diffraction pattern occurs.   But later scientists discovered that light is formed by a stream of particles called photons.

Later scientists did the experiment by shooting stream of electrons, hydrogen atoms (mainly proton) and even Bucky Ball (60 carbon atoms) and the results were the same as the light. The particles showed the diffraction pattern.

Scientists decided to run the the experiments by shooting individual particles instead of a stream of particles and the results were the same diffraction pattern.

In order to understand how individual particles form diffraction pattern, scientist used particle detector, but the pattern of the particles changed, instead of a diffraction pattern, the particles formed two strips.  When they stopped the detector, the particles formed a diffraction pattern.

This raised the question regarding influence of the observer on the particle pattern.

Then scientist did something interesting and they observed something even more weird, they turned the detector on but did not record the data and they noted that the particles formed the diffraction pattern but when they started recording the particles formed the two-strip pattern.   This suggested that the particles are not influenced by the detector but also by the recording.

The perplexing question is: how the particles knew whether they are observed or not and whether they are recorded or not.

Note that when the particles are being observed/recorded, they move in straight lines forming two strips behind the two slits, but when they are not recorded they behave in haphazard matter.

No one yet has been able to come with solid scientific answer to this question, So, this question remains to be answered by anyone of our youth and if he/she did, they are most likely to join this group of scientists (Noel prize Winners in Physics).

But until now, there is no physical explanation for this behavior except to consider that particles have conscious and awareness when someone is observing and recording their motion.

Eugene P Wagner who is one of the leading physicits of the 20th century and the 1963 Nobel Prize winner in Physics reached this conclusion that everything in the universe has conscious, as he said:

“It will remain remarkable, in what ever way our future concepts may develop, that the very study of the external world led to the scientific conclusion that the content of the consciousness is the ultimate universal reality.”

This affirms Allah’s revelation to us that everything in the universe is fully aware of Him and in a state of continuous Tasbeeh.  The question is: are we fully aware of Allah and are frequent in His Tasbeeh.

This also may explain why Allah has observers and recorders over all what we do to ensure that every atom in out body stays in the straight path in full obedience to Allah.  But, it is we, whom Allah has subjugated everything in this world to us, are the ones who force them to deviate from the straight path and that is where distress and chaos happen to our body and to our environment.

The wonder of creation is that the whole universe sings the praise of Allah and prostrates to Him. Peace in the universe can only occur if man has the wisdom to join these creations in their submissiveness to Allah.

We pray to Allah to give us the wisdom and guide us to maintain harmony with the rest of creations by being in total awareness of Allah and in state of continuous Tasbeeh and glorification of Him.

If you want to list to study this experiment further, you can consult several youtube videos:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nRSBaq3vAeY
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfPeprQ7oGc

Allah also teaches us that He assigned observers to record everything we do

سَوَآءٌ۬ مِّنكُم مَّنۡ أَسَرَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ وَمَن جَهَرَ بِهِۦ وَمَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡتَخۡفِۭ بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَارِبُۢ بِٱلنَّہَارِ (١٠) لَهُ ۥ مُعَقِّبَـٰتٌ۬ مِّنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ يَحۡفَظُونَهُ ۥ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ (الرّعد(

It is the same (to Him) whether any of you conceal his speech or declare it openly, whether he hides by night or goes forth freely by day. (10) For him (each person), there are angels in succession, before and behind him. They guard him by the Command of Allah.” [Al-Ra’ad 13:10-11]

وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦ‌ۖ وَيُرۡسِلُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَفَظَةً حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ تَوَفَّتۡهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ (٦١)

“He is the Irresistible, Supreme over His slaves, and He sends guardians (angels guarding and writing all deeds) over you, until when death approaches one of you, Our Messengers take his soul, and they never neglect their duty” (Al-An’am 6:61)

كَلَّا بَلۡ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ (٩) وَإِنَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَحَـٰفِظِينَ (١٠) كِرَامً۬ا كَـٰتِبِينَ (١١) يَعۡلَمُونَ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ (الانفِطار(

“Nay! But you deny the Judgement. (9) There are over you guardians, (10) Honorable and recording (your deeds).,” (Al-Infitar 62:9-12)

Quantum physics

لَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسۡجُدُ لَهُ ۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَڪَثِيرٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۖ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ‌ۗ وَمَن يُہِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ ۥ مِن مُّكۡرِمٍ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۩

Have you not seen that whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the all beasts treading the earth and many of mankind willingly prostrate themselves to Allah? (Al-Hajj 22:18)

There other narration to the same account but they are all similar.

وفي رواية: فلما كان يوم الجمعة قعد النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم على المنبر، فصاحت النخلة التى كان يخطب عندها حتى كادت أن تنشق. وفي رواية: فصاحت صياح الصبي، فنزل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، حتى أخذها فضمها إليه، فجعلت تئن أنين الصبي الذي يسكت حتى استقرت ، قال: “بكت على ما كانت تسمع من الذكر” ((رواه البخاري))

Another narration is: The Prophet ﷺ used to stand by a tree or a date-palm on Friday (to give the Khutbah). Then an Ansari woman or man said, “O Messenger of Allah! Shall we make a pulpit for you?” He replied, “If you wish.” So they made a pulpit for him and when it was Jumah, the Prophet ﷺ sat on the pulpit [to deliver the Khutbah] and the trunk of the date- palm on which he used to recline cried out as if it would split asunder.

Another narration is: It cried like a child and the Prophet ﷺ descended (from the pulpit) and embraced it while it continued moaning like a child being quietened. The Prophet ﷺ said, “It was crying for (missing) what it used to hear of Dhikr near it.”

Quotes

“It will remain remarkable, in what ever way our future concepts may develop, that the very study of the external world led to the scientific conclusion that the content of the consciousness is the unltimate universtal reality.”  (Eugene P Wagner, one of the leading physicits of the 20th century and the 1963 Nobel Prize winner in Physics  for his contributions to the theory of the atomic nucleus and the elementary particles, particularly through the discovery and application of fundamental symmetry principles. Born in 1902 and died in 1995).

“Science cannot solve the ultimate mystry of nature because, in the last analysis, we ourselves are a part of the mystry that we are trying to solve.”’ (Max Planck, German theoretical physicist whose work on quantum theory won him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1858.  Born in 1858 and died in 1947.)

The Unique Creation of Adam

الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا

Last week I provided an opinion on the creation of mankind and I said that the question of the origin of man has always been perplexing to philosophers, scientist and theologians.

You may ask why we even care about understanding the creation of mankind since we believe that Allah created Adam and we all came from Adam. You may also argue that no one really knows the ultimate truth and any opinion will be a mere speculation since Allah said:

مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ خَلْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمَا كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُدًا

“I did not have them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation; and I would never take misleaders for helpers.” (Al-Kahf 18:51)

However, your lack of interest may not be totally justified because of three main reasons:

1) The Quran asks us to study the origin of creation as Allah says:

قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ ڪَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ‌ۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأَخِرَةَ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ قَدِيرٌ۬ (العنكبوت)

Say: “Travel in the land and see how He (Allah) originated the creation, and then Allah will bring forth the last creation (i.e. resurrection after death). Verily, Allah is Able to do all things.” (Al-Ankaboot 29:20)

2) The Quran includes many verses that discuss the creation of man and this indicates that the subject is important. The Quran gives us several key stages of the creation as Allah says:

وَقَدۡ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَطۡوَارًا (١٤)

And He created you in different stages.” (Nuh 71:14)

The different stages that Allah identified for us include: Water (مَآءِ), plant (نَبَاتً۬), Dust (تُرَابٍ۬), Mud (طِينٍ۬), Decayed mud (حَمَإٍ۬ مَّسۡنُونٍ۬), Ringing clay (صَلۡصَـٰلٍ۬), Make progeny of a drop of despised fluid (سُلَـٰلَةٍ۬ مِّن مَّآءٍ۬ مَّهِينٍ۬), Fashioning it (سَوَّٮٰهُ), Blowing in him Allah’s spirit (وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦ‌).

وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ بَشَرً۬ا (٥٤)

“And it is He Who has created man from water. (Al-Fourqan 25:54)

وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتً۬ا (١٧)

“And Allah made you to grow out the earth as plant” (Nuh 71:17)

وَمِنۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦۤ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابٍ۬ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرٌ۬ تَنتَشِرُونَ (الروم )

“And among His Signs that He created you from dust, and then you are human beings scattered! (Al-Rome 30:20)

ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنِ مِن طِينٍ۬ (٧)

Who made everything He has created good, and He began the creation of man from clay. (Al-Sajda 32:7)

وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِن صَلۡصَـٰلٍ۬ مِّنۡ حَمَإٍ۬ مَّسۡنُونٍ۬ (٢٦)

“And indeed, We created man from ringing clay of decayed mud. (Al-Hijr 15; 26)

ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنِ مِن طِينٍ۬ (٧) ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسۡلَهُ ۥ مِن سُلَـٰلَةٍ۬ مِّن مَّآءٍ۬ مَّهِينٍ۬ (٨) ثُمَّ سَوَّٮٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦ‌ۖ (٩)

He, Who made well whatever He created, and He began the creation of man from clay; (7) Then He made his progeny from a drop of despised fluid; (8) Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit. (Al-Sajda 32:7-9)

3. There are many scientific discoveries that appear to conflict with some ahadeath that can create doubt in the mind of many particularly our youth and thus need to be addressed to resolve any apparent conflict.

Abi Ummah (أبي أمامة) said:

عن أبي أمامة أن رجلا قال : ( يا رسول الله أنبيٌّ كان آدم ؟ قال : نعم ، قال : فكم كان بينه وبين نوح ؟ قال : عشرة قرون ) رواه ابن حبان في ” صحيحه ” والحاكم في ” المستدرك ” وقال : هذا حديث صحيح على شرط مسلم ، والطبراني في ” المعجم الكبير ” ، وصححه الألباني بشواهده.

A man said, O’ Messenger of Allah, was Adam a prophet, he (PBUH) said: Yes. The man asked: How long was it between Adam and Noah. The Prophet said: “Ten Quroun”

Al-Tabarani (الطبراني) reported the same hadeath but added the man asked:

ويذكر الطبراني أن رجلا قال: “يا رسول الله، أنبيّ كان آدم؟” قال: ((نعم))، قال: كم بينه وبين نوح؟” قال: ((عشرة قرون))، قال: “كم بين نوح وإبراهيم؟” قال: ((عشرة قرون))، قال: “يا رسول الله، كم كانت الرسل؟” قال: ((ثلاث مئة وخمسة عشر))

How long was it been Noah and Ibrahim? The Prophet (PBUH) said: Ten Quroon. The man then asked: O Messenger of Allah, what was the number of the messengers? The Prophet (PBUH) said: three hundred and fifteen (315).

Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس) said:

قال ابن عباس: وبين آدم ونوح عشرة قرون، وبين نوح وإبراهيم عشرة قرون، وبين إبراهيم وموسى 700 سنة، وبين موسى وعيسى 1500 سنة، وبين عيسى ونبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم 600 سنة

Between Adam and Noah is ten Quroun and Between Noah and Ibrahim is ten Quroun and between Ibrahime and Musa is 700 years and between Musa and Isa is 1500 years and between Isa and our Prophet is 600 years.

Since the Prophet (PBUH) was born about 1400 years ago, adding these numbers one can conclude that Prophet Adam came to the earth at 20 Quroun plus 4200 years.

The Question is how long is the 20 Quroun? The English translation of the term Quran is century, i.e. 100 years but this obviously wrong because the difference between Adam and Noah cannot be 1000 years because each one of them lived 1000 years.

Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن ابن عباس ـ رضي الله عنه ـ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: كان عمر آدم ألف سنة.

“The age of Adam was 1000 years”.

Regarding Prophet Noah he lived at least 1000 years, Allah says:

وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامً۬ا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمۡ ظَـٰلِمُونَ (١٤)

“And indeed, We sent Nuh (Noah) to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood overtook them while they were wrong-doers,” (Al-Ankaboot 29:14)

The term Qarrn is a measure of the time two people who are born at the same time be companions and from the term Qarn came the term Qareem as in:

فَأَقۡبَلَ بَعۡضُہُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ (٥٠) قَالَ قَآٮِٕلٌ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ إِنِّى كَانَ لِى قَرِينٌ۬ (٥١)

“Then they will turn to each other, mutually questioning. (50) A speaker of them will say: “Verily, I had a close companion.” (Al-Saffat 37: 50-51)

So, the “Qarn” is the likely life time of a person and since both Prophet Adam and Ibrahime lived 1000 years. So, the Quarn that was mentioned in the Prophet’s hadeath is not 100 years but 1000 years. This implies that Prophet Adam came to the earth about 24, 200 (twenty-four thousand and two hundred years) ago.

The challenge is how to resolve this apparent contradiction since traveling in the earth to study the origin of man, we discover that the oldest fossil of a human like skeleton that walked the Earth is about 3.2 million years ago. Scientist called this skeleton Lucy and it was found in Ethiopia.

Ten nearly complete skeletons of human like were discovered in 1969 in Qafzeh Cave in Israel and date back to around 100,000 years ago.

A complete human like skeleton was discovered near the Neanderthal area in Germany. It is very closely related to modern humans with over 99.5% of the DNA the same. The estimated age of the skeleton is 170,000 years. The Neanderthal man is not considered to be the modern man but scientists suggest that it is connected to it and this connection may have happened about 50 thousand years ago.

This is close to the estimated 25,000 age of the modern man based on the hadeath. The question becomes who are those Human like who lived on the earth 100’s of thousands of years ago before Prophet Adam

The Quran gives us some clues. Allah says;

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً

“And when your Lord told the angels: I am placing a “Khalifa” in the earth.” (Al-Baqara 2:30)

The tern Khalifa is often translated as vicegerent, deputy but it can also be translated as successors as in:

فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفٌ أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّہَوَٲتِ‌ۖ (٥٩)

“Then, came after them successors who neglected the prayers and followed lusts.” (Maryam 19:59)

This could mean that Prophet Adam and his progeny came to earth as successors of others who lived here. Allah also says:

وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡغَنِىُّ ذُو ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ‌ۚ إِن يَشَأۡ يُذۡهِبۡڪُمۡ وَيَسۡتَخۡلِفۡ مِنۢ بَعۡدِڪُم مَّا يَشَآءُ كَمَآ أَنشَأَڪُم مِّن ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوۡمٍ ءَاخَرِينَ (١٣٣)

And your Lord is Rich (All-Independent), full of Mercy, if He so wills, He can take you away, and in your place make whom He wills as your successors, as He raised you from the seed of other people. (Al-Anaam 6:133)

This verse implies that there were other people ahead of us and we came after them.

In all of these interpretations, it is important that we do not put restriction on Allah’s choices by our limited and biased knowledge; Allah says:

وَرَبُّكَ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيَخۡتَارُ‌ۗ مَا ڪَانَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ‌ۚ سُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَتَعَـٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِڪُونَ (٦٨)

And your Lord creates whatsoever He wills and chooses, no choice have they (in any matter). Glory be to Allah, and exalted He is above all that they associate (as partners with Him). (Al-Qasas 28:68)

Last week I explained an opinion for understanding verses 30-33: in surat Al-Baqara. Allah says:

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

“And when your Lord told the angels: I am placing a vicegerent (Khalifa) in the earth, they said: will You place in it someone who will cause mischief in it and shed blood, while we, we hymn Your praise and glorify Your holiness? He said: I know that which you do not know.” (Al-Baqara 2:30)

How did the angels know that the descendants of Adam will cause mischief and shed blood, In addition to the explanation I gave last week, one possible explanation is that Allah told them about the attributes of this new creation? This explanation may be justified because the angels told Allah:

قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ

“They said: Glory to You: we have no knowledge except what You have taught us, You are the all-knowing, the all Wise” (Al-Baqara 2:31-32)

Last time we offered one answer to the Question what were the angels hiding since Allah told them:

إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ

“I know what is unseen in the heavens and the earth and I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.” (Al-Baqara 2:33)

If we accept the suggestion that Allah explained to the angels the attributes of man and these included the evil side as well as the good side, the angels made their statement by focusing on the potential evil side of man and concealed in their statement the good and righteous side of this new creation.

Another point is explaining verse 172 from Surat Al-Araf in which Allah says:

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ

“When your Lord brought the offspring from the backs of the children of Adam, and made them bear witness about themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, indeed, we bear witness. Lest you might say on the Day of Resurrection: we were unaware of this?” (Al-Araf 7:172)

This verse suggests that we were created at the time of creation of Adam and this can be explained by the verses in Surat Al-Sajda in which Allah says:

ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنِ مِن طِينٍ۬ (٧) ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسۡلَهُ ۥ مِن سُلَـٰلَةٍ۬ مِّن مَّآءٍ۬ مَّهِينٍ۬ (٨) ثُمَّ سَوَّٮٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦ‌ۖ (٩)

He, Who made well whatever He created, and He began the creation of man from clay; (7) Then He made his progeny from a drop of despised fluid; (8) Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit. (Al-Sajda 32:7-9)

In these verses, there appears to be a step that occurred before Allah completed fashioning Adam and breathing in him the spirit which is the creation of Adam’s progeny. This step explains the hadeath that was reported by Imam Al-Tirmizi (الترمذي) and narrated by Abu Hurayrah (أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه), the Prophet (. PBUH) said:

“لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة”

“When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back and every soul of his offspring that Allah will create until the Day of Judgement fell from his back.

Remarks

1. Science does not always provide absolute truth but Allah’s revelation does. As far current scientific discoveries, it seems that they do not contradict the divine revelation.

2. Hope that I presented reasonable and consistent explanation of Adam’s and our creation based on the divine revelation.

3. But at the end it is up to you to accept this analysis or the analysis by others or offer you own an alternative scenario.

4. To complete the subject, the following are the verses that are used by those who propose a divine evolution of Prophet Adam from a human like creation:

Basis for those who suggest intelligent evolution form Human Like Creation: There are some Islamic scholars who suggests an intelligent evolution and that Adam evolved from the top of development from a human-like. They suggest that Adam evolved by Allah from a woman and support their opinion to the following verses that I have interpreted differently conforming the first creation.

وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡغَنِىُّ ذُو ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ‌ۚ إِن يَشَأۡ يُذۡهِبۡڪُمۡ وَيَسۡتَخۡلِفۡ مِنۢ بَعۡدِڪُم مَّا يَشَآءُ كَمَآ أَنشَأَڪُم مِّن ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوۡمٍ ءَاخَرِينَ (١٣٣)

And your Lord is Rich (All-Independent), full of Mercy, if He so wills, He can take you away, and in your place make whom He wills as your successors, as He raised you from the seed of other people. (Al-Anaam 6:133)

ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۥ‌ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنِ مِن طِينٍ۬ (٧) ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسۡلَهُ ۥ مِن سُلَـٰلَةٍ۬ مِّن مَّآءٍ۬ مَّهِينٍ۬ (٨) ثُمَّ سَوَّٮٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦ‌ۖ (٩)

He, Who made well whatever He created, and He began the creation of man from clay; (7) Then He made his progeny from a drop of despised fluid; (8) Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit. (Al-Sajda 32:7-9)

إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَ‌ۖ خَلَقَهُ ۥ مِن تُرَابٍ۬ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ ۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ (٥٩)

“The similitude of Jesus before God is as that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him: ‘Be’ and he was.” (Al-Imran 3:59)

يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٍ۬ وَٲحِدَةٍ۬ وَخَلَقَ مِنۡہَا زَوۡجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنۡہُمَا رِجَالاً۬ كَثِيرً۬ا وَنِسَآءً۬‌ۚ

“O mankind! Be dutiful to your Lord, Who created you from a single soul and from it He created her mate, and spread from them many men and women” (Al-Nisa 4:1)

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٍ۬ وَٲحِدَةٍ۬ وَجَعَلَ مِنۡہَا زَوۡجَهَا لِيَسۡكُنَ إِلَيۡہَا‌ۖ

“He is the One who has created you from a single soul, and out of her created her mate, to live in comfort with her.” (Al-Araf 7:189)

title: Amr Ibn Al -Aas (عمرو بن العاص)
excerpt:
