content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله.

Today Inshallah, I will give a brief account on the life of one of the Prophet’s companion and he is Amr Ibn AL-Aas. But before we discuss his life let me correct two misconceptions about him.

1. Amr ibn Al-Aas did not lead the Muslim army to invade or occupy Egypt, he rather went to liberate Egypt.

During the time of the revelation, the middle east was ruled by two opposing super powers, the Roman (Byzantine) Empire and the Persian Empire. Every country was occupied by one of them. Egypt was occupied by the Byzantine empire that oppressed the Egyptian thru heavy taxes and prosecution of anyone who objects to the tyrant rule.

This is important to keep in mind to realize that when Amr ibn Al-Aas entered Egypt, he did not enter as conqueror or as invader but rather as liberator. During Amr battles with the Roman army in Egypt, he ensured that the fight does not affect any of the local Egyptians. Upon the victory of the Muslim Army in Egypt, most the Egyptians embraced Islam. The reason for that goes back far before Islam.

At about 318 AD, religious turmoil started in Egypt because of the presence of two major churches. One in the North in Alexandria and was led by Bishop Alexander and one in the south and was let by a high priest called Arius.

Arius teaching was based on the following: “Christ was not one with the Creator, he was rather the Logos, the first and the highest of all created beings.”

Bishop Alexander objected to teaching of Arius, particularly, he had large followers and their number was continuously increasing. This is not the topic of today.

But it way of general interest to hear some of the arguments that Arius made: He said:
“If the Son had been begotten of the Father, it must have been in time, the Son therefore, could not be co-eternal with the Father.”

2. Amr ibn Al-Aas did not play a trick on Abu Musa al-Ashari (أبو موسى الأشعري) during the arbitration process.

During the Battle of Siffin (صفين) between the army of Ali and Muawiya, the recommendation was made for arbitration to stop the bloodshed between Muslims. The arbiters were Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, representing Ali, and 'Amr ibn al-'As, representing Muawiya.

The story that is often reported in history books that Amr tricked Abu Musa is not true as it has been documented by some scholars. It is logical that a man like Abu Musa who was wise and learned companion of the Prophet would not be easily tricked.

The true story is that both Amr and Abu Musa met and they agreed to a ruling which is to stop conflicts and let the Muslims decide for themselves.

We can discuss the details of the whole fitnah another day, but I just wanted to correct the false story that Amr ibn Al-Aas was a cheater or played a trick on Abu Musa.

Now, who is Amr Ibn Al-Aas.

Amr ibn al-Ās (عمرو بن العاص) (583 CE- January 6, 664 CE).
He was 13 years younger than Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) (570 CE – 8 June 632 CE) and he was 2 years older than Sayenda Omar ibn Al-Khattab.

His father was Al-Aas ibn Wa’il (العاص بن وائل السهمي ), one of the chiefs of Banu Sahm (بني سهم) clan of the Quraysh. He was a very rich and influential man in Mecca.

Amr’s mother was Salma bint Harmalah aka “Al-Nabighah” (سلمى ابنة حرملة، كانت تلقب بالنابغة), the granddaughter of:
سلمى بنت خزيمة بن الحارث بن كلثوم بن حريش بن سواءة بن جوشن بن عمرو بن عبد الله بن خزيمة بن الحارث بن سواءة بن عامر بن صعصعة.

Amr grow up to be great fighter and became known for his intelligent and tactics during the battles.

Amr was also very eloquent and combined with his intelligence, he was often selected as representative of Quraysh in many diplomatic missions.

He was also a trader and used to accompany caravans along the commercial trading routes through Asia and Africa. He visited Abyssinia (Ethiopia) many times and he knew the King of Abyssinia, An- Najaashiy (Negus).

Like the other Quraysh chiefs, he opposed Islam in the early days. Because of his relationship with An- Najaashiy (Negus), he was the one that the Quraysh sent to Abyssinia to convince the King to hand over the Muslims who migrated there to flee the prosecution of Quraysh. However, he failed to convince the King after he heard the Muslims and Ja’far ibn Abi Talib.

After the migration of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to Madina, Amr took part in all the battles that the Quraysh fought against the Muslims including Badr, Uhud and Al-Khandaq.

Amr ibn al-Ās was married to Umm Kulthum bint Uqba but he divorced her when she embraced Islam. She was one of the first women who migrated to Madinah.

Amr Ibn Al-‘Aas was not among the earliest ones to embrace Islam. He embraced Islam with Khalid Ibn al-Waleed and Uthman ibn Talha in the year 8 AH.

It is surprising that his Islam began at the hands of Al-Najaashiy in Abyssinia. In his final visit to Abyssinia, Amr asked the King about Mohammad (PBUH). The King asked Amr:
“How could you not believe in Mohammad and follow him, when he is truly a Messenger from Allah?”

Amr then asked An- Najaashiy,
“Is he thus?”

An Najaashiy answered,
“Yes, so obey me, O `Amr, and follow him, for indeed, by Allah, he is on the path of truth and he will certainly triumph over those who oppose him.”

Amr left straight to the port area, where he found a ship ready to sail. He went on board and sailed to Shuaibah (the port for Mecca at the time).

He bought a camel and traveled on toward Madinah. He passed through Marr Al-Zahran and went on until he reached Al-Hadda. There he saw two men who had also come to stay in Madinah.

One of them was inside the tent; the other was holding the reins of their two camels. Amr recognized Khalid ibn al-Waleed. Khalid said to Amr:
‘The way has become clear. The man is certainly a Prophet, and by Allah, I am going to become a Muslim. How much longer should I delay?’

Amr Ibn al-As answered,
‘I am travelling for the same reason. I have just returned from Abyssinia where An- Najaashiy (Negus) has already become a Muslim.’

Uthman ibn Talhah (عثمان بن طلحة) came out of the tent and they stayed there together that night.

So, the three of them traveled to Medinah to meet the Prophet (PBUH). When the Prophet (PBUH) saw them coming, he said to his companions:
“Mecca has surely given to you the flesh of its liver.”, meaning its most noble leaders.”

Khalid ibn Al-Waleed went first and declared the Shahadah and gave his pledge of loyalty to the Prophet (PBUH). Then Uthman ibn Talhah followed.

Amr was the third. Amr said: When I sat down opposite to the Prophet (PBUH) and said: I will give my pledge on one condition. The Prophet (PBUH) asked: “What is your condition?”. Amr said: “That all my past sins be forgiven.”

The Prophet (PBUH) said to me: “O Amr! Do you not know that embracing Islam wipes out all previous sins? When you embrace Islam, all your past sins are forgiven. When you emigrate for the cause of God, your emigration wipes out your past sins; and the Hajj (pilgrimage) also wipes out your past sins.”

I then declared the Shahadah and swore allegiance to him.

Following his conversion to Islam in the year 8 AH (629 CE), Amr rose quickly through the Muslim hierarchy. The Prophet (PBUH) put him in charge of an army of 300 to a mission called “Dhat as-Salasil”.

Dhat as-Salasil is a spot situated ten days’ walk north of Madinah. The news came to the Prophet (PBUH) that some tribes were gathering to attack Madinah.

When Amr reached there, he found that the enemy was much larger in number than he expected. He sent for reinforcement.

The Prophet (PBUH) sent to him 200 led by Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah (أبا عبيدة بن الجراح) among them were Abu Bakr and Omar.

When the reinforcement reached, Abu Ubayda wanted to lead the prayer, but Amr said: No, I am the commander and you are just a reinforcement. Abu Ubayda being the person he was, did not want to cause any conflict and he let Amr lead the prayer.

What Amr did is actually proper based on the Prophet’s commands regarding who should lead the prayer.
وعن أَبي مسعودٍ عُقبةَ بنِ عمرٍو البدريِّ الأنصاريِّ  قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُول اللَّه ﷺ: يَؤُمُّ الْقَوْمَ أَقْرَؤُهُمْ لِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ، فَإِنْ كَانُوا فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ سَوَاءً فَأَعْلَمُهُمْ بِالسُّنَّةِ، فَإِنْ كَانُوا فِي السُّنَّةِ سَوَاءً فَأَقْدَمُهُمْ هِجْرَةً، فَإِنْ كَانُوا فِي الْهِجْرَةِ سَوَاءً فَأَقْدَمُهُمْ سِلْمًا، وَلَا يَؤُمَّنَّ الرَّجُلُ الرَّجُلَ فِي سُلْطَانِهِ، وَلَا يَقْعُدْ فِي بَيْتِهِ عَلَى تَكْرِمَتِهِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ. (رواه مسلم)

“The person who can best read the Book of Allah will lead the people (in prayer). If they are equal in reading, then the one who has the most knowledge of the Sunnah. If they are equal in the Sunnah, then the one who migrated first. If they are equal in migration, then the one who embraced Islam first. Let not a person lead the prayer in the place of the person in authority and let him not sit in his place of honor, except by his permission.” (Reported by Muslim)”

This hadeath clearly give the highest priority is given to the person in authority and Amr was in Authority as the commander of the army.

After they returned to Madinah, some of the companions complained to the Prophet (PBUH) about Amr’s behavior during the mission. One of the complaints was that he did not allow them to light fire at night despite the cold weather. Amr explained that he did not want the enemy to know their location or their number. The Prophet (PBUH) accepted his reasoning.

The second complaint was related to Amr leading the prayers without “Ghusl” washing after Janabah and only doing “Tayammum” (dry ablution with sand).

When the Prophet (PBUH) asked him about it, Amr said: “O Messenger of Allah, it was extremely cold and I feared for my life if I used water. And I remembered the verse of Allah:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَأۡڪُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٲلَكُم بَيۡنَڪُم بِٱلۡبَـٰطِلِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَـٰرَةً عَن تَرَاضٍ۬ مِّنكُمۡ‌ۚ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمۡ رَحِيمً۬ا (٢٩)

“O you who believe! Eat not up your property among yourselves unjustly except it be a trade amongst you, by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves. Surely, Allah is Most Merciful to you. (Al-Nisa 4:29)

فضحك رسول الله ‏ ‏صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ ‏ولم يقل شيئا ) سنن أبي داود(
The Prophet (PBUH) laughed and did not say anything.

Amr was dispatched by the Prophet (PBUH) to Oman where he played a key role in the conversion of the local rulers, the two brothers Jaifer and ‘Abd, sons of Al-Julanda.

He carried a letter from the Prophet (PBUH) to them:
‏(‏بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم‏.‏ من محمد رسول الله إلى جيفر وعبد ابني الجلندي، سلام على من اتبع الهدي، أما بعد‏:‏ فإني أدعوكما بدعاية الإسلام، أسلما تسلما، فإني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الناس كافة، لأنذر من كان حياً ويحق القول على الكافرين، وإنكما إن أقررتما بالإسلام وليتكما، وإن أبيتما أن تقرا بالإسلام فإن ملككما زائل عنكما، وخيلي تطأ ساحتكما، وتظهر نبوتي على ملككما‏)‏‏.‏

“In the Name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the messenger of Allah to Jaifer and ‘Abd, sons of Al-Julanda. Peace be upon him who follows the right path. I invite you to the call of Islam. Embrace Islam and you will be safe. I am the messenger of Allah to all mankind to warn those who are alive and that the word (of Allah) may be proved true against the disbelievers. If you accept Islam, I will keep you as rulers of your land. But if you refuse, your kingdom will vanish, and my horsemen will occupy your land and my prophethood will prevail over your kingdom.”

‘Amr bin Al-’As narrates that when he arrived in Oman and before he was admitted into the audience of the two kings, he met ‘Abd, who was the younger but more approachable.

‘Amr told Abd:
I am the messenger of Allah’s Messenger coming with a letter from him to both, you and your brother.

‘Abd said:
You have to see my brother and read to him the letter you are carrying. He is my senior in both age and kingship. But tell me what are you calling for?

‘Amr replied:
أدعو إلى الله وحده لا شريك له، وتخلع ما عبد من دونه، وتشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله‏.‏
To invite you to believe in Allah Alone with no associates and discard any other deities and testify that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger.

‘Abd said:
يا عمرو، إنك ابن سيد قومك فكيف صنع أبوك‏؟‏ فإن لنا فيه قدوة
O ‘Amr! Your father was the chief of your people, tell me what did your father do because we consider him as a role model.

Amr said:
مات ولم يؤمن بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ووددت أنه كان أسلم وصدق به، وقد كنت أنا على مثل رأيه حتى هداني الله للإسلام
He died before believing in Muhammad (PBUH); I have wished that he had embraced Islam and been truthful to it. I was following his path until Allah guided me to Islam.

‘Abd:
When did you embrace Islam?

‘Amr:
When I was at Al-Nagashi (Negus’s) court. By the way, Negus did also enter into the fold of Islam.

‘Abd:
What was his people’s reaction?

‘Amr:
They approved of him and many followed his steps.

‘Abd:
How about the bishops and monks?

‘Amr:
Some of them did the same.

‘Abd:
Beware ‘Amr, there is no worst character in a man than lying.
(إنه ليس من خصلة في رجل أفضح له من الكذب‏).

‘Amr:
I never tell lies; moreover, our religion never allows it.
(ما كذبت، وما نستحله في ديننا)

‘Abd: Has Heraclius been informed of the Islamization of Negus?
(ما أرى هرقل علم بإسلام النجاشي)

‘Amr: Yes, of course.

‘Abd: How did you happen to know that?

‘Amr:
كان النجاشي يخرج له خرجاً، فلما أسلم وصدق بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال‏:‏ لا والله لو سألني درهماً واحداً ما أعطيته‏.‏ فبلغ هرقل قوله، فقال له أخوه يناق‏:‏ أتترك عبدك لا يخرج لك خرجاً، ويدين ديناً محدثاً‏؟‏ قال هرقل‏:‏ رجل رغب في دين واختاره لنفسه، ما أصنع به‏؟‏ والله لولا ضني بملكي لصنعت كما صنع‏.‏

Negus used to pay land tax to Hercules, but when he embraced Islam, he swore he would discontinue that tax. When this news reached Heraclius, his brother told him: are you going to leave one of your subjects stop paying you the tax and to believe in a new religion? Heraclius replied: The man liked a religion and chose it for himself, what can I do? By Allah, if I were not so attached to my kingdom, I would have done exactly what he did.

Abd: Look Amr to what you are saying.

Amr: By Allah, I am telling you the truth.

‘Abd: What does your Prophet command you to do?

‘Amr:
يأمر بطاعة الله عز وجل وينهي عن معصيته، ويأمر بالبر وصلة الرحم، وينهي عن الظلم والعدوان، وعن الزنا، وعن الخمر، وعن عبادة الحجر والوثن والصليب‏.‏
He commands us to obey Allah, the All- Mighty, the All-Glorious, and prohibits from committing sins. He commands us to be righteous and maintain the bonds of kinship. He prohibits from injustice, aggression, adultery, intoxicants, and the worship of stones, idols, or the cross.

‘Abd:
ما أحسن هذا الذي يدعو إليه، لو كان أخي يتابعني عليه لركبنا حتى نؤمن بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونصدق به، ولكن أخي أضن بملكه من أن يتركه فيصير ذنباً

Fair words and fair beliefs are those he is calling for. I wish my brother would follow me to believe in Muhammad [pbuh] and profess his religion, but my brother is too possessive of his kingship to become a subordinate.

‘Amr:
إنه إن أسلم مَلَّكَهُ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على قومه، فأخذ الصدقة من غنيهم فيردها على فقيرهم
Should he accept Islam; the Prophet would give him authority over his people and asks him to take zakat from the rich among them and return it to their poor.

‘Abd:
That is fair behavior. But what is this zakat you have mentioned?

‘Amr:
فأخبرته بما فرض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصدقات في الأموال، حتى انتهيت إلى الإبل
I described to him the divine injunction about the zakat and listed to him all the rules for the zakat.

‘Abd:
I don’t see from our people except being tight with money, I doubt it that many of them will accept it.
(والله ما أري قومي في بعد دارهم وكثرة عددهم يطيعون لهذا)

Amr stayed for some days to be admitted into Jaifer’s court until he was finally granted this permission. He read the letter of the Prophet (PBUH).

After a private talk with his brother and reconsidering the whole situation, both brothers embraced Islam.

The Prophet (PBUH) later made governor of the region until shortly after the Prophet’s death. Sayedna Abu Bakr then confirmed him in his post.

During the caliphate of Sayedna Omar assigned Amr to lead the army against the Byzantine in Syria in 634.

Amr was very daring and unhesitant. However, it was his great skill to get himself out of a destructive trap that he fell into.

When Artubun (ارطبون) invited Amr to talk, Amr accepted though he knew the danger but he wanted to see the fort from inside.

Amr met the commander, and their meeting ended. While Amr was on his way out of the fort, he glimpsed a look from the commander to one of his guards which he understood as a signal to kill him.

Instead of running away, Amr did something very clever.

He met the commander and said to him,
“An idea came across my mind I wanted you to know. I have with me, where we are camped, a group from the best of the Prophet’s companions and the leaders of the army. I was thinking to bring them to you so that they hear what I heard from you and maybe we can reach a peace treaty.”

The Roman commander Artubun (ارطبون) felt that Amr had granted him the opportunity of a lifetime. To kill all the leaders in one time.

Secretly he gave his order to put off the plan that was devised to assassinate Amr, and he saw Amr off at the gate with a big smile and handshake.

In the morning Amr returned to the gate if the fort with few men from his army with the rest of the army behind him and they conquered the fort.

After this victory, Amr convinced Sayenda Omar to allow him to liberate Egypt from the Byzantine.

In 43 hijra year and at the age of 81, death caught up with Amr Ibn Al-Aas in Egypt, where he was ruler.

During his last moments, he wept for a long time and said:
“In the first part of my life I was a disbeliever, and I was one of the fiercest people against the Prophet. Had I died then, I would have definitely gone to Hell. Then Allah put the love of Islam in my heart, and I went to the Prophet and swore allegiance to him. At that time, I loved no one more than him, and I could not even look at him directly out of respect. Had I died then, I would have hoped to be among the people of Paradise. Then I was given positions of authority and I do not know how I have fared.”

“Then he raised his sight to the sky in awe, calling upon his Lord, the Merciful, the Magnificent, with a humble heart.”

“Allah, I am not innocent, so forgive me. I am not mighty, so help me. And if Your mercy does not come to my rescue, I will surely be among the losers.”

And he continued in his yearning and his prayers until his spirit ascended to Allah and his last words were:
“There is no god but Allah.”

May Allah forgive Amr Ibn Al-As and grant his Jannah for what he has done for the sake of Islam,

Dua

title: The Unique Creation of Man
excerpt:

content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله

A question that has been perplexing to philosophers, scientist and theologians is the origin of man and two schools have emerged.  The creationist school believe that man was created as he is now by Allah and the father of all mankind is Prophet Adam. This school considers that thru the ages there were minor evolutionary changes that occurred in the physical features such as skin color.  These minor changes are influenced by the environment and the genetic makeup of the parents.

The second school is the evolutionist school that promotes the idea that the current man was developed through an evolutionary process.  Those who follow this school differ regarding whether this evolutionary process is random process or intelligent process.  While the theory of evolution may have metrics for animals and birds but when it came to man, it cannot be proven with any level of certainty.  The reason for the lack of certainty is that the creation of man cannot be deprived of celestial knowledge that can only be provided by divine revelation.  This point is clearly emphasized in the Quran:

مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ خَلْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمَا كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُدًا

“I did not have them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation; and I would never take misleaders for helpers.” (Al-Kahf 18:51)

In this talk, I am going to try, inshallah to explain the verses in the Quran in which Allah opened the door of heaven to us to reveal the story of our creation.  The story of the creation of man is the first story in the Quran and it is provided in verses 30-33 in Surat al-Baqara.  The creation of man is mentioned in several other chapters because of its importance and our keen interest.  But, let us focus for now on the first introduction of the story in Surat Al-Baqara.  Allah says:

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

“And when your Lord told the angels: I am placing a vicegerent (Khalifa) in the earth, they said: will You place in it someone who will cause mischief in it and shed blood, while we, we hymn Your praise and glorify Your holiness? He said: I know that which you do not know.”  (Al-Baqara 2:30)

وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنْبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَاءِ هَؤُلَاءِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ

“And He taught Adam all the names; then He placed them before the angels and said:  Tell me their names if you are truthful.  They said: Glory to You: we have no knowledge except what You have taught us, You are the all-knowing, the all Wise” (Al-Baqara 2:31-32)

قَالَ يَا آدَمُ أَنْبِئْهُمْ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ فَلَمَّا أَنْبَأَهُمْ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ

“He said:  o Adam, tell them their names.  When he told them their names, Allah said: Didn’t I tell you that I know what is unseen in the heavens and the earth and I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.” (Al-Baqara 2:33)

In analyzing these verses, I want to address the following 3 questions:

1. How did the angles know than man will cause mischief in the earth and shed blood? The speculative answer to this question may have prompted some Muslims to suggest that evolution occurred by suggesting that man-like people inhabited the earth and caused mischief and shed blood.  But some interpreters of the Quran suggested that the earth was inhabited by the jinn and they are the ones who caused mischief and shed blood.
2. When the angels made their statement, they apparently haven’t not stated the complete truth because they were hiding something and this why Allah told them: “I know what you revealed and what you have concealed”. The question is what information did the angels conceal that is related to the nature on man?
3. What are the names that Allah taught Adam and the angels did not know? But in answering this question, it may be important to rationalize that the names must be related to something that refutes the angels’ claim that this man will cause mischief and shed blood while they hymn Allah’s praise and glorify His holiness.

Let first link these verses to another set of verses in Surat Al-Araf.  In verse 11, Allah reveals important information that happened before Allah’s command to the angels to prostrate to Adam.  The information is related to the creation of all human being including you and I at the same time as Allah says:

وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ

“We created you, then shaped you; then We said to the angels prostrate to Adam and they prostrated except Iblis who was not among those who prostrated.” (Al-Araf 7:11)

This verse implies that the creation of mankind was done in three steps with some time delay between as implied by the article (ثُمَّ) meaning “then”.  The first step is the creation of all human beings (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ), then the second stage of shaping all of us (ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ).  The third step is Allah’s command to the angels to prostrate to prophet Adam.

The open question is at what stage Allah told the angels that He is making/assigning a khalifa in the earth (إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً).  It has to be before Allah asked the angels to prostrate to Adam to be consistent with the verses in Surat Al-Baqara.  But it is reasonable to assume that Allah told them that He will assign a khalifa in earth after He created and shaped all human beings.

After our creation we died and only Prophet Adam remained. After this death, we will come alive through the womb of our mothers to live on earth for a while and then die again to be raised alive again in the Day of Judgement. This means that we are subjected to two deaths (death after our creation and death after living in earth) and we have two lives (life in earth and then life in the hereafter).  This is clear in the Quran as Allah informs us by saying:

قَالُوا رَبَّنَا أَمَتَّنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ فَاعْتَرَفْنَا بِذُنُوبِنَا فَهَلْ إِلَى خُرُوجٍ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ

They said: “O our Lord, You have made us to die twice and have brought us to life twice!  (Ghafer 40:11).

كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتًا فَأَحْيَاكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ

“How can you disbelieve in Allah when you once were dead and He gave you life, then he will make die once more and then He brings you back to life, and unto Him you will return.” (Al-Baqara 2:28)

There are several ahadeath that provide more insight on the details of our creation in heaven.   In a hadeath reported by Imam Al-Tirmizi (الترمذي) and narrated by Abu Hurayrah (أبي هريرة -رضي الله), the Prophet (PBUH) said:

“ لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة وجعل بين عيني كل إنسان منهم وبيصا من نور ثم عرضهم على آدم فقال: أي ربي من هؤلاء؟ قال: هؤلاء ذريتك فرأى رجلا منهم فأعجبه وبيص ما بين عينيه فقال: يا رب من هذا؟ قال: هذا رجل من آخر الأمم من ذريتك يقال له: داود قال: يا رب كم عمره؟ قال: ستون سنة قال: أي رب أعطه من عمري أربعين سنة فأخذ الله عليه الميثاق فلما انتهت المدة جاء ملك الموت ليقبض روح آدم فقال: أولم يبق من عمري أربعين؟ قال: أولم تعطها لابنك لداود؟ فنسي آدم ونسيت ذريته وجحد آدم وجحدت ذريته وخطئ آدم فخطئت ذريته ”

“When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back and every soul of his offspring that Allah will create until the Day of Judgement fell from his back. Allah put on the forehead of every one of them a flash of light, then showed them to Adam. Adam asked: “My Lord who are they? Allah said: They are your offspring.

Adam saw one of them and he was charmed by a bright flash between his eyes. He asked: My Lord, who is this? Allah said: he is a man from the late nations from your descendants and his name is Dawoud (David).

Adam asked:  My Lord, what is his age?  Allah said: sixty years.

Adam said: My Lord give him from my age 40 years.  Allah took the covenant from Adam that is his demand.

When the angel of death came to Adam, he protested and said there are forty years remaining in my life. The angel of death, didn’t you give it to your son Dawoud (David)

Adam forgot and all his children forget. Adam denied it and all his children deny.  Adam made mistake and all his children make mistakes.

In another similar hadeath reported also by mam Al-Tirmizi (الترمذي) and also narrated by Abu Hurayrah but through others, that the age of every person was written on his forehead and this how Adam knew the age of prophet Dawoud, also Allah told Adam that his age is 1000 years, this is when Adam told Allah to give Dawoud 40 years of his.

In another similar hadeath that was narrated by Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس) in which its stated:

قال ابن عباس : إن الله لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره ، وأخرج ذريته كلهم كهيئة الذر ، فأنطقهم فتكلموا ، وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ، وجعل مع بعضهم النور ، وإنه قال لآدم : هؤلاء ذريتك أخذ عليهم الميثاق : أنا ربهم ، لئلا يشركوا بي شيئا ، وعلي رزقهم . قال آدم : فمن هذا الذي معه النور؟ قال : هو داود . قال : يا رب كم كتبت له من الأجل؟ قال : ستين سنة . قال : كمت كتبت لي؟ قال : ألف سنة ، وقد كتبت لكل إنسان منهم كم يعمر وكم يلبث . قال : يا رب زده . قال : هذا الكتاب موضوع فأعطه إن شئت من عمرك! قال : نعم . وقد جف القلم عن أجل سائر بني آدم ، فكتب له من أجل آدم أربعين سنة ، فصار أجله مائة سنة ، فلما عمر تسع مائة سنة وستين سنة جاءه ملك الموت; فلما رآه آدم قال : ما لك؟ قال له : قد استوفيت أجلك . قال له آدم : إنما عمرت تسع مائة وستين سنة ، وبقي أربعون سنة . قال : فلما قال ذلك للملك ، قال الملك : قد ، أخبرني بها ربي . قال : فارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ! فرجع الملك إلى ربه ، فقال : ما لك؟ قال : يا رب رجعت إليك لما كنت أعلم من تكرمتك إياه . قال الله : ارجع فأخبره أنه قد أعطى ابنه داود أربعين سنة .

The light of the face of the descendants was not on all of them but only some and among them with the brightest was Prophet Dawoud.  This hadeath implies that those who have light were the Prophets and the righteous.

Another hadeath reported by Ubay ibn Kaab (أبي بن كعب) in which the Prophet (PBUH) said that Adam saw the prophets with sharp light over them (ورأى الأنبياء فيهم مثل السرج عليهم). This hadeath and the previous one clearly indicate that the Prophets were identified at that time by the light over them.

While the descendants of Adam were standing, Allah took the pledge from all of them including you and I to worship none but Him.  This is revealed to us verses 172 and 173 of Surah Al-Araf in which Allah said:

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ

“When your Lord brought the offspring from the lions of the children of Adam, and made them bear witness about themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, indeed, we bear witness. Lest you might say on the Day of Resurrection: we were unaware of this.  Or lest you say, it was our forefathers who were polytheists and we are their late offspring, will You destroy us for what futile men have done?” (Al-Araf 7:172-173)

In interpreting this verse Ubay ibn Kaab (أبي بن كعب) narrated ahadeath in which the Prophet (PBUH) said that Adam saw the prophets with sharp light over them when the descendants of Adam took the pledge. At that time, Allah took a second and special pledge from those Prophets.

عن أبي بن كعب في قوله : ( وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم ) قال : جمعهم ، فجعلهم أزواجا ، ثم صورهم فاستنطقهم فتكلموا ، ثم أخذ عليهم العهد والميثاق وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ” ألست بربكم قالوا بلى ” قال : إني أشهد عليكم السماوات السبع [ والأرضين السبع ] ، وأشهد عليكم أباكم آدم أن تقولوا يوم القيامة : لم نعلم بهذا ، اعلموا أنه لا إله غيري ولا رب غيري ولا تشركوا بي شيئا ، إني سأرسل إليكم رسلي يذكرونكم عهدي وميثاقي ، وأنزل عليكم كتبي . قالوا : شهدنا بأنك ربنا وإلهنا ، لا رب لنا غيرك ، ولا إله لنا غيرك ، ورفع عليهم آدم – عليه السلام – ينظر إليهم ، فرأى الغني والفقير وحسن الصورة ودون ذلك ، فقال : يا رب لولا سويت بين عبادك ؟ قال : إني أحببت أن أشكر ، ورأى الأنبياء فيهم مثل السرج عليهم ، خصوا بميثاق آخر في الرسالة والنبوة ، وهو قوله تعالى : وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم إلى قوله : عيسى ابن مريم – عليهما السلام – كان في تلك الأرواح ، فأرسله إلى مريم – عليها السلام –

This scene of having all of Adam’s descendant standing in front of Allah will be repeated again on the Day of Judgement as Allah describes it to us in Surat Al-Kahf as He says:

وَعُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا

“And they will be marshaled before your Lord in lines, (with the announcement), “Now you have come back to Us as We created you the first time; yet you thought We wouldn’t make an appointed time for you. “(Al-Kahf 18:48)

The assembly of verses clearly show than we have not evolved but rather we, all,  were created by Allah at the time of Adam’s creation.  Therefore, none of us is an accident, our parents may not have planned us, but Allah did.  Long before we were conceived in our mothers’ womb, we were conceived by Allah.

From these verses, it is expected that the angels were witnessing all these events.  The question is at what point Allah told them that He will make Adam and his descendants khalifa on earth.  The likely time is after we faced our first death and only Adam remained. Therefore, the angels must have seen the light on the face of some of Adam’s descendants.  One of those whom the light was bright on his face was Dawoud,

Now, let us connect the dots and explain the verses in Surat Al-Baqara.

1. The angels were aware of Adam and his decedents’ but did not know their role until Allah told them that He will make Adam khalifa on earth.
2. The angels expressed concern that those descendants will cause mischief and shed blood. But Allah told them that they do not know.
3. Allah taught Adam all the names (الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا), but the names must be the names of those who will refute the angels claim.  Who are best to refute the angels claim other those on whose face there were light and one of them is Prophet Dawoud.  The names that Adam learnt are the names of all Prophets whom the angels saw but did not know their names.
4. This hypothesis explains why Allah told the angels that He knows what they declared and what they were concealing. The angels were concealing that among the descendants of Adam there will be Messengers of Allah and Prophets and those will neither cause mischief nor shed blood.  In fact, those descendants will hymn Allah’s praise and glorify His holiness more than the angels. This is also supported by why prophet Dawoud specifically was identified in the hadeath.  Two observations:
    1. In the whole Quran the title Khalifa was stated only twice, one related to prophet Adam and the second time to Prophet Dawoud.

    يَـٰدَاوُ ۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَـٰكَ خَلِيفَةً۬ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ

    “O Dawoud! Verily! We have placed you as “khalifa” a vicegerent on earth.” (Sad 38:26)

    1. The Quan clearly identifies prophet Dawoud as the one with whom many creations join him in Glorifying Allah,

    وَسَخَّرۡنَا مَعَ دَاوُ ۥدَ ٱلۡجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحۡنَ وَٱلطَّيۡرَ‌ۚ َ

    “And We subjected the mountains and the birds to glorify Our Praises with Dawoud (David)” (Al-Anbiya 21:79)

    وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُ ۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِ‌ۖ إِنَّهُ ۥۤ أَوَّابٌ (١٧) إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُ ۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِىِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ (١٨) وَٱلطَّيۡرَ مَحۡشُورَةً۬‌ۖ كُلٌّ۬ لَّهُ ۥۤ أَوَّابٌ (١٩)

    “ And remember Our slave Dawoud (David), endued with power. Verily, he was ever oft-returning in all matters and in repentance. (17) Verily, We made the mountains to glorify Our Praises with him in the early evenings and early mornings. (18) And (so did) the birds assembled all obedient to him [to glorify Allah’s Praises along with him]. (Sad 38:17-19)

The last point in refuting the angels claim by them admitting man has actually worshipped Allah more than them.  The Prophet (PBUH) said:

قال رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلّم-: «يوضع الميزان يوم القيامة فلو وزن فيه السموات والأرض لوسعت، فتقول الملائكة يارب لمن يزن هذا، فيقول الله تعالى لمن شئت من خلقي، فتقول الملائكة ” سبحانك ما عبدناك حق عبادتك، ويوضع الصراط مثل حد الموسى، فتقول الملائكة من تجيز على هذا، فيقول من شئت من خلقي، فيقولون سبحانك ما عبدناك حق عبادتك

“The balance is placed on the Day of Resurrection, the heavens and the earth can be easily weight with it. The angels asked: “O Lord, who will be weigh by this? Allah says: Whoever I wish from my creation. So the angels will say, “We have not worshipped you as you deserve to be worshipped.

Then the Sirat will be place with a razor edge.  The angels say: who is permitted to pass on this? Allah says: whoever I wish from my creation. They will say: , and you will be from my creation. The angels will say: We have not worshipped you as you deserve to be worshipped”.

This implies that those whom Allah will weight with the scale and will pass across the Sirat are those who have worshipped Allah more the angels to deserve this honor.  While the angels may worship Allah more in quantity but they do not face difficulties, temptations and calamities that man faces and challenges his commitment for worship.  But those who are able to continue to worship and paise Allah in face of all these challenges are the one who really the ones whose worship of Allah is the worthiest.

Last point to make is related to Allah response when the angels questions many suitability to be khalifa and Allah told them (إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) “I know that which you do not know”. If Allah said (انى اعلم ما لن تعلموه), it would have meant I know what you would not know.  But when Allah said: (إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) “I know that which you do not know””, this means that you don’t know now but you may know in the future.

Hope that I presented reasonable and consistent explanation of man’s creation based on the divine revelation.  But at the end it is up to you to accept this analysis or the analysis by others or offer you own an alternative scenario

Dua

title: On the Occasion of Rabi al-Awwal – Islam in Two Words
excerpt:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله .

Today is November 3rd, 2019, Rabi…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينة ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله .

Today is November 3rd, 2019, Rabi al-Awwal 6, 1441 AH. About 1450 years ago on the same month of Rabi Al-Awwal, something important happened. A person was born who changed the face of history and without him, we would not have been here today. On this month, Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) was born. As discussed last week, his birth was expected by many Christian and Jewish scholars. In fact, the name Mohammad for the upcoming Prophet was also known.

It is reported that few years before the birth of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH), while one of the Arab tribes from Mecca was travelling north, they met a Christian monk who asked them where they had come from. When they replied that they were from Mecca, he told them that Allah would soon send a prophet from their area who would guide them to a new way of life. They asked about the name of this prophet and the monk told them that his name would be Mohammad.

Some of the Arabs who heard this prophesy hoped that such a Prophet will be from among them and called their new born son Mohammad. Five (5) children who were born before the birth of Prophet Mohammad were called Mohammad and they were:

1. Mohammad ibn Sufian ibn Mugashee (محمد بن سفيان بن مجاشع)
1. Mohammad ibn Ahiha ibn Galah al-Awsee (محمد بن احيحه بن الجلاح الاوسي)
2. Mohammad ibn jasan al-gahfi (محمد بن جسان الجعفى)
3. Mohammad ibn Baraa Al-Bikry (محمد بن براءة البكرى)
4. Mohammad ibn Khosaee Al-Salame (محمد بن خزاعى السلمى)

A sixth one was born after the birth of Prophet Mohammad and was also called Mohammad
1. Mohammad ibn Musaylamah al-Ansari (محمد بن مسيلمة الانصارى).

It may have been of Allah’s plan that several people are called Mohammad as protection for Prophet Mohamad (PBUH).

You all know the detailed account of the birth of Prophet Mohammad (PBUH) and therefore, I’ll not discuss it. However, I’ll, inshallah, discuss the last few days of his life on earth that also occurred in this month of Rabi al-Awwal. The reason, I am focusing on this part of the Prophet’s life because it is expected that when a person is on his death bed, he will be giving the most important advices to his family.

This is what we expect the Prophet (PBUH) would have done and he (PBUH) did; therefore, we should always keep his last advice in our mind.

Before I discuss the last few days in the life of the Prophet (PBUH), let me address an issue that appears to always create controversy among Muslims at the time of the Prophet’s birthdate. This issue is the concept of Bida (بدعة) (Innovation)

There are two key hadeath on the subject that are often quoted:

It was common that the Prophet (PBUH) say in the he beginning of the Friday Khutba:
(إن أصدق الحديث كتاب الله، وأحسن الهدي هدي محمد، وشر الامر محدثاتها، وكل محدثة بدعة، وكل بدعة ضلالة، وكل ضلالة في النار. ) سنن ابن ماجه- سنن النسائي – مسند أحمد-صحيح مسلم
“The most truthful speech is the book of Allah and the best guidance is the guidance of Mohammad and the worst of matters is novelty and every novelty is Bidah (innovation) and every Bidah (innovation) is misguidance and every misguidance leads to the Hell fire”.

The Prophet (PBUH) also said:
عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (من أحدث في أمرنا هذا ما ليس منه، فهو رد ) رواه البخاري ومسلم
“Whoever introduces in our matter (i.e. Islam) that which is not from it, it is rejected”.

What is the Bidah (innovation)?
Linguistically, Bidah (innovation) is bringing something original that did not exist before.
Bidah (innovation) is related to the word ‘Ibdaa” (إبداع) (Creative) that is used when you describe the work poets, artists and scientists. Allah describes Himself as the Innovator, Creator, Originator of the heavens and earth:

بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ
“Originator (Creator) of the heavens and the earth: when He decrees a matter, He said to it: “Be,” and so it becomes. “(Al-Baqara 2:117)

While the Prophet (PBUH) condemned making a Bidah (innovation), he (PBUH) encouraged making new Sunnah (norm, custom) as he said:

عن المنذر بن جرير عن أبيه - عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال “من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة كان له أجرها وأجر من عمل بها من بعده من غير أن ينتقص من أجورهم شيء ومن سن في الإسلام سنة سيئة كان عليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها من بعده من غير أن ينتقص من أوزارهم شيء) صحيح مسلم- مسند أحمد -سنن ابن ماجه- سنن الدارمي
“Whoever establishes in Islam a good sunnah he will have its reward and the rewards of everyone who follows it without reducing the reward of the followers and whoever establishes in Islam a bad sunnah he will have its penalty and the penalties of everyone who follows it without reducing the penalty of the followers.”

There are some scholars who consider introducing anything that the Prophet (PBUH) did not do is prohibited Bidah (بدعة). They even consider the word good Bidah (بدعة حسنة) which is reported that Khalifa Omar (RA) used to describe his decision to institute the congregational Taraweeh prayer as unacceptable and prohibited.

But there are other scholars such as Al-Izz Ibn Abdul Salam Al-Qurafi (ra) who consider the term “good Bidah” (بدعة حسنة) as acceptable Islamic term and they differentiate between “good Bidah” and “bad or prohibited Bidah”. They consider a prohibited Bidah is anything that is not of the religion and is claimed to be part of the religion or instituting something in the religion that is not obligatory and declare it as obligatory.

They consider any innovation in the Shariah forbidden because Allah declared that He already completed our religion, as He said:
الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا
“Today, I have completed your religion for you, fulfilled My favor upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion.” (Al-Maeda 3:5)

Allah also says:
أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ شَرَعُوا لَهُمْ مِنَ الدِّينِ مَا لَمْ يَأْذَنْ بِهِ اللَّهُ وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةُ الْفَصْلِ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
“Do they have partners who legislate for them some religious matters without the permission of Allah? Had it not been for the decisive statement, the matter would have been decided among them. The wrong-doers will have a grievous Penalty.” (Al-Shura 42:21)

Whether one uses the term Good Bidah (بدعة حسنة) or use the term good Sunnah (سنة حسنة), the important issue is to seek the Prophet’s criterion for assessing what is truly prohibited Bidah. The key hadeeth is the statement of the Prophet (PBUH) that was related by Sayeda Aysha (RA) which is:

عن عائشة رضي الله الله : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من أحدث في أمرنا هذا ما ليس منه فهو رد )سنن ابن ماجه, مسند أحمد, صحيح مسلم (
“Whoever introduces something new (innovates) in our matter (i.e. Islam) that is not from it, it is rejected”.

The key term in this hadeath is the Prophet’s use of the proposition “Minhu” (منه) which is translated is “from it” and he (PBUH) did not use the proposition “Fihi” (فيه) which is translated as “in it”. There us subtle difference between the two terms “in it” and “from it”.

As example, sitting together so everyone reads separate part of the Quran is considered acceptable Bidah by those who focus on the content which in this case is reading the Quran which is obviously part of the religion even though neither the Prophet (PBUH) nor the companions used this form of sitting together. But others who focus on the form and not on the content will consider this activity as prohibited Bidah.

This difference occurred even among the companions of the Prophet (PBUH) after his death with some considering an action prohibited Bidah while others consider it good Bidah.

As an example, Abduallah ibn Omar considered praying the Duhaa (ضحى) in the Masjid as prohibited Bidah (innovation). Here, the objection was not for the prayer itself which is Sunanh, but for doing it in the Masjid.
عن مجاهد قال دخلت أنا وعروة بن الزبير المسجد فإذا عبد الله بن عمر جالس إلى حجرة عائشة والناس يصلون الضحى في المسجد فسألناه عن صلاتهم فقال بدعة )صحيح مسلم -صحيح البخاري- مسند أحمد (

On the other hand, Sayedan Omar considered holding the Tarweeh prayers in the Masjid under a single Imam as good and desirable Bidah (innovation), though some companions objected to his ruling on the ground that the Prophet (PBUH) did not institute it.
يحدثنا التاريخ أن عمر بن الخطاب دخل المسجد النبوي في ليلة من ليالي رمضان فوجد الناس يصلون النوافل أوزاعاً، فرأى أن يجمعهم على إمام واحد، فجمعهم على أبي بن كعب، فلما خرج في الليلة التالية وجد الناس خلف إمام واحد منتظمين يصلون في حركة واحدة متسقة، فقال: نعم البدعة جاء بها عمر

Even scholars who consider all innovations as prohibited, accept innovations that have been instituted by some companions and consider them as good, though other companions objected to them as Bidah at that time; these include:

1. Assembling the Quran in one book. Sayedna Abu Bakr was reluctant when the idea was first introduced by Sayedna Omar because the Prophet (PBUH) did not do it.
2. The addition of a second call for the prayer during the Jummah prayer by Sayedna Othman.
3. The arrangement of the Quran the way we have it now on the instructions of Sayedna Othman. - عثمان للقرآن على الترتيب الذي عليه المسلمون حتى اليوم
4. Placing dots on the words of the Quran. نقط يحيى بن يعمر المصاحف. رواه أبو داود السجستاني
5. The placing of grammatical marking on the words of the Quran on the advice of Sayedna Ali. – وضع أبي الأسود الدُّؤَليِّ قواعد النحو بعد استشارة علي كرم الله وجهه

One major reason for the strong sensitivity of some scholars to anything that was not done by the Prophet (PBUH) is their classification of certain clear violations to the instructions of the Prophet (PBUH) as being Bidah (innovations). As an example, many scholars consider building mosques on the grave of righteous people and the travel of people to visit these Mosques, and also holding an annual celebration at them, as Bidah (innovation) that leads to acts of Shirk. However, these acts should not be classified as Bidah (Innovations) because they are in clear violation of commands by the Prophet (PBUH) who said:

عبد الله بن الحارث النجراني قال حدثني جندب قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول قبل أن يموت بخمس من كان قبلكم كانوا يتخذون قبور أنبيائهم وصالحيهم مساجد ألا فلا تتخذوا القبور مساجد إني أنهاكم عن ذلك ) صحيح مسلم (

“People before you used to take the graves of their prophets and righteous people as mosques and I prohibit you from doing the same.”

There are some issues that create controversy and division among Muslims that are not wise to discuss because there are differing opinions among scholars regarding whether thay are good innovations of prohibited innovations.

If you are really interested in the subject, you should read the basis on which each group of scholars derived their opinion and follow the one that your heart feels more comfortable with. But you should respect the opinion of others who may feel more comfortable with the basis of the other opinion.

Our attention should always be focused on uniting the Muslims and curbing these differences. This is not simply an act of being overly accommodative, as some may contend, but, respect of scholarly opinions that are also based on proofs from Islamic Law. It is important to maintain the unity among Muslims which is an obligation. Allah said:

وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلا تَنَازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ ) الأنفال 8:46)
“Obey Allah and His Messenger; and do not fall into disputes, lest you lose heart and lose your power; and be patient and persevering: for Allah is with those who patiently persevere.” (Al-Anfal 8:46)

وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا وَاخْتَلَفُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ وَأُوَلَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ ) آل عمران 3:105)
“Be not like those who are divided amongst themselves and fall into disputations after receiving Clear Signs: for them is a dreadful Penalty (Al-Imran 3:105).

So, respect those who want to take the occasion of the birth of the Prophet (PBUH) and hold respectable events to study his life and say prayers on him. No one will ever force you to engage if you don’t want to.

Back to the subject which is reflecting on the last few days in the Life of the Prophet (PBUH)

On the early days of Safar in the eleventh year of Al-Hijra, the Prophet [PBUH] entered the Masjid and ascended the pulpit and addressed the people by saying:

(إني فرط لكم، وأنا شهيد عليكم، وإني والله لأنظر إلى حوضي الآن، وإني أعطيت مفاتيح خزائن الأرض، ولكني أخاف عليكم أن تنافسوا فيها).
“I may precede you and I have been made witness upon you. By Allah, you will meet me at the basin very soon. I have been given the keys of worldly treasures. By Allah, I do not fear for you the return to being polytheists after me. But I do fear that you will start competing in the acquisition of worldly riches (enticing you to fight each other).” [Sahih Al-Bukhari 2/585]

The Start of the Disease
On Monday the twenty-ninth of Safar in the eleventh year of Al- Hijra, the Prophet (PBUH) participated in funeral rites in Al-Baqee‘. On the way back he suffered a headache and his temperature rose so high but he (PBUH) continued to lead the prayers for eleven days though he was sick.

Five days before death
On Wednesday, the 7th of Rabi Al-Awal in the twelveth year of Al- Hijra, the Prophet’s temperature rose so high signaling the severity of his disease. He asked that they pour water on him to bring the temperature down to allow him to talk to the people.” When this was done, he (PBUH) felt well enough to enter the Mosque and sat on the pulpit with the people gathering around him. He (PBUH) said:

(لعنة الله على اليهود والنصارى، اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد) (لا تتخذوا قبري وثناً يعبد).
“The curse of Allah befalls upon the Jews and Christians for they have made their Prophets’ tombs places of worship, do not make my tomb a worshipped idol.”

Then he invited the people to take recompenses for any injuries he might have inflicted on them, saying:

(من كنت جلدت له ظَهْرًا فهذا ظهري فليستقد منه، ومن كنت شتمت له عِرْضاً فهذا عرضي فليستقد منه).
“He whom I have ever lashed his back, I offer him my back so that he may avenge himself on me. He whom I have insulted, here I am offering myself that he may avenge himself.”

He, then, descended, and performed the noon prayer. Again, he returned to the pulpit and sat on it and said

(إن عبداً خيره الله بين أن يؤتيه من زهرة الدنيا ما شاء، وبين ما عنده، فاختار ما عنده)
“Allah has given a slave the opportunity to make a choice between whatever he desires of this world provisions, and what Allah He has with Him. He chose what is with Allah.”

Upon hearing what the Prophet (PBUH) said, Abu Bakr started weeping and shouted:
فديناك بآبائنا وأمهاتنا
‘We sacrifice our fathers and mothers for your sake.’

People wondered why Abu Bakr got very emotional since the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) was only talking about a slave of Allah who was granted the right to choose between the best fortunes of this world and the bounty of Allah in the Hereafter.

Four days before his death
In spite of the strain from the disease and the pain that the Prophet (PBUH) was suffering, he continued to lead the prayers until Thursday, the 8th of Rabi Al-Awal. On that day the Prophet (PBUH) led the Maghrib prayer and commanded three things:
1. Other than Islam, no other religion should remain in Arabia.
2. Delegations should always be honored and entertained.
3. The mobilization of Osama’s army should continue.
The Prophet (PBUH) returned to his room and laid down with severe pain.

The Last Day Alive
On Monday, the 12th day of Rabi Al awl, pain grew so much severe, but the Prophet (PBUH) was able to remove the cover over his face and said several times to his family and companions who were around him:

(الصلاة، الصلاة، وما ملكت أيمانكم)،
“The prayers, the prayers! And those who are under your responsibility”.

These were the last two words of advice/commands that the Prophet (PBUH) said to the Muslims.
These two words summarize the whole Islam, the relationship with the creator and the relationship with the created.
These two words represent the measure of success on earth, cleansing our soul thru prayers and demonstrating the purity of our soul thru treatment of others
These two words consolidates all the obligations in Islam that every Muslim must ensure their implementation to their fullest. Ignoring this command of holding fast of the prayers will take the person out the fold of Islam. The prophet (PBUH) said:

عن بريدة بن الحصيب رضي الله عنه رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ” العهد الذي بيننا وبينهم الصلاة فمن تركها فقد كفر ” رواه احمد وابو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه
“The covenant between us is the prayer, and whoever neglects it has disbelieved.”

Fulfilling one’s responsibility towards all those who are under his control and they could be the spouse, the children, other family members and employees. The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (أَلَا كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ، وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ،...
Indeed, every one of you is shepherd and everyone is responsible for his flock.
This means treating them justly, giving them their rights, honoring them, treating them fairly and remembering that Allah is watching you all the time.

The End:
After uttering these two words, the Prophet (PBUH) put his hand in a water container next to him; he (PBUH) and wiped his face and pointed to everyone to leave to the room and pointed to Sayeda Aisha to come close and she held his head over her thighs and after few minutes he (PBUH) raised his hand and said:

قَالَتْ عَائِشَةَ - رضي الله عنها كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ َرَأْسُهُ عَلَى فَخِذِي غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ أَفَاقَ فَأَشْخَصَ بَصَرَهُ إِلَى سَقْفِ الْبَيْتِ ثُمَّ قَالَ اللَّهُمَّ الرَّفِيقَ الأَعْلَى فَكَانَتْ آخِرَ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا اللَّهُمَّ الرَّفِيقَ الأَعْلَى) رواه البخاري (4463) ومسلم (2444)
“O, Allah, the Companion of the High, the Companion of the High”.

And his righteous soul departed his body to be with the Most High.

Dua

title: Those Who are Given Over by Allah to the Evil Forces
excerpt:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله

You have most likely met people who are…
content:
الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا
وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدًا عبده ورسوله

You have most likely met people who are very educated and you wonder how can they not realize that their belief or lack of does not make any sense.  You must have also seen reports about people who commit major atrocities and wonder how can any human being commit such crimes. 

The Quran is unique because it very hard to confront a question without finding in it an answer to the question or a hint to lead you to the answer.  Regarding this unique feature of the Quran, Allah tells us in Surat Al-Nahl that it contains everything

وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ تِبۡيَـٰنً۬ا لِّكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةً۬ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ (٨٩)

We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur’an) as an exposition of (explaining) everything, a guidance, a mercy, and glad tidings for the Muslims. (Al-Nahl 16:89)

Allah also said:

ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء

“We have neglected nothing in the Book” (Al-An’am 6:38)

كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ} [إبراهيم: 1]

“ (This is) a Book which We have revealed unto you (O Muhammad SAW) in order that you deliver mankind, with the will of their Lord, out of darkness into light leading them to the Path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. ” (Ibrahime 14:1)

Abdullah ibn Abbas said

(لو ضاع مني عقال بعير لوجدته في القرآن) عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنه

“Even if the halter (rope) of my camel is lost, I will find it in the Book of Allah.

Abu Hurrirah reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ” إن الله سبحانه وتعالى لو أغفل شيئاً لأغفل الذرة والخردلة والبعوضة ” رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره ، وأبو الشيخ بن حيان في ” كتاب العظمة .

“If Allah almighty had overlooked something, he would have omitted the atom, the mustard seed and the mosquito.”

So, we should find that answer to these complex questions in the Quran.  This answer may come in terms of a divine rule that those people are subjected to.  In this regard, we can find in the Quran a critical rule that implies that Allah has established evil forces in this world to be assigned to those whose arrogance to prevent them from accepting His guidance.  Allah gives those people many chances to repent and return to Him, but at some point, Allah no longer is interested in guiding them and he unleashes on them the evil forces to keep them astray from the truth and encourage them to commit injustices and beautify for them immorality.   This rule is derived from the following verses:

سَأَصۡرِفُ عَنۡ ءَايَـٰتِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كُلَّ ءَايَةٍ۬ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِہَا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرُّشۡدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً۬ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً۬‌ۚ ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّہُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡہَا غَـٰفِلِينَ (١٤٦)

“I shall turn away from My Ayat (verses, revelation) those who behave arrogantly on the earth, without a right, and (even) if they see all the Ayât (proofs, verses, revelations, etc.), they will not believe in them. And if they see the way of righteousness, they will not adopt it as the Way, but if they see the way of error, they will adopt that way, that is because they have rejected Our Ayât (proofs, revelations, etc.) and were heedless (to learn a lesson) from them” (Al-Araf 7:146)

وَيَوۡمَ يُحۡشَرُ أَعۡدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ (١٩) حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَہِدَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَـٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٠) وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَہِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَا‌ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ۬ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ۬ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ (٢١) وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡہَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَـٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَـٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرً۬ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ (٢٢) وَذَٲلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمۡ أَرْدَٮٰكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرِينَ (٢٣) فَإِن يَصۡبِرُواْ فَٱلنَّارُ مَثۡوًى لَّهُمۡ‌ۖ وَإِن يَسۡتَعۡتِبُواْ فَمَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُعۡتَبِينَ (٢٤) ۞ وَقَيَّضۡنَا لَهُمۡ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُواْ لَهُم مَّا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيہِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ وَحَقَّ عَلَيۡہِمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فِيٓ أُمَمٍ۬ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ‌ۖ إِنَّہُمۡ كَانُواْ خَـٰسِرِينَ (٢٥)

“And (remind them of) the day when the enemies of Allah will be musterted towrads the Fire, so they will be driven into it (19)
------
And We have assigned them intimate companions (in this world), who beautified for them, what was before them (evil deeds) and what was behind them (denial of the the Hereafter as regards punishment or reward). And thus the Word (i.e. the punishment) is justified against them along the communities that passed before them from the jinn and men. Indeed they (all) are the losers.” (Fussilat 41:25)

وَمَن يَعۡشُ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ نُقَيِّضۡ لَهُ ۥ شَيۡطَـٰنً۬ا فَهُوَ لَهُ ۥ قَرِينٌ۬ (٣٦) وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّہُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ (٣٧)

“And whosoever turns away blindly from the remembrance of Al-Rahman (Allah), We appoint for him Shaitân (a devil) to be an intimate companion to him. (36) And verily, they (devils) hinder them from the (right) Path while they think that they are guided.” (Al-Zukhruf 43:36-37)

أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمۡ أَزًّ۬ا (٨٣) فَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ عَلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۖ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمۡ عَدًّ۬ا (٨٤)

“Have you not seen that We have sent the Shayâtin (devils) onto the disbelievers to incite them with all their incitements. (83) So make no hurry about them; We are but counting for them a countdown (the remaining number of the days of the life that they may increase in evil and sins).” (Maryam 19:83-84)

You may say why Allah created these evil forces and why Allah pushes those evil forces on those who reject the truth so they can transgress even further. 

The answer is quite simple,

لَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفۡعَلُ وَهُمۡ يُسۡـَٔلُونَ (٢٣)

“He cannot be questioned as to what He does, while they will be questioned.” (Al-Anbiya 21:23)

So, asking why Allah does something is not befitting because it is not proper for a slave to ask the master. We must realize that whatever rule Allah establishes, it must be for good reason and there must be a wisdom behind it even if we never understood this wisdom. 

Allah does not owe us any explanations and while understanding can wait, submission cannot, if we are true believers.  Insisting on knowing why Allah established certain rules is a sign of arrogance and Allah gave this grave warning to those who are arrogant:

سَأَصۡرِفُ عَنۡ ءَايَـٰتِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ (١٤٦)

“I shall turn away from My Ayât those who behave arrogantly on the earth, without a right,” (Al-Araf 7:146)

The Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن عبدالله بن مسعودٍ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ((لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرةٍ من كبرٍ)) رواه مسلم

“No one will enter Paradise who has an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart”.

The wise person should instead of focusing on why Allah assign evil forces to certain people to make Hell justifiable for them, is to focus on avoiding of being one of those people. 

You may also ask but those evil people hurt good people and here you need to understand a key nature of this life which is:  Life is time for testing.  Everyone will be subjected to regular testing to assess who truly deserves to be in Heaven and who truly deserves to be in Hell. 

The concept of life as a test has been made abundantly clear in many verses in the Quran. Allah says in surah Al-Ankabout:

أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا أَنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لَا يُفْتَنُونَ (2) وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكَاذِبِينَ (3) أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ أَنْ يَسْبِقُونَا سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ (4) مَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَاءَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ لَآتٍ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (5)

“Do people think that they will be left alone on saying, “We believe,” and that they will not be tested? We did test those before them, so Allah can affirm who the truthful are and who the liars are. Do those who do evil think that they will get unnoticed by Us? How foolish is their judgment! For those who hope to meet Allah, the time appointed by Allah is surely coming: and He hears and knows all things.” (Al-Ankabout 29:2-5)

Allah also says:

كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ (35)

“Every soul shall have a taste of death: and We test you with misfortune and with blessing by way of trial. To Us you must return.” (Al-Anbiaa 21:35)

While we may not know when or how we are going to be tested, we can predict the nature of some of the tests from the Quran and we can also learn how we should respond to these tests, as Allah says in surah Al-Baqara:

وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ وَالْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَنْفُسِ وَالثَّمَرَاتِ وَبَشِّرِ الصَّابِرِينَ (155) الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (156) أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ (157)

“We shall surely test you with some fear and hunger, and some loss in wealth, lives and the fruits of your labor. But give glad tidings to those who are patient.  Who say when misfortune strikes them: We belong to Allah and to Him is our return; they are those on whom Allah grants blessing and mercy, and they are the rightly guided.”? (2:155-157).

But Allah is merciful and Just and thus, no one will be subjected to a test that he/she cannot handle.  Allah says:

وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۖ وَلَدَيْنَا كِتَابٌ يَنطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ ۚ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ) المؤمنون - الآية 62(

“And We do not impose a burden on anyone except according to his capacity, and with Us is a Record which speaks the truth, and they will not be wronged.” (Al- Mumenoon 23:62)

There should be no doubt in our mind that the presence of evil in the world does not negate the perfection of Allah’s actions.  The real question is how do we react to evil? 

Obviously if you see evil in the world and stand idle complaining about it, you would have failed the test. 

The Prophet (PBUH) has taught us three ways to remove evil in his famous Hadeeth that is reported in Muslim and was narrated by Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( من رأى منكم منكرا فليغيره بيده ، فإن لم يستطع فبلسانه ، فإن لم يستطع فبقلبه ، وذلك أضعف الإيمان ) رواه مسلم .

“Whoever sees an evil must correct it with his hand, if he cannot then by his tongue, if he cannot, then by his heart and this is the weakest of faith”.

So, if you cannot do anything about evil, you should at least reject it with heart by not supporting those who are doing it in anyway. 

But, this discussion about the presence of evil and assigning evil forces to encourage evil people to transgress further raises the old philosophical argument that is framed as follows:

Since Allah knows all what the person will do
And since Allah’s knowledge is perfect and never wrong
Then the person must do what Allah has already known

This implies that the person is compelled to do what Allah has already known. How can this be justice to justify punishing such a person?

This philosophical argument must be false because we know that Allah is the absolute Just and He will never do injustice to anyone. Allah says:

وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمً۬ا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ مَّا ڪَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ (٢٨١)

“And be fearful of the Day when you shall return to Allah. Then every person shall be paid what he has earned, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly” (Al-Baqara 2:281)

إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا وَلَٰكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ) يونس – الآية 44(

“Surely, Allah does not wrong people at all; but people do wrong themselves” (Younes 10: 44)

But this philosophical argument that since Allah knows in advance what I’ll do wrong, I must do it and thus how can I be responsible for it, is false for several reasons:

First: The clear teaching of Islam that every person has free will and that no one will be held accountable for what he does under force. Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet (PBUH) said:

عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (إن الله تجاوز عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استُكرهوا عليه) حديث حسن رواه ابن ماجة والبيهقي وغيرهما

Verily Allah has pardoned for my nation their mistakes, their forgetfulness, and that which they have been forced to do under duress. [reported by Ibn Majah, Al-Bayhaqi, and others]

(The exception to forgiveness for doing something under duress is what the action involves hurting others such as killing.  It is not acceptable for a person to save his own life on the expense of another person life.)

But, even announcing disbelieve, Allah does not hold the person accountable if he declared the disbelief under duress, Allah says:

من كفر بالله من بعد إيمانه إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان (النحل :106)

“Whoever disbelieved in Allah after his belief, not the one who is compelled under duress while his heart is content with belief.” (Al-Nahl 16:106)

Allah does not leave anyone one without guidance but only those who reject the guidance are let astray, Allah says:

إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا

“We guided him to the path; he will either be grateful or be ungrateful.”(Al-Insan 76:3)

The verse state that Allah has programmed every one of us with an innate (intrinsic, inborn, natural, imposed) guidance to know Allah and equipped us with the capacity to differentiate truth from falsehood. 

But if this is not sufficient, Allah provides guidance thru instructions by appointing prophets and messengers to teach and manifest His revelations.  Allah refers to this element of universal guidance in in Surah Fusulat (فصلت) when Allah discussed the people of Thamud and the guidance sent to them thru Prophet Saleh. Allah says regarding Thamud:

وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَى عَلَى الْهُدَى فَأَخَذَتْهُمْ صَاعِقَةُ الْعَذَابِ الْهُونِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ) فصلت(

“As to the Thamud, We gave them guidance, but they preferred blindness (of heart) to Guidance: so the stunning Punishment of humiliation seized them, because of what they had earned.’ (Fusulat 41:17)

Therefore, we must realize that Allah does not let people go astray until they truly deserve it after they exhaust all their opportunities for guidance and remain steadfast on their rejection of all sources of guidance and continue with their mischief. 

وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

“And when it is said to them: do not make mischief in the earth, they say: we are only improving matters.  They are indeed making mischief but they are not aware of it.” (Al-Baqara 2:11-12)

So, we know that Allah does not punish anyone who is forced to do evil and thus it is illogical that Allah Himself will be forcing people to do evil and then punish them.  Also, Allah does leave people to go astray until they have exhausted all their opportunities to be guided. 

The argument that Allah pre-knowledge of what people will do is reason for them doing evil is refuted on humanistic level and legal one.  We know that we have free will and we only do what we want to do and legally courts differentiate between premeditated and unintentional actions. 

The reason for the confusion happens because we as human beings have limited abilities to rationalize the absolute attributes of Allah and thus, we cannot relate to His infinite knowledge, infinite justice, infinite power, etc.  The philosophical argument states:

Since Allah knows all what the person will do
And since Allah’s knowledge is perfect and never wrong (because they are infinite)
Then the person must do what Allah has already known

Any time we talk about something infinite our logic fails, here is an example:

You will have no objections if I say:
Since x + a   = x + b
Then a = b
This means that if “x” equals 10 and “a” equals 7, then “b” must also be equal 7. 

This is only valid is “x” is finite but if “x” is so large that it is infinity (∞), this logic fails because I can say:
∞ + 10 = ∞ + 1000
But we know that 10 is not equal to 1000.  The reason is that for an infinite number all the following relationships are valid

∞+a=∞          ∞−a=∞
∞∗a=∞           ∞÷a=∞

So, you cannot use logic that is based on finite input to apply to an infinite input. 

There is another point that makes the whole argument wrong because the way it is made, it jumps between different attributes of Allah.  The statements are related to Allah’s knowledge but having knowledge does not mean having external impact.  External impact can only be achieved by another attribute which is ultimate ability (قدرة). 

Knowledge cannot create external impact unless they are associated with ability.  So, if you really want to frame the argument, you should say as follows:

Since Allah has full knowledge of what you will do
Since having knowledge will have no external influence
My action is based solely on my will and Allah does not force me to do them. 

While Allah offers guidance to all people, there is unique guidance that Allah only offers to those who accept the innate guidance created in them and the guidance offered by the revelation through the Prophets, this is the guidance of support. 

This concept of this guidance of support of those who accepted the universal guidance is illustrated by the following verse in Surah Mohammad:

وَالَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زَادَهُمْ هُدًى وَآتَاهُمْ تَقْوَاهُمْ  )محمد(

“But to those who consent to be guided, He increases their guidance, and bestows on them their piety and restraint (from evil).” (Muhammad 47:17)

This point is emphasized when you read that Allah increases the guidance of those who are already guided, as He says:

وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى   )مريم(

“Allah increases guidance for those who are guided” (Maryam 19:76)

So, when Allah speaks about not guiding someone, he is peaking about the guidance of support that He offers only to those who deserve it by accepting the universal guidance.  So, when we read the following verse in Surah Al-Qasas, we recognize that Allah is speaking about the special guidance which is guidance of support:

إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ

“You will not be able to guide every one whom you love; but Allah guides those whom He wishes and He knows best those who accepted guidance. (Al-Qasas 28:56)

In addition to the universal guidance and the support guidance, there is actually a third type of guidance and this is the sustaining guidance.  It is the guidance that you need to properly answer the angles in the grave about who is lord and who is your messenger.  Allah says:

يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ ۖ وَيُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الظَّالِمِينَ ۚ وَيَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ )إبراهيم(

Allah reinforces those who believe with the proper response, in this world and in the Hereafter; but Allah leaves the wrongdoers to go astray: Allah does whatever He wills. (Ibrahime 14:27)

You also need this guidance to project light in front of you to stay on the path to heaven. In this regard Allah says:

سَيَهْدِيهِمْ وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَهُمْ وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ عَرَّفَهَا لَهُمْ ) محمد(

“He will guide them and improve their condition, and admit them to the Garden which He has announced for them. (Mohammad 47:5-6)

Allah also says regarding this guidance, that it will take a form of light:

يَوْمَ تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ يَسْعَى نُورُهُمْ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ بُشْرَاكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ ) الحديد(

“On that day you will see the believing men and the believing women with their Light streaming on ahead of them and off their right: (their greeting will be): “Good News for you this Day, gardens through which rivers flow to live in forever. That is indeed the highest Achievement.” (Al-Hadead 57:12)

Dua
